MECOENATES GRATIOSI, PATRONI SUMMI, FAUTORES MAXIMI,

GNome Prophetica, נדיב נדיבות יעץ quam à teneris, Symboli loco, elegi, digna est, quæ semper resonet in auribus nostris, imò, quæ aureis literis scribatur in cordibus nostris. Vulgarius reddidit: Princeps quæ digna sunt Principe, cogitabit, Non emendat, pro more ac instituto suo, Hosiander, (id enim nominis Theologo fuit,) vocem autem נדיב κατ' ἀντονομασίαν accepit, de Principe Regum terræ, Christo Jesu Ap. I, 5. qui opponatur stulto, Anti-Christo puta, quem præprimis, ob Epicureismum notorium, Psal. XIV, 1. sq. descriptum, hic respici vult. Ecquis enim ei opponetur rectius, quam ipsa sapientia hypostatica, Filius Dei, Prov. VIII, 23. c. IX, 13. Luc. XI, 49. Stultus fatua, id est, impia, perversa loquetur, & cor ejus faciet iniquitatem, non pie & bene administrabit Rempublicam: ut perficiat simulationem, seu hypocrisin, ut loquatur ad Dominum fraudulenter, id est, hoc aget; ut instruat hypocriticam Religionem, & ut vacuam faciat animam esurientis, & potum sitienti auferat: id est, eò comparata erunt omnia, ut suorum misero- rum subditorum opes exhauriat, eosque esurire & sitire sinat, ut habet Osiandrina paraphrasis. For- tè, nec incommodè, de fame ac siti spirituali accipietur, ex Am. VIII, 11. sq. Zach. IX, 17. Deut. VIII, 3. Matth. IV; 4. Huicenim consulere, pn Principis opus est, cum maximè principa- le, Esa. XLIX, 23. Psal. XXIV, 7. in quo præit Rex Regum, Dominus Dominantium Apoc. XVII, 14. c. XIX, 16. Rectori, Principibus, Dominis omnibus, Iob. VI, 15. 27. 32. sq. Prov. XIX, 5. Esa. LV, 2. Apoc. II, 17. Esa. XXX, 20. 21. Jer. III, 15. Psalm. XXIII, 1. Apoc. VII, 17. Addit Propheta: Et ipse super Ducis; seu Principes (Apostolos) stabit, id est, eminebit præ Apostolis, & omnibus aliis, præcipuè Ecclesiæ Doctoribus: Illi enim omnes ad pedes Ejus, ceu Magistri unici, sedebunt, Matth. XXIII, 10. Act. XXII, 3. Lyranus, Thomas, Hugo, Vatablus, B. Lutherus, Cramerus in Summariis: Sanctius, Cor- nelius à Lapide, Menochius, Tirinus, Adamus Sasbouth, Emanuel Saa, de Ezechia, & jam Hugo Gro- tius (pessime conferens Esa. IX, 6.) Hieronymus verò Procopius, Cyrillus Alexandrinus, Haymo, Brentius, Osiander, Hutterus in Summariis, Paraphrastæ Vinarienses: Oecolampadius item, Zwin- glius, Calvinus, Piscator, Iunius, Paraphrasta Belgici, Amama, alii, de Christo. Tirinus de Eze- chia, ut typo, de Christo, ut antitypo, interpretantur, ac duces de Apostolis, quos ita vocat Hieropsaltes in Epithalamio Christi, constitues eos Principes, super omnem terram Ps. XLV, 17. & Ps. LXIIX, 28. Principes Juda Duces eorum. Osiander, ut dixi, Anti-Christum Regem impio- rum primipilum, & præcipuum, in antithefi notari potissimum vult, qui præ aliis נבל stul- tus, vel Epicureus, & avarus, cujus cupiditatem hactenus mundus explere non potuit, nec non hy- pocritarum pessimus: quamvis fortè alios non excludat.

Sed dictum primo sensu generale est. Vox נדיב de quovis munifico adhibetur, Exod. XXXV, 5. 22. De populo Domini sancto Ps. CX, 5. Populus tuus עמר נדבות liberalitatem, vel spontane- us, Ps. CXIX. v. 108. Oblationes spontaneas oris mei (τὰ ἑκούσια) accepta nunc Domine: Idcircò γενικῶς hæc interpretati sunt Vatablus & Musculus: Ille, liberalis liberalia consultat: hic, beneficus benefica cogitat. Nec aliter in translatione sua Megalander: Fürsten sollen Fürstliche Gedancken haben: Quos illud Davidicum dispersit, dedit pauperibus, omninò decet. Eò etiam abit Commentarius ejus Latinus: Habet liberales cogitationes, quomodo prosit, & commodet omnibus. Sentit enim se ideò institutum, ut PROSIT potius, quam PRAESIT, ut serviat potius, quam domine- tur. Subordinatæ sunt, non oppositæ ἰκθέσεις. Quod in genere dicitur de bono, cur non

EPISTOLA DEDICATORIA.

ad optimum liceat applicare? aut si de idea Principis, vel optimo Principum κυριολέκτως agar, quid prohibet, id de universis intelligere, quum omnes ad instar illud se componere debeant. Sic alibi ὅι ό nomen נדיב generaliter accipientes, transtulerunt, ἄρχων, Princeps, Job. XII, 21. c. XXI, 28. c. XXIV, 18. Pf. XLVI, 9. LXXXII, 10. CVI, 40. CXII, 7. CXVII, 9. CXLV, 2. Esa. XIII, 2. βασιλεὺς Rex, Proverb. XIX, 6. τύρανν Proverb. IIX, 16. (ubi tamen Aquila, & Theodo- tio ἐξουσιαζόμενοι, B. Lutherus die Könige) vel πρόθυμ, Promtus, Paral. XXIIX, 21. 2. Paral. XXIX 31. vel καταδεχόμεν, suspiciens, Exod. XXXV, 5. vel δικαι, Justus, Prov. XVII, 7. In nostro textu variant: Priorem vocem exponunt, οἱ ἐυσεβεις, pii, posteriorem συνετὰ, sapientia vel prudentia. Est etiam, ubi interpretentur illam ὁι δυνάται potentes, Jud. V, 9. 1. Reg. II, 8. Prov. XVII, 27. c. XXV, 7. & verbum cognatum ισχύει VALET. Deut. XVI, 10. vocem נדיבה ἡγεμονικῶς, principalis reddidere Pf. L, 13. B. Lutherus sanctus exposuit: in verbis immediatè hic sequentibus, placuit LXX. in- terpp. vertere βουλὴν consilium. Quæ verò rectius eodem cum prioribus sensu accipit ὁ πάνυ. Qui autem factum, quod etiam semel interpretati sint ἡ ἐλπὶς, spes, nimirum Job. XXX, 15. vel quod ὁμολόγως manifestè transtulerint: Quod tamen non plus vice simplici observo in Concordan- tiis Kircherianis utilissimis, Hos. XIV. 5. Item: quod ὁμολογίαν confessionem, Deuter. XII. 6. Eze- chiel, XLVI. 13. Amos IV. 1. προσφερόμενα, oblata, Exod. XXXVI, 2. σφάγιον, victima, Levit. XXII, 23. δῶμα donum, Deut. XXIII, 24. II. Par. XXXI, 14. selegerint, non capio, nisi fortè respexerint, quod cum voluntate & consilio eligatur hæresis. Et, ut ad principium redeamus, PRIN- CIPEM, inquam, ἀρχὴν principium, Psalm. CIX. 4. vel quod hæc voluntaria esse debeant, & ἀφαίρεσμα separatio, Exod. XXXV. v. 27. ut & αἵρεσις Electio, Lev. XXII. v. 18. 21. Nam cæteroquin frequentissime allibuit ipsis τὸ ἑκούσιον, voluntarium, Lev. VII, 6. c. XXIII, 38. Num. XXIX. 39. Efdr. I. 4. 6. c. VIII. 26. Psalm. LIII. 6. LXVII, 10. CXIX. 107. & καθ̔εκούσιον Num. XV. 3. E quibus, si cum nostro ea contendas aphorismo, multa peti possent, sive similitudinis, sive exemplo- rum gratia, ad sensum dilucidandum, & ad amplificationem dictorum non jucundam fa- cientia, quem morem magnis & ingeniosis Oratoribus Ecclesiasticis, (ad applicationem enim non tam judicium, quam ingenium ςοχαςικὸν requiritur) non ingratum, auditorio & dulcem & fructuosum esse, si opportune adhibeatur, negari non potest,

Sed ad apophthegma Propheticum! Significata præcipua vocis, ut solet, diligenter colligit Kircherus: נדיב Spontaneus, liberalis, munificus, beneficus, habens animum heroicum ad benefaciendum. Addidit: Vocantur ita communiter Magistratus, & Principes, qui à Deo excitati, ut in subditos se beneficos, & liberales exhibeant. Verbum יעץ est proponere in animo, consulere, seu consilium inire, consultare, deliberare, decernere, quod consilium sit quasi stratum seu stragu- lum super quo actiones consistunt, βουλεύειν, συμβουλεύειν, συνάγειν, συνετίζειν, ἀγγέλλειν, ἀπαγγέλλειν, γινώσκειν, secundum LXX. viralem versionem. Cognata sunt illa pleraque: Nam consi- lium cum annunciatur, in notitiam venit: Nec ignorari potest, cum decernitur, nec con- sultatio institui cum alio, sine animi sensuum manifestatione, vel annuntiatione, nec delibera- mus nobiscum, quin animo nostro quid proponamus, nec decernimus, quin penes mentem nostram quid statuamus, aut expendamus, eligendum id sit, an non? Principis ergo, & cujusvis renati, qui Spiritu S. (Spiritu principali Davidi dicto, Psalm. LI, 3.) instructus, & ad offerenda Deo sacrificia sive Levitica, sive mystica, πρόθυμ, h. e. pransus & paratus est, voluntaria, inquam, & spontanea, quæ sola, si per fidem sistantur, Deo grata sunt, virtus propria est liberalitas, & munificentia in medium promptè consulendi, quod ex usu fiet, cum publico, tum privato, inque rem conferendi, quod aliis inserviat, qui consilio, vel auxilio egeant.

Tales ἄρχοντες sunt & Doctores Ecclesiæ, etsi non ut ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύειν, vel κα- τεξουσιάζειν, sed ut Principes vel Duces spirituales ἐυεργέται esse debeant. Matth. XX, 25. Luc. XXII. verf. 25. memores illius Petrini I. Ep. IV. 10. ἕκαςος καθὼς ἔλαβε χάρισμα, εις ἑαυτὺς αὐτὸ διακονῦντες, ὡς καλοὶ οἰκονόμοι ποικίλης χάριτος θεοῦ: Et quod Paulus habet II. Cor. IX. 7. ἰλαρὸν δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεὸς: Maximè verò, quod Christus, in exemplum nobis propositus, verus ille נדיב, Paulo Actor. XX. 35. memorante, dixit: Μακάριόν ἐςι διδόναι μᾶλλον, ἢ λαμβάνειν. Quod qui negli- gunt, paganis gemini habendi, è quibus Delus Timoclis, Athenæo lib. VIII. cap. 11. lauda- tus, contrarium τῶ נדיב gnomen suam fecit: ἀνόητος ὁ διδὺς, ἐυτυχὴς δὲ ὁ λαμβάνων: Insanus est qui dat, beatus, qui accipit: Quid? deteriores sunt Ethnicis sanioribus, quorum mentem Plutarchus π. Φιλοπλυτ: expressit: οἱ μᾶλλον ἐθέλουσι πλουτεῖν, καὶ κακοδαιμονοῦντες, ἢ μακάριοι γενέσθαι δόντες ἀργύριον. Demosthenes utique rogatus, quid Deo simile haberent homines; respondit, benefa- cere, testis Maximus I. serm. X. Xenophontis etiam dictum minimè paganum fuit: Multo præ- clarius ac laudabilius esse beneficiorum, quam trophæorum multitudinem post se relinquere. Verita- tem verbi Jesu, quod filiis hujus seculi vèrè παράδοξον, & olim inter ἄγραφα fuit, confirmant, nosque ad praxin aphorismi excitant, rationes ejusdem probè hic recolendæ, quas aliorum verbis exprimere juvat. Tunc bene, quod Gregor. M. lib. XXVIII. Moral. cap. 6. optime mo- nuit, multiformis Dei gratia dispensatur, quando acceptum donum etiam ejus, qui hæc non habet, credi- tur, quando propter eum, cui impenditur sibi datum putatur. Hæc summa est, ait de Doctoribus alter Gregorius ὁ Θεόλογος, Nazianzenus Episcopus, orat. 1. Apol. ut possint purgari primum, deinde purgare, sapientia instrui, atque ita ALIOS SAPIENTES REDDERE, lumen fieri, & ALIOS COLLUSTRARE, accedere ad Deum, & alios adducere, sanctificari, & aliis sanctitatem afferre. Nihil enim profecto, docente eodem Theologo 1. Orat. XVI. DIVINUM habet homo, quam benefacere. Nulla devotione fidelium, inquit Leo M. Serm. in Quadrages. magis Dominus dele- ctatur; quam ista, qua pauperibus ejus impenditur, & ubi curam misericordiæ invenit, ibi imaginem suæ pietatis agnoscit. Non timeatur in iis expensis defectio facultatum, quoniam ipsa benignitas ma- gna substantia est, nec potest largitatis deesse materies, ubi Christus pascit, & pascitur. In omni hoc opere illa intervenit manus, quæ panem frangendo auget, & erogando multiplicat. Securus & hila- ris sit eleemosynæ distributor, quia tunc maximum lucrum habebit, quando sibi minimum reservaverit, dicente B. Apostolo Paulo; Qui autem administrat semen seminanti, & panem ad manducandum præ- stabit, & multiplicabit semen vestrum, & augebit incrementa, frugum justitiæ vestræ, in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Dare signum est abundantiæ, accipere egestatis, inquit Augustinus lib. III. contra Max. c. 14. Ideoque beatior est impartientis largitas, quam accipientis penuria, & habet Cassianus lib. X. de justit. renunc. c. 18. 19. Nam secundum Vallesium, Sacr. Phil. c. 88. liberalis largi- tionis extremum non est bonorum vacuitas, sed adjectio potiorum, puta honestatis & honoris. Ac- ceptio vero est egestatis. Honorabilior quippe est, qui dat, vilior, qui accipit, docente Hieronymo ad Nep. Ex adverso ut hoc παραφυαδικῶς adjicere liceat, in malis & injuriis beatius est acci- pere, quam dare. Quo de homiliam edidit S. Chrysost. num. LXXVIII. ad pop. Antiochen. Quod melius est injuriam pati, quam inferre. Patienti enim jus totum referat cælum, sanctorum cives efficit, à peccatis absolvit, coronat justitia. Hoc ergo fac, monet aureum os, & in cælum re- spiciens cogita, quod illic super Cherubim sedenti factus es similis. Proinde non minus verè, quàm concinnè Artaxerxes ὁ μακρόχειρ, Longimanus dictus, quem Estheræ maritum, sed præ- ter meritum, cùm Josepho, Sulpitio Severo, Nicephoro, Cardinali è Societate Jesu, ψευδωνύμως, & κατ' ἀντίφρασιν ita dicta, quod de alterius nomine initiali vulgò creditur, eruditione cæteros hujus seculi facile præcellente, Bellarmino nempe, nec non gemino ejusdem purpurato, ac Jesuitis (Efavitas rectius dixeris) aliis, Sanctio, Petavio, Saliano, Henrico Philippi, Autore item Compendii Chronolog. Historici Gothani, non pauci è Chronologis, euntes, non qua eundum est, sed qua itur, fecere: cum sequi potius hic cum Brentio, & Funccio debuerint B. Lutherum, quod Dario Hystaspidæ, templi restauratori præcipuo, populi Domini sospitatori, hæc relin- quenda sit pietatis & munificentiæ gloria. Longimanum enim verius Artachsastam, cujus edictum & munificentia, in cultum divinum impensa, prorsus ἀξιομνημόνευτος, & Rege tanto digna, ab ipso Spiritu S. celebratur, aliisque principibus פריצים in exemplum sistitur, Esther. VII. cum veteres plerique Chronologi Julius Africanus, Eusebius, Hieronymus, & Patres non pauci, Græci & Latini, tum Recentiores temporum Scriptores, & Pontificii & Reformati, Usserius, Bailius, Lansbergius, Samsonius; & Evangelici, Chytræus, Christian Matthiæ, Joh. Cluve- rus, Gottfried Vogelius, Schillingius, Langius, Autores compend. Histor. Eccles. Ernestin. statuerunt: De quibus quantum satis in Chronico nostro sacro. Dixisse ille fertur, Plutarcho in Apopth. Reg. commemorante: Sibi tanquam principi, manum ad dandum, dextram scilicet, esse longissi- mam, sinistrum vero contractam, & brevissimam: Regalius enim esse addere, quam adimere. Nam & Deus ad dandum est longimanus, ad accipiendum verò brevimanus, imò nullimanus.

Liberalitas ejusmodi dubio procul à gratis agnoscetur mentibus, in communicatio- ne Bibliorum Illustratorum Veteris & Novi Testamenti, in Systematis LL. CC. exhibitione, in aliis, cum exegeticis, tum elenchticis, adversus Novatores potissimum, utputa Socinianos, Arminianos, Calixtinos, Cothurnum metaxycum ex inferis resuscitantes, Grotium, Nicolai, Fanaticos alios, publicæ luci donatis: Quæ quanti constiterint, quantilli autem jam veniant, συγκρίσει pru- denti æstiment Lectores: Jugulum enim Novatorum ferire, citra ambiguum difficilius est, quàm veteribus resistere. In hoc enim conflictu præivere alii. At illic sine duce pugnan- dum erat, ubi lubricitas adversariorum sæpè ne id quidem permittebat, ut agnoscerentur antagonistæ versipelles, & variegati.

Eâdem liberalitate sisto Ecclesiæ, sisto Saxoniæ Nostræ inclutæ, sisto Nominibus ve- stris Excellentissimis QUARTUM TOMUM BIBLIORUM ILLUSTRATO- RUM, in hisce oris Saxonicis, & cœptorum & ad finem, Deo soli sit honor & gloria! perdu- ctorum: Postquam enim primum POTENTISSIMO ELECTORI JOHANNI GEOR- GIO II. Ah vivat hoc conclamato tempore, floreatque Rutæ instar Princeps summè Ne- cessarius Ecclesiæ quàm diutissimè. Consecravi alterum SERENISSIMO ELECTORA- TUS HÆREDI, JOHANNI GEORGIO III. Quem vitæ redditum servet manus divina Ecclesiæ solatio quàm felicissimè! Tertium Illustrissimis & Celsissimis Juventutis Principi- bus JOHANNI GEORGIO IV. & FRIEDERICO AUGUSTO, boni ominis nomina! sive GRATIA PLENUM sive GRATIOSUM, QUIA PERPETUO PRO PATRIA VIGILANTEM alterum, alterum PACE, id est, salute omnigenâ DI- VITEM & SEMPER AUGUSTUM nuncupatum. Præstet tales saluti terrarum Saxonicarum, Imperio, Ecclesiæ universæ, precor, & nunquam non precaturus sum, dum Spiritus hos reges artus; quid restabat, quàm ut QUARTUM Inclutis Ordinibus, summis istis Capitibus sanctè devotis, & humiliter subjectis inscriberem ? Quo ipso tum gratias pro beneficiis mihi exhibitis publicè peragere, tum verò ulteriorem gratiam, studiis & viribus in hac ætate senectâ exhaustis reverenter ambire, & ut confido, humiliter exam- bire ausus sim. Agnofcunt certus sum, Incluti Ordines, summâ & nunquam satis depræ- dicandâ gratiâ præ aliis regnis & provinciis, has imprimis terras Electorales affectas esse, quod ex hisce oris, & initio quidem ex Academiâ hâcce lux veræ religionis in totum orbem se diffuderit, & è mediis tenebris Babylonicæ Confusionis iterum emersa: quod eadem à tenebris stygiis ultrà sesquiseculum integrum in decimum annum asserta: quo à Syncreti- ca Caligine, viciniæ incumbente, vindicata: Venerabuntur, indubiè, clementiam Regis Exercituum, qui concessit, ut Germanico idiomate, nequicquam contrà fulminante Capi- tolio Romano, legerentur Sacra Biblia, curâ & diligentiâ incredibili B. Lutheri, verè Thean- dri, elegantissimè atque efficacissime; non sine assistente Spiritu translata. Suscipient, quodin fontibus etiamnum hodiè, sicut superiori seculo divino munere factum, si non felicius, legan- tur. Æstimabuntjetiam aliquo pretio successus divinitus concessos, quod integram Scriptu- ram S. V. & N. Test. in Saxonicâ Electorali Universitate ac innumeris gravissimisque Viri, & re & nomine Magni,sed infelicis curiæ Romanæ Advocati, infelicioris Scripturarum Aristar- chi, infelicissimi interpretis, vindicare, pristinoque nitori restituere licuerit, & univer- sas Scripturas Propheticas, libros omnes veteris Testamenti Historicos, item Novi Testa- menti, cum totâ Epistola ad Romanos, vere aurea, gemmeaque, priori ad Corinthios, parte aliqua Epistolæ posterioris ad eandem Ecclesiam, nec non ad Thessalonicenses, deni- que Apocalypseos etiam Johanneæ disputationibus publicis, exemplo, quod credo, inau- dito, luxerit. Non nobis Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo, Domine, sit gloria; iterum iterum- que voveo. Quæ omnia ita pro virili conatus sum exequi, ut ubique cum fidei analogia è parallelis Scripturæ universæ in solis disco exposita, sanctorum Patrum saniores interpreta- tiones, Doctorum quoque Recentiorum, imprimis Megalandri Lutheri explicationes, con- tra quorumvis hæreticorum & fanaticorum depravationes ex ipsis fontibus assereretur, ade- oque depositum cœleste Ecclesiarum nostrarum in tuto collocaretur. Quod num assecutus sim, Ecclesiæ judicio piè committo. Sectatum me id undiquaque esse læta conscientia asse- rere possum; consectatum ubique esse, absit, ut tam suffenus mihi sim, ut unquam vendi- tem, quod à nullo mortalium putari posse, certissimus sum. Solus id posse debet Roma- nus Episcopus, & quia debet, gratiam Deo, sit id simul queat, redditurus est, cur id non exequatur, hoc est, cur non glossam perpetuam in totam Scripturam S. adornet, & de Ca- thedra, in qua vult infallibilis esse, promulget ab omnibus citra ullam contradictionem,uti de vulgata editione sine ulla menda pronunciare in Bullis suis Sixtus V. & Clemens VIII. ma- gna orbis sibi devoti seductione, siquidem plus quam mille locis Clementina & Sixtina edi- tiones sese adversa fronte concutiant, ausi sunt proclamare. Alterum ergò Pontificum istorum Spiritum prolixe mentitum esse oportet: & hæc est illa decantata infallibilitas, uni- cum & summum principium fidei Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

Suscipite animæ generosæ, piæque, hoc quicquid est operæ Vestræ Patriæ dicatæ, meque respicere gratiose ne dedignemini. Sic iterum respiciat vos gratia Divina, & consilia vestra nunquam non salutaria esse jubeat ad Magni Principis beneplacitum, & egregium Publicum florentes in seculo hocce omni opum, honorum, & felicissimorum ingente, & muneribus Vestris laudatissimis, incrementorum vigore, ut æternum in altero seculo beati vireatis, at- que fulgeatis.

V.V. Illustrium & Amplissimorum Nominum

Cultor perpetuus, Intercessor apud Deum indefessus,

ABRAHAM CALOVIUS, D.

L. S. B. I. D. I.

INgenui Candoris, animique grati est, non tacere, per quem profeceris. Et in sacris maximè studiis multum refert, non esse, aut videri velle αὐτοδίδακτον. Tales enim qui sunt, singulares esse amant. Quod in his fugiendum literis, quæ præ aliis ὁμοψήφους desiderant. Ideo jubemur Prophetias non spernere, & Spiri- tus Prophetarum Prophetis subjecti sunto. Hæc causa fuit, cur CATENAS, quas veteres vocarunt, semper amarim, ex Auctoribus Græcis & Latinis contextas: & hæc nostra aliquod instar earum exhibere voluerim: eaque fini autorum verba, quæ quam facile fuisset propriis commutare, nisi lucrum temporis in describendis iisdem eligendum fuisset, quo opus mihi cummaxime, Spar- ta illa in amanuensem, non sine dispendio sumtuum devoluta. Gratiora sunt &dulciora, quæ ex ipsis fontibus scaturiunt. Nec ulla ita autoribus fieri potest injuria, ac ne pærsumi quidem ab aliis, qui sic etiam eo facilius carrere possunt iisdem, nec necessum habent, sumtus eorum causa facere: Ita magis quoque evitari possunt sphalmata, quæ é MS. sæpe ἀνεξερευνήτω, nasci solent. Autores, qui ad- hibiti, ea ratione sua non privantur laude: & cum censura forte notandi fuere, quæ verò semper co- mis & amica, ut penes orthodoxos imprimis par erat, & qualem sibi, cum usus fert, optaret quis- que, adhibita. Tum Heterodoxis quoque suum tribuere, jus & æquum postulabat, sive in refellen- dis erroribus, seu in calculo, quem merebantur. Quorum consensus veritati firmandæ, aliisque con- ciliandæ, dissensus eidem ἐκ ἐναντίας illustrandæ, sæpe numero inservit. Jussi itaque eos ἰδίᾳ γλώσσῃ loqui, ne querantur se non intelligi. Nec ὀι ἀμφίβιοι neglecti sunt, aut honore suo, cum nervum attigerunt, privati. Nam quandoque etiam est olitor valde opportuna loquutus. Patres præcipue, GRE- GORII, CHRYSOST. HIERONYMUS, ARETAS, ANDR. CÆSARIENSIS, THEOPHYL. ut αὐτολέξει perciperentur opera danda videbatur, & inter eos B. LUTHERUS Noster ὁ πάνυ, interpres profecto accuratissimus. Quod emphases, orationis elegantia, gravitas, suavitas, harmonia, suo jure poscebant. Huic in explicatione Geneseos, Psalmorum, Epistolarum ad Romanos, ad Galatas & Apo- calypseos, magnam partem acceptum ferre convenit genuinum S. Apostolorum sensum: quemadmo- dum, quæ exposuit in Harmonia Evangelistarum, & in Genesi ut & in Cantico Cant. nec non in prioribus ad Romanos, in Petrina utraq; in Apocalypsi, in quam egregiam operam etiam collocavit B. Cluverus, pal- mam aliis ambiguam reddidit B. Gerhardus, & quæ quoad ultimum scriptum fideliter ipsum (Gerhardum dico) secuta est Paraphrasis Vinariensis: in Epistolam ad Hebræos in ἀνεκδότοις B. Dorschaus, in Jobum, Dn. D. Sebastian Schmidius, in Paulinas & Johanneas Epistolas B. Ægid. Hunnius, in c. II. Jacobi B. Hülsemannus, in totam Epistolam B. Brockmandus. Accensendi non præter meritum illis WELLERI, OSIANDER, CHEM- NITIUS, POLYCARPUS, & WILHELMUS LYSERI, GERHARDUS, πολλῶν ἀντάξιος ἄλλων, ejus- que filius JOHANNES ERNESTUS, HUNNII, MYLII, PHIL. NICOLAI, GESNERUS, RUNGI- US, BALDUINUS, WINCKELMANNUS, HOEUS, HULSEMANNUS, ἀκριβείᾳ nemini secundus, eidemque geminus DORSCHEUS, BROCHMANDUS, CLUVERUS, HOPFNERUS, MENTZE- RUS, MEISNERUS, BEHMIUS senior, in Chronologia potissimum (Junior Parentis vestigia & orto- doxiam deseruit) FEUERBORNIUS, MYSLENTA, TARNOVII, DANNHAUERUS, ὀι νῦν ἐν ἁγίοις, DN. GEIERUS, SCHMIDIUS, alii, quorum MS. ἀνεκδότοις ex parte quoque grata manu ac mente usus sum, quos omnes, jam in cælis triumphantes, ceu Patres in Christo veneror, ut alios jam non commemo- rem, quos vero index ad calcem non tacebit.

Peculiariter autem, qui GROTIO alitubi confutando symbolum quoddam tulere, audiendi fue- re, RIVETUS, MARESIUS, BAILIUS, & qui forte occurrebant alii, & reliqui in Catalogo Autorum producti.

Jam si pauca quis hic mea esse dixerit, me non habebit diffitentem. Causam, cur malim aliorum assecla esse, quam ἀυτοδίδακτος, jam adduxi. Si vilia, nec magni momenti, nihil vile & exiguum esse in Scripturis sciat, & sufficere, si non inutilia, quanto magis, si necessaria agnoscantur, quemadmo- dum hæc ob Grotii corruptelas, ad quas dijudicandas non omnes æque exercitatos habent sensus, à non paucis æstimantur. Denique προθύμως illud Hieronymi in Prolog. Galeat. ad XXXV. ς. Exod. meum hic facio. In templo DEI offert unusquisque quod potest, alii aurum, argentum, & lapides pretiosos, alii byssum & purpuram: nobiscum bene agitur, si obtulerimus pelles, & caprarum pilos.

HARMONIA MNOV-ANTIQUAM dixi: Novam, quod nullam viderim hoc pacto adornatam: Antiquam: quod unicè, veram illam censeam: Antiquissimum enim quodque verissimum. Antiquam, quod vestigia Patrum legerim, qua Canones de harmonia traditos; Antiquam, quod etsi ὀλικῶς ea nuspiam reper- ta, κατὰ μέρη tamen, quoad illam partem in hoc, quoad aliam partem in illo veterum fundata sit. Com- mentariis Evangelii vix egere judicabam, postquam Grotius iisdem annotatis suis percruditis lucem aliquam affundere visus est; Sed in censura, quando ea adhibenda fuit, ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ pro re nata, & uti ferebat occasio, aliorum contuli sententias, & quam credidi veriorem, elegi, verbis etiam autorum, quos ὁμοψήφες inveni, comprobavi, vel autoritate, nuda citatione designata, non minus, quam ra- tionibus textualibus firmavi: quandoque & contrarias suorum rationes, Grotii autem semper, cum non sine omni ratione dissentire videtur, discussi: E scriptis etiam nostris nondum editis nonnulla ad uberiorem textuum dilucidationem, cum vindiciis adversus dissidentes, σποραδικῶς adducere, haud superforaneum, aut inutile existimavi. Recentiores insuper sententias, in quas forte incidi, cum cura omnes conquirere non permiserunt labores concatenati passim censui. Hæreticis justum elen- chum, ex monitu Apostoli, ἀποτόμως institutum opposui, orthodoxis modestiam debitam exhibui. Ne- que veritus sum τὰ ἴδια ἀνερεῖν: Et quæ alias scripsi recognita emendare. Quo fine annos, quibus sin- gula edita sunt effigiei præfixæ adjeci. Dies enim diem docuit, & nomen meum inter eos, qui scri- bendo proficiunt, non dubito referre. Rarò produxi ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν, vel propria meletemata, nec nisi cum certus sui, ea Spiritus S. intentioni consentanea esse, quæ ne quidem pro ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει habenda. Nam à singularitatis studio semper alienus esse studui, Chemnitianum illud observans: Τὰ κοινὰ κοινῶς, & τὰ καινὰ κοινῶς, verbis propriis, & stylo didactico, quem requirit Apostolus, non calamistrato, vel ni- mis troporum & figurarum affectatione obscurato, lubens usus sum. Ad id docendi genus Chemnitio, Gerhar- do aliisque magnis viris probatur à teneris assuetus. Barbariem & solecismos, nisi cum termini artium ἐξ ἀνάγκης in usum vocandi, vel ab aliis vocati fuere, studiose effugi. Atque his ita operam dedi. Historica post Chronologiam V. T. & Chronotaxin Actis Apostolicis præmissam, non adeò prolixâ com- mentatione, & συνεχείας ratione, quæ in Evangeliis, vel ex Harmonia dispalescit, indigere existimavi, ubi tamen indiguêre, partibus officii non defui: Brevioribus ergò lineis Acta expediri poterant; In commentationibus verò ad Epistolas Pauli, & aliorum Apostolorum, ob dogmatum fidei assertionem, ma- jori opus fuit curâ. Et planè singularis, & novella in plerisque GROTIANA non tantum de Anti- Christo, sed etiam de Christo, ejus regno, Ecclesia, & hostibus cum spiritualibus, tum corporalibus sententia: Ideò novus Elenchus, novum studium, idque eò accuratius postulari videbatur, quò or- natius novit Vir Magnus Helenam suam condecorare, ne refutationis αἴτησις τῇ ἐν ἀρχῇ objectari jure possit, ut autem πολυλογία vitaretur, quæ uno alterove loco dicta vel tractata jam erant, de quibus conserendis loca Scripturæ à Grotio, vel in notis nostris observata vel indices, plerumque commonefa- cere poterunt, non visum fuit repetere, nisi fortè, cum prior tractatio memoriâ excidit. In sententiis verioribus eligendis nihil datum abs me studio partium, vel ex eo constabit, quod tum facilè calculum ad- diderim heterodoxis autoribus, cum sensum Scripturæ S. assecuti sunt, quam fidei nostræ sociis: Nam pla- cebat mihi illud Primafii: Quin etiam à TICONIO Donatista ea, quæ sano congruebant sensui, desloravi, & ex eis, quæ eligenda fuerant, exundantia reprimens, importuna resecans, & impolita componens Catholico moderamini tempera- vi: Sicut autem pretiosa in stercore gemma à prudenti viro reperta colligi, & ingenua dignitati sua restitui debet: ita un- decunque veritas elucescat, Catholicæ deserenda est unitati. Unica intentio fuit, à sensu, & intentione Spiritus S. non deviare. Quam si assecutus sum, quod in omnibus sperare aut præsumere non ausim, DEO mecum gratias age, si minus, infirmitati humanæ id donabis. Sphalmata tamen, si quæ ossendent, no- lim mihi imputari: Fortè nec Correctori aut Amanuensi, nam ἀυτόγραφον non semper æquè legi potuisse, facilè concedo. Nonnunquam Grotius ipse, vel typographus, aut librarii in culpâ fuerunt. In rele- ctione operam quam potui, adhibui, sed quia festinanda interdum illa fuit, fieri potuit, ut errores re- linquerentur sine emendatione. Συνεχείας ratio non semper reddita, imprimis ubi vel luculenta è no- strâ explicatione visa, aut Grotiana, vel é Grotii sensu eruenda, non incommoda mihi credita. Cujus annotationes ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ tum tacitè approbo, cum censurâ adversâ eas sive ἐπ᾿ ἀυτοφώρῳ, sive alio in loco haud notavi. Minutiora sine censurâ reliqui, sive quod in medio relinquenda, seu quod minima non curet prætor. Minima, scilicet quoad Grotiana: Nam in scripturis tale nihil æstimandum: Qui mi- nimum apicem in lege, Scriptura S. solverit, minimus in regno cælorum vocabitur, h.e. nullus. Qui in uno est reus, reus est omnium: Omnia enim ab uno sunt, unius veritatis, unius autoritatis, æquè infallibilia ac divi- na, ideòque æquè inviolabilia. Dogmata præcipua in sede primaria, vel locis classicis imprimis tracta- vi, ut siceat hinc Locos Communes per totum Systema Theologicum more indicis Tiriani, vel Dn. D. OLEARII nostri, Theologi summi, & Fratris intimi, summo loco honorandi, in Commentariis B. Balduini obser- vato, adornare, solideque, ut in Domino persuasus sum, comprobare, singulis ad locum suum plenè, & ex dictis eò pertinentibus universis, revocatis, atque digestis, ut adeò continuatione Systematis superse- dere possim, si forte telam ejus senectus præsciderit: Quam tamen, ultimâ manu huic Biblico operi imposita, ξ. θ. aggrediar, utinam eo tenore absolvendam, quo cœpta est. Non enim tantum senten- tiæ inde meæ, ejusque fundamenta; sed & adversariorum ἀντίθεσις & ἔλεγχος colligetur, quantum sufficit. Adducti sunt plerique, si à recentioribus fanaticis discesseris: Horum enim obscura & nomina, & sæpé sententiæ. Nec datum fuit eos conferre, seu quod haberi apud nos nequiverint, seu quod tempore tum excluderer, cum ad eosdem deferebar. Non autem hic tacendus mihi, sed debitâ diligentiæ exqui- sitioris laude mactandus est ἀκροατὴς quondam & συζητητής meus perindustrius, vir plurimum Reverendus Dn. M. Ioh. Andr. Lucius, Μεσεκκλησιαστὴς Dresdenfis Aulicus, cujus operâ in annotandis Interpp. non ra- rò me usum profiteor. Cæterum vir quidam præclarus indicem istius Systematis ex Anti-Grotianis prioris editionis, qui si continuarit, vel ipsam διήγησιν simul transcribere, cum meis, tum Grotii verbis, non gravabitur, quam- vis opus sit magni laboris; spondeo tamen sim, fore id quoque magni usus: cujus gratiâ adhibendi o- mnino erunt, non sine sumtibus, amanuenses, sed & illis, & τῇ ἐργοδιώκτῃ polliceor redhostimen- tum. Prius autem index iste integer conficiendus, & mecum communicandus erit, usum polliceor non collectori tantum, sed & Lectori cuivis. Quid enim utilius Theologiâ Biblicâ? sine Scripturâ Theologia ne meretur quidem Theologia dici. Erubescat Theologus loqui sine Scripturâ: Physicus sine naturâ, vel documento naturæ: nisi Scriptura ejus vicem suppleat. Quæ ἀποδειξις tum sufficit, non tantum argumenta Topica: ut scioli nonnulli hodie, non sine contemtu Scripturæ, sentiunt: Usus autem τῆς ἑρμηνείας mediis illis sum, quæ in scripto, propter oracula quædam, etsi tædiosa prolixitate tradita, non inutili, de interpretatione Scripturæ laudavit B. Franzius noster; ob quæ posthumenda quando- que M.ignorum Virorum autoritas fuit. Argumentum capitum, cum partitionibus & librorum, & sectionum, ubique adjeci. Τῇ ἀκριβείᾳ potius quam verborum elegantiæ studui. Quæ si cum paraphrasi, ex opere Biblico contexta, & ubi forsan illud deficit, ex Osiandrina vel Vlnariensi textus dilucidatione suppleta adornanda, divulgetur, additis in argu- mento commatibus, textui respondentibus, quæ per festinationem prætermissa sunt, (totum enim penè textum vel caput argumentum quodlibet summatim exhibet) nec inutilis, nec ingrata illa, meo arbitrio, foret opella: Meditabor ipse tale quid, sub Summariis & partitionum Scripturæ titulo, si superstitem servabit divina benignitas. Eâ enim ratione & facilius memoriæ imprimi poterit in cursoria Bibliorum lectione, illis semper repetitis, series Biblica, & rectius in accurata obtinebitur sensus Scripturæ literalis. Quod uni- cum votum, unicum studium meum fuit. Illud, si mediante bocce impetravi, est de quo non tam mihi, quam Ecclefiæ, cui hæc destinata, gratuler. Tale compendium Deo dante, Harmonia, qua textus paral- leli folum citati, non exscripti, contineantur, sed textura simul monstretur per Evangelistas eadem tra dentes harmonice pariter etiam sequi poterit, ut & distractis in Minori formâ exemplaribus, προθήκη ad Tomos Biblicos APPARATUS cum SUPPLIMENTO ad Biblia illustrata utriusque Testamenti, com- prehendens I. CRITICUM BIBLICUM II. GENESIN MOSAICAM commentario uberrimo exposi- tam: III. Dicta Classica, præexistentiam Filii DEI ante Nativitatem é Mariâ Virgine adstruentia vindicata: utpote Gen. III. 15. I. 9. c. VIII. 41. Gal. III. 23. 1. Joh. I. 20. 1. Reg. II. 19. c. I. 10. c. VIII. 58. c. IV. c. IV. 9. 10. 14. Job. XIX. 25. c. I. 14. c. XI. 27. Eph. I. 22. c. V. 20. Ps. II. 7. c. I. 15. c. XVI. 28. c. III. 17. Jud. v. 14, XVI. 8. cap. III. 15. c. XVII. 5. 7. Col. I. 16. 17. Apoc. I. 8. XLV. 8 c. III. 17. c. XVII. 8. Ebr. I. 22. c. I. 11. CX. 1. c. III. 13. 31. c. VIII. 32. c. II. 5. c. II. 8. Es. IX. 6. c. V. 35. Act. VII. 56. c. II. 14. 15. c. III. 21. c. XLIII. 9. c. V. 14. 23. 24. 30. 37. c. X. 10. c. III. 7. c. XXI. 6. c. III. 16. c. XXII. 13.

IV. THEOLOGIAM APOSTOLICAM ROMANAM, vel quæ κατὰ ad Romanos Epistolâ tradita per oracula XXII. adversus varias corruptelas Pontificiorum, Calvinianorum, Socinianorum, aliorumque hete- rodoxorum luculenter adserta. V. VESTIBULUM in Epistolam ad Ebræos, quo pleraque ad autori- tatem Canonicam, autorem ministerialem, linguam originalem, occasionem, scopum, methodum, partitionem, præ- stantiam denique ac dignitatem hujus Epistolæ facientia panduntur, præmissa oratione de prærogativis, quibus Epistola hæc præ cæteris N. T. scriptis eminet, atque excellit.

De Apocalypsi multa essent, quæ forsan non ἀκαίρως nec ἀκάρως monerentur. Videbit autem ul- tro lector æquus, non minorem in illa adhibita fuisse operam, quam in Epistolas cæteras Apostolicas (quum & ἀποκάλυψις forma epistolari scripta & inscripta sit) ut verus sensus cum perpetua συνεχείᾳ red- deretur, & LL. CC. non tam evolverentur, quam innuerentur. Ita enim illa adornata à Spiritu S. est, juxta cum visionibus, prædictione ἀποςασίας à fide, ac seductionis ad hæreses, cum aliorum, tum im- primis Anti-Christi Romani, veram doctrinam & æternum Evangelium sisteret, & confirmaret, quem- admodum ex plerisque capp. religionis unicè salvificæ hic non obscure propositis, sed luculenter ex- positis: Sententias quæ nimis ἐιδικῶς vel specialiter determinatæ à nonnullis, utpote à D. Joh. Coccejo, ut & è nostris B. D. G. B. M. I. D. aliisque, minus autem περιςατικῶς vel circumstantialiter, ut ita vocem, in Apocalypsi designata, sunt, y. g. de exercitu superiorum ligistico, de Bello Bohemico, de parrici- dio nuperrimo Anglicano, de concussione regnorum Angliæ Cromvellana, & conflicti Batavis, de victoriis item Suecicis, gloriosissimi GUSTAVI ADOLPHI, & repressione Anti-Chri- stiani moliminis &c. ἐκ προαιρέσεως, & de industria sicco pede præteream, ne alios vellicare, vel citra rationem in iis, quæ prorsus ἀσήπηκτα, & ingeniosa tantum ἐυρήματα humana censui, occupari velle vi- derer. Satis munere me functum meo ratus, si certiora. qualia omnino sunt, quæ Megalander Luthe- rus, solidius confirmarem, quam in talibus plane incertis operosius laborarem.

Quibus omnibus non incommode subjungentur Vaticiniorum & Oraculorum divinorum ἐξηγή- σεις Academicæ, quæ per publica Programmata, seu Facultatis Theologicæ, seu Academiæ causa pro- positæ hic & Regiomonti sunt, utpote non parum facientes ad sensum Scripturæ uberius illustrandum, & confirmandum. Ideoque plenior hic habebitur de plerisque, quæ adhuc forte é nostra sacratiori penu vel suppellecti desiderari poterat, tractatio: adeoque absolventur ea ratione Biblia illustrata Quinque Tomis Exegeticis.

Ne autem studiis obsim Polemicis, quum quæ ad bella Domini fecerunt, per disputationes in di- versis locis propositas, sed facile distractas, non possint omnia obtineri, neque amplius in officinis Bibliopolarum reperiantur, & à non paucis tamen quandoque curiose quærantur: in eo sum, ut tri- bus Tomis Scripta Elenchtica complectar, sve edita hactenus, sive adhuc ἀνέκδοτα, Latini & Germanici idiomatis: eademque, si quidem cum Viro integerrimo, in Illustri quadam Republica Bibliopola famigeratissą, propagandi gloriæ divinæ nominis studioso, jam convenerim, Ecclesiæ emendatiora sistam. Epitomen Bi- blicam, partitiones Codicis Sacri, cum summariis capitum exhibiturus separatim, in forma minori, quæ tanquam Enchiridion vel manuale facilius portari queat, fortassis sistam, vel, cum eam forte quæris, è Bibliis Illustratis jam excipere possit, ad capita novam temporis periodum inchoantia, simul Chronologiam, quæ non ita obvia est omnibus, adjiciam: donec illa omnia, una cum Paraphrasi Biblica, & locorum parallelorum potiorum προθήκῃ utilissima, imo maximopere necessaria, si DEUS vi- tam & gratiam suffecerit adjicere licuerit. Tandem ne didactica nomina cum Paræneticis imperfecta relinquantur, cum à plurimis Tomorum Quatuor Systematis Theologici, (in quibus proposuimus Sacram παιδείαν, vel ςοιχειωλογίαν, qua Isagogen ad Theologiam: θεοφανείαν, sive patefactionem di- vinam. Secundum naturam, & mysterium imprimis SS. Trinitatis: κτισιογραφίαν, de operibus crea- tionis, & speciatim de Angelis: nec non ἀνθρωπονομίαν, de homine, qua lex ei cum inscripta tum præscripta fuit) continuatione desiderari videam, & quotidianis fere convitiis ad absolvendos eosdem provocer, aggressus & illam, ξὺν θεῷ. sum operam, & divina gratis Quatuor subsequentes Tomos jam expedivi, utpote παιδαγωγίαν νομικὴν, legalem hominis per peccatum à DEO alienati manuductionem, quâ ad Christum veluti manu injecta, per legem ceu pædogogum, uti Gal. III. 25. vocatur, perducimur,

& ita ad Deum reducimur: γεισογνωσίαν, de persona & officio Christi justam informationem: ἐκκλη- σιομετρίαν, de Ecclesia, ejusque juxta ætates, ante diluvium, post diluvium, ante captivitatem Ba- bylonicam, circa eandem, post liberationem ex eadem: sub Christo item in diebus carnis ejus, & tem- poribus Apostolorum, usque ad Constantinum M. dehinc sub Anti-Christo, & ex ea ad Reformatio- nem B. Lutheri, denique exinde usque ad consummationem seculi, & excidium ac supplicium novis- simum Anti-Christi, qua religionem, & conditionem fidelium, sub varia illarum diversarum ætatum specie, ac figura, & status vel Monarchias diversas, mensura, seu Oeconomia circa eandem divinam, & μυστηριοσοφίαν, sapientiam cœlestem de mysteriis divinis, Sacramentorum utriusque Testamenti. Supersunt adhuc tres Tomi, Nomocanon nempe divinus, vel νομοθεσία; Soteriologia Christiana, quæ continet nostram ad Christum vocationem, a Christo impetratam illuminationem, & conversionem, fidei in Christum donationem, cum naturæ fidei explicatione accuratiori hodie ob Arminianos Syncre- tistas maximopere necessaria m justificationem per solam in Christum fidem, unionem cum Christo, & inhabitationem, & immanens Christi in nobis gaudium & exhilarationem, in Spiritu Sanctificatio- nem, & in sanctitate conservationem, adeoque in fide perseverantiam; eique contrariam à fide defe- ctionem vel Apostasiam à fide, quæ degenerat denique in peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum, & blasphe- miam Spiritus: pœnitentiam item extra peccatum in Spiritum S. & æternam tandem glorificationem. Et ἐσχατολογία sacra, ad quam refero etiam ἀθανασίαν practicam, seu artem bene moriendi. Hos meos conatus qualescunque, & vitam ac sanitatem tuum erit, Lector Benevole, piis precibus, quemadmodum ego tuos in studiis progressus, amæbæis paratus sum, juvare ac provehere. Ita nos Deus utrinque gratia sua fecundet, sospitet! Datum Witebergæ, Die Epiphanias Dominicæ, Anno χριστογονίας CIƆ IƆCLXXVI.

ABRAHAM CALOVIVS, D.

Reverendissimo & Magnifico Viro, DN. D. ABRAHAM CALOVIO.

ORbem miraris totum potuisse Columbum Per mare navigii vertere nave sui, Per brevia & sirtes sulcans varia æquora, donec Portus quos potuit, fortiter obtinuit: Pergito mirari, Lector, novus ecce Columbus, Quj longè major, quàm prior, alter adest. Qui mare sulcavit, quo non est altius ullum, Quod perscrutari non valet ulla bolis. Scilicet Oceanum, mysteria QUANTA vegentem! Quæ nequeunt sciri, vel ratione capi. Imò quæ ratio contemtim ridet, & ad quæ Fastidita suo nauseat ingenio. Ut simul in scopulos animæ non credita cedant, Ceu contra ad vitam credita sola valent. Quæ quis non stupeat? non singula dicat abyssos? Inque super cælis non numeraret aquis? Et tamen hoc uno conterita volumine, totum Quod sensu absolvunt BIBLIA SACRA suo; Jam sic lustratum studio atque labore CalovI Progressus calami, remigioque sui. Ut qui Scripturæ nunc sacræ navigat æquor, Nil planè metuat, quod remoretur iter, Aut intellectus eclipsin forte relinquat, Omneque nunc pateat, quod fuit ante latens. Tu modò siste gradum, Lector, qui Biblia tractas, Atque opus hoc oculis intueare tuis.

Quid vis deponam? Mecum tu faberis ipse, Cum remis novus hic ecce! Columbus adest! Qui freta, qui scopulos, qui divae mentis abyssos Perfretat, & planam monstrat ubique viam.

Sic consummatissimi Theologi, Dn. Autoris Opus Biblicum aestimat Tobias Wagner, D. Universit. Tubingensis Cancellarius.

Optime Scripturae Interpres, Praesulque sacrorum, Qui scriptis juvenes, voceque pascis oves: Spiritus aetherea sanctus te afflavit ab arce, Et calamum & linguam nocte dieque regit: CALOVI, talem te scriptis exseris orbi Doctiloquis, qualem secula rara ferunt. Namque Prophetarum multi explicuere libellos, Scriptaque Jessaei vatis amata piis. Sed tua nunc reliquos superant, laudemque merentur Illustrata novis Biblia sancta notis. Nil restat, nisi quod vivas post fata superstes, Et veniant coelo praemia digna Tibi. In labores Biblicos Honoratissimi Dn. Collegae scrib. Johannes Meisnerus, D.

Lutherus Cathedra columen sublime, CALOVI Atque Sionei gloria prima jugi; Enthea Scriptorum seges, exhaustique labores Immortale CUI Nomen in orbe locant: Ecquis erit tandem Meritorum margo Tuorum? Otia qua calamo gratior hora feret? GROTIUS en stratus rursum Tibi porrigit herbam, Multiplicans cladis certa trophea sua. Caetera filescant, praesentem Fama Triumphum Digno per populos are loquetur anus. Purior his palmis Ecclesia porro fruatur, ET SERVENT NOBIS TE BONA FATA DIU!

Ita maxime Reverendo, Ampl. & Excell. Dn. D. ABRAHAM CALOVIO, Theologo de Ecclesia Christi praeclarissime merito, Affini, Compatri, Collegae, & in Christo Jesu Fra- tri suo venerando, ac sincere dilecto, de exantlato labo- re ex animo gratulatur Johannes Andreas Quenstedt/ SS. Theol. D. & Prof. Publ.

## 1:1 Introduction: On the Illustrated Bibles of the Great Calovius, by D. Fried. Rappolt, Public Professor of
ON THE ILLUSTRATED BIBLES OF THE GREAT CALOVIUS, BY D. FRIED. RAPPOLT, PUBLIC PROFESSOR OF THEOLOGY IN THE ACADEMY OF LEIPZIG.

Therefore, the final touch has been applied with no small effort to the book and the magnificent work, which our age has long desired for its own benefit, and which the coming age will admire, having been polished and finished with serious art. For the profane wisdom of GROTIUS had plunged the divine oracles of the BIBLES into dense darkness and the rust of genius, and had forced a deceptive meaning into a sphere not its own. The persistent labor of this man wiped that away, as did his industry, always approved by God, and his holy ardor, which knew not how to be bent, and he brought back the truth, as if the black night had been driven away, and brought the day.

And now those things have once again revealed themselves to the assemblies of the pious with a more illustrious light, the blind darkness of GROTIUS having been dispelled, and that which the wanton hand of the rest of the lost men of darkness had poured over them. Just as a more beautiful chariot yokes its horses, and Phoebus turns a new face to the world, when he frees himself from his former rust, and shines forth after the labors of stolen light. What do you ask? To them (which a long day may recount, and the annals may store up, and a grateful future generation may proclaim!) CALOVIUS was the sun alone.

First thanks to GOD, who gave the sacred Bibles to the assemblies of the pious by the secret art of the Spirit. Highest thanks to GOD, who has preserved the Bibles for all time, this being the provident care of the highest GOD. Full thanks to GOD, who continually fills great men with the Holy Spirit, so that they may cultivate the Holy Scriptures. Let most devoted thanks be perpetually to JEHOVAH, who prepares the CALOVIAN Bibles for us. The Church adorns CALOVIUS with many merits, since he brought forth the Holy Scriptures along with other writings. The SWORD-BEARING AUGUSTUS, A HERO OF A CELEBRATED NAME, praises the Noble Work with august signs. The Saxon world, preserving LUTHER'S BIBLE, admires the BIBLE of the great CALOVIUS. And the WITTEBERG School rejoices in this deposit: the sacred Bibles, the highest Good. Our School saw and received the great Labors of CALOVIUS, and says thanks even to GOD. It saw the auspicious beginning, and the middle of the Labor, and the end was imposed, a clause grateful to GOD. A clause grateful to the good crowns every happy work, and GOD shall be celebrated in all things. HUGO GROTIUS was fashioning the immense efforts of Hercules; he was like a great Goliath, craftily insulting the armies of the Lord with horrendous attempts, corrupting the inspired words of GOD. The hidden poison, enclosed in a specious covering, will cause very many damages in the Flocks of the Lord. HUGO had fashioned Notes, which he himself would have more rightly inscribed as spurious, or rather as deaths. The harmful poisons were creeping far and wide, and were giving the hearts of many to be destroyed. For these, a Physician had to be sought, not a Galen in art, but one full of the Divine Power, moved by the Spirit of the Father. The Davidic Hero, alone in these fields of the Lord, was sufficient for the Herculean monsters of Goliath. CALOVIUS, full of the great Spirit of David, has now caused the great trifler to fall. This GROTIUS has badly compiled many heretics into one heap, a woeful work of fraud. He noted the dreams of the Jewish Nation, the figments of the Rabbis: who would approve of them? They are worthless, which a mind not sane has brought forth for the Calvinists, the Socinians, and the false Arminian brothers: and those which the crowd is accustomed to love as the ψευδερμηνείας (false interpretations) of the Papists, these GROTIUS thinks are Notes. O too ill-fated offspring of notes, with a suspect mother, they are the work of corrupted reason. Ah, would that GROTIUS had stood in the sphere of reason, he would have always brought back great Names for himself: let the same man be heard as great in the objects of reason, and let him profit his own with the dexterity of his judgment. But in the Scriptures his Reason is worth nothing anywhere, GROTIUS, or any other, who is wise by reason. The sayings of the Lord are valid, let our presumption cease, let it cease to command in the mysteries of God. The CALOVIAN Hand has duly cleansed this stable of Augeas, these tremendous monsters of monsters. The right hand of Calovius, with the sling of David, has removed every evil from the divine Word. He restored the most holy Bibles to their ancient splendor, and removed the masks which Grotius had wickedly brought. The Calovian faith clearly showed that the Notes were by no means notes, but many trifles of Grotius. May the Calovian faith continue to wage the wars of JEHOVAH, by which the House of the Lord stands and falls. May the same man defend and explain the holy Bibles of GOD, and bring pure food to the flocks of Christ! May the HERO always carry victorious arms in these lands, by which the fierce crowd of Satan is put to flight! May the Spirit grow immensely, and may He breathe the high rewards of eternal salvation upon the holy flocks! May the Calovian Hand, by divine gift, fill the world evermore with good writings and merits! May the Holy Bibles bring forth great fruits with weight for the Church and the School, and for pious Christians! May Calovius live, thrive, and flourish well for all time, and may he promote all the advantages of the pious! LIVE FOR GOD, VENERABLE FATHER, AND YOU HAVE LIVED ENOUGH FOR YOURSELF! Live for all good men, live for me and mine. May you fill the climates of the world here with immense merits, so that there may always be great honor for you in heaven! And sated with merits and life, ascend at last to the heavenly stars, only after long delays!

To this VENERABLE LORD and FATHER-IN-LAW, a father in Christ to be honored with the greatest effort, for his complete and most useful work on the Bibles, Johannes Deutschmann, Doctor and Professor of Sacred Theology, Ephorus of the Elector's Students, and Dean for the time being, offered his congratulations with all his heart, out of a sense of duty, piety, and gratitude.

Therefore your divine Virtue lacks rest, until it crowns the begun work with an illustrious end. Virtue once began to weave a noble work; it began the work, that was of the ancient covenant: Hugo Grotius had once corrupted the instruments of GOD, and had taken away God from them, oh the crime! Substituting men for Christ, whom the Spirit had inspired the Prophets to know and to teach as God: a sacrilegious deed! Your Virtue, Great CALOVIUS, did not endure it further, by restoring God. The work stands forth, and is read in a thick double volume, and I glory in being a part of that book. The oracles of the other covenant follow, as the body follows its own shadow in the light. This too was a great crime! Hugo had violated them by substituting his own profane German glosses. This book, which you see here present, has removed these shadows which that darkling had made for the sun. Now take away your veil, O Jew, in the serene sun, and do not shine any longer in the shadows, O Socinus. There will be no excuse for you hereafter, while Christ shines as a star in full light. And the chariots which seemed to fight among themselves now go together in accordance with the canons. By the virtue of the Great CALOVIUS reconciling the wheels, so that you may see that each is governed by one Spirit. There will not be lacking, O HIGHEST MAN, the grace of GOD for you for such (grant me pardon for the word, I pray) merits.

Balthasar Bebelius, Doctor.

Let the great monuments of Tostatus, Tirinus, or Menochius, or Lapide, or Riocela, or the Tiber be silent. Nor let the Gloss of Strabus or Lyranus exalt itself further, or those things which Calvin or Pelikan possess.

The short Library begins to obstruct the Illustrated Bible of Calovius with these lights. Grotius is not the only one attacked: but the heretical sense of the victim falls with such an interpreter.

To the venerable Lord Godfather, kinsman, and father in Christ, Samuel Pomarius, D.D., Superintendent of Lübeck, congratulates with all his heart and soul on this immense biblical labor of another Adamantius and Chalcenterus, happily exhausted amidst other concatenated works and the alternating turns of health in this encroaching age.

Subtle Grotius, in what he covered of the sacred Bible, the care of the great Calovius has uncovered the work. He offers poisoned draughts to minds; the latter corrects the evil with life-giving art. The world provides a light reward, but in time, grace worthy of such great books will not be lacking. After long and heavy labors exhausted, the honor of even Polus* endures with a right mind. We also, holy Father, pray for mild fates for you, that the times of your teaching may be long.

I, Johannes Acoluthus, Doctor of Sacred Theology, Professor of the same at Wrocław, Pastor at St. Elizabeth's, and Inspector and Consistory Assessor of the remaining Evangelical Churches and Schools in the same place, wished to congratulate from the heart the holy Church of God on this incomparable Treasure, and the magnificent Lord Author on his overcome supreme labors.

To the most Reverend man, and truly great in the glory of learning, fame, and merits toward the Church and the right faith of God, Abraham Calovius, etc., etc., etc., whom I must always hold in the place of a father, Georgius Green, Professor of History at Wittenberg, composed these humble iambics when he was publishing the final volumes of the Illustrated Bible.

That which is more lasting than bronze and for all the ages of the world, a stupendous work for posterity, and of simple truth and never-deceitful peace, here the keen and candid defender, the great Calovius, prepares, stitched together with art. The world of the Britons awaits, the bold Dutchman marvels, who is more learned than Grotius, whom the first and last world celebrates with clear voices, who is greater in genius? Calovius is illustrious. He does not offer light from the profane light of the nations to the heavenly oracles; the Arian brings these, malignant and impious torches: but the most pious Calovius joins lights kindled from the divinely inspired light. As a noble painter once covered with a silent veil what he could not attain, so I pursue the glory of Calovius with the sacred honor of silence, for which neither my pen nor my right hand suffices. The world of mortals does not grasp the honor of Calovius: the sincere ardor and labor which he contributed to the truth and the upright faith in Christ shines among the stars. Indeed, the name of this great man stands established among the stars. To express much in a word: Calovius is the greatest divine in heaven and on earth.

If anyone should say that I owe what I have written on the Gospels to others who have exercised themselves on the same subject, he will neither lie entirely nor speak entirely the truth. I do not deny that I have profited from all those who have written heretofore; nay, I even rejoice and glory in it. Therefore, consider me to owe thanks to them all, as if I had named them individually. I have, however, for the most part refrained from reciting names, because I see that in this factious age, that serves more to obscure judgment than to clarify it. For my part, when I was annotating these things as a captive, when I was completing them as a private citizen, and when I was publishing them while established in some honor, my purpose was always not to serve any of those parties into which we Christians have been divided by the great evil of our age, but to serve all Christians plainly, and to direct my own efforts toward the knowledge of Evangelical truth and the increase of that piety toward which we ought to strive with all zeal, if we wish to be reckoned as belonging to so great a name. Furthermore, whoever reads both the writings of others and these of ours with care will see that, even when I follow the opinions of others, new arguments are added by me to support them, and when I differ from others on that point, the reasons why I do so are diligently set down by me. I testify, however, that if anything has been written by me anywhere that conflicts with those senses of Holy Scripture which the Christian Churches have held by persistent consensus since the earliest age—which I am confident will not be found—I hold it as unwritten and am most ready to change it.

Ε Π Ι Κ Ρ Ι Σ Ι Σ (CRITIQUE).

I shall not touch upon the boasting of Grotius, which might seem excessive regarding ALL who wrote on the Gospels before him, once they have been perused. Nor shall I speak of the reason for the omitted names, sought from a factious age. And that Grotius belonged to no party and to all, not only these annotations but his other Biblical and Polemical writings sufficiently testify. You might deservedly call his theology purely Elective and truly αἱρετικὴν (heretical), were it not that Atheism sometimes betrays itself in it, which is worse than any heresy. He professes of his own accord that his purpose was always to serve no party. But which parties? Those which he has embraced within the scope of the Christian name. Under which, without ambiguity, he also includes Socinians and Arminians—the former denying the Most Holy Trinity and the incarnation and satisfaction of the Son of God, the latter denying that the same is necessary to be believed? Although this ἀπισία (unbelief) of his is clearer from other commentaries and later writings of Grotius than from the present annotations on the books of the Gospels. But it is more certain than certain that the knowledge of Evangelical truth, to which he testifies his own is directed, cannot consist with the ignorance or denial of the one true God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and of Christ the God-man and his merit. For in these, as truth itself testifies in John 17:3, eternal life is situated. Nor is there true piety when the true object of worship in the supreme precept of the law is unknown; for this is to serve an unknown God and not to know what we worship. Trust is the mother of true piety, without which it is impossible to please God. But there can be no such trust if one calls into doubt the redemption of Christ, God and Man, as it is handed down in the Gospel. Finally, in this he will not easily find assent in any part of the Christian name that communicates through symbols, because he asserts with such confidence that he has written nothing in these pages that conflicts with those senses of Scripture which the Christian Churches have held by persistent consensus since the earliest age. Although it is ambiguous where that antiquity of the first age is to be sought, since the Church did not remain a Virgin long after the departure of the Apostles, and few writers of certain faith survive from the first and second centuries from whom that sense could be indubitably sought. What also is the persistent sense of the Christian Church, and where it may be found, not even Grotius himself, that glutton for books, could define. And without doubt, the genuine sense is more rightly drawn from the letter itself and the continuity of the sacred texts and parallel passages than from uncertain tradition. The legitimate and safe exposition of Scripture is according to the Scriptures themselves; this is the rule of St. Irenaeus, easily the most ancient of the Fathers, book 4, chapter 63, and that sense is sound, with the same author in book 2, chapter 13, and safe, which is placed openly and without ambiguity by the very words in the Scriptures. But if it be said that the Roman Pontiff, whose advocate Grotius acted, cherishes that sense of the Church received from the first age in the shrine of his breast, and brings it forth as occasion arises when he pronounces from the chair, why then does he not finally adorn and promulgate from the chair, for the infallible assistance of the Holy Spirit which he peddles, a perpetual commentary, superior to all exception, according to that primitive and Apostolic sense? Whether those who venerate Him by those names would prefer to argue for the envy or the negligence of the most holy Father, the vicar of Christ, the head of the Church, let them see to it themselves. However, how ready and prepared Grotius was to hold as unwritten and to change what in his writings were clearly demonstrated to conflict with the proper senses of Holy Scripture, and of which he was entirely convicted, his Amoebaean and Polemical writings with Rivet, Maresius, and others show. When he could do nothing else, he returned insults, by way of thanks, for the truth shown to him. But this character of the man has already been detected by those with whom he had dealings.

Latin:

IN BIBLIA ILLUSTRATA MAGNI CALOVII D. FRIED. RAPPOLT, THEOL PROF. PUBL. IN ACAD. LIPSIENSI.

Ergo umbilicus mole non parva libro Operique summa splendido imposita est manus, Quod nostra dudum commodo affectum suo Optavit aetas, postera emirabitur Exasciatum & arte confectum gravi. Divina nempe BIBLIORUM oracula Densis tenebris ingenique aerugine Profana GROTI merserat sapientia, Sensusque fallax non suo orbi obtruferat. Abstersit illa pertinax Viri labor, Deoque semper approbata industria Ardorque sanctus, nescius flecti, & mertum Reduxit, atra Nocte ceu pulsa, diem.

Jamque illa rursus se piorum cœtibus Illustriore prodidere lumine Soluta cæca GROTII caligine, Et quam proterva cæterorum Natio Tenebrionum perdita offudit manu. Ut nempe currus pulchrior jungit suos, Orbique vultum Phœbus obvertit novum, Cum se priore liberat ferrugine, Raptæque lucis post labores emicat. Quid quæris? Ipsi (longa quod memoret dies, Fastique condant, gensque grata prædicet Futura!) Soli sol fuit CALOVIUS.

GRatia prima DEO, qui Biblia sacra piorum Cœtibus arcana Flaminis arte dedit. Gratia summa DEO, qui Biblia tempus in omne Servavit, summi hæc provida Cura DEI. Gratia plena DEO, qui Sancto Flamine replet Usque Viros Magnos, ut Sacra Scriptua colant. Gratia perpetuò sit devotissima IOVÆ Biblia qui nobis CALOVIANA parat. CALOVIUM decorat meritis Ecclesia multis, Cum Scriptis aliis quod Sacra Scripta tulit. ENSIFER AUGUSTUS, CELEBRANDI NOMINIS HEROS, Augustis signis Nobile laudat Opus. Orbis Saxonicus, LUTHERI BIBLIA servans Magni miratur BIBLIA CALOVII. Et Schola WITTEBERGENSIS lætatur in isto Deposito: Summum Biblia sacra Bonum. Vidit, & excepit magnos Schola nostra Labores CALOVII, & grates dicit ad usque DEO. Vidit & auspicium faustum, mediumque Laboris, Finis & impositus, clausula grata DEO. Clausula grata bonis felix opus omne coronat, Et DEUS in cunctis concelebrandus erit. Herculis immensos fingebat GROTIUS HUGO Conatus, Goliath grandis ad instar erat, Agminibus Domini vafer ausibus insultabat Horrendis, vitians enthea verba DEI. Occultum virus, specioso tegmine clausum, In Gregibus Domini plurima damna dabit. Finxerat HUGO Notas, quas sæpius inscripsisset Rectius Ipse nothas, vel magis inde neces. Noxia serpebant longe, lateque venena, Pectora multorum conficienda dabant. His Medicus quærendus erat, non arte Galenus, Numine sed plenus, Flamine motus Avê. Herculeis Goliath monstris Davidicus Heros Unus in his Domini sufficiebat agris. CALOVIUS, magno Davidis Flamine plenus, Nugonem magnum nunc cecidisse dedit. Hæreticos multos male compilavit in unum GROTIUS hic cumulum, flebile fraudis opus. Somnia Judaicæ Gentis, figmenta notavit Is Rabbinorum: quis probet illa? nequam, Quæ Calvinisequis, Socinis, Arminianis Fratribus & falsis mens male sana tulit: Quasque Papistarum ψευδερμηνείας amore Turba solet, putat hæc GROTIUS esse Notas. O nimis infaustos, suspecta matre, notarum Fœtus, corruptæ sunt rationis opus. GROTIUS ah utinam rationis in orbe stetisset, Usque reportasset Nomina magna sibi: Magnus in objectis rationis & audiat Idem, Prosit judicii dexteritate suis. Ast in Scripturis Ratio sua nil valet usquam, GROTIUS, aut alius, qui ratione sapit. Dicta valent Domini, cesset præsumtio nostra, Cesset in arcanis, induperare Dei. Augiæ hoc stabulum, monstrorum monstra tremenda, Rite repurgavit CALOVIANA Manus. Dextera CALOVII funda Davidis aperta Verbi divini sustulit omne malum. Biblia restituit veteri sacro-sancta nitori, Sustulit & larvas, quas male Nugotulit. Esse Notas minimè, sed nugas Grotia multa, Monstravit clarè CALOVIANA fides. CALOVIANA fides pergat bellare JEHOVÆ Bella, quibus Domini statque, caditque, Domus. BIBLIA sacra DEI defendit, & explicat idem Et Gregibus Christi pabula pura ferat! Semper in his terris HEROS victricia portet Arma, quibus Satanæ Turba fugatur atrox! Spiritus immensum crescat, spiretque salutis Æternæ Gregibus præmia celsa sacris! CALOVIANA Manus divino munere mundum Scriptis & meritis repleat usque bonis! BIBLIA Sancta ferat magnos cum pondere fructus Ecclesiæ atque Scholæ, Christicolisque piis! CALOVIUS vivat, vigeat, bene floreat omni Tempore, promoveat commoda cuncta piûm! VIVE DEO, VENERANDE PATER, TIBI satque vixisti! Vive Bonis cunctis, vive mihi atque meis. Immensis meritis repleas hic climata mundi, Semper ut in cœlis sit Tibi magnus honor! Et meritis vitaque satur conscendito tandem Non nisi post longas cœlica in astra moras!

His VENERANDO DOMINO SOCERO, Patri in Christo maxi- mopere colendo, de absoluto utilissimo Bibliorum opere ex debito pietatis & gratitudinis affectu ὁλοψύχως gratulabatur Johannes Deutschmann D. SS. Theol. P. P. Alumn. Elect. Ephorus & p. t. Decanus.

ERgò quiete caret Tua Virtus enthea, donec Illustri cœptum fine coronet opus, Cœpit opus quondam contexere nobile virtus Cœpit opus, prisci fœderis illud erat: Instrumenta DEI quondam corruperat Hugo Grotius, & tulerat, proh scelus! inde Deum; Substituens homines Christo, quem nosse Prophetis, Quemque docere Deum Spiritus indiderat: Sacrilegum facinus! tua Virtus, Magne CALOVI Non tulit ulterius, restituendo Deum. Prostat opus, gemino legiturque volumine spissum, Et pars istius glorior esse libri. Alterius subeunt oracula fœderis,umbram Ut sequitur corpus lumine quodque suam. Hoc quoque grande nefas! temeraverat Hugo profanis Glossis germanis substituendo suas. Sustulit has tenebras, quas iste tenebrio soli Fecerat, hic præsens, quem legis, ecce, liber. Velamen Judæe tuum nunc tolle, sereno Sole, nec in tenebris porro, Socine, mica. Nulla super-posthac erit excusatio vobis, Dum Christus pleno lumine stella nitet. Quæque videbantur secum pugnare quadrigæ Nunc juxta canonas convenienter eunt. Conciliante rotas Magni virtute CALOVI, Ut videas uno Flamine quasque regi. Non deerit, VIR SUMME, DEI Tibi gratia tantis Pro (veniam verbo da, precor) his meritis.

Balthasar Bebelius, D.

QUod ære sit perennius Cunctisque mundi seculis, Opus stupendum posteris, Et veritatis simplicis Pacisque nunquam subdolæ, Hic arte consutæ mala, Assertor acer, candidus, MAGNUS PARAT CALOVIUS. Exspectat orbis Brittonum, Miratur audax Battavus, Quis Grotio sit doctior, Quem primus orbis & ultimus Claris celebrat vocibus, Quis major ingenio cluat? ILLUSTRIS EST CALOVIUS. Non hic profana gentium De luce lucem porrigit Oraculis cœlestibus, Hæc Arrianus admovet, Faces malignas impias: Sed Entheo de lumine Accensa, jungit lumina PIISSIMUS CALOVIUS. Non orbis hic mortalium Capit decus Calovii: Refulget inter sidera Sincerus ardor, & labor, Quem veritati contulit, Etre cta de Christo fides. Quin inter astra conditum Stat nomen ingentis VIRI. Ut multa verbo proferam: In cœlo & orbe maximus DIVINUS EST CALOVIUS.

SI quis dicat, me, quæ ad Ev- angelia scripsi, debere aliis, qui se in eodem argumento ex- ercuerunt, is neque penitus mentietur, neque penitus ve- rum dicet. Ego per omnes eos, qui scripsere antehac, pro- fecisse me non diffiteor, quin gaudeo etiam, gloriorque. Ita- que me omnibus eis gratiam habere puta, quasi nominat- sem singulos. Peperci autem plerumque recitandis no- minibus, quod ea videam factioso hoc seculo magis ad oblimandum quam ad defecandum judicium valere. Mi- hi autem, cum ista annotarem captivus, cum perfice- rem privatus, cum ederem in aliquo jam honore con- stitutus, propositum semper fuit, non alicui earum in- servire partium, in quas ingenti seculi nostri malo divisi sumus Christiani, sed Christianis plane omnibus, mea- que dirigere ad notitiam Evangelicæ veritatis, & incre- mentum pietatis ejus, ad quam omni studio debemus contendere, si ex tanto nomine censeri volumus. Cæ- terum videbit qui & priorum & hæc nostra scripta cum cu- ra leget, etiam tunc cum aliorum sequor sententias, no- va à me adjungi argumenta, quibus eas sustentem, & cum ab aliis ab eo, rationes cur id faciam, diligenter à me adscribi. Testor autem, si quid usquam à me scri- ptum est pugnans cum iis sacræ scripturæ sensibus, quos Ecclesiæ Christianæ à prima ætate acceptos perseverante consensu tenuere, quod repertum non iri satis confido, me id pro non scripto habere, ac mutare paratissimum.

Ε Π Ι Κ Ρ Ι Σ Ι Σ.

Non perstringam gloriationem Grotianam, quæ nimia videri queat de OMNIBUS, qui ante ipsum in Evangelia scripserunt, evolutis. Neque de causa nominum prætermissorum dicam, à fa- ctioso seculo petita. Et nullarum partium fuisse Gro- tium & omnium, non tam hæc annotata, quam cætera & Biblica, & Polemica Vira scripta satis te- stantur. Theologiam ejus mere Electivam, & vere αἱρετικὴν esse, merito dixeris, nisi quod Athei- smus quandoque in ea se prodat, hæresi quavis pe- jor. Nulli servire partium propositum semper sibi fuisse, ultro profitetur. Sed quarum partium? Quas nominis Christiani complexus est ambitu. Sub quibus, procul ambiguo, etiam Socinianos, & Arminianos comprehendit, illos Sacrosanctam Trinitatem, & incarnationem ac satisfactionem Filii Dei negantes, hos eandem creditu necessa- riam inficiantes? Quanquam hæc ejus ἀπισία ex aliis commentationibus, & scriptis posterio- ribus Grotii luculentior sit, quam è præsentibus in Evangeliorum libros annotationibus. Evan- gelicæ vero veritatis notitiam, ad quam sua dire- cta testatur, consistere non posse cum ignoran- tia, vel abnegatione unius veri Dei Patris, Filii & Spiritus sancti, & Christi θεανθρώπου meriti- que ejus, certo certius est. In his enim sita est, ve- ritate ipsa teste Joh. XVII. 3. vita æterna. Neque pie- tas vera est, cum λατρείας in supremo legis præce- pto verum objectum ignotum est; hoc enim est ἀγνώστῳ Θεῷ servire, & nescire, quid adoremus. Fi- ducia veræ pietatis mater est, sine qua Deo pla- cere impossibile est. Ea vero nulla esse potest, si Christi Dei & Hominis redemptionem, qualis in Evangelio tradita est, in dubium quis vocet. In eo denique in nulla Christiani nominis parte, qua per symbola communicant, assensum facile inve- niet, quod tanta fiducia asseverat: se nihil in hisce scripsisse, quod cum iis scripturæ sensibus pugnet, quos Ecclesiæ Christiana à prima ætate acceptos per- severante sensu tenuere. Quanquam ubi quæren- da sit antiquitas illa primæ ætatis, ambiguum sit, quum Ecclesia post excessum Apostolorum diu non manserit Virgo, & pauci superent certæ fidei Scriptores, è primo ac secundo seculo, è qui- bus sensus ille indubitato peti possit. Quinam etiam Ecclesiæ Christianæ sensus perseverans sit, & ubi ille reperiatur, nec Grotius ipse, librorum hel- luo, definire potuit. Et rectius sine dubio sensus genuinus ex ipsa litera, & textuum sacrorum συνεχείᾳ, ac parallelis locis depromitur, quam ex incerta traditione. Legitima & sine periculo est expositio scripturæ secundum ipsas scripturas, regula est S. Irenæi, Patrum facile antiquissimi, l. IV. c. 63. isque sanus, eodem l. II. c. 13. autore, sensus est, & sine periculo, qui aperte & sine ambiguo ipsis dictio- nibus in scripturis ponitur. Quod si Pontificem Romanum, cujus Advocatum egit Grotius, in scrinio pectoris sui, sensum illum Ecclesiæ à prima ætate acceptum fovere, ac pro re nata, cum de cathedra pronunciat, eundem proferre, dicatur, cur non adornat tandem, promulgatque de ca- thedra, pro infallibili Spiritus Sancti, quam ven- ditat, assistentia, commentarium perpetuum, omnique exceptione superiorem juxta illum sen- sum primævum & Apostolicum. Invidiæmne po- tius, an negligentiam sanctissimi Patris, vicarii Christi, capitis Ecclesiæ arguere malint, qui illis no- minibus Eum venerantur, ipsi viderint. Quam pransus autem & paratus fuerit Grotius pro non scripto habere, ac mutare, quæ in scriptis ejus cum scripturæ sacræ sensibus propriis pugnare, lucu- lenter demonstrata sunt, & de quibus ipse omni- no convictus fuit, Amabæa & Polemica ejus cum Riveto, Maresio, aliis docent. Cum aliud non potuit, convitia, gratitudinis ergo, pro veritate ostensa, reddidit. Sed hæc Viri indoles ab iis, qui- buscum res ipsi fuit, jam detecta est.

## 1:1 Introduction: In the Name of Jesus. Prolegomena to the New Testament
In the name of Jesus. Prolegomena to the New Testament.

Before we approach the individual books of the New Testament, for the sake of preparation, some things must be premised in general: I. ON THE TITLE, which is as follows:

ΤΑ ΤΗΣ ΚΑΙΝΗΣ ΔΙΑΘΗΚΗΣ.

It seems likely to the blessed D. Johann Gerhard that it has its origin from St. John, the Apostle and Evangelist, who collected the Holy Canonical Books written by divine inspiration by the Evangelists and Apostles after the Ascension of Christ the Savior into heaven, and arranged them in order, having prefixed this inscription: τὰ τῆς καινῆς Διαθήκης. It is helpful here to subjoin what Hugo Grotius prefixed to his Annotations on the books of the Gospels concerning the Title of the New Testament, and to add our own observations to them.

Latin:

I. N. J. PROLEGOMENA IN NOVUM TESTAMENTUM.

ANtequam ad libros No- vi Testamenti singulos ac- cedamus, παρασκευῆς ἕ- νεκα in genere nonnulla prælibanda sunt: I. DE TITULO, qui sic habet:

ΤΑ ΤΗΣ ΚΑΙΝΗΣ ΔΙΑΘΗΚΗΣ.

Illum à S. Johanne, Apostolo, & Evangelista originem habere B. D. Joh. Gerhardo verisimile videtur, qui S. Libros Canonicos post Christi Sal- vatoris Ascensionem in cœlum ab Evangelistis & Apostolis divina inspiratione scriptos collegerit, & in ordinem redegerit hac ἐπιγραφῇ præmis- sa τὰ τῆς καινῆς Διαθήκης. Juvat autem hic, quæ Annotationibus suis in libros Evangeliorum de Titulo Novi Testamenti præmisit Hugo Grotius, subjicere, nostrasque ad ea observationes iisdem subjungere.

## 1:1 Introduction: Grotian Preface on the Title of the New Testament:
GROTIAN PREFACE ON THE TITLE OF THE NEW TESTAMENT:

Ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη.] Men are bound to men in three ways: by law, by pledge, and by testament: which are so distinct among themselves that they nevertheless cohere by a community of right; whence Aristotle, following the Sophist Lycophron, defined law by the name of συνθήκη, and after him Demosthenes, because Papinian transferred the term to a pledge, and the pacts of contracts are called laws, and the will of the testator is called law, and the word 'testament' was born here as proper to bequeathing. For (as it was in the Twelve Tables) as each person has bequeathed his property, so let it be law. Among the Greeks, there is a word that encompasses those three things, διατίθεσθαι, which Plato uses regarding laws, Aristophanes regarding a pledge, and Isocrates and others regarding a testament. Consequent to this is the noun διαθήκη, which extends just as widely: for it designates a testament most frequently, and is used for a pledge in the Aristophanes I mentioned, and was used for laws by the Orphics and Pythagoreans. For these called the norms of living prescribed for their flock διαθήκας. There is also a sanction common to laws and pledges. For pacts, especially public ones which are called treaties, were accustomed in antiquity to be sanctioned by the slaughter of a beast, and the word 'sanctioning' itself, as has been rightly observed by Servius, is derived from blood, which is the reason that moved the Hebrew masters to believe that ברית is derived from ברא, which is used for 'to cut,' and the Latins to derive fœdus from feriendo (striking). And hence 'to strike a treaty' is a mode of speaking equally used by Hebrews, Greeks, and Latins: concerning which matter an opportunity will be given to treat again at chapter XXVI. In laws, however, that part is called the sanction which consecrates the blood of the delinquent to the law. Hence the Hebrews often explain the words ברית and חוק one by the other. Again, law has this in common with a testament, that neither requires an agreement. For both the heir, by the very fact that he is heir, must perform the deed of the deceased, and one subject to the authority of another, by the very fact that he is subject, must obey the laws of the same. An agreement, however, agrees with a Testament in this, that both the beginning of contracting and of entering an inheritance is usually free: but that of subjection is not, as it descends in many places from origin alone. Since these things are so, it may be asked why the seventy Interpreters, whom all the Hellenists followed, and among them the holy men who wrote the Gospels and Epistles, preferred to interpret the Hebrew word ברית as διαθήκη rather than as συνθήκη, as Aquila did, or otherwise, especially since the richness of the Greek language supplies many words of that meaning. It seems to me, therefore, that they looked to the fact that the Hebrew word ברית extended more broadly than the Greek συνθήκη, or any other that possesses a similar force. For συνθήκη receives the power of a bond from the consenting testimony of two wills. But what Moses and others call ברית is for the most part of such a kind that it requires no consent of the other party, since the power of binding resides in it from the sole command and authority of the superior, for instance God, who nevertheless sometimes of his own accord also binds himself by promising: as the authors of laws are accustomed to do whenever they add rewards to laws. But because those most learned elders were striving to express one Hebrew word with one Greek word, therefore even where ברית pertained to mutual agreements, as in 1 Kings 5:12 and elsewhere, they preferred to use the general word διαθήκη: I believe because they thought the word ברית itself was also born from another notion of the word ברא. For just as ברא properly means 'to create,' so by right of similarity it signifies 'to order' and 'to dispose' (διατίθεσθαι): from which it happened that the Hellenist Jews even extended τό κτίζειν, which corresponds to the Hebrew ברא, to that meaning. For that passage in Jesus Sirach, Eccl. 11:16, cannot be taken otherwise: πλάνη κὴ σκότος ἁμαρτωλοῖς συνέκτισται, and 39:34: πῦρ κὴ χάλαζα κὴ λιμὸς κὴ θάνατος· πάντα ταῦτα εἰς ἐκδίκησιν ἔκτισται. and 40:1: ἀχολία μεγάλη ἔκτισαι παντὶ ἀνθρώπῳ. and ibid. 9: θάνατος κὴ ἒρις, κὴ ῥομφαία κὴ αἶμα, ἐπαγωγή λιμῦ κὴ συντρίμματος κὴ μάστιγος, ἐπὶ τὰς ἀνόμος ἐκτίσθη. Hence also Peter calls the authority instituted by men, or regarding human affairs, ἀνθρωπίνην κτίσιν. Moreover, that the words διατίθεσθαι and διαθήκης were used by the Hellenists in a broader sense than that to which the word συνθήκης could be extended is shown to us by the passage in Luke 22:29, and much more by Ecclesiasticus 38:37, where διαθήκη κρίματος is nothing other than judicial law. Having seen why the Hellenists interpreted ברית as διαθήκη, it follows that we see why the ancient Christians preferred to call this book καινὴν διαθήκην rather than καινὸν νόμον, especially since the Hebrews called the Pentateuch specifically, and all the books pertaining to the sacred codex commonly, תורה or νόμον, and Christian doctrine by its own right claims the name of law for itself, as in Gal. 6:2, James 2:8. I think, therefore, that the ancient Christians looked primarily to the very words of Christ, who, about to sanction his most consummate doctrine with his death, called it by the name of a new ברית. For he undoubtedly used that word, for which Greek writers, in the manner of the seventy men, placed the word διαθήκης. Moreover, the added mention of blood in Matt. 26:28, Mark 14:24, Luke 22:20 shows that the notation of a covenant was properly regarded by Christ. Which the writer of the Epistle to the Hebrews explains accurately. Mindful of which saying, the Apostles wished to be called and considered ministers of the new covenant, 2 Cor. III. 6. Added to this was the fact that the word for covenant explained somewhat more clearly the supreme goodness and condescension of God, as one who, having sent Jesus Christ to us, had not dealt with us by supreme right, as legislators are wont to do, nor imperiously and threateningly, which is the wonted voice of laws, but very gently and with great courtesy, and plainly as those are wont to do who contract with one another in good faith.
