Whence it is not a wonder that other discordant things also occur in the Menschian Harmony, since he did not hesitate to build his own things upon such hypotheses; such as, for example, that paradox that he wishes the 5th, 6th, and 7th Chapters of Matthew, which most, if not all, Interpreters rightly refer to a single sermon of Christ, to be the sum and the first chapters of several sermons of the first Galilean journey, collected and for a certain cause placed before the miracles of the 8th and 9th Chapters, related not in a natural but in an arbitrary order, and he judged that many more such examples occur in the Harmony. But an accurate collation of the Evangelists will clearly teach, provided that false preconceived opinions are first dismissed, that no Evangelist wrote in a disorderly or confused manner—what they call an arbitrary order—that all recorded the series of events and sayings in order, that all mutually explain one another no less in regard to order than in regard to their sentiments, that no anticipation or ὑστερησις easily occurs, unless the matter itself requires it and such things have a place according to the custom of historians, that all wrote so divinely inspired that they drew nothing from memory, nor placed anything there by their own counsel, and as there is one Spirit who moved them, one author of Scripture, of whom the holy Evangelists were only organs and amanuenses, so it is one work, woven through all, in such a way that both individuals can be read in their own order, and from all of them a certain μονοτέσσαρον or τεσσαρεσμόνον can be made, which coheres perfectly, without any foreign addition or necessary insertion, without any hiatus or any lacuna. Which wonderfully both delights and confirms the attentive reader, so that he has no need to doubt in any way concerning the παναρμονία and divinity of the Holy Gospel, which is in truth one work woven by those four most holy men, and he may the more rightly imprint upon his mind the natural series of all acts or deeds. To say nothing of the fact that such a joining together may deservedly be held as a commentary on the four holy Evangelists, shedding light upon one another, even though each one of them also shines with his own native light. To me, certainly, it has been a source of the greatest pleasure to behold before my eyes and to πρὸς ὄμμα ποιεῖν for others that perpetual series and harmony; the clarity of which lends light to the whole history. Whence, for the sake of the same, I have not doubted to assume one or another history or sentence as having been done or uttered twice, or recorded by different Evangelists with almost the same circumstances and words, especially where the consideration of time or even place proved a diversity, rather than to admit confusion or an arbitrary order, or whatever memory shall suggest. Concerning which matter, having been warned already before, similar things have been observed by almost all writers of Harmony, and that others cannot do otherwise, unless they offer violence to history, and wish it to be deprived of both its eyes. However, regarding time, we do not depart from the ancient authority of the Church, as far as the time of the conception and birth of Christ asserted in our Chronology, and thus neither regarding the time of the conception and birth of John, nor regarding the time of the Baptism of Christ, since Christ spent only three years and some months in his office, about half an angelic week, and no more than four Passovers are found in the Evangelical history, as we show in the same place; therefore, according to the same, the Harmony is most correctly woven, and the opinion both of Tossanus concerning three, and of Scaliger concerning five Passovers of Christ, must be entirely dismissed; as well as that of Gerhard Mercator and Theobald Meuschius concerning four full years of the Ministry of Christ: which has no foundation, and produces wonderful confusion. Whence also that arbitrary distribution of the journeys of Christ toward or from Jerusalem, devised by Meuschius, of twelve annual feasts, must be amended, so that three journeys may correspond to each year. But let us go to the present matter, and let us show how the holy Historians observe the natural series of words and deeds: having premised to the others the preface of St. Luke, whom also Ammonius Alexandrinus, Andreas Osiander, B. Chemnitius, Cornel. Jansenius, Theobaldus Meuschius, Andr. Selmatterus, Rupertus Erythropilus, Eilhardus Lubinus, Johannes Cluderus placed in the first position: Since also in the order of time in which the Gospels of ST. LUKE and ST. JOHN, which enjoy proems, were written, that one is prior: and the preface of St. Luke is general, concerning the Evangelical History, as it had been delivered by the Apostles, and at that time received by the Church with certain faith: But the summary Chapters of that which is in the Proem of John are set forth: whence the Johannine proem is not so conveniently placed before by Tatianus and Calixtus, and by the latter, indeed, the preface of Luke is even undeservedly omitted entirely, and Chapter I, v. 5, et seqq., is proposed for exposition after Chapter III, from verse 23 to 38. And these things in advance. There follows again

Latin:

I. N. J. PROLEGOMENA DE SCRIPTORIBUS HARMONICIS ET QUIBUSDAM IN HARMONIA OBSERVANDIS.

Inter omnes divinas autoritates, quæ Sanctis literis continen- tur, Evangelium merito ex- cellit; Quod enim lex & prophetæ futurum prænun- ciaverint, hoc redditum at- que completum in Evangelio demonstratur. Hisce auspicatus est D. AURE- LIUS AUGUSTINUS eruditissimos libros de consenfu Evangelistarum, Evangelium Historiam vitæ JESU CHRISTI dixit, à Sancta Qua- driga Evangelistarum descriptam: Quæ vere HISTORIARUM HISTORIA est, si- ve personæ, cujus vita describitur, dignitatem, sive rerum, quæ gestæ sunt, Majestatem, sive formæ scriptionis divinitatem, sive fructuum salutarium, qui inde redundant, utilitatem, si- ve ipsorum etiam Scriptorum autoritatem respi- ciamus. Nam non tam Evangelistæ scripse- runt, quam Christus per eosdem; Ideo S. Au- gustinus cum prolixe libro I. de consensu Evang. eorum vanitatem, qui discipulos Christi Ev- angelicum conscribentes ideo contemnendos pu- tabant, quia ipsius Scripta nulla proferebantur à fidelibus, retulisset, ita ex vero conclusit: Ita- que cum illi scripserunt, quæ ille ostendit & dixit, nequaquam dicendum est, quod ipse non scripse- rit: quandoquidem membra ejus id operata sunt quod dictante Capite cognoverunt. Quicquid e- nim ille de suis factis & dictis non legere voluit, hoc scribendum illis tanquam suis manibus impera- vit.

I. DE SCRIPTORIBUS HAR- MONICIS.

Quum autem non leves in Historia Evange- lica occurrant difficultates Variantibus sæ- picule ut apparet, quatuor illis Christi amanuen- sibus, Viri Magni ad eandem ordine digerendam, & factorum scriptorum consonantiam aut de- monstrandam, aut vindicandam non proletariam adhibuerunt operam.

Primum autem manum huic labori sanctissi- mo admovisse THEOPHILUM Antioche- næ Ecclesiæ septimum post Petrum Apostolum Episcopum, qui sub Marco Antonino Vero flo- ruit, circa annum Christi 120. Hieronymo in Ca- talogo Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum perhiben- te, vitamque ad Commodi usque protraxit tempora, ut è libris ejus ad Autolycum, appa- ret; (unde perperam is cum Theophilo, cui S. Lucas Evangelium & Acta Apostolica inscripsit, à Gvilielmo Archiepiscopo Tyri libr. Histor. sacr. c. IX. confunditur) B. Chemnitio, Historiam Scholasticam, eundem illis, qui ex quatuor u- num conscripserunt, accensentem, laudanti fa- cile annuerem, si tale quid è meliori autoritate constaret. Sed nec S. Hieronymus in Catalogo Scriptorum, nec quisquam alius meminit, talis cujusdam scripti S. Theophili: Quæ vero in Epi- stola Hieronymi, ad Algasham quæst. VI. Tom. III. Operum pag. 163. referuntur, quod Theophi- lus quatuor Evangelistarum dicta in unum opus com- pigens ingenii sui monumenta reliquerit, non ad μονοτέσσαρον quoddam, sed ad libros Commen- tariorum seu allegoriarum in sacra IV. Evangelia, qui in Bibliotheca veterum Patrum Margarini de Labigne, Doctoris Sorbonici editione tertia Co- lonienfi Anno 1619. Tom. II. pag. 145. seqq. ha- bentur, pertinere ex eo manifestum est, quod omnia quæ de Villico iniquo Luc. XVI. prolixe loco citato adfert Hieronymus in libro III. isto- rum Commentariorum iisdem verbis legantur, in quibus vero non Harmoniæ Evangelicæ, sed pa- rabolicæ explicationi dictorum quorundam in Scriptis Evangelistarum operam navavit Theo- philus.

TATIANUS autem, Theophilo ætate suppar, Justini Martyris discipulus è Philosopho Platonico, Christianus, præceptori dum is vi- veret, in fide ὁμόδοξος tantæ quondam æsti- mationis, ut ad eum Romæ profitentem se ex oriente Rhodon contulerit teste Eusebio l. V. Hi- stor. Eccles. cap. XII. sed postea ob præsumtionem Magisterii & hæreticorum Sectator & Princeps hærefeos novæ Encratitarum Jactus (vid. Iren. Lib. I. cap. XXXI. Tertull. de præscription. c. LII.

c. LII. Eusebius l. IV. Histor. Eccles. c. XXVII.) primus ex iis, quorum superat memoria, videtur, qui Διὰ τεσσάρων ἐ quatuor Evangelistis unum contexuit opus: de quo Eusebius l. c. Tatianus con- glutenationem quandam & conciliationem, nescio, quomodo structam Diatessaron nominavit, quam et- iamnum quidam circumferunt: & Theodoreus l. c. Haeretic. fabul. Tatianus composuit etiam Evange- lium, quod dicitur Diatessaron amputatis genealo- giis, & aliis, quae ostendunt, Dominum natum esse ex Davide secundum Carnem. Eo autem usi non solum sunt, qui sunt illius Sectae, sed hi etiam qui dogmata Apostolica sequuntur, compositionis fraudem non a- gnoscentes, sed simplicius eo tanquam libro compen- dioso utentes. Victor Capuanus Episcopus visus est se invenisse hoc Tatiani opus, cum fortuito in ma- nus incideret simile Scriptum sine autoris nomi- ne, cui Titulus Diapente, idque Tatianum adhuc adhaerentem Justini lateri eruditionis illius merito adornasse, conjicit. Sed non uno modo fallitur Vi- ctor: Nam nec Titulus operis Tatiani Diapente fuit, nec Evangeliorum Harmonia vocabatur qua- lem inscriptionem ei fecit Victor, sed Diatessaron ut Eusebius, Theodoretus, Nicephorus, aliique uno perhibent ore: nec Tatianus patria Alexandrinus, uti Victoris ἐπιγραφὴ habet sancta quatuor Evan- geliorum Harmonia Tatiano Alexandrino auctore; sed Syrus natione fuit, ut è Clemente Alexandr. III. stromati Epiphanio haeres. XLVI. & Theodoreto constat: nec denique, quod praecipui commatis est, characteris operis Tatiani ab Eusebio & Theo- doreto designati libro illi fortuito invento congru- unt; nam non ita abjectim habendus hic, ut ab Eu- sebio habetur Tatiani conglutinatio, nescio, quomo- do structa: nec amputatae in illo sunt genealogiae Christi, sive Matthaei, sive Lucae, aut quae ad Chri- stum secundum carnem è Davide natum faciunt, nec manus profana emendationis, vel potius corru- ptionis illatae scripto isti sunt, quas Victor ipse Ta- tiano operi illatas dicit, nec COMPENDIUM ha- beri potuit Evangelistarum, quod de Tatiani li- bro profitetur Theodoretus, scriptum fortuito in- ventum, eorumq; loco surrogari; quia verba ipsa Evangelistarum exhibet, non sententias, vel argu- menta solum complectitur: Quae omnia ἐ ψευδω- νύμως dicto Tatiani opere à Victore Capuano di- vulgato dispalescunt: prout id cum praefatione Victoris in Tomo II. Bibliothecae Patrum pag. 183. seqq. exhibetur. Et quomodo Victor ille Ca- puanus non ἑαυτομαχεῖ, cum manus profanas in suo putatitio Tatiano (utut immerito) notat, & profectum tamen id operis à Tatiano adhuc lateri Justini adhaerente, antequam ab Ecclesia defice- ret, affirmat? Sequuti nihilo secius Victorem in scripto illo Tatiano adserendo alii sunt, Six- tus Senensis l. IV. Bibl. S. in Tatiano, & Georgius Ederus l. III. Oeconom. Biblior. aliique; Genui- num autem Tatiani opus exhibetur Tomo III. Bi- blioth. Patrum pag. 22. ex Ottomari Luscinii inter- pretatione sub titulo Evangeliorum quatuor Nar- ratio, etsi falso id autorem praese ferat Ammo- nium Alexandrinum, cujus Harmoniam eam narrationem esse temere existimavit, quum ean- dem non Ammonii Alexandrini, sed Tatiani Syri esse facile constet; siquidem ei omnia illa exacte competant, quae Eusebius, & Theodoretus de Diatessaro Tatiani prodiderunt, ut post Baro- nium ad Ann. Christi 174. Bellarmin. in Catalo- go Eccles. Script. Possevinum in Apparatu sub voce Ammonii, (etsi hic sibi contradicat, cum Ottomarum Luscinium Ammonium scriptum trans- tulisse, ait) in Bibliothecae Patrum laudata edi- tione monitum est, quod Victor Capuanus Har- moniam Ammonii & Diatessaron Tatiani perpe- ram confuderit. Incipit autem Tatiani opus à proœmio Johannis, & continua serie per sen- tentias succinctas ex Evangelistis juxta ordinem rerum, primum quæ tradidêre illi de Christo us- que ad Baptismum & tentationem Christi, & præconio in finibus Zabulon & Naphtalim, co- agmentat, amputata tamen utraque & Matthæi, & Lucæ Genealogia Christi; tum vero ordine gesta tribus annis prædicationis Dominicæ, eleganter persequitur.

Initium ita habet: In principio erat Verbum, per quod condita sunt omnia, in fine tandem tempo- rum caro factum Johan. I. Idque novo nascendi mo- do ex Virgine Maria Joseph cuidam nuptui tradita Matth. I. Sed Gabrielis Paranymphi cœlestis nun- tio gravida Luc. I. Quæ res maritum Joseph sa- cramenti nescium traxit in admirationem, ut nisi divino fuisset edoctus oraculo, consilium de Vir- gine deserenda, ita ut conceperat animo, haud du- bie implesset, &c. De opere isto B. Chemni- tius Harmon. Evang. prolegom. c. 3. hæc ha- bet: quia fragmentum illud, quod Luscinius sub nomine Ammonii edidit ipsius non esse antea mani- feste ostendimus, non tamen contendere velim, sic- ut affirmare non possum nec ausim, Theophili hæc esse. Quia tamen veteris Scriptoris esse non est dubium, & ejus usus aliquis ad nostri instituti ra- tionem esse potest, nominemus sane illud Theophili Harmoniam. Servatur autem in illa Harmonia peculiaris quædam ratio; ordo enim historiarum sua quadam serie connectitur, ipsa autem historia non integre describuntur, sed tantum capita seu argumenta earum breviter recitantur, & notantur loca ubi apud Evangelistas extant. Recte vir magnus observavit, Harmoniam illam non esse Ammonii; non autem eandem Theophili Antio- cheni aut alterius cujusdam, sed Tatiani esse, jam in luce positum est: Quod vero Tatiano adscri- bit opus B. Chemnitius non Tatiani est, sed Am- monii.

AMMONIUS enim Alexandrinus, Origenis præceptor, dimidio seculo post, circa annum nempe Christi 226. tempore Alexandri Impera- toris, quem Sixtus Senensis in Bibl. cum Suida, De Volaterano, l. XIII. Anthropol. asinum, animal omnium stupidissimum, doctrinæ suæ auditorem ha- buisse, ridicule perhibet, inter multa ingenii sui, & præclara monumenta, ut Hieronymus habet in Catalogo, Evangelicos Canones excogitavit, quos postea sequutus est Eusebius Cæsariensis. Quos Canones alios Harmoniam Evangelicam vocare, notat Bellarminus in descriptoribus Ecclesiasticis, Tit. Ammonii. Sed aliud opus esse Harmoniam Evangelicam Ammonii Alexandrini, aliud Canones Evangelicos, res ipsa docet. Harmoniam Zacharias Chrysopolitanus Episcopus ante quin- gentos annos commentariis illustravit, quos ex sententiis Patrum in unam catenam contextis co- aptavit, ediditque eandem Victor Capuanus Epi- scopus circa annum Domini 450. è solis Evange- listarum Verbis contextam. Etsi ut dixi, fal- so eam pro Tatiani opere habuerit, quæ ipsa ex- hibetur Tomo II. Bibliothec. Patrum p. 184. & in- cipit à præfatione Lucæ c. I. 1-5. cui subjungitur illis initium Johannis c. I, 1-5. ac porro quæ Lucæ c. I. habet: Tum Genealogia Matthæi (cui quædam è Lucæ Genealogia inserta) & reliqua Capitis I. Matthæi, ac deinde nativitas, & circumcisio, ac præsentatio in templo è Lucæ c. II. Magorum Histo- rià è Matthæo II. cum consequentibus ex eodem cápite &c. De qua ἐπίκρισιν B. Chemnitii nostri, etsi ὁ μακαρίτης, Victorem Capuanum sequutus, Harmoniam illam inter Orthodoxographa Basileæ editam, Tatiano tribuerit, cum ratione in eadem observata, subjicimus: Singulis, inquit, Histo- riis & concionibus singula attribuit Capita (sicut usi- tate nunc loquimur) atque ita totum contextum divi- dit in 181. Capita. Ubi vero eadem Historia ab aliis etiam Evangelistis pluribus, aut variatis circum- stantiis, describitur, retinet quidem in pleris- que Matthæi contextum, addit autem & interserit illi suo loco præcipuas circumstantias ab aliis etiam notatas. Non enim solicitus est singulorum verba, aut minutiores circumstantias anxie annumerare in serie seu ordine Historiarum ad nullius Evangelistæ contextum Harmoniam suam præcise alligavit: sed quæ discretà narratione à quatuor Evangelistis ex- positæ sunt, in ordinem, quo ipse judicavit illa se consequi debere, redegit. Rationem ordinis, quam in singulis Historiis certo loco collocandis & disponendis sequutus sit, non exponit. Et ordo e- jus in plerisque historiis inde perturbatior factus est, quod omnia acta publici Ministerii Christi intra curriculum unius anni concludit, & distincta illa festa Paschatis Johan. II. & VI. ad unicum illud, quod Matth. XXVI. describitur, contorquet. Multa tamen non inutiles commonefactiones de ordine historiarum ex illa Tatiani (Ammonii di- cendum erat) Harmonia sumi possunt. Atque ita non abnuente B. Chemnitio, huic harmo- niæ convenit, quod postea B. Chemnitius de ratione ab Ammonio Alexandrino observata, ex Eusebio in Epistola ad Carpianum annotavit: quod scilicet contextum seu ordinem Matthæi sibi proposuerit Ammonius, & ex reliquis Evangelistis, ubi vel eadem, vel similia describuntur, ea excerpta & quasi in unum congesta contextui Matthæi an- nexuerit. Hæc ergo de Harmonia Ammo- nii. Canones vero ejus Evangelicos longe alios fuisse, vel ex Hieronymo constare potest: qui praefatione in IV. Evangelia ad Damasum, testa- tur, se Canones, quos Eusebius, AMMONIUM sequutus, in decem numeros ordinavit, sicut in Græco habentur, expressisse; quæ ejus Tabulæ Tomo IX. oper. Hieronym. sub initium, oculis lectorum expositæ sunt; quale quid, seu Cano- nes illos decem Eusebii seu Hieronymi Tabulas respicias, nihil comparet in Harmonia Ammo- nii Capitibus 181. comprehensa, prout ea in Bi- bliotheca Patrum exhibita est: neque sane nume- ros istos invenit in libro, in quem fortuito inci- dit Victor Capuanus; ideoque ipse conatus est, eosdem illi adjicere; Hoc igitur Evangelium; in- quit, in præfatione sua, Victor, cum absque nu- meris reperissem, quos Ammonius mirabili studio reperit, Eusebius vero Cæsarea Episcopus Palæsti- næ ab eo accipiens diligenter excoluit, quibus com- muniter ab Evangelistis dicta, propriis sunt notu- lis declarata, Domino adjuvante, studium laboris impendi, ut memoratos numeros per loca congrua diligenter adfigerem.

Hæc ergo sunt, quæ etiam Eusebius, Evan- gelicos Canones, Ammonii in decem numeros ordinando, quæ Hieronymus, interpretando Canones Eusebii, quæ Victor Capuanus eos- dem Harmoniæ Ammonianæ affigendo, ad hunc scopum contulere. Quorum vero nume- rorum usum nunc quidem magnum non esse, probe monuit B. Chemnitius, siquidem longe aliter tum Capita Evangelistarum distincta fuerint, quam hodie, in nostris editionibus; Unde ex an- tiquitate nihil superat quod ad rem faciat, præ- ter illud Tatiani Diatessaron, & jam dictam Har- moniam Ammonii: Nam quod Trithemius apud Possevinum in voce Tatiani, Victori Capuano Diatessaron adscripsit, in eo falsus omnino fuit, quum Victor ille solum Ammonii scri- ptum ediderit, eique numeros adjecerit, non vero peculiare opus Harmonicum adorna- vit.

Facit tamen huc è meliori antiquitate etiam S. Augustinus, qui circa annum Domini 420. te- ste Epistola XXI. quæ est ad Isichium, floruit, & libros IV. præclaros de CONSENSU Evan- gelistarum, reliquit, in quorum primo qui- dem generalia tantum habentur, in reliquis autem tribus speciatim & ordine expenduntur Historiæ & conciliationes Evangelistarum insti- tuuntur.

Sequioribus autem ætatibus præcipue florue- runt Marianus Fuldensis, natione Scotus, qui anno 1086. de concordantia Evangeliorum li- brum unum composuit. Petrus Comestor, Hi- storiæ Scholasticæ autor, circa Annum 1150. qui cum totam Vet. Testam. Historiam, tum Hi- storiæ etiam Evangelicæ Harmoniam adorna- vit: Thomas Aquinas circa annum 1270. conti- nuum in IV. Evangelia scripsit. Bonaventura Cardinalis, qui eodem fere tempore Medita- tionem Vitæ Domini nostri JESU CHRI- STI scripsit, in qua IV. Evangelia in unam re- degit historiam. Guido Perpinianus Hispanus Majoricensis Episcopus ad imitationem Augu- stini scripsit de Concordantia Evangelistarum Anno 1320. Petrus Izuzquius ex Navarra Hi- spaniæ, ordinis Prædicatorum, seriem S. Evan- gelii JESU CHRISTI ex Quatuor Evange- liis concinnavit. Rupertus Goulletus Doctor Pa- risiensis Tetramonon Evangelicum conscri- psit. Simon Cassianus de gestis Salvatoris IV. Evangelia ordine disposuit Anno 1350. Circa i- dem tempus: Ludolphus Saxo, Carthusianus in Monasterio Argentinensi, è quatuor Ev- angelistis unam vitæ Christi historiam colle- git, non minus B. Chemnitio nostro, quam Sixto Senensi laudatus. Johannes Ganuet ordi- nis Carmelitan. Lector, Moguntinus Anno 1440. scripsit de concordia Evangelistarum. Do- minicus Nanus Mirabellius artium Doctor anno no 1470. Monotessaron collegit, conferens cum sententiis Evangelicis dicta Philosopho- rum, etiam Mahometi, teste Sixto Senensi. Johannes Gerson, Academiæ Parisiensis Cancel- larius eruditissimus μονοτέσσαρον de concordantia Evangelistarum adornavit, continuans ordi- nem Historiæ Evangelicæ à S. Augustino cœ- ptum, Anno 1419. vita functus. Diegus Deza Archi-Episcopus Hispalensis Anno 1500. Mono- tessaron reliquit commentariis illustratum; ibialservatum Simon Corroyus, ordinis Cœlesti- ni, juxta eundem Senensem, Anno eodem 1500. Monotessaron in Evangelia composuit, quod Pandectam Evangelicam appellavit. An- tonius Brucchius à Königstein collegit breve Evangeliorum Monotessaron Anno Domini CIO IO XLI. Alanus Copius Lovanii Anno CIO IO LXXII. Paulus de Palacio Anno CIO IDC V. Severinus Lubomiltius, Cracoviæ Ann. CIO IDC VI. Gorwaldus Meschius &c. Andreas Osiander, qui B. Chemnitio præco- ne, maximo labore, & singulari ingenii acu- mine, nova prorsus ratione, Harmoniam Hi- storia Evangelica contexuit, ita, ut nullam histo- riam exceptis duabus Matthæi, de evulsis spicis, & sanam manu arida, extra contextum, quo in singu- lis Evangelistis descriptæ sunt, loco movere, & trans- ponere cogatur, qui Anno 1552. Regiomonti Borus- sorum decessit. Quem, uti a B. Chemnitio ob- servatum, sequuti maxime sunt Molineus & Codo- mannus, qui vero ne quidem duas illas historias Matth. XII. de spicis & de manu arida transponi, sed diversas esse ab iis, quæ a Marco & Luca de- scriptæ sunt, volunt.

His addendi porro e Pontificiis Cornelius Jan- senius Episcopus Gandavensis, in Concordia Ev- angelica, Sebastianus Barradius Lusitanus Jesuita, spisso IV. Tomorum volumine Historiam, & Concordiam Evangelicam, at minori judicio & ἀκρισίᾳ, expediens: Bartholomeus item Riccius in Vita Domini nostri Jesu Christi ex verbis Ev- angeliorum, Anno 1610. Coloniæ edita, & qui- dam Beaulxamis, Antonio Possevino, in apparatu sub Ammonio, laudatus; e Reformatis Johannes Calvinus in Harmonia Evangelica ex Evangelistis tribus composita, Genevæ Ann. 1595. edita: Dis- positio & perioche Historiæ Evangelicæ per IV. Ev- angelistas contexta e Commentariis Henrici Bul- lingeri in forma Enchiridii redacta: Gerhardus Mercator in Harmonia Wisburgi Clivorum An. 1592. Theobaldus Meuschius in Harmonia Evan- gelica An. 1604. Andreas Selmatterus in Sympho- nia nova Evangelistarum Basileæ edita An. 1613. C. commemorat & Daniel Tossanus in literis ad Theob. Meuschium Anno 1549. 23. Nov. datis Harmoniam, quam se concinnare ait, in qua non plura in curriculo Ministerii Christi numerat pa- schata, quam tria, quum Mercator & Meuschius quinque assignent. Idem Tossanus commemo- rat ibidem & alios Autores Harmoniarum: præ- ter alios, inquit, scripsit quidam Codomannus Har- moniam Germanicam in quarto, quam tamen non vidi. Recusa est hoc anno Johannis Rubi Dua- censis Theologi Harmonia nonnihil recognita. Prod- iit & Harmonia quædam Lichæ Anno 1605. per Bernhardum Copium. Gerhardus Johannes Vossius Amstelodami Anno 1656. Harmoniæ Evangeli- cæ tres libros edidit de passione, morte ac resurrectio- ne, & Ascensione Christi, in cujus limine seorsim se de munere prophetico Christi pariter egisse, eoque tum prædicationem Evangelii, tum confirmationem ejus per miracula retulisse, perhibet. E nostris D. Paulus Crellius superiori seculo An. 66. e delinea- tione B. Pomerani hic publice proposita Harmo- niæ Evangelicæ, quam morte præventus vix in- choatam reliquerat, Harmoniam suam extru- ctam esse, profitetur, quam latino & germanico idiomate adornavit. Expedita tamen a B. Bu- genhagio fuit Harmonia passionis, mortis & resur- rectionis Christi in his Ecclesiis recepta. B. D. Micrælius in Syntagm. Hist. Eccles. laudat Erasmi Alberti Harmoniam Evangeliorum pag. 458. libri III. sed quam videre non contigit. Georgius Wirth Phil. & Med. Doct. apud Lipsienses vitam, vel Ev- angelia Jesu Christi e IV. Evangelistis descripsit, quod opus Francofurti ad Mœnum Anno 1594. prodiit. Edidit & D. Eilhardus Lubinus, Pro- fessor Theol. Rostochiensis Harmoniam, cui ti- tulum fecit Quadripartita Evangelica Historia Monas Anno 1616. nec non M. Rupertus Ery- thropilus Pastor Hannoveranus, qui Germani- co idiomate divulgavit Harmoniam Historicam IV. Evangelistarum complectentem Ministerium

- & Vitam Christi. Prodiit Magdeburgi An. 1609. - Laudatur & Harmonia Joh. Avenarii Anno 1583. - Henr. Büntingii 1592. Bartholomai Radmanni - Francof. ad Oder. Ann. 1600. Nicolai Selnecceri - Lips. Ann. 1604. Baazii Lincopiens. &c. Qui- - bus vero omnibus novissimè ferè divulgata B. Joh. - Cluveri Harmonia Evangelica nervosè ac solidè - concinnata palmam facile præripit. Adornavit - & B. Christophorus Althoferus Harmoniam Evan- - gelicam, quæ annis proximis prodiit. Calix- - tina Concordia ob varios errores tùm in Harmo- niam, & Historiam, tùm in dogmata fidei impin- gentes in censum vix venit. Omnium autem hos in studio Antecessorum conatum & diligentiam lon- go post se intervallo reliquisse incomparabilem Theo- logum Dn. D. Mart. Chemnitium, quem ut in reli- quis suis scriptis alios, ita in Harmonia seipsum supe- rare non immeritò ab Eruditis judicari Magnus noster, GERHARDUS, parens, ὁ μακαρίτης ex vero judicat. Cui verò, cum morte præventus aureo isti operi ultimam manum imponere non potuerit, Theologum itidem pereximium Dn. D. Polycarpum Lyserum Seniorem, Virum de Ecclesiis Saxonicis præsertim Electoralibus præclarissimè me- ritum in Harmonico opere fideliter pertexendo, di- vinâ providentiâ, successisse agnoscit, eoque ma- gnas Benignissimo Deo gratias deberi, profitetur is, qui felicissime saluberrimo labori clausulam im- posuit nunquam satis laudatus B. GERHAR- DUS noster: de quo præclarissimo Harmoniæ Evangelicæ CHEMNITIO-LYSERO-GER- HARDINÆ opere judicium nomine Collegii Theologici hujus Academiæ Anno 1651. latum, & editioni novæ præfixum, & Consiliis Theologicis Wittebergensibus part. I. Titulo I. n. IV. insertum hic totum repetitum volumus, adeoque opus illud omnibus verbi Dei cultoribus SS. Theolo- giæ, & Ministerii candidatis, ceu Thesaurum Ev- angelicum, auro & gemmis contra pretiosum, iterum iterumque serio commendamus.

II. DE RATIONE NOSTRÆ HARMONIÆ.

UT vero laudatissimi Autores nulli, sanctis- sima sua opera, vel legem ἀνυπεύθυνον præscriptam voluere, ab ordine quem observant, ac digestione, quam per omnia instituunt, nuspi- am discedendi; vel meditationi & scrutinio Har- moniæ sacræ accuratiori obicem posuere, ita cum in vindiciis Evangelistarum adversus Hug. Gro- tium, quo cum Vossius non raro mirum quantum Harmoniam perturbat, & μονοτέσσαρον Evange- licum discerpit, occuparer, plus viæ simplici ob- servari, omnino peculiarem Harmoniæ adhiben- dam adhuc esse operam, eamque e solis vitæ Do- mini Scriptoribus accuratius inter se collatis, si præceptis opinionibus nuntium in nonnullis mit- tamus, expeditissimam erui posse, censui, quam Dei gratia nunc me eruisse, adeo non ambigo, ut HARMONIAM insignem e solis Evangelistis liquidissimam facillime sola coagmentatione ver- borum divinorum amanuensium complendam, publico Ecclesiæ judicio exhibere minime verear. In qua Hypothesin Andreæ Osiandro, Molineo, & Codomanno B. Chemnitii verbis paulo ante tribu- tam, antequam eandem ipsorum fuisse seu lege- ram, seu observaram, mihi cum ipsis quantenus communem esse, nunc demum deprehendo, ubi e solis, quod iterum repeto, Evangelistis συνάφειαν συναγωγὴν, & εἱρμὸν τ᾽ ἀκολουθίας jam, Deo lar- giente per universam Historiam expediveram: De nulla scil. historia extra contextum, quo ab Evangelistis consignata, loco movenda, & transponenda. Quanquam num illi eandem ra- tionem in ordine & Harmonia inierint, aut qua dexteritate Evangelia digesserint, nondum di- cere habeam, quum μονοτέσσαρα, aut τετράμο- va eorum ne videre quidem, nedum conferre potuerim: Nisi quod dum hæc scribo, mihi of- ferantur Andr. Osiandri Harmonia Evangelica Libri IV. Græce & Latine, quæ fortassis, si va- carit, in ἐξηγήσεσι, alicubi subjungenda, dein- ceps conferam. Distribuit is Harmoniam in quatuor libros; quorum primus a conceptione Jo- hannis Baptistæ, usque ad ordinationem duodecim Apostolorum: secundus ab ordinatione Apostolo- rum usque ad migrationem e Galilæa in Judæam: tertius, a migratione in Judæam, usque ad ulti- mam concionem Christi in templo habitam: quar- tus, ab ultima concione passionem, resurrectio- nem, ascensionem, Spiritusque Sancti missio- nem, usque ad initium Evangelii per Apostolos bique prædicati, justum & genuinum rerum a

Christo gestarum ordinem complectitur. Ita Osi- ander. Cæterum nixus ego sum in hac mea di- gestione & Harmonia post seriem naturalem Evangelistarum, quam omnino observare opor- tet, imprimis duobus istis HISTORIÆ o- culis; CHRONOLOGIA nempe & TO- POGRAPHIA; adeoque circumstantiarum temporis & loci rationem vel maxime haben- dam duxi. Ubi ergo diversitatem temporis & loci animadverti, etsi quædam penes alios Ev- angelistas similiter circumstantiæ deprehendan- tur, coactus omnino sum, cum alii eandem bi- storiam cum inversione Scriptorum Evangeli- corum, & circumstantiarum, quæ ad hic, & nunc adstringunt, statuunt, diversas ponere bi- storias; quod, etsi rarius factum, lucem insi- gnem attulit harmoniæ, & omnia in aprico & plano constituit. Religio autem fuit, diversi- tate loci & temporis id aperte, juxta ipsammet S. S. literam, poscente, ubi omnia deinceps or- dine fluunt quam convenientissime, si sancto- rum Dei virorum unice insistatur vestigiis, pro una historia, volentibus, nolentibus cæteris Ev- angelistis, habere, & per coactam aliquam reca- pitulationem, quam Augustinus & Ticonius, aut rememorationem, quam Gerson vocat, quicquid uni aut alteri Patrum sequius forte visum, eos- dem conciliare. Quod est sensum inferre Scri- pture, non efferre e Scriptura. Nam dubium sane non est, inquit B. Chemnitius Prolegom. c. V. easdem conciones sæpius a Christo repetitas, & varia miracula, quæ similia fuerunt sæpius ab ipso facta. Quæ AUREA seu regula seu observa- tio probe animis infigenda. Placent & illa, quæ præclare Magnus Chemnitius ibidem illustra- tionis causa subjicit: Cum certum etiam hoc sit, non omnia esse diversa, quæ a diversis Evangelistis descripta sunt, sed plerunqve eadem, variatis paulisper circumstantiis, a diversis Scriptori- bus esse repetita: non igitur, NISI EXI- GENTE QUASI NECESSITATE, talium circumstantiarum, quæ ita CERTE & MANIFESTÆ SINT, ut ad diversita- tem non tam persuadere, quam COGERE vi- deantur, illa, quæ res ipsa testatur, eadem esse, diversa facienda sunt. Alias enim collatio circumstantiarum, quæ in earundem historia- rum descriptione apud diversos Evangelistas ex- tant, quæ lux & Historia Evangelica, -perit. Quando vero MANIFESTÆ circumstantiæ DIVERSITATEM oftendunt, APPA- RENTIA SIMILITUDINIS non debet CONFUSIONEM ORDINIS ET HI- STORIARUM facere. Quæ vero magis MANIFESTÆ sunt DIVERSITATIS cir- cumstantiæ, quam TEMPORIS, & LOCI? quæ magis cogunt, ac necessitatem imponunt diversas constituere historias, etsi nonnullæ aliæ circumstantiæ apparentem similitudinem præ se ferant? Unde B. Chemnitius hanc præscripsit Regulam, observatu summopere necessariam, nec unquam temere violandam in Prolegom. c. V. §. Decimo sexto: Quando vero diversa sunt LOCA, TEMPORA, PERSONÆ, OC- CASIONES, & FINES, tunc propter SI- MILITUDINEM, quæ DIVERSIS TEMPORIBUS repetitæ sunt, non sunt con- fundenda, sed distinguenda. Illustrat hoc e Luca: Hoc modo de MULTIS Historiis, quæ a Nono capite Lucæ ad decimum octavum describuntur, & cum præcedentibus magnam similitudinem habent, judicium recte formatur. Illustre exemplum est in Leprosi a Marcoc. I. 40. seqq. Luc. V. 12. de- scripta sanatione, & illa, quam Matth. c. IIX. 1. seqq. exhibet: de quo quidem B. Lyserus Harm. c. LII. titubanter loquitur: vel anticipa- tionem esse, vel diversam bistoriam: At B. Che- mnitius sine hæsitatione ob evitationem convulsio- nis ordinis bistoriarum, & ob temporis locique rationem cogi se fatetur, historias illas, licet SI- MILES, distinctas tamen in Harmonia pone- re: ut alius sit leprosus Marci (& Lucæ) alius Matthæi, licet doctrina utriusque eadem sit. Qua- lia plura observata sunt a B. Chemnitio, ut & B. Lysero, addo, & a B. Gerhardo.

Quæ ergo circumstantiarum, temporis maxi- me ac loci evidens diversitas ipsum coëgit, ut tales Historias, utut specietenus in plerisque dictis, aut factis similes, diversas fecerit, eadem me quoque cogit ad alias historias in multis si- miles, at in conditionibus & circumstantiis indi- viduantibus omnino discrepantes, quoad hic & nunc, & alias περιστάσεις pro diversis haben- das: ubi ex illa accuratiori circumstantiarum observatione magna lux toti relationi Histori- cæ, & ordini ac consequentiæ Evangelistarum, nec minus Harmoniæ Evangelicæ accedit: Quæ omnia præconceptis opinionibus de iisdem Hi- storiis per recapitulationem, aut nad' ὕσερον πρό- τερον vel πρωθύσερον recensitis, præferenda ef- se, equis cordatus, ac pius lector dubitabit? Qua- les omnino causæ non persuadent, sed adigunt, ut socrum Petri non una, sed gemina vice a Christo a febri liberatam, diversitate temporis id flagitante, semel Marc. I. 29. Luc. IV. 38. iterum anno sequenti post concionem montanam, Matth. IIX. ac diversos fuisse, quos aridam ma- num habentes sanavit Dominus, alterum Marc. III. 1. Luc. VI. 6. seqq. alterum Matth. XII.15. asseram: Paralyticum item, quem per lectum demissum Marcus II. 3. seqq. Luc. V. 18. seqq. narrant, diversum constituam a Paralytico Mat- thæi c. IX. 1. seqq. & quæ hujusmodi pauca alia, in quibus ob evidentem necessitatem a Chemnitio- Lyseriana Harmonia discedendum fuit. Simi- lia enim miracula Christum sæpius DIVERSO TEMPORE, DIVERSISSIMISQUE IN LOCIS edidisse, dubium est nullum, ait ipse

& Lyserus Harmon. c. LII. Et laudanda hic est B. Chemnitii modestia, circa historiam de Paraly- tico, Harmon. c. XLIII. quam eandem a Mat- thaeo pariter & Marco ac Luca traditam esse ar- bitratus est: Quia non sunt prorsus evidentes & necessariae demonstrationes, sed PROBABI- LES tantum narrationes, seu CONJECTU- RAE, volui eas Lectori non cum SEQUEN- DI NECESSITATE, sed cum judicandi LIBERTATE proponere. Quum ergo e circumstantiis luculenter invenerim, diversos esse Paralyticos, bona gratia beati Viri ab ejus sententia hic recedo. Quales causae etiam in a- liis in Harmonia nostra παρ' ὅραμα ponentur: unde omnia clara & perspicua evadent, in con- cordia Evangelica, quae alias intricata, minime- que luculenta remanere oportet. Illustrari id potest exemplo duorum caecorum, & muti dae- monis penes diversos Evangelistas, quorum oc- casione S. Augustinus l. II. de consens. Evangeli- star. cap. 29. easdem illas observationes tradidit, seduloque notandas monuit: Hoc de duobus caecis, & de muto daemonio, solus Matthaeus (c.

IX.) ponit. Illi enim duo caeci, de quibus & a- lii narrant, non sunt isti, sed tamen simile fa- ctum est: ita ut si ipse Matthaeus non etiam illius fa- cti meminisset: posset putari hoc, quod nunc narrat, dictum fuisse etiam ab aliis duobus. Quod com- mendare memoriae diligenter debemus, esse quaedam facta similia: quod probatur, cum idem ipse Ev- angelista utrumque commemorat: ut si quando ta- lia singula apud singulos invenerimus, atque in eis contrarium, quod solvi non possit, occurrat nobis, non hoc esse factum, sed aliud simile, vel similiter factum. Quod iterum inculcat S. Au- gustinus sub finem cap. XXX. Sape rursus ad- moneo, quod oportet meminisse lectorem, ne tali admonitione saepissime indigeat, aliis atque aliis sermonum suorum locis, dominum multa iterasse quae alibi jam dixerat: ne forte ipsorum locorum ordo, cum vel ex alio Evangelista non convene- rit alicui eorum, hinc putet esse contrarium: cum intelligere debeat iterum alibi dici, quod jam alib. dictum erat: nec tantum de dictis, verum et- iam de factis observari debere. Nihil enim prohibet hoc idem iterum factum credere. Ca- lumniari autem Evangelio, dum non credit iterum factum, quod iterum fieri non potuisse nemo con- vincit, sacrilegae vanitatis est. Ita ex hac obser- vatione admittit Augustinus diversas, etsi si- miles esse exprobrationes Matth. XI. & Luc. X. descriptas, quod etiam ratio temporis cogit: Quanquam enim suam illam distinctionem inter ordinem recordationis Evangelistae, & ordinem rerum ipsarum huc adferat, magis tamen eo in- clinat, quod diversae sint exprobrationes, cap. XXXII. ita differens: Sequitur Matthaeus, & dicit: Tunc caepit exprobrare civitatibus, in qui- bus factae sunt plurimae virtutes ejus, quia non egissent paenitentiam, &c. usque ad illud ubi ait: Terrae Sodomorum remissius erit in die judicii, quam tibi. Etiam hoc commemorat Lucas, con- tinuato cuidam sermoni Domini etiam haec ex ipsius ore conjungens: unde magis videtur ipse hoc ordine illa commemorare, quo a Domino di- cta sunt. Matthaeus autem sua recordationis or- dinem tenuisse: aut si illud quod idem Matthaeus ait, Tunc caepit exprobrare civitatibus: sic ac- cipiendum putatur, ut punctum ipsum temporis voluisse credatur exprimere in eo quod dictum est, Tunc: non autem ipsum tempus aliquanto latius, quæ hæc multa gerebantur & dicebant: r: quisquis hoc credat, credat etiam hoc esse bis dictum. Cum enim & apud unum Evangelistam, in eniantur quædam quæ bis dixerit Dominus: sicut & apud eundem Lucam de non tollenda pera in via, & si- milibus cæteris, duobus locis dictum a Domino in- venitur: quid mirum si & aliquid alius bis di- ctum singillatim a singulis dicitur eodem ordine, quo dictum est? Et ideo diversus ordo apparet in sin- gulis, quia & tunc quando ille, & tunc quando iste commemorat dictum est. Quod ipsum etiam B. Polycarp. Lyserus circa exprobrationem Christi observavit Harmon. capit. LVI. peric. III. Hæc vero pars Historiæ, quæ agit de in- crepatione civitatum quarundam, controversa est, quo loco & ordine sit collocanda. Lucas e- nim c. X. vers. 13. annotavit, illam factam esse tunc, cum septuaginta discipuli ad prædicandum ablegarentur. Et cum reversi essent, addit Lu- cas expressam notationem temporis: eadem scil. hora Christum dixisse: Confiteor tibi Pater, &c. ut videri possit, hanc præsentem περικοπὴν undecimi capitis Matthæi usque ad finem, extra ordinem per Anticipationem positam, eo referen- dam esse. Et illam rationem multi sequuntur. Sed hæc περικοπὴ, quoad textum, & quoad sensum, tam apte & commode cohæret cum præce- dentibus, & cum sequentibus, ut sine injuria & obscuratione sensus & doctrinæ non inde eximi, & alio transferri posse videatur. Præbet enim occa- sionem dulcissima exclamatio Christi: Venite ad me omnes, &c. & sternit pulcherrimam viam historiæ de peccatrice, Luc. VII. t. Sicuti, ju- vante Domino, postea ostendemus. Probo igi- tur Augustini sententiam, qui existimat, ean- dem illam Christi concionem bis fuisse habitam: se- mel sicut Matthæus describit: postea vero alio tem- pore & alia occasione fuisse repetitam, sicuti Lucas cap. X. vers. 13. describit. Nam & aliquando idem Evangelista idem a Christo bis vel aliquoties fuisse sive dictum sive factum narrat. Illustre et- am exemplum occurrit Matth. XII. 22. & Luc. XI. 14. ubi sic habet B. Lyserus Harmon. cap. LIX. in ratione ordinis: Scrupulum autem inji- cere videtur, quod Lucas simile miraculum & con- certationem, non hoc ordine, sed in ultima pro- fectione Christi cap. XI. vers. 14. describit, & ta- men omnia ita refert, ut videantur prorsus ea- dem esse, & non nisi semel uno loco & tempore facta. Sed nihil absurdi erit, si intelligamus bi- storian, quam Lucas dicto in loco describit, non eandem esse cum hac, quæ Matth. XII. vers. 22. & Marc. III. vers. 22. extat, sed in ultima pro- fectione Christi accidisse. Nam in sequentibus manifeste deprehendetur, quæ Lucas a cap. IX. vers. 51. describit, ea omnia in tertio anno mini- sterii Christi facta esse, licet tam conciones, quam miracula magna ex parte cum iis, quæ in priori- bus annis evenerunt, ita conveniant, & iisdem verbis describantur, ut prorsus eadem esse videan- tur. Sed eadem sæpius accidisse quis dubitabit? Cum etiam hac ipsa historia per multa conveniat cum illo miraculo, quod Matthæus cap. IX. vers. 32. annotavit, ubi etiam testatur, Christum eje- cisse Dæmonium mutum. Et inde secutam esse Pha- risæorum calumniam, quod Dæmones per Princi- pes Dæmoniorum ejiciat. Cum ergo in uno eodem- que Evangelista idem miraculum bis factum, & utrobique eandem calumniam inde ortam esse lega- mus: cur non duobus diversis temporibus dicta fa- ctaque, etsi similia, statuamus, quæ a duobus

Evangelistis destribuentur? Quæ monita perne- cessaria utinam semper a S. Augustino, ut & B. Lysero in Harmonia observata fuissent, cum temporis & loci ratio eadem requisivit, major si- ne dubio lux affulsisset in digerenda & eruenda Harmonia. Nec enim Concordantiis vulgaribus in Codicibus appositis, quantum ad rationem or- dinis, fides haberi potest, quæ sæpe solum ad consonantiam sententiarum ostendendam faciunt: Quod etiam in hac apologia Christi a Marco cap. III. vers. 22. - 30. proposita deprehenditur. Eam enim, etsi cum Matth. XII. 24. confe- rant Concordantiæ, adeoque B. Lyserus ad idem tempus referat, non tamen ad idem tempus re- ferri posse, ordo rerum gestarum docet: quum illa apologia cæci, qui & mutus fuit, sana- tionem sequatur apud Matthæum, illa vero a- pud Marcum jam ante ablegationem Apostolo- rum, utpote demum Marc. VI. 2. factam contigerit. Sed hæc & hujusmodi alia, in quibus par ratio, par necessitas, ex Harmonia nostra constabunt liquidissime. Unum adhuc monendum in antecessum, ducem ordinis non tam S. Marcum, quam Lucam eligendum nos censuisse, ut faciliora reddantur, quæ cætero- quin admodum difficilia, & perplexa forent. Id enim Marco propositum fuisse, Matthæi Ev- angelium in ordinem redigere, quod nonnullis visum fuit, non temere dixerim, quum Mat- thæi Evangelium satis ordinatum sit, modo se- ries rerum gestarum & temporum recte obser- vetur. Sed hæc omnia in clara luce ponen- tur per ipsam Harmoniæ nostræ συνίχνειαν & συνάφειαν. Quam uti luculenter privatim, divina adjutus παραδόσει, expedivi, semet- ipsam satis adserentem, id non abs re tamen fue- rit, si notis quibusdam, imprimis Harmonicis, vel εἱρμον τῆς ἀκολυθίας concernentibus, ne di- versis aliorum opinionibus, quæ sæpe certissima quæque incerta reddunt, luculentissima obscuri- tate involvunt, dubius reddatur lector, μονολεσ- χαρgν nostrum muniatur, atque confirmetur Operæ autem pretium erit adhuc paulo opero- sius de duce ordinis in antecessum disserere, ut mens nostra, & fundamentum nostræ sententiæ certius constet.

phonia τῶνα Evangelistarum uti eam, Anno 1613. Basileæ cum approbatione Ordinis Theolo- gici Basiliensis editam, vocavit, in Isagoge ad symphoniam, asserunt vel MATTHÆUM neglexisse ordinem summaque libertate usum esse, Marcum autem id egisse, ut ordinem in Historiam ejus Evangelicam induceret persuasi sunt. Quæ nec Spiritui Sancto, cujus amanuenses; si noh calami fuêre S. Evangelistæ conveniunt, ut- pote non confusionis, sed ordinis autori, nec Scriptoribus Canonicis digna sunt, quasi sine ordine Historiam quæ omnino ordinem poscit, consignarint, & quam pie aut prudenter hoc Spiritui Sancto impingatur, quod per Mat- thæum primum confuse Historiam Evangelicam veluti protruserit, deinde vero per Marcum ejus Epitomatorem id egerit, ut indigestæ Mat- thæi narrationi ordo aliquis conciliaretur, judi- candum relinquimus. Nec placere cordatis illa Selmætteri περιβολὴ poterit, quam vero cum Daniele Tossano (in literis ad Theobaldum Meuschium 4. Januar. Ann. 1598. datis) com- munem habet: Evangelistis (si forte Johannem quadantenus exceperis) non propositum fuisse Christi annales multo minus ejus Ephemerides con- scribere, sed ex infinito illo divine dictorum, fa- ctorumque numero ejus quædam tam ad fidem & vitam formandam sufficienter prout INCIDE- RUNT, consignare omnibus interea ad Filii DEI tum mortem, tum a morte ad immortalitatem re- surrectionem, ut salutis nostræ fundamenta pri- ma & summa, festinantibus. Non mirum certe si quis Judæorum Rabbinus, aut quis Ma- nes, vel Marcion, aut Celsus vel Porphyrius in modernis atheis redivivus, ut Selmætteri verbis utamur) talem scribendi rationem si ab Evangeli- stis usurpata foret, despiciat, ut indignam five testibus idoneis sive Scriptoribus θεοπνευςοις, quorum profecto non est, quidquid INCI- DERIT, conscribere, ordinemque negli- gere, & in Historia vite consignanda ad mortem festinare. Quæ etiam ab ipsa lectione S. Ev- angelistarum ceu falsa ἐγκλήματα facile convincuntur. De cætero non negamus S. MARCUM in ordine naturali Historiæ merito etiam observari, cæteris paribus, & sine præ- judicio S. MATTHÆI, quem B. PO- MERANUS noster secutus est in delineatio-

III. DE DUCE ORDINIS ET QUIBUSDAM IN ORDINE OBSERVANDIS.

S. LUCAS, cujus laus magna in Evangelio fuit per omnes Ecclesias II. Cor. IIX. 18. qui- que ἀκριβῶς, omnia persequutus ἄνωθεν inde ab initio est, ac καθεξῆς justo ordine, divino afflatus Spiritu, Historiam Evangelicam con- signavit Luc. I. 3. merito Dux ordinis consti- tuitur, qui etiam ea, qua de conceptione, na- tivitate, ac circumcisione JOANNIS Baptistæ & JESU CHRISTI dicenda erant, cum plusculis aliis solus annotavit, quemadmodum plerumque dicta & disputationes Christi S. Jo- hannes solus, quum ab aliis præterita ellent, ita dirigente Spiritu Sancto, conscripsit. Nec vero hic audiri merentur, qui Marcum in par- ticularibus historiis ab Johanne omissis, & a tri- bus prioribus Evangelistis pertractatis quoad eo- rum ordinem antecellere cum Andrea Selmættero Helvetio verbi Dei administro Reformato in Sym- ne Harmoniæ publice hic proposita, cujus e- laborationi beata ejusdem ἀνάλυσις intercessit, quam vero D. PAULUS CRELLIUS ex- pediit, quemadmodum S. MATTHÆUM Tiani Διατέσσαρον primo loco observavit, & ad eundem in plerisque quæ ab aliis communia sunt, cæteros revocavit; quod non fecisset, si ἀτάκτως & cum frequente transpositione ejus Historia consignatam judicasset. De S. LU- CA vero non præter rem observavit B. Chemni- tius in prolegom. cap. 2. eundem præfari, se id- co post alios scripturum, ut & ALTIUS histo- riam Evangelicam ordiatur, & ORDINE quodam illam contexat, sicut in multis ordinem Historiarum per circumstantias notet, ut in pleris- que cum Marco IN ORDINE conveniant, ut eo nomine à Tertulliano non invenuste scriptum I.uce DIGESTUM Historiæ Evangelicæ vocetur: (utut quædam, quorum ordo ex Matthæo & Marco manifestus sit, ipse per narra- tionis occasiohem aliquando loco non suo posue- rit, quod de paucis quibusdamπροθύμως largi- mur:) Idque inferre etiam voculam καθεξῆς non omnino in Prolegom. C. V. dissitetur B. Chemnitius, nimirum quod deinceps continua narratione distin- cte & distribute quasi per gradus reliqua velit adde- re. Vulgata reddit, ex ordine. Beza notat pro- prie esse continenter, additque non inconsiderate : Facit hic locus ut in harmonia Evangelistarum scri- benda certiorem ordinem servari putemus, si cum his, quæ habent communia reliqui ad Lucam potius accommodentur quam Lucas ad cæteros. Et hanc laudem, observata eadem emphasi hujus vocis jam pridem tribuit quoque S. LUCÆ Ambrosius Me- diolanensis Episcopus, quod scilicet καθεξῆς, id est distincte & distribute scripserit, ut solent ii, qui ad scribendam historiam aliquod judicium adfe- runt. Atque ita reddidit etiam Erasmus Schmi- dius noster verba Lucæ: visum est & mihi postquam pervestigavi a primo initio omnia exacte diligentiis ordine tibi (illa) scribere. Quod ALTIUS ordiri historiam velit jam voce ἄνωθεν indicarat, quæ idem est, quod ἀπ' ἀρχῆς Act. XXVI. 5. & teme- re ut adverbium loci a Gomaro accipitur, ac postea ad Deum, quasi e locis supernis a Deo accepisse hæc Lucam, innuatur, refertur. Dicitur enim o- mnia a principio accurate assequutus: non quod propinquus fuerit curiose personis omnibus, uti Syrus habet, interprete Ludovico de Dieu, sed quod o- mnia mente assecutus fuerit, ut Arabs habet, non se- cus ac si rebus illis gestis ipse intersuerit, ut Ca- pellus vocis παρηκολουθηκότι emphasin expen- dit. Quod agnoscit etiam Theobaldus Meuschius Inspector Atzeanus in Harmonia Evangelica, in prolegomen: quod nempe Lucas naturali serie, juxta leges historiæ, scripserit utplurimum, neque transpositionibus usus sit, nisi parvis & manifestis, id quod probat ex ipsius præfatione ubi dicit, se omnia ab initio ordine scripsisse: Deinde, ex eo quoque, quod Marcus conformiter cum ipso graditur : quod fieri non posset si uterque vel alter ex ipsis arbitraria methodo uteretur. Refellit etiam Meuschius con- trariam aliorum, imprimis D. Danielis Tossani sui, suppresso tamen ejus nomine, sententiam; cu- jus elenchum subjicere placet. Nec mihi, ait, objiciatur, hanc naturalem seriem Historiæ Evange- licæ nullo modo inveniri posse cum Evangelistarum nullus, in narrando eam servarit : sed singuli aliquid gestorum & dictorum Christi absque certo ordine, prout recordarentur, (verba hæc sunt Tossani) collegerint. Ego enim id pernego, & contra affir- mo, ex diligenti collatione omnium, naturalem seriem cum factorum tum dictorum Christi optime colligi posse. Evangelistæ enim singulari instinctu Spiritus Sancti ita scripserunt, ut ubi unus vel alter a naturali serie paulum deflexit, ibi alius juxta le- gem historiæ narrationem contexat. Imo (quod mi- randum est) etsi nullus alium imitatus est (Johannem excipio, qui dicitur alios vidisse & non nisi παρα- λειπόμενα scripsisse) sed quisque pro se absque alio scripsit: tamen se mutuo in narrando ita excipiunt, ut ubi hic desinit, ille incipiat. Nec consideran- ti difficile est consilium Spiritus Sancti advertere: voluit enim sic acuere nostram diligentiam, in le- gendis ac conjungendis omnibus Evangelistis, & inde nos de veritate totius historiæ & doctrinæ reddere cer- tiores. Cum videlicet videamus tantam esse consonan- tiam inter Evangelistas, qui tamen seorsim & obiter lecti prorsus inter se pugnare & rapsodias tantum collegisse videntur. Quapropter mihi quidem non est dubium, non solum summam esse inter Evangelistas consensum, de rebus ipsis : sed etiam singulos legem historiæ sic observasse, ut ex collatione omnium series naturalis, & ita ipse consensus facile colligi & demon- strari possit, utut perplexe singuli seorsim narrare videantur. Quin etiam hoc addo: absque collatio- ne omnium & indagatione seriei naturalis, neque certitudinem, neque perfectam sententiam singulo- rum haberi posse, ut mirer tam paucos Doctores, cum veteres, tum recentiores in Harmonia Evange- lica laborasse. Hæc omnia Meulchius: quæ omni- no probamus. Quibus tamen quomodo hypothe- ses ejus quibus ceu fundamentis innititur, satis non conveniant, equidem non intelligo: utpote quod Matthæum dicat, uti fere ordine ARBITRARIO, præsertim a Cap. V. usq; ad XIV, quod sæpe Evan- gelista ad unam concionem assumant quædam ex alia & ita duas diversas, similes tamen quoad argumen- tum aut cognatas conjungant. Quodque Matthæus præsertim conciones diversi temporis sæpe in unum colligat locum: quæ certe nec seriei naturali histo- riæ, nec legibus Historiographicis congruunt. Unde alia etiam absona in Harmonia Menschiana occurrere, mirum non est, quum ejusmodi hypo- thesibus sua superstruere non dubitarit; quale est v. g. illud paradoxon, quod Capita V. VI. & VII. Matthæi, quæ plerique, si non omnes Interpre- tes & merito ad unicam Christi concionem refe- runt, Summam esse velit & Capita, aliquot concio- num prima peragrationis Galilææ, collectarum & propter certam causam miraculis IIX. & IX. Capi- tis præmissarum non naturali sed arbitrario ordine relata, & talium exemplorum multo plura in Har- monia occurrere, censuerit. Sed accurata collatio Evangelistarum luculenter docebit, modo falsæ dimittantur prius mente conceptæ opiniones, nullum Evangelistarum tumultuarie vel confusè, quod illi vocant ordinem arbitrarium, scripsisse, o- mnes seriem rerum gestarum, ac dictorum or- dine consignasse, omnes mutuo se ratione ordinis non minus, quam ratione sententiarum, expli- care, nullam facile anticipationem nullum vσε- ρηστέρησιν, nisi ubi res ipsa ferat, & ex more historicorum, talia locum habent, occurrere, o- mnes ita divinitus inspiratos scripsisse, ut nihil ex memoria deprompserint, aut suopte consilio posue- rint, & uti unus est Spiritus, qui eos egit, unus Scripturæ autor, cujus organa tantum, & ama- nuenses Sancti Evangelistæ fuerunt, ita unum esse opus, per omnes contextum, sic, ut & singuli ordi- ne legi possint suo, & ex omnibus μονοτέσσαρον vel τεσσαρεσμόνον quoddam confieri possit, opti- me cohæreas, sine ulla additione peregrina, aut inserione necessaria, sine ullo hiatu, aut lacuna ul- la. Quod mirifice & delectat, & confirmat at- tentum Lectorem, ne de παναρμονίᾳ, & divini- tate S. Evangelii; quod revera unum est a qua- tuor-Viris illis sanctissimis contextum, ullatenus ambigere opus habeat, seriemque naturalem o- mnium Actorum, vel Factorum rectius animo suo imprimere queat. Ut taceam, quod talis coag- mentatio instar Commentarii haberi merito possit in quatuor Sanctos Evangelistas, sibi mutuo lu- cem affundentes, etsi unusquisque eorum et- iam propria & nativa luce fulgeat. Mihi certe summæ voluptati fuit, præ oculis intueri aliisque πρὸς ὄμμα ποιεῖν perpetuam istam & seriem & harmoniam; Cujus perspicuitas toti Historiæ lu- cem fœneratur. Unde ejusdem gratia non dubi- tavi, potius unam atq; alteram historiam, vel sen- tentiam ceu bis gestam, aut prolatam circumstan- tiis & verbis pene iisdem a diversis consignatam Evangelistis, maxime ubi temporis vel etiam loci ratio diversitatem convincebat, assumere, quam confusionem vel ordinem arbitrarium, aut quem memoria suggesserit, admittere. Qua de re jam antea monitum, penes omnes propemodum Harmoniæ Scriptores similia observata, nec a- liter posse alios, nisi vim historiæ inferant, eam- que utroque oculo suo privatam velint. De tempore autem non recedimus a prisca Ec- clesiæ autoritate, quoad tempus conceptionis, & nativitatis Christi in Chronologia nostra asser- tum, adeoque nec quoad conceptionis & nativitatis Johannis, nec quoad Baptismi Christi tempus, quum tres annos, & aliquot menses tantum exege- rit Christus in officio suo, dimidiam circiter septi- manam angelicam, nec nisi quatuor paschata in Ev- angelica historia reperiantur, ut ibidem ostendi- mus, ideo juxta eadem rectissime Harmonia con- texitur, nunciusque omnino mittendus est sen- tentiæ tum Tossani de tribus, tum Scaligerianæ de quinque paschatibus Christi; nec non Gerhardi Mercatoris & Theobaldi Meuschii de quatuor inte- gris Ministerii Christi annis: quæ nec funda- mentum habet, & miram parit confusionem. Unde etiam emendanda illa arbitraria profectio- num Christi distributio versus vel ab Hierosolymis excogitata a Meuschio, XII. festis anniversariis factarum, ut singulis annis tres profectiones conve- niant. Sed eamus in rem præsentem, & quomodo se- riem naturalem dictorum & factorum observent sancti Historici, ostendamus: præmissa cæteris præfatione S. Lucæ, quem etiam Ammonius Ale- xandrin. Andreas Osiander, B. Chemnitius, Cornel. Jansenius, Theobaldus Meuschius, Andr. Selmatte- rus, Rupertus Erythropilus, Eilhardus Lubinus, Johannes Cluderus primo loco posuere: Siquidem & ordine temporis, quo scripta sunt Evangelia S. LUCÆ & S. JOHANNIS, quæ procœmiis gau- dent, illud prius est: & præfatio S. Lucæ generalis est, de Historia Evangelica, sicut ab Apostolis tra dita, & ab Ecclesia certa fide tunc recepta fuerat: Ejus vero quæ sunt summaria Capita in Johannes Proœmio exponitur: unde non ita commode Johanneum procœmium a Tatiano, & Calixto præ- mittitur, ab hoc vero immerito etiam tum Lucæ præfatio plane omittitur, tum Cap. I. v. 5. seqq. post Capit. III. a vers. 23. ad 38. expositionem propo- nitur. Atque hæc in antecessum. Sequitur ite- rum

## 1:1 Introduction: I. N. J. Proem of St. Luke, in Which the Cause, Manner, and End of the Εὐαγγελιογραφίας (g
I. N. J. PROEM OF ST. LUKE, In which the cause, manner, and end of the Εὐαγγελιογραφίας (Gospel-writing) is set forth.

§. I. In the beginning, ST. LUKE gives the cause of the εὐαγγελιογραφίας (Gospel-writing), and at the same time builds up its credibility from the παραδόσει (tradition) of those who from the beginning were αὐτόπται (eyewitnesses) and ὑπηρέται τοῦ λόγου (ministers of the Word), the incarnate Word.

LUKE CHAPTER I.

Vers. 1. Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us.

Vers. 2. Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word.

[Under those 'many' he does not understand Matthew, nor Mark, much less John, who at that time had not yet undertaken the writing of the Gospel, but other non-Canonical writers, whom divine providence allowed to perish; but when he appeals to the παράδοσιν or tradition, which could be had at that time, while the disciples of Christ, the hearers, and spectators of the events were living, but now is pretended by a most vain reasoning, he by no means denies or detracts from τὴν θεοπνευστίαν (divine inspiration). For this can well consist with that. For this was added in the act of writing; it did not remove, but perfected the knowledge which the holy amanuenses of God possessed. Moreover, some take the word λόγου for the thing done: most explain it concerning the doctrine of the Gospel: But because they are said to be not only ὑπηρέται (ministers), but also αὐτόπται (eyewitnesses), whom St. Luke regards; τοῦ λόγου, it seems to us that the hypostatic λόγος (Word) should be understood, whom they served (for they hardly served most of the things done) and of whom they were αὐτόπται (eyewitnesses) no less than αὐτήκοοι (ear-witnesses), from whom St. Luke received many things: which sense is excellently confirmed from the collation of 1 John I. 1, ὃ ἑωράκαμεν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς &c. (which we have seen with our eyes, etc.).

§. II. Furthermore, St. Luke indicates from where he wishes to begin, and with what assurance, and in what order he wishes to proceed, addressing Theophilus, to whom he dedicates the Gospel.

Vers. 3. It seemed good to me also, having followed all things diligently from the beginning, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus.

[The word ἔδοξε does not denote a hasty thought or an uncertain opinion, but occurs even regarding those things which are established or decreed by certain counsel and serious deliberation, with the Holy Spirit Himself confirming or inspiring. Acts 15:28: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us. He denotes the beginning, from where he wishes to repeat the history, with the word ἄνωθεν; he gains credibility for himself with the words παρηκολουθηκότι πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς: finally, he indicates the order with the word καθεξῆς: concerning which it has already been spoken.]

§. III. Finally, he assigns the end of the writing as ἀσφάλειαν [certainty] concerning the discourses about which Theophilus had been informed.

Vers. 4. That you may know the certainty of those words in which you have been instructed.

[The emphasis is on the word ἐπιγινώσκειν, which Theophylact notes: we know unknown things, we ἐπιγινώσκομεν [know thoroughly], when we diligently and more certainly know those things which were previously known in some way. By this word the LXX interpreters not only translate the word ידע [to know], and נכר, which implies accurate recognition, distinguishing true from false, doubtful from certain; but also the word שכל in Job 34:27, which implies exquisite study and an intent mind: as also the word בין in Prov. 19:8, which, as Kircher notes in his Concordances, properly signifies to intend, consider, and care for intrinsically in the mind and intellect with order and a certain disposition, distinction, and judgment; what kind of thing it is, not otherwise than in architecture a house is proportionally distinguished into its rooms, regions, and parts.] The word κατηχήθης refers to the mode of information, which was done through κατήχησις, by word of mouth (from κατά and ἠχεῖν, to sound) and indeed by a voice of doctrine returned with a reciprocal sound, namely resounding and echoing in the mouth of those teaching and those learning, which instruction they call ἠχώδη, because it is done κατ' ἠχὼ. Compare Acts 18:25, Gal. 6:6. It is evident, therefore, that things written by divine inspiration bring greater ἀσφάλειαν [certainty] than discourses handed down by word of mouth, even by the very hearers and spectators of Christ, and that Holy Scripture brings ἀσφάλειαν [certainty] and a more certain ἐπίγνωσιν [thorough knowledge] to tradition. But these things are concerning the preface of St. Luke. There follows

Latin:

I. N. J. PROOEMIUM S. LUCÆ, In quo causa, modus & finis Εὐαγγελιογρα- φίας exponitur.

§. I. Initio causam εὐαγγελιογραφίας reddit S. LUCAS, ejusque fidem simul è παραδόσει ad- struit eorum, qui ab initio fuerunt αὐτόπται, & ὑπηρέται τοῦ λόγου, Verbi incarnati.

LUCÆ CAPUT I.

Vers. 1. Quoniam quidem multi conati sunt ordinare narrationem, quæ in nobis completæ sunt, rerum.

Vers. 2. Sicut tradiderunt nobis, qui ab initio ipsi viderunt, & ministri fuerunt sermonis.

[Sub multis illis non Mattheum, nec Marcum, nedum Johannem, qui tum nondum aggressus erat scriptionem Evangelii, sed alios non-Canoni- cos Scriptores, quos passa est divina providen- tia interire intelligit; cum autem ad παράδοσιν vel traditionem provocat, quæ tum haberi poterat, viventibus Christi discipulis, auditoribus, & spe- ctatoribus rerum, nunc autem vanissima ratione prætenditur, nequaquam τὴν θεοπνευστίαν abne- gat, aut eidem derogat. Hæc enim cum illa pro- be consistere potest. Nam hæc in actu scribendi ac- cessit; nec sustulit, sed perfecit notitiam, quam habuere sancti Dei amanuenses. Cæterum vo- cem λόγου accipiunt nonnulli pro re gesta: pleriq; de doctrina Evangelii explicant: Verum quia non tantum ὑπηρέται, sed etiam αὐτόπται fuisse di- cuntur, quos S. Lucas respicit; τοῦ λόγου, videtur nobis λόγος hypostaticus intelligendus, cui ser- vierunt (rebus vero gestis plerisque haud inservie- re) & cujus αὐτόπται non minus, quam αὐτήκοοι fuere, a quibus multa accepit S. Lucas: qui sensus eximie confirmatur è collatione 1. Joh. I. 1. ὃ ἑω- ρήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς &c.

§. II. Porro unde ordiri, & qua fide, quove ordine procedere velit, indicat S. Lucas, Theo- philum, cui nuncupat Evangelium, compellans.

Vers. 3. Visum est & mihi, assecuto omnia a principio diligenter, ex ordine tibi scribere, opti- me Theophile.

[Vox ἔδοξε non tumultuariam cogitationem, aut incertam opinionem notat, sed de iis etiam, quæ certo consilio, & gravi deliberatione statuuntur vel decernuntur, ipso quoque Spiritu S. confirman- te, vel inspirante, occurrit. Act. XV. 10. Visum est Spiritui S. & nobis. Initium, unde repetere ve- lit Historiam, voce ἄνωθεν denotat; Fidem au- tem conciliat sibi vocibus παρηκολουθηκότι πᾶ- σιν ἀκριβῶς: ordinem denique voce καθεξῆς indicat: de quibus jam dictum.]

§. III. Tandem finem assignat scriptionis ἀσ- φάλειαν de sermonibus, de quibus informatus erat Theophilus.

Vers. 4. Ut cognoscas eorum verborum, de quibus eruditus es, veritatem.

[Emphasis est in voce ἐπιγινώσκειν, quam no- tat Theophylactus: γινώσκομεν ignota, ἐπιγινώσ- κομεν, quando ea, quæ antea utcunque cognita fue- runt, diligenter & certius cognoscimus. Qua vo- ce non tantum exponunt LXX. Interpretes ver- bum ידע scivit, & נכר, quod accuratam agnitio- nem infert, vera a falsis, dubia a certis discernen- tem; sed etiam verbum שכל Iob. XXXIV. 27. quod exquisitum studium, animumque intentum im- portat: ut & verbum בין Prov. XIX. 8. quod Kir- chero in Concordd. notante, proprie significat in- trinsecus in mente, & intellectu ordine, & certa qua- dam dispositione, distinctione & judicio intendere, considerare & curare; qualis res sit, non aliter quam in architectonica domus in sua habitacula, regiones & partes proportionaliter distinguitur. Vox κατη- χήθης modum informationis respicit, quæ fiebat per κατήχησιν, viva voce (a κατ' & ἠχεῖν voce sonare) & quidem voce doctrinæ sono reciproco reddita, in ore scilicet docentium, & discentium resonante & re- meante, quam institutionem ἠχώδη vocant, quod fiat κατ' ἠχὼ. Confer. Actor. XVIII. 25. Gal. VI. 6. Patet ergo, quod divina inspiratione scripta majorem ἀσφάλειαν adferant, quam sermones vi- va voce traditi, etiam ab ipsis auditoribus, & specta- toribus Christi, quodque traditioni ἀσφάλειαν & certiorem ἐπίγνωσιν adferat Scriptura sacra. Sed hæc de præfatione S. Lucæ. Succedit

## 1:1 Introduction: Prologue of St. John
PROLOGUE OF ST. JOHN.

In which the main chapters of the Gospel, the incarnation of the eternal λόγος, his sojourn on earth, and the manifestation of divine glory are exhibited, not neglecting the testimony of John the forerunner concerning the λόγος.

§. I. The eternity and true Deity of the λόγος.

JOHN. CHAP. I.

Ver. 1. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

Ver. 2. This was in the beginning with God.

[The summary chapters of what is to be delivered in the Gospel are concerning the incarnation of the eternal Word and his acts on earth, and concerning the testimony of his forerunner John about him. Therefore, this prologue of St. John deals primarily with the pre-eternal προϋπάρξει (pre-existence) of the Word and his temporal ἐνσαρκώσει (incarnation), not neglecting, as we have said, the testimony of St. John the Baptist concerning the same; since both the mission and testimony of this forerunner of Christ, and the coming of the Word himself into the world, and what he did for the sake of our salvation, were to be described. Therefore, St. John, the eagle of the Evangelists, flies higher to the very eternity of the WORD, his existence with GOD the Father, his true Deity, and his eternal pre-existence with the Father. In the beginning of the creation of all things, the λόγος (Word), the Son of God, was not finally made or begotten, but already existed, and thus is truly eternal; moreover, he existed with God the Father, as one from whom he is distinct τῇ ὑποστάσει (in person), and in whom the Son was from eternity, the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, v. 18. But lest the Word be believed to be different from the Father in Deity, or τῇ ὀυσίᾳ (in essence), as he is distinguished from him τῇ ὑποστάσει (in person), St. John adds, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος, and the Word was God, i.e., as equally true God as the Father, or rather, the same God as to essence. Finally, lest any doubt remain concerning the pre-eternity and pre-existence, and the distinction from the Father, and the Deity of the λόγος (Word), he embraces all those in one sentence: ὗτος, this (which was the predicate in the preceding proposition, who is the λόγος) ἦν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν, was in the beginning, as the eternal God, and not indeed finally made in time, with God the Father. God with God, the λόγος (Word) with the Father, in whose bosom he was. They are therefore distinguished by persons: but because the λόγος (Word) is God just as the Father is, and there is no God except one in nature and essence, therefore the Word and the Father are not distinguished by Deity or divine essence, but are one, John X. 30, 1 John V. 7.]

§. II. Through the λόγος (Word) all things were created.

Ver. 3. All things were made through him, and without him was made nothing that was made.

[Having asserted the eternal Deity of the λόγος (Word), he testifies that he is the same true creator of all things, because there is no true God except the creator of heaven and earth: which, since God is said to have created heaven and earth in the beginning, Gen. I. 1, the λόγος (Word), the Son of God, created all things with the Father, and the Father did not indeed found anything without the λόγος (Word). He says that all things were founded through the λόγος (Word), not as through a medium or instrument, because in the beginning there was nothing outside of God, and the Word was true and eternal God: but that the Father founded all things through the Son as the co-eternal and co-essential hypostatic Word, who was from eternity with God, and who was God: and indeed all things without exception: therefore it is added, and without him was made nothing that was made. Therefore the λόγος (Word) cannot be numbered among those things which were made, or among creatures, as he is the one through whom all things were made and founded in the beginning of all things. Concerning which see the special treatise on this, 'In the beginning was the Word,' asserting the pre-eternal existence and Deity of the Son of God against the Socinians and Arians.]

§. III. In the λόγος (Word) was life, which was the light of men.

Verse 4. In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

[He descends from the general work of creation to those things which concern the species, both all living things, and especially man: concerning whose eternal life St. John was about to say that the λόγος willed to become man, c. XXI. 31. And therefore, not only was life in him from eternity ὑσιωδῶς (essentially), as he who is life itself; but also from him is the life of all living things ἐνεργητικῶς (actively), just as he also teaches all the light which is in men, i.e., that he himself is the author and cause of all life, and also of illumination and spiritual light; who, by procuring spiritual life for us in particular, and thus vivifying us, illuminates us, or renders us partakers of light, and by illuminating us through the word, vivifies us: for neither can light exist without life, nor spiritual life without light in man. Therefore we are truly illuminated unto eternal life, because he is the light to us, in whom was life from eternity, and who is eternal life itself, 1 John I. 2. 5. c. V. 11.]

§. IV. The light shining in darkness, not apprehended by the darkness.

Verse 5. And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.

[Now he explains the reason why most are not illuminated by this light. It is not situated in the light, because the λόγος willed to be the light of men; nor only when there were as yet no darknesses in man, as he who had been created in the image of God, in knowledge and wisdom, Col. III. 10. Gen. I. 26. But also when, through the apostasy, there was nothing but mere darkness in the world: for that light shines in darkness: Φαίνει (it shines) implies a perpetual act: it never is not, and nowhere is not shining in darkness: in men overwhelmed by spiritual darkness, who were mere darkness, Eph. V. 8, devoid of all spiritual light: for whose sake, that they might be illuminated, that light shines, ever since the rise of darkness, that true and great light, as one that would illuminate every man, as far as it is in itself, v. 9. But the reason why most are not illuminated is that the darkness did not admit or receive the light, οὐ κατέλαβεν (it did not apprehend it).] Just as the Sun is both inclined and powerful to diffuse its light through all rooms, yet some things remain dark, either because of a lack of windows, or because they are covered with thick veils; so the λόγος, the Sun of righteousness, that true light, is both able and eager to illuminate the hearts of all men through the radiance of the Gospel, but most remain in darkness, they do not receive the light, either because they lack windows, i.e., they have not ears to hear, or because their hearts are covered with thick linens of errors and vices. Luke VIII. 12. Darknesses are men, subject to the darkness of the mind, of ignorance and errors, Job XII. 35, Eph. IV. 18, the darkness of the heart, of vices and sins, which are the works of darkness, Rom. XIII. 12, the darkness of affliction, Is. V. 13, Lam. III. 3, and the darkness of damnation, which is the outer darkness, Matt. XXII. 13.

§. V. John sent, that he might testify concerning that true light, that through him they might believe.

Verse 6. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

Verse 7. This man came for a testimony, that he might bear witness concerning the light, that all might believe through him.

Verse 8. He was not that light, but [was sent] that he might bear witness concerning the light.

Verse 9. That was the true light, which illuminates every man coming into this world.

[Because he said that the light SHINETH in darkness in the present tense, he refers indeed to the continuous act of shining, but primarily also to that time when that light arose for the world, when the dayspring from on high visited us, ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει, καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις Luc. I. 79., which the Baptist, as the Morning Star, had to testify concerning the peculiar rising of that light in the world indicating that the sunrise is imminent. John therefore treats of him, and indicates his mission and testimony concerning this light, as an office for which he was sent, and the end of the testimony, that all might believe through him: and thus he distinguishes him from that great light which illuminates every man. Therefore, the cause why all men are not illuminated is not to be cast upon God or the Word of God, since God sends heralds of the Word so that ALL may believe, and for that end the Word is preached; nor is it to be cast upon that great light, which, as far as concerns the gracious will, the merit of illumination, and the means which are destined for all on account of the same, illuminates every man, even if all are not illuminated in the second act, by the fault of men themselves. Furthermore, that illumination is most simply understood from the antithesis of darkness, as has been rightly noted by the blessed Chemnitz: For 1. against the darkness of ignorance, he illuminates us by the revelation of the Word and the illustration of the Spirit unto true knowledge. 2. Against the darkness of sin, he illuminates us by the imputation of righteousness, the remission of sins, and the renovation begun in this life. 3. Against the darkness of the wrath of God, he illuminates the face of God upon us by grace, reconciliation, and adoption, just as Scripture speaks, Num. VI. 25. 4. Against the darkness of miseries, he shines upon us by consolation, mitigation, and liberation. 5. Against the outer darkness of death and damnation, he illuminates us with life and eternal salvation, 2. Tim. I. 10. He illuminated life, Col. I. v. 12, unto the lot of the saints in light. Moreover, that ἐρχόμενον εἰς τ᾿ κόσμον could be referred to τὸ Φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν, so that the advent of that true light into this world is indicated, just as in the following verse it is immediately said to have been in the world, and v. 11 to have come into his own: and v. 14 to have dwelt among men having been made flesh: concerning which matter we have spoken in the loc. cit.

§. VI. He was in the world, created through him. But the world did not know him.

Vers. 10. He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him.

[That 'he was in the world' is understood either of the beginning of the light, which shone for man after the fall, since from then on he was known by few: or rather of the fullness of time, when the Son of God came into the world born of a woman, Gal. IV. 4. But the world is said to have been made through him, so that, when he himself, the creator of the world, wished to come into the world for our sake, the extreme indignity of the matter might be noted, that the world, the greatest part of men in the world, refused to receive him, and did not even know him. Therefore, the world is accused here of ungrateful spirit and stupor, as Cyril says, which both ignored its own author and did not bring forth the good fruit of its own illumination.]

§. VII. And although he came into his own, yet he was not received by his own.

Vers. 11. He came into his own, and his own did not receive him.

[Εἰς τὰ ἴδια. The world pertains to τὰ ἴδια. But he came more specifically to τὰ ἴδια: where oi ἴδιοι did not receive him; both regarding men in general, because he came to men, who are his own, above other creatures: and regarding the Jews in particular, to whom he had been sent primarily, and who were his peculiar possession, and his ἴδιοι, whom he had separated for himself as a people, and from whom he willed to be born according to the flesh. Concerning which Cyril says: It is no wonder if the world did not recognize the only-begotten, which has turned aside from the right way of understanding, when even the people themselves, whom God chose for himself as peculiar above others, rejected him present in the flesh, and would not receive him who had come for the salvation of all. Let the blessed Chemnitz be added: When he first says 'the world did not receive,' he shows the sad blindness of fallen nature to be such that it cannot recognize Christ by the natural powers of reason. But when he adds 'his own,' who had the Word, to whom he came in assumed flesh with doctrine and miracles, did not receive him, he shows extreme malice joined to blindness, because they resisted the Holy Spirit, who wished to illuminate them by the given Word.]

§. VIII. Concerning the ἐξουσία [authority] of those who received the λόγος [Word], and who they are that received him.

Ver. 12. But as many as received him, to them he gave the power to become the sons of God, to them that believe in his name.

V. 13. Who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

[The words καταλαμβάνειν in v. 5, παραλαμβάνειν in v. 11, and λαμβάνειν in v. 12 could perhaps be distinguished. But here they seem to be almost synonyms: for the darkness is said not to have comprehended [the light], which not only cannot comprehend, but cannot even apprehend the light as long as it remains darkness: just as οἱ ἴδιοι [his own] are said not to have received him coming εἰς τὰ ἴδια [to his own]: but believers are said to λαμβάνειν, to receive the Son of God: whence the Syrian rendered both λαμβάνειν and παραλαμβάνειν with the same word קבל. These words, however, explain each other: that we ought to receive the Son of God through faith in such a way that we take him to ourselves, as it were, when he offers himself to us, and strive to embrace and comprehend him entirely. But the ἐξουσία [authority] is given to those who receive him by the λόγος [Word] himself, that they may become the sons of God: which is a notable argument for the deity of the λόγος: for to grant the right and dignity that one may become a son of God belongs to no one but God alone: where the blessed [Chemnitius] has clearly warned Chemn. that it is not power or faculty that is implied, as if we could, if we pleased, become sons of God by the powers of free will; for those who have received the Son of God are already in act the sons of God: For we are all the sons of God through faith, Gal.
