Mark 1:21. And they enter into Capharnaum: and straightway on the sabbath days he entered into the synagogue, and taught them.

Verse 22. And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

Luke 4:31. And he went down into Capharnaum, a city of Galilee, and there he taught them on the sabbath days.

Verse 32. And they were astonished at his doctrine, for his word was with power.

§. III. He delivers one possessed in the same synagogue: rebuking the demon testifying about him, whence his fame spreads everywhere, Mark 1:23-28; Luke 4:33-37.

Mark 1:23. And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit: and he cried out.

Verse 24. Saying: What have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know who thou art, the Holy One of GOD.

Vers. 25. And Jesus rebuked him, saying: Hold thy peace, and go out of the man.

Vers. 26. And the unclean spirit tearing him, and crying out with a loud voice, went out of him.

Vers. 27. And all were amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying: What thing is this? what is this new doctrine? for with power he commandeth even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.

Vers. 4. And the fame of him went out forthwith into all the country of Galilee.

Luke IV. 33. And in the synagogue there was a man who had an unclean devil, and he cried out with a loud voice.

Vers. 34. Saying: Let us alone, what have we to do with thee, Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

Vers. 35. And Jesus rebuked him, saying: Hold thy peace, and go out of him. And when the devil had thrown him into the midst, he went out of him, and hurt him nothing at all.

Vers. 36. And there came fear upon all, and they talked among themselves, saying: What word is this? for with power and authority he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they go out.

Vers. 37. And the fame of him was divulged into every place of the region.

Capernaum, a pleasant village, Schöndorff, by some called כפר נחום which is propitiation, or כפר נחם repentance, as if to say the propitiation of the penitent, was situated in the middle of the twelve tribes of Israel: for it had towards the North three tribes, Naphtali, Asher, and Zebulun: and towards the South four tribes, Benjamin, Judah, Dan, and Simeon: towards the West were situated to this city Issachar, Ephraim, and the half tribe of Manasseh: towards the East, however, beyond the Jordan and the sea of Tiberias, Reuben, Gad, and the half of Manasseh. Furthermore, it was situated in the land of Gennesaret, on the western and northern shore of the Jordan, 14 miles from Jerusalem towards the North, at which same interval it was distant from the Gentile region of Tyre and Sidon in the borders of both Galilees: which some refer to the tribe of Zebulun, others to the tribe of Naphtali, because near Capernaum the boundaries of the strong tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali met. And it was a most beautiful emporium; which because it was near the sea of Gennesaret, and the Jordan, and the passage through it was for the regions beyond the river to the great sea, and it held a middle position between the Jews and the Gentiles, being distant by an equal interval from Jerusalem and from Tyre and Sidon, therefore it was convenient for the habitation, doctrine, and miracles of Christ, for his fame to be spread abroad through various regions. It was the chief city of all Galilee. Whence Caesar had his Centurion there: Herod his Palatine, or petty king: the Chief Priests their Ruler of the Synagogue.

CHAPTER VIII. The mother-in-law of Peter, and the restoration of many other sick persons.

§. I. Having left the school with his disciples, he came into the house of Peter, and by the extension of his hand, rebuking the fever, he healed his mother-in-law who was suffering from a fever, Mark I. 29-31. Luke IV. 38-39.

Mark I. 29. And immediately going out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

Verse 30. But the mother-in-law of Simon was lying down with a fever, and immediately they tell him about her.

Verse 31. And approaching, he raised her up, having taken her hand: and the fever left her immediately, and she served them.

Luke IV. 38. But Jesus rising from the synagogue, entered into the house of Simon. And the mother-in-law of Simon was held by great fevers: and they asked him for her.

Verse 39. And standing over her, he commanded the fever: and it left her. And immediately rising, she served them.

§. II. In the evening many sick persons were brought to him, all of whom he healed by the laying on of hands. He also cast out demons from many with a rebuke, not permitting them to testify about him, Mark I. 32-34. Luke IV. 40. 41.

Mark I. 32. And when evening had come, when the sun had set, they were bringing to him all who were ill, and those having demons:

Vers. 33. And all the city was gathered at the door.

Vers. 34. And he cured many that were vexed with various diseases, and he cast out many devils, and he suffered them not to speak, because they knew him.

Luc. IV. 40. And when the sun was set, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him. And he laying his hands on every one of them, cured them.

Vers. 41. And devils went out from many, crying out and saying: Thou art the Son of GOD: and rebuking them he suffered them not to speak, for they knew that he was Christ.

§. III. Withdrawing in the morning into a desert place for the sake of praying, he is sought by Peter and others, to whom however he says: That the Gospel must be preached to others also, and he preaches throughout all Galilee, and casts out devils, Marc. I. 35-39. Luc. IV. 42-44.

Marc. I. 35. And rising very early, going out he went into a desert place, and there he prayed.

Vers. 36. And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.

Vers. 37. And when they had found him, they said to him: All seek for thee.

Vers. 38. And he saith to them: Let us go into the neighbouring towns and cities, that I may preach there also: for to this purpose am I come.

Vers. 39. And he was preaching in their synagogues, and in all Galilee, and casting out devils.

Luke IV. 42. And when it was day, going out he went into a desert place, and the multitudes sought him, and came even unto him: and they detained him, that he should not depart from them.

Verse 43. To whom he said: Because I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.

Verse 44. And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

CHAPTER IX. The confirmation of Peter and the other disciples in their office after the miraculous catch of fish.

§. I. About the sea of Gennesaret, as the people flocked and pressed upon him, Christ teaches from Simon's boat in the sea.

Luke 5, v. 1. And it came to pass, that when the multitudes pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret.

Verse 2. And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.

Verse 3. And entering into one of the ships, which was Simon's, he desired him that he would draw back a little from the land. And sitting he taught the multitudes out of the ship.

§. II. He commands them to launch out into the deep, and casting the net they enclose a great multitude of fishes.

Verse 4. Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon: Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

Verse 5. And Simon answering, said to him: Master, we have laboured all the night, and have taken nothing: but at thy word I will let down the net.

Verse 6. And when they had done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net was breaking.

Verse 7. And they beckoned to their partners that were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they were almost sinking.

§. III. He raises up Peter, who was terrified with his companions, and appoints him a fisher of men.

Verse 8. Which when Simon Peter saw, he fell down at Jesus's knees, saying: Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

Verse 9. For amazement had surrounded him, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken.

Verse 10. And so also were James and John the sons of Zebedee, who were partners of Simon. And Jesus saith to Simon: Fear not: from henceforth thou shalt be catching men.

Verse 11. And having brought their ships to land, leaving all things, they followed him.

CHAPTER X. The healing of a certain leper.

§. I. When he was in a certain city, Christ healed a certain leper, Luke 5:12-14. Mark 1:40-45.

Luke V. 12. And it came to pass, when he was in one of the cities, behold a man full of leprosy, who seeing Jesus, and falling on his face, besought him, saying: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

Verse 13. And stretching out his hand he touched him, saying: I will: Be thou made clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

Verse 14. And he charged him that he should tell no man: but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.

Mark 1. 40. And there came a leper to him, beseeching him: and kneeling down said to him: If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

Verse 41. And Jesus having compassion on him, stretched forth his hand: and touching him, saith to him: I will: Be thou made clean.

Verse 42. And when he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.

Verse 43. And he strictly charged him, and forthwith sent him away:

Verse 44. And saith to him: See thou tell no one: but go, show thyself to the high priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.

Verse 45. But he being gone out, began to publish and to blaze abroad the word: so that now he could not openly go into the city, but was without in desert places, and they flocked to him from all sides.

[B. Chemnitius acknowledges that this leper is different from the leper healed by Matthew in chapter VIII, even though the words and circumstances agree: let him be compared here in Harmon. chapter XLII. See also what we noted below in Art. II. chapter VI. However, that city in Galilee, in which Christ taught, seems to have been ἀνώνυμος, Luke IV. 43, 44, and in the sea of Gennesaret he confirmed Peter with his companions for the fishing of men by a miraculous catch of fish. chapter V. 1. following to 11.

§. II. The fame of him being spread abroad, many flock to Christ, that they may hear him, and that they may be cured.

Verse 15. But the fame of him went abroad the more, and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be cured of their infirmities.

§. III. Christ withdraws into the desert for the sake of praying.

Verse 16. But he himself withdrew into the desert, and prayed.

CHAPTER XI.

The healing of a certain paralytic in Capernaum.

§. I. Jesus comes again into Capernaum, and many were gathered to him, to whom he preached, Mark 2:1, 2. There were also present Pharisees and experts in the Law, and by the power going out from him many were healed, Luke 5:17.

Mark 2:1. And again he entered Capernaum after some days,

Verse 2. And it was heard that he was in the house, and many gathered, so that there was no room, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.

Luke 5:17. And it came to pass on one of the days, and he himself was sitting teaching. And there were Pharisees sitting, and doctors of the law, who had come from every village of Galilee, and Judea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was there to heal them.

§. II. A paralytic was brought, whom they had let down through the roof, to whom, when he forgave his sins, and the Pharisees and Scribes accused him, Christ demonstrates by his healing that the power of forgiving sins had been given to him, Mark 2:3-13. Luke 5:18-26.

Mark II. 3. And they came to him bringing a paralytic, who was carried by four.

Verse 4. And when they could not bring him to him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was: and opening it, they let down the bed, in which the paralytic was lying.

Verse 5. And when Jesus had seen their faith, he said to the paralytic: Son, thy sins are forgiven thee.

Verse 6. And there were some of the Scribes sitting there, and thinking in their hearts:

Vers. 7. Why does this man speak thus? He blasphemes: Who can forgive sins, but GOD alone?

Vers. 8. And immediately Jesus knowing in his spirit, that they so thought within themselves, saith unto them: Why think ye these things in your hearts?

Vers. 9. Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy: Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say: Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

Vers. 10. But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy.)

Vers. 11. I say unto thee: Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

Vers. 12. And immediately he arose, and, taking up the bed, went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified GOD, saying: We never saw it on this fashion.

Vers. 13. And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

Luke V. 18. And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

Vers. 19. And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

Vers. 20. And when he saw their faith, he said: Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

Vers. 21. And the scribes and Pharisees began to think, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but GOD alone?

Vers. 22. But when Jesus knew their thoughts, answering, he said to them: What are you thinking in your hearts?

Vers. 23. Which is easier to say: Your sins are forgiven you; or to say: Arise, and walk?

Vers. 24. But that you may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, (he says to the paralytic) I say to you, arise; take up your bed, and go into your house.

Vers. 25. And immediately rising up before them, he took the bed on which he lay: and went away to his house, glorifying GOD.

Vers. 26. And astonishment seized all, and they glorified GOD. And they were filled with fear, saying: For we have seen wonderful things today.

CHAPTER XII. The calling of Matthew and its consequences.

§. I. Jesus, having gone out, called Levi the son of Alphaeus from the custom house, Mark II. 14-15. Luke V. 27. 28.

Mark II. 14. And when he was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the custom house, and he said to him: Follow me. And rising up he followed him.

Vers. 15. And it came to pass, as he was sitting at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat down together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, who also followed him.

Luke 5:27. And after these things he went out, and saw a publican named Levi, sitting at the tax office, and said to him: Follow me.

Verse 28. And leaving all things, rising up he followed him.

§. II. The banquet of Levi, in which, while the Pharisees and lawyers were murmuring because he was taking food with publicans and sinners, Christ answers that the sick have need of a physician, and that he came to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous, Mark 2:16, 17. Luke 29-32.

[But this banquet with the Apology, and the question concerning fasting subjoined, seem to some to be related here by Mark and Luke by way of πρόληψις (prolepsis), on the occasion of the calling of Matthew, even if they happened at another time. Conf. Harm. Chemnit. cap. XLII. But that there is no need for that πρόληψις, the order and the series flowing most excellently teaches, provided it be noted that a repeated or confirmed calling of Matthew is described by Matthew himself in chapter 9:9, as having been done after the sermon on the mount. However, those who disagree here suppose that Mark is the simplest and most correct guide of order, who reduced the histories of Matthew into a certain order: which hypothesis the thing itself confirms is not necessary; just as it is also not likely that Matthew the Apostle so neglected order that there was need of Mark's writing, by which Matthew, equally ἰσόπνευστος (inspired by the same Spirit), and furthermore an Apostle, might be reduced into order. And the blessed Chemnitius acknowledges that he does not have necessary demonstrations for his opinion, but only probable reasons, and leaves to the judgment of each person whether he wishes to follow his opinion, or indeed that of Osiander, Molinæus, and Codomannus, by which some histories in Mark and Luke are established as different from similar ones described by Matthew; which, however, are clearly different, is evident from the diversity of time and other circumstances. We are speaking of certain ones, about which it will be clear in the progress; but we do not, with Osiander, make the same histories of the raised daughter of some ruler, and of the woman with the issue of blood healed, to be different.]

Mark 2:16. And the Scribes and Pharisees seeing that he was eating with publicans and sinners, said to his disciples: Why does your Master eat and drink with publicans and sinners?

Verse 17. Having heard this, Jesus says to them: They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick: for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.

Luke 5:29. And Levi made a great banquet for him in his house, and there was a great crowd of publicans and others who were reclining with them.

Verse 30. And the Pharisees and their Scribes were murmuring, saying to his disciples: Why do you eat and drink with publicans and sinners?

Verse 31. And Jesus answering, said to them: They that are whole do not need a physician, but they that are sick.

Ver. 32. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

§. III. To some asking why the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast so certainly, but the disciples of Christ do not, Christ replies: that the guests do not fast while the bridegroom is still present, nor should an old garment be mended with a new patch, or new wine be poured into an old wineskin, Mark II. 18-22. Luke V. 33-39.

Mark II. 18. And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting: and they come and say to him: Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?

Ver. 19. And Jesus said to them: Can the children of the bridechamber fast, as long as the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

Ver. 20. But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them: and then they shall fast in those days.

Ver. 21. No man seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: otherwise it takes away the patch from the old, and a greater tear is made.

Verse 22. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins: otherwise the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine will be spilled, and the wineskins will perish: but new wine must be put into new wineskins.

Luke 5. 33. But they said to him: Why do the disciples of John fast frequently, and make supplications, likewise also those of the Pharisees: but yours eat and drink.

Verse 34. To whom he said: Can you make the children of the bridegroom fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

Verse 35. But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, then they will fast in those days.

Verse 36. And he spoke also a parable to them: That no one puts a piece from a new garment into an old garment: otherwise he both tears the new, and the piece from the new does not match the old.

Verse 37. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins: otherwise the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it itself will be spilled, and the wineskins will perish.

Verse 38. But new wine must be put into new wineskins, and both are preserved.

Verse 39. And no one drinking old wine, immediately wants new, for he says: The old is better.

SECTION II.

ARTICLE II.

THE ACTS OF CHRIST FROM THE SECOND PASSOVER TO THE THIRD.

CHAPTER I.

The healing of the lame man in Bethesda, and the Apology of Christ.

§. I. Jesus healed a lame man in Bethesda at the feast of the Passover.

Ver. 1. After these things there was a feast day of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

Ver. 2. Now there is at Jerusalem a sheep-pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches.

Ver. 3. In these lay a great multitude of impotent folk, of blind, halt, withered, waiting for the moving of the water.

Ver. 4. For an angel of the Lord went down at a certain season into the pool: and the water was troubled. And whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.

Ver. 5. And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years.

Ver. 6. When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole?

Verse 7. The invalid answered him: Sir, I have no man, when the water has been troubled, to put me into the pool: for while I am coming, another descends before me.

Verse 8. Jesus says to him: Arise, take up your bed, and walk.

Verse 9. And immediately that man was made whole: and he took up his bed and walked. And it was the Sabbath on that day.

§. II. The Jews rebuke the man who was healed, because on

the Sabbath he carried his bed: he appeals to the command of him by whom he had been healed, not knowing who he was.

Verse 10. The Jews therefore said to him who had been healed: It is the Sabbath, it is not lawful for you to take up your bed.

Verse 11. He answered them: He who made me whole, he said to me: Take up your bed, and walk.

Verse 12. They asked him therefore: Who is that man who said to you: Take up your bed, and walk?

Verse 13. But he who had been made whole did not know who it was. For Jesus had withdrawn from the crowd gathered in the place.

§. III. Jesus, having found the man who was healed, warns him not to sin again: he indicates to the Jews that it is Jesus who healed him; they seek to kill Jesus because he did this on the Sabbath.

Verse 14. Afterward Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him: Behold, you are made whole: sin no more, lest something worse happen to you.

Vers. 15. That man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.

Vers. 16. Therefore the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the Sabbath.

§. IV. Jesus defends the deed by the perpetual operation of his Father, whence they strive all the more to slaughter him, because he made himself equal to GOD the Father. Which indeed Christ asserts in a brilliant Apology, and thus clearly confirms his ὁμοουσίαν with the Father.

Vers. 17. But Jesus answered them: My Father works until now, and I work.

Vers. 18. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him: because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also said that God was his Father, making himself equal to GOD. Jesus therefore answered, and said to them:

Vers. 19. Amen, amen I say to you: The Son cannot do anything of himself, unless he sees the Father doing it; for whatever he does, these things the Son also does in like manner.

Vers. 20. For the Father loves the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does: and he will show him greater works than these, that you may wonder.

Vers. 21. For as the Father raises the dead, and gives them life: so also the Son gives life to whom he will.

Vers. 22. For neither does the Father judge any man: but has given all judgment to the Son.

Vers. 23. That all may honor the Son, as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father, who sent him.

Vers. 24. Amen, amen I say to you, that he who hears my word, and believes him who sent me, has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.

Vers. 25. Amen, amen I say to you, that the hour comes, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of GOD, and they who hear shall live.

Vers. 26. For as the Father has life in himself: so he has given to the Son also to have life in himself.

Vers. 27. And he has given him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of man.

Vers. 28. Do not marvel at this, because the hour is coming, in which all who are in the graves will hear the voice of the Son of GOD:

Ver. 29. And they shall come forth, who have done good, unto the resurrection of life: but they who have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.

Ver. 30. I can do nothing of myself. As I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just: because I seek not my own will, but the will of him who sent me.

§. V. Jesus appeals to the testimony of John, of his own works, of his Father, and even of Moses himself.

Ver. 31. If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.

Ver. 32. There is another who bears witness of me: and I know that the witness which he bears of me is true.

Ver. 33. You sent unto John: and he bore witness to the truth.

Ver. 34. But I do not receive testimony from man: but I say these things, that you might be saved.

Ver. 35. He was a burning and a shining lamp. And you were willing for a time to rejoice in his light.

Ver. 36. But I have a greater witness than John. For the works which the Father has given me to accomplish, these very works which I do, bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me:

Ver. 37. And the Father who sent me, he himself has borne witness of me: neither have you ever heard his voice, nor seen his form.

Vers. 38. And you do not have his word abiding in you: because, whom he sent, him you do not believe.

Vers. 39. Search the scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me:

Vers. 40. And you will not come to me, that you might have life.

Vers. 41. I do not receive glory from men.

Vers. 42. But I have known you, that you do not have the love of God in you.

Vers. 43. I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me: if another shall come in his own name, him you will receive.

Vers. 44. How can you believe, who receive glory from one another; and do not seek the glory that is from God alone?

Vers. 45. Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one who accuses you, Moses, in whom you hope.

Vers. 46. For if you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me also: for he wrote of me.

Vers. 47. But if you do not believe his writings: how will you believe my words?

CHAPTER II.

The defense of the disciples plucking ears of grain on the Sabbath.

§. I. On the second-first Sabbath, the disciples of Christ rub ears of grain while they go through the cornfields, Mark II. 23, Luke VI. 1.

Mark II. 23. And it came to pass again, as the Lord was walking through the cornfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to go forward and to pluck the ears of grain.

Luke VI. 1. And it came to pass on the second-first Sabbath, as he was passing through the cornfields, his disciples were plucking the ears of grain and were eating, rubbing them with their hands.

[Concerning the second-first Sabbath, we have spoken at Luke VI. 1, that it was the weekly and ordinary Sabbath which followed the Sabbath of the feast of the Passover, which opinion of Epiphanius, Theophylact, Blessed Luther, Ludovicus de Dieu, and others is proven there. However, this history is not to be confused with that one, although very similar, which Matthew described in chapter XII: because they differ greatly in time: For the present one happened on the weekly Sabbath after the second Passover of Christ: But that one, which Matthew describes, occurred when the third Passover was imminent: This former one preceded the mountain sermon of Christ: but that latter one followed the mountain sermon of Christ entirely, with many other things intervening. Although the healing of the withered hand followed both, yet the healing of a certain man having a withered hand followed the former on a Sabbath not the same, or second-first, but the following one: But a similar cure followed the latter on a certain weekly Sabbath, not the second-first, but before the feast of the Passover, and that indeed imminent; and on that very same one on which the Apostles rubbed the ears of grain. Therefore, the rule handed down at the beginning from St. Augustine, Blessed Chemnitz, and Blessed Osiander is to be recalled here, that the same histories, as far as words and deeds are concerned, are not rarely not the same, but different, namely when the circumstances of time, place, and others prove their diversity, since nothing prevents the same words and deeds from being said and done by Christ at a different time and place. And I have already noticed by the observation of Blessed Chemnitz that Molineus and Cadomannus also agree with this opinion of ours, after I had already placed the same in the Harmony: however much I am ignorant of their reasons, being still destitute of their writings: But all things seem so clear to me in the Evangelical series.

§. II. The Pharisees rebuke this as illicit on the Sabbath, Mark II. 24, Luke VI. 2.

Mark II. 24. But the Pharisees were saying to him: Behold, why do they do on the Sabbaths what is not lawful?

Luke 6:2. But some of the Pharisees said to them: Why do you do what is not lawful on the sabbaths?

§. III. Christ defends this by the example of David (1 Sam. 21:6) and because the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath, Mark 2:25-28, Luke 6:3-5.

Mark 2:25. And he said to them: Have you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry, he and they that were with him?

Verse 26. How he went into the house of God under Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the loaves of proposition, which was not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave to them who were with him:

Verse 27. And he said to them: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.

Verse 28. Therefore the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath.

Luke 6:3. And Jesus answering them, said: Have you not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was hungry, and they that were with him:

Verse 4. How he went into the house of God, and took and ate the loaves of proposition, and gave to them that were with him, which it is not lawful to eat but only for the priests?

Verse 5. And he said to them: That the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath.

CHAPTER III. The withered hand and the healing of many sick.

§. I. On another Sabbath, when a certain man having a withered hand was present in the Synagogue, and the Pharisees were watching Christ, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, Christ, perceiving their thoughts, asked: is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do evil? He healed him, Mark III. 1-5. Luke VI. 6-10.

Mark III. v. 1. And he entered again into the Synagogue: and there was a man there having a withered hand.

Ver. 2. And they were watching him, if he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might accuse him.

Ver. 3. And he saith to the man having the withered hand: Stand forth in the midst.

Ver. 4. And he saith to them: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it? But they were silent.

Ver. 5. And looking round about on them with anger, being grieved for the blindness of their heart, he saith to the man: Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth, and his hand was restored to him.

Luke VI. ver. 6. And it came to pass also on another Sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue, and taught. And there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.

Ver. 7. And the Scribes and Pharisees were watching, if he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find whereof to accuse him.

Ver. 8. But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man who had the withered hand: Rise and stand in the midst. And rising he stood.

Vers. 9. But Jesus said to them: I ask you, if it is lawful to do good on the sabbaths, or to do evil? to save a life, or to destroy it?

Vers. 10. And looking round about on them all, he said to the man: Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth, and his hand was restored.

§. II. The Pharisees then consulting with the Herodians about killing Jesus, Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea: a great multitude followed him, so that he had need to go aboard a boat, Mark III. 6-9. Luke VI. 11.

Mark III. 6. And the Pharisees going out, immediately made a consultation with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

Vers. 7. But Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee and Judea followed him,

Vers. 8. And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan: and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing what he did, came to him.

Vers. 9. And he spoke to his disciples, that a small boat should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.

Luke VI. 11. But they were filled with madness, and talked one with another, what they might do to Jesus.

§. III. He healed many, and cast out demons, whom he rebuked for confessing him, that they should not make him known, Mark III. 10-12. His fame spread throughout all Syria, hence from every side the sick and those possessed by demons were brought to him, Matthew IV. 24. 25.

Mark 3:10. For he healed many, so that as many as had plagues pressed upon him to touch him.

Verse 11. And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him: and cried out saying:

Verse 12. You are the Son of GOD. And he strictly charged them that they should not make him known.

Matthew 4:24. And his fame went throughout all Syria, and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatick, and those that had the palsy, and he healed them.

Verse 25. And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judaea, and from beyond Jordan.

[His fame was spread abroad into all the regions lying round about far and wide, Idumaea, Palestine, Syrophoenicia, Syria of Damascus, Syria of Antioch, Coele-Syria, Arabia, not only into the neighboring ones, Judaea, Peraea, Batanaea, Galilee, Decapolis, Samaria. For all these regions, and certain others related to them, are comprehended under the name of Syria, whose boundaries are described: from the North, Cilicia; from the South, Egypt; from the West, the Great Sea, which is also called the Syrian Sea; from the East, the river Euphrates.

CHAPTER IV. The Election of the Apostles.

§. I. For the sake of prayer Christ ascends the mountain and stays there by night.

Luke 6:12. And it came to pass in those days that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to GOD.

§. II. In the morning he calls together his disciples and chooses twelve from them, who are named Apostles, and are listed.

Mark III. 13. And going up into a mountain, he called unto him whom he himself would: and they came unto him.

Verse 14. And he made that there should be twelve with him; and that he might send them to preach.

Verse 15. And he gave them power to cure infirmities, and to cast out devils.

Verse 16. And he gave Simon the name Peter:

Verse 17. And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and he gave them the name Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

Verse 18. And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite.

Verse 19. And Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Luke VI. 13. And when day was come, he called his disciples, and he chose twelve of them, (whom also he named Apostles)

Verse 14. Simon, whom he surnamed Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,

Verse 15. Matthew and Thomas, James of Alphaeus and Simon, who is called Zelotes.

Ver. 16. And Judas of James, and Judas Iscariot, who was the traitor.

CHAPTER V. Christ's long sermon on blessedness, with vindications of the law from Pharisaic corruptions and various admonitions.

§. I. The sermon to the disciples and the people, which he delivered having been established on a plain before a great crowd, therefore ascending a mountain with his disciples, Matt. V. 1. 2. Luke VI. 17-19.

Matt. V. 1. And Jesus seeing the crowds, went up into a mountain, and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him.

Verse 2. Opening his mouth he taught them, saying.

Luke VI. 17. And coming down with them, he stood in a level place, and the crowd of his disciples, and a copious multitude of the people from all Judea, and Jerusalem, and the seacoast, and Tyre, and Sidon.

Verse 18. Who had come to hear him, and to be healed of their infirmities. And those who were troubled by unclean spirits were cured.

Verse 19. And all the crowd sought to touch him: because power went out from him, and healed all.

Osiander, in his annotations to the Harmony, book I, chapter XXIX, says that those are not uncommonly mistaken who think the sermon described by Matthew is the same as the one we read in Luke chapter VI: But although he acknowledges that they have many things in common, he could bring forward no solid reason why it is necessary to establish distinct histories here. For the fact that he says almost an entire year intervened between this and that is proven by no evidence from him, and is rejected with the same ease with which it is asserted. He appeals to his Elenchus: but that is assumed, not proven. And therefore it does not appear why we should desert the common opinion. And that all things are correct regarding the εἱρμὸν ἀκολουθείας [sequence of events], the order shown by us, if it is compared with the Evangelists with accurate study, will easily convince the attentive reader.

That mountain is shown a quarter of a German mile from Capernaum towards the south-west near the bank of the Sea of Galilee, of exceptional height, adorned with various kinds of herbs and flowers, fertile and pleasant; from which the whole Sea of Galilee is seen, as well as the regions of Ituraea and Trachonitis as far as Lebanon, with the mountains of Sanir and Hermon, and a great part of upper and lower Galilee.

§. II. He taught who are truly blessed, Matt. V. 3-12. Luke VI. 20-23. and who on the contrary are unhappy, 24-26.

Matth. V. 3. Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Vers. 4. Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the earth.

Vers. 5. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

Vers. 6. Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall be filled.

Vers. 7. Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

Vers. 8. Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see GOD.

Vers. 9. Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of GOD.

Vers. 10. Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Vers. 11. Blessed are you when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly, for my sake.

Vers. 12. Be glad and rejoice, for your reward is very great in heaven. For so they persecuted the prophets that were before you.

Luc. VI. 20. And he, lifting up his eyes to his disciples, said: Blessed are ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 21. Blessed are you who hunger now: for you shall be filled. Blessed are you who weep now: for you shall laugh.

Vers. 22. Blessed shall you be when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake.

Vers. 23. Rejoice in that day, and be glad: for behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

Vers. 24. But woe unto you that are rich, for you have your consolation.

Vers. 25. Woe unto you that are full: for you shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep.

Vers. 26. Woe, when men shall speak well of you, for in like manner did their fathers to the false prophets.

§. III. Concerning the duty of the disciples, which is illustrated by the likenesses of salt and light.

Matth. V. 13. You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt have lost its savour, wherewith shall it be salted? It is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.

Vers. 14. You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hid.

Vers. 15. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it gives light unto all that are in the house.

Vers. 16. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father, which is in heaven.

§. IV. On the purpose of the coming of Christ, and true salvific righteousness.

Vers. 17. Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets: I have not come to abolish, but to fulfill.

Vers. 18. For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one apex will pass from the law, until all things are done.

Vers. 19. Whoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whoever shall do and teach them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

Vers. 20. For I say to you, that unless your righteousness shall abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

§. V. Vindications of the commandment concerning not killing.

Vers. 21. You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill: and whoever shall kill, shall be liable to judgment.

Vers. 22. But I say to you: that everyone who is angry with his brother, shall be liable to judgment. And whoever shall say to his brother, raca: shall be liable to the council. And whoever shall say, you fool: shall be liable to the fire of hell.

Vers. 23. If therefore you offer your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you:

Vers. 24. Leave your gift there before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to your brother: and then coming you shall offer your gift.

Vers. 25. Be in agreement with your adversary quickly, while you are in the way with him: lest perhaps the adversary deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer: and you be cast into prison.

Ver. 26. Amen I say to you, you shall not go out from there, until you pay the last farthing.

§. VI. Vindications of the commandment concerning not committing adultery.

Ver. 27. You have heard that it was said to them of old: You shall not commit adultery.

Ver. 28. But I say to you, that whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her, has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

Ver. 29. And if your right eye scandalizes you, pluck it out, and cast it from you: for it is expedient for you that one of your members should perish, rather than that your whole body should go into hell.

Ver. 30. And if your right hand scandalizes you, cut it off, and cast it from you: for it is expedient for you that one of your members should perish, rather than that your whole body should go into hell.

Ver. 31. And it has been said: Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a bill of divorce.

Ver. 32. But I say to you: That whosoever shall put away his wife, excepting for the cause of fornication, makes her to commit adultery: and he that shall marry her that is put away, commits adultery.

§. VII. Vindications of the commandment concerning not swearing falsely.

Ver. 33. Again you have heard that it was said to them of old: You shall not forswear yourself: but you shall perform your oaths to the Lord.

Ver. 34. But I say to you, not to swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of GOD:

Ver. 35. Nor by the earth, for it is his footstool: nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great king:

Ver. 36. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white, or black.

Ver. 37. But let your speech be, yea, yea: no, no: and that which is more than these, is of evil.

§. VIII. Against private revenge, and concerning the love of one's neighbor, even an enemy; Matt. V. 38-48. Luke VI. 27-35.

Matt. V. 38. You have heard that it hath been said: An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.

Ver. 39. But I say to you, not to resist evil: but if any man strike thee on thy right cheek, turn to him also the other.

And to him that will contend with thee in judgment, and take away thy coat, let go thy cloak also unto him.

And whosoever will force thee one mile, go with him other two.

Give to him that asketh of thee: and to him that would borrow of thee, turn not away.

Ver. 43. You have heard that it hath been said: Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thy enemy.

Ver. 44. But I say to you: Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you: and pray for them that persecute and calumniate you:

That you may be the children of your Father, who is in heaven: who maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad: and raineth upon the just and the unjust.

Vers. 46. For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even the tax collectors do this?

Vers. 47. And if you greet your brothers only, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do this?

Vers. 48. You therefore must be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect.

Luc. VI. 27. But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.

Vers. 28. Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who abuse you.

Vers. 29. And to him who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other also. And from him who takes away your cloak, do not withhold your tunic either.

Vers. 30. Give to everyone who begs from you; and of him who takes away your goods, do not ask them back.

Vers. 31. And as you wish that men would do to you, do so to them likewise.

Vers. 32. And if you love those who love you, what thanks is it to you? For even sinners love those who love them.

Vers. 33. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what thanks is it to you? For even sinners do the same.

Vers. 34. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what thanks is it to you? For even sinners lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

Vers. 35. But love your enemies: do good, and lend, hoping for nothing therefrom: and your reward shall be great, and you shall be the children of the Highest, for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

§. IX. Concerning alms to be dispensed without boasting.

Matt. VI, 1. Take heed that you do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you shall have no reward of your Father, which is in heaven.

Vers. 2. Therefore when you do your alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.

Vers. 3. But when you do alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand does:

Vers. 4. That your alms may be in secret: and your Father, who sees in secret, shall reward you.

§. X. Concerning the establishing of prayer, and the form of prayer with an explanation of the fifth petition.

Vers. 5. And when you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men: amen I say to you, they have received their reward.

Vers. 6. But you, when you pray, enter into your closet, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret: and your Father, who sees in secret, shall reward you.

Vers. 7. But when you pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

Vers. 8. Be not you therefore like unto them: for your Father knows what things you have need of, before you ask him.

Vers. 9. Thus therefore shall you pray: Our Father, who art in heaven: hallowed be thy name.

Vers. 10. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, and on earth.

Vers. 11. Give us this day our supersubstantial bread.

Vers. 12. And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

Vers. 13. And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil. Amen.

Ver. 14. For if you forgive men their sins, your heavenly Father will also forgive you your offenses.

Ver. 15. But if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive you your sins.

§. XI. On observing fasting without hypocrisy.

Ver. 16. And when you fast, do not become sad like the hypocrites: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear to men to be fasting. Amen, I say to you, they have received their reward.

Ver. 17. But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face.

Ver. 18. That you may not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father, who is in secret: and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.

§. XII. On gathering treasures not on earth, but in heaven.

Ver. 19. Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth: where rust and moth consume: and where thieves break through, and steal.

Ver. 20. But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven: where neither rust, nor moth consumes; and where thieves do not break through, nor steal.

Ver. 21. For where your treasure is, there is your heart also.

§. XIII. On simplicity of heart.

Verse 22. The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.

Verse 23. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great will that darkness be?

§. XIV. Concerning serving GOD alone, not Mammon, and without distrust regarding food and clothing, and seeking first the kingdom of GOD and his righteousness.

Verse 24. No one can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other: or he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve GOD and mammon.

Verse 25. Therefore I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you shall eat, nor for your body, what you shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

Verse 26. Look at the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns: and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?

Verse 27. And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to his stature?

Verse 28. And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil, neither do they spin.

Verse 29. And I say to you, that not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these.

Verse 30. But if GOD so clothes the grass of the field, which today is, and tomorrow is cast into the oven: how much more you, O you of little faith?

Verse 31. Therefore do not be anxious, saying: What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or with what shall we be clothed?

Verse 32. For the Gentiles seek after all these things. For your Father knows that you need all these things.

Vers. 33. Seek therefore first the kingdom of GOD, and his righteousness: and all these things shall be added unto you.

Vers. 34. Be not therefore anxious for the morrow. For the morrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient unto the day is its own evil.

§. XV. Concerning mercy, Luke VI. 36-42. Matthew VII. 1-5.

Luke VI. 36. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

Vers. 37. Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned. Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven.

Vers. 38. Give, and it shall be given unto you: a good measure, and pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

Vers. 39. And he spake also a parable unto them: Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

Vers. 40. The disciple is not above his Master: but every one when he is perfected shall be as his master.

Vers. 41. And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

Vers. 42. Or how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye: and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother's eye.

Matthew VII. 1. Judge not, that ye be not judged.

Ver. 2. For with what judgment you judge, you shall be judged, and with what measure you measure, it shall be measured to you.

Ver. 3. And why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, and do not see the beam in your own eye?

Ver. 4. Or how do you say to your brother: Let me cast out the speck from your eye: and behold a beam is in your own eye?

Ver. 5. Hypocrite, cast out first the beam from your own eye, and then you shall see to cast out the speck from your brother's eye.

§. XVI. Concerning not casting what is holy to dogs.

Ver. 6. Do not give what is holy to dogs, neither cast your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them with their feet, and turning, tear you.

§. XVII. Exhortation to prayer.

Ver. 7. Ask, and it shall be given to you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.

Ver. 8. For everyone who asks, receives: and he who seeks, finds: and to him who knocks, it shall be opened.

Ver. 9. Or what man is there among you, whom if his son asks for bread, will he reach him a stone?

Ver. 10. Or if he asks for a fish, will he reach him a serpent?

Verse 11. If therefore you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your Father, who is in heaven, give good things to those who ask him?

§. XVIII. Whatever we wish that should be done to us, let us do to others.

Verse 12. Therefore all things, whatsoever you wish that men should do to you, do you also to them. For this is the law and the prophets.

§. XIX. Let us strive to enter through the narrow gate.

Verse 13. Enter through the narrow gate: for the gate is wide, and the way is broad, that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it.

Verse 14. How narrow is the gate, and constricted the way, that leads to life: and there are few who find it.

§. XX. Let us beware of false prophets. Matt. VII. 15-20. Luke VI. 43-45.

Matt. VII. 15. Beware of false prophets who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

Ver. 16. By their fruits you shall know them. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

Ver. 17. Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit: but the evil tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

Ver. 18. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit: neither can an evil tree bring forth good fruit:

Ver. 19. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire.

Ver. 20. Therefore by their fruits you shall know them.

Luke VI. v. 43. For there is no good tree that bringeth forth evil fruit: nor an evil tree that bringeth forth good fruit.

Ver. 44. For every tree is known by its fruit. For men do not gather figs from thorns: nor do they gather a grape from a bramble bush.

Ver. 45. A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil. For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

§. XXI. Concerning hypocrites who are also famous for notable gifts. Matt. VII. 21-23. Luke VI. 46.

Matt. VII. v. 21. Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he who does the will of my Father, who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 22. Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name done many mighty works?

Ver. 23. And then I will declare to them: That I never knew you: depart from me, you who work iniquity.

Luke VI. 46. But why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do the things which I say?

§. XXII. Conclusion of the sermon on the mount concerning hearers who convert into practice what they have heard, similar to prudent architects building on rock, and concerning foolish architects, Matt. VII. 24-27. Luke VI. 47-49.

Matt. VII. 24. Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, shall be likened to a wise man, who builds his house upon a rock,

Ver. 25. And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house, and it did not fall: for it was founded upon a rock.

Ver. 26. And everyone who hears these words of mine, and does not do them, shall be like a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:

Ver. 27. And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the ruin of it.

Luke VI. v. 47. Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them: I will show you what he is like.

Verse 48. He is like a man building a house, who dug deep, and laid a foundation upon a rock: and when a flood occurred, the river burst against that house, and could not move it: for it had been founded upon a rock.

Verse 49. But he who heard, and does not do, is like a man building his house upon the earth without a foundation: against which the river burst, and immediately it fell: and the ruin of that house was great.

§. XXIII. The admiration of the people because of Christ's sermon, Matt. VII. 28. 29.

Matt. VII. v. 28. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished the words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching.

Verse 29. For he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes, and Pharisees.

CHAPTER VI. The healing of lepers, the Centurion's servant, and others.

§. I. A leper comes to meet Christ descending from the mountain, whom he cleanses.

Matt. VIII. v. 1. And when he had descended from the mountain, great crowds followed him.

Ver. 2. And behold, a leper coming, worshipped him, saying: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

Ver. 3. And Jesus stretching forth his hand, touched him, saying: I will: Be thou made clean. And forthwith his leprosy was cleansed.

Ver. 4. And Jesus saith to him: See, tell no man: but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

This leper of Matthew is different from the leper in Luke ch. V. 12, however much the petition of the leper, and the response and command of Christ, consist of almost the same words: because they differ both by reason of place: that leper of Luke was healed in a certain city, which is not held of this one, but the contrary, because Christ descending from the mountain betook himself to no other city than Capernaum, Matth. VIII. 1, which is never so indefinitely described as μία τ πόλεων, but is either designated by its own name, or called the city of Christ: and that before the entry of Jesus into Capernaum the leper present met him is clear from a comparison of v. 1 and 5: and by reason of time. For the healing of this one was done after the sermon on the mount; but the healing of that one in Luke long preceded the mountain sermon of Christ: Which diversity of time and place compels us to establish different persons and histories here.

§. II. Entering Capernaum, he restored the centurion's servant, Matth. VIII. 5-13. Luc. VII. 1-10.

Matth. VIII. 5. And when he had entered into Capernaum, there came to him a centurion, beseeching him.

Ver. 6. And saying: Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, and is grievously tormented.

Ver. 7. And Jesus saith to him: I will come and heal him.

Ver. 8. And the centurion making answer, said: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

Ver. 9. For I also am a man subject to authority, having under me soldiers, and I say to this man: Go, and he goeth; and to another: Come, and he cometh; and to my servant: Do this, and he doeth it.

Ver. 10. And Jesus hearing this, marvelled, and said to them that followed him: Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith in Israel.

Vers. 11. But I say to you, that many shall come from the East and West, and shall recline with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven:

Vers. 12. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

Vers. 13. And Jesus said to the Centurion: Go, and as you have believed, so be it done to you. And the boy was healed in that hour.

Luke VII. v. 1. And when he had finished all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capharnaum.

Vers. 2. And a certain centurion's servant, who was ill, was about to die: who was precious to him.

Vers. 3. And when he had heard of Jesus, he sent to him the elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.

Verse 4. And when they had come to Jesus, they besought him earnestly, saying to him: That he is worthy that thou shouldst grant this to him.

Verse 5. For he loveth our nation: and he hath built us a synagogue.

Verse 6. And Jesus went with them: and when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying: Lord, do not trouble thyself: For I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof.

Verse 7. For which cause neither did I think myself worthy to come to thee: but say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

Verse 8. For I also am a man subject to authority, having under me soldiers: and I say to this one, go, and he goeth; and to another, come, and he cometh; and to my servant, do this, and he doeth it.

Verse 9. Which Jesus hearing, marvelled: and turning to the multitude that followed him, he said: Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith, not even in Israel.

Verse 10. And they who were sent, returning home, found the servant who had been sick, whole.

[Andreas Osiander imagines a double centurion, one of Matthew, another of Luke; although the histories are very similar, Annot. in libr. 1. Harmon. cap. XXXVII. But his reasons are not of such weight that we should dismiss those which so clearly exhibit the same history, and establish diverse histories on account of some difficulties that are only apparent, but easily reconcilable: since in the Chemnitz Harmony they are solved without trouble.

§. III. He healed Peter's mother-in-law again, Matt. VIII. 14. 15. And in the evening he cured a huge multitude of the sick: And by that very thing the prophecy of Isaiah was fulfilled (chap. LIII. 4.) Matt. VIII. 16. 17.

Matt. VIII. v. 14. And when Jesus was come into Peter's house, he saw his mother-in-law lying, and sick of a fever.

Vers. 15. And he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she arose, and ministered unto them.

Vers. 16. And when evening was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word: and healed all that were sick.

Vers. 17. That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying: Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.

[That this healing of Peter's mother-in-law and of others is different from that which is described in Mark 1:30-34 and Luke 4:38-41, the circumstance of time proves. For that one occurred before Christ's sermon on the mount; but this one occurred after Christ had delivered the same and descended from the mountain, as is clear from Matthew 8:1.

CHAPTER VII.

The raising of the son of the widow of Nain.

§. I. As Christ was entering the city of Nain, the funeral of the son of a certain widow came to meet him, whom Christ consoles, and raises the son with a word.

Luke VII. v. 11. And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

Vers. 12. Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

Vers. 14. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

Vers. 14. And he came near, and touched the bier. (But they who were carrying him, stood still,) And he said: Young man, I say to thee, arise.

Vers. 15. And he that was dead, sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

§. II. He is thence proclaimed as a great Prophet, and the fame of him is spread throughout all Judea, Luke VII. 16. 17. The fame of the miracles being carried even to John provided the cause for John's embassy to Christ, which is here commemorated by Luke κατ᾿ πρόσληψιν, Luke VII. 18--28. with the consequences, vers. 29--35.

Vers. 16. And there came a fear on all: and they glorified GOD, saying: That a great prophet is risen up among us: and that GOD hath visited his people.

Vers. 17. And this rumour went forth throughout all Judea concerning him, and through all the country round about.

Vers. 18. And John's disciples told him of all these things.

Vers. 19. And John called to him two of his disciples, and sent them to Jesus, saying: Art thou he that art to come, or look we for another?

Vers. 20. And when the men were come unto him, they said: John Baptist hath sent us to thee, saying: Art thou he that art to come, or look we for another?

Vers. 21. (And in that same hour, he cured many of their diseases, and hurts, and evil spirits: and to many that were blind he gave sight.)

Vers. 22. And answering, he said to them: Go and relate to John what you have heard and seen: The blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead rise again, to the poor the gospel is preached.

Vers. 23. And blessed is he whosoever shall not be scandalized in me.

Vers. 24. And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak to the multitudes concerning John: What went you out into the desert to see? a reed shaken with the wind?

Vers. 25. But what went you out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, they that are in costly apparel and delicacies are in the houses of kings.

Vers. 26. But what went you out to see? A prophet? Yea, I say to you, and more than a prophet:

Vers. 27. This is he, of whom it is written: Behold, I send my angel before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee.

Vers. 28. For I say to you: Among those that are born of women, there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist. But he that is the least in the kingdom of God, is greater than he.

Vers. 29. And all the people hearing, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

Vers. 30. But the Pharisees and the lawyers despised the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized by him.

Vers. 31. And the Lord said: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? And to what are they like?

Vers. 32. They are like to children sitting in the marketplace, and speaking one to another, and saying: We have piped to you, and you have not danced: we have mourned, and you have not wept.

Verse 33. For John the Baptist came, neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: He has a demon.

Verse 34. The son of man came eating and drinking, and you say: Behold a gluttonous man, and a drinker of wine; a friend of publicans and sinners.

Verse 35. And wisdom is justified by all her children.

[Buntingius thinks that this raising of the widow's son in Nain, four miles from Capernaum, took place in the month of May, when he was going up to Jerusalem for the feast of Pentecost, which is twelve miles distant from Nain.

CHAPTER VIII. The absolution of the sinful woman.

§. I. Christ being received at a banquet by a Pharisee, a certain sinful woman waters his feet with tears, and dries them with her hair, and kisses them, and anoints them with ointment.

Verse 36. And one of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house and sat down to eat.

Verse 37. And behold, a woman that was in the city, a sinner, when she knew that he sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment.

Verse 38. And standing behind at his feet, she began to wash his feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment.

§. II. Christ convinces his host Simon by a certain parable and argument that many sins have been forgiven the woman, because she has loved much: and thus that her sins are publicly forgiven; and because he was tacitly accused of that matter, he teaches that she obtained that forgiveness itself by faith, and thus he sends her away in peace.

Verse 39. And the Pharisee, who had called him, seeing it, spoke within himself, saying: This man, if he were a prophet, would surely know who and what manner of woman this is that touches him: for she is a sinner.

Vers. 40. And Jesus answering, said to him: Simon, I have something to say to thee. But he said: Master, say it.

Vers. 41. Two debtors were to a certain creditor: one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

Vers. 42. And whereas they had not wherewith to pay, he forgave them both. Which therefore doth love him most?

Vers. 43. Simon answering, said: I suppose that he to whom he forgave most. And he said to him: Thou hast judged rightly.

Vers. 44. And turning to the woman, he said to Simon: Dost thou see this woman? I entered into thy house, thou gavest me no water for my feet; but she with tears hath washed my feet, and with her hairs hath wiped them.

Vers. 45. Thou gavest me no kiss; but she, since she came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

Vers. 46. My head with oil thou didst not anoint; but she with ointment hath anointed my feet.

Vers. 47. Wherefore I say to thee: Many sins are forgiven her, because she hath loved much. But to whom less is forgiven, he loveth less.

Vers. 48. And he said to her: Thy sins are forgiven thee.

Vers. 49. And they that sat together at meat began to say within themselves: Who is this that forgiveth sins also?

Vers. 50. And he said to the woman: Thy faith hath made thee safe: Go in peace.

CHAPTER IX. Miraculous apology for the casting out of demons, and the Parable of the seed and the lamp.

§. I. Christ preaches from town to town about the kingdom of GOD: whom the Apostles and some pious women follow.

Luke VIII. v. 1. And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and showing the glad tidings of the kingdom of GOD: and the twelve were with him.

Ver. 2. And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,

Ver. 3. And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.

[In the month of June, Büntingius, in the place cited, is the authority that Jesus, having returned from Jerusalem to Galilee, 14 miles from the feast of Pentecost, undertook a visitation through individual cities and villages, and when he had walked about thus for some time, he finally returned home to his own city, Capernaum, and there healed a demoniac who was blind, deaf, and dumb.

§. II. In a certain house, being reproached by the Pharisees as if he casts out a demon through Beelzebub, he defends himself sharply.

Mark III. v. 20. And they come into an house, and the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

Ver. 21. And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

Ver. 22. And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.

Ver. 23. And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

Vers. 24. And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

Vers. 25. And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

Vers. 26. And if Satan rise up against himself, he is divided, and cannot stand, but hath an end.

Vers. 27. No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

Vers. 28. Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

Vers. 29. But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation.

Vers. 30. Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

§. III. A great multitude being gathered, Christ proposes and explains the parable of the seed of the word, Luke 8:4-15; likewise concerning the lamp not to be hidden, with a warning that the truth be properly attended to: because to him that hath shall be given: concerning the growth of the seed and the mustard seed: and on the occasion of the presence of his mother and brethren, those are called the mother and brethren of the Lord who hear the word of God and do it, Luke 8:16-21; Mark 3:31-35; ch. 4:1-34.

Luke 8:4. And when much people were gathered and were hastening to him from the cities, he said by way of a parable:

Verse 5. A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.

Verse 6. And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.

Verse 7. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.

Verse 8. And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

Verse 9. And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?

Verse 10. And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of GOD: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.

Verse 11. Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of GOD.

Verse 12. Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.

Verse 13. They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.

Verse 14. And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

Vers. 15. But that which fell into good ground: these are they, who in a good and perfect heart, hearing the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit in patience.

Vers. 16. Now no man lighting a lamp covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it upon a candlestick, that they that come in may see the light.

Vers. 17. For there is not any thing secret that shall not be made manifest, nor hidden, that shall not be known and come abroad.

Vers. 18. Take heed therefore how you hear. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given: and whosoever hath not, that also which he thinketh he hath, shall be taken away from him.

Vers. 19. And his mother and brethren came unto him; and they could not come at him for the crowd.

Vers. 20. And it was told him: Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.

Vers. 21. Who answering said to them: My mother and my brethren are they who hear the word of GOD, and do it.

Marc. III. 31. And his mother and his brethren come; and standing without, they sent unto him, calling him.

Vers. 32. And the multitude sat about him; and they say to him: Behold thy mother and thy brethren without seek thee.

Vers. 33. And answering them, he said: Who is my mother and my brethren?

Vers. 34. And looking round about on them who sat about him, he saith: Behold my mother and my brethren.

Vers. 35. For whoever shall do the will of GOD, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.

Marc. IV. v. 1. And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.

Vers. 2. And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine.

Vers. 3. Hearken: Behold, there went out a sower to sow.

Vers. 4. And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

Vers. 5. And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

Vers. 6. But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

Vers. 7. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

Vers. 8. And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

Vers. 9. And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

Vers. 10. And when he was alone, those who were with him with the twelve asked him about the parable.

Vers. 11. And he said to them: To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of GOD: But to them that are without, all things are done in parables:

Vers. 12. That seeing they may see, and not see: and hearing they may hear, and not understand: lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them:

Vers. 13. And he saith to them: Know you not this parable? and how shall you know all parables?

Vers. 14. He that soweth, soweth the word.

Vers. 15. And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown, and when they have heard, immediately satan cometh, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

Vers. 16. And these are they likewise who are sown on the stony ground: who when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy:

Vers. 17. And have no root in themselves, but are temporal: then when tribulation and persecution ariseth for the word, immediately they are scandalized.

Vers. 18. And others are they who are sown among thorns: these are they that hear the word.

Vers. 19. And the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts after other things entering in choke the word, and it is made fruitless.

Vers. 20. And these are they who are sown upon the good ground, who hear the word, and receive it, and yield fruit, the one thirty, another sixty, and another an hundred.

Vers. 21. And he said to them: Doth a candle come in to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?

Vers. 22. For there is nothing hidden, which shall not be manifested: nor has it been made secret, but that it may come into the open.

Vers. 23. If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.

Vers. 24. And he said to them: Take heed what you hear. In what measure you shall mete, it shall be measured to you, and more shall be added to you.

Vers. 25. For he that has, to him shall be given: and he that has not, even that which he has shall be taken away from him.

Vers. 26. And he said: So is the kingdom of GOD as if a man should cast seed into the ground.

Ver. 27. And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.
