Ver. 43. And they took up the remnants, twelve full baskets of fragments, and of the fishes.

Verse 44. Now those who ate were five thousand men.

Luke IX. Verse 10. And the Apostles returned, and told him all that they had done: and taking them, he withdrew apart into a desert place, which is Bethsaida.

Verse 11. And when the crowds had known this, they followed him: and he received them, and spoke to them of the kingdom of God, and healed those who were in need of care.

Verse 12. And the day had begun to decline. And the twelve coming said to him: Dismiss the crowds, that going into the towns and villages, which are round about, they may lodge, and find food: because we are here in a desert place.

Verse 13. But he said to them: Give them to eat. But they said: We have no more than five loaves, and two fishes: unless perhaps we should go and buy food for all this multitude.

Verse 14. Now there were about five thousand men. But he said to his disciples: Make them sit down by companies of fifty.

Verse 15. And they did so. And made them all sit down.

Verse 16. And taking the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed them: and he broke, and distributed to his disciples, to set before the crowds.

Verse 17. And they all ate, and were filled. And there were taken up fragments which remained to them, twelve baskets.

John VI. Verse 1. After these things Jesus went over the sea of Galilee, which is that of Tiberias:

Verse 2. And a great multitude followed him, because they saw the miracles which he did on them that were diseased.

Verse 3. Jesus therefore went up into a mountain; and there he sat with his disciples.

Vers. 4. Now the Passover, the feast day of the Jews, was near.

Vers. 5. When Jesus therefore had lifted up his eyes, and saw that a very great multitude came to him, he said to Philip: Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat?

Vers. 6. And this he said to try him: for he himself knew what he would do.

Vers. 7. Philip answered him: Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one may take a little.

Vers. 8. One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, saith to him:

Vers. 9. There is a boy here, that hath five barley loaves, and two fishes: but what are these among so many?

Vers. 10. Jesus therefore said: Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. The men therefore sat down, in number about five thousand.

Vers. 11. Jesus therefore took the loaves: and when he had given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down: and in like manner of the fishes as much as they would.

Vers. 12. And when they were filled, he said to his disciples: Gather up the fragments that remain, lest they be lost.

Vers. 13. They gathered up therefore, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which remained over and above to them that had eaten.

Vers. 14. Those men therefore, when they had seen what a sign Jesus had done, said: This is of a truth the prophet, that is to come into the world.

[Concerning the differences which seem to occur in this history among the Evangelists, let Pelargus be consulted on John, fol. 70, seq.]

§. III. Having dismissed the disciples and the people, he went up the mountain alone for the sake of prayer: and in the fourth watch, when the boat was in the middle of the sea, he walked on the sea. Where, when he ordered Peter to come to him, he began to sink from fear; but he is saved by the Lord: and thus they arrive by boat at the land of Gennesaret, Matt. XIV. 23-34. Mark VI. 45-53. John VI. 15-21.

Matt. XIV. v. 23. And having dismissed the crowd, he went up into the mountain alone to pray. And when evening had come, he was there alone.

V. 24. But the boat was being tossed by the waves in the middle of the sea: for the wind was contrary.

V. 25. And in the fourth watch of the night, he came to them walking upon the sea.

V. 26. And seeing him walking upon the sea, they were troubled, saying: It is a ghost. And they cried out for fear.

V. 27. And immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: Have confidence: it is I, do not be afraid.

V. 28. And Peter answering, said: Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you upon the waters.

V. 29. But he said: Come. And Peter descending from the boat, walked upon the water, that he might come to Jesus.

V. 30. But seeing the strong wind, he was afraid: and when he had begun to sink, he cried out saying: Lord! save me.

V. 31. And immediately Jesus extending his hand, caught him, and said to him: O you of little faith, why did you doubt?

V. 32. And when they had climbed into the boat, the wind ceased.

V. 33. But those who were in the boat came and worshipped him, saying: Truly you are the Son of God.

V. 34. And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.

Mark VI. v. 45. And immediately he compelled his disciples to get into the boat, that they might go before him to the other side to Bethsaida, while he himself dismissed the crowd.

V. 46. And when he had dismissed them, he went away into the mountain to pray.

V. 47. And when evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he alone on the land.

V. 48. And seeing them laboring in rowing (for the wind was against them) and about the fourth watch of the night he came to them walking upon the sea: and he intended to pass by them.

V. 49. But they, when they saw him walking upon the sea, thought it was a ghost, and cried out.

V. 50. For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he spoke with them, and said to them: Take courage, it is I, do not be afraid.

V. 51. And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were more exceedingly amazed within themselves.

V. 52. For they did not understand about the loaves; for their heart was hardened.

V. 53. And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.

John VI. v. 15. When Jesus therefore had perceived that they would come to take him by force, to make him a king, he fled again into the mountain himself alone.

V. 16. And when evening was come, his disciples went down unto the sea.

V. 17. And when they had entered into a ship, they came over the sea toward Capernaum: and it was now dark: and Jesus was not come to them.

V. 18. And the sea arose by reason of a great wind that blew.

V. 19. So when they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the ship: and they were afraid.

V. 20. But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.

V. 21. Then they willingly received him into the ship: and immediately the ship was at the land whither they went.

CHAPTER XX. Christ heals many sick in the region of Gennesaret.

§. I. In the land of Gennesaret, into which Christ came, very many sick are brought to him, and are healed. Matt. XIV. 35. Mark VI. 54. 55.

Matth. XIV. v. 35. And when the men of that place had recognized him, they sent into all that region, and brought to him all who were ill.

Marc. VI. v. 54. And when they had come out of the boat, they immediately recognized him:

Vers. 55. And running through that whole region, they began to carry about on mats those who were ill, wherever they heard he was.

§. II. Also in the villages, cities, and countrysides, wherever he came, he was asked to permit only the fringe of his garment to be touched, and all were healed. Matth. XIV. 36. Marc. VI. 56.

Matth. XIV. v. 36. And they begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched it were made well.

Marc. VI. v. 56. And wherever he entered, into villages, or towns, or cities, they placed the sick in the streets, and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment: and as many as touched him were made well.

CHAPTER XXI. The Capernaum Sermon.

§. I. The people marvel how Jesus, when the disciples had crossed by boat alone, arrived across the sea: others, when they sought him in vain in the desert, finally cross the lake themselves, and find him in the land of Gennesaret.

John 6:22. On the next day, the crowd that stood across the sea saw that there was no other boat there except one, and that Jesus had not entered into the boat with his disciples, but his disciples had gone away alone:

Verse 23. But other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread, after the Lord had given thanks.

Verse 24. When therefore the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they got into the boats and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus.

Verse 25. And when they had found him across the sea, they said to him: Rabbi, when did you come here?

§. II. They are admonished concerning seeking spiritual food: and are instructed about the true heavenly bread in the Capernaitic school.

Verse 26. Jesus answered them and said: Amen, amen I say to you: you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.

Verse 27. Do not work for the food which perishes, but for that which remains unto eternal life, which the Son of man will give to you. For him has God the Father sealed.

Verse 28. They said therefore to him: What shall we do, that we may work the works of God?

Verse 29. Jesus answered and said to them: This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.

Verse 30. They said therefore to him: What sign then do you do, that we may see and believe you? What do you work?

Verse 31. Our fathers ate manna in the desert, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat.

Vers. 32. Jesus therefore said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you: Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.

Vers. 33. For the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.

Vers. 34. They said therefore to him: Lord, always give us this bread.

Vers. 35. But Jesus said to them: I am the bread of life: he who comes to me shall not hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.

But I said to you, that you have both seen me, and do not believe.

Vers. 37. All that the Father gives me shall come to me: and him who comes to me, I will not cast out:

V. 38. Because I came down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.

Vers. 39. Now this is the will of the Father who sent me: that all that he has given me, I should not lose of it, but should raise it up in the last day.

Vers. 40. And this is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son, and believes in him, may have everlasting life, and I will raise him up in the last day.

Vers. 41. The Jews therefore murmured at him, because he had said: I am the living bread, which came down from heaven,

And they said: Is not this Jesus the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say: that I came down from heaven?

Vers. 43. Jesus therefore answered and said: Murmur not among yourselves:

Vers. 44. No man can come to me, except the Father, who hath sent me, draw him, and I will raise him up in the last day.

Vers. 45. It is written in the Prophets: And they shall all be taught of God. Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned, cometh to me.

Vers. 46. Not that any man hath seen the Father, but he who is of God, he hath seen the Father.

Vers. 47. Amen, Amen I say to you: He that believeth in me, hath everlasting life.

Vers. 48. I am the bread of life.

Vers. 49. Your fathers did eat manna in the desert, and are dead.

Vers. 50. This is the bread descending from heaven: that if any man eat of it, he may not die.

V. 51. I am the living bread, which came down from heaven.

Vers. 52. If any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give, is my flesh, for the life of the world.

Vers. 53. The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying: How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

Vers. 54. Then Jesus said to them: Amen, Amen I say unto you: Except you eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, you shall not have life in you.

Ver. 55. He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, has eternal life: and I will raise him up on the last day.

Ver. 56. For my flesh is food indeed: and my blood is drink indeed.

Ver. 57. He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, abides in me, and I in him.

Ver. 58. As the living Father has sent me, and I live because of the Father: so he who eats me, he also shall live because of me.

Ver. 59. This is the bread which came down from heaven. Not as your fathers ate manna, and are dead. He who eats this bread shall live forever.

Ver. 60. These things he said in the synagogue, teaching in Capernaum.

[This discourse is referred by some to the acts of Christ's ministry from the third Passover to the fourth. But there are diverse opinions of theologians concerning that Passover. Some, and among them Bünting, maintain that Christ celebrated this Passover at Jerusalem, and from there, because of the snares of the Jews, withdrew himself again into Galilee, John VII. 1. But B. Lyser, in his Harmony of the Gospels, ch. LXXIX, leans toward the opinion of those who think that Jesus did not go up to Jerusalem for this third feast of the Passover; but instead of it, delivered this Capernaitic discourse:

Because the brothers in John 7:3 rebuke him, because he no longer goes up to Jerusalem for the feasts. 2. Because in John ch. 7:21, Christ says to the Jews in Jerusalem at the Feast of Tabernacles: I have done one work, and you all marvel, and you seek to kill me: looking back to that miracle, which he had performed at the Feast of Passover in John 5:9 at the pool of Bethesda in the second year of his ministry. It seems, therefore, that he performed no further miracles in Jerusalem up to that time. 3. Because none of the Evangelists reported anything about the sermons or the miracles of that feast. However, the blessed Lyser leaves it free for the reader to follow whichever opinion he wishes, nor does he deny that it is dangerous to deny that Christ attended the Feast of Passover: since the law of Moses commanded in many places that every male should visit this feast day annually: and Christ was most observant of his Father's law. Nor do the disciples in John 7:3 rebuke the Lord because he no longer attends the feasts, but they urge and advise him to attend the Feast of Tabernacles. Nor can those words of Christ in John 5:21 be taken so simply, as if Christ had performed only one miracle in Jerusalem: since in John 2:23 it is said that many believed in him because of the many miracles performed in Jerusalem at the first Passover: but this must be understood κατά τι [in a certain respect]: namely, concerning the Passover feast of the previous year: during which he had performed that one miracle on the Sabbath, because of which they were plotting against his life. And could he not have been present at the third Passover feast, even if he performed no miracles then? There is, therefore, no reason why we should conclude that Christ disregarded the law.

§. III. He reminds his murmuring disciples about the ascension of the Son of Man. Peter confesses that Christ has the words of life.

Verse 61. Many therefore of his disciples, when they heard this, said: This is a hard saying, and who can hear it?

Verse 62. But Jesus, knowing within himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: Does this offend you?

Verse 63. If therefore you shall see the Son of Man ascending where he was before?

Verse 64. It is the spirit that gives life: the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life.

Verse 65. But there are some of you who do not believe. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that did not believe, and who would betray him.

Verse 66. And he said: Therefore I said to you, that no one can come to me, unless it has been given to him by my Father.

Verse 67. From this time many of his disciples went back: and no longer walked with him.

Verse 68. Jesus therefore said to the twelve: Will you also go away?

Verse 69. Simon Peter therefore answered him: Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.

And we have believed and have known that you are the Christ the Son of God.

§. IV. He teaches that Judas is a devil.

Verse 71. Jesus answered them: Have I not chosen you twelve: and one of you is a devil?

Verse 72. Now he was speaking of Judas Iscariot the son of Simon: for he was about to betray him, whereas he was one of the twelve.

SECTION III. ARTICLE III. THE ACTS OF THE MINISTRY OF CHRIST FROM THE THIRD PASSOVER TO THE FOURTH. CHAPTER I.

The Pharisees, in Galilee, are rebuked on account of traditions.

§. I. Jesus went about in Galilee, because the Pharisees were lying in wait for him in Judea.

Verse 1. After these things Jesus walked in Galilee; for he would not walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.

[After the long sermon delivered in Capernaum, it is probable that Christ proceeded to Jerusalem for the third Passover of his ministry: which, although it may not be expressly commemorated, since he seems to have performed no miracles there at that time, when at the previous Passover the Jews had lain in wait for his life on account of the one miracle of the lame man healed at the pool of Bethesda, nor had that slipped from memory, even at the following third Passover of the feast of Tabernacles John VII. 21. It is gathered, however, from John VII. 1. that he surely did not wish to linger long in Judea, on account of the persecution of the Pharisees, but immediately after the Passover feast was finished, he withdrew himself in turn into Galilee: and by going about those lands he instituted an ecclesiastical visitation everywhere.]

§. II. The Pharisees (coming from Jerusalem) accuse the disciples of Christ, because they transgress their traditions, Matt. XV. 1. 2. Mark VII. 1-5.

Matt. XV. v. 1. Then came to him from Jerusalem Scribes and Pharisees, saying:

Ver. 2. Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the Elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.

Mark VII. v. 1. And there gathered together unto him the Pharisees and certain of the Scribes, which came from Jerusalem.

Ver. 2. And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with common, that is to say, unwashen, hands, they found fault.

Ver. 3. For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the Elders:

Ver. 4. And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not: and many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, and brazen vessels, and of tables:

Ver. 5. Then the Pharisees and Scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the Elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

§. III. Christ in turn asks why the Pharisees transgress divine commandments, e.g., concerning the honor of parents.

Matt. 15:3. But he answering, said to them: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for your tradition? For God said:

Ver. 4. Honor thy father and mother: and he that shall curse father or mother, let him die the death.

Ver. 5. But you say: Whosoever shall say to father or mother, Whatsoever gift is from me, shall profit thee:

And he shall not honor his father or his mother, and you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition.

§. IV. He convicts the Pharisees of hypocrisy, even from Isaiah (ch. 29:13), and teaches that God is worshipped in vain by the commandments of men, Matt. 15:7-9, Mark 7:6-13.

Matt. 15:7. Hypocrites, well hath Isaias prophesied of you, saying:

Ver. 8. This people honors me with their lips: but their heart is far from me.

Ver. 9. But in vain they worship me, teaching the doctrines and commandments of men.

Mark VII. v. 6. But he answering, said to them: Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

Ver. 7. But in vain they worship me, teaching the doctrines and precepts of men.

Ver. 8. For leaving the commandment of God, you hold the traditions of men, the washings of pitchers, and of cups, and many other things like to these you do.

Ver. 9. And he said to them: Well do you make void the commandment of God, that you may keep your own tradition.

Ver. 10. For Moses said: Honor your father, and your mother. And: He that shall curse father, or mother, let him die the death.

Ver. 11. But you say: If a man shall say to his father, or mother, Corban (which is a gift) whatsoever from me, shall profit you:

Ver. 12. And you suffer him no more to do anything for his father, or mother,

Ver. 13. Making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have delivered: and many other such like things you do:

§. V. He teaches what things render a man unclean, and he explains this to the disciples who were asking about the scandalized Pharisees, convincing them that the Pharisees are blind teachers, Matt. XV. 10-20. Mark VII. 14-23.

Matth. XV. v. 10. And having called the crowds to him, he said to them: Hear, and understand.

Vers. 11. Not that which enters into the mouth defiles a man, but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles a man.

Vers. 12. Then his disciples approaching, said to him: Do you know that the Pharisees, having heard this word, were scandalized?

Vers. 13. But he answering said: Every plant, which my heavenly Father has not planted, shall be rooted up.

Vers. 14. Let them alone: they are blind, and leaders of the blind. And if a blind man leads a blind man, both fall into the pit.

Vers. 15. And Peter answering, said to him: Explain this parable to us.

Vers. 16. But he said: Are you also still without understanding?

Vers. 17. Do you not understand that everything which enters into the mouth goes into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

Vers. 18. But the things which proceed out of the mouth come from the heart, and they defile a man:

Vers. 19. For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.

Vers. 20. These are the things which defile a man. But to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a man.

Mark VII. v. 14. And calling the crowd to him again, he said to them: Hear me all of you, and understand.

V. 15. There is nothing from outside a man that entering into him can defile him, but the things which proceed from a man are those that defile a man.

Vers. 16. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.

Vers. 17. And when he had entered into the house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the parable.

Vers. 18. And he said to them: Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not understand that everything from outside entering into a man cannot defile him:

V. 19. Because it does not enter into his heart, but goes into the belly, and goes out into the draught, purging all foods?

Vers. 20. And he said, that the things which come out of a man, those defile a man.

Vers. 21. For from within out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

V. 22. Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.

Vers. 23. All these evils proceed from within, and defile a man.

CHAPTER II. The faith of the Canaanite woman.

§. I. As Christ was going into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, a Canaanite woman met him, seeking the deliverance of her demon-possessed daughter. Christ at first is silent: after [saying] he was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel, he speaks: but she persists in entreating, Matt. XV. 21-25. Mark VII. 24-26.

Matt. XV. v. 21. And Jesus went out from thence, and withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.

Vers. 22. And behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried out, saying to him: Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David: my daughter is grievously vexed by a demon.

Vers. 23. But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying: Send her away: for she crieth after us.

Vers. 24. But he answering said: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

Vers. 25. But she came and worshipped him, saying: Lord, help me.

Mark VII. v. 24. And from thence he arose and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon: and entering into a house, he would have no man know it, but he could not be hid.

Vers. 25. For a woman, as soon as she heard of him, whose daughter had an unclean spirit, came in and fell at his feet.

Ver. 26. For she was a Gentile woman, a Syrophoenician by race. And she asked him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

[Büntingius conjectures that this retreat was made in the month of May on account of the persecution of the Pharisees, and makes the journey fourteen miles.]

§. II. Christ warns that bread should not be snatched from the children and thrown to the dogs; but she retorts that crumbs are not denied to the dogs, and she is heard, Matt. XV. 26-28. Mark VII. 27-30.

Matt. XV. v. 26. Who answering said: It is not good to take the bread of the children, and to cast it to the dogs.

Ver. 27. But she said: Yes, Lord: for the whelps also eat of the crumbs which fall from the table of their masters.

Ver. 28. Then Jesus answering, said to her: O woman, great is thy faith: be it done to thee as thou wilt. And her daughter was healed from that hour.

Mark VII. v. 27. Who said to her: Suffer the children to be first filled: for it is not good to take the bread of the children, and to cast it to the dogs.

Ver. 28. But she answered, and said to him: Yes, Lord, for the whelps also eat under the table of the crumbs of the children.

Ver. 29. And he said to her: For this saying go thy way, the demon is gone out of thy daughter.

Ver. 30. And when she was come to her house, she found the girl lying upon the bed, and the demon gone out.

CHAPTER III. The healing of the deaf and dumb, and the feeding of 4000 men.

§. I. He returns from the borders of Tyre and Sidon to the Sea of Galilee through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.

Mark VII. v. 31. And again departing from the borders of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.

[He returns into Trachonitis across the Jordan to the Sea of Galilee for 16 miles, healing a deaf and dumb man on the journey.]

§. II. A deaf and dumb man is brought to him, to whom he restores hearing and speech.

Vers. 32. And they bring to him a deaf and dumb man, and they besought him that he would lay his hand upon him.

Vers. 33. And taking him aside from the crowd, he put his fingers into his ears: and spitting, he touched his tongue:

Vers. 34. And looking up to heaven, he groaned, and said to him: Ephphatha, which is, be opened.

Vers. 35. And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke correctly.

Vers. 36. And he charged them that they should tell no man. But the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal did they publish it:

Vers. 37. And so much the more did they wonder, saying: He hath done all things well: he hath made both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

§. III. While he himself is sitting on the mountain, very many sick people are brought, all of whom he heals.

Matt. XV. v. 29. And when Jesus had passed from thence, he came near the Sea of Galilee: and going up into a mountain, he sat there.

Vers. 30. And great crowds came to him, having with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others: and they cast them at his feet, and he healed them:

Vers. 31. So that the crowds marveled; seeing the mute speaking, the lame walking, the blind seeing: and they glorified the God of Israel.

§. IV. He feeds a gathered crowd of 4000 men in the desert with seven loaves and a few small fish, and thus sends them away, and he himself crosses over into the borders of Magdala. Matth. XV. 32-39. Marc. VIII. 1-10.

Matth. XV. v. 32. But Jesus, having called his disciples together, said: I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with me for three days, and they have nothing to eat: and I do not wish to send them away fasting, lest they faint on the way.

Vers. 33. And the disciples say to him: Whence then for us in the desert so many loaves, that we may satisfy such a great crowd?

Vers. 34. And Jesus said to them: How many loaves do you have? But they said: Seven, and a few small fish.

Vers. 35. And he commanded the crowd to sit down upon the ground.

Vers. 36. And taking the seven loaves, and the fish, and giving thanks, he broke them, and gave them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.

Vers. 37. And they all ate, and were satisfied: And what remained of the fragments, they took up seven baskets full:

Vers. 38. Now there were those who ate, four thousand men, besides children and women.

Vers. 39. And, the crowd having been sent away, he went up into a small boat: and came into the borders of Magedan.

Mark VIII. v. 1. In those days when there was a great crowd again, and they had nothing to eat, calling his disciples to him, he says to them:

Vers. 2. I have compassion on the crowd: for behold, they have already stayed with me for three days, and have nothing to eat:

And if I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way: for some of them have come from afar.

And his disciples answered him: From where will anyone be able to satisfy them with bread here in the wilderness?

And he asked them: How many loaves do you have? Who said: Seven.

And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves, giving thanks he broke them, and gave them to his disciples, that they might set them before them, and they set them before the crowd.

And they had a few small fish: and he blessed them also, and ordered them to be set before them.

And they ate, and were satisfied, and they took up what had remained of the fragments, seven baskets.

Now there were those who had eaten, about four thousand: and he dismissed them.

And immediately getting into the boat with his disciples, he came into the parts of Dalmanutha. [Namely, one and a half miles.]

CHAPTER IV.

The sign of Jonah given again to the Pharisees.

§. I. The Pharisees, as also the Sadducees, betake themselves to Christ, and tempt him, that he might show them a sign from heaven. Matt. XVI. 1. Mark VIII. 11.

Matt. XVI. v. 1. And the Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, tempting: and asked him that he would show them a sign from heaven.

Mark VIII. v. 11. And the Pharisees came out, and began to dispute with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

§. II. Christ rebukes them, because, while observing the signs of natural weather, they are unable to discern the signs of this time (of his advent).

Matt. XVI. v. 2. But he answering, said to them: When it is evening, you say: It will be fair weather, for the sky is red;

Ver. 3. And in the morning! Today there will be a storm, for the sky is red and lowering.

Ver. 4. You know then how to discern the face of the sky: but can you not know the signs of the times?

§. III. He denies that any sign other than that of Jonah will be given to them, Matt. XVI. 4. Mark VIII. 12.

Matt. XVI. v. 4. A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign: and a sign shall not be given it, but the sign of Jonah the prophet.

Mark VIII. v. 12. And sighing in his spirit, he says: Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen I say to you, if a sign shall be given to this generation.

§. IV. Having left them, he crossed the sea by ship, Matt. XVI. 4. Mark VIII. 13.

Matt. XVI. v. 4. And having left them, he went away.

Mark VIII. v. 13. And leaving them, he went up again into the ship, and went across the sea.

CHAPTER V.

Concerning the leaven of the Pharisees, and the Sadducees.

§. I. Having returned across the sea to Galilee to the other bank, he warns his disciples, who had forgotten the loaves, to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, the Sadducees, and the Herodians, and he corrects the disciples who understood this as referring to a lack of bread, by calling to mind the twofold miraculous feeding, Matt. XVI. 5-11. Mark VIII. 14-21. And only then did the disciples perceive that he had spoken of the leaven of doctrine, Matt. XVI. 12.

Matt. XVI. v. 5. And when his disciples had come across the strait, they had forgotten to take bread.

Vers. 6. Who said to them: Look, and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

Vers. 7. But they thought within themselves, saying: Because we have taken no bread.

Vers. 8. And Jesus knowing it, said: Why do you think within yourselves, O you of little faith, for that you have no bread?

Vers. 9. Do you not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves for the five thousand men, and how many baskets you took up.

Ver. 10. Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand men, and how many baskets did you take up?

Ver. 11. Why do you not understand that I did not say to you concerning bread: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?

Ver. 12. Then they understood that he had not said to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

Mark VIII. v. 14. And they forgot to take bread: and they had but one loaf with them in the boat.

Ver. 15. And he charged them, saying: Take heed, and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and the leaven of Herod.

Ver. 16. And they reasoned among themselves, saying: Because we have no bread.

Ver. 17. Jesus knowing this, saith to them: Why do you reason, because you have no bread? do you not yet know, nor understand? have you still your heart blinded?

Ver. 18. Having eyes, see you not? and having ears, hear you not? And do you not remember,

Ver. 19. When I broke the five loaves among five thousand: how many baskets full of fragments took you up? They say to him: Twelve.

Ver. 20. When also the seven loaves among the four thousand: how many baskets of fragments took you up? And they say to him: Seven.

Ver. 21. And he said to them: How do you not yet understand.

Undoubtedly, by a voyage of one mile, he approached Bethsaida, where that warning was set forth.

§. II. There also, outside Bethsaida, he healed a blind man, who at first saw men as if he were seeing trees, but afterwards began to see clearly.

Vers. 22. And they come to Bethsaida, and they bring a blind man to him, and they were asking him to touch him.

Vers. 23. And having taken the hand of the blind man, he led him outside the village: and spitting into his eyes, having laid his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw anything.

Vers. 24. And looking up, he said: I see men as trees walking.

Vers. 25. Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes: and he began to see, and he was restored, so that he saw all things clearly.

Vers. 26. And he sent him to his house, saying: Go into your house: and if you enter into the village, tell no one.

CHAPTER VI. Peter's confession concerning Christ.

§. I. Christ comes into the borders of Caesarea Philippi, where he asks his disciples what others think of him: when they report various opinions, he asks again what the disciples themselves conclude about him? In whose name Peter, answering, gives a confession concerning Christ Matt. XVI. 13-16. Mark VIII. 27-29. Luke IX. 18-20.

Matth. XVI. v. 13. And Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi: and he was asking his disciples, saying: Whom do men say that the Son of man is?

Vers. 14. But they said: Some John the Baptist, others however Elijah, and others indeed Jeremiah, or one of the Prophets.

Verse 15. Jesus says to them: But who do you say that I am?

Verse 16. Simon Peter answering said: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.

Mark VIII. v. 27. And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and in the way he asked his disciples, saying to them: Whom do men say that I am?

Verse 28. Who answered him, saying: John the Baptist, others Elias, and others as one of the Prophets.

V. 29. Then he says to them: But who do you say that I am? Peter answering, says to him: You are the Christ.

Luke IX. v. 18. And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples also were with him: and he asked them saying: Whom do the crowds say that I am?

Verse 19. But they answered and said: John the Baptist, and others Elias, and others that one of the former prophets has risen.

Verse 20. But he said to them: But who do you say that I am? Simon Peter answering said: The Christ of God.

[If you listen to Bünting, Christ went up to Jerusalem around the end of the month of May at an interval of 14 miles, where the feast of Pentecost was impending, so that he might celebrate it there according to the law of Exodus XXIII. But when the feast of Pentecost was finished, he returned again at an interval of 14 miles into Galilee to his own city, Capernaum: and from there in the month of June he traveled into the borders of the Gentiles, where Peter made his confession about Christ in the borders of Caesarea Philippi, which was distant 12 miles from Capernaum.]

§. II. He declares Peter blessed, and teaches concerning the building of the Church upon this Rock, and commits to Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

Matth. XVI. v. 17. And Jesus answering, said to him: Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-Jona: because flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee, but my Father who is in heaven.

Vers. 18. And I say to thee, that thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

Vers. 19. And to thee I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, it shall be loosed also in heaven.

§. III. He forbids the disciples to tell others that he is Christ: because the Son of man must yet suffer and rise again. Luc. IX. 21. 22. Matth. XVI. 20. 21. Marc. VIII. 30. 31.

Luc. IX. v. 21. But he strictly charging them, commanded they should tell this to no man.

Vers. 22. Saying: The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the ancients and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day rise again.

Matth. XVI. v. 20. Then he commanded his disciples, that they should tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.

Vers. 21. From that time Jesus began to shew to his disciples, that he must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things from the ancients and scribes and chief priests, and be killed, and the third day rise again.

Marc. VIII. v. 30. And he strictly charged them that they should not tell any man of him:

Verse 31. And he began to teach them that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and by the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed: and after three days rise again.

§. IV. He rebukes Peter for speaking against him. Matt. 16:22, 23. Mark 8:32, 33.

Matt. 16:22. And Peter taking him, began to rebuke him, saying: Lord, be it far from thee: this shall not be unto thee.

Verse 23. Who turning, said to Peter: Get thee behind me, Satan, thou art a stumbling block unto me: because thou dost not relish the things that are of God, but the things that are of men.

Mark 8:32. And he spoke the word openly. And Peter taking him, began to rebuke him:

Verse 33. Who turning, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, saying: Get behind me, Satan, because you do not savor the things that are of God, but the things that are of men.

CHAPTER VII. Concerning the following of Christ.

§. I. A little child having been called to him, and the disciples, Christ preaches concerning his following.

Matthew XVI. v. 24. Then Jesus said to his disciples. If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up my cross, and follow me.

Verse 25. For he that will save his life, shall lose it: but he that shall lose his life for my sake, shall find it.

Verse 26. For what does it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, and suffer the loss of his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

Mark VIII. v. 34. And calling the multitude together with his disciples, he said to them: If any man will follow me, let him deny himself: and take up his cross, and follow me.

Verse 35. For whosoever will save his life, shall lose it: but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel, shall save it.

Verse 36. For what shall it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, and suffer the loss of his soul?

Verse 37. Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

Luke 9:23. And he said to all: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.

Verse 24. For whosoever will save his life, shall lose it: for whosoever shall lose his life for my sake, shall save it.

Verse 25. For what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, and cast away himself?

§. II. Concerning the coming of the Son of man in glory and future reward.

Matt. 16:27. For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels: and then will he render to every man according to his works.

Mark 8:38. For he that shall be ashamed of me, and of my words, in this adulterous and sinful generation: the Son of man also shall be ashamed of him, when he shall come in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

Luke 9:26. For he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of man shall be ashamed, when he shall come in his majesty, and that of his Father, and of the holy angels.

§. III. Concerning the Son of man coming in his kingdom to be seen by some then present.

Matth. XVI. v. 28. Truly I say to you; there are some standing here, who shall not taste death, until they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

Marc. VIII. v. 39. And he said to them: Truly I say to you, that there are some standing here, who shall not taste death, until they see the kingdom of God coming in power.

Luc. IX. v. 27. But I say to you truly: there are some standing here, who shall not taste death, until they see the kingdom of God.

CHAPTER VIII. The Transfiguration of Christ.

§. I. After six days Christ is transfigured on the mountain before Peter, James & John, & there appe-

ar- pear Moses & Elijah, talking with him about his departure from Jerusalem.

Matth. XVII. v. 1. And after six days Jesus takes Peter, & James, & John his brother, and leads them up into a high mountain apart.

Vers. 2. And he was transfigured before them. And his face shone as the Sun: and his garments became white as snow.

Vers. 3. And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elias talking with him.

Vers. 4. And Peter answering, said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Mark IX. v. 1. And after six days Jesus taketh Peter and James and John: and leadeth them up into a high mountain apart by themselves, and he was transfigured before them.

Vers. 2. And his garments became shining, and exceeding white as snow, such as no fuller upon earth can make white.

Vers. 3. And Elias appeared to them with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

Vers. 4. And Peter answering, saith to Jesus: Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias:

Vers. 5. For he knew not what he said: for they were struck with fear.

Luke IX. v. 28. And it came to pass about eight days after these words, that he took Peter and James and John, and ascended into a mountain to pray.

Vers. 29. And whilst he prayed, the shape of his countenance was altered: and his raiment was white and shining.

Vers. 30. And behold two men were talking with him. And they were Moses and Elias.

Vers. 31. They appeared in majesty: and they spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.

Vers. 32. But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep. And waking, they saw his majesty, and the two men that stood with him.

Vers. 33. And it came to pass, as they were departing from him, Peter said to Jesus: Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.

(Six days are indicated from the confession made by Peter to the transfiguration of Christ: but it is said that this happened on the eighth day, namely, counting the days of the confession and of the transfiguration of Christ, which is believed to have happened on Mount Tabor, 12 miles from Caesarea Philippi towards the south-southwest.

§. II. The voice heard from heaven concerning the Son of God. The disciples, falling down, are raised up, and being awakened, they see only Jesus present, and are forbidden to manifest this vision before the resurrection of Christ.

Matth. XVII. v. 5. As he was yet speaking, behold a bright cloud overshadowed them. And lo a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.

Vers. 6. And the disciples hearing, fell upon their face, and were very afraid.

Vers. 7. And Jesus came and touched them: and said to them: Arise, and fear not.

Vers. 8. And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, but only Jesus.

Vers. 9. And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying: Tell the vision to no man, till the Son of man be risen from the dead.

Marc. IX. v. 6. And there was a cloud overshadowing them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my most beloved son: hear him.

Verse 7. And immediately looking around, they saw no one anymore, except Jesus only with them.

Verse 8. And as they were coming down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

Verse 9. And they kept the word to themselves, questioning what it meant: When he had risen from the dead.

Luke 9:34. While he was saying these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them: and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.

Verse 35. And a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, listen to him.

Verse 36. And while the voice was speaking, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent, and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

§. III. The doubt of the disciples concerning the return of Elijah decided by Christ with a repeated prediction concerning the passion of the Son of Man.

Matthew 17:10. And the disciples asked him, saying: Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?

Verse 11. But he answering, said to them: Elijah indeed is to come, and will restore all things.

Vers. 12. But I say to you, that Elias has already come, and they did not know him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of man is to suffer from them.

Vers. 13. Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them of John the Baptist.

Mark IX. v. 10. And they asked him, saying: Why then do the Pharisees and Scribes say that Elias must come first?

Vers. 11. Who answering, said to them: Elias, when he shall come first, shall restore all things: and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things and be despised.

Vers. 12. But I say to you, that Elias also has come (and they did to him whatever they wished) as it is written of him.

CHAPTER IX. Of the lunatic son cured.

§. I. As Christ was descending from the mountain to the disciples, seeing the crowd, and the lawyers disputing with the disciples, he asks about the subject of the conversation.

Vers. 13. And coming to his disciples, he saw a great crowd around them, and the scribes disputing with them.

Vers. 14. And immediately all the people seeing Jesus, were astonished and struck with fear, and running up, they greeted him.

Vers. 15. And he asked them: What are you disputing about among yourselves?

Luke 9:37. And it came to pass on the following day, when they were coming down from the mountain, a great crowd met them.

§. II. The father of the lunatic complains that the demon could not be expelled from his son by the disciples. Christ, having sharply rebuked their unbelief and demanded faith, delivers the lunatic.

Matthew 17:14. And when he had come to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling before him, saying: Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic and suffers badly: for he often falls into the fire, and frequently into the water.

Verse 15. And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.

Verse 16. And Jesus answering, said: O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him here to me.

Verse 17. And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out from him, and the boy was cured from that hour.

Verse 18. Then the disciples approached Jesus privately, and said: Why could we not cast him out?

Verse 19. Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief. For truly I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, Move from here to there, and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.

Verse 20. But this kind is not cast out except by prayer and fasting.

Mark 9:16. And one of the crowd answering, said: Master, I have brought my son to you having a mute spirit:

Verf. 17. Whoever, wherever he seizes him, dashes him down, and he foams, and gnashes his teeth, and withers: and I told your disciples to cast him out, and they could not.

Verf. 18. Who answering them, said: O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him to me.

Verf. 19. And they brought him. And when he had seen him, immediately the spirit troubled him: and being thrown to the ground, he wallowed foaming.

Verf. 20. And he asked his father: How long a time is it, since this has happened to him? But he said: From infancy:

Verf. 21. And frequently he cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him. But, if you can do anything, help us, having compassion on us.

Verf. 22. But Jesus said to him: If you can believe, all things are possible to him that believes.

Verf. 23. And immediately the father of the boy crying out, with tears said: I believe, Lord: help my unbelief.

Verf. 24. And when Jesus saw the crowd running together, he threatened the unclean spirit, saying to him: Deaf and dumb spirit, I command you, go out of him: and enter no more into him.

Verf. 25. And crying out, and tearing him much, he went out of him, and he became as one dead, so that many said: That he is dead.

Verf. 26. But Jesus holding his hand, lifted him up, and he arose.

Verf. 27. And when he had entered into the house, his disciples asked him privately: Why could we not cast him out?

Verf. 28. And he said to them: This kind can go out by nothing, but by prayer, and fasting.

Luke IX. v. 38. And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying: Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son, for he is my only one:

Ver. 39. And behold, a spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out, and it throws him into convulsions, and tears him, with foaming, and it hardly departs from him, lacerating him:

Ver. 40. And I besought thy disciples to cast him out, and they could not.

Ver. 41. But Jesus answering, said: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and suffer you? Bring thy son here.

Ver. 42. And as he was approaching, the demon threw him down and tore him.

Ver. 43. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and restored him to his father.

CHAPTER X. A sermon concerning the passion and resurrection of Christ.

§. I. When they were passing through Galilee, he preaches to the disciples concerning the death of the son of man, and concerning the resurrection.

Matth. XVII. v. 21. And while they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: The Son of man is to be delivered into the hands of men.

Vers. 22. And they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise again.

Marc. IX. v. 29. And departing from there they were passing through Galilee: and he did not want anyone to know.

Vers. 30. But he was teaching his disciples, and saying to them: For the Son of man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and having been killed he will rise again on the third day.

Luc. IX. v. 44. But all were astonished at the greatness of God: and while all were marveling at all things which he was doing, he said to his disciples: Lay these words in your hearts: For it will come to pass that the Son of man is to be delivered into the hands of men.

[In the month of July, traveling through Galilee, he confirmed his teaching with stupendous miracles, which when the disciples were admiring, he brought back to their memory concerning his cross and death.

§. II. The disciples understand nothing of these things, and therefore they are saddened.

Matt. 17:22. And they were exceedingly sorrowful.

Mark 9:31. But they were ignorant of the word: and they feared to ask him.

Luke 9:45. But they were ignorant of this word, and it was veiled before them, that they might not perceive it: and they feared to ask him about this word.

CHAPTER XI. Concerning the payment of the stater.

§. I. The tax is demanded from Christ in Capernaum: who asks of Peter, whether the tax is demanded from strangers, or indeed from children.

Matt. 17:23. And when he had come to Capernaum, those who received the didrachma came to Peter, and said to him: Does your master not pay the didrachma?

Verse 24. He says: Yes. And when he had entered into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying: What does it seem to you, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive tribute or tax? From their sons, or from strangers?

Verse 25. And he said: From strangers. Jesus said to him: Therefore the sons are free.

§. II. Yet for the sake of avoiding scandal, with the stater extracted from the fish, from the sea, he paid the tax for himself and Peter.

Vers. 26. But that we may not scandalize them, go to the sea, and cast a hook: and that fish which shall first come up, take; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a stater: take that, and give to them for me and thee.

CHAPTER XII. The contention of the disciples concerning primacy.

§. I. The disciples contended among themselves on the way concerning primacy: concerning which Christ inquires coming home into Capernaum.

Matth. XVIII. v. 1. At that hour the disciples came to Jesus saying: Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heaven?

Marc. IX. v. 32. And they came to Capharnaum. And when they were in the house, he asked them: What did you treat of in the way?

Vers. 33. But they held their peace. For in the way they had disputed among themselves, which of them should be the greater.

Vers. 34. And sitting down, he called the twelve, and saith to them: If any man desire to be first, he shall be the last of all, and minister of all.

Luc. IX. v. 46. And there entered a thought into them, which of them should be greater.

§. II. Christ sets a certain little child before them as an example of humility.

Matt. 18:2. And Jesus calling a little child unto him, set him in the midst of them.

Ver. 3. And he said: Amen I say to you, unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 4. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 5. And he that shall receive one such little child in my name, receiveth me.

Mark 9:35. And taking a child, he set him in the midst of them: whom when he had embraced, he saith to them:

Ver. 36. Whosoever shall receive one such child as this in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

Luke 9:47. But Jesus seeing the thoughts of their heart, took a child; and set him by himself,

Ver. 48. And said to them: Whosoever shall receive this child in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth him that sent me. For he that is the lesser among you all, he is the greater.

§. III. Christ answers John, who was interrupting about someone casting out demons.

Mark IX. v. 37. John answered him, saying: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, who does not follow us, and we forbade him.

Verse 38. But Jesus said: Do not forbid him: for there is no one who shall do a miracle in my name, and can soon speak evil of me.

Verse 39. For he who is not against you, is for you.

Verse 40. For whoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ's: Amen I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.

Luke IX. v. 49. And John answering, said: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him: because he does not follow with us.

V. 50. And Jesus said to him: Do not forbid: for he who is not against you is for you.

§. IV. Christ warns about scandal.

Matthew XVIII. v. 6. But he who shall scandalize one of these little ones who believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone be hanged about his neck, and he be drowned in the depth of the sea.

Verse 7. Woe to the world because of scandals. For it is necessary that scandals come: but nevertheless woe to that man by whom the scandal comes.

Verse 8. But if your hand, or your foot causes you to stumble; cut it off, and cast it from you: it is good for you to enter into life maimed, or lame, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into eternal fire.

Verse 9. And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from you: it is good for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire.

Mark IX. v. 41. And whoever shall cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble: it is better for him if a millstone were hung about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

Verse 42. And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is good for you to enter maimed into life, than having two hands to go into hell; into unquenchable fire:

Verse 43. Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.

Verse 44. And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is good for you to enter into eternal life lame, than having two feet to be cast into the hell of unquenchable fire.

Verse 45. Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.

Verse 46. But if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out: it is good for you to enter into the kingdom of God one-eyed, than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire:

Verse 47. Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.

§. V. He warns not to despise little ones.

Matt. XVIII. v. 10. See that you do not despise one of these little ones: for I say to you, that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father, who is in heaven.

Verse 11. For the Son of man has come to save that which was lost.

Verse 12. What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has gone astray: does he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains, and go to seek the one that has gone astray?

Vers. 13. And if it happen that he find it: Amen I say to you, that he rejoiceth more upon it, than upon the ninety-nine that have not gone astray.

Vers. 14. So it is not the will before your Father, who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

§. VI. He admonishes concerning salt and concerning peace.

Marc. IX. v. 48. For every one shall be salted with fire, and every victim shall be salted with salt.

Vers. 49. Salt is good: but if the salt shall become unsavory, with what will you season it? Have salt in you, and have peace among you.

CHAPTER XIII. Hospitality denied to Christ in Samaria and concerning the three who desired to be companions of the journey. §. I. He goes secretly to the Feast of Tabernacles, because he refused to go with his brothers. Which deed was done when the days of his assumption were being fulfilled.

Joh. VII. v. 2. Now the festival day of the Jews, the Scenopegia, was near.

Vers. 3. His brothers therefore said to him: Pass from hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see thy works, which thou dost.

Vers. 4. For no man doth anything in secret, and he himself seeketh to be in public: if thou do these things, manifest thyself to the world.

Vers. 5. For neither did his brothers believe in him.

Vers. 6. Jesus therefore said to them: My time has not yet come: but your time is always ready.

Vers. 7. The world cannot hate you: but me it hates: because I bear witness of it, that its works are evil.

Vers. 8. You go up to this feast day, but I do not go up to this feast day: because my time is not yet fulfilled.

Vers. 9. When he had said these things, he himself remained in Galilee.

Vers. 10. But when his brothers had gone up, then he also went up to the feast day, not openly, but as it were in secret.

Luke IX. v. 51. And it came to pass, while the days of his assumption were being fulfilled, that he also steadfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem.

[Intending to make a journey in the month of August through Samaria, so that by visiting the churches little by little he might go up to Jerusalem for the feast of tabernacles, he approached Capernaum, two and a half miles from the borders of the Samaritans. However, it is not to be believed that this is the Lord's final journey to the feast of the Passover, which Osiander rashly asserting, snatches away everything that follows from here in the history of Luke from c. IX. 51 to that final journey. For the feast of tabernacles intervenes, which was still to be visited by Christ, and was visited. Nor indeed were the days of his assumption already completed, but it was ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι, that they might be completed, as St. Luke notably speaks. For there still remained a six-month space of Christ's course in these lands.]

§. II. When the Samaritans would not receive him on the way, James and John wish to call down fire from heaven, whom Christ indeed rebukes.

Vers. 52. And he sent messengers before his face: and going they entered into a city of the Samaritans, to prepare for him.

Vers. 53. And they did not receive him, because his face was as of one going to Jerusalem.

Vers. 54. And when his disciples James and John had seen it, they said: Lord, wilt thou that we say that fire come down from heaven, and consume them?

Vers. 55. And turning, he rebuked them, saying: You know not of what spirit you are.

Vers. 56. The Son of man came not to destroy souls, but to save. And they went into another village.

[Although it is evident, even from John IV. 40, that hospitality was not entirely denied to the Jews by the Samaritans, yet at that time, when the Jews were traveling to Jerusalem for the more solemn feasts, the Samaritans were more difficult, because they considered that their own temple, built on Mount Gerizim, was being treated with contempt, in which they contended that one ought to worship, and not in the Jerusalem temple, as observed here by B. Lyserus, Harmon. c. XCV.

§. III. To someone wishing to join himself as a companion, he says that the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.

Vers. 57. And it came to pass, as they were walking in the way, a certain man said to him: I will follow you whithersoever you go.

Vers. 58. Jesus said to him: The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests: but the Son of man has not where to lay his head.

§. IV. Another wishes first to bury his parent; to whom he says: Let the dead bury their dead. But you go, and announce the kingdom of God.

Vers. 59. But he said to another: Follow me. And he said: Lord, suffer me first to go, and to bury my father.

Vers. 60. And Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their dead. But you go, and announce the kingdom of God.

§. V. To a third, who first wished to bid farewell to his household, he says: he is not fit for the kingdom of God, who has put his hand to the plow, and looks back.

Vers. 61. And another said: I will follow you, Lord; but permit me first to take leave of those who are at my house.

Vers. 62. Jesus said to him: No man putting his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

CHAPTER XIV. The sending out of the seventy disciples.

§. I. Jesus, sending out others, namely seventy disciples, warns them to pray to the Lord of the harvest for the harvesters, and says that he is sending them out like lambs into the midst of wolves.

Luke X. v. 1. After these things, however, the Lord designated also other seventy-two: and sent them two by two before his face, into every city and place where he himself was about to come.

Vers. 2. And he said to them: The harvest indeed is great, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he may send laborers into his harvest.

Vers. 3. Go: Behold I send you as lambs among wolves.

[This sending out seems to have taken place in the month of September, at the time of the second harvest, which immediately preceded the feast of tabernacles Lev. XXIII. Christ, having already undertaken the final visitation throughout all Palestine, sent out the LXX disciples into Galilee, thus for the second time thrusting forth laborers into his harvest, saying again: The harvest indeed is copious, but the laborers are few. Luke X. 2. Which expression seems to have been taken from the present matter, namely from the harvest.]

§. II. The instruction of these disciples, whom he also adorns with the gift of healing.

Vers. 4. Do not carry a money bag, nor a wallet, nor sandals, and greet no one along the way.

Vers. 5. Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace to this house:

Vers. 6. And if a son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon him; but if not, it shall return to you.

Vers. 7. And remain in the same house, eating and drinking the things that are with them: for the laborer is worthy of his hire. Do not pass from house to house.

Vers. 8. And into whatsoever city you shall enter, and they shall receive you, eat what things are set before you:

Vers. 9. And heal the sick that are therein, and say to them: The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

Vers. 10. But into whatsoever city you shall enter, and they shall not receive you, going out into the streets thereof, say:

Vers. 11. Even the very dust of your city that cleaveth to us, we wipe off against you: yet know this, that the kingdom of God is at hand.

Vers. 12. I say to you, that it shall be more tolerable at that day for Sodom, than for that city.

§. III. Again he cries out woe because of Chorazin and Bethsaida, and predicts the casting down of Capernaum.

Vers. 13. Woe to thee, Corazin, woe to thee, Bethsaida: for if in Tyre and Sidon had been wrought the miracles that have been wrought in you, they had long ago sat in sackcloth and ashes, doing penance.

Vers. 14. But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment, than for you.

Vers. 15. And thou, Capharnaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

§. IV. He who contemns or receives the disciples of Christ, contemns or receives Christ himself.

Vers. 16. He that heareth you, heareth me: and he that despiseth you, despiseth me. And he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me.

CHAPTER XV. Christ teaches at the feast in Jerusalem, whom the priests and Pharisees wished to apprehend; but the servants return with the business undone. Nicodemus pleads his cause.

§. I. The Jews seek Christ at the feast, and diverse judgments are passed concerning him.

John VII. v. 11. The Jews therefore sought him at the feast day, and said: Where is he?

Vers. 12. And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him. For some said: He is a good man. But others said: No, but he seduceth the people.

Vers. 13. Yet no man spoke openly of him, for fear of the Jews.

§. II. In the midst of the feast he teaches in the temple, and warns those who marvel that his doctrine is not his own, but the Father's, and since no one keeps the law of Moses, why do they attempt to kill him, and that because of health restored to a miserable man on the Sabbath.

Vers. 14. Now about the midst of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.

Vers. 15. And the Jews wondered, saying: How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?

Vers. 16. Jesus answered them, and said: My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.

Vers. 17. If any man will do his will: he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.

Vers. 18. He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

Vers. 19. Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keepeth the law?

Vers. 20. Why do you seek to kill me? The crowd answered and said: You have a demon: who seeks to kill you?

Vers. 21. Jesus answered and said to them: I have done one work, and you all marvel.

Vers. 22. Therefore Moses gave you circumcision: (not because it is from Moses, but from the fathers) and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man.

Vers. 23. If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath, so that the law of Moses may not be broken: are you angry with me, because I made a man entirely whole on the Sabbath?

Vers. 24. Do not judge according to appearance, but judge a just judgment.

§. III. As some were wavering concerning his person, he teaches that he was sent by the Father. Whence they wished to apprehend him: but many from the people believed in him.

Vers. 25. Some therefore from Jerusalem were saying: Is this not he, whom they seek to kill?

Vers. 26. And behold he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Have the princes truly known that this is the Christ?

Vers. 27. But we know this man, whence he is: but when Christ comes, no one knows whence he is.

Vers. 28. Jesus therefore cried out in the temple teaching, and saying: You both know me, and you know whence I am: and I have not come of myself, but he is true, who sent me, whom you do not know.

Vers. 29. I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.

Vers. 30. They sought therefore to apprehend him: and no one laid hands upon him, because his hour had not yet come.

Verse 31. But many of the crowd believed in him, and were saying: When Christ comes, will he perform more signs than those which this man performs?

§. IV. The Pharisees, together with the chief priests, being indignant at this, send servants to apprehend Christ.

Verse 32. The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him: and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to apprehend him.

§. V. Christ teaches that he will shortly be sought in vain: which the Jews do not understand.

Vers. 33. Jesus therefore said to them: Yet a little while I am with you: and I go to him that sent me.

Vers. 34. You shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, you cannot come.

Vers. 35. The Jews therefore said among themselves: Whither will this man go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?

Vers. 36. What is this saying that he said: You shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, you cannot come?

§. VI. On the last day of the feast Christ publicly cries out. Whoever thirsts, let him come to me, and drink. He who believes in me, from his body shall flow rivers of living water. Whence various judgments arise concerning Christ.

Vers. 37. And on the last, the great day of the festivity, Jesus stood and cried out, saying: If any man thirst, let him come to me, and drink.

Vers. 38. He that believes in me, as the scripture says, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.

Vers. 39. Now this he said of the Spirit, which they should receive who believed in him: for as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.

Vers. 40. Of that crowd therefore, when they had heard these his words, they said: This is the prophet indeed.

Vers. 41. Others said: This is the Christ. But some said: Does Christ come out of Galilee?

Vers. 42. Does not the Scripture say: That Christ comes from the seed of David, and from the town of Bethlehem, where David was?

Vers. 43. So there was a dissension in the crowd because of him.

§. VII. The servants sent to apprehend him return and proclaim him.

Vers. 44. And some of them wanted to apprehend him: but no one laid hands upon him.

Vers. 45. The ministers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees. And they said to them: Why have you not brought him?

Vers. 46. The ministers answered: Never did man speak like this man.

Vers. 47. The Pharisees therefore answered them: Are you also seduced?

Vers. 48. Has any one of the rulers believed in him, or of the Pharisees?

Vers. 49. But this crowd, which does not know the law, are accursed.

§. VIII. Nicodemus warns that the law condemns no one unheard: he receives no answer, other than that no prophet arises from Galilee.

Vers. 50. Nicodemus said to them, he who came to him by night, who was one of them:

V. 51. Does our law judge a man, unless it first hear from him, and know what he does?

V. 52. They answered, and said to him: Art thou also a Galilean? Search the Scriptures, and see, that out of Galilee a prophet doth not rise.

Vers. 53. And every man returned to his own house.

CHAPTER XVI. Christ absolves the adulteress, and demonstrates that he is the light of the world.

§. I. In the evening, having gone out to the Mount of Olives, in the morning

Christ returned into the temple, and taught the people; an adulteress is brought to him, that they might tempt him; but writing on the ground, he commands that he who is without sin should cast the first stone. Whereupon they withdraw themselves from the temple in order, and the adulteress is truly absolved by Christ.

John VIII. v. 1. And Jesus went unto the mount of Olives:

Vers. 2. And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and sitting down, he taught them.

Vers. 3. And the scribes and Pharisees bring unto him a woman taken in adultery: and they set her in the midst,

Vers. 4. And said to him: Master, this woman was even now taken in adultery.

Vers. 5. Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such a one should be stoned. But what sayest thou?

Vers. 6. And this they said tempting him, that they might be able to accuse him. But Jesus bowing himself down, wrote with his finger on the ground.

Vers. 7. When therefore they continued asking him, he lifted himself up, and said to them: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

V. 8. And again stooping down, he wrote on the ground.

Vers. 9. But hearing this, they went out one by one, beginning at the eldest: and Jesus alone remained, and the woman standing in the midst.

Vers. 10. Then Jesus lifting up himself, said to her: Woman, where are they that accused thee? hath no man condemned thee?

She said: No man, Lord. And Jesus said: Neither will I condemn thee: Go, and now sin no more.

[These events, and those which follow, seem to fall in the month of November: because he spent the night on the Mount of Olives, and taught by day in the Jerusalem temple: at which time the adulteress was brought to him, and the disputes with the Jews were held.]

§. II. Christ professes himself to be the light of the world, and asserts that this testimony is true, because he came from God, and goes to God; and that not he alone, but the Father also testifies the same. But that the Jews knew neither him nor the Father.

Vers. 12. Again therefore Jesus spoke to them, saying: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

Vers. 13. The Pharisees therefore said to him: Thou givest testimony of thyself: thy testimony is not true.

Vers. 14. Jesus answered, and said to them: Although I give testimony of myself, my testimony is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go: but you know not whence I come, or whither I go.

Vers. 15. You judge according to the flesh: I judge not any man.

Vers. 16. And if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone: but I, and the Father that sent me.

Vers. 17. And in your law it is written, that the testimony of two men is true.

Vers. 18. I am he that beareth witness of myself: and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.

Vers. 19. They said therefore unto him: Where is thy Father? Jesus answered: Neither know ye me, nor my Father: if ye knew me, perhaps ye would know my Father also.

Vers. 20. These words spake Jesus in the treasury, teaching in the temple: and no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come.

§. III. He convinces the Jews that, if they do not believe in him, they will die in their sins.

Verse 21. Jesus therefore said to them again: I go, and you shall seek me, and you shall die in your sin. Whither I go, you cannot come.

Verse 22. The Jews therefore said: Will he kill himself, because he said: Whither I go, you cannot come?

Verse 23. And he said to them: You are from beneath: I am from above. You are of this world, I am not of this world.

Verse 24. Therefore I said to you, that you shall die in your sins: for if you believe not that I am he, you shall die in your sin.

Verse 25. They said therefore to him: Who art thou? Jesus said to them: The beginning, who also speak to you.

Verse 26. I have many things to speak and to judge of you: but he that sent me is true: and I speak the things in the world which I have heard of him.

Verse 27. And they understood not that he called God his Father.

§. IV. He appeals to the exaltation of the Son of man, from whence they shall recognize him: Therefore many believed in him.

Verse 28. Jesus therefore said to them: When you shall have lifted up the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father hath taught me, these things I speak:

Verse 29. And he that sent me is with me, and he hath not left me alone: for I do always the things that please him.

Verse 30. As he spoke these things, many believed in him.

Ver. 31. Jesus therefore said to those Jews who believed in him: If you abide in my word, you shall truly be my disciples:

Ver. 32. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free.

§. V. The unbelievers boasted that they were the seed of Abraham; but he teaches that this was only according to the flesh, not according to the spirit, because they were seeking to kill him.

Ver. 33. They answered him: We are the seed of Abraham, and we have never been slaves to anyone: how do you say: You shall be free?

Ver. 34. Jesus answered them: Amen, amen I say to you: that everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

Ver. 35. Now the slave does not remain in the house forever: but the son remains forever.

Ver. 36. If therefore the son sets you free, you shall be truly free.

Ver. 37. I know that you are the children of Abraham: but you seek to kill me, because my word does not take hold in you.

Ver. 38. I speak what I have seen with my Father: and you do what you have seen with your father.

Ver. 39. They answered and said to him: Abraham is our father. Jesus says to them: If you are the children of Abraham, do the works of Abraham.

Ver. 40. But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you, which I heard from God: this Abraham did not do.

Ver. 41. You do the works of your father. Therefore they said to him: We are not born of fornication: we have one Father, God.
