Ver. 42. Jesus therefore said to them: If God were your Father, you would surely love me. For I proceeded and came from God: for I came not of myself, but he sent me.

Ver. 43. Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word.

Ver. 44. You are of your father the devil: and you wish to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and stood not in the truth: because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own, because he is a liar, and the father of it.

§. VI. He appeals to the truth of his sermons and the innocence of his life: the Jews slander him as being a Samaritan (regarding his doctrine) and having a devil (by which they desire to disparage the holiness of his life); he, however, defends himself, that he does not have a devil, because he honors the Father: and that his word is the word of life: and he defends this against their slanders even by the example of Abrahamic faith in himself; asserting also his πρὸ ὕπαρξιν before Abraham. Whence the Jews wished to stone him, but he passed through the midst of them.

Ver. 45. But if I speak the truth, do you not believe me?

Ver. 46. Which of you will convict me of sin? If I speak the truth to you, why do you not believe me?

Ver. 47. He who is of God, hears the words of God. Therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God.

Ver. 48. The Jews therefore answered, and said to him: Do we not say well, that you are a Samaritan, and have a devil?

Ver. 49. Jesus answered: I have not a devil: but I honor my Father, and you have dishonored me.

Ver. 50. But I do not seek my own glory: there is one who seeks, and judges.

V. 51. Amen, amen I say to you: if anyone shall keep my word, he shall not see death forever.

Vers. 52. The Jews therefore said: Now we know that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets: and thou sayest: If any man keep my word, he shall not taste death for ever.

Vers. 53. Art thou greater than our father Abraham, who is dead? and the prophets are dead. Whom dost thou make thyself?

Vers. 54. Jesus answered: If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing: it is my Father that glorifieth me, of whom you say that he is your God.

Vers. 55. And you have not known him; but I know him: and if I shall say that I know him not, I shall be like to you, a liar. But I do know him, and do keep his word.

Vers. 56. Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day: he saw it, and was glad.

Vers. 57. The Jews therefore said to him: Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?

Vers. 58. Jesus said to them: Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was made, I am.

Vers. 59. They took up therefore stones to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple.

CHAPTER XVII. The healing of the blind man.

§. I. Jesus seeing a blind man while passing by, the disciples ask whether he was born blind, or whether his parents sinned; but they receive the answer that neither he nor his parents deserved this (above others): but that the glory of God was to be manifested, and he healed the blind man.

John IX. v. 1. And Jesus passing by, saw a man who was blind from his birth:

Vers. 2. And his disciples asked him: Rabbi, who sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be born blind?

Vers. 3. Jesus answered: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.

Vers. 4. I must work the works of him that sent me, whilst it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.

Verse 5. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

Verse 6. When he had said these things, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and anointed the clay upon his eyes,

Verse 7. And said to him: Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which is interpreted, Sent). He went therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

[B. Lyserus admits in Harm. c. CIV that as many of all the Ecclesiastical Doctors, both ancient and modern, as have written an Evangelical Harmony, immediately append the ninth chapter of John, together with a great part of the tenth, to the eighth chapter. He says it is a serious matter to depart from that common opinion, which is indeed confirmed by the authority of so many most illustrious men, but that certain reasons not to be despised seem to exist, for which it might be permitted for him to depart from it. But we do not see them to be of such moment that we should disregard the εἱρμὸν τῆς ἀκολουθείας (chain of sequence) in John, which without doubt moved all the doctors, and disregard the authority of all. For as to what he chiefly assumes, that according to that opinion Christ remained in Jerusalem continuously for almost three months from the beginning of the Feast of Tabernacles to the Feast of Dedication, and thus after the stones were taken up: we truly judge that that opinion does not necessarily imply that. Since it is by no means inconvenient that he betook himself again to Jerusalem for the Feast of Dedication: indeed, B. Lyserus himself in the same place wishes that mention is still made in Luke of Christ making a journey to Jerusalem twice before the passion, namely in Luke 13:22 and c. 17:11.]

§. II. The neighbors inquire about him, and bring him to the Pharisees, who judge that Christ is not from God because he healed on the Sabbath, though some contradict them: whom the healed blind man acknowledges as a Prophet.

Verse 8. The neighbors therefore, and they who had seen him before, that he was a beggar, said: Is not this he that sat, and begged? Some said: This is he.

Verse 9. But others said: No, but he is like him. But he said: I am he.

Verse 10. They said therefore to him: How were thy eyes opened?

Verse 11. He answered: That man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed my eyes, and said to me: Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash. And I went, I washed, and I see.

Verse 12. And they said: Where is he? He saith: I know not.

Vers. 13. They bring him to the Pharisees, who had been blind.

Vers. 14. Now it was the Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.

Vers. 15. Therefore the Pharisees asked him again how he had received his sight. But he said to them: He put clay upon my eyes, and I washed, and I see.

Vers. 16. Some of the Pharisees therefore said: This man is not from God, who does not keep the Sabbath. But others said: How can a sinful man do these miracles? And there was a division among them.

Vers. 17. They say therefore to the blind man again: What do you say about him, who opened your eyes? But he said: That he is a Prophet.

§. III. The parents of the blind man are asked about the truth of the matter, they answer, and say that the son himself should be asked, who confesses that, although he was born blind, he received sight from Christ, and therefore that Jesus is from God: for which he is cast out by the priests.

Vers. 18. The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him who had seen:

Vers. 19. And they asked them, saying: Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?

Vers. 20. His parents answered them and said: We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:

V. 21. But how he now sees, we do not know. Or who opened his eyes, we do not know: ask him: he is of age, let him speak for himself.

Vers. 22. His parents said these things because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had already conspired that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.

Vers. 23. Therefore his parents said: Because he is of age, ask him.

Vers. 24. They called therefore again the man that had been blind, and said to him: Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.

V. 25. He said therefore to them: If he is a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see.

Vers. 26. They said therefore to him: What did he do to thee? How did he open thy eyes?

Vers. 27. He answered them: I have told you already, and you have heard: why would you hear it again? will you also become his disciples?

Vers. 28. They reviled him therefore, and said: Be thou his disciple; but we are the disciples of Moses.

Vers. 29. We know that God spoke to Moses: but as for this man, we know not from whence he is.

Vers. 30. That man answered, and said to them: Why, herein is a wonderful thing, that you know not from whence he is, and he hath opened my eyes:

Vers. 31. Now we know that God doth not hear sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doth his will, him he heareth.

Vers. 32. From the beginning of the world it hath not been heard, that any man hath opened the eyes of one born blind.

Vers. 33. Unless this man were of God, he could not do any thing.

Vers. 34. They answered, and said to him: Thou wast wholly born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.

§. IV. Jesus asks whether he believes in the Son of God, and testifies that he himself is he, and that he came into the world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind. Therefore the Pharisees ask, whether they themselves are blind? He answers, if you were blind, you would not have sin, but now because you say, you are seeing, your sin remains.

Vers. 35. Jesus heard that they had cast him out: and when he had found him, he said to him: Do you believe in the Son of God?

Vers. 36. He answered and said: Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?

Vers. 37. And Jesus said to him: You have both seen him, and he who is speaking with you, he is the one.

Vers. 38. But he said: I believe, Lord. And falling down he worshipped him.

Vers. 39. And Jesus said: For judgment I came into this world: that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.

Vers. 40. And some of the Pharisees who were with him heard, and said to him: Are we also blind?

Vers. 41. Jesus said to them: If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say: We see. Your sin remains.

CHAPTER XVIII.

A sermon concerning the sheepfold and the good shepherd.

§. I. He teaches that the priests are thieves, not shepherds:

he teaches: that he is the door, and that he has come, so that we may have life and abundance.

Verse 1. Amen, amen I say to you: he who does not enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, he is a thief and a robber.

Verse 2. But he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

Verse 3. To him the gatekeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out.

Verse 4. And when he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them: and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.

Verse 5. But they do not follow a stranger, but flee from him: because they do not know the voice of strangers.

Verse 6. Jesus spoke this proverb to them. But they did not understand what he was saying to them.

Verse 7. Jesus therefore said to them again: Amen, amen I say to you, that I am the door of the sheep.

Verse 8. All as many as have come are thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not hear them.

Verse 9. I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved: and he will go in and go out, and will find pasture.

Verse 10. The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and may have it more abundantly.

§. II. That he is that good shepherd laying down his soul for the sheep, loving the sheep intimately, and that he will gather other sheep to the fold ἀντιξυσίας to lay down his life and in turn to take it up.

Vers. 11. I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives his soul for his sheep.

Vers. 12. But the hireling, and he who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming, and leaves the sheep, and flees: and the wolf snatches, and scatters the sheep:

Vers. 13. But the hireling flees, because he is a hireling, and he does not care about the sheep.

Vers. 14. I am the good shepherd: and I know mine, and mine know me.

Vers. 15. As the Father knows me, and I know the Father: and I lay down my soul for my sheep.

Vers. 16. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: and them I must bring, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one fold, and one shepherd.

Vers. 17. Therefore the Father loves me: because I lay down my soul, that I may take it again.

Vers. 18. No one takes it from me: but I lay it down of myself, and I have power to lay it down: and I have power to take it again: This commandment I have received from my Father.

§. III. Dissensions among the Jews concerning this discourse of Christ.

Vers. 19. A dissension was made again among the Jews because of these words.

Vers. 20. But many of them were saying: He has a demon, and is mad: why do you hear him?

Verse 21. Others were saying: These are not the words of one who has a demon: can a demon open the eyes of the blind?

CHAPTER XIX. The report of the seventy disciples returning.

§. I. They report what they have done, and among other things also that demons were subject to them; but they are warned to rejoice in this, that their names are written in heaven.

Luke 10, verse 17. But the seventy-two returned with joy, saying: Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name.

Verse 18. And he said to them: I was seeing Satan falling like lightning from heaven.

Verse 19. Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the might of the enemy: and nothing shall harm you.

Verse 20. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you: but rejoice that your names are written in the heavens.

[That return to Christ either happened on the journey, when after the feast of tabernacles was finished Christ again departed from Jerusalem and undertook a journey, so that they met him outside Jerusalem. In which way some think the parable about the man descending from Jerusalem, who fell among robbers, was taken from the present event: or, which is more likely, while he was still staying in Jerusalem: because the question by the lawyer seems to have been instituted there, not on the journey, and from there he betook himself to Bethany, where Martha lived with Mary, distant scarcely half a mile from Jerusalem.]

§. II. Jesus with joy celebrates the Father, because he manifested to the little ones things hidden from the wise.

Verse 21. In that same hour he exulted in the Holy Spirit, and said: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father: for so it has pleased you.

Verse 22. All things have been delivered to me by my Father: And no one knows who the Son is, except the Father; and who the Father is, except the Son, and to whom the Son wills to reveal him.

§. III. He declares those eyes blessed, which see what the disciples see. Which many Kings and Prophets desired.

Vers. 23. And turning to his disciples, he said: Blessed are the eyes, which see the things that you see.

Vers. 24. For I say to you, that many Prophets and Kings have desired to see the things that you see, and have not seen them; and to hear the things that you hear, and have not heard them.

CHAPTER XX. A lawyer, tempting Jesus, is informed who his neighbor is.

§. I. A lawyer asks what must be done to inherit eternal life: and he is referred to the law: the sum of which he brings forward, and is commanded to do it.

Vers. 25. And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, tempting him, and saying: Master, by doing what shall I possess eternal life?

Vers. 26. But he said to him: What is written in the law? how do you read?

Vers. 27. He answering said: You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind: and your neighbor as yourself.

Vers. 28. And he said to him: You have answered rightly: do this, and you shall live.

[He is referred to the law, and commanded to do it, because he was asking what he ought to DO to obtain life; but he is not taught that he or any other mortal can do or perfectly fulfill the law.]

§. II. The lawyer, desiring to justify himself,

he asks, who is his neighbor? and he is convinced by the parable, that the Samaritan showing mercy to a man lethally wounded is his neighbor (even if he were a Jew).

Ver. 29. But he, wishing to justify himself, said to Jesus: And who is my neighbor?

Ver. 30. And Jesus taking up the word, said: A certain man was descending from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers, who also stripped him: and having inflicted wounds, they went away, leaving him half-dead.

Ver. 31. And it happened that a certain priest was descending by the same way: and having seen him, he passed by.

Ver. 32. Likewise also a Levite, when he was near the place, and saw him, passed by:

Ver. 33. But a certain Samaritan making a journey, came near him: and seeing him, was moved with compassion.

Ver. 34. And approaching, he bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine: and placing him on his own beast, he led him to an inn, and took care of him.

Ver. 35. And the next day he brought out two denarii, and gave them to the innkeeper, and said: Take care of him: and whatsoever you shall spend over and above, I, when I return, will repay you.

Ver. 36. Which of these three seems to you to have been a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?

Ver. 37. But he said: He who showed mercy to him. And he, Jesus, said: Go, and do you likewise.

CHAPTER XXI. The conversation of Christ with Martha concerning the one thing necessary.

§. I. Jesus, coming to Bethany, is received by Martha.

Vers. 38. Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house;

§. II. Mary, sitting at the feet of Jesus, listens to Jesus; Martha is busy in order to serve him; and she complains about Mary, because she leaves the ministry to her alone. But Jesus answers: that one thing is necessary: that Mary has chosen the best part.

Vers. 39. And she had a sister called Mary, who also sitting at the Lord's feet, heard his word.

Vers. 40. But Martha was busy about much serving: who stood, and said: Lord, hast thou no care that my sister hath left me alone to serve? Speak to her therefore, that she may help me.

Vers. 41. And the Lord answering, said to her: Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things.

Vers. 42. But one thing is necessary.

Vers. 43. Mary hath chosen the best part, which shall not be taken away from her.

CHAPTER XXII. Jesus again teaches a formula for praying, and exhorts to prayer.

§. I. After Jesus had prayed somewhere, he is asked by one of his disciples to teach them to pray, as John had taught his disciples.

Vers. 1. And it came to pass, that as he was in a certain place praying, when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.

The occasion here is therefore different, namely, when JESUS was praying, and when he was asked by a certain disciple; not, indeed, as in Matthew 6, in the middle of a sermon; the place is different, and the time is different, because that formula was in the sermon delivered on the mount, this one long after the mountain sermon: inasmuch as it is recounted in Luke chapter 6; the reason prescribed is different: because there it was αὐτομάτως, when he was warning against πολυλογία in Pharisaical prayers: here, because he was asked, by the example of John, to teach the manner of praying: therefore there is no contradiction, not even an apparent one, if one considers the diversity of the history, because the final clause subjoined in Matthew is omitted here: inasmuch as it is not even an essential part of the prayer. It does not please the Jesuits, Maldonado, Cornelius à Lapide, and Jansenius, that the formula of prayer was delivered twice by the Lord: whence they twist themselves here regarding the order of the Evangelists: which, however, the imprudent Calixtus thought should be held in contempt here: But the diversity of time sufficiently convinces that the formula, previously proposed in general on the mount, was repeated here: now, however, delivered separately to the disciples, who, when they asked, 'teach us to pray,' Christ signified that there was no need for a new formula of prayer, repeating the same one which he had previously delivered, inasmuch as it commends itself by brevity, perfection, order, efficacy, and necessity: which Tertullian, in his book on Prayer, chapter 1, deservedly calls the breviary of the whole Gospel: concerning which Augustine, Epistle 121, chapter 12, says: 'If you run through all the words of the holy prayers, you will find nothing which this Lord's prayer does not contain and conclude.'

§. II. The formula of prayer prescribed by the Lord.

Verse 2. And he said to them: When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.

Verse 3. Give us this day our daily bread.

Verse 4. And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil.

§. III. The parable, by commands and promises, excites one to pray.

Verse 5. And he said to them: Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go to him at midnight, and say to him: Friend, lend me three loaves.

Verse 6. Because my friend has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.

Verse 7. And he from within answering should say: Do not be troublesome to me, the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed, I cannot rise and give to you.

Verse 8. And if he shall persevere knocking: I say to you, even if he will not give him by rising because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise, and give him as many as he needs.

Vers. 9. And I say to you: Ask, and it shall be given to you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.

Vers. 10. For everyone who asks, receives: and he who seeks, finds: and to him who knocks, it shall be opened.

Vers. 11. But which of you, if his father asks for bread, will he give him a stone? Or a fish: will he give him a serpent instead of a fish?

Vers. 12. Or if he shall ask for an egg: will he reach him a scorpion?

Vers. 13. If you therefore, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your heavenly Father give his Spirit to those who ask him?

CHAPTER XXIII. The casting out of a mute demon, and an apologetic response against those who slander.

§. I. He casts out a mute demon: the people marvel at it: some slander him regarding Beelzebub, others by testing him desired a sign from heaven.

Ver. 14. And he was casting out a demon, and it was mute. And when he had cast out the demon, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marveled.

V. 15. But some of them said: by Beelzebub the prince of demons he casts out demons.

Ver. 16. And others, testing him, sought a sign from heaven from him.

§. II. He refutes the blasphemy concerning Beelzebub, and shows himself to be more powerful than the Devil.

Ver. 17. But he, as he saw their thoughts, said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and house will fall upon house.

Ver. 18. But if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? because you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub.

Ver. 19. But if I cast out demons by Beelzebub: by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

Ver. 20. But if I cast out demons by the finger of GOD: then the kingdom of GOD has come upon you.

Vers. 21. When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, those things which he possesseth are in peace.

Vers. 22. But if a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he will take away all his armour wherein he trusted, and distribute his spoils.

Vers. 23. He that is not with me, is against me: and he that gathereth not with me, scattereth.

§. III. He warns concerning the ejected demon returning to his house.

Vers. 24. When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest: and not finding, he saith: I will return into my house whence I came out.

Vers. 25. And when he is come, he findeth it swept and garnished.

Vers. 26. Then he goeth, and taketh with him seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and entering in they dwell there. And the last state of that man becomes worse than the first.

§. IV. On the occasion of a woman proclaiming his mother blessed, he teaches that those who hear the word of God and keep it are blessed.

Vers. 27. And it came to pass, as he spoke these things, a certain woman from the crowd, lifting up her voice, said to him: Blessed is the womb that bore thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked.

Vers. 28. But he said: Yea rather, blessed are they who hear the word of God, and keep it.

§. V. He denies that any sign other than that of Jonah will be given to a wicked generation: and he teaches that it will be condemned by Jonah, and the Queen of the South, and the Ninevites of old.

Vers. 29. And when the crowds were gathering together, he began to say: This generation is a wicked generation: it seeketh a sign, and a sign shall not be given it, but the sign of Jonah the Prophet.

Vers. 30. For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites: so shall the Son of man be to this generation.

Vers. 31. The Queen of the South shall rise in the judgment with the men of this generation, and shall condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon: and behold, more than Solomon is here.

Vers. 32. The men of Nineveh shall rise in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, more than Jonah is here.

§. VI. Meanwhile, he warns that a light is not to be hidden under a bushel, and by a similar light of the body's eye, he exhorts men to sincerity (of faith and life).

Vers. 33. No man lighteth a candle, and putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel: but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.

Vers. 34. The light of the body is thine eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.

Vers. 35. Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.

Vers. 36. If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.

CHAPTER XXIV. The rebuke of the Pharisees and Lawyers on account of hypocrisy committed at a banquet.

§. I. He is invited to lunch by a Pharisee, who is surprised that he approached with unwashed hands: whence Christ warns about hypocrisy, that the Pharisees cleanse the outside of the vessels, but are inwardly full of rapine and malice, and think they are cleansed by alms.

Vers. 37. And as he spake, a certain Pharisee besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.

Vers. 38. But the Pharisee began to reason within himself, saying, why he had not been baptized before dinner.

Vers. 39. And the Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter; but that which is within you is full of rapine and iniquity.

Vers. 40. Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without, make also that which is within?

Vers. 41. But yet that which remaineth, give alms; and behold, all things are clean unto you.

§. II. Woe is denounced against the Pharisees who take care of tithes, but neglect judgment and charity; likewise because of their pride and because, walking over monuments, they do not notice them.

Vers. 42. But woe to you, Pharisees, because you tithe mint, and rue, and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the charity of God: now these things you ought to have done, and not to leave those undone.

Vers. 43. Woe to you, Pharisees, who love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and salutations in the market place.

Vers. 44. Woe to you, because you are as monuments which appear not, and men that walk over them are not aware.

§. III. To the lawyer applying these things to himself, he says woe also to them, because they impose on others burdens that are unbearable, which they themselves do not touch with a finger: that they build the sepulchres of the prophets, whom their fathers killed, consenting to their work: and he predicts that they will also kill the prophets and apostles to be sent by wisdom, so that all the blood of the prophets is to be required of this generation from Abel even to Zacharias: finally, that having the key of knowledge they do not enter, and they hinder others who wish to enter.

Verse 45. But one of the lawyers answering, saith to him: Master, in saying these things, thou reproachest us also.

Verse 46. But he said: Woe to you lawyers also, because you load men with burdens which they cannot bear, and you yourselves touch not the packs with one of your fingers.

Verse 47. Woe to you, who build the monuments of the prophets: and your fathers killed them.

Verse 48. Truly you bear witness that you consent to the doings of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and you build their sepulchres.

Verse 49. For this cause also the wisdom of God said: I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute:

Verse 50. That the blood of all the prophets which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,

Verse 51. From the blood of Abel, unto the blood of Zacharias, who was slain between the altar and the temple. Yea I say to you, it shall be required of this generation.

Verse 52. Woe to you lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge, you yourselves have not entered, and those that were entering, you have hindered.

§. IV. The lawyers and Pharisees from that time lay in wait for him, that they might catch him in his words.

Verse 53. And as he was saying these things to them, the Pharisees and the lawyers began to urge him grievously, and to oppress his mouth about many things,

Verse 54. Lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch something from his mouth, that they might accuse him.

CHAPTER XXV. Various instructions proposed to the disciples in a great gathering of the crowd, concerning avoiding the Pharisaic leaven, concerning not fearing men, concerning blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, concerning the assistance to be provided by the Holy Spirit to martyrs.

§. I. A great confluence of people of several thousands, where the disciples were warned about avoiding the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

Verse 1. And when many multitudes were surrounding [him], so that they trampled upon one another, he began to say to his disciples: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

§. II. Because nothing is hidden that is not to be manifested, that they themselves are not to be feared, who can kill the body, but him who can cast into Gehenna, with a view to divine providence, which extends itself both to sparrows and the hairs of the head, and the reward of confession and the punishment of the denial of the Lord.

Verse 2. But nothing is covered that shall not be revealed: nor hidden, that shall not be known.

Verse 3. For what you have said in darkness shall be said in the light: and what you have spoken into the ear in the chambers shall be preached on the housetops.

Verse 4. But I say to you my friends: Be not afraid of those who kill the body, and after these things have nothing more that they can do.

Verse 5. But I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after he has killed, has power to cast into hell. So I say to you, fear him.

Verse 6. Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?

Verse 7. But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not therefore fear: you are of more value than many sparrows.

Verse 8. But I say to you: Everyone whoever shall have confessed me before men, and the Son of man shall confess him before the Angels of God.

Verse 9. But he who shall have denied me before men, shall be denied before the Angels of God.

§. III. Concerning blasphemy against the Son of man and against the Holy Spirit.

Verse 10. And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but to him who shall have blasphemed against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven.

§. IV. Concerning the assistance of the Holy Spirit, when a case is to be pleaded by the disciples of Christ in synagogues, or before magistrates.

Verse 11. But when they shall bring you into the synagogues, or to magistrates and powers, do not be anxious how or what you should answer, or what you should say.

Verse 12. For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say.

CHAPTER XXVI.

Christ refuses to preside over the dividing of an inheritance, and publicly dissuades from avarice.

§. I. Someone soliciting him to order his brother to divide the inheritance, Christ denies, but says he was not appointed a judge for such things.

Verse 13. But a certain man from the crowd said to him: Master, tell my brother that he divide the inheritance with me.

Verse 14. But he said to him: Man, who appointed me a judge or divider over you?

§. II. He warns everyone to beware of avarice, having proposed a parable about a rich steward whose soul is suddenly summoned.

Vers. 15. And he said to them: See, and beware of all avarice: for a man's life does not consist in the abundance of the things which he possesses.

Vers. 16. And he spoke a similitude to them, saying: The land of a certain rich man brought forth plenty of fruits:

Vers. 17. And he thought within himself, saying: What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?

Vers. 18. And he said: This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and will build greater: and into that will I gather all things that are grown to me, and my goods.

Vers. 19. And I will say to my soul: Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years: take thy rest, eat, drink, make good cheer.

Vers. 20. But God said to him: Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee: and whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?

Vers. 21. So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich towards God.

CHAPTER XXVII.

The disciples are warned about avoiding excessive anxiety regarding food and clothing, and about seeking the kingdom of God without fear: about alms, about true treasure, and that they should be prepared by the example of the vigilant servant for the coming of the Lord, and about future dissensions among relatives.

§. I. Excessive and pagan anxiety about food and clothing is forbidden. The ravens and the lilies of the field are set before the disciples as an example: they are commanded to seek the kingdom of God, and that the little flock should not fear, and that they should gather treasure for themselves in heaven, and similar things.

let them be as servants, who await the return of the Lord from the wedding.

Verse 22. And he said to his disciples: Therefore I say to you: Do not be anxious for your life, what you shall eat, nor for your body, what you shall put on.

Verse 23. The life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.

Verse 24. Consider the ravens, for they do not sow, nor do they reap, which have no storehouse, nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than they?

Verse 25. And which of you by taking thought can add one cubit to his stature?

Verse 26. If therefore you are not able to do even that which is least, why are you anxious about the rest?

Verse 27. Consider the lilies, how they grow: they do not labor, nor do they spin: and I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these.

Verse 28. And if God so clothes the grass, which is in the field today, and tomorrow is cast into the oven: how much more you, O you of little faith?

Verse 29. And do not you seek what you shall eat, or what you shall drink: and do not be lifted up on high:

Verse 30. For all these things the nations of the world seek. But your Father knows that you need these things.

Verse 31. Nevertheless seek first the kingdom of God, and his justice: and all these things shall be added to you.

Vers. 32. Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.

Vers. 33. Sell what you possess, and give alms. Make to yourselves bags which grow not old, a treasure in heaven that faileth not: where no thief approacheth, nor moth corrupteth.

Vers. 34. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

Vers. 35. Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands,

And you yourselves like to men who wait for their lord, when he shall return from the wedding: that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open to him immediately.

Vers. 37. Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh, shall find watching: Amen I say to you, that he will gird himself, and make them sit down to meat, and passing will minister unto them.

Vers. 38. And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

Vers. 39. But this know ye, that if the householder did know at what hour the thief would come, he would watch indeed, and would not suffer his house to be broken through.

And be you also ready; for at what hour you think not, the Son of man will come. [This discourse is distinct from that which Matthew recorded in chapter VI, although much analogous; distinct, I say, by reason of time, because that was held long before Christ began to preach about the beatitudes, Matth. V; by reason of place, because that was held on a mountain, this not so; by reason of the object, because this was said to the Apostles, that in general to the people; by reason of the subject matter, because here they are warned not to fear, because it is the Father's will to give them the kingdom, and that they should sell all and give alms, and they are subsequently stirred up to vigilance, which was not done there. Finally, that discourse which is described in Matth. C. V, VI, and VII is summarily repeated here, and the clause delivered there is sealed, Luc. VI.

therefore that discourse described by Matthew was instituted and finished long before the present admonitions.

§. II. To Peter asking whether these things are said to the disciples, Christ answers: how much is required in a faithful and prudent steward: and he illustrates that by the contrary.

Vers. 41. But Peter said to him: Lord, do you speak this parable to us, or also to all?

Vers. 42. And the Lord said: Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent steward, whom the Lord has set over his household, to give them their measure of wheat in due time?

Vers. 43. Blessed is that servant, whom, when his Lord comes, he shall find doing so.

Vers. 44. Truly I say to you, that he will set him over all that he possesses.

Vers. 45. But if that servant says in his heart: My Lord is delaying his coming: and begins to strike the menservants and maidservants, and to eat, and to drink, and to be drunk:

Vers. 46. The lord of that servant will come in the day that he does not expect, and at the hour that he does not know, and will cut him asunder, and will place his portion with the unbelievers.

Vers. 47. And that servant, who knew the will of his lord, and did not prepare, and did not do according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes:

Vers. 48. But he who did not know, and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few. And to everyone to whom much is given, much will be required of him: and to whom they have entrusted much, they will ask more of him.

§. III. Concerning the fire which Christ was about to kindle, but only after the baptism had been established: and concerning the dissensions about to arise among close relatives on account of the Gospel.

Vers. 49. I have come to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I wish, but that it be kindled?

Vers. 50. But I have a baptism to be baptized with: and how I am constrained until it is accomplished?

Vers. 51. Do you think that I have come to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but separation:

Vers. 52. For from this time there will be five in one house divided, three will be divided against two, and two against three:

Vers. 53. Father against his son, and son against his father, mother against daughter, and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

CHAPTER XXVII.

Christ preached again concerning the signs of the weather and concerning reconciliation.

§. I. These things were said to the people concerning the sign of rain and heat: that they recognize the former from the signs, but not likewise the present time of grace.

Vers. 54. And he said also to the crowds: When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately it is said: A rainstorm is coming: and so it happens.

Vers. 55. And when the south wind is blowing, you say: That there will be heat: and it happens.

Vers. 56. Hypocrites, you know how to test the face of the sky and the earth: but how is it that you do not test this time?

Vers. 57. And why do you not judge for yourselves what is just?

Vers. 58. And when you go with your adversary to the ruler, on the way take pains to be delivered from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison.

Vers. 59. I say to you, you will not depart from there until you pay even the very last mite.

[Matt. XVI. 2. et seqq. at another time, and in another place, and on another occasion, and to others, not to the people, but to the Pharisees and Sadducees tempting the Lord, similar things to these were said about tempests: with the sign of Jonah added. Matt. V. 25. in the sermon on the mount there is also an analogous exhortation concerning reconciliation, but proposed in the vindications of the fifth commandment.]

CHAPTER XXIX.

Exhortation to repentance, on the occasion of the report concerning human blood mixed with sacrifices, and the parable of the unfruitful fig tree.

§. I. It is reported to Christ by certain ones at the same time concerning Pilate, that he had mixed the blood of the Galileans with their sacrifices, whom he warns that they would similarly perish unless they repented, with the introduction also of the death of some by the ruin of the tower of Siloam.

Luke XIII. v. 1. And there were present some at that very time, reporting to him concerning the Galileans, whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.

Ver. 2. And answering he said to them: Do you think that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?

Ver. 3. No, I say to you: but unless you have repented, you shall all likewise perish.

Ver. 4. As those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them: do you think that they also were debtors above all men dwelling in Jerusalem?

Ver. 5. No, I say to you: but if you do not repent, you shall all likewise perish.

§. II. He adds a parable concerning a fig tree unfruitful for three years, to be tolerated for one more year by the intercession of the vinedresser.

Vers. 6. And he spoke this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.

Vers. 7. And he said to the dresser of the vineyard: Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none: cut it down therefore; why does it even occupy the ground?

Vers. 8. But he answering, says to him: Lord, let it alone this year also, until I dig about it, and cast in dung.

Vers. 9. And if indeed it bear fruit: but if not, in the future you shall cut it down.

CHAPTER XXX.

Concerning the woman sick for 18 years healed on the Sabbath: which act he defends. Similar things concerning a grain of mustard seed, and leaven mixed into flour.

§. I. In a certain synagogue on the Sabbath day a woman is healed by Christ, who for 18 years had a spirit of infirmity.

Vers. 10. And he was teaching in their synagogue on the Sabbaths.

Vers. 11. And behold a woman, who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years: and was bowed together, and could not look up at all.

Vers. 12. Whom when Jesus saw, he called her to him, and said to her: Woman, you are released from your infirmity.

Vers. 13. And he laid his hands upon her, and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

§. II. The ruler of the synagogue accuses Jesus of the violation of the Sabbath; who convicts him by the example of an ox or an ass, which is led to water on the Sabbath, whence he is publicly confounded, but the people rejoice over the glorious deeds of Christ.

Verse 14. And the ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered and said to the crowd: There are six days in which it is necessary to work: in these therefore come and be healed, and not on the day of the Sabbath.

Verse 15. But the Lord answering him said: Hypocrites, does not each one of you on the Sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the manger, and lead it away to water?

Verse 16. And ought not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the day of the Sabbath?

Verse 17. And when he said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced in all the things that were gloriously done by him.

§. III. The kingdom of heaven is compared to a grain of mustard seed.

Verse 18. He said therefore: To what is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I liken it?

Verse 19. It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his garden, and it grew, and became a great tree: and the birds of the air rested in its branches.

§. IV. Again it is compared to leaven mixed with flour.

Verse 20. And again he said: To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?

Verse 21. It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.

[These parables were previously brought forth also around the sea, Matt. XIII. 3-33, along with many others, now repeated in the Synagogue in the fourth year of the ministry. Δὶς & τρὶς τὰ καλά.]

CHAPTER XXXI. On the fewness of those who are to be saved, and the conversion of the Gentiles.

§. I. He teaches through towns and villages, heading toward Jerusalem.

Verse 22. And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and making his journey to Jerusalem.

[At the approach of the Feast of Dedication.]

§. II. Being asked by someone whether few are to be saved, he warns that we must strive to enter through the narrow gate.

Verse 23. And someone said to him: Lord, are there few who are saved? But he said to them:

Verse 24. Strive to enter through the narrow gate: for many, I say to you, will seek to enter, and will not be able.

[Which he had already warned about long ago in the sermon on the mount, Matt. VII. 13. All harmonic writers, as the blessed Lyserus admits in Harmon. Cap. CXVII, agree that these things cohere with verse 24 of Luke Chapter XIII, from which consensus he himself departs, because these things which are related in verse 25 and following happened ἐν ἀυτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, on the day he was warned to depart from there because of the snares of Herod, v. 31, which could have happened nowhere except in Peraea or Galilee, which were subject to Herod. But what prevents him from having traveled through Galilee and Peraea while heading to Jerusalem for the Feast of Dedication? Just as again after the Feast of Dedication, having left Jerusalem, he betook himself into Peraea, where John had baptized, John X. 40. For the blessed Lyserus also thinks in Harmon. cap. CXIX that the banquet and the healing of the dropsical man in Luke XIV happened in Peraea.] §. III. In vain, the gate of heaven being closed, does he testify that those who will stand outside will knock at the gate. But the Patriarchs and all the Prophets will be seen in the kingdom of GOD: with whom many coming from the East and other regions will sit down, and the last shall be first.

Luke XIII. 25. When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

Vers. 26. Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

Vers. 27. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

Vers. 28. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

Vers. 29. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

Vers. 30. And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.

[Christ had said things analogous to some of these in Matt. VIII. 11. and repeats a similar epiphonema in Matt. XIX. 30. XX. 16. But these things, which are held here, were said on the SAME day on which Herod's snares were announced to Christ, as follows in v. 31.]

CHAPTER XXXII. What is to be announced to Herod the fox. Jerusalem, the slayer of the Prophets, would not be gathered, and is finally to be devastated.

§. I. On the same day the Pharisees announce that Herod is lying in wait for the life of Christ, and therefore he must yield to him: but he himself orders it to be told to Herod the fox, that he is still working for two days, and on the third day will have an end, but in Jerusalem itself.

Luke XIII. 31. The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.

Vers. 32. And he said to them: Go, and tell that fox; Behold I cast out devils, and do cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I am consummated.

Vers. 33. Nevertheless I must walk today and tomorrow and the day following: because it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

§. II. Jesus complains of Jerusalem, which slays the prophets, whom he wished to gather in vain, whence her house is to be deserted.

Vers. 34. Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children, as a bird doth her nest under her wings, and thou wouldest not?

Vers. 35. Behold your house shall be left to you desolate. And I say to you, that you shall not see me, till the time come, when you shall say: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

[The words here are almost the same as in Matt. XXIII. 37, but these were spoken earlier, and on the occasion of the report of the Pharisees concerning Herod's snares, and on the same day that the preceding things were proposed; whence it is ὀφθαλμοφανερῶς clear that this prophecy is different, as regards time, occasion, and other περιστάσεις.]

CHAPTER XXXIII. At a Sabbath banquet he heals a dropsical man at the house of a Pharisee, and speaks concerning the πρωτοκλισίᾳ, and the inviting of the needy, with the addition of a parable concerning the great banquet.

§. I. The Pharisees lie in wait for Christ at a banquet, setting before him a dropsical man, whom he heals; and he defends the deed with a comparison of an ox and an ass fallen into a pit, which are accustomed to be pulled out on the Sabbath.

Luke XIV. 1. And it came to pass, when Jesus went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the sabbath day, to eat bread, that they watched him.

Vers. 2. And behold there was a certain man before him that had the dropsy.

Vers. 3. And Jesus answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

Vers. 4. But they held their peace. But he, taking hold of him, healed him and sent him away.

Vers. 5. And answering them, he said: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fall into a pit, and will not immediately draw him out on the sabbath day?

Vers. 6. And they could not answer him these things.

[B. Lyserus in Harmon. c. CXIX thinks these things were done in Peraea.]

§. II. An admonition concerning choosing a lower place at a banquet, so that we may be invited to occupy a higher place: because he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

Vers. 7. And he spoke also a parable to those who were invited, observing how they chose the first seats, saying to them:

Vers. 8. When you are invited to a wedding, do not sit down in the first place, lest perhaps one more honorable than you be invited by him:

Vers. 9. And he who invited you and him come and say to you: Give place to this man: and then you begin with shame to take the lowest place.

Vers. 10. But when you are invited, go, sit down in the lowest place: that when he who invited you comes, he may say to you: Friend, go up higher. Then there will be glory for you before those who sit at table together with you:

Vers. 11. Because everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

§. III. A rule concerning inviting the poor, who cannot remunerate; which will be repaid in the resurrection of the just.

Vers. 12. And he said also to him who had invited him: When you make a dinner or a supper, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor your rich neighbors: lest perhaps they also invite you back, and a recompense be made to you.

Vers. 13. But when you give a banquet, call the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind:

Vers. 14. And you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you: for it will be repaid to you at the resurrection of the just.

§. IV. When he was proclaimed blessed who eats in the kingdom of GOD; the parable concerning the great banquet, and the despisers of the same, and those invited who were in the streets and lanes, and also those who were found in the highways and hedges, with the despisers excluded, is proposed.

Vers. 15. When one of those who reclined at table with him heard these things, he said to him: Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 16. But he said to him: A certain man made a great dinner, and invited many.

Vers. 17. And he sent his servant at the hour of dinner to say to those invited, that they should come, because all things are now ready.

Vers. 18. And they all began at once to make excuses. The first said to him: I have bought a farm, and I must needs go out and see it: I pray you, have me excused.

Verse 19. And another said: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee, have me excused.

into the world, you say: Because I blaspheme: because I said I am the Son of GOD?

Verse 20. And another said: I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

Verse 37. If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.

Verse 21. And the servant returning, told these things to his lord. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the feeble, and the blind, and the lame.

Verse 38. But if I do, though you will not believe me, believe the works: that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.

§. IV. When they wanted to apprehend Jesus, he went out of their hands.

Verse 22. And the servant said: Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.

Verse 39. They sought therefore to take him: and he escaped out of their hands.

Verse 23. And the lord said to the servant: Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

CHAPTER XXXV. A sermon on following Christ.

Vers. 24. But I say to you, that none of those men who were invited shall taste my supper.

§. I. Jesus went away across the Jordan to that place where John had baptized, and many believe in him.

CHAPTER XXXIV. A disputation held at the Feast of Dedication, concerning Jesus, whether he is the Christ?

John X. v. 40. And he went away again across the Jordan, into that place where John was baptizing at first: and he remained there.

§. I. The Feast of Dedication took place. The Jews in Solomon's porch ask whether he is the Christ? Jesus answers that he has already professed it, and that his works testify of him, but they do not believe, because they are not his sheep.

Vers. 41. And many came to him, and said: Because John indeed did no sign.

Vers. 42. But all things, whatsoever John said about this, were true. And many believed in him.

John X. 22. And the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem: and it was winter.

Vers. 23. And Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's porch.

Vers. 24. The Jews therefore surrounded him, and said to him: How long do you hold our soul in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.

Vers. 25. Jesus answered them: I speak to you, and you do not believe: the works that I do in the name of my Father, these bear witness of me:

Vers. 26. But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep.

Vers. 27. My sheep hear my voice; and I know them, and they follow me:

Vers. 28. And I give them eternal life; and they shall not perish forever, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.

[Osiander thinks this departure is the same, annot. in l. II. cap. XL. Harmon. Evang., as that which is commemorated in Matt. XIX. 1: But others, and among them the blessed Lyserus in Harm. cap. CXVI, distinguish them more correctly: because here indeed the Lord is led by John out of Judea into Perea beyond the Jordan, where he remained for some time, from there however he himself returned into Judea, and there finished the remainder of the visitation of the churches, the blessed Lyserus judges: and that the sermons, disputations, and admonitions which Luke noted in chapters XIV, XV, XVI, XVII pertain to this: but that he moved from Judea when Luke writes in chapter XVII. 11, 'And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee,' attributing half a month to the stay in Judea, but a month's space to the journey through Samaria and Galilee, in which those things happened which Luke recounts in chapter XVII and at the beginning of XVIII: and thus he teaches that Jesus, after those sermons, namely after the parable of the Pharisee and the Publican, departed from Galilee and went again into Perea, Matt. XIX. 1. But those words in Matt. XIX. 1, καὶ ἐγένετο, ὅτι ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς λόγες τέτες, do not refer to the parable of the publican and pharisee, which is described by Luke alone, but to the preceding sermons recorded by Matthew. Nor, when it is said in Luke XVII. 11 that he went to Jerusalem, is the terminus a quo designated as Judea, since Perea can be understood, into which he had betaken himself, and in which he is said to have remained. καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ. John X. 40. Whence that excursion into Judea rests on no foundation: but because he remained in Perea, the sermons, disputations, and admonitions described by Luke from chapter XIV, XV, XVI up to chapter XVII. 11 were without doubt held there: until he moved from Perea, about to go through Samaria and Galilee to Jerusalem: which is hinted at in the same place in chapter XVII. 11. Therefore those sermons in Matt. XVIII. 1, including also the parable of the unmerciful servant described in the preceding chapter Matt. XVIII, together with those which were recounted by Luke, are comprised, as is gathered from the collation of Matt. XVIII. 7, Luke XVII. 1, and Matt. XVIII. 28 with Luke XVII. 3. Nevertheless, the departure from Galilee again... Vers. 29. My Father who gave to me, is greater than all: and no one is able to snatch from the hand of my Father.

Vers. 30. I and the Father are one.

§. I. The Jews take up stones, that they may stone him: Jesus asking for the cause, they allege blasphemy, because, being a man, he makes himself God.

Vers. 31. The Jews therefore took up stones, that they might stone him.

Vers. 32. Jesus answered them: Many good works I have shown you from my Father, for which of those works do you stone me?

Verse 33. The Jews answered him: For a good work we do not stone you, but for blasphemy: and because you, being a man, make yourself God.

§. III. Jesus teaches that those to whom the word of God was made are also called gods: but that he himself is also the Son of God, sent by the Father into this world, and that he sufficiently proves it by his works.

Verse 34. Jesus answered them: Is it not written in your law: that I said, you are gods?

Verse 35. If he called them gods, to whom the word of GOD was made, and the scripture cannot be broken:

Verse 36. Whom the Father has sanctified, and sent into the world, that it was done in Peraea is clear from Matt. XIX. 1.

§. II. As a great crowd followed him, he preached about following him, having left behind relatives and taken up the cross.

Luke XIV. 25. And great crowds were going with him: and turning, he said to them:

Vers. 26. If anyone comes to me, and does not hate his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and furthermore even his own soul, he cannot be my disciple.

Vers. 27. And whoever does not carry his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

[B. Lyserus in Harmon. ch. CXX thinks that this crowd followed him as he was crossing from his homeland into Judea, but it is more likely that many followed Jesus as he was about to depart from Jerusalem into Peraea, because many there believed in him, John X. 42, who clung to him: For afterwards he came from Galilee finally into Peraea, accompanied by many crowds, Matt. XIX. 1, 2, Mark X. 1.

§. III. Parables about one intending to build a tower calculating the cost; and about a King intending to go to war first establishing a military plan.

Vers. 28. For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expenses that are necessary, to see if he has enough to complete it;

Vers. 29. Lest, after he has laid the foundation, and is not able to complete it, all who see it begin to mock him,

Vers. 30. Saying: That this man began to build, and was not able to finish?

Vers. 31. Or what king, about to go to engage in war against another king, does not sit down first and consider if he can meet with ten thousand him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

Vers. 32. Otherwise, while he is yet far off, sending an embassy, he asks those things that are for peace.

Vers. 33. So therefore every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses, cannot be my disciple.

§. IV. Concerning salt that has become foolish.

Vers. 34. Salt is good. But if the salt shall have lost its flavor, with what shall it be seasoned?

Vers. 35. It is useful neither for the land, nor for the dunghill, but it shall be cast out: He that has ears to hear, let him hear.

CHAPTER XXXVI. The reception of sinners, and its defense through a triple parable.

§. I. Publicans and sinners approach Christ, that they may hear him, at which the Pharisees murmur, because he receives sinners.

Luke XV. 1. And publicans and sinners were drawing near to him, that they might hear him.

Vers. 2. And the Pharisees and Scribes murmured, saying: That this man receives sinners, and eats with them.

§. II. Christ defends this with the parable of the lost sheep, which the shepherd, having left the others in the desert, seeks until he finds it.

Vers. 3. And he spoke this parable to them, saying:

Verse 4. What man of you, who has a hundred sheep: and if he has lost one of them, does he not leave the ninety-nine in the desert, and go after that which was lost, until he finds it?

Verse 5. And when he has found it, he lays it upon his shoulders, rejoicing: Verse 6. And coming home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them: Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep which was lost.

Verse 7. I say to you, that even so there will be joy in heaven over one sinner doing penance, more than over ninety-nine just, who need no penance.

§. III. Likewise the parable of the lost drachma, which the woman seeks.

Verse 8. Or what woman having ten drachmas, if she has lost one drachma, does she not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek diligently, until she finds it?

Verse 9. And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying: Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma which I had lost?

Verse 10. So, I say to you, there will be joy before the angels of GOD over one sinner doing penance.

§. IV. Finally, the parable of the prodigal son, who, led by penance, returns to the Father, and is received with joy.

Verse 11. And he said: A certain man had two sons:

Verse 12. And the younger of them said to his father: Father, give me the portion of substance that falls to me. And he divided unto them his substance.

Verse 13. And not many days after, gathering all together, the younger son went abroad into a far country, and there wasted his substance by living riotously.

Vers. 14. And after he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land, and he began to be in want.

Vers. 15. And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country. And he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

Vers. 16. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

Vers. 17. And when he came to himself, he said: How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

Vers. 18. I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee:

Vers. 19. I am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

Vers. 20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

Vers. 21. And the son said unto him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, I am no more worthy to be called thy son.

Vers. 22. But the father said to his servants: Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

Vers. 23. And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

Vers. 24. For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

Vers. 25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing:

Vers. 26. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

Vers. 27. And he said to him: Thy brother is come, and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe.

Vers. 28. And he was angry, and would not go in. His father therefore coming out, began to entreat him.

Vers. 29. And he answering, said to his father: Behold, for so many years do I serve thee, and I have never transgressed thy commandment, and yet thou hast never given me a kid to make merry with my friends:

Vers. 30. But after this thy son is come, who hath devoured his substance with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.

Vers. 31. But he said to him: Son, thou art always with me, and all I have is thine:

Vers. 32. But it was fit that we should make merry and be glad, for this thy brother was dead, and is come to life again; he was lost, and is found.

CHAPTER XXXVII. Concerning the unjust Steward, and concerning avarice spoken to the disciples.

§. I. Concerning the Steward, who had dissipated his Master's goods, being deposed, preparing friends for himself; with an admonition concerning preparing friends for ourselves who may receive us into everlasting dwellings.

Luke XVI. v. 1. And he said also to his disciples: There was a certain rich man who had a steward: and the same was accused unto him, that he had wasted his goods.

Ver. 2. And he called him, and said to him: What is this I hear about you? Render an account of your stewardship: for now you can no longer be steward.

Ver. 3. But the steward said within himself: What shall I do, because my lord takes away from me the stewardship: I am not able to dig, I am ashamed to beg.

Ver. 4. I know what I will do, so that, when I have been removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

Ver. 5. Therefore, having called together each of his lord's debtors, he said to the first: How much do you owe my lord?

Ver. 6. But he said: A hundred jars of oil. And he said to him: Take your bond: and sit down quickly, write fifty.

Ver. 7. Then he said to another: And you, how much do you owe? Who said: A hundred cors of wheat. He said to him: Take your letters, and write eighty.

Ver. 8. And the lord praised the steward of iniquity, because he had acted prudently: because the children of this world are more prudent than the children of light in their generation.

Ver. 9. And I say to you: make for yourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity: that, when you have failed, they may receive you into eternal tabernacles.

§. II. He who is not faithful in the unrighteous mammon, how will he be faithful in true goods?

Ver. 10. He who is faithful in the least, is faithful also in the greater: and he who is unrighteous in a little, is unrighteous also in the greater.

Ver. 11. If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon: who will entrust to you what is true?

Ver. 12. And if you have not been faithful in that which is another's: who will give you that which is your own?

§. III. No one can serve two masters, God and Mammon.

Vers. 13. No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other: or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve GOD and mammon.

CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Pharisees justify themselves, having rejected the Evangelical doctrine, while others force their way into the kingdom of God. And concerning divorce. And concerning the rich glutton.

§. I. The Pharisees, given to avarice, mock Christ (who was rebuking avarice); Christ reproaches them, because they justify themselves out of pride, which is abominable to God; and although the law and the prophets were to prophesy until John, but from then on the kingdom of God is announced through the Gospel, they reject it, while others take it by a certain force: even though it is certain that not even a dot of the law can perish.

Luke XVI. 14. And the Pharisees, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.

Vers. 15. And he said to them: You are they who justify yourselves before men: but God knows your hearts: for that which is high to men, is an abomination before God.

Vers. 16. The law and the prophets were until John: from that time the kingdom of God is evangelized, and every one uses violence toward it.

Vers. 17. And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than for one dot of the law to fall.

§. II. The Pharisees are warned that through divorce (such as they approved) adultery is committed by him who puts away his wife, and by him who marries her who is put away.

Vers. 18. Everyone who puts away his wife, and marries another, commits adultery: and he who marries her that is put away from her husband, commits adultery.

[Andr. Osiander, Cornel. Jansenius, and others refer to this period what is contained in Matt. XIX. 3. ff. and Mark X. 2: but these things happened at a different time: For what Luke relates here was still done during the previous excursion into Perea made from the Jerusalem Feast of Dedication, John X. 40, from which he later undertook a journey through Samaria and Galilee, Luke XVII. 11. But what Matthew relates happened when, on another excursion through Galilee, he turned aside into Perea, Matt. XIX. 1, after he had already passed through the midst of Samaria, and there had healed ten lepers, Luke XVII. 11, 12, ff., and had carried out those things which Luke reports to have followed there in chapter XVII, for the rest up to verse 15 of chapter XVIII. But as for what Osiander supposes, that Christ did not return to Galilee after the Feast of Dedication, he is entirely mistaken in that: Since Luke explicitly reports that he went to Jerusalem through Samaria and GALILEE, ch. XVII. 11. He came therefore indeed into Samaria, he came also into Galilee on that journey; which Osiander himself in his Harmony acknowledged to have been undertaken after the feast of the Dedication. But Osiander erred most of all in this, that he believed those things which are recounted by Luke from chapter IX. 51 onwards to have happened after the return from the feast of Tabernacles indicated in John VII, nay rather to have occurred on the final journey to Jerusalem, which opinion is manifestly proven to be false from Luke XIII. 22 and Chapter XVII. 11 compared with Luke XVIII. 31, and it produces notable confusion in the Evangelical history. To what Osiander urges, that mention is made of the completion of the days of the ἀναλήψεως of the Lord, Luke IX. 51, I respond that it is not said that the days of the assumption had already been completed, but that this was done ἐν τῷ συμπληρῶσθαι, while they were being fulfilled: because, to wit, that journey was undertaken in the last half-year. Nor indeed could all those things which are reported to have happened in Luke Chapter IX. 51, up to Chapter XVIII, have happened in that short time of the last journey undertaken towards Jerusalem: and Christ from the feast of dedication before the winter solstice, when he was completing the thirty-third year of his age, betook himself to Bethabara, and wintered there for some time.

§. III. The parable of the rich glutton and the needy Lazarus.

Luke XVI. v. 19. There was a certain rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen: and feasted sumptuously every day.

Vers. 20. And there was a certain beggar, named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, full of sores,

Vers. 21. Desiring to be filled with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table; and no one gave to him: but the dogs also came, and licked his sores.

Vers. 22. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the Angels into Abraham's bosom. And the rich man also died, and was buried in hell.

Vers. 23. And lifting up his eyes, when he was in torments, he saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom:

Vers. 24. And he crying out said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, to cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

Vers. 25. And Abraham said to him: Son, remember that thou didst receive good things in thy lifetime, and Lazarus likewise evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

Vers. 26. And in all these things, between us and you there is a great chaos fixed: so that they who wish to pass from hence to you, cannot, nor can they come from thence hither.

Vers. 27. And he said: I beseech thee therefore, father, that thou wouldst send him to my father's house.

Vers. 28. For I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torments.

Vers. 29. And Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets: let them hear them.

Vers. 30. But he said: No, father Abraham: but if someone should go to them from the dead, they will do penance.

Vers. 31. But he said to him: If they do not hear Moses and the prophets; neither will they believe if someone should rise from the dead.

[By which lack of mercy and contempt of Moses and the Prophets is seen to be noted in the Pharisees.]

CHAPTER XXXIX. Concerning scandal, and fraternal forgiveness.

§. I. The disciples are again warned about avoiding scandal.

Luke XVII. 1. And he said to his disciples: It is impossible that scandals should not come: but woe to him through whom they come.

Vers. 2. It is more useful for him if a millstone be placed around his neck, and he be cast into the sea, than that he should scandalize one of these little ones.

§. II. Concerning rebuking a sinning brother, and concerning forgiving the same: as also concerning the degrees of admo-

nition, and concerning the binding and loosing of sins in the Church, to whose prayers GOD assents, Christ is present to the congregation.

Matt. XVIII. v. 15. But if your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.

Ver. 16. But if he does not hear you: take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand.

Ver. 17. And if he does not hear them: tell the church. But if he does not hear the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector.

Ver. 18. Amen I say to you, whatever you bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven: and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven.

Ver. 19. Again I say to you, that if two of you shall agree on earth, concerning any matter whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done for them by my Father, who is in heaven.

Ver. 20. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

Luke XVII. v. 3. Take heed to yourselves: If your brother sins against you, rebuke him: and if he repents, forgive him.

Ver. 4. And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turns back to you, saying: I repent, forgive him.

§. III. To Peter asking how often one must forgive a neighbor, whether it is sufficient to forgive seven times? Christ responds, having recited the parable of the King demanding an account from his servants.

Matth. XVIII. v. 21. Then Peter came to him and said: Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?

Vers. 22. Jesus says to him: I do not say to you up to seven times; but up to seventy times seven.

Vers. 23. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is likened to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.

Vers. 24. And when he had begun to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.

Vers. 25. But since he did not have the means to pay, his master ordered him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

Vers. 26. But that servant falling down, begged him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.

Vers. 27. And the master of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave the debt.

Vers. 28. But that servant going out, found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii: and seizing him, he choked him, saying: Pay what you owe.

Vers. 29. And his fellow servant falling down, begged him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.

Vers. 30. But he would not: but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay the debt.

Vers. 31. But his fellow servants, seeing what was happening, were very saddened: and they came and told their master all that had been done.

Vers. 32. Then his master called him,

And he said to him: Thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all the debt, because thou besoughtest me:

Ver. 33. Shouldst not thou then have had compassion also on thy fellow servant, even as I had compassion on thee?

Ver. 34. And his lord being angry, delivered him to the torturers until he paid all the debt.
