Ver. 35. So also shall my heavenly Father do to you, if you forgive not every one his brother from your hearts.

CHAPTER XL. Concerning the power of faith, and concerning servants doing their duty, yet being unprofitable.

§. I. The Apostles seek the strengthening of faith: to whom he preaches concerning the power of faith, even if it be like a grain of mustard seed.

Luke XVII. v. 5. And the Apostles said to the Lord: Increase our faith.

Ver. 6. And the Lord said: If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this mulberry tree: Be thou rooted up, and be thou transplanted into the sea: and it would obey you.

§. II. Concerning a servant doing his duty, does he deserve anything?

Ver. 7. But which of you having a servant plowing, or feeding cattle, who will say to him, when he is come in from the field: Immediately go, sit down to meat?

Vers. 8. And does he not say to him: Prepare what I may sup, and gird yourself, and serve me, until I eat and drink, and after these things you will eat and drink?

Vers. 9. Does he have gratitude to that servant, because he did what he had commanded him?

Vers. 10. I do not think so. So also you, when you have done all things which have been commanded to you, say: We are unprofitable servants: we have done what we ought to do.

CHAPTER XLI. The healing of the ten lepers.

§. I. Jesus sets out for Jerusalem through Samaria and Galilee.

Luke XVII. v. And it came to pass, as he was going to Jerusalem, he was passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.

[Christ seems to have undertaken this journey around the end of the month of February in the 34th year of his age: for up to this point he remained in Perea, where the preceding sermons and deeds occurred, as we said at ch. XXXVII. And this is finally the last journey to Jerusalem for the σταυρώσιμον Passover, voluntarily undertaken: in which, by passing through Samaria and Galilee, and by departing again from Galilee into Perea, Matt. XIX. 1, he finally instituted some visitation of the churches.]

§. II. Ten lepers met him, whom he heals, and sends to the priests.

Vers. 12. And as he was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met him, who stood afar off;

Vers. 13. And they lifted up their voice, saying: Jesus, master, have mercy on us.

Vers. 14. When he saw them, he said: Go, show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were cleansed.

§. III. One alone, and he a Samaritan, returned and gave glory to GOD.

Vers. 15. And one of them, when he saw that he was cleansed, returned, with a loud voice magnifying GOD.

Vers. 16. And he fell on his face before his feet, giving thanks: and this was a Samaritan.

Vers. 17. And Jesus answering, said: Were not ten cleansed? and where are the nine?

Vers. 18. There is no one found who returned and gave glory to GOD, except this foreigner.

Vers. 19. And he said to him: Arise, go: for thy faith hath made thee whole.

CHAPTER XLII. Concerning the coming of the kingdom of GOD, and the last times.

§. I. To the Pharisees asking when the kingdom of GOD comes, Christ answers that it does not come with observation. Luke XVII. 20. And being asked by the Pharisees: When comes the kingdom of GOD? answering them, he said: The kingdom of GOD comes not with observation.

Vers. 21. Neither shall they say: Behold here, or behold there. For behold the kingdom of GOD is within you.

§. II. But he preaches to the disciples concerning the desire for one day of the Son of man, and concerning the day of his coming being like lightning: that he himself must first suffer, and be rejected. Vers. 22. And he said to his disciples: The days will come when you shall desire to see one day of the Son of man, and you shall not see it.

Vers. 23. And they will say to you: Behold here, and behold there. Do not go, nor follow them.

Vers. 24. For as the lightning flashing under heaven, shines upon those things which are under heaven: so shall the Son of man be in his day.

Vers. 25. But first he must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation.

§. III. The last times are compared to the days of Noah under the flood, and of Lot under the burning of Sodom, with warnings added, that they should hasten, mindful of Lot's wife, and save their soul; since of two lying in a bed, and two grinding together, the one or the other shall be taken, the one or the other shall be left: but where the carcass is, there the gathering of the eagles. Vers. 26. And as it happened in the days of Noah, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.

Vers. 27. They were eating, and drinking: they were marrying wives, and were given to marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark: and the flood came, and destroyed all.

Vers. 28. Likewise as it happened in the days of Lot: They were eating, and drinking: they were buying:

Vers. 29. But on the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed all:

Vers. 30. According to these things shall it be, on the day when the Son of man shall be revealed.

Vers. 31. In that hour, he who shall be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not descend to take them away; and he who is in the field, likewise let him not return back.

Vers. 32. Be mindful of Lot's wife.

Vers. 33. Whosoever shall seek to save his soul, shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose it, shall make it alive.

Vers. 34. I say to you: in that night there shall be two in one bed; one shall be taken, and the other shall be left:

Vers. 35. Two shall be grinding together; one will be taken, and the other will be left: two in the field; one will be taken, and the other will be left.

Verse 36. They answering say to him: where, Lord?

Verse 37. Who said to them: Wheresoever the body shall be, thither will the eagles also be gathered together. [Similar things are found in Matt. 24:27 ff., but the diversity of time sufficiently proves that those discourses are different.]

CHAPTER XLIII. A parable teaching that one ought always to pray.

§. I. Concerning the judge who feared neither God nor men, yet was overcome by a widow through continual supplications.

Luke 18:1. And he spoke also a parable to them, that we ought always to pray, and not to faint,

Verse 2. Saying: There was a judge in a certain city, who feared not God, nor regarded man.

Verse 3. And there was a certain widow in that city, and she came to him, saying: Avenge me of my adversary.

Verse 4. And he would not for a long time. But afterwards he said within himself: Although I fear not God, nor regard man:

Verse 5. Yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest by her coming she weary me.

§. II. How much more will GOD deliver those crying out to him day and night.

Vers. 6. But the Lord says: Hear what the judge of iniquity says:

Vers. 7. And will not GOD bring about justice for his elect who cry to him day and night, and will he have patience with them?

Vers. 8. I tell you that he will quickly bring about justice for them. Nevertheless, when the Son of man comes, do you think he will find faith on the earth?

CHAPTER XLIV. The parable of the Pharisee and the publican.

§. I. When some were justifying themselves, Christ proposed the parable concerning the justification of the publican, relying on the grace of GOD, over the Pharisee, who was boasting of his own works.

Vers. 9. And he also spoke this parable to some who trusted in themselves as if they were just, and despised others.

Vers. 10. Two men went up into the temple to pray: one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

Vers. 11. The Pharisee standing, prayed these things to himself: GOD I give thanks to you, because I am not as the rest of men: extortioners, unjust, adulterers: as also this publican.

Vers. 12. I fast twice in the week: I give tithes of all that I possess.

Vers. 13. And the publican standing afar off, would not so much as lift up his eyes towards heaven: but struck his breast, saying: GOD be merciful to me a sinner.

Vers. 14. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other:

§. II. Axiom concerning the exalting of those who humble themselves, and the humbling of those who exalt themselves.

Vers. 14. For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled: and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

CHAPTER XLV. Christ's fuller instruction concerning divorce.

§. I. Jesus came from Galilee into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan; where a great crowd followed him, and he healed them.

Matth. XIX. 1. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these discourses, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.

Vers. 2. And great crowds followed him, and he cured them there.

Marc. X. 1. And rising from thence he came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan; and the crowds gather to him again: and, as he was accustomed, he taught them again.

§. II. The Pharisees propose a question concerning divorce for the sake of testing him: Christ recalls them to the primordial law of matrimony (Genef. II. 24.)

Matth. XIX. 3. And the Pharisees came to him testing him, and saying: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife, for any cause whatsoever?

Verse 4. Who answering, said to them: Have you not read, that he who made man from the beginning, made them male and female? and said:

Verse 5. For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh.

Verse 6. Therefore now they are not two, but one flesh. What therefore GOD hath joined together, let no man put asunder.

Mark X. 2. And the Pharisees coming to him asked him: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.

Verse 3. But he answering, said to them: What did Moses command you?

Verse 4. Who said: Moses permitted to write a bill of divorce, and to put her away.

Verse 5. To whom Jesus answering, said: Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.

Verse 6. But from the beginning of the creation, GOD made them male and female.

Verse 7. For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife;

Verse 8. And they shall be two in one flesh: therefore now they are not two, but one flesh.

Verse 9. What therefore GOD hath joined together, let no man put asunder.

§. III. The Pharisees reply concerning the bill of divorce: to whom it is answered, that it was only permitted, and that on account of their σκληροκαρδίαν.

Matth. XIX. 7. They say to him: Why then did Moses command to give a bill of divorce, and to put her away?

Vers. 8. He saith to them: Because Moses permitted you to put away your wives because of the hardness of your heart.

Vers. 9. But I say to you, that whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and he that shall marry her that is put away, committeth adultery.

§. IV. The disciples ask privately, and he answers them again: He who separates himself from his spouse, and marries another, is an adulterer.

Marc. X. 10. And in the house again his disciples asked him concerning the same thing.

Vers. 11. And he saith to them: Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.

Vers. 12. And if the wife shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.

§. V. When the disciples replied,

Ver. 10. His disciples say to him: If the case of a man with his wife be so, it is not expedient to marry.

Ver. 11. Who said to them: Not all accept this word, but those to whom it has been given.

Ver. 12. For there are eunuchs, who were so born from their mother's womb: and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven. He that can take it, let him take it.

CHAPTER XLVI.

Jesus wishes little children to be brought to him, and teaches that the kingdom of GOD must be attained in their manner; and to a certain ruler wishing to attain eternal life through works, he proposes the precepts of the law, and advises that he sell all things and give to the poor.

§. I. Little children are brought to Jesus: but the disciples refuse them. Whom, however, Christ commands to be brought to him.

Matth. XIX. v. 13. Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray. And the disciples rebuked them.

Vers. 14. But Jesus said to them: Suffer the little children, and do not forbid them to come to me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 15. And when he had laid hands upon them, he went away from there.

Mark 10:13. And they were bringing little children to him, that he might touch them. But the disciples were rebuking those who brought them.

Verse 14. When Jesus saw them, he was indignant, and said to them: Suffer the little children to come to me, and do not forbid them: for of such is the kingdom of GOD.

Luke 18:15. And they were bringing to him also infants, that he might touch them. Which when the disciples saw, they were rebuking them.

Verse 16. But Jesus calling them together, said: Suffer the children to come to me, and do not forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of God.

§. II. Christ testifies that whoever does not receive the kingdom of GOD as an infant, he does not enter the kingdom of GOD.

Mark 10:15. Amen I say to you: Whoever shall not have received the kingdom of GOD as a little child, shall not enter into it.

Verse 16. And embracing them, and laying his hands upon them, he was blessing them.

Luke 18:17. Amen I say to you: Whoever shall not have received the kingdom of GOD as a child, shall not enter into it.

§. III. A certain very rich ruler asks what he ought to do to inherit eternal life, to whom GOD proposes some of the commandments of the Decalogue, concerning the love of one's neighbor, which when he boasts that he has kept them all, he commands him to sell all his possessions and give to the poor: whereupon he went away sad.

Matt. XIX. 16. And behold, one approaching, said to him: Good Master, what good shall I do, that I may have eternal life?

Ver. 17. Who said to him: Why do you ask me about the good? One is good, GOD. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.

Ver. 18. He says to him: Which? But Jesus said:

You shall not commit murder: You shall not commit adultery: You shall not steal: You shall not bear false witness:

Ver. 19. Honor your father, and your mother: and you shall love your neighbor as yourself.

Ver. 20. The young man says to him: All these I have kept from my youth, what is still lacking to me?

Ver. 21. Jesus says to him: If you wish to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

Ver. 22. But when the young man had heard the word, he went away sad: for he was having many possessions.

Mark X. v. 17. And when he had gone out into the way, a certain one running up, with knee bent before him, asked him: Good Master, what shall I do, that I may receive eternal life?

Vers. 18. But Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one, GOD.

Vers. 19. You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery: Do not kill: Do not steal: Do not bear false witness: Do not defraud: Honor your father and mother.

Vers. 20. But he answering said to him: Master, all these I have observed from my youth.

Vers. 21. But Jesus looking at him, loved him, and said to him: One thing is lacking to you: go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

Vers. 22. Who being saddened at the word, went away sorrowful: for he was one having many possessions.

Luke XVIII. 18. And a certain ruler asked him, saying: Good Master, by doing what shall I possess eternal life?

Vers. 19. But Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good, except God alone.

Vers. 20. You know the commandments: You shall not kill: You shall not commit adultery: You shall not steal: You shall not bear false witness: Honor your father and mother.

Vers. 21. Who said: All these I have kept from my youth.

Vers. 22. Which being heard, Jesus said to him: One thing still is lacking to you: sell all, whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

Vers. 23. Having heard these things, he was saddened: because he was very rich.

§. IV. How difficult it is for a rich man to be saved.

Matt. XIX. v. 23. But Jesus said to his disciples: Amen I say to you, that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 24. And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Ver. 25. And when they heard this, the disciples wondered very much, saying: Who then can be saved?

Ver. 26. And Jesus looking on, said to them: With men this is impossible: but with GOD all things are possible.

Mark X. 23. And Jesus looking round about, saith to his disciples: How hardly shall they that have money enter into the kingdom of GOD!

Ver. 24. And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus again answering, saith to them: Children, how hard is it for them that trust in money to enter into the kingdom of GOD!

Ver. 25. It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 26. Who were more astonished, saying to themselves: And who can be saved?

Vers. 27. And Jesus looking upon them, saith: With men it is impossible, but not with GOD: for all things are possible with GOD.

Luke XVIII. v. 24. And Jesus seeing him become sad, said: How difficultly shall they that have money enter into the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 25. For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 26. And they that heard said: And who can be saved?

Vers. 27. He said to them: The things that are impossible with men, are possible with GOD.

§. V. Peter insists that they have left all things, what they shall have from it? Jesus answers that they themselves shall judge the 12 tribes of Israel; and he teaches concerning the rewards of those who for his sake leave their relatives and their goods: he warns, however, that sometimes the first become the last, and vice versa.

Matt. XIX. 27. Then Peter answering, said to him: Behold we have left all things, and have followed thee: what therefore shall be for us?

Vers. 28. But Jesus said to them: Amen I say to you, that you, who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Vers. 29. And everyone who shall have left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for my name's sake, shall receive a hundredfold, and shall possess eternal life.

Vers. 30. But many that are first shall be last, and the last first.

Mark 10. 28. And Peter began to say to him: Behold, we have left all things, and have followed you.

Vers. 29. Jesus answering, said: Amen I say to you: There is no man who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields, for my sake, and for the gospel's sake,

Vers. 30. Who shall not receive a hundred times as much, now in this time, houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and fields, with persecutions, and in the world to come eternal life.

Vers. 31. But many that are first shall be last, and the last first.

Luke 18. 28. And Peter said: Behold, we have left all things, and have followed you.

Vers. 29. Who said to them: Amen I say to you, there is no man that has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of GOD.

Vers. 30. And shall not receive much more in this time, and in the world to come eternal life.

CHAPTER 47. The parable of the laborers in the vineyard.

§. I. The kingdom of heaven is compared to a householder hiring laborers into his vineyard.

Matt. XX. v. 1. The kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard.

Ver. 2. And when he had agreed with the laborers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

Ver. 3. And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.

Ver. 4. And he said unto them: Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right, I will give you.

Ver. 5. And they went their way. Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour: and did likewise.

Ver. 6. And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing, and saith unto them: Why stand ye here all the day idle?

Ver. 7. They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them: Go ye also into my vineyard.

§. II. The pay is distributed to the laborers from the last to the first, namely to each one. Those murmuring, however, are dismissed with a just response; and it is concluded that the first shall be last, and the last first.

Ver. 8. So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward: Call the laborers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

Vers. 9. When therefore they had come, who had come about the eleventh hour, they received each a denarius.

Vers. 10. But the first coming, they thought that they would receive more: but they also received each a denarius.

Vers. 11. And receiving it, they murmured against the householder.

Vers. 12. Saying: These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day, and the heat.

Vers. 13. But answering one of them, he said: Friend, I do you no injury: did you not agree with me for a denarius?

Vers. 14. Take what is yours, and go: but I wish to give to this last even as to you.

Vers. 15. Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?

Vers. 16. So shall the last be first, and the first last: for many are called, but few are chosen.

SECTION III. HISTORY OF THE LAST PASSOVER OF CHRIST, into which falls the History of the LORD'S PASSION AND THE RESURRECTION THAT FOLLOWED IT.

ARTICLE I. HISTORY OF THE PASSION AND DEATH AND BURIAL OF THE LORD.

TITLE I. Presenting the antecedents.

CHAPTER I. The signification of the lethal sickness of Lazarus.

§. I. Lazarus lies mortally ill in Bethany.

John XI. v. 1. Now a certain man was ill, Lazarus of Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

Ver. 2. (It was Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair: whose brother Lazarus was ill.)

[The more remote antecedents of the fourth and final Passover of Christ are both the resurrection of Lazarus and the consultation of the Priests and Pharisees concerning the killing of Christ. Mary, the sister of Lazarus, is mentioned here by anticipation as the one who had anointed the Lord; which story is finally described in John 12:3 ff. This illness of Lazarus occurred in the month of March of the thirty-fourth year of Christ.]

§. II. Jesus, being summoned by the sisters of Lazarus, says that the illness is not unto death, but for the glory of God: and he remains for two more days: then indeed he says to his disciples, let us set out again into Judea, who dissuade him from it in vain: Thomas at last advises that they follow him.

John 11:3. His sisters therefore sent unto him, saying: Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.

Ver. 4. And Jesus hearing it, said to them: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified by it.

Ver. 5. Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister Mary, and Lazarus.

Ver. 6. When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he remained then indeed in the same place two days.

Ver. 7. Then after this he said to his disciples: Let us go into Judea again.

Ver. 8. The disciples say to him: Rabbi, the Jews now sought to stone thee, and goest thou thither again?

Ver. 9. Jesus answered: Are there not twelve hours of the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world:

Ver. 10. But if he walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.

Ver. 11. These things he said, and after that he said to them: Lazarus our friend sleepeth: but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.

Vers. 12. His disciples therefore said: Lord, if he sleeps, he will be safe.

Vers. 13. But Jesus had spoken of his death: but they thought that he spoke of the rest of sleep.

Vers. 14. Then therefore Jesus said to them plainly: Lazarus is dead.

Vers. 15. And I rejoice for your sakes, that you may believe, that I was not there. But let us go to him.

Vers. 16. Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: Let us also go, that we may die with him.

[Christ was still staying then at Bethabara in Peraea, about the middle of the month of March, at a distance of four miles from Bethany, where Lazarus was lying ill. The messenger came to Christ on Friday, if you listen to Bünting, on the fourteenth day from the death of Christ: he delays for two more days, that is, through the day of Saturday and Sunday; on which day, a little before dawn, Lazarus expired, and was buried around midday. Others designate an earlier time; B. Gerhard in his Harmony, chapter CXLI, establishes that the resurrection of Lazarus preceded the passion of Christ by approximately one month: but the opinion of Bünting seems to approach the Evangelical account more closely.]

CHAPTER II. The prediction of the passion, death, and resurrection of Christ.

§. I. Christ, setting out for Jerusalem, predicts his passion, death, and resurrection.

Matth. XX. 17. And Jesus going up to Jerusalem, took the twelve disciples aside, and said to them:

Vers. 18. Behold we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man shall be betrayed to the chief priests, and to the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,

Vers. 19. And they shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify, and the third day he shall rise again.

Mark 10:32. And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem: and Jesus went before them, and they were amazed: and they that followed were afraid. And taking again the twelve, he began to tell them what things should happen to him.

Vers. 33. For behold we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man shall be betrayed to the chief priests, and to the scribes, and to the ancients, and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles:

Vers. 34. And they shall mock him, and spit on him, and scourge him, and kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

Luke 18:31. And Jesus took unto him the twelve, and said to them: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things shall be accomplished which were written by the prophets concerning the Son of man.

Vers. 32. For he shall be delivered to the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and scourged, and spit upon:

Vers. 33. And after they have scourged him, they will put him to death, and the third day he shall rise again.

[Jansenius, Baronius, Barradius, and others hold that this journey was undertaken from the city of Ephrem towards Bethany, which is near Jerusalem: and therefore they place this prediction, and the petition of the sons of Zebedee, and likewise the healing of the blind men, after the resuscitation of Lazarus; but it is more correctly understood as the journey from Perea into Judea, and of that arrival of Christ in Bethany, which preceded his withdrawal into the desert. For in Perea he received the news about Lazarus, therefore he said in John 11:7: Let us go into Judea again: and so he soon entered upon that journey, having taken his disciples with him: to whom he announces at the same time something more than what he had indicated before: namely, so that they might know that he would not only resuscitate Lazarus, but soon also that he himself would succumb to the ignominious death of the Cross. Therefore, on Monday, which Büntingius makes the 23rd of March and the equinoctial day, he seems to have traveled from Bethabara, at a distance of almost two miles, to the city of Jericho.]

§. II. The disciples understood none of these things.

Vers. 34. And they understood none of these things, and this word was hid from them, and they understood not the things that were said.

The more immediate antecedents of the passion of Christ, which occurred before Holy Week, are noted as six: (1) The prediction of the passion, death, and resurrection of Christ. (2) The petition of the mother of the sons of Zebedee. (3) The healing of the blind men. (4) The conversion of Zacchaeus. (5) The recitation of the parable concerning the ten talents entrusted to the servants. (6) The anointing of Christ by Mary.

However, that prediction seems to have been made on the Friday immediately preceding the Friday of the σταυρώσιμον, when, namely, he was beginning his journey toward Jerusalem.

CHAPTER III. The petition of the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

§. I. The mother of the sons of Zebedee strives to entreat the first seats in the kingdom of Christ for her sons: which the sons themselves, James and John, are also said to have requested.

Matth. XX. 20. Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshipping and asking something of him.

Vers. 21. Who said to her: What do you want? She says to him: Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand, and one at your left, in your kingdom.

Marc. X. 35. And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approach him, saying: Master, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.

Vers. 36. But he said to them: What do you want me to do for you?

Vers. 37. And they said: Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand, and another at your left hand, in your glory.

§. II. Christ asks whether they can drink his cup? When they affirmed this, he responds. That to sit at his right and left is given only to those for whom it has been prepared by the Father.

Matth. XX. 22. But Jesus answering, said: You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup which I am about to drink? They say to him: We can.

Vers. 23. He says to them: You will indeed drink my cup: but to sit at my right hand or left, is not mine to give to you, but to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.

Mark 10:38. But Jesus said to them: You know not what you ask: can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism wherewith I am baptized?

Verse 39. But they said to him: We can. But Jesus said to them: You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink; and with the baptism wherewith I am baptized, you shall be baptized:

Verse 40. But to sit on my right hand, or on my left, is not mine to give to you, but to them for whom it is prepared.

§. III. The other disciples being indignant, Christ warns that worldly princes rule, but that ministry becomes them: as the Son of man himself came, that he might serve, and give his life a ransom for many.

Matt. 20:24. And the ten hearing it, were moved with indignation against the two brethren.

Verse 25. But Jesus called them to him, and said: You know that the princes of the Gentiles lord it over them; and they that are the greater, exercise power upon them.

Verse 26. It shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be the greater among you, let him be your minister:

Verse 27. And he that will be first among you, shall be your servant.

Verse 28. Even as the son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many.

Mark 10:41. And the ten hearing it, began to be much displeased at James and John.

Vers. 42. But Jesus calling them, saith to them: You know, that they who seem to rule over the Gentiles, lord it over them: and their princes have power over them.

Vers. 43. But it is not so among you, but whosoever will be greater, shall be your minister:

And whosoever will be first among you, shall be the servant of all.

Vers. 45. For the Son of man also is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many.

CHAPTER IV. The healing of the blind man, and the conversion of Zacchaeus.

§. I. Before the entry into Jericho, a certain blind man was healed by the Lord.

Luke XVIII. 35. And it came to pass, when he drew nigh to Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side, begging.

Vers. 36. And when he heard the multitude passing by, he asked what this meant.

Vers. 37. And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.

Vers. 38. And he cried out, saying: Jesus Son of David, have mercy on me.

Vers. 39. And they that went before, rebuked him, that he should hold his peace. But he cried out much more: Son of David, have mercy on me.

Vers. 40. But Jesus standing still ordered him to be brought to him. And when he had come near, he asked him.

Vers. 41. Saying: What do you want me to do for you? But he said: Lord, that I may see.

Vers. 42. And Jesus said to him: Receive your sight, your faith has made you whole.

And immediately he saw, and followed him, glorifying GOD. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to GOD.

[This blind man is expressly said to have been healed upon Christ's entry into Jericho. He must therefore be entirely distinguished from those blind men who were healed by the Lord when he was departing from Jericho, as Matthew and Mark report.]

§. II. Zacchaeus desires to see Jesus from a tree; who orders him to come down, and stays with him in Jericho, and declares that salvation has now come to his house, inasmuch as the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.

Mark X. 46. And they come to Jericho,

Luke XIX. 1. And entering, he was passing through Jericho.

Vers. 2. And behold a man named Zacchaeus: and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich:

Vers. 3. And he sought to see Jesus, who he was: and he could not because of the crowd, because he was small of stature.

Vers. 4. And running ahead he climbed into a sycamore tree, that he might see him: for he was about to pass that way.

Vers. 5. And when he had come to the place, Jesus looking up saw him: and said to him: Zacchaeus, make haste and come down: for today I must stay at your house.

Vers. 6. And making haste he came down, and received him rejoicing.

Vers. 7. And when all saw it, they murmured, saying that he had turned aside to a man who is a sinner.

Vers. 8. But Zacchaeus standing, said to the Lord: Behold, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.

Vers. 9. Jesus said to him: Today salvation has come to this house: because he also is a son of Abraham.

Vers. 10. For the son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost.

[He came therefore to Jericho on Monday: and there he stayed overnight.]

CHAPTER V. The parable concerning the ten talents entrusted to servants.

§. I. When he was nearer to Jerusalem, and the disciples thought that the kingdom of God was now about to be manifested, he proposed the parable of the nobleman departing into a far country to obtain a kingdom, entrusting ten talents to ten servants; whose citizens, however, rejected his rule.

Luke XIX. 11. As they heard these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was near Jerusalem: and because they thought that the kingdom of GOD would immediately be manifested.

Verse 12. He said therefore: A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

Verse 13. And having called his ten servants, he gave them ten minas, and said to them: Trade until I come.

Verse 14. But his citizens hated him: and sent an embassy after him, saying: We will not have this man to reign over us.

§. II. After the kingdom was obtained, he demanded an account of the interest of the talents; to one, who had gained ten talents, he gave ten cities; to another, who had gained five, he gave five cities; from the third, who had gained nothing, he took away the talent, and granted it to the first, with the added epiphonema: To him that hath shall be given, and from him that hath not, shall be taken away even that which he seemeth to have.

Verse 15. And it came to pass, that he returned having received the kingdom: he commanded the servants to be called, to whom he gave the money, that he might know how much each had traded.

Verse 16. And the first came, saying: Lord, thy mina has gained ten minas.

Verse 17. And he said to him: Well done, good servant, because thou hast been faithful in a little, thou shalt have authority over ten cities.

Verse 18. And the other came, saying: Lord, thy mina has made five minas.

Verse 19. And to this one he said: And be thou also over five cities.

Vers. 20. And another came, saying: Lord, behold thy mina, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:

Vers. 21. For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up what thou didst not lay down, and thou reapest what thou didst not sow.

Vers. 22. He saith to him: Out of thy own mouth I judge thee, thou wicked servant: thou knewest that I am an austere man, taking up what I laid not down, and reaping what I did not sow:

Vers. 23. And why didst thou not give my money into the bank, that at my coming, I might have exacted it with usury?

Vers. 24. And he said to them that stood by: Take the mina away from him, and give it to him that hath ten minas.

Vers. 25. And they said to him: Lord, he hath ten minas.

Vers. 26. But I say to you, that to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound: and from him that hath not, even that which he hath shall be taken from him.

§. III. He takes care that his enemies, who refused his rule, be killed, and thus he set out for Jerusalem.

Vers. 27. But as for those my enemies, who would not have me reign over them, bring them hither, and kill them before me.

Vers. 28. And having said these things, he went before, going up to Jerusalem.

CHAPTER VI. The healing of two blind men after the departure from Jericho.

§. I. A great multitude followed Jesus as he was leaving Jericho.

Matth. XX. 29. And as they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him:

Marc. X. 46. And as he was setting out from Jericho, and his disciples, and a very great multitude.

§. II. The son of Timaeus and a certain other blind man, sitting by the way, were healed.

Matth. XX. 30. And behold two blind men sitting by the way, heard that Jesus was passing by: and they cried out, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son of David.

Vers. 31. And the crowd rebuked them, that they should hold their peace. But they cried out the more, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son of David.

Vers. 32. And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said: What will you that I should do to you?

Vers. 33. They say to him: Lord, that our eyes may be opened.

Vers. 34. And Jesus having compassion on them, touched their eyes. And immediately they saw, and followed him.

Marc. X. 46. The son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus the blind man, was sitting by the way begging.

Verse 47. And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me.

Verse 48. And many rebuked him, that he should hold his peace. But he cried the more a great deal: Son of David, have mercy on me.

Verse 49. And Jesus stood still and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him: Be of better comfort: rise, he calleth thee.

Verse 50. And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to him.

Verse 51. And Jesus answered and said unto him: What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him: Rabboni, that I may see.

Verse 52. And Jesus said unto him: Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

He departed from Jericho on Tuesday, intending to go to Bethany, which is distant from there by not quite three miles; and having already left the city, he restored sight to the son of Timaeus, as also to another blind man; concerning whom, let those things be seen which we have said regarding Matthew.

CHAPTER VII. The resuscitation of Lazarus.

§. I. As Christ was coming to Bethany, Lazarus had already lain in the tomb for four days, and many Jews had come there to console his sisters; Martha, meeting Jesus, says: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother would not have died; yet I know that GOD will give thee whatsoever thou askest. Jesus answers: Thy brother shall rise again; and upon her understanding this concerning the resurrection at the last day, Jesus testifies that he is the resurrection and the life, and Martha professes her faith that he is the Christ, the Son of GOD.

John 11:17. Then Jesus came: and he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.

Vers. 18. (Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.)

Vers. 19. Many of the Jews, however, had come to Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.

Vers. 20. Martha, therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him: but Mary sat at home.

Vers. 21. Martha therefore said to Jesus: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died:

Verse 22. But even now I know that whatever you ask of GOD, GOD will give to you.

Verse 23. Jesus says to her: Your brother will rise again.

Verse 24. Martha says to him: I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.

Verse 25. Jesus said to her: I am the resurrection and the life: he who believes in me, even if he has died, will live:

Verse 26. And everyone who lives and believes in me will not die forever. Do you believe this?

Verse 27. She says to him: Yes Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ the Son of the living GOD, who has come into this world. [This happened on Wednesday, namely the sixth day from when Christ had received the news about the lethal illness of Lazarus.] §. II. Mary, called by her sister, hastens to Christ; the Jews follow her; falling at the feet of Jesus, she says: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died; Jesus, seeing everyone weeping, asks where Lazarus has been laid, and having wept himself, subject to the diverse judgments of the Jews, he orders the sepulchral stone to be removed; Martha replying that he already stinks, he says: Did I not tell you, if you believe, you will see the glory of the Lord.

Verse 28. And when she had said these things, she went away and called Mary her sister in silence, saying: The Master is here and is calling you.

Verse 29. As soon as she heard, she rises quickly and comes to him.

Verse 30. For Jesus had not yet come into the village: but was still in that place where Martha had met him.

Verse 31. The Jews therefore, who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose quickly and went out, followed her, saying: Because she is going to the monument to weep there.

Verse 32. Mary therefore, when she had come where Jesus was, seeing him, fell at his feet and says to him: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

Vers. 33. Jesus therefore when he saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, groaned in spirit, and troubled himself.

Vers. 34. And he said: Where have you laid him? They say to him: Lord, come and see.

Vers. 35. And Jesus wept.

Vers. 36. The Jews therefore said: Behold how he loved him.

Vers. 37. But some of them said: Could not he, who opened the eyes of the man born blind, have caused that this man should not die?

Vers. 38. Jesus therefore again groaning in himself, came to the monument; now it was a cave: and a stone was laid over it.

Vers. 39. Jesus saith: Take away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith to him: Lord, by this time he stinketh, for he is now of four days.

Vers. 40. Jesus saith to her: Did I not say to thee, that if thou believe, thou shalt see the glory of GOD?

§. III. The stone having been removed, Jesus giving thanks to GOD for the hearing, cries out, Lazarus come forth, and the dead man came out immediately, whence many of the Jews believed in him, but others reported it to the Pharisees.

Vers. 41. They took therefore the stone: and Jesus lifting up his eyes, said: Father, I give thee thanks, because thou hast heard me.

Vers. 42. And I knew that thou hearest me always, but because of the people who stand about, I said it: that they may believe, that thou hast sent me.

Vers. 43. When he had said these things, he cried out with a loud voice: Lazarus, come forth.

Vers. 44. And he who had been dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes, and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus said to them: Loose him, and let him go.

Vers. 45. Many therefore of the Jews, who had come to Mary and Martha, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in him.

Vers. 46. But some of them went to the Pharisees, and told them what Jesus had done.

CHAPTER VIII. The bloodthirsty council.

§. I. The council convened by the Priests and Pharisees because of the signs of Christ, because they fear that all will believe in Christ, and thus the Romans will take away both the people and the region.

Johan. XI. 47. The chief priests and the Pharisees therefore gathered a council, and said: What are we doing, for this man does many signs?

Vers. 48. If we let him alone so, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come, and take away both our place and nation.

[On the day after the raising of Lazarus, which was Thursday, that council was immediately held, in which the killing of Christ was decreed.]

§. II. The counsel of Caiaphas the High Priest, that it is better that one man should die for the people, than that the whole people should perish. Which Caiaphas prophesied concerning the death of Jesus for the people, and the gathering together of the children of GOD.

Vers. 49. But one of them, Caiaphas by name, being the high priest that year, said to them: You know nothing at all,

Vers. 50. Nor do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.

Verse 51. But he did not say this of himself, but being high priest of that year, he prophesied that Jesus was to die for the nation,

Verse 52. And not only for the nation, but that he might gather together in one the children of GOD that were dispersed.

§. III. From that time they deliberated about the manner of killing Jesus.

Verse 53. From that day therefore they devised to kill him.

CHAPTER IX. The withdrawal of Christ into the small town of Ephrem, and the decree of the Pharisees concerning seeking and apprehending Christ.

§. I. Jesus went away near the desert into the city of Ephraim.

John XI. 54. Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but went away into the region near the desert, into the city which is called Ephrem, and he was staying there with his disciples. (Therefore, on that very day on which the bloody decree against Jesus was made, he withdrew into that city near the desert at an interval of two and a half miles, so that he might avoid the snares of the Jews.) §. II. But with the Passover approaching, and many traveling to it, it was asked about him in the temple, why he does not come to the feast? But the priests and Pharisees published an edict about revealing him, if anyone should know where he is.

Verse 55. Now the Passover of the Jews was near: and many went up to Jerusalem from the region before the Passover, that they might sanctify themselves.

Verse 56. They were seeking Jesus therefore: and they were talking among themselves, standing in the temple: What do you think, that he does not come to the feast day?

Verse 57. Now the chief priests and Pharisees had given a command, that, if anyone should know where he is, he should report it, so that they might apprehend him.

CHAPTER X. Mary's anointing of Jesus in Bethany.

§. I. Jesus is received by guests in Bethany six days before the Passover, with Martha serving him, and Lazarus reclining at the table,

John XII. 1. Jesus therefore six days before the Passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus had been dead, whom Jesus raised.

Verse 2. And they made a supper for him there: and Martha was serving, but Lazarus was one of those reclining with him. [He returned to Bethany from Ephraim at an interval of two and a half miles on Friday, which Büntingius makes March 27th, beginning around evening on the sixth day before the feast of the Passover: and therefore he thinks that the Lord rested in Bethany on March 28th, which was the Sabbath, which was the sixth day before the Passover.] §. II. Mary anoints Jesus, and wipes his anointed feet with her hair. Judas murmurs because of this, but Jesus says it was done for the sake of his burial.

Verse 3. Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of pure nard, precious, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.

Verse 4. Therefore one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was about to betray him, said:

Verse 5. Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii, and given to the poor?

Verse 6. He said this, however, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, he carried what was put into it.

Verse 7. Jesus therefore said: Let her alone, that she may keep it for the day of my burial.

Verse 8. For you always have the poor with you: but you do not always have me. [That this happened in the house of Simon the leper, Matt. XXVI. 6. Mark XIV. 3. report, according to this recollection, relating this history (on the occasion of the described betrayal by Judas, by whom that anointing was blamed).] §. III. A great crowd flocks to Bethany, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus: whence the priests seek to kill Lazarus also.

Verse 9. A great crowd of the Jews therefore learned that he was there: and they came, not for Jesus' sake only, but that they might see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

Verse 10. But the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also:

Verse 11. Because many of the Jews were going away on his account, and were believing in Jesus.

[And all these things happened before the great week, now follow those things which happened in the great week itself: And indeed on the first day of the week, Palm Sunday, as they call it, these things happened; namely, the entry into the city, the casting out of those selling and buying from the temple, and towards evening the departure from the city.

CHAPTER XI.

The reception of Christ about to enter Jerusalem upon a donkey: And his tears as he approaches the city, and his prophecy, and the commotion in the city upon his entry.

§. I. Jesus, approaching Jerusalem, sends disciples from Bethphage to the Mount of Olives: that they might bring him a donkey with its colt from the village; and that was done to fulfill the prophecy of the Prophet (Zech. IX. 9.) Whom they received with a votive exclamation Hosanna, which does not please the Pharisees, but Jesus says: if these should be silent, the stones will cry out; some were saying: you will accomplish nothing, Behold the whole world has gone after him.

Matt. XXI. v. 1. And when they had drawn near to Jerusalem, and had come to Bethphage at the mount of Olives: then Jesus sent two disciples,

Ver. 2. Saying to them: Go into the village, which is over against you, and immediately you shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them to me:

Ver. 3. And if any man shall say anything to you, say, that the Lord has need of them: and immediately he will let them go,

Ver. 4. Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet saying:

Ver. 5. Tell the daughter of Sion: Behold thy king comes to thee meek, sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of her that is used to the yoke.

Ver. 6. And the disciples going, did as Jesus commanded them.

Ver. 7. And they brought the ass and the colt: and laid their garments upon them: and made him sit thereon.

Ver. 8. And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way: and others cut boughs from the trees, and strewed them in the way:

Ver. 9. And the multitudes that went before and that followed, cried, saying: Hosanna to the son of David: blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.

Mark XI. v. 1. And when they were drawing near to Jerusalem and Bethany at the mount of olives, he sends two of his disciples.

Vers. 2. And he saith unto them: Go into the village, which is over against you, and immediately entering into it, you shall find a colt tied, upon which no man yet hath sat: loose him, and bring him.

Vers. 3. And if any man shall say to you: What do you? say that the Lord hath need of him: and straightway he will let him come hither.

Verse 4. And going away they found the colt tied before the door without in the crossway: and they untie him.

Verse 5. And certain of them that stood there said to them: What do you, untying the colt?

Verse 6. Who said to them, as Jesus had commanded them, and they let them go.

Verse 7. And they brought the colt to Jesus: and they lay their garments upon him, and he sat upon him.

Verse 8. And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down boughs from the trees, and strewed them in the way.

Verse 9. And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying: Hosanna:

Verse 10. Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord: Blessed be the kingdom of our father David that cometh: Hosanna in the highest.

Luke 19:29. And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples.

Verse 30. Saying: Go into the town which is over against you: at your entering into which, you shall find the colt of an ass tied, on which no man ever hath sat: loose him, and bring him hither.

Verse 31. And if any man shall ask you: Why do you loose him? you shall say thus to him: Because the Lord hath need of him.

Vers. 32. But they who had been sent went away: and they found the colt standing, as he had told them.

Vers. 33. And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: Why are you untying the colt?

Vers. 34. But they said: Because the Lord has need of it.

Vers. 35. And they led it to Jesus. And casting their garments upon the colt, they set Jesus upon it.

Vers. 36. And as he went, they spread their garments in the way.

Vers. 37. And when he was now drawing near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began rejoicing to praise GOD with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,

Vers. 38. Saying: Blessed is he who comes as king in the name of the Lord, peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.

Vers. 39. And some of the Pharisees from the crowds said to him: Master, rebuke your disciples.

Vers. 40. To whom he said: I tell you that if these keep silent, the stones will cry out.

Johan. XII. v. 12. On the next day, a great crowd that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem:

Vers. 13. They took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried out: Hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel.

Vers. 14. And Jesus found a young donkey, and sat upon it, as it is written.

Vers. 15. Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt.

These things his disciples understood not at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.

Vers. 17. The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.

Vers. 18. For this cause the people also met him:

for that they heard that he had done this miracle.

Vers. 19. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.

§. II. When he was nearer to the city, he wept over it, and foretells its siege and devastation.

Luke 19. v. 41. And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it, saying:

Vers. 42. If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

Vers. 43. For the days shall come upon thee, and thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and shall compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side.

Vers. 44. And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

§. III. When he was entering Jerusalem, the whole city was moved: but the people were saying: This is Jesus the Prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.

Matth. XXI. v. 10. And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?

Vers. 11. And the multitudes said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.

CHAPTER XII.

The reformation of the temple, and the miraculous healing in the temple.

§. I. Jesus entered the temple and cast out those who sold and bought, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and said: It is written (Isaiah LVI. 7.) My house is the house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves (Jeremiah VII. 11.) and he taught daily in the temple, but the priests and the scribes sought to kill him, but the people clung to him.

Matth. XXI. v. 12. And Jesus went into the temple of GOD, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,

Vers. 13. And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

Mark XI. v. 11. And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple:

And entering into the temple, he began to cast out those selling in it, and those buying,

Verse 46. Saying to them: It is written: That my house is a house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.

Verse 47. And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes, and the leaders of the people were seeking to destroy him.

Verse 48. And they were not finding what they might do to him. For all the people were hanging on him, listening.

§. II. The blind and the lame came to him, and he healed them, and the priests and the experts in the law were seeing the miracles which he was performing.

Matthew 21:14. And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple: and he healed them.

Verse 15. But the chief priests and the scribes, seeing the wonderful things which he did.

CHAPTER XIII. The acclamation of the boys, and the address to the Greeks: and a voice from heaven, with information added by Christ.

§. I. The boys in the temple cry out Hosanna to the Son of David, whom he defends against the priests and the experts in the law (from Psalm VIII. 3.)

Matt. XXI. v. 15. And the boys crying out in the temple, and saying: Hosanna to the son of David: they were indignant,

Ver. 16. And they said to him: Do you hear what these are saying? But Jesus said to them: Have you never read: That out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you have perfected praise?

§. II. To the Greeks desiring to see Jesus, and indicating this to Philip and Andrew, Jesus preaches about the time of the glorification of the Son of man, and about a grain of wheat, when it has died in the earth, bearing fruit.

John XII. v. 20. Now there were certain Gentiles among those who had come up to worship at the feast day.

Ver. 21. These therefore approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: Sir, we wish to see Jesus.

Ver. 22. Philip comes and tells Andrew: Andrew again and Philip told Jesus.

Ver. 23. But Jesus answered them, saying: The hour has come that the Son of man should be glorified.

Ver. 24. Amen, amen I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falling into the ground, shall have died;

Verse 25. It remains alone. But if it shall have died, it brings forth much fruit. He who loves his soul will lose it: and he who hates his soul in this world, keeps it unto eternal life.

Verse 26. If anyone serves me, let him follow me: and where I am, there also my servant will be. If anyone shall have served me, my Father will honor him.

§. III. As Jesus is praying, a voice is heard publicly from heaven concerning the glorification of the divine name. Which he says was made for the sake of the people.

Verse 27. Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause I came into this hour.

Verse 28. Father, glorify thy name. There came therefore a voice from heaven: I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.

Verse 29. The crowd therefore, which stood and had heard, was saying that it had thundered. Others were saying: An angel has spoken to him.

Verse 30. Jesus answered and said: This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.

§. IV. Furthermore, Jesus preaches concerning the judgment of the world, and the casting out of the prince of the world, and the drawing of all men to himself when the Son of man shall have been lifted up from the earth: and when the people object that Christ remains forever according to the law (Psalm 110:5), and thus ask who that Son of man is, he warns that they must believe in the light as long as they still have it.

Verse 31. Now is the judgment of the world: now the prince of the world will be cast out.

Verse 32. And I, if I shall have been lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.

Verse 33. (but he was saying this, signifying by what death he was about to die.)

Verse 34. The crowd answered him: We have heard from the law that Christ remains forever: and how do you say: The Son of man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of man?

Verse 35. Jesus therefore said to him: Yet a little while the light is in you. Walk while you have the light, that darkness may not overtake you: and he who walks in darkness does not know where he is going.

Verse 36. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be sons of light. Jesus spoke these things: and he went away, and hid himself from them.

§. V. Although he performed miracles before them, yet they did not believe in him: that the saying of Isaiah (ch. LIII. 1. & ch. VI. 9.) might be fulfilled, who, having seen his glory, spoke of him: yet many of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him.

Verse 37. But though he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him.

Verse 38. That the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he said: Lord, who has believed our report? and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?

Verse 39. Therefore they could not believe, because Isaiah said again.

Verse 40. He has blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart: that they may see with their eyes, and not understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.

Verse 41. Isaiah said these things, when he saw his glory, and spoke of him.

Verse 42. Nevertheless, even among the rulers many believed in him: but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, that they might not be cast out of the synagogue.

Verse 43. For they loved the glory of men more than the glory of GOD.

§. VI. Jesus cried out, and said, he who believes in me, believes in him who sent me: I have come as a light into the world, that he who believes in me, may not remain in darkness. He who does not believe, the word which I have spoken will judge him.

Vers. 44. Jesus however cried out, and said: He who believes in me, does not believe in me, but in him who sent me.

Vers. 45. And he who sees me, sees him who sent me.

Vers. 46. I have come as a light into the world: that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.

Vers. 47. And if anyone hears my words, and does not keep them: I do not judge him: for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.

Vers. 48. He who rejects me, and does not receive my words: has one who judges him; the word which I have spoken, that will judge him on the last day.

Vers. 49. Because I have not spoken on my own authority, but the Father who sent me, he himself gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.

Vers. 50. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore, what I speak, just as the Father has told me, so I speak.

§. VII. Having left them, in the evening he betook himself to Bethany.

Matth. XXI. v. 17. And having left them, he went out of the city into Bethany: and he stayed there.

Marc. XI. v. 11. And when he had looked around at everything, as it was already evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

(And these things for Palm Sunday. Now follow those which were done on the day after Palm Sunday, or on Monday.)

CHAPTER XIV. The cursing of the fig tree, and the new reformation of the temple.

§. I. Upon entering the city in the morning, being hungry, seeking fruit on a fig tree, he found none.

Matt. XXI. v. 18. And in the morning returning into the city, he hungered.

Ver. 19. And seeing one fig tree by the way, he came to it: and found nothing in it but leaves only.

Mark XI. v. 12. And the next day when they came out from Bethany, he hungered.

Ver. 13. And when he had seen afar off a fig tree having leaves, he came, if haply he might find any thing thereon; and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves: for it was not the time of figs.

§. II. He curses the fig tree: which immediately withered.

Matt. XXI. v. 19. And he saith to it: May fruit never grow from thee for ever. And the fig tree was withered away immediately.

Mark 11:14. And answering he said to it: May no one ever eat fruit from you anymore. And his disciples heard it.

§. III. Coming to Jerusalem, having entered the temple, he cast out those buying and selling: nor did he permit that anything be carried through the temple; and he said, is it not written: My house is a house of prayer (Isa. 56:7) but you have made it a den of thieves (Jer. 7:11)

Verse 15. And they come to Jerusalem. And when he had entered into the temple, he began to cast out those selling and buying in the temple: and he overturned the tables of the money-changers, and the chairs of those selling doves.

Verse 16. And he did not allow that anyone should carry a vessel through the temple:

Verse 17. And he was teaching, saying to them: Is it not written: That my house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations: But you have made it a den of thieves.

§. IV. When these things were reported to the lawyers and priests, they were seeking how they might kill him: but they were afraid because of the people.

Verse 18. Which being heard, the chief priests and scribes were seeking how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because the whole crowd was marveling at his teaching.

§. V. In the evening he went out of the city again.

Verse 19. And when evening had come, he was going out of the city.

[And these things have been recounted, which were done on Monday: furthermore follow those things which happened on Tuesday.]

CHAPTER XV. A sermon held on the occasion of the withered fig tree being seen.

§. I. In the morning as they were entering the city again, the disciples marvel that the fig tree had withered so quickly, and Peter asks about it.

Matt. XXI. v. 20. And the disciples seeing it, wondered, saying: How is it presently withered?

Mark XI. v. 20. And when they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.

Ver. 21. And Peter remembering, said to him: Rabbi, behold the fig tree, which thou didst curse, is withered away.

§. II. Jesus preaches about the power of faith, to move the mountains themselves, and the efficacy of prayers, and about forgiving one's neighbor when we pray.

Matt. XXI. v. 21. And Jesus answering, said to them: Amen I say to you, if you shall have faith, and stagger not, not only this of the fig tree shall you do, but also if you shall say to this mountain, take up, and cast thyself into the sea, it shall be done.

Ver. 22. And all things whatsoever you shall ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive.

Mark XI. v. 22. And Jesus answering saith to them: Have the faith of GOD.

Vers. 23. Amen I say to you, that whosoever shall say to this mountain: Be thou removed and be cast into the sea; and shall not stagger in his heart, but shall believe that whatsoever he saith shall be done, it shall be done for him.

Vers. 24. Therefore I say to you, all things, whatsoever you ask when you pray, believe that you shall receive, and they shall come unto you.

Vers. 25. And when you shall stand to pray, forgive, if you have anything against any man: that your Father also, who is in heaven, may forgive you your sins.

Vers. 26. But if you will not forgive: neither will your Father, who is in heaven, forgive you your sins.

CHAPTER XVI. A conversation with the priests, lawyers, and elders of the people, concerning the authority of teaching: and a parable spoken against them.

§. I. When he was teaching in the temple, they asked by what power he did this? But Jesus in turn asks, whence was the baptism of John? Matth. XXI. v. 23. And when he was come into the temple, there came to him as he was teaching, the chief priests and ancients of the people, saying: By what authority dost thou these things? And who hath given thee this authority?

Vers. 24. And Jesus answering, said to them: I will also ask you one word, which if you shall tell me, I will also tell you by what authority I do these things.

Vers. 25. The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or from men? But they thought within themselves, saying:

Vers. 26. If we shall say, from heaven, he will say to us: Why then did you not believe him? But if we shall say, from men, we are afraid of the people: for all held John as a prophet.

Vers. 27. And answering Jesus, they said: We know not. And he said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

Marc. XI. v. 27. And they come again to Jerusalem. And when he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests and the scribes and the ancients.

Verse 28. And they say to him: In what power do you do these things? And who gave you this power, that you should do these things?

Verse 29. But Jesus answering, said to them: I will also ask you one word, and answer me: and I will tell you, in what power I do these things.

Verse 30. The baptism of John was from heaven, or from men? Answer me.

Verse 31. But they thought within themselves, saying: If we say, from heaven, he will say: Why then did you not believe him?

Verse 32. If we say, from men, we fear the people, for all held John, that he was a prophet indeed.

Verse 33. And answering they say to Jesus: We do not know. And Jesus answering says to them: Neither do I tell you, in what power I do these things.

Luke XX. v. 1. And it came to pass on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple, and preaching the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came together with the elders,

Vers. 2. And they say, speaking to him: Tell us, by what authority dost thou these things? Or, who is he that hath given thee this authority?

Vers. 3. But Jesus answering, said to them: I will also ask you one word. Answer me:

Vers. 4. The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?

Vers. 5. But they thought within themselves, saying: Because if we say, from heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him?

Vers. 6. But if we say, of men, the whole people will stone us: for they are certain that John is a prophet.

Vers. 7. And they answered, that they knew not whence it was.

Vers. 8. And Jesus said to them: Neither do I tell you, by what authority I do these things.

§. II. The parable of the two sons sent into the vineyard.

Matt. XXI. v. 28. But what think you? A certain man had two sons, and coming to the first, he said: Son, go today, work in my vineyard.

Vers. 29. But he answering, said: I will not. And afterwards, moved by repentance, he went.

Vers. 30. And coming to the other, he said in like manner. And he answering, said: I go, sir, and he went not.

Vers. 31. Which of the two did the will of the father? They say to him: The first. Jesus saith to them: Amen I say to you, that the publicans and the harlots shall go into the kingdom of GOD before you.

Vers. 32. For John came to you in the way of justice, and you did not believe him: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: but you, seeing it, did not even have repentance afterwards, that you might believe him.

§. III. The parable concerning the vineyard let out, and servants sent to bring the fruits, but treated badly, and finally the son sent, but killed: Jesus asks what the Lord of the vineyard will do to them? And when they answered that he would miserably destroy those wicked men and let out the vineyard to others, he applies it (from Psalm CXVIII. 22) and teaches that the kingdom of GOD will be taken from the Jews and delivered to the Gentiles. Understanding that this was said against them, they sought how they might apprehend him, but they feared the people, who acknowledged him as a Prophet.

Vers. 33. Hear another parable: There was a man, a householder, who planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it, and dug in it a winepress, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a strange country.

Vers. 34. And when the time of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen that they might receive the fruits thereof.

Vers. 35. And the husbandmen, having laid hands on his servants, beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.

Vers. 36. Again he sent other servants more than the former, and they did to them in like manner.

Vers. 37. And last of all he sent to them his son, saying: They will reverence my son.

Vers. 38. But the husbandmen seeing the son, said among themselves: This is the heir, come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.

Vers. 39. And having seized him, they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him.

Vers. 40. When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do to those husbandmen?

Vers. 41. They say to him: He will bring those evil men to an evil end; and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen, that shall render him the fruit in due seasons.

Vers. 42. Jesus saith to them: Have you never read in the scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner? By the Lord this has been done, and it is wonderful in our eyes?

Vers. 43. Therefore I say to you, that the kingdom of GOD shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof.

Vers. 44. And whosoever shall fall upon this stone, shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder.

Vers. 45. And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they knew that he spoke of them.

Vers. 46. And seeking to lay hands on him, they feared the multitudes: because they held him as a prophet.

Mark XII. v. 1. And he began to speak to them in parables: A certain man planted a vineyard, and made a hedge about it, and dug a place for the wine fat, and built a tower, and let it to husbandmen, and went into a far country.

Vers. 2. And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive of the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.

Vers. 3. Who having laid hands on him, beat him, and sent him away empty.

Vers. 4. And again he sent to them another servant: and him they wounded in the head, and treated with insults.

Vers. 5. And again he sent another, and him they killed: and many others: some beating, others indeed killing.

Vers. 6. Therefore still having one most beloved son: him also he sent to them last, saying: Because they will reverence my son.

Vers. 7. But the husbandmen said to one another: This is the heir: come, let us kill him: and the inheritance shall be ours.

Vers. 8. And laying hold of him, they killed him: and cast him out of the vineyard.

Vers. 9. What therefore will the Lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the husbandmen: and will give the vineyard to others.

Vers. 10. Have you not read this scripture: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is made the head of the corner.

Vers. 11. By the Lord hath this been done, and it is wonderful in our eyes?

Vers. 12. And they sought to lay hold on him: and they feared the people, for they knew that he spoke this parable to them. And leaving him, they went their way.

Luke XX. v. 9. And he began to speak to the people this parable: A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it out to husbandmen: and he was abroad for a long time.

Vers. 10. And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard. Who beating him, sent him away empty.

Ver. 11. And he proceeded to send another servant: but they, beating him also and treating him with contumely, sent him away empty.

Ver. 12. And he proceeded to send a third: who also, wounding him, cast him out.

Ver. 13. But the lord of the vineyard said: What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: perhaps, when they see him, they will reverence him.

Verse 14. When the tenants saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying: This is the heir; let us kill him, that the inheritance may become ours.

Verse 15. And they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?

Verse 16. He will come and destroy those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others. Which when they heard, they said: God forbid.

Verse 17. But he looking on them, said: What is this then that is written: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?

Verse 18. Whosoever shall fall upon that stone, shall be bruised: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

Verse 19. And the chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him the same hour: but they feared the people: for they knew that he spoke this parable to them.

§. IV. The parable concerning the marriage of the King, and the servants sent out being despised and killed, and the slaughter of those murderers, and the invitation of other guests: the casting out of the hypocrite destitute of a wedding garment.

Matt. 22:1. And Jesus answering, spoke again in parables to them, saying:

Verse 2. The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king, who made a marriage for his son.

Verse 3. And he sent his servants to call them that were invited to the marriage, and they would not come.

Vers. 4. Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those who were invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the wedding.

Vers. 5. But they neglected it: and went away, one to his farm, another indeed to his business:

Vers. 6. But the rest laid hold of his servants, and having treated them with contumely, killed them.

Vers. 7. But when the king had heard, he was angry: and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

Vers. 8. Then he saith to his servants: The wedding indeed is ready, but they that were invited, were not worthy.

Vers. 9. Go ye therefore into the highways, and whosoever you shall find, call to the wedding.

Vers. 10. And his servants going forth into the ways, gathered together all that they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was filled with guests.
