Vers. 11. And the king went in to see the guests, and he saw there a man who had not on a wedding garment.

Vers. 12. And he saith to him: Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? But he was silent.

Vers. 13. Then the king said to the ministers: Having bound his hands and feet, cast him into the exterior darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

Vers. 14. For many are called, but few are chosen.

CHAPTER XVII. The Pharisees' questioning about paying tribute to Caesar. §. I. The Pharisees hold a council about ensnaring Christ in his speech.

Matt. XXII. v. 15. Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk

§. II. They send disciples with the ministers of Herod, and ask, whether tribute should be given to Caesar? Jesus demands a coin, and asking about the inscription, warns that the things which are Caesar's should be given to Caesar, and the things which are God's, to God. Marveling at this answer, they leave Jesus.

Vers. 16. And they send unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying: Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man: for thou regardest not the person of men:

Vers. 17. Tell us therefore, what thinkest thou, is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?

Vers. 18. But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said: Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?

Vers. 19. Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.

Vers. 20. And Jesus saith unto them: Whose is this image, and superscription?

Vers. 21. They say unto him: Caesar's. Then saith he unto them: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.

Vers. 22. And when they had heard these words, they marveled, and left him, and went their way.

Mark 12:13. And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they might catch him in his words.

Ver. 14. Who when they were come, say unto him: Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of GOD in truth, is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or shall we not give?

Ver. 15. But he, knowing their craftiness, said unto them: Why tempt ye me? Bring me a penny, that I may see it.

Ver. 16. And they brought it. And he saith unto them: Whose is this image, and superscription? They say unto him: Caesar's.

Ver. 17. And Jesus answering said unto them: Render therefore unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and unto GOD the things that are GOD's. And they marvelled at him.

Luke 20:20. And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.

Ver. 21. And they asked him, saying: Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly: and acceptest not the person of any, but teachest the way of GOD in truth:

Ver. 22. Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?

Ver. 23. But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them: Why tempt ye me?

Ver. 24. Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said: Caesar's.

Ver. 25. And he said unto them: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto GOD the things which be GOD's.

Vers. 26. And they could not reprehend his word before the people: and marveling at his answer, they held their peace.

CHAPTER XVIII.

The temptation of the Sadducees concerning the resurrection.

§. I. On the same day the Sadducees approach Jesus, and raise a question from Moses concerning the wife of the seven brothers, whose wife she shall be in the resurrection?

Matt. XXII. v. 23. On that day the Sadducees came to him, who say there is no resurrection: and they asked him,

Ver. 24. Saying: Master, Moses said: If anyone shall have died not having a son, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.

Ver. 25. Now there were with us seven brothers: and the first, having taken a wife, died: and not having seed, left his wife to his brother.

Ver. 26. In like manner the second, and the third, even to the seventh.

Ver. 27. And last of all the woman also died.

Ver. 28. In the resurrection therefore whose wife shall she be of the seven? for all had her.

Mark XII. v. 18. And the Sadducees came to him, who say there is no resurrection: and they asked him saying:

Ver. 19. Master, Moses wrote for us, that, if anyone's brother shall have died, and left a wife, and shall not have left children, his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.

Ver. 20. There were therefore seven brothers: and the first took a wife, and died not having left seed.

Ver. 21. And the second took her, and died: and neither did this one leave seed. And the third in like manner.

Vers. 22. And the seven took her in like manner: and left no seed. Last of all the woman also died.

Vers. 23. In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise again, whose wife of them shall she be? for seven had her to wife.

Luke XX. v. 27. And there came to him some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection, and they asked him,

Vers. 28. Saying: Master, Moses wrote unto us: If any man's brother die, having a wife, and he leave no children, that his brother should take her to wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

Vers. 29. There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.

Vers. 30. And the next took her, and he also died without a son.

Vers. 31. And the third took her. And in like manner all seven, and they left no seed, and died.

Vers. 32. Last of all the woman also died.

Vers. 33. In the resurrection therefore, whose wife of them shall she be? for seven had her to wife.

§. II. Jesus teaches that in the resurrection there will be no place for marriage, but that we shall be like the angels.

Matt. 22:29. Jesus answering, said to them: You err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of GOD:

Ver. 30. For in the resurrection, they shall neither marry, nor be married: but shall be as the angels of GOD in heaven.

Mark 12:24. And Jesus answering, said to them: Do you not therefore err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of GOD?

Ver. 25. For when they shall rise again from the dead, they shall neither marry, nor be married, but are as the angels in heaven.

Ver. 34. And Jesus said to them: The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:

Ver. 35. But they that shall be accounted worthy of that world, and of the resurrection from the dead, shall neither marry, nor take wives:

Ver. 36. Neither can they die any more: for they are equal to the angels, and are the children of GOD, being the children of the resurrection.

§. III. Jesus convinces them from Moses concerning the resurrection of the dead (Ex. 3:6) with the astonishment of the people.

Matt. 22:31. But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that which was spoken by GOD saying to you:

Vers. 32. I am the GOD of Abraham, and the GOD of Isaac, and the GOD of Jacob? He is not the GOD of the dead, but of the living.

Vers. 33. And the crowds hearing, were amazed at his doctrine.

Mark XII. v. 26. But concerning the dead, that they rise again, have you not read in the book of Moses, how God spoke to him at the bush, saying: I am the GOD of Abraham, and the GOD of Isaac, and the GOD of Jacob?

Vers. 27. He is not the GOD of the dead, but of the living. You therefore do greatly err.

Luke XX. v. 37. But that the dead rise again, Moses also showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord, the GOD of Abraham, and the GOD of Isaac, and the GOD of Jacob.

Vers. 38. But God is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.

Vers. 39. And some of the scribes answering, said to him: Master, thou hast said well.

CHAPTER XIX. The temptation of the lawyers concerning the greatest commandment, and their confusion concerning the Messiah, the son of David.

§. I. The Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered together and sent forth lawyers: of whom one, tempting him, asks about the chief commandment: Christ proposes the sum of the law according to the first and second table.

Matthew XXII. v. 34. But the Pharisees hearing that he had put the Sadducees to silence, came together:

Ver. 35. And one of them, a doctor of the law, asked him, tempting him.

Ver. 36. Master, which is the great commandment in the law.

Ver. 37. Jesus said to him: Thou shalt love the Lord thy GOD with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind.

Ver. 38. This is the greatest and the first commandment.

Ver. 39. And the second is like to this: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

Ver. 40. On these two commandments dependeth the whole law, and the prophets.

Mark XII. v. 28. And one of the scribes came, and heard them reasoning together, and seeing that he had answered them well, asked him which was the first commandment of all.

Ver. 29. And Jesus answered him: For the first commandment of all is: Hear, O Israel: the Lord thy GOD is one GOD:

Ver. 30. And thou shalt love the Lord thy GOD with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind, and with all thy strength. This is the first commandment. Ver. 31. And the second is like it: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. There is no other commandment greater than these.

Ver. 32. And the scribe said to him: Well, Master, you have spoken in truth, that there is one GOD, and there is no other besides him.

Ver. 33. And that he be loved with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength: and to love one's neighbor as oneself is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.

Ver. 34. And Jesus, seeing that he had answered wisely, said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one dared to question him anymore.

Luke 20:40. And they dared not question him anything anymore.

§. II. When the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asks about Christ, whose son he is? When they answer, David's, he raises a doubt, why David calls him his Lord, (Ps. 110:1) at which they were silenced, nor did they dare to question him anymore.

Matt. 22:41. And when the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them, Ver. 42. Saying: What do you think about Christ? Whose son is he? They say to him: David's.

Ver. 43. He says to them: How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying:

Ver. 44. The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.

Verse 45. If therefore David calls him Lord, how is he his son?

Verse 46. And no one was able to answer him a word; nor did anyone dare from that day to question him any more.

Mark XII. v. 35. And Jesus answering said, teaching in the temple: How do the scribes say that Christ is the son of David?

Verse 36. For David himself says in the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.

Verse 37. David therefore himself calls him Lord, and whence is he his son? And a great crowd heard him gladly.

Luke XX. v. 41. But he said to them: How do they say that Christ is the son of David? Verse 42. And David himself says in the book of Psalms: The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand,

Verse 43. Until I make your enemies your footstool?

Verse 44. David therefore calls him Lord: and how is he his son?

CHAPTER XX. Concerning the Pharisees to be heard, not to be imitated. A threefold woe spoken to the Pharisees and lawyers: with a repeated complaint, that they were unwilling to be gathered.

§. I. Jesus said to the people and the disciples: The lawyers and the Pharisees sit in the chair of Moses, all things, whatever they shall say to you, observe, but do not do according to their works. They say, they do not.

Matt. XXIII. v. 1. Then Jesus spoke to the crowds, and to his disciples, Vers. 2. Saying: The scribes and Pharisees have sat on the chair of Moses.

Vers. 3. All things therefore, whatsoever they shall say to you, observe, and do: but according to their works do not: for they say, and do not.

§. II. Concerning their heavy burdens, which they themselves do not touch with a finger.

Vers. 4. For they bind heavy and insupportable burdens, and lay them on men's shoulders; but with a finger of their own they will not move them.

§. III. Concerning their hypocrisy in their works, as also in their phylacteries.

Vers. 5. And all their works they do for to be seen of men: for they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge their fringes.

§. IV. Concerning pride: that they covet the highest place, to be honored in the marketplace, and wish to be called Rabbi: whereas yet there is only one Master, Christ; and one Father in heaven: and those who humble themselves are to be exalted.

Vers. 6. And they love the first places at feasts, and the first chairs in the synagogues,

Vers. 7. And greetings in the marketplace, and to be called by men Rabbi.

Vers. 8. But be not you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, and all you are brethren.

Vers. 9. And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your father, who is in heaven.

Vers. 10. Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, Christ.

He that is the greatest among you, shall be your servant.

And whosoever shall exalt himself, shall be humbled: and he that shall humble himself, shall be exalted.

Mark 12. v. 38. And he said to them in his doctrine: Beware of the scribes, who love to walk in long robes, and to be saluted in the marketplace,

Vers. 39. And to sit in the first chairs in the synagogues, and to have the highest places at suppers.

Luke 20. v. 45. And all the people hearing, he said to his disciples:

Vers. 46. Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love salutations in the marketplace, and the first chairs in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts.

§. V. Woe to those hypocrites, who shut the kingdom of heaven against men, and they themselves do not enter.

Matt. 23:13. But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you shut the kingdom of heaven before men, for you do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to enter.

§. VI. Woe to hypocrites devouring the houses of widows, and pretending prayers.

Verse 14. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you eat the houses of widows, praying long prayers: for this you shall receive greater judgment.

Mark 12:40. Who devour the houses of widows under the pretext of long prayer: these shall receive greater judgment.

Luke 20:47. Who devour the houses of widows, feigning long prayer. These shall receive greater condemnation.

§. VII. Woe to hypocrites, going about sea and dry land to make a proselyte, and making him a son of hell.

Matt. 23:15. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because you go about sea and dry land to make one proselyte: and when he has been made, you make him a son of hell twofold more than yourselves,

§. VIII.

§. VIII. Woe to blind guides, teaching that an oath by the temple and altar is nothing, but that those are liable who swear by the gold of the temple and the gift on the temple.

Vers. 16. Woe to you blind guides, who say: Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing: but he that shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.

Vers. 17. Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?

Vers. 18. And whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing: but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor.

Vers. 19. Ye blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?

Vers. 20. He therefore that sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things which are upon it.

Vers. 21. And whosoever shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein:

Vers. 22. And he that sweareth by heaven, sweareth by the throne of GOD, and by him that sitteth thereon.

§. IX. Woe to hypocrites tithing mint, and leaving the weightier things of the law, straining out a gnat, and swallowing a camel.

Vers. 23. Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees hypocrites: who tithe mint, and anise, and cummin, and have left the weightier things of the law, judgment, and mercy, and faith, these things you ought to have done, and not to leave those undone.

Vers. 24. Blind guides, who strain out a gnat, but swallow a camel.

§. X. Woe to hypocrites cleansing platters on the outside, even if on the inside they are full of rapine and uncleanness.

Vers. 25. Woe to you Scribes and Pharisees hypocrites, because you cleanse that which is on the outside of the cup and the dish: but within you are full of rapine and uncleanness.

Vers. 26. Blind Pharisee cleanse, cleanse first that which is within the cup and the dish, that that which is on the outside may become clean.

§. XI. Woe to hypocrites like unto whited sepulchres.

Vers. 27. Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees hypocrites: because you are like to whited sepulchres, which from without appear to men beautiful, but within are full of dead men's bones and all filthiness.

Vers. 28: So you also outwardly indeed appear to men just: but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy, and iniquity.

§. XII. Woe to hypocrites adorning the sepulchres of the Prophets and the just, sons of the Prophets, filling the measure of their Fathers: because those whom Christ will send, Prophets, Wise men and Scribes, they will kill and persecute, that there may come upon them all the just blood, from Abel to Zacharias the son of Barachias.

Vers. 29. Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees hypocrites, who build the sepulchres of the prophets, and adorn the monuments of the just,

Vers. 30. And you say: If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets.

Vers. 31. Therefore you are witnesses to yourselves, that you are the sons of them who killed the Prophets.

Vers. 32. And you fill up the measure of your fathers.

Vers. 33. Serpents, generation of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of hell?

Vers. 34. Therefore behold I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes, and some of them you will kill, and

you will crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and will persecute from city to city:

Vers. 35. That upon you may come all the righteous blood, which has been shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, son of Barachias, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.

Vers. 36. Amen I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

§. XIII. Christ complains of Jerusalem, that he wished to gather her children like a hen, but they would not; and he threatens the devastation of the house, and that they shall not see him, until they shall say, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

Vers. 37. Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets, and stone those who are sent to you, how often would I have gathered your children, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not?

Vers. 38. Behold your house will be left to you desolate.

Vers. 39. For I say to you, you will not see me from now on, until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

CHAPTER XXI. The poor widow's rich alms.

§. I. Jesus sees how they were putting gifts into the treasury, but a poor widow put in two mites.

Mark XII. v. 41. And Jesus sitting opposite the treasury, was watching how the crowd was casting money into the treasury, and many rich people were casting in much.

Verse 42. And when one poor widow had come, she cast in two mites, which is a farthing,

Luke 21:1. And looking up, he saw them that cast their gifts into the treasury, the rich.

Verse 2. And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in two mites.

§. II. Having called the disciples, he teaches that that widow had cast in more than all.

Mark 12:43. And calling his disciples, he saith to them: Amen I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than all they who have cast into the treasury.

Verse 44. For all they did cast in of their abundance: but she of her want cast in all, even all she had, her whole living.

Luke 21:3. And he said: Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than all.

Verse 4. For all these have of their abundance cast into the offerings of GOD: but she of her want, hath cast in all the living that she had.

And all these things were done on Tuesday in the temple. Now the Evangelists report concerning those things which were said on the same day upon leaving the temple and on the Mount of Olives.

CHAPTER XXII. Concerning the instruction of the temple.

§. I. To Jesus as he was leaving the temple, the disciples show the building of the temple, who teaches that the whole of it was going to be destroyed.

Matt. XXIV. 1. And Jesus went out from the temple, and was going. And his disciples came to him, to show him the buildings of the temple.

Ver. 2. But he answering said to them: Do you see all these things? Amen I say to you, there shall not be left here a stone upon a stone, that shall not be destroyed.

Mark XIII. v. 1. And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples saith to him: Master, behold what manner of stones, and what buildings.

Ver. 2. And Jesus answering, saith to him: Do you see all these great buildings? There shall not be left a stone upon a stone, that shall not be destroyed.

Luke XXI. v. 5. And some saying of the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said:

Ver. 6. These things which you see, the days will come, in which there shall not be left a stone upon a stone, that shall not be destroyed.

§. II. On the Mount of Olives the disciples, especially Peter, and James, and John, ask when that shall be: and what shall be the sign of his coming, and of the end of the world?

Matt. XXIV. v. 3. And as he was sitting upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the consummation of the world?

Mark 13:3. And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately:

Verse 4. Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?

Luke 21:7. And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?

§. III. Jesus answers concerning the signs of the destruction of the temple: false Christs, various wars, pestilence, famine, earthquakes, the betrayal of the disciples, false prophets about to arise, and the Gospel being preached throughout the whole world.

Matthew 24:4. And Jesus answering said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you,

Verse 5. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.

Verse 6. And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.

Verse 7. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.

Verse 8. All these are the beginning of sorrows.

Vers. 9. Then they will deliver you up to tribulation, and will kill you: and you will be hated by all nations for my name's sake.

Vers. 10. And then many will be scandalized, and will betray one another, and will hate one another.

Vers. 11. And many false prophets will arise, and will seduce many.

Vers. 12. And because iniquity has abounded, the charity of many will grow cold.

Vers. 13. But he that shall persevere to the end, he shall be saved.

Vers. 14. And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole world, for a testimony to all nations: and then shall the consummation come.

Mark XIII. v. 5. And Jesus answering, began to say to them: Take heed, lest any man seduce you.

Vers. 6. For many will come in my name, saying, I am he: and they will seduce many.

Vers. 7. And when you shall hear of wars and rumors of wars, fear not: for such things must needs be: but the end is not yet.

Vers. 8. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom upon kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in places, and famines. These things are the beginning of sorrows.

Vers. 9. But look to yourselves. For they will deliver you up to councils, and in the synagogues you will be beaten, and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony unto them.

Ver. 10. And the Gospel must first be preached to all nations.

Ver. 11. And when they shall lead you, delivering you up, do not premeditate what you shall speak: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye, for it is not you that speak, but the Holy Spirit.

Ver. 12. And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his son: and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall put them to death.

Ver. 13. And you shall be hated by all men for my name's sake. But he that shall endure unto the end, he shall be saved.

Luke XXI. v. 8. Who said: Take heed that you be not seduced: for many will come in my name, saying, that I am he: and the time is at hand: go not therefore after them.

Ver. 9. And when you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified: these things must first come to pass, but the end is not yet immediately.

Ver. 10. Then he said to them: Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

Ver. 11. And there shall be great earthquakes in divers places, and pestilences, and famines, and terrors from heaven, and there shall be great signs.

Ver. 12. But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and into prisons, dragging you before kings and governors, for my name's sake.

Ver. 13. And it shall happen unto you for a testimony.

Ver. 14. Lay it therefore up in your hearts, not to premeditate how you shall answer.

Vers. 15. For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist and contradict.

Vers. 16. Moreover, you will be betrayed by parents, and brothers, and kinsmen, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.

Vers. 17. And you will be hated by all for my name's sake:

Vers. 18. And a hair from your head will not perish.

Vers. 19. In your patience you will possess your souls.

§. IV. Jesus adds that, when the abomination of desolation, of which Daniel (chap. IX. 27.) speaks, is seen, one must flee; that there will be great tribulation, that one must not believe false Christs and false prophets: and that the coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning.

Matth. XXIV. v. 15. When therefore you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place: let him who reads understand:

Vers. 16. Then, those who are in Judea, let them flee to the mountains.

Vers. 17. And he who is on the housetop, let him not come down to take anything out of his house.

Vers. 18. And he who is in the field, let him not turn back to take his garment.

Vers. 19. But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days.

Vers. 20. But pray that your flight may not be in winter, or on the Sabbath.

Vers. 21. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be.

Vers. 22. And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved: but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.

Vers. 23. Then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is Christ, or there: do not believe it.

Vers. 24. For false Christs and false prophets will arise: and they will give great signs and wonders, so that even the elect (if it were possible) might be led into error.

Vers. 25. Behold, I have told you beforehand.

Vers. 26. If therefore they say to you: Behold, he is in the desert; do not go out; behold, he is in the inner rooms, do not believe it.

Vers. 27. For as the lightning comes from the East, and appears even to the West: so also will be the coming of the Son of Man.

Ver. 28. Wheresoever the body shall be, there will the eagles be gathered together.

Mark XIII. 14. But when you shall see the abomination of desolation, standing where it ought not: he that readeth, let him understand: then let them that are in Judaea flee unto the mountains:

Ver. 15. And let him that is on the housetop not descend into the house, neither enter therein, to take any thing out of his house.

Ver. 16. And let him that shall be in the field not turn back to take up his garment.

Ver. 17. And woe to them that are with child, and that give suck in those days.

Ver. 18. But pray that these things happen not in winter.

Ver. 19. For in those days shall be such tribulations, as were not from the beginning of the creation which GOD created, until now, neither shall be.

Ver. 20. And unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh should be saved: but for the sake of the elect which he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.

Ver. 21. And then if any man shall say to you: Lo, here is Christ; lo, he is there: do not believe.

Ver. 22. For there will rise up false Christs and false prophets, and they shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.

Ver. 23. Take you heed therefore: behold I have foretold you all things.

Luke 21:20. And when you shall see Jerusalem compassed about with an army, then know that the desolation thereof is at hand:

Verse 21. Then let them that are in Judea flee unto the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

Verse 22. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

Verse 23. But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! For there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.

§. V. And Jerusalem shall be trodden down, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Luke 21:24.

Verse 24. And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

CHAPTER XXIII.

Concerning the signs of the final coming of the Lord, and vigilance.

§. I. After those days the sun and the moon shall be darkened, the stars shall fall from heaven, the powers of heaven shall be shaken, and then shall appear the sign of the Son of man, and all the tribes of the earth shall mourn.

Matthew 24:29. Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:

Vers. 30. And then the sign of the Son of man will appear in heaven: and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn: and they will see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with much power and majesty.

Mark XIII. 24. But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its splendor.

Vers. 25. And the stars of heaven will be falling, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

Vers. 26. And then they will see the Son of man coming in the clouds with much power and glory.

Luke XXI. 25. And there will be signs in the sun, and moon, and stars, and on the earth distress of nations because of the confusion of the roaring of the sea and the waves.

Vers. 26. Men withering away for fear, and expectation of those things which are coming upon the whole world. For the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

Vers. 27. And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty.

§. II. The sending forth of the angels to gather the elect.

Matthew XXIV. 31. And he will send his angels with a trumpet, and a great voice: and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the ends of the heavens even to their boundaries.

Mark 13:27. And then he will send his angels, and will gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

§. III. That the liberation of the disciples is then approaching.

Matthew 24:32. And learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender, and the leaves have sprouted, you know that summer is near;

Verse 33. So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.

Mark 13:28. And learn the parable from the fig tree. When its branch has already become tender, and the leaves have sprouted, you know that summer is near.

Verse 29. So also you, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.

Luke 21:28. But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up your heads: because your redemption is approaching.

Verse 29. And he spoke to them a parable: Behold the fig tree, and all the trees:

Vers. 30. When they now put forth their fruit, you know that summer is near.

Vers. 31. So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of GOD is near.

§. IV, That these things will certainly happen: but that the day is not known.

Matth. XXIV. 34. Amen I say to you, that this generation will not pass away, until all these things happen.

Ver. 35. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Ver. 36. Lest, when he comes suddenly, he find you sleeping.

Ver. 36. But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but the Father alone.

Ver. 37. And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch.

Mark XIII. v. 30. Amen I say to you, that this generation shall not pass, until all these things be done.

Luke XXI. v. 34. And take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and the cares of this life: and that day come upon you suddenly:

Ver. 31. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Ver. 35. For as a snare shall it come upon all that sit upon the face of all the earth.

Vers. 32. But of that day or hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.

Luc. XXI. v. 32. Amen I say to you, that this generation shall not pass away, till all things be done.

Vers. 36. Watch ye therefore, praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of man.

Vers. 33. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away:

CHAPTER XXIV. The parable of the ten virgins.

§. V. Concerning security in the last times, such as it was in the time of Noah: and extreme danger: because of two men or two women, one or the other shall be taken, one or the other shall be left.

§. I. The kingdom of heaven is compared to ten virgins, five foolish, five wise, of whom the former took lamps without oil, the latter with oil. But all sleep.

Matth. XXIV. v. 37. And as in the days of Noah, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

Matth. XXV. v. 1. Then shall the kingdom of heaven be like to ten virgins: who taking their lamps, went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.

Vers. 38. As they were in the days before the flood eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until that day in which Noah entered into the ark.

Vers. 2. But five of them were foolish, and five wise:

Vers. 39. And they did not know, until the flood came, and took them all away: so also will be the coming of the Son of man.

Vers. 3. But the five foolish, having taken their lamps, did not take oil with them:

Vers. 4. But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

Vers. 40. Then two will be in the field: one will be taken, and one will be left.

Vers. 5. And while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.

Vers. 41. And two women grinding at the mill: one will be taken, and one will be left.

§. II. At midnight, the bridegroom arriving, all arise; the foolish seek oil from the wise in vain, these enter the wedding with the bridegroom, and the door is shut, while those seek in vain that the doors be opened to them: and therefore Jesus warns that we should watch.

§. VI. Therefore we must watch, because the hour of the coming is unknown, and drunkenness and worldly care must be avoided, and thus we must pray. The example of the householder fearing the thief. The parable of the faithful servant and of the unfaithful one is also repeated.

Vers. 6. And at midnight a cry was made: Behold the bridegroom comes, go out to meet him.

Vers. 42. Watch therefore, because you do not know at what hour your Lord will come.

Vers. 7. Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.

Vers. 43. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up.

Vers. 8. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.

Vers. 44. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.

Vers. 9. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Vers. 45. Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?

Vers. 10. And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.

Vers. 46. Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

Vers. 11. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.

Vers. 47. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.

Vers. 12. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

Vers. 48. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming;

Vers. 13. Watch therefore, because you know not the day nor the hour.

CHAPTER XXV. The parable of the talents repeated a little differently than above.

Vers. 49. And shall begin to strike his fellow servants, and shall eat and drink with drunkards.

Vers. 50. The lord of that servant shall come in the day that he hopeth not, and at the hour that he knoweth not:

§. I. A certain man going abroad entrusted to three servants, to one five talents, to another three, to the third one; of whom the first gained five more, the second likewise two talents: the third, being slothful, gained nothing with his talent.

Vers. 51. And shall separate him, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

Mark XIII. v. 33. Take ye heed, watch, and pray: for ye know not when the time is.

V. 14. For even as a man going into a far country, called his servants, and delivered to them his goods.

Vers 34. As a man, who going into a far country, left his house, and gave authority to his servants to every work: and commanded the porter to watch.

Vers. 15. And to one he gave five talents, and to another two, and to another one, to every one according to his proper ability, and went immediately.

Vers. 35. Watch ye therefore, (for you know not when the lord of the house cometh: at even, or at midnight, or at the cock crowing, or in the morning,)

Ver. 16. But he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made other five talents.

Ver. 17. Likewise he also who had received two, gained two others.

Ver. 18. But he who had received one, going away dug in the earth, and hid the money of his Lord.

§. II. The Lord, demanding an account, appointed him who had gained five talents over many things, and commanded him to enter into the joy of his Lord: which same thing was also done to the other. But from the third, as if evil and slothful, the talent is taken away, and given to him who had ten talents. For to him who has it shall be given, from him who has not shall be taken away that which he has. The useless servant is moreover ordered to be cast into darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth.

Ver. 19. But after a long time the Lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.

Ver. 20. And he who had received five talents coming forward, offered five other talents saying: Lord, you delivered five talents to me, behold I have gained five others besides.

Ver. 21. His Lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant, because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things, enter into the joy of your Lord.

Ver. 22. And he also who had received two talents came, and said: Lord, you delivered two talents to me, behold I have gained two others.

Ver. 23. His Lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant, because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things, enter into the joy of your Lord.

Ver. 24. But he who had received one talent coming forward, said: Lord, I know that you are a hard man, you reap where you have not sown, and gather where you have not scattered:

Ver. 25. And being afraid I went, and hid your talent in the earth: behold you have what is yours.

Ver. 26. But his Lord answering, said to him: Wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I do not sow, and gather where I have not scattered:

Vers. 27. You ought therefore to have committed my money to the bankers, and I coming would have received back what is mine, with interest.

Vers. 28. Take therefore the talent from him, and give it to him who has ten talents;

Vers. 29. For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance: but from him who does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away from him.

Vers. 30. And cast the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

CHAPTER XXVI.

On the progress of the final judgment.

§. I. When the Son of man shall appear in his glory, all shall be gathered unto him, and he shall separate the sheep from the goats; placing the former on the right, the latter on the left.

Vers. 31. And when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he shall sit upon the seat of his majesty:

Vers. 32. And all nations shall be gathered before him, and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats:

Vers. 33. And he shall set the sheep indeed on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

§. II. The address to those who shall stand on the right: come, blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom which has been prepared for you from the foundation of the world: inasmuch as they fed the hungry, gave drink to the thirsty, took in the stranger, clothed the naked, visited the sick, and came to the prisoner, because what they did to the least of the brethren, they did to him.

Vers. 34. Then the king shall say to those who will be on his right: Come, blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

Vers. 35. For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink: I was a stranger, and you took me in:

Vers. 36. Naked, and you covered me: sick, and you visited me: I was in prison, and you came to me.

Vers. 37. Then the just shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, and fed thee: thirsty, and gave thee drink?

Vers. 38. And when did we see thee a stranger, and took thee in: or naked, and covered thee?

Vers. 39. Or when did we see thee sick, or in prison, and came to thee?

Vers. 40. And the king answering, shall say to them: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.

§. III. The address to those who shall stand on the left: depart you cursed into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels: inasmuch as they did not feed the hungry, etc.

Vers. 41. Then he shall say also to them that shall be on his left hand: Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire which was prepared for the devil, and his angels.

Vers. 42. For I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me not to drink:

Vers. 43. I was a stranger, and you took me not in: naked, and you covered me not: sick, and in prison, and you did not visit me.

Vers. 44. Then they also shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to thee?

Vers. 45. Then he will answer them, saying: Amen I say to you: As long as you did it not to one of these least, neither did you do it to me.

§. IV. And these shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting.

Vers. 46. And these shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting.

[These things therefore λεχθέντα pertain to Tuesday. Now those things which happened on Wednesday, the fourth day of the week, two days before the Passover, are set forth.]

CHAPTER XXVII. The prediction of the Passion of JESUS.

§. I. A summary account of the preceding events, handed down by Luke, is set forth, that Jesus taught in the temple during the day, but remained at night on the Mount of Olives: and that the people flocked to the temple in the morning to hear him.

Luke XXI. v. 37. And in the daytime he was teaching in the temple; but at night, going out, he abode in the mount that is called Olivet.

Vers. 38. And all the people were coming early to him in the temple, to hear him.

§. II. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples: You know, that after two days shall be the pasch, and the Son of man shall be delivered up to be crucified.

Matt. XXVI. 1. And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples:

Verse 2. You know that after two days the Passover will come, and the Son of man will be delivered up to be crucified.

CHAPTER XXVIII. The counsel of the priests and lawyers concerning apprehending Jesus, and the covenant of Judas.

§. I. They are gathered in the palace of the high priest Caiaphas, deliberating how they may apprehend Jesus with guile and kill him: but not on the feast day, lest a tumult should arise. Where also the anointing of Jesus done in Bethany is treated.

Ver. 3. Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered together into the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas:

Ver. 4. And they took counsel, that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.

Ver. 5. But they said: Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar among the people.

Ver. 6. Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

Ver. 7. There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat.

Ver. 8. But the disciples seeing it, had indignation, saying: To what purpose is this waste?

Ver. 9. For this might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.

Ver. 10. And Jesus knowing it, said to them: Why do you trouble this woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.

Ver. 11. For you have the poor always with you: but me you have not always.

Ver. 12. For she in pouring this ointment upon my body, hath done it for my burial.

Ver. 13. Amen I say to you, wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, that also which she hath done, shall be told for a memory of her.

Mark XIV. v. 1. Now the Passover and the Unleavened Bread were after two days: and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might take him by craft, and kill him.

Ver. 2. But they were saying: Not on the feast day, lest perhaps there should be a tumult among the people.

Ver. 3. And when he was at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, and was reclining: there came a woman having an alabaster jar of ointment of spikenard precious, and having broken the alabaster jar, she poured it upon his head.

Ver. 4. And there were some indignant within themselves, and saying: Why has this waste of the ointment been made?

Ver. 5. For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii, and given to the poor. And they were murmuring against her.

Ver. 6. But Jesus said: Let her alone, why are you troublesome to her? She has wrought a good work in me.

Ver. 7. For you always have the poor with you; and when you will, you can do them good: but me you do not always have.

Ver. 8. She has done what she had: she has anticipated the anointing of my body for the burial.

Ver. 9. Amen I say to you: Wheresoever this Gospel shall be preached in the whole world, that also which she has done, shall be told in memory of her.

Luke XXII. v. 1. Now the feast day of the Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching:

Vers. 2. And the chief priests and scribes were seeking how they might kill Jesus: but they feared the people.

[This is done καθ' ὕστερον πρότερον: because Christ was not then in Bethany any longer, but in Jerusalem: and from the occasion, namely that Judas murmured against the pouring out of the oil, John XII. 4. seqq., whose betrayal Matthew and Mark now set out to relate.]

§. II. Judas offers himself to betray Jesus: they make a bargain with him, and offer 30 pieces of silver.

Matth. XXVI. v. 14. Then went one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, unto the chief priests:

Vers. 15. And said unto them: What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they appointed unto him thirty pieces of silver.

Vers. 16. And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

Marc. XIV. v. 10. And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them.

Vers. 11. And when they heard it, they were glad: and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

Luc. XXII. v. 3. Then entered Satan into Judas, surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.

Vers. 4. And he went away, and spoke with the chief priests and magistrates, how he might betray him to them.

Vers. 5. And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

Vers. 6. And he promised. And he sought an opportunity, that he might betray him without tumults.

[So much then for the events of Wednesday of Holy Week; now follow the acts of Thursday, which we call, indeed, the fifth day of the week.]

CHAPTER XXIX. Preparation and eating of the Paschal lamb.

§. I. On the first day of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover had to be eaten, the disciples ask where the Passover is to be prepared, and they are sent to a certain man in the city, with whom Jesus wished to eat the Passover, who therefore prepares it.

Matth. XXVI. v. 17. And on the first day of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying: Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?

Vers. 18. But Jesus said: Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him: The Master saith: My time is near at hand, I will keep the Passover at thy house with my disciples.

Vers. 19. And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them, and they prepared the passover.

Marc. XIV. v. 12. And on the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the passover, the disciples say to him: Whither wilt thou that we go, and prepare for thee, that thou mayest eat the passover?

Vers. 13. And he sends two of his disciples, and says to them: Go into the city: and a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you, follow him:

Vers. 14. And wheresoever he shall enter, say to the master of the house, that the master says: Where is my refectory, where I may eat the passover with my disciples?

Vers. 15. And he will show you a large dining room, furnished: and there prepare for us.

Vers. 16. And his disciples went, and came into the city: and they found, as he had said to them, and they prepared the passover.

Luc. XXII. v. 7. And the day of unleavened bread came, on which it was necessary that the passover should be killed.

Vers. 8. And he sent Peter and John, saying: Going, prepare for us the passover, that we may eat.

Vers. 9. But they said: Where do you want us to prepare?

Vers. 10. And he said to them: Behold, as you enter into the city, a certain man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you: follow him into the house into which he enters.

Vers. 11. And you shall say to the master of the house: The Master says to you: Where is the guest chamber, where I may eat the passover with my disciples?

Vers. 12. And he will show you a large dining room furnished, and there prepare.

Vers. 13. And going they found, as he said to them, and they prepared the passover.

Thus, during the day, the preparation for the Passover was dealt with; but at the approach of the night, the meal took place. Here, the τὰ παρασκευαστικά for the passion of Jesus are to be observed: which, as they occurred on the part of the Jews intending the passion for him, were noted in the preceding chapter, namely the counsel and the pact entered into with Judas; so, on the part of Jesus, by whom that passion was to be undergone, these things are recorded: first the eating of the Paschal Lamb, then the washing of the feet, and what follows thereafter. Which pertain to the things immediately preceding the passion. On Thursday, says Bünting, the second of April, when the feast day of Unleavened Bread was already approaching for the fourth Paschal ministry of Christ, the disciples of Christ prepared themselves for the eating of the Paschal lamb: and when about the evening of this day the first day of Unleavened Bread began according to the law of God, on which it was necessary for the Passover to be sacrificed, Christ sent Peter and John, that they might prepare the paschal banquet: Christ himself also, having returned to Jerusalem from Bethany with the rest of his disciples at the interval of half a mile as the day was darkening, at the proper time, at the beginning of the fourteenth day of the first month Abib, or Nisan, which began from the evening of this day, celebrated the Passover with his disciples, which he thinks was done between the sixth and seventh hour of the evening, but others between the third and fifth, as will be said a little later.

§. II. Sitting at the table, Jesus testifies to his desire to eat the Passover with them before his passion: because from then on he was not going to eat it with them, until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

Verse 14. And when the hour had come, he reclined, and the twelve Apostles with him.

Verse 15. And he said to them: With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

Verse 16. For I say to you, that from this time I will not eat it, until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

§. III. The paschal lamb is eaten by Jesus and the disciples.

Matt. XXVI. v. 20. And when evening had come, he was reclining with his twelve disciples.

Mark XIV. v. 17. And when evening had come, he came with the twelve.

The legitimate time for eating the Paschal lamb was between the two evenings, Exod. XII. 6. Cajetan, Masius, Scaliger, Casaubon, Schindler, and B. Gerhard explain that this is between the ninth hour, or our third in the afternoon, and the eleventh, which is our fifth in the afternoon. See B. Gerhard, Harm. Evang. c. CLXIX. p. 1265.

§. IV. He distributed the farewell cup, and said that he would no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.

Luke XXII. v. 17. And having taken the cup, he gave thanks, and said: Take and divide it among yourselves.

Verse 18. For I say to you, that I will not drink of the generation of the vine, until the kingdom of God comes.

CHAPTER XXX. The washing of the Apostles' feet.

§. I. Having set forth the love of Jesus toward the Apostles, St. John relates how, after supper, having laid aside his garments, when he had taken a towel and girded himself, he washed the disciples' feet.

John XIII. v. 1. Before the feast day of the Passover, Jesus knowing that his hour was come, that he should pass out of this world to the Father: having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them unto the end.

Verse 2. And when supper was done, the devil having now put into the heart that Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, should betray him:

Verse 3. Knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God, and goes to God:

Verse 4. He rises from supper, and lays aside his garments: and having taken a towel, he girded himself.

Ver. 5. Then he pours water into a basin, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.

§. II. He instructs Peter, who is refusing, so that he may consent.

Ver. 6. He comes therefore to Simon Peter. And Peter says to him: Lord, do you wash my feet?

Ver. 7. Jesus answered and said to him: What I am doing, you do not know now, but you will know hereafter.

Ver. 8. Peter says to him: You shall never wash my feet. Jesus answered him: If I do not wash you, you will have no part with me.

Ver. 9. Simon Peter says to him: Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.

Ver. 10. Jesus says to him: He who has bathed does not need, except to wash his feet, but is clean all over.

§. III. He says that they are clean, but not all, because he knew well his betrayer.

Ver. 10. And you are clean, but not all.

• Ver. 11. For he knew who it was that would betray him: therefore he said: You are not all clean.

§. IV. Reclining again, he admonishes that they also ought to wash one another's feet: hinting again from Scripture (Ps. XLI. 10.) at the betrayer: he who eats bread with me, will lift up his heel against me.

Verse 12. After therefore he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments: when he had sat down again, he said to them: Do you know what I have done to you?

Verse 13. You call me Master, and Lord: and you say well: for so I am.

Verse 14. If then I have washed your feet, Lord, and Master: you also ought to wash one another's feet.

Verse 15. For I have given you an example, that, as I have done to you, so you also should do.

Verse 16. Amen, amen I say to you: The servant is not greater than his Lord: neither is the apostle greater than he that sent him.

Verse 17. If you know these things, you shall be blessed, if you do them.

Verse 18. I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled: He that eateth bread with me, shall lift up his heel against me.

Verse 19. At present I tell you, before it come to pass: that, when it shall come to pass, you may believe that I am he.

Verse 20. Amen, amen I say to you: He that receiveth whomsoever I send, receiveth me: and he that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.

CHAPTER XXXI. Prediction concerning his betrayal.

§. I. While they were eating, Jesus said that one of them would betray him.

Matth. XXVI. v. 21. And as they were eating, he said: Amen I say to you, that one of you is about to betray me.

Marc. XIV. v. 18. And when they were at table and eating, Jesus saith: Amen I say to you, that one of you who eateth with me shall betray me. [Which is to be understood of the common supper; for the Paschal lamb had already been eaten before the washing of the feet. There is therefore no anticipation here: even though Luke subjoins the prediction of the betrayal to the celebration of the Eucharist. For this was a repeated and new prediction.]

§. II. The disciples are saddened, and ask, who it is? Jesus, pointing him out, gravely dissuades him from the betrayal.

Matth. XXVI. v. 22. And being very saddened, they began every one to say: Is it I, Lord?

Vers. 23. But he answering, saith: He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, he shall betray me.

Vers. 24. The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man shall be betrayed: it were better for him, if that man had not been born.

Mark XIV. v. 19. But they began to be sorrowful, and to say to him one by one: Is it I?

Vers. 20. Who said to them: One of the twelve, who dippeth his hand with me in the dish.

Vers. 21. And the Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man shall be betrayed: it were better for him, if that man had not been born.

§. III. To Judas asking: Is it I? It is answered: You have said it.

Matt. XXVI. n. 25. And Judas that betrayed him, answering, said: Is it I, Rabbi? He said to him: You have said it.

CHAPTER XXXII. The institution of the Holy Supper.

§. I. While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, and said: Take, eat, this is my body. Luke adds: which is given for you. Do this in commemoration of me.

Vers. 26. And whilst they were at supper, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and broke, and gave to his disciples, and said: Take, and eat: this is my body.

Mark XIV. v. 22. And whilst they were eating, Jesus took bread; and blessing broke, and gave to them, and said: Take, this is my body.

Luke XXII. v. 19. And having taken bread, he gave thanks, and broke, and gave to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you: do this in commemoration of me.

§. II. Having taken the cup, he gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying: Drink all of it: this is my blood of the New Testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. Mark adds: And they all drank of it, Luke has it thus: This cup (is) the New Testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

Matt. XXVI. v. 27. And taking the cup he gave thanks: and gave to them, saying: Drink ye all of this. Ver. 28. For this is my blood of the New Testament, which shall be shed for many unto the remission of sins.

Mark XIV. v. 23. And having taken the cup, giving thanks he gave to them: and they all drank of it. Ver. 24. And he said to them: This is my blood of the New Testament, which shall be shed for many.

Luke XXII. v. 20. In like manner the cup also, after he supped, saying: This is the cup the New Testament in my blood, which shall be shed for you.

[The cup is said to be shed in the original text, because clearly the cup exhibits the blood, which was shed for us: Τῦτο τὸ ποτήριον, ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί με, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυνόμενον. Luke XXII. 20.]

§. III. Concerning the new drink in the kingdom of the Father.

Matth. XXVI. v. 29. But I say to you: I will not drink from henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it with you new in the kingdom of my Father.

Marc. XIV. v. 25. Amen I say to you, that I will drink no more of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it new in the kingdom of God.

CHAPTER XXXIII. Repeated prediction concerning the betrayal of Judas.

§. I. The prediction itself.

Luc. XXII. v. 21, But yet behold the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.

Vers. 22. And indeed the Son of man goeth, according to that which is determined: but yet woe to that man by whom he shall be betrayed.

Joh. XIII. v. 21. When Jesus had said these things, he was troubled in spirit; and he testified, and said: Amen, amen I say to you, that one of you shall betray me.

[Troubled in spirit, because Judas could not be recalled from his crime, which he had in mind, even by the distribution of the bread, which was the communion of his body, and of the blessed cup, which was the communion of his blood, yet for a second time, which is his μακροθυμία, he wished to dissuade the same: which was done by an individual and most open designation.]

§. II. The mutual look of the disciples.

Luke 22:23. And they began to inquire among themselves, which of them it was that should do this.

John 13:22. The disciples therefore looked one on another, doubting of whom he spoke.

[Whether because they had not sufficiently noticed before who was dipping with Jesus in the dish, or because they were rendered doubtful and astonished, and the memory of it had slipped their minds, being intent upon the holy Eucharist, especially when they saw the bread and blessed wine being distributed equally to all.]

§. III. Peter signals to John to ask who the betrayer is to be. To whom Jesus, responding by dipping the bread, points him out.

Verse 23. Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.

Verse 24. Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, and said to him: Who is it of whom he speaks?

Verse 25. He therefore, leaning back on Jesus' breast, says to him: Lord, who is it?

Verse 26. Jesus answered: It is he to whom I shall give the dipped bread. And when he had dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.

[Before, he only said: 'He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me,' Matt. 26:23, Mark 14:20; but now he himself handed the dipped bread to Judas, and thus designated him. Before, when he had noted Judas dipping with him, he added in Matthew and Mark: 'Woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! It had been good for that man if he had not been born.' Here, after the morsel was handed to Judas, he said nothing of the sort, but because Satan immediately entered into Judas, and the matter was now desperate, he said rather: 'That thou doest, do quickly.' After the former dissuasion, Judas still remained and was present at the holy Eucharist itself; but after this designation, when he had received the morsel, Judas went out immediately, John 13:30; and when he had gone out, Jesus did not celebrate the holy Eucharist, but said: 'Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.' I see nothing that prevents Jesus from having designated his betrayer a second time, and in a different manner, as the circumstances demanded. Thus there is no need for a recollection or a hysteron proteron in Matthew and Mark, and everything proceeds in order, and those things serve to declare more and more the admirable long-suffering of our Savior.]

§. IV. Judas, having received the morsel, occupied by Satan, went out.

Vers. 27. And after the morsel, Satan entered into him. And Jesus said to him: What you do, do quickly.

Vers. 28. But no one of those reclining at table knew for what purpose he had said this to him.

Vers. 29. For some thought, because Judas had the money box, that Jesus had said to him: Buy those things which we need for the feast day: or that he should give something to the poor.

Verse 30. When therefore he had received the morsel, he went out immediately. And it was night.

[Blessed Gerhard understands this as the deep and dead of night, H. E. c. CXXXII. p. 100, provided that the second watch has already passed, according to Theophylact: But I do not see how these things agree with those which are read in Harm. Pass. c. II. p. 8 concerning the first cockcrowing, which happens around the second watch of the night, or around the ninth or tenth hour according to our clock, at which time Peter had already denied Jesus for the first time. And therefore it is more correctly said that the night had begun, or that it was the beginning of the night when Judas went out, which happened after the sacramental supper: For there still intervene the lengthy discourses of Christ, the agony in the garden, the apprehension and leading away to the Sanhedrin, which require an interval of more than one hour.]

CHAPTER XXXIV. The contention of the disciples concerning primacy.

§. I. They contend among themselves, which of them ought to be considered the greatest.

Luke 22:24. And there was also a contention among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.

§. II. The diversity of the great ones in an earthly kingdom, and of the disciples of Christ, who are recalled to the example of Christ.

Verse 25. And he said to them: The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

Verse 26. But you shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that does serve.

Verse 27. For whether is greater, he that sits at meat, or he that serves? is not he that sits at meat? but I am among you as he that serves.

§. III. The promise of the kingdom and of sitting at table in the kingdom of the Lord, and the judging of the XII tribes of Israel.

Verse 28. But you are they who have continued with me in my temptations:

Verse 29. And I appoint to you, as my Father has appointed to me, a kingdom,

Verse 30. That you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom: and may sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

CHAPTER XXXV. Certain sayings of Christ after the departure of Judas.

§. 1. When he had gone out, Jesus spoke concerning his glorification.

John XIII. v. 31. When therefore he had gone out, Jesus said: Now is the Son of man glorified: and God is glorified in him.

Verse 32. If God be glorified in him, God also will glorify him in himself; and will immediately glorify him.

§. II. He told the disciples that he would be with them for a little while longer; thereafter he would not be found.

Verse 33. Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You shall seek me: and as I said to the Jews: Whither I go, you cannot come: so I say to you now.

§. III. A new commandment concerning charity.

Verse 34. A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another, as I have loved you, that you also love one another.

Verse 35. By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one to another.

CHAPTER XXXVI. Prediction of Peter's fall.

§. I. Peter asks whither the Lord is going, and promises that he is willing to lay down his life for Jesus.

Verse 36. Simon Peter says to him: Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered: Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now: but thou shalt follow me afterwards.

Verse 37. Peter says to him: Why can I not follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thee.

§. II. Jesus answers that Satan desires the sifting of the disciples: but that he has interceded for Peter, and that he, once converted, ought to strengthen his brethren.

Luke XXII. v. 31. And the Lord said: Simon, Simon, behold Satan has desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:

Verse 32. But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and thou, being once converted, confirm thy brethren.

§. III. Peter protests that he is prepared to go with Jesus into prison and to death.

Verse 33. Who said to him: Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison and to death.

§. IV. Jesus replies that he will deny him three times before the cock crows.

Vers. 34. But he said: I say to you, Peter, the cock shall not crow today, until you deny that you know me. And he said to them:

John XIII, v. 38. Jesus answered him: Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you: The cock shall not crow, until you deny me three times.

CHAPTER XXXVII. Concerning the impending danger, and the necessity of a sword.

§. I. He asks whether, even though they were sent out without money bags and sandals, they lacked anything: and upon their answering in the negative, he advises them that now, they should sell what they have and buy themselves swords.

Luke XXII, v. 35. When I sent you without money bag, and wallet, and sandals, did you lack anything?

Vers. 36. But they said: Nothing. He said therefore to them: But now he who has a money bag, let him take it; likewise also a wallet: and he who does not have one, let him sell his tunic, and buy a sword.

§. II. He predicts his passion, that he is to be numbered among the transgressors.

Vers. 37. For I say to you, that this which is written must yet be fulfilled in me: And he was reckoned with the wicked. For those things which concern me have an end.

§. III. Upon their saying that two swords were present, he says: It is enough.

Verse 38. But they said: Lord, behold, here are two swords. But he said to them: It is enough.

CHAPTER XXXVIII. The consolation of the disciples sorrowful on account of the death of JESUS.

§. I. Proposition: let not your heart be troubled, you believe in God, and you believe in me, is confirmed by the mansions in heaven, through the approach of preparing a place for them, and the return to them, so that they also may be brought to where he himself is.

John XIV. v. 1. Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God, and believe in me.

Verse 2. In my Father's house there are many mansions, if not, I would have told you: Because I go to prepare a place for you.

Verse 3. And if I shall go, and prepare a place for you: I will come again, and will take you to myself, that where I am, you also may be.

Verse 4. And whither I go, you know, and the way you know. [He says the disciples know the end of the way, and the way itself, because they could and ought to have known it, even from the Capernaum discourse John VI. 41. 51. 62. to say nothing of other discourses of Christ John VII. 33. ch. VIII. 23.

and following, ch. XII. 23. 24. 44. and following. Moreover, this long sermon described in ch. XIV. XV. XVI. of John, with the most fervent prayer, was delivered after supper and the celebration of the Sacrament, and that still in the upper room, with Judas the traitor having already gone out. It finished perhaps around the eighth hour. For around the fifth the eating of the Paschal lamb took place: which was followed by the washing of the feet, the common supper, and the Sacrament of the Eucharist, along with the sermon of Christ and the prayer περιαγωνιῳ: and also the Eucharistic hymn: which having been sung, he went out to the Mount of Olives: but that departure seems to have taken place after the eighth hour according to our clock.

§. II. To Thomas asking where he is going, and about the way, Jesus responds.

Verse 5. Thomas says to him: Lord, we do not know where you are going: and how can we know the way?

Verse 6. Jesus says to him: I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father, except through me.

Verse 7. If you had known me, you would have known my Father also: and from now on you know him, and have seen him.

[Euthymius explains the response of Christ well: I am the way, because no one comes to the Father, except through me: for no one knows the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son wishes to reveal him: for nothing is known except by truth: I am the life, because no one lives, except through me. And Augustine, tractate XXII on John: Do you wish to walk? I am the way: Do you not wish to be deceived? I am the truth: Do you not wish to die? I am the life. These things your Savior says to you: there is nowhere for you to go, except to me: there is nowhere for you to go, except through me.]

§. III. Philip asking for the Father to be shown to him, he teaches that he is in the Father, and the Father is in him, and he appeals to his works, and promises that those who believe in him will do even greater works.

Verse 8. Philip says to him: Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.

Verse 9. Jesus says to him: Have I been with you for so long a time: and you have not known me? Philip, he who sees me, sees also the Father. How do you say: Show us the Father.

Verse 10. Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? The words which I speak to you, I do not speak from myself. But the Father remaining in me, he himself does the works.

Verse 11. Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me?

Verse 12. Otherwise believe because of the works themselves. Amen, amen I say to you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he also shall do, and greater than these shall he do: because I go to the Father.

§. IV. He promises the hearing of prayers.

Verse 13. And whatsoever you shall ask the Father in my name, that will I do: that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

Verse 14. If you shall ask anything of me in my name, that I will do.

§. V. He exhorts them to keep his commandments, and promises the Spirit of truth: and that they shall see him again.

Verse 15. If you love me, keep my commandments.

Verse 16. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, that he may abide with you forever,

Verse 17. The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him, nor know him. But you shall know him, because he shall abide with you, and shall be in you.

Verse 18. I will not leave you orphans: I will come to you.

Verse 19. Yet a little while: and the world sees me no more. But you see me: because I live, and you shall live.

Verse 20. In that day you shall know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.

Verse 21. He who has my commandments, and keeps them, he it is who loves me. But he who loves me, will be loved by my Father: and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.

§. VI. Judas asking why he was about to manifest himself to them, and not to the world, Jesus warns of the gracious indwelling in those who hear his word, and promises the Holy Spirit to teach them all things.

Verse 22. Judas says to him, not the Iscariot; Lord, what has happened, that you are about to manifest yourself to us, and not to the world?

Verse 23. Jesus answered and said to him: If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and will make our dwelling with him:

Verse 24. He who does not love me, does not keep my words. And the word, which you have heard, is not mine: but the Father's, who sent me.

Verse 25. These things I have spoken to you, while remaining with you.

Verse 26. But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will bring to your remembrance all things, whatsoever I shall have said to you.

[There was a doubt from verse 19 that the world is no longer to see Christ, but the disciples are to see him again; and that Christ wishes to manifest himself to those who love him v. 21. but that promise of seeing him again was different from the other concerning his manifestation: For the former was made peculiarly to the Apostles; the latter concerns all who love Christ: The former implies an external and corporal manifestation; the latter an internal and spiritual one. Concerning the former, he delivered something in v. 28, but he began to discourse more fully on the same in ch. XVI. 16; but the latter he confirms repeatedly to those who keep and guard his word through faith, and love him, that he wishes not only to deign to visit them with a further and more inward manifestation, but also to make his dwelling within them with the Father and the Holy Spirit: where he implicitly distinguishes between the external manifestation, which occurs by the preaching of the Gospel and miracles, and was looked to by Judas, who raised the doubt, how it happens that he wishes to manifest himself not to the world, but to the Apostles, when the Messiah had been promised to the whole world? and the internal, which pertains to the salutary fruit of preaching, and happens to the faithful alone and friends of Christ, who receive and keep the word of the Gospel through faith, who truly love Christ, and is joined with the special love of God the Father, and the gracious indwelling of the Holy Trinity. Knowledge of Christ is indeed required, so that we may love Christ, but to those who receive the word of Christ by faith, and embrace Christ with true love, Christ wishes to manifest himself more intimately, both by richer illumination and confirmation of faith, in the kingdom of grace, where they walk by faith, not by sight.
