II Cor. V. 7. and then indeed in the kingdom of glory to offer himself to be seen face to face, I Pet. I. 7. 8. 9. 1. John III. 2. Concerning which Emyffenus (in Pelarg.) says excellently: A great question, and a most noble solution to the question: therefore, he says, I do not manifest myself to the world, that is, to the lovers of the world: because they do not love me: which is proven most openly from this, because they do not keep my word. But my disciples and faithful ones, because they love me, and because they keep my commandments, are worthy that I should manifest myself to them; so that, wisdom being known, they may be wise, justice being known, they may be just, truth being known, they may be truthful, and life being known, they may live eternally. For CHRIST is all these things, all these things are manifested in CHRIST. Christ therefore rendered the reason why He does not manifest Himself to the world, namely because the world does not love Christ: nor does it hear His word, but despises it, even though it is the very word of God the Father.

§. VII. Concerning His peace and departure to the Father.

Verse 27. Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you: not as the world gives, do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

Verse 28. You have heard that I said to you: I go away, and come to you. If you loved Me, you would surely rejoice, because I go to the Father: for the Father is greater than I.

Verse 29. And now I have told you before it comes to pass: that, when it has come to pass, you may believe.

Verse 30. I will not speak much more with you, for the prince of this world comes, and has nothing in Me.

Verse 31. But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father gave Me commandment, so I do. Arise, let us go from here.

CHAPTER XXXIX. Exhortation of the disciples to perseverance in faith and love.

§. I. Jesus compares Himself to the vine, the faithful to the branches, grafted into Him (through faith), and bearing fruit: but he who does not remain in Him is cut off and cast into the fire.

John XV. v. 1. I am the true vine: and My Father is the husbandman.

Vers. 2. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he will take it away: and every one that bears fruit, he will prune it, that it may bring forth more fruit.

Vers. 3. Now you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.

Vers. 4. Abide in me: and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine: so neither can you, unless you abide in me.

Vers. 5. I am the vine, you are the branches: he who abides in me, and I in him, he bears much fruit: for without me you can do nothing.

Vers. 6. If anyone does not abide in me: he shall be cast out, as a branch, and shall wither, and they shall gather him, and cast him into the fire, and he burns.

§. II. He admonishes that they should abide in his word and love.

Vers. 7. If you abide in me, and my words abide in you: whatever you shall wish, you shall ask, and it shall be done for you.

Vers. 8. In this is my Father glorified, that you bear much fruit, and become my disciples.

Vers. 9. As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Abide in my love.

Vers. 10. If you keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love, just as I also have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.

Vers. 11. These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be fulfilled.

Vers. 12. This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you.

§. III. He exhorts to mutual love.

Vers. 13. Greater love than this no one has, that one should lay down his life for his friends.

Vers. 14. You are my friends, if you do what I command you.

Vers. 15. I will no longer call you servants: for the servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends: because all things, whatsoever I have heard from my Father, I have made known to you.

Vers. 16. You have not chosen me: but I have chosen you, and appointed you, that you should go, and bring forth fruit; and that your fruit should remain: that, whatsoever you shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.

Vers. 17. These things I command you, that you love one another.

CHAPTER XL. A forewarning against the hatreds and persecutions of the world.

§. I. Why the world hates the disciples; namely, on account of the name of Jesus.

Vers. 18. If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before you.

Vers. 19. If you were of the world, the world would love what was its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.

Vers. 20. Remember my word, which I said to you: The servant is not greater than his master. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you: if they have kept my word, they will keep yours also.

Vers. 21. But they will do all these things to you for my name's sake: because they do not know him who sent me.

Vers. 22. If I had not come, and spoken to them, they would not have sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin.

Vers. 23. He who hates me, hates my Father also.

Vers. 24. If I had not done among them the works which no one else did, they would not have sin: but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

Vers. 25. But that the word might be fulfilled which is written in their law: That they hated me without a cause.

§. II. The testimony of the Paraclete concerning Jesus.

Vers. 26. But when the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness concerning me:

Vers. 27. And you will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.

§. III. The prediction concerning the excommunication and killing of the disciples.

John XVI. Vers. 1. These things I have spoken to you, that you may not be scandalized.

Vers. 2. They will put you out of the synagogues: but the hour is coming, that everyone who kills you will think that he is offering service to God.

Vers. 3. And they will do these things to you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.

Vers. 4. But these things I have spoken to you: that, when their hour shall come, you may remember that I told you.

CHAPTER XLI. An explanation of Christ's departure to the Father.

§. I. The alleviation of the disciples' sadness on account of the departure to the Father, from the mission of the Paraclete, whose office is described.

Vers. 5. But these things I did not tell you from the beginning, because I was with you. And now I go to him who sent me; and none of you asks me, Whither goest thou?

Vers. 6. But because I have spoken these things to you, sadness has filled your heart.

Vers. 7. But I tell you the truth, it is expedient for you that I go: for if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you: but if I go, I will send him to you.

Vers. 8. And when he shall come, he will convict the world of sin, and of justice, and of judgment.

Ver. 9. Of sin indeed, because they have not believed in me:

Ver. 10. But of justice, because I go to the Father, and you shall see me no longer.

Ver. 11. And of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.

Ver. 12. I have yet many things to say to you: but you cannot bear them now.

Ver. 13. But when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth; for he shall not speak of himself: but what things soever he shall hear, he shall speak; and the things that are to come, he shall show you.

Ver. 14. He shall glorify me: because he shall receive of mine, and shall show it to you.

Ver. 15. All things whatsoever the Father hath, are mine. Therefore I said, that he shall receive of mine, and shall show it to you.

§. II. The question of the disciples concerning those words of Christ: a little while, and you shall not see me; again a little while, and you shall see me.

Ver. 16. A little while, and now you shall not see me; and again a little while, and you shall see me: because I go to the Father.

Ver. 17. Some of his disciples therefore said one to another: What is this that he saith to us: A little while, and you shall not see me: and again a little while, and you shall see me, and, because I go to the Father?

Ver. 18. They said therefore: What is this that he saith, A little while? We know not what he speaketh.

Verse 19. Now Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them: Do you inquire among yourselves about this, that I said, A little while, and you will not see me: and again a little while, and you will see me.

§. III. Prediction of sorrow, but to be turned into joy, from the vision of Jesus.

Verse 20. Amen, Amen, I say to you: that you will lament and weep, but the world will rejoice: and you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

Verse 21. A woman when she is in labor has sorrow, because her hour has come: but when she has brought forth the child, she no longer remembers the anguish for joy, because a man is born into the world.

Verse 22. And you therefore now indeed have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice: and your joy no one will take from you.

Verse 23. And in that day you will ask me nothing.

§. IV. Promise of the hearing of prayers made in the name of Jesus.

Verse 23. Amen, Amen I say to you: if you ask the Father anything in my name, he will give it to you.

Verse 24. Until now you have asked nothing in my name: Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.

Verse 25. These things I have spoken to you in proverbs. The hour comes when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but I will announce to you plainly about the Father.

Verse 26. In that day you will ask in my name: and I do not say to you, that I will ask the Father for you:

Verse 27. For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came forth from God.

Verse 28. I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.

§. V. The disciples' profession concerning Jesus is subjoined.

Verse 29. His disciples say unto him: Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb.

Verse 30. Now we know that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.

§. VI. An admonition concerning the dispersion, with the promise of peace, which they are to have in Jesus' victory over the world.

Verse 31. Jesus answered them: Do ye now believe?

Verse 32. Behold, the hour cometh, and is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

Verse 33. These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

CHAPTER XLII. Περιευχης Christ's prayer. §. I. Jesus prays for his own glorification.

Verse 1. These words spake Jesus: and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:

Vers. 2. As you have given him power over all flesh, that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him.

Vers. 3. And this is eternal life: That they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.

Vers. 4. I have glorified you on earth: I have finished the work which you gave me to do:

Vers. 5. And now glorify me, O Father, with yourself, with the glory which I had with you before the world was.

§. II. He prays for his disciples, that they may be preserved in his name, and be one, and be sanctified in divine truth.

Vers. 6. I have manifested your name to the men whom you gave me out of the world: They were yours, and you gave them to me; and they have kept your word.

Vers. 7. Now they have known that all things, whatsoever you have given me, are from you:

Vers. 8. For the words which you gave me, I have given to them: and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from you, and they have believed that you sent me.

Vers. 9. I pray for them: I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me: because they are yours:

Vers. 10. And all mine are yours, and yours are mine: and I am glorified in them.

Vers. 11. And now I am not in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, whom you have given me: that they may be one, as we also are.

Vers. 12. While I was with them, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me, I have guarded: and none of them has perished, except the son of perdition, that the scripture might be fulfilled.

Vers. 13. But now I come to you: and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.

Vers. 14. I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

Vers. 15. I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one.

Vers. 16. They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

Vers. 17. Sanctify them in the truth. Your word is truth.

Vers. 18. As you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world.

Vers. 19. And for their sake I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in the truth.

§. III. He prays for those who are to believe through the word of the disciples, and that they may be one, and that they may be where he is, and see his glory.

Vers. 20. I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word:

Verse 21. That they all may be one, as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.

Verse 22. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one.

Verse 23. I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.

Verse 24. Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.

Verse 25. O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.

Verse 26. And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare it: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them.

CHAPTER XLIII. The Eucharistic hymn and the prediction of the scandalization of the disciples, and of Peter's denial.

§. I. After the prayer he sang a hymn.

Matt. XXVI. Verse 30. And when they had sung an hymn. Mark XIV. v. 26. And when they had sung an hymn. John XVIII. v. 1. When Jesus had spoken these words. [For so it is held after the prayer of Mark's προαγώνιον (agony). John XVIII. 1. When he had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron: and Matthew and Mark testify that they went out when the hymn was sung. Therefore all these things were still done in the upper room.]

§. II. Then having gone out across the brook Cedron to the Mount of Olives, and there into a garden.

He went out with his disciples across the brook Cedron, where there was a garden, into which he himself and his disciples entered.

§. III. On the way he predicts to the disciples that all will be scandalized in him this night, just as it is written (Zach. XIII. 7.), but that he himself, after the resurrection, will go before them into Galilee.

Matth. XXVI. v. 31. Then Jesus says to them: All you shall be scandalized in me this night. For it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be dispersed. Vers. 32. But after I shall have risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

Marc. XIV. v. 27. And Jesus says to them: You will all be scandalized in me this night, because it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be dispersed. Vers. 28. But after I shall have risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

§. IV. Peter, on the other hand, protests regarding himself: Jesus again predicts that he will deny him three times before the cock crows: Peter, however, says in return that even if he must undergo death, he will not deny Jesus. The others also said similar things.

Matth. XXVI. v. 33. And Peter answering, said to him: Although all shall be scandalized in thee, I will never be scandalized. Vers. 34. But Jesus said to him: Amen I say to thee, that in this night, before the cock crow, thou wilt deny me thrice. Vers. 35. Peter saith to him: Yea, though I should have to die with thee, I will not deny thee. And in like manner said all the disciples.

Marc. XIV. v. 29. But Peter said to him: Although all shall be scandalized in thee, yet not I.

Vers. 31. But he spoke more: Even if it should be necessary for me to die together with you, I will not deny you. And likewise all were saying.

§. II. But he denied before them all (for the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself) saying, I know not what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew. Matt. XXVI. 70. Mark XIV. 68. Luke XXII. 57. John XVIII. 17. 18.

Matt. XXVI. Verse 70. But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.

Mark XIV. Verse 68. But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.

Luke XXII. Verse 57. And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.

John 18:17. He says: I am not.

Verse 18. Now the servants and officers were standing by the coals, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves: and Peter was also with them, standing and warming himself.

[The first cockcrowing was accustomed to happen around the tenth hour: and at that time Peter's first denial took place.

CHAPTER X. Jesus' examination concerning his disciples and doctrine.

§. I. The high priest's interrogation concerning the disciples and concerning the doctrine of Jesus?

Verse 19. The high priest therefore asked Jesus about his disciples, and about his doctrine.

§. II. Jesus answered: I have spoken openly in the synagogue, and in the temple, and I have spoken nothing in secret. Why do you ask me? Ask those who have heard what I have spoken to them.

Verse 20. Jesus answered him: I have spoken openly to the world: I have always taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I have spoken nothing in secret.

Verse 21. Why do you ask me? Ask those who have heard what I have spoken to them: behold, these know what I have said.

CHAPTER XI.

The slap inflicted upon Jesus, and his apology.

§. I. But one of the ministers gave a slap to Jesus, saying: Do you answer the High Priest so?

Vers. 22. And when he had said these things, one of the ministers standing by gave a slap to Jesus, saying: Do you answer the High Priest so?

§. II. What Jesus answered him.

Vers. 23. Jesus answered him: If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why do you strike me?

§. III. For Annas had sent Jesus bound to Caiaphas.

Vers. 24. And Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the High Priest.

CHAPTER XII.

False testimonies against Jesus.

§. I. And the chief priests and all the council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might deliver him to death: and they found none, though many false witnesses had come forward. Matth. XXVI. 59. 60. Marc. XIV. 55. 56.

Matth. XXVI. Vers. 59. And the chief priests, and all the council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might deliver him to death:

Verse 60. And they did not find, when many false witnesses had come forward.

Mark XIV. Verse 55. But the Chief Priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus, so that they might deliver him to death: and they were not finding it.

Verse 56. For many were speaking false testimony against him: and the testimonies were not consistent.

§. II. But finally two false witnesses came, and said: This man said: I am able to destroy the temple of God, and after three days rebuild it. And the Chief Priest rising, said to him: Do you answer nothing to the things which are testified against you? But Jesus was silent. Matthew XXVI. 60. 61. 62. 63. Mark XIV. 57. 58. 59. 60. 61.

Matthew XXVI. Verse 60. But finally two false witnesses came:

Verse 61. And they said: This man said: I am able to destroy the temple of God, and after three days rebuild it.

Verse 62. And the Chief Priest rising, said to him, Do you answer nothing to the things which are testified against you?

Verse 63. But Jesus was silent.

Mark XIV. Verse 57. And certain men rising up were bearing false testimony against him, saying:

Vers. 58. For we have heard him saying: I will destroy this temple made with hands, and within three days I will build another not made with hands.

Vers. 59. And their testimony was not consistent.

CHAPTER XIII.

Jesus is accused of blasphemy by Caiaphas, and is condemned, on account of the confession openly made.

§. I.

§. I. The High Priest adjures Jesus to say whether he is the Son of God. Matt. xxvi. Verse 63. Mark xiv. Verse 61.

Matt. XXVI. Verse 63. And the chief priest said to him: I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us if you are the Christ the Son of God.

Mark XIV. Verse 61. Again the high priest asked him, and said to him: Are you the Christ the son of the Blessed?

§. II. Jesus answered: You have said it: I am. Matt. xxvi. 64. Mark xiv. 62.

Matt. XXVI. Verse 64. Jesus says to him: You have said it:

Mark XIV. Verse 62. But Jesus said to him: I am:

§. III. And you shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of the power of God, and coming with the clouds of heaven. Matt. XXVI. 64. Mark XIV. 62.

Matth. XXVI. Vers. 64. Nevertheless I say to you, hereafter you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

Marc. XIV. Vers. 62. And you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.

§. IV. Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying: He has blasphemed: what further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard the blasphemy; what do you think? Matth. xxvi. 65. 66. Marc. xiv. 63. 64.

Matth. XXVI. Vers. 65. Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying: He has blasphemed; what further need have we of witnesses: behold, now you have heard the blasphemy.

Vers. 66. What do you think?

Marc. XIV. Vers. 63. And the high priest, rending his clothes, says: What further need do we have of witnesses?

Vers. 64. You have heard the blasphemy: what do you think?

§. V. But they answering condemned him, and said: He is guilty of death, Matth. xxvi. 66. Marc. xiv. 64.

Matth. XXVI. Vers. 66. But they answering said: He is guilty of death.

Marc. XIV. Vers. 64. Who all condemned him to be guilty of death.

[Augustine, book III de Cons. Evang. chap. 7, maintains that this condemnation for blasphemy happened only in the morning in the second assembly, which is indeed reported here κεφαλαιωτικῶς by Matthew and Mark: but if we consult Luke, it is better to say that these things happened indeed at night: but in the morning Jesus was examined again, and condemned a second time. Which is also gathered from Matthew ch. XXVII. 1. v. Mark XV. 1.]

CHAPTER XIV. The spitting upon Jesus, the buffeting, and the mockery.

§. I. Then they did spit in his face, and buffeted him. Matth. xxvi. 67. Marc. xiv. 65.

Matth. xxvi. 67. Then they did spit in his face, and buffeted him:

Marc. XIV. Vers. 65. And some began to spit on him.

§. II. And others struck him with the palms of their hands on his face, even the ministers, veiling his face, and saying to him: Prophesy unto us, O Christ, who is he that struck thee. Matth. xxvi. 67. 68. Marc. xiv. 65.

Matth. XXVI. Vers. 67. And others struck him with the palms of their hands on his face,

Ver. 68. Saying: Prophesy to us, O Christ, who is it that struck thee.

Mark XIV. Ver. 65. And to uncover his face, and to strike him with blows: and to say to him: Prophesy. And the servants struck him with blows.

[Which spitting, buffeting, and mockery seems to have been done while the Pharisees, Priests, and Elders of the people were still present and conniving, if not cooperating: who therefore, after they had agreed upon the sentence of death, left Jesus to the lust of the cohort of soldiers, so that the comedy begun by their servants might be continued more freely by these men; but they departed with the condition that they would meet again in the morning in the Sanhedrin.]

CHAPTER XV. Peter's second and third denial, and his repentance.

§. I. And as Peter was going out of the gate, another maid saw him, and said to those who were there: This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth. And again he denied with an oath: That I do not know the man. Matt. XXVI. 71. 72. Mark XIV. 69. 70. Luke XXII. 58. John XVIII. 25.

Matt. XXVI. Ver. 71. And as he was going out of the gate, another maid saw him: and said to those who were there: This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth.

Ver. 72. And again he denied with an oath, that I do not know the man.

Mark XIV. Ver. 69. And when a maid had seen him again, she began to say to the bystanders: That this man is one of them.

Verse 70. But he denied it again.

Luke XXII. Verse 58. And after a little while another seeing him, said: Thou also art one of them. But Peter said: O man, I am not.

John XVIII. Verse 25. And Simon Peter was standing and warming himself; they said therefore to him: Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said: I am not.

§. II. And after a little while, at an interval of about one hour, those who were standing by approached, and said to Peter (one especially of them, a servant of the high priest, a kinsman of him whose ear Peter cut off): Truly thou also art one of them. Did I not see thee in the garden with him? For thou art also a Galilean. Thy speech makes thee manifest. Then he began to curse (to anathematize) and to swear, that he did not know the man: and immediately, while he was yet speaking, the cock crowed again. Matt. XXVI. 73. 74. Mark XIV. 70. 71. 72. Luke XXII. 59. 60. John XVIII. 26. 27.

Matthew XXVI. Verse 73. And after a little while those who were standing by approached, and said to Peter: Truly thou also art one of them: for thy speech also makes thee manifest.

Verse 74. Then he began to curse and to swear, that he did not know the man: and immediately the cock crowed.

Mark XIV. Verse 70. And after a little while those who were standing by said again to Peter: Truly thou art one of them: for thou art also a Galilean.

Verse 71. But he began to anathematize and to swear: I do not know this man of whom you speak.

Verse 72. And immediately the cock crowed a second time.

Luke 22. Verse 59. And after an interval of about one hour, another man affirmed, saying: Truly this man also was with him: for he is also a Galilean.

Verse 60. And Peter said: Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, as he was yet speaking, the cock crew.

John XIII. Verse 26. One of the servants of the high priest, a kinsman to him whose ear Peter cut off, saith to him: Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

Verse 27. Peter therefore denied again: and immediately the cock crew.

§. III. And the Lord turning looked on Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as he had said: Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And going out, he wept bitterly. Matt. XXVI. 75. Mark XIV. 72. Luke XXII. 61. 62.

Matt. XXVI. Verse 75. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus which he had said: Before the cock crow, thou wilt deny me thrice. And going forth, he wept bitterly.

Mark XIV. Verse 72. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said unto him: Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he began to weep.

Luke XXII. Verse 61. And the Lord turning looked on Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as he had said: Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

Verse 62. And Peter went out and wept bitterly.

[Peter's two denials were made around the eleventh and twelfth hour, when the second cockcrowing is accustomed to be heard under μεσονύκτιον.]

CHAPTER XVI. Repeated beatings and mockings of Jesus.

§. I. And they mocked him, beating him: and they blindfolded him, and struck his face.

Verse 63. And the men who held Jesus mocked him, beating him.

Verse 64. And they blindfolded him, and struck his face, and asked him, saying: Prophesy, who is it that struck you.

[Luke teaches that these things happened after Peter's denial, and the final cockcrowing, and by those who were holding Jesus. A similar comedy was acted before by others, and by the ministers, and is now instituted anew, with only the persons changed. Thus, what remained of the night was spent in mockings.]

§. II. And many other blasphemies they spoke against him.

Verse 65. And many other things blaspheming they said against him.

[For with such mockings, beatings, and blasphemies, the soldiers and guards wished to pass the night time and shake sleep from their eyes, until the morning time and the new meeting of the Sanhedrin. And these things pertain to Thursday. Now follow those things which were done on Friday, which for the Jews was the Preparation of the Passover: in which, if it is begun from our sixth hour, these things happened: 1. Proceedings before the Council. 2. Proceedings before Pilate. 3. The leading out and crucifixion of Christ. 4. The consequences.]

CHAPTER XVII. A new Council against Jesus; and a new examination, whether he is the Christ?

§. I. And as it became day (morning having been made) the elders of the people, and the chief priests, and the scribes gathered together, that they might deliver him to death. Matt. xxvii. 1. Mark XV. 1. Luke XXII. 66.

Matt. XXVII. Vers. 1. And when morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to put him to death.

Mark XV. Vers. 1. And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council.

Luke XXII. Vers. 66. And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together.

§. II. And they led him into their council, asking whether he is the Christ?

Vers. 66. And they led him into their council.

Vers. 67. Saying: If thou art the Christ, tell us.

§. III. The response of Christ and the repeated prediction of the sitting at the right hand of God.

Vers. 67. And he said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe me.

Vers. 68. And if I also ask you, you will not answer, nor will you let me go.

Verse 69. From this time on, the Son of man will be sitting at the right hand of the power of God.

§. IV. Being asked whether he is the Son of God, he openly confesses it.

Verse 70. But they all said: Are you then the Son of God? He said: You say that I am.

§. V. Accepting this confession themselves, they desire no other testimony.

Verse 71. But they said: What further testimony do we need? For we have heard it ourselves from his own mouth.

[These things were done in the other examination concerning Jesus, whether he is the Christ, instituted by the High Priest in the morning. For the answer they had received at night, they desired to grasp again in the morning, and Christ did not refuse to render it again, as a faithful confessor: because in it the unity of the matter was situated, and as far as the ὁμολόγησιν (confession) of Christ was concerned, and it was established before his enemies, though with a different end, the former for the salvation of men, the latter for the extermination of the Savior of men. Calvin and Grotius indeed deny that the assessors of this Council had departed, but because Luke openly commemorates that they had gathered again in the morning, there is no doubt that they instituted the Sanhedrin again in the morning, so that they might execute the plan they had begun.]

CHAPTER XVIII. The despair of Judas.

§. I. Judas, seeing that they wanted to lead Jesus away bound, so that they might hand him over to Pilate, and that Jesus had thus been condemned by the council, led by repentance, returned the thirty pieces of silver.

Matt. XXVII. Verse 2. And they led him away bound, and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the Governor.

Verse 3. Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that he was condemned; led by repentance, returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

[Therefore, these things were done while they were still gathered in the council; it is said, however, that their whole multitude rose up and led Jesus to Pilate, Luke XXIII. 1. Which was therefore done after Judas was finished. Therefore, the words of Matthew are to be understood thus: Then, that is, still in the same council.]

§. II. Judas confesses the sin, that he betrayed innocent blood.

Vers. 4. Saying: I have sinned, betraying just blood.

§. III. He is dismissed without consolation.

Vers. 4. But they said: What is that to us? see thou to it.

§. IV. Therefore, having cast down the silver pieces in the temple, he departed, ending his life with a noose.

Vers. 5. And casting down the silver pieces in the temple, he departed, and going away he hanged himself with a noose.

§. V. The chief priests fear to put the silver pieces into the treasury: as the price of blood.

Vers. 6. But the chief priests having taken the silver pieces, said: It is not lawful to put them into the treasury: because it is the price of blood.

§. VI. Therefore they bought with them the potter's field, for the burial of strangers.

Vers. 7. And having taken counsel, they bought with them the potter's field, for the burial of strangers.

Vers. 8. For this cause that field was called Haceldama, that is, the field of blood, even to this day.

§. VII. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy.

Vers. 9. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the Prophet, saying: And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was prized, whom they prized of the children of Israel.

Verse 10. And they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed me.

CHAPTER XIX. JESUS delivered to Pilate.

§. I. The people led Jesus to Pilate Mark 15:1. Luke 23:1 from Caiaphas into the praetorium, and that in the morning John 18:28.

Mark XV. Verse 1. Binding Jesus they led him away and delivered him to Pilate.

Luke XXIII. Verse 1. And the whole multitude of them arising, they led him to Pilate

John XVIII. Verse 28. Then they lead Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium: and it was morning.

§. II. But they did not enter into the praetorium, that they might not be defiled, because of the Passover.

Verse 28. And they themselves did not enter into the praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but that they might eat the Passover.

§. III. Pilate went out to them, and inquired about the points of the accusations.

Ver. 29. Pilate therefore went out to them, and said: What accusation bring you against this man?

§. IV. A general response, that he is a malefactor.

Ver. 30. They answered and said to him: If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to you.

§. V. Pilate commands: that they judge him according to their law.

Ver. 31. Pilate therefore said to them: Take him you, and judge him according to your law:

§. VI. The Jews confess: that it is not lawful for them to condemn anyone to the cross.

Ver. 31. The Jews therefore said: It is not lawful for us to put any man to death.

Ver. 32. That the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he said, signifying what death he was to die.

CHAPTER XX. The accusation of Jesus before Pilate concerning sedition, and his silence.

§. I. Pilate again called Jesus into the Praetorium.

Ver. 33. Pilate therefore went into the praetorium again, and called Jesus.

§. II. But they began to accuse him of

many things, Mark 15:3, as subverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, Luke 23:2.

Mark 15:3. And the chief priests accused him of many things.

Luke 23:2. And they began to accuse him, saying: We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ a King.

§. III. Jesus' silence to those accusations.

Matthew 27:12. And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

§. IV. To Pilate saying, how many things they witness against him? he answered nothing. Matthew 27:13, 14. Mark 15:4, 5.

Matthew 27:13. Then saith Pilate unto him: Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee.

Verse 14. And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.

Mark 15, verse 4. But Pilate asked him again, saying: Do you answer nothing? See how many things they accuse you of.

Verse 5. But Jesus answered nothing more: so that Pilate wondered.

CHAPTER XXI. Jesus' confession to the interrogation of Pilate, and Pilate's testimony of innocence.

§. I. Jesus is interrogated by the Governor, whether he is the King of the Jews? Matt. XXVII. 11. Mark xv. 2. Luke XXIII. 3. John XVIII. 33.

Matthew XXVII. Verse 11. But Jesus stood before the Governor, and the Governor asked him, saying: Are you the King of the Jews?

Mark XV. Verse 2. And Pilate asked him: Are you the King of the Jews?

Luke XXIII. Verse 3. But Pilate asked him, saying: Are you the King of the Jews?

John XVIII. Verse 33. And he called Jesus, and said to him: Are you the King of the Jews?

§. II. He answers: whether he says this of himself, or not?

Vers. 34. Jesus answered: do you say this of yourself, or did others tell you about me?

§. III. Pilate refers this to the Jews: to whom JESUS replies, that his kingdom is not of this world.

Vers. 35. Pilate answered: Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests have delivered you to me: what have you done?

§. IV. To Pilate asking again whether he were a King? Jesus answered, that he altogether professes the truth. John 18. 37. Matthew 27. 11. Mark 15. 2. Luke 23. 3.

John 18. Vers. 37. Pilate therefore said to him: Are you a King then? Jesus answered: you say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, that I should bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth, hears my voice.

Vers. 38. Pilate says to him: What is truth?

Matthew 27. Vers. 11. Jesus says to him: You say it. Mark 15:2. But he answering says to him: You say it.

Luke 23:3. But he answering says: You say it.

§. V. When Jesus had said this, Pilate went out to the Jews, testifying to them that he found no case against him. John 18:38. Luke 23:4.

CHAPTER XXII. The accusation of seduction through false doctrine.

§. I. The Jews cry out that Jesus has stirred up the people with his doctrine.

§. II. Pilate asked whether he was a Galilean, Galilee having been mentioned.

Verse 6. But Pilate, hearing of Galilee, asked if the man were a Galilean.

CHAPTER XXIII. The sending of Jesus to Herod, and his return with a symbol of innocence.

§. I. Pilate sent Jesus back to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at that time.

Verse 7. And when he knew that he was of Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem in those days.

[The Lord was sent to Herod Antipas after the seventh hour of the morning.]

§. II. Herod, hoping for some miracle from Jesus, rejoices and questions him about many things, but receives no answer.

Verse 8. And Herod, seeing Jesus, was very glad: for he was desirous to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him: and he hoped to see some miracle done by him.

CHAPTER XXIV. Pilate, having praised the innocence of Jesus, wishes to release Jesus, but the people urge that he be taken away and Barabbas released instead.

§. I. Pilate, having made a convocation, openly testifies that he finds no cause for the commotion of the people in Jesus, nor does Herod: and therefore he wishes to release him after having chastised him.

Vers. 13. But Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the magistrates and the people.

Vers. 14. He said to them: You have brought this man to me, as one who turns away the people: and behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no cause in this man regarding those things in which you accuse him:

Vers. 15. But neither did Herod: for I sent you back to him: and behold, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.

Vers. 16. I will therefore release him after having chastised him. [This happened at the eighth hour of the morning on Friday.]

§. II. He asks therefore whether they wish Jesus to be released according to the custom of the Feast, or rather Barabbas the murderer? Matt. XXVII. 15. 16. 17. 18. Mark XV. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. Luke XXIII. 17. John XVIII. 39.

Matt. XXVII. Vers. 15. Now on the solemn day the Governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whom they would have.

Vers. 16. And he had then a notable prisoner, who was called Barabbas.

Vers. 17. When they were gathered together, therefore, Pilate said: Whom will you that I release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?

Vers. 18. For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Marc. XV. Vers. 6. Now upon the feast day he was wont to release unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they demanded.

Vers. 7. And there was one named Barabbas, who was bound with them that had made insurrection, who had committed murder in the insurrection.

Vers. 8. And when the multitude had ascended, they began to desire him to do as he had ever done unto them.

Vers. 9. But Pilate answered them, and said: Will you that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

Vers. 10. For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.

Luc. XXIII. Vers. 17. For of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast.

Johan. XIIX. Vers. 39. But you have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the Passover: will you therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

§. III. He is warned by his wife concerning the innocence of JESUS.

Matth. XXVII. Vers. 19. When he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying: Have thou nothing to do with that just man; for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

§. IV. The Jews demand the release of Barabbas. Matth. XXVII. 20. Marc. XV. 11.

Matth. XXVII. Vers. 20. But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitudes that they should ask for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.

Marc. XV. Vers. 11. But the chief priests stirred up the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.

§. V. But the Governor still insists, whom do they wish to be released? But they all cried out: Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas. Luc. XXIII. 18. 19. Matth. XXVII. 21. Joh. XIIX. 40.

Luc. XXIII. Vers. 18. And the whole multitude cried out together, saying: Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas.

Vers. 19. Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.

Matth. XXVII. Vers. 21. But the governor answering said to them: Whether will you have of the two to be released unto you? But they said: Barabbas.

Joh. XIIX. Vers. 40. Then cried they all again, saying: Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.

CHAPTER XXV. Pilate again gives testimony of Jesus' innocence, and wishes to free him, but the people urge with a great shout that he be crucified.

§. I. Pilate wishing to release Jesus again, the people shout that he be crucified. Luke XXIII. 20. 21. Matthew XXVII. 22. Mark XV. 12. 13.

Luke XXIII. Vers. 20. But Pilate spoke to them again, wishing to release Jesus.

Vers. 21. But they shouted back, saying: Crucify, crucify him.

Matthew XXVII. Vers. 22. Pilate said to them: What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ? They all say: Let him be crucified.

Mark XV. Vers. 12. But Pilate answering again, said to them: What then do you want me to do with the King of the Jews?

Vers. 13. But they shouted again: Crucify him.

§. II. Pilate on the other hand testifies to the innocence of Jesus; but the people persist with shouts. Luke XXIII. 22. 23. Matthew XXVII. 23. Mark XV. 14.

Luke 23:22. But he said to them the third time: Why, what evil hath this man done? I find no cause of death in him: I will chastise him therefore, and release him.

Verse 23. But they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified: and their voices prevailed.

Matthew 27:23. And the governor said to them: Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying: Let him be crucified.

Mark 15:14. And Pilate said to them: Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more: Crucify him.

CHAPTER XXVI. Pilate adjudges Christ to death, having nevertheless again borne witness to his innocence.

§. II. Then he released Barabbas unto them: and having scourged Jesus, he delivered him to their will. Matthew 27:26. Mark 15:15. Luke 23:24, 25.

Matthew 27:26. Then he released to them Barabbas: and having scourged Jesus, he delivered him unto them to be crucified.

Mark 15:15. And so Pilate, willing to satisfy the people, released Barabbas unto them: and delivered up Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

Luke XXIII. Vers. 24. And Pilate adjudged that their petition should be granted.

Vers. 25. And he released unto them him who for murder and sedition had been cast into prison, whom they were requesting: but Jesus he delivered to their will.

[At the ninth hour of the morning Jesus was condemned by Pilate, and adjudged to death.]

§. I. But Pilate seeing that he was prevailing nothing, washed his hands before the people, testifying that he was innocent of the blood of this just man, but the people cried out: His blood be upon us, and upon our children.

Matt. XXVII. Vers. 24. But Pilate seeing that he was prevailing nothing, but rather that a tumult was being made, taking water he washed his hands before the people, saying: I am innocent of the blood of this just man: see you to it.

Vers. 25. And the whole people answering said: His blood be upon us and upon our children.

CHAPTER XXVII. The scourging and crowning, and the mocking of Jesus, and the repeated testimony of his innocence.

§. I. Pilate caused Jesus to be scourged.

John XIX. Vers. 1. Then therefore Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.

[Not in his own person, as Bede c. XV. of Mark thought: for this was unseemly for the Governor, but through the lictors.]

§. II. The soldiers, having gathered the whole cohort, took him, and put a scarlet cloak around him, and plaiting a crown of thorns, they placed it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand. Matth. XXVII. 27. 28. 29. Marc. XV. 16. 17. Joh. XIX. 2.

Matth. XXVII. V. 27. Then the soldiers of the Governor taking Jesus into the praetorium, gathered unto him the whole cohort.

Vers. 28. And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak around him:

Vers. 29. And plaiting a crown of thorns, they placed it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand.

Marc. XV. Vers. 16. And the soldiers led him into the courtyard of the praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.

Vers. 17. And they clothe him in purple, and plaiting a crown of thorns, they place it upon him.

Joh. XIX. Vers. 2. And the soldiers plaiting a crown of thorns placed it upon his head, and put a purple garment around him.

§. III. With bended knee they mocked him, and spitting upon him, they struck his head with a reed. Matth. XXVII. 29. 30. Marc. XV. 18. 19. Joh. XIX. 3.

Matt. XXVII. Vers. 29. And bending the knee before him, they mocked him, saying: Hail, King of the Jews.

Vers. 30. And spitting upon him, they took the reed, and struck his head.

Mark XV. Vers. 18. And they began to salute him: Hail, King of the Jews.

Vers. 19. And they struck his head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowing their knees, they worshipped him.

John XIX. Vers. 3. And they came to him, and said: Hail, King of the Jews, and they gave him blows.

[The abduction into the courtyard and the stripping preceded the scourging, as a περιπαρεσκευὴ; the putting on of the cloak, the crowning, and the mockery followed.]

§. IV. Pilate went out again, saying to them: Behold the man.

Vers. 4. Pilate therefore went out again, and says to them: Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no cause in him.

Vers. 5. Jesus therefore went out, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple garment. And he says to them: Behold the man.

CHAPTER XXIX. The repeated clamor of the chief priests that Jesus be crucified, with the accusation of blasphemy.

§. I. The chief priests and ministers, when they saw him, cried out, crucify, crucify him.

Vers. 6. When therefore the chief priests and ministers had seen him, they cried out, saying: Crucify, crucify him.

§. II. Pilate orders them to crucify him themselves; for he finds no cause in him.

Vers. 6. Pilate says to him: Take him you, and crucify him: for I find no cause in him.

§. III. The Jews answered that he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God: upon hearing which Pilate feared the more.

Verse 7. The Jews answered him: We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.

Verse 8. When therefore Pilate had heard this saying, he feared the more.

CHAPTER XXIX. Pilate, having returned into the praetorium, examined Jesus again in order to release him, but, overcome by the clamors of the Jews, he finally handed him over for crucifixion.

§. I. Having entered the praetorium again, (Pilate) asked Jesus, whence are you? But he gave him no answer.

Verse 9. And he entered the praetorium again, and says to Jesus: Whence are you? But Jesus gave him no answer.

§. II. When Pilate appealed to his power, Jesus answered: You would have no power against me, unless it had been given to you from above.

Verse 10. Pilate therefore says to him: Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have power to crucify you, and I have power to release you?

Verse 11. Jesus answered: You would have no power at all against me, unless it had been given to you from above: therefore he who delivered me to you has the greater sin.

§. III. From then on Pilate sought to release him.

Verse 12. From then on Pilate sought to release him.

§. IV. But the Jews cried out: If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar.

Vers. 12. But the Jews cried out, saying: If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.

§. V. Pilate, therefore, out of fear of Caesar, sitting again on the judgment seat in Gabbatha, about the sixth hour of the preparation of the Passover, said to the Jews: Behold your king. But as they cried out that he should crucify him, and Pilate replied, asking if they wished their King to be crucified, they answered: We have no king but Caesar; and therefore he finally handed Jesus over to them, that he might be crucified.

Vers. 13. But when Pilate had heard these words, he brought Jesus out, and sat on the judgment seat in the place that is called Lithostrotos, but in Hebrew Gabbatha.

Vers. 14. And it was the preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour: and he says to the Jews: Behold your King.

Vers. 15. But they cried out: Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate says to them: Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered: We have no king but Caesar.

Vers. 16. Then therefore he handed him over to them, that he might be crucified.

CHAPTER XXX. The leading away of Jesus to crucifixion.

§. I. They put his own clothes on Jesus. Matt. xxvii. 31. Mark xv. 20.

Matt. xxvii. v. 31. And after they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him, and put his own clothes on him:

Mark XV. v. 20. And after they had mocked him, they took the purple off him and put his own clothes on him.

§. II. He is led out to be crucified. Matt. 27:31. Mark 15:20. John 19:16.

Matt. 27:31. And they led him away to crucify him.

Mark 15:20. And they lead him out to crucify him.

[Which was done between the tenth and eleventh hour before noon.

CHAPTER XXXI. The carrying of the cross by Jesus and Simon of Cyrene.

§. I. Bearing the cross, he goes out to the place of Calvary.

John 19:17. And bearing his own cross he went forth into that which is called the place of Calvary, in Hebrew Golgotha.

§. II. But they took a certain man, named Simon, and compelled him to take up his cross. Matt. 27:32. Mark 15:21. Luke 23:26.

Matt. 27:32. And as they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to carry his cross.

Mark 15:21. And they compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene (who was coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus), to carry his cross.

Luke 23:26. And as they led him away, they seized one Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to carry it behind Jesus.

CHAPTER XXXII. The sermon of Jesus delivered to the women lamenting during the procession.

§. I. A great multitude followed him, and women also, who were lamenting.

Verse 27. And there followed him a great multitude of the people and of women, who were mourning and lamenting him.

§. II. He warns them to lament for their own children.

Verse 28. But Jesus turning to them, said: Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me: but weep for yourselves and for your children:

Verse 29. For behold, the days are coming in which they will say: Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that have not borne, and the breasts that have not nursed.

Vers. 30. Then shall they begin to say to the mountains: Fall upon us: and to the hills: Cover us.

Vers. 31. For if in the green wood they do these things, what shall be done in the dry?

CHAPTER XXXIII. The leading away to the place of Calvary.

§. I. He is led to the place of Golgotha.

Mark XV. v. 22. And they bring him into the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, the place of Calvary.

§. II. And with him were led two thieves.

Vers. 32. And there were also two other malefactors led with him, to be put to death.

§. III. At length they came to the place Golgotha.

Matt. XXVII. v. 33. And they came to the place, which is called Golgotha, which is the place of Calvary.

CHAPTER XXXIV. The offering of wine mixed with gall.

§. I. Wine mixed with gall was given to him. Matt. XXVII. 34. Mark xv. 23.

Matt. XXVII. v. 34. And they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall:

Mark XV. v. 23. And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh:

§. II. But when he had tasted it, he would not drink it. Matt. XXVII. 34. Mark xv. 23.

Matt. XXVII. v. 34. And when he had tasted it, he would not drink.

Mark 15:23. And he did not receive

CHAPTER XXXV. The crucifixion of Jesus.

§. I. Coming to the place of Calvary, they crucified him. Luke 23:33. John 19:18. Matthew 27:35. Mark 15:24.

Luke 23:33. And after they came to the place which is called Calvary, there they crucified him.

John 19:18. Where they crucified him.

Matthew 27:35. And after they crucified him.

Mark 15:24. And crucifying him.

§. II. That it was done at the third hour.

Vers. 25. And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

[The third hour from the handing over done by Pilate, which was the very midday, or the twelfth according to our reckoning, as we have taught in the Chronicon.

§. III. There were also crucified with him two thieves. Matth. XXVII. 38. Marc. xv. 27. 28. Luc. XXIII. 33. Joh. XIX. 18.

Matth. XXVII. v. 38. Then were two thieves crucified with him: one on the right hand, and one on the left.

Marc. xv. v. 27. And with him they crucify two thieves: the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.

Vers. 28. And the Scripture was fulfilled, which saith: And he was numbered with the transgressors.

Luc. XXIII. v. 33. And the thieves, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

John 19:18. And with him two others on this side and that, but Jesus in the middle.

CHAPTER XXXVI. The placing of the title.

§. I. And Pilate also wrote a title, and placed it upon the cross: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews. John 19:19. Matt. 27:37. Mark 15:26. Luke 23:38.

John 19:19. And Pilate also wrote a title, and placed it upon the cross. And it was written: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.

Matt. 27:37. And they placed over his head his cause written: This is Jesus the King of the Jews.

Mark 15:26. And the title of his cause was inscribed: KING OF THE JEWS.

Luke 23:38. And there was also a superscription written over him in Greek and Latin and Hebrew letters: This is the King of the Jews.

§. II. This title therefore many of the Jews read, written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.

Ver. 20. Many of the Jews therefore read this title: because the place where Jesus was crucified was near to the city. And it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.

Ver. 21. The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate: Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.

Ver. 22. Pilate answered: What I have written, I have written.

CHAPTER XXXVII. Prayer for his crucifiers.

§. I. But Jesus prayed that the Father would forgive them.

Luke xxiii. Ver. 34. But Jesus was saying: Father, forgive them:

§. II. Because they know not what they do.

Ver. 34. For they know not what they do.

CHAPTER XXXVIII. The division of the garments.

§. II. And after they had crucified him, they divided his garments, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet (Psalm XXII. 19.) Matth. XXVII. 35. Mark XV. 24. Luke xxiii. 34. John xix. 24.

Matt. XXVII. 35. They divided his garments, casting lots, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet saying: They divided my garments among themselves, and upon my vesture they cast lots.

Mark XV. v. 24. They divided his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.

Luke xxiii. v. 34. And dividing his garments they cast lots.

John xix. v. 23. The soldiers therefore, when they had crucified him, took his garments (and made four parts, to every soldier a part) and also his coat.

§. II. But concerning the coat, because it was seamless, they cast lots.

Vers. 23. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

Vers. 24. They said therefore one to another: Let us not rend it, but let us cast lots for it, whose it shall be. That the Scripture might be fulfilled, saying: They have parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture they have cast lots. And the soldiers indeed did these things.

§. III. After the division of the garments, Jesus is kept on the cross.

Matt. 27:36. And sitting down they watched him.

CHAPTER XXXIX. The mocking and blaspheming of the crucified Jesus.

§. I. And they that passed by blasphemed him. Matt. 27:39, 40. Mark 15:29, 30.

Matt. 27:39. And they that passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads.

Verse 40. And saying: Ah, thou that destroyest the temple of God, and in three days buildest it up again, save thyself: if thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

Mark 15:29. And they that passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying: Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and in three days buildest it up again.

Verse 30. Save thyself, coming down from the cross.

§. II. Similarly also the Chief Priests with the Scribes and Elders. Matt. XXVII. 41. 42. 43. Mark XV. 31. 32.

Matt. XXVII. v. 41. Similarly also the chief priests mocking with the Scribes and Elders, said:

Vers. 42. He saved others, himself he cannot save: if he is the king of Israel, let him descend now from the cross, and we will believe him.

Vers. 43. He trusted in God, let him deliver him now if he wants: For he said: Because I am the Son of God.

Mark XV. v. 31. Similarly also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the Scribes said: He saved others, himself he cannot save.

Vers. 32. Let Christ the king of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe.

§. III. Thus also the people watching mocked him.

Luke XXIII. v. 35. And the people stood watching, and the princes with them mocked him, saying: He saved others, let him save himself, if this is Christ the chosen of God. [Inverted speech: for according to the decree of God set forth in Holy Scripture it should be established thus: Because he is the chosen Christ of God, he ought to save others, but not save himself from the cross, but complete the business of redemption.]

§. IV. The soldiers also mocked him, offering him vinegar.

Vers. 36. And the soldiers also mocked him, coming and offering him vinegar:

Vers. 37. And saying: If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself. [He joined this mockery with the similar mockery of the people, even though it did not happen immediately, but a little while after it, as we learn from John.]

§. V. As also the thieves crucified with him. Matt. XXVII. 44. Mark XV. 32. Luke XXIII. 39.

Matt. XXVII. v. 44. And the thieves also, who were crucified with him, reproached him.

Mark XV. v. 32. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.

Luke XXIII. v. 39. And one of those thieves who hung there blasphemed him, saying: If you are the Christ, save yourself and us. [Synecdoche: it is either an enallage of number in Matthew and Mark, when they report of two thieves what one of them did.]

CHAPTER XL. The conversion of the thief on the cross.

§. I. But the other answering, rebuked the other.

Vers. 40. But the other answering, rebuked him, saying: Do you not fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?

Vers. 41. And we indeed justly: for we receive the due rewards of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

§. II. He asked of Jesus that he would be mindful of him in his kingdom.

Vers. 42. And he said unto Jesus: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom.

§. III. To whom Jesus promised paradise.

Vers. 43. And Jesus said unto him: Amen I say to thee, this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.

CHAPTER XLI. Jesus commends John to his mother, and his mother to John.

§. I. Jesus seeing his mother, and the disciple whom he loved, saith to his mother: Woman, behold thy son.

John XIX. v. 25. Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.

Vers. 26. When Jesus therefore had seen his mother and the disciple standing, whom he loved, he saith to his mother: Woman, behold thy son.

§. II. But he commended his mother to his disciple, who immediately took her into his own.

Vers. 27. After that, he saith to the disciple, Behold thy mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own.

CHAPTER XLII. The complaint of Jesus on the cross during the greatest eclipse of the Sun.

§. I. Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land, unto the ninth hour. Matt. XXVII. 45. Mark XV. 33. Luke XXIII. 44. 45.

Matt. XXVII. v. 45. Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land, unto the ninth hour.

Mark XV. v. 33. And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.

Luke XXIII. v. 44. And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.

Verse 45. And the sun was darkened.

§. II. About the ninth hour Jesus cried out: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? Matt. XXVII. 46. Mark XV. 34.

Matt. XXVII. v. 46. And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

Mark 15:34. And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me.

§. III. But some standing there said: This man calleth Elias. Matt. 27:47. Mark 15:35.

Matt. 27:47. But some standing there, and hearing, said: This man calleth Elias.

Mark 15:35. And some of the bystanders hearing said: Behold he calleth Elias.

CHAPTER XLIII. The thirst of Jesus and the drinking on the cross.

§. I. Afterwards that the Scripture might be fulfilled (Ps. 69:22) Jesus cried out: I thirst.

John 19:28. Afterwards Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, saith: I thirst.

§. II. But they offered a sponge full of vinegar to his mouth. John 19:29. And offering it he said: Let be, let us see if Elias will come to take him down, Matt. 27:48. Mark 15:36. such as others also seem to have said Matt. 27:49.

John XIX. v. 29. A vessel therefore was set full of vinegar. And they putting a sponge full of vinegar about hyssop, offered it to his mouth.

Matt. XXVII. v. 48. And immediately one of them running, having taken a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

Ver. 53. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they came into the holy city, and appeared to many.

Mark XV. v. 36. And one running, and filling a sponge with vinegar, and putting it about a reed, gave him to drink, saying: Let us see if Elias comes to take him down.

CHAPTER II. The conversion of the centurion under the cross.

§. I. The centurion struck with fear.

Matt. XXVII. v. 49. But the others said: Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to deliver him.

Ver. 54. Now the centurion, and they that were with him watching Jesus, having seen the earthquake, and the things that were done, were greatly afraid.

CHAPTER LXIV. It is consummated.

§. II. The centurion converted, and confessing the Son of God. Matt. XXVII. 54. Mark XV. 39. Luke XXIII. 47.

§. Single. Having received the vinegar he exclaimed: It is finished.

Matt. XXVII. v. 54. Saying: Truly this was the Son of God.

John XIX. v. 30. When therefore Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: It is finished.

Mark XV. v. 39. And the centurion, who stood over against him, seeing that he so crying out had expired, said: Truly this man was the Son of God.

CHAPTER XLV. The last word of Jesus on the cross, and his death.

Luke XXIII. v. 47. And the centurion seeing what had been done, glorified God, saying: Truly this man was just.

§. I. Finally, crying with a loud voice, Jesus commended his Spirit to the Father.

CHAPTER III. The πάθη (sufferings/passions) of others.

Luke XXIII. v. 46. And Jesus crying with a loud voice said: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

§. I. The crowd struck their breasts.

Vers. 48. And all the crowd of them that were together at that sight, and saw the things that were done, returned striking their breasts.

§. II. And thus Jesus expired. Luke XXIII. 46. Matthew XXVII. 50. Mark XV. 37. John XIX. 30.

Luke XXIII. v. 46. And saying these things, he expired.

§. II. Women looking on from afar. Luke XXIII. 49. Matthew XXVII. 55. 56. Mark XV. 40. 41.

Matthew XXVII. v. 50. And Jesus again crying with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

Vers. 49. All his acquaintance stood afar off; and the women, who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.

Mark 15:37. But Jesus, having cried out with a loud voice, breathed his last.

John 19:30. And bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.

Matthew 27:55. And there were many women there looking on from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him:

Verse 56. Among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

[The Lord died on the cross at the ninth hour, as the Jews count it, which is our third hour in the afternoon, so that he hung on the cross for three hours.

Mark 15:40. There were also women looking on from afar: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joseph, and Salome.

TITLE II. THE CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEATH OF THE LORD, ESPECIALLY HIS BURIAL.

Verse 41. And when he was in Galilee, they followed him and ministered to him, and many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.

CHAPTER I. Miracles immediately following the death of Christ.

CHAPTER IV. The opening of Jesus' side.

§. I. The rending of the veil. Matt. XXVII. 51. Mark XV. 38. Luke XXIII. 45.

Matt. XXVII. v. 51. And behold, the veil of the temple was rent in two parts, from the top even to the bottom.

Mark XV. v. 38. And the veil of the temple was rent in two, from the top even to the bottom.

Luke XXIII. v. 45. And the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.

§. II. The soldiers, having broken the legs of the thieves, when they saw that Jesus was already dead, did not break his legs.

§. II. Earthquake.

Matt. XXVII. v. 51. And the earth did quake:

Ver. 32. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him:

§. III. The rending of the rocks.

Ver. 51. And the rocks rent.

§. IV. The opening of the graves, that the bodies might come forth.

Ver. 33. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs.

Ver. 52. And the graves were opened: and many bodies of the saints which slept, arose.

§. III. But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.

Ver. 34. But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately there came out blood and water.

Ver. 35. And he who saw it has borne witness, and his witness is true: and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.

§. IV. Which things were done so that the Scripture Exod. XII. 46. might be fulfilled, as also Zech. XII. 10.

Ver. 36. For these things were done, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: You shall not break a bone of it.
