CHAPTER V.

The burial of JESUS.

§. I. Joseph of Arimathea begged the body of Jesus from Pilate. Matt. XXVII. 57. 58. Mark xv. 42. 43. 44. 45. Luke XXIII. 50. 51. 52. John XIX. 38.

Matt. XXVII. v. 57. When it was evening, there came a certain rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who himself also was a disciple of Jesus.

Ver. 58. This man went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given.

Mark 15:42. And when evening had now come (because it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath.)

Verse 43. Joseph of Arimathea, a noble councilor, came, who himself was also waiting for the kingdom of God: and he went in boldly to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.

Verse 44. But Pilate wondered if he had already died; and having summoned the centurion, he asked him if he were already dead.

Verse 45. And when he had learned it from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

Luke 23:50. And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a councilor, a good and just man:

Verse 51. He had not consented to their counsel and deeds, from Arimathea, a city of Judea, who himself was also waiting for the kingdom of God.

Verse 52. This man went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.

John 19:38. And after these things, Joseph of Arimathea (because he was a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one for fear of the Jews) asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave permission.

§. II. He came therefore and took the body of Jesus. And Nicodemus also came with him, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes.

Ver. 38. He came therefore and took the body of JESUS.

Ver. 39. And Nicodemus also came (who had come to Jesus at night at the first) bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.

§. III. Joseph wrapped the body of Jesus in a clean linen cloth. Matt. XXVII. 59. Mark XV. 46. Luke XXIII. 53. John XIX. 40.

Matt. XXVII. v. 59. And Joseph having taken the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.

Mark XV. v. 46. And Joseph having bought a linen cloth and taking him down, wrapped him in the linen cloth.

Luke XXIII. v. 53. And having taken it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth.

John XIX. v. 40. They took therefore the body of Jesus, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.

§. IV. And he placed it in his own tomb. Matt. XXVII. 60. Mark XV. 46. Luke XXIII. 53. John XIX. 41. 42.

Matt. 27:60. And he laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out of the rock:

Mark 15:46. And he laid him in a tomb, which had been hewn out of the rock.

Luke 23:53. And he laid it in a hewn tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.

John 19:41. Now there was in the place where he was crucified a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.

Verse 42. There therefore, because of the Jewish Preparation Day, since the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus.

[The burial of Christ took place at the tenth hour according to the Jewish reckoning, which is our fourth hour in the afternoon: so that two hours still remained for the first day of the burial: from which until the fourth hour of the Lord's day, when he rose, thirty-six hours are counted according to Augustine, Lib. IV. de Trinit. cap. 6. For how many hours Jonah was also in the belly of the whale, as Isidore of Pelusium notes, l. c. Epist. cxlv.]

§. V. And having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, he departed. Matt. 27:60. Mark 15:46. Luke 23:54.

Matt. 27:60. And he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, and departed.

Mark 15. v. 46. And he rolled a stone to the door of the sepulchre.

Luke 23. v. 54. And it was the day of the Preparation, and the sabbath drew on.

§. VI. And the women who had followed after saw the sepulchre, and how his body was laid. Luke 23. v. 55. Matt. 27. 61. Mark 15. 47.

Luke 23. v. 55. And the women also, which came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulchre, and how his body was laid.

Matt. 27. v. 61. And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

Mark 15. v. 47. And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.

CHAPTER VI. The sealing of the sepulchral stone.

§. I. The chief priests and Pharisees ask for Jesus' sepulchre to be guarded.

Matt. XXVII. v. 62. Now the next day, that followed the day of preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,

Ver. 63. Saying: Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive: After three days I will rise again.

Ver. 64. Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day: lest perhaps his disciples come, and steal him away, and say unto the people: He is risen from the dead: and the last error shall be worse than the first.

§. II. Which being obtained, they also seal the stone.

Ver. 65. Pilate said to them: You have a guard: go, guard it as you know how. Ver. 66. But they going, secured the sepulchre, sealing the stone with the guards.

§. III. The women returned from the monument.

Luke XXIII. v. 56. And returning. [That they, full of grief, immediately thought about anointing Jesus, does not seem likely to B. Bugenhagen & B. Gerhard, and the setting of the sun was already imminent: and scarcely three hours remained until the solemn Sabbath would dawn or begin. Thus far, therefore, those things which were done on the day of Friday, which we call, or the day of Christ's παρασκευῆς. The day of rest, or the Sabbath, follows.]

tus, when the sting of death was crushed, and the darkness of it illuminated by the rising Lord of heavenly powers, the trembling of the underworld is stirred. Chrysologus in Sermon LXXIV. The earth trembled, because the Ruler ascended from the underworld, Chaos is moved, the depths of the earth are split apart, the earth fears, the weights of the mountains tremble, the foundations of the world are shaken, Tartarus is seized, the infernal regions are brought to a halt, death is brought forward, which, reaching out against the guilty, ran into the Judge; having dominated the servants, it raged against the Lord; raging against men, it leaped upon God. That Christ rose at dawn, and around the rising of the sun, Jerome Epist. CL. to Hedibia q. 4, Augustine in Ps. LVI. 9, Eusebius l. 1. demonstr. Evangel. c. last, Bede and others establish.

CHAPTER VII. The rest of the Sabbath.

§. I. But on the Sabbath the women rested.

Ver. 56. And on the Sabbath indeed they rested according to the commandment. [On which the Lord Jesus also rested in the sepulchre, who earned eternal rest for us.]

§. II. The rolling away of the stone done by the Angel.

Ver. 2. For an Angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and approaching, rolled back the stone, and was sitting upon it. [Not because of Christ's resurrection, but because of the manifestation of Christ's resurrection. For therefore the Angel, having rolled back the stone, sat upon it, so that he might teach that Christ had risen. For the resurrection had already taken place before the stone was rolled back, as Calvin admits in his Harmony of the Gospels, that Christ had risen before the sepulchre was opened by the angel. And with great consensus the ancients teach that Christ rose while the sepulchre was still closed. See what [is written] at Matt. XXVIII. 2.]

ARTICLE II. THE HISTORY OF THE RESURRECTION AND THE APPEARANCES OF THE LORD.

CHAPTER I. The women procure and prepare spices for the anointing of Jesus.

§. I. When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, Mary of James, and Salome procured spices, that they might anoint Jesus. Mark 16:1. Then they prepared the spices and ointments, Luke 23:56.

§. III. The appearance of the angel and the terror of the guards.

Verse 3. His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing like snow. Verse 4. And for fear of him the guards were terrified, and became as dead men.

CHAPTER III. The journey of the women to the sepulcher, and the appearance, and the address made by the angel to the women.

Mark 16:1. And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary of James, and Salome bought spices, that coming they might anoint Jesus. Luke 23:56. They prepared spices and ointments. [St. Luke indeed says 'and returning (from the tomb) they prepared spices,' but not in the sense that this was done immediately after they returned: for he does not add a determination of time: nor does that brief space between the burial of Jesus and the setting of the sun admit of it; rather, Luke explains himself with the following words: 'and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment': implying that that preparation was made when the Sabbath was past, just as St. Mark teaches, finally διαγενομένε Σαββάτε the women procured the spices.

§. I. The week being finished, when the light of the first day of the week first showed itself, the women run out very early to the sepulcher, carrying the spices which they had prepared, Matt. 28:1. Mark 16:2. Luke 24:1. John 20:1.

Matt. 28:1. In the end of the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulcher. Mark 16:2. And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they come unto the sepulcher, the sun being now risen. Luke 24:1. Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulcher, bringing the spices which they had prepared. John 20:1. The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulcher: and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulcher. [Καί τινες σὺν ἀυταῖς: which words the Latin Vulgate rashly omits.

CHAPTER II. The earthquake, and the stone rolled away from the sepulcher by the angel.

§. II. The concern of the women regarding the sepulchral stone.

§. I. The earthquake.

Matt. XXVIII. v. 2. And behold, there was a great earthquake.

Mark XVI. v. 3. And they said among themselves: Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the monument? Vers. 4. And looking, they saw the stone rolled back: for it was very great.

The time of the same is not expressly stated: but it is gathered from Matthew that it preceded the arrival of the women at the sepulcher: who found the Angel already sitting upon the rolled-back stone. In this earthquake, Blessed Luther judges that Jesus descended to the underworld, and rose again from the dead. Hilary, ch. XXXIII. on Matthew, near the end: The shaking of the earth at the morning hour of the Lord's day is a sign of the resurrection

§. III. Mary's running to Peter.

John XX. v. 2. She ran therefore and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved.

§. IV. The entry of the others into the sepulcher. The sight and speech of the angel. Matt. XXVIII. 5. 6. 7. Mark XVI. 5. 6. 7. Luke XXIV. 3-8.

Matt. XXVIII. Vers. 5. And the angel answering, said to the women: Fear not you: for I know that you seek Jesus, who was crucified.

Vers. 6. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was laid.

Vers. 7. And going quickly, tell ye his disciples that he is risen: and behold he will go before you into Galilee; there you shall see him: lo, I have foretold it to you.

Mark XVI. Vers. 5. And entering into the sepulcher, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed with a white robe: and they were astonished.

Vers. 6. Who saith to them: Be not affrighted; you seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified: he is risen, he is not here, behold the place where they laid him.

Vers. 7. But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, as he told you.

Luke XXIV. Vers. 3. And entering in, they found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

Vers. 4. And it came to pass, as they were astonished in their mind about this, behold, two men stood by them in shining apparel.

Vers. 5. But as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them: Why seek ye the living among the dead.

Vers. 6. He is not here, but is risen: Remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee.

Saying: That the Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified: and the third day rise again.

And they remembered his words.

[Whether it was the same Angel who had rolled back the stone, or another, matters little; at least the women do not seem to have seen him sitting upon the stone, otherwise Mary Magdalene would also have seen the same one, indeed the others entering at last, by the testimony of Mark, saw that preaching Angel, or rather two Angels, of whom one of them preached to them, as is to be gathered from Luke by comparison. I would judge it more probable, however, that that Angel seen by the guards was different from these two who were seen by the women, just as their duties, which they performed, were different, and the form of their appearance was different: since the aspect of the former was terrible; but these two men appeared in shining raiment, or, as Mark has it, in a white robe, not to terrify and put to flight, but to raise up the dismayed women and send them away to the disciples.]

§. V. They went out from the monument with haste to the disciples. Matth. XXVIII. v. 8. Marc. XVI. 8.

Matth. XXVIII. Vers. 8. And they went out quickly from the monument with fear and great joy.

Marc. XVI. Vers. 8. But they going out, fled from the monument: for trembling and fear had invaded them, and they said nothing to any man: for they were afraid.

CHAPTER IV. The running of Peter and John to the sepulchre, as also Mary Magdalene. §. I. Mary Magdalene complains to Peter and John about the Lord having been taken away.

John 20:2. And she says to them: They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.

§. II. They run to the tomb. Luke 24:12. John 20:3, 4.

Luke 24:12. But Peter rising ran to the tomb.

John 20:3. Peter therefore went out, and that other disciple, and they came to the tomb.

Verse 4. And they were both running together: and that other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the tomb.

§. III. John sees only the linen cloths.

Verse 5. And when he had stooped down, he saw the linen cloths lying, yet he did not enter.

§. IV. Which Peter also saw alone with the napkin John 20:6, 7, 8, 9. Luke 24:12.

John 20:6. Simon Peter therefore came following him, and entered into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths lying.

Vers. 7. And the napkin that had been upon his head, not placed with the linen cloths, but wrapped up separately in one place.

Vers. 8. Then therefore that disciple also entered, who had come first to the monument, and saw, and believed.

Vers. 9. For they did not yet know the Scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

Luc. XXIV. Vers. 12. And stooping down he saw the linen cloths laid by themselves.

§. V. These things having been seen, they depart again. Joh. XX. 10. Luc. XXIV. 12.

Joh. XX. Vers. 10. The disciples therefore went away again to their own home.

Luc. XXIV. Vers. 12. And he went away, wondering with himself at what had happened.

[Which Luke related there according to ὕστερον πρότερον as if it happened after the apparition of Jesus, which had happened to the women: which however it is certain finally happened after the apparition with which the Lord deigned to favor Mary Magdalene, inasmuch as it was the first of all the apparitions of JESUS after the resurrection.]

§. VI. But Mary weeps at the monument.

John 20. Verse 11. But Mary stood at the tomb outside, weeping:

[She had therefore returned with those disciples to the tomb, inasmuch as from it, upon her first excursion, she had indicated to them that the stone had been taken away from the tomb, and the Lord taken away John 20. 2.

CHAPTER V. The angelic apparition made to Mary.

§. I. Two angels appear to Mary.

Verse 11. While therefore she was weeping, she stooped down, and looked into the tomb,

Verse 12. And she saw two angels in white, sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been placed.

§. II. They ask about the cause of her weeping.

Verse 13. They say to her: Woman, why do you weep? She says to them: Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.

CHAPTER VI. The apparition of JESUS made to Mary Magdalene.

§. I. JESUS appears to Mary, but is believed to be the gardener. John 20. v. 14. 15. Mark 16. v. 9.

John 20. Verse 14. When she had said these things, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing: and she did not know that it was Jesus.

Verse 15. Jesus says to her: Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking? She, thinking that he was the gardener, says to him: Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.

Mark 16:9. Now when he rose early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

§. II. But being recognized by her when he addresses her by her own name, Mary, he does not wish to be touched by her; he sends her to his brothers.

Verse 16. Jesus says to her: Mary. She turned and says to him, Rabboni, which is called Teacher.

Verse 17. Jesus says to her: Do not touch me: for I have not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brothers, and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.

§. III. Who announces to the disciples that she has seen the LORD. John 20:18. Mark 16:10.

John 20:18. Mary Magdalene came announcing to the disciples: That I have seen the Lord, and these things he said to me.

Mark 16:10. She went and announced it to those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.

§. IV. But they themselves did not believe him.

Vers. 11. And they, hearing that he was alive, and had been seen by her, did not believe.

CHAPTER VII. The appearance of JESUS made to other women returning from the sepulcher.

§. I. And behold, (as the women were running to announce the angelic vision to the disciples) Jesus met them.

Matth. XXVIII. Vers. 8. Running to announce to his disciples.

Vers. 9. And behold Jesus met them, saying: Hail. But they approached, and held his feet, and worshipped him.

§. II. He sent them that they ought to announce it to the brethren.

Vers. 10. Then Jesus said to them: Do not be afraid. Go, announce to my brethren, that they may go into Galilee, there they shall see me.

Luc. XXIV. Vers. 9. And returning from the monument, they announced all these things to those eleven, and to all the others.

Vers. 10. Now it was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary of James, and the others who were with them, who told these things to the Apostles.

Vers 11. And these words seemed to them as nonsense, and they did not believe them.

CHAPTER VIII. The lie suggested to the guards concerning the body of Jesus being stolen away.

§. I. The report of the guards to the Priests.

Matth. XXVIII. V. 11. And when they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city, and reported to the chief priests all that had been done.

§. II. The council held concerning it, and its conclusion.

Vers. 12. And having gathered with the Elders, after taking counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,

Vers. 13. Saying: Say, that his disciples came by night, and stole him away while we were sleeping.

Vers. 14. And if this should be heard by the Governor, we will persuade him, and make you secure.

§. III. The execution of the conclusion.

Verse 15. But they, having taken the money, did as they were instructed, and this report has been spread among the Jews even to this day.

CHAPTER IX. The apparition of Jesus made to the disciples at Emmaus.

§. I. The apparition of Jesus in an unknown form. Mark xvi. 12. Luke xxiv. 13-16.

Mark XVI. Verse 12. After this, however, he was manifested in another form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country.

Luke XXIV. Verse 13. And behold, two of them were going on that very day to a village, which was at a distance of sixty stadia from Jerusalem, named Emmaus.

Verse 14. And they were talking to each other about all these things which had happened.

Verse 15. And it came to pass that while they were talking and questioning together, Jesus himself drew near and went with them.

Verse 16. But their eyes were held so that they did not recognize him.

§. II. The conversation instituted with the disciples.

Verse 17. And he said to them: What are these words which you are exchanging with each other, as you walk, and are sad?

Vers. 18. And one answering whose name was Cleophas, said to him: Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things that have been done there in these days?

Vers. 19. To whom he said, What things? And they said: Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet, mighty in work and word before God and all the people:

Vers. 20. And how our chief priests and princes delivered him to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

Vers. 21. But we hoped, that it was he that should have redeemed Israel: and now besides all this, today is the third day since these things were done.

Vers. 22. Yea and certain women also of our company affrighted us, who before it was light were at the sepulchre,

Vers. 23. And not finding his body, came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.

Vers. 24. And some of our people went to the sepulchre, and found it so as the women had said, but him they found not.

§. III. Their rebuke and instruction.

Vers. 25. And he said to them: O foolish, and slow of heart to believe in all things which the prophets have spoken!

Vers. 26. Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and so to enter into his glory?

§. IV. Interpretation of the Scripture of Moses and the Prophets.

Vers. 27. And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded to them in all the scriptures, the things that were concerning him.

§. V. Jesus is asked to stay with the disciples.

Vers. 28. And they drew near to the village whither they were going: and he made as though he would go further.

Vers. 29. And they constrained him, saying: Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is now far spent. And he went in with them.

§. VI. He is recognized when he blessed and broke the bread: and he vanishes.

Vers. 30. And it came to pass, while he sat at meat with them, he took bread and blessed and brake, and gave to them.

Vers. 31. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him: and he vanished out of their sight.

§. VII. Those disciples hasten to the Apostles, and there they hear that the Lord had appeared to Simon.

Vers. 32. And they said one to another: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the Scriptures?

Vers. 33. And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem: and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,

Vers. 34. Saying: The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.

[The prior appearance, therefore, was that which was made to Simon: inasmuch as it had already been reported to the other Apostles: although it does not exist described ἀξιωματικῶς, only indicated here and in 1 Cor. xv. 4 by a word.]

§. VIII. And they report the apparition made to them. Luke xxiv. 35. Mark xvi. 13.

Luke XXIV. Vers. 35. And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

Mark XVI. Vers. 13. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them.

[Although therefore they professed: The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon, yet they did not embrace it with full faith, but either reported it historically, or were very doubtful, and hesitated: because it is openly said here that they did not believe, and a little later they are rebuked for their unbelief. Mark XVI. 1.

CHAPTER X.

The apparition of JESUS made to the disciples, Thomas being absent.

§. I. Lastly (on that day of the resurrection) JESUS appeared to the disciples gathered in Jerusalem, the doors being shut. Mark xvi. 14. Luke xxiv. 36. John xx. 19.

Mark XVI. Vers. 14. Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat,

Luke XXIV. Vers. 36. While they were speaking these things, JESUS stood in the midst of them, and said to them: Peace be to you: it is I, fear not.

John XX. Vers. 19. When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut, where the disciples were gathered together for fear of the Jews, JESUS came, and stood in the midst, and says to them: Peace be to you.

§. II. When he was believed to be a ghost, he showed them his hands and feet, upbraiding them for their incredulity. Luke xxiv. 37. 38. 39. 40. Mark xvi. 14. John xx. 20.

Luke XXIV. Vers. 37. But they being troubled and terrified supposed that they saw a spirit.

Vers. 38. And he says to them: Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?

Vers. 39. See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle, and see: for a spirit has not flesh and bones, as you see me have.

Vers. 40. And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

Mark XVI. Vers. 14. And he upbraided them with their incredulity and hardness of heart: because they did not believe them who had seen him after he was risen.

John 20:20. And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side.

It is apparent from this that what the women, Simon, and the disciples from Emmaus reported, was interpreted by them as nothing other than that some apparition or spirit had appeared to them.

§. III. In order to confirm those who were wavering, he took food in their presence.

Luke 24:41. And while they still did not believe for joy, he said: Have you anything here to eat?

Verse 42. And they offered him a piece of a broiled fish, and a honeycomb.

Verse 43. And when he had eaten before them, taking the leftovers he gave them to them.

§. IV. He opened their understanding of the Scripture, from which joy arose. Luke 24:44-48. John 20:20.

Luke 24:44. And he said to them: These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and in the Prophets, and in the Psalms concerning me.

Verse 45. Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures,

Vers. 46. And he said to them: Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead the third day:

Vers. 47. And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name unto all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

Vers. 48. And you are witnesses of these things.

Joh. XX. Vers. 20. The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord.

§. V. The mission of the Apostles.

Vers. 21. JESUS therefore said to them again: Peace be to you. As the Father hath sent me, I also send you.

§. VI. The breathing of the Holy Spirit and the granting of the power to remit and retain sins.

Vers. 22. When he had said this, he breathed on them; and he said to them: Receive ye the Holy Ghost.

Vers. 23. Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them; and whose sins you shall retain, they are retained.

CHAPTER XL

The appearance of Jesus with Thomas present.

§. I. Thomas's incredulity.

Vers. 24. But Thomas, one of the twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

Vers. 25. The other disciples therefore said to him: We have seen the Lord. But he said to them: Unless I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.

§. II. Thomas's conversion, and confession.

Verse 26. And after eight days, his disciples were again inside, and Thomas with them. Jesus came, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said: Peace be to you.

Verse 27. Then he says to Thomas: Reach hither thy finger, and see my hands, and bring hither thy hand, and put it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

Verse 28. Thomas answered and said to him: My Lord, and my God.

Verse 29. Jesus says to him: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed.

§. III. The end of Christ's miracles. John XX. 30. 31. Acts I. 3.

John XX. Verse 30. Many other miracles indeed did Jesus in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book.

Verse 31. But these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, and that believing, you may have life in his name.

Acts I. Verse 3. To whom also he showed himself alive after his passion by many proofs, appearing to them for forty days, and speaking of the kingdom of God. [But especially for the third time he manifested himself to certain disciples from Galilee, concerning which it now follows.]

CHAPTER XII.

The manifestation of Jesus at the Sea of Tiberias.

§. I. Jesus appears to the fishing disciples.

John XXI. Verse 1. After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias: and he manifested himself in this way:

Verse 2. There were together Simon Peter and Thomas, who is called Didymus, and Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.

Verse 3. Simon Peter says to them: I am going fishing. They say to him: We are coming with you too. And they went out and climbed into the boat: and that night they caught nothing.

Verse 4. But when morning had now come, Jesus stood on the shore: yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.

§. II. He is recognized by the miracle of the fish caught.

Verse 5. Jesus therefore says to them: Children, do you have any food? They answered him: No.

Verse 6. He says to them: Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it in because of the multitude of the fish.

Ver. 7. That disciple therefore, whom JESUS loved, said to Peter: It is the LORD. Simon Peter, when he had heard that it is the LORD, girt his coat about him (for he was naked) and cast himself into the sea.

Ver. 8. But the other disciples came in the ship (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits) dragging the net with fishes.

§. III. A new miracle of the fish placed upon the coals, and of the bread found.

Ver. 9. As soon then as they were come to land, they saw coals of fire laid, and fish laid thereon, and bread.

§. IV. The number of the fish caught.

Ver. 10. Jesus saith to them: Bring of the fish which you have now caught.

Ver. 11. Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, one hundred and fifty-three: and although there were so many, the net was not broken.

§. V. He distributes the fish and bread to the disciples. Which was his third manifestation.

Ver. 12. Jesus saith to them: Come, dine. And none of them who were at meat durst ask him: Who art thou? knowing that it is the LORD.

Ver. 13. And Jesus cometh, and taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish in like manner.

Ver. 14. This is now the third time that Jesus was manifested to his disciples, after he was risen from the dead.

CHAPTER XIII.

The conversation of Jesus with Peter, whom He establishes in his Apostleship, and informs of the manner of his martyrdom.

§. I. The sheep are committed to Peter to be fed, and that for the third time.

Verse 15. When therefore they had dined, JESUS says to Simon Peter: Simon son of John, do you love me more than these? He says to Him: Yes LORD: You know that I love You. He says to him: Feed my lambs.

Verse 16. He says to him again: Simon son of John, do you love me? He says to Him: Yes LORD: You know that I love You. He says to him: Feed my lambs.

Verse 17. He says to him the third time: Simon son of John, do you love me? Peter was grieved, because He said to him the third time: Do you love me? And he said to Him: LORD, You know all things, You know that I love You. JESUS says to him: Feed my sheep.

§. II. The prediction of Peter's martyrdom.

Verse 18. Amen, Amen I say to you, when you were younger you used to gird yourself and walk where you wanted: but when you have grown old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you, and lead you where you do not want.

Verse 19. And this He said, signifying by what death he would glorify God.

CHAPTER XIV.

The conversation of Christ with Peter concerning John.

§. I. Peter is ordered to follow Christ, and when John was also following, he asks about him.

Vers. 19. And when he had said this, he says to him: Follow me.

Vers. 20. Peter, turning around, saw that disciple whom Jesus loved following, who also reclined at supper upon his breast, and said: Lord, who is it that betrays you?

Vers. 21. When Peter therefore had seen him, he says to JESUS: LORD, but what about this man?

§. II. Christ's answer, misunderstood by the disciples, is vindicated.

Vers. 22. Jesus says to him: If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.

Vers. 23. This saying therefore went out among the brothers, that that disciple does not die. And he did not say to him Jesus: He does not die: but: If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?

Ver. 24. This is that disciple who bears witness of these things, and wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.

CHAPTER XV. The appearance of Jesus in Galilee with the solemn confirmation of the Apostleship, and the institution of the ministry.

§. I. The departure of the disciples into Galilee.

Matt. XXVIII. Ver. 16. But the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into the mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

§. II. Jesus worshipped by some, while others doubted him.

Ver. 17. And seeing him, they worshipped: but some doubted.

[Not from the eleven disciples, to whom he had already communicated the Holy Spirit by breathing on them, John XX. 22. But from the number of those 500 whom the Apostle pointed out, I. Cor. XV. Philippus Lansbergius, Chronol. S. l. III. c. 20, observes that Christ first revealed himself to the Apostles on the day of the resurrection: eight days later to the same, Thomas being present: the second eight days later, likewise on the Lord's day, he presented himself to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias: the third eight days after the resurrection, he appeared likewise on the Lord's day to those more than five hundred brethren. The fourth eight days later, he was seen particularly by James. On the fifth eight-day period from the resurrection, he manifested himself to the eleven Apostles when they had come into Galilee: when he confirmed them in the ministry: and finally, on the sixth eight-day period from the resurrection, he appeared to the disciples in Jerusalem on the day of the ascension: and on the following Sabbath Pentecost was fulfilled, on which the Holy Spirit was sent. But since it is not likely that such a frequent assembly, and the appearance made in it, was entirely omitted by the Evangelists, it is better to conclude that those five hundred brethren were present together at this manifestation made to the Apostles, which is also the opinion of Cornelius Jansenius and B. Gerhard. Nor is it certain that all the appearances took place on Lord's days: that certainly most recent one, on the fortieth day, not as Lansbergius wishes, on the forty-first day from the resurrection, could not have fallen on a Lord's day, which it is beyond controversy was the forty-third day from the day of the resurrection. Although indeed, as Jansenius notes, there are those who say that the appearance made to the five hundred brethren happened only after the ascension, the Pauline enumeration, 1 Cor. XV. 6, openly protests against this; after the appearance made to the twelve Apostles on the first day of the resurrection, the Lord is said to have appeared to the five hundred brethren, then to James, and finally to all the Apostles: since therefore he undoubtedly appeared to all the Apostles before the ascension, and that on the very day of the ascension, it cannot be denied that the one in which he was seen by the five hundred brethren happened before the ascension.]

§. III. The profession of JESUS concerning the power given to him.

Vers. 18. And Jesus coming, spoke to them, saying: All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.

§. IV. The sending forth of the Apostles to preach the Gospel, and to baptize: Matth. XXVIII. 19. 20. Marc. XIV. 15. 16.

Vers. 19. Going therefore, teach all nations: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

Vers. 20. Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you:

Marc. XVI. Vers. 15. And he said to them: Going into the whole world, preach the Gospel to every creature.

Vers. 16. He that believeth and is baptized, shall be saved: but he that believeth not, shall be condemned.

§. V. Signs promised for the sake of confirming the Gospel.

Vers. 17. And these signs shall follow them that believe: In my name they shall cast out devils: they shall speak with new tongues:

Vers. 18. They shall take up serpents; and if they shall drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them: they shall lay their hands upon the sick, and they shall recover.

§. VI. The promise of the perpetual presence of JESUS.

Ver. 20. And behold I am with you all days even unto the consummation of the world.

CHAPTER XVI. The last apparition of Jesus made to the Apostles, on the very day of the Lord's Ascension.

§. I. The Apostles, having been gathered, are commanded to await in Jerusalem the promise of the Father. Acts I. 4. 5. Luke XXIV. 49.

Acts I. Ver. 4. And eating together, he commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but should wait for the promise of the Father: Which you have heard (he says) by my mouth:

Ver. 5. For John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days hence.

Luke XXIV. Ver. 49. And behold I send the promise of my Father upon you: but stay you in the city, until you be endued with power from on high.

[The Vulgate wrongly translated that συναλιζόμενος in Acts I. 4 as 'eating together': from which it might be gathered that that command was given in the first apparition made to the Apostles in Jerusalem after the resurrection, described by Luke in c. XXIV from verse 36 to 48, where the Lord wished to eat with the Apostles, that they should not depart from Jerusalem: for afterwards it is not read that he ate with the Apostles again, nor was it done in this last apparition. Beza therefore rendered the Greek word: 'And assembling with them', and Camerarius in his notes on this passage teaches that it ought to be explained as 'gathering (the Apostles)'. He is said to have gathered the Apostles, because by the instinct of the Holy Spirit he made them come together, and appearing to them when gathered, he gave that command. For that this was not given in that last apparition, even though it is immediately joined to it by Luke in the Evangelical History, is evident from these things: (1.) Because he had ordered them to go into Galilee, and there promised a singular manifestation to the Apostles and his brethren; therefore they were not to sit in Jerusalem from that time, as is commanded here. (2.) Because an apparition to the Apostles, with Thomas present, also intervened. (3.) Because the Lord appeared particularly to James after that manifestation which was made to the Apostles in Jerusalem on the very day of the Lord's Resurrection, as the Apostle testifies in I Cor. XV. 7. (4.) Because he did not appear to them on that very day as regards the present manifestation, but 'for forty days', as St. Luke himself testifies in Acts I. 3. Just as also (5.) he is read to have appeared to certain Apostles at the sea

At Tiberias, before he had yet presented himself in that solemn manifestation in Galilee to all the Apostles and others gathered there: which was the prior appearance in Galilee, made after he had already offered himself to be seen by the Apostles twice in Jerusalem: for it is called by John the third manifestation made to the disciples, ch. XXI. 14. This, therefore, is the fourth appearance made to the Apostles, and the last appearance of Christ.

§. II. The conversation of the disciples with Jesus concerning the time of the restoration of the kingdom of Israel.

Ver. 6. Therefore those who had gathered were asking him, saying, Lord, if at this time you will restore the kingdom of Israel?

Ver. 7. But he said to them: It is not for you to know the times or moments which the Father has placed in his own power.

Ver. 8. But you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit coming upon you, and you shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the end of the earth.

[Although he does not answer directly concerning the time of the restoration of the kingdom of Israel by precisely defining the time, because it is not for them to know the moments which the Father has placed in his own power: nevertheless, they are not dismissed without an answer to the question proposed: since he teaches that they will bear witness first in Jerusalem and all Judea, then in Samaria, and once the proclamation of the Gospel has been completed there, they will preach in the whole world, even to the furthest ends of the earth; and that all this is according to the direction of the Holy Spirit with whom they are to be clothed; all of which certainly contributes to the restoration of the kingdom of Israel.]

CHAPTER XVII. The ascension of Jesus into heaven.

§. I. Where and when he ascended into heaven. Mark XVI. 19. Luke XXIV. 50. 51. Acts I. 9.

Mark XVI. Ver. 19. And the Lord Jesus indeed, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven, and sat at the right hand of God.

Luke 24:50. And he led them out as far as Bethany: and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.

Verse 51. And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he departed from them, and was carried up into heaven.

Acts 1:9. And when he had said these things, while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight.

[That this was done on the Mount of Olives, we learn from Acts 1:12.]

§. II. The angelic discourse concerning the ascent into heaven, and the return.

Verse 10. And while they were beholding him going up into heaven, behold two men stood by them in white garments.

Verse 11. Who also said: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up into heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

CHAPTER XVIII. The return of the disciples to Jerusalem.

§. I. How they returned to Jerusalem. Luke 24:52. Acts 1:12.

Luke XXIV. Vers. 52. And they worshipping returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

Acts I. v. 12. Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount, which is called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, having a Sabbath day's journey.

§. II. What they did there having returned.

Luke XXIV. v. 53. And they were always in the temple, praising and blessing God, Amen.

CHAPTER XIX. The universal proclamation of the Apostles.

§. I. The departure of the Apostles into the world, to preach the Gospel.

Mark XVI. Vers. 20. But they going forth preached everywhere.

[This was not done immediately after the Ascension of Christ: for first they were to be endued with power from on high: and besides, they were to preach in Judea alone at the beginning, before they turned themselves, increasing, to the whole world. St. Mark therefore has summarized the matter.]

§. II. The cooperation of the Lord.

Vers. last. The Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following.

§. III. Conclusion of the Evangelical History.

John XXI. Vers. last. And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.

JESUS, TO THEE BE GLORY, FOR EVER AND EVER! AMEN.

Latin:

I. N. J. HARMONIA EVANGELICA DE VITA JESU CHRISTI, AD CON- CINNANDUM NOVUM MONO- TESSARON.

SECTIO PRIOR DE ACTIS ANTE CHRISTI MINISTE- RIUM PUBLICUM. ARTICULUS I. DE CONCEPTIONF, NATIVITATE ET ÆTATE PUERILI AC JUVENILI CHRISTI. CAPUT I. Præcursoris Christi S. Iohannis Baptistæ pa- rentes describuntur, ac Nativitas & offici- um ejus προδρομυτικὸν a Gabriele annun- ciantur.

§. I. Post designationem temporis Johannis pa- rentes a statu, pietate & ἀτεκνίᾳ describit S. Lucas.

LUCÆ CAPUT I.

Vers. 5. Fuit in diebus Herodis, regis Judææ, sa- cerdos quidam nomine Zacharias, de vice Abia; & uxor illius de filiabus Aaron, & nomen ejus Elisab.

Vers. 6. Erant autem justi ambo apud Deum, incedentes in omnibus mandatis & justificationi- bus Domini sine querela.

V. 7. Et non erat illis filius, eo quod esset Elisa- beth sterilis, & ambo processissent in diebus suis.

[Herodis, vulgo Ascalonitæ, vel Magni dies, i. e. tempora regiminis designantur, de quo confera- tur Sect. VIII. q. VII. p. 134. Chronici Sacri. Zacha- rias ἱερεὺς Sacerdos fuit ex Ephemeria Abia: non vero Sacerdos summus vel Pontifex. De Ephe- meriis diximus ad Grotium h. l.]

§. II. Prænunciatio Nativitatis Johannis per Angelum Gabrielem Parenti Zachariæ facta, ejus- que officium e Malachia: (c. IV. 5.) in cujus si- gnum Pater mutus sit, finitis muneris diebus do- mum se conferens, & ex eo gravida facta per quinque menses se occultans.

Vers. 8. Factum est autem cum Sacerdotio fun- geretur in ordine vicis suæ ante Deum:

Vers. 9. Secundum consuetudinem Sacerdotii, sorte exiit, ut incensum poneret, ingressus in tem- plum Domini.

Vers. 10. Et omnis multitudo populi erat orans foris hora incensi.

Vers. 11. Apparuit autem illi Angelus Domini, stans a dextris altaris incensi.

Vers. 12. Et Zacharias turbatus est videns, & timor irruit super eum.

Vers. 13. Ait autem ad illum Angelus: Ne ti- meas Zacharia, quoniam exaudita est deprecatio tua: & uxor tua Elisabeth pariet tibi filium, & vo- cabis nomen ejus Joannem.

Vers. 14. Et erit gaudium tibi, & exultatio, & multi in nativitate ejus gaudebunt.

Vers. 15. Erit enim magnus coram Domino: & vinum & siceram non bibet, & Spiritu sancto re- plebitur adhuc ex utero matris suæ.

Vers. 16. Et multos filiorum Israel convertet ad Dominum Deum ipsorum.

Vers. 17. Et ipse præcedet ante illum in spiritu & virtute Eliæ: ut convertat corda patrum in fi- lios, & incredulos ad prudentiam justorum, para- re Domino plebem perfectam.

Vers. 18. Et dixit Zacharias ad Angelum: Un- de hoc sciam? ego enim sum senex, & uxor mea processit in diebus suis.

Vers. 19. Et respondens Angelus dixit ei: Ego sum Gabriel, qui asto ante Deum: & missus sum loqui ad te, & hæc tibi evangelizare.

Vers. 20. Et ecce eris tacens, & hæc fiant pro eo, quod non credidisti verbis meis, quæ implebun- tur in tempore suo.

Vers. 21. Et erat plebs expectans Zachariam, & mirabantur, quod tardaret ipse in templo.

Vers. 22. Egressus autem, non poterat loqui ad illos, & cognoverunt, quod visionem vidisset in tem- plo. Et ipse erat innuens illis & permansit mutus.

Vers. 23. Et factum est, ut impleti sunt dies of- ficii ejus, abiit in domum suam.

Vers. 24. Post hos autem dies concepit Elisab. uxor ejus, & occultabat se mensib. quinq; dicens:

Vers. 25. Quia sic fecit mihi Dominus in die- bus, quibus respexit auferre opprobrium meum inter homines.

CAPUT II. Conceptio Jesu ab eodem Angelo Mariæ vir- gini intimata & explicata.

§. I. Mense a conceptione Johannis sexto Na- zaretham missus Gabriel Mariæ Virgini annunciat conceptionem, & nativitatem Jesu, ejusque per- sonam, & officium imprimis Regium describit.

Vers. 26. In mense autem sexto, missus est An- gelus Gabriel a Deo in civitatem Galilææ, cui no- men Nazareth.

V. 27. Ad virginem desponsatam viro, cui nomē erat Joseph, de domo David, & nomen virg. Maria.

Vers. 28. Et ingressus Angelus ad eam dixit: A- ve gratia plena: Dominus tecum: benedicta tu in mulieribus.

Vers. 29. Quæ cum audisset, turbata est in ser- mone ejus, & cogitabat, qualis esset ista salutatio.

Vers. 30. Et ait Angelus ei: Ne timeas Maria, invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum.

Vers. 31. Ecce concipies in utero, & paries fi- lium, & vocabis nomen ejus Jesum.

V. 32. Hic erit magnus, & Filius altissimi vocabi- tur, & dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David Pa- tris ejus: & regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum.

Vers. 33. Et regni ejus non erit finis.

§. II. Maria, quo pacto id fieri possit, quum nul- lum unquam virum cognoverit, sciscitans in- formatur ab Angelo de conceptione ex Spiritu S. & obumbratione virtutis altissimi, unde sanctum ex ea natum Filius altissimi futurum sit.

Vers. 34. Dixit autem Maria ad Angelum: Quo- modo fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco?

Vers. 35. Et respondens Angelus dixit ei: Spi- rit. S. superveniet in te & virtus altissimi obum- brabit tibi: Ideoque & quod nascetur ex te san- ctum, vocabitur Filius Deus.

§. III. Confirmatur Maria ab Elisabethæ steri- lis fœcundatione, & divina omnipotentia, seque submittit divinæ voluntati.

Vers. 36. Et ecce Elisabeth cognata tua, & ipsa concepit filium in senectute sua, & hic mensis sex- tus illi, quæ vocatur sterilis.

Vers. 37. Quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum.

Vers. 38. Dixit autem Maria: Ecce Ancilla Do- mini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum. Et dis- cessit ab illa Angelus.

[Factum id anno Mundi 4000. d. 26. Martii.]

CAPUT III. Maria visitat Elisabetham, & excepta ab ea- dem ceu mater Domini hymno celebrat Dominum, eique per tres menses inservit.

§. I. Maria tendit super montana in civitatem Juda in domum Zachariæ, ac salutata Elisabetha Johannis in utero matris conclusi saltu fœtus ejus excipitur.

V. 39. Exurgens autem Maria in dieb. illis abiit in montana cum festinatione, in civitatem Juda.

Vers. 40. Et intravit in domum Zachariæ, & salutavit Elisabeth.

Vers. 41. Et factum est, ut audivit salutationem

Mariæ Elisabeth, exultavit infans in utero ejus.

[Maria per montana Gilboa, Garizon Hebal & Ephraim ambulavit milliaribus & in montana Ju- dææ ad urbem Sacerdotalem & refugii Hebron: ubi Abraham, Isaac & Jacob olim sepulti sunt.]

§. II. Maria benedicta, ceu Mater Domini, ac beata ob fidem, & fructus ventris ejus benedictus ab Elisabetha Spiritus S. plena prædicatur.

Vers. 41. Et repleta est Spiritu S. Elisabeth.

Vers. 42. Et exclamavit voce magna, & dixit: Benedicta tu inter mulieres, & benedictus fructus ventris tui.

Vers. 43. Et unde hoc mihi, ut veniat mater Domini mei ad me?

Vers. 44. Ecce enim, ut facta est vox saluta- tionis tuæ in auribus meis, exultavit in gaudio fans in utero meo.

Vers. 45. Et beata, quæ credidisti, quoniam perficientur ea, quæ dicta sunt tibi a Domino.

§. III. Hymnus Mariæ, quo beneficia sibi & toti generi humano exhibita celebrat.

Vers. 46. Et ait Maria: Magnificat anima mea Dominum:

Vers. 47. Et exultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo.

Vers. 48. Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ: ecce enim ex hoc beatam me dicent omnes generationes.

Vers. 49. Quia fecit mihi magna, qui potens est, & sanctum nomen ejus.

Vers. 50. Et misericordia ejus a progenie in progenies timentibus eum.

Vers. 51. Fecit potentiam in brachio suo: di- sperfit superbos mente cordis sui.

Vers. 52. Deposuit potentes de sede, & exal- tavit humiles.

Vers. 53. Esurientes implevit bonis, & divites dimifit inanes.

Vers. 54. Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recor- datus misericordiæ suæ.

Vers. 55. Sicut locutus est ad Patres nostros, Abraham, & semini ejus in secula.

§. IV. Maria per tres menses penes Elisa- betham commorata domum proficiscitur.

Vers. 56. Mansit autem Maria cum illa quasi mensibus tribus, & reversa est in domum suam.

[Mense Junio labente: An. M. 4000. B. Bün- tingius factum id putat 2. die Julii, nato jam & cir- cumciso Johanne Baptista: Sed alii pudorem vir- ginalem non admisisse censent, ut nativitatem Jo- hannis expectaret, in qua re parum situm est: quia Spiritus sanctus talia direxit pro lubitu.]

CAPUT IV. Iohannis nativitas, Hymnus Zachariæ, cum incremento & corroboratione Iohannis in Spiritu. §. I. Filius Elisabethæ natus, ejusque circumci- sio cum impositione nominis, quo non Zacharias, sed Johannes vocatus est, nomen istud approban- te Zacharia, vinculo linguæ soluto cum omnium admiratione.

Vers. 57. Elisabeth autem impletum est tem- pus pariendi, & peperit filium.

Vers. 58. Et audierunt vicini & cognati ejus, quia magnificat Dominus misericordiam suam cum illa, & congratulabantur ei.

Vers. 59. Et factum est in die octavo, venerunt circumcidere puerum, & vocabant eum nomine Patris sui Zachariam.

Vers. 60. Et respondens mater ejus, dixit: Ne- quaquam, sed vocabitur Johannes.

Vers. 61. Et dixerunt ad illam. Quia nemo est in cognatione tua, qui vocetur hoc nomine.

Vers. 62. Innuebant autem patri ejus, quem vellet vocari eum.

Vers. 63. Et postulans pugillarem scripsit, di- cens: Johannes est nomen ejus. Et mirati sunt universi.

Vers. 64. Apertum autem est illico os ejus, & lingua ejus, & loquebatur benedicens Deum.

Vers. 65. Et factus est timor super omnes vi- cinos eorum, & super omnia montana Judææ di- vulgabantur omnia verba hæc.

Vers. 66. Et posuerunt omnes, qui audierant, in corde suo, dicentes: Quis, putas, puer iste erit? Etenim manus Domini erat cum illo.

§. II. Zacharias Spir. S. repletus vaticinatur, Deum ob erectum cornu salutis celebrans.

Vers. 67. Et Zacharias Pater ejus repletus est Spiritu S. & prophetavit dicens:

Vers. 68. Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui visitavit, & fecit redemptionem plebis suæ.

Vers. 69. Et erexit cornu salutis nobis, in do- mo David pueri sui.

Vers. 70. Sicut locutus est per os sanctorum, qui a seculo sunt, prophetarum ejus.

Vers. 71. Salutem ex inimicis nostris, & de ma- nu omnium, qui oderunt nos.

Vers. 72. Ad faciendam misericordiam cum patribus nostris, & memorati testamenti sui san- cti.

Vers. 73. Jusjurandum, quod juravit ad Abra- ham patrem nostrum, daturum se nobis.

Vers. 74. Ut sine timore, de manu inimico- rum nostrorum liberati, serviamus illi.

Vers. 75. In sanctitate & justitia coram ipso, omnibus diebus nostris.

§. III. Porro vaticinatur Zacharias de officio filii prophetico, & προδρομευτικῷ ejusque fine communicatione cognitionis salutis.

Vers. 76. Et tu puer Propheta Altissimi voca- beris: præibis enim ante faciem Domini parare vias ejus.

Vers. 77. Ad dandam scientiam salutis plebi e- jus, in remissionem peccatorum eorum.

Vers. 78. Per viscera misericordiæ Dei nostri, in quibus visitavit nos, oriens ex alto.

Vers. 79. Illuminare his, qui in tenebris, & in umbra mortis sedent: ad dirigendos pedes no- stros in viam pacis.

§. IV. Johannes crescit & confortatur Spiri- tu, in deserto manens, usque ad diem ἀναδείξεως coram populo. Quæ ad 30. ætatis annum refe- renda, h. e. ad mundi annum 4030. Hic tamen attexitur, ut summaria complexio vitæ ejus ad tempus ministerii, siquidem nihil amplius de Jo- hanne narrare voluerit Spiritus S. donec muneris ejus auspicium describeret.

Vers. 80. Puer autem crescebat, & conforta- batur Spiritu: & erat in desertis usque in diem o- stensionis suæ ad Israel.

CAPUT V.

Iosephi Genealogia a Matthæo pertexta: quem, cum gravidam sponsam deserere vel- let, monuit Angelus, quod in ipsa natum e Spiritu S. esset, ideoque assumsit Ma- riam, donec Iesum filium pareret.

§. I. Genealogia Christi per tres tesseradeca- das inde ab Abrahamo texta: Prima usque ad Da- videm.

Vers. 1. Liber generationis Jesu Christi filii David, filii Abraham.

Vers. 2. Abraham genuit Isaac. Isaac autem genuit Jacob. Jacob autem genuit Judam, & fratres ejus.

Vers. 3. Judas autem genuit Phares, & Zaram de Thamar. Phares autem genuit Esron. Esron autem genuit Aram.

Vers. 4. Aram autem genuit Aminadab. Ami- nadab autem genuit Naasson. Naasson autem genuit Salmon.

Vers. 5. Salmon autem genuit Booz de Rahab. Booz autem genuit Obed ex Ruth. Obed autem genuit Jesse. Jesse autem genuit David Regem.

§. II. Secunda tesseradecas a Salomone se por- rigit ad captivitatem Babylonicam.

Vers. 6. David autem Rex genuit Salomonem ex ea, quæ fuit Uriæ.

Vers. 7. Salomon autem genuit Roboam. Roboam autem genuit Abiam. Abias autem ge- nuit Asa.

Vers. 8. Asa autem genuit Josaphat. Josa- phat autem genuit Joram. Joram autem genuit Oziam.

Vers. 9. Ozias autem genuit Joatham. Joa- tham autem genuit Achaz. Achaz autem genuit Ezechiam.

Vers. 10. Ezechias autem genuit Manassen. Manasses autem genuit Amon. Amon autem ge- nuit Josiam.

Vers. 11. Josias autem genuit Jechoniam & fra- tres ejus in transmigratione Babylonis.

§. III. Tertia tesseradecas a transmigratione Babylonis porrigitur usque ad Christum.

Vers. 12. Et post transmigrationem Babylo- nis Jechonias genuit Salathiel. Salathiel autem genuit Zorobabel.

Vers. 13. Zorobabel autem genuit Abiud. Abiud autem genuit Eliacim. Eliacim autem genuit Azor.

Vers. 14. Azor autem genuit Sadoc. Sadoc au- tem genuit Achim. Achim autem genuit Eliud.

Vers. 15. Eliud autem genuit Eleazar. Elea- zar autem genuit Mathan. Mathan autem ge- nuit Jacob.

Vers. 16. Jacob autem genuit Joseph virum Mariæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocatur Chri- stus.

§. IV. Josephi propositum, & divinum de non deserenda Maria mandatum in somnio per Angelum datum; ejusque causa conceptio e Spiritu S. Jesu Salvatoris.

[Animadvertit Josephus, Mariam gravidam esse sine dubio, postquam ea domum reversa est ab Elisabetha, cui per tres menses affuit. Quarto enim mense notæ sese produnt. Facta ergo hæc sunt mensis Julii initio circiter.]

Vers. 18. Christi autem generatio sic erat: Cum esset desponsata mater ejus Maria Joseph, antequam convenirent, inventa est in utero ha- bens de Spiritu S.

Vers. 19. Joseph autem vir ejus, cum esset ju- stus, & nollet eam traducere, voluit occulte dimit- tere eam.

Vers. 20. Hæc autem eo cogitante, ecce An- gelus Domini apparuit in somnis ei, dicens: Jo- seph, fili David, noli timere accipere Mariam conjugem tuam: quod enim in ea natum est, de Spiritu S. est.

Vers. 21. Pariet autem filium: & vocabis no- men ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum faciet popu- lum suum a peccatis eorum.

§. V. Confirmatio ejusdem ex Esaia de virgi- nali partu Cap. VII. 14.

Vers. 22. Hoc autem totum factum est, ut adim- pleretur, quod dictum est a Domino per Prophe- tam dicentem :

Vers. 23. Ecce virgo in utero habebit, & pariet filium : & vocabunt nomen ejus Emmanuel : quod est interpretatum Nobiscum Deus.

§. VI. Mandati Angelici exequutio in assum- tione Mariæ, quam non cognovit Joseph, donec primogenitum, cui nomen Jesus, pareret.

Vers. 24. Exurgens autem Joseph a somno, fe- cit, sicut præcepit ei Angelus Domini, & accepit conjugem suam.

Vers. 25. Et non cognoscebat eam, donec pe- perit filium suum primogenitum : & vocavit no- men ejus Jesum.

CAPUT VI.

Nativitas Christi, ejusque annunciatio, & celebratio angelica : cum profectione, rei exploratione, & divulgatione pastorali. §. I. Describitur nativitas Christi, quoad cir- cumstantias temporis, Edicti Augusti de censu sub præside Syriæ Quirinio : Loci, in Bethlehem, quo se contulit Joseph cum Maria, quia è genere Da- vid erat : Modi, in humili statu : quod natus pri- mus filius Mariæ, & fasciis iuvolutus in præsepi repositus sit.

Vers. 1. Factum est autem in diebus illis, exiit edictum a Cæsare Augusto, ut describeretur uni- versus orbis.

Vers. 2. Hæc descriptio prima facta est (a) præ- side Syriæ Cyrino.

Vers. 3. Et ibant omnes, ut profiterentur sin- guli in suam civitatem.

Vers. 4. Ascendit autem & Joseph a Galilæa de civitate Nazareth, in Judæam in civitatem Da- vid, quæ vocatur Bethlehem : eo quod esset de do- mo & familia David.

Vers. 5. Ut profiteretur cum Maria desponsa- ta sibi uxore prægnante.

[Profecto illa è Nazareth in Bethlehem octo- decim milliarium fuit, eademque mense Decem- bri suscepta.]

Vers. 6. Factum est autem, cum essent ibi, im- pleti sunt dies, ut pareret.

Vers. 7. Et peperit filium suum primogeni- tum, & pannis eum involvit, & reclinavit eum in præsepio : quia non erat eis locus in diversorio.

[Die 25. Decembr. Anno M. 4000.]

§. II. Pastoribus in agro Bethlehemitico ea- dem nocte annunciatur ab Angelo Domini clari- ritate circumdato gaudium magnum & catholi- cum Nativitatis in civitate David Servatoris Christi, addito signo infantis involuti fasciis & præsepi reposito.

Vers. 8. Et pastores erant in regione eadem vigilantes, & custodientes vigilias noctis super gregem suum.

Vers. 9. Et ecce Angelus Domini stetit juxta illos, & claritas Dei circumfulsit illos, & timue- runt timore magno.

Vers. 10. Et dixit illis Angelus : Nolite timere : ecce enim Evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, quod erit omni populo.

Vers. 11. Quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator, qui est Christus Dominus, in civitate David.

Vers. 12. Et hoc vobis signum : Invenietis in- fantem pannis involutum, & positum in præsepio.

§. III. Hymnus exercitus Angelici in honorem recens nati Servatoris decantatur.

V. 13. Et subito facta est cum Angelo multitudo militiæ cœlestis, laudantium Deum, & dicentium:

Vers. 14. Gloria in altissimis Deo, & in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis.

§. IV. Pastores proficiscuntur in Bethlehem, in- veniunt matrem & Infantulum in præsepi: & ver- bum ab Angelo prædicatum divulgant, aliis id ad- mirantibus, Maria vero in corde retinente & ex- pendente, ac redeuntes ad agru, Deum celebrant.

Vers. 15. Et factum est, ut discesserant ab eis An- geli in cælum: pastores loquebantur ad invicem: Transeamus usq; Bethlehem, & videamus hoc ver- bum, quod factum est, quod Deus ostendit nobis.

Vers. 16. Et venerunt festinantes: & invenerunt Mariam & Joseph, & infantem positu in præsepio.

Vers. 17. Videntes autem cognoverunt de ver- bo, quod dictum erat illis de puero hoc.

Vers. 18. Et omnes, qui audierunt, mirati sunt: & de his, quæ dicta erant a pastoribus ad ipsos.

Vers. 19. Maria autem conservabat omnia ver- ba hæc, conferens in corde suo.

Vers. 20. Et reversi sunt pastores glorificantes & laudantes Deum in omnibus, quæ audierant & viderant, sicut dictum est ad illos.

CAPUT VII.

Circumcisio & Denominatio Jesu.

§. I. Octavo post nativitatem die circumcisus est Christus. [Die sc. 1. Januarii, Ann. M. 4001.]

V. 21. Et postquam consummati sunt dies octo, ut circumcideretur puer: vocatum est nomen e- jus Jesus.

§. II. Nomen Jesu, quo denominatus ante- quam in utero conciperetur, ipsi impositum.

V. 21. Quod (nomen Jesus) vocatum est ab An- gelo, priusquam in utero conciperetur.

CAPUT VIII.

Adventus Magorum ex Oriente, & ad man- datum divinum per aliam viam regressus.

§. I. Nato Jesu in Bethlehem tempore Regis Herodis Magi ex Oriente Hierosolymam ve- niunt, &, ubi recens natus Rex Judæorum sit? sciscitantur, quem visa ejus stella adoraturi adve- nerint.

Vers. 1. Cum ergo natus esset Jesus in Bethle- hem Juda in diebus Herodis regis, ecce Magi ab Oriente venerunt Jerosolymam.

Vers. 2. Dicentes: ubi est, qui natus est, Rex Judæorum? vidimus enim stellam ejus in Orien- te, & venimus adorare eum. [Magos è Persia venisse non dubitamus. Susa autem Magorum in Persia Gymnasium ab Hiero- solymis distat milliaribus 230. versus Orientem.]

§. II. Territo Herode, cum Hierosolyma tota, Concilio coacto indagatum, ubi Christus nasci de- buerit, & designata Bethlehem è Michea (c. V. 2.)

Vers. 3. Audiens autem Herodes rex, turbatus est, & omnis Jerosolyma cum illo.

Vers. 4. Et congregans omnes principes sacer- dotum, & scribas populi, sciscitabatur ab eis, ubi Christus nasceretur.

Vers. 5. At illi dixerunt ei: in Bethlehem Judæ Sic enim scriptum est per Prophetam:

V. 6. Et tu Bethlehem terra Juda, nequaquam minima es in principibus Juda: ex te enim exiet dux, qui regat populum meum Israel.

§. III. Convocatis Magis, ut cognosceret He- rodes, quo tempore apparuerit stella, dimittit eos in Bethlehem, simulans se etiam infantulum ado- raturum, quibus proficiscentibus stella, quam vi- derant, præit, donec eo pervenirent, ubi infantu- bis erat: quem invenientes adorarunt, muneribus auri, thuris & myrrhæ oblatis.

[Quæ oblatio 6. Jan. An. M. 4001. contigit.]

V. 7. Tunc Herodes clam vocatis Magis diligen- ter didicit ab eis tempus stellæ, quæ apparuit eis.

V. 8. Et mittens illos in Bethlehem, dixit: Ite, & interrogate diligenter de puero: & cum inveneri- tis, renunciate mihi, ut & ego veniens adorem eum.

Vers. 9. Qui cum audissent Regem, abierunt: & ecce stella, quam viderant in Oriente, antecedebat eos, usque dum veniens staret supra, ubi erat puer.

Vers. 10. Videntes autem stellam gavisi sunt gaudio magno valde.

Vers. 11. Et intrantes domum, invenerunt pue- rum cum Maria matre ejus, & procidentes adora- verunt eum: & apertis thesauris suis, obtulerunt ei munera, aurum, thus, & myrrham.

[Bethlehem Hierosolyma distabat milliari u- no, ac dimidio.]

§. IV. Magi jussi in somno non redire ad He- rodem per aliam viam redeunt in patriam.

Vers. 12. Et responsio accepto in somnis ne redi- rent ad Herodem, per aliam viam reversi sunt in regionem suam.

[Per interstitium circiter ducentorum & tri- ginta milliarium.]

CAPUT IX.

Præsentatio Christi in templo, & testificatio Simeonis & Hannæ.

§. I. Exortis diebus purificationis, Jesus Hie- rosolymam adductus, ut Domino præsentaretur secundum legem (Exod. XXXIV. 19. Num. VIII. 17.) & ut sacrificia ordinata offerrent (Lev. XII. 8.)

Vers. 22. Et postquam impleti sunt dies purga- tionis ejus secundum legem Moysi, tulerunt illum in Jerusalem, ut sisterent eum Domino.

Vers. 23. Sicut scriptum est in lege Domini: Quia omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam, san- ctum Domino vocabitur.

Vers. 24. Et ut darent hostiam secundum quod dictum est in lege Domini, par turturum aut duos pullos columbarum.

[Adduxerunt Joseph & Maria Jesulum Bethle- hema Hierosolymam, milliari uno ac dimidio, tri- ginta tribus diebus post circumcisionem. Præces- sisse autem præsentationem Christi adventum Ma- gorum, non vero hunc longe post præsentationem Jesu contigisse (quod vult Andr. Osiand. post Eu- sebirum & Epiphanium, ut & Anton. Alexandr.) cum B. Chemnitio non tantum è voce παιδίον ἐν- τῷ, Matth. II. 1. quæ de puero recens nato legitur, Ebr. XI. 23. & perticula idè colligimus: Sed etiam quod Nazaretham non Bethlehemam post purifi- cationem parentes Jesu demigrasse dicantur, Luc. II. 39. Magi autem puerum cum matre in Bethle- hem invenerint. Atque ita ordo historiarum opti- me sibi cohæret, quod interea, dum Herodes re- ditum Magorum expectat, puer in templo Do- mini sistitur, cumque fama de testificatione Si- meonis & Hannæ non urbem tantum, sed totam Judæam pervageretur, intellexit inde Herodes, se a Magis delusum. Nec vero necessum est, Magos ex intimis, vel extremis Persiæ recessibus educe- re; qui facile intra 30. dies, si septem forte dies commorationi in Jerusalem & Bethlehem tribuan tur, inter suum emetiri potuerint, & ita ante tem- pus purificationis & advenire, & discedere.]

§. II. Simeonis descriptio eique factum oracu- lum, de videndo Christo Domini, qui instinctu Spiritus S. in templo comparens Jesum in brachia suscipit, Deum celebrat, & ἀνάλυσιν precatur, quia

το σωτήριον Domini oculis suis viderat, lucem gentium & gloriam Israelis: & admirantibus Patre & Matre benedicens ipsis, matri prædicit, Jesum positum in ruinam & resurrectionem multorum, & signum contradictionis, unde gladius per animam ejus transiturus.

Vers. 25. Et ecce homo erat in Jerusalem cui nomen Simeon, & homo iste justus & timoratus, expectans consolationem Israel, & Spir. S. erat in eo.

V. 26. Et responsum acceperat a Spir. S. non visurum se mortem, nisi prius videret Chr. Domini.

Vers. 27. Et venit in Spiritu in templum. Et cum inducerent puerum Jesum parentes ejus, ut facerent secundum consuetudinem legis pro eo.

Vers. 28. Et ipse accepit eum in ulnas suas, & benedixit Deum, & dixit:

Vers. 29. Nunc dimittis servum tuum Domine, secundum verbum tuum, in pace.

V. 30. Quia viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum,

Vers. 31. Quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum.

Vers. 32. Lumen ad revelationem gentium, & gloriam plebis tuæ Israel.

Vers. 33. Et erat pater ejus & mater mirantes super his, quæ dicebantur de illo.

Vers. 34. Et benedixit illis Simeon, & dixit ad Mariam matrem ejus: Ecce positus est hic in ruinam, & in resurrectionem multorum in Israel, & insignum, cui contradicetur.

V. 35. Et tuam ipsius animam pertransibit gladius, ut revelentur ex multis cordib. cogitationes.

§. III. Hanna Prophetissa, filia Phanuel, de genere Aser, vidua 84. annorum, Deo perpetuo in templo serviens, eadem hora Dominum prædicavit, & de eo loquuta est omnibus expectantibus λύτρωσιν in Hierusalem.

V. 36. Et erat Anna Prophetissa, filia Phanuel, de tribu Aser: hæc processerat in dieb. multis, & vixerat cum viro suo annis septem a virginitate sua.

Vers. 37. Et hæc vidua usque ad annos octoginta quatuor: quæ non discedebat de templo, jejuniis & obsecrationibus serviens nocte ac die,

Vers. 38. Et hæc, ipsa hora superveniens, confitebatur Domino: & loquebatur de illo omnibus, qui expectabant redemptionem Israel.

§. IV. His omnibus secundum legem finitis tendunt vicissim in Galilæam in civitatem suam Nazareth. [Sed mox in via monentur de fuga in Ægyptum, ne opus habeant per totam Judæam, ipsamque Hierosolymam, primum Nazaretham ire, & inde iterum fugam arripiendo, Judæam, atque Regiam Herodis sedem, pertransire, quum Regi infantulum subducere vellent. Vid. Anti-Grot. ad Luc. II. 22. p. 37.]

Vers. 39. Et ut perfecerunt omnia secundum legem Domini, reversi sunt in Galilæam in civitatem suam Nazareth.

CAPUT X. Fuga in Ægyptum, & infanticidium Herodis, eoque mortuo revocatio ex Ægypto, & habitatio in Nazareth.

§. I. Joseph ab Angelo in somno monitus, ut in Ægyptum fugiat, donec revocetur, ob intentatam Jesu mortem, eo, nocte illa statim cum infante, ac matre ejus iter ingressus, sese recipit, usq; ad mortem Herodis ad complendam Prophetiam (Hos. II. 1.) Quam de revocatione Filii Dei proprii ex Ægypto secundum literam agere in Bibl. illustr. Tom. II. part. II. pag. 743. ostensum.

Vers. 13. Qui (Magi) cum recessissent, ecce An- lus Domini apparuit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, & accipe puerum, & matrem ejus, & fuge in Ægyptum, & esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi. Fu- turum est enim, ut Herodes quærat puerum ad perdendum eum.

Vers. 14. Qui consurgens, accepit puerum & matrem ejus nocte, & secessit in Ægyptum.

Vers. 15. Et erat ibi usque ad obitum Herodis, ut adimpleretur, quod dictum est a Domino per Prophetam dicentem: Ex Ægypto vocavi Filium meum.

[Numerantur Hierosolyma ad Gosen Ægypti regionem septuaginta circiter milliaria.]

§. II. Herodes sese a Magis deceptum sentiens masculos bimos & minores ætate in Bethlehem, & finibus ejus interfici curat. Ubi impletum vati- cinium Jeremiæ (Cap. XXXI. 15.)

[Jeremiam ibi sensu literali de ploratu ex in- fanticidio illo oriundo vaticinari l. c. ostendimus Tom. II. part. I. pag. 447.

Vers. 16. Tunc Herodes videns, quoniam illu- sus esset a Magis, iratus est valde, & mittens occidit omnes pueros, qui erant in Bethlehem, & in omni- bus finibus ejus, a bimatu & infra, secundum tempus, quod exquisierat a Magis.

Vers. 17. Tunc adimpletum est, quod dictum est per Jeremiam Prophetam dicentem.

Vers. 18. Vox in Rama audita est, ploratus & ululatus multus: Rachel plorans filios suos, & noluit consolari, quia non sunt.

§. III. Mortuo Herode per Angelum in terram Israelis redire jussus, & cum Archelaum filium re- gnare audiret, sibique metueret, mandato divino in Galilæam se contulit, & in Nazareth habitavit, ut impleretur, quod dictum est a Prophetis, Naza- ræus vocabitur.

(Ubi id dictum disquirimus in Anti-Grotian. ad h. l.)

[Reditus autem contigit An. M. circiter 4002. Tatianus continuum septennium in Ægypto Je- sum egisse ait, alii quadriennium, alii biennium eligunt. Sed in Chron. Sacr. sect. VIII. q. 7. do- cuimus, inter nativitatem Jesu & mortem Hero- dis ad summum nonnisi annum & tres menses in- tercessisse, ideo non multum ultra annum in Æ- gypto relictus fuit Jesus.]

(Reversi autem ad oppidum Nazareth sunt in- tercapedine circiter sexaginta sex milliarium.)

Vers. 19. Defuncto autem Herode, ecce Ange- lus Domini apparuit in somnis Joseph in Ægypto;

Vers. 20. Dicens: Surge, & accipe puerum & matrem ejus, & vade in terram Israel: defuncti sunt enim, qui quærebant animam pueri.

Vers. 21. Qui consurgens, accepit puerum & matrem ejus, & venit in terram Israel.

Vers. 22. Audiens autem, quod Archelaus re- gnaret, in Judæa pro Herode patre suo, timuit illo ire: Et admonitus in somnis, secessit in partes Ga- lilææ.

Vers. 23. Et veniens habitavit in civitate, quæ vocatur Nazareth: ut adimpleretur, quod dictum est per prophetas: Quoniam Nazaræus vocabitur.

CAPUT XI.

De profectu pueri Jesu, & profectione ad fe- stium Paschatos, ubi cum Doctoribus con- tulit, redituque in patriam.

§. I. Jesus crescit, & roboratur Spiritu plenus sapientia, & gratia Dei cum ipso.

[Plenus sapientia divina & infinita per unionem hypostaticam communicata: quia in ipso habita- bat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter, Col. II.

9. & reconditi erant omnes sapientiæ & cognitionis thesauri, v. 3. Crescit autem & confortatur Spiritu non quoad illam donorum Spiritus hypostaticam communionem, sic enim acceperat Spiritum ουκ εκ μετρου non ad mensuram, adeoq; immensa ratione, infinita sc. dona, & ενεργηματα vere divina, Joh. III. 34. sed quoad sapientiæ habitualis participationem, quæ donum Spiritus erat ipsi ut homini, in unione quidem personali, non tamen per & propter unionem personæ communicatum. Sed qua fieri voluit, & factus erat in oμοιωματι ανθρωπων in similitudine aliorum hominum, Phil. II. 7. Profecit, inquam, quoad eam sapientiam, quæ subjective, actualiter & formaliter menti inhærebat, non quoad eam sapientiam, qua cum tota plenitudine divinitatis σωματικως & personaliter possidebat: vid. quæ diximus Exam. Doct. Reformat. de pers. Christi Contr. VII. p. 369. Damasc. distinguit inter ea, quæ Christus homo habuit τη χαριτι gratia, uti cæteri homines, & quæ δια την προς τον λογον ενωσιν propter unionem personale habuit, & ad hæc την των απαντων omnis cognitionem refert. L. II. de Orth. fid. c. 22.

Vers. 40. Puer autem crescebat & confortabatur, plenus sapientia: & gratia Dei erat in illo.

§. II. Parentes Jesu quotannis in Paschatos festo Hierosolymam tendentes filium duodecim annos habentem secum adducunt, sed in reditu desiderant, quærunt, in templo, in medio Doctorum, quibuscum conferebat, cum omnium admiratione inventum redarguunt, sed monentur, quod esse ipsum oporteat in iis, quæ Patris sui sunt.

Vers. 41. Et ibant parentes ejus per omnes annos in Jerusalem, in die solemni Paschæ.

Vers. 42. Et cum factus esset annorum duodecim, ascendentibus illis Jerosolymam secundum consuetudinem diei festi.

Vers. 43. Consummatisque diebus, cum redirent, remansit puer Jesus in Jerusalem, & non cognoverunt parentes ejus.

Vers. 44. Existimantes autem illum esse in comitatu, venerunt iter diei, & requirebant eum inter cognatos & notos.

Vers. 45. Et non invenientes, regressi sunt in Jerusalem, requirentes eum.

Vers. 46. Et factum est, post triduum invenerunt illum templo sedentem in medio doctorum, audientem illos, & interrogantem eos.

Vers. 47. Stupebant autem omnes, qui eum audiebant, super prudencia & responsis ejus.

Vers. 48. Et videntes admirati sunt. Et dixit mater ejus ad illum: Fili, quid fecisti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus & ego dolentes quærebamus te.

Vers. 49. Et ait ad illos: Quid est, quod me quærebatis: nesciebatis, quia in his, quæ Patris mei sunt, oportet me esse?

Vers. 50. Et ipsi non intellexerunt verbum, quod locutus est ad eos.

§. III. Nazaretham descendit cum parentibus ipsis subditus, & profecit sapientia, ætate & gratia apud Deum & homines.

[Non intellexisse dicuntur, v. 50. & retinuit tamen mater verba illa in corde suo, v. 21. Etiam non intellectum verbum Domini retinendum, donec dante Deo intellectum ejus assequamur. Nazareth autem Hierosolyma distabat sedecim milliarium intervallo. Et pertinent hæc ad Mensem Nisan Anni 4013.]

Vers. 51. Et descendit cum eis, & venit Nazareth: & subditus illis. Et mater ejus conservabat omnia verba hæc in corde suo.

Vers. 52. Et Jesus proficiebat sapientia & ætate, & gratia apud Deum & homines.

SECTIO I. ARTICULUS II. DE CHRISTI IN ÆTATE VIRILI NOTIFI- CATIONE, ET AD OFFICIUM INAUGURATIO- NE, AC PRÆPARATIONE.

CAPUT I. Iohannis Baptisma & præconium cum corre- ptione Pharisæorum & Sadducæorum, po- pulique informatione, inprimis vaticina- torium de Christo.

§. I. Præmisso titulo, Marc. I. 1. tempus voca- tionis Johanneæ ratione imperantium & sacerdo- tum summorum definitur, Luc. III. 1. 2. & locus at- que officium designatur, Luc. III. 3. ejusdemque ex Esaia (Cap. XL. 3. seqq.) confirmatio, Luc. III. 4. 5. 6. S. Matthæus indefinite tempus designat, & lo- cum in deserto Judææ, concionem autem voce με- τανοεῖτε, & ratione addita ἤγγικε γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν ὀυρανῶν comprehendit, & confirmationem pariter ex Esaia petit Cap. III. 1-3. subjuncta vesti- tus & cibi Johańci genere & confluxu populi, qui baptismum suscipit confessione peccatorum edi- ta, v. 4. 5. 6. a quibus S. Marcus initium Evange- lii de Jesu Christo filio Dei facit, addito tamen ad- huc alio (Mal. III. 1.) vaticinio. Marc. I. 1-7. (Ini- tium præconii Johannei Anno M. 4030. contigit, forte in tubarum festo primo die Mensis septimi, vel Thisri, qui Septembri respondet. Cæterum de temporis designatione a S. Luca facta, vid. quæ in Chron. Sacr. de locis Propheticis Esaiæ & Ma- lachiæ, quæ ad illa in Annotat. dicta sunt.

Marc. I. v. 1. Initium Evangelii Jesu Christi, Filii Dei.

Luc. III. v. 1. Anno autem quintodecimo Impe- rii Tiberii Cæsaris, procurante Pontio Pilato Ju- dæam, tetrarcha autem Galilææ Herode. Philip- po autem fratre ejus tetrarcha Iturææ, & Tracho- nitidis regionis, & Lysania Abilinæ tetrarcha.

Vers. 2. Sub principibus sacerdotum Anna & Caipha: factum est verbum Domini super Johan- nem Zachariæ filium in deserto.

Vers. 3. Et venit in omnem regionem Jordanis, brædicans baptismum pœnitentiæ in remissio- nem peccatorum.

Matth. III. v. 1. In diebus illis venit Johannes Baptista prædicansin deserto Judææ.

Vers. 2. Et dicens: Pœnitentiam agite, appro- pinquat enim regnum cælorum.

Vers. 3. Hic est enim, qui dictus est per Esaiam prophetam dicentem: Vox clamantis in deserto: Parate viam Domini: rectas facite semitas ejus.

Luc. III. v. 4. Sicut scriptum est in libro sermo- num Esaiæ prophetæ: Vox clamantis in deserto: Parate viam Domini: rectas facite semitas ejus.

Vers. 5. Omnis vallis implebitur: & omnis mons & collis humiliabitur, & erunt prava in di- recta & aspera in vias planas.

Vers. 6. Et videbit omnis caro salutare Dei.

Marc. I. v. 2. Sicut scriptum est in Esaia pro- pheta: Ecce ego mitto angelum meum ante fa- ciem tuam, qui præparabit viam tuam ante te.

Vers. 3. Vox clamantis in deserto: Parate viam Domini, rectas facite semitas ejus.

Vers. 4. Fuit Johannes in deserto baptizans, & prædicans baptismum pœnitentiæ in remissio- nem peccatorum. [Subintellige in Malachia 5) Nominatur unus Prophetarum, nimirum antiquior & præcipuus, & adducitur tamen simul alterius Prophetæ va- ticinium, utpote non modo ὁμόψηφον, sed &

priori inpixum, ejusdemque velut exequutionem ob oculos ponens, quod insuper ideo præmittitur, ut Veteris Testam. clausulæ, & initii Evangelii, Novi Testam. convenientia clarius exhibeatur.]

Matth. III. v. 4. Ipse autem Joannes habebat vestimentum de pilis camelorum, & zonam pelliceam circa lumbos suos: esca autem ejus erat locustæ, & mel silvestre.

Vers. 5. Tunc exibat ad eum Jerosolyma, & omnis Judæa, & omnis regio circa Jordanem.

Vers. 6. Et baptizabantur ab eo in Jordane, confitentes peccata sua.

Marc. I. v. 5. Et egrediebatur ad eum omnis Judææ regio, & Jerosolymitæ universi, & baptizabantur ab illo in Jordanis flumine confitentes peccata sua.
