IV. namely that Christ distinguishes these degrees, in the manner of the Hebrews, and teaches that all these are worthy of the punishment of hell, which is explained by judgment, and council, and Gehenna, according to the lesser or greater degree of the punishment of hell, for a lesser punishment is signified by judgment, a greater by council, and the greatest by Gehenna.

The same is the explanation of Strabus in the ordinary gloss, that it could not be expressed by proper and certain modes, it is distinguished by certain similarities. For by these three, judgment, council, Gehenna, different mansions in eternal damnation are significantly expressed according to the mode of the sin. Therefore, there is no distribution here of punishments, eternal, temporal, and very brief, but only of eternal ones: the different degree of which, with an allusion made to the different deaths among the Jews, the Lord insinuates, with words taken from Jewish custom.

Therefore, the fire of Gehenna does not here denote eternal punishment literally, but a kind of temporal death, and that the most bitter among the Jews; but with respect to the intention of Christ, which is gathered from this allusion to Jewish custom, it insinuates a greater degree of eternal punishment, just as in the rest regarding the liability of judgment and the sanhedrin, lesser degrees of eternal punishment are insinuated. Conf. Spanhemius l. c. The sense of the whole verse was not unsuitably explained by the blessed Glassius from the blessed Selneccer: i.e., You Pharisees estimate only external homicide as worthy of capital punishment (which is accustomed to be inflicted by the judgment of 23); holding other sins, by which one does not descend to the same, as trifles, unworthy of a graver punishment. But I say to you, that in the judgment of God the matter stands far otherwise. For in it, the internal affection of unjust anger, animosities, and enmity is also held for homicide, which for that reason, if I may speak humanly, and wish to look at your order of judgments. order of judgments, would deserve to be punished by the punishment with which you take care that external homicide is punished. Again, he who furthermore brings forth signs of external anger in gestures and any biting speech whatsoever (such as the word Raca is); he would be worthy of a greater degree of punishment, so that, indeed, the Sanhedrin or the great council (which is accustomed to judge only of the most grave matters) would pass a sentence of death upon him. And what finally is to be said of him who vomits forth calumnies with black bile, from an indignant stomach, other than that, without any examination of the cause in judgment, he is most worthy to be cast into the fire of hell as a disgrace and reproach, that is, to be burned alive? From this rite of your judgments and punishments, learn to estimate sins rightly, and to acknowledge their foulness, along with the most sorrowful guilt, which is the eternal punishment of the underworld, with which those who do not obtain remission in this age will be afflicted, sinning against these and other commandments of God in heart, gesture, tongue, and deed itself, etc. Undoubtedly Christ employs those words of judgment, the sanhedrin, and the fire of hell, opposing his own sentence to that of the Pharisees, by accepted usage and custom, which the opposition demands, and which must be made in the same manner and sense, according to the laws of contradiction; You say that he who kills a man is liable to judgment; but I say that he who is rashly angry with his brother is liable to judgment, and he who says 'Raca' to him is liable to a greater guilt, the sanhedrin, and he who calls him a fool is liable to the greatest punishment, such as is considered by you to be worthy of the fire of hell. What Christ insinuates, or rather properly intends, in divine judgment through these degrees of punishments in this figurative and parabolic speech, he also declares in clear words concerning the implacable man being consigned to prison until he pays the last farthing, that is, forever. For since Christ has threatened the eternal punishment of the infernal prison to him who refuses to be reconciled to his brother, it is easily understood that those who conceive and foster anger against a brother, and who mock with sarcastic gestures and injurious words from a malignant affection, and are thus judged by Christ to transgress against the fifth commandment in mind, gesture, and mouth, are therefore pronounced guilty of the judgments, the Sanhedrin, and the fire of hell, not that some temporal judgment or punishment, which is by no means to be feared on account of anger conceived in the mind, is being referred to and designated, but rather an eternal one, even if under that distinction of the degrees of infernal punishments, which was found to be accepted among the Jews in capital punishments, such as beheading, stoning, and burning alive. Nor is there any reason why it should be objected here that by Gehenna eternal punishments are always designated in the New Testament: because the reason for other passages is different, since here a manifest allusion is made to the different degrees of death among the Jews, whereas elsewhere mention is made of Gehenna alone, without comparison. And thus Grotius rightly says: just as here the more severe punishments of the future age are compared to the fires of Gehenna, so elsewhere, by a comparison passing into custom, punishments of the other age are signified by this very name. There is no doubt that this also represents the eternal fire of Gehenna, but it also represents human judgment as divine, and the Sanhedrin as the tribunal of God, not because there are different tribunals in the heavens, but because a more serious guilt is punished by God with a more serious punishment, a lighter one with a lighter one, yet every one is liable to eternal punishment: just as Maldonatus also admits, that Christ teaches that both he who is angry, and he who calls his brother a light person, and he who calls him a fool, are worthy of the same punishment of hell, though not of the same severity of punishment. Moreover, because the name of Gehenna occurs here, which was later transferred to express hell, we only add that it was derived from the valley of Hinnom, from the words גיא (valley) and הנום (Hinnom, which was a man's name), and therefore it seems to be used for expressing the place of eternal punishment because in that valley or Tophet there was once the seat of the devil, who raged most atrociously against men, to whom in the image of Moloch they offered the flames of fire to be most cruelly tortured: if indeed there was also an image of hell there, the seat of the devil and a place of torments (taking the word 'place' in a broad sense) for men who served the devil, the most atrocious of men. For other reasons for the appellation, if you wish, see B. Gerhard, Book on Hell, § 8.

Latin:

Vers. 22. Ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν] Sapientissime Christus de- licta omnia refert ad ejusdem generis præcepta. Nam quia ex ira atque convitiis nasci solent homicidia, ut mode ex Aristotele recitabamus, ὁ θυμὸς πᾶν Φόνου αἴτιον, ideo iram ejusque propagines ad præceptum de homicidio re- fert.

Non allegat Christus legem prout à Mose, vel Deo potius tradita, sed prout à Pharisæis & scribis interpolata erat: quod verba ipsa, quibus utitur, docent. Cum enim legem vel scripturam V. T. citat, solet iisdem verbis, vel quibus LXX. Inter- pretes usi sunt, eandem adducere. Quod hic fa- ctum non est. Et quod Pharisæorum corruptelis, non sententiæ Mosaicæ suam opponat sententiam, ex eo etiam liquet, quod Moses homicidium prohibens non tantum externam cædem, sed sub homicidii specie synecdochice omne, quod phra- si scripturæ homicidium est, complectatur, ac vo- ce illa κατ' ἐπίτασιν doceat, odium, iram, simul- tatem, excandescentiam, & id genus alios affectus in Dei oculis esse homicidia, imo omnem eum, qui non diligit proximum suum, homicidam esse, & in mor- te manere, 1. Joh. II. 14. 15. Imo principaliter hoc in vindicando quinto præcepto doceat, iram inordinatam hic prohibitam esse. Nam si cædes ab ira inordinata separetur, peccatum non est, ut in Magistratu videmus, cum cædem infligit prome- ritam eum non peccare, contra hoc præceptum, nec homicidium committere. Unde non addit Christus hic novum præceptum de ira, sed cæci- tatem Pharisæorum ostendit, quod non intelli- gant iram inordinatam primo ac per se hic prohibi- tam esse, consequenter autem cædem hominis eam- que non per se, sed quatenus ex inordinata ira ori- tur: quia iram talem prohibitam esse, sive ad cæ- dem usque procedat, sive non: adeoque prohi- bitum etiam omnino esse quicquid ex ira inordi- nata oritur, seu verbum maledicum, seu vultus hostilis, seu ipsum homicidium. Quo facit illud Matth. XV. 19. Ex corde exeunt homicidia. De cætero facile annuimus ἔνοχος τῇ κρίσει dici, qui reus est capitalis supplicii: atque à Pharisæis eum solum, qui cædem externam commiserit, & pro homicida, & judicii reum habitum, hoc est, di- gnum, qui pœna capitali afficiatur. Num vero per κρίσιν judicium illud XXIII. virorum intelliga- tur, dubium quibusdam videtur. Nonnulli e- nim judicium trium virorum intelligunt, eique non tantum cognitionem, de causis pecuniariis, sed etiam in criminibus & capitalibus convenisse putant, utpote cum res minime dubia fuerit. Quibus accedit B. Chemnitius in Harm. cap. LI. pericop. III. p. m. 563. ita de tribus diversis ju- diciis penes Judæos differens: 1. In judicio sede- bant triumviri pronunciantes de causis, quæ erant manifesti juris: ut de pœna homicidii. 2. In qua- libet civitate Israel erat parvum synedrion constans ex XXIII. judicibus. Illi judicabant de causis, quæ aliquid habebant controversiæ. 3. Hierosolymis erant LXXII. judices, qui de summis causis cogno- scebant Deut. XVII. 8. 9. Quem sequutus est B. Gerhardus Homil. II. Domin. VI. post Trinit. pag. 334. Sed verosimilion est eorum sententia, qui non ad judices pedaneos, & confessum triumvi- rorum in minoribus oppidis, sed ad judices in portis civitatum, quæ numerum habebant civium ad minimum CXX. judicia capitalia pertinuisse existimant: quemadmodum & Judæi primum il- lud judicium & infimum vocarunt דיין ממונות judicium causæ pecuniariæ, secundum vero & me- dium דיין נפשות judicium animarum, præter quod erat tertium vel supremum in metropoli Ju- dæis בית דין domus judicii ἐξοχικῶς dictum, & Synedrium magnum, ad differentiam secundi, quod Synedrium parvum dicebatur. De quo vid. ex Rambam vel Maimon. & R. Bechai Buxtorf. in abbrev. Ebr. pag. 17. Schindler. in Lex. voc. שׁפט, quibus adstipulantur Selneccerus, Glaffius, Winstrupius, alii; Angelus Caninius in Loc. Nov. Testam. pag. 62. e Talmud Massechet Synhedrion refert itidem ea ratione tres classes ju- dicum, primam domus judicii triumvirum, ad quam minores causae, ut furti, injuriarum privata- rum, male tractationis ac denique dine Mamonoth deferebantur, domus judicii viginti trium, vel sy- nedrii parvi, in quo causae majores, nempe capi- tales, cognoscebantur, & domus judicii LXXI. vel Synedrii magni, in quo causae gravissimae, quae per- tinebant ad summam Reip. tractari solebant, quia scriptum illic ita: Non pronunciant judicium de tri- bu, nec de Pseudo-Propheta, nec de summo sacer- dote, nisi de sententia curiae LXXI. Atque ita se rectius habet gradatio in subsequentibus Christi verbis, quibus poenam eandem irae temerariae, ge- stibus ex iracundia profectis & verbis calumniosis denique, vel convitiis, aeternae nempe mortis de- finit, solum diversos poenarum gradus designat: quia in κρίσει judicio XXIII. virorum poena capita- lis, & in synedrio ἐξοχικῶς dicto itidem, sed gra- vior dictabatur, sed gravissima omnium erat illa ignis gehennae, in valle Ben Hinnon: ut ad formu- lam judiciorum, & suppliciorum Judaicorum capi- talium, sed gradus disparis, hic respiciatur. Si in judicio triumvirorum capitis poena dictata, qua- nam illa fuit? & quae gravior ista in XXIII. virorum consessu dictanda? aut num ideo gravior poena definita, quod minus manifesti juris, & difficilioris cognitionis fuerit delictum, quod in hoc conses- su dijudicandum? Ideoque non male observat Grotius, in judicio vel synedrio parvo, de quo hic ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει, poenam gladii homicidis di- statam, quae ibi fuerit usitatissima, synedrio autem magno reservata crimina graviori poena, quae ipsila- pidationis est, ab eodem affecta: denique gravis- simam poenam designari vocibus εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.

Vers. 22. ὁ ὀργιζόμενος] In hac tractatione diligenter distinguenda sunt τὸ πάθος, ἡ ὁρμὴ, ἡ συγκατάθεσις. Πά- θος est ut facultas illa, qua irascimur, τὸ θυμοειδές, quod a natura nobis insitum evelli nequit, & in rebus est mediis, quibus recte aut secus uti liceat. Quia autem pars ista a- nimi, in qua sunt τὰ πάθη per se est ἄλογος, inde fit, ut non exspectato rationis judicio ὁρμαὶ se exserant: quae nisi diligenter refrenentur, solet sequi συγκατάθεσις, cum scil. pars illa, quae data est moderandis affectibus, habenis re- missis trahi se patitur. Est igitur, ut Gellius dicit, συγκα- τάθεσις voluntaria, sitque hominis arbitratu: sed & primi illi motus, quos Philosophi comparant oculorum nictibus, ne aut durent diu, invalescant, diligenti attentione atque exercitatione, ante omnia vero Dei spiritu, obtineri solet. Oportet igitur, ut Plutarchus loquitur, τὰς ἑκάστοτε προ- σπιπτούσας ὀργὰς διορθοῦν καὶ διαπίνειν. Deinde addit: ἀπ' ἐ- πιμελείας εἰς αὐτὰ δεῖ κῃ μελέτης. Alii ὁρμὰς vocant προπα- θείας: easdem autem adultas vocant πάθη. Hieronymus epistola ad Demetriadem: Difficile quin potius impossibile per- turbationis initiis carere quempiam, quae significantius Graeci προπαθείας vocant. Idem ad Eustochium de custodia vir- ginitatis: Ille laudatur, ille praedicatur qui ut coeperit cogitare sordida statim interficit cogitatus, & allidit ad petram. Petra autem Christus est. Ipsa quoque πάθη gradibus quibusdam distingui solent.

Haec Socinianorum & Pontificiorum lucernam olent. Nimirum συγκατάθεσις pro peccato habetur, motus autem primi dum saltim non durent, aut in- valescant, haud item: facileque Grotius acquievit Senecae judicio, quod hic ceu egregium laudat e libr. de Ira II. cap. 4. Et ut scias quemadmodum incipiant affectus, aut crescant aut efferantur; est primus motus non voluntarius, quasi praeparatio affectus, & qua- dam comminatio; alter cum voluntate non contuma- ci, tanquam oporteat me vindicari, cum læsus sim: aut oporteat hunc pœnas dare, cum scelus fecerit. Tertius motus est jam impotens, qui non, si oportet, ulcisci vult: sed utique, qui rationem evicit. Pri- mum illum animi ictum effugere ratione non possu- mus: sicut ne illa quidem quæ diximus accidere corpo- ribus, ne nos oscitatio aliena solicitet, ne oculi ad intentionem subitam digitorum comprimantur. Ista non potest ratio vincere: consuetudo fortasse & assi- dua observatio extenuet. Alter ille motus, qui judi- cio nascitur, judicio tollitur. Quod monitum sane in homine Christiana disciplina non imbuto satis eximium; at nos non tantum ex hac informatio- ne Christi ὁ ὀργιζόμενος εἰκῆ, sed ex ipsa decalogi lege NON CONCUPISCES, novimus, ipsos mo- tus etiam primos iræ, cum ea εἰκῆ subrepit nobis, etsi ratio eos vincere non possit, & exserant sese ὁρμαί illæ ac προπαθείαι quas vocant, non exspe- ctato rationis judicio, atque ut Hieronymus Epist. ad Demetriadem loquitur, difficile, quin potius im- possibile sit perturbationis initiis carere quempiam, peccatum esse veri nominis. Nam impossibilitas illa non est à natura, qualis ea à Deo instituta, sed qualis peccato hominis culpa corrupta, ideoque Deus citra injustitiam, id quod culpa nostra nunc impossibile nobis, à nobis reposcit, ac nisi præ- stetur peccati damnare potest. Neque τὸ ἑκύ- σιον ad peccati formam requiritur: Sed omnis ἀνο- μία est ἁμαρτία seu voluntaria sit, seu involuntaria, 1. Joh. III. 4. ideoque non à nostra voluntate, sed ab ἀνομίᾳ & repugnantia adversus legem æstimari & definiri debet peccatum: juxta quam etiam pri- mariæ temerariæ ὁρμὴ ut pravus cordis motus, est ἀνομία, repugnans legi, NON CONCUPI- SCES, & opus carnis Galat, V. 20. Coloss. III. 8.

Τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτῦ] Id est, alteri cuivis. Hebraïsmus. Nam Hebæi ita loqui solent Gen. XXVI. 31. Joel. II. 8. etiam de rebus inanimis, ut Exod. XXVI. 3. Ezech. I. 9. & 23. III. 13. Hic igitur frater, est homo quivis. Sic infra: Nisi remi- seritis hominibus.

Εἰκῆ] Merito hoc additum. Neque enim iracundus est quisquis irasci solet, sed qui οἷς οὐ δεῖ, κὰι ἐφ’ οἷς οὐ δεῖ, κὰι μᾶλλον ἡ δεῖ, ut Aristoteles loquitur. Est igitur εἰκῆ aut sine causa, aut etiam fine modo. Illa ira optimam causam habet, quæ con- cipitur ex dolore læsi numinis, qualis illa fuit Christi Marc. III. 5. Sed & in humanis rebus honesta esse potest ira, præ- sertim cum non tam nostra, quam aut virtutis ipsius, aut etiam hominum aliorum res agitur: cumque dicere licet illud Sosiphanis :

Νῦν σοι πρὸς ὄψιν θυμὸς ἐξάτω γέρον, Νῦν δεῖ γὰρ ὀργὴν, ἡνίκ’ ἀδικον, λαβεῖν.

Sed tunc quoq; oportet nos παραδεξαμένους ᾗ θυμὸν ὡς σύμ- μαχον ἀρετῆς, ἀπολάυειν ὅσον χρησιμόν ἐστι· τὸ δὲ πολὺ αὐτοῦ κὰι τὸ ἐπιπόλαιον ἐκκείνειν κὰι ἐκβάλλειν τῆς ψυχῆς, ut Plutarchi u- tar,verbis. In modo autem comprehenditur,tum ne plus æ- quo irascamur,tum ne æquo diutius. Adversus priorem par- tem hujus cautionis delinquunt οἱ ὑπὸ μικρῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀνυπερβλήτως ὀργιζόμενοι, qui, ut ajebat Philosophus Apol- lonius, non permittunt delinquentibus scire quando plus minusve deliquerint. In alteram partem peccant illi, qui plumbeas, & quod dici solet immortales iras gerunt, quos Arianus comparat τοῖς λεπτοῖς πυρέττουσι. Hæc est nimirum radix illa πικρίας in corde germinans, quam caveri præcipit scriptor ad Hebræos XII. 15. quo & illud Pauli monitum pertinet, cum nos ita vult irasci ut ne peccemus, id est, ne æqui modum excedamus, quod ipse ita explicat, ne ad So- lis occasum producamus iram Ephes IV. 25. Et hæc dicta sunto quo rectius intelligatur vis vocis εἰκῆ, quam quidem Syrus interpres tam propriam atque significantem hoc lo- co existimavit, ut retinere eam maluerit, quam vertere. Quominus accedendum Hieronymo hanc vocem eraden- ti ex quorundam exemplarium fide, præsertim cum & Græcos interpretes eam legisse appareat, & Justinus ipse improferat hanc sententiam epistola ad Zenam & Sere- num: deinde & Irenæus duobus locis lib. II. cap. LVI. & lib. IV. cap. XXXI. Multo credibilius est, inductam ab iis qui metuebant ne hic omnis ira ex justa aliqua causa pro- cedens probari videretur, cum vox εἰκῆ, ut diximus, latius pateat.

ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.] Legisperiti, inquit Christus, ea tantum pro delictis habent, quæ solent legitimis pœnis coërceri: ideoque ab homicidio absterrent homines, quia homicidas gladio feriri lex imperat. At ego etiam iracundiam volo caveatis, certo persuasi ei quoque pro- positam esse pœnam in sæculo altero, non minus gra- vem, quam ea est, quam hic homicidæ sustinent. Quod si quis iracundiæ maledicentiam adjunxerit, is pœnam ista graviorem feret, qualis est pœna lapidatio- nis, aut etiam, si atrocior fuerit maledicentia, exqui- sitiores cruciatus sentiet, quales esse illorum solent, qui in valle Hinnomi lentis ignibus ustulantur. Hæc mi- hi simplicissima videtur hujus loci παράφρασις, cujus rationes membratim reddemus. Κρίσιν ut commate præcedenti didicimus est consessus XXIII. virum, quan- quam & magnus senatus, de quo post acturi sumus, vo- catus est דין, unde is qui alter erat à principe senatus vocari solebat אב בית דין: πατὴρ τοῦ οἴκου τῆς κρίσεως, sicut & vicissim consessus XXIII. judicum appellabatur συνέδριον: Sed distinctionis causa videtur usu receptum, ut consessus ille singularium civitatum κρίσις, summus au- tem ille συνέδριον vocaretur. Κρίσεως autem pœna usita- tissima erat gladius, quia de homicidiis inibi cognosce- batur, ut & Moses nos docet, & Christus commate an- tecedente. Volens autem indicare Christus pœnarum gradus futuros in altero seculo pro delictorum gradibus, ei rei extra causæ similitudinem adhibuit diversarum mor- tum quæ populo notæ, cruciatus magnitudine differe- bant.

ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ] Repetendum ἀπὸ κοινοῦ quod præcessit εἰκῆ ὀργιζόμενος. Agit enim de eo qui temerariæ ira- cundiæ indulgere solitus etiam ad maledicta prorumpat. Nam ut Ariston dixit, τὴν κακολογίαν ἡ ὀργὴ φαίνεται ἀπο- γεννῶσα ὥςτε ἡ μήτηρ ἐκ ἀστῖα. Vox Raca, quod mutata vocali Syrorum sermo raca pronuntiat, minus aliquid est quam μωρέ. Significationem autem habet vani, quod & Latinis in convitio: ut vane Ligur: senior vanissime. Non est autem in ipsa voce crimen positum. Quippe & ar- gumenta novit dixit Jacobus III. 20. quod est proprie Ri- ca (nam & Græci quidam interpretes quod est Judic. XI. 3. אנשים ריקים verterunt ἄνδρες κενοὶ, & Hesy- chius ῥακὰ κενός) & illud quod diximus μωροὶ, ad Pharisæos Christus extulit infra XXIII. 17. 19. & ἀνοήτους discipulos suos vocat Christus, Luc. XXIV. 25. & Galatas Paulus Gal. III. 1. 3. ut jam omittam quæ duriora sunt, ut progenies vi- perarum, simulatores, atque alia ejusmodi. Sed nimi- rum dicta sunt hæc ab iis, quibus alios castigandi officium incumbebat, quique nihil in eo privatim spectabant, ex causis gravissimis, atque eo proposito ut aliorum animi talibus stimulis ex veterno excitarentur. At Pharisæi non tantum modum non servabant, sed innocentissimum quemque convitiis impetebant animo malevolo, quod Christus & ipsius sectatores sæpissime sunt experti. Nimi- rum hic quoque morbus ab aliquoties jam indicato er- rorum fonte processerat. Lex enim Mosis id genus inju- rias non exsequebatur, nisi quis aut parentibus, aut Principi maledixisset.

Recte in hac paraphrasi sententiam Christi op- ponit Grotius legisperitorum doctrinæ. Non er- go Christus ceu novus legislator divinam legem perficit, quod cum Socinianis & Pontificiis statuit Grotius, præceptis nempe quibusdam exactiori- bus munire legem voluisse Christum asserens pag. 65. sed corruptelas Pharisæorum & Legisperito- rum reprehendit, & legis sensum vindicat: cu- jus scopum fuisse homines quam optimos efficere, supra pag. 63. professus est Grotius: qui vero scopus frustra legi præfixus à Deo fuisset, si ipsa per se absque additamentis exactioribus Christi, quæ fingit, non potuisset homines, quam opti- mos, quantum ad doctrinam, & institutionem efficere. Quod si Christo, legis interprete optimo, docente pœnam infernalem iracundiæ temerariæ gestus ac verba maledica, ipse etiam iræ temerariæ affectus internus, promereantur, nullum dubium esse potest in lege cum gestibus & verbis maledicis à temeraria iracundia redundan- tibus affectumque iræ temerariæ prohibitum fuis- se: ubi enim nulla lex, ibi nulla prævaricatio: ubi prævaricatio nulla, ibi nec pœna ulla, nedum æ- terna, & infernalis locum habet. Quod vero Grotius legem id genus injurios, cum quis Ricæ fratri dicit, aut fatue, non exsecutam fuisse, ait, nisi quis aut Parentibus aut Principi maledi- xiffet, ad impunitatem tantum in foro soli & judi- cio divino facit, nec immunitatem reatus per le- gem Mosis conciliat, qui maledictionis fulmen in omnes, qui non omnia verba legis servant, vi- brat.

Ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ] Quia hic primum hæc vox oc- currit, quanquam ab aliis multa satis dicta sunt, addam tamen quæ historiæ lucis aliquid afferant. Sicut in me- moriam duodecim liberûm marium primi gradus quos genuerat Jacobus, factæ sunt tribus duodecim & Phylar- chæ totidem, ita in memoriam eorum capitum quæ Jaco- bus in Ægyptum adduxerat, Israelitæ, ut qui à cæteris seor- sim habitarent, viros septuaginta [aut potius septuaginta duos, qua de re dicemus ad Lucam] sibi præfecerunt, qui res eorum curarent ac moderarentur quantum regia impe- ria permittebant. Hi ab ætate ex qua legebantur senes sunt vocati, unde & apud Græcos γερουσία, & apud Roma- nos Senatus vocabulum. Sed & apud Homerum est: Βουλὴ δὲ πρῶτον μεγαθύμων ἷζε γερόντων.

Apud hos senes ante alios jubetur Moses exponere man- data, quæ à Deo acceperat, Exod. III. 16. quod & fecit, Exod. IV. 29. Ex horum numero & illi videntur fuisse à quibus Ægyptii ἐργοδιῶκται quotidiani laboris rationem exi- gebant, v. 14. Postea cum soceri consilio Moses judices constituisset qui lites minores dijudicarent, causarum ma- jorum cognitio penes Mosem solum mansit, ad quem & de minoribus causis difficiliores controversiæ referebantur, Exod. XVIII. 22. Ergo ad id tempus septuaginta illi nullam habebant judicandi potestatem: cujus rei indicium est quod Moses jussus cum Aarone, Naddabo, Abihu & illis se- ptuaginta (nam numerus iste diserte exprimitur) ad mon- tem accedere, cum deinde solus à Deo in montis verticem se vocaretur, jussit inferius subsistere septuaginta senes. Sunt, inquit, vobiscum Aaron & Hur, si quis aliquid habet con- troversiæ, illos accedat, Exod. XXIV. 14. ubi aperte Moses pro absentiæ suæ tempore suas judicandi partes non illis se- ptuaginta, sed Aaroni & Huri delegat. Aliquanto demum post tempore cum quereretur Moses isti quoque supremo- rum judiciorum ac relationum oneri se non suffi ere, ita ad eum locutus est Deus: Num. XI. 16. Sume tibi è senibus Israelitis septuaginta, quos seis populi senatores & moderatores. Habebant ergo jam tum curam rerum populi: deinde eos Deus spiritu novo, judiciali scilicet, instruens, jubet partem oneris ferre, quod solus Moses hactenus sustinuerat: id au- tem est, ut diximus, supremorum judiciorum & relatio- num. Eorum autem verborum quæ Deuteronomii legun- tur XVII. 8. hæc videtur esse sententia: cum Sacerdotes opi- mo fruentes otio omnibus sapientiæ partibus præter cæte- tos operam darent, æquum erat ex horum numero ali- quammultos allegi in ordinem illum, cui jam suprema etiam judicia credita fuisse diximus: quanquam nemi- nem fuisse qui originis dignitate eum locum sibi posset vindicare, scripsit Maimonides, atque adeo ne Pontifi- cem quidem maximum eo adlectum, nisi de sapientia ipsius probe constaret: quam in rem instituta erat δοκι- μασία, quæ manuum impositione obsignabatur. Sed ut dixi florentibus Hebræorum rebus fieri aliter non poterat, quin in Sacerdotum classe plurimi reperirentur digni eo loco. His addebantur alii, qui in aliis tribubus doctrina & sanctimonia eminebant. Ita enim vox ראשי accipienda videtur 2. Par. XIX. 8. Quamobrem Moses Deutet. XIX. 17. de falsi testimonii cognitione agens & senatum hunc describens, Sacerdotes & judices nominat. Alibi autem ubi agitur de exploranda diligentia judicum inferiorum in conquirendo homicida, soli Sacerdotes, tan- quam ejus Senatus pars præcipua, nominantur: additurq; ex eorum præscripto omnes controversias & vulnerum quæ- stiones definiendas. Quoties autem Deus cælesti indicio a- liquem populo præfecerat, qualis fuit Josua, Gedeon, Jeph- thes, Samson, Samuel, eis etiam citta Senatum judicandi jus erat, ut appatet Jud. IIX. Vocabantur autem tales Reipublicæ liberæ summi magistratus ac velut Interreges שופטים, quod nomen etiam vicinæ gentes usurparunt. Nam & apud Tyrios Interreges ita vocabantur: ex quorum Archivis hæc adfert Josephus: μετὰ τῦτον δικασταὶ κατεστάθησαν καὶ ἐδίκα- σαν ἐκνίβαλος βασιλέως μῆνας δύο, χέλης ἀβδαίε μῆνας δέκα, ἄββαρος ἀρχιερέως μῆνας τρεῖς, μύτγονος καὶ γε- ράστρατος τῶ ἀσδηλίμε δικασταὶ ἔτη ἕξ: ubi δικαστὰς haud dubie Josephus vertit quos Tirii vocabant שופטים. Nam & Tyriorum coloni Carthaginienses idem nomen re- tinuerunt, quod Romani Scriptores Suffetem pronuntiant: litera Schin emollita, quomodo Ephraimitæ in eam partem vergentes pronunciabant. Josephus talem à Deo exci- tatum præsidem etiam Prophetam vocat, quia Prophetiæ dono, ut Josua aut Samuel, aut alio non dissimili ipsos ani- mante & successus dante, præfulgere solebant, quod & Maimonides notat ducis dubitantium libro II. c. 45. iis- dem, quanquam nimis proprie, ob potestatem ἀνυπεύθυ- νον & regum datur nomen Jud. IX. 6. & XVIII. 1. Quibus vero temporibus neminem talem Deus excixerat, recurren- dum omnino erat ad Senatum, in quo ferme eminebat Pon- tifex Maximus. Nam & Moses ut modo diximus cum abes- se à populo cogeretur, Aaroni partes suas mandabat. Hoc jure Heli Sacerdos summus principatum in Republica ob- tinuit, idemque observatum fuit Asmonæorum temporibus. Vult igitur Deus à Judicibus civitatum, si quid incidisset ob- scurius, quod aut juris subtilioris, aut etiam medicinæ peri- tiam desideraret, adiri Pontificem Maximum ut eruditione præstantem: sive eum qui à Deo excitus Suffetis dignita- tem obtineret. Horum responso parere omnes tum mino- res judices, tum privati jubebantur, proposita etiam mor- tis pœna in contumaces. Indicat autem Deus sedem ejus Senatus fore in loco publicorum conventuum, qui primum habiti sunt Silunte, postea Hierosolymis. Quod ergo dicitur commate 9. Adibis Sacerdotes Leviticos & Suffetem, explicandum est ex eo quod sequitur commate 12. Sacer- doti vel Suffeti. Nam in Hebraismo non minus quam in linguis omnibus receptum est ut conjunctiva vim habeat disjungendi. Neque vero alia fuerunt judicia Sacerdo- tis, alia Senatus, id enim omnes Hebræorum magistri constanter negant. Josephus, qui patriæ suæ morem igno- rare non potuit, clare ostendit eundem fuisse consessum, ita enim loquitur secundo adversus Appionem: κὴ γὰρ ἐπό- πται πάντων κὴ δικασταὶ τῶν ἀμφισβητουμένων οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐτάχθη- σαν. Idem nos docet Philo: Συνέδρευον μὲν οἱ ἱερεῖς, libro de vita Mosis. Et in libro de principe constituendo: ὅταν ἐν ἀ- μαυρὰν ποιῆται τὴν ἀντίληψιν τῶν πραγμάτων ἀσάφεια κὴ πολὺ σκότος ἀπεργαζομένων παραιτείσθω τὰς κρίσεις κὴ ἀναπεμπέτω πρὸς ἀκριβεστέρους δικαστάς· ἔτοι δὲ τίνες ἂν εἶεν ἢ ἱερεῖς κὴ ὁ τῶν ἱερέων ἔξαρχος ἡγεμών. Qui omnes quanquam in tam nota historia testes haberi debent locupletes, tamen idem veritatis discendæ cupidis ex sacro codice demonstrare non est difficile. Nam primum hoc ipso loco non distinguun- tur causarum genera, neque vero causæ ullæ nominantur, quæ proprie videri possint sacerdotales, sed si quid contro- versi incidisset, de homicidio, de lite, de vulnere, juben- tur adiri Sacerdotes, aut is quem Suffetem diximus nomina- ri. Rursum sine ullo causarum discrimine, quod hi pronun- tiaverint, id omnes jubentur exsequi. Pœna in nec parentes eadem. Deinde vero constat tam inter Hebræos, quam in- ter recentiores interpretes à Josaphato Rege restituta fuis- se judicia ad vetus instar. Esdras autem, aut quisquis est Pa- ralipomenon scriptor, primum narrat ab optimo Rege constitutos judices civitatum suiq; officii admonitos. Tum pergens, At Hierosolymis, inquit, (nempe in urbe publi- corum conventuum ut lex jubebat) constituit Josaphat è Le- vitis & Sacerdotibus (quia inter eos ut diximus maximam hominum peritorum copiam erat reperire) & ex præcipuis Israeliticarum gentium ad judicia Dei & ad lites, qui redierunt Hierosolyma. Judicia Dei ex notissimo Hebraismo judicia significat, quæ non humano arbitratu sed ex legis jussu peragenda sunt. Sequitur in historia: Præcepit autem eis Rex in hunc modum: Hoc agite, religiose, fideliter at- que sincero animo: Quæcunque lis ad vos relata fuerit à popularibus vestris qui in civitatibus morantur, de discrimine homicidiorum, de lege, de præcepto, de institutis, de judiciorum ordine, admonete eos ne rei Deo teneantur, Deique vehe- mens ira vobis popularibusque vestris incumbat. Hoc, in- quam, agite, ne fontes sitis. Ecce quam aperte omnes il- los quos Hierosolymis constituerat de omni causarum ge- nere vult cognoscere. Neq; his obstat quod sequitur. Enim- vero Amarias Sacerdos princeps vester in omni negotio Dei, & Sabadias filius Ismaëlis domus Judæ in omni nego- tio Regio, & magistri Levitæ vobis adsunt. Estote bono ani- mo, & hoc agite. Deus bono aderit. Nam primum hinc quoque apparet in eodem Senatu fuisse agitatas res Dei, id est legis, & res regias: ei autem Senatui inter fuisse & Ama- riam, sive is Pontifex Maximus, sive alius Sacerdos se- fuerit, & Sabadiam. Neque posse per Dei negotia res so- lis Sacerdotibus mandatas intelligi, palam est ex altero ejus historiæ loco, ubi Hebronitæ quidam narrantur à Davide præfecti partibus Rubenis, Gadis & Manassis, impositisque omni negotio tum Dei tum Regis. Solebant ergo utrius- que generis negotia tum judiciorum, tum deliberatio- num politicarum à Senatu tractari. Sed nimirum hæc est dicti loci παράφρασις: Nolite animum despondere quasi pa- res non sitis tanto oneri, inopia eruditionis quæ ad res tan- tas desideretur. Habetis viros egregios qui vobis consilio prælucere possint: qualis est princeps vestri Senatus Ama- rias sacerdos, vir in judiciis versatissimus: quod si quid inci- derit ad civilem magis prudentiam quam à juris cognitio- nem pertinens, adest vobis Sabadias Ismaelides, qui in eo deliberandi genere primas obtinet: deinde habetis assesso- res Levitas, multarum artium peritia excellentes. Tantum bene animati este & æquo bonoque operam date, Deus cæ- tera secundabit. Videtur omnino Sabadias fuisse princeps Senatus. Nam vocem נגיד Hebræi per ראש exponunt. Ita autem constat appellatum senatus principem. Ex his quæ diximus apparet etiam regno constituto magnam fuis- se Senatus auctoritatem & regiæ velut parem: quippe ut Hebræi magistri recte notant, Rex ipse de quibusdam cau- sis non judicabat, & sua judicia non nisi gladio exsequeba- tur: Atq; huc pertinere videtur quod dicit Sedecias, Senato- ribus Jeremiam Prophetam ad mortem deposcentibus, Rex contra vos nihil potest. Quin ne venisse quidem Regem in Se- natum, ne sua sententia aliis censendi adimeret libertatem, Hebræi notant: excepto Davide. Quod diximus cum Jose- pho, Philone, cumque ipsis sacris literis in summo hoc sena- tu fuisse Sacerdotes, non refellitur historia Jeremiæ quæ est libri ejus cap. XXVI. ubi Sacerdotes videntur accusare Jere- miam, & Senatores absolvere. Nam ut taceam posse videri magis esse disputationem collegarum inter se, qualis de- scribitur Joh. VII. 50. & Actor. V. 35. quam legitimam ac- cusationem judicantibus aliis, certum est multos fuisse Sacerdotes extra Senatum, & si qui eorum accusatoris personam susceperint sibimet judicandi ademisse potesta- tem. Erant quidem munia Sacerdotalia, docere popu- lum universum & singulos consulentes tum de rebus aliis, tum præsertim de iis omnibus quæ ad sacra cæremo- niasque pertinerent Levit. X. 10. 11. Ezech. XLIV. 23. Agg. II. 12. 13. Præterea sicut aliæ tribus suos habebant mo- deratores qui tribus communia curarent, ita & in Levitica tribu Sacerdotum potissimi tribus suæ rebus erant præpositi, per quos curabatur perceptio & erogatio decimarum aliarumque obventionum, quæ Sacerdotum ac Levitarum alimentis, templique usibus erant destinata, ut videre est 2. Reg. XXII. & 2. Paral. XXXIV. & apud Jo- sephum pluribus locis Sed hæc omnia nihil ad judiciariam potestatem pertinebant, quæ non erat penes collegium aliquod mere Sacerdotale aut Leviticum, sed penes Senatum quem dixi, cujus bona pars ex Sacerdotibus con- stabat, ut aliquot petitis ex Mose testimoniis supra probatum est. Ideo de Sacerdotibus, ut in eo Senatu præcipuis per Ezechielem dicitur: In causis cognoscendis jus servanto, secundum jura legesque & statuta mea judicanto, cap. XLIV. 24. Idem vero Ezechiel ali- quanto ante describens corruptos mores populi, speciatim meminerat Senatus magni, septuaginta senes nominans, & eorum principem Jaazaniam IIX. 11. In exilio Baby- lonico hos septuaginta auctoritatem suam apud Judæos retinuisse non est dubitandum. Imo & judicia capitalia ab hoc Senatu exercita concessu Regum Persarum tradunt Hebræi. Domum autem reversis judiciaria potestas con- cessa est à Rege Artaxerxe Esdræ VII. 25. 26. Postea armis adversus Antiochum reddita libertate, summa rerum penes hunc senatum fuit, unde & sceptrum regium in curia asser- vabatur. Erat autem curia in ipso templo parte Austrina, vo- cabaturq; לשכת הגזית conclave excisi lapidis. Mansit is ordo continua surrogatione, per manuum, ut dixi- mus, impositionem, ad Herodem usque Magnum, cujus po- tentiam atque audaciam magis magisq; contra leges insur- gentem, cum non in tempore severis, ut oportuit, judiciis repressissent Senatores, Deo ita res disponente, graves ne- glecti muneris pœnas dedêre, interfecti ab Herode omnes, extra unum Sameam, quem talia monentem sæpe contem- serant. In peremptorum locum Herodes alios surrogavit, suam haud dubie factionem, ex iis qui beneficio ipsius ad Sacerdotia aut honores alios pervenerant. Sed & ante non parum imminuta erat Senatus Hierosolymitani au- ctoritas, cum post Pompeji victoriam Gabinius Syriæ præses alios quatuor consessus erexisset Gadaris; Ama- thunte, Hierichunte, Sephoris, sed non pari jure cum Hie- rosolymitano. Nam Herodes nondum rex de rebus in Galilæa gestis causam dixit apud Senatum Hiero- solymitanum. Fuerunt ergo consessus illi curandæ magis reipublicæ quam judiciorum causa instituti, aut si & judiciorum causa, sub Senatu tamen Hierosolymitano. Quin & extra Palæstinam Judæi ad exemplum hujus Sy- nedrii senatus suos habebant. Ita γερουσίας Judæorum A- lexandriæ habitantium mentio est apud Philonem. Ipse Josephus simili Senatorum numero γερουσίαν in Galilæa constituit, cum bello inibi præfectus esset. At Senatus Hie- rosolymitani arctior facta est potestas Augusti temporibus, cum pars Judææ potior in provinciam esset redacta, consti- tuto, ut ferme in omnibus provinciis Romani imperii, ne Senatus quenquam mortis supplicio afficeret nisi Romani præsidis consensu : servata ei reliqua judiciaria potestate. Et hoc est quod ajunt Thalmudici titulis de Synedrio & de Sabbato, judicia animarum, id est capitalia, ablata fuisse ab eo Senatu XL. annis ante excidium urbis. Nam exci- sis demum à Tito Hierosolymis, simul & is senatus plane interiit. Nomen usitatissimum hujus Senatus fuit συνέδριον, non quod alii quoque judicum cœtus non ita appellaren- tur,sed quod ob excellentiam proprie maximus ille con- sessus eo nomine honestaretur, qui & Athenis atq; in aliis Græcis civitatibus usus erat ejusdem nominis. Postquam Macedones in partibus præpolluerant, ut multæ aliæ voces Græcæ ita hæc quoque in Hebræorum sermonem migravit. Itaque Thalmudistis vocatur hic senatus modo סנהדרין simpliciter, modo cum additamento סנהדרין גדולה זו συνέδριον τό μέγα. Vox hæc συνέδριον pro senatu, aut etiam pro Senatus curia posita conspicitur multis in locis in Evange- lica historia & Actis Apostolicis. Vocatur & γερουσία in e- dicto Antiochi & alibi apud Josephum Judith. XI. 11. I. Mac- cab. XII. 6. 2. Maccab. & 3. Maccabæorum non longe ab initio, itemque Actor. V. 21. quo nomine etiam Spartiatæ utebantur. Item πρεσβυτέριον τῶ λαῶ Luc. XXII. 66. ut di- stinguatur à consessibus civitatum, qui itidem πρεσβυτέρια vocabantur. Senatores ipsi modo communiter vocantur πρεσβύτεροι aut etiam άρχοντες τῶ λαῶ, Josepho etiam γνώ- ριμοι τῶ δήμῳ, modo distincte appellantur hi qui Senatores erant extra Sacerdotes. Adsidebant his consilii causa legis periti, ut ante diximus, οἱ γραμματεῖς τῆς βυλῆς, ut Josephus loquitur qui Aristæum quendam eo honoris nomine indi- gitat, unde passim videmus eum Senatum hisce partibus describi, præcipuis Sacerdotibus, senibus aliis, & legisperi- tis. His explicatis ad Christi verba veniamus. Si quis recte advertat ad ea crimina, quæ soli summo synedrio re- servabantur, inveniet gravissimis eorum pœnam lapidatio- nis aut usu, aut lege esse constitutam: quæ ad ipsos etiam falsos Prophetas & perduellionis reos pertinebat Deuter. XVII. 5. Reg. XXI. 10. Quare hanc pœnam ut gladio gra- viorem in secundo gradu positam arbitror.

Εἰς τὴν γέενναν τῆ πυρός) Hic jam tertius sequitur gra- dus. Ut autem priores duo gradus enunciati sunt per comparationem aspectabilium cruciatuum, ita & hic ter- tius. Cum autem supra lapidationem nulla pœna in usu Judaico esset [nam ignis pœna non erat lenti vivi combu- stio, sed immissio in viscera candente ellychnio] quæsivit Christus aliunde nomen horrendi cruciatus, qui & gla- dium & lapidationem excederet. Nota autem res erat Judæis omnibus, quomodo extra urbem Hierosolyma ma- jores ipsorum turpiter imitati crudelem Phœnicum super- stitionem instituissent miseros infantes ignibus ad mortem usquam cruciare, circumstrepentibus interim tibiis tympa- nisque, ne dolore expressus clamor exaudiretur. Locus tam sævo sacro dicatus Tophet dicebatur: Ipsius loci locus amplior, vallis filiorum Hinnomi, גי הנום quod po- steriorum temporum pronunciatio extulit γέενα. Quod autem ex Hebræis magistris affertur in eundem locum de- lata fuisse cadavera, cum Jeremiæ vaticinio congruit VII. 32. cœptumque id fieri temporibus Josuæ 2. Reg. XXIII. 10. Nam is legitur eum locum polluisse: illatis nimirum ca- daveribus, Mos enim erat Judæis loca vetitis cæremoniis usurpata eo modo impura atque abominanda efficere, ut videre est dicto capite XXIII. 16. Sic Samaritas narrat Jose- phus odio Judaici templi διάρῥιψιν ἀνθρωπείων ὀστῶν ἐν ταῖς στοαῖς ποῆσαι Originum XXVIII. 3. sed hoc ad verborum Christi explicationem non pertinet. Apparet enim à Christo cruciatum & quidem gravissimum indicari. Sic- ut autem hic graviora futuri seculi supplicia Gehennæ igni- bus comparantur: ita alibi comparatione in consuetudi- nem migrante hoc ipso nomine pœnæ ævi alterius signifi- cantur. Et hoc sensu vox hæc invenitur in paraphrasi Hierosolymitana, Gen. III.

Plausibilis nec inconcinna videtur Grotii ex- plicatio de diversis mortis generibus, cui id impri- mis favet, quod gehennæ ignis proprie mortem il- lam atrocem in valle Hinnon respiciat potius quam combustionem, quæ pœnæ loco decernebatur. A- tur. Alii tamen tertium hunc gradum pœnæ ca- pitalis etiam à synedrio deducunt, & ἀπὸ κοινοῦ vo- ces præcedentes repetunt ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρὸς: quibus accedit Dn. Win- strupius, cum Spanhemio, & aliis, gehennam ignis proprie nihil aliud significare docens hoc loco, quam שרפה vivicomburium, quo comburendi non in succenso rogo cremabantur, sed liquefà- cto metallo in os infuso necabantur; Cui senten- tiæ hæc favent (1.) Quod de pœnis in judicio assigna- tis hic sermo fit, qualis non erat illa ustulatio in- ter candentia statuæ Molochi brachia. Quæ nec pœna erat, nec in judiciis Judaicis decernebatur: Sed mos profanus, & idololatricus fuit per κακο- ζηλίαν à Judæis assumtus. (2.) Quod gravissima pœnarum inter Judæos fuerit non lapidatio, sed combustio. Quo facit observatio B. Glassii è Schi- kardo, quam is in tract. de Jur. Reg. c. IV. ex Thalmud. adduxit: Præter decollationem seu gla- dium (quo solo plectere delinquentes Regi licebat) sy- nedrium habebat tria suppliciorum genera: strangu- lationem, lapidationem, & combustionem. Combu- rendi non in succenso rogo cremabantur, ut venefica no- biscum, sed liquefacto metallo in os infuso necaban- tur etiam in fœtida palude. Solent alias 4. ista ge- nera pœnarum hoc ordine recenseri ab Ebræis 1. הרג vel הרג כסיף occisio gladii, vel decollatio. 2. חנק strangulatio. 3. סקילה lapidatio, & 4. שרפה combustio: quæ quatuor genera sup- pliciorum dicuntur tradita לבית domui judicii. (3.) Quo facit quod observat B. Chemnitius p. 563. in judicio certis delictis certæ pœnæ erant determina- ta & definitæ, ut de homicidio: in synedriis vero pro qualitate & enormitate delictorum de pœnis gravio- ribus & atrocioribus imponendis deliberabatur. Ge- henna vero pœna erat in illa politia cum æterna abo- minatione conjuncta. Fit enim inter gradus politica- rum pœnarum mentio etiam gehennæ. Cadavera enim eorum, qui propter maleficia supplicio affecti erant, plerumque sepeliebantur sicut Christi & Ste- phani, sed tanta poterat esse atrocitas & abominatio delicti, ut vel malefici in loco abominabili Tho- phet interficerentur, Jer. VII. 32. aut cadavera eorum in locum illum infamem, vel sine sepultura projicerentur, vel sibi sepelirentur. Projiciebantur autem vel sepeliebantur talia cadavera in valle fi- liorum Hinnomi. Ille enim locus in sorte tribus Ben- jamin Jos. XV. 8. & XIX. 16. propter immanem i- dololatriam, quæ ibi exustis per ignem in honorem Molochi parvulis exercebatur, 2. Par. XIIX. 3. con- taminatus, infamis, & abominandus per Josiam re- gem redditus erat, & appellatus Thophet. 2. Reg. XXIII. 10. ut cadavera & ea, quæ summa abomina- tioni erant extra Ierusalem in illum locum projiceren- tur. Et Jer. c. VII. v. 31. 32. & XIX. 6. 11. 12. 13. Deus ipse atrocissimas suas pœnas hac valle describit, in- quiens: Non dicetur amplius vallis interfectionis & sepelient in Thophet, eo quod non sit locus &c. Neque dubium est Spanhemio dub. CXXXIX. p. 802. etiam illos, qui damnati erant ad ignem Hieroso- lymis in valle Hinnon exustos, unde obnoxium esse ge- hennæ igni est, eodem autore, obnoxium esse igni accen- so in valle Hinnon. (4.) B. Glassius observat nihil commodius adferri à sapientia potuisse, quam eos, qui ore & lingua prævaricantur, ut metallum liquefactum vicissim ori eorum infundatur, dignos esse.

Opponi autem merito Grotiana interpretatio verborum Christi Pontificiorum, quorum causam li- benter egit hic advocatus, ψευδερμηνεία potest. A- gnoscit enim diversos gradus pœnæ infernalis designa- ri similitudine diversarum mortium, quæ populo no- ta cruciatus magnitudine differebant. Bellarminus contra ut peccatum dari natura sua veniale hisce Christi verbis extorqueat, l. 1. de amiss. grat. & stat. pecc. c. IX. in mentem ejus pervertit: manifestum convitium, judice Christo, facit reum gehennae igni, ac per hoc est peccatum mortale: Iracundia sono vocis expressa, sed ad malum convitii non pertingens, facit reum concilii, i. e. non constat, an mereatur gehen- nam, sed aut ea poena, aut minore digna est. In- veniuntur igitur peccata quaedam, quae leviora sunt, quam ut gehennam ignis mereantur. Atqui Christus non tantum manifestum convitium, sed etiam ira- cundiam sono vocis, aut gestu expressam, & ipsam i- ram temerariam, utut extra non prorumpentem, homicidia esse docet, aeternaeque poenae natura sua hominem obnoxium facere, etsi poenae aeternae gradus constituat, sub diversarum mortium simili- tudine. Non ergo per τὴν γεένναν τοῦ πυρὸς in hisce verbis ad literam significatur ignis infernalis, sed mortis apud Judaeos in valle Hinnom usitata suppli- cium ceu gravissimum & atrocissimum, etsi Christum adumbrare eodem voluisse gravissimum supplicium in altero seculo, dubitandum non sit. Huc enim tendere sententiam Christi e consequentibus col- ligitur, versu nempe 25. 26. ut & 30. ubi voce gehen- nae infernus ipse diserte exprimitur. Quum itaque Scribae & Pharisaei in quinto praecepto actum so- lum externum homicidii prohibitum crederent, & uti eidem soli in judicio synedrii parvi capitalis poena dictabatur, sic in judicio divino reatum poe- nae in altero seculo eodem solo contrahi censerent: Christus ex adverso definit, praeter externum ho- micidium alia lege quinti praecepti comprehendi, ac prohiberi homicidia; utpote iracundiam teme- rariam intus se continentem, iracundiam erumpen- tem in injuriam, vel contemptum externum proxi- mi, & iracundiam erumpentem in convitium grave, ac eorum omnium tantum esse reatum coram Deo, ut mereantur omnia poenam alterius seculi aeternam, sub diversis tantum supplicii aeterni gra- dibus: quemadmodum diversi gradus mortis erant, decollatio in parvo synedrio, lapidatio in synedrio magno dictari solita, & gehenna ignis. - Petitus ob- servat non dici ut in praecedentibus ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ γεέννᾳ τοῦ πυρὸς, sed mutato loquendi genere ἔνο- χος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γεένναν τοῦ πυρὸς, & ex verbis Davi- dis Kimchi ad Ps. XXVII. colligit, in vallem Hinnonis Hierosolymis projecta fuisse haec insepulta cadavera: deinde, ubi cadavera putruissent, ossa illorum fuisse igne combusta, qui huic fini perpetuo ardebat in hac val- le. Unde ab hoc igne perpetuo vallis Hinnonis factum putamus, ut Gehenna dicatur infernus in quo perpe- tuus est ignis, non vero, ut volunt eruditi, à Topheth il- lius vallis, ubi Molocho pueros comburebant. Hinc igi- tur exponi debent verba Christi, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γεένναν τοῦ πυρὸς, id est debet damnari εἰς τὴν γεέν- ναν, quemadmodum dicitur apud Graecos Scriptores, εἰς κόρακας, apud Latinos, ad Gemonias scalas, & si qua sunt hujusmodi: debet insepultus projici in Ge- hennam, sive vallem Hinnonis, quod est longe omnium gravissimum, & ignominiosissimum, & capitis poenae superadditur maxime infame. Quam sententiam suo loco relinquimus. Sensus ergo est, tale discrimen, quale inter obnoxium esse judicio, concilio, & ge- hennae ignis, inter Judaeos reperiebatur, in tri- bunali divino reperiri inter tria ista homicidiorum genera: quod agnoscit Vincent. Regius Jesuita, part. II. diluc. Evang. l. IV. c. IV. quod nempe Chri- stus distinguat hos gradus, Ebraeorum more, & doceat, omnes istos esse dignos poena inferni, quae per judi- cium, & concilium, & gehennam explicetur juxta tamen minorem majoremve gradum poenae inferni, nam minorem poenam significari per judicium, majorem per concilium, maximam per gehennam.

Eadem & Strabi explicatio est in gloss. ordinat. quod propriis & certis modis exprimi non potuit, quibus- dam similitudinibus distinctum est. His enim tribus judicio, concilio, gehenna diversæ mansiones in æter- næ damnatione pro modo peccati signanter exprimun- tur. Nulla itaque hic distributio suppliciorum, æ- ternorum, temporalium, & brevissimorum, sed æter- norum tantum : quorum diversus gradus, allusione facta ad diversas mortes, penes Judæos, insinuat Dominus, verbis petitis à consuetudine Judaica.

Non ergo gehennæ ignis hic æternam pœnam quoad literam notat, sed genus mortis tempora- riæ, est acerbissimæ inter Judæos; respectu autem intentionis Christi, quæ ex hac allusione ad Judai- cam consuetudinem colligitur, majorem gradum insinuat pœnæ æternæ, uti reliquis de reatu judicii & synedrii minores gradus æternæ pœnæ insinuantur. Conf. Spanhemius l. c. Sensum totius versiculi non incommode è B. Selneccero exposuit B. Glassius: q. d. Vos Pharisæi capitali supplicio (quod à judicio 23. irrogari solet) dignum æstimatis homicidium so- lum externum; alia peccata quibus ad eædem non de- scenditur, pro leviculis, pœna graviore indignis haben- tes. At ego dico vobis, quod in judicio Dei longe secus se res habeat. In eo enim pro homicidio etiam habetur in- ternus iræ injustæ, simultatum & inimicitiæ affectus, qui ob id, si humanitus loqui, & vestrum ad judiciorum. ordinem respicere velim, ea merito plectendus esset pœ- na qua vos externum plecti curatis homicidium. Rur- sus, qui iræ insuper externæ in gestibus & sermone quo- cunque mordaci indicia profert (quale vox Raca est;) is gradu supplicii majori dignus esset, ut nimirum San- hedrin seu concilium magnum, (quod nonnisi de rebus gravissimis judicare solet) de eo ferret mortis sen- tentiam. Et quid de eo tandem dicendum, qui calu- mnias cum bile atra, ex stomacho indignabundo, evo- mit, quam quod absque causæ in judicio cognitione ulla, tanquam dedecus & opprobrium, in gehennam ignis ut projiciatur, h. e. vivus comburatur, sit dignis- simus, Ex hoc judiciorum & suppliciorum vestratium ritu discite peccata rite æstimare, & fœditatem eo- rum, cum reatu tristissimo, agnoscere, qui est æ- terna inferorum pœna, qua qui remissionem hoc in sæculo non consequentur, adficientur contra hæc & alia Dei præcepta, corde, gestu, lingua, facto ipso peccantes &c. Nimirum adhibet Christus verba illa judicii, synedrii, gehennæ ignis, suam sententiam Pharisaiæ opponens, usu & more recepto, quod postulat oppositio, quæ eodem modo & sensu fieri, juxta leges contradictionis debet; Vos dicitis judicii reum esse, qui homi- nem interficit; Ego vero dico reum esse judicii, qui temere irascitur fratri, majori autem reatui sy- nedrio obnoxium qui Raca ei dicit, maximo suppli- cio, quale vobis censetur Gehennæ ignis dignum, qui eum stultum dicit. Quid in judicio divino per hof- ce gradus pœnarum in diversis judiciis figurata & parabolica hac loquutione Christus subinnuat, imo proprie intendat, id declarat quoque verbis luculentis, de homine implacabili carceri manci- pando, donec extremum obulum persolvat, hoc est, in æternum. Cum enim ille qui fratri reconci- liari renuit, æternum carceris infernalis supplicium minatus sit Christus, facile intelligitur, eos qui i- ram adversus fratrem concipiunt & fovent, qui- que gestibus sarcasticis, & verbis injuriosis ex affectu maligno subsannant, & ita contra præceptum quin- tum, animo, gestu, & ore à Christo judicantur prævaricari, cum judiciis, Synedrio, & igni ge- hennæ ideo rei pronunciantur, non temporale ali- quod judicium, aut supplicium, quod ob iram ani- mo conceptam metuendum minime est, sed æter- num similiter respici ac designari, etsi sub isto graduum pœnarum infernalium discrimine, qua- re in pœnis capitalibus deprehendebatur apud Judæos receptis, uti erant decollatio, lapidatio, vi- vicomburium. Nec est,quod hic opponatur,per gehennam ignis semper in N. Test. designari pœnas æternas: quia dispar aliorum locorum est ratio, quum hic mani- festa fiat allusio ad diversos gradus mortis penes Ju- dæos,gehennæ vero solius alibi tantum mentio fiat, sine comparatione. Atque ita recte Grotius: sicut hic graviora futuri seculi supplicia gehennæ ignibus comparantur, ita alibi comparatione in consuetudinem migrante hoc ipso nomine pœna ævi alterius significan- tur. Non dubium,quin hoc quoque gehennæ ignis æter- num ignem repræsentet, sed & judicium humanum repræsentat divinum, & synedrium tribunal Dei, non quod diversa sint tribunalia in cælis, sed quia gravior reatus graviore pœna plectitur à Deo, levior leviore, omnis vero æternæ pœnæ obnoxius: quemadmodum etiam Maldonatus fatetur, Christum & eum qui ira- scitur, & eum qui fratrem suum levem, & eum, qui stultum appellat, eadem inferni pœna, non eadem pœnæ gravitate dignum docere. Cæterum quia hic gehennæ nomen occurrit, quod translatum postea ad infernum exprimendum, id tantum addimus, à valle Hinnom vocibus גיא vallis & הנום Hinnom(quod viri nomen erat) id depromptum,ideo loco æterni supplicii exprimendi adhiberi videri,quod in val- le illa seu Tophet olim diaboli sedes fuerit,atrocis- sime sævientis in homines, cui in Molochi imagi- ne offerebantur ignis flamma crudelissime tor- quendi: siquidem imago inferni illic etiam fuerit, sædis diaboli & loci cruciatuum, (voce loci ὡς ἐν πλάτει acccepta) hominum qui diabolo servie- runt, atrocissimorum. Alias rationes appellationis si lubet vid. ap. B. Gerhard. L. de inferno, §. 8.

## 5:23
Verse 23. προσφέρῃς) That is, you desire to offer, you are going to offer, as the following clause shows. For an offering is properly made when a thing is placed upon the altar.

δῶρον σῦ) The Syriac is קורבנך. It signifies by that name, elsewhere indeed money which was put into the treasury, but here a voluntary sacrifice, the rite of which is prescribed in Lev. 1:2, where the same Hebrew word is to be found. It is more fully called δῶρον τὸ ἐπάνω τῦ θυσιαςηρίυ below in XXIII. 18. There is also a case where that which was offered by the command of the law comes under the name of δῶρον, as below in VIII. 4. There are two things which Christ teaches us by this characterization: first, although true religion toward God excels other duties, that is not to be extended to the observation of rites. For the duties of benevolent charity are to be preferred to ritual care: which he pursues more broadly below in ch. IX. 13 and ch. XII. 7. Then, that sacred rites, however sumptuous or laborious, do not even please God when they are celebrated by a mind seething with anger or hatred, which the history of Cain clearly places before our eyes: namely because, as Seneca also saw, the honor of God is not in victims, even if they are the best and shine with gold, but in the pious and upright will of those who worship. Plato in the second Alcibiades: 'It would be terrible if the gods looked at our gifts and sacrifices, and not at the soul, whether one happens to be holy and just.' Philo on victims: 'He wishes to instruct us himself through symbols, that whenever they approach the altars, either to pray or to give thanks, they should bring no infirmity or passion to the soul.' But on the contrary, the experts of the law and the Pharisees thought that sacrifices and gifts offered to the temple were valid for the expiation of all faults which judges do not punish, even without the amendment of the mind.

ὁ ἀδελφός σε) That is, another, as has just been said.

ἔχει τι κατὰ σῦ) That is, he has something about which he could complain. For the same expression is taken in Rev. II. 4, 12, 20, for which Paul says: μεμφὴν πρὸς τινα ἔχειν in Col. III. 13. These seem to me to cohere with the preceding in this way. Since you have now understood how greatly the lust for being angry and reviling displeases God, the first thing would be to take diligent care against every such offense: But if, however, through human infirmity such a thing has happened to you, there remains πλῦς ὁ δεύτερος, namely that you wash it away by swift repentance; that will happen if you, who were the first to offend, are also the first to enter the way of peace: and that indeed so promptly that there is nothing, however specious, which you should think ought to be preferred to that concern.

Latin:

Vers. 23. προσφέρῃς) Id est, offerre cupias, oblatum eas, ut sequens comma ostendit. Nam proprie fit obla- tio cum res altari imponitur.

δῶρον σῦ) Syrus קורבנך.Significat autem eo nomi- ne, alibi quidem pecunia quæ in gazophylacium mitteba- tur, hic vero sacrificium voluntarium, cujus ritus præscribi- tur Lev. I. 2. ubi eandem vocem Hebræam reperire est I- dem plenius vocatur δῶρον τὸ ἐπάνω τῦ θυσιαςηρίυ infra XXIII. 18. Est & ubi id quod ex imperio legis offerebatur, venit δῶρε nomine,ut infra VIII. 4. Duo autem sunt quæ per hunc χαρακτηρισμὸν Christus nos docet: primum quan- quam vera religio in Deum cæteris officiis præstat,id tamen non protendendum ad rituum observationem. Charitatis enim benevolæ officia rituali curæ antevertenda: quod latius infra prosequitur c. IX. 13. c. XII. 7. Deinde ne pla- cere quidem Deo sacra quantumvis sumtuosa aut operosa quæ animo celebrantur ira aut odio æstuante, quod clare nobis ob oculos ponit Caini historia: nimirum quia, ut Seneca etiam vidit, non in victimis, licet optimæ sint, au- roque præfulgeant, Dei sit honos, sed in pia ac recta vo- luntate venerantium. Plato Alcibiade secundo: δεινὸν ἂν εἴη πρὸς τὰ δῶρα κὶ τὰς θυσίας ἀποβλέπωσιν ἡμῶν, οἱ θεοὶ, ἀλλὰ μὴ πρὸς τὴν ψυχὴν, ἄν τις ὅσιος κὶ δίκαιος ὢν τυγχάνῃ. Philo de vi- ctimis: Βύλεται ἀυτὸς ἀναδιδάξαι διὰ συμβόλων, ὁπότε προσέρ- χοιντο εἰς βωμὸς, ἢ ἐυξόμενοι ἢ ἐυχαριςήσοντες, μηδὲν ἀῤῥώςη- μα ἢ πάθος ἐπιφέρεσθαι τῇ ψυχῇ. At contra legis periti & Pharisæi sacrificia & dona templo oblata valere putabant ad expiationem omnium culparum, quas judices non pu- niunt, etiam citra animi emendationem.

ὁ ἀδελφός σε) Id est alter, ut modo dictum est.

ἔχει τι κατὰ σῦ) Id est, habet,quo de queri posset. Ita enim locutio eadem sumitur Apoc. II. 4. 12. 20. pro quo Paulus dicit: μεμφὴν πρὸς τινα ἔχειν Col. III. 13. videntur mihi hæc cum præcedentibus hoc modo cohærere. Cum jam intelle- xeritis quantopere Deo displiceat irascendi & conviriandi libido, primum quidem fuerit ab omni tali delicto diligen- ter sibi cavere: Quod si quid tamen per humanam infirmi- tatem tale tibi evenerit,superest πλῦς ὁ δεύτερος, nempe ut celeri pœnitentia idipsum eluas, id fiet si qui prior offendi- sti prior quoque ineas pacis viam: & id quidem properiter adeo ut nihil sit, quantumvis speciosum quod ei curæ præ- vertendum putes.

## 5:24
Verse 24. Διαλλάγηθι) It is not always διαλλαγῆναι, which the scholiast on Thucydides wants, 'to be reconciled and made friendly to him': for here it is attributed to him who is anxious about restoring friendship, just as also καταλλάττεσθαι to God. The Latins also use 'redire in gratiam' in either sense. The sense, however, is that one must devote effort to return to favor with him whom we have offended by a more atrocious look or deed: but that is usually done by testifying that we do not wish what was done, which the Latins call 'satisfacere'. For the outcome is not always in our hand. But just as Christ here urges him who has offended to seek peace, so in Mark XI. 25 he warns him who has been offended not to make himself difficult about forgiving the injury, which Paul explains clearly in Colossians III. 13.

St. Chrysostom understands the admonition of Christ not only concerning him who has offended, but also concerning the offended or injured party, the Syriac version not denying it, 'if anyone has something against you', that is, if you do not get along well with another, but someone bears enmity toward you, whether deserved or undeserved, devote effort so that a composition may be made, either by seeking reconciliation if you have offended, or by dismissing it if you have been offended. And therefore Chrysostom thinks that it was not said 'reconcile yourself to your neighbor', but 'be reconciled' (διαλλάγη), which is fitting for both the offender and the offended, or 'seek reconciliation', or 'allow yourself to be reconciled'. But that phrase, 'if he has something against you', is forensic, and properly sounds of the injured party, who has a cause for complaining about someone (Acts XIX. 33, ch. XXIV. 30, Rev. II. 4, II. 30). The former exhortation, therefore, v. 23, 24, is more correctly understood with Augustine concerning that part which gives offense, so that one may strive to appease the offended party and return to favor with him: but the latter, v. 25, pertains to the offended party, so that it also may be inclined and ready for reconciliation, and not be too morose and rigid toward its adversary who had caused the injury, lest on account of rigid implacability they be delivered to the judge, even to pay their debt, Matt. 18:31. This is the explanation of the blessed Chemnitz, Chytraeus, and Hunnius: Piscator and Spanheim judge that this exhortation also pertains to the offending party: to whom Grotius agrees, ἴσθι εὐνοῶν is clearly the same as what had been said before, διαλλάγηθι. But since Christ urges reconciliation, He wished to prescribe to each party its own duty, and commanded the offending party to request and seek forgiveness, v. 23, 24; but to the offended party He commanded that it easily grant pardon to the one requesting the same, and benevolently forgive. Which the added reason also confirms: because the offended neighbor is a debtor before God, who owes the offender the forgiveness of a fault, when he seeks the forgiveness of a fault from God, Matt. 6:12, not about to obtain grace from God if he denies pardon to his neighbor, but rather to be delivered by this adversary, his neighbor, through groans and sighs, on account of the denied reconciliation, to the supreme judge, and to be cast into prison, from which there is no exit, on account of an implacable spirit. For although a neighbor ought not to sigh for the sake of vengeance, even against an implacable person, James 5:9, yet when he is distressed in spirit and groans on account of the denied grace, and deplores the hardness of the implacable neighbor, he is said metonymically to deliver him to the judge, because those groans are the cause why that implacable person is drawn by God the judge to sentence and punishment: although he does not properly deliver him by accusing and demanding vengeance, he delivers him nevertheless by leaving vengeance to God, Rom. 12:19. Finally, to those who deny grace to a brother seeking pardon, it is more fitting what Grotius observes from the book Tanaith was believed by the Hebrews, that the living are accused before God by the dead, to whom they were not reconciled in this life. Although indeed it is the duty of him who has injured his neighbor to seek reconciliation, which is also commonly observed in the forum, as in reconciliation the one who offends first extends his right hand to the offended party: yet Christian charity through συγκατάβασιν easily humbles itself, and succors the infirmity of the neighbor who is difficult about requesting reconciliation, as the occasion arises, so that even if someone has been injured, he may nevertheless offer and seek reconciliation, in order to free the soul of the brother by whom he was offended: since we ought to do good even to those who pursue us with hatred (Matt. 5:44) and (Rom. 12:10), just as GOD himself, although offended by us, deigned to anticipate us with love and to reconcile us to himself (1 John 4:19, Rom. 5:10, 2 Cor. 5:19). ἐλθὼν) This word is redundant, as in Diphilus ἄπεστ᾽ ἀπελθὼν and often in these books. πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρον σε) That is, complete the offering by placing the gift upon the altar: for he had said before, leave the gift before the altar. Vers. 25. ἴσθι εὐνοῶν) It is clearly the same as what was said before, διαλλάγηθι. But they err who drag these things into more obscure allegories, since these sayings of Christ are quite popular. Only this is to be noted, that from what we see happening among men, we are taught the conjecture to be taken as to what is to be expected from God, which Luke 12:58 clearly indicates. Among men, he who yields in time settles on more favorable terms. But he who stubbornly contends in judgment is condemned in full, and is forced without grace to satisfy the judgment. So also before God, against whom those who injure another man directly also primarily offend, timely repentance obtains pardon, while delay provokes severity. This is without doubt the meaning of the words: but because it is sufficiently manifest where the comparison tends, therefore here, as often elsewhere, the ἀνταπόδοσις (apodosis) is left unsaid. Moreover, it is perhaps not foreign to this place that we learn from the book Tanaith that it was believed by the Hebrews that the living are accused before God by the dead, those to whom they were not reconciled in this life. ὁ κριτής σε παραδῷ ὑπηρέτῃ) τῷ πράκτορι Luke 12:58. In Hebrew it would be לשוטר, in Latin it must be called viator. For thus in Roman Law the executors of lawsuits are called, as Tribonian himself explains in Inst. de Actionib. §. Tripli. The Greek jurists call them ἐκβιβαστὰς. There is, however, a very similar use of the word παραδιδόναι in Aristides regarding the art of oratory: ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἐλέγχῃ τὰ ἀδικήματα ῥήτωρ νῦν παραδίδωσι τῷ δικαστῇ· ὁδ᾽ ἀκούσας κὶ μαθὼν παραδίδωσιν ἀυτοὺ ὑπηρεταῖς. εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ) Hence it appears that among the Jews, just as among the Greeks and Romans, those who did not pay their debts were accustomed to be thrown into prison. See L. I, C. Qui bonis ced. possint. Add what is below, 18:29. Vers. 26. κοδράντην) Quadrans, the smallest in the class of coins. Plutarch in Cicero: τὸ λεπτότατον τῶ χαλκᾶ νομίσματος κοαδράντην ἐκάλει. Juvenal: Pieria quadrans tibi nullus in arca. Hence the meretrix quadrantaria. In Horace, and those who are not yet washed with a farthing. For such was the price for which commoners were washed in the baths. Hence it is clear that the similitude is taken from a creditor and debtor, whom Christ wishes, by a friendly and peaceful transaction while they are on the way to the judge, to anticipate the judge's sentence so that the implacable party does not have to experience the rigor of the judge, so that we may be taught by this parabolic speech that reconciliation must be entered into while we are on the way and in the time of grace, lest in the final judgment we feel the rigor of the supreme judge: which sense Grotius also handed down. Only this is to be noted, that from what we see happening among men, we are taught the conjecture to be taken as to what is to be expected from GOD, which Luke 12:58 clearly indicates. Among men, he who yields in time settles on more favorable terms: but he who stubbornly contends in judgment is condemned in full, and is forced without grace to satisfy the judgment: So also before GOD, against whom those who injure another man directly also primarily offend, timely repentance obtains pardon, while delay provokes severity. This is without doubt the meaning of the words, but because it is sufficiently manifest where the comparison tends, therefore here, as often elsewhere, the ἀνταπόδοσις is left unsaid. Quadrans is said to be from the fourth part of an as: which Greek word was also given citizenship, as the Evangelists especially are accustomed to use Latin words as if they were Greek. Luke said ἔσχατον λεπτόν, the last mite, which is half the part of a quadrans, Mark 12:42. That proverbial expression, however, to pay to the last farthing: is about one who, when he is dealt with by strict law, as Cicero said in the last epistle to Atticus, to pay to the number: when the impossibility of payment is noted: just as it was impossible for the servant debtor thrown into prison to pay ten thousand talents, Matt. 18:25, 30. And so Christ teaches that there is no payment of debt or remission of sin after this life, just as he himself interpreted these things in Matt. 6:15, if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive you your sins. And therefore the Papists are clearly opposed to the mind and purpose of Christ, while they promise from these words a payment after this life in purgatory, Stapulens., Bellarm., Corn. à Lap., Tirinus, when the purpose of Christ is to dissuade men from enmities, the avenging of injuries, and tenacious remembrance and an implacable spirit by the danger of eternal and never-ending punishment, as August., Chrysost., Theophyl., and other Ancients teach. Whence they acknowledge that purgatory cannot be proven from this place, along with Hugo Cardinalis, Venerable Bede, and Dionysius the Carthusian, Thomas, Joh. Ferus, Franciscus Lucas, Toletus, Emanuel Sa, Barradius, Jansenius, Maldonatus, and Stapleton. Grotius also disapproves, and teaches that those who drag these things into more obscure allegories are in error, since these sayings of Christ are quite popular, even if elsewhere, namely in Consult. ad Cassandr. chapter on the purgatorial sacrifice, Grotius supports it.

Latin:

Vers. 24. Διαλλάγηθι) Non est semper διαλλαγῆναι quod vult Scholiastes ad Thucydidem τὸ δ᾽, ἀυτοῦ ἔχθρᾱ παρα- κληθῆναι κᾲ φιλιοθῆναι ἀυτῷ: Nam & hic ei tribuitur, qui de restituenda amicitia sollicitus est, quomodo & καταλλάτ- τεσθαι θεῷ. Etiam Latini utrovis sensu dicunt redire in gra- tiam. Sensus autem est, dandam operam ut cum eo quem atrociore vultu aut facto offendimus, redeamus in gratiam: id autem fieri solet testando nolle nos factum, quod Latini satisfacere vocant. Eventus enim non semper in nostra est manu. Sed ut hic eum qui læsit ad quærendam pacem Christus excitat, ita apud Marcum XI. 25. eum qui læsus est monet, ne difficilem se præbeat ad condonandam in- juriam, quod dilucide explicat Paulus Coloss. III. 13.

S. Chrysostomus intelligit admonitionem Christi non solum de eo, qui læsit, sed etiam de offenso vel læso, non abnuente Syriaca versione, si quis habet aliquid adversus te, hoc est, si tibi cum alio non bene convenit, sed aliquis inimicitias tecum gerit, sive me- ritas, sive immeritas, da operam, ut fiat compositio, sive petendo reconciliationem, si læsisti, sive dimittendo si læsus sis. Atque ideo existimat Chrysostomus non es- se dictum reconcilia tali proximum, sed reconciliare διαλλάγη, quod & offendenti & offenso convenit, vel quære reconciliationem, vel patere te reconciliari. Sed phrasis illa, si habet aliquid adversus te, forensis est, & proprie sonat de parte læsa, quæ causam habet conquerendi de aliquo Act. XIX. 33. c. XXIV. 30. Ap. II. 4. II. 30. Prior ergo parænesis v. 23. 24. rectius de parte ea, quæ offendit, accipitur cum Augustino, ut studeat offensum placare, & in gratiam cum eo redire: posterior vero v. 25. ad partem offensam per- tinet, ut ea etiam prona ac prompta sit ad reconci- liationem, nec nimis morosa & rigida adversario suo, qui læserat, ne propter rigidam implacabilita- tem tradantur judici, ad persolvendum etiam de- bitum suum Matth. XIIX. 31. Quæ est B. Chemnitii, Chytræi & Hunnii explicatio: Ad partem quidem lædentem Piscator & Spanhemius hanc quoq; paræ- nesin spectare censent: quibus annuit Grotius ἴσθι εὐνοῶν plane idem est, quod ante dictum erat διαλλά- γηθι. Sed quum Christus ad reconciliationem hor- tetur, utrique parti suum officium præscribere vo- luit, ac partem offendentem jussit condonationem postulare ac quærere v. 23. 24. parti autem offensæ præcepit, ut facile veniam concedat postulanti e- andem, ac benevole ignoscat. Quod etiam ratio addita confirmat: quia proximus offensus est debi- tor coram Deo, qui debet offenso condonationem delicti, cum à Deo condonationem delicti expetit Matth. VI. 12. non impetraturus gratiam à Deo, si proximo deneget veniam, quin tradendus ab hoc ἀντιδίκῳ proximo, gemitibus & suspiriis, ob denega- tam reconciliationem, summo judici, & in carcerē, è quo nullus exitus, compingendus, ob animum implacabilem. Etsi enim vindictæ causa non debeat suspirare proximus, etiam adversus implacabilem Jac. V. v. 9. tamen cum animo angitur & gemit, ob denegatam gratiam, ac deplorat duritiem pro- ximi implacabilis, metonymice tradere eum judici di- citur, quia gemitus illi causa sunt, cur à judice Deo implacabilis ille ad sententiam & pœnam trahatur: Utut proprie non tradat, accusando & vindictam po- stulando, tradit tamen vindictam Deo relinquendo, Rom. XII. 34. His denique qui fratri veniam peten- ti gratiam denegant, magis convenit, quod ex libro Tanaith observat Grotius Hebræis creditum, à mor- tuis accusari apud Deum vivos eos, quibus in hac vita conciliati non fuere. Etiamsi vero ejus qui læ- sit proximum, sit quærere reconciliationem, quod etiam in foro communiter, ut in reconciliatione primum porrigat dextram offensæ parti qui offen- dit, observari solet: Christiana tamen charitas per συγκατάβασιν se facile demittit, ac proximi infirmitati, qui difficilis ad reconciliationem po- stulandam est, pro re nata fuccurrit, ut etiam si læ- sus quis sit, offerat tamen, atque expetat reconci- liationem, ut fratris à quo offensus est, animam li- beret: siquidem & illis benefacere debeamus, qui nos odio prosequuntur Matth. V. v. 44. & charita- te fraterna alii alios prævenire debeamus. Rom. XII. 10. quemadmodum DEUS ipse, etsi offensus à nobis, dignatus prævenire nos amore, sibique reconciliare 1. Joh. IV. 19. Rom. V. 10. 2. Cor. V. 19. ἐλθὼν) παρέλκε hæc vox, ut apud Diphilum ἄπεστ᾽ ἀπελθὼν & in his libris sæpe. πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρον σε) Id est, consumma oblationem, munus imponendo altari: ante enim dixerat, relinque munus pro altari. Vers. 25. ἴσθι εὐνοῶν) Plane idem est quod ante dictum erat διαλλάγηθι. Errant autem qui hæc trahunt ad ἀλληγο- ρίας obscuriores, cum hæc dicta Christi sint admodum po- pularia. Tantum id notandum est, ex eo quod inter ho- mines fieri videmus, doceri nos conjecturam capiendam quid à Deo sit exspectandum, quod aperte indicat Lucas XII. 58. Inter homines benignioribus conditionibus depa- ciscitur qui cedit in tempore. At qui pertinaciter judicio contendit, is in solidum condemnatur, & sine gratia cogi- tur judicatum facere. Sic & apud Deum, in quem præci- pue delinquunt etiam quorum injuria directe hominem al- terum petit, matura pœnitentia veniam impetrat, dilata se- veritatem provocat. Hæc sine dubio verborum sententia: sed quia satis manifestum est quo tendat comparatio, ideo hic, ut alibi sæpe, ἀνταπόδοσις subticetur. Cæterum non alienum forte ab hoc loco est, quod ex libro Tanaith disci- mus, Hebræis creditum à mortuis accusari apud Deum vi- vos eos, quibus in hac vita conciliati non fuere. ὁ κριτής σε παραδῷ ὑπηρέτῃ) τῷ πράκτορι Lucas XII. 58. In Hebræo fuerit לשוטר, Latine dicendum est viatori. Ita enim in Jure Romano appellantur executores litium, ut explicat ipse Tribonianus Inst. de Actionib. §. Tripli. Græci Jurisconsulti vocant ἐκβιβαστὰς. Est autem vocis πα- ραδιδόναι usus valde similis apud Aristidem pro arte orato- ria : ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἐλέγχῃ τὰ ἀδικήματα ῥήτωρ νῦν παραδίδωσι τῷ δικαστῇ· ὁδ᾽ ἀκούσας κὶ μαθὼν παραδίδωσιν ἀυτοὺ ὑπηρεταῖς. εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ) Hinc apparer apud Judæos, itidem ut apud Græcos Romanosque, solitos fuisse in carcerem conjici, qui se ære alieno non exsolvebant. Vide L. I, C. Qui bonis ced. possint. Adde quod infra est XVIII. 29. Vers. 26. κοδράντην) Quadrans minimum in nummorum genere. Plutarchus Cicerone: τὸ λεπτότατον τῶ χαλκᾶ νομίσματος κοαδράντην ἐκάλει. Juvenalis: Pieria quadrans tibi nullus in arca. Hinc meretrix quadrantaria. Apud Horatium, & qui non- dum are lavantur. Tanti enim plebeji lavabantur in bal- nei. Hinc patet, similitudinem adhiberi à creditore & debitore, quos Christus vult amica & placida transactione dum in via sunt ad judicem sententiam judicis prævenire ne rigorem judicis experiri necesseum habeat pars implacabilis, ut doceamur hac parabolica loquutione, ineundam esse, dum in via sumus, & tempore gratiæ, reconcilia- tionem, ne in extremo judicio sentiamus summi judicis rigorem: Quem sensum tradidit etiam Grotius. Tantum id notandum est, ex eo quod inter homines fieri videmus, doceri conjecturam ca- piendam, quid à DEO sit exspectandum, quod aperte indicat Lucas XII. 58. Inter homines beni- gnioribus conditionibus depaciscitur qui cedit in tem- pore: at qui pertinaciter judicio contendit, is in soli- dum condemnatur, & sine gratia cogitur judicatum facere: Sic & apud DEUM, in quem præcipue de- linquunt etiam quorum injuria directe hominem al- terum petit, matura pœnitentia veniam impetrat, dilata severitatem provocat. Hæc sine dubio ver- borum sententia, sed quia satis manifestum est, quo tendat comparatio, ideo hic, ut alibi sæpe, ἀν- ταπόδοσις subticetur. Quadrans à quarta parte assis dicitur: quæ vox Græca etiam civitate dona- ta, uti cumprimis Evangelistæ solent Latinas voces tanquam Græcas usurpare. Lucas ἔσχατον λεπτόν ultimum minutum dixit, quod est dimidia quadrantis pars Marc. XII. 42. Loquutio autem illa proverbialis est, ad ultimum quadrantem solve- re: de eo qui cum agitur summo jure, prout Ci- cero Epist. ult. ad Atticum dixit ad numerum sol- vere: quando solutionis impossibilitas notatur: u- ti servo debitori in carcerem conjecto impossibile erat decem millia talentum exsolvere Matth. XIIX. 25. 30. adeoque docet Christus, nullam post hanc vitam esse debiti solutionem, vel peccati remissio- nem, quemadmodum ipse hæc interpretatus est Matth. VI. 15. si non remiseritis hominibus, nec Pater vester remittet vobis peccata vestra. Ideoque menti & scopo Christi plane adversantur Pontificii, dum ex his verbis solutionem post hanc vitam in purgato- rio promittunt, Stapulens. Bellarm. Corn. à Lap. Tirinus, quum propositum Christi sit periculo æ- ternæ & nunquam finiendæ pœnæ homines ab inimicitiis, injuriarum ultione, ac tenaci recor- datione animoque implacabili dehortari, ut Au- gust. Chrysost. Theophyl. aliique Veteres docent. Unde purgatorium ex hoc loco probari non posse agnoscunt cum Hugone Cardinali Vener. Beda & Dionysio Carthusiano, Thomas, Joh. Ferus, Franci- scus Lucas, Toletus, Emanuel Sa, Barradius, Jan- senius, Maldonatus, & Stapletonus. Improbat etiam Grotius, & errare docet eos, qui hæc tra- hunt ad ἀλληγορίας obscuriores, cum hæc dicta Christi sint admodum popularia, etsi alias, in Consul. nempe ad Cassandr. cap. de sacrificio purgatorio pa- trocinetur Grotius.

## 5:27
Vers. 27. ὁ μοιχεύσεις) לא תנאף which most Hebrews explain as concerning intercourse with a married woman, which is treated in Deut. XXII. 22. Aben Ezra thinks the meaning should be extended more broadly to all non-conjugal Venus. And indeed, just as πορνεία sometimes signifies μοιχεία, as below v. 32, c. XIX. 19, so it is not new that what would properly be called πορνεία is called μοιχεία. Thus Jupiter is said to have committed adultery (μοιχεῦσαι) with Danae in Lucian, and Ovid calls Medea an adulterous virgin. However, even πορνεία was forbidden among the Jewish people to this extent, that girls were not permitted to lead the life of a harlot, and he who had defiled an unmarried woman was compelled to marry her, or if the parents were unwilling, to provide a dowry, and she who had married with a polluted body, or had withdrawn herself to another while she was a betrothed woman, underwent the penalty of stoning, all of which can be seen in Deut.
