Concerning the Hebrew Gospel of Matthew, which Grotius has as the original text, it was dealt with at the threshold.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Ὡσανὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαβὶδ] Vox ὡσανὰ ex verbo & particula Hebræa constans pro ipso hymno usurpatur, ut is παῖαν Græcis. Nam ea interpretatio hic & infra commate 15. convenientior quam ut βaῖα significet. Sensus est: hy- mnum hunc bene ominantem canimus regi Messiæ. Quæri potest, cum ritus ferendi τὰ βαῖα sive θύρσους ἐκ φοινίκων καὶ κι- τρίων, ut Josephus loquitur, & acclamandi Hosana perti- neat ad τὰ ὀχοφόρια (ξυλοφόρια idem Josephus vocat) quæ incidebant in mensem Septembrem, ut apparet Levit.xxiii. 39.40; quomodo nunc longo alio anni tempore sint usur- pata. Sciendum igitur constanter fuisse Judæis creditum, fe- stus dies non tantum memoriam continere Ægyptiaci exi- tus, sed & præsagium temporum Messiæ. Itaque etiam ho- die Judæi ἐν τοῖς ὀχοφορίοις dicunt optare se ut eum in mo- dum lætos dies agere possint regnante Messia, devictisque hostibus. Plebis igitur illa pars quæ miraculis Jesu adducta certo sibi persuaserat hunc verum esse Messiam, velut imple- to præsagio, ritus & verba τῆς ὀχοφορίας recte usurpat. Sic- ut & in nova dedicatione templi sub Hasmonæis eadem læ- titiæ publicæ signa usurpata legimus 2. Macc. X. 7. & 1. Macc. XIII. 51. & Apoc. XVII. 9. Videtur autem ritus ramos ge- standi ut multa alia à Judæis ad Græcos pervenisse. Nam Clemens notat ex Orpheo ramos adorantibus dari solitos. Et Athenis inter festos dies erant τὰ ὀχοφόρια.

Duobus modis τὸ ὡσανὰ Ebr. הושע נא usur- patur: primo pro formula acclamationis è Psalm. CXIIX. 24. adhibetur, Salva obsecro, vel salu- tem, quæso, affer: quam adhibere solebant Judæi imprimis in scenopegiorum festo, frondes & ramos portantes & cantantes quotidie Hosanna, creberrima vocis repetitione ad nomina DEI, Propter te DEUM deorum Hosanna, pro- pter te DOMINUM Hosanna &c. ad attri- buta divina: propter veritatem tuam Hosanna, propter Testamentum tuum Hosanna. Et porro addebane his rebus, quibus gratulabantur templum electorum Hosanna, montem Moria, Hosanna &c. ac deinde iterum ad nomina Dei redeuntes clamabant: DOMINE Salvator, Hosanna; Redemptor & Salvator Hosanna &c. & postmodum per antiphonam, Quæso redime surcu- lum plantationis tuæ, cui succinitur, & Hosanna, &c. Vid. Andr. Osiander l. III. Annot. ad c. xxxvi. Harm. Deinde vox illa pro ipsis arborum ramis accipitur, quas in publica solemnitate festi taber- naculorum gestabant, juxta legem Lev. XXIII. 40. qui à Judæis voce ista appellantur, quod Ho- sanna toties acclamare consueverint, cum eos portarent, uti in Talmud dicitur nectere Hosan- nas: quo sensu hic accipi nonnulli cum Schindlero putant. Sed rectius pro acclamatione hoc loco habetur è Litaniis Judaicis (nam illa cantica ge- mina erant nostris Litaniis) repetita, vel potius è Ps. CXIIX. desumta: qui de adventu & passione Christi agit, siquidem Hieronymo docente, hunc Psalmum Judæi de adventu Messiæ ideo accepe- rint. Quum ergo Hosanna jam non in festo ta- bernaculorum, sed extraordinarie circa Festum Paschatos in honorem Christi decantarint, nul- lum dubium est, factum id esse peculiari Dei dire- ctione, ut Jesus Nazarenus ceu verus Messias hac acclamatione exciperetur: quanquam non displi- ceat Grotii sententia, quod festos dies Paschatos non solum exitus Ægyptiaci memoriam, sed etiam præsagium temporum Messiæ continere Judæis credi- tum fuerit. Quod ergo ad sensum vocis, non repugnamus multum traditæ interpretationi: Hymnum hunc bene ominantem canimus Regi Mes- siæ: uti Theophyl. & Euthymius notant quosdam per Osanna intelligere hymnum, sive laudem: quo re- dire videtur Justini in qq. ad resp. ad orth. interpre- tatio q. L. quod Osanna sit μεγαλωσύνη ὑπερκειμέ- νη magnificentia excellens, & Clementis Alex. l. 1. Pæd. c. 5. quod lucem, & gloriam, & laudem significet. Si tamen κτ' πόδα reddatur, simplicior erit interpre- tatio, utpote consonans Psalmo, è quo vox illa de- sumpta est, hoc modo: Salutem, quæso, adfer, vel Salva, obsecro: Filio David sc. hoc accinimus, vel ominamur, vel precamur. Nam ut recte Casau- bonus in Exerc. p. 449. adversus Baroninm, qui nullum congruentem sensum fore objicit, si eo sensu hoc Osanna accipiatur, quo in Psalmo observat, mos est in omnibus linguis, ut in ejusmodi acclamationi- bus sententiæ semiplenæ efferantur, atq; audientibus relinquantur supplenda verba ad sensum perficien- dum necessaria: aut si non placeat abrupta vel se- miplena oratio: reddere licebit hoc pacto gratula- torium carmen: Hosanna, id est, salutem quæso adfer, vel prosperitatem concede Filio David: quia verbum הוֹשִׁיעָה etiam construitur cum tertio casu Jos. X. 6. Jud. VII. 2. 2. Sam. X. 11. Ps. XLIV. 4. Ps. XXCVI. 16. Ps. XCIIX. 1. Ps. CXVI. 6. ut analoga sit acclama- tio illi, vivat Rex 1. Sam. X. 24. 1. Reg. I. 34. Non de- sunt quidem qui populum hoc Hosianna sibi à Chri- sto salutem precari velint, quæ Hieronymi, Bedæ, Anshelmi, Thomæ, Lyrani, Abulensis est sententia: sed præstat vi collationis Psalmi hæc intelligere, ceu gratulationem Messiæ factam, qua eidem à Deo prosperitatem & felicitatem voveant, ac pre- centur: cui sensui etiam ea, quæ sequuntur, favent.

ἐυλογημέν® ὁ ἐρχόμεν® ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίε] Ex Ps. CXVIII. 26. Felix sit; aut fiat, ut Latini acclamabant. Ἐν ὀνόματι κυ- ρίε, divino mandato, ac potestate.

ἐυλογημέν® sc. ἔστω, benedictus sit à Deo, cumu- letur omnigena benedictione Domini, ὁ ἐρχόμενος nomen est Messiæ Matth. XI. 3. Luc. VII. 19. Joh. I. 15. Qui venire debuit Domini jussu, & voluntate, ac gratiosa οἰκονομίᾳ divinæ : Elias Rabbi formulam illam, Benedictus qui venit Rex in nomine Domi- ni, quæ hic apud Lucam cap. XIX. 38. legitur, Ju- dæos olim in Sacrificiorum oblationibus cecinis- se, perhibet: quæ erant figura Christi, qui ceu agnus Dei hic sistit sese ad oblationem corporis sui.

Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις] In Evangelio Hebraico legebatur ברמם ut nos docet Hieronymus ad Damasum. Hoc autem non puto ad designationem Dei pertinere, sed idem valere, quod summe: ut si Latine dicas terq; quaterq;. Ita Hebreum במרומים & Græce voces ἐν ὑψίστοις inter- pretibus LXX. inveniuntur Ps. CXLVIII. 1. & alibi. Eo- demque sensu במרום & Græce ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις Psalmo XCII. 4.

Sensus ille Grotii exemplis caret. Quæ adfe- runtur, æque dubia sunt. Nec apparet, cur non pro- prie ut sonant, accipienda sint verba: si Grotii more Hosianna τεχνικῶς accipiatur pro Hymno, annon sensus planus erit, Hymnum illum in hono- rem Dei in altissimis habitantis canimus, vel Hosian- na audiatur in altissimis. Si pro gloria & laude accipiatur, consonabit illis Lucæ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις. Nostra autem interpretatione, salva ὀ ἐν ὑψίστοις, qui (es) in altissimis; qui Deus es in excelsis, ut elli- psis sit articuli ὁ, vel subaudiatur participium ὁ ὤν. Simpliciter salva in altissimis; quia salus consum- matur in cœlis. Vossius diversam acclamatio- nem facit, priorem cum pullum asinæ ascendisset Christus; alteram postquam devenit ad descen- sum montis Oliveti, l. I. Harm. Evang. c. IV. §. 7. & 9. sed ea colligi ex Evangelistis non potest. Vero autem affine est, quia diversimode referunt Evangelistæ acclamationem, alios è turba & di- scipulis ita ut Matthæus habet, alios ita ut alii Ev- angelistæ habent acclamasse, sensu eodem. In templo tamen nova postmodum facta est Christo congratulatio, pueris clamantibus Hosianna Filio David, Matthæo teste infra v. 15. De Evangelio Matthæi Ebræo, quod pro originali textu habet Grotius, in limine actum.

## 21:10
Verse 10. All the city was shaken] And the city was moved, Ruth I. v. 19.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις] ותהם העיר Ruth. I. v. 19.

## 21:11
Vers. 11. ὁ προφήτης] Whom we have hitherto acknowledged as a Prophet, we now venerate as a true king.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ὁ προφήτης] Quem hactenus ut Prophetam agnovimus, nunc ut verum regem veneramur.

## 21:12
Vers. 12. εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ] Christ had given some specimen of his kingdom in the hearts of men by the summoning of the donkeys: he now produces a greater and most admirable one in cleansing his Father's house, venerable by no external force, but by divine power alone. From this also the nature of his kingdom is made understood, because, as if inaugurating his kingdom, he enters not a citadel but a temple.

Τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ] It had indeed been rightly established by the experts in the Law, that those who owed victims or gifts by law or vow, especially if they lived far from Jerusalem, could bring money from home, and in exchange for it procure for themselves in Jerusalem a victim or whatever was to be donated, naturally by that law which is concerning tithes, Deut. XIV. 24, 25, 26, extended by no unfair interpretation to other types of similar deeds. But it was by no means fitting for that to be done in the temple, especially at that time when that place of the temple (for these things were done in the outermost part which was called the court of the Gentiles) ought to have called to the Gentiles who were about to convert to the true religion, as Isaiah had predicted. Therefore, it is significantly stated in Mark in this history ὅτι ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. For it is to be noted that most prophecies of that kind have a double sense: the former plain and architectural, which had a tacit condition, if the Jews, upon the arrival of the Messiah, as they ought to have, had shone forth in piety to the other nations: the latter allegorical, which was fulfilled when the Jews were rejected and the Gentiles substituted.

We have often refuted the fiction concerning a double sense, that the perpetual preservation of the Temple and ceremonial rites was promised to the Jews under a condition; it will be taught by no testimony of Scripture. Those sacred rites were to last only until the Messiah, and upon the arrival of the body, the shadows were to vanish: and that was absolutely determined, just as the very

ANNOTATIONS ON MATTHEW CH.

Chrysostom wishes it to be indicated by the ejection of the victims that the time would come when vows and prayers would be duly offered instead of sacrifices. The Gentiles could be joined to the Jews even though the Temple was to be destroyed and the Levitical rites were to be abolished: just as they have indeed been joined to them entirely. For the Jews were not simply rejected. And through that calling and joining or aggregation of the Gentiles, the Prophetic prediction was fulfilled in the literal sense, i.e., properly intended by the Holy Spirit. Concerning which we have dealt in its proper place, i.e., in the Annotations on Eph. LVI. Furthermore, regarding the money-changers, Blessed Jerome thinks thus: namely, that they were placed in the Temple so that those who came into the temple and did not have money to purchase sacrifices could have it on loan. But here we easily agree with those things which Grotius has.

* κολλυβισῶν] κόλλυβον is what they commonly call exchange, ἀλλαγὴ ἀργυρίου according to Pollux. Cicero in the Verrines says that a deduction was made for the collybus, and in a letter, that there is enough loss in the collybus. John also calls these same money-changers κερματιστὰς. Because there were things in the temple which, according to the law or customs, had to be paid in sacred shekels, therefore the money-changers had tables placed in the temple, seeking a small profit from the office of exchanging.

Τὰς περισερὰς] As those with which the poor discharged their duty in place of greater victims: as can be seen throughout in Moses, and Luke II. 24. However, the prefect of offerings was accustomed to give these to those offering for a received price, as Maimonides notes in his book on Sacred Instruments, chapter 7, with which the book Schekalim, chapter 5, section 1, agrees.

Latin:

Vers. 12. εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ] Regni sui in hominum ani- mos specimen aliquod Christus dederat asinorum accitu: majus nunc & maxime admirabile edit in purganda æde paterna, nulla vi externa, sola divina virtute venerabilis. Hinc quoque regni sui ingenium dat intelligi, quod re- gnum velut auspicatus non arcem sed templum ingreditur.

Τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ] Recte quidem à Legisperitis erat constitutum, ut qui victimas aut dona ex lege aut voto deberent, præsertim si procul Hierosolymis habitarent, possent pecuniam domo adferre, proque ea Hierosolymis victimam aut quod donandu esset sibi com- parare, nimirum lege ea quæ est de decimis Deut. XIV. 24. 25. 26. ad alias factorum similium species non iniqua interpre- tatione producta. Sed id in templo fieri minime oportuit, eo præsertim tempore quo is templi locus (facta enim hæc in parte extima quæ gentium dicebatur) vocare debebat gentibus ad veram religionem se converturis, ut prædixe- rat Esaias. Ideo significanter apud Marcum est in hac hi- storia ὅτι ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. Notandum enim est, pleraque vaticinia ejus ge- neris duplicem habere sensum, priorem planum & ἀρχιτέκ- τονον, qui tacitam habebat conditione, si Judæi sub adven- tum Messiæ, ut debebant, gentibus cæteris pietate præluxis- sent: alterum ἀλληγορικὸν, qui impletus est rejectis Judæis & surrogatis gentibus.

Commentum de duplici sensu profligavimus sæpius, sub conditione Judæis promissam fuisse per- petuam Templi & sacrorum ceremonialem conser- vationem, nullo scripturæ testimonio docebitur. Sacra illa durare tantum ad Messiam usq; & adven- tante corpore umbræ evanescere debebant: id- que absolute definitum erat, quemadmodum ipsa

ANNOTATA AD MATTHÆI C

victimarum ejectione id indicatum vult Chrysost. fore tempus quo pro sacrificiis vota & preces rite offerentur. Adjungi gentes Judæis poterant etiamsi destruendum Templum, & abolenda fuerint sacra Levitica : quemadmodum etiam omnino adjunctæ illis sunt. Nec enim simpliciter rejecti sunt Judæi. Et per illam vocationem & adjunctionem vel aggregationem gentium impletum est sensu literali, h. e. à Sp. S. proprie intento vaticinium Propheticum. De quo suo loco, h. e. in Annotat. ad Ef. LVI. egimus. Cæterum de nummulariis ita B. Hieronymus censet: nimirum positos in Templo fuisse, ut qui venirent in templum nec haberent pecuniam ad sacrificia comparanda, mutuo eam habere possent. Sed facile hic annuimus iis, quæ habet Grotius.

* κολλυβισῶν] κόλλυβον est quod vulgo cambium vocant, ἀλλαγὴ ἀργυρίου Polluci. Cicero in Verrina ait deductionem factam pro collybo, & in epistola, detrimenti satis esse in collybo. Eosdem hos mensarios etiam κερματιστὰς Johannes vocat. Quia in templo erant quæ ex lege aut moribus siclis sacris pendi debebant, ideo argentarii mensas in templo positas habebant, lucellum ex permutandi officio aucupantes.

Τὰς περισερὰς] Ut quibus defungebantur pauperes vice majorum victimarum : ut passim in Mose videre est, & Luc. II. 24. Has autem solebat accepto pretio dare offerentibus præfectus oblationum, ut notat Maimonides de Instrumentis sanctis cap. 7. cui consentit liber Schekalim cap. 5. sect. 1.

## 21:13
V. 13. Λῃστῶν] From the LXX version in Jeremiah. By a similar translation, Aeschines said λῃστάς τῶν πραγμάτων. Therefore, that word in this place sounds not so much like a thief as a plunderer: in which sense it is also found in Xenophon in the second book of Greek history. But the Chaldeans also use the Greek word in that meaning. Thus the Ishmaelites לסטים עם are a plundering people to Jonathan, Gen. XXI. 13. There is no doubt that the priests stipulated a part of the gain for the use of the temple; οἶκον ἐμπορίου is in a similar history in John II.

Latin:

V. 13. Λῃστῶν] Ex versione LXX. apud Jeremiam. Simili tralatione λῃστάς τῶν πραγμάτων dixit Æschines. Itaque vox ista hoc loco non tam latronem quam prædonem sonat: quo sensu & apud Xenophontem reperitur Græcæ historiæ secundo. Sed & Chaldæi vocem Græcam eo significatu usurpant. Sic Ismaëlitæ לסטים עם populus prædator Jonathani Gen. XXI. 13. Dubium non est quin pro usu templi partem quæstus stipulati fuerint sacerdotes οἶκον ἐμπορίου est in simili historia apud Johannem II.

## 21:16
Vers. 16. κατηρτίσω] The LXX sometimes express the metaphorical meaning of the verb יסד with a less figurative word, as here καταρτίζειν, and in Esther I. 8, ἐπιτάττειν.

Αἶνον] Thus also עז which is likewise used metaphorically. The LXX translate it with various nouns, as the subject matter requires: as here αἶνον, in Psalm CXXXII. 8, ἁγίασμα. However, it happens in this testimony of the Psalm, as I have said several times, that what David had said figuratively περὶ νηπίων κὰι θηλαζόντων, understanding innocent and simple ones, is fulfilled in Christ while preserving that meaning, and at the same time according to the more proper meaning of the word νηπίων. For we have already read that there were boys in the crowd of those crying out.

It had to be proven that this happens in this testimony of the Psalm; it should not be merely asserted. That the Psalm deals with Christ according to a direct and unique sense, because the Holy Spirit does not delight in homonymy and various senses, we have shown abundantly in the Anti-Grotian vindications of that Psalm, and because it is explained by Matthew concerning the heralds of Christ, with νηπίοις understood properly, why, having dismissed the proper meaning, would we depart to a figurative and improper one approved by the Holy Spirit? For lest anyone suspect that infants are meant, not boys, but those devoid of malice, for this reason he also placed their table, calling them sucklings, as Chrysostom says. Lightfoot: Boys, he says, or from their earliest years, were taught to handle the bundles, and to shake them, and while shaking them to sing Hosanna. Succah. ch. 3, bal. ult. קטן היודע לנענע חייב לולב A little child, as soon as he knows how to shake the bundle, is bound to carry the bundle. Where the Gemara says thus: The Rabbis teach, As soon as a little child can be taught to shake the bundle, he is bound to carry the bundle: as soon as he knows how to veil himself, he should put on the fringes; as soon as he knows how to guard his father's Phylacteries, he should put on his own: as soon as he can speak, his Father should teach him the law, and the recitation of the Phylacteries,

Latin:

Vers. 16. κατηρτίσω] Tralatitiam significationem verbi יסד interdum voce minus figurata exprimunt LXX. ut hic καταρτίζειν, Ester I. 8. ἐπιτάττειν.

Αἶνον] Sic & עז quod itidem tralative usurpatur. LXX. variis nominibus vertunt, prout fert subjecta materia : ut hic αἶνον, in Psalm. CXXXII. 8. ἁγίασμα. Usu venit autem in hoc Psalmi testimonio quod aliquoties diximus, ut quod David περὶ νηπίων κὰι θηλαζόντων dixerat figurate, innocentes & simplices intelligens, id in Christo impletum sit salvo isto significatu, & simul juxta magis propriam vocis νηπίων significationem. Nam & pueros fuisse in clamantium turba jam legimus.

Usu venire id in hoc Psalmi testimonio probandum erat ; non nude asserendum. Psalmum de Christo agere secundum directum & unicum sensum, quia ὁμωνυμία, & variis sensibus non gaudet Spiritus S. in vindiciis Psalmi istius Anti-Grotianis affatim ostendimus, & quia de Christi præconibus explicatur à Matthæo, νηπίοις proprie intellectis, cur missa propria significatione Spiritus S. probata ad figuratam abiremus, & impropriam. Ne enim infantes dici quis suspicetur, non pueros, sed malitia expertes, hac de causa etiam mensam ipsorum apposuit lactantes vocans, dicente Chrysostomo. Lightfootus: Pueri, inquit, vel à primis annis, edocti sunt fasciculos tractare, atque agitare, atque agitantes Hosanna canere. Succah. cap. 3. bal. ult. קטן היודע לנענע חייב לולב Parvulus, quamprimum agitare fasciculum novit, tenetur ad gestandum fasciculum. Ubi sic Gemara : Tradunt Rabbini, Quamprimum parvulus edoceri potest agitare fasciculum, tenetur ad gestandum fasciculum : quamprimum novit se velare, induat fimbrias ; quamprimum novit Phylacteria patris custodire, induat propria : quamprimum fari potest, doceat eum Pater legem, & recitationem Phylacteriorum,

## 21:17
Vers. 17. ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως] So that he might remove as far as possible from himself every suspicion of an affected earthly kingdom: which the city, populous in itself, could foster, the gathering from elsewhere for feast days, and the night time opportune for such attempts, compare what is in John VI. 15 and below ch. XXVI. 55.

Ηὐλίσθη] The Greeks often use this word to translate לִין which is to stay overnight. But this word can be taken properly here to signify to spend the night in the open air: for Luke seems to signify this when he says that Christ ηὐλίζετο on the Mount of Olives every night, ch. XXI. 37. And otherwise this was customary for him, as often as he was free for prayers outside of the order.

PART II. The cursing of the fig tree and the power of faith.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως] Ut omnem effectati regni terrestris suspicionem quam longissime a se amo- veret: quam fovere poterat urbs per se populosa, con- cursus aliunde ad festos dies, & nocturnum tempus ejus- modi conatibus oportunum, confer quod est Job. VI. 15. & infra c. XXVI. 55.

Ηὐλίσθη] Utuntur hac voce Graeci saepe, ut vertant לִין quod est pernoctare. Sed potest hic proprie sumi haec vox, ut significet sub dio agere: id enim significare vide- tur Lucas, cum dicit Christum singulis noctibus ηὐλίζε- το in monte Oliveti c. XXI. 37. Et alioqui solenne hoc ipsi erat, quoties extra ordinem precibus vacabat.

PARS II. Maledictio fici & fidei vis.

## 21:19
Vers. 19. And seeing a fig tree] What was said generally by Dionysius Thrax the grammarian, I fear regarding the ancients. For they thought that some things were not only through speech, but also through symbols, ἐνόμιζον γὰρ γ' ὧν ἃ διὰ λέξεως μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ συμβόλων ἔνιοι τὰς πράξεις, that is most true concerning the Hebrews and their neighbors. Thus some of the Prophets had their heads beaten, others took on iron horns, others bound shackles around themselves. When the most merciful Lord had prefigured his eternal benefits toward us with countless miracles, he shadowed forth the severity of the judgment that awaits unfruitful men with one sign only, and that not in a man, but in a tree that would not feel: so that we might be certain that the sterility of good works is punished by the gratuitous removal of fruitfulness. See those things which are at Hebrews VI. 8, which contain the interpretation of this place. Philo not badly interprets allegorically, ἀλληγορικῶς, those eunuchs who are forbidden by Moses to be admitted into the sacred council as τοὺς ἀρετῆς ἀγόνους, κάρπιση ἐκτετμημένους.

Concerning this approach to the fig tree, Chrysostom in the Catena of the Greek Fathers edited by Possinus: He approached the fig tree not indeed because he desired to taste fruit from it, since he knew perfectly well that it was not the season for eating figs: but seeking an occasion to curse it. As if to avenge that other tree of the same kind situated in paradise: which both by the appearance of its fruit offered an effective allurement to sin to our first parents; and to them, after they had fallen, offered its leaves for the covering of their nakedness, from which they made girdles for themselves by sewing them together. Therefore, in order to show that he was the same one who had once spoken to the authors of the human race in Paradise, he curses this tree, because it had been the cause of sin. This is also a figure of the pleasure that allures and maddens us. For just as the fig tree grows easily from the richness of the soil without any greater care or cultivation by men: so the pleasures of the senses flow forth from the unlabored use of nature; whereas virtue requires the exertion of effort aided by the divine Spirit.

Latin:

Vers. 19. καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν] Quod generaliter dictum est a Dionysio Thrace grammatico vereor de antiquis. ἐνόμιζον γὰρ γ' ὧν ἃ διὰ λέξεως μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ συμβόλων ἔνιοι τὰς πράξεις, id de Hebraeis eorumque vicinis verissimum est. Sic Prophetarum alii contundi sibi capita fecerunt, alii cornua sumserunt ferrea, alii sibi circumdedere com- pedes. Clementissimus Dominus cum innumeris mira- culis sua in nos aeterna beneficia figurasset, severitatem judicii, quod infrugiferos homines manet, uno duntaxat signo, idque non in homine, sed in non sensura arbore, adumbravit: ut certi essemus bonorum operum sterilitat tem gratis foecundantis ademtione puniri. Vide ea quae ad Hebraeos VI. 8. quae hujus loci interpretationem cond- nent. Philo spadones qui in sacrum concilium a Mose admitti vetantur ἀλληγορικῶς non male interpretatur τοὺς ἀ- ρετῆς ἀγόνους, κάρπιση ἐκτετμημένους.

De hoc accessu ad ficum Chrysoft. in Caten. Graec. Patr. a Possino edita: Accessit & ad ficum non ideo quidem quod gustare pomum ex illa cupe- ret, quippe qui praeclare nosset non esse id tempus ve- scendarum ficuum: sed ejus devovenda occasionem quaerens. Quasi ad ulciscendam illam aliam ejus- dem generis in paradiso sitam arborem: quae & spe- cie fructuum, illecebram peccandi efficacem primis obtulit parentibus; & eisdem, postquam lapsi sunt, ad tegumentum nuditatis folia sua praebuit, ex qui- bus consutis sibi perizomata fecerunt. Ut igitur ostenderet eundem se esse qui olim in Paradiso huma- ni generis autoribus locutus esset, hanc devovet arba- rem, quod ea peccati fuisset causa. Est & haec figura voluptatis quae nos allicit & dementat. Ut enim fi- cus sine majori aliqua hominum cura cultuve uber- tate soli facile provenit: sic voluptates sensuum irela- borato profluunt naturae usu: cum virtus contentione studii divino Spiritu adjuti egeat.

## 21:21
Vers. 21. Do not doubt] That διακρίνεσθαι is the same as διστάζειν, to which τὸ πιστεύειν is opposed, we noted at chapter XIV.

To this mountain] See above chapter XVII. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 21. μὴ διακριθῆτε] διακρίνεσθαι esse idem quod διστάζειν, cui opponitur τὸ πιστεύειν, annotavimus ad caput XIV.

Τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ] Vide supra cap. XVII. 20.

## 21:22
Vers. 22. All things] See above chapter XIIX. 19.

PART III. A collation concerning the power of JESUS to teach.

Latin:

Vers. 22. πάντα] Vide supra cap. XIIX. 19.

PARS III. Collatio de IESV potestate docendi.

## 21:23
Vers. 23. Teaching] For he was teaching publicly in the temple the same things he had taught in Galilee, proposing likewise what ought to be believed and done, the rewards of obedience, the remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life. These are the things which Matthew encompasses with this one word, but Luke with two, διδάσκειν and ἐυαγγελίζεσθαι.

The remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life are purely gratuitous gifts, not rewards of obedience. They are received freely through faith, offered in the Gospel: they are not obtained through our obedience or holiness. Acts X. 43. Rom. III. 28. chapter VI. 13. Gal. III. 2.

the chief priests and the elders of the people] and the scribes, which Mark adds. To these three classes of men, the pontiffs indeed as Elders, as part of the Senate, but the experts in the law as their assessors and counselors the great Sanhedrin is described, as we have said elsewhere: to whose office it belonged to discern true and false Prophets. Thus also the Jews relate that legates were sent by the Sages of Israel to Bar-Kochba. But they approached Jesus having first taken counsel, how they might bring destruction upon him, irritated because of his overturning their market in the temple, as Mark notes in chap. XI. 18. Hither, therefore, all that speech tended.

ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ] Whence is this authority of yours? For it was the right of the Sanhedrin to grant the right of teaching in the temple: but from them Christ had received no right. It remained, therefore, that he should defend himself by the command of God, whose supreme right it was over the temple.

ταῦτα ποιεῖς] Namely, that you teach publicly. For Luke shows clearly enough that this question pertains most especially to this. The Jews imitate the question of the Samaritans to Ezra V. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 23. Διδάσκοντι] Docebat enim publice in templo eadem quae in Galilaea docuerat, continentia quid cre- dendum faciendumque esset proponens itidem praemia obedientiae, remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum Sanctum & vitam aeternam. Haec sunt quae hac una voce Mat- thaeus, Lucas autem duabus διδάσκειν & ἐυαγγελίζεσθαι complectitur.

Remissio peccatorum, Spiritus Sanctus & vi- ta aeterna dona mere sunt gratuita, non vero obedientiae praemia. Per fidem accipiuntur gra- tis in Evangelio oblata: non per obedientiam, vel sanctitatem nostram impetrantur Actor. X. 43. Rom. III. 28. cap. VI. 13. Gal. III. 2.

οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ] καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς quod addit Marcus. His tribus hominum generibus, pontifi- cibus quidem Senioribus, ut parte Senatus, legispe- ritis autem, ut eorum assessoribus & consiliariis discri- bitur Synedrium magnum, ut alibi diximus: cujus officio incumbebant veros falsosque Prophetas discernere. Sic & ad Barchochebam à Sapientibus Israëlis missos legatos narrant Judæi. Adierunt autem isti Jesum capto ante con- silio, quomodo ei perniciem possent accersere, irritati ob traductam suam in templo nundinationem, ut notat Mar- cus cap. XI. 18. Huc igitur tota ista tendebat oratio.

ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ] Unde tibi jus istud? Nam Synedrii erat jus docendi in templo concedere: ab iis autem nullum jus Christus acceperat. Supererat igitur ut Dei mandato se tueretur, cujus in templum jus summum erat.

ταῦτα ποιεῖς] Nempe quod publice doces. Huc enim potissimum pertinere hanc quæstionem Lucas satis aper- te ostendit. Imitantur Judæi Samaritarum quæstionem ad Esdram V. 3.

## 21:24
Vers. 24. ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον] A counter-question, such as is noted by the Grammarians on the third Eclogue of Virgil: and it appears not rarely in the books of the Socratics. The ancient Latins called it a Tuscan quarrel. Horace said to resolve strife with strife. Christ instituted this question in such a way that it becomes most manifest from it that he had just causes for not answering their interrogation. For how would they have believed him alleging a divine command, who had not believed John, whom nevertheless they did not dare to openly deny was sent by God?

Grotius refers this Ἀντερώτησιν not reverently enough to a Tuscan quarrel, and to that saying of Horace, to resolve strife with strife. The question was most useful; through which those who were opposed could be led to the recognition of the Messiah. For if the Baptism of John was from heaven, and John himself was a Prophet, who testified concerning Jesus, that he is the Messiah, they ought by all means to have received him as a Teacher, nay, as the Redeemer promised to the world: not to call his doctrine and power of teaching into doubt.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον] ἀντερώτησις, qualis à Grammaticis notatur ad Ecclogam Virgilii tertiam: & in Socraticorum libris non raro apparet. Latini veteres Tuscum jurgium appellabant. Litem lite resolvere di- xit Horatius. Hanc autem quæstionem ita Christus in- stituit, ut manifestissimum inde fiat justas ipsum causas habuisse ad ipsorum interrogationem non respondendi. Quomodo enim credidissent alleganti mandatum divi- num, qui Johanni non crediderant, quem tamen à Deo missum aperte diffiteri non audebant?

Ἀντερώτησιν hanc non satis reverenter Gro- tius ad Tuscum jurgium refert, & ad illud Horatii li- tem lite resolvere. Quæstio erat maxime utilis; per quam ad agnitionem Messiæ produci poterant οἱ ἐξ ἐναντίοις. Si enim de cœlo Baptisma Jo- hannis, & Johannes ipse Propheta fuit, qui te- status est de Jesu, quod sit Messias, suscipere o- mnino eum debuerunt ceu Doctorem, imo Re- demptorem mundo promissum: non doctri- nam ejus, & potestatem docendi in dubium vo- care.

## 21:25
Vers. 25. ἐξ οὐρανοῦ] The Hebrews recite among the names of God שמים: but it is more true that it is used figuratively for the King of heaven. Thus the host of the heavens, Dan. IV.

οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ] Both in other things, and in the testimony which he bore concerning me.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ἐξ οὐρανοῦ] Hebræi inter Dei nomina recitant שמים: sed verius est figurate pro rege regiam nomi- nari. Sic exercitus cælorum Dan. IV.

οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ] Tum in cæteris, tum in testimonio quod de me perhibuit.

## 21:26
Vers. 26. ἔχουσι] With a certain firm persuasion, as Luke expresses it.

ὡς προφήτην] That is, as a man divinely aroused, just as the preceding things prove.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ἔχουσι] Firma quadam persuasione, ut Lucas exprimit.

ὡς προφήτην] Id est, ut hominem divinitus excitatum, quemadmodum superiora evincunt.

## 21:27
Vers. 27. οὐκ οἴδαμεν] Christ expresses a profession of ignorance from those who were accustomed to boast that the ἀναμφίστητον (indisputable) judgment for discerning true and false Prophets rested with them.

Latin:

Vers. 27. οὐκ οἴδαμεν] Ignorantiæ professionem ab illis Christus exprimit, qui jactare solebant penes se esse judi- cium ἀναμφίστητον ad discernendos veros ac falsos Pro- phetas.

## 21:29
Vers. 29. ὕστερον δὲ θέλω] The image of the publicans and harlots, who had lived for a long time as if they denied that rights were born to them, having been ignorant of piety: confessing their disease by their dress and gait, as he says.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ὕστερον δὲ θέλω] Imago publicanorum & mere- tricum, qui diu ita vixerant, quasi jura negarent sibi na- ta, τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἠγνοηκότες: morbum cultu incessuque fatentes, ut ille ait.

## 21:30
Vers. 30. ἐγὼ Κύριε] The correct reading, with the Syrian also acknowledging it, and among the Greeks Theophylact and Euthymius: thus Gen. XXII. 1. & 11. ch. XXVII. 13. ch. XXXVII. 13. & 1 Sam. III. several times הנני, to the LXX Interpreters ἰδὲ ἐγὼ is of the same value as the Latin 'here I am' (præsto adsum). I do not doubt that other readings were born from interpretation. This son is an image of the princes of the Jews, who by speech and countenance professed piety, but in reality were proud, envious, cruel men.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ἐγὼ Κύριε] Recta lectio Syro etiam agnoscen- te, interque Græcos Theophylactus & Euthymius: ita Gen. XXII. 1. & 11. c. XXVII. 13. c. XXXVII. 13. & 1. Sam. III. aliquoties הנני LXX. Interpretibus ἰδὲ ἐγὼ idem va- let quod Latine præsto adsum. Lectiones alias ex inter- pretamento natas non dubito. Filius hic imago est prin- cipum Judæorum, qui oratione ac vultu pietatem profite- bantur, revera homines superbi, invidi, crudeles.

## 21:31
Vers. 31. προάγουσι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν] They are your leaders and show-ers of the way to the kingdom of heaven, namely, of repentance: thus the Greeks often use προάγειν & προάγεσθαι. And that this is the meaning, and that it is not about the final judgment here, is apparent from what follows: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες ὐ μετεμελήθητε. You did not follow those who were leading you rightly, of whom you ought to have been the leaders.

Latin:

Vers. 31. προάγουσι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν] Duces vo- bis monstratoresque sunt itineris ad regnum cælorum, pœnitentiæ scilicet: ita προάγειν & προάγεσθαι sæpe u- surpant Græci. Atque hunc esse sensum, non autem de extremo judicio hic agi, apparet ex eo quod sequitur ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες ὐ μετεμελήθητε. Non secuti estis illos recte du- centes quorum vos duces esse oportuit.

## 21:32
Vers. 32. ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης] The translation begun in the word προάγουσι seems to be continued. For he calls the very dogma of John, if I am not mistaken, the way of righteousness, which from the added sign is called τὸ βάπτισμα τῆς μετανοίας: For that is the path to that true righteousness which CHRIST teaches.

That former observation seems not inelegant, and thus there is no need to explain the comparative through the negative; because there is no comparison thus: even if the passage is understood by most as being about the final judgment, and they make it a comparative locution, but in a negative sense. But that the very dogma of John should be called Baptism, and that it was only a path to the true righteousness which Christ taught, can in no way be admitted. For besides doctrine, or the office of teaching, St. John also dispensed baptism. Therefore, the Sacrament is not to be confused with doctrine. Nor did John only teach those things which could show the way to the true righteousness to be delivered by Christ, but he taught that very righteousness itself: for just as Christ delivered the knowledge of salvation, and taught that we are constituted just before God by his righteousness alone, and attain the kingdom of heaven, so also did St. John Luc. I. 22. Ioh. I. 17. 29. c. III. 34. 35. 36. Nor is there any other way of the righteousness of the kingdom of heaven than that which was shown by Christ himself: which John himself showed: who delivered the counsel of God concerning salvation Luc. VII. 30. and showed him, in whom alone is salvation Iob. I. 29. Actor. IV. 12. and he is said to have come to them in the way of righteousness, not because he came only on the journey and progress toward that righteousness which Christ taught, but because he showed that way in which there is righteousness: and thus inculcated that very righteousness itself, for the phrase 'way of righteousness' in Scripture is doctrine concerning righteousness Matth. XXII. 26. Marc. XII. 14. Luc. XX. 21. Actor. XVI. 17. c. XIIX. 25. 26. cap. XIX. 9. cap. XXII. 4. c. XXIV. 14. 22. To come therefore in the way of righteousness is to come in, or with, the doctrine concerning true righteousness. And thus also Christ himself came in the way of righteousness Es. LXIII. 1. Ps. XL. 10. 11. And therefore this doctrine was to be received by faith: because the righteousness announced and offered in the Gospel cannot be received by us otherwise than through faith: But it is a depravation of the words of Christ when Grotius translates faith in v. 32 as obedience to precepts. οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ you did not have faith in him; explaining it thus: you did not obey his precepts. For that he says πιστέυειν is often to show in reality that one has faith in someone's words, τὸ πείθεσθαι: in that does not consist the nerve of the matter, or the hinge of the question. When John required faith, demonstrating that Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, he was certainly not delivering some moral precept to which obedience was to be rendered, even if he also instructed those believing in Christ about a holy life: but this he intended, this he did, which John the Evangelist testifies concerning him: He came for a testimony, to testify concerning that light, that all might believe THROUGH HIM Joh. I. 7. Since therefore the Pharisees did not believe John, who was showing the way of righteousness, namely, that we have righteousness in Christ alone in his active and passive obedience, they are argued of his unbelief, concerning which Ioh. III. 36. he who does not believe in the Son, or into the Son, will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

ἐκ ἐπιστεύσατ᾿ αὐτῷ] You did not obey his precepts. For πιστεύειν is often to show in reality that one has faith in someone's words, τὸ πείθεσθαι.

PARS IV. Parable spoken against the Pharisees.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης] Continuari videtur trans- latio cœpta in voce προάγουσι. Nam ὁδὸν δικαιοσύνης ap- pellat, ni fallor, ipsum dogma Iohannis, quod ex figno addito vocatur τὸ βάπτισμα τῆς μετανοίας: Id enim ad ve- ram illam justitiam, quam CHRISTUS docet, iter est.

Prior illa observatio non inelegans videtur, atque ita opus non est comparativam exponere per negativam; quia nulla sic comparatio: etsi de extremo judicio à plerisque locus intelli- gatur, ac comparativam loquutionem faciant, sed sensu negativo. Quod autem ipsum dogma Johannis Baptismus dicatur, idque iter tantum fuerit ad veram justitiam quam Christus docuit, admitti nullatenus potest. Nam præter doctri- nam, vel officium docendi dispensabat etiam S. Johannes baptismum. Non ergo confundendum Sacramentum cum doctrina. Neque solum ea docebat Johannes quæ iter monstrare possent ad veram justitiam à Christo tradendam, sed ipsam illam justitiam docebat: nam uti Christus cogni- tionem salutis tradidit, suaque unius justitiæ nos coram Deo justos constitui, & regnum cœlorum adipisci docuit, ita & S. Johannes Luc. I. 22. Ioh. I. 17. 29. c. III. 34. 35. 36. Nec alia via est justitiæ regni cœlorum, quam ea quæ à Christo ipso est monstrata: quam ipse Johannes monstravit: qui tradidit consilium Dei de salute Luc. VII. 30. eum- que monstravit, in quo uno est salus Iob. I. 29. Actor. IV. 12. venisse autem adipsos dicitur in via justitiæ, non quod tantum in itinere, & progres- su ad illam justitiam, quam Christus docuit, ve- nerit, sed quod viam eam ostenderit, in qua est justitia: adeoque ipsam illam justitiam incul- carit, nam via justitiæ phrasi Scripturæ est doctri- na de justitia Matth. XXII. 26. Marc. XII. 14. Luc. XX. 21. Actor. XVI. 17. c. XIIX. 25. 26. cap. XIX. 9. cap. XXII. 4. c. XXIV. 14. 22. venire ergo in via justitiæ est venire in, vel cum doctrina de ve- ra justitia. Atque ita etiam Christus ipse venit in via justitiæ Es. LXIII. 1. Ps. XL. 10. 11. Ideoque hæc doctrina fide erat suscipienda: quia justitia in Ev- angelio annunciata & oblata aliter à nobis accipi nequit, quam per fidem: Depravatio autem est verborum Christi, cum fidem v. 32. Grotius vertit in obsequium præceptorum. οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ non habuistis ipsi fidem; sic exponens: præceptioni- bus ipsius non obtemperastis. Nam quod ait πι- στέυειν sæpe esse reipsa ostendere fidem se alicujus di- ctis habere τὸ πείθεσθαι: in eo non consistit ner- vus rei, aut cardo quæstionis. Cum fidem re- quirebat Johannes, demonstrans agnum illum Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi, certe non ali- quod morale præceptum tradebat, cui obedientia præstanda, etsi credentes in Christum etiam de vita sancta instruxerit: sed hoc intendebat, hoc agebat, quod Johannes Evangelista de ipso testa- tur: Ipse venit ad testimonium, ut testaretur de lumi- ne illo, ut omnes crederent PER IPSUM Joh. I. 7. Quum ergo Johanni ὁδὸν δικαιοσύνης monstran- ti, justitiam nempe, nos in Christo solo habere in obedientia ejus activa & passiva, non credidere Pharisæi, ἀπισίας ejus arguuntur, de qua Ioh. III. 36. qui non credit Filio, vel in Filium, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super ipsum.

ἐκ ἐπιστεύσατ᾿ αὐτῷ] Præceptionibus ipsius non obtem- perastis. Nam πιστεύειν sæpe est reipsa ostendere fidem se alicujus dictis habere, τὸ πείθεσθαι.

PARS IV. Parabola in Pharisæos dicta.

## 21:33
Vers. 33. ἀμπελῶνα] He bent the similitude of the vineyard, customary among the ancient Prophets, into a slightly different sense, so that he might render the retribution more conveniently. For among them the vineyard corresponds to the Hebrew people: but here to the knowledge of the law and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which are soon called the kingdom of heaven.

There is no reason why we should not accept the vineyard as the Church, just as it is frequently accepted among the Prophets. It is unusual in sacred writings for the knowledge of the law and the gifts of the Holy Spirit to be indicated by a vineyard. These pertain rather to the fruits of the vineyard. And since to cast out of the vineyard, by the interpretation of Grotius himself, is to make one excommunicated v. 39, certainly by the vineyard is understood not the knowledge of the law and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, of which they could not deprive the Son: but the Synagogue and the Church. Concerning this vineyard Chrysostom says: The vineyard, he says, is the people of the Jews, planted in the land of promise, the hedge is the Law, prohibiting the Jews from mixing with the Gentiles. The winepress, the altar. The tower, the Temple. The husbandman, the teachers.

But the Householder went abroad: that is, God, dissembling the crimes of the Jews with long-suffering, bore with them; which same patience Scripture expresses elsewhere by another metaphor, saying that God slumbers and sleeps: because He does not immediately exact the punishments for sins. Cyril in Nicet. Cat. And the vineyard is indeed Israel, as the Psalmist says; Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt, and Isaiah says, a vineyard was made for the beloved. But God planted it, and went abroad for a long time, or exercised it with long-suffering: yet He seems to have taken care of the region, and to have had it in mind, for there was no intermediate time in which prophets and righteous instructors were not sent by God. But these were unbelieving, and sent away those who were sent to them empty and treated with ignominy.

Φραγμὸν ἀυτῷ περιέθηκε] It is not necessary to explain the hedge, the tower, and the winepress one by one, since in general they all signify those things which pertain either to protection or to ornament: in short, all the benefits by which we are provoked by God to good fruit, as can be seen in Isaiah.

Ληνὸν] Mark uses ὑπολήνιον, the LXX in Isaiah use προλήνιον: and certainly the word ὀρύσσειν sufficiently shows that a pit is meant, which is called a winepress by synecdoche, whereas otherwise a winepress is the whole machine consisting of the press and the pit. Homer in the description of the vineyard in Iliad 2. ᾿Αμφὶ δὲ κυανέην καπετὸν. Where the Scholiast says a hollow digging, a trench: Eustathius says a winepress.

Ἐξέδοτο ἀυτὸν] With a certain agreement for the fruits, which kind of tenants the Romans call sharecroppers. For it follows, he sent to receive the fruits of it.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ἀμπελῶνα] Vineæ similitudinem veteribus Pro- phetis usitatam in sensum paulo alium inflexit, ut commo- dius redderet ἀνταπόδοσιν. Nam apud illos vinea populo Hebræo respondet: hic autem notitiæ legis & donis Spi- ritus S. quæ mox vocantur regnum cœlorum.

Nihil causæ est, cur non vineam de Ecclesia ac- cipiamus, quemadmodum frequenter apud Pro- phetas accipitur. Notitiam legis, & dona Sp. S. per vineam indigitari in sacris insolens est. Ad fructus potius vineæ hæc pertinent. Et cum ejicere è vinea interprete ipso Grotio, sit facere ἀποσυνάγωγον v. 39. utiq; per vineam non notitia legis, & dona Sp. S. quibus Filium privare non potuêre: sed Synagoga, & Ecclesia intelligitur. De vinea hac Chrysost. Vinea, inquit, populus Iudæorum est, in terra promissionis plantatus, sepes est Lex, probi- bens Iudæos à commixtione Gentium. Torcular, al- tare. Turris, Templum. Agricola, Doctores.

Peregrinatus autem est Paterfamilias: hoc est, Deus diuturna longanimitate Judæorum scelera dissimulans tulit, quam eandem patientiam alia alibi Metaphora Scriptura exprimens, dormitare dormireq́ue dicit Deum: quod non statim exigat peccatorum pœnas. Cyrillus in Nicet. Cat. Ac vinea quidem est Israel, ut ait Psalmista; Vineam ex Ægypto transtulisti, ac Isaïas vinea, inquit, facta est dilecto. Plantavit autem eam Deus, ac longo tempore peregre profectus est, sive longanimitate exercuit: videtur tamen curam gessisse regionis, & eam habuisse in mente, nullum enim tempus intermedium fuit, quo non à Deo missi fuerint Prophetæ, justique instructores. Hi vero increduli fuêrunt, eosque qui missi erant, affectos ignominia vacuos dimiserunt.

Φραγμὸν ἀυτῷ περιέθηκε] Sepem, turrim, torcular nihil necesse est sigillatim explicare, cum in universum ii omnia significentur quæ aut ad tutelam aut ad ornatum pertinent: omnia denique beneficia quibus ad bonam frugem à Deo provocamur, ut apud Esaiam videre est.

Ληνὸν] Marcus ὑπολήνιον, LXX. apud Esaiam προλήνιον: & certe verbum ὀρύσσειν satis ostendit lacum significari qui συνεκδοχικῶς torcular dicitur, cum alioqui torcular sit tota machina constans ex prælo & lacu. Homerus in vineæ descriptione Iliados 2. ᾿Αμφὶ δὲ κυανέην καπετὸν. Ubi Scholiastes κοιλὸν ὄρυγμα, ταφρὸν: Eustathius ληνὸν.

Ἐξέδοτο ἀυτὸν] Certa fructuum pactione, quod genus colonos Romani partiarios vocant. Sequitur enim ἀπέστειλε λαβεῖν τὲς καρπὸς ἀυτᾶ.

## 21:35
Vers. 35. ἔδειραν] δέρω is put for δαίρω. In Mark it is read expressly δέροντες: and in Luke δείραντες, as also in the Acts several times, where δέρων in ch. XX. 19 is beating: and εἰς πρόσωπον δέρειν in 2 Cor. XI. 20. Wherefore this reading is not to be changed. But by this word seem to be indicated especially the insults which Jeremiah endured: just as you may not wrongly refer killing to Isaiah, and stoning to Zechariah the son of Jehoiada. See Acts VII. 51. Heb. XI. 37. 2 Kings XXI. 10, 16. Jer. XLIV. 4, 5, 6. 2 Chron. XXXVI. 16. Neh. IX. 26.

Latin:

Vers. 35. ἔδειραν] Ponitur δέρω pro δαίρω. Apud Marcum expresse legitur δέροντες: & apud Lucam δείραντες, ut & in Actis aliquoties, ubi & δέρων c. XX. 19. est cædens: & εἰς πρόσωπον δέρειν 2. Cor. XI. 20. Quare lectio hæc mutanda non est. Videntur autem hoc verbo præcipue indicari contumeliæ quas Jeremias pertulit: sicut occidere ad Esaiam, lapidare ad Zachariam Jojadæ filium non male referas. Vide Act. VII. 51. Hebr. XI. 37. 2. Reg. XXI. 10. 16. Jer. XLIV. 4. 5. 6. 2. Par. XXXVI. 16. Neh. IX. 26.

## 21:37
V. 37. ἐντραπήσονται ὲ υἱόν μυ] These words show not what would happen, but what would be expected by right and merit. Therefore Luke added ἴσως: which locution is used when it is attributed to God in the Holy Scriptures, but it must be understood in a manner worthy of God, not to exclude foreknowledge, but to note the contingency in its causes as viewed in the event: which the ancients also noted.

Latin:

V. 37. ἐντραπήσονται ὲ υἱόν μυ] Ostendunt hæc verba non quid futurum esset, sed quid jure ac merito expectaretur. Ideo Lucas ἴσως addidit: quæ locutio est ubi in sacris literis & Deo tribuatur, sed intelligenda θεοπρεπῶς, non ut præscientiam excludat, sed ut notet eventus in causis suis spectati τὸ ἐνδεχόμενον: quod & veteres notarunt.

## 21:38
Vers. 38. ἀποκτείνωμεν ἀυτὸν] The very words of the brothers concerning Joseph, Gen. XXXVII. 20.

κατασχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν ἀυτᾶ] By these words it is shown that the priests and princes of the Jewish people strove with the utmost zeal to force the divine law to serve their own ambition and gain: which is the same as if a tenant were to misappropriate the possession from the master. For we have said elsewhere that by the word inheritance the full right of ownership is indicated.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ἀποκτείνωμεν ἀυτὸν] Ipsa verba fratrum de Josepho Gen. XXXV. 11. 40.

κατασχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν ἀυτᾶ] His verbis ostenditur Sacerdotes ac Principes Judaici populi hoc egisse summo studio, ut divinam legem cogerent ambitioni suæ & quæstui inservire: quod idem est ac si colonus domino possessionem intervertat. Nam κληρονομίας voce jus plenum dominii indicari alibi diximus.

## 21:39
Vers. 39. ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τῦ ἀμπελῶν@] That is, they rejected, as is said below. They made him excommunicated, and as a lawless man they saw to it that he was killed by profane men: and thus they themselves killed him more than the Roman governor, who, resisting for some time, finally gave in to their wickedness.

Latin:

Vers. 39. ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τῦ ἀμπελῶν@] Id est, ἀπεδοκίμασαν, ut dicitur infra. Fecerunt ἀποσυνάγωγος, & ut hominem ἄνομον curarunt eum à profanis hominibus occidi: atque adeo ipsi magis eum occiderunt quam Romanus præses, qui aliquandiu reluctans tandem manus dedit illorum improbitati.

## 21:41
Vers. 41. κακὲς κακῶς ἀπολέσει] A locution taken from the purest Greek speech, of which this interpreter shows himself not unskilled several times. From a comparison of other writers it appears that the senators first said this simply, ignorant of where the sense of the saying would lead: but when Christ had more openly signified that these things pertained to them, they averted the omen from themselves.

Grotius speaks of the Canonical Writer as if he were a common one, writing in a human manner, not piously enough. And he always assumes that we have only an interpreter, not a source. Furthermore, that comparison with Luke XX. v. 15 and Ps. CXVIII. 22 and the reconciliation is not disapproved. They first passed judgment themselves, as Matthew has it: afterwards, noticing that they were being touched, they denied that they would be such, and would deserve such a punishment. But Christ explicitly applies it to them. See similar cases, 2 Sam. XII. 5 seqq., 1 Kings XX. 39 seqq. Which are more correct than Heinsius's suspicion about a corrupt text, which is unworthy to be brought here.

ἀποδώσουσι] They will render. But a tree is also said to render fruit, Rev. XXII. 2, just as for the Latins a field renders or pays its produce.

the fruit in its season] in its season Ps. I. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 41. κακὲς κακῶς ἀπολέσει] Locutio petita ex purissimo sermone Græco, cujus se non imperitum aliquoties ostendit hic interpres. Ex collatione aliorum scriptorum apparet primum hoc simpliciter dixisse Senatores, ignaros quo sensus dicti evaderet: cum vero Christus apertius significasset ad ipsos hæc pertinere, avertisse à se omen.

Loquitur de Scriptore Canonico tanquam de vulgari, humano more scribente, Grotius non satis pie. Et semper interpretem nos habere tantum assumit, non fontem. Cæterum collatio illa cum Luc. XX. v. 15. ac Ps. LXII. 9. & conciliatio non improbatur. Primum ipsi tulêre sententiam, ut habet Matthæus: postea animadvertentes se tangi, negarunt tales se futuros, eamque pœnam promerituros. Sed Christus diserte illis id applicat. Similia vid. 2. Sam. XII. 5. seqq. 1. Reg. XX. 39. seqq. Quæ rectius se habent, quam Heinsiana de textu corrupto suspicio, indigna, quæ huc adferatur.

ἀποδώσουσι] Perfolvent. Sed & arbor dicitur καρπὸν ἀπο- διδόναι Apoc. XXII. 2. ut Latinis ager frugem reddere aut perfolvere.

τὺς καρπὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς] בעתו Pf. I. 3.

## 21:42
Vers. 42. have you never read] Jesus shows by the testimony of the Psalm, which they themselves also interpreted according to the more mystical sense concerning the affairs of the Messiah, that what they thought could by no means fit them, pertained most especially to them, and consequently to the common people. Nor did Rabbi Solomon accept that passage otherwise.

We have said in our vindications of the same Psalm that the ancient Jews understood Psalm 118 concerning the Messiah not only in the mystical sense, which Grotius calls it, but in the literal sense. And that it treats of the Messiah according to the letter is manifest both from the Psalm itself and from this interpretation of Christ. Let those things which we have said there be seen.

the builders] That is, the architects, using the participle for a noun in the Hebrew manner. Thus are called the Senators of the great Sanhedrin to whom was entrusted the guardianship of religion no less than of the republic. Peter teaches this, who, addressing the same men, says: by you, the builders, Acts 4:11. Thus also Plato and Aristotle call political science architectonic, and Cicero called architects of the building of the republic.

into the head of the corner] All these things are from the Septuagint version. The meaning of corner can indeed not inappropriately be referred to the joining of the election of the Jews and the people of the Gentiles, but since mention is made here simply of the rejection of the Jews and the substitution of the Gentiles, and Peter says this prophecy was fulfilled before the calling of the Gentiles had begun, Acts 4:11, it will be better for the word corner to indicate that power which is accustomed to be in corners, of supporting the building: whence it has come about that the leaders of the people are everywhere called by the Hebrews 'pinoth', and by the Hellenists 'goniai', as in 1 Sam. 14:36. Peter and Paul in their epistles, if I am not mistaken, called it the cornerstone in the same sense.

These things are not opposed, but subordinated: that the power of supporting the building is designated, and that the notion of the joining of the election of the Jews and of the Gentiles is considered at the same time: nor is that rejection of the Jews indicated here in such a way that the election is also excluded, or that the substitution of the Gentiles is opposed to the accession of them to the remnants of the people of God; but since it ought to have been established from the Prophets concerning the calling and gathering of the Gentiles, the malice of the Jews is indicated here, because of which, with that people almost entirely rejected, there is need for the substitution of another people, with the elect remnants nevertheless saved, which teaches that that substitution would be a gathering into the place of those who were failing for the surviving elect. Finally, when Peter says this prophecy was fulfilled before the calling of the Gentiles, he refers by that most especially to its former part, this is the stone rejected BY YOU architects: as for the latter part, although it was made the head of the corner especially with regard to the joining of the Gentiles and the election of the Jewish people after Peter had entered unto the Gentiles: yet that joining existed also in a certain way before Christ had yet come into the flesh, in the time of the Old Testament, if indeed even then the Gentiles were already built upon this foundation, outside of which there can be no other, 1 Cor. 3:11, and which sustains the universal Church of all times, Matt. 16:15, Tit. 2:20, Heb. 13:8, nor can it be doubted that in the Pauline passage especially, Eph. 2:20, that conjunction of Gentiles and Jews is considered. Ammonius in this place in the Catena on Matthew. Of Nicetas: But the sacred Scriptures liken the connection of two peoples, I mean Israel and the Gentiles, to a corner; for the Savior established the two peoples into one new man: and this thing was likened to a corner joining two walls, for as a corner is the union of two walls, connecting them to each other with an indissoluble bond, so also here the corner, namely the holy

The Church is the union of two peoples, bound together by the reason of one faith, joining them into one conspiracy, whose cornerstone is Christ, as the head of the whole body. And Cyril: The blessed David admired that corner, or the meeting of two peoples into identity, saying: this was done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes. Therefore, this stone is indeed salutary because of the corner made by him; but it was crushed by those who remained outside the intellectual and spiritual gathering. For to them Christ is a stone of stumbling, and a rock of scandal. Whom Irenaeus preceded, lib. IV. c. 42. Christ is the highest cornerstone sustaining all things, and gathering into one faith of Abraham those who are fit from both Testaments for the edification of God.

αὕτη] That the Hebrews express the neuter in the feminine also occurs among the Hellenists, as in Psalm CVII. 4. Nor, however, does anything prevent it from being able to be referred to γωνίαν both in Hebrew and in Greek and in Syriac, just as Theophylact interprets it here. The Hebrew construction opposes it being adapted to the word head. The matter, however, comes to the same thing.

ἡμῶν] Of the pious, of course, as what follows in the Psalm demands that this be understood.

Latin:

Vers. 42. οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε] Quod minime in se quadra- re posse arbitrabantur, id ad ipsos potissimum, ad plebem autem consequenter pertinere Jesus ostendit Psalmi testi- monio, quem ipsi quoque κατὰ τὸ μυστικώτερον de rebus Messiæ interpretabantur. Neque aliter eum locum acce- pit Rabbi Salomon.

Non tantum sensu mystico, quem vocat Gro- tius, sed literali Psalmum CXIIX. de Messia intel- lexisse Judæos veteres, in vindiciis ejusdem di- ximus. Et quod secundum literam de Messia agat, tum è Psalmo ipso, tum ex hac interpre- tatione Christi manifestum est. Videantur quæ illic diximus.

οἱ οἰκοδομῦντες] Id est οἱ ἀρχιτέκτονες, more Hebræo parti- cipium pro nomine. Ita vocantur Senatores magni Syne- drii quibus mandata erat non minus religionis, quam rei- publicæ tutela. Docet hoc Petrus, qui eosdem alloquens. ὑφ’ ὑμῶν, inquit, τῶν οἰκοδομόντων Act. IV. 11. Sic & Plato & Aristoteles τὴν πολιτικὴν ἐπιστήμην vocant ἀρχιτεκτονικὴν, & Cicero architectos reipublicæ ædificandæ dixit.

εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας] Omnia hæc ex versione LXX. γωνίας significatio potest quidem non incommode ad commissu- ram referri τῆς ἐκλογῆς τῶν Ἰυδαίων & gentium populi, sed cum hic simpliciter rejectionis Judæorum & surrogationis gentium fiat mentio, & Petrus ante inchoatam gentium vocationem hoc vaticinium dicat impletum Act. IV. 11. satius erit anguli voce indicari eam vim, quæ esse in angu- lis solet, sustinendi ædificii: unde factum est, ut & primo- res populi passim Hebræis פנות appellentur, Hellenistis autem γωνίαι, ut I. Sam. XIV. 36. ἀκρογωνιαῖον λίθον eodem, ni fallor, sensu dixerunt Petrus & Paulus in Epistolis.

Non opposita hæc sunt, sed subordinata: vim sustinendi ædificii designari, & notionem commis- suræ τ᾽ ἐκλογῆς τῶν Ἰυδαίων, & gentilium simul respi- ci: neque ita rejectio illa Judæorum hic indica- tur, ut ἐκλογὴ etiam excludatur, aut surrogatio gentium accessioni earum ad populi Dei reli- quias opponatur; sed quum de vocatione & aggre- gatione gentium è Prophetis constare debuerit, malitia Judæorum tanta hic indicatur, ob quam populo isto propemodum toto rejecto alterius populi surrogatione opus sit, salvis tamen reliqui- is electis, quæ istam surrogationem in locum de- ficientium aggregationem fore ad electos super- stites docens. Denique cum ante vocationem gentium Petrus impletum dicit hoc vaticinium, re- spicit illo priorem potissimum ejus partem, hic lapis ille est à VOBIS architectis reprobatus: quoad posteriorem vero etsi in caput anguli factus præcipue sit, quantum ad commissuram gentium & electionis populi Judæorum postquam Petrus ad gentes ingressus est: fuit tamen etiam illa commissura certa ratione antequam adhuc in carnem venit Christus, tempore Veteris Testa- menti, siquidem etiam tum gentiles super hoc fundamentum exstructi jam sunt, extra quod a- liud esse non potest 1. Cor. III. 11. quodq; sustentat universam Ecclesiam omnium temporum Matth. XVI. v. 15. Tit. II. v. 20. Ebr. XIII. v. 8. neque dubitari potest in loco imprimis Paulino Eph. II. 20. eam conjunctionem gentium & Judæorum re- spici. Ammonius in h. l. in Caten. in Matth. Nicetæ: Angulo autem assimilant sacræ Scripturæ connexio- nem duorum populorum, Israelis inquam ac Gen- tium; constituit enim Salvator duos populos in unum novum hominem: assimilata autem est hæc res an- gulo duos parietes conjungenti, ut enim angulus duo- rum murorum unio est, ad invicem eos connectens indissolubili nexu, ita etiam hic angulus sancta scil.

Ecclesia, duorum populorum facta unio est unius fi- dei ratione invicem colligata, in unam conspiratio- nem eos compingens, cujus angularis lapis Christus est, tanquam caput totius corporis. Et Cyrillus: Admiratus est angulum illum, sive duorum popu- lorum in identitatem conventum beatus David, di- cens: à Domino factum est istud, & est mirabile in oculis nostris. Itaque salutaris quidem hic la- pis angulo ab eo facto; contritus est autem ab iis qui extra intellectualem ac spiritualem manserunt con- cursum. Ipsis enim Christus petra offensionis est, & lapis scandali. Quibus præivit Irenæus lib. IV. c. 42. Christus lapis summus angularis omnia susti- nens, & in unam fidem Abrahæ colligens eos, qui ex utroque Testamento apti sunt in ædificationem Dei.

αὕτη] Quod Hebræi neutrum muliebriter enuntiant et- iam apud Hellenistas occurrit, ut Psal. CVII. 4. Nec tamen quicquam obstat quominus & in Hebræo & in Græco & in Syriaco possit ad γωνίαν referri, quomodo & Theophylactus hic interpretatur. Capitis voci quominus aptetur repu- gnat Hebræa constructio. Res tamen eodem recidit.

ἡμῶν] Piorum scilicet, ut quæ in Psalmo sequuntur in- telligi hoc postulant.

## 21:43
Vers. 43. διὰ τῦτο] For this reason, because you have rejected this stone and are going to reject it further, these things will happen to you.

ἡ βασιλεία τῦ Θεῦ] I agree with Origen and Jerome interpreting the kingdom of God as the knowledge of divine law, as I also said before. See also what was noted above on chapter III. Among the punishments of the Jewish nation, none is more noble than that, after Christ was repudiated, they were not only deprived of the gift of Prophecy entirely, so that that very light, once the peculiar star of the Hebrew nation, passed from it to the Christians, but that all that knowledge of the law which could be acquired by human resources was turned into the most rotten fables with which the Talmudic book abounds, certainly such that he who puts faith in them should be judged to be destitute not only of the divine spirit, but also in a great part of common sense.

It will never be proven from the Scriptures that the knowledge of divine law comes under the name of the kingdom of God. There is indeed in the kingdom of God a knowledge of divine law as well, but neither does this obtain the first place in the kingdom of God; is not the knowledge of salvation (Luke I. 77) also far more excellent, that knowledge in which eternal life consists (John XVII. 3), and yet it itself is not the kingdom of God. The knowledge of divine law was not to be taken away first from the Jews, but it had already been lost by their own fault. Nor was any law to be handed over to the nations other than the saving knowledge of the Gospel. Therefore, by the kingdom of God is understood the right to the kingdom of God, or the dignity of the Church, which was first in the possession of the Jews: but it was transferred to the nations because of their unbelief and extreme ingratitude.

ποιῦντι ὴὺς καρπὺς αὐτῆς.] Not only fruits of repentance, as the Baptist commanded (Luke III. 8), but what is more, the fruit of the kingdom or of the Spirit, of which Paul treats (Rom. VI. 22, Eph. V. 9, and Gal. V. 22). Moreover, ποιῦντι is put for ποιήσοντι. For it is not the impelling cause, but the one moving by way of an end that is indicated here, as also in Eph. II. 10.

Vain is that distinction of the fruit of repentance and the fruit of the kingdom and the Spirit: for all fruits of repentance are fruits of the Spirit, and of the kingdom of God: of the former as the principal cause: of the latter as the proper seat, because they are produced only in the Church, and as the Subject, because they are produced only by those who are children of the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 43. διὰ τῦτο] Propterea quia hunc lapidem rejeci- stis ampliusque rejecturi estis, ista vobis evenient.

ἡ βασιλεία τῦ Θεῦ] Origeni & Hieronymo assentior regnum Dei notitiam divinæ legis interpretantibus, ut & ante dixi. Vide & quæ supra notata sunt ad cap. III. Inter pœnas Iudaicæ gentis nulla est nobilior, quam quod post Christum repudiatum non modo Prophetiæ dono omni- no sunt privati, ita ut illud ipsum lumen olim & sidus pe- culiare gentis Hebraicæ ex eo ad Christianos transierit, sed quod & omnis illa scientia legis quæ humanis præsidiis comparari poterat, versa est in putidissimas fabulas quibus scatet Thalmudicus liber, tales certe, ut qui eis fidem adhi- beat judicandus sit non modo divino spiritu, sed magna etiam parte sensus communis esse destitutus.

Nunquam id è Scripturis probabitur, notitiam divinæ legis regni Dei nomine venire. Est qui- dem in regno Dei notitia etiam legis divinæ, sed neque hæc τὸ πρωτῦον obtinet in regno Dei; an- non etiam notitia ♰ σωτηρίας Luc. I. 77. longe præ- stantior est, notitia illa in qua æterna vita consistit Joh. XVII. 3. neque ipsum est regnum Dei. No- titiæ legis divinæ non auferenda primum erat à Judæis, sed propria ipsorum culpa jam perdita erat. Nec tamen tradenda gentibus legis, quam salvifica Evangelii notitia. Per regnum ergo Dei jus ad regnum Dei, vel dignitas Ecclesiæ intelligitur, quæ erat primum penes Judæos: sed translata est propter ipsorum ἀπισίαν & ingratitudinem ex- tremam ad gentes.

ποιῦντι ὴὺς καρπὺς αὐτῆς.] Non tantum καρπὺς μετανοίας, ut Baptista jubebat Luc. III. 8. sed quod plus est καρπὸς τῆς βασιλείας sive τῦ πνεύματος, de quibus agit Paulus Rom. VI. 22. Ephes. V. 9. & Gal. V. 22. ποιῦντι autem positum pro ποιήσοντι. Non enim causa impellens, sed movens per modum finis hic indisatur, ut & Eph. II. 10.

Vana est illa fructus pœnitentiæ & fructus regni, & Spiritus distinctio: omnes enim fructus pœni- tentiæ Spiritus fructus sunt, & regni Dei: illius ut causæ principalis: hujus ut sedis propriæ, quia non nisi in Ecclesia fiunt,& Subjecti, quia non nisi ab istis qui filii sunt Ecclesiæ.

## 21:44
Vers. 44. ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τουτον συνθλασθήσεται] Christ brings forward the mention of the stone made from the similitude of a building to another, and Peter imitating him (2 Ep. II. 7). The sense of this clause is: He who will strike against him while he is still acting on earth will feel his own weakness to his own detriment: like an earthen vessel dashed against a rock. The Greeks translate the Hebrew רצץ sometimes as to strike or to beat, as in Deut. XXXII. 39, Job V. 18, sometimes as to break or to crush, as in 2 Sam. XXII. 39, Psalm C. 5, 6.

Here, according to Lightfoot, there is a clear allusion to the manner of stoning, concerning which Sanhedr. cap. 6. hal. 4 speaks thus: The place of stoning was twice the height of a man: from the slope one of the witnesses cast him down to the ground, striking him upon the loins; if he died from that, it is well: if not, the second witness casts a stone upon his heart, &c. Gemara Bab. R. Simeon Ben. Eleazar says, There was a stone there, as much as two could carry, this they cast upon his heart. They did not only cast upon this stone in the days of his flesh, but also afterwards, nay, whoever are unbelievers strike against the same, 1. Petr. II. But the rest concerning the judgment of the Jews is rightly accepted, not however as applying to them alone, or excluding other enemies of Christ, even though they are primarily struck by this discourse. Concerning which Nazianzen in Caten. Nicet. He introduced two destructions here, one indeed from the fact that they would strike and be scandalized, for this is: he who will fall upon this stone will be broken: the other truly from their captivity, and calamity, and total destruction, which he clearly revealed saying: they will crush him: by these he also hints at his own resurrection.

Latin:

Vers. 44. ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τουτον συνθλασθήσεται] Lapi- dis factam mentionem ab ædificii similitudine ad alteram Christus producit, & eum imitans Petrus 2. Ep. II.7. Sensus hujus particulæ est. Qui in ipsum adhuc in terris agentem impinget, sentiet imbecillitatem suam damno suo: ut testa saxo illisa. Hebræum רצץ Græci modo vertunt πατάσσειν aut παίειν, ut Deutcr. XXXII. 39. Iob. V. 18. modo θλᾶν aut συνθλᾶν, ut 2. Sam. XXII 39. Psal. C. 5. 6.

Alluditur hic, Lightfootho autore, plane ad mo- dum lapidationis, de quo sic Sanhedr. cap.6.hal.4. Locus lapidationis altitudine excepit duplicem ho- minis staturam: inde è clivo eum in terram præcipi- tavit unus è testibus, in lumbos impactum, si inde moriatur, bene: sin minus, testis alter lapidem ei im- pingit in cor, &c. Gemara Bab. R. Simeon Ben. Elea- zar dicit, Lapis illic erat, quantum duo portarent, hunc impegerunt in cor ejus. Non tantum impegerunt in hunc lapidem in diebus carnis, sed etiam postea, imo quicunq; in- creduli sunt in eundem impingunt 1. Petr. II. Recte autem reliqua de judicio Judæorum, non autem so- lo accipiuntur, vel exclusis aliis hostibus Christi, etsi illi primo hac oratione feriuntur. De quo Nazianzenus in Caten. Nicet. Duas perditiones hic induxit, unam quidem ex eo quod impingerent, ac scandalizarentur, hoc enim est: qui ceciderit su- per lapidem istum, confringetur: aliam vero à ca- ptivitate eorum, ac calamitate, ac totali perditione, quam clare aperuit dicens: conterent eum: hisce etiam resurrectionem suam innuit.

## 21:45
Vers. 45. οἱ Φαρισαῖοι] Of which sect many of the Senators were.

Latin:

Vers. 45. οἱ Φαρισαῖοι] Cujus instituti aliquam multi e- rant Senatorum.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The parable concerning the King preparing a wedding for his son, spoken likewise to the Priests and Elders of the people, to which many invited refuse to come, and some affect the servants with injuries and kill them, for which robbers the city is ordered to be burned and they themselves to be killed: others gathered from the villages appear, and among them one destitute of a wedding garment is bound and cast into outer darkness. The Pharisees asking about the tribute to be given to Caesar are dispatched, and the Sadducees are convinced concerning the woman of seven husbands from Moses regarding the resurrection of the dead: likewise also a Scribe asking about the greatest commandment, to whom a full answer having been returned, a question about Christ being David's son and Lord (from Ps. CX. 1.) is proposed in turn, but he could answer nothing.

There are five parts: I. The parable concerning the royal wedding, to v. 14. II. The case concerning the tribute of Caesar, to v. 22. III. The case concerning the woman of seven husbands in the resurrection, to v. 33. IV. The question concerning the greatest commandment, to v. 40. V. The counter-question concerning the Messiah as David's son and Lord, to v. 46.

PART I. The parable concerning the Royal wedding.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Parabola de Rege filio nuptias parante, ad Sa- cerdotes & Seniores populi itidem dicta, ad quas plerique invitati venire recusant, nonnulli servos injuriis afficiunt, & inter- ficiunt, quorum latronum civitas incendi, ipsi vero occidi jubentur: alii è vicis colle- cti comparent, & inter hos veste nuptiali destitutus ligatur, & in exteriores tene- bras projicitur. Pharisæi de censu quæ- rentes Cæsari dando expediuntur, & Sad- ducæi de muliere septem virorum è Mose de resurrectione mortuorum convincun- tur: nec non Scriba de maximo præcepto quærens, cui reddito responso abundanti quæstio de Christo Davidis filio & Domi- no (è Ps. CX. 1.) vicissim proponitur, sed ni- hil respondere potuit.

Partes sunt quinque: I. Parabola de nuptiis regiis, ad v. 14. II. Casus de censu Cæsaris, ad v. 22. III. Casus de muliere septem virorum in re- surrectione, ad v. 33. IV. Quæstio de maximo præcepto, ad v. 40. V. ᾿Αντερώτησις de Messia Davidis filio & Domino, ad v. 46.

PARS I. Parabola de nuptiis Regiis.

## 22:2
Vers. 2. Γάμους] γάμοι here are not the marriage itself, but the banquet, as the Syrian translates, which is soon called a lunch: elsewhere a supper: and as Plautus said a wedding supper, just as the word for weddings is used by Terence and others. But just as the kingdom of heaven, as we have often seen already, sometimes signifies the state of the kingdom of the Messiah in this age, sometimes the state of the future age, because the former is a certain foretaste of the latter, so also by the wedding banquet elsewhere that happiness which will follow the general resurrection is signified, but here the gifts destined for the assembly of the pious are signified. However, there is no doubt that Christ recited the same comparisons at different times. Thus, he repeats this one, also used elsewhere, in such a way that, having regard for the men he was addressing, he adds certain peculiarities touching them especially by way of accumulation.

Grotius wishes it to be noted that not the marriage itself, but the banquet is signified, as the Syrian translates, through which he thinks the gifts destined for the assembly of the pious are signified. Others understand the wedding, and most indeed understand the spiritual wedding of the Church with Christ, yet some, with the blessed Chemnitz and Gerhard, wish the personal wedding of the Word and the assumed flesh to be designated. But those are better known in the Scriptures, 2 Cor. XI. 2, Eph. V. 32, Apoc. XXI. 2, 9, nor is there need that one thing be understood by τὸ ἄριστον, the lunch, in v. 4, and another by γάμους in v. 1, since it is easily granted that a wedding banquet is denoted in both.

tius. And because that was prepared for the Son, the Son himself is the Bridegroom, whose Bride is the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 2. Γάμους] γάμοι hic sunt non ipsum matrimo- nium, sed convivium, ut vertit Syrus, quod mox dicitur prandium: alibi cœna: & ut cœnam nuptialem Plautus di- xit, quomodo & nuptiarum vox Terentio atque aliis usur- patur. Sicut autem regnum cœleste, ut sæpe jam vidimus, modo statum regni Messiæ in hoc sæculo significat, modo statum futuri sæculi, quia ille hujus quoddam est πρόγευ- σμα, ita & nuptiali convivio alibi felicitas illa quæ resurre- ctionem generalem sequetur, hic vero dona piorum cœtui destinata significantur. Dubitandum autem non est quin Christus easdem comparationes diversis temporibus reci- taverit. Ita hanc alibi quoque usurpatam nunc ita repetit, ut hominum quos compellabat rationem habens, peculia- ria quædam ipsos præcipue tangentia cumuli vice adjungat.

Non ipsum matrimonium, sed convivium no- tari vult Grotius, uti vertit Syrus, per quod dona piorum cætui destinata significari putat. Alii nu- ptias, & plerique quidem spirituales Ecclesiæ cum Christo intelligunt, nonnulli tamen cum B. Che- mnitio, & Gerhardo personales τοῦ Λόγου & carnis as- sumtæ nuptias designari volunt. Sed illæ in Scri- pturis magis notæ sunt, 2. Cor. XI. 2. Eph. V, 32. Apoc. XXI. 2.9. neque opus est ut aliud per τὸ ἄρι- στον prandium intelligatur v. 4. aliud per γάμους v. 1. utrobiq; convivium nuptiale notari facile da-

tius. Et quia Filio paratum illud, Sponsus Filius ipfe est, cujus Sponsa est Ecclesia.

## 22:3
Vers. 3. καλέσαι ἰὺς κεκλημένυς.] For it was the custom to call twice, as we shall note in Luke. But these κεκλημένοι are the Jews, the people in covenant with God, to whom the coming of the kingdom of the Messiah was announced long before by the Prophets, and finally by John, Christ himself, and his Apostles, so that they might prepare themselves for that kingdom through repentance.

Not that it was the custom to call twice, as Grotius thinks, but that by the repetition of the calling, which happened more than once and is not to be restricted to a binary number, the divine Φιλανθρωπία & μακροθυμία is signified. And is there not mention here of a threefold calling already made: for first the κεκλημένοι are named, whom he then ordered to be called by sending out servants v. 3. πάλιν ἀπόςειλεν ἄλλυς δέλυς v. 4. Therefore not only the Prophets & Apostles, and two callings of the Jews are noted, but it is implied that they were invited frequently. How often have I wanted to gather you? Matt. XXIII. v. 37.

Latin:

Vers. 3. καλέσαι ἰὺς κεκλημένυς.] Nam bis vocare moris erat, ut ad Lucam notabimus. Hi autem κεκλημένοι sunt Judæi, foederatus Deo populus, quibus adventus regni Messiz multo ante per Prophetas, postremo per Johan- nem. Christumque ipsum & ejus Apostolos est annuntia- tus, ut se per pœnitentiam ei regno præparent.

Non quod bis vocare moris erat, ut Grotius cen- set, sed quo iteratione vocationis, quæ plus vice simplici facta, nec ad binarium tantum adstrin- genda, Φιλανθρωπία & μακροθυμία divina desi- gnetur. Et annon trinæ hic vocationis mentio jam facta: primum enim nominantur κεκλημένοι, quos καλέσαι deinde jussit servis emissis v. 3. πάλιν ἀ- πόςειλεν ἄλλυς δέλυς v. 4. Non ergo tantum Prophetæ & Apostoli, duæque vocationes Judæo- rum notantur, sed crebro eosdem invitatos esse innuitur. Quoties volui vos congregare? Matth. XXIII. v. 37.

## 22:4
Vers. 4. πάλιν ἀπέςειλεν ἄλλως] A more open invitation made through the Apostles, both the former ones and others added to them, and their helpers, after Christ had been resurrected, taken up into heaven, and the Spirit sent from above, when nothing further of divine liberality could, I will not say be required, but not even be wished for.

Τὰ σιτιςὰ] In which category were calves, μέχρι σιτεντοὶ not only in Athenaeus, but also in Luke XV. 23 and in the Greek of Jeremiah XLVI. 21, and poultry of the coop. To these the word altilium, to those saginatorum, corresponds more correctly according to Latin usage.
