XL. 13. ubi LXX. ετι τρεις ημεραι, cum tamen quod ibi dicitur impletum sit ipso die tertio ut appa- ret ibidem commate 20. ita Christus ipse apud Marcum VIII. 31. dicit oportere se μετα τρεις ημερας αναστη- ναι. Ita מקץ שבע שנים Deut. XV. 1. LXX. ver- tunt δι επτα ετων (quomodo & Josephus loquitur, & supra XXVI. 61. & Marci XIV. 58. scriptum est δια τριων ημερων) At eadem verba Hebræa ubi de eadem re agitur Jer. XXXIV. 14. Græce non tam κατ' λεξιν, quam κατ' διανοιαν vertuntur οταν πληρωθη εξ ετη, quomodo & Rabbinorum eruditissimi exponunt Ab- raham & Kimchi. At Deuteronomii XXXI. 10. He- bræismo retento verterunt μετα επτα ετη. Simile est Joh. XX. 26. μεθ' ημερας οκτω ubi Syrus, ut & hoc loco illud μετα reddidit verbum verbo בתר cum apud Marcum explicet per ל quod respondet voci εν. Hæc ibidem. Quæ confirmantur iis quæ Beza & Ludov. de Dieu hic habent, quæ etiam apud Baldui- num Wæleum legi possunt in hunc locum, longeque saniora sunt hac observatione Grotiana. Nam bonitas DEI sic prædicanda, ut non derogetur ve- ritati divinæ. Quomodo autem ille de 400. an- norum servitute calculus sese habeat, alias expo- suimus.

## 8:32
Vers. 32. παρρησια) כגלא, the Syrian [is] correct. Without wrappings. παροιμιαν ουδεμιαν λεγων, as John explains this word, that is, λογω α'σχηματιστω, in simple and naked speech: not through figures, as before in John II. 19, c. III. 14, c. VI. 51. προθυμιαν is in the same sense in Dio.

PART V. Exhortation to the cross, and the confession of Jesus.

Latin:

Vers. 32. παρρησια) כגלא Syrus recte. Sine involucris. παροιμιαν ουδεμιαν λεγων ut Johannes hanc vocem explicat, id est λογω α'σχηματιστω, simplici ac nuda oratione: non per fi- guras, ut ante Joh. II. 19. c. III. 14. c. VI. 51. προθυμιαν eo- dem sensu est apud Dionem.

PARS V. Adhortatio ad crucem, & confessionem Iesu.

## 8:35
Ver. 35. φύσει] εὑρήσει Matth. X. 39. where see what has been noted.

Latin:

Vers. 35. φύσει] εὑρήσει Matth. X. 39. ubi quæ notata vide.

## 8:38
Ver. 38. ἐπαισχυνθῇ] The Latins indeed say 'erubescere aliquem' [to blush at someone], but in a far different sense, for that which is to revere. And in that way the Greeks use αἰσχύνεσθαι with the fourth case [accusative]. Here, however, it is ἐπαισχύνεσθαι, to be unwilling to acknowledge someone because we are ashamed of his abject lot: just as Paul also uses it in Rom. I. 16. There is, moreover, a notable ἀντίθετον [antithesis] in this speech of Christ. For on the opposite side correspond any man and Christ, not to acknowledge and not to be acknowledged, the humble state of Christ and the glorious state, this perverse world and the holy Angels.

Μοιχαλίδι] Matth. XII. 39. Thus the world is deservedly called, that is, the greater part of the human race, on account of the defection from the one true God, and his worship, Job. XVII. 25.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ἐπαισχυνθῇ] Dicunt quidem Latini erubescere aliquem, sed sensu longe alio, pro eo quod est revereri. At- que eo modo αἰσχύνεσθαι cum casu quarto Græci usurpant. Hic autem est ἐπαισχύνεσθαι agnoscere aliquem nolle, quod abjectæ ejus sortis nos pudeat: quomodo & Paulus usur- pat Rom I. 16. Est autem in hac Christi oratione insigne ἀν- τίθετον. Nam ex adverso respondent homo quilibet & Chri- stus, non agnoscere & non agnosci, status Christi humilis & status gloriosus, mundus hic perversus & sancti Angeli.

Μοιχαλίδι] Matth. XII. 39. Ita merito vocatur mundus, id est, major pars humani generis, ob defectionem ab uno vero Deo, & ejus cultu, Job. XVII. 25

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

JESUS, having taken Peter, James, and John, is transfigured before them, and a voice is heard from heaven, which vision they are forbidden to divulge until the Son of man rises from the dead: concerning which voice of resurrection, and inquiring about the coming of Elijah, they are taught that Elijah has already come. The father of the lunatic, seeking why the disciples could not free his son, is warned that he should only believe, that all things are possible to faith, and he asks that his unbelief be helped, and his son is freed from the deaf and dumb spirit, the reason being given why he could not be cast out by the disciples. The disciples are informed about the passion, death, and resurrection of the Son of man: but they perceive nothing of these things. They contend about primacy, and a little child having been set in their midst, they are warned toward humility. But when they wished to forbid one in another's name casting out demons in the name of Jesus, they are commanded to permit it. They are admonished concerning the rewarding of benefits, and concerning scandal, and also concerning having salt with them.

There are six parts: I. The transfiguration of Christ, to v. 13. II. The liberation of the lunatic from the dumb and deaf spirit, to v. 29. III. The prediction of the passion and resurrection of Christ, to v. 32. IV. The correction concerning primacy, to v. 38. V. The admonition concerning not forbidding another casting out demons, to v. 41. VI. The information concerning avoiding scandal, and having salt, to v. 50.

PART I. The transfiguration of Christ.

Ver. 1. καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς] I wonder that this comma [clause] in certain codices begins a new section, since it adheres more correctly to the preceding ones: in which way the Greeks seem to have instituted the division.

ἐν δυνάμει] By the power of the Holy Spirit.

Latin:

CAPUT IX. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

IESUS, assumto Petro, Iacobo, & Iohanne, transfiguratur coram ipsis, & vox de cælo auditur, quam visionem divulgare prohi- bentur, donec Filius hominis à mortuis re- surgat: de qua resurrectionis voce, & de adventu Eliæ quærentes, Eliam jam ve- nisse docentur. Lunatici pater querens, quod filium suum liberare nequeant disci- puli, monetur, ut tantum credat, fidei omnia possibilia esse, petitque incredulitati suæ succurri, & filius ejus liberatur à surdo & muto spiritu, causa reddita, cur ille ejici a discipulis nequiverit. Discipuli informan- tur de passione, morte, & resurrectione Filii hominis: sed nihil eorum percipiunt. Contendunt de primatu, & puerulo in me- dio eorum constituto ad humilitatem mo- nentur. Cum vero alieno in nomine Iesu dæmonia ejicienti id prohibere vellent, ju- bentur id permittere. De remuneratione beneficiorum, & de scandalo, nec non de se- cum habendo sale commonefiunt.

Partes sunt sex: I. Christi transfiguratio, ad v. 13. II, Lunatici à spiritu muto & surdo liberatio, ad v. 29. III. Passionis & resurrectionis Christi præ- dictio, ad v. 32. IV. De primatu correptio, ad v. 38. V. De alieno dæmonia ejiciente non prohi- bendo monitio, ad v. 41. VI. De scandalo caven- do, & sale habendo informatio ad v. 50.

PARS I. Christi transfiguratio.

Vers. 1. καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς] Miror hoc comma in quibusdam codicibus inchoare novam sectionem, cum rectius adhæ- reat præcedentibus: quomodo divisionem instituisse vi- dentur Græci.

ἐν δυνάμει] Per vim Spiritus sancti.

## 9:3
Ver. 3. στίλβοντα] ἐξαστράπτοντα Luke: flashing, 'the astrologers call the stars that are in motion στίλβοντας [glittering],' says the interpreter of Apollonius.

οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται λευκᾶναι] Such as no fuller on earth can make white. A not dissimilar way of speaking is found in Horace.

souls than which the earth has borne none whiter.

Latin:

Vers. 3. στίλβοντα] ἐξαστράπτοντα Lucas: fulgurantia, οἱ ἀστρόλογοι τοὺς ἐν κινήσει ὄντας ἀστέρας στίλβοντας καλοῦσιν, inquit Apollonii interpres.

οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται λευκᾶναι] Quam candi- da nullus in terris fullo fecerit. Non dissimile loquendi genus apud Horatium.

animæ quales neque candidiores Terra tulit.

## 9:6
Vers. 6. ἔμφοβοι] The same word [is found in] Heb. XII. 21.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ἔμφοβοι] Eadem vox Hebr. XII. 21.

## 9:10
Vers. 10. Τί ἐστι τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι] They hoped for a general resurrection, as Martha did in John XI. 24, both from the tradition of the elders and from the most manifest teaching of Christ: yet not sufficiently understanding what kind of thing it would be! And that in this age someone truly dead could truly return to life could not enter their minds. Wherefore it follows that either they did not think the souls of those who had been raised by the Prophets and by Christ up to that point had been entirely ἐν ᾅδου, that is, separated from the body, or that this too, like many other things before the abundance of the Holy Spirit, had slipped into oblivion for them through thoughtlessness. See also below 33.

Not only could the dogma of the resurrection of the dead be held from the tradition of the elders beyond the teaching of Christ, but also from the Scriptures of the Old Testament, in which the Jews themselves do not deny that it is proposed, and Christ confirmed it against the Sadducees in Matt. XXII.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Τί ἐστι τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι] Generalem resur- rectionem, ut Martha Joh. XI. 24. tum ex traditione ma- jorum tum ex apertissima Christi doctrina sperabant: qua lis tamen ea futura esset non satis intelligentes! Ac in hoc ævo aliquem vere mortuum in vitam revera posse in men- tem ipsis venire non poterat. Quare sequitur aut qui a Pro- phetis, & Christo resuscitati erant hactenus eorum animas non putaverint plane fuisse ἐν ᾅδου, hoc est a corpore separa- tas, aut id quoque, ut alia multa ante ubertatem Spiritus sancti per incogitantiam ipsis in oblivionem verterit. Vi- de & infra 33.

Non solum ex traditione majorum præter do- ctrinam Christi haberi poterat dogma de resurre- ctione mortuorum, sed etiam e Scriptis Vet. Test. in quibus id propositum esse, nec ipsi Judæi ne- gant, & adversus Sadducæos Christus confirmavit Matth. XXII.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. ὅτι λέγουσιν] Thus the Hebrews use their כי for 'why', Is. XXIX. 16. Thus also below IX. 28. This is to be numbered among the Hebraisms of Mark.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ὅτι λέγουσιν] Sic Hebræi כי suum pro cur usur- pant, Es. XXIX. 16. Sic & infra IX. 28. Hoc Hebraismis Marci annumerandum.

## 9:12
Vers. 12. Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστᾷ πάντα] He recites μὲν ῥητικῶς a saying frequent in the mouths of the lawyers; which he concedes to be true in a certain sense.

καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν ὑιὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενωθῇ] The 'Son of Man' is the Messiah, as Daniel calls him; ἐξουθενεῖν, as we just said, is for the Hellenists the same as ἀποδοκιμάζεσθαι, and corresponds to that בזה נפש of Isaiah XLIX. 7. If it is true that Elijah will restore all things, that is, as the lawyers interpret it, will cause the Messiah to be received with grateful hearts by all the Jewish people, how then will the faith in other prophecies stand, which show that the Messiah is to suffer many things (which Isaiah said most openly) and be rejected by the leaders of the people (which David signified διὰ τύπου), nay, why is the Messiah called the son of man, which name indicates an abject lot? In a similar way πῶς is taken in Matthew XXII. 45.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστᾷ πάντα] μὲν ῥητικῶς recitat dictum frequens in ore legisperitorum; quod certo sensu verum esse concedit.

καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν ὑιὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενωθῇ] υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου est Messias, quomodo eum appellat Daniel; ἐξουθενεῖν, ut modo diximus Hellenistis idem est quod ἀποδοκιμάζεσθαι, & convenit cum illo Esaiæ בזה נפש XLIX. 7. Si verum est Eliam omnia restituturum, id est, quemadmodum legisperiti interpretantur, effecturum ut a populo omni Judaico Messias gratis animis accipiatur, quo- modo igitur constabit fides aliis vaticiniis, quæ ostendunt fore, ut Messias multa patiatur (quod apertissime dixit E- saias) & rejiciatur a primoribus populi, (quod David διὰ τύπου significavit) imo cur Messias dicitur filius hominis, quod nomen sortem abjectam indicat? Simili modo πῶς sumitur Matthæo XXII. 45.

## 9:13
Vers. 13. ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν] Nay, he says, so far are all the Jews from being led to the obedience due to the Messiah by the work of Elijah, that he himself who is called Elijah had to suffer most atrocious things from the Jews.

καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπ᾿ ἀυτόν] Since the Prophet calls the Baptist Elijah, by this very fact it is given to be understood that Ahabs and Jezebels would not be lacking to him.

We easily admit these things concerning the passage in Daniel VII. But we observe here a Grotian self-contradiction: inasmuch as he understood the passage in Dan. VII. 14 in his annotations on the Old Testament not of Christ the Son of Man, but of the Roman people. He is even sounder in this place than in the aforementioned annotations concerning the passage in Is. XLIX. 7, which we also examined there. However, it should not be conceded that David signified the rejection of Christ only διὰ τύπου: for according to the literal sense, David speaks in Psalm CXVIII of no one else being rejected by the leaders of the people than the Messiah, as we showed there. But as for that 'as it is written of him', the persecution of John is believed to be indicated too obscurely by the name of Elijah attributed to him, which John could have been by reason of the Spirit, even if he did not suffer the things that Elijah did, to whom he was certainly not at all similar in the manner of his death, and therefore those words 'as it is written' pertain to the main point which was said about the coming of Elijah, to which only the other is added for the sake of identifying Elijah: namely, that Elijah has come, and indeed [he has come] to him to whom they did whatever they wished, just as it is written that he would come. Cf. Heinsius and from him Walaeus on this passage.

Yet the explanation of v. 12 by Lud. de Dieu may not seem inappropriate. The sense is: Elijah will be the precursor of the Messiah, and he will establish all things which God promised, and will set them in their place, even this very thing which is written concerning the Son of man, that he will suffer many things, &c., which indeed he performed excellently, when, pointing him out with his finger, he said, Behold the lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world. For the sense of those words is, Behold him who, bearing the sins of the world like a lamb, will suffer many things, will be killed, and will be accounted as nothing. The Arab translated accurately: Then he said to them, that Elijah has already come first, and rectified all things, and that which was written concerning the Son of man, that he will suffer many things and will be rejected. That is, this also he rectifi- he rectified what was written concerning the sufferings of the Son of man. Because, to be sure, the Jews were not judging correctly about that matter. And in that sense ἀποκαθιςᾷ is also correctly translated as he will restore. Yet πῶς γέ- γραπται can also be translated as, he will restore all things, and how it is written concerning the Son of man. That is, among other things he will also restore this, how it is written concerning the sufferings of Christ, he will teach it openly, clearly, and correctly. I prefer that, because it retains the proper and genuine meaning of τοῦ πῶς. This is Lud. de Dieu.

PART II. The deliverance of the lunatic from a mute and deaf spirit.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν] Imo, inquit tantum abest, ut Eliæ opera omnes Judæi sint ad obedientiam Messiæ debi- tam perducendi, ut ipse qui Elias dicitur debuerit a Judæis atrocissima perpeti.

καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπ᾿ ἀυτόν] Cum Baptistam Eliam vocet Propheta, hoc ipso intelligi datur non defuturos ipsi Acha- bos & Jezebeles.

Facile hæc admittimus de loco Danielis VII. Ἑαυτομαχίαν autem Grotianam hic observamus: siquidem locum Dan. VII. 14. in annotatis Vet. Test. non de Christo Filio hominis, sed de populo Romano intellexerit. Sanior etiam est hoc loco, quam in prædictis annotatis circa locum Es. XLIX. 7. quem ibi etiam expendimus. Rejectionem autem Chri- sti solum διὰ τύπου significasse Davidem haud conce- dendum: nam secundum sensum literalem de nullo alio a primoribus populi rejiciendo loqui- tur David Psal. CXVIII. quam de Messia, ut illic ostendimus. Quod vero ad illud sicut scriptum est de eo, nimis obscure indicata creditur nomine Eliæ Johanni tributo hujus persequutio, quam E- lias ratione Spiritus Johannes esse potuerit, et- iam si non ea passus, quæ Elias, cui utique in mortis genere similis minime fuit, ideoque verba illa sicut scriptum est, ad præcipuum, quod de Eliæ adventu dictum pertinent, cui alterum so- lum additur, dignoscendi Eliæ causa: nimirum Eliam venisse, & eum quidem cui fecerunt, quæ cunque voluerunt, sicut ipsum venturum esse scri- ptum est. Conf. Heinsius & ex eo Walaus in h. l.

Non inconcinna tamen videri possit Lud. de Dieu explicatio v. 12. Sensus est: Elias præcursor erit Messiæ, & omnia quæ promisit Deus, stabiliet, suoque in loco constituet, etiam hoc ipsum, quod de Filio hominis scriptum est, quod multa patie- tur, &c. quod sane egregie præstitit, ubi digito eum demonstrans dixit, Ecce agnus Dei qui tollit pec- cata mundi Eorum enim verborum sensus est, Ecce enim qui peccata mundi instar agni portans multa patietur, occidetur & pro nihilo habebitur. Accurate transtulit Arabs. Tunc dixit eis, quod Elias jam venit primum, & rectificavit omnia, & quod scriptum fuit de Filio hominis, quod patie- tur multa & reprobabitur. Id est, hoc etiam restifi- rectificavit, quod de passionibus Filii hominis scriptum erat. Quia nempe non recte de ea re judi- cabant Judæi. Atque eo sensu ἀποκαθιςᾷ recte etiam vertitur restituet. Potest tamen πῶς γέ- γραπται etiam verti, restituet omnia, & quomodo scriptum sit de Filio hominis. Id est, inter cætera hæc etiam restituet, quomodo de passionibus Christi scriptum sit, id palam, clare & recte docebit. Id præfero, quia propriam & genuinam τοῦ πῶς signi- ficationem retinet. Hæc Lud. de Dieu.

PARS II. Lunatici à spiritu muto & surdo liberatio.

## 9:16
Ver. 16. πρὸς αὐτοὺς) The Syrian reads thus, understanding the disciples, which verse 14 above seems altogether to require. Ver. 18. ῥήσσει αὐτὸν καὶ ἀφρίζει) ῥήσσει means he shakes together, for which Mark above in chapter I and in this place said twice σπαράσσει, Luke distinguishes in chapter IX. 42. And the Syrian here seems to have read σπαράσσει for ἀφρίζει: although μετὰ ἀφρῦ is also found in Luke. I think ῥήσσειν means he dashes down, as the Syrian and the old Latin interpreter understood it. And Tertullian translates that passage of Matthew VII. 6, μήποτε ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς, as, lest they overturn you, in Ad Uxorem II. Thus the Greeks elsewhere translate רצץ as ῥηγνύειν, elsewhere as καταβάλλειν. And פטר elsewhere as ῥηγνύναι, elsewhere as ῥάσσειν, or ἐδαφίζειν. Moreover, there is ἐδαφίζειν in that καὶ ἀφρίζει. For αὐτός is understood. חמק (τερίζει καὶ ξηραίνεται) It withers יבש, as in Zech. XI. 17. Ver. 20. καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν εὐθέως τὸ πνεῦμα) ἰδὼν must altogether be construed with πνεῦμα, namely according to the meaning. For it is just as if it were said, a demon. And thus it appears the Syrian understood it. ἐσπάραξεν αὐτόν) The Syrian seems to have read ἔῤῥηξεν, the Latin ἐτάραξεν. Both seem to have been born from interpretation. ἀφρίζων) The Syrian seems not to have understood the word ἀφρίζων in this place, and ἀφρίζων in Luke, unless perhaps he read πρίζων here, and πρίζει above. Luke defends our reading: and it is consistent with the matter. For it is joined to that madness. See the history which is in I Sam. XXI and Josephus there: likewise the writer of the book περὶ ἱερῆς νόσου which is among the Hippocratic writings. Ver. 21. παιδιόθεν) Mark calls even a twelve-year-old girl a child, as appears above in chapter V. 39, 42. Nor did the Syrian understand it otherwise here, as we noted on Matthew. The LXX generally translate נער παιδάριον. But that which comes from the same root, מנעריו Gen. VIII. 21, is ἐκ νεότητος. Ver. 22. εἴτε δύνασαι βοήθησον ἡμῖν) In a few words both something of faith shines forth, and that indeed small: which nevertheless Christ does not despise. Ver. 23. τὸ εἰ δύνασαι πιστεῦσαι) An elliptical expression which you will best supplement by adding βοηθήσω σοι. To believe, if only you can do that, will be for your salvation. Thus below ἡ πίστις σῶσε σωσιν, unless we prefer that the τὸ here is redundant, as it is almost in Luke XXII. v. 2. It is better to say the particle τὸ is redundant here: so that there is no need for this supplement. Capellus thinks the words can be distinguished thus, τὸ εἰ δύνασαι, πιστεῦσαι, so that it is an elliptical speech, and the sense is, Believing is required of you, or, You must believe, or, it behooves you to believe, if you indeed can do that. Thus Christ returns to that man his own words εἴ τι δύνασαι, as if he were saying: You say to me, if you can do anything; but I say to you: if you can believe, thus I will help you, for all things are possible to him who believes: which Walaeus approves. πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι) All things can be effected (by GOD, of course) for the use of those who believe. Ver. 24. βοήθει μοι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ) What is lacking to my trust, supply by your goodness. For that he should have hoped for an increase of trust from Jesus, and indeed suddenly, is hardly credible. As credible as it was to Grotius that he hoped then that what was lacking to his trust would be supplied by goodness, so credible is it that he hoped for an increase of trust from the same: and which is more to be admitted, whether that anything can be obtained by τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, by unbelief, or that a weak faith can be helped and the same be strengthened? Therefore interpreters commonly understand the prayer as being about the strengthening of a weaker faith, which was almost a certain unbelief and for the sake of true humility is so called. It is a sign of great sincerity, says our B. Lyserus in Harm. cap. LXXXIX. p. 1298, that he does not hide the struggle of faith and diffidence in himself. You would have found those who in such a case would have professed faith with a full mouth, of which they were nevertheless destitute, as if they could deceive divine wisdom with lying words. But he acts sincerely here. Because he feels that he is weaker than is fitting, he directs his prayers the more ardently, he explicitly confesses his imperfect faith, and implores the help of Christ, that he may heal this. Ver. 25. ἐπισυντρέχει) By the particle ἐπὶ I think motion to a place is signified, so that the sense is, to run together to him, as the Syrian took it. - καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς) That is because that incursion of the demon, after the example of the lunatic disease, had its intervals. Ver. 28. ὅτι) For τί ὅτι or διὰ τί, as also above in verse 11. Compare with both places in Matthew.

PART III. The prediction of the passion and resurrection of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 16. πρὸς αὐτοὺς) Ita Syrus legit, discipulos intelligens, quod omnino exigere videtur comma 14. supra. Vers. 18. ῥήσσει αὐτὸν καὶ ἀφρίζει) ῥήσσει συνταράσσει, pro quo Marcus supra cap. I. & hoc loco bis dixit σπαράσσει, distinguit Lucas c. IX. 42. Et Syrus hic pro ἀφρίζει legisse videtur σπαράσσει: cum tamen μετὰ ἀφρῦ sit etiam apud Lucam. Puto ῥήσσειν esse solo allidit, quomodo accepit Syrus & vetus interpres Latinus. Et Tertullianus illud Matthæi VII. 6. μήποτε ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς vertit, ne vos evertant, ad uxorem II. Sic רצץ Græci alibi vertunt ῥηγνύειν, alibi καταβάλ- λειν. Et פטר alibi ῥηγνύναι alibi ῥάσσειν, vel ἐδαφίζειν. Est au- tem ἐδαφίζειν in illo καὶ ἀφρίζει. Subauditur enim αὐτός. חמק (τερίζει καὶ ξηραίνεται) Tabescit יבש, ut Zach. XI. 17. Vers. 20. καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν εὐθέως τὸ πνεῦμα) Omnino ἰδὼν construendum est cum πνεῦμα, nimirum κατὰ τὸ σημαινόμε- νον. Perinde enim est quasi diceretur δαίμων. Atque ita apparet Syrum accepisse. ἐσπάραξεν αὐτόν) Syrus legisse videtur ἔῤῥηξεν, Latinus ἐ- τάραξεν. Utrumque ab interpretamento natum videtur. ἀφρίζων) Videtur Syrus non intellexisse vocem ἀφρίζων hoc loco, & ἀφριζαρud Lucam, nisi forte hic πρίζων, & supra πρίζει legerit. Nostram lectionem defendit Lucas: & rei convenit. Est enim conjunctum id insaniæ. Vide histo- riam quæ est I. Sam. XXI. & ibi Josephum: item scriptorem libri περὶ ἱερᾶς νόσου qui est inter Hippocratea. Vers. 21. παιδιόθεν) Marcus παιδίον vocat etiam puellam duodecennem, ut apparet supra cap. V. 39.42. Neq; aliter hic Syrus accepit, ut notavimus ad Matthæum. נער παιδά- ριον plerunque vertunt LXX. At illud, quod indidem venit, מנעריו Gen. VIII. 21. ἐκ νεότητος. Vers. 22. εἴτε δύνασαι βοήθησον ἡμῖν) In paucis verbis & fidei aliquid elucet, & id sane exiguum: quod tamen Chri- stus non aspernatur. Vers. 23. τὸ εἰ δύνασαι πιστεῦσαι) Ἐλλειπτικὸς λόγος quem optime supplebis addito βοηθήσω σοι. Confidere, si modo id potes, erit tibi saluti. Ita infra ἡ πίστις σῶσε σωσιν te nisi ma- limus τὸ hic παρέλκειν, quomodo ferme apud Lucam XXII. v. 2. Præstat dicere particulam τὸ hic παρέλκειν: ne opus sit hoc supplemento. Capellus putat ita pos- se verba distingui, τὸ εἰ δύνασαι, πιστεῦσαι, ut sit el- liptica oratio, sensusque sit, Credere a te exigitur, vel, Credendum tibi est, sive, oportet te credere, si tu quidem id possis. Sic Christus reponit homini illi sua verba εἴ τι δύνασαι, quasi dicat: Tu mihi dicis, si quid potes; Ego vero tibi dico: si tu potes credere, sic te juvabo, omnia enim sunt possibilia credenti: quod approbat Walæus. πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι) Omnia effici possunt (à DEO scilicet) in usum confidentium. Vers. 24. βοήθει μοι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ) Quod fiduciæ meæ deest bonitate tua supple. Nam ut augmentum fiduciæ ab Iesu speraverit, & quidem subito, vix credibile est. Quam credibile fuit Grotio, sperasse tunc à bonitate suppletum iri quod deerat fiduciæ, tam credibile est augmentum fiduciæ Christi ab eo- dem sperasse: & utrum magis admittendum, an quod τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, incredulitate quid impetrari pos- sit, an quod infirmæ fidei succurri, eademque robo- rari queat? Ideo communiter Interpretes preca- tionem intelligunt de corroboratione infirmioris fi- dei, quæ pene ἀπιστία quædam fuerit atque veræ humilitatis causa ita vocetur. Magna ingenuitatis est, ait B. Lyserus noster in Harm. cap. LXXXIX. p. 1298. quod luctam fidei & diffidentiæ in se non dis- si- fimulat. Invenisses, qui in tali casu pleno ore fidem professuri fuissent, qua tamen destituerentur, quasi divinam sapientiam mendacibus verbis fallere pos- sent. Sed hic ingenue agit. Quia sentit se infirmio- rem esse quam par sit, preces, eo ardentius intendit suam imperfectam fidem diserte confitetur, & Christi opem, ut huic medeatur implorat. Vers. 25. ἐπισυντρέχει) Particula ἐπὶ puto motum ad lo- cum significari, ut sensus sit, concurrere ad ipsum, quomo- do sumpsit Syrus. - καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς) Id ideo, quia incursus iste dæmonis, ad exemplum lunaticimorbi, sua habebat intervalla. Vers. 28. ὅτι) Pro τί ὅτι aut διὰ τί, ut & supra commate 11. confer cum utroque Matthæi loca.

PARS III. Passionis & resurrectionis Christi prædictio.

## 9:30
Ver. 30. παρεπορεύοντο) That is, they were traveling by the side of the road, they were going by a byway, not by the royal road. For Christ wished to be alone with the disciples. παραπορεύεσθαι is indeed sometimes to pass by, or even to go at the side of another with a dative. But that it should be said that those who are on the same journey are παραπορεύεσθαι, that is, to travel together, does not seem to bear analogy. In the same sense as I interpret here, Mark also used παραπορεύεσθαι above in chapter II. 23. For there too Christ was traveling through private fields, not by the public road. And thus the Greeks translate עבר as παραπορεύεσθαι in Deut. II. 18, although they have used that word more loosely elsewhere. Ver. 31. παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων) I think it can rightly be referred to the permission of God the Father: because it is said of men. Ver. 32. τὸ ῥῆμα) Not about death, for they were affected with sadness because of that, Matt. XVII. 23, but about the manner of death, namely, a violent one, Luke IX. 45. & at the same time about the resurrection as above in verse 11. They did not understand how these things cohered with the prophecies concerning the kingdom of the Messiah.

PART IV. The rebuke of the disciples contending about primacy.

Latin:

Vers. 30. παρεπορεύοντο) Id est παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπορεύοντο diverticulo ibant, non via regia. Solus enim esse cum di- scipulis Christus volebat. Est quidem παραπορεύεσθαι inter- dum præterire, aut etiam cum Dativo ad latus alterius ire. Sed ut qui in eodem sint itinere dicatur παραπορεύεσθαι, id est, una iter facere non videtur ἀναλογία pati. Eodem quo hic interpretor sensu Marcus παραπορεύεσθαι & supra usurpa- vit cap. II. 23. Nam & ibi Christus per agros privatos, non per viam publicam iter faciebat. Et sic עבר Græci ver- tunt παραπορεύεσθαι Deut. II. 18. quanquam alibi ea voce la- xius usi. Vers. 31. παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων) Puto recte refer- ri posse ad permissionem Dei patris: quia dicitur ἀνθρώπων. Vers. 32. τὸ ῥῆμα) Non de morte, nam ob eam tristitia af- ficiebantur Matth. XVII. 23. sed de modo mortis, violento scilicet Luc. IX. 45. & simul de resurrectione ut supra com- mate 11. Non intelligebant quomodo hæc cum vaticiniis de regno Messiæ cohærerent.

PARS IV. Discipulorum de primatu contendentium cor- reptio.

## 9:34
Vers. 34. Who is greater) Namely among themselves; for they had agitated that first in silent thought, then also in words among themselves. But when invited by Christ to say what it was they had been disputing about, they are indeed silent on that, but they propose the question more generally and honestly, who was to be the greatest in the kingdom of the Messiah, with no mention made of themselves. Vers. 35. ἔσται) This will be the condition of my kingdom, that those who are to perform the greatest functions are not to receive greater advantages, but are to endure more labor for the benefit of others. See Matt. XX. 26. Vers. 36. ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸν) See below X. 16. The LXX translate the Hebrew חבק as ἐναγκαλίζεσθαι Prov. VI. 10. Others translate it as περιλαμβάνειν, as 2 Kings IV. 16. and Eccles. III. 5. Gen. XXIX. 3. Elsewhere συνέχεσθαι ἀγκάλαις Prov. V. 20. It is not badly translated, therefore, as embracing. For he was not so small an infant that he had to be carried in the arms: since he ran up when called by Christ, as we learn from Matthew. Indeed, Christ placed the boy beside himself as Luke narrates in chapter IX. 47. By the embrace, Christ testified to the love with which he pursues simple age and men who compose themselves to that simplicity. Vers. 37. τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων) A metaphor from comparison. For he calls those boys who, like boys, are free from ambition and similar vices. See on Matthew. - καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἐμὲ δέξηται) Matt. X. 40. οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται) The word 'only' is added by way of interpretation: but it is frequently accustomed to be understood in a two-membered sentence of this kind. Gen. XXXII. 28. John XII. 44. Elsewhere a similar ellipsis is more correctly expressed by 'as well as': as below chapter XIII. 11. John VII. 6.

PART V. Admonition concerning not prohibiting one who is not of our company from casting out demons.

Latin:

Vers. 34. τίς μείζων) Scilicet inter ipsos; id enim taci- ta primum cogitatione, deinde & verbis inter se agitaverant. At à Christo invitati ut dicerent quid essent de quo disce- ptassent, id quidem tacent, sed generalius & honestius pro- ponunt quæstionem, quis in regno Messiæ maximus esset futurus, nulla sui facta mentione. Vers. 35. ἔσται) Hæc erit regni mei conditio, ut qui maxi- mas obituri sunt functiones, non majora percepturi sint commoda, sed plus toleraturi laboris in aliorum utilitatem. Vide Matth. XX. 26. Vers. 36. ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸν) Vide infra X. 16. He- bræum חבק LXX. vertunt, ἐναγκαλίζεσθαι Prov. VI. 10. A- lii vertunt περιλαμβάνειν, ut 2. Reg. IV. 16. & Eccles. III. 5. Gen. XXIX. 3. Alibi συνέχεσθαι ἀγκάλαις Prov. V. 20. Non male igitur vertitur complectens. Neque enim erat tam parvus infans ut ulnis gestandus esset: quippe qui vocatus à Christo accurrerit, ut ex Matthæo discimus. Imo Chri- stus puerum juxta se constituit ut Lucas narrat cap. IX. 47. Amplexu Christus amorem testatus est quo simplicem æta- tem & homines ad eam simplicitatem se componentes pro- sequitur. Vers. 37. τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων) Metaphora ex compara- tione. Pueros enim vocat qui puerorum instar ab ambi- tione & similibus vitiis vacant. Vide ad Matthæum. - καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἐμὲ δέξηται) Matth. X. 40. ἐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται) Μόνον ex interpretamento adjectum: sed frequenter solet in hujusmodi bimembri oratione subau- diri. Gen. XXXII. 28. Iohan. XII. 44. Alibi similis ἴα- ψις per tam & quam rectius exprimitur: ut infra cap. XIII. 11. Ioh. VII. 6.

PARS V. De alieno dæmonia ejiciente non prohibendo monitio.

## 9:38
Vers. 38. In your name) You being named. For there was a formula for exorcists: In the name of Jesus of Nazareth come out: as also in healings Acts III. 6. This formula, however, just as it was effective in all believers by Christ's promise (concerning which we shall speak elsewhere), so it sometimes had its power even

Pronounced by good intermediaries, and that for the honor of Jesus, as we have shown elsewhere from Origen. However, this person whom John is dealing with seems neither to have been as wicked as the sons of Sceva were, nor yet so devoted to Jesus as to surrender himself into his discipline: but with a middling affection, not thinking ill of Jesus: for Christ's words seem to signify that.

ὃς ἐκ ἀκολυθεῖ ἡμῖν] He does not join himself to our company, nor does he profess himself to be of your flock.

ἐκωλύσαμεν αὐτὸν] Not out of envy, but out of an unthinking zeal for the master, similar to Joshua in Num. XI. 28, not yet understanding that which Paul said: 'in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice, yes, and will rejoice' Phil. I. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 38. τῷ ὀνόματί σου) Te nominato. Formula enim erat exorcistis: In nomine Iesu Nazareni egredere: ut & in sanatiomibus Act. III. 6. Hæc autem formula, sicut in fide- libus omnibus efficax erat ex Christi promissione (qua de se agemus alibi) ita interdum vim suam habebat etiam

Per mtauos bonos pronuntiata, idque ad honorem Jesu, ut ex Origene alibi ostendimus. Videtur autem iste de quo agit Johannes neque tam pravus fuisse quam erant Scevæ filii, neque tamen ita addictus Jesu ut se in ejus disciplinam traderet: sed medio affectu, non male de Jesu sentiens: id enim significare videntur Christi verba.

ὃς ἐκ ἀκολυθεῖ ἡμῖν] Non se adjungit nostro comitatui, ne- que profitetur se tui gregis.

ἐκωλύσαμεν αὐτὸν] Non invidia, sed improvido in magi- strum studio, similes Josuæ Num. XI. 28. nondum intelli- gentes illud quod dixit Paulus: παντὶ τρόπῳ εἴτε προφάσει εἴ- τε ἀληθείᾳ χριστὸς καταγγέλλεται· κὰι ἐν τούτῳ χαίρω ἀλλὰ κὰι χαρή- σομαι Phil. I. 18.

## 9:39
Vers. 39. ὃς δυνήσεται ταχὺ] This δυνήσεται is to be understood morally. For a man so vain will scarcely be found who, at the same time, is going to speak ill of him by the power of whose name he uses against demons.

Latin:

Vers. 39. ὃς δυνήσεται ταχὺ] Hoc δυνήσεται moraliter in- telligendum. Vix enim reperietur homo tam vanus qui sub idem tempus sit obtrectaturus ei cujus nominis vi ad- versum dæmonas utitur.

## 9:40
Vers. 40. καθ’ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν] Thus the best Codices: thus the Syriac: thus the Arabic: thus the Latin. Wherefore it ought not to have been changed. It was a proverb worn by common use, and it matters not whether it is uttered in the first, second, or third person. For it is an indefinite statement pertaining to anyone. This adage has a place whenever some matter is to be promoted by taking up resources from wherever possible. Famous is the voice of Gaius Caesar, who said that those who were not against him would be counted among his own. How this does not conflict with that which is said in Matth. XII. 30, see in the annotations there.

The audacity of Beza is deservedly noted, because he changed the text, since not more than two of Stephanus's Codices read ἡμῶν, while others consistently have ὑμῶν, and versions and interpreters agree with these.

Latin:

Vers. 40. καθ’ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν] Ita optimi Codices: ita Syrus: ita Arabs: ita Latinus. Quare mutari non debuit. Proverbium erat usu communi tritum, quod prima an se- cunda an tertia persona efferatur nihil refert. Nam inde- finita oratio est ad quosvis pertinens. Locum habet hoc adagium quoties res aliqua assumtis undicunque subsidiis promovenda est. Celebris est Caji Cæsaris vox, qui me- dios dicebat sibi suorum numero futuros. Quomodo non pugnet cum eo quod dicitur Matth. XII. 30. vide in inibi annotatis.

Merito notatur audacia Bezæ, quod mutarit tex- tum, quum non nisi duo Codices Stephani le- gant ἡμῶν, alii ὑμῶν constanter habeant, & his a- stipulentur versiones & Interpretes.

## 9:41
Vers. 41. ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς] The little word γὰρ seems to require some coherence with the preceding. Nor does it stand in the way that Matthew recounts these things at another time. For, as with other wise men, so with Christ, certain maxims were so familiar that he often repeated them. Christ had said that the business of the Gospel must be promoted by all means, that is, as it is said, with sails and oars. He now adds, to confirm that, that even the smallest benefits bestowed upon that business by any man, even one not of the right faith, will have their reward, and conversely, that he who has brought even the slightest impediment to that business will not go unpunished.

ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μῦ, ὅτι χριστῦ ἐσε] For my sake: and therefore because you are my disciples and ministers.

PARS VI. Information concerning avoiding scandal and having salt.

Latin:

Vers. 41. ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς] Vocula γὰρ videtur ali- quam cum superioribus cohærentiam requirere. Nec ob- stat quod alio tempore Matthæus ista recitat. Nam ut aliis sapientibus ita Christo sententiæ quædam erant adeo fami- liares ut eas sæpe repeteret. Dixerat Christus omnibus modis, id est ut dicitur, velis remisque promovendum Evangelii negotium. Addit jam, ut id confirmet, etiam minima beneficia à quosvis homine, etiam non rectæ fidei, ei negotio impensa suam mercedem habitura, & contra non impune laturum qui vel minimum ei negotio impedimen- tum attulerit.

ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μῦ, ὅτι χριστῦ ἐσε] Mea causa: atque ideo quod mei estis discipuli & ministri.

PARS VI. De scandalo cavendo & sale habendo infor- matio.

## 9:42
Vers. 42. καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον] συμφέρει αὐτῷ Matthew: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ Luke: in which places μᾶλλον, which is expressed here, is understood. Nor do I doubt that here καλὸν μᾶλλον is ἄμεινον, as the Syriac also takes it. For the Hebrews, because they lack comparatives, paraphrase them in this way. Moreover, Mark is accustomed to 'hebraize'. But the Greeks also say ἄμεινον μᾶλλον, and καλὸν with μᾶλλον suppressed in the same sense, as here also in the following clauses. Similar is: 'it is more blessed to give than to receive': that is, μακαριώτερον. Act. XX. 35.

Latin:

Vers. 42. καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον] συμφέρει αὐτῷ Matthæus: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ Lucas: quibus locis μᾶλλον quod hic ex- pressum est subauditur. Neque dubito hic καλὸν μᾶλλον esse ἄμεινον, quomodo accipit & Syrus. Hebræi enim quia comparativis carent eos hoc modo circumloquun- tur. Solet autem Marcus έβραΐζειν. Sed & Græc. ἄμεινον μᾶλλον dicunt, & καλὸν suppresso μᾶλλον eodem sensu, ut hic quoque commatibus sequentibus. Simile est: μακάριόν ἐστι διδόναι μᾶλλον ἢ λαμβάνειν: id est μακαριώτερον. Act. XX. 35.

## 9:43
Vers. 43. εἰς τὴν ζωήν] Which he soon interprets as βασιλείαν τῦ θεῦ.

τὸ ἄσβεστον] αἰώνιον Matthew: who also said ἄσβεστον elsewhere III, 12. See the passage in Is. I. 31.

Latin:

Vers. 43. εἰς τὴν ζωήν] Quam mox interpretatur βασι- λείαν τῦ θεῦ.

τὸ ἄσβεστον] αἰώνιον Matthæus: qui & ἄσβεστον dixit alibi III, 12. Vide locum Es. I. 31.

## 9:44
Vers. 44. "their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched"] The very words of the LXX Interpreters: "for their worm shall not die; and their fire shall not be quenched." Is. LXVI. 24. It seems that the prophet, at first glance in this whole prophecy, signifies, as often elsewhere, that the nations will be assumed into the people of God, who serve God not according to the rites of the flesh, but according to the law of the Spirit. But those who have despised salutary admonitions (the Jews, namely) will perish most miserably: because "until the consummation and desolation," as it is in Daniel, has been decreed against them: which is illustrated by two comparisons: fire, indeed, which signifies God's most burning and unsparing wrath: "for our God is a consuming fire" Hebr. XII. 29. Deut. IV. 24 and in the same way the same Isaiah elsewhere, dealing with the severe judgment of God, had said: "It shall not be quenched night and day: its smoke shall ascend forever: from age to age it shall be a desolation:" and what follows in ch. XXXIV 10. with which words it is worth the effort to compare those which are in the epistle of Jude 7. Then also the worm which is accustomed to cling to corpses, until they are not entirely consumed. But just as the destruction of Jerusalem and the disasters annexed to it presented a most manifest image of the general judgment, so Christ with the best right adapts what was said about that time to eternal punishments, in the describing of which the very propriety of the words, as has already been observed often in prophecies containing places, serves the custom. For that "does not die" and "is not quenched" in the Jerusalem destruction indeed has its sense restricted and limited according to the nature of the subject matter, but in the punishments of the other life it has another [sense] according to their literal meaning, here the interpreters [derive it] from the preceding, "of those who do not cut off the scandals," that is, of those who indulge their vices. The writer of Ecclesiasticus VII. 19: "the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worm." And the writer of Judith XVI. 21: "to give fire and worms into their flesh:" whence it appears that the sentiment was common among the Jews.

Grotius explains the passage of Is. LXVI. 24, which is added here concerning the extreme devastation of Jerusalem by fire and the worm which is accustomed to cling to corpses, according to the letter and as a type of eternal condemnation: But just as here it is a matter of eternal condemnation in the literal sense, so also in that, and no other sense, one ought to understand the Prophetic passage. Concerning which we have spoken in the Annotations on Is. LXVI. 24.

Latin:

Vers. 44. ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν ὐ τελευτᾷ́ κὰι τὸ πῦρ ὐ σβέννυται] Ipsa verba LXX. Interpretum: ὁ γὰρ σκώληξ αὐτῶν ὐ τελευ- τήσει· κὰι τὸ πῦρ αὐτῶν ὐ σβεσθήσεται. Es. LXVI. 24. Videtur I to- phera primo quidem aspectu significare toto isto vaticinio, quod alibi sæpe, fore ut gentes assumantur in populum Dei, qui non secundum ritus carnis, sed secundum legem Spiritus Deo serviant. Eos vero qui salutares admonitio- nes contempserint (Judæos scilicet) miserrime perituros: quia ἕως συντελείας ἐρήμωσις, ut apud Danielem est, adver- sus eos sit decreta: quæ duabus comparationibus illustra- tur: ignis quidem qui Dei iram flagrantissimam & nor par- centem significat: κὰι γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον Hebr. XII. 29. Deut. IV. 24 eodemque modo idem Esaias alibi de severo Dei judicio agens dixerat: Noctu diuque non extin- guetur: in perpetuum ascendet fumus ejus: ab ætate in æta- tem erit desolatio: & quæ sequuntur c. XXXIV 10. cum qui- bus verbis operæ pretium est conferre ea quæ in epistola sunt Judæ 7. deinde & vermis qui hærere cadaveribus so- let, de nec plane sint absumta. Sicut autem excidium Hiero- solymorum & ei annexę clades manifestissimam prætule- runt generalis judicii imaginem, ita Christus optimo jure quod de illo tempore dictum est aptat in perpetua suppli- cia, quibus describendis ipsa verborum proprietas, quod sæpe in vaticiniis τόπων continentibus observatum jam est, more inservit. Nam illud ὁ τελευτᾷ & ὁ σβέννυται in Hiero- solymitano quidem excidio habet suum sensum pro ratione materiæ restrictum ac limitatum, in pœnis autem vitæ alte- rius alium κατὰ τὸ κυριολογούμενον αὐτῶν hic interpretes ex superioribus, τῶν τὰ σκάνδαλα ἐκ ἀποκοπτόντων, id est eo- rum qui vitiis suis indulgent. Scriptor Ecclesiastici VII. 19. ἐκδίκησις ἀσεβῦς πῦρ καὶ σκώληξ. Et Scriptor Judithæ XVI. 21. δῦναι πῦρ κὶ σκώληκας εἰς σάρκας αὐτῶν: unde appa- ret tritam fuisse inter Judæos sententiam.

Locum Esa. LXVI. 24. qui hic adjicitur de de- vastatione extrema Hierosolymæ per ignem & vermem qui cadaveribus hærere solet, secundum literam & in typo æternæ condemnationis, explicat Grotius: Sed uti hic de æterna condemnatione literali sensu agitur, ita etiam eo, non alio sensu in- telligere Propheticum locum oportet. Quo de diximus in Annot. ad Esa. LXVI. 24.

## 9:47
Vers. 47. "Gehenna of fire"] Matth XVIII. 9. Vers. 49. "For everyone shall be salted with fire and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt"] This passage, which has tortured the wits of many learned men, is to many now suspect. I remember the incomparable man Joseph Scaliger telling me that the reading must be changed and "for every burnt offering" (πᾶσα γὰρ πυρά) should be written. He wanted the word "pyra" to be a new word coined by Mark to express the force of the Hebrew word אשה. But that word "pyra" is read neither among the Greeks nor any Hellenist. But what is אשה to the Hebrews, the Hellenists are accustomed to translate almost as "offering" (κάρπωμα). Furthermore, so that I may not dare to change anything, such a consensus of the codices deters me: nor indeed is it necessary, since a sense sufficiently convenient and, if I am not mistaken, best fitting this place is not lacking from the conceived words. First, "everyone" (πᾶς) here is "anyone," as Aristophanes: "everyone is a fool, trust everyone hither." Sophocles: "for everyone is with God, and laughs and laments." Luc. XVI. 16. "everyone forces his way into it." Then indeed by understanding "of them" (αὐτῶν) here: so that it may signify anyone of those of whom he has treated until now, who namely thinks that he must indulge in depraved affections, similar is that in Luc VI. 40: "but everyone when he is perfected shall be as his teacher:" for there too it is understood from the preceding "of the disciples." Thus Euripides in Hercules Furens: "everyone lifting his foot," namely "of the children," of whom he had treated above, and in Aristophanes' Birds, when he says "and everyone moves his claws hooked," it is understood from those things which precede "of the hawks": and in Peace "everyone" namely "of the farmers" of whom the discourse is. Now indeed "to be salted" (ἁλίζεσθαι) is to be consumed, which is said not only of things salted, as the origin of the word suggests, but also of other things. For it answers to the Hebrew נמלח in Is. LI. 6: "like smoke they shall be consumed" (כעשן נמלחו). Symmachus: "that the heavens shall be salted like smoke." Aquila: "the heaven shall be diminished like smoke," the Jerusalemite comes: "they shall pass away" (ירזון). Hence garments are said to be "consumed" (מרחים) Jer. XXXIIX. 11. literally "salted" or "consumed." And to the Chaldeans and Arabs "malah" (מלח) is to consume: to Homer also "to salt" (ἁλιῶσαι) is to render vain. But the mode of consuming is twofold: for either the whole thing perishes, as in those things which are consumed by fire: for fire is accustomed to spare no part: but "it consumes everything" (πάντα ἐξαναλίσκει) as Philo speaks in the book on the life of Moses: or having consumed some part, what remains is preserved, as happens in those things which are seasoned with salt. The same Philo in "On the Creation of the World" says, "salts are sprinkled on meats so that they might not easily rot." In the book "On the Sacrifices" he says thus: "whatever they (the salts) are sprinkled upon, they preserve." And in the book "On those who sacrifice" again: "salts are a preservative of bodies." Known is that which Varro said from Cleanthes: "The soul was given to the swine for salt, lest it should rot." And for the sake of this thing the most learned Abarbaniel noted that salt was used in the sacrifices of the Hebrews. This custom, as others, flowed also to the nations. Servius on the eighth eclogue: "The pious meal is the chaste mill-cake: salted: for both signify the same thing." Christ illustrates the twofold mode of consuming with the known example of the twofold "offering": that is, "korbanim." For some of these, consisting of the flesh of cattle, were consumed by fire in their entirety as a testimony to the divine glory, so that nothing remained: which were called "whole burnt offerings" (ὁλοκαυτώματα), of which it is treated in Lev. 1. others, however, were seasoned with fine flour and salt, of which see the "Commanding Precepts" LXII, and these are particularly called "sacrifices" (θυσίαι): for so the law has in Lev. II. 13 among the LXX whom Mark follows, "and every gift of your sacrifice shall be salted with salt." For the word "minchah" (מנחה) the LXX translate not only here, but also elsewhere as "sacrifice" (θυσίαν), as Gen. IV. 3. and Lev. VII. 9. Suidas: "Mana" (the most learned Drusius rightly advised that "manaa" should be read) "sacrifice": nor indeed is that error of Suidas in that place found only from the proximity of the words; but from Jer. XVII. 16 "mana" is written, when from the Hebrew it appears that "manaa" should be read,

which Jerome also noted. Thus in Baruch 1:10 it is written μάννα for qdo, which Theodoretus rightly reads as μαννὰ. The same error occurs in Jer. 48 according to the Greek edition. But it is read correctly written in Ezech. 45 at the end: Chrysostom also writes it correctly in his second letter to Theodore from Dan. 2:46. Christ therefore compares the impious to τοῖς ὁλοκαυτώμασι: for he had also said above that they are cast εἰς πῦρ ἄσβεστον. Now indeed, τὸ πῦρ τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων was also πῦρ ἄσβεστον. Philo περὶ θυόντων: πῦρ ἐπὶ τῦ θυσιαστηρίυ (he is speaking of the altar τῶν ὁλοκαυλωμάτων) καυθήσεται διὰ παντὸς ἄσβεσον. That fire was accustomed to consume the entire ὁλοκαυτώματα, a word which not only Philo uses, but also Theophrastus when describing the ὁλοκαυτώματα of the Jews, as cited by Porphyry. Thus also the wrath of God against the impious is, as we have said, πῦρ ἀναλίσκον. Deut. 4:24, Heb. 12:29. Burnt offerings are expended only so that the supreme right of God may appear, with no benefit to men: thus also there will be no other use for the wicked than that they be the material upon which divine justice exercises itself. And hence it is that the wicked are everywhere called victims destined for divine wrath among the Prophets, Is. XXXIV. 6, Jer. XII. 3, XLVI. 10, Ezech. XXI. 9, 10, XXXIX. 17. Add Dan. VII. 11. But those who have piety at heart are deservedly compared to that sacrifice so specifically named. These are they whom Paul admonishes to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, Rom. XII. 1. And Peter says they are appointed to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God, I. ep. II. 5. And to the same point pertain those things which are read in Isaiah a little before the words already cited by Christ, ch. LXVI. 20, where in the Hebrew there is the word מנחה and in the Greek θυσίας. To which that saying of Ignatius also seems to me to allude: 'Let me be food for the beasts, through whom it is possible to attain to God; I am the wheat of God, and I am ground by the teeth of beasts that I may be found pure bread of God.' For מנחה, that is, θυσία, was from ground wheat, that is, from fine flour as we have said: and the cakes which were made from it, חלות to the Hebrews, are called ἄρτοι in Greek both by the LXX and by Josephus, Antiquities III. cap X. Not dissimilar is the fact that the scholiasts on Homer and Aristophanes note that τὰς ὀλοχύτας, τὰ πόπανα, and τὰ πλακύντια are called προθύματα. Such a θυσία, however, is pleasing to God only if whatever is rotten, that is, evil affections (which Christ called σκάνδαλα), is eaten away by diligent care and meditation, just as salt is accustomed to eat away rottenness. Thus Paul wishes our speech to be seasoned with salt, Col. IV. 6, that is, in which there is nothing rotten, Eph. IV. 9. And that the law of God is signified by salt, the Hebrews note on Levit. I. This salting of the soul is followed by the incorruption of the soul, as Paul speaks, Ephes. VI. 4, Tit. II. 7, which incorruption of the soul is also going to produce incorruption for the body, Rom. II. 7, 1 Cor. XV. 42, 50, 53, 54, 2 Tim. I. 10. Thus the whole man, with depraved affections consumed, is preserved for eternity: while the fire that will not fail consumes the others entirely. Christ therefore says the same thing here as above, that the whole man must be redeemed by the loss of a part. Altogether, some consumption is owed to man, either by way of salting or by way of fire. The latter is for the wicked, the former for the pious.

Grotius deservedly rejects the suspicion of Joseph Scaliger concerning a mistake, as if it should be read πᾶσα γὰρ πυρία, which others also, and especially Spanheim, refute; and the unanimous consensus of the Codices (which indeed Grotius ought to have attended to elsewhere as well) destroys it. He wishes the meaning, however, to be this: that those who grant indulgence to depraved affections are to be consumed entirely by fire like burnt offerings in the Old Testament; but that those who offer themselves to God in a spiritual sacrifice are to be seasoned like a Mincha with salt, so that whatever is rotten or of evil affections may be eaten away by diligent care and meditation, just as salt is accustomed to eat away rottenness. Altogether, he says, some consumption is owed to man, either by way of salting or by way of fire. The latter is for the wicked, the former for the pious. In the former member Maldonatus has ὁμόψηφον, who explains it thus: all those whose fire will not be extinguished will be salted with fire, that is, seasoned, roasted; he who judges: in the latter part there is an allusion to the Levitical Law, just as every victim is salted with salt: but there, fire will be in place of salt, by whose perpetual torments they will be tortured. But in truth, the Jesuit himself attributes little to this opinion, which he does not wish to hand over to the reader as a prejudice, but as something to be judged: and he confesses that he has found no author who has handed down the same. Cloppenburg, however, did not depart much from this gloss in Spicileg. Scholast. Sacrific. prior., when he explains it thus: the worm will not die, because the whole will be salted with fire, as ἁλίζειν πυρὶ

is to make fuel for eternal fire, because salt is a symbol of eternity, Num. XVIII. 9, 2 Corinth. XIII. 5, or the whole will be salted with fire, who indeed has offended someone, so that πᾶς may be ἄρτιος, the whole perfect man with all his members will be tortured by fire. But he who explains the latter words thus: 'and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt: salt is good': as if he were saying, 'But it is better to be salted with the salt of the covenant unto eternal life, such as are the sacrifices sprinkled with the salt of the covenant, offering themselves to God, mortifying their earthly members.'

But the opinion of others is more correct, who interpret it either of the fire and salt of the word and doctrine (which we approve more) or of the fire and salt of the cross, or of the maceration of oneself, because the Word is compared to fire, Jerem. V. 24, ch. XXIII. 29, Mal. III. 2, Luc. XII. 49, and not undeservedly is it compared to salt, because it spiritually preserves the soul by consuming depraved humors. Thus also the cross is denoted by fire, 1 Cor. III. 15, and cleanses the old man like salt, so that an allusion is made to Levit. II. 13, that it is better for us to be seasoned and offered in this spiritual life with fire and salt like victims, than to be consumed by unquenchable fire; as the blessed Luther explains in a marginal gloss concerning the fire and salt of doctrine and the word, which makes for the maceration and crucifixion of the old Adam, the explanation of which others have also embraced, even if the Weimar Paraphrasts join the other [interpretation] concerning the fire and salt of the cross. See B. Lyferus in his Harmony, as well as Beza & Junius, Theophylact & Bede, and among the ancient Doctors Spanheim, who embraces the latter view: The Lord calls that maceration fire, he says, both because it truly burns and torments a man, and by way of ἀντίθεσιν to the fire mentioned before, as if he were to say, those who have regard for their own desires will be subject to eternal fire, but it is better for you not so much to be tormented by another fire, as to be, as it were, seasoned and salted. The Lord therefore opposes fire to fire, the present to the future, the seasoning fire to the burning fire, which fire he establishes as equally necessary for his disciples as salt is for offerings. For since putrefaction is naturally inherent in us, as long as we are in the state of wayfarers, there is need of some salt which may resist that putrefaction and subdue it, lest we rot or cease to be a sacrifice pleasing to God.

But the opinion of Grotius is by no means to be approved, because by the word πᾶς, everyone is understood who comes into comparison with the sacrifice to be seasoned with salt. Therefore, those of whom he had treated before are not noted: And what kind of sense would this be, everyone of those whose fire will not be extinguished will be salted with fire. (2.) Because sacrifices of a different kind are not introduced here, ὁλοκαυτώματα & Mincha, of which some are seasoned with fire, others with salt, but it is said of all sacrifices in general that they are to be seasoned with salt: and they are compared to those who wish to present themselves as sacrifices to God. (3.) Because he warns how the members of the old Adam are to be mortified, so that we may escape that fire ἄσβεστον. (4.) Because the consequences agree better with our explanation, as will now be said. (5.) It is inconvenient for salt to denote the act itself as Grotius wishes: since the medium of seasoning, not the act, is designated by it.

Latin:

Vers. 47. γέενναν τῦ πυρὸς] Matth XVIII. 9. Vers. 49. πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ἁλισθήσεται κὶ πᾶσα θυσία ἁλὶ ἁλι- σθήσεται] Locus hic qui multorum eruditorum torsit inge- nia, multisque modo suspectus est. Memini virum in- comparabilem Josephum Scaligerum mihi dicere mutan- dam lectionem & scribendum πᾶσα γὰρ πυρά. Volebat autem πυριὰν vocem esse novam a Marco confictam ad ex- primendam vim vocis Hebrææ אשה. Sed ea vox πυρὰ neque apud Græcum neque apud Hellenistam ullum legi- tur. Quod autem Hebræis est אשה id ferme κάρπωμα solent vertere Hellenistæ. Præterea ne quid mutare au- deam, absterret tanta codicum consensio: neque vero ne- cesse est, cum non deficiat a conceptis verbis sensus satis com- modus & huic loco, ni fallor, optime conveniens. Primum agitur πᾶς hic est quivis, ut Aristophan. ἰσίγα πᾶς, διῦρο πᾶσι πῖστευ. Sophocles: σὺ γὰρ θεῷ πᾶς κὶ γελᾷ κ᾿ ὀδύρεται. Luc. XVI. 16. πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται. Deinde vero subintelli- gendo hic αὐτῶν: ut lignificetur quilibet eorum de qui- bus egit hactenus, qui scilicet pravis affectibus indulgen- dam putat, simile est illud Luc VI. 40. κατηρτισμένῶ δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλῶ αὐτῶ: nam & ibi ex præcedenti- bus subintelligitur τῶν μαθητῶν. Sic Euripides Hercule Fu- rente: πᾶς τ᾿ ἀνίσχων πόδα, nempe τῶν παίδων, de quibus e- gerat supra, & apud Aristophanem Avibus, cum dicit χωρεῖ δὲ πᾶς τις ὄνυχας ἠγκυλωμένῶ subauditur ex his quæ præce- dunt τῶν ἱεράκων: & in pace πᾶς scilicet τῶν γεωργῶν de qui- bus sermo. Jam vero ἁλίζεσθαι est consumi, quod non de salitis tantum, ut fert vocabuli origo, sed & de aliis rebus dicitur. Respondet enim Hebræo נמלח Esa. LI. 6. כעשן נמלחו כרשמים. Symmachus ὅτι οἱ ὐρανοὶ ὡς καπνὸς ἁλινώσονται. Aquila ὁ ὐρανὸς ὡς καπνὸς μειωθήσεται, Hierosolymitanus venit ירזון transibunt. Hinc tatæ ve- stimenta dicuntur מרחים Jer. XXXIIX. 11. ad verbum ἁ- λιότιντα aut ἁλινθέντα. Et Chaldæis & Arabibus מלח est consumere: Homero quoque ἁλιῶσαι irritum reddere. Est autem consumendi modus duplex: aut enim res tota perit, ut in his quæ igne consumuntur: ignis enim nulli parti solet parcere: sed πάντα ἐξαναλίσκει ut loquitur Philo libro de vita Mosis: aut parte aliqua consumta servatur quod reliquum est, ut accidit in his quæ sale condiuntur, Idem Philo περὶ κοσμοποιΐας ait, τὲς ἅλας τοῖς κρέασι παρα- σπαρῆναί ἵνα μὴ ῥαδίως φθείροιτο. In libro autem περὶ τῶν τῦ θυσίας sic ait: οἷς ἂν περισπασθῶσιν (οἱ ἅλες) διατηρῦσι. Et libro περὶ θυόντων iterum: φυλακτήριον οἱ ἅλες σωμάτων. Notum illud quod ex Cleanthe Varro dixit: Animam suille pecori pro sale datam ne putisceret. Et hujus rei causa salem in sacris Hebræorum usitatum notavit doctissimus Abarba- niel. Mos hic, ut & alii, ad gentes quoque manavit. Ser- vius ad VIII. eclogam: Far pium est mola casta: salsa: utrum- que enim idem significat. Duplicem consumendi modum illustrat Christus noto exemplo duplicem προσφορᾶν: id est קרבנים. Nam harum aliæ constantes ex pecudum carne totæ quantæ erant in testimonium divinæ gloriæ igne ab- sumebantur, ita ut superesset nihil: quæ vocabantur ὁλοκαυ- τώματα, de quibus agitur Lev. 1. aliæ vero è simila sale con- diebantur, de quibus vide Præceptorum Jubentium LXII, exque peculiariter vocantur θυσίαι: ita enim habet lex Le- vit. II. 13 apud LXX quos Marcus sequitur, κὶ πᾶν δῶρον θυ- σίας ὑμῶν ἁλὶ ἁλισθήσεται. Nam vocem מנחה LXX. non hic tantum, sed & alibi vertunt θυσίαν, ut Gen. IV. 3. & Lev. VII. 9. Suidas: Μάνα (recte monuit doctissimus Drusius le- gendum μαναὰ) θυσία: neque vero hoctantum Suidæ in lo- co is error ex vocum vicinitate reperitur; sed a Jer. XVII. 16. μάνα scribitur, cum ex Hebræo appareat legendum μαναὰ,

quod & Hieronymus monuit. Sic Baruchi I. 10. scribitur μάννα pro qdo μαννὰ recte legit Theodoretus. Idem error Jer. XLIIX. secundum Græcam editionem. At recte scri- ptum legitur Ezech. XLV. in fine: recte etiam scribit eam Chrysostomus in secundo ad Theodorum ex Dan. II. 46. Impios igitur comparat Christus τοῖς ὁλοκαυτώμασι: nam & supra dixerat eos conjici εἰς πῦρ ἄσβεστον. Jam vero & τὸ πῦρ τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων erat πῦρ ἄσβεστον. Philo περὶ θυόν- των: πῦρ ἐπὶ τῦ θυσιαστηρίυ (agit de altari τῶν ὁλοκαυλωμάτων) καυθήσεται διὰ παντὸς ἄσβεσον. Ignis ille solebat tota ὁλοκαυ- τώματα ἀναλίσκειν, quo verbo non Philo tantum utitur, sed & Theophrastus describens Judæorum ὁλοκαυτώματα, ci- tante Porphyrio. Sic & Dei ira adversus impios est, ut dixi- mus, πῦρ ἀναλίσκον. Deut. IV. 24. Hebr. XII. 29. Impen- duntur ὁλοκαυτώματα tantum ut appareat jus summum Dei nullo hominum bono: sic & impiorum non alius erit usus quam ut materia sint in quam se divina justitia exerceat. At- que hinc est, quod passim apud Prophetas impii divinæ iræ destinati victimæ vocantur Es. XXXIV. 6. Jer. XII. 3. XLVI. 10. Ezech. XXI. 9. 10. XXXIX. 17. Adde Dan. VII. 11. At quibus pietas cordi est merito comparantur ᾗ θυσίᾳ ita spe- cialiter dictæ. Hi sunt quos Paulus admonet παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἐνάρεστον τῷ θεῷ Rom. XII. 1. Et Petrus constitutos dicit ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας ἐνπροσδέκτυς τῷ θεῷ, I. ep. II. 5. Atque eodem pertinent ea quæ apud E- saiam leguntur paulo ante verba à Christo jamjam citata c. LXVI. 20. ubi est in Hebræo vox מנחה in Græco θυσίας. Quo & illud Ignatii mihi videtur alludere: ἄφετέ με θηρίων εἶναι βρῶμα, δι ὧν ἔνι θεῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν· σῖτός εἰμι τῦ θεῦ, καὶ δι ὀ- δόντων θηρίων ἀλήθομαι ἵνα καθαρὸς ἄρτος θεῦ εὑρεθῶ. Nam מנחה id est θυσία erat ἐκ σίτυ ἀλεσθέντος, id est ex simila ut diximus: & placentæ quæ inde fiebant חלות Hebræis, ἄρ- τοι vocantur Græce tum à LXX. tum ab Josepho Originum III. cap X. Non dissimile quod τὰς ὀλοχύτας, τὰ πόπανα, τὰ πλακύντια vocari προθύματα notant ad Homerum & Aristo- phanem Scholiastæ. Talis autem θυσία ita demum Deo placet, si quicquid est putredinis, hoc est malorum affe- ctuum (quos σκάνδαλα dixit Christus) exedatur diligenti cura ac meditatione, quomodo sal exedere solet putredi- nem. Sic sermonem nostrum Paulus Col. IV. 6. vult esse ἅλατι ἠρτυσμένον, id est in quo nihil sit σαπρὸν Eph. IV. 9. Et per salem significari Dei legem, notant Hebræi ad Levit. I. Hanc animi salsuram sequitur, animi ἀφθαρσία ut Pau- lus loquitur Ephes. VI. 4. Tit. II. 7. quæ animi ἀφθαρσία etiam corpori paritura est ἀφθαρσίαν Rom. II. 7. 1. Cor. XV. 42. 50. 53. 54. 2. Tim. I. 10. Ita totus homo consumtis pravis affectibus in æternum conservatur: cum cæteros to- tos absumat non defiturum incendium. Idem ergo hic dicit Christus quod supra, partis jactura redimendum es- se totum hominem. Omnino aliqua desumtio homini de- betur, aut per modum salsuræ aut per modum incendii. Hæc impiorum est, illa piorum.

Josephi Scaligeri suspicionem de mendo, quasi legi debeat πᾶσα γὰρ πυρία, merito reprobat Grotius, quam & alii, imprimis vero Spanhemius refellunt; & satis consensus unanimis Codicum (quem vero etiam alias attendere debebat Gro- tius) profligat. Sensum autem hunc esse vult: Igne consumendos totos ut ὁλοκαυτώματα in Vet. Te- stam. qui pravis affectibus indulgentiam præstant; Sa- le vero instar Mincha condiendes esse, qui se Deo offe- runt in spirituali sacrificium, ut quicquid est putredi- nis vel malorum affectuum, exedatur diligenti cu- ra atque meditatione, quomodo sal exedere solet pu- tredinem. Omnino, inquit, aliqua consumtio ho- mini debetur, aut per modum salsuræ, aut per modum incendii. Hæc impiorum est, illa piorum. In priori membro Maldonatum habet ὁμόψηφον, qui ita explicat, omnes illos quorum ignis non ex- tinguetur, igne salientur, id est, condientur, torre- buntur; qui censet: in posteriori alludi ad Legem Leviticam, sicut omnis victima sale salitur: sed il- lic pro sale ignem futurum, cujus perpetuis cruciati- bus torquebuntur. Verum enim vero parum ipse Jesuita huic tribuit sententiæ, quam non vult le- ctori ut præjudicatam, sed ut judicandam trade- re: & fatetur, se nullum auctorem invenisse, qui eandem tradiderit. Non multum tamen ab hac glossa discessit Cloppenburgius in Spicileg. Scholast. Sacrific. prior. cum ita explicat, vermem non mo- riturum, quia totus igne salietur, ut ἁλίζειν πυρὶ

sit fomitem facere ignis æterni, quia Sal æterni- tatis Symbolum Num. XVIII. 9. 2. Corinth. XIII. 5. vel totus igne salietur, qui nempe offenderit ali- quem, ut πᾶς sit ἄρτιος totus perfectus mem- bris suis omnibus igne cruciabitur. Qui vero posteriora verba sic exponit: omnis autem hostia sale salietur: bonum est sal istud: quasi dicat, Melius autem est sale fœderis saviri ad vitam æter- nam, quales sale fœderis aspersæ hostiæ sunt se- ipsos Deo offerentes, mortificantes membra terre- stria.

Sed rectius aliorum habet sententia, qui vel de igne ac sale verbi & doctrinæ (quod magis probamus) vel de igne & sale crucis, aut macera- tionis sui ipsius interpretantur, quia Verbum igni comparatur Jerem. V. 24. cap. XXIII. 29. Mal. III. 2. Luc. XII. 49. nec immerito confertur sali, quid spiritualiter animam servet, humores pravos consumendo. Sic & crux per ignem denotatur 1. Cor. III. 15. hominemque veterem instar salis mundat, ut allusio fiat ad Levit. II. 13. quod sa- tius sit nos in hac vita spirituali igne, & sale sicut victimas condiri & offerri, quam igne inextingui- bili consumi; uti explicat B. Lutherus in glossa mar- gin. de igne ac sale doctrinæ & verbi, qui ad mace- rationem & crucifixionem veteris Adami facit, cu- jus explicationem etiam alii amplexi sunt, etsi Vinarienses Paraphrastæ alteram de igne ac sale crucis conjungant. Vid. B. Lyferus in Harmon. nec non Beza & Junius, Theophyl. & Beda, & ex antiquis Doctoribus Spanhemius posteriorem am- plexus: Ignem vocat Dominus macerationem il- lam, inquit, tum quia revera urit, & cruciat ho- minem, tum per ἀντίθεσιν ad ignem de quo ante men- tio, quasi dicat, illi qui cupiditatum suarum ratio- nem habent igni æterno erunt obnoxii, præstat vero vos alio igne non tam cruciari, quam velut condiri & saliri. Opponit ergo Dominus ignem igni, præsen- tem futuro, ignem condientem igni exurenti, quem ignem æque necessarium statuit Discipulis suis, ac sal oblationibus. Quum enim putredo nobis sit insita naturaliter, quamdiu in statu viatorum sumus, o- pus necessario aliquo sale, qui resistat isti putredini & illam edomet, ne computrescamus vel desinamus esse hostia Deo grata.

Nullatenus autem probanda Grotii sententia, quia voce πᾶς omnis intelligitur, qui in compara- tionem cum hostia sale condiendi venit. Non ergo illi, de quibus antea egerat, notantur: Et qualis hic sensus esset, omnis illorum quorum ignis non extinguetur igne salietur. (2.) Quia non di- versi generis hostiæ hic introducuntur, ὁλοκαυτώ- ματα & Mincha, quarum aliæ igne, aliæ sale con- diantur, sed in genere de omnibus hostiis dicitur, quod condiendiæ sale sint: iisque conferuntur, qui se Deo hostias sistere volunt. (3.) Quia monet, quomodo mortificanda sint membra veteris Adami, ut ignem illum ἄσβεστον effugiamus. (4.) Quia con- sequentia magis conveniunt nostræ explicationi, uti jam dicetur. (5.) Salem actum ipsum ut Gro- tius vult, notare inconveniens est: quum me- dium condiendi, non actus eo designetur.

## 9:50
Vers 50. καλὸν τὸ ἅλας] Mention of salt having been made, Mark adds another saying of Christ in passing: but in which salt does not designate the act itself, as above, but that man in whom this act is performed: namely, the Christian who must ward off τὸ σαπρόν not only from himself but also from others. See Matt. V. 13. ἄναλον γίνηται] Μωρανθῇ Matthew and Luke. ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε] There is no other dogma that can restore those who fall away from Christ's saving discipline. See what [is written] on Matthew.

ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλας] Here he returns to the prior meaning of salt. Moreover, τὸ ἅλας, as we have said, is attentive meditation for the purging of the affections, among which the most violent are ambition and envy, on the occasion of which Christ had arrived at this discourse.

καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις] 2 Cor. XIII. 11. 1 Thess. V. 13. The pursuit of peace is a great part of that purging which is treated here.

There is no need for a different acceptance of salt: nor is it fitting here to leap from one sentiment to another, and return to the prior meaning, where everything coheres most excellently. For if the Salt of doctrine be rendered insipid or foolish through corruptions of the word, with what then shall we be seasoned? Therefore, we must always have incorrupt doctrine with us, along with the pursuit of peace and mutual concord. Concerning which, B. Lyserus, col. 1331, Harm. When ministers of the word are negligent in their office anywhere, or they themselves prostitute their authority by perverse doctrine or an evil example of life, then all their discipline collapses, scandals arise everywhere, so that public vices can be corrected by no one's authority, and restrained by no one's command. Have salt in yourselves, etc. He wishes that individuals, as well as the whole Church, and in this especially the ministers of the word, should have in themselves the salt of wisdom, namely, of sincere doctrine, Spirit, and discipline: and at the same time be studious of peace and mutual concord. For these are two principal ornaments, and especially salutary goods of the Church. Concerning which the Lord also treats in Zechariah c. VIII. 19. Love truth and peace only. And he who strives to promote these two goods of the Church, he will not ambitiously and foolishly wrangle about primacy in the Church, as the Apostles had just done, which disease Christ desires to cure with this precept. Spanheim, however, [thinks] the Lord wishes to further commend the utility of our voluntary maceration, and as he called it fire, both because of the fire mentioned before, and because of its nature; so the Lord here calls the same thing salt because of the mention made of salt used in offerings, and because of the suitability of that maceration with salt. He adds, therefore, καλὸν, that is, χρήσιμον, that that salt is useful, if it be applied appropriately: but if it be destitute of its virtue in seasoning a man and preparing him salutarily, there is no other seasoning given further. Therefore, His disciples ought to apply themselves studiously to this, that they may have salt in themselves, not of wisdom only, but also of the necessary acrimony both toward themselves and toward others, yet such as does not hinder their mutual peace.

Latin:

Vers 50. καλὸν τὸ ἅλας] Salis facta mentione aliam obi- ter Christi sententiam Marcus adjicit: sed in qua sal non ipsum actum, ut supra, designat, sed eum hominem in quo actus iste peragitur: Christianum scilicet qui non à se tantum sed & ab aliis arcere debet τὸ σαπρόν. Vide Matth. V. 13. ἄναλον γίνηται] Μωρανθῇ Matthæus & Lucas. ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε] Nullum aliud dogma est quod re- parare eos possit qui à Christi salutari disciplina deficiunt. Vide quæ ad Matthæum.

ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλας] Hic redit ad priorem salis significationem. Est autem τὸ ἅλας ut diximus attenta meditatio ad purgandos affectus quos inter violentissimi sunt ambitio & invidia, quorum occasione in hanc sermonem Christus devenerat.

καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις] 2. Cor. XIII. 11. 1. Thess. V. 13. Pacis studium magna pars est ejus de qua hic agitur purgationis.

Non opus est diversa salis acceptione: neque convenit hic saltus ab una sententia ad aliam, & reditus ad priorem significationem, ubi omnia cohærent optime. Si enim Sal doctrinæ per corruptelas verbi insulsum, vel fatuum reddatur, quonam tandem condiemur? Habere igitur incorruptam doctrinam nobiscum semper debemus cum studio pacis & concordiæ mutuæ. De quo B. Lyserus col. 1331. Harm. Quando alicubi verbi ministri in suo officio sunt negligentes, aut ipsi prava doctrina vel malo vitæ exemplo autoritatem suam prostituunt, tum omnis disciplina eorum corruit, passim scandala enascuntur, ita ut publica vitia nullius autoritate corrigi, nullius imperio coërceri possint. Habete in vobis ipsis salem &c. Vult, ut tum singuli, tum tota Ecclesia, & in hac præcipue verbi ministri, habeant in se salem sapientiæ, nempe sinceræ doctrinæ, Spiritus ac disciplinæ: ac simul sint pacis, ac mutuæ concordiæ studiosi. Hæc enim sunt duo principalia ornamenta, & cumprimis salutaria Ecclesiæ bona. De quibus etiam apud Zachariam Dominus agit c. VIII. 19. Veritatem tantum & pacem diligite. Et qui hæc duo Ecclesiæ bona promovere studet, ille non ambitiose & stulte de primatu in Ecclesia altercabitur, ut modo Apostoli fecerant, cui morbo Christus hoc præcepto mederi cupit. Spanhemius aut Dominum ulterius commendare velle utilitatem voluntariæ macerationis nostræ, & ut illam ignem vocavit tum ob ignem ante commemoratum, tum ob naturam ejus; sic Dominum hic eandem salem vocare ob mentionem factam salis adhibiti in oblationibus, & ob convenientiam macerationis istius cum sale. Addit ergo, καλὸν, hoc est, χρήσιμον utilem esse illam salem, si commode adhibeatur: sin virtute sua destituatur in homine condiendo, & salutariter præparando, non dari ulterius condimentum aliud. Debere itaque Discipulos suos in id studiose incumbere, ut salem in se habeant non sapientiæ tantum; sed & acrimoniæ necessariæ tum erga se, tum erga alios, talem tamen qui non obstet paci illorum mutuæ.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Jesus, coming into the regions of the Jewish land, with the people flocking together, teaches; but the Pharisees, asking about divorce, are informed, as are the disciples privately. Infants are brought, whom he embraces. On the way, he tests a young man who was persuaded that he had fulfilled the law, concerning selling all things so that they might be given as alms to the poor, and taking up the cross; and he teaches how difficult it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven, and to Peter, who testifies that he has deserted all things, he promises remuneration, but affirms that the last shall be first. On the journey toward Jerusalem, having taken the Apostles, he predicts his passion and resurrection; and to James and John, who are seeking the πρωτοκλισίαν, he predicts his cup to be drunk and his baptism to be received, and he exhorts the disciples to humility by his example, and near Jericho he restores sight to the blind Bartimaeus. There are two parts: I. The remainder regarding the journey undertaken for the last Passover: (1) Information concerning divorce, to v. 12. (2) Admonition concerning infants to be admitted to him, to v. 16. (3) The testing of the rich man striving for salvation through the law, to v. 27. (4) Confirmation of Peter concerning future remuneration, to v. 31. II. The undertaking of the journey to the last Passover, and in it (1) Prediction of the passion and resurrection, to v. 34. (2) Admonition of James and John seeking primacy, to v. 45. (3) Healing of the blind Bartimaeus, to v. 52.

PART I. The remainder regarding the journey undertaken by Christ for the last Passover.

I. Information concerning divorce.

Vers. 1. διὰ τοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου] I take Tà here as ὀδευτέοντος. For thus you may find τὸ πέραν elsewhere, Matt. VIII. 18, 28, ch. XIV. 22, ch. XVI. 5, Mark above IV. 35, ch. VI. 21, ch. VI. 45, ch. VIII. 13, Luke VIII. 22. He was going through the places which were called beyond or near the Jordan into that part of Judea in which Aenon is. See John III. 22, ch. X. 40.

See what we have said regarding Matt. XIX. 1.

συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι] Crowds coming together from all sides, which Matthew called ἠκολούθησαν: John ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.

ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς] He was making the place noble by John’s baptism, and even more noble by his teaching and miracles, exciting men to admiration of himself by the very comparison of things. See the similar passages of Matthew and John.

Latin:

CAPUT X. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Iesus in loca terræ Iudaicæ veniens, populo accurrente, docet, Pharisæi autem de divortio quærentes informantur, ut & privatim discipuli. Adducuntur infantes, quos amplexatur. In via juvenem, qui legem se implevisse persuasus erat, tentat, de vendendis omnibus, ut pauperibus, eleemosynæ dentur, & cruce tollenda, docetque quam difficile sit divitem regnum cœlorum ingredi, ac Petro, qui omnia se deseruisse testatur, remunerationem spondet, novissimos vero primos futuros affirmat. Initinere versus Hierosolymam assumtis Apostolis prædicit passionem & resurrectionem suam, & Iacobo ac Iohanni πρωτοκλισίαν petentibus; calicem suum potandum, & baptismum suum suscipiendum prædicit, ac discipulos exemplo ad humilitatem hortatur, & circa Iericho Bartimæo cæco visum restituit. Partes duæ sunt: I. Reliqua ad iter ultimi Paschatis susceptum: (1) Informatio de divortio, ad v. 12. (2) De infantibus ad se admittendis admonitio, ad v. 16. (3) Divitis per legem ad salutem contendentis probatio, ad v. 27. (4) Petri de remuneratione futura confirmatio, ad verf. 31. II. Itineris adultimum Pascha susceptio, & in eo (1) Passionis & resurrectionis prædictio, ad verf. 34. (2) Jacobi & Johannis primatum expetentium commonitio, ad v. 45. (3) Bartimæi cæci sanatio, ad v. 52.

PARS I. Reliqua ad iter ultimi Paschatos à Christo susceptum.

I. Informatio de divortio.

Vers. 1. διὰ τοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου] Tà hic sumo ὀδευτέοντος. Nam ita τὸ πέραν & alibi reperias, Matth. VIII. 18. 28. cap. XIV. 22. c. XVI. 5. Marc. supra IV. 35. c. VI. 21. c. VI. 45. c. VIII. 13. Luc. VIII. 22. Per loca quæ vocabantur uls aut propter Jordanem ibat in eam usque Judææ partem in qua est Ænon Vide Joh. III. 22. c. X. 40.

Vid. quæ ad Matth. XIX. 1. diximus.

συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι] Undique convenientes, quod Matthæus dixit ἠκολούθησαν: Johannes ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
