οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ποιμένες] The Syriac and Latin interpreters rightly omitted οἱ ἄνθρωποι. For it is a pleonasm from Hebraism, as Matth. VII. 9. ch. XI. 19. ch. XIII. 45. 52. ch. XVIII. 13. and elsewhere passim. ἄνθρωποι ποιμένες אַנְשֵׁי רֹעֵי צֹאן Gen. XLVI. 32. Διέλθωμεν] The Syriac translated נֵרַד let us descend, which is accustomed to be said when we seek more southern places. But if this is rightly said, and at the same time it is true what the describers of Palestine say, that that cave was situated to the east of the town, it remains that we say it was in a middle position between the North and the East

Δὴ] If it must be translated (for it is omitted by the Syrian and Latin without any loss of sense), I would prefer to translate it as 'come now' rather than 'indeed'. For the former is of one inciting, the latter of one conceding.

ἕως Βηθλεὲμ] This word can be understood no less of the continuous buildings than of the town. For ἕως sometimes includes what follows, sometimes excludes it.

τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ γεγονὸς] הדבר הזה this thing: as we said above regarding the preface. The LXX also translate דבר as ῥῆμα, Judg. 8. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ποιμένες] Bene omiserunt Syrus & Latinus interpretes οἱ ἄνθρωποι. Est enim πλεονασμὸς ex Hebraismo, ut Matth. VII. 9. cap. XI. 19. c. XIII. 45. 52. c. XVIII. 13. & alibi passim. ἄνθρωποι ποιμένες אַנְשֵׁי רֹעֵי צֹאן Gen. XLVI. 32. Διέλθωμεν] Syrus transtulit נֵרַד descendamus, quod dici solet cum loca australiora petimus. Quod si recte di- ctum est, & simul verum est quod dicunt descriptores Pa- læstinæ ad ortum ab oppido sitam fuisse speluncam istam, restat dicamus fuisse medio situ inter Septentrionem & Ortum

Δὴ] Si vertendum sit (nullo enim sensus damno o- mittitur à Syro & Latino) malim vertere agedum, quam sa- ne. Nam illudexcitantis, hoc concedentis est.

ἕως Βηθλεὲμ] Potest hæc vox non minus de continenti- bus ædificiis quam de oppido intelligi. Nam ἕως id quod se- quitur modo includit, modo exclusit.

τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ γεγονὸς] הדבר הזה rem hanc: ut diximus supra ad anteloquium. דבר ῥῆμα vertunt & LXX. Judic. 8. 1.

## 2:16
Vers. 16. τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσήφ] Who, having undoubtedly observed the piety of the shepherds, told them their own stories.

Latin:

Vers. 16. τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσήφ] Qui procul- dubio pietate pastorum conspecta narrarunt eis suas dula- olas.

## 2:17
Vers. 17. διεγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος] διεγνώρισαν is used as an active in a neutral sense, as if he were saying they spread the report about this matter, that is, they divulged the thing. The Syrian has אוֹדעו למלתא more correctly than the Latin. διαγνωρίζειν is indeed ambiguous, but what follows demands this sense rather.

Latin:

Vers. 17. διεγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος] διεγνώρισαν activum ponitur neutraliter, quasi dicat famam sparsertunt de hac re, id est rem divulgarunt אוֹדעו למלתא habet Syrus rectius quam Latinus. Est quidem διαγνω- ρίζειν ambiguum, sed quæ sequuntur hunc potius sensum postulant.

## 2:19
Vers. 19. συνέβαλεν] צפנה as in Job XXXII. 12. συμβάλλουσα] Luke uses συμβάλλειν quite in the Greek manner, which others call διαλογίζεσθαι, as appears in Acts 9.15, ch. 17.18, ch. 18. 27. But just as διαλογίζεσθαι is properly said of several people talking among themselves, and improperly of one who reasons with himself, so too is συμβάλλειν. That abuse of the word διαλογίζεσθαι which I mentioned appears in Matt. 16.7, 8, ch. 21. 25, Mark 2.6, 8, below ch. 5. 22, ch. 12. 17, John 11. 50. Mary does here what the mother of Samson once did, Judg. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 19. συνέβαλεν] צפנה ut Jobi XXXII. 12. συμβάλλουσα] συμβάλλειν dicit Lucas satis Græce, quod alii διαλογίζεσθαι, ut apparet Actor 9.15. cap. 17.18. cap. 18. 27. Sicut autem διαλογίζεσθαι proprie dicitur de pluribus inter se colloquentibus, improprie de eo qui secum ipse dis- fertat, ita & συμβάλλειν. Vocis διαλογίζεσθαι ea quam dixi κατάχρησις apparet Matth. 16.7. 8. c. 21 25. Marci 2.6. 8. infra c. 5. 22. c. 12. 17. Joh. 11. 50. Facit hic Maria quod olim mater Samsonis Judic. 13.

## 2:20
Vers. 20. οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον, καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτοὺς] Not only those visible signs, but much more what they had heard from Joseph and Mary, agreed with the words of the Angel.

PARS II. The Circumcision of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 20. οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον, καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτοὺς] Non tantum signa illa visibilia, sed multo magis quæ au- dierant ex Josepho & Maria congruebant cum dictis An- geli.

PARS II. Circumcisio Christi.

## 2:21
Vers. 21. καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ] Said by synecdoche, to signify that the time which had been appointed by the law for circumcision was fulfilled: the last day of which time was the eighth from the birth. And so, not the last day itself, but that period of days is indicated in this way: similar to which is what we noted at Matt. 17. 1. Compare the Greek interpretation, Gen. 50. 2. See also Gen. XXV. 24, Luke I. 57, Acts II. 1, with Gen. XVII. 12, Lev. XII. 2. Now they gathered for the sake of the circumcision in the solemn manner, so that other friends might also deliberate with Mary and Joseph about the naming, as was done in the history of the circumcision of John, Luke I. 25 seqq. Whence some, thinking the particle καὶ here is not redundant, understand 'being' to these words, namely, τοῦ περιτέμνειν. And the parents and relatives of Jesus were gathered: but such assumed things of scripture are not to be admitted. Others more correctly understand 'he was circumcised', which can be elicited from the verb τοῦ περιτέμνειν. Now Christ willed to be circumcised partly to demonstrate the truth of human nature, that he had assumed not just an external appearance, but a true body: for circumcision, as Bernard says in Sermon I on the Circumcision, proves the truth of the humanity assumed: and partly to prove his origin from the seed of Abraham: because circumcision was a mark and sign by which that [people] was distinguished from all other nations, so that it might be established from which people the Messiah was to be expected; whence as long as it was necessary for the Israelites to be separated from the nations on account of the Messiah who was to arise from their blood, for so long the sign of circumcision was valid: and then especially for the certification of the merit and redemption of Christ. For since he had no need of circumcision for his own sake and for the sake of regeneration, being devoid of all sin, he underwent it for our sake, partly so that he might fulfill this part of righteousness also, Matt. III. 15, and subject himself to the law to fulfill it for us, and constitute himself a debtor to the whole law, Gal. IV. 4, ch. V. 3, which was required for the merit of righteousness and salvation, Rom. VIII. 3, ch. V. 18, 19, partly so that by the shedding of blood in this infancy he might confirm, and render certain, his future passion and shedding of blood, necessary for the sake of satisfaction for us and our redemption, as if a pledge had been given: and then finally for the sanctification of circumcision. For just as he willed to consecrate baptism by his own baptism, so too he willed to consecrate circumcision by his own circumcision as a means of initiation and salvation: for this passion of Christ also profited in that way both forward and backward, Heb. XIII. 8. καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ [Ἰησῦς] The reading is not to be changed. For in the connections of history, the copula among the Hebrews is ו, which the Hellenists imitate. Thus above in verse 15 and below in verse 17. Now Luke says the name was imposed at that time, solemnly of course, with many present from the family of David who had come to the same place to register.

PART III. The Presentation of Christ in the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 21. καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ] Συνεκδοχικῶς dictum, ut significaretur impletum id tempus quod ex lege circumcisioni erat præstitutum: cujus temporis dies ulti- mus erat à natali octavus. Itaque non dies ipse ultimus, sed illa dierum περίοδος sic indicatur: cui simile est quod anno- tavimus ad Matth. 17. 1. Confer Græcam interpretationem, Gen. L. 2. Vid. & Gen. XXV. 24. Luc. I. 57. Actor. II. 1. cum Gen. XVII. 12. Lev. XII. 2. Convenerunt autem cir- cumcisionis causa more solenni, ut de nomine im- ponendo deliberarent cum Maria & Josepho ami- ci etiam alii, ut in historia circumcisionis Johan- nis Luc. I. 25. seqq. factum. Unde nonnulli particu- lam καὶ hic non παρέλκειν putantes ad hæc verba τοῦ περιτέμνειν scil. ὄντα subintelligunt. Et congregati essent parentes & cognati Iesu: sed talia assumta scripturæ admittenda non sunt. Rectius alii sub- intelligunt circumcisus est, quod è verbo τοῦ περιτέμνειν elici potest. Circumcidi autem voluit Christus tum ob demonstrandam naturæ humanæ veritatem, quod non externam tantum speciem, sed verum corpus susceperit: Circumcisio enim, Bernardo Serm. I. de circumcis. dicente, veritatem probat susceptæ humanitatis: tum ad probandam è semine Abrahæ originem: quia circumcisio erat nota & signum, quo illud ab omnibus aliis gentibus dif- cernebatur, ut constaret ex quo populo exspe- ctandus esset Messias; unde quamdiu Israelitas propter Messiam ex illorum sanguine oriundum à gentibus separatos esse oportuit; tamdiu signum circumcisionis valuit: tum imprimis ob meriti & redemptionis Christi certificationem. Nam quum sui causa & ob regenerationem opus non haberet circumcisione, utpote peccati omnis expers, no- stri causa eandem suscepit, partim ut hanc quo- que partem justitiæ impleret, Matth. III. 15. seque legi ad eandem pro nobis implendam subjiceret, ac debitorem se legis universæ constitueret, Gal. IV. 4. c. V. 3. quod ad meritum justitiæ & salutis re- quirebatur, Rom. VIII.3. c.V.18.19. partim ut effu- sione sanguinis in hac infantia futuram passionem & effusionem sanguinis, satisfactionis pro nobis & redemptionis nostræ causa necessariam, veluti arrha data, confirmaret, certamque redderet: tum denique ob circumcisionis sanctificationem. Ut enim baptismo suo baptismum, ita & circumci- sione sua circumcisionem consecrare voluit ceu medium initiationis & salutis: nam & haec Christi passio ea ratione profuit antrorsum & retrorsum, Ebr. XIII. 8. καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ [Ἰησῦς] Non est mutanda lectio. Nam in connexionibus historiae copula apud Hebraeos וא־ פלאך quos imitantur Hellenistae. Ita supra commate 15. & infra V. 17. Nomen autem Lucas tunc dicit impositum, so- lenniter scilicet, praesentibus multis ex Davidis familia qui ad profitendum eodem venerant.

PARS III. Praesentatio Christi in templo.

## 2:22
Vers. 22. αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωσέως] Since most codices, even that one conspicuous for its age which is in England, have αὐτῶν, and Origen, a diligent collator of copies, read it thus, and the Syriac likewise, this reading was by all means to be retained. For the Arabic is more recent than the Syriac, and not rarely follows the Latin. It offends the Latin interpreter that καθαρισμὸς implies some impurity, which cannot be attributed to Jesus. But it must be known that this impurity is nothing other than a bond imposed by the law; by which both mother and infant were for a certain time kept away first from the contact of men, then from public assemblies. From contact indeed the infant until the eighth day: the mother likewise if she had borne a male: but if a female until the fourteenth day: but from public assemblies, the mother until the fortieth day from birth if she had borne a male; if a female, until the seventy-fourth: but the infant if he had been separated from the mother, until the completed month: but if he were with the mother, until the same time as the mother, because then the mother was considered a participant in the maternal impurity, as has been rightly observed by some from a collation of the laws which exist in Leviticus and Numbers. Some think that this legal impurity was a testimony of that viciousness which is born in men, which the Hebrews call יצר הרע, to which also that of Philo seems to pertain when he says: ὅτι παντὶ γεννητῷ, κἂν σπυδαῖον ἦ παρ᾽ ὅσον ἦλθεν εἰς γένεσιν συμφυὲς τὸ ἁμάρτανειν ἐστι: to which is similar that in Sopater the Philosopher: σύμφυτον τὸ ἁμάρτανειν ἀνθρώποις: and in Hierocles: τί ἂν πρὸς τὴν λυγρὰν τάυτην νοσοπαθον ἅμα καὶ σύμφυλον ἔριν λεγομένην ἐξευρήσομεν τὴν ἐκ τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν παρὰ φύσιν διατεθέντων ἐγειρομένην, κὰι διὰ τοῦτο ὡς οἰκεῖον κα- κὸν λεληθότως βλάπτειν ἐοικυῖαν; Celsus, πέφυκε τὸ ἀνθρώπων νοι φῦλον ἁμαρτάνειν. The Pythagoreans, as can be seen in Iamblichus, call this principle τὸ παραπεφυκὸς ἡμῖν ἀπὸ τῆς γενέσεως αἰλότριον ζῶον & πολυκέφαλον θηρίον & θνητόν τι ζωῇς ἔνδυμα. By Aristotle it is called τι πεφυκὸς ἀντιβαῖνον τῷ λόγῳ. Arnobius spoke of the vice of innate infirmity: but if the law looked to that cause, there was no reason why in the birth of the female sex the times should be doubled: for which no probable reason can be brought, unless it be that those who bear females are accustomed to suffer longer from a flow: because the contact of which was harmful, for that reason the woman was kept away from public assemblies. Someone will think that this opinion is opposed by the fact that a woman who has given birth, when she is purified, is ordered to offer two animals or birds, one for a burnt offering, the other לחטאת περὶ ἁμαρτίας, as the LXX have it. For Origen also urges that word in the seventh book against Celsus: οἱ δὲ προφῆται μυστικώ μενοι οἱ ϊι περὶ τῶν γενέσεως πραγμάτων σοφὸν, θυσίαν περὶ ἁ- μαρτίας λέγουσιν ἀναφέρεσθαι, κὰι περὶ τῶν ἀξιογεννημένων, ὡς οὐ κα- θαρῶν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας. But it is accepted among the Hebrews that they call חטאת also that obligation which is contracted from the law without any fault of man. Thus a Nazirite, who happens unknowingly to touch the body of a dead person, is likewise ordered to offer for a burnt offering and περὶ ἁμαρτίας, with the cause added מאשר חטא על הנפש, that is, ὅτι ἥμαρτε περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς, concerning that corpse, Num. 6.11, that is, he is guilty of having touched a corpse, just as the Latins say guilty of a vow. Thus also the water of purification which restored a man to assemblies is called water of חטאת, i.e., of sin, Num. 19. And what was offered by those with scabs, by those who were γονοῥῥυεῖς, by a woman who had suffered a flow of menses, is called περὶ ἁμαρτίας, Levit. 16, 19, ch. 15, 15, 30. In this way can be explained that which to some seems to be said by the Writer to the Hebrews, that our Lord offered also περὶ ἰδιῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, so that by the name of ἁμαρτιῶν is understood neither vice nor any viciousness, as things which were very far from Him, but the mortal condition of the body, which kept Him away from heaven, just as legal impurity kept someone away from the temple. Compare the passage of the same Epistle, ch. 5, 3, 7. This is what Paul says, ὁμοίωμα τῆς σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, Rom. 8, 3. And in this manner Hilary, Oecumenius, and others interpret also that of Paul, Rom. 6, 10, ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ, that is, by that mortal body such as is the body subject to sin: as we said at Matt. 22, 51. But as to what some argue, that the law which was produced by Moses concerning purification did not pertain to Mary, because the law deals only with those who from male seed conceive, it conflicts, if I am not mistaken, with the words of Luke, nor can it be proven from Moses. For תוריע which the LXX translate σπερματίση is not passive, but active, and as if you were to say when she has brought forth offspring: which general statement is then distributed into two species of male-bearing and female-bearing, as is accustomed to be done among the Hebrews. The same word is in Gen. I. 11. עשׁב מזריע זרע where the LXX have σπεῖρον σπέρμα, Aquila σπερματίζον.

We deservedly retain the reading found in almost all Greek Codices: which Beza rashly moved from its place, and Casaubon rejects: But the Mosaic Law Lev. XII. 6 did not look only to legal impurity of this kind. But primarily to original sin, of which that legal impurity was a testimony of congenital depravity: whence v. 2 it is said: A woman when she has brought forth a female, or has conceived from male seed and brought forth: which since it does not happen without sin Job XIV. 4. Ps. LI. 5. who will believe that there was no regard for this evil of ours, related to us, in the mind of the supreme Legislator? Add that among the doves to be offered, one לחטאת had to be offered for an offering for sin, v. 8. which Origen urges VII. against Celsus: and that for this reason a mother bringing forth a daughter was held unclean longer than one who brought forth a son, because sin was introduced through a woman.

But in vain does Grotius object that it is accepted among the Hebrews that they call חטאת also that obligation which is contracted from the law without any fault of man: as when a Nazarite has unknowingly touched the body of a dead person Num. VI. 11. and when the water of purification, which rendered a man fit for assemblies, is called water of חטאת that is, of sin Num. XIX. and what was offered by those with skin diseases, by those who were γονοῥῥυεῖς, by a woman who had suffered a flow of menses, Lev. XIV. 19. XV. 15. 30. I reply that the word חטאת altogether regards sin, if not always proximately, yet remotely: and indeed that there are not only voluntary transgressions of the law in the judgment of God, but any ἀνομίαν, even involuntary, even of the ceremonial law, not only the moral.

But wrongly, and only in a heretical sense, does Grotius drag the passage Heb. V. 3. 7. here with the Socinians, as if it were said that our Lord offered also περὶ ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν, and by their name is understood the mortal condition, which kept Him from heaven, just as legal impurity kept someone from the temple. For it is indeed said of the Priests of the Old Testament that they offered for their own sins: but that is not applied to the archetype: while they agree only in certain things, which pertain to the proper nature of the figure and foreshadowing. Nor does the condition of mortality ever come under the name of ἁμαρτίας in the Scriptures, nor is such a condition attributed to Christ as would have excluded Him from heaven, just as legal impurity once excluded the Jews from the temple: because it is certain that Christ, who by nature was not more subject or liable to death, nor had principles of corruption or mortality in Himself, than the first Adam created in a state of integrity ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ, underwent death of His own accord and willingly, and laid down His soul for us ἀυτεξυσίως: and since He was in the form of God, and therefore in heaven, and could have enjoyed heavenly glory, He emptied Himself for our sake, and assumed the form of a servant, from Phil. II. 6. it is evident: whence He was not kept from heaven by the condition of a mortal body, but He willed to enter into heavenly glory only by the free and voluntary offering of His body, which was not liable to death, for our sins, and by the delivery of His life as the price of redemption Luke XXIV. 25. Job X. 17. 18. who ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῶ χαρᾶς, ὑπέμεινε σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τῦ θρόνυ τῦ Θεῦ ἐκάθισεν Heb. XII. 2.

Nor indeed in Rom. VIII. 3. is the mortal condition of the body indicated by ὁμοίωμα τῆ σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, but the likeness of other affections with our flesh liable to sin: such as are: to suffer hunger and thirst, to be wearied, to weep, to be saddened, and similar conditions, yet devoid of sin, and harmless. And Grotius himself explains that locution otherwise in his annotations on Rom. VIII. 3. ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, that is, that He might be treated in such a way as the guilty are accustomed to be treated, Is. LIII. 12. Mark XV. 28. Phil. II. 8. For that the body of Christ was by nature liable to diseases and death and corruption is by no means to be admitted.

But that passage in Rom. VI. 10. ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ does not mean what it says, that he died to τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, that is, to the mortal body, such as a body exposed to danger: but what the letter sounds, that he died to SIN, that is, because of sin, as we taught in our refuted Socinianism, not his own, but ours, which Grotius himself acknowledged in his Defensio fidei Catholicae de satisfactione Christi: nor did that gloss of Grotius, concerning the mortal body designated by ἁμαρτία, approve itself in its proper place in his annotations on Rom. VI, 10. where he explained it concerning the punishments of sins, and rendered the Apostle's sentiment thus: Christ once died to those evils which he was sustaining on account of our sins.

Moreover, Grotius nevertheless acknowledges here, and does not deny, original sin, and that depravity which is recognized in men, which he notes is called יצר הרע by the Hebrews, and to which he refers that saying of Philo: ὅτι παντὶ γεννητῷ, κἂν σπουδαῖον ᾖ παρ᾽ ὅσον ἦλθεν εἰς γένεσιν συμφυὲς τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐστιν: which, however, just as it was entirely unknown to the philosophers, so it is rashly proven from Sopater, Hierocles, Iamblichus, and Aristotle, even though some analogies occur among them, since original sin is hidden from all human reason, and is established only by divine revelation.

But if it be asked, how is purification expressed with the plural pronoun αὐτῶν concerning both Mary and Christ, if Levitical impurity is not being looked at, but true sin, since neither was Mary contaminated by sin through the conception or birth of the God-man, nor can that depravity be attributed to this most holy fetus? Resp. Immanuel willed to subject himself to circumcision, and likewise to purification and presentation in the temple, not for his own sake, but for ours, not out of necessity, but out of the freedom of his economy and humiliation, not as if he were subject to the law in himself, but as one voluntarily subject to it for us, not because he was pressed by the guilt of any sin, but because he was held in divine judgment as our Mediator and Vessel, guilty of our sin by a voluntary derivation into himself, and willed to fulfill all righteousness in our place: just as he also deigned to be made sin for us, even though he knew no sin, 2 Cor. V. 21. and he underwent death on account of our sin, when he himself was free from sin and immune to death. Christ therefore subjected himself to this law, to show that the figures of the law were fulfilled in him: as one who was about to make purification of our sins by himself, Heb. I. 3. that is, that he was that true little lamb, by whose holocaust the uncleanness of the woman who has given birth and of the infant is expiated, of which that Levitical purification was a figure, as the blessed Chemnitz says here: who piously judges that this was the reason why the parents of the Lord did not offer a lamb, which they could easily have purchased with the gifts offered by the Magi, but a pair of doves: For because the true lamb was present, they did not offer the typical one.

Ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς ἱεροσόλυμα] About to fulfill two laws at once, one which was concerning the purification of the woman who has given birth, the other which was concerning the redemption of the firstborn: which could not be done within a month: after a month it could be done. I believe, however, that these things which follow were done in some part of the Temple with few people aware, and those faithful: and for that reason the report of these things did not reach Herod.

It seems that one must also agree with those who maintain that the angel appeared to Joseph on the night following the purification, when he was on the journey from Jerusalem to return to Nazareth in Galilee, and gave the command concerning the flight into Egypt. For it is not likely that Joseph traveled again through all of Judea, and Jerusalem itself, where Herod was acting, when he wished to withdraw the child from the hands of Herod and commit himself to the flight into Egypt that had been commanded. Cf. Harmon. B. Chemnitii c. X. where he proves that the arrival of the Magi happened before the days of the purification.

Latin:

Vers. 22. αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωσέως] Cum plerique codices, etiam ille vetustate conspi- cuus qui in Anglia est, habeant αὐτῶν, Origenes diligens exemplarium collator ita legerit, nec aliter Syrus, erat o- mnino lectio haec retinenda. Nam Arabs Syro recentior est, & non raro Latinum sequitur. Offendit Latinum inter- pretem quod καθαρισμὸς impuritatem aliquam supponat, quae Jesu tribui non possit. Sed sciendum est impuritatem hanc nihil esse aliud quam vinculum a lege injectum; quo & mater & infans certo tempore primum ab hominum contactu, deinde a publicis coetibus arcebantur. A conta- ctu quidem infans ad diem usque octavum: mater itidem si marem peperisset: sin foeminam ad diem decimum quar- tum: a publicis autem coetibus, mater ad diem a partu qua- dragesimum si marem peperisset; si foeminam, ad septuage- simum quartum: infans vero si a matre sepositus esset, ad mensem exactum: sin cum matre esset, ad idem tempus cum matre, quia tunc particeps censebatur maternae impu- ritatis, ut recte ex collatione legum quae in Levitico & Nu- meris exstant, a quibusdam observatum est. Putant qui- dam hanc impuritatem legalem testimonium fuisse vitiosi- tatis ejus quae hominibus agnascitur quam יצר הרע He- braei vocant, ad quam & illud Philonis pertinere videtur cum ait: ὅτι παντὶ γεννητῷ, κἂν σπυδαῖον ἦ παρ᾽ ὅσον ἦλθεν εἰς γένεσιν συμφυὲς τὸ ἁμάρτανειν ἐστι: cui simile illud apud So- patrem Philosophum: σύμφυτον τὸ ἁμάρτανειν ἀνθρώποις: & apud Hieroclem: τί ἂν πρὸς τὴν λυγρὰν τάυτην νοσοπαθον ἅμα καὶ σύμφυλον ἔριν λεγομένην ἐξευρήσομεν τὴν ἐκ τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν παρὰ φύσιν διατεθέντων ἐγειρομένην, κὰι διὰ τοῦτο ὡς οἰκεῖον κα- κὸν λεληθότως βλάπτειν ἐοικυῖαν; Celsus, πέφυκε τὸ ἀνθρώπων νοι φῦλον ἁμαρτάνειν. Pythagorici, ut apud Jamblichum vi- dere est, principium hoc vocant τὸ παραπεφυκὸς ἡμῖν ἀπὸ τῆς γενέσεως αἰλότριον ζῶον & πολυκέφαλον θηρίον & θνητόν τι ζωῇς ἔνδυμα. Aristoteli vocatur τι πεφυκὸς ἀντιβαῖνον τῷ λόγῳ. Arnobius dixit vitium infirmitatis ingenitae: sed eam causam si lex respiceret, non erat cur in femini sexus partu tempo- ra duplicarentur: cujus nulla afferri ratio probabilis potest, nisi quod quae foeminas pariunt diutius solent profluvio la- borare: cujus contactus quia erat noxius, ideo publicis coe- tibus mulier arcebatur. Obstare huic sententiae putabit ali- quis, quod puerpera cum lustratur offerre jubetur duas pe- cudes aut aves, alteram in holocaustum, alteram לחטאת περὶ ἁμαρτίας, ut habent LXX. Nam & Origenes eam vo- cem urget septimo adversus Celsum: οἱ δὲ προφῆται μυστικώ μενοι οἱ ϊι περὶ τῶν γενέσεως πραγμάτων σοφὸν, θυσίαν περὶ ἁ- μαρτίας λέγουσιν ἀναφέρεσθαι, κὰι περὶ τῶν ἀξιογεννημένων, ὡς οὐ κα- θαρῶν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας. Sed receptum est apud Hebraeos ut חטאת vocent etiam obligationem illam quae ex lege sine ulla hominis culpa contrahitur. Sic Nazaraeus, quem in- scium contigerit mortui corpus, itidem jubetur offerre in holocaustum & περὶ ἁμαρτίας addita causa מאשר חטא על הנפש ὅτι ἥμαρτε περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς, circa illud cadaver Num. VI. II. id est, reus est tacti cadaveris, quemadmodum Latini dicunt voti reum. Sic & aqua lustralis quae hominem re- debat coetibus, vocatur aqua חטאת i. e. peccati, Num. 19. Et quod offerebatur a scabiosis, ab his qui erant γονοῥῥυεῖς, a foemina quae mensium profluvium erat passa, dicitur περὶ ἁμαρτίας, Levit. 16, 19. c. 15, 15. 30. Quomodo exponi potest id quod quibusdam videtur dicere Scriptor ad Hebraeos Dominum nostrum obtulisse etiam περὶ ἰδιῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, ut ἁμαρτιῶν nomine intelligatur neque vitium neque vitiositas ulla, ut quae ab ipso longissime abfuerint, sed conditio mor- talis corporis, quae a coelo ipsum arcebat, sicut immunditia legalis aliquem arcebat a templo. Confer locum ejusdem Epistolae cap. 5, 3. 7. Hoc est quod Paulus dicit ὁμοίωμα τῆς σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, Rom. 8, 3. Atque hunc in modum Hilarius, Oecumenius & alii interpretantur & illud Pauli Rom. 6, 10. ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ, id est corpore il- lo mortali quale est corpus peccato obnoxium: ut diximus ad Matth. 22, 51. Quod autem quidam disputant lege quae de purificatione est apud Mosem prodita ad Mariam non pertinuisse, quia lex de eis tantum agat quae ex virili satu concipium,pugnat,ni fallor,cum Lucæ verbis neq; probari potest è Mose. Nam תוריע quod LXX. vertunt σπερμα- τίση nōn est passivum, sed activum, & quasi dicas cum pro- lem genuerit : quod dictum generale deinde in duas species ἀῥῥενοτοκίας καὶ θηλυτοκίας distribuitur,ut apud Hebræos fie- ri solet. Eadem vox est Gen. I. 11. עשׁב מזריע זרע ubi LXX. σπεῖρον σπέρμα, Aquila σπερματίζον.

Retinemus merito lectionem in Codicibus Græcis pene omnibus repertam : quam temere lo- co movit Beza, reprobatque Casaubonus : Non au- tem ad ejusmodi legalem solum impuritatem re- spexit Lex Mosaica Lev. XII.6. Sed imprimis ad originale peccatum, cujus vitiositatis congenitæ te- stimonium erat illa impuritas legalis: unde v. 2. di- citur: Mulier cum fœminificaverit, vel ex semine virili conceperit & pepererit : quod quum non fiat sine peccato Job. XIV. 4. Ps.LI. 5. ecquis mali istius nobis cognati nullum in mente summi Legislato- ris sanctissima respectum fuisse credet? Adde quod inter columbas offerendas una לחטאת ad oblatio- nem pro peccato offerri debuerit, v. 8. quod urget Origenes VII. advers. Celsum : quodque ideo mater pariens filiam diutius immunda habita sit, quam quæ filium peperit, quia peccatum per mulierem inductum est.

Nequicquam vero Grotius obvertit receptum apud Ebræos esse, ut חטאת vocent etiam obliga- tionem illam, quæ ex lege sine ulla hominis culpa con- trahitur: uti cum Nazaræus inscius contigerit mor- tui corpus Num.VI. 11. & cum aqua lustralis,quæ ho- minem reddebat cœtibus,vocatur aqua חטאת id est, peccati Num. XIX. & quod offerebatur à scabiosis, ab his qui erant γονοῥῥυεῖς, à fæmina quæ mensium pro- fluvium erat passa, Lev. XIV.19. XV.15.30. Resp. vo- cem חטאת omnino peccatum respicere, si non semper proxime,remote tamen: nec vero peccata tantum esse in judicio Dei voluntariam transgres- sionem legis,sed quamvis ἀνομίαν, etiam involun- tariam, etiā legis ceremonialis,non moralis tantū.

Perperam vero,nec nisi sensu hæretico huc cum Socinistis trahit Grotius locum Ebr. V.3.7. ac si di- caturDominum nostrum obtulisse etiam περὶ ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν, eorumq; nomine intelligatur conditio mortalis, quæ à cælo ipsum arcuerit, sicut immundi- tia legalis aliquem arcuit à templo. Nam de Sacer- dotibus quidem Vet.Test.dicitur,quod pro pecca- tis propriis obtulerint: non autem id applicatur ad archetypum: dum in quibusdam solum, quæ ad propriam figuræ & adumbrationis rationem fa- ciunt,conveniant, Neq; uspiam vel conditio morta- litatis ἁμαρτίας nomine venit in Scripturis, vel Christo talis conditio tribuitur, quæ ipsum excluse- rit à cœlo, sicut immunditia legalis à templo Judæos quondam exclusit: quia Christum,qui per naturam morti subjectus, vel obnoxius non magis fuit, aut principia corruptionis, vel mortalitatis in se ha- buit, quam primus Adam in statu integritatis ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ conditus,ἐξυσίας sponte, & ultro mor- tem subiisse, & ἀυτεξυσίως animam suam posuisse pro nobis, certum est: & quum in forma Dei, ad- eoque in cœlo fuerit,& cœlesti gloria frui potue- rit, propter nos se exinanivisse, ac formam servi assumsisse, è Phil. II.6. constat: unde non conditione mortalis corporis arcebatur à cœlo, sed non nisi li- bera & voluntaria corporis sui natura morti non obnoxii pro peccatis nostris oblatione, & vitæ suæ in pretium redemptionis traditione, intrare in gloriam cœlestem voluit Luc.XXIV. 25. Job.X. 17.18. qui ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῶ χαρᾶς,ὑπέ- μεινε σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τῦ θρόνυ τῦ Θεῦ ἐκάθισεν Ebr. XII. 2.

Nec verò Rom. VIII. 3. per ὁμοίωμα τῆ σαρκὸς ἁ- μαρτίας conditio mortalis corporis, sed similitudo aliarum affectionum cum carne nostra peccato obno- xia indigitatur: quales sunt: famem & sitim pati, delassari, lacrymari, contristari, & similes, peccati tamen expertes, & innoxiæ conditiones. Et expli- cat illam loquutionem Grotius ipse aliter in annot. ad Rom. VIII. 3. ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, id est, ut tractaretur sic, quomodo nocentes tractari so- lent, Es. LIII. 12. Marc. XV. 28. Phil. II. 8. Morbis enim & morti, ac corruptioni obnoxium natura fuisse corpus Christi minime admittendum.

Locus vero ille Rom. VI. 10. ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανε τῇ ἁ- μαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ non id sibi vult, quod τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, id est, corpore mortali, quale est cor- pus periculo obnoxium, mortuus sit: sed quod so- nat litera, quod PECCATO sit mortuus, id est, pro- pter peccatum, ut in Socinismo profligato docui- mus, non proprium, sed nostrum, quod Grotius i- pse agnovit in defens. fid. Cathol. de satisfact. Chri- sti: neque se probavit Grotio illa de corpore mor- tali per ἁμαρτίαν designato glossa in sede propria annot. ad Rom. VI, 10. ubi de pœnis peccatorum exposuit, & sententiam Apostoli ita reddidit: Chri- stus semel defunctus est malis illis, quæ ob peccata no- stra sustinebat.

Cæterum agnoscit tamen Grotius hic, non ne- gat peccatum originis, & vitiositatem eam, quæ ho- minibus agnoscitur, quam יצר הרע Hebræis dici no- tat, & ad quam refert illud Philonis, ὅτι παντὶ γεν- νητῷ, κἂν σπουδαῖον ᾖ παρ᾽ ὅσον ἦλθεν εἰς γένεσιν συμφυὲς τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐστιν: quæ vero uti ignota prorsus fuit Philosophis, ita temere probatur è Sopatre, Hierocle, Jamblicho, Aristotele, utut analo- ga nonnulla apud ipsos occurrant, quum omni ra- tioni humanæ absconditum sit, nec nisi divina con- stet revelatione peccatum originis.

Si autem quæratur, quomodo & de Maria & de Christo, pronomine plurali αὐτῶν καθαρισμὸν ef- feratur, si non Levitica impuritas respiciatur, sed verum peccatum, quum nec Maria peccato con- taminata fuerit per conceptionem aut partum θε- ανθρωπου, nec fœtui huic sanctissimo vitiositas illa tribui possit? Resp. Uti circumcisioni, ita & pu- rificationi, ac præsentationi in templo sese subjicere voluit Immanuel, non sui, sed nostri causa, non ex necessitate, sed οἰκονομίας & ταπεινώσεως libertate, non ut legi per se obnoxius, sed ut eidem pro nobis sponte subjectus, non quod peccati ullius reatu urgeretur, sed quod nostri peccati reus ceu Me- diator & Vas noster ultronea in se derivatione in judicio divino haberetur, omnemque justitiam loco nostri implere voluerit: quemadmodum et- iam peccatum pro nobis fieri dignatus est, etsi pec- catum non nosset 2. Cor. V. 21. & mortem subiit propter peccatum nostrum, quum ipse liber à pec- cato, immunis à morte esset. Christus igitur huic legi se subjecit, ut ostenderet figuras legis in se im- pleri: utpote qui per semetipsum facturus esset pu- rificationem peccatorum nostrorum Ebr. I. 3. h. e. se esse verum illum agniculum, cujus holocausto ex- pietur immundities puerperæ, & infantis, cujus fi- gura erat illa Levitica purificatio, ut hic B. Chemni- tius: qui pie censet, hanc fuisse causam, cur non agnum, quem ditati muneribus a Magis oblatis faci- le comparare potuissent Parentes Domini, sed par columbarum obtulerint: Quia enim verus agnus aderat, typicum non obtulerunt.

Ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς ἱεροσόλυμα] Simul duabus legibus de- functuri, una quæ erat de purificatione puerperæ, altera quæ erat de redemptione primogeniti: quæ intra mensem fieri non poterat: post mensem poterat. Existimo autem hæc quæ sequuntur in parte aliqua Templi gesta paucis consciis, iisque fidis: ac ob id horum famam ad Herodem non pervenisse.

Videtur etiam iis subseribendum esse, qui nocte purificationem sequente angelum Josepho apparuisse, cum in itinere esset ex Hierosolymis in Galilæam Nazarethum rediturus, & mandatum de fuga in Ægyptum dedisse statuunt. Non enim verisimile est ex Nazareth iterum per totam Judæam, ipsam- que Hierosolymam, ubi agebat Herodes, transi- visse Josephum, quum manibus Herodis puerum subducere vellet, fugæque demandatæ in Ægy- ptum se committeret. Conf. Harmon. B. Chemni- tii c. X. ubi probat, Magorum adventum ante dies purificationis contigisse.

## 2:23
Vers. 23. διανοῖγον μήτραν) Thus the LXX speak, Num. 8:16, and Philo on the sacrifice of Cain and Abel: and in the book on the honors of the Priests in the law of Exodus, from which these words are taken, not κατὰ πόδας but κατὰ διάνοιαν, the Greeks have it thus: 'Sanctify to me every firstborn, first-begotten, and opening every womb among the sons of Israel, from man to beast, because it is mine.' But just as a womb is called closed by the Hebrews if it is sterile, so it is called opened if it gives proof of its fertility. It formerly pertained to the firstborn to perform the sacred rites: the Levites were substituted in their place: yet a trace of the old law remained in that the firstborn males had to be presented in the temple and redeemed with five shekels. Luke said nothing about this money with which the infant was redeemed, because there was nothing remarkable in it, since the same amount was commanded for both the rich and the poor. For, says Philo, 'since the birth of children is accustomed to happen equally to the most brilliant and to the most obscure, he deemed it right to legislate an equal contribution.' Similar is the fact that the bodies of the rich and the poor were buried at equal expense. Thus the Hebrews taught that we are admonished by both birth and death of that equality which nature has established among men. Philo, allegorizing the law concerning the consecration of firstborn males, refers it to the most excellent actions of our soul to be dedicated to God, in the places already mentioned, and also in the book on the heir of divine things.

We approve the explanation of the Grotian phrase: just as a womb is called closed by the Hebrews if it is sterile, so it is said to be opened if it gives proof of its fertility. Hence, the discussion here as to whether Mary gave birth with a closed or an open womb is superfluous; for it cannot be taught from the allegation of the Mosaic passage that she gave birth with an open one. But that she gave birth with a closed womb, the ancients taught with great consensus. Ambrose Ep. XXCI. Nyssenus hom. de occurf. Dn. Leo serm. I. & II. de Nat. Dn. Fulgent. serm. de laud. Mar. Euseb. Emiss. hom. in Pl. 113, 1. Damasc. lib. IV. de Ort. Fid. c. 14. &c. But as for what Grotius thinks, that Jesus was redeemed with five shekels like other infants, although Luke has nothing about it because there was nothing remarkable in it, since the same amount was commanded for both the rich and the poor, he does not deserve assent in this: for from the silence of Luke it is rather gathered that the infant was indeed presented to the Lord, but no redemption was made: because this infant did not have to be redeemed like others (Num. 18:15), but to redeem the human race (Matt. 20:28), nor to be removed from the care of sacred things, which formerly pertained to the firstborn until the Levites were substituted in his place, but to be consecrated to the Lord to undertake this care throughout the whole Church, of which the Levites bore the type.

Latin:

Vers. 23. διανοῖγον μήτραν) Ita loquuntur LXX, Num. 8,16.& Philo de sacrificio Caini & Abelus: & libro de hono- ribus Sacerdotum in lege Exodi unde hæc verba depromta sunt non κατὰ πόδας sed κατὰ διάνοιαν, ita habent Græci: ἁ- γίασόν μοι πᾶν πρωτότοκον πρωτογενὲς κὶ ἀνοῖγον πᾶσαν μήτραν ἐν τοῖς ὑίοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπυ ἕως κτήνυς, ὅτι ἐμοί ἐστιν. Sicut autem clausus uterus dicitur Hebræis qui sterilis est, ita a- periri qui experimentum dat suæ fœcunditatis. Ad primo- genitos olim spectabat circa sacrorum: eorum in locum surrogati sunt Levitæ: mansit tamen veteris juris vestigium in eo quod sisti in templo mares primogeniti debuerint & quinque siclis redimi. De pecunia hac qua redimebatur in- fans, nihil dixit Lucas, quia nihil in eo erat insigne cum & divitibus & pauperibus tantundem esset imperatum. ἐπειδὴ γὰρ, inquit Philo, ἡ παίδων γένεσις ἐν ἴσῳ κί τοῖς λαμπροτάτοις κί τοῖς ἀφανεστάτοις εἴωθε συμβαίνᾳ, ἴσην ἐδικαίωσε κί τὴν εἰσφο- ρὰν νομοθετῆσαι. Simile est quod pari sumtu corpora divi- tum & pauperum sepeliebantur. Ita docebant Hebræi & nascendo & moriendo nos admoneri ejus quam natura in- ter homines constituit paritatis. Legem de consecratione marium primogenitorum Philo ἀλληγορῶν ad præstantissi- mas animi nostri actiones Deo dicandas refert, dictis jam locis, item libro de hærede rerum divinarum.

Probamus explicationem Phraseos Grotia- næ: sicut clausus uterus Ebræis dicitur qui sterilis est, ita aperiri dici, qui experimentum dat suæ fœ- cunditatis. Unde hic supervacanea est disputatio clausone utero, an aperto peperit Maria? non e- nim aperto peperisse ita ex allegationeMosaici lo- ci doceri poterit. Quam vero utero clauso peperisse magno consensu veteres docuere. Ambrosius Ep. XXCI. Nyssenus hom. de occurf. Dn. Leo serm. I. & II. de Nat. Dn. Fulgent. serm. de laud. Mar. Eu- se b. Emiss. hom. in Pl. 113, 1. Damasc. lib. IV. de Ort. Fid. c. 14. &c. Quod autem Grotius putat, Jesum more aliorum infantum quinque siclis redemptum fuisse, etsi Lucas de eo nihil habeat, quia nihil in eo insigne fuit, quum & divitibus & pauperibus tan- tundem imperatum esset, in eo assensum non me- retur: nam è silentio Lucæ potius colligitur, præ- sentatum quidem Domino fuisse infantem, nul- lam autem redemtionem factam: quia infans hic non redimi debuit more aliorum Num. XVIII. 15. sed redimere genus humanum, Matth. XX. 28. nec cura sacrorum eximi, quæ ad primogenitos o- lim spectabat, donec in eum locum Levitæ surro- gati sunt, sed Domino ad hanc curam per univer- sam Ecclesiam subeundam consecrari, cujus ty- pum Levitæ gesserunt.

## 2:24
Vers. 24. θυσίαν) The word θυσίας is taken here generally, for it includes both the burnt offering and the sin offering. Origen, in the place already mentioned, and others after him, thought this sacrifice was properly offered for the infant, misled by the words of the law poorly understood: 'And when the days of her purification for a son or for a daughter are fulfilled, she shall bring a yearling lamb,' and the rest. For he thought that 'for a son or for a daughter' referred to 'she shall bring,' when it refers to 'purification': so that the sense is: when the mother is to be purified from the birth of a male or female. There were indeed days appointed for the purification of the infant, but no sacrifice. For its impurity came from the mother.

Ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσὺς περιστερῶν) A manifest sign of poverty. For the law was that a lamb should be offered with a bird: but for those whose means did not allow it, it was permitted to fulfill it with two birds: from which it can be understood that not much gold was given by the Magi, indeed for the sake of showing honor, not for exercising liberality: as was their custom to approach their Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 24. θυσίαν) θυσίας vox hic generaliter sumitur, in- cludit enim & ὁλοκαύτωμα, & τὸ περὶ ἁμαρτίας. Hanc θυσίαν putavit Origenes, dicto jam loco, & post eum alii proprie oblatam pro infante, quem fefellerunt verba legis male ac- cepta: κό ὅταν ἀναπληρωθῶσιν αἱ ἡμέραι καθάρσεως ἀυτῆς ἐφ' ὑῷ ἢ ἐπὶ θυγατρὶ, προσοίσει ἀμνὸν ἐνιαύσιον & cætera. Puta- vit enim illud ἐφ' ὑῷ ἢ ἐπὶ θυγατρὶ referri ad προσοίσει cum referatur ad καθάρσεως: ut sensus sit: cum purificanda est mater à partu maris aut feminæ. Infantis purificationi e- rant quidem dies præstituti, sed nullum sacrificium. Ejus enim impuritas à matre veniebat.

Ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσὺς περιστερῶν) Manifestum in- dicium paupertatis. Nam lex erat ut agnus cum avicula offerretur: sed quorum res id non ferret, iis permissum de- fungi duabus aviculis: unde intelligi potest auri non mul- tum à Magis datum, quippe honoris habendi causa, non exercendæ liberalitatis: quomodo mos illis erat Reges su- os accedere.

## 2:25
Vers. 25. εὐλαβὴς) A word peculiar to Luke, who uses it twice besides, Acts 2:25 and ch. 8:2, in imitation of the Hebrews, by whom a religious man is called ירא, but usually with the name of God added, as in Is. 50:10. And thus the ancient Christians called bishops by a title almost peculiar to them, 'most religious.' When he said 'just and devout,' he encompassed all parts of duties. Thus above ch. 1:75, 'in holiness and righteousness.'

προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τῦ Ἰσραὴλ) Thus Mark said of Joseph of Arimathea, 'waiting for the kingdom of God,' from which we understand that by these words are especially indicated those spiritual benefits of the Messiah: although it is also credible that the restoration of the Republic was hoped for by them. So also below 38, 'waiting for the redemption in Jerusalem.'

But from where is that credible? Is it because the false opinion of the Jews concerning the bodily kingdom of the Messiah clung to some, that it must also be attributed to Simeon, in whom was the Holy Spirit, and to other believers? What kind of consolation and redemption they expected appears sufficiently from the Canticle of Zechariah (Luke 1:71, 74) and of Simeon (ch. 2:30): which has nothing in common with the restoration of the Jewish polity. I pass over the fact that this Simeon is believed to be the son of Hillel, whom they say was removed from his office with his parent, because he resisted the common opinion of the Jews concerning the bodily kingdom of the Messiah. Capellus notes that the phrase was familiar and very well known at that time, by which they signified the coming of the Messiah, to wait for the consolation of Jerusalem or Israel.

πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἧν ἐπ’ αὐτόν) Regarding this manner of speaking, see what was said above in ch. I. 35 & 66. Thus we pursue propriety; it seems that this Simeon did not indeed keep secret what he had seen: (for prophecy had long since ceased) but a divine inspiration: for this is what is distinctly called רוח הקדש by the Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 25. εὐλαβὴς) Vox Lucæ peculiaris, qui bis præterea usurpat, Act. II, 25. & c. VIII. 2. Hebræorum imitatione qui- bus religiosus dicitur ירא, sed plerumque addito Dei no- mine, ut Es. L. 10. Atque ita Christiani veteres Episcopos quasi peculiari titulo vocabant εὐσεβεστάτυς. Cum dixit δί- καιον & εὐσεβῆ omnes officiorum partes complexus est. I- ta supra c. 1. 75. ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ.

προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τῦ Ἰσραὴλ) Ita de Josepho Ari- mathensi Marcus dixit προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τῦ θεῦ, unde intelligimus his præcipue verbis indicari beneficia il- la Messiæ πνευματικά: quanquam & Reipublicæ restitutio- nem ab illis speratam credibile est. Sic & infra 38. προσδε- χομένοις λύτρωσιν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις.

Unde vero credibile id est? Num quod non- nullis hæserit opinio falsa Judæorum de corporali regno Messiæ, etiam Simeoni, in quo Spiritus sanct. erat, aliisque fidelibus eadem tribuenda? Qualem παράκλησιν, & λύτρωσιν illi expectarint e Canti- co Zachariæ Luc. I. 71. 74. & Simeonis cap. II. 30. sa- tis apparet: quæ nihil commercii habet cum poli- tiæ Judaicæ restitutione. Taceo quod Simeon iste Hillelis filius credatur, quem cum parente ab of- ficio suo remotum dicunt, ideo quod communi Judæorum opinioni de regno Messiæ corporali refragaretur. Capellus notat phrasin tum temporis familiarum & notissimam fuisse, qua adventum Messiæ significarint, expectare consolationem Jeru- salem vel Israelus.

πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἧν ἐπ’ αὐτόν) De hoc loquendi genere vide quæ dicta supra c. I. 35. & 66. Sic proprietatem sectamur, videtur hic Simeon non quidem clam habuisse visa: (ces- sabat enim pridem προφητεία) sed afflatus divinus: id e..im distincte רוח הקדש Hebræis dicitur.

## 2:26
Vers. 26. ὑπὸ τῦ πνεύματος) Not by an Angel nor by a voice which they call בת קול, but by inspiration.

μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον) Just as it is said to taste death, as in Matt. XVI. 28, so also to see death, as in Ps. LXXXIX. 49. For the names of the most familiar senses are adapted to the signification of any experience whatsoever.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ὑπὸ τῦ πνεύματος) Non per Angelum neque per vocem quam בת קול vocant, sed δι ἐπιπνοίας.

μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον) Sicut γεύεσθαι θανάτυ dicitur, ut Matth. XVI. 28. sic & ἰδεῖν θάνατον, ut Ps. LXXXIX. 49. Nomina enim notissimorum sensuum ad cujusvis experimenti signi- ficationem aptantur.

## 2:27
Vers. 27. ἐν τῷ πνεύματι) By the instigation of the spirit. So also below in IV. 13. See what is said regarding Matt. IV. 1.

τὺς γονεῖς) It is not surprising that Joseph is called by this name, since legal experts also hold that a mother-in-law and a stepmother take the place of mothers: and in Plautus there is the mother who gave the breast: and in Gen. XXXVII. 35 it appears that daughters-in-law are included under the name of daughters.

κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον) Namely, to present to the Lord as he said above, and to offer the redemption.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ἐν τῷ πνεύματι) Instigante spiritu. Sic & in- fra IV. 13. Vide quæ ad Matth. IV. 1.

τὺς γονεῖς) Non mirum est Josephum hoc nomine ap- pellari, cum etiam socrum & novercam jurisconsulti tra- dant esse matrum loco: & apud Plautum est mater quæ mamman dedit: & Gen, XXXVII. 35. filiarum nomine apparet nurus comprehendi.

κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον) Nempe παραστῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ ut supra dixit, & offerre τὴν λύτρωσιν.

## 2:29
V. 29 νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δῦλόν συ δέσποτα κατὰ τὸ ῥημά σε ἐν εἰρήνῃ] ἀπολύεις ἐν εἰρήνῃ, that is, you dismiss me happily. The present for the future. Pious men are said by the Hellenists to be dismissed when they die, as in Tobit III. 6, so the LXX in Num. 20 at the end, that Aaron was dismissed, and in Gen. XX. 2 Abraham says, I am being dismissed childless: where the Targum says I depart from the world, just as Festus also says that for the ancient Romans death was called a departure. Marcus Antoninus calls dying to be dismissed. Of the same kind is that, depart in peace; for he who dismisses is gracious, as we have noted elsewhere that Plutarch and Themistius speak. Moreover, in this manner of speaking there is a manifest profession of a hoped-for life hereafter: since the body is held to be a bond of the soul, whence the Greeks coined the word δέμας. That phrase, however, in peace, is used everywhere regarding a happy death, as in Gen. XV. 15, 2 Kings XXII. 20, Psalm IV. 9. Solent autem ita de se loqui, who have obtained the sight of the desired object, as if now nothing could be added to them for the happiness of life. Thus Jacob to his son Joseph in Gen. XLVI. 30, I shall die from now on since I have seen your face. Imitating which, the writer of Tobit makes the old man Tobit speak thus in ch. XI. 8, I have seen you, my child, from now on I shall die. In Papinius, an old nurse addresses the twins:

Until I restore you, fit and whole, to the bridal chambers: dismiss me, O Fates, weary of life.

In hac loquutione manifestam esse professionem speratæ vitæ alterius, Grotius rightly acknowledges, since the body is held to be a bond of the soul, whence the word δέμας, and death is a departure, and a certain setting forth. Compare Gen. XX. 2, Num. XX. 29, Tob. III. 6. That phrase, however, in peace, is used everywhere regarding a happy death, as in Gen. XV. 15, 2 Kings XXII. 20, Psalm IV. 9. Rashly, therefore, does Grotius elsewhere deny that in the Old Testament a promise of eternal life was made: because neither faith, nor hope, nor the profession of faith or hope exists without the Word of divine promise which is the sole foundation of faith and hope. Vers. 30. τὸ σωτήριόν σε) The LXX sometimes are accustomed to place σωτήριον where in the Hebrew there is ישועה, as Ps. 98, 3. εἶδοσαν πάντα τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς τὸ σωτήριον τῦ θεῦ ἡμῶν, and 1. Sam. 2, 1. Elsewhere they translate σωτηρίαν, as Gen. 49, 18. Es. 52, 10. where there is that same sentiment which is in the said Psalm: just as Luke also said above κέρας σωτηρίας. Therefore here the abstract is placed for the concrete, σωτήριον or σωτηρίαν αὐτῦ Τῦ σωτῆρος, just as we also say in Latin, you are my salvation. In Isaiah 46, 13. God speaking about the Messiah similarly says תשועתי my salvation, that is from me, and in the same chapter 49, 6. ישועתי in the same sense. Vers. 31. ὅ ἡτοίμασας) You have prepared, that you might show, clearly. Thus Peter said σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι 1. Ep. I. 5. κατὰ πρόσωπον) In the sight of.

Grotius acknowledges that the Hebrew ישועה and the LXX interpreters' τὸ σωτήριον Ps. 98, 3. and σωτηρίαν Gen. 49, 18. Es. 52, 10. are placed for the concrete τῦ σωτῆρος, nor does he doubt that in Es. 46, 13. and c. 49, 6. God is speaking about the Messiah, תשועתי my salvation, that is, from me. Why therefore did he twist those passages elsewhere in his annotations on the Old Testament? See what he has at verse 32, with which compare, if you please, our Anti-Grotian notes on Isaiah at the cited place.

Latin:

V. 29 νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δῦλόν συ δέσποτα κατὰ τὸ ῥημά σε ἐν εἰρήνῃ] ἀπολύεις ἐν εἰρήνῃ, id est, feliciter me dimittis. Præ- sens pro futuro. ἀπολύες Hellenistis dicuntur pii cum mo- riuntur, ut Tobiæ III. 6. ita LXX. Num. 20. in fine ὅτι ἀπελύ- θη ᾿Ααρὼν, & Gen. XX. 2. Abraham ait, ἐγὼ ἀπολύομαι ἔτερ- κνῶ: ubi Targum אזל מן עלמא abeo ex hoc mundo, quomodo & Festus ait Romanis antiquis mortem dictam abitionem. Marcus Antoninus mori vocat ἀπολελύσθαι. Ejusdem est illud ἄπιθι ἐν ἵλεως· ὁ γὰρ ὁ ἀπολύων ἵλεως quo- modo & Plutarchum & Themistium loqui alibi notavimus. Est autem in hoc loquendi genere manifesta professio spe- ratæ vitæ alterius: cum corpus habeatur pro animi vincu- lo, unde dictum δέμας volunt Græci. Illud autem ἐν εἰρήνῃ de felici morte passim usurpatur, ut Gen. XV. 15. 2. Reg. XXII. 20. Psal. IV. 9. Solent autem ita de se loqui, qui rei o- ptatæ conspectum sunt adepti, quasi jam nihil possit illis ad felicitatem vitæ accedere. Ita Iacobus ad Josephum filium Gen. XLVI. 30. ἀποθανῦμαι ἀπὸ τῦ νῦν ἐπεὶ ἑώρακα τὸ πρόσ- ωπόν συ. Quod imitatus Scriptor Tobiæ, Tobiam senem ita loqui facit c. XI. 8. ἷδόν σε παιδίον ἀπὸ τῦ νῦν ἀποθανῦμαι. Apud Papinium senex altor gemellom alloquitur:

Donec te thalamis habilem intagramq; resignem: Hoc fatis & fessum vita dimittite Parcæ.

In hac loquutione manifestam esse professionem speratæ vitæ alterius, recte agnoscit Grotius, cţm corpus habeatur pro animæ vinculo, unde dictum δέμας, & mors abitio, ac profectio quædam sit. Conf. Gen. XX. 2. Num. XX. 29. Tob. III. 6. illud autem ἐν εἰρήνῃ de felici morte passim usurpetur, ut Gen. XV. 15. 2. Reg. XXII. 20. Psal. IV. 9. Temere ergo alias negat Grotius, in V. Test. promissionem vitæ æternæ factam esse: quia nec fides, nec spes, nec professio fidei, aut spei sine Verbo promissionis divinæ locum habet: quod unicum fidei, & spei fundamentum est. Vers. 30. τὸ σωτήριόν σε) σωτήριον solent interdum ponere LXX. ubi in Hebræo est ישועה, ut Ps. 98, 3. εἶδοσαν πάντα τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς τὸ σωτήριον τῦ θεῦ ἡμῶν, & 1. Sam. 2, 1. Alibi ver- tunt σωτηρίαν, ut Gen. 49, 18. Es. 52, 10. ubi eadem illa quæ in dicto Psalmo sententia est: ut & Lucas supra dixit κέρας σω- τηρίας. Est ergo hic abstractum pro concreto positum, σωτή- ριον sive σωτηρίαν αὐτῦ Τῦ σωτῆρος, sicut & Latine dicimus, tu mea es salus. Apud Esaiam 46, 13. Deus loquens de Mes- sia similiter ait תשועתי salus mea, id est à me, & apud eundem cap. 49, 6. ישועתי sensu eodem. Vers. 31. ὅ ἡτοίμασας) Parasti, ut ostenderes scilicet. Ita σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι dixit Petrus 1. Ep. I. 5. κατὰ πρόσωπον) In conspectu.

Agnoscit Grotius, Ebræum ישועה & LXX. Inter- pretum τὸ σωτήριον Ps. 98, 3. & σωτηρίαν Gen. 49, 18. Es. 52, 10. pro concreto τῦ σωτῆρος poni, neq; dubitat Es. 46, 13. & c. 49, 6. Deum de Messia lo- qui, תשועתי salus mea, id est, à me. Cur itaque alio detorsit illa loca in annotatis ad Vet. Testamentum? Vide quæ habet ad vers. 32. cum quibus confer, si lubet, nostra Anti-Grotiana ad Esaiam loc. citatis.

## 2:32
Vers. 32. φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν) From two prophecies, of which one is at the said place of Isaiah 49, 6. δέδωκά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν. Which passage most openly shows that the benefits of the Messiah were to reach not only to the Israelites, but also to other nations. The other is at the said Ps. 98, 3. ἐνώπιον ῷ ἐθνῶν ἀπεκάλυψε τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἀυτῦ. Moreover, having compared these passages, this seems to be the construction of Luke's words: by a transposition which is most common in Luke. φῶς ἐθνῶν εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν, namely τῆς δικαιοσύνης θεῦ. For as Paul says δικαιοσύνη θεῦ ἐν χρισῳ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, Rom. 1. 17. Although I do not deny that ἀποκάλυψιν can be understood as the very power of seeing which is given to the nations through this light. For thus גלה in Hebrew, in Greek ἀποκάλυψιν, is found to be used in Psalm 119, 18. And Irenaeus thus accepts this passage κατ’ ἔκθεσιν for the revelation of the eyes of the Gentiles.

κὴ δόξαν λαῦ σε Ἰσραὴλ] From Isaiah at the said place 46, 13. הפארתי לישראל τῷ Ἰσραὴλ δόξασμα. Paul to the Rom. 9, 4. Ἰσραηλῖται ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία κὴ ἡ δόξα. The Messiah is the glory of Israel, because he was born from the Israelites, lived among them, and called the nations to the religion of Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 32. φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν) Ex duobus vaticiniis quorum alterum est dicto Esaiæ loco 49, 6. δέδωκά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν. Qui locus apertissime ostendit Messiæ beneficia, non ad Israelitas tantum, sed & ad gentes alias perventura. Alte- rum dicto Psal. 98, 3. ἐνώπιον ῷ ἐθνῶν ἀπεκάλυψε τὴν δικαιο- σύνην ἀυτῦ. Videtur autem collatis his locis hæc esse con- structio Lucæ verborum : per trajectionem quæ Lucæ est u- sitatissima. φῶς ἐθνῶν εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν, scilicet τῆς δικαιοσύνης θεῦ. Nam ut Paulus ait δικαιοσύνη θεῦ ἐν χρισῳ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, Rom. 1. 17. Quanquam non nego ἀπο- κάλυψιν posse intelligi ipsam videndi potestatem quæ gen- tibus datur per hoc lumen. Nam ita גלה Hebraice, Græce ἀποκάλυψιν, usurpatum invenire est Psalmo 119, 18. Et Ire- næus sic accipit hunc locum κατ’ ἔκθεσιν ad revelationem o- culorum Gentium.

κὴ δόξαν λαῦ σε Ἰσραὴλ] Ex Esaia dicto loco 46, 13. הפארתי לישראל τῷ Ἰσραὴλ δόξασμα. Paulus ad Rom. 9, 4. Ἰσραηλῖται ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία κὴ ἡ δόξα. Messias gloria Israelis, quia ex Israelitis natus, inter ipsos vixit, & gentes vocavit ad religionem Israelis.

## 2:33
V. 33. θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλημένοις περὶ αὐτῦ) λαλεμένοις is to be taken without a definition of time, so that those things which were said by the Angel as well as those which were said by Elizabeth, Zechariah, and Simeon may be understood.

Latin:

V. 33. θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλημένοις περὶ αὐτῦ) λαλε- μένοις sumendum sine temporis definitione, ut intelligantur tam quæ ab Angelo erant dicta quam quæ ab Elisabetha, Zacharia, Simone.

## 2:34
Vers. 34. ἐυλόγησεν αὐτὸς) He blessed Joseph and Mary, whose mention preceded, he followed with all good things. πρὸς Μαριάμ) Taught by the instinct of the Spirit that she was a mother without a father, when otherwise the parts of a father ought to have been prior. κεῖται) I accede to those who think that not a mere event, but also the counsel of God is signified. For κεῖται is τίθεται, the active of which verb Paul and Peter use in the cited passages for the following words. But as the decrees of God are various, so the use of this word κεῖται is to be distinguished. Paul uses it concerning the calling to the promulgation of the Gospel Phil. I. 17. concerning the calling of Christians to the patience of evils 1. Thess. 3, 3. concerning the principal intention of God in the giving of the carnal law through Moses 1. Tim. 1. 9. But since Simeon said above, for all peoples, and therefore for all men, who are contained in all peoples, that this salvation is proposed by divine counsel, the thing itself leads us entirely to distinguish diligently the divine decrees. For God wills some things primarily, others however consequently, or as the most ancient of the Christians speak, by way of following or by way of circumstance: which some also call secondarily. If men are looked at nakedly, God undoubtedly desires the salvation of all seriously. But at the same time, with circumstances assumed, such as that some fall through ignorance of the truth and a certain common weakness, others however through a certain contempt of divine things: which they either hold in no place, or certainly postpone to honors, riches, and the advantages of this world, while in the meantime they are the greatest pretenders of piety: God wills the inner intentions of both these and those to be directed, which indeed he effected through the word of the Gospel.

εἰς πτῶσιν) This is what Isaiah had said about the Messiah, with Paul interpreting Rom. 9, 33. and Peter 1. Ep. 2, 8. that he would be for both houses of Israel, as much for the Palestinians as for those in the dispersion, but especially for the Jerusalemites לצור מכשול πέτραν σκανδάλυ, not indeed for all, but as Peter speaks for those who stumble at the word 1. Petr. 2, 8. It is the same as what the Lord says in John, that he came so that those seeing might become blind 9, 39. i.e. so that those who had previously received much light, but had loved the works of darkness, might show in reality that they were light-shunners and dark-dwellers, which was not equally evident before. For with the heavenly doctrine laid open without wrappings with such efficacy of miracles, but in such a way that it drew many inconveniences with it, the mask of holiness was taken away from those men. For nothing could be pleaded why they did not receive the doctrine of Christ except the mind of the flesh. Thus therefore the Gospel is, for those who are perishing, that is, for those who can truly be said to seek destruction ὀσ μὴ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον 2. Cor. II, 16. Moreover, they are said to fall because they were standing before, that is, they were judged pious. A similar opposition is in Paul, let him who thinks he stands see that he does not fall 1. Cor. X. 12.

τῇ ἀνάστασιν) of those who are being saved, as Paul speaks in the said passage to the Corinthians. Christ in John: so that those who do not see, may see: that is, so that those whom ignorance of good things had hindered in their mind, that impediment being removed, they might willingly embrace the truth joined with trouble. These are said to rise because they were as if lying in the mud of ignorance.

To be observed here above all is the confession of Grotius, that in Is. 8, 14. a prophecy is held concerning the Messiah, from the infallible interpretation of Paul, and Peter, and that the times of the New Testament are looked to. What then, was he snatched away by a spirit of error and dizziness when he was writing his annotations on the Old Testament, so that he interprets this prophecy far otherwise, and openly departs from the explanation handed down by the Holy Spirit in the New Testament? See what is said there, and what is opposed to it.

εἰς ζημεῖον) This word is variously explained. I do not doubt that the passage of Isaiah is being referred to, where he says that he and his children were appointed לאתות ולמופתים c. 8, 18. Σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, as the LXX have it. Which the writer to the Hebrews shows ought to be referred to Christ and Christ's disciples διὰ τύπυ, c. II. 13. Similar is what Ezekiel says, that he would be למופת εἰς τέρας. The sense of Simeon's words is that Christ would be conspicuous to the whole world both by the holiness of his life and by his prodigious works.

ἀντιλεγόμενον) Simeon wonderfully compares the abundance of grace with the outcome. He had said that Jesus would be σωτήριον ἐνώπιον πάντων τῶν λαῶν: but he added that he would be εἰς πτῶσιν πολλῶν. But he says that he would be a sign, but one that is spoken against, that is, that many would oppose the manifest truth, ἀντιλογία corresponding to the Hebrew ריב, which is translated both as contradiction and strife, and indeed properly signifies calumnies, but in such a way that it often includes the deeds accompanying the calumny. The writer to the Hebrews concerning Christ: ἀναλογίσασθαι γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτολῶν εἰς ἀυτὸν ἀντιλογίαν. Thus Ps. 18, 44. the LXX translate מריבי as contradictions. Similar is the fact that they use βλασφήμια not only of words, but also of deeds, as can be seen in 1 Macc. II. 6.

Grotius does not doubt that the passage of Isaiah c. 8, 18 is being referred to, but he wrongly thinks that the Prophet says that he and his children were appointed εἰς σημεῖα & τέρατα, which we are taught in Heb. II. 13 ought to be referred to Christ and Christ's disciples, not indeed διὰ τύπυ only, but according to the literal sense: for the preceding parts in the prophecy of Isaiah according to the letter do not treat of Isaiah, but of Christ, who alone is עמנואל: concerning whom Grotius himself has already acknowledged that it was treated in the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ἐυλόγησεν αὐτὸς) Josephum & Mariam quorum præcessit mentio, bonis omnibus prosecutus est. πρὸς Μαριάμ) Spiritus instinctu edoctus eam esse matrē sine patre, cum alioqui priores esse patris partes debuissent. κεῖται) Accedo iis qui putant non nudum eventum, sed & consilium Dei significari. Nam κεῖται est τίθεται, cujus verbi Activum Paulus & Petrus usurpant locis citandis ad verba sequentia. Sed ut varia sunt Dei decreta, ita vocis hujus κεῖ- ται usus est distinguendus. Paulus de vocatione ad promul- gationem Evangelii usurpat Phil. I. 17. de vocatione Chri- stianorum ad patientiam malorum 1. Thess. 3, 3. de præci- pua Dei intentione in ferēda lege carnali per Mosem 1. Tim. 1. 9. At cum supra dixerit Simeon, omnibg populis, ac pro- inde hominibus omnibg, qui in omnibg populis continen- tur, salutem hanc esse propositam divino consilio, omnino res ipsa eo nos ducit ut diligēter distinguamg divina decre- ta. Nam alia vult Deus προηγυμένως, alia vero ἑπομένως, sive ut vetustissimi Christianorum loquuntur ἐκ παρακολυθήσεως sive ἐκ περιστάσεως: quod & δεύτερως dicunt quidam. Nude si homines inspiciantur, haud dubie omnium salutem Deus serio desiderat. At simul assumtis circumstantiis, ut quod alii ignorantia veri & communi quadam imbecillitate labun- tur, alii vero contemtu quodam rerum divinarum: quas aut nullo habent loco, aut certe honoribus, divitiis atq; id geng commodis postponunt, cum interim pietatis oftentatores sint maximi: vult Deus & horum & illorum intima studia deregi, quod sane effecit per Evangelii sermonem.

εἰς πτῶσιν) Hoc est quod de Messia dixerat Esaias interpre- te Paulo Rom. 9, 33. & Petro 1. Ep. 2, 8. fore eum utrique do- mui Israel, tam Palæstinis quam τοῖς ἐν διασπορᾷ, præcipue vero Hierosolymitis לצור מכשול πέτραν σκανδάλυ, non omnibus quidem, sed ut Petrus loquitur τοῖς προσκόπτεσι τῷ λόγῳ I. Petr. 2, 8. Idem est quod apud Johannem dicit Do- minus venisse ut videntes cæci fierent 9, 39. i. e. ut qui pri- dem multum lucis acceperant, sed amaverant opera tene- brarum, reipsa ostenderent se esse lucifugas & tenebriones, quod ante non æque constabat. Nam patefacta doctrina cœlesti sine involucris tanta cum efficacia miraculorū, sed ita ut secum traheret multa incommoda, detracta est illis hominibg' sanctimoniae persona, Nihil enim causari poterat cur Christi doctrinam non reciperent nisi τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκός. Sic igitur Evangelium est, τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις id est his qui vere dici possunt exitium quaerere ὀσ μὴ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον 2. Cor. II, 16. Dicuntur autem illi cadere quia antea sta- bant, id est, pii judicabantur. Similis oppositio apud Pau- lum ὁ δοκῶν ἐστάναι βλεπέτω μὴ πέσῃ 1. Cor. X. 12.

τῇ ἀνάστασιν) τῶν ζωζομένων ut dicto ad Corinthios loco Paulus loquitur. Christus apud Iohannem: ut qui non vi- dent, videant: id est, ut quibus ignorantia rerum bonarum animum impedierat, eo impedimento remoto verum cum molestia conjunctum libenter amplecterentur. Hi surgere dicuntur quia velut jacebant in ignorantiae luto.

Observanda hic imprimis confessio Grotii, quod Es. 8, 14. vaticinium habeatur de Messia, ex infallibili interpretatione Pauli, & Petri, & tem- pora N. Test. respiciantur. Quod ergo erroris ac vertiginis spiritu abreptus fuit, cum annot. ad V. T. conscriberet, ut hoc vaticinium longe aliter in- terpretatur, & ab explicatione Spiritus S. in N.T. tradita palam discederet? Vid. quae illic dicta, ei- que opposita sunt.

εἰς ζημεῖον) Varie exponitur haec vox. Ego non dubito re- spici Esaiae locum, ubi is se & liberos suos dicit constitutos לאתות ולמופתים c. 8, 18. Σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, ut habent LXX. quod Scriptor ad Hebraeos ostendit ad Christum & Christi discipulos διὰ τύπυ referri debere, c. II. 13. Simile est quod Ezechiel dicit se futurum למופת εἰς τέρας. Sensg ver- borum Simeonis est, Christum & vitae sanctimonia admi- rabili & prodigiosis operibus toti mundo conspicuum fore.

ἀντιλεγόμενον) Mire Simeon gratiae ubertatem cum even- tu comparat. Dixerat fore Jesum σωτήριον ἐνώπιον πάντων τῶν λαῶν: sed addidit fore εἰς πτῶσιν πολλῶν. Sed dicit eum fore σημῖον, sed ἀντιλεγόμενον, id est, quamvis perspicuae ve- ritati multos adversaturos ἀντιλογία respondens ריב He- braeo, quod & ἀντιλογία & μάχη vertitur, proprie quidem calumnias significat, sed ita ut & facta calumniam comitan- tia saepe includat. Scriptor ad Hebraeos de Christo: ἀναλο- γίσασθαι γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτολῶν εἰς ἀυτὸν ἀντιλογίαν. Sic Psal. 18, 44. מריבי ἀντιλογίων ver- tunt LXX. Simile est quod βλασφήμια non de dictis tantum, sed & de factis usurpant, ut videre est 1. Macc. II. 6.

Non dubitat Grotius respici Esaiae locum c. 8, 18. sed perperam putat Prophetam se, & liberos suos dici constitutos εἰς σημεῖα & τέρατα, quod Ebr. II. 13. docemur ad Christum & Christi discipulos referri debere, non sane διὰ τύπυ tantum, sed se- cundum sensum literalem: nam antecedentia in va- ticinio Esaiae secundum literam non de Esaia, sed de Christo, qui solus עמנואל est, agunt: de quo Gro- tius ipse jam agnovit, ibidem actum esse.

## 2:35
Vers. 35. καὶ (καὶ σοῦ δὲ ἀυτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία) He spoke with a conjunction in the Hebrew manner, which otherwise we would say so that a sword shall pierce even your own soul: provided that what follows clearly coheres again with those things which had preceded. The Hebrews often use the word for sword when it is a matter of calumny: Ps. LV, 22, where in the Greek καὶ ἀυτοὶ (οἱ λόγοι) εἰσὶ βολίδες. But Ps. LVII. 6. καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα ἀυτῶν μάχαιρα ὀξεῖα. An old Greek poet: Ξίφει τιτρώσκ' σῶμα, τὸ δὲ νῦν λόγῳ. Nor do I doubt that this proverb was common among the Hebrews, concerning a sword piercing the soul, whenever it was a matter of atrocious calumny. For in Ps. 105, where it treats of Joseph, when mention had been made of his bonds, the Psalmist adds ברזל באה נפשו, the sense of which passage, although the Greeks explain it otherwise, seems entirely to be that by calumny (namely, the false accusation of adultery) a most grievous pain was added to his soul in addition to all the vexations of his body, no differently than if he were pierced through with the sharpest iron. But what was said of Joseph pertained to Christ himself διὰ τύπυ; Simeon rightly transferred it to the mother, as one who was about to perceive no less pain from the most atrocious calumnies against her son than the son himself. The romphaea of the Thracians, like the framea of the Germans, is a type of shorter spear, suitable for the use that a sword provides. And so the LXX and other interpreters express with that Greek word the Hebrew words that signify both a spear and a sword.

ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶζιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν οἱ διαλογισμοὶ) Thus Paul said φανερῶζαι τὰς βυλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν 1 Cor. 4, 5. But there it seems to be a matter of the judgment after this life: here of those judgments which God exercises through the Gospel even in this age. Thus the writer to the Hebrews calls the Gospel λόγον κριτικὸν ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας. This power of the Gospel is often so exerted that it appears even to men, who look into the matter a little more attentively.

Latin:

Vers. 35. καὶ (ζὲ δὲ ἀυτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία) Cum copula dixit more Hebraeo, quod alioqui diceremus adeo ut tuum quog animum gladius sit transitur: usnam quae sequuntur manifeste iterum cohaerent cum his quae praeces- ferant. Gladii vocem saepe usurpant Hebraei, ubi de calu- mnia agitur: Psal. LV, 22. ubi in Graeco καὶ ἀυτοὶ (οἱ λόγοι) εἰσὶ βολίδες. Pl. autem LVII. 6. καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα ἀυτῶν μάχαιρα ὀξεῖα. Graecus poëta vetus: Ξίφει τιτρώσκ' (ῶμα, τὸ δὲ νῦν λόγῳ. Neque dubito, quin proverbium hoc apud Hebraeos fuerit usitatum, de gladio animum transeunte, quoties de atroci calumnia agebatur. Nam in Ps. 105. ubi de Iosepho agitur, cum vinculorum ejus facta esset mentio, adjicit Psalmogra- phus ברזל באה נפשו cujus loci sensus, quanquam aliter exponentibus Graecis, omnino esse videtur calumniam (fal- sam nempe adulterii accusationem) ad omnes corporis ve- xationes gravissimum dolorem animo ipsius accessisse, non aliter quam si ille acutissimo ferro transadigeretur. Quod autem de Iosepho dictum, ad ipsum Christum διὰ τύπυ per- tinebat, recte Simeon ad matrem transtulit, ut quae atrocis- simis in filium calumniis non minus doloris erat perceptu- ra, quam filius ipse. Romphaea Thracum, ut Germano- rum framea, est hastae brevioris genus, habilis ad usum quem gladius praebet. Itaque Hebraeas voces tam quae ha- stam quam quae gladium significant illa voce Graeca expri- munt LXX. & alii interpretes.

ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶζιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν οἱ διαλογισμοὶ) Sic φανερῶζαι τὰς βυλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν dixit Paulus 1 Cor. 4, 5. Sed ibi de judicio post hanc vitam agi videtur: hic de illis ju- diciis quae per Evangelium Deus exercet in hoc etiam secu- lo. Sic ad Hebraeos Scriptor Evangelium vocat λόγον κρίτι- κὸν ἐνθυμήσεων κὴ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας. Haec Evangelii vis saepe ita exseritur, ut etiam hominibus, paulo attentius rem intro- spectantibus, appareat.

## 2:36
V. 36. daughter of Phanuel) This is not added in vain. For the time had come that the mystery which lay hidden under this name should be fulfilled, Gen. 32, 30. Thus in the name of Anna there is a signification of thanks, in Aser of blessedness.

If the mystery concerning Christ lay hidden under the word פנואל in Gen. XXXII. 30, which is to be fulfilled in the time of the N.T., why then did Grotius prefer to explain the man who wrestled there as an Angel, rather than as the Son of God? See what we have said on that passage.

prophetess) Taken in this broader sense, women are so called who were sometimes visited by the Holy Spirit. Others had formerly been prophetesses by ordinary office, like Deborah, which kind of prophetess in either sex was ceasing at that time.

from her virginity) It is a great praise of a woman among almost all nations not to repeat marriages. Tacitus on the women of the Germans: Thus they receive one husband just as they receive one body and one life: so that there is no thought beyond, no longer desire, so that they may love not as a husband but as a marriage. It should be read, so that they may love not as a husband but as a marriage. Therefore they abstain, he says, from second marriages, lest they seem to have loved the marriage, not him to whom they were married. Tertullian in two books on this matter recites the privileges of those who have had one husband among the Romans and other nations. But also by Roman laws many things were established to restrain the license of such marriages. When the ancient Christians could not show that the repetition of marriage was prohibited by any edict of Christ, they nevertheless dissuaded it by all means: so that presbyters would not even be present at the celebration of repeated marriages, lest by their presence they might seem to approve of a thing that was indeed permitted but less praiseworthy. There exists a canon of the Synod of Neocaesarea on this matter. Clement of Alexandria in Stromata IV does not poorly express the sentiment of ancient Christianity on this matter: 'And the Apostle also grants a second marriage by way of concession on account of incontinence and burning, since even this one does not sin according to the covenant; for it has not been forbidden by the law, but he does not fulfill the perfection of the life according to the Gospel by way of intensity; but he procures for himself heavenly glory by remaining by himself and keeping the union dissolved by death undefiled.' The same in Strom. II. 'We bless this as having been given by God as an intercession; but we admire monogamy and the modesty concerning the one marriage; and we say that one must suffer together and bear one another's burdens.' Tertullian in his book to his Wife concerning marriage with Gentiles: 'Since the continence of the flesh which ministers to widowhood is great, it can seem so much the more excusable if it is not sustained: for the pardon of difficult things is easy.' Prudentius in his hymn on Laurentius: 'You see the consecrated virgins, you marvel at the intact aged women, and after the loss of the first bed, ignorant of a second fire. This is the necklace of the Church, with these gems she is adorned.'

Latin:

V. 36. θυγάτηρ Φανουὴλ) Non frustra hoc additur. Tem- pus enim venerat, ut impleretur mysterium quod sub hoc nomine latebat, Gen. 32, 30. Sic in Annæ vocabulo gra- tiæ, in Aser beatitudinis est significatio.

Si mysterium de Christo sub voce פנואל latuit Gen. XXXII. 30. quod implendum in N.T. est tem- pore. Cur ergo illic virum colluctatorem expli- care maluit Grotius de Angelo, quam de Filio Dei? Vid. quæ ad illum locum diximus.

προφῆτις) Ita laxius sumto vocabulo dicuntur feminæ quæ interdum à Spiritu sancto invisebantur. Aliæ olim fue- rant προφήτιδες munere ordinario, ut Debora, quod genus prophetarum in utroque sexu tum cessabat.

ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας ἀυτῆς) Magna laus mulieris apud natio- nes pene omnes, non repetere nuptias. Tacitus de Germa- norum feminis: Sic unum accipiunt maritum quomodo unum corpus unamque vitam: ne ulla cogitatio ultra, ne longior cupi- ditas, ne tanquam maritum sed tanquam matrimonium ament. Legendum, ne tanquam non maritum sed matrimoniu ament. Ideo abstinent, inquit, secundis nuptiis, ne videātur nuptias amasse, non eum cui nupserant. Tertullianus duobus hac de re libris recitat privilegia univirarum apud Romanos & alias gentes. Sed & legibus Romanis multa constituta sunt ad ea- rum nuptiarum licentiam refrenandam. Veteres Christiani cum non possent ullo Christi edicto prohibitam matrimonii repetitionem ostendere, omnibus tamen modis eam diffua- debant: ita ut nec repetitarum nuptiarum celebritati inter- esse vellent presbyteri, ne præsentia sua probare viderentur rem permissam quidem sed minus laudabilem. Exstat ea de re canon Synod Neocæsariensis. Sententiam hac de re Chri- stianismi veteris non male exprimit Clemens Alexandrinus stromateon IV. κᾀκεῖνο ὁ ἀπόστολος δι᾽ ἀκρασίαν κᾀ πύρωσιν κατὰ συγγνώμην δευτέρου μεταδίδωσι γάμου, ἐπεὶ καὶ ὗτος οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει μὲν κατὰ διαθήκην· ὐ γὰρ κεκώλυται πρὸς τοῦ νόμου, ὐ πληροῖ δὲ τῆς κατὰ τὸ ἐυαγγέλιον πολιτείας τὴν κατ᾽ ἐπίτασιν τελειότητα· δό- ξαν δὲ ἀυτῷ ὀράνιον περιποιεῖ μείνας ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῷ καὶ τὴν διαλυθεῖ- σαν θανάτῳ συζυγίαν ἄχραντον φυλάσσων. Idem Strom. II. ἡμεῖς ἐντυχίαν μὲν κᾀ τῦτο δεδόσθαι ὑπὸ τῦ θεῦ μακαρίζομεν· μονογαμίαν δὲ κᾀτὴν περὶ τὸν ἕνα γάμον σεμνότητα θαυμάζομεν· συμπάσχειν δὲ δεῖν λέγοντες καὶ ἀλλήλων τὰ βάρη βαστάζειν. Ter- tullianus libro ad Uxorem de matrimonio cum gentilibus: Quando grandis est continentia carnis quæ viduitatem mini- strat, tanto, si non sustineatur, ignoscibilis videri potest: diffici- lium enim facilis est venia. Prudentius in Laurentium hymno: Cernis sacratas virgines, Miraris intactas anus, Primique post damnum tori Ignis secundi nescias. Hoc est monile Ecclesiæ, His illa gemmis comitur.

## 2:37
Vers. 37. In fastings and prayers) We said that these are accustomed to be joined together at Matthew 17, 21. We remember having mentioned above that a portion of the Israelites was accustomed to assemble at the temple, with times distributed for that purpose, so that they might be free for prayers.
