De vocis hujus interpretatione non quidem quot capita,tot sententiæ,magna tamen est discre- pantia. In certas classes distribuit autorum senten- tias præcipuas, seduloque expendit Robert. Bai- lius in oper. Hist. & Chron. l. II. C. XII. p. 74. seq. post B. Chemnitium nostrum in Harm. Evang. C. XLV. & novem aut decem recensuit sententias: quot etiam ab aliis fere recensentur, à Dn. D. Se- bastian Schmieden,& Dn. D. Henr. Müllero, in Dis- putat. de Sabbato Deuteroproto. Cæterum præ- tereunt hanc vocem non tantum Syrus & Arabs, sed etiam Persicus & Æthiopicus Interpretes; Nec placet quicquam Erasmo & Maldonato, quod de ea voce seu apud veteres, seu recentiores legerunt. Facile autem annuimus, non intelligi festum ali- quem diem extra Sabbatum, non tam quia otium in aliis diebus feriatis vigore legis divinæ non adeo rigide observatur ut in festo hebdomadico,vel die Sabbati quam quia expresse à Luca vocatur Sab- batum,quæ vox significatione famosiori accipien- da, nec temere, illa posthabenda, maxime quia v. 6. etiam Sabbati hebdomadalis mentio fit his verbis, ἐγένετο δὲ κὴ ἐν ἑτέρῳ (αββάτῳ: neque temere eo- rum probamus sententiam qui δευτερόπρωτον ita exponunt,ut nomen sit multis diebus conveniens,cum Lucas hoc nomine usus sit, ut certus dies intellige- retur.B.Chemnitius ita procedit: omnino tale sabba- tum illud secundo primum fuit,in quo juxta legem ni- hil operari licebat. Ejus autem tria sunt genera: Sab- batum scilicet ordinarium septimæ cujusque diei; dein- de prima & ultima dies in magnis festis. Vocabulum vero δευτερόπρωτον indicat, non intelligendam esse primam diem festi,nec Sabbatum, quod extra magna festa, Septimo semper die,celebrabatur. Erit ergo vel ultima dies festi, vel Sabbatum ordinarium quando incidebat in dies intermedios magni alicujus festi: vel quando prima, vel ultima dies festi incidebat in ipsum Sabbatum. Hoc igitur ipsi certum est,Sab- batum secundo primum ad unum aliquod ex magnis & solemnioribus festis pertinere. Ideoque disquirit, quodnam illud festum sit? Tubarum & propitiatio- nis festum non esse inde docet, quod hæc festa uni- co tantum die constiterint: Marcus vero nomina- rit in hac historia Sabbata, & vocabulum δευτερό- πρωτον respectum indicet ad plures dies.De Festo etiam tabernaculorum id non posse intelligi, quia discipuli evellunt, & confricant spicas quod men- si Septembri,in Palæstina præsertim, nullo modo convenit: Reliqua igitur sunt adhuc duo Festa: Paschatis,& Pentecostes. Et de Pentecoste quidem conantur aliqui hanc historiam interpretari, quia Lev. XXIII. 16. Pentecoste vocatur solennitas Messis primitiarum,sicut & Num. XXVIII. 26. Sed res pla- na est inquit B. Chemnitius, si descriptiones festorum diligenter considerentur.Nam Lev.XXIII. 15. Secun- da die in festo Paschatis primitiæ spicarum offereban- tur: & tunc Deut. XVI.9. falx mittebatur in se- getes. Textus etiam Lev. XXIII. 10. dicit: Cum mes- sueritis segetem, offeretis manipulum spicarum: & addit v. 14. Nec tosta nec cocta comedetis ex se- gete, priusquam oblatio spicarum facta sit altera die Paschæ. Hæ descriptiones quasi intento digito monstrant,intelligendum esse festum Paschatis in histo- ria Lucæ. Post oblationem enim spicarum licebat eas confricare,& grana ita manducare. Hæc B. Che- mnitius; qui porro ultimam diem Paschatos deu- τερόπρωτον dictum vult, quia æque sancta fuit ac celebris sicut prima: Quæ etiam est sententia Brentii, Osiandri, & Flacii, nec non Aretii & Antonii Walei; cui vero duo opponuntur imprimis (1) quod in die Paschatos seu azymorum ultimo cibos parare etiam licuerit, & spicas vellere: quodque (2) festum Scenopegias etiam duos dies festos habue- rit, unde incertum relinquatur, quodnam festum hic indigitetur, vel quodnam sit illud δευτερόπρω- τον σάββατον. Sed priori occurri poterit, si di- catur non tantum ultimus fuisse Paschatis dies, sed etiam Sabbatum ordinarium vel hebdomadale: posteriori vero satisfactum jam à B. Chemnitio, quod festo tabernaculorum, utpote quod in mensem Septembrem incidit, non conveniat evulsio & frica- tio spicarum.

Paulo aliter explicat Epiphanius hæres. XXX. Ebion. n. 32. Post factam azymorum diem, defini- tam Sabbati diem, in Sabbato ex natura, quod post azymorum diem in Sabbatum computatum fuit, in- venti transeuntes per sata. Hæc Epiphanii ita acci- piunt Casaubonus, Petavius, & Bailius, quod intel- lexerit Sabbatum naturale, post primum azymo- rum: unde Bailius observat secundum Epiphanium Sabbatum secundoprimum fuisse primum Sabba- tum ordinarium, vel hebdomadale post solenne Paschatis, quod δεύτερον vocetur, quia tempore secundum, & posterius festo Paschatos est, πρώ- τον vero, quia dignitate Paschate prius, & omni festo alio extraordinario. Scaliger eandem am- plexus opinionem vocem inde deducit: quod ἀ- πὸ τꭍ͂ Πάσχατος, id est, à die 16. Mensis Nisan, quo oblatio fiebat frugum, lex jubet septem septima- nas numerare Lev. XIII. 15. Deut. XVI. 9. adeoque septem Sabbata usque ad festum Pentecostes, unde primum ἀπὸ τῆς δευτέρας τꭍ͂ πάσχατος Sabbatum dictum δευτερόπρωτον; secundum δευτεροδεύτερον, tertium δευτερότριτον, & ita porro: quam explica- tionem alii deinceps amplexi sunt, etiam B. Ger- hardus noster in Harm. C. CLXVI. p. 1074. eamque adversus Petavium, & alios defendit Bailius l. c.

Non autem placet Grotio sententia Scaligeri ob duas rationes; ad quas nonnulla respondet Bailius: Priori, quod non detur hujusmodi compositio- nis exemplum, reposuit: Præter multa, quæ Sca- liger in Canonib. Isagog. habet exempla, quid ullo exempli opus est, ubi res est manifesta? Non diffite- tur Grotius masculinum δεύτερος & neutrum δεύ- τερον recte componi cum πρῶτος, quid ergo impedit fœmininum δευτέρα fundare compositionem cum eo- dem? imprimis cum Dei expressum mandatum nume- randi ἀπὸ τῆς δευτέρας huic compositioni optimum fundamentum præbeat. Sed è mandato DEI, si maxime præcessisset ἀπὸ τꭍ͂ πάσχα numeratio- nem institutam minime deduci potest, δευτερόπρω- τον inde componi posse: ut taceam, quod nomen δευτέρας Lev. XXIII. 15. non habeatur. Poste- rius Grotii argumentum est, non mandavit Deus numerare Sabbata à secundo azymorum, sed tan- tum dies, à quibus Pentecoste nomen habet. Re- spondet Bailius, non tantum dies, sed diserte Sab- bata, & hebdomadas à secundo azymorum numerari mandat Deus Levit. XXIII. 15. Ubi tamen regeri potest; aliud esse numerari hebdomadas vel cir- culum septenarum dierum, quod DEUS jussit, aliud numerare Sabbata; illas (septimanas) o- mnino septem à festo Paschatos ad Pentecosten intercedere necessum est, non item septem Sab- bata. Nam si Pascha in diem sextum septima- næ incidat, à secunda Paschatis ad Pentecosten solum sex, non septem Sabbata intervenient. Se- ptimum enim Sabbatum cum ipso Pentecoftes die coincidat. Neque probavit Scaliger ita voca- ta esse Sabbata inter Pascha & Pentecosten inter- media, secundo primum, secundo tertium, &c. quum nec è scriptura, nec scriptis Ebræorum ul- lum fundamentum proferre potuerit.

Non autem fortasse mirum Scaligerum multos habuisse asseclas, Piscatorem, Casaubonum, Ju- nium, Drusium, Coccejum, Bailium, Calix- tum, Frieschmutium, Hackspanium, Erasmum Schmiedium, Wilh. Langium, Quislorpium, item- que Didac. Stellam, Vasquem, Barradium, Pe- tavium, Cœlestinum de monte Mariano, Josephum de Voisin, & Lightfotum, quia in aliis multo gra- vioribus παρεράμασι, ob autoritatem, qua in Chronologicis pollebat, sectatores habuit non paucos nec infimi commatis. Quanquam vero Scaligeriana illa τοῦ δευτεροπρώτου Etymologia, & numeratio Sabbatorum septem, indiculo ab eo exhibita, non nitatur solido fundamento, senten- tia tamen Epiphanii, quod Sabbatum proximum à festo azymorum intelligatur, actutum reproban- da non est. Quum alia possit denominationis ra- tio dari: quod nempe Sabbatum dicatur δευτερό- πρωτον, quia secundum est tempore, utpote po- sterius Sabbato vel festo Paschatos: primum autem tum dignitate, tum etiam certa ratione τοῦ χρόνου vel tempore, respectu scilicet diei oblationis primi- tiarum: quia ab illo proximum naturale Sabba- tum ea voce designatur.

Non multum abit altera Epiphanii explicatio, imo consonare priori videtur, quæ hæresi LI. quæ ἀλόγων est, habetur: Ubi Sabbatum primum vo- cat naturale Sabbatum, secundum vero legale, & a legali Sabbato Paschatos proximum naturale vel hebdomadarium Sabbatum composita voce δευτε- ρόπρωτον appellasse censeri potest. Nec absimilis vocis est interpretatio, (de voce loquimur, non de re significata) de Sabbato hebdomadali, quod antecefsit immediate Sabbatum festivum, utpote cum dies festus in Parasceven Sabbati hebdomada- lis vel diem Veneris incidit, ut Sabbatum hebdo- madale immediate sequatur, ac dies Saturni vel Sabbati tum dicatur Sabbatum δευτερόπρωτον, h. e. Sabbatum secundum respectu præcedentis festi ceu prioris, & primum, quod hoc Sabbatum sit Sabbatorum principalissimum: Quo pacto habet Theophylacti interpretatio: Judæi, inquit, omne festum Sabbatum vocabant. Requies enim est Sab- batum. Sæpius ergo occurrebat festum in Parasce- ve. Et vocabant Parasceven Sabbatum propter Festum, principale autem Sabbatum vocabant se- cundoprimum; quia secundum erat, præeunte alio festo, & Sabbato: primum autem, quia tanquam hebdomale & ordinarium dignitate superabat quod- vis extraordinarium. Cui gemina est Chrysosto- mi explicatio: Quid est secundoprimum? quando duplex cessatio erat, & Sabbati principalis, & fe- sti consequentis. Non enim duplicem cessationem in unum diem collocat: quia alterum facit τοῦ Σαββάτου τοῦ κυρίου principalis Sabbati, alteram ἑτέρας ἑορτῆς διαδεχομένης alterius festi consequen- tis. Differt solum Theophylactus à Chrysostomo: quod ille festum dicat non consequens, sed ante- cedens: & τὸ δευτερόπρωτον in Sabbatum natu- rale vel hebdomadale, incidisse, hic vero in Sabbatum legale, vel festivum consequens natu- rale Sabbatum.

Ab utroque vero abit Cornel. Jansenius, Au- gustinus, Torniellus, Thomas Cartwrightus cum Mariano Victorio, & Luca Brugensi δευτερόπρω- τον dicentes Sabbatum, cum festus dies, seu Sab- batum legale, & Sabbatum hebdomale in unum diem incidunt. Quibus vero sententiis id imprimis opponitur, quod incertum reddant diem, quem tamen certo designatum hac voce voluit Evange- lista, fatentibus iisdem autoribus: siquidem non in Paschatis festo cum Sabbato concurrente so- lum, sed etiam in aliis ea ratione σάββατον δευ- τερόπρωτον notari posset. At Lucas non ait fa- ctum id esse in quodam Sabbato δευτεροπρώτῳ, sed simpliciter factum in Sabbato secundoprimo. Si tamen excipiatur, vel reponatur, festum Pa- schale intelligi è designatione spicarum, atque i- ta etsi voce δευτεροπρώτυ non exprimatur præ- cise festum, è subjecta tamen materia id consta- re, probabilitatis laudem opinionibus illis non facile quis ambiguam reddet.

Isidori Pelusiotæ hæc fuit sententia, per Sabba- tum secundoprimũ intelligendum esse primum azy- morum diem. Δευτερόπρωτον inquit, dicitur quod secundum erat Paschatis, primum autem a- zymorum. Vespera enim mactantes Pascha sequen- ti azymorum congregabant festum, quod etiam δευτερόπρωτον vocabant, propter quod secunda esset Paschatos, prima autem azymorum. Diem hunc Sabbatum appellant; quia tota hebdomas Pa- schatis erat festiva, adeoque ex septem Sabbatis constabat: primum quia primum erat azymorum: secundum, quia secundus Paschatis. Quæ et- iam Euthymii est explicatio, & Suidæ. Cæte- rum Baronii παρόραμα in inferenda Isidori sententia notat Bailius l. c. Non autem calculum meretur Isidorus. Nam primus Azymorum non erat tale festum, in quo non licuerit para- re, quæ spectabant ad victum; id enim in omni- bus diebus Paschatis, & azymorum licebat. Dn. D. Sebast. Schmidius sententiam Isidori eo suf- ficienter refutari censet, quod diem festum pri- mum Paschatis, & primum azymorum diversos fe- cerit. Siquidem licet Pascha decimo quarto die Mensis Nisan mactatum sit, non tamen hic fuerit dies festus per se, nec primus Paschatis: quia Pa- scha comestum est post occasum solis, postquam cœ- pit nox diei decimiquinti, eademque nox, & diei primi festi Paschatis & Azymorum fuit. Quando vero Num. XXXIII. 3. dicitur, à crastino Paschatos, sen- sum esse, ait, qui comestionem Paschatis sequutus est, seu qui noctem Paschalem sequutus.

B. Lutheri sententiam, qui Stapulensem sequu- tus videtur, etiamsi non intelligatur de die festum quodvis, sed de die primum festivum Paschatos se- quente, ex eadem ratione subvertunt multi, quod dies illa primam, quæ sanctissima fuit, sequuta non æque sancta & celebris fuerit, utpote quam ideo non πρωτόπρωτον, sed δευτερόπρωτον dictam volunt, unde in eadem operari licuit: quum contra Lucas testetur Sabbatum illud, quod designat hac voce, adeo sanctum habitum, ut eo evulsio, & confrica- tio quarundam spicarum grandis violatio Sabbati censeretur. Non deest tamen quod pro illa ex- plicatione sententiæ B. Lutheri reponi possit: Nam si dies illa Sabbatum Paschale sequens Sab- batum fuisse dicatur hebdomadale, nulla erit illa objectio.

Occurrunt & aliæ sententiæ sed noviter exco- gitatæ, una Cloppenburgii, altera Capelli, tertia Constant. l'Empereur, quarum priores duas Bald. Walaus adduxit: verum tanti eas non æstimamus, quæ hic recenseantur, nedum quibus confutandis immoremur: Et profligavit satis easdem Dn. D. Sebastian. Schmidius noster, nec non Robert. Bai- lius, quos adeat cui libet. Revertendum nobis ad

Qui indulgere sibi quoque vult post tot alios censendi libertatem, ac si novi quicquam ex- cogitarit: sed sententia ejus, quod Sabbatum δευ- τερόπρωτον intelligendum sit de Pentecoste, quæ se- cunda solennitas sit post Pascha, non nova est: Multorum enim jam fuit tam ex Pontificiis, quam Protestantibus, quam Maldonatus, Cornelius a La- pide, Mercator, Piscator aliique amplexi sunt, & a multis jam confutata: quam etiam S. Chemnitius l. c. profligavit, ut & Petavius animadversion. in Epiphanii hæres. XXX. & LI.

Neque vero probatum est, quod tria illa festa Paschatos, Pentecostes, & Scenopegias vocata sint πρῶτα, quia maxima fuere, nedum quod Penteco- stes festum δευτερόπρωτον nominatum sit, aut σκη- νοπηγίας τριτόπρωτον. De Paschatos festo con- cedimus id dictum הראשון quod etiam Græcis πρῶτον vocatum quondam esse e nescio quo Πάτρα κηρύγματι probare vult Grotius: De aliis autem fe- stis, quod δευτεροπρώτα vel τριτοπρώτα nomen habuerint, nihil adferre habuit. Nec historia præ- sens ad festum Pentecostes referri potest: tum quia Sabbatorum hic mentio fit, quum in festo Penteco- stes unum tantum Sabbatum fuerit, tum quia in Sabbato δευτεροπρώτῳ non licuit parare, quæ ad victum faciebant, quod in festo Pentecostes omni- no licuit: quum etiam in Paschate ipso concessum fuerit Ex. XII. 16. tum quia contextus historiæ pro- bat, non circa festum Pentecostes, sed Paschatos e- andem contigisse, ut ostendunt B. Chemnitius, Jan- senius, Barradius, tum quia in Judæa messis hordeacea circa festum Paschatos celebrata, postquam in se- cundo die Paschatos oblatio frugum vel manipuli spicarum facta est, quemadmodum triticei primi- tiarum panes in festo Pentecostes offerendi erant illudque sequebatur triticea messis, quæ gemina distincta messis in Judæa observata est a B. Chemni- tio e Ruth. II. 23. Jer. XXIII. 11. 15. Exod. IX. 31. cap. XXXIV. 22. Quod vero dicit Grotius spicas virentes secundo azymorum die oblatas tantum dicis causa, id valde temere & prophane dictum non immerito vi- detur Bælio: quia manipuli oblatio stricte valde & solemniter a Deo injuncta fuit, & ante eam diserte prohibitus omnis esus novarum frugum: ast Mai- monide teste, apud Ainsvworthum in Lev. XXIII. 1. Spicæ illæ non virentes erant, sed maturæ, ex qui- bus trituratis gomer farinæ DEO secundo azymo- rum offerri oportuit.

Expensis ita variis de Sabbato secundoprima sententiis, apparet cæteras adductas plerasque re- cte explicatas non destitui sua probabilitate, Gro- tianam vero præ aliis hactenus a nobis adductis re- jiciulam esse; id enim omnino ex historia consta- re, quod Sabbatum δευτερόπρωτον circa Festum non Pentecostes, sed Paschatos inciderit. Num autem in unum diem concurrens Mosaicum Sabbatum cum Sabbato naturali: an vero Sabbatum seu immedia- te seu mediate consequens, aut dies etiam festus ulti- mus Paschatos intelligatur, non multum in Chro- nologia vel Historia referre censemus: neque o- pus est, ut observantia illa strictior, quam urge- bant oi ἐξ ἐναντίας adversus discipulos Christi ad legis interdictum, quod ipsi prætendebant, refera- tur, quum interdicto legis illi inhæserint juxta suas δευτερώσεις, aut Cabalam, quam a Mose acceptam jactabant, intellecto; quod hic a Christo directe nec probatur, nec improbatur, nec nisi ad sum- mum ab exemplis solum, legis interdicto (ex men- te legislatoris intellecto) haud contravenisse Apo- stolos docetur. Quod vero nonnullis videtur, verba Pharisæorum accusatoria ita accipienda esse, quod discipuli faciant ὃ ὐκ ἔξεστι, idque insuper ἐν

τῶν σάββασι facere non vereantur: illud autem ὅ ὐκ ἔξεςι de comestione spicarum ante oblationem, quae festo Paschatos fieri debuit, intelligi velint, non satis firmo consistit talo. Sane censet Dn. D. Schmied, nihil impedire, quo minus ita accipi verba Pharisaeorum possint: Ecce discipuli tui faciunt, quod nondum licet hoc tempore facere, & quidem quod rem adgravat, in Sabbato, quodque satis accommodata huic accusationi sit defensio Christi, quippe in qua Dominus non excusat tantum violationem Sabbati per exemplum Sacerdotum, sed etiam comestionem rei illicitae exemplo Davidis Matth. XII. 45. Fatetur tamen ipse Levit. XXIII. 14. solum de ordinario usu spicarum in cibis sermonem esse, quando fruges in panes faciendos adhibentur, aut ad coquendas pultes, aut conficienda tosta, quod à Chaldaeo, R. Salomone & R. Meir probat, ad quem usum culinarem vellicatio spicarum, & affricatio ad comedendum non pertinebat.

Caeterum non inconcinnam adfert Dn. D. Schmidius, laudata disputatione de Sabbato δευτεροπρώτῳ, explicationem, quod per illud intelligatur Sabbatum alterum in anno Ecclesiastico, qui initium cepit a Mense Nisan, ut primum Sabbatum hebdomadarium dictum sit πρωτόπρωτον, alterum δευτερόπρωτον: quia duto illa Sabbata, vel duae hebdomades ante Pascha id peculiare habebant, ut dicerentur פרס הפסח dimidium Paschatis, & Sabbatum anni secundum nomine primi appellari potuerit, quia dicebatur à Judaeis Sabbatum magnum, atque ita vocatur etiam in Calendariis Judaeorum. Quae explicatio uti multo convenientior est Scaligeriana, erudite à Dn. D. Schmidio confutata, ita grato eam susciperemus animo, nisi nostro judicio haec obstarent, (1) quod ex antiquitate doceri nequeat, ita vocata esse priora anni Ecclesiastici Sabbata πρωτόπρωτον & δευτερόπρωτον. (2) quod illa Sabbati magni denominatio recentior & obscurior sit, quam ut ejus rationem habuerit Lucas. (3) Nec ratio apparet, cur Sabbatum magnum dicitur alterum in anno Ecclesiastico Sabbatum: quicquid sit de Rabbinica appellatione. (4) Si secundum anni Sabbatum notaretur, δευτεροσάββατον potius, quam δευτερόπρωτον dicendum fuisset. (5) plerique interpretes sequutum esse hoc Sabbatum, non antecessisse Pascha statuunt, à quorum communi fere sententia non videtur temere recedendum. (6) Neque apparet, cur Epiphanii sententia deserenda sit, prout ea antea explicatade Sabbato hebdomadali, quod sequutum est Festum Paschatos: cum qua B. Lutheri sententia facile conciliatur, si diem Paschatos sabbatum festivum immediate sequentem hebdomadale fuisse Sabbatum assumatur, quia Lucas Sabbatum vocat) cui consonat etiam Theophylacti explicatio, neque multum aliena est Ludovici de Dieu interpretatio: Atque illud ipsum, inquit, δευτερόπρωτον vocatum puto, quia inter duo alia Sabbata primum nempe Azymorum & septimum interjacens proximum erat primo, illudque statim excipiebat. Hoc dicô: primus Paschatis erat πρῶτον Σάββατον, quod deinde sequebatur hebdomadale Sabbatum, erat δευτερόπρωτον. Addit quidem, septimus tum festi dies erat τρίτον Sabbatum. Sed id minus verisimile est.

Dubium illud, quod movetur, duram nimis esse compositionem δευτερόπρωτον dici secundum & primum; secundum ratione ordinis, primum ratione dignitatis, moveri etiam potest contra sententiam de secundo Paschate anni Ecclesiastici, qua nempe id secundum dicitur, ratione tempo- ris, at primi nomine designatum creditur ratione dignitatis, quia dicebat Sabbatum magnum. Sed hæc de Sabbato δευτεροπρώτῳ dicta sunt.

## 6:5
Verse 5.

τῷ τῶν σαββάτων [on the Sabbath] Regarding what some codices have inserted here, about him who was doing work on the Sabbath, to whom it was said by Christ that he was blessed if he knew what he was doing; but if not, that he was a violator of the law and a spurious person, I do not doubt. For neither the ancient metaphrasts, nor those who write on this passage, mention that history. Which also conflicts with the perpetual institution of Christ, who, acting as a teacher here, granted no indulgence to anyone regarding the Hebrew law. For that power was reserved for his own heavenly kingdom. I think, therefore, it was added by some Marcionite.

PART II. The healing of the withered hand on the Sabbath.

Latin:

Vers 5.

τῷ τῶν σαββάτων] Quod hîc habent insertum nonnulli co- dices, de eo qui Sabbato opus famulum faciebat, cui di- ctum sit à Christo, beatum esse ipsum si nosset quid ageret; sin minus legis violatorem, spurium esse non dubito. Nam neque metaphrastæ veteres, nec qui ad hunc locum scri- bunt ejus meminerunt historiæ. Qui & pugnat cum per- petuo Christi instituto, qui doctorem hîc agens, nemini legis Hebrææ gratiam fecit. Erat enim ea potestas cœlesti regno ipsius reservata. Puto igitur ab aliquo Marcionita adjectum.

PARS II. Manus aridæ in Sabbato sanatio.

## 6:6
Verse 6. ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτῶ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρὰ [a man and his right hand was withered] A Hebraism for ἄνθρωπος ί ἡ χεὶρ ἦν ξηρὰ [a man whose hand was withered].

Latin:

Vers. 6. ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτῶ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρὰ] Hebrai- smus pro ἄνθρωπος ί ἡ χεὶρ ἦν ξηρὰ.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

κατηγορίαν αὐτῶ [an accusation against him] Sufficiently Greek: nor is there any doubt about the reading: κατηγορία [accusation] with a similar sense is found in Demosthenes. Genitives are often accustomed to signify the object. Thus below ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τῶ Θεῶ [in prayer to God]. Moreover, ἵνα εὑρίσκωσι κατηγορίαν [that they might find an accusation] is the same as in Daniel ch. VI. 4. להשכחה עלה [to find occasion against him].

Latin:

Vers 7.

κατηγορίαν αὐτῶ] Satis Græce: nec de lectione dubitan- dum: κατηγορία με fimili sensu est apud Demosthenem. So- lent Genitivi sæpe objectum significare. Ita infra ἐν τῇ προ- σευχῇ τῶ Θεῶ. Est autem ἵνα εὑρίσκωσι κατηγορίαν idem quod in Daniele c. VI. 4. להשכחה עלה.

## 6:9
Verse 9.

ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς τι] The Syriac reads it thus, but as if it referred to the following words in the sense of questioning: τί instead of πότερον, just as we also read in Matthew 21:31, τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο instead of πότερος. But if you prefer to refer it to the preceding words, the sense will be: There is something I would ask you. And I prefer that, because Christ also begins a questioning elsewhere with a similar preface, Matthew 21:24, where ἵνα λόγον is what τι is here.

ἀπολέσαι] That is, ἀποκτεῖναι, as Mark speaks. See what [I wrote] on Matthew.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς τι] Ita legit & Syrus, sed ut ad sequentia referret interrogandi sensu: τί pro πότερον, sicut & apud Matthæum legimus XXI. 31. τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο pro πότερος. Quod si ad priora referre malis: sensus erit: Est quod vos interrogem. Atque id præfero: quia & alibi simili præ- fatione Christus interrogationem exorditur, Matth. XXI. 24. ubi ἵνα λόγον est quod hic τι.

ἀπολέσαι] Id est, ἀποκτεῖναι ut Marcus loquitur. Vide quæ ad Matthæum.

## 6:10
Verse 10.

καὶ ἐποίησεν ὕτω] He did as he was commanded: that is, he stretched out his hand, which the Syriac set forth explicitly, as did the Latin: as they are accustomed to interpret words more freely at times.

ἀποκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτῶ] I repeat here what I said in the case of Mark, that those words ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη seem to have been added from Matthew: for many codices do not have them, nor does the Latin recognize them. The Syriac recognizes that ὡς ἡ ἄλλη, not that ὑγιὴς.

Grotius rashly suspects those words to be interpolated: for although they are not held in the Latin codex, the Syriac nevertheless set them forth as ὡς ἡ ἄλλη, and most Greek codices have them, which are called into doubt without sufficient cause.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

καὶ ἐποίησεν ὕτω] Fecit ut erat jussus: id est, extendit manum, quod explicate posuit Syrus ut & Latinus: ut so- lent liberius interdum verba interpretari.

ἀποκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτῶ] Quod apud Marcum dixi hic repeto, verba illa ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη videre ex Matthæo adscripta: nam multi Codices non habent: nec agnoscit Latinus. Syrus agnoscit illud ὡς ἡ ἄλλη, non illud ὑγιὴς.

Verba illa irreptitia esse temere suspicatur Grotius: etsi enim in Latino non habeantur Codi- ce, Syrus tamen illa exposuit ὡς ἡ ἄλλη, & habent illa plerique Codices Græci, qui citra causam suf- ficientem in dubium vocantur.

## 6:11
Verse 11.

ἄνοιας] שכעין that is, anger: Philemon well [says]: We are all mad whenever we are angry.

Τί ἂν ποιήσειαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ] Namely, that they might remove him from their midst: just as is clear from Mark.

PART III. The election of the twelve Apostles.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ἄνοιας] שכעין id est ira: Bene Philemon: Μαινόμεθα πάντες ὁπόταν ὀργιζώμεθα.

Τί ἂν ποιήσειαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ] Nempe ut eum è medio tolle- rent: quemadmodum ex Marco liquet.

PARS III. Duodecim Apostolorum electio.

## 6:12
Verse 12.

εἰς τὸ ὄρος] The well-known mountain on the seacoast, as we learn from Mark ch. III. 7. & 13.

PART IV. Christ’s Sermon to the disciples.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

εἰς τὸ ὄρος] Notum montem in ora maritima, ut ex Mar- co discimus c. III. 7. & 13.

PARS IV. Christi ad discipulos Concio.

## 6:17
Ver. 17.

καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔση ἐπὶ τόπυ πεδινῦ] That is, from a higher retreat he betook himself to a level place on the mountain capable of holding a larger crowd, so the discourse which follows was delivered ἐπὶ τόπυ πεδινῦ, in a plain בפקעתא as here in the Syriac, and nevertheless on a mountain, which Matthew’s narrative seems altogether to require. There are those who think the narratives in Matthew and Luke are of a different time: and indeed, just as narratives of an event that agree in circumstances are not to be rashly referred to different matters, so nothing forbids the same or similar discourses from having been delivered more often, especially those containing precepts for the whole of life, which could not be repeated too often. But what moves me not to think the narratives are different is not only the same beginning and the same conclusion, but much more the fact that both writers say that after this discourse was delivered, Christ returned to Capernaum and there healed the centurion’s servant. Christ could, however, have stood on this plain while he restored the sick to health, which Luke mentions, and then sat down in the manner of a teacher when he began his precepts, as Matthew indicates.

Osiander indeed wishes there to be two different sermons, and that Matthew's was held toward the beginning of the second year, two months before Passover: but Luke's around Pentecost: But because he is thus forced to make different people out of one Centurion and one Capernaite synagogue ruler. The blessed Chemnitz judges that there is one sermon described by Matthew and Luke: who deserves to be compared here in chapter LI of the Harmony. Regarding the place in which the sermon was held, the blessed Chemnitz says that although Luke testifies that Jesus descended from the mountain before the sermon, and healed many in a level place; he does not expressly say that the sermon was also held in that field. For the place πεδινὸς signifies a low-lying site, and is opposed to mountainous places, Jos. XI. 15, Judith XV. 3, and is rendered by the Syrian as פקע which denotes a plain in a valley.

ὄχλος μαθητῶν ἀυτῦ] Do not understand only the Apostles: for he just called them disciples from whom the beloved Apostles were chosen. They are distinguished, however, from the rest of the people, who did not follow Christ as assiduously as those disciples. In this number of disciples must also be placed certain women of Galilee, and those seventy mentioned by Luke, and many others.

So also in Matthew ch. V, verse 1, the disciples are not only the Apostles, because toward the end of the sermon he said that the crowds were astonished at his teaching: Whence there is no need, as with Augustine, to posit that Christ delivered the same sermon first at greater length to the Apostles, but soon after, when he had descended, repeated it more briefly and as it were in summary to the crowds on the plain.

τῆς παραλίυ] The Syrian translates it as ספר ימא, that is, the port of the sea, in the way the Hebrews call the maritime coast. For Deuteronomy 1, v. 7, ארץ הכנעני וחוף הים is the maritime land of Canaan. So also Jos. IX. v. 1. Moreover, that whole maritime coast, in which Tyre and Sidon are, is called the kingdom of Tyre and Sidon, as in Matthew XV. 21, Mark III. 8, ch. VII. 24.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔση ἐπὶ τόπυ πεδινῦ] Id est de subli- miore secessu contulit se in planitiem montis capacem ma- joris turbæ, ita sermo qui sequitur habitus est ἐπὶ τόπυ πε- δινῦ, in planide בפקעתא ut hic apud Syrum, & nihilo- minus in monte, quod omnino exigere videtur Matthæi narratio. Sunt qui putant diversi temporis esse narrationes apud Matthæum & Lucam: & sane sicut facti narrationes circumstantiis congruentes non temere ad res diversas re- ferendæ sunt, ita sermones nihil vetat sæpius habitos eos- dem aut similes, præsertim continentes vitæ totius præce- pta, quæ non potuerunt nimium sæpe repeti. Sed me ne diversas esse narrationes putem, movent non tantum exordium idem, eademque peroratio, sed multo magis quod uterque scriptor hoc sermone habito Christum ait rediisse Capharnaum atque ibi sanasse Centurionis servum. Stetisse autem potuit Christus in hac planitie dum ægrotos valetudini restituit, quod dicit Lucas, deinde sedisse docto- ris in morem, cum præcepta exordiretur, ut Matthæus in- dicat.

Osiander sane duas diversas esse conciones vult, & Matthæi quidem habitam sub initium anni se- cundi, duobus mensibus ante Pascha: Lucæ vero circa Pentecosten: Sed quia ita cogitur ex uno Centurione & ex uno archisynagogo Capernaiti- co diversos facere. B. Chemnitius unam esse con- cionem à Matthæo & Luca descriptam judicat: qui hic conferri meretur cap. LI. Harmoniæ. De loco in quo habita concio ita B. Chemnitius, quod Lucas quidem testetur Jesum descendisse de monte an- te concionem, & in loco campestrali multos sanasse; non autem expresse dicat, quod in illo campo habi- ta etiam sit concio. Locus enim πεδινὸς significat humilem situm, & opponitur locis montanis Jos. XI. 15. Judith. XV. 3. & à Syro redditur פקע quod planitiem in valle notat.

ὄχλος μαθητῶν ἀυτῦ] Noli solos Apostolos intelli- gere: nam μαθητὰς modo dixit eos ex quibus dilecti sunt Apostoli. Distinguuntur tamen à cætero populo, qui non tam assidue Christum sectabatur, atque illi μαθηταὶ. In hoc numero μαθητῶν ponendæ sunt etiam fœminæ quæ- dam Galilææ, & illi apud Lucam LXX. pluresque alii.

Sic etiam apud Matth. cap. V. vers. 1. μαθηταὶ non soli sunt Apostoli, quia sub finem concionis dixit, obstupuisse turbas super doctrina ejus: Unde non opus, ut cum Augustino statuatur Christum eandem concionem primum Apostolis prolixius habuisse, mox vero cum descendisset turbis in planitie brevius, & quasi per compendium eam repetivisse.

τῆς παραλίυ] Syrus vertit ספר ימא, id est, portum maris, quomodo Hebræi vocant oram maritimam. Nam Deuter. 1, v. 7. ארץ הכנעני וחוף הים est παράλιος γῆ Χαναὰν. Sic & Jos. IX. v. 1.. Vocatur autem tota illa ora maritima, in qua sunt Tyrus & Sidon, regno Tyri & Sidonis, ut Matth. XV. 21. Marc. III. 8. c. VII. 24.

## 6:18
Verse 18.

·· οἱ ὀχλέμενοι] I do not disapprove of that of the old interpreter who said 'who were vexed.' For the grammarians teach that the word 'to vex' is much more vehement than the common people think, regarding that line of Maro: - - - Delichias vexasse rates.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

·· οἱ ὀχλέμενοι] Non improbo illud veteris interpretis qui vexabantur. Nam vexandi verbum multo esse vehe- mentius quam vulgus putat, docent Grammatici ad illud Maronis: - - - Delichias vexasse rates.

## 6:19
Verse 19.

παρ’ ἀυτῦ ἐξήρχετο] It is signified that the efficacy was not adventitious, but intrinsic to Christ from the divine nature. See below VIII. 46, Matthew IX. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

παρ’ ἀυτῦ ἐξήρχετο] Significatur non adventitia fuisse ef- ficacia, sed Christo intrinseca ἐκ τῆς θείας φύσεως. Vide infra VIII. 46. Matth. IX. 5.

## 6:21
Verse 21.

οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν] That is, those who here endure hunger and thirst, not for any reason, but because they are held by the highest desire for divine justice to be propagated in themselves and others. Thus it agrees excellently with Luke and Matthew. And so Clement of Alexandria interpreted it: 'those who hunger and thirst,' he says, 'for righteousness.' See the example in Paul, I Cor. IV. 11 and 2 Cor. XI. 27.

Μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν ὅτι γελάσεται] He describes mourning by tears and joy by laughter in a popular way. For in Matthew it is 'to mourn' and 'to be comforted.' Thus soon 'to leap' is put for 'to rejoice': elsewhere 'to exult'.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν] Id est, qui hic famem sitimque tolerant, non quavis de causa, sed quia summo tenentur desiderio divinæ justitiæ in se atque aliis propagandæ. Ita optime convenit Lucæ & Matthæo. Atque ita interpretatus est Clemens Alexandrinus: τὲς πεινῶντας καὶ διψῶντας, inquit, διὰ τὴν δικαιοσύνην. Vide exemplum in Paulo I. Cor. IV. 11. & 2. Cor. XI. 27.

Μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν ὅτι γελάσεται] Populariter lu- ctum lacrymis, gaudium risu describit. Nam apud Mat- thæum πενθεῖν & παρακαλεῖσθαι. Ita mox σκιρτᾷν pro gau- dere ponitur: alibi ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι.

## 6:22
Verse 22.

ὅταν ἀφορίζωσιν ὑμᾶς] To separate properly corresponds to the Hebrew ברל ומנרה. For what is among the teachers of the Hebrews מנודה is the same as to separate in the Christian canons. John said to make excommunicated. Josephus to cast out from the order. This custom did not have its origin from the words of the law, for by its prescription lesser offenses were expiated by sacrifices, for greater ones a fine or even lashes were imposed, for the greatest crimes the punishment was death, of exile there was no mention. But since there were many offenses not explicitly named in the law, the interpretation of the wise established separation between lashes and sacrificial expiation, especially against those who, having been warned, did not amend their life. For the Hebrews hand down that נידוי was in use while Solomon's Temple stood. A greater necessity for this institution arose from the time the people were led away into Babylon and lost with their liberty the right of public judgments. For natural reason itself compelled a return to those coercions which could be carried out without the usurpation of public power,

For we read that the Druids also did this in Gaul, that those who did not stand by their decrees, they would interdict from sacrifices. Those who were thus interdicted (says Caesar) are held in the number of the impious and the wicked. Everyone avoids them, they flee their approach and conversation, lest they receive any harm from the contagion. Not unlike these were those at Rome formerly who were called sacred and detestable, and who, as unworthy of life, were interdicted from water and fire. And in Greece those excluded from the market and harbors and those proclaimed outcasts. There is a clear description of this rite in Sophocles' Oedipus Tyrannus: I forbid that man, whoever he is, of this land of which I hold the power and the thrones, either to receive him, or to speak to him, or to make him a partner in prayers to the gods or in sacrifices, or to share the holy water.

Xenophon on Hiero: many laws have been made for the polluted murderer not even for his companion to be clean. In the Epistle of Philip to the Athenians: as the people spoke of this so as to exclude them from the mysteries. The scholiast of Aristophanes: according to custom, murderers do not partake of the sacrifices. To natural reason were added certain examples and arguments derived by reasoning from the law. For when God had granted to Cain, though He had committed the punishment of death for parricide, a certain broad flight, He had inflicted it in such a way that He wished him to be held detestable by all at the same time. Ancient Greece observed something similar to this in the case of murderers. Furthermore, since one suffering from a foul scab was kept away by the law from all commerce with men, lest the disease harm others by transmission, it was not an unfair inference, if nothing more severe could be done, that this at least should be established against wicked men, who both harmed others by the contagion of their example and sprinkled the whole people with the stain of a common disgrace, from which the people could not be freed except by some manifest detestation of the crime. Although it was also the duty of individuals to avoid and shun those whom they knew to be involved in a graver fault, in order to cast shame upon them, yet in notorious crimes the matter itself demanded some common public notice. That, in the times of the Babylonian exile, was not in the power of the priests, nor in the power of the interpreters of the law, but in the power of the Exilarch and the elders added to him, whom, although stripped of supreme power, all the Jews revered in place of magistrates, and obeyed their decrees. But as often as autonomy and the right of public punishment, short of the power of death, was granted to the Jews, other punishments were added to separation: by which very fact it is clear that the right of separation was a part of authority. Therefore, in the times of Ezra, with an assembly proclaimed in Jerusalem, whoever did not present himself is bound to this punishment והוא יבדל מקהל הגולה, that is, and he himself shall be separated from the assembly of the colony. The LXX translate it thus: and he himself shall be separated from the church of the colony. Josephus: he shall be alienated from the multitude, whence we understand that assembly, whence they are called excommunicated, does not signify the school, but the whole gathering of the people. For we have said elsewhere that קהל is translated sometimes as assembly, sometimes as church. Ezra had made this decree, being indeed constituted Ethnarch by the King, by the counsel of the great assembly, that is, of the Sanhedrin and other leaders of the people: for so we read in the decree בעצת השרים והזקנים LXX. as in the council of the rulers and of the elders. The Hebrew teachers say this decree was made by the higher and lower college of judges, that is, the Senate of the people and the urban one. In the same place, relegation from the assembly has joined to it the taking away of substance, as Josephus speaks, the anathema of property, as the LXX, that is, the consecration of goods. Similar is what Nehemiah says of the son-in-law of Sanballat expelled by him, namely by the same power by which he had punished others found guilty of offenses with a curse, plucking of hair, and lashes. Judea having been reduced by the Romans to the manner of a province, the status was almost the same as in the times of Ezra and Nehemiah. For with the power of killing taken away or curtailed, the rest of the public judgments were left to the Jews. Wherefore what John says in chapter IX. 22. the Jews agreed that if anyone should confess Him to be the Christ, he should be excommunicated, is entirely to be understood of a decree either of the Sanhedrin, or also of the great assembly, of which assembly we have spoken elsewhere. Nor does it pertain to anything else what is in the same John, saying: they did not confess the Pharisees, lest they should be excommunicated, chapter XII. v. 42. For although the Sadducees often attained to the highest honors by the favor of the Romans, as being less suspected of revolutionary things, it is not to be doubted, however, that the greater part of the Sanhedrin was from the Pharisees. For John also in chapter VII. verse 45, circumlocutes the Sanhedrin by the name of the chief priests and Pharisees. Thus Nicodemus and Gamaliel were Pharisees and members of the Sanhedrin. Indeed, most of the scribes were of his sect, chapter XXIII. v. 9. But also other sects which did not mix themselves in the republic, such as were especially the Essenes, from whom was collected a great multitude of Christians, whence certain Hebrews said that they were the same as the Nazarenes and Essenes, necessarily employed the ἀφορισμὸν (excommunication) to protect their institutions. There were indeed other punishments in use among them, such as long periods of dry-eating, fasts, and other things of that kind, which the Jews even now practice among themselves: but since neither their assemblies nor the leaders of those assemblies possessed the τὸ ἀναγκαστικὸν (coercive power), the extreme to which one could arrive against the contumacious was relegation from the assembly, as Josephus teaches us. The Pythagoreans followed the same custom: for whoever did not observe the rules of that institution was barred from the assembly, and all held him for dead, so much so that they even built a κενοτάφιον (cenotaph) for him. Moreover, it is to be noted that there were many species of ἀφορισμὸς. The first species is the bare ἀφορισμὸς, obtaining the name of the genus נדוי (niddui). Those who were branded with this mark, while the Temple stood, approached the Temple, as a learned man among the Hebrews has noted: but they undoubtedly stood outside the περίβολον (enclosure), which distinguished the Gentiles from the Israelites. For the οἱ ἀφωρισμένοι (excommunicated) were meanwhile held in the place of Gentiles. The ancient Christians (who, as we have often noted, willingly followed all the approved institutions of the Jews) called these τοὺς ἐν προσκλαύσει (those in the state of weeping), who did not pray with the rest, but entrusted their petitions for mercy to the faithful, as Tertullian speaks, meanwhile squalid and mourning: which the Jews also observe now: they called the same χειμαζομένους (the storm-tossed), because they were tossed as if outside the harbor of the Church in the deep sea of the world. But after some time had passed, they were admitted closer to such a mournful state of guilt: for which admission other Christians made fewer or more degrees: concerning which there will be a place to speak elsewhere. The second species of ἀφορισμὸς was חרם (cherem) and Ἀνάθεμα (anathema) to the Greeks, by which he who had offended was devoted as sacred to certain gods, as to God the avenger. The Jews seem to have used this against those who defected from the entire profession of the law, whom they call מומרים (mumrim), and we call apostates, to whom they consider equal those who, after admonition, name God contumeliously. They not only avoided familiar commerce with these, but did not even deem them worthy of being greeted lightly. John describes this in his Epistle: Do not receive him into your house and do not say greeting to him; for he who says greeting to him shares in his evil works. But the very formula of the anathema is pronounced by Paul against Alexander, the corrupter of doctrine: May the Lord repay him according to his works, 2 Tim. IV, verse 14. In this place, the Samaritans were to the Jews what they held in a much worse position than the Gentiles. For on behalf of the Gentiles, if they requested it, sacrifices were made in the temple, as Josephus and Philo teach us, and it is sufficiently gathered from the words of Solomon, 1 Kings VIII. 41, but not so for a defector. Thus also in the Church of the Christians, the faithful interposed their prayers for the lapsed who were doing penance, but not so for the deserters of Christianity, to whom, through those first centuries, were equated those who had either contracted a habit of sinning, or had been caught in such grave offenses that it was not credible that they could have fallen into the mind of one retaining any piety, such as deliberate idolatry, homicide, adultery, John in his 1st Epistle, chap. V, v. 9: there is a sin unto death; I do not say that one should pray for that. Clement of Alexandria, Strom. VII: but never for the harm of men in such a prayer. unless they are contriving the return of justice, and the Gnostic will manage the request for those who have become past feeling. See how they invoked the severe judgments of God against deserters and others who denied piety by their deeds, if perhaps by that reason they might be led to repentance. Therefore Paul adds that they may be disciplined, speaking of Hymenaeus and Alexander, 1 Tim. I, v. 20. Similar is that in the Psalm: Fill their faces with shame, that they may seek thy name, O Lord, Psalm LXXIII. 17. Such were those whom the Apostles delivered to Satan, for temporal vexation. But if any who had fallen into such destruction drew many into the same, not that common anathema was exercised against them, but one more grave and atrocious. This the Hebrews call שמ-אתא and שם God comes: for שם, that is, the name, they say for God; Paul says anathema Maranatha מרן אתא with the same meaning. For מרן is Lord. By that word God is prayed to, that He may as soon as possible take such a malefactor and seducer from the number of men. Wherefore an example of this anathema is Galat. V, verse 12: I wish that those who unsettle you would even mutilate themselves. It appears from these things which we have said that the Christians followed the example of the Jews in the custody of discipline, but especially of the Essenes, as those who were merely private, without any authority, just as the Christians were. Among the ancient institutions of the Essenes, this was also one: if any, not yet having completed the space of the prescribed penance, were to fall ill to the danger of death, they would receive them to communion: which Josephus calls receiving them in their last breaths. They did this, however, considering the suffering until death as sufficient for their sins. It is certain that the same was observed by the Christians in ancient times by suitable witnesses, the fathers of the Nicene Synod, whom nothing of the ancient customs of the Church could escape. Concerning those who are departing, they say, the ancient and canonical law shall be kept even now, so that if anyone is departing, he should not be deprived of the final and most necessary provision. Again, just as among the Essenes the judgment of such a matter was not in the power of a few, but in the power of the assembly into which no less than a hundred men would gather, as Josephus teaches, so also among the ancient Christians, with the Bishop and Elders presiding, but with the knowledge and consent of the multitude of the brethren, judgments of morals were exercised, 1 Cor. V, verse 4: when you are gathered together, 2 Cor. II, v. 6: the punishment by the many. Thus Eusebius records that it was customary in ancient times for an examination to take place with the multitude present. Tertullian, in his Apologeticus, having spoken of the assembly and congregation, adds: There also are exhortations, corrections, and divine censure: for judgment is passed with great weight, as is fitting among those who are certain that they are in the sight of God, and it is the highest anticipation of the future judgment if anyone has so offended that he is banished from the communion of prayer and assembly and all holy intercourse. Approved elders preside. A more illustrious description of the ἀφορισμᾶ could not be brought forward. Add that in the book to his wife: It is established that believers entering into marriages with Gentiles are fornicators and are to be excluded from all communion of the brotherhood according to the letter of the Apostle, who says that with such a one one should not even take food. In the book on Monogamy he said to drive away from communion: in the book on Modesty: We remove the impious furies of lusts, both against bodies and against sexes beyond the laws of nature, not only from the threshold, but from every roof of the Church. But the ἀφορισμὸς ἐπ᾽ ἀναθέματι, which the Greeks also call ἀποκήρυξιν τελείαν, the same writer calls relegating to perpetual separation, which he says is used against those ejected again and again. The passage is in the book against heretics, Origen, ἀπελαύνειν τῶ κοινᾶ & ἀποκωλύειν ἥκειν ἐ- πὶ τὸν κοινὸν σύλλογον. Cyprian sometimes says ἀφορίζειν for to abstain, sometimes he circumlocutes with other words, such as to exclude from communion, to restrain, to prohibit: to cast out of the Church, to exclude, to drive away. If anyone reads the Epistles of this most holy man, he will easily recognize that almost the entire vigor of Christian discipline consisted in these judgments: and indeed not only were those who contumaciously rejected warnings banished from the intercourse of the pious in perpetuity, that is, without a time limit, but also for a time those who offered hope of repentance: and those who wish this custom to be removed from the Church inflict a most serious wound upon discipline, which, given the so corrupted morals of Christians, it would be of the greatest value to restore to its ancient severity: so far is it from the case that any part of it should be allowed to become lax. Nor is a special precept required for this matter: since, the assembly of the Church having been once established by Christ, all those things must be considered commanded without which the purity of that assembly cannot be maintained. There are others who approve of abstention, but do not approve of ἀνάθεμα. And yet there ought to be a distinction between those who listen to warnings and those who are refractory. Now indeed we have said that ἀνάθεμα is nothing other than ejection without a time limit, which nevertheless does not always preclude a return for those led to repentance. Certainly, although the ancient church, when the διακρίσεις πνευ- μάτων were vigorous, could judge more certainly concerning the souls of men, there are nevertheless certain offenses so atrocious that, if contumacy is added, no one can fail to see that they are ἁμαρτίας ὡς θάνατον: for such, while they remain such, the Church does not intercede with the suffrage of prayers: which is open only to penitents: generally, however, for these, as for infidels, it wishes for a better mind. Chrysostom, where he says that ἀνάθεμα is to be pronounced against deeds, not against men, understands that strict ἀνάθεμα by which God is asked to take someone from the midst. The use of this is indeed rarer: yet not non-existent. For against Julian, when he added to his defection machinations for the overthrow of Christianity, the Church used this weapon of extreme necessity, and was heard by God. There were also those who thought that these judgments of the Church should be inhibited as often as God granted Christian powers to the age: for which matter they use the example of the Jews, among whom the Sanhedrin had that right of pronouncing those to be ἀποσυναγώγες. To whom I would easily grant that there is some authority of pious Kings even in these matters. For both John, Bishop of Rome, asks the Emperor Justinian on behalf of the Nestorians and others, that if they should wish to return to the unity of the Church after having put aside their own error and having cast off their perverse intention, he should receive them into his communion: and in Ivo of Chartres an old chapter is read, from which it is clear that those whom the King had admitted to his table after some offense were accustomed to be admitted to the communion of the Church. But these things do not have the effect that the liberty of the Church to judge should be taken away: nor does the argument sought from the Jews proceed. For among them the whole law by which they were to be judged was adapted to a carnal people, so that it bound all citizens equally: and therefore the Republic and the church were the same. But the laws of Christ require much more than in common is usually, or even can be, prescribed to the citizens of any empire: for a great part of mankind always minds the things of the flesh. Wherefore civil laws indeed perform their duty if they restrain the more serious crimes and those most harmful to society: but those things which are sinned against the laws of love, against meekness, against patience, are placed outside the common laws: yet not outside those laws which Christ prescribes to those who follow Him and according to which that assembly selected from the world ought to judge. Wherefore Constantine and the Emperors who followed him rightly left to the Church its own judgments, and moreover fortified them with their own laws: as can be seen in the Acts of the Synods and the laws recorded in the code. And I have wished thus far to admonish those who are more unjust against the discipline of the Church. It remains that those who exercise the same should remember how great a burden is imposed upon them. It is a known saying of the ancient Jews which Maimonides mentions: if anyone has excluded an innocent person from communion, he himself falls out of the right of communion. Just as we also read in the Constitutions of Clement: ἡ καθάρα ἐπιστρέψει εἰς κεφαλὴν τῶ ἀδίκως ἀυτὸν ἐκπέμψαντος, which equity Cyprian followed, and according to the custom of those most holy times pronounces thus concerning Felicissimus: let him receive the sentence which he first spoke. However, unjust and harsh judgments are wont to be exercised not so much in the examination of morals (for here censure is for the most part too indulgent, so far is it from being more rigid than is fair) as concerning questions of dogmas and rites. Which happened to the Apostles and ought to terrify the rash, and comfort the pious. Christ foretold to them that it would come to pass that they would be pronounced ἀποσυνάγωγοι John XVI. 2. which He here called ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς. Nor did the impotent [authority] of old stand within the first degree of ἀφορισμᾶ, as when those were judged to be ἀποσυνάγωγοι who confessed that Jesus was the Messiah, John IX. 22. ch. XII, 42. but when after the resurrection of Jesus His dogma grew strong with great increases, and the liberty of rites was gradually taught more clearly, the ἀνάθεμα was added: of which Justin mentions against Trypho. For he says that certain Jews were accustomed ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καταναθεματίζειν τὲς ἐπὶ τὸν χριστὸν πιστεύοντας. And in another place he says that the ἀρχισυναγώγες after prayer were accustomed to mock Christ. Again elsewhere he addresses the Jews thus: καὶ νῦν τὲς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ’ ἀυτὸν (τὸν χριστὸν) καὶ τὸν πέμψαντα ἀυτὸν παντοκράτορα καὶ ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων Θεὸν ἀθετεῖτε καὶ ὅσον ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἀτιμάζετε, καταρώμενοι ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν τὲς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ τὸν χριστόν. Those who now read through the Talmudic books or even the rituals of the Jews know that these things are true. For everywhere in them Christians are devoted to curses. Trypho himself in Justin says that it was commanded to the Jews by the Doctors μηδενὶ τῶν χριστιανῶν ὁμιλεῖν μηδὲ κοινωνῆσαι τῶν λόγων. Epiphanius likewise testifies concerning his own age: The words are: ἀνισάμενοι ἕωθεν (οἱ Ἰυδαῖοι) καὶ μέσης ἡμέρας καὶ περὶ τὴν ἑσπέραν ἐν ταῖς ἀυτῶν συναγωγαῖς, ἐπαρῶνται ἀυτοῖς καὶ ἀναθεματίζεσι, φάσκοντες, ὅτι ἐπικαταράσαι ὁ Θεὸς τὲς Ναζωραίως. Which he interprets as if said about one sect of Christians, when in reality it pertained to all Christians, whom the Jews called and even now call Ναζωραίως.

Nor is that tradition of the Hebrews concerning שמתא while the temple of Solomon stood worthy of belief, unless it be confirmed from elsewhere, nor can it be taught from the law that sacrifices were ordained to expiate lesser crimes in the civil forum: which were rather divinely sanctified, so that crimes might be expiated before God, and those offering might obtain remission of sins, just as is evident from Leviticus. Furthermore, Grotius has brought forward many learned things here concerning the three kinds of ἀφορισμᾶ, namely concerning נדוי: by which mark those who were censured were compelled to remain outside τὸν περίβολον, which distinguished the Gentile from the Israelites, and they were held in the place of Gentiles: and חרם ἀνάθεμα by which he who had sinned was devoted as sacred to certain curses, as to God the avenger: in which place were the Samaritans, for the Jews held these to be worse than Gentiles, and מוסרין ἀποστάται: Finally שם אתא or מרן אתא The Lord comes: by which kind of ἀφορίσεως were marked seducers, who having fallen into grave exile would draw many into the same. With which let those things be compared which Bald. Walæus produced from Selden and Capellus on John IX. v. 22.

καὶ ἐκβάλωσι τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν] ἐκβάλειν is not here to erase from a white board or diptychs: for that was sufficiently comprehended by the word ἀφορίζεσθαι: but just as ὀνειδίζειν is to assail those present with reproaches, so ἐκβάλειν τὸ ὄνομα ὡς πονηρὸν is to spread abroad the name of those absent, as of wicked men, with rumors. For it is a Hebraism הוציא שם רע Deuter. XXII. v. 19. ἐξέβαλε, or as the LXX translate it ἐξέ- νεγκεν ὄνομα πονηρὸν. This happened to the Apostles then especially when an embassy was sent from the Sanhedrin to all the Jews throughout the world to defame the Christian dogma, which matter we have mentioned elsewhere from Justin.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ὅταν ἀφορίζωσιν ὑμᾶς] Ἀφορίζειν proprie respondet He- bræo ברל ומנרה Nam quod apud Hebræorum magistros est מנודה idem est τὸ ἀφορίζειν in canonibus Christianis. Jo- hannes dixit ἀποσυνάγωγον ποιεῖν. Josephus ἐκβάλλειν τῆ τάγματος. Mos hic ex legis verbis ortum non habuit, nam ex ejus præscripto minora delicta sacrificiis expiabantur, majoribus mulcta aut etiam verbera indicebantur, maxi- morum criminum pœna mors erat, exilii nulla mentio. Sed cum multa essent delicta in lege non diferte nominata, sapientum interpretatio inter verbera & victimalem expia- tionem constituit τὸν ἀφορισμὸν, præcipue in eos, qui mo- niti viram non emendabant. Nam נידוי in usu fuisse stante Salomonis Templo tradunt Hebræi. Major hujus instituti necessitas nata est, ex quo populus in Babyloniam abdu- ctus cum libertate amisit jus publicorum judiciorum. Ipsa enim naturalis ratio coëgit ad eas coërcitiones recurrere quæ sine usurpatione publicæ potestatis expediri poterant,

Namque hoc & in Gallia Druides fecisse legimus, ut qui decretis non starent, eos sacrificiis interdicerent. Quibus ita interdictum erat (inquit Cæsar) ii numero impiorum ac sceleratorum habentur. Iis omnes decedunt, aditum sermo- nemque defugiunt, ne quid ex contagione incommodi accipiantur. His non dissimiles erant Romæ olim qui sacri & intestabiles dicebantur, & quibus ut vita indignis aqua atque igni in- terdicebatur. Et in Græcia εἰ ἀγορᾶς καὶ λιμένων εἰργόμενοι & οἱ ἐκκηρυττόμενοι. Est descriptio hujus ritus luculenta apud Sophoclem Oedipo Tyranno: Τὸν ἄνδρ᾽ ἀπαυδῶ τοῦτον ὅστις ἐστὶ γῆς Τῆς δ᾽ ἧς ἐγὼ κράτη τε κᾐ θρόνους νέμω, Μήτ᾽ εἰσδέχεσθαι, μήτε προσφωνεῖν τινα, Μήτ᾽ ἐν θεῶν εὐχαῖσι μήτε θύμασιν Κοινὸν ποιεῖσθαι, μήτε χέρνιβας νέμειν.

Xenophon de Hierone: πεποίηνται πολλοὶ νόμοι τῷ μιαρῷ φόνη μὴ δὲ τὸν συνόντα καθαρεύειν. In Epistola Philippi ad Athenienses: ὡς τοῦτο ἐλάλουθεν ὁ δῆμος ὥστε μυστηρίων εἴρ- γειν αὐτούς. Scholiastes Aristophanis: κατὰ τὸ ἔθος οἱ ἀν- δροφόνοι μὴ μεταλαμβανόντων τῶν θυσιῶν. Ad naturalem ratio- nem accesserunt exempla quædam & argumenta per ra- tiocinationem ex lege derivata. Nam Caino Deus cum mortis pœnam parricidio commiseram indulsisset, latam quandam fugam infliwerat, sed ita ut ipsum simul omni- bus detestabilem haberi vellet. Cui simile quid vetus Græcia in homicidis observabat. Præterea cum turpi sca- bie laborans ex lege arceretur ab omni hominum com- mercio, ne scilicet morbus transitione aliis noceret, non iniqua erat collectio, si nihil posset gravius, hoc certe in homines facinorosos constituendum, qui & exempli con- tagio læderent alios, & populum omnem communis probri labe aspergerent, unde liberari populus non pote- rat, nisi manifesta quadam sceleris detestatione. Quan- quam autem singulorum quoque officium erat eos quos gravioris culpæ affines nossent defugere ac declinare, quo pudorem eis injicerent, in famosis tamen criminibus res ipsa exigebat communem aliquam notionem. Ea tem- poribus Babylonici exsilii, fuit non penes Sacerdotes, neque penes legis interpretes, sed penes Αἰχμαλωτάρ- χην & ei additos seniores, quos quanquam summo im- perio exutos Judæi omnes magistratuum vice revereban- tur, eorumque decretis parebant. Quoties vero Judæis αὐτονομία & jus publicæ animadversionis, citra necis potestatem, fuit concessum, accesserunt ad ἀφορι- σμοὺ pœnæ aliæ: quo ipso liquet ἀφορισμοῦ jus fuisse par- tem imperii. Itaque Esdræ temporibus cœtu indicto Hierosolymis qui se non stitiffet huic pœnæ obstringitur והוא יבדל מקהל הגולה, id est, κᾀ αὐτὸς ἀφορίσε- ται ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς ἀποικίας. LXX. ita vertunt: καὶ αὐτὸς διασταλήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἀποικίας. Jo- sephus: ἀπαλλοτριωθήσεται τῷ πλήθει, unde intelligimus συναγωγὴν, unde ἀποσυνάγωγοι dicuntur non significare τὸ διδασκαλεῖον, sed omnem populi conventum. Nam קהל modo συναγωγὴν, modo ἐκκλησίαν verti alibi diximus. Fecerat hoc decretum Esdras quippe Ethnarcha à Rege constitutus, de consilio συναγωγῆς μεγάλης, id est, Synedrii & aliorum populi principum: ita enim legimus in decreto בעצת השרים והזקנים LXX. ὡς ἐν ᾗ βουλῇ τῶν ἀρχόντων κᾀ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων. Hebræi magistri dicunt factum hoc de- cretum à collegio judicum superiore & inferiore, id est, Senatu populi & urbano. Ibidem relegatio à cœtu conjun- ctam habet ἀφαίρεσιν τῆς ὀσίας, ut Josephus loquitur, ἀνα- θεματισκὸν τῆς ὑπάρξεως, ut LXX. id est, bonorum confe- crationem. Simile est quod Nehemias dicit Sanballatæ ge- nerum à se expulsum, nimirum eadem potestate qua alios delictorum compertos maledicto, depilatione, verberibus castigarat. Redacta à Romanis in provinciæ modum Ju- dæa, status ferme idem fuit, qui Esdræ & Nehemiæ tem- poribus. Nam ademta aut accisa interficiendi potestate, cætera publicorum judiciorum Judæis relinquebantur. Quare quod ait Johannes cap. IX. 22. συνέθεντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ Χριστὸν, ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται, omnino intelligendum de decreto aut Synedrii, aut et- iam συναγωγῆς μεγάλης, de quo cœtu alibi diximus. Ne- que alio pertinet quod apud eundem est Johannem dict. τοὺς Φαρισαίους οὐχ᾽ ὡμολόγουν· ἵνα μὴ ἀποσυνάγωγοι γένωνται, cap. XII. v. 42. Quanquam enim Sadducæi sæpe ad sum- mos honores perveniebant Romanorum gratia, utpote minus suspecti rerum novarum, dubitandum tamen non est, quin pars major Synedrii ex Pharisæis fuerit. Nam & Johannes capite VII. vers. 45. Synedrium cir- cumloquitur nomine ἀρχιερέων κᾀ Φαρισαίων. Ita Nico- demus & Gamaliel erant Φαρισαῖοι & συνέδροι. Quin & plerique γραμματεῖς ejus erant Sectæ, cap. XXIII. v. 9. Sed & Sectæ aliæ quæ se reipublicæ non miscebant, quales præcipue erant Esseni, è quibus collecta est ma- gna multitudo Christianorum, unde eosdem esse Nazi- ræos & Essenos dixerunt Hebræi quidam, ad tuenda instituta sua, necessario ἀφορισμὸν usurpabant. Erant quidem inter ipsos in usu pœnæ etiam aliæ, ut longæ ξηροφαγίαι, jejunia, atque alia id genus, quæ nunc etiam Judæi inter se exercent: sed cum neque cœtus ipsorum neque ejus cœtus præsides haberent τὸ ἀναγκαστικὸν, extre- mum quo deveniri poterat adversus contumaces, erat à cœtu relegatio, ut Josephus nos docet. Secuti sunt morem eundem Pythagorei: nam qui non serva- bat ejus instituti regulas cœtu arcebatur, eumque omnes pro mortuo habebant, ita ut & κενοτάφιον ei struerent. Cæterum notandum est ἀφορισμοῦ plures fuisse species. Prima species est nudus ἀφορισμὸς generis obtinens no- men נדוי. Qui hac nota inusti erant stante Templo accedebant ad Templum, ut ex Hebræis vir doctus notavit: sed haud dubie consistebant extra τὸν περίβο- λον, qui distingvebat ἐθνικοὺς ab Israëlitis. Nam οἱ ἀφωρισμένοι interim ἐθνικῶν loco habebantur. Christiani veteres (qui, ut sæpe notavimus, omnia proba Judæo- rum instituta libenter sequebantur) hos vocabant τοὺς ἐν προσκλαύσει qui non cum cæteris orabant, sed fidelibus le- gationes deprecationis injungebant, ut Tertullianus lo- quitur, squallidi interim & mœrentes: quod & nunc Iu- dæi observant: eosdem vocabant χειμαζομένους, quod velut extra Ecclesiæ portum in mundi alto jactarentur. Sed post decursum tempus aliquod tam mœsti reatus; propius admittebantur: cujus admissionis Christiani alii pauciores, alii plures gradus fecére: de quibus alias erit agendi locus. Altera ἀφορισμοῦ species erat חרם et Ἀνά- θεμα Græcis, qua is qui deliquerat divis quibusdam, ut Deo ultori sacer devovebatur. Videntur hoc usurpasse Iudæi adversus eos qui à tota legis professione deficie- bant, quos ipsi vocant מומרים, nos ἀποστάτας, quibus pares censent eos, qui post admonitionem Deum contume- liose nominant. Horum non modo familiare commer- cium vitabant, sed nec dignos arbitrabantur quos leviter salutarent. Describit hoc Johannes in Epistola: μὴ λαμ- βάνετε εἰς οἰκίαν καὶ χαίρειν αὐτῷ μὴ λέγετε· ὁ γὰρ λέγων αὐ- τῷ χαίρειν κοινωνεῖ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ τοῖς πονηροῖς. Sed ipsa ἀναθέματος formula a Paulo adversus Alexandrum doctrinæ adulteratorem pronunciatur: ἀποδῴη ἀυτῷ ὁ κύ- ριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ἀυτοῦ, 2. Timoth. IV. vers. 14. Hoc lo- co Iudæis erant Samaritæ quos multo pejore loco quam ἐθνικοὺς habebant. Nam pro Gentibus, si id postularent, sacrificia fiebant in templo, ut nos docent Iosephus & Phi- lo, & satis colligitur ex verbis Salomonis 1. Reg. VIII. 41. at pro defectore non item. Sic & in Ecclesia Christiano- rum pro lapsis pœnitentiam agentibus fideles preces suas interponebant, non item pro desertoribus Christianismi, quibus per prima illa sæcula æquabantur hi qui aut pec- candi consuetudinem traxerant, aut in tam gravibus deli- ctis deprehensi erant quæ credibile non erat cadere potu- isse in animum pietatis aliquid retinentem, qualia erant ex deliberato idololatria, homicidium, adulterium, Ioh. in I. Epist. cap. V. v. 9. ἐστὶν ἁμαρτία πρὸς θάνατον· ὀ περὶ ἐκείνης λέγω ἵνα ἐρωτήσῃ. Clemens Alexandrinus Strom. VII. ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἐπὶ τῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βλάβῃ τῇ τοιᾷδε συγχρήσιον ἐυχῇ ποτε. πλὴν εἰ μὴ τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῆς δικαιοσύνης τε- χναζόμενοι τοῖς δ᾽ ἀπηλγηκόσιν ὁ γνωστικὸς οἰκονομήσει τὴν αἴτησιν. Vide ut adversus desertores & alios factis pieta- tem abnegantes severa Dei judicia invocaverint, si forte ea ratione ad resipiscentiam perducerentur. Ideo addit Paulus ἵνα παιδευθῶσι de Hymeneo & Alexandro loquens 1. Timoth. I. v. 20. Simile est illud in Psalmo: Imple vul- tum eorum ignominia, ut quærant nomen tuum Domine, Psal. LXXIII. 17. Tales erant quos Apostoli Satanæ tra- debant, ad temporalem vexationem. Quod si qui in tale exitium lapsi multos eodem traherent, in eos exercebatur non illud commune ἀνάθεμα, sed gravius atque atro- cius. Id Hebræi vocant שמ-אתא et שם Deus venit: nam שם id est nomen pro Deo dicunt Paulus dicit ἀνάθεμα Μαραναθὰ מרן אתא eodem significatu. Nam מרן est Dominus. Ea voce oratur Deus, ut quamprimum talem maleficum & seductorem tollat ex hominum numero. Quare hujus ἀναθέματος exemplum est Galat. V. vers. 12. ὄφελον καὶ ἀποκόψονται οἱ ἀναστατῶντες ὑμᾶς. Apparet ex his quæ diximus in disciplinæ custodia secutos Christianos ex- emplum Iudæorum, sed Essenorum præsertim, ut qui es- sent mere privati, sine ullo imperio, quemadmodum & Christiani. Inter vetera Essenorum instituta & hoc erat, si qui nondum impleto indictæ pœnitentiæ spatio ad mor- tis periculum ægrotarent, eos ad communionem recipe- rent: quod ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἀναπνοιαῖς ἀναλαμβάνειν vocat Josephus. Faciebant autem hoc αἰτικανὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἁμαρ- τήμασιν ἀυτῶν τὴν μέχρι θανάτου βάσανον ἡγύμενοι. Idem à Christianis antiquitus observatum constat idoneis testibus, patribus Synodi Nicænensis quos veterum Eccle- siæ morum nihil latere poterat. περὶ δὲ τῶν ἐξοδευόντων, inquiunt, ὁ παλαιὸς καὶ κανονικὸς νόμος, φυλαχθήσεται καὶ νῦν, ὥςε ἔιτις ἐξοδεύοι τοῦ τελευταία καὶ ἀναγκαιοτάτου ἐφοδίε μὴ ἀποςερεῖσθαι. Rursus, sicut apud Essenos judicium tantæ rei non erat penes paucos, sed penes cœtum in quem convenirent homines non minus centum, ut Jose- phus docet, ita & apud Christianos veteres præsidente quidem Episcopo & Senioribus, sed conscia & consen- tiente fratrum multitudine morum judicia exercebantur, 1. ad Corinth. V. vers. 4. συναχθέντων ὑμῶν, 2. Corinth. II. v. 6. ἐπιτιμία ὑπὸ πλειόνων. Sic Eusebius memorat anti- quitus ἐξέτασιν fieri solitam πλῆθες παρόντος. Tertullia- nus Apologetico cum de cœtu & congregatione locutus esset, subjungit: Ibidem etiam exhortationes, castigatio- nes, & censura divina: nam & judicatur magno cum ponde- re ut apud certos de Dei conspectu, summumque futuri judicii præjudicium est, si quis ita deliquerit, ut à communicatione orationis & conventus & omnis sancti commercii relegetur. Præsident probati quique seniores. Non poterat illustrior adferri descriptio τᾶ ἀφορισμᾶ. Adde illud in libro ad u- xorem: Fideles Gentilium matrimonia subeuntes, stupratores esse constat & arcendos ab omni communicatione fraternitatis ex literis Apostoli, dicentis cum ejusmodi nec cibum sumen- dum. Libro de Monogamia dixit à communicatione depel- lere: libro de Pudicitia: Libidinum furias impias & in cor- pora & in sexus ultra jura naturæ, non modo limine, verum omni Ecclesiæ tecto submovemus. At ἀφορισμὸς ἐπ᾽ ἀναθέματι quam & ἀποκήρυξιν τελείαν Græci vocant, idem scriptor vo- cat in perpetuum discidium relegare, quod usurpatum ait ad- versus semel atque iterum ejectos. Locus est libro adversus hæreticos, Origenes, ἀπελαύνειν τῶ κοινᾶ & ἀποκωλύειν ἥκειν ἐ- πὶ τὸν κοινὸν σύλλογον. Cyprianus ἀφορίζειν modo dicit absti- nere, modo aliis vocibus circumloquitur, ut à communica- tione arcere, cohibere, prohibere: de Ecclesia ejicere, excludere, depellere. Cujus quidem viri sanctissimi Epistolas si quis le- gat, facile cognoscet totum ferme Christianæ disciplinæ vi- gorem in istis judiciis constitiisse: neque vero eos tantum qui contumaciter monita respuebant in perpetuum, id est, sine præfinitione temporis, à commercio piorum relega- tos, sed ad tempus etiam eos qui spem præberent pœni- tentiæ: quem morem qui ex Ecclesia sublatum volunt gravissimum infligunt vulnus disciplinæ, quam corruptis adeo Christianorum moribus ad veterem severitatem re- duci maximum sit operæ pretium: tantum abest ut ulla ejus pars reliqua luxari debeat. Neque ad eam rem pecu- liare præceptum desideratur: cum Ecclesiæ cœtu à Chri- sto semel constituto, omnia illa imperata censeri debeant, sine quibus ejus cœtus puritas retineri non potest. Sunt alii qui abstentionem probent, ἀνάθεμα non probent. Atqui discrimen esse debet audientium monita, & refra- ctariorum. Jam vero diximus nihil aliud esse ἀνάθεμα quam sine præfinitione temporis ejectionem, quæ tamen pœnitentia ductis reditum non semper præcludit. Cer- te quanquam vetus ecclesia, cum vigerent διακρίσεις πνευ- μάτων, certius de animis hominum judicare potuit, sunt tamen quædam deli&a tam atrocia, ut si contumacia accedat, nemo non videat esse ἁμαρτίας ὡς θάνατον: pro talibus, dum tales manent, Ecclesia non intercedit pre- cum suffragio: quod solis pœnitentibus patet: genera- liter tamen his,ut & infidelibus, mentem optat meliorem. Chrysostomus ubi ἀνάθεμα pronunciandum ait adversus facta, non adversus homines, intelligit destrictum illud ἀνάθεμα quo Deus rogatur ut aliquem è medio tollat. Hujus sane rarior est usus: non tamen nullus. Nam in Julianum, cum defectioni adderet machinationes ever- tendi Christianismi, usa est Ecclesia isto extremæ necessi- tatis telo, & à Deo est exaudita. Reperti sunt & qui ju- dicia ista Ecclesiæ putarent inhibenda, quoties Chri- stianas potestates Deus concederet seculo: quam in rem utuntur exemplo Judæorum apud quos Synedrium ha- bebat jus illud pronuntiandi ἀποσυναγώγες. Quibus ego illud facile largiar, piorum Regum nonnullam esse etiam ad res istas auctoritatem. Nam & Johannes Ro- mæ Episcopus Justinianum Imperatorem rogat pro Ne- storianis atque aliis, ut si proprio deposito errore & prava intentione depulsa ad unitatem Ecclesiæ reverti voluerint, in suam eos communionem recipiat: & apud Ivonem Carnutensem legitur capitulum vetus, ex quo constat ad communionem Ecclesiæ admitti solitos quos post deli- ctum aliquod Rex mensæ suæ adhibuisset. Sed hæc non eo valent ut libertas judicandi tollatur Ecclesiæ: neque procedit petitum à Judæis argumentum. Nam apud eos lex tota ex qua judicabitur erat accommoda- ta populo carnali, ita ut cives omnes æqualiter ob- stringeret: ac proinde idem erant Respublica & ἐκκλησία. At Christi leges multo plus exigunt quam in commune- civibus imperii alicujus præscribi solet, aut etiam potest: semper enim magna pars hominum φρονεῖ τὰ τῆς σαρκός. Quare civiles quidem leges suo funguntur officio, si graviora & societati maxime nocentia delicta coerceant: at quæ contra dilectionis, contra mansuetudinis, contra patientiæ leges peccantur extra communes leges sunt posita: non etiam extra eas leges, quas se sectantibus Christus præscribit & secundum quas judicare debet ille selectus ex mundo cœtus. Quare recte Constantinus & eum secuti Imperatores reliquerunt Ecclesiæ sua judicia, atque ea insuper suis legibus munierunt: ut videre est in Actis Synodorum & legibus in codicem relatis. Et hos quidem qui iniquiores sunt adversus Ecclesiæ disciplinam monitos hactenus volui. Superest ut qui eandem exercent meminerint quantum sit ipsis onus impositum. Scitum est veterum Judæorum cui Maimonides meminit: si quis innocentem à communione arcuerit, ipsum excidere jure communionis. Sicut & in Clementis constitutionibus legimus: ἡ καθάρα ἐπιστρέψει εἰς κεφαλὴν τῶ ἀδίκως ἀυτὸν ἐκπέμψαντος, quam æquitatem secutus Cyprianus, ex more illorum sanctissimorum temporum de Felicissimo ita pronunciat: accipiat sententiam quam prior dixit. Solent autem injusta atque immitia judicia exerceri non tam in morum examine (nam hic nimium plerunqne indulget censura, tantum abest, ut æquo sit rigidior) quam circa quæstiones dogmatum rituumque. Quod Apostolis accidit & terrere temerarios debet, & pios solari. Prædixit illis Christus fore ut ἀποσυνάγωγοι pronunciarentur Ioh. XVI. 2. quod hic dixit ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς. Neque intra primum ἀφορισμᾶ gradum stetit impotens olim, ut cum ἀποσυνάγωγοι judicati sunt qui Iesum esse Messiam faterentur, Ioh. IX. 22. c. XII, 42. sed cum post Iesu resurrectionem ejus dogma magnis auctibus invalesceret, & libertas rituum paulatim clarius doceretur, accessit ἀνάθεμα: cujus meminit Iustinus adversus Tryphonem. Ait enim quosdam Iudæos solitos ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καταναθεματίζειν τὲς ἐπὶ τὸν χριστὸν πιστεύοντας. Et alio quodam loco ait τὲς ἀρχισυναγώγες μετὰ τὴν προσευχὴν solitos Christum ἐπισκώπτειν. Rursum alibi Iudæos ita alloquitur: καὶ νῦν τὲς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ’ ἀυτὸν (τὸν χριστὸν) καὶ τὸν πέμψαντα ἀυτὸν παντοκράτορα καὶ ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων Θεὸν ἀθετεῖτε καὶ ὅσον ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἀτιμάζετε, καταρώμενοι ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν τὲς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ τὸν χριστόν. Hæc vera esse norunt etiam qui nunc Thalmudicos libros aut etiam ritualia Iudæorum perlegunt. Passim enim diris ibi devoventur Christiani. Ipse apud Iustinum Tryphon Iudæis præceptum ait à Doctoribus μηδενὶ τῶν χριστιανῶν ὁμιλεῖν μηδὲ κοινωνῆσαι τῶν λόγων. Epiphanius item de sua ætate testatur: Verba sunt: ἀνισάμενοι ἕωθεν (οἱ Ἰυδαῖοι) καὶ μέσης ἡμέρας καὶ περὶ τὴν ἑσπέραν ἐν ταῖς ἀυτῶν συναγωγαῖς, ἐπαρῶνται ἀυτοῖς καὶ ἀναθεματίζεσι, φάσκοντες, ὅτι ἐπικαταράσαι ὁ Θεὸς τὲς Ναζωραίως. Quod ille tanquam de una Christianorum secta dictum interpretatur, cum revera ad omnes Christianos pertineret, quos Iudæi appellabant atque etiam nunc appellant Ναζωραίως.

Nec traditio illa Ebræorum de שמתא stante Salomonis templo usitato, fide digna est, nisi aliunde firmetur, nec è lege doceri potest sacrificia ordinata esse ad expianda minora delicta in foro civili: quæ potius divinitus erant sanctita, ut coram Deo expiarentur delicta, & offerentes remissionem peccatorum consequerentur, quemadmodum ex Levitico constat. Cæterum multa erudita hic attulit Grotius de tribus generibus ἀφορισμᾶ utpote de נדוי : qua nota institi consistere cogebantur extra τὸν περίβολον, qui distinguebat ἐθνικὸς ab Israëlitis, & in ἐθνικῶν loco habebantur: & חרם ἀνάθεμα quo is, qui deliquerat, diris quibusdam, ut Deo ultori sacer devovebatur: quo loco erant Samaritæ, hos enim Judæi deteriores Ethnicis habebant, & מוסרין ἀποστάται: Denique שם אתא vel מרן אתא Dominus venit: quo ἀφορίσεως genere notati sunt seductores, qui in grave exilium lapsi multos eodem traherent. Cum quibus conferantur quæ è Seldeno, & Capello ad Joh. IX. v. 22. produxit Bald. Walæus.

καὶ ἐκβάλωσι τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν] ἐκβάλειν non est hic ex albo aut diptychis expungere: id enim verbo ἀφορίζεσθαι satis erat comprehensum: sed sicut ὀνειδίζειν est præsentes convitiis proscindere, ita ἐκβάλειν τὸ ὄνομα ὡς πονηρὸν absentium nomen, ut improborum hominum, differre rumoribus. Est enim Hebraismus הוציא שם רע Deuter. XXII. v. 19. ἐξέβαλε, aut ut LXX. vertunt ἐξέ- νεγκεν ὄνομα πονηρὸν. Contigit hoc Apostolis tunc præci- pue cum à Synedrio legatio ad omnes per orbem Iudæos missa est ad infamandum dogma Christianum, quam rem ex Iustino alibi memoravimus.

Just as the happiness of the other life is depicted by a banquet, so is the opposite state by hunger and thirst.

## 6:30
Ver. 30.

καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ, μὴ ἀπαίτει] αἴρειν here means not to extort by force, but to use as one's own. Thus also below in chapter XIX. v. 21. αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας. The sense is: if anyone should use what is yours or what is owed to you as his own, do not rigidly urge your right against him to the detriment of mutual love.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ, μὴ ἀπαίτει] αἴρειν est hic non vi extorquere, sed pro suo uti. Sic & infra cap. XIX. v. 21. αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας. Sensus est: si quis quod tuum est aut tibi debetur pro suo usurpet, noli rigide adversus eum jus tuum cum detrimento mutuæ dilectionis urgere.

## 6:32
Ver. 32.

ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐσὶ] Thus Plautus uses gratia, that is, thanks are owed to you. For the dative here seems altogether to require that we understand χάριν not as a benefit, but as the repayment of a benefit. What, he says, can you expect from God in the way of thanks for such an act? Thus χάριν ἔχειν is to give thanks below in chapter XVII, v. 9. Heavenly grace is called χάρις here in one way, and in another way in several places in Paul. In Paul, because it is liberally promised, since the Lord owed us nothing by right, indeed we ourselves were debtors on many counts: here, however, because it has regard to good deeds: in which way it is also called a reward in this place in Matthew: but it is grace because of the benevolent affection of the giver; it is a reward because of the promise.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐσὶ] Ita Plautus est gratia, id est, gratia tibi debetur. Omnino enim dativus hic videtur exigere ut χάριν intelligamus non beneficium, sed beneficii re- pensationem. Quam, inquit, ex tali facto à Deo potestis gratiam exspectare? Sic χάριν ἔχειν est gratias agere infra cap. XVII. v. 9. Aliter hic gloria cœlestis χάρις dicitur, a- liter apud Paulum aliquot locis. Apud Paulum quia li- beraliter promissa, cum ex jure Dominus nihil nobis de- beret, imo nos ipsi multis nominibus essemus debitores: hic vero quia respectum habet ad bene facta: quomodo & merces dicitur hoc loco apud Matthæum: sed gratia ob benevolum dantis affectum: merces ob promissionem.

## 6:34
Vers. 34.
