Deus erat Ver- bum, ubi λόγος subjectum est, praedicatum DEUS: τὸ πνεῦμά ἐςι τὸ ζωοποιοῦν, id quod vivificat, seu principium, causa, fons & origo vivificationis & vitae nostrae est Spiritus, vel spiritualis illa in Christo natura. Quem sensum confirmat (1) oppositio car- nis, & Spiritus, quae non de modo intellectus sonat, sed de re & natura carnali, spirituali naturae op- posita, (2) materia substrata: quia de virtute vi- vificationis Christi actum, ideo monstrandum, un- de eam caro habeat, nimirum non ex se, & per se, sed à Spiritu, & propter unionem hypostaticam cum divina natura. (3) Attributi conditio; quia vivi- ficatio proprium est Spiritus, non vero sensus spi- ritualis cujusvis dicti: (4) Alterius sententiae col- latio, quia etsi homo animalis & carnalis ac ratio corrupta Spiritui opponatur, non tamen opponi- tur ei explicatio, vel sensus carnalis: nec caro us- piam est sensus carnalis, aut Spiritus sensus spiri- tualis, Rom. VIII. 8. τὸ φρόνημα σαρκὸς dicitur prudentia carnalis, vel quicquid sapit caro sine spiri- tu, & ex se, vel suo ingenio, non autem caro ipsa ac- cipitur pro sensu carnali. Si Spiritus est sensus spiri- tualis, num in verbis sequentibus etiam ita spiri- tus accipiendus? Verba quae ego loquor Spiritus sunt, id est, sensus spiritualis sunt. Quae causae mo- vent nos, ut priorem sensum omnino hic praefe- rendum censeamus.

ἡ σὰρξ ὐκ ὠφελεῖ ὐδὲν) Caro milla, ne mea quidem, potest vitam dare æternam. Est enim pabulum temporarium.

Impia hæc est interpretatio, in Zwinglio pridem damnata, de carne Christi intellecta: quam qui manducat, vitam æternam habet. Illam Christus diserte vivificam dixit; nonne ergo Christo pa- lam contradicunt, qui eam nihil prodesse ajunt, aut pabulum eam tantum temporarium faciunt, quod non prosit ad vitam æternam. Etsi ergo caro meri hominis, (ac, si Christus talis fuisset, ipsius etiam caro) nihil prosit, tamen quia caro Christi in hypo- stasi ē λόγε subsistit, & vitæ ē λόγε particeps, cum pro mundi vita data est, tum etiam vivificat actu eos, qui illa fruuntur per fidem, adeoque & meri- tis & efficacia prodest ad salutem, à blasphemia non absunt, qui Christi carnem nihil prodesse di- cunt. Id ergo κατ’ ἄνϑρωπον solum asseritur: Ca- ro meri hominis, & spiritu destituta nihil prodest: unde agnoscere Capernaitæ debebant, carnem Christi non esse ψιλῶ ἀνθρώπε, nec spiritu vivifi- cante destitui, quæ pro mundi vita data, vereq; dat vitam, ceu panis vitæ. Ita Cyrillus explicat, carnem absq; spiritu à divinitate separatam non prodesse quicquam ad donandam vitam æternam.

Τὰ ῥήματα, ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ ὑμῖν, πνῦμά ἐσι) Præcepta mea, quæ morte mea, quam carnis & sanguinis nomine significa- vi, sancientur, pertinent ad animi actiones. Ergo πνεῦμα hỳc significat πνευματικά, quomodo ferme πνεῦμα etiam sumitur 2. Cor. III. v. 7. significans Christi præcepta cordi inscripta, id est cor conformatum Christi præceptis.

Tà ῥήματα non sunt præcepta Christi: sed ver- bum Evangelii, quod ipse prædicavit: nec carnis & sanguinis nomine mors ejus significatur, quia carnis & sanguinis particeps factus est, ut mortem subiret, & carnem pro mundi vita daret, sangui- nemq; suum pro nobis effunderet. De cætero verba Christi πνεῦμα esse hoc sensu, quod πνευματικά sint, non abnuimus; ἐμφατικώτερον tamen est, quod πνεῦμα dicatur, non πνευματικά, quia spiri- tu animata sunt: nec nudus verborum sonus, aut sensus etiam, ut in verbo quovis humano, hic spe- ctandus in verbis Christi, sed vis illa vivificandi, regenerandi, convertendi, salvandi, quam à spiritu habet. Unita nempe est cum verbo SS. Trinitas, quæ per verbum ad nos venit, & mansionem apud nos facit, Joh. XIV. 23. ac peculiariter id tribuitur Spiritui S., ad quem opus sanctificationis pertinet. Id ergo est quod docere vult Christus: unius Spi- ritus, vel divina naturæ est vivificare, sine quo caro nihil prodesfet: vi cujus caro mea etiam est vivifica, per & propter unionem hypostaticam. Ita verba quoq; ipsa, quæ ego loquor, non sunt inania, aut vel- uti alia hominis nudi verba, sed spiritu divino, & virtute cælesti animata per unionem mysticam: quia non nudus sonus & sensus, aut materiale & for- male solum in illis spectari debet, quum efficacia divina præditi sint, utpote quæ πνεῦμα sunt, seu divino Spiritui unita, à quo vim divinam vivificādi obtinent. Perquam cruda & frigida est Grotii glossa, Verba mea spiritus sunt, id est præcepta mea ad animi actiones pertinent. De quo in schola Ca- pernaitica quæstio hic mota non fuit. Neq; 2. Cor. III. 7. per spiritum animi actiones spirituales intel- liguntur: quomodo enim illæ vivificent? uti nec per carnem actiones carnales: sed caro literam legis, Spiritus Evangelium & verba Spiritus designat: quia lex occidit, Evangelium vero est verbum vitæ.

καὶ ζωή ἐσιν) καὶ pro ideo. Quia ad animi actiones perti- nent, ideo ad vitam æternam proficere possunt, quæ alia re nulla est parabilis, dicitur autem vita id quo vita æterna pa- ratur, ut infra XII 50. XVII. 3. Hinc mox vocantur ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίε, ubi genitivus, ut sæpe, continet effecti signifi- cationem.

Vitam æternam actionibus nostris animi parabi- lem esse, crassus error est, in Socinianis & Pontifi- ciis jam profligatus: quibus adhuc eo gravius errat Grotius, quod addit, æternam vitam re nulla alia parabilem esse. Sic enim meritum Christi excludi- tur, quod unum fide apprehensum nobis æternam conciliat salutem; nec à Pontificiis excluditur. Dicuntur autem verba Christi spiritus & vita per hendyaden, quod sint Spiritus vivificans, quum Spiritu vivificante animata sint, qui cum verbo u- nitus δύναμιν ζωοποιητικὴν eidem largitur, ac fa- cit, ut sit verbum vitæ, Actor. V. 20. Phil. II. v. 16. vitæ æternæ, Joh. VI. 68. vivum & efficax, Ebr. IV. v. 12. potentia Dei ad salutem, Rom. I. 16. animasq; nostras salvare possit, Jac. I. 21. Aut si placet καὶ pro ideo positum esse; ideo quia Spiritus sunt, vivi- fica sunt, quia τὸ πνεῦμα ἐςι τὸ ζωοποιοῦν, id quod nos vivificat, est Spiritus, principium omnis vitæ, in quo vita illa est, quæ est lux hominum Joh. I. 4. à quo & caro Christi habet, quod vivifica est, & panis vitæ, nos ad vitam æternam pascens, & ver- bum Christi, quod vita sit.

## 6:64
Verse 64. But there are some of you who do not believe) But I do not wonder that these things are received perversely by you. For there are not a few of yours who do not place faith in me, and that because of the pride and contumacy of their mind.

For he knew from the beginning) Now from the beginning, from the time they had begun to follow him, he had known the mind of each one. Thus ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς [from the beginning], Luke 1:2.

And who is he that shall betray him) He knew that not only in the rest of the crowd following him, but also in the number of the twelve, there was one who did not have a mind addicted to him, and who, by heaping crimes upon crimes, would arrive at the betrayal of his master. Let the certain foreknowledge of evil actions be noted here.

Latin:

Vers. 64. Ἀλλ’ εἰσὶν ἐξ ὑμῶν τινὲς οἳ ὀυ πισέυωσιν) Sed non miror perverse hæc à vobis accipi. Sunt enim vestrorum non pauci qui fidem mihi non adhibent, idque ob animi superbiam ac contumaciam.

ᾔδει γὰρ ἐξ ἀρχῆς) Jam ab initio ex quo eum sectari cœ- perant, noverat cujusque animum. Sic ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς Luc. I. 2.

Καὶ τίς ἐςιν ὁ παραδώσων ἀυτὸν) Non tantum in reliqua sectantium se turba, sed & in numero duodecim sciebat u- num esse, qui animum sibi addictum non haberet, & qui scelera sceleribus cumulando ad magistri proditionem per- venturus esset. Notetur hic malarum actionum certa præ- notio.

## 6:65
Verse 65. For this reason I have said to you) Because I knew this to be true, therefore I had just said those things which exist in verse 44.

unless it be given to him from my Father) Here he calls that 'to give to someone' which above he called 'to draw someone,' namely, to give so that he may believe in Christ inwardly, which is not given except to the pious, the modest, and those eager to learn. Thus the Jurisconsults often note that that is understood to be given, which has also been accepted.

Latin:

Vers. 65. Διὰ τῦτο εἴρηκα ὑμῖν) Quia hoc verum esse sciebam, ideo modo dixeram ea quæ exstant commate 44.

ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον ἀυτῷ ἐκ τῦ πατρός με) Hic dare alicui vocat quod supra aliquem trahere, dare scilicet ut penitus Christo credat, quod non datur nisi piis, modestis, descen- di avidis. Sic Jurisconsulti notant sæpe datum id intelligi, quod & acceptatum sit.

## 6:66
Verse 66. back) That is, they returned whence they had come. Thus ἀποτρέφεσθαι εἰς ὀπίσω [to turn back] in the Psalms and elsewhere. Thus Luke 17:33, below 18:6, they were alienated back, Isa. 1:4.

They no longer walked with him) They did not even return to follow him.

Latin:

Vers. 66. εἰς ὀπίσω) Id est, redierunt unde venerant. Sic ἀποτρέφεσθαι εἰς ὀπίσω in Psalmis & alibi. Sic Luc. XVII. 33. infra XVIII. 6. ἀπηλλοτριώθησαν εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, Esa. I. 4.

Οὐκέτι μετ’ ἀυτῦ περιεπάτων) Ne reverfi quidem sunt ut eum sectarentur.

## 6:67
Verse 67. Do you also wish to go away?) He shows that he seeks the ministry of no one for his own sake: and that he does not even want disciples unless they are willing.

Latin:

Vers. 67. Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε ὑπάγειν) Ostendit se nullius ministerium sui causa quærere: ac ne velle quidem discipu- los nisi volentes.

## 6:68
Verse 68. Simon Peter) More fervent than the others and therefore taking up the discourse in the name of the society,

to whom shall we go away?) The Scribes teach nothing of the sort. Matt. 7:29. But John the Baptist himself referred us to you.

You have the words of eternal life) He affirms that he feels the same as what Christ had just said, that his discourses are guides to eternal life.

Latin:

Vers. 68. Σίμων Πέτρ@) Cæteris fervidior ac proinde societatis nomine sermonem suspiciens,

πρὸς τίνα ἀπελευσόμεθα) Nihil tale docent Scribæ. Matth. VII. 29. Johannes autem Baptista ipse nos ad te re- legavit.

Ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίε ἔχεις) Affirmat idem se sentire quod Christus modo dixerat, ipsius sermones duces esse ad vitam æternam.

## 6:69
Verse 69. And we have believed) We have long since believed this, as John and you yourself affirm.

And we have known) Nay, we are as it were certainly convinced, both by the sight of the miracles and by the efficacy and authority of the discourse. Thus also above c. V. 42, after we believe is placed we know; Clement in Stromata VI says that gnostic faith is situated in firm apprehension.

that you are the Christ) And therefore faith is to be had in you in all things, both those which we grasp and those which we do not. In the same sense Martha affirms the same thing soon after about Jesus, c. XI. 31.

the Son of the living God) Not of Joseph, as the others had just said. See Matt. XVI. 16.

Latin:

Vers. 69. Καὶ ὑμεῖς πεπιςεύκαμεν) Jam pridem Johanni tibique affirmanti id credidimus.

Καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν) Imo certo quasi persuasi sumus, tum miraculorum conspectu, tum sermonis efficacia atque au- ctoritate. Sic & supra c. V. 42. post πισέυομεν ponitur ὅιδα- μεν, Clemens Stromatum VI. πίσιν γνωσικὴν sitam ait ἐν βεβαίᾳ καταλήψει.

ὅτι σὺ ὁι ὁ χρισὸς) Ac proinde tibi in omnibus tum quæ capimus, tum quæ non capimus fidem habendam. Eodem sensu idem mox de Jesu Martha affirmat, c. XI. 31.

ὁ ὑὸς τῦ Θεῦ τῦ ζῶντ@) Non Josephi, ut modo cæteri dixerant. Vide Matth. XVI. 16.

## 6:70
Verse 70. I have chosen the twelve) Into a closer degree of friendship, into companionship.

εἷς διάβολός ἐςιν) Those who plot evil against the innocent are called διάβολοι, as in Mark 3:38. This word does not only correspond to the word Satan, which the Syrian here employs, and which we discussed in Matthew 16:23, but also to the word צר, as when this name is attributed to Haman in Esther ch. 7:4, 8:1. Christ indicates that Peter thought better of his companions than the reality warranted, and by the example of one he renders the others anxious. It seems, however, that Judas even then wished ill to Jesus because His precepts differed greatly from his own pursuits.

That sense of the word devil cannot be proven in the cited passage of Mark; indeed, the word devil is never used by Mark. Jerome wishes Judas to be called by that name because he slandered the miracles of Christ, thinking they were done by magic. Cyril wishes Judas to be called so emphatically to exaggerate his malice, which is more diabolical than human: and just as, he says, he who adheres to God becomes one Spirit with him, so he who adheres deeply to the Devil becomes himself in a way a Devil. Heinsius shows from Pindar and Eustathius that the word is used among the Greeks for the extremely impious: Judas is also called so as a whisperer and informer from John XII. 5, because he was also distinguished by that vice. D. Tarnovius: One of you will fall away, like the Devil, from a comparison with John VIII. 44. But an example of the Grotian meaning has not yet been observed.

Latin:

Vers. 70. τὲς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην) In propiorem amicitiæ gradum, in contubernium.

εἷς διάβολός ἐςιν) Qui innocentibus malum struunt vo- cantur διάβολοι ut Marc. I. 38. Neque tantum respondet hæc vox voci Satana, quam hic usurpat Syrus, de qua egi- mus Matth. XVI. 23. sed & voci צר ut cum Amani hoc no- men tribuitur Esther c. VII. 4. VIII. 1. Indicat Christus me- lius Petrum de sodalibus suis sentire quam res haberet, & unius exemplo cæteros sollicitos reddit. Videtur autem Judas jam tum Jesu male voluisse quod ejus præcepta ab ipsius studiis plurimum discreparent.

Sensus ille vocis διαβόλε Marci loco allegato probari nequit, imo nunquam vox διαβόλυ à Mar- co adhibita. Hieronymus Judam eo nomine id- ctum vult, quia calumniatus est miracula Christi, exiftimans ea Magice fieri. Cyrillus ἐμφατικῶς fic appellatum vult Judam ad exaggerandam ejus ma- litiam, quæ diabolica magis quam humana : & quemadmodum, inquit, qui adhæret Deo, unus Spiritus fit cum eo : Ita qui penitus adhæret Diabo- lo, & ipse quodammodo fit Diabolus. De extreme impio vocem adhiberi apud Græcos, Heinsius ex Pindaro & Eustathio docet: Susurronem & dela- torem ita etiam dictum Judam è Joh. XII.5 quod illo etiam vitio insignis fuerit. D. Tarnovius : Unus ex vobis deficiet similis Diabolo, è collatione Joh.VIII.44. Grotianæ vero fignificationis exem- plum hactenus nondum observatum.

## 6:71
V. 71. And he spoke of Judas) John added this so that no one might suspect this was said about any other of the Apostles.

Latin:

V. 71. Ἐλεγε δὲ τὸν Ἰύδαν) Hoc addidit Johannes ne quis de alio quo Apostolorum dictum hoc suspicaretur.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

Jesus, traveling through Galilee, being solicited about attending the feast of tabernacles, warns that his time for entering Jerusalem openly has not yet come, but afterwards he went there anyway, where he was sought by the Jews, who held diverse opinions about him; he taught, however, publicly in the temple to the admiration of the Jews, testifying that his doctrine was that of him by whom he was sent, and that he sought only his honor, that none of them kept the law of Moses, and yet they sought his death for a single work on the Sabbath, namely, of a man healed, in which they do not hesitate to perform circumcision. But to some who were doubting whether he was the Christ, because they knew where he was from, he replies: that he was not sent by himself, but by the Truthful One, whom they did not know: for which some wanted to apprehend him, but many believed in him because of the miracles. Jesus says that he is still with them for a short time, and will soon go where they cannot come, which they not understanding thought he would go to the Greeks; but Jesus on the last day of the feast taught publicly about the discourses of the water of life and the giving of the Holy Spirit; some hold him to be a Prophet, others the Christ, others raise a doubt because Christ ought to come not from Galilee, but from Bethlehem. But the priests and Pharisees sent servants to capture him, and when they did not dare to do so, Nicodemus warns that no one judges the law before the case is known; to which they retort that no Prophet arises from Galilee, and they depart with the matter unfinished.

There are three parts: I. His secret journey to the feast of tabernacles, to v. 13. II. His public profession concerning the divinity of his doctrine, with an Apology for the man healed on the Sabbath and the consequences, to v. 36. III. The solemn promise of the Holy Spirit to those who shall have believed in him, and the account of the various judgments concerning him.

PART I. His secret journey to the feast of tabernacles.

Vers. 1. Καὶ περιεπάτει) הִתְהַלֵּךְ which the Syriac has here most frequently signifies to dwell and abide in some place. The Hellenists translate this περιπατεῖν, as in Dan. IV. 26, above VI. v. 66, below XI. 54.

ANNOTATIONS ON JOHN.

μετὰ ταῦτα) That is, even after those things which have already been narrated had happened, he continued to live in Galilee, from whence he had come there: which was narrated above VI. 1.

Why should the customary and proper sense of the word περιπατεῖν not be retained, since he did not stay in one place, but walked through the cities and villages of Galilee, and preached everywhere in the same, Christ? For that conversation was of six months, which flowed between the feast of the Passover, which is celebrated in the first month, and the feast of Tabernacles, which was held in the seventh month, Matt. XVIII. Pelargus noting on this passage.

οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν) It seems the most ancient reading was οὐκ ἐδύνατο, which was changed by the fastidious, as if it did an injury to Christ's power: when it signifies nothing other than that he could not safely dwell in Jerusalem at that time, with the recent fame ignited, and the hatreds not yet sufficiently extinguished.

What, I pray, is the cause for this suspicion of an altered text, given such a great consensus of Codices, and words, and interpreters? Beautifully here Augustine, tractate XXVIII on John: He who had the power to overcome all, wished to decline persecutions for the sake of his faithful, in whom such power does not reside: so that he might teach that sometimes they are to be declined: because one must not rashly rush into the midst of dangers.

οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι) The common people incited by the leaders, through sedition as often: which kind of death, as not being suitable to the Father's institution, Christ avoided.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Iesus Galilæam peragrans de festo tabernacu- lorum frequentando solicitatus, suum tem- pus nondum adesse monet palam ingredien- di Hierosolymam, postea autem etiam se eo contulit, ubi quærebatur à Iudæis, diversa judicia de eo ferentibg; docebat tamẽ publi- ce in templo cum admiratione Iudæorum, testatus, suam doctrinam ejus esse, à quo missus est, seœ, ejus honorem unice quærere, neminem ex ipsis Mosis legem servare, & quærere tamen ipsos suam cædem ob unicum in Sabbato opus, sanati scilicet hominis, in quo ipsi circumcisionem peragere non dubi- tant. Nonnullis autem ex eo ipsum Chri- stum esse ambigentibus, quod scirent unde ipse esset, respondet: se non à seipso, sed à Verace missum, quem ipsi non norint: unde ipsum quidă apprehendere volebant, multi autem ob miracula in ipsum credebant. Ie- sus se exiguo tempore ipsis adhuc adesse, brevi iturum eo, quo ipsi venire nequeant, quod non intelligentes eum ad Græcos pro- fecturum censebant; Iesus autem ultimo festi die de sermonibus aquæ vitæ, & Spiri- tu S. donando publice docuit, alii eum Pro- phetam, alii Christum habent, alii dubium movent, quod Christus non è Galilæa, sed Bethlehem prodire debeat. Sacerdotes au- tem & Pharisæi servos ad eum capiendum emittebant, his vero id non audentibant, Nicodemus monet, non judicare quemquam legem, antequam causa cognoscatur; cui re- gerunt, quod nullus Propheta è Galilæa o- riatur, req; infecta discedunt.

Partes sunt tres: I. Clancularia ad festum ta- bernaculorum profectio, ad v. 13. II. Publica de divinitate doctrinæ suæ professio, cum Apologia sa- nati id Sabbato hominis & consequentibus, ad v. 36. III Spiritus S. illis, qui in se crediderint, solennis promissio, & diversorum judiciorum de ipso relatio.

PARS I. Clancularia ad festum tabernaculorum profectio.

Vers. 1. Καὶ περιεπάτει) הִתְהַלֵּךְ quod hic habet Syrus fre- quentissime significat in loco aliquo degere atque versari. Id περιπατεῖν vertunt Hellenistæ, ut Dan. IV. 26. supra VI. v. 66. infra XI. 54.

ANNOT. AD JOHAN.

μετὰ ταῦτα) Id est, etiam postquam acciderant, quæ jam narrata sunt, perrexit vivere in Galilæa, ex quo eo venerat: quod narratum est supra VI. 1.

Cur non retinendus sensus usitatus, & proprius verbi περιπατεῖν, quum non uno loco commorato sit, sed civitates & vicos Galilææ perambularit, & passim in eadem prædicarit Christus? Conversa- tio enim illa fuit sex mensium, qui interfluxerunt inter festum Paschatos, quod primo mense celebra- tur, & festum Scenopegiæ, quod septimo agebatur mense Matth. XVIII. Pelargo notante in h. l.

οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν) Videtur antiquissima lectio fuisse οὐκ ἐδύνατο quod mutatum à delicatis, quasi Christi potentiæ injuriam faceret: cum nihil aliud significet quam non potuisse eum tuto eo tempore Hierosolymis versari, accensis recente fa- ma, nec dum satis restinctis odiis.

Quænam, obsecro, causa in tanto consensu Codicum, & verborum, & interpretum, hujus suspicionis immutati textus? Pulchre hic August. tr. XXVIII. in Joh. Qui potestatem habuit omnes su- perandi, persecutiones voluit declinare propter suos fideles, quibus talis non inest potestas: ut doceat ali- quando esse declinandas: quia in media pericula te- mere non est irruendum.

οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι) Plebs incitatu primorum, per seditionem ut sæpe: quod genus mortis ut non aptum Patris instituto vi- tabat Christus.

## 7:2
Vers. 2. ἡ σκηνοπηγία) As often as John explicitly mentions a proper name of time or place, he does it mostly with Emphasis. The Scenopegia recalled to the Jews that time when they had lived in a military fashion in vast and uncultivated places under the protection of God, Lev. XXIII. 43.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ἡ σκηνοπηγία) Quoties temporis aut loci nomen proprium diserte memorat Johannes, facit id plerumque cum Emphasi. Scenopegia Judæis in memoriam revocabat tempus illud, quo in locis vastis atque incultis sub Dei præ- sidio militariter habitaverant, Lev. XXIII. 43.

## 7:3
V. 3. οἱ ἀδελφοὶ) Galilean kinsmen of Mary, whose descendants a later age called desposynous.

Μετάβηθι) It is of those urging: depart from these hiding places: for Galilee was an ignoble region compared to the Jerusalemite part, where the senate is, where such a multitude of people, such a multitude of foreigners.

ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου) Who there began to be your listeners and supporters.

τὰ ἔργα σου ἃ ποιεῖς) This is because he had done greater and more things in Galilee than in Judea.

Latin:

V. 3. οἱ ἀδελφοὶ) Galilæi cognati Mariæ, quorum poste- ros δεσποσύνους vocavit ætas posterior.

Μετάβηθι) Excitantium est: excede ex his latebris: nam Galilæa ignobilis erat regio præ parte Hierosolymitana, ubi senatus, ubi tanta populi, tanta exterorum multitudo.

ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου) Qui ibi cœperunt auditores tui & fautores esse.

τὰ ἔργα σου ἃ ποιεῖς) Hoc ideo, quia majora & plura in Galilæa fecerat, quam in Judæa.

## 7:4
V. 4. οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἐν κρυπτῷ τι ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ) It is a Hebraism placing a copula for a relative. For no one does anything in secret who desires to be famous, which they themselves opined about Christ, measuring another by their own character. For they themselves sought glory for themselves from his fame: This, as is credible, especially wishing, that Jesus' authority be approved by the Sanhedrin. See below 26.

ἐν παῤῥησίᾳ εἶναι) To be clear. For the Jews received the word παῤῥησία from the Macedonians, but with an extension of meaning: for it often signifies security leading to confidence, as Lev. XXVI. 13. and below XI. 54. Heb. X. 19. sometimes the clarity of a name or deed, Col. II. 15. as noted by others.

εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς) ποιεῖν here signifies in the power of doing perpetually. If you can, they say, and where and as often as you wish to do such things, to change water into wine, to multiply loaves as if to infinity.

Φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ) To a great multitude of men, such as is at Jerusalem as below XII. 19.

Latin:

V. 4. οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἐν κρυπτῷ τι ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ) Est Hebraismus copulam ponens, pro relativo. Nemo enim clam sua agit qui celeber esse cupiat, quod ipsi de Christo opinabantur, ex suo ingenio metientes alienum. Nam ipsi ex ipsius cele- britate sibi gloriam quærebant: Hoc, ut credibile est, præ- cipue optantes, ut Jesu auctoritas à Synedrio approbaretur. Vide infra 26.

ἐν παῤῥησίᾳ εἶναι) Clarus esse. Nam vocem παῤῥησίας à Macedonibus acceperunt Judæi, sed significatu extensione: sæpe enim significat securitatem ad fiduciam, ut Levit. XXVI. 13. & infra XI. 54. Hebr. X. 19. interdum claritatem nominis aut facti, Col. II. 15. ut ab aliis notatum.

εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς) ποιεῖν hic potestate in perpetuam faciendi significat. Si potes, inquiunt, & ubi & quoties vis talia fa- cere, aquam mutare in vinum, panes quasi in infinitum multiplicare.

Φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ) Magnæ hominum multitu- dini, qualis est Hierosolymis ut infra XII. 19.

## 7:5
V. 5. ἐπίστευον) Not entirely, not as they ought. They hoped for something great from him, but they had determined nothing certain among themselves, nor did they obey him.

His kinsmen seem to have given this advice, because they themselves did not believe, that he should go into Judea to the experts in the law, who might pass a better judgment on his signs than the Galileans, who were for the most part unlettered and ignorant: although they pretend this reason, so that the disciples there might also see his works, and Christ himself might become known to all in a celebrated place and time.

Latin:

V. 5. ἐπίστευον) Non omnino, non ut oportebat. Spera- bant aliquid magni de illo, sed nihil certi apud se consti- tuerant, neque ei parebant.

Consilium hoc videntur consanguinei illi dedis- se, quia ipsi non credebant, ut in Judæam proficisce- retur ad legis peritos, qui melius de signis judi- cium ferrent, quam Galilæi ἀγράμματοι fere & ignari: Etsi prætexant hanc causam, ut & discipu- li istic videant opera ejus, & Christus ipse loco ac tempore celebri omnibus innotescat.

## 7:6
V. 6. ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς ὔπω πάρεστιν) Feast days have their own καιροὺς מועדים Lev. XXIII. 4. the καιρὸς τῆς σκηνοπηγίας is the time for gathering the fruits of the field into the barn, ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ γῇ τῶν ἔργων τῶν ἄγρου, Exod. XXIII 16. It is Christ's custom to elude those who come for the sake of tempting him through allegorical expressions. Thus he acted concerning the destruction of the Temple, thus concerning the eating of his body and blood; most things are of this kind. They wanted Jesus to go up to Jerusalem, because it was already the time for gathering the fruits; Christ artfully indicates that the time for gathering his own fruits had not yet arrived. ὔπω, he says, it has not yet come. For it was to come both after the Passover and after Pentecost: that is, after his death and resurrection, and after the inscription of the new law in the hearts of the Apostles through the Spirit. For not long after, the faithful began to be gathered everywhere in the world, and the name of JESUS began to be celebrated, in παῤῥησίᾳ. Thus συνάγειν is taken above IV. 36.

ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος) It is always ready for you to gather your fruits, the favor of men and the comforts of this life.

It is not asserted with sufficient reverence concerning Christ, the best and heavenly Master, and the very Son of God, and Teacher of the world, who wishes all to come to the knowledge of the truth, that he was accustomed to ELUDE men through allegorical expressions. Nor do the examples concerning the destruction of the Temple, the eating of his body, or this passage teach that. In which part Grotius imitates the impious language of the Socinians and Drejer. Furthermore, καιρὸς τῆς σκηνοπηγίας does not signify the time of gathering fruits, but the feast of Scenopegia, even if this was celebrated at that time when the fruits were being gathered: nor does Christ name the καιρὸν τῆς σκηνοπηγίας: or indicate that he is looking toward the gathering of spiritual fruits to be instituted after the resurrection. He says simply that his time had not yet come: but he does not hint that it was to come with his impending passion and the resurrection that would follow; nor could he hint that: because he was not expecting a fourth Passover, but was betaking himself to Jerusalem at this very feast of tabernacles. However, there is no contradiction in the fact that he says here: my time has not yet come, therefore I will not go up to that feast: and that he nevertheless betook himself to Jerusalem for that feast. Various answers are brought forward, which Pelargus collected, and from him the blessed Waltherus: the sixth of which is approved by them, namely that some rightly maintain that the negation is not absolute but feigned, and restricted (in the Greek text) containing in itself something of an affirmation, because the particle ὔπω NONDUM is added, as if to say: not at this time, but he will go up when the time is fulfilled. But Grotius prefers the Latin text here, and decides that this was entirely the old reading ἐγὼ ὀυκ ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην! But what is the very grave cause for which he here accuses all the Greek Codices of corruption? If, says Grotius, ὔπω had been there in Porphyry's time, he would never have slandered Christ from this place regarding a lie; for in the word ὔπω would have been the solution of the knot, which others, to escape, wrote ὔπω, others ὀυκ ἀναβαίνω νῦν, others again deleted ταύτην. But be it that there was a variety of Codices, and Porphyry read it as purely negative, whose accusation is found in book II of Jerome against Pelagius, must that reading which is now found in all the Codices therefore be rejected? But in truth, even if the negative is retained, I do not go up, the sense is still clear, namely that Christ does not go up with the disciples, or does not go up openly, or with a common progressive movement: since he was not ignorant of the secret machinations of his adversaries; whence he is said to have gone up indeed, but after his brothers had gone up, and not with them, and to have gone up ὀὐ φανερῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ v. 10. therefore there is no difficulty here: nor is there any need to invent with Grotius another and mystical sense here, which certainly rests on no foundation. He said here (these are Grotius's words) ἑορτὴν ταύτην just as ἐκ τοῦτο γεννήματος ἲ ἀμπέλου Matt. XXVI. 29. in both cases in a mystical sense the feast of tabernacles of Christ is that time when churches began to be established everywhere, Apoc. XIII. 6. when Japheth also began to dwell in the tents of Shem, according to the mystical sense, Gen. X. 27. The discussion was not about the time of establishing the Churches, but about the feast of tabernacles. Nor does any trace of that appear in the text: and without that foreign sense, which has not come into anyone's mind until now, nor could have come, the matter can be resolved in the way we have stated.

Latin:

V. 6. ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς ὔπω πάρεστιν) Dies festi habent suos καιροὺς מועדים Lev. XXIII. 4. καιρὸς τῆς σκηνοπηγίας est tem- pus colligendarum in horreum frugum agri, ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ γῇ τῶν ἔργων τῶν ἄγρου, Exod. XXIII 16. Mos Christi est, eos qui tentandi causa adveniunt, per allegoricas locutiones e- ludere. Sic de Templo destruendo, sic de manducando corpore & sanguine suo egit, pleraque sunt ejusmodi. Vo- lebant Jesum adscendere Hierosolyma, quia jam ipsum tempus esset colligendarum frugum, Christus artificiose in- dicat suarum frugum colligendarum tempus nondum ad- venisse. ὔπω ait, nondum venit. Venire enim debebat & post Pascha & post Pentecosten: id est post mortem & resurre- ctionem, & post inscriptionem legis novæ in cordibus Apostolorum per Spiritum. Non multo enim post cœ- perunt colligi fideles ubique terrarum, & nomen JESU cœpit esse celebre, in παῤῥησίᾳ. Sic συνάγειν sumitur supra IV. 36.

ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος) Vobis sem- per promtum est colligere fructus vestros, hominum gra- tiam & hujus vitæ commoda.

Non satis religiose de Christo, optimo, & cœ- lesti Magistro, ipsóque Dei Filio, ac Doctore orbis, qui omnes vult ad agnitionem veritatis venire, af- firmatur, quod homines consueverit per allegoricas locutiones ELUDERE. Nec id exempla de Tem- plo destruendo, de corpore suo manducando, aut hic locus docent. Qua in parte Socinianorum & Dreje- ri impiam linguam imitatur Grotius. Porro καιρὸς τῆς σκηνοπηγίας non significat tempus colligendarum frugum, sed festum Scenopegias, etsi hoc isto tem- pore, cum fruges colligerentur, celebraretur: nequ; Christus nominat καιρὸν τῆς σκηνοπηγίας: aut indi- cat, se spiritualium frugum collectionē post resur- rectionem instituendam respicere. Simpliciter di- cit, nondum venisse tempus suum: non autem quod venturum id sit, imminente passione sua, eamq; in secutura resurrectione, innuit; nec id innuere po- terat: quia non expectabat quartum Pascha, sed hoc ipso festo tabernaculorum Hierosolymam se confe- rebat. Nulla autem in eo est ἀντιλογία, quod hic dicit: nondum tempus meum venit, ergo non adscendā ad festum illud: & quod nihilominus se Hierosoly- mam illo festo contulerit. Variæ adferuntur re- sponsiones, quas collegit Pelargus, & ex eo B. Wal- therus: quarum sexta illis probatur, quod nempe εὐλόγως statuant nonnulli, non absolutam sed simula- tam esse negationem, & restrictam (in Græco textu) affirmationis aliquid in se continentem, quia adjecta sit particula ὔπω NONDUM, q. d. non hoc, sed im- pleto se ascensurum tempore. Sed Grotius præfert hic Latinum textum, ac decernit, omnino hanc fuisse veterem scripturam ἐγὼ ὀυκ ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην! Quænam vero tam gravis causa, ob quam corruptionis hic arguat omnes Græcos Codi- ces? Si, inquit Grotius, ὔπω fuisset Porphyrii tem- pore, nunquam hinc Christum calumniatus esset de mendacio; nam in voce ὔπω fuisset nodi solutio, quem ut evaderent alii ὔπω scripserunt, alii ὀυκ ἀναβαίνω νῦν alii rursum deleverunt ταύτην. At esto, varietas fue- rit Codicum, & Porphyrius legerit pure negative, cujus criminatio l. II. Hieron. adv. Pelag. habetur, num ideo illa, quæ in Codd. omnibus jam reperi- tur lectio, reprobanda? Verum enim vero etiamsi negativa retineatur, non ascendo, sensus in vado ad- huc est, nimirum non ascendere Christum cum di- scipulis, vel non ascendere palam, aut motu progres- sivo communi: quum non ignorarit adversariorum suorum occultas molitiones; unde ascendisse qui- dem ipse dicitur, sed postquam ascenderunt fratres ejus, non vero cum iisdem, & ascendisse ὀὐ φανερῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ v. 10. ideo nulla hic difficultas: nec opus est cum Grotio alium, & mysticum hic co- minisci sensum, qui nullo certe nititur fundamen- to. Dixit hic (verba Grotii sunt) ἑορτὴν ταύτην sic- ut ἐκ τοῦτο γεννήματος ἲ ἀμπέλου Matt. XXVI. 29. utrumq; sensu mystico festum tabernaculorum Christi est illud tempus, quo constitui passim Ecclesiæ cœpe- runt, Apoc. XIII. 6. cum habitare etiam Japhet cœpit in tabernaculis Sem, juxta sensum mysticum, Gen. X. 27. Non sermo erat de tempore constituendarum Ecclesiarum, sed de festo tabernaculorum. Nec de illo vestigium ullum in textu apparet: & sine isto peregrino sensu, qui nulli hactenus in mentem ve- nit, aut venire potuit, res expediri potest eo, quo diximus, modo.

## 7:7
V. 7. ὀὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς) By a certain general hatred, of course, such as that with which Christ was received, and for a long time Christians: for that is not born, except from a dogma which is repugnant to the affections of the greater part of men. ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἀυτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα ἀυτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι) The integrity of my dogma, compared with their life, shows how foul that is. See above

Latin:

V. 7. ὀὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς) Generali quodam odio scilicet, quale fuit quo Christus exceptus est, & diu Christiani: nam illud non nascitur, nisi ex dogmate quod maxime partis hominum affectibus repugnat. ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἀυτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα ἀυτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι) Probitas dogmatis mei collata cum ipsorum vita quam ea foeda sit ostendit. Vide supra III. 19. Conf. Sap. II. 12.

## 7:8
V. 8. Go you up to this feast) This was entirely an ancient reading, for if ὔπω had been there in Porphyry's time, he would never have slandered Christ from this passage regarding a lie: for in the word ὔπω would have been the solution of the knot, which, in order to escape, some wrote ὔπω, others ὐκ ἀναβαίνω νῦν, others again deleted ταύτην. For all of which there is no need. He said here ἑορτὴν ταύτην, just as ἐκ τοῦ γεννήμαῒ @ τῆς ἀμπέλε. Matt. XXVI. 29. Both in a mystical sense: the feast of tabernacles of Christ is that time when churches began to be established everywhere, Apoc. XIII. 6. when Japheth also began to dwell in the tents of Shem, according to the mystical sense, Gen. X. 27.

for my time is not yet fulfilled) πληρῦσθαι or συμπληρῦσθαι is properly said of a certain time which must be awaited, as Lev. XXV. 20. Num. VI. 5. Act. II. 1. VI. 23. Gal. IV. 4. Luc. XXI. 24. First it was necessary for Jesus to be established as king: then his sceptre had to go out from Sion: finally he had to fix the very broad seats of his kingdom.

These things according to that new interpretation, which we have already touched upon, Grotius. But we have warned that there is no need for it. Those words harmonize with those which are held at John II. 4. ὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα με. For just as there he says his hour has not yet come, and soon performs what was requested by his Mother, so he acted here also; and by this he warned that the opportunity of times was known to no one but himself, and that this was his primary concern, that he might fulfill the whole economy, and therefore that he deservedly avoided dangers of any kind: which those things also hint at: the world cannot hate you, but it hates me: therefore since it is always permitted for you to go where you wish, because nothing stands in the way, I must act circumspectly, and the opportunity must be reserved for me alone, nor must my counsel be communicated to others, much less will I expose myself by traveling openly with others, knowing and being aware of the danger. Whence regarding those words v. 10. 8 Φανερῶς, Grotius is not wrong, lest if the people were to come from Galilee all the way to Jerusalem in a large retinue, he would further inflame the spirits stirred up against him.

Latin:

V. 8. Ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην) Omnino fuit haec vetus scriptura, nam si ὔπω fuisset Porphyrii tempore, nunquam hinc Christum calumniatus esset de mendacio: nam in voce ὔπω fuisset nodi solutio, quem ut evaderent alii ὔπω scripserunt, alii ὐκ ἀναβαίνω νῦν, alii rursum deleverunt ταύτην. Quibus omnibus nihil opus. Dixit hic ἑορτὴν ταύτην, sicut ἐκ τότε γεννήμαῒ @ τῆς ἀμπέλε. Matt. XXVI. 29. Utrumq; sensu mystico: festum tabernaculorum Christi est illud tempus quo constitui passim Ecclesiae coeperunt, Apoc. XIII. 6. cum habitare etiam Japhet coepit in tabernaculis Sem, juxta sensum mysticum, Gen. X. 27.

ὅτι ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς ὔπω πεπλήρωται) πληρῦσθαι aut συμπληρῦσθαι proprie dicitur de certo tempore quod exspectandum est ut Lev. XXV. 20. Num. VI. 5. Act. II. 1. VI. 23. Gal. IV. 4. Luc. XXI. 24. Primum oportebat Jesum regem constitui: deinde exire debebat sceptrum ejus ex Sione: postremo figere debebat latissimas regni sui sedes.

Haec juxta illam novellam interpretationem, quam jam attigimus, Grotius. Sed ea opus non esse monuimus. Verba illa consonant iis, quae Job. II. 4. habentur ὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα με. Nam quemadmodum illic nondum venisse horam suam dicit, & mox praestat, quod à Matre poscebatur, ita etiam hic egit; eoque monuit, opportunitatem temporum non alii, quam sibi notam, id autem sibi cumprimis curae esse, ut oeconomiam totam expleat, ideoque pericula quaecunq; merito & se cavere: quod illa etiam innuunt: non potest mundus vos odisse, me autem odit: itaque cum vobis semper liceat abire, quo vultis, quia nihil obstat, mihi circumspecte agendum, ac soli mihi reservanda opportunitas, nec aliis communicandum consilium meum, multo minus cum aliis palam proficiscendo me exponam sciens prudens periculo. Unde ad illa v. 10. 8 Φανερῶς non male Grotius, ne si populus magno comitatu à Galilaea usque Hierosolyma veniret, concitatos in se animos magis accenderet.

## 7:9
V. 9. He remained in Galilee) He stayed for some time as the following things show.

Latin:

V. 9. ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ) Substitit aliquamdiu ut sequentia ostendunt.

## 7:10
V. 10. 8 not openly but as it were in secret) Lest if the people were to come from Galilee all the way to Jerusalem in a large retinue, he would further inflame the spirits stirred up against him.

Latin:

V. 10. 8 φανερῶς ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ) Ne si populus magno comitatu à Galilaea usque Hierosolyma veniret, concitatos in se animos magis accenderet.

## 7:11
V. 11. The Jews therefore) It is often John's custom to take the word 'Jews' by way of eminence, to signify the senators, as appears shortly at 23. See above V. 16.

were seeking him at the feast) They were wondering that he was hiding, who was accustomed to show himself at such times and to provide an opportunity for himself to be heard.

where is that man) Contemptuously, as Matt. XXVII. 63. So also below 35.

Latin:

V. 11. οἱ ὖν Ἰεδαῖοι) Mos saepe est Iohanni vocem Ἰουδαίων sumere κατ' ἐξοχὴν, ut senatores significet, ut apparet mox 23. Vide supra V. 16.

ἐζήτεν ἀυτὸν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ) Mirabantur eum latere qui solitus erat, se talibus ostendere & audiendi sui copiam facere.

ποῦ ἐσιν ἐκεῖνος) Contemtim ut Matt. XXVII. 63. Sic & infra 35.

## 7:12
v. 12. Much murmuring) Whispers.

that he is good) The Galileans said this mostly, who had experienced his kindness both in deeds and in his words.

πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον) As if he were teaching to despise the Sabbath,

Latin:

v. 12. Γογγυσμὸς πολὺς) Susurri.

ὅτι ἀγαθός ἐσιν) Hoc dicebant maxime Galilaei, qui & fatis & verbis ipsius comitatem erant experti.

πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον) Quasi doceret contemnere Sabbatum,

## 7:13
V. 13. ὐδεὶς μέν τοι) This κ' ὄψιν is to be referred to those who are better disposed.

παῤῥησίᾳ) In the presence of all or many, so that it could be reported to the ears of the senators.

PART II. Public profession concerning the divinity of his Doctrine, with an apology for the man healed on the Sabbath and the consequences.

Latin:

V. 13. ὐδεὶς μέν τοι) Hoc κ' ὄψιν ad melius sentientes referendum est.

παῤῥησίᾳ) Coram omnibus aut multis, ita ut ad senatorum aures renuntiari posset.

PARS II. Publica de divinitate Doctrinae sua professio, cum apologia sanati in Sabbato hominis & consequentibus.

## 7:14
V. 14. Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης) We have said at Matt. xxvi. 5 that the whole time of eight days, of which the first and last were properly sacred, is also called a feast by Josephus. Jesus was waiting for that time when the Jews, being free from sacrifices, could be more at leisure for hearing

ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν κὶ ἐδίδασκε) Then for the first time he came there to teach. The conjunction is used for a final clause.

We add the annotation of B. Quistorpius, cited by Walaeus: V. 9. it is said that he remained in Galilee, in this verse it is said that he went up to the feast, v. 14. that in the middle of the feast he went up into the temple: there is no contradiction here. For he followed his brothers who were going to the Feast immediately on the first day of the feast, with whom, as God had commanded, he celebrated the feast for seven days; for he is not to be thought to have done anything against the law. But he went up into the temple only in the middle of the feast, for the feast is not celebrated in the temple, but in the field, in constructed tabernacles.

Latin:

V. 14. Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης) ἑορτὴν etiam Iosepho dici totum tempus octo dieru, quorum primus & ultimus proprie sacri erant, diximus ad Matt. xxvi. 5. Exspectabat Iesus id tempus quo Iudaei à sacrificiis vacui magis possent vacare auditioni

ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν κὶ ἐδίδασκε) Tum primum eo venit ad docendum. Copula pro finali.

Addimus B. Quistorpii annotationem, à Walaeo adductam: V. 9. dicitur mansisse in Galilaea, hoc versu dicitur ascendisse ad festum, v. 14. medio festo ascendisse in templum: nulla hic est pugna. Nam praecedentes ad Festum fratres statim insecutus est primo festi die, quibuscum, ut Deus mandarat, per septiduum festum celebravit; non enim putandus est, contra legem quidquam fecisse. Medio autem festo demum ascendit in templum, non enim in templo, sed in campo, in ex- structis tabernaculis festum celebratur.

## 7:15
V. 15. ἐθαύμαζον) See Matt. XIII. 55. The scribes and the craftsman are contrasted, Syr. XXXVIII. 25. 28.

πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδε) ספרה The Syrian, the book, namely of the law, which is τὰ ἱερὰ γράμματα, 2 Tim. III. 15; therefore those who are called teachers of the law are the same as the scribes.

μὴ μεμαθηκώς) No teacher had seen him in the flock of his disciples.

It can also be understood of him who is plainly ἀγράμματος, and unlettered, such as Christ was considered. But let us leave to everyone here free judgment concerning the mind of those censors. Ambrose, book II. on the faith, ch. 4. Since he teaches without the learning of letters, he seems to teach not as a man, but rather as God, who had not learned doctrine, but had found it.

Latin:

V. 15. ἐθαύμαζον) Vide Matth. XIII. 55. Opponuntur γραμματεῖς & τέκτων Syr. XXXVIII. 25. 28.

πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδε) ספרה Syrus, librum, legis scilicet, quæ τὰ ἱερὰ γράμματα, 2. Tim. III. 15. ideo qui νομο- διδάσκαλοι vocantur, iidem & γραμματεῖς.

μὴ μεμαθηκώς) Nemo præceptor in discipulorum suorum grege eum viderat.

Potest etiam intelligi de eo, qui plane sit ἀγράμ- ματος, & illiteratus, qualis Christus habebatur. Sed liberum hic cuivis relinquamus judicium de men- te illorum censorum. Ambros. l. II. de fid. c. 4. Cum sine eruditione literarum doceat, non quasi homo, sed potius ut Deus videtur docere, qui doctrinam non didicerat, sed invenerat.

## 7:16
V. 16. ἡ ἐμὴ διδαχὴ) Which is brought forth by my mouth.

οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ) It is not something that I have acquired for myself by my own industry, so that from it, as men are accustomed to do, I might seek glory. See shortly 18.

ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με) He instilled in me what I should say, above III. 32.

Latin:

V. 16. ἡ ἐμὴ διδαχὴ) Quæ meo ore promitur.

οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ) Non est aliquid quod industria mea mihi comparaverim, ut inde, quod homines solent, gloriam ve- ner. Vide mox 18.

ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με) Is mihi indidit quid dicerem, su- pra III. 32.

## 7:17
V. 17. ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν) If anyone is so disposed in mind that he is willing to embrace with an obedient spirit whatever will of God is revealed to him, however much it may be contrary to the affections of the flesh.

γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς) He at last will be fit to judge concerning my teaching, since he has a mind that is not hindered: just as eyes judge correctly concerning colors only when they are not suffused with any corrupt humor. For otherwise, we do not easily believe those things which we would wish to be false. Add that God illuminates those who do not patronize their own vices. It is Plato's: ᾖ καθαρῷ γὰρ καθαροῦ ἐφάπτεσθαι οὐ θεμιτόν. And so that is also true: τῷ γὰρ ποιοῦντι τὸ θεῖον ξυλλαμβάνει. Chrysostom in IX. ad Rom., when he had interpreted προσκόπτειν as ἀπιστεῖν, adds: "But stumbling comes from not paying attention, from being occupied with other things."

ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ) See above V. 30.

Dubium, quod hic occurrit, sic expedit Camero: Since no one can do the will of God whom he has not acknowledged, what is it that Christ says here, if anyone is willing to execute his will, he will judge, or will know, concerning the doctrine? For he wishes (as it seems) that to precede which by its nature follows, namely, he wishes executing the will to precede, but judging concerning the doctrine to follow; but the matter seems to be the opposite, for it is necessary that judgment precede, and the will follow. Nor is it right here to argue with some in such a way that we say it is one thing to wish to do the will of the Father, but another to give it effect: For truly he who is seriously led by a zeal for true piety, he is already by this very fact, without controversy, pious: But he who has no piety which truly precedes the knowledge of doctrine, since the rule of all piety is doctrine. Itaq; aliud respondendum est: Namely, Christ does not say he will know concerning the doctrine simply, but, he will know περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς: for not every doctrine is ἡ διδαχὴ, only ἡ διδαχὴ κατ' ἐξοχὴν is called (in this place indeed) the preaching of Christ, which does not exclude all preceding knowledge, but only that which (as we have already said) can be called Doctrine κατ' ἐξοχὴν. Thus when in chapter 1 of this Gospel Christ says, no one has ever seen the Father, the Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has revealed him to us, not every preceding revelation is excluded, nor every knowledge of the truth, but only a certain singular and principal knowledge, which differs not in species, but in degree from that knowledge of which the author was Christ acting on earth. Which example, however, is not approved by us. Because no one knows anything about spiritual things without the manifestation of the Son of God, Matt. XI. 26.

Latin:

V. 17. ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν) Si quis ita animo comparatus sit, ut qualemcunque voluntatem Dei sibi re- velatam, quantumcunque carnis affectibus contrariam, ob- sequenti animo amplecti velit.

γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς) Is demum aptus erit ut judicet de meo dogmate, quippe mentem habens non impeditam: sicut oculi de coloribus tum demum recte judicant cum nullo pravo humore suffusi sunt. Alioqui enim quæ falsa es- se vellemus, ea non facile credimus. Adde quod Deus illu- strat eos qui vitiis suis non patrocinantur. Platonis est ᾖ κα- θαρῷ γὰρ καθαροῦ ἐφάπτεσθαι οὐ θεμιτόν. Adeo & illud verum: τῷ γὰρ ποιοῦντι τὸ θεῖον ξυλλαμβάνει. Chrysostomus in IX. ad Rom. cum προσκόπτειν interpreta- tus esset ἀπιστεῖν addit: τὸ δὲ προσκόπτειν ἐκ τοῦ μὴ προσέχειν γίνεται, ἐκ τοῦ πρὸς ἕτερα κεχρῆσθαι.

ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ) Vide supra V. 30.

Dubium, quod hic occurrit, sic expedit Came- ro: Cum nemo possit facere voluntatem Dei quam non agnoverit, quid est quod Christus hic dicit, si quis voluerit ejus voluntatem exequi, judicabit, vel co- gnoscet, de doctrina? Vult enim (uti videtur) ante- cedere id quod natura sua sequitur, nempe vult ante- cedere, exequi voluntatem, sequi autem judicare de doctrina, at contra se res habere videtur, necesse est enim præcedere judicium, voluntatem autem sequi. Neq; fas est hic cum nonnullis ita argutari, ut dica- mus, aliud esse, velle facere voluntatem Patris, aliud vero eam effectam dare: Nam profecto qui serio du- citur veræ pietatis studio, is jam hoc ipso sine contro- versia, pius est: At cui nulla est pietas quæ vere do- ctrinæ cognitionem præcedat, cum pietatis omnis re- gula sit doctrina. Itaq; aliud respondendum est: Nem- pe, non dicit Christus, cognoscet de doctrina simpli- citer, sed, cognoscet περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς: non enim omnis doctrina est ἡ διδαχὴ, tantum ἡ διδαχὴ κατ' ἐξοχὴν vocatur, (hoc quidem loco) Christi prædicatio, quæ non excludit omnem præcedaneam cognitionem, sed eam tantum quæ (uti jam diximus) κατ' ἐξοχὴν Doctrina dici possit. Sic quum c. 1. hujus Evangelii Christus di- cit, Patrem nemo vidit unquam, Filius, qui est in si- nu Patris, nobis eum revelavit, non excluditur omnis præcedens revelatio, neq; omnis cognitio veritatis, sed duntaxat singularis quædam cognitio ac præcipua, quæ non specie, sed gradu distat ab ea cognitione, cujus author fuit Christus agens in terris. Quod tamen ex- emplum nobis non probatur. Quia nemo quic- quam de rebus spiritualibus novit sine manifesta- tione Filii Dei, Matth. XI. 26.

## 7:18
v. 18. ὁ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν, τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ) There is no one who falsely proclaims himself sent by God, unless by that thing he hunts for honor and the advantages that follow honor. No one is evil for nothing. ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ i.e., bringing forth his own thoughts, when he should prefer the command of God.

ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν) Whose words and deeds look to nothing else than that God be honored: and who because of these things says nothing for favor, suppresses nothing of saving truth however bitter: he does not covet honors, he is content with a very meager life,

ὄντο̂ ἀληθής ἐστι) He is worthy to be believed, see above V. 31.

κὰι ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ ὐκ ἔστι) Here unrighteousness and truth are opposed, 1 Cor. XIII. 6. and imposture is called the deceit of unrighteousness, 2 Thess. II. 10. The sense is: the charge of falsehood against him is not credible, since the motive for lying is absent.

Latin:

v. 18. ὁ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν, τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ) Nemo est qui se à Deo missum falso prædicet, nisi ea re honorẽ & quæ honorẽ. sequuntur commoda venetur. Nemo gratis malus est. ἀφ' ἑ- αυτοῦ i. e. sua cogitata proferens, cum Dei mandatu præferat.

ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν) Cujus & verba & facta non alio spectant, quam ut Deus honoretur: quiq; pro- pter ea nihil ad gratiã dicit, nihil veri salutaris quamvis acer- bi subticet: honores non ambit, vita tenuissima contentus est,

ὄντο̂ ἀληθής ἐστι) Hic dignus est, cui fides habeatur, su- pra V. 31.

κὰι ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ ὐκ ἔστι) Hic ἀδικία & ἀληθεία opponun- tur, 1. Cor. XIII. 6. & impostura vocatur ἀπάτη τῆς ἀδικίας , 2. Thess. II. 10. Sensus est: falsi crimen de eo credibile non est cum absit mentiendi causa.

## 7:19
V. 19. Οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τ̀ νόμον) Deut. XXXIII. 4. He returns to what he had said, that his doctrine was condemned by them because they did not have a ready mind to obey God. Which he proves from the law of Moses, which they could not deny was from God, which they denied concerning Christ's doctrine. That excellent Moses, whose teacher you boast of being.

Οὐδείς ἐξ ὑμῶν ποιεῖ τ̀ νόμον) That is, you do not have a serious purpose to order your life according to that law. Thus Paul calls those who seriously compose themselves to the norm of the law ποιῶν άς νόμυ, even if they perhaps slip in minor matters, Rom. II. 13. See Matt. VII. 23. That 'no one' must be understood ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ concerning the greatest part, as Ps. XIV. 3. Rom. III. 10.

Christ is not speaking of a serious purpose of fulfilling the law, but of the actual fulfillment of the law: and he denies it not only to most, but to all; nor are they considered ποιη- τὰ νόμυ according to the law who slip in some, even minor, matters. For whoever offends in one is held guilty of the whole law. Therefore that 'no one' is to be understood properly and universally, as it sounds, not restrictedly: nor is Ps. XIV. 3. Rom. III. 10. taken restrictedly, but plainly universally, as shown there.

τί με ζητεῖτε ἀποκτεῖναι;) Even by this it appears how far you are from obedience to the law itself, when you wish to put to death me, your innocent fellow-countryman, who has deserved well of you. He attributes to the people, however, that which was proper to the leaders of the people.

Latin:

V. 19. Οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τ̀ νόμον) Deut. XXXIII. 4. redit ad id quod dixerat, suum dogma ab iis ideo damnari, quod animum non haberent promtum, ut Deo obedirent. Quod probat ex lege Mosis, quam à Deo esse negare non poterant, quod de Christi dogmate negabant. Moses ille eximius, quo magistro vos jactatis.

Οὐδείς ἐξ ὑμῶν ποιεῖ τ̀ νόμον) Id est non est vobis serium propositum vitam vel ad illam legem instituendi. Sic ποιῶν άς νόμυ vocat Paulus eos qui ad legis normam serio se com- ponunt, etiamsi forte in minutulis lapsent Rom. II. 13. Vide Matth. VII. 23. Illud autem nemo intelligendum ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ de maxima parte ut Ps. XIV. 3. Rom. III. 10.

Non de serio proposito legem implendi, sed de a- ctuati legis impletione loquitur Christus: nec eam plerisque tantum, sed omnibus denegat; neque ποιη- τὰ νόμυ secundum legem habentur, qui in nonnullis etsi minutulis lapsent. Nam qui in uno offenderit, to- tius legis reus habetur. Ideo illud nemo proprie, & universaliter, ut sonat, non restricte intelligendum: neque Ps. XIV. 3. Rom. III. 10. restricte, sed plane universaliter accipitur, ut illic ostensum.

τί με ζητεῖτε ἀποκτεῖναι;) Vel hoc ipso apparet quam longe ab sitis ab ipsius legis obedientia, cum me popularem vestrum innocentem, bene de vobis meritum, vultis morte afficere, Tribuit autem populo id quod proprium erat pri- morum populi.

## 7:20
V. 20. Δαιμόνιον ἔχεις) The Greeks would say δαιμονᾷς, you are insane: that you are driven by a fury. See Matt. XI. 18. It was not credible to the common people that there was anyone among the people who was plotting the death of Jesus. But certainly Jesus had gained for himself such authority by his deeds that nothing affirmed by him ought to be rashly rejected.

Latin:

V. 20. Δαιμόνιον ἔχεις) Græci dicerent δαιμονᾷς insanis: fu- riz te agitari. Vide Matt. XI. 18. Non fiebat credibile plebi, quenquam in populo esse qui necem Jesu machinaretur. At certe eam sibi autoritatem factis pepererat Jesus, ut nihil ab ipso affirmatum temere deberet rejici.

## 7:21
V. 21. Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησυ̂ς) When he was reviled, he did not revile in return, 1 Pet. II. 22. He responds to the insult by teaching.

ἓν ἔργον ἐποίησα) I did one work, and not a troublesome one, on the Sabbath, by healing a sick man with a word.

κὰι πάντες θαυμάζετε) Which he soon explains as 'you are angry at me.' Thus θαυμάζειν is put for 'to be offended,' Eccl. V. 7. Eccles. XI. 21.

Latin:

V. 21. Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησυ̂ς) λοιδορύμενο̂ ὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, I. Pet. II. 22. Ad convitium docendo respondet.

ἓν ἔργον ἐποίησα) Unum nec molestum opus Sabbato fe- ci, ægrotum voce sanando.

κὰι πάντες θαυμάζετε) Quod mox explicat ἐμοὶ χολᾶτε Sic θαυμάζειν pro offendi ponitur Eccl. V. 7. Eccles. XI. 21.

## 7:22
V. 22. Διὰ τῦτο) ἀκούσατε: supply, hear what I shall say. Because you are offended by that deed, accept my defense. Thus often לכן and על־כן among the Hebrews, as Hos. II. 14.

Quæ non improbamus. Dievius's interpretation tends almost to this, that the sense here is: As to this matter, so that διὰ τῦτο is the same as לכן or על זאת, concerning this matter, as Gen. IV. 15. Hos. II. 14. Who brings forward yet another explanation, that indeed διὰ τῦτο is the same as δι᾿ ὅ, and that על־כן, which signifies not only 'therefore,' but also 'because,' as Gen. XXVIII. 26. Ps. XLII. 7. Num. X. 30. 'Because Moses gave you circumcision,' etc. Franciscus Junius, conformably to that former Dievian one, explains it thus: i.e., 'So that you may see my innocence, here is my defense for you.' Tarnovius had already handed down the Grotian sense: While he says διὰ τῦτο, understand ἀκύετε, 'therefore hear.' A similar locution exists, Matt. XVIII. 22, 23, as Piscator observed. Grotius perhaps followed one or the other of these. Which indeed are more correctly situated than the way Schmidius, against the testimony of the codices, along with Theophylact and Casaubon, drew that διὰ τῦτο to the preceding θαυμάζετε; who certainly acknowledges that there is perhaps no example of this phrase, θαυμάζειν διά τι.

Moses gave you circumcision) He commands it in Lev. XII. 3.

Not that it is of Moses) An explanation of what was said before: not that I say it was first instituted by Moses.

But of the fathers) ἐκ for παρὰ: It comes from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man) That is, a boy, בן אדם. Thus below in VII. 23, that κὰι is explanatory. As if he were saying, therefore, out of reverence for the institution of the fathers, you perform the work on the Sabbath. The opinion of the Hebrews is מילה דוחה את השבת. Circumcision pushes aside the Sabbath.

Latin:

V. 22. Διὰ τῦτο) ἀκούσατε: supple, audite quod dicam. Quia eo facto offendimini, accipite meam purgationem. Sic sæpe לכן & על־כן apud Ebræos, ut Os. II. 14.

Quæ non improbamus. Eo fere abit Dievii in- terpretatio, quod hic sensus sit: Quod ad hanc rem, ut διὰ τῦτο idem sit, quod לכן vel על זאת, de hac re, ut Gen. IV. 15. Os. II. 14. Qui aliam adhuc profert explicationem, quod nempe διὰ τῦτο idem sit quod δι᾿ ὅ, & quod על־כן, quod non tantum si- gnificat propterea, sed etiã propterea quod, ut Genes. XXVIII. 26. Ps. XLII. 7. Num. X. 30. Propterea quod Moses vobis dedit circumcisionem &c. Franciscus Junius priori illi Dievianæ conformiter h. m: ex- ponit: q. d. Propterea ut meam innocentiam videa- tis, en vobis defensionem meam. Grotianum vero sensum jam tradiderat Tarnovius: Dum dicit διὰ τῦτο, subintellige ἀκύετε, propterea audite. Similis loquutio extat, Matth. XVIII. 22. 23. ut observavit Piscator. Horum forte alterutrum sequutus est Grotius. Quæ sane rectius se habent, quam quod Schmidius contra Codd. fidem cum Theophylacto & Casaubono illud διὰ τῦτο ad præcedens θαυμά- ζετε traxit; qui utiq; agnoscit, non dari fortassis ex- emplum hujusce phraseos, θαυμάζειν διά τι.

Μωσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὴν περιτομὴν) Præcipit Lev. XII. 3.

Οὐκ ὅτι ἐκ τῦ Μωσέως ἐστιν) Explicatio ante dicti: non quod dicam à Mose primum institutam.

Ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ τῶν πατέρων) ἐκ pro παρὰ: Venit ab Abrahamo, I- saaco & Jacobo.

κὰι ἐν Σαββάτῳ περιτέμνετε ἄνθρωπον) Id est puerum בן אדם. Sic infra XVI. 21. illud κὰι est rationale. Quasi di- cat, propterea, reverentia patr i instituti opus facitis Sabba- to. Sententia est Hebræorum מילה דוחה את השבת. Circumcisio pellit Sabbatum.

## 7:23
V. 23. if a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath) If this is permitted and right, in which so many things concur that could seem servile unless they were undertaken for the sake of piety.

that the law of Moses may not be broken) That that commandment may remain, concerning performing circumcision on the eighth day, given by God, written down by Moses, above in verse 23.

that I have made a man whole on the Sabbath) Paralysis had occupied the whole man, and I freed him, which work not only pertains more to the honor of God than circumcision, but is also a benefit in itself, and therefore is contained in the precepts of nature, which are older than circumcision itself, just as circumcision is older than the rigid rest of the Sabbath commanded by Moses: and therefore it is preferred to the Sabbath. If a ritual law yields to an older ritual one, how much more to a law inscribed by nature upon hearts, that we should help the miserable on any occasion?

Latin:

V. 23. εἰ περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπο̂ ἐν Σαββάτῳ) Si hoc licet & fas est, in quo tam multa concurrunt quæ servi- lia videri possent nisi pietatis causa susciperentur.

ἵνα μὴ λυθῇ ὁ νόμο̂ Μωσέως) Ut maneat præceptum illud, de octavo die facienda circumcisione, à Deo datum, à Mose perscriptum, supra 23.

ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ὑγιῆ ἐποίησα ἐν Σαββάτῳ) Paralysis to- tum hominem occupaverat, & ego eum liberavi, quod opus non tantum ad Dei honore magis pertinet quam circum- cisio, sed & per se beneficium est, ac proinde continetur in naturæ præceptis, quæ antiquiora sunt ipsa circumcisione, sicut circumcisio est antiquior rigido otio Sabbati per Mo- sen imperato: ac propterea Sabbato præfertur. Si lex ritualis cedit rituali antiquiori, quanto magis legi per naturam cor- dibus inscriptæ ut quavis occasione miseros juvemus?

## 7:24
V. 24. Do not judge according to appearance) With persons set aside, regarding whom favor or hatred are wont to arise, to look at the bare matter; ὄψις here is פנים, which is wont to be translated as πρόσωπον. The sense is taken from Deut. I. 17, XVI. 19.

But judge righteous judgment) From Zech. VII. 9. Do not condemn in me what you permit to yourselves.

Latin:

V. 24. Μὴ κρίνετε κατ᾽ ὄψιν) Sepositis personis circa quas favor aut odium nasci solent, rem nudam spectare, ὄψις hic est פנים quod πρόσωπον verti solet. Sensus desumtus est ex Deut. I. 17. XVI. 19.

Ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνατε) Ex Zach. VII. 9. Ne in me damnate quod vobis permittitis.

## 7:25
v. 25. of the Jerusalemites) Thus they are often called in Josephus and Mark I. 5.

whom they seek to kill) For these, as citizens, could know the hatred of the leaders toward Jesus more closely than those who had come into the city from other parts, whom he just now indicated by the name of the crowd.

Latin:

v. 25. ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμιτῶν) Sic sæpe apud Josephum vo- cantur & Marc. I. 5.

ὃν ζητῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι) Nam hi ut cives propius nosse pote- rant odium procerum in Jesum quam qui ex aliis partibus in urbem venerant, quos modo ὄχλο nomine significavit.

## 7:26
V. 26. παῥῥησίᾳ λαλεῖ) Openly, as above 13.

Οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγυσι) Not even he is forbidden to teach by the Sanhedrin.

Ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν) Ἀληθῶς, that is, by certain proofs. Thus below XVII. 8, which those who did not understand placed ἀληθῶς before ἐστιν, which the Syriac followed; afterwards both crept into certain codices.

οἱ ἄρχοντες) The Syriac קשישין, that is, the Elders, the Senators of the great Sanhedrin, in whose power was the investigation concerning true or false prophets. See what is said at Luke XIV. 1 and Matthew V. 21.

Latin:

V. 26. παῥῥησίᾳ λαλεῖ) Palam ut supra 13.

Οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγυσι) Ne docere quide à Synedrio vetatur.

Ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν) Ἀληθῶς id est certis indiciis. Sic inf. XVII. 8. quod qui nō intellexerunt posuerunt ἀληθῶς ante ἐστιν, quod secutus est Syrus, postea utrumq; in quosdā codices irrepsit.

οἱ ἄρχοντες) Syrus קשישין id est Seniores Senatores ma- gni Synedrii, penes quos cognitio erat de prophetis veris aut falsis. Vide quæ ad Luc. XIV. 1. & Matth. V. 21.

## 7:27
v. 27. ὅταν ἔρχηται) He will come: thus γινώσκει, he will know.

πόθεν ἐστι) From what Father he is born, for that is the answer to the question πόθεν, 1 Sam. XXX. 13, 2 Sam. I. 13. From a mystical interpretation of the passage, Behold a virgin shall conceive, and other similar ones by chance, among certain Jews the rumor had prevailed that the Father of the Messiah could not be indicated. (But they had persuaded themselves that they knew his Father, namely Joseph.

It is not about the Father but about the fatherland; nor indeed was there a question about the Father among the Jews, who knew that the Messiah would be the son of a Virgin not from a mystical but from a literal sense of Is. VII. 14 (which is to that passage). But as for the reconciliation of v. 42, the opinion of Maldonatus does not displease, namely that there were others who say here, no one knows whence he is, thinking that nothing had been handed down about that matter in the scriptures, as being commoners and unlearned, and others who said later: From the seed of David and from the town of Bethlehem, and that these were more learned.

Latin:

v. 27. ὅταν ἔρχηται) Veniet: sic γινώσκει sciet.

πόθεν ἐστι) Quo Patre natus sit, id enim respondetur ad quæstionem πόθεν 1. Sam. XXX. 13. 2. Sam. I. 13. Ex mysti- ca interpretatione loci, Ecce virgo pariet, & aliis sorte simili- bus apud quosdam Judæos fama invaluerat Messiæ Patrem indicari non posse. (At hujus Patrem nosse se sibi persuase- rant, Josephum scilicet.

Non de Patre sed de patria sermo est; neq; vero de Patre quæstio erat apud Judæos, qui Messiam Virginis filium fore non ex mystico sed literali sensu Ef. VII. 14. (quod de ad illum locum) nove- rant. Quod vero ad conciliationem v. 42. attinet, non displicet Maldonati sententia, quod nempe a- hii fuerint, qui hic dicunt, nemo scite, unde sit, existi- mantes nihil de ea re traditum esse in scripturis, ut- pote plebeji & imperitii alii, qui postea dixerunt: Ex semine David & de Bethlehem castello, hosque doctiores fuisse.

## 7:28
V. 28. ἔκραξεν) He raised his voice so that all might hear. κὰμὲ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί) I think it should be read with a question: do you then really know from what Father I am begotten? Nor do I think Tertullian read it otherwise, who cites it thus against Praxeas: Neither do you know me whence I am, explaining the interrogation negatively. Christ, just as he leads the discourse from common water to spiritual, from the food of the body to the food of the soul, so he leads it from an earthly Father to a heavenly one. κὰ ἀπ᾽ ἐμαυτῦ ὐκ ἐλήλυθα) κὰ for But. But indeed I did not thrust myself into this office, but he who sent me, he is my Father. Thus ἐρχόμενος above I. 15, ἐλήλυθας III. 2, and elsewhere.

Ἀλλ᾽ ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με) Understand Father, according to the meaning, for in the word πόθεν this was contained. Thus above, the true bread VI. 32. Above, the Father is added several times to he who sent me, V. 30, 37, VI. 38, 44. He who sent me, he is truly my Father.

ὃν ὑμεῖς ὐκ οἴδατε) You do not know what his character is, what his affection is toward the human race, with what worship he is pleased. See above I. 18 and what was said there.

Nay, you do not even know as to his essence, because he who ignores the Son, ignores the Father, John V. 23.

Latin:

V. 28. ἔκραξεν) Intendit vocem ut omnes audirent. κὰμὲ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί) Puto legendum cum interroga- tione: itane verǫ me nostis quo sim Patre genitus? Nec ali- ter puto legisse Tertullianum: qui ad Praxeam sic citat, Neque me scitis unde sim, interrogationem negative expo- nens. Christus sicut ab aqua vulgari ad spiritualem, à cibo corporis ad cibum animi, ita à Patre terrestri ad cœlestem sermonem traducit. κὰ ἀπ᾽ ἐμαυτῦ ὐκ ἐλήλυθα) κὰ prò At. At sane ego me huic muneri non ingessi, sed qui me misit, is Pater est meus. Sic ἐρχόμενος supra I. 15. ἐλήλυθας III. 2. & alibi.

Ἀλλ᾽ ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με) Subintellige πατὴρ, κατὰ τὸ σημαινόμενον, nam in voce πόθεν hoc inerat Sic supra ὁ ἄρ- τον ὁ ἀληθινός VI. 32. Supra aliquoties voti ὁ πέμψας με ad- ditur πατὴρ V. 30. 37. VI. 38. 44. Qui me misit, is vere est Pater meus.

ὃν ὑμεῖς ὐκ οἴδατε) Nescitis quo sit ingenio, quo affectu erga genus humanum, quo cultu delectetur. Vide supra I. 18. & quæ ibi dicta.

Imo etiam nescitis quoad essentiam, quia qui ignorai Filium, ignorat Patrem, Joh. V. 23.

## 7:29
V. 29. ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν) I know him intimately, who he is, what he wills, what he thinks, what laws he prefers to which. These things are to be referred to the previous question about the healing on the Sabbath.

ὅτι παρ᾽ αὐτῦ εἰμι) I derive authority and power from him to perform such great miracles: which is said below at X. 36 to have been sanctified by the Father: thus πόθεν ἐστι is used in Matt. XXI. 25 and below at IX. 29. There is an allusion to that which was said above, πόθεν ἐστιν, in another sense.

Κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν) and from him I have also received commands: above III. 17, 34. By reason of both this sanctification and this mission, he rightly proves below also at X. 37 that God is called his Father.

He teaches not whence he is, but rather from whom he has his doctrine. Nor does he here or anywhere else call God his Father by reason of sanctification or mission: which I have already refuted in the Socinians. Because he is Father by reason of generation: nor is he properly called Father in relation to the Son, but κατ᾽ ὑπεροχήν Joh. X. 37.

X. 37. He who was sent and sanctified is the Son, he who sent and sanctified is the Father, etc., but not by reason of the mission and sanctification. Compare what is added against Crellius in Natural and Revealed Theology, book 1.

Latin:

V. 29. ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν) Ego eum quis sit, quid velit, quid cogitet, quas leges quibus præferat, intime novi. Referenda hæc ad superiorem quæstionem de sanatione in Sabbato.

ὅτι παρ᾽ αὐτῦ εἰμι) Ab ipso duco autoritatem & potesta- tem miracula tāta faciendi:quod infra X. 36. dicitur à Patre esse sanctificatum: sic πόθεν ἐστι sumitur Matt. XXI. 25. infra IX. 29. Allusio est ad illud supra dictū πόθεν ἐστιν sensu alio.

Κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν) ab ipso & mandata accepi : supra III. 17. 34. Ratione hujʋ tum sanctificationis tum missionis Deum recte Patrem suum dici infra quoque probat X. 37.

Non unde sit, sed potius à quo habeat doctrinam suam, docet. Neq; vel hic vel uspiam alias Deum Patrem suum dicit ratione sanctificationis, aut mis- sionis:quod in Socinianis jam profligavirno.quia Pa- ter est ratione generationis: nec proprie Pater di- citur in ordine ad Filium sed κατ᾽ υπεροχεξίαν Joh. X. 37.

X. 37. Ille qui missus & sanctificatus est Filius, qui misit & sanctificavit Pater &c. non autem ratione missionis & sanctificationis. Conf. quæ contra Crel- lium in Theol. natural. & revel. adh. l.

## 7:30
Verse 30. They sought therefore to take him) Some of those standing by wished to lay hands on him, namely to bring him to the Sanhedrin, to which they knew it would be pleasing.

his hour) The time of the passion chosen by the Father as most opportune for human salvation: John often calls it the hour, VIII. 20 and elsewhere. See the response to the Orthodox CXXII in the works of Justin. Before that time, wills, however evil, were restrained from their effect by a certain divine power.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πιάσαι) Quidam ex adstantibus manus ei injicere volebant, nempe ut eum ad Synedrium adducerent, cui id sciebant gratum fore.

ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ) Tempus passionis à Patre electum ut opor- tunissimum saluti humanæ: id sæpe horam vocat Johannes VIII. 20. & alibi. Vide responsionē ad Orthodoxos CXXII. in Justini operibus. Ante id tempus voluntates quamvis malæ ab effectu divina quadam vi inhibebantur.

## 7:31
V. 31. they believed in him) Not as in Christ (for they doubted about him), but as in a man sent by God.

more signs) For John himself also passed over many, below XX. 30, XXI. 25.

Latin:

V. 31. ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν) Non ut in Christum, (nam de eo dubitabant) sed ut in hominem à Deo missum.

πλείονα σημεῖα) Nam plurima ipse etiam Johannes subti- cuit, infra XX. 30. XXI. 25.

## 7:32
Verse 32. Murmuring about him) Muttering these things secretly. Thus, murmuring about him, above 12.

The Pharisees and the chief priests sent) That is, they discuss the matter in the Sanhedrin, both the leaders of the priests and others of the Pharisaic sect, of whom the former feared the diminution of their dignity, the latter of their traditions, since the people had begun to think so well of Jesus. See below XI. 47; but the Sadducees did not care about those things, being contemptuous of traditions and relying on dignities, by Roman power, not by popular favor.

officers) שוטרים who executed the judgments of the senators.

Latin:

Vers. 32. Γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ) Clam hæc mussitantem. Sic γογγυσμὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ, supra 12.

Ἀπέστειλαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι κὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς) Id est rem ut serunt in Synedrio tum Pontificum primores, tum alii sectæ Pha- risaïcæ, quorum illi dignitatis, hi traditionum suarum im- minutionem metuebant, quandoquidem populus tam be- ne de Jesu sentire cœperat. Vide infra XI. 47. sed Sadducæi ista non curabant, traditionum contemtores, & ad dignita- tes nixi, Romana potestate non aura populari.

ὑπηρέτας) שוטרים qui senatorum judicia exsequebatur.

## 7:33
V. 33. yet a little while I am with you) He shows that all his actions are done by a special and excellent divine arrangement, and at the same time that their attempt is vain, because they were prevented from harming him even now, and would be much more so after he had ascended into heaven. He passes over his death in silence, because it did not pertain to what is being treated here.

and I go to him who sent me) To report on my mission, as if he were saying: see how the messenger is to be treated by you.

Latin:

V. 33. ἔτι μικρὸν χρόνον μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι) Ostendit omnia sua agi dispositu divino speciali atque eximio, & simul vanum esse ipsorum conatum, quia & nunc nocere ipsi impediren- tur, & posthac ubi in cœlum ipse ascendisset multo magis. Mortem suam in medio positam silentio transit, quia non pertinebat ad id quod hic agitur.

κὶ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸ πέμψαντά με) Renuntiaturus legationem, quasi dicat videre quomodo tractandus sit vobis legatus.

## 7:34
V. 34. You will seek me and will not find me) This is not said by one reproaching, but is spoken commonly to good and bad, as appears below XIII. 33. It is characteristic of the Hebrews to use a copula added to the indicative for the subjunctive, which they lack. The sense therefore is: If you seek me, I shall not appear. In this sense this phrase is found in Ps. X. 15, XXXVII. 10, Is. XLI. 12, Hos. II. 7.

and where I am, you cannot come) Do not read ὧ with Nonnus, which is poetic and unknown to our writers. Both εἰμὶ here and δύνασθε are for the future. See Matt. XVII. 11. Thus below XII, where this sense is repeated. ὑπάγω is for ὑπάξω: although this is said to the Apostles there for a different end than it is here to the populace: there as to friends, here as to enemies.

Latin:

V. 34. Ζητήσετέ με κὶ ὐκ εὑρήσετε) Non est hoc expro- bantis, sed communiter dictum bonis & malis apparet in- fra XIII. 33. Hebræorum est indicativo adjecta copula uti pro subjunctivo quo carent. Sensus ergo est: Si me quæratis non comparebo. Hoc sensu phrasis hæc reperitur Psal. X. 15. XXXVII. 10. Es. XLI. 12. Os. II. 7.

κὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ, ὑμεῖς ὖ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν) Noli cum Nonno ὧ legere, quod Poëticum est, & nostris scriptoribus in- cognitum. Tam εἰμὶ hic est pro futuro quam δύνασθε. Vide Matth. XVII. 11. Sic infra XII. ubi hic sensus repetitur. ὑπά- γω est pro ὑπάξω: quanquam alio fine ibi Apostolis hoc di- citur quam hic plebi: ibi ut amicis, hic ut inimicis.

## 7:35
V. 35. Among themselves) Among one another as in Matt. XVI. 7. & elsewhere.

that we shall not find him) That is, that we cannot find him, as the Syrian here translates it very well. Thus 2 Sam. VII. 18. In Greek: who am I, O Lord, O Lord, and what is my house, that you have loved me up to this point. That you might love me.

into the dispersion of the Greeks) The word dispersion for Jews speaking Greek, who are customarily called Hellenists, signifies those places in which the descendants of Israel were living in exile: מזרה as can be seen in Deut. XXX. 4. Neh. I. 9. Ps. CXLVII. 2. But there were two noble dispersions, the former of the Babylonians, the latter of the Greeks: that is, the one which happened under the Chaldeans, this which happened under the Macedonians, for the Hebrews call the kingdom of the Macedonians יון the kingdom of the Greeks. The sense is: will he go to Antioch or Alexandria, where many of the Israelites migrated under the successors of Alexander? But they ask this rather than about the regions under the Parthian, because Syria & Egypt were less far away from Judea & very many came from there to Jerusalem on feast days; not so from the parts of Media.

Latin:

V. 35. Πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς) Inter se ut Matth. XVI. 7. & alibi.

ὅτι ἡμεῖς ὐκ ἑυρήσομεν αὐτὸν) Id est ut eum invenire non possimus, ut hic optime vertit Syrus. Sic 2. Sam. VII. 18. Græ- ce: τίς εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κύριέ με, κύριε, κὶ τίς ὁ οἶκός με, ὅτι ἠγάπησάς με ἕως τούτων. Ut me diligeres.

εἰς τὴν διασπορὰν τῶν ἑλλήνων) Vox διασπορᾶς Judæis Græce loquentibus, quos Hellenistas dici mos habet, signi- ficat ea loca in quibq Israëlis posteri exsulabant: מזרה ut vi- dere est Deut. XXX. 4. Neh. I. 9. Ps. CXLVII. 2. Nobiles au- tem διασποραὶ erant duæ, prior Babyloniorum, altera Græ- corum: id est illa quæ sub Chaldæis, hæc quæ sub Macedo- nibus contigerat, nam regnum Macedonum Hebræi vo- cant יון regnum Græcorum. Sensus est: ibitne Antiochiam aut Alexandriam quo multi Israëlitarum migrarunt sub successoribus Alexandri? Hoc autem potius quærunt quam de regionibus sub Partho, quia Syria & Ægyptus minus lon- ge aberant à Judæa & plurimi inde Hærosolyma festis diebq veniebant: non item ex Mediæ partibus.

## 7:36
