Non di- cam quod ita cœna Paschalis cum dimissoria, quam vocant, & mensis secundis confundatur, juxta ri- tus quos observat ex Rabbinis Josephus Scaliger lib. VI. de emend. tempor. pag. 372. Hanc e- nim cœnam, quæ Pascha excipere consueverat, a- pud Judæos nihil aliud fuisse docet, quam aceta- rium quoddam ex intybis & lactucis agrestibus, quarum quia tristis & amarus est succus, ex aceto & aliis embamma conficiebant, in quod azyma & amara illa olera intingebantur. Etsi in aliis sole- mnibus (Pentecostes, & Scenopegias) epulis sa- crificii, vel hostiæ immolatæ finitis aliam cœnam, quam dimissoriam vocant vel secundas mensas bella- riis instruerent Judæi, in Paschate tamen interdi- cebantur convivæ omni genere bellariorum, & em- bammate solum illo contenti esse debebant, juxta Scaligerum: quod excipiebat poculum ὑμνήσεως seu laudationis, post illud vero interdictum erat, a- liquid cibi aut potus sumere. Quod ergo Grotius vult, cœnam justam celebrari adhuc consuevisse post θύσιμον, ut & post μνημονευτικὸν, quod commentus est, Pascha, id Canoni Paschali Ju- dæorum refragari docet Scaliger. Quicquid autem de Judæorum ritibus & canone sit, nam eodem ritu à Christo, quo à Judæis, Pascha ce- lebratum fuisse, eo nempe, quem Canones in Digestis Thalmudicis designant, annuere Scalige- ro adhuc nondum possumus, maxime, quum solam comestionein agni Paschalis videatur cœnam facere, sequutam vero cœnam per in- tinctionem azymi, ex ritu Judaico, describere; quæ umbræ cœnæ Paschalis, Paschati nempe à Judæis excogitatio, & sine agno Paschali cele- brari solito (quod Pascha commemorativum vocat Grotius) convenit, non Paschati à Christo cele- brato: utpote quod nec sine agno Paschali, nec sine herbis amaris ac pane azymo, sed Paschali agno cum herbis amaris, & azymo pane come- sto, juxta divinam institutionem peractum fuit. Neque passumus Scaligero in eo calculum adde- re, quod de iterata pedum lotione tradit. Ita enim habet Scaliger: Nam hoc ultimum (Pascha) reliquis antecedentibus simile fuisse nemo negave- rit, & antecedentia eodem ritu à Christo, quo à Judæis celebrata. Celebrata igitur tam illa, quam hoc ultimum, eo ritu, quem exposuimus. Nam & lotio iterata fuit, ut in aliis Paschatibus, pri- mum quidem ex consuetudine quotidiana, ut dis- cumberet, & agnum comederet, deinde δείπνε γε- νομένε, ex ritu Paschatis. Petrus itaque non, quod iterum lavare necesse sit, miratur, ut qui sci- ret in prima Azymorum hoc solere fieri, & lotio- nem iterari, sed quod discipulus à Magistro, fa- mulus à Domino, homuncio à vero Deo διακονεῖται. Rursus duplex est cœna in continenti, cum duæ lotio- nes utramque præeant, una ordinaria, in qua a- gnus quoque comeditur: altera, quia κλάσις τẽ ἄρτε ἀζύμε, & intinctio azymi in tryblio embam- matis, Joh. XIII. 26. Probare hæc conatur qui- dem Scaliger, sed citra successum: Si, inquit, Christus, ut quidam hostes bonarum literarum per- tendunt, non obstrinxis se ritibus Judæorum: quare igitur omnia hic fiunt, quæ in rituali Judaico extant? Quare omnia simillima sunt? At non hostes bona- rum literarum acturum sunt, qui superstitionum & rituum à Judæis contra legem divinam inve- ctorum hostes sunt, neque credunt, relicta lege Dei iisdem sese obstrinxisse Christum. Omnia autem à Christo observata esse, quæ in rituali Ju- daico extant, à veritate alienum esse censemus; nam uti dictum est, Christus non celebravit Pa- scha, sine agno Paschali, ut Judæi id celebrant: neque secundum rituale Judæorum agnum Pa- schalem comedit sine pane azymo & herbis amaris: nec de gemina pedum lotione apud Evangelistas ul- lum reperitur verbum, imo nec de cœna vulgari post Paschalem cœnam celebrata, vel in lege di- vina mandatum habetur, vel ex Historia Evange- lica quicquam solidi doceri potest: ut alia tacea- mus, quæ non simillima esse omnia, sed multum diffimilia, quæ à Christo observata sunt, edo- cent. Ita omnino sentio, obscuratum tantum ef- se textum sacrum ab illis, qui ritus Judaicos ob- servatos à Christo censuerunt, eosque ex ritua- libus eorum eruerunt, qui relictis illis satis dilu- cidus est, ac perspicuus, nullisque adeo difficul- tatibus involutus.

τẽ διαβόλε ἤδη βεβληκότ@ εἰς καρδίαν Ἰύδα] Hic quo- que illud βεβληκότ@ intelligendum cum effectu, nempe ut Judas hoc consilium Diaboli receperit. Simile loquen- di genus supra jam aliquoties observavimus. Sic tentare Satan dicitur cum tentationi succumbitur, I. Cor. VII. v. 5.

ἵνα ἀυτὸν παραδῷ] Habet & hoc ἔμφασιν. jam consilio se tradendi capto, tam propinquo periculo, non omisit testari curam suam pro discipulis, etiam pro illo nefario, si forte adhuc resipisceret.

## 13:3
Vers. 3.

εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησẽς ὅτι πάντα δέδωκεν ἀυτῷ ὁ πατὴρ εἰς τὰς χεῖρας [But Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands] He says this: He performed such a humble service not unaware of his own dignity: for it increases the estimation of the deed that such a great and such a one did this. But by to give understand here, to promise that he will give. For all things have been delivered to him (that is, power over all things which conduce to the Church, Matt. XXVIII. 18.) after his ascension into heaven, Acts II. 36.

All things had been given to Christ not only by way of promise, but also by way of possession: although he did not always exercise the power of all things, which he had as regards κτῆσιν (acquisition), as far as χρῆσιν (use) was concerned, but when, where, and how it pleased him. For the intervening κένωσις (emptying) and ταπείνωσις (humiliation) demanded that, Phil. II. Nor indeed could he have been said to have emptied himself of the use of majesty in the state of humiliation, unless he had had and possessed the same.

And that he came forth from God] That he had proceeded, having been sent to the human race from God. Thus above c. 8, 42.

And goes to God] And that he was to be received into the palace of God, into the fellowship of the kingdom. All these things wonderfully describe his dignity.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησẽς ὅτι πάντα δέδωκεν ἀυτῷ ὁ πατὴρ εἰς τὰς χεῖρας] Hoc dicit, Tam humile obsequium fecit non inconscius suæ dignitatis: id enim auget facti æstima- tionem quod tantus ac talis hoc fecerit. Dare autem hic intellige, promittere daturum. Nam tradita illi sunt omnia (id est potestas in omnia quæ Ecclesiæ conducunt, Matth. XXVIII. 18.) post ascensum in cœlum Actorum II. 36.

Data Christo omnia erant non solum qua pro- missionem, sed etiam qua possessionem: etsi potesta- tem omnium, quam quoad κτῆσιν habebat, non semper exerceret, quantum ad χρῆσιν, sed, quan- do, ubi, & quomodo libuit. Id enim κένωσις & ταπείνωσις interveniens poscebat Phil. II. Ne- que sane evacvasse se dici potuisset usu majestatis in statu exinanitionis, nisi eandem habuisset ac pos- sedisset.

καὶ ὅτι ἀπὸ Θεῦ ἐξῆλθε] A Deo ad genus humanum mis- sum se prodiisse. Sic supra c. 8, 42.

καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὑπάγει] Et se receptum iri in Dei regiam, in consortium regni. Omnia hæc mirifice describunt ejus dignitatem.

## 13:4
Verse 4.

He rises from supper] It was not customary for the supper, even of the lamb, to be taken by those standing after the times of the exodus. But in a memorial supper, such as this was, they entirely sat or reclined, and even now it is sat. Therefore, that being finished, Christ arose and washed feet before the full and ordinary supper, which was accustomed to be done before suppers.

Having dismissed the fiction concerning a memorial supper distinct and separate from the eating of the Paschal lamb, although there are not wanting those among our own who understand ἐκ τῦ δείπνε (from supper) as the common supper, we easily agree that the Paschal Supper is designated here: For that being completed, yet the tables not being removed, Christ employed this ceremony, not out of Jewish custom, but for the sake of spiritual signification. For the Jews were accustomed to be washed before the eating of the Passover; which Christ here, by no means binding himself to Jewish rites after the eating of the Paschal lamb, undertook in his disciples: not for a full and ordinary supper: concerning which nothing is held in the text, which also it is not evident that Christ had ordered to be prepared, nor that it was prepared, but to signify the necessity of spiritual ablution, and for the preparation or readiness for the most sacred Sacrament of the Eucharist.

And lays aside his garments] This word is of those which have a singular meaning with a plural sound, as we noted at Matt. XVII. 2. The Hebrew שלמה is usually translated thus, by which is properly signified the outer garment which is accustomed to be laid aside by those ministering. Philo concerning the priests: 'For being loosened in tunics only, they gird themselves, that they may bring the sacrifices for the libations, and other things useful for the sacrifice, having been prepared with unhesitating speed.'

And having taken a towel] This word had reached the Jews from the Romans just as it had the Greeks. It is written לנטית; the grammarians explain it as סדין, as here the Syrian ܦܪܝܢܐ (findonem), the Arab منشفة (a drying cloth), for the following things show that this towel served for that purpose.

He girded himself] His loins, as the Hebrews and this Syrian say. That is the habit of those ministering, by which they might be more ready, Luke XVII. 8. 'girding yourself, serve,' and among the Latins, ministers and temple-servants are called succincti (girded). The verb διαζώννυαι is read twice in this place and below in chapter 21, 7. It is also found in Lucian.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ἐγείρεται ἐκ τῦ δείπνυ] Non solebat cœna etiam agni a stantibus sumi post exitus tempora. In cœna autem me- morali qualis hæc erat omnino sedebatur aut accumbeba- tur, & nunc etiam sedetur. Itaque ea confecta surrexit Christus & ad cœnam plenam atque ordinariam pedes la- vit, quod ante cœnas fieri erat solitum.

Misso commento de cœna memoriali distincta & separata ab agni Paschalis esu, quanquam non desint è nostris, qui ἐκ τῦ δείπνε de cœna vulgari intelligant, facile annuimus Paschalem Cœnam hic designari: Ea enim peracta mensis tamen non re- motis Christus hanc ceremoniam, non ex consue- tudine Judaica, sed significationis spiritualis cau- sa adhibuit. Nam Judæi ante Paschatis comestio- nem solebant ablui; quod hic Christus, minime se adstringens ad Judaicos ritus post esum agni Pa- schalis in discipulis suis suscepit: non ad cœnam plenam atque ordinariam: de qua nihil in textu habetur, quam etiam nec parari jusserat Christus, nec paratam esse constat, sed ad significandam ablu- tionis spiritualis necessitatem, & ad parasceven vel præparationem ad sacratissimum Eucharistiæ Sa- cramentum.

κὴ τίθησι τὰ ἱμάτια] Hæc vox ex illis est quæ plurali sono singularem habent significatum, ut notavimus ad Matth. XVII. 2. verti ita solet Hebræum שלמה, quo proprie si- gnificatur extimus amictus qui à ministrantibus deponi so- let. Philo de sacerdotibus: ἀνείμενος γὰρ ἐν μόνοις χιτωνίσκοις ζώσει, ἱερεῖα τῆ τὰς σπονδὰς, κὰι τά αλλα χρησιμα θυσίας προσά- γυσιν εἰς ἀυπέρθετον τάχῶ ἠσκημένοι.

κὴ λαβὼν λέντιον] Hæc vox à Romanis ut ad Græcos ita & ad Judæos pervenerat. Scribitur לנטית exponunt Grammatici סדין ut hic Syrus ܦܪܝܢܐ findonem, Arabs منشفة absterforium, nam ei fini serviisse hoc linteum sequentia ostendunt.

διέζωσεν ἑαυτὸν] Lumbos suos ut loquuntur Hebræi & hic Syrus. Is habitus ministrantium, quo expeditiores essent, Luc. XVII. 8. περιζωσάμενο διακόνει, & Latinis ministri & popæ succincti vocantur. Verbum διαζώννυαι bis hoc loco legitur & infra cap. 21, 7. est & apud Lucianum.

## 13:5
Verse 5.

He pours water into the basin] He omits no part of the ministry. He pours water into the basin, having taken it, of course, from those water-jars which stood by according to custom. See what we said at chapter 2 above.

ἤρξατο νίπτειν τὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν] First he speaks generally of the washing of the disciples' feet, then he narrates specifically the words of Peter. For ἤρξατο νίπτειν is nothing else than ἔνιψε, as we said on Luke 3:8, so Acts 1:1 and often elsewhere.

ἐκμάσσειν] As is the custom.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

βάλλει ὕδωρ εἰς τὸν νιπτῆρα] Nihil ministerii omittit. Aquam infundit pollubro, sumtam scilicet ex hydriis illis quæ pro more adstabant. Vide quæ diximus ad cap. 2. supra.

ἤρξατο νίπτειν τὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν] Primum dicit ge- neraliter lotos pedes discipulorum, deinde specialiter nar- rat Petri verba. Nam ἤρξατο νίπτειν nihil est aliud quam ἔνιψε, ut diximus Luc. III. 8. sic Act. I. 1. & alibi sæpe.

ἐκμάσσειν] Ut moris est.

## 13:6
Verse 6.

ἔρχεται ὖν] ἐν here is more specific to one narrating the matter, nor is it impossible that the beginning was made by Peter.

Cύ με νίπτεις τὺς πόδας] You, the Son of God, [wash] mine, a sinner's? See Matthew 16:6 and Luke 5:8 and compare Matthew 3:14, where there is a not dissimilar opposition, νίπτεις, that is, you wish to wash. Just as λιθάζετε above in chapter 10:32.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ἔρχεται ὖν] ἐν hic est specialius rem enarrantis, nec impossibile est à Petro factum initium.

Cύ με νίπτεις τὺς πόδας] Tu Dei Filius, meos peccatoris? Vide Matth. XVI. 6. & Luc. V. 8. & Conf. Matth. III. 14. ubi oppositio non dissimilis, νίπτεις, id est vis lavare. Si- cut λιθάζετε supra c. 10, 32.

## 13:7
Verse 7.

ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ σὺ ἐκ οἶδας ἄρτι] You do not yet grasp what I am doing, that is, to what end that which I do tends.

γνώσῃ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτα] Namely, when in your Apostolic function and in similar diligence you will purge what of filth shall remain in Christians. See Luke 22:32 and add 1 Peter 2:1.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ σὺ ἐκ οἶδας ἄρτι] Nondum capis quid agam, id est quo tendat quod ago.

γνώσῃ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτα] Nempe cum in Apostolica functio- ne & in simili sedulitate purgabis quod sordium in Christianis restabit. Vide Luc. XXII 32. & adde 1. Petr. II. v. 1.

## 13:8
Verse 8.

οὐ μὴ νίψῃς τοὺς πόδας μου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα] I will never suffer this. Thus above in chapter 10:20 and elsewhere. Moreover, this proceeded from a mind indeed reverent, but not sufficiently attending to that which Christ was saying and intimating.

ἐὰν μὴ νίψω σε] It is the custom of Christ to ascend from things that are seen to a more sublime sense: unless I wash you, that is, unless I also wash away by word and spirit what remains in you less pure, consider too high an estimation of yourself, Matthew 26:33, indulgence, ibid. 40, irascibility 51, fear 70, 74, which filth how Christ purged in Peter can be seen in the stated places. But also as many discourses as follow in John pertain to this washing. See Matthew 3:11.

οὐκ ἔχεις μέρος μετ' ἐμοῦ] You will not be a partaker of my goods. If this expression is taken from Deuteronomy 14:27, chapter 17:1, and elsewhere. That we may be co-heirs of Christ, it does not suffice to have turned the mind away from more serious vices unless we also render our steps daily more purged from earthly contagions.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

οὐ μὴ νίψῃς τοὺς πόδας μου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα] Nunquam hoc patiar. Sic supra c. 10, 20. & alibi. Est autem hoc profectum ex animo quidem reverente, sed non satis attendente ad id quod Christus dicebat & innuebat.

ἐὰν μὴ νίψω σε] Mos Christi est à rebus quæ aspiciuntur ad sensum sublimiorem ascendere: nisi te lavero, id est nisi & sermone & spiritu eluero quod in te restat minus puri, puta nimiam de te ipso existimationem, Matth. XXVI. 33. indulgentiam, ibidem 40. iracundiam 51. formidinem 70. 74. quas sordes quomodo purgaverit in Petro Christus videre est dictis locis. Sed & quotquot apud Johannem sequuntur sermones, ad hanc lotionem pertinent. Vide Matth. III. 11.

οὐκ ἔχεις μέρος μετ' ἐμοῦ] Non eris particeps meorum bonorum. Si hæc locutio sumitur Deut. XIV. 27. cap. XVII. 1. & alibi. Ut Christi cohæredes simus, non sufficit à vitiis gravioribus animum avertisse nisi & gressus nostros quotidie reddamus à terrenis contagiis purgatiores.

## 13:9
Verse 9.

ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν κεφαλήν] That is, my whole self, just as we said above in chapter 11, 44, that the whole body is signified by the words for hands and feet.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν κεφαλήν] Id est totum me, sicut manuum & pedum vocibus totum corpus significari diximus supra c. 11, 44.

## 13:10
Verse 10.

ὁ λελουμένος] That is, he who has once brought his mind to obey the Gospel; this is explained by Christ himself below in chapter 15, 3. Add the passage in Acts 15, 9, where what is attributed to the Gospel in the cited passage of John chapter 15 is attributed to faith, because the word cleanses only if it is mixed with faith, Heb. IV, verse 2.

οὐ χρείαν ἔχει ἢ τοὺς πόδας νίψασθαι] He has need only of this, that he cleanse himself from those things which are recognized as they occur. A simile taken from those who leave the bath with bare feet. The writer on the washing of feet in the works of Cyprian. We said above that those once washed by baptism do not need that same bath further. But this bath was instituted for daily excesses, and constant reflection, coming even to the latest things, ought to examine all works and individual thoughts, and to correct and wash the affections running through vices, carrying the wandering and unstable soul through vanities: and to leave nothing in this life unexamined, which has not been expiated by groans and sighs. To Philo, feet signify τὰς ἐπιβάσεις τῶν αἱρεζόντων. Alleg. II. On the life of Moses, he interprets feet for the third time as τὴν περὶ τὸν βίον διέξοδον. Cyril in the ninth book against Julian: ἐν τῇ θεοπνεύστῳ γραφῇ τὴν τοῦ ποδὸς βάσιν τὴ ὅλοι εἶθ' ὅτε τὸν πόδα δέχεσθαί, πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν αἰνιγματωδῶς τῆς ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν πρακτέων ὁδῶ. Compare the law in Levit. VI, 24.

Cyprian in his sermon on the washing of feet, Ambrose on those who are being initiated chapter 1, Augustine tractate LVI on John, Bernard in his sermon on the Supper, understand the former words concerning the spiritual washing of Holy Baptism: he who is washed through baptism does not need to be washed, so as to repeat Baptism; the latter words, unless he wash his feet, concern washing through penance, so that if any filth has reached the feet, if some sin has occurred after Baptism, it may be washed away through penance. This explanation is approved by Johannes Ferus, and defended by Michael Medina against Dominicus à Soto: See Sixtus Senensis, book VI, Bibl. ann. CCIX. Similar is the interpretation of Chrysostom, Cyril, Theophylact, and Euthymius, who by the washing understand the remission of sins; he who is spiritually washed from sins, having obtained their remission, has no need except to wash his feet, that is, because of the infirmities of the flesh, vicious affections, and sins still daily adhering to him, he has need of washing. But the Grotian interpretation confuses faith with obedience, the effect of faith: for our hearts are not purified by the fact that we bring our mind to obedience, or by the purpose of obeying divine precepts, but by faith, Acts XV, 9, by which alone we obtain the remission of sins, Acts X, 43, and in that sense we are said to be cleansed by the word, John XV, 3, insofar as it is mixed with faith, Heb. IV, 2, not the word of precept, or moral word, but the word of grace, or the Gospel.

ἀλλ’ ἐστὶ καθαρὸς ὅλος) Namely, as to the rest of the body, except for the feet: for the discourse is restricted more universally from what was said above, as in 1 Cor. XV. 27.

κὴ ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστι) By the purpose of the mind: the spirit is willing, Matt. XXVI. 41, which is a pure heart, 2 Tim. II. 22.

ἀλλ’ ὀὑχὶ πάντες) He pricks the conscience of Judas, who was impure by the very purpose of his mind, retaining within himself the plans of evil deeds.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ὁ λελουμένος] Id est qui semel in animum induxit Evangelio obsequi, ita hoc explicatur ab ipso Christo infra cap. 15, 3. Adde locum Actor. 15, 9. ubi fidei tribuitur quod dicto Johannis loco cap. 15. tribuitur Evangelio, quia sermo ita demum purgat si cum fide misceatur, Hebr. IV. vers. 2.

οὐ χρείαν ἔχει ἢ τοὺς πόδας νίψασθαι] Hoc tantum ei opus est ut ab iis se purget quæ ex occasione agnoscuntur. Similitudo sumta ab his qui à balneo nudis pedibus abeunt. Scriptor de ablutione pedum in operibus Cypriani. Supra diximus semel lotos baptismate, eodem lavacro ulterius non egere. Sed hoc lavacrum quotidianis est excessibus institutum, & jugis retractatio usque ad novissima veniens, omnia debet opera & cogitatus singulos perscrutari, & affectus per vitia discurrentes, vagam instabilemque animam per inania evehentes corrigere & lavare: nec quicquam in hac vita prætermittere indiscussum, quod gemitibus & suspiriis non fuerit expiatum. Pedes Philoni significant τὰς ἐπιβάσεις τῶν αἱρεζόντων. Alleg. II. de vita Mosis tertio interpretatur pedes τὴν περὶ τὸν βίον διέξοδον. Cyrillus libro contra Julianum nono : ἐν τῇ θεοπνεύστῳ γραφῇ τὴν τοῦ ποδὸς βάσιν τὴ ὅλοι εἶθ' ὅτε τὸν πόδα δέχεσθαί, πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν αἰνιγματωδῶς τῆς ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν πρακτέων ὁδῶ. Confer legem Levit. VI, 24.

Cyprianus sermon. de ablut. ped. Ambrosius de his qui initiantur cap. 1. Augustin. tract. LVI. in Johan. Bernhardus sermon. de Cœna de spirituali lotione S. Baptismi priora verba intelligunt, qui lotus est per baptismum, non opus habet ut lavetur, ut Baptismum iteret; posteriora, nisi ut pedes lavet, de ablutione per pœnitentiam, ut si quid sordium pedibus accessit, si post Baptismum aliquod peccatum contigit, per pœnitentiam abluatur. Quam explicationem probat Job. Ferus, & adversus Dominicum à Soto tuetur Mich. Medina: Vid. Sixt. Senens. lib. VI. Bibl. ann. CCIX. Affinis est interpretatio Chrysostomi, Cyrilli, Theophylacti, & Euthymii, qui per lotionem remissionem peccatorum intelligunt, qui spiritualiter lotus est à peccatis, obtenta eorum remissione, is non indiget nisi ut pedes lavet, hoc est, propter infirmitates carnis vitiosi affectus, & peccata ipsi adhuc adhærentia quotidiana opus habet lotione. Grotiana vero interpretatio confundit fidem cum obsequio effectu fidei: non enim per id, quod animum inducamus ad obsequium, vel per propositum obediendi præceptis divinis, sed per fidem purificantur corda nostra Actor. XV. 9. qua sola remissionem peccatorum consequimur, Act. X. 43. & eo sensu verbo mundari dicimur, Joh. XV. 3. quatenus id fide miscetur Ebr. IV. 2. non verbo præcepti, vel morali, sed verbo gratiæ, vel Evangelii.

ἀλλ’ ἐστὶ καθαρὸς ὅλος) Nempe cætero corpore, exceptis pedibus : nam universalius restringitur ex superiori sermo- ne, ut 1. Cor. XV. 27.

κὴ ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστι) Animi proposito : τὸ πνεῦμα πρό- θυμον Matth. XXVI. 41. quæ καθαρὰ καρδία, 2. Tim. II. 22.

ἀλλ’ ὀὑχὶ πάντες) Conscientiam Judæ vellicat, qui pro- posito ipso animi erat impurus, retinens intra se malorum facinorum consilia.

## 13:12
Vers. 12.

ἀναπεσὼν πάλιν) To the proper or domestic supper, which he finished by instituting the sacrament of his passion.

There is no trace of a proper supper celebrated after the Paschal supper. Nor is it likely that Christ wished to hold a proper supper after the Paschal lamb had been eaten: nor is anything indicated about its preparation being arranged by the disciples. He did indeed recline in turn, the tables not yet having been removed, and having exhorted the disciples to humility by his own example, which he had set before them by the washing of feet, he wished to recall Judas, to whom he gave the dipped morsel, from the crime of betrayal, and soon after instituted the Sacrament of his body and blood, without another supper. The Jews were indeed accustomed to end celebrated feasts with a banquet: but at the feast of the Passover, as appears from the ritual of the Jews, they presented only a salad of endives and wild lettuces, into which the unleavened bread was dipped: but that was not a supper: nor is it certain that this was observed by Christ in that way; indeed, the bitter herbs with the unleavened bread belonged to the Passover itself and the eating of the Paschal lamb: and therefore there was no need for such second courses.

γινώσκετε τί πεποίηκα ὑμῖν) Do you sufficiently perceive what sort of thing this is? He speaks of the humility of the mystery: for they were not to understand the mystical sense until after they had received the Spirit.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ἀναπεσὼν πάλιν) Ad cœnam justam sive domesticam, quam finivit instituto passionis suæ sacramento.

De cœna justa post cœnam Paschalem celebrata nullum habetur vestigium. Nec verisimile est Christum voluisse post comestum agnum Pa- schalem adhuc cœnam justam peragere : neque de ejus apparatu à discipulis instituto quicquam signatum est. Recubuit quidem vicissim, mensis nondum remotis, & cohortatus discipulos ad humilitatem ab exemplo suo, quod lotione pedum ipsis præfuerat, Judam cui offulam intin- ctam dedit, adhuc revocare à scelere proditionis voluit, mox Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis sui, citra aliam cœnam instituit. Consueverunt quidem Judæi festa celebria convivio finire : sed in festo Paschatos, ut è rituali Judæorum ap- paret, solum acetarium ex intybis & lactucis a- grestibus, in quod azyma intingebantur, exhibe- bant : Illa vero non erat cœna: neque à Christo id ita observatum esse constat, imo herbæ amaræ cum azymis ad ipsum Pascha & comestionem agni Paschalis pertinebant : ideoque talibus mensis se- cundis opus non erat.

γινώσκετε τί πεποίηκα ὑμῖν) An quale hoc sit satis animad- vertitis ? Agit de humilitate mysterii : nam mysticum sen- sum non nisi post acceptum spiritum erant intellecturi.

## 13:13
Vers. 13.

Φωνεῖτέ με ὁ διδάσκαλος) Thus among Horace, a poet is addressed. φωνεῖν here is the same as to name, and this is a μίμησις such as in Jerem. XXII. 18. For as often as the Apostles spoke among themselves about Christ, they said, the Lord said this, the master did this, רבי מרי often among the Hebrews.

καλῶς λέγετε) You do not attribute anything foreign to me through flattery: I am master by teaching, Lord by redeeming.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

Φωνεῖτέ με ὁ διδάσκαλος) Sic apud Horatium Poëta salutor. φωνεῖν idem hic est quod nominare, & est hic μί- μησις qualis Jerem. XXII. 18. Nam Apostoli quoties inter se agebant de Christo dicebant, Dominus hoc dixit, magi- ster hoc fecit, רבי מרי sæpe apud Hebræos.

καλῶς λέγετε) Nihil mihi alienum per adulationem ad- scribitis : magister sum docendo, dominus redimendo.

## 13:14
Vers. 14.

If I, being so much your superior, did not refuse to undergo this lowly service for your sake, who are so much inferior. See Matt. 11:29.

Much more ought you, who are fellow servants, to perform similar duties, in humility counting others better than yourselves, Phil. 2:3.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

εἰ οὖν ἐγὼ ἔνιψα ὑμῶν τὺς πόδας) Si ego tanto vobis supe- rior non recusavi hoc vile ministerium subire in gratiam vestri, qui tanto inferiores estis. Vide Matth. XI. 29.

ἀλλήλων νίπτειν τὺς πόδας) Multo magis vos qui conser- vi estis, debetis similia officia deferre, τῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ ἀλλήλυς ἡγύμενοι ὑπερέχοντας ἑαυτῶν, Phil. II. 3.

## 13:15
Verse 15. ὑπόδειγμα) An example to be imitated. Thus Luke 5:10.

As I have done) In the manner of the act: as this word is often taken. In certain churches, the very form of the act was even retained as a sacrament of precept, as in Milan up to the time of Ambrose.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ὑπόδειγμα) Exemplum imitandum. Sic Luc. V. 10.

καθὼς ἐγὼ ἐποίησα) In genere actus : quomodo sæpe hæc vox sumitur. In quibusdam Ecclesiis etiam ipsa actus species in sacramentum præcepti retenta est, ut Mediola- ni usque ad Ambrosii tempora.

## 13:16
Verse 16.

Truly, truly I say to you) Because the Apostles were to be princes of the Church both in the authority of their office and the eminence of their gifts, he therefore fortifies them against the pride that is accustomed to accompany eminence, and shows that the more sublime they will be, the more it will be their duty to submit themselves to the needs of others. See Matt. 20:25 and what is said there.

A servant is not greater than his master) A common proverb, Matt. 10:24, below ch. 15:20. He tacitly repeats what he had said, that he was their master by their own confession, wherefore they ought not, however excellent the position in which they were placed, to consider that unworthy which he himself had not refused.

Nor is an apostle greater than he who sent him) ἀπόσολος here is not a name for a special office, but a general name, signifying one sent with commands, as Heb. 3:1, Phil. 2:25. Thus the Hebrew שלוח is translated in 1 Kings 15:6. But what he had just called master, he now calls sender, because he had instructed them in this, that he might make use of their work.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν) Quia Apostoli futuri erant prin- cipes Ecclesiæ & muneris auctoritate, & donorum emi- nentia, ideo eos munit contra superbiam quæ eminentiam comitari solet, & ostendit quo sublimiores erunt eo magis ipsorum fore officii ut se aliorum usibus submittant. Vide Matth. XX. 25. & quæ ibi dicta.

ὀὑκ ἔστι δῦλος μείζων τῦ κυρίε αὑτῦ) Tritum proverbium, Matth. X. 24. infra c. 15, 20. Repetit tacite quod dixerat se ipsorum esse dominum ipsorum confessione, quare non debere eos quantumvis in loco excellente positos se indi- gnum ducere, quod ipse non detrectasset.

ὀὑδὲ ἀπόσολος μείζων τῦ πέμψαντος αὐτόν) ἀπόσολος hic non specialis muneris, sed generale nomen est, missum cum mandatis significans, ut Hebr. III. 1. Phil. II. 25. Sic He- bræum שלוח vertitur 1. Reg. XV. 6. Quod autem modo dixerat magistrum, nunc dicit mittentem, quia in hoc eos instituerat ut eorum opera uteretur.

## 13:17
Verse 17. If you know these things) If you believe these things to be true. Thus above ch. 4:35 and elsewhere.

Blessed are you if you do them) Because faith that is not active harms more than it helps, James 4:17.

PART II. The repeated indication of the betrayal, and the designation of the traitor.

Latin:

Vers. 17. εἰ ταῦτα οἴδατε) Si hæc creditis vera. Sic supra c. 4, 35 & alibi.

μακάριοί ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε αὐτά) Quia fides non opero- sa nocet magis quam prodest, Jac. IV. 17.

PARS II. Iterata proditionis fignificatio, & prodito- ris designatio.

## 13:18
Verse 18. I do not speak of you all) I do not hope so well of all.

ἐγὼ οἶδα ὃς ἐξελεξάμην) I know intimately those whom I have chosen for myself as companions. For this election is ascribed to Christ, that which is to faith to the Father. Thus ἐκλέγειν is used in Luke 6:70, below ch. 15, 16, 19, Acts 1:2. As if he were to say, both then when I made him an apostle, I knew he was fickle, and now I know he is treacherous. See above ch. 6:64.

ἀλλ' ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ) ἐλευσεως. It happens conveniently that what David once complained was done to him by Ahithophel is done again and indeed more eminently; for the Hebrews, and specifically the Chaldean paraphrast, interpret Psalm 41 and Psalm 55 concerning him. Tacitly he simultaneously prophesies that the end of Judas will be similar to what that of Ahithophel had been.

ὁ τρώγων μετ' ἐμοῦ τὸν ἄρτον) Whom I had made a participant of my table, which is also among the nations a sacred sign of friendship, 1 Cor. 5:11. See also Mark 14:18.

ἐπῆρεν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τὴν πτέρναν αὐτοῦ) For ἐπῆραι here in the Hebrew is הגדיל which is, he used magnificently. The sense therefore is: he pressed and trampled me with a raised foot: for that is more correct than to say it is alluded to runners or wrestlers.

Latin:

Vers. 18. οὐ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν λέγω) Non de omnibus tam bene spero.

ἐγὼ οἶδα ὃς ἐξελεξάμην) Novi eos intime quos mihi in comites delegi. Hæc enim electio Christo adscribitur, ea quæ est ad fidem patri. Sic ἐκλέγειν usurpatur Luc. VI. 70. infra c. 15, 16. 19. Act. I. 2. Quasi dicat, & tunc quum eum apostolum feci, scivi esse levem, & nunc scio esse perfidum. Vide supra c. 6, 64.

ἀλλ' ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ) ἐλευσεως. Commode hoc acci- dit ut iterum & quidem eminentius fiat, quod olim sibi ab Achitophele factum est conquestus David; nam de eo Ps. XLI. & Psal. LV. interpretantur Hebræi, & nominatim Chaldæus paraphrastes. Tacite simul vaticinatur Judæ si- milem fore exitum, qualis Achitophelis fuerat.

ὁ τρώγων μετ' ἐμοῦ τὸν ἄρτον) Quem mensæ meæ partici- pem feceram, quod etiam apud gentes sacrum amicitiæ signum, 1. Cor. V. 11. Vide & Marc. XIV. 18.

ἐπῆρεν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τὴν πτέρναν αὐτοῦ) Pro ἐπῆραι hic in He- bræo est הגדיל quod est, magnifice usurpavit. Sensus ergo est: pede sublimi me pressit atque calcavit: id enim rectius quam ut ad cursores aut luctatores alludi dicatur.

## 13:19
Vers. 19.

ἀπ' ἄρτι λέγω ὑμῖν πρὸ τοῦ γενέσθαι) And I show myself to be conscious of thoughts and future things.

ἵνα ὅταν γένηται, πιστεύσητε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι) Namely, he whose type David bore. Unless I had said it, it could offend you when this had happened. But now you ought to be confirmed all the more: for to believe here is to be taken as the increase of faith, as above ch. 2:11 and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ἀπ' ἄρτι λέγω ὑμῖν πρὸ τοῦ γενέσθαι) Et cogitationum & re- rum futurarum conscium me ostendo.

ἵνα ὅταν γένηται, πιστεύσητε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι) Nempe is cujus typum gessit David. Nisi dixissem, poterat ubi evenisset hoc vos offendere. At nunc tanto magis confirmari de- betis: nam credere hic de augmento fidei accipiendum, ut supra c. 2, 11. & alibi.

## 13:20
Vers. 20.

ὁ λαμβάνων ἐάν τινα πέμψω) He shows that the ministries enjoined upon them will not lack their comforts. For God wishes in turn that Christians should show all services to the Apostles, which he himself will liberally reward. See Matt. 10:41. ἐάν τινα here is whosoever, as in Acts 9:2 and elsewhere.

ἐμὲ λαμβάνει) He does me as great a favor as if he were receiving me into hospitality. See Matt. 25:40.

ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ λαμβάνων, λαμβάνει τὸν πέμψαντα) What is performed for me, the Father interprets as performed for himself, Matt. in the cited place ch. 10:41.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ὁ λαμβάνων ἐάν τινα πέμψω) Ostendit ministeria ipsis in- juncta non caritura suis solatiis. Nam velle Deum vicis- sim ut Christiani Apostolis omnia officia exhibeant, quæ ipse large sit remuneraturus. Vide Matth. X. 41. ἐάν τινα hic est quemcunque, ut Act. IX. 2. & alibi.

ἐμὲ λαμβάνει) Perinde mihi gratum facit, ac si me in ho- spitium reciperet. Vide Matth. XXV. 40.

ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ λαμβάνων, λαμβάνει τὸν πέμψαντα) Quod mihi præstatur, id pater sibi præstitum interpretatur, Matth. di- cto loco c. 10, 41.

## 13:21
Vers. 21.

ἐταράχθη τῷ πνεύματι) He was troubled in spirit, both by the consideration of the danger and by the horror of the crime. See above chapter II, 33.

καὶ ἐμαρτύρησε) Having openly professed what he had said more covertly, that it would come to pass that he would be betrayed by one of the disciples. μαρτυρεῖν is accustomed to be placed absolutely where something is regarded which has preceded, as we said above c. 12, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ἐταράχθη τῷ πνεύματι) Animo commotus est & periculi consideratione & sceleris horrore. Vide supra cap. II, 33.

καὶ ἐμαρτύρησε) Palam professus quod dixerat tectius, fo- re ut ab uno discipulorum proderetur. μαρτυρεῖν solet ab- solute poni ubi aliquid respicitur quod præcessit, ut dixi- mus supra c. 12, 12.

## 13:22
Vers. 22.

ἔβλεπον ἓν) Struck by the atrocity of the thing, which was scarcely credible to upright and entirely unsuspicious minds.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ἔβλεπον ἓν) Perculsi rei atrocitate vix credibili animis probis minimeque suspicacibus.

## 13:23
Vers. 23.

ἐν κόλπῳ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ) In the bosom. Pliny: Having embraced in his lap, says Apuleius.

ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς) Whom Jesus loved more familiarly than the others. By this modest circumlocution John is accustomed to designate himself, as below c. 19, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

ἐν κόλπῳ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ) In sinu Plinius: Complexus gremio di- xit Apulejus.

ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς) Quem familiarius cæteris Jesus dilige- bat. Hac modesta circumlocutione se designare solet Io- hannes, ut infra c. 19, 26.

## 13:24
Vers. 24. νεύει ἦν τούτῳ) He nods to him to ask. Thus νεύειν δικαια in the Greek Prov. IV. 25. Peter desires this both so that the innocent may be beyond suspicion, and so that they may beware of the impure one.

Latin:

Vers. 24. νεύει ἦν τούτῳ) Innuit ei ut interrogaret. Sic νεύειν δικαια in Græco Prov. IV. 25. Cupit autem hoc Pe- trus tum ut innoxii extra suspicionem sint, tum ut sibi ca- veant ab impuro.

## 13:25
Vers. 25. ἐπιπεσὼν δὲ ἐκεῖνος ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος) Moving himself closer to his ear.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ἐπιπεσὼν δὲ ἐκεῖνος ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος) Propius se ad aurem admovens.

## 13:26
Vers. 26. ᾧ ἐγὼ βάψας, τὸ ψωμίον ἐπιδώσω, ἐπιδώσω for δώσω, as Matth. VII. 9. 10. Luc. IV. 17. c. XXIV. 30. Actor. XV. 30. Christ shows his supreme gentleness, who even now provokes the perfidious one to repentance by a certain testimony of love.

ἐμβάψας τὸ ψωμίον) Not the bitter herbs which had already been removed with the ritual supper: but into the broth of the domestic supper. מרק for the Hebrews Jud. VI. 19. 20. Is. LXV. 4.

But there is nothing here about broth or a domestic supper: nor are these words to be taken in that way: for even if the ritual or Paschal supper had been completed, the morsel (τὸ ψωμίον) and the bitter herbs (πικρίδες) with the dish (τρυβλίῳ) were nevertheless left on the table, when Christ rose to wash the feet of the disciples, Matth. XXVI. 23. Marc. XIV. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ᾧ ἐγὼ βάψας, τὸ ψωμίον ἐπιδώσω, ἐπιδώσω pro δώσω, ut Matth. VII. 9. 10. Luc. IV. 17. c. XXIV. 30. A- ctor. XV. 30. ostendit Christus summam suam lenitatem qui nunc etiam perfidiosum amoris quodam testimonio ad resipiscentiam provocat.

ἐμβάψας τὸ ψωμίον) Non οἷς ταῖς πικρίδας quæ erant jam sublatæ cum cœna rituali: sed in jusculum cœnæ domesti- cæ. מרק Hebræis Iud. VI. 19. 20. Es. LXV. 4.

At de jusculo, aut cœna domestica nihil hic ha- betur: nec hæc verba eo accipienda: nam etiamsi peracta esset cœna ritualis vel Paschalis, in mensa tamen relictum, cum ad pedes discipulorum ab- luendas surgeret Christus, τὸ ψωμίον, & πικρίδες cum τρυβλίῳ Matth. XXVI. 23. Marc. XIV. 20.

## 13:27
V. 27. λέγει ἦν αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς) When he saw that he was not moved even by this, but rather was hardening more and more.

Then Satan entered into him) Thus also Luke speaks of Judas, XXII. 3. It is to be understood here that εἰσῆλθε means he entered deeply, which is said in Acts V. 3, Satan filled the heart; where there is nothing more that resists, the light of right reason having been gradually extinguished.

ὃ ποιεῖς) What you wish to do, as above 6.

Ποίησον τάχιον) This is proverbial, do what you do, in a Latin epigram: Seneca, do if you do anything. In Plautus in the Trinummus: Act if you act at all. The same in the Persa: If you are going to do this, do it. δρᾶγ’ εἴ τι δράσεις in Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis, however, signifies: I do not hinder, I am prepared to bear it. See 2 Maccabees VII. 30, what are you waiting for? Nor is it much different above II. 19, destroy this temple. Τάχιον for quickly, the comparative for the positive, as ocius in Latin.

Latin:

V. 27. λέγει ἦν αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς) Cum ne sic quidem eum flecti- videret sed magis magisque obdurescere.

Τότε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ἐκεῖνον ὁ Σατανᾶς) Sic & Lu- cas de Juda loquitur, XXII. 3. Intelligendum hic εἰσῆλθε penitus intravit, quod dicitur Act. V. 3. ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατα- νᾶς τὴν καρδίαν· ubi nihil amplius est, quod resistat, lumine rectæ rationis paulatim extincto.

ὃ ποιεῖς) Quod facere vis, ut supra 6.

Ποίησον τάχιον) Est hoc proverbiale fac quod facis in lati- no epigrammate: Seneca fac si quid facis. Plauto in Tri- nummo: Age si quid agis. Idem Persa: Hoc si facturus face. δρᾶγ’ εἴ τι δράσεις apud Euripidem Iphigenia in Aulide, si- gnificat autem: non impedio, ferre paratus sum. Sit 2. Maccab. VII. 30. τίνα μένετε; nec longe aliter supra II. 19. λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τῦτον. Τάχιον pro cito, comparativum pro positivo, ut ocius latine.

## 13:28
Vers. 28. No one of those reclining knew for what he said to him) No one understood the force of those words, not even John; for he did not think the crime was so near.

Latin:

Vers. 28. Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τῶν ἀνακειμένων πρὸς τί εἶπεν αὐτῷ) Ne- mo vim illorum verborum intellexit, ne Johannes quidem; neque enim existimabat tam prope esse facinus.

## 13:29
Vers. 29. For some thought) Others than John.

Ἐπεὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον εἶχεν) Above XII. 6.

Ἀγόρασον ὧν χρείαν ἔχομεν εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν) Victims. For although Christ had in some way anticipated the Paschal Supper, as has been said on Matthew, they suspected nevertheless some other cause rather than that he was to die so soon, namely before the following evening.

τοῖς πτωχοῖς ἵνα τὶ δῷ) ἵνα placed after, as in Rom. XI. 31.

Latin:

Vers. 29. Τινὲς γὰρ ἐδόκεν) Alii quam Johannes.

Ἐπεὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον εἶχεν) Supra XII. 6.

Ἀγόρασον ὧν χρείαν ἔχομεν εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν) Victimas. Quan- quam enim Christus Paschaticam Cœnam aliquo modo anticipaverat, ut dictum est ad Matthæum, suspicabantur tamen aliam quamvis causam potius, quam quod tam cito, ante sequentem vesperam scilicet, esset moriturus.

τοῖς πτωχοῖς ἵνα τὶ δῷ) ἵνα postpositum, ut Rom. XI. 31.

## 13:30
Vers. 30. He went out, and it was night) The beginning of the night, for the discourses that follow were drawn out into the deep night. See what [is written] on Matthew.

Latin:

Vers. 30. Ἐξῆλθεν, ἧν δὲ νύξ) Initium noctis, nam qui se- quuntur sermones in multam noctem protracti. Vide quæ ad Matth.

## 13:31
V. 31. Ὄτε ἐξῆλθε) So the very many Greek codices and the Syriac have it, and they connect it with the preceding. For those who have ὅτε ὆ν ἐξῆλθε are none other than those who have been entirely made to conform to the Latin exemplar.

PART III.

A sermon on the Glorification of Christ and the duty of mutual love.

Now the Son of man is glorified) It has already sufficiently appeared through these proofs and works, to which an end must now be put, that I have been sent by God: even by the very judgment of the hidden traitor. See above XII. 28. and VIII. 54.

And God is glorified in him) Through him: because both the proofs excite to the true worship of God, and Jesus had perpetually ascribed his very works to God the author. See VII. 18.

Latin:

V. 31. Ὄτε ἐξῆλθε) Ita habent, & cum superioribus conne- ctunt Græci codites longe plurimi & Syrus. Nam qui habent ὅτε ὆ν ἐξῆλθε non alii sunt quam qui toti facti sunt ad Lati- num exemplar.

PARS III.

Concio de Christi Glorificatione & dilectionis mutua debito.

Νῦν ἐδοξάσθη ὁ ὑὸς τῦ ἀνθρώπε) Satis jam appa- ruit per hæc documenta & opera, quibus jam finis im- ponendus est me à Deo inissum: etiam ipso judicio laten- tis proditoris. Vide supra XII. 28. & VIII. 54.

Καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ) Per ipsum: quia & docu- menta ad verum Dei cultum excitant, & opera ipsa sua Jesus Deo auctori perpetuo adscripserat. Vide VII. 18.

## 13:32
Vers. 32. If God is glorified in him) If for since. Thus Matt. XXII. 45. and elsewhere. He uses an axiom known among the Hebrews, which exists in 1 Sam. II. 30. where in the Greek God speaks thus: those who glorify me I will glorify.

And God shall glorify him in himself) Not through Angels but through himself, through signs in the sun and earth, through the resurrection from the dead, the lifting up into heaven, and the giving of a name above every name. See the said place XII. 28.

And he shall straightway glorify him) Immediately at the very point of death he will begin to render testimony to him, so that those who look on will be about to say, this is truly the son of God: nor will he leave him in death except for a very little time.

Latin:

Vers. 32. εἰ ὁ Θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ) εἰ pro quandoqui- dem. Sic Matth. XXII. 45. & alibi. Utitur axiomate noto inter Hebræos, quod extat 1. Sam. II. 30. ubi in Græ- co Deus sic loquitur τὺς δοξάζοντάς με δοξάσω.

Καὶ ὁ Θεὸς δοξάσει αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ) Non per Angelos sed per seipsum, per signa in sole & terra, per resuscitationem è mortuis, evectionem in cœlum, & donationem nominis supra omne nomen. Vide dictum locum XII. 28.

Καὶ εὐθὺς δοξάσει αὐτὸν) Statim in ipso mortis puncto in- cipiet ei testimonium reddere, ita ut qui aspiciant dicturi sint, hic vere filius Dei est: neque in morte eum relinquet nisi perpauxillo tempore.

## 13:33
Vers. 33. Little children) Christ in his death found that most sad, that it would affect his own with most grievous sorrow: therefore he applies all comforts to them, even endearments of words such as this, little children. Thus Gal. IV. 19. 1 John II. 1. 12. 28. III. 7. 18. IV. 4. V. 21.

Yet a little while I am with you) Namely, by this daily presence. For after the resurrection he was present only economically. Thus above VII. 33. XII. 35. below XVI. 10.

You shall seek me) If by chance you seek me afterwards: as we explained above VII. 34.

And as I said to the Jews) In the said place VII. 34.

And to you I say now) The place is inaccessible. You cannot come there by any human aid.

Latin:

Vers. 33. Τεκνία) Christus in morte sua illud reperiebat tristissimum quod gravissime mœrore suos esset affectura: itaque omnia illis solatia adhibet, etiam verborum blandi- menta quale hoc τεκνία. Sic Gal. IV. 19. 1. Joh. II. 1. 12. 28. III. 7. 18. IV. 4. V. 21.

Ἔτι μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι) Nempe quotidiana hac præsen- tia. Nam post resurrectionem adfuit tantum οἰκονομικῶς Sic supra VII. 33. XII. 35. infra XVI, 10.

Ζητήσετί με) Si forte quæratis me postea: ut exposuimus supra VII. 34.

Καὶ καθὼς εἶπον τοῖς Ἰυδαίοις) Dicto loco VII. 34.

Καὶ ὑμῖν λέγω ἄρτι) Locus est inaccessus. Non pote- stis eo venire ulla humana ope.

## 13:34
Vers. 34. A new commandment I give to you) As those departing are accustomed to give commands to their own. But he calls it new, because he does not treat of the common love of all, nor of that which is bestowed because of consanguinity or benefits received, but of the special love of Christians among themselves as they are such. Therefore below he calls this his own, as it were, proper commandment 21. Let us love one another, just as he gave the commandment, 1 John III. 23. To this points that of the Apostle: for you yourselves are taught of God to love one another. John however in his first Epistle II. 7. and second 6. when he says this precept is old and given from the beginning, understands the beginning of the Gospel and Christianity. Jerome in his Commentary on the Epistle of John: John the Apostle, being admonished by the brethren why he always inculcated saying: Little children, love one another: replied because it is the commandment of the LORD, and if it alone be done, it suffices. Where he calls it the LORD'S commandment, because as we have already said it is his own and peculiar. And it alone suffices, because, if it be done as it ought, it cannot but proceed from the love of God, since our own love draws us back from that.

for this reason, that it treats of the special love of the faithful: because the mutual love of the faithful flourished in every age, and ought to have flourished, nor are the faithful in the N. T. bound to love one another for any other reason than the faithful of old loved one another in the O. T.: just as also the same faith in the Messiah obtained in both, Acts XV. 10. Heb. XIII. v. 8. with this sole exception, that the righteous of old believed in the Messiah to be exhibited, but we believe in the Messiah exhibited. It is not therefore called new because this commandment was finally delivered by Christ in the N. T., since Christ did not deliver the commandment concerning love as new, but was accustomed to repeat and inculcate it as old, and from the Old Testament, Matt. XXII. 19. Luke X. 25. Lev. XIX. 18. nor by John 1 Epist. II. 7. & 2. Epist. v. 6. is it called old, because it was given from the beginning of the Gospel and Christianity, since he was not ignorant that it was delivered in the O. T.: both as regards the common love of one's neighbor, and as regards the Φιλαδελφίαν of those who are blood-relatives in the faith, Ps. CXXXIII. 1. Wherefore it is called new (1) because it ought always to be new and fresh in us, and held in the chief place, never to be antiquated or postponed: because that is called new which is excellent, Ps. XCVI. 1. XCVIII. This precept of charity always remains new, for however much we may have shown the duties of charity to our neighbors, we nevertheless always remain debtors to this law, Rom. XIII. 8. (2) because it has been renewed by Christ, and vindicated from Pharisaical corruptions in such a way that it could be reckoned as new, (3) because it has been illustrated by the new example of Christ, in whom we have the idea of true love, (4) because it has been newly sanctioned by the death of Christ, 1 John III. 16. Thus Irenaeus b. IV. c. 15. Christ did not bring forward anything greater than the precept of love, but renewed this very thing for his disciples. Which is acknowledged by those among the Papists who otherwise judge a more perfect degree of love to have been prescribed by Christ, Pererius the Jesuit Disp. XLI. on John in this place, saying: The precept of love is not new simply and altogether, because it had been even in the old law, and from the beginning of the world: but it was new, because it had been renewed by Christ, declared in a new way, and confirmed by his new and admirable example. This precept can also be called new (5) because it pertains to the new man renewed through the Holy Spirit, and is not fulfilled except by the new spirit received from Christ, Gal. IV. 14. Finally (6) it is new, because it was promulgated in a new way: Moses demands perfect love, and accuses when it is not performed, and teaches, and covers the adhering imperfection and uncleanness by his own merit. Moses only commands love, but he does not provide the strength to perform it; but he is a schoolmaster unto Christ, in whom is not only the end of this law, but from whom also the spirit of charity is had, Christ therefore commands in such a way that he simultaneously bestows upon us the Spirit and the strength to perform what is commanded, 2 Cor. III. 7. Gal. III. 2.

That you love one another) As brothers, as fellow-disciples. As I have loved you, that you also love one another) He explains what kind of love he requires: namely, that we not only prefer others to ourselves in the things of this life, 1 Cor. X. 24. but also that we do not shrink from any inconveniences for the eternal salvation of others, not even death, for this is that love of Christ, with which he loved us: below XV. 13. Wherefore because he himself laid down his soul for us, we also ought to lay down our souls for our brothers. 1 John III. 16.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ἐντολὴν καινὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν) Ut solent abeun- tes mandata suis dare. Novum autem dicit, quia non agit de dilectione communi omnium, nec de ea, quæ ob con sanguinitatem aut beneficia accepta impenditur, sed de speciali Christianorum inter se qua tales sunt. Itaque in- fra hoc suum quasi proprium sibi mandatum vocat 21. Di- ligamus invicem, sicut ipse dedit mandatum, 1. Joh. III. 23. Huc illud spectat Apostoli: αὐτὸς γὰρ ὑμᾶς θεοδιδακτοί ἐσε εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾷν ἀλλήλυς. Johannes autem in Epistola priore II. 7. & secunda 6. præceptum hoc vetus & ab initio da- tum cum ait, initium Evangelii & Christianismi intelligit. Hieronymus Commentario ad Epistolam Johannis, Jo- hannes Apostolus à fratribus admonitus, cur semper inculca- ret dicens: Filioli, diligite alterutrum: respondit quia præce- ptum DOMINI est, & si solum fiat, sufficit. Ubi DO- MINI præceptum vocat, quia ut jam diximus ejus pro- prium est ac peculiare. Et solum sufficit, quia, si fiat ut oportet, non potest non ex Dei amore proficisci, cum nostri amor inde nos retrahat.

ideo, quod de speciali dilectione fidelium agat: quia dilectio mutua fidelium omni seculo viguit, & vigere debuit, nec alia ratione fideles in N. T. se diligere tenentur, quam olim in V. T. se diligebant fideles: quemadmodum etiam eadem in Messiam fides utrobique obtinuit, Actor. XV. 10. Ebr. XIII. v. 8. eo solum excepto, quod antiqui justi cre- diderint in Messiam exhibendum, nos autem in Messiam exhibitum credamus. Non ergo novum dicitur, quod hoc mandatum demum à Christo in N. T. traditum sit, quum Christus mandatum de dilectione non ut novum tradiderit, sed ut vetus, & è Vet. Test. repetere & inculcare consueverit, Matth. XXII. 19. Luc. X. 25. Levit. XIX. 18. nec à Johanne 1. Epist. II. 7. & 2. Epist. v. 6. vetus dicatur, quod ab initio Evangelii & Christianismi id datum sit, siquidem in V. T. id traditum esse non ignora- vit: cum quoad communem proximi dilectio- nem, tum quoad Φιλαδελφίαν eorum, qui con- sanguinei sunt in fide, Ps. CXXXIII. 1. Quapropter novum dicitur (1) quia semper novum & recens in nobis esse, atque præcipuo loco haberi debet, nunquam antiquari, aut posthaberi: quia novum dicitur, quod eximium est Ps. XCVI. 1. XCVIII. Semper hoc præceptum charitatis novum manet, nam utut charitatis officia proximis exhibueri- mus, semper tamen hujus legis debitores mane- mus, Rom. XIII. 8. (2) quia à Christo renovatum, & à corruptelis Pharisæicis vindicatum ita est, ut pro novo censeri potuerit, (3) quia novo exemplo Christi illustratum est, in quo ideam habemus veræ dile- ctionis, (4) quia morte Christi noviter sancitum est, 1. Joh. III. 16. Sic Irenæus l. IV. c. 15. Christus aliud majus præcepto dilectionis non detulit, sed hoc ipsum renovavit discipulis suis. Quod agnoscit è Pontifi- ciis alioquin perfectiorem gradum dilectionis à Christo præscriptum censentibus, Pererius Jesui- ta Disp. XLI. in Joh. h. l. Præceptum, inquiens, dile- ctionis non est novum simpliciter & omnino, quia fuerat etiam in lege veteri, & ab initio mundi: no- vum autem erat, quia renovatum à Christo fuerat, novo modo declaratum, novoque & admirabili suo exemplo confirmatum. Novum etiam (5) dici potest hoc præceptum, quia ad novum hominem per Spi- ritum S. renovatum pertinet, & non nisi novo spiri- tu à Christo accepto impletur, Gal. IV. 14. Denique (6) novum est, quia novo modo promulgatum: Mo- ses dilectionem perfectam exigit, eaque non præ- stita accusat, & docet, & adhærentem imperfectio- nem & immunditiem merito suo tegit. Moses tan- tum præcipit dilectionem, vires autem præstandi non sufficit; ast pædagogus est ad Christum, in quo non tantum τέλος hujus legis, sed à quo etiam spi- ritus charitatis habetur, Christus ergo ita præcipit, ut Spiritum & vires præstandi, quod jubetur, no- bis simul largiatur, 2. Cor. III. 7. Gal. III. 2.

Ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους) Ut fratres, ut condiscipulos. Καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους) Exponit, qualem dilectionem requirat: nempe ut non tantum in re- bus hujus vitæ alii alios nobis præferamus, 1. Cor. X. 24. verum etiam ut pro aliorum salute æterna nulla incommo- da defugiamus, ne mortem quidem, Hæc enim est illa Chri- sti dilectio, qua nos dilexit: inf. XV. 13. Quare quia ipse a- nimam suam pro nobis posuit, & nos debemus pro fratribus nostris animas ponere. 1. Joh. III. 16.

## 13:35
Verse 35. By this shall all men know, that you are my disciples) The disciples of the lawyers were known by certain received opinions and interpretations of the law, the Pharisees by their habit and ceremonies, the disciples of John the Baptist by the austerity of their life and their fasts: but by what shall the disciples of Christ be known, if not by the imitation of their master, i.e., mutual love? By this mark that Church of the first times was distinguished, when the heart and soul of the believers was one, Acts IV. 32. Tertullian in his Apology: But the operation of such great love brands us with a mark among some. See, they say, how they love one another. For they themselves hate one another, and how they are prepared to die for one another be. For they themselves will be more prepared to kill one another. Presently, therefore, because we are mingled in mind and soul, we doubt nothing about the sharing of property. All things are held in common among us except wives. Minutius: Thus we love with mutual affection, which you grieve at; since we do not know how to hate: Thus we, which you envy, call ourselves brothers, as all being of one God the Parent, as partners in faith, as co-heirs of hope. What would those Christians say now if they saw our times, if I will not say the harshest disputes, but the most savage wars of Christians among themselves, and what obstacles? If they heard the marks of the Church brought forward by the loud clamors of those contending, all of them rather than that one which the Master assigned? Ἐὰν ἀγάπην ἔχητε ἐν ἀλλήλοις) That is, among yourselves. Thus Mark IX. 50. εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις (have peace among yourselves).

PART IV. Prediction concerning the threefold denial of Peter.

Latin:

Vers. 35. Ἐν τούτῳ γνώσονται πάντες, ὅτι ἐμοὶ μαθηταί ἐστε) Discipuli legisperitorum ex receptis quibusdam sententiis & interpretationibus legis noscebantur, Pharisæorum ex habitu & ceremoniis, Johannis Baptistæ ex vitæ austeritate & jejuniis: at discipuli Christi, quo cognoscentur nisi imita- tione magistri, i. e. mutua dilectione? Hac nota insignis fuit illa primorum temporum Ecclesia, cum esset credentium cor unum & anima una Act. IV. 32. Tertullianus Apologeti- co: Sed ejusmodi vel maximæ dilectionis operatio nobis notam inurit apud quosdam. Vide, inquiunt, ut invicem se diligant. Ipsi enim invicem oderunt, & ut pro alterutro mori parati sint. Ipsi enim ad occidendum alterutrum paratiores erunt. Mox Itaque quia animo animaque miscemur, nihil de rei communicatione dubitamus. Omnia indiscreta sunt apud nos præter uxores. Minutius: Sic mutuo, quod doletis, amore diligimus; quoniam odisse non novimus: Sic nos, quod invidetis, fratres vocamus ut unius Dei Parentis omnes, ut consortes fidei, ut spei cohæredes. Quid nunc illi dicerent Christiani si nostra viderent tempora, si, non dicam lites asperrimas, sed sævissima bella Christianorum inter se, & quas obreculas? si notas Ecclesiæ audirent magnis certantium clamoribus adferri omnes potius, quam illam quam Magister assignavit? Ἐὰν ἀγάπην ἔχητε ἐν ἀλλήλοις) Id est inter vos. Sic Marc. IX. 50. εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.

PARS IV. Prædictio de trina negatione Petri.

## 13:36
Verse 36. Ποῦ ὑπάγεις (Where are you going?) Peter thought the Lord was preparing a journey into distant places, full of inconveniences.

Ὅπου ὑπάγω οὐ δύνασαί μοι νῦν ἀκολουθῆσαι (Where I am going you cannot follow me now) By his testimony Christ indicates that he does not yet have enough courage to undergo death, through which the journey into heaven lies.

Ὕστερον δὲ ἀκολουθήσεις μοι (But you will follow me later) Strengthened by the Spirit. See below XXI. 18. ὕστερον (later), eventually, at some time, as the Syriac translates it here.

Latin:

Vers. 36. Ποῦ ὑπάγεις) Existimavit Petrus Dominum iter parare in locos longinquos, plenum incommodis.

Ὅπου ὑπάγω οὐ δύνασαί μοι νῦν ἀκολουθῆσαι) Teste indicat Christus nondum illi sat esse animi ut mortem subeat, per quam iter sit in cœlum.

Ὕστερον δὲ ἀκολουθήσεις μοι) Spiritu firmatus. Vide infra XXI. 18. ὕστερον tandem, aliquando, ut hic vertit Syrus.

## 13:37
Verse 37. Διά τί οὐ δύναμαί σοι ἀκολουθῆσαι ἄρτι (Why can I not follow you now?) What hinders? Do you think any hardship of the journey terrifies me?

τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπέρ σου θήσω (I will lay down my life for you) If there be need, I will even expose myself to the danger of death for your sake. We have spoken about this phrase in X. 11. & following.

Latin:

Vers. 37. Διά τί οὐ δύναμαί σοι ἀκολουθῆσαι ἄρτι) Quid impedit? Putasne ulla itineris molestia me terreri:

τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπέρ σου θήσω) Si opus sit, etiam mortis discrimini me pro tuo capite objiciam. De hac phrasi diximus X. 11. & seqq.

## 13:38
Verse 38. τὴν ψυχήν σου ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ θήσεις (Will you lay down your life for me?) Is it really so? Is there nothing so grave that you will not undergo it for me? This is pronounced in such a way that it can be understood from it that he who asks does not believe it at all.

Οὐ μὴ ἀλέκτωρ φωνήσει (The rooster will not crow) With that more familiar crowing which is called the cockcrow κατ' ἐξοχὴν (by way of eminence).

Ἕως οὗ ἀπαρνήσῃ με τρίς (Until you deny me three times) That is, you will deny that you know me three times before the rooster crows. John and Luke narrate this as having been said in the house. Wherefore it is credible that in Matthew and Mark there is a hysteron proteron: so that τότε (then) is, around that time, as we noted regarding Matthew.

Latin:

Vers. 38. τὴν ψυχήν σου ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ θήσεις) Itane vero? nihil tam grave est, quod non pro me sis subiturus? Hoc ita pronunciatur, ut inde intelligi possit minime eum qui interrogat, id credere.

Οὐ μὴ ἀλέκτωρ φωνήσει) Cantu illo notiore & qui κατ' ἐξοχὴν gallicinium dicitur.

Ἕως οὗ ἀπαρνήσῃ με τρίς) Id est prius ter negabis me tibi cognitum quam gallus cantet. Johannes & Lucas hoc narrant ut in domo dictum. Quare credibile est apud Matthæum & Marcum esse ὑπάτοδον : ut τότε sit, circa illud tempus, quomodo ad Matthæum notavimus.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Jesus encourages his dismayed disciples with faith in God and in himself, and with the hope of a dwelling in heaven, and of his own return. He instructs Thomas, who was asking about the way and the destination, that no one comes to the Father except through him; he instructs Philip, who was seeking to be shown the Father, concerning his indwelling (περιχωρήσει) in the Father, with his works bearing witness; and he promises to those who believe the power of working miracles (θαυματουργίαν) and the granting of all things which they might ask, along with another Paraclete, and the manifestation of his own perfection upon his return, and a gracious indwelling, provided they keep his word: since they are to be taught all things and reminded of all things by the Holy Spirit. Furthermore, he bequeaths his peace to them; and he removes their fear regarding his departure, because of the joy resulting from his departure to the Father, and the victory over the prince of the world.

There are four parts. I. Consolation concerning his departure, to v. 4. II. Instruction of Thomas concerning the way and the end, and of Philip concerning the Father, that he is in him and is seen, to v. 11. III. Promise of the gift of miracles, and of the hearing of prayers, of the assistance of the Paraclete, and of his return and further manifestation, to v. 26. IV. The legacy of his peace, with the removal of all fear, to v. 31.

PART I. Jesus' consolation concerning his departure.

Vers. 1. Let not your heart be troubled) He saw them moved by the preceding discourses concerning his death, concerning dangers, concerning denial. Therefore he raises them up.

Believe in God) Just as from your earliest age you have learned to place your trust in God, as the author and preserver of all things: as in Ps. LXXVIII. 7. for 'as' is understood here as above V. 17. and below 19.

And believe in me) So also place your trust in me, who am present and known, as the author and preserver of the Church. I myself, being so loving of you, will be your helper.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Jesus discipulos consternatos fide in Deum & sese, ac spe mansionis in cœlis, & reditus sui erigit. Thomam quærentem de via & termino, quod non nisi per se ad Patrem quis veniat, Philippum Patrem sibi monstrari expetentem de περιχωρήσει in Patre, operibus suis attestantibus, instruit ac credentibus θαυματουργίαν & exauditionem omnium, quæ petierint, promittit, cum Paracleto alio, & sui sub reditum perfectioni manifestatione, ac gratiosa inhabitatione, modo verbum suum servarint: siquidem à Sp. S. omnia docendi sint, ac de omnibus commonendi: Porro pacem suam ipsis legat: & pavorem ex abitu adimit, ob gaudium ex abitu ad Patrem, & principis mundi victoriam.

Partes sunt quatuor I. Consolatio de abitu suo, ad v. 4. II. Informatio Thomæ de via & termino, & Philippi de Patre, quod in se sit & conspiciatur, ad v. 11. III. Promissio doni miraculorum, & exauditionis precum, assistentiæ Paracleti, & reditus sui ac ulterioris manifestationis, ad v. 26. IV. Legatio pacis suæ, cum ademtione omnis timoris, ad v. 31.

PARS I. Consolatio Jesu de abitu suo.

Vers. 1. Μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία) Videbat eos commotos antecedentibus, de sua morte, de periculis, de abnegatione sermonibus. Itaque eos erigit.

Πιστεύετε εἰς τὸν Θεόν) Sicuti à prima ætate didicistis fiduciam collocare in Deo, ut rerum omnium autore & conservatore: ut in Ps. LXXVIII. 7. nam sicut hic subauditur ut supra V. 17. & infra 19.

Καὶ εἰς ἐμὲ πιστεύετε) Ita & in me coram conspectum notumque fiduciam collocate ut Ecclesiæ auctorem & conservatorem. Ego ipse, adeo amans vestri, ero adjutor vester.

## 14:2
Vers. 2. There are many mansions) You will not be excluded. There is room for many also. Μονὴ is a place of dwelling, which he will immediately call τόπον, I Macc. VII. 39. there was no place for them. The ancients do not wrongly understand the multitude of places as having differences of degrees. Clement Strom. VI. sheep are deemed worthy of mansions according to their faith. Tertullian in Scorpiaco: How are there many mansions with the Father if not for the variety of merits? how also will star differ from star in glory, if not for the diversity of rays?

But if not I would have told you) The Syrian punctuates here, and I do not doubt that this is correct. For εἰ δὲ μὴ is very often in these books, if it were not so, if there were no place for you, I would have told you this openly, as is my custom, I would have taken away from you a vain hope. But now I have said to Peter, and in Peter to all, that it will eventually come to pass that you will follow me there.

Latin:

Vers. 2. Μοναὶ πολλαί εἰσι) Non excludemini. Locus est & pluribus umbris. Μονὴ est habitandi locus, quod statim di- cet τόπον, I. Macc. VII. 39. μὴ ὄρε αὐτοῖς μονή. Multitudi- nem autem locorum non male veteres intelligunt cum gra- duum differentiis. Clemens Strom. VI. πρόβατα αὔταις μονὴς ἀναλογῶς τῆς πίσεως κατηξιωμένα. Tertullianus Scorpiaco : Quomodo multæ mansiones apud Patrem si non pro varietate meritorum? quomodo & stella à stella distabit in gloria, nisi pro diversitate radiorum?

Εἰ δὲ μὴ εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν) Hic interpungit Syrus, nec dubito quin id rectum sit. Nam εἰ δὲ μὴ sæpissime in his libris est, ni ita esset, si locus non esset vobis, aperte hoc dixissem vobis, ut mos meus est, ademissem vobis spem inanem. Nunc au- tem Petro & in Petro omnibus dixi, futurum tandem ut me illuc sequamini.

## 14:3
Vers. 3. I go to prepare a place for you) A similitude taken from one of the companions, who, having gone ahead on a journey to an inn, assigns rooms there to the others and ensures that they are ready for those arriving.

If I go) ἐὰν here means after, as above XII. vers. 32.

I come again and will take you to myself) The similitude is continued. For those who have arrived first at an inn are accustomed to go out to meet the others who are now arriving and to bring them in. The angel to the Apostles Acts I. 11. this Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will so come in the way you saw him going into heaven.

That where I am) Εἰμὶ that is, I will be. As above VII. 34.

And you may be) Consorts, partakers of my happiness Rom. VIII. 17.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Πορεύνομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν) Similitudo sum- ta ab uno comitum, qui in itinere prægressus ad diversorium ibi cæteris cubicula assignat & efficit ut venientibus parata sint.

Ἐὰν πορευθῶ) ἐὰν hic valet postquam, ut supra XII. vers. 32.

Πάλιν ἔρχομαι καὶ παραλήψομαι ὑμᾶς πρὸς ἐμαυτόν) Con- tinuatur similitudo. Nam solent qui primi in diversorium venerunt, cæteris jam adventantibus obviam procedere & eos introducere. Angelus ad Apostolos Actor. I. 11. ὅ- τῳ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναληφθεὶς ἀφ' ὑμῶν, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.

Ἵνα ὅπε εἰμὶ ἐγὼ) Εἰμὶ id est ero. Ut supra VII. 34.

Καὶ ὑμεῖς ἦτε) Consortes, participes meæ felicitatis Rom. VIII. 17

## 14:4
Vers. 4. And where I go you know) It is a manner of speaking when we wish to say that we have said enough. You have where I am going. For he had already named the house of the Father.

And the way you know) You have also by what way I go there. For what he had said, that he would no longer be seen, and what he had immediately added concerning his love, was a circumlocution for the death to be undergone for them.

PART II. Information of Thomas concerning the way and the destination, and of Philip concerning the Father, that he is in Christ, and is seen.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Ὅπε ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε) Mos est loquendi cum dicere volumus, satis nos dixisse. Habetis quo vadam. Nam domum Patris jam nominaverat.

Καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν οἴδατε) Habetis & qua via eo vadam. Nam quod dixerat se non amplius conspiciendum & quod statim addiderat de sua dilectione, circumlocutio erat mortis pro ipsis subeundæ.

PARS II. Informatio Thomæ de via & termino, & Phi- lippi de Patre, quod in Christo sit, & conspiciatur.

## 14:5
Vers. 5. Thomas) Slower than the others in matters of faith.

We do not know where you go) Thomas, hindered either by slowness of wit or by sadness, had not understood what Jesus meant, and therefore, making a conjecture from himself, he did not think the others had understood either.

How can we know the way) A way is a relation to something, namely from one terminus to another. But if the goal is unknown, the way cannot be conceived under the aspect of a way.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Θωμᾶς) Cæteris tardior ad res fidei.

Οὐκ οἴδαμεν πῦ ὑπάγεις) Thomas sive ingenii tarditate si- ve mœstitia impeditus non intellexerat quid Jesus signifi- caret, ac proinde de se conjecturam faciens, nec cæteros intellexisse existimabat.

Πῶς δυνάμεθα τὴν ὁδὸν εἰδέναι) Via est ἓν πρός τι, nempe à termino ad terminum alterum. Quod si ignoretur quæ sit meta non potest via sub ratione viæ concipi.

## 14:6
Vers. 6. I am the way) Christ, in order to show how much he had care for his own, answers nothing about himself, but indicates to them more fully how they too can arrive at the Father. Christ, calling himself the way, seems to allude to the passage in Isaiah 35:8. By calling himself the way, he understands his own actions, by the example of which, as a paved road, we must walk.

And the truth) The Gospel, the word of truth, Eph. 1:13. A discourse having nothing false mixed in. Christ, calling himself the truth, that is, the teacher of truth, indicates that faith is to be had in him: that what he promises will come to pass.

And the life) That is, the giver of eternal life, as above in 11:25. This is a great thing, that Christ himself has the right to give eternal life. For that has the greatest force so that we may imitate him and believe in him.

No one comes to the Father) He puts obtaining eternal life for the same thing as coming to the Father: because that eternal life will be with the Father.

Except through me) That is, unless one has me, and imitates me, as the preceding things show.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς) Christus ut ostenderet quantum haberet suorum curam, de se nihil respondet, sed ipsis ple- nius indicat quomodo ipsi quoque ad Patrem pervenire possint. Videtur autem Christus se viam dicens alludere ad locum, Esaiæ XXXV. 8. Se autem nominans viam, a- ctiones suas intelligit per quarum exemplum tanquam stra- tum iter nobis ambulandum est.

Καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια) Evangelium λόγῳ ἀληθείας Eph. I. v. 13. Sermo nihil falsi admixtum habens. Christus se veritatem, id est veri doctorem vocans, indicat sibi fidem habendam: eventurum quod pollicetur.

Καὶ ἡ ζωὴ) Id est dator vitæ æternæ, ut supra XI. 25. mul- tum hoc est quod Christus ipse vitæ æternæ dandæ jus ha- bet. Id enim ut eum imitemur utque ei credamus vim habet maximam.

Οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν πατέρα) Pro eodem ponit vitam æ- ternam consequi, aut ad Patrem venire: quia vita illa æ- terna erit apud Patrem.

Εἰ μὴ δι' ἐμῦ) Id est nisi mihi habeat, meque imitetur, ut ostendunt præcedentia.

## 14:7
Vers. 7. If you had known me) If you rightly knew me, my properties, which shine forth in my actions.

And you would have known the Father) By the same token you would have known the Father, in whom are the same properties of goodness, justice, and wisdom. Such is that saying: He who rightly knows both, will know both. See above VIII. 19.

And from now on you know him) As if one were to say to someone who has seen the image of another, and does not fail to know whose image it is, now you know him from his features.

And you have seen him) Namely in me, his likeness.

Latin:

Vers. 7. Εἰ ἐγνώκειτέ με) Si recte me noscetis, proprietates meas, quæ in actionibus elucent.

Καὶ τὸν πατέρα με ἐγνώκειτε ἂν) Eadem opera Patrem nos- setis, in quo eædem sunt proprietates bonitatis, justitiæ, sa- pientiæ. Tale est illud: Qui utrambis recte norit, ambas noverit. Vide supra VIII. 19.

Καὶ ἀπ' ἄρτι γινώσκετε αὐτὸν) Ut si quis dicat ei qui ima- ginem alicujus vidit, nec nescit cujus sit imago, jam illum nosti ex lineamentis.

Καὶ ἑωράκατε αὐτὸν) Nempe in me, ejus effigie.

## 14:8
Vers. 8. Show us the Father) He had read that God had sometimes appeared to the fathers in various ways; he would like this to be granted to him as well.

And it is enough for us) We will not be troublesome to you by asking further.

Latin:

Vers. 8. Δεῖξον ὑμῖν τὸν πατέρα) Legerat Deum variis mo- dis interdum apparuisse patribus; hoc vellet & sibi conce- di.

Καὶ ἀρκεῖ ἡμῖν) Non ultra interrogando molesti tibi eri- mus.

## 14:9
Vers. 9. Have I been so long time with you, and hast thou not known me?] That is, since I have been dealing with you so long and so familiarly, you do not yet know what kind of person I am. Certainly you ought to have known: and if you had known sufficiently, you would already be able to know what kind of person the Father is.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Τoσoῦτον χρόνον μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι, κὴ οὐκ ἔγνωκάς με;] Id est cum tamdiu tam familiariter vobiscum agam, non- dum me nostis qualis sim. Certe nosse debebatis: & si satis nossetis, jam & scire possetis qualis sit Pater.

## 14:10
Vers. 10. That I am in the Father] Through the purpose of obedience, as we explained at X. 38.

We have spoken of the true sense at John X. 38. The Son is said to be in the Father for the same reason that the Father is in the Son: Whence the pious ancients explained this concerning the ὁμοουσίᾳ of the Father and the Son, and their mutual περιχωρήσει. Hilary, book IX, on the Trinity: The Father is to be believed to be in the Son and the Son in the Father through the unity of nature, through the power of virtue, through the equality of honor, through the generation of birth. Cf. Damascene, book I, on the Orthodox Faith, ch. II.

And the Father in me still] Through efficacy.

The words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself] The reason for the former member is rendered: I speak nothing not commanded by the Father. Above VII. 17.

But the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works] The reason for the other member, for the Father works through me, and thus shows himself to be in me. For μένειν to John is to be in. As above V. 8. The properties of God are known from the works, which were never brought forth greater and more numerous than through Christ: so that it was much more clearly possible to conceive the wisdom, goodness, and power of God in these, than in those visions which happened to the Prophets, and by which those properties were only shadowed forth through likenesses and figures. Nonnus briefly explains the two members we have mentioned, by which the conjunction of the Father and the Son is indicated, thus:

As my begetter exists with me, because I myself am of the same nature as the parent, I speaking, and he acting.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ] Per obedientiae proposi- tum, ut exposuimus X. 38.

De vero sensu diximus ad Joh. X. 38. Eadem ratione Filius in Patre esse dicitur, qua est Pater in Filio: Unde exposuere id pii veteres de ὁμο- υσίᾳ Patris & Filii, mutuaque περιχωρήσει. Hilar. lib. IX. de Trin. Credendus est Pater in Filio & Filius in Patre per naturae unitatem, per virtutis potesta- tem, per honoris aequalitatem, per nativitatis gene- rationem. Conf. Damasc. lib. I. de Orthodox. Fid. c. II.

Καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔτι] Per efficaciam.

Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ ὑμῖν ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ] Ratio redditur prioris membri nihil loquor non imperatum a Patre. Supra VII. 17.

Ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων αὐτὸς ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα] Ratio membri alterius, nam Pater per me operatur, atque ita o- stendit se esse in me. Nam μένειν Johanni est inesse. Ut supra V. 8. Dei proprietates ex operibus cognoscuntur, quae nunquam majora & plura quam per Christum sunt e- dita: ita ut in istis sapientiam Dei, bonitatem, potentiam multo apertius fuerit concipere, quam in visionibus illis, quae Prophetis contigerunt, & quibus illae proprietates tan- tum per similitudinem figuras adumbrabantur. Duo quae diximus membra, quibus conjunctio Patris & Filii indica- tur breviter sic exponit Nonnus:

Ὡς συνέμοι τελέθει γενέτης ἐμὸς, ὅττι κὴ αὐτὸς Σύμφυτος εἰμι τοκῆϊ, ἐγὼ λαλέων, ὁ δὲ ῥέζων.

## 14:11
Vers. 11. Believe me] Believe my words, which contain nothing that is not divine, that I am most closely joined to the Father.

Or else believe me] If you do not wish to believe my words.

Believe me for the very works' sake] At least believe on account of the works, which are such that they could not proceed unless from God. Above III. 2. V. 36. X. 37.

PART III.

The promise of the gift of miracles, of the hearing of prayers, of the assistance of the Paraclete, and of the return and further manifestation.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Πιστεύετέ μοι] Verbis meis nihil non divinam continentibus credite, me Patri esse conjunctissimum.

Εἰ δὲ μὴ] Si verbis credere non vultis.

Διὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτὰ πιστεύετέ μοι] Saltem credite ob opera quae talia sunt ut nisi a Deo proficisci nequeant. Supra III. 2. V. 36. X. 37.

PARS III.

Promissio doni miraculorum, exauditionis precum, assistentiae Paracleti, & reditus ac ulterioris manifestationis.

## 14:12
Verse 12. Amen, Amen] He continues to console.

The works that I do, he also shall do] He will cast out demons, he will heal diseases, he will raise the dead. This promise, however, must be understood according to those things which were said at Mark 16:17.

And he shall do greater things than these] He will speak in every kind of language for the conversion of all nations. The greatest sign, as Chrysostom notes, of the glory of Christ is that those things were done through one who was absent which he had not accomplished while present.

Brentius more correctly understands 'greater' not by reason of form or quality, but by reason of the efficacy and fruit of a more abundant proclamation. Compare what is said at Acts 5:16. Rupertus interpreted it in this way regarding the conversion of countless numbers through the variety of languages. Origen, Homily VI on Isaiah: You will do greater works, because I made them rise from the dead corporally: You will make them rise from the dead spiritually. I poured this sensible light into the blind: You will give spiritual light to those who do not see. Elsewhere, namely in Homily VII on Numbers, Origen has it thus: Truly it seems greater to me that a man placed in the flesh, fragile and perishable, yet girded by the faith of Christ and his word, overcomes giants and legions of demons; although it is he himself who conquers in us, yet it is more that he conquers through us than that he conquers through himself.

Because I go to the Father; and whatever you ask in my name, that I will do; that the Father may be glorified in the Son] These things are to be read in one spirit, and the Hebraisms are to be noted: 'I go and I will do,' that is, having gone, I will accomplish. The simile is taken from one who, having gone to a king, commends the desires of his friends in his presence.
