Neque enim Spi- ritus Sanct. de creatura quae Patri est subdita & Fi- lio fuerat accepturus, quod ait de meo accipiet, sed utique de Patre,de quo procedit Spiritus, de quo est natus & Filius. Dionys. Carthusian. in h. l. Omnia quae Pater habet mea sunt, non solum per fruitionem, ut dixerunt haeretici, sed per sub- stantialem identitatem, continentiamque realem, id est totam suam essentiam, potestatem, perfectio- nem Pater Filio communicavit, imo quicquid Patri convenit, competit Filio, sed relatione seu proprie- tate naturali, in qua distinguitur, excepta. Conf. Epiphan. haeref. LXIX. contr. Ariomanit. Na- zianz. Orat. XLIX. Idacius Clarus l. III. advers. Va- rimund. Theophyl. in h. l. &c.

## 16:16
Verse 16.

Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με) That is, after a little time you will not see me. The same Hebraism above XIV, verse 19. This is to be understood of the space which remained until death. καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν) And again after a little interval, namely as much as intervened between death and the resurrection. καὶ ὄψεσθέ με) Again you will enjoy the sight of me: You will see me and I will see you, as he explains presently. We will see one another. ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα) For I will not remain in death, but I will go to the Father, making a passage as it were through you. Above VII. 33. XIII. 3. 33. XVI. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με) Id est post exiguum tempus me non videbitis. Idem Hebraismus supra XIV. vers. 19. Intelligendum hoc de spatio, quod ad mortem restabat. καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν) Et rursus post exiguum intervallum, nempe quantum inter mortem & resurrectionem inter- cessit. καὶ ὄψεσθέ με) Iterum fruemini meo conspectu: Vide- bitis me & ego vos videbo, ut mox explicat. Videbimus alter alterum. ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα) Non enim manebo in mor- te, sed ad Patrem ibo, transitum quasi per vos faciens. Supra VII. 33. XIII. 3. 33. XVI. 5.

## 16:17
Verse 17.

ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν) Some is understood. Such places we have noted some, Matt. XXVII. 9. πρὸς ἀλλήλους) Muttering so that they could not be heard. Τί ἐστι τοῦτο ὃ λέγει ἡμῖν μικρὸν) They could not bring themselves to believe that death was so near at hand.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν) Subauditur τινες. quales locos aliquot notavimus, Matth. XXVII. 9. πρὸς ἀλλήλους) Mussitando ut exaudiri nequirent. Τί ἐστι τοῦτο ὃ λέγει ἡμῖν μικρὸν) In animum inducere non poterant mortem tam propinquam instare.

## 16:19
Verse 19.

ἔγνω οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς) By his own divine power.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ἔγνω οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς) Vi sua divina.

## 16:20
Verse 20.

κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε ὑμεῖς) When I am captured, crucified, dead. See Luke XXIII. 27. ὁ δὲ κόσμος χαρήσεται) The soldiers will mock me. Matt. XXVII. verse 27. also the Jews and their leaders, in the same place

39. 40. 41. The Pharisees will triumph as if I were defeated. 63.

But your sorrow shall be turned into joy) It shall be changed into joy: It shall be turned into joy, as this Latin has it. It is a Hebraism which the Syriac has correctly expressed here.

Vers. 20.

κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε ὑμεῖς) Me capto, crucifixo, mor- tuo. Vide Luc. XXIII. 27. ὁ δὲ κόσμος χαρήσεται) Illudent mihi milites. Matth. XXVII. vers. 27. etiam Judaei eorumque proceres, ibidem

39. 40. 41. Pharisaei tanquam me devicto triumpha- bunt. 63.

Ἀλλ’ ἡ λύπη ὑμῶν εἰς χαρὰν γενήσεται) Mutabitur in gaudium: Vertetur in gaudium, ut hic Latinus. Est He- braismus quem hic recte expressit Syrus.

## 16:21
Ver. 21.

a woman when she is in travail hath sorrow) He illustrates the matter with an excellent comparison. Everywhere the greatest pains are compared to childbirth.

because her hour is come) The time of sorrows.

A man) Thus we say, Remember that you are a man born.

into the world) Because she has increased the human race with new offspring.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ἡ γυνὴ ὅταν τίκτῃ λύπην ἔχει) Egregia comparatione rem illustrat. Passim dolores maximi parturigini comparan- tur.

ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα αὐτῆς) Tempus dolorum.

Ἄνθρωπον) Sic dicimus, Hominem natum te memi- neris.

εἰς τὸν κόσμον) Quod genus humanum nova prole au- xerit.

## 16:22
Ver. 22.

And ye now therefore have sorrow) For a short time, like a woman in labor. That ancient manuscript in England has ἕξετε instead of ἔχετε.

But I will see you again) I will be present with you, seeing and to be seen.

and your heart shall rejoice) For the fulfillment see below XX. 20.

and your joy no man taketh from you) αἴρει for ἀρεῖ, such as we have often had already: and understand by joy, the cause of joy: eternal life: and the power of Christ. This cause of joy will not cease, even after he shall have been withdrawn a second time from their sight: for he will be where his enemies cannot harm him. Above VII. 34. Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more Romans VI. 9. Wherefore Christians, though they see him not, yet believing, rejoice with joy unspeakable. I Peter I. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

Λύπην μὲν νῦν ἔχετε) Ad breve tempus ut puerpera. Antiquus ille in Anglia manuscriptus pro ἔχετε habet ἕ- ξετε.

Πάλιν δὲ ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς) Adero vobis conspiciens & con- spiciendus.

κὴ χαρήσεται ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία) Implementum vide infra XX. 20.

κὴ τὴν χαρὰν ὑμῶν ὐδεὶς αἴρει ἀφ’ ὑμῶν) αἴρει pro ἀρεῖ qua- lia jam saepe habuimus: & gaudium intellige, causam gau- dii: perpetuam vitam: ac potestatem Christi. Haec causa gaudii non cessabit, etiam postquam secundo subtractus erit ipsorum conspectui: erit enim ubi inimici ei nocere nequeant. Supra VII. 34. Christus a mortuis excitatus non mo itur amplius Roman. VI. 9. Quare Christiani non videntes quidem eum, sed credentes, gaudent gaudio in- explicabili. I. Petr. I. 7.

## 16:23
Ver. 23.

κὴ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ) When you will rejoice for my sake, although I am absent.

Ἐμὲ ὐκ ἐρωτήσετε ὐδέν) Because ἐμὲ precedes, I am entirely of the opinion that this clause is opposed to that which follows. The Apostles were distressed because they were not going to have Jesus present. For if there was any evil or danger, they would run back to him, they would solicit him with prayers. Matt. VIII. 25. Thus above Martha and Mary were saying: Lord, if you had been here, our brother would not have died.

ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα) Let nothing disturb you in this, that you will not be able to implore me while present: approach the Father himself with prayers.

τῷ ὀνόματί με) As is the custom of the Church to pray, Through our Lord Jesus Christ. See what is above XIV. 13. 14.

Δώσει ὑμῖν) This is to be understood under certain tacit conditions: concerning which it has been treated both in the place already mentioned and Matt. XVIII. 19. XXI. 22.

PARS III. Concerning the hearing of prayers, consolation regarding peace and victory over the world.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

κὴ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ) Cum gaudebitis mei causa, quam- vis absentis.

Ἐμὲ ὐκ ἐρωτήσετε ὐδέν) Quia ἐμὲ praecedit, omnino sen- tio hoc membrum oppositum esse ei quod sequitur. An- gebantur Apostoli quod Jesum non habituri erant praesen- tem. Quia si quid esset mali aut periculi ad eum recurre- bant, ipsum precibus sollicitabant. Matth. VIII. 25. Sic su- pra Martha & Maria dicebant: Domine, si fuisses hic, frater noster non esset mortuus.

ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα) Nihil hoc vos turbet quod me praesentem implorare non poteritis: ipsum Patrem pre- cibus adite.

τῷ ὀνόματί με) Sicut mos est Ecclesiae orare, Per Do- minum nostrum Jesum Christum. Vide quae supra XIV. 13. 14.

Δώσει ὑμῖν) Intelligendum hoc sub tacitis quibusdam conditionibus: de quibus actum & dicto jam loco & Matth. XVIII. 19. XXI. 22.

PARS III. De precum exauditione, pace & mundi victo- ria consolatio.

## 16:24
Vers. 24.

ἕως ἄρτι ὐκ ἠτήσατε ὐδὲν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί με) That custom of praying was unknown, and it received its power especially from the obedience of Christ rendered in death.

Although prayers were not made in the name of JESUS of Nazareth before it was established concerning that subject, that he is the Son of God, the promised Messiah of the world, yet the faithful in the O.T. also asked to be heard on account of the Lord, i.e., on account of the Messiah. Compare Daniel IX. 17. Psalm XXV. 11. XXXIV. 4. and Exod. XXIII. 21. as well as Psalm CXXXII. 10. with Ezek. XXXIV. 23. The disciples indeed acknowledged and confessed Christ JESUS, but they had not yet been accustomed to pour out prayers in the name of JESUS, because their faith was less firm, and they had him present, and did not doubt that he would intercede and pray for them of his own accord. And these things are rightly explained κατὰ ἀντι: that the disciples, who were quite unrefined in the acknowledgment of Christ, are said not to have done this, which they did only according to that small measure of their knowledge and faith, so that this, namely, is understood comparatively, in contrast to that efficacy of the Holy Spirit with which they were afterwards endowed, and which shone upon the whole world through their ministry. But especially to be observed is the explanation of the blessed Luther, which he has in his commentary on this chapter, Vol. VII. Jena, German, fol. 206, that Here the distinction between the Old and New Testament is handed down. He wishes thereby to give the distinction between the Old and New Testament, and between his forerunners and his future or present reign; although the dear fathers and prophets also prayed before, in the right spirit and faith, but yet only toward the future Christ, now however it shall no longer be called praying toward Him as the future one, but in the name of Him who has already come, fulfilled the Scripture, and now mightily reigns. Such prayer shall now begin (he wishes to say) after his suffering and ascension, when the Gospel is to be revealed and preached to the whole world by me, that I have come and accomplished everything that was prophesied of me, blotted out sin, strangled death, destroyed hell, and opened heaven: And now through such new preaching also institute a new divine service, in which all distinction of outward manner, places, gestures, etc., is abolished, and everything is drawn to me and directed toward me, so that henceforth no other prayer or divine service shall be valid than that which happens in faith in me, or is prayed and done in my name, I who have now come and am revealed through the Gospel. Although those prayers made through Christ and in his name receive their force especially from the obedience of Christ rendered in death, yet that force extends not only to later times, but also to earlier ones. For the passion of Christ was profitable before it existed, and its force extends itself forward and backward. Heb. XIII. 8. Rev. XIII. 8. Acts XV. 18.

Ask and you shall receive) See the example in Acts V. 24. and compare 33. That your joy may be full) That the joy which has come to you through my exaltation may be perfected. Concerning the expression see above XV. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ἕως ἄρτι ὐκ ἠτήσατε ὐδὲν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί με) Ignoratus erat ille precandi mos, & vim suam praecipue accepit ex obedientia Christi in morte praestita.

Etsi non factae precationes in nomine JESU Nazareni sint, antequam de subjecto illo con- staret, quod sit Filius Dei, promissus mundi Mes- sias, fideles tamen in V. T. petierunt etiam propter Dominum h. e. propter Messiam exaudiri. Con- fer. Daniel. IX. 17. Psal. XXV. 11. XXXIV. 4. & Exod. XXIII. 21. nec non Psal. CXXXII, 10. cum Ezech. XXXIV. 23. Agnoverunt quidem discipu- li Christum JESUM & confessi sunt, sed nondum consueverant in nomine JESU preces fundere, quia minus firma fuit ipsorum fides, eumque prae- sentem habebant, & ultro pro se intercedere at- que orare non dubitabant. Et recte haec κατὰ ἀντι explicantur: quod discipuli, qui admodum rudes in agnitione Christi essent, hoc dicantur non fecis- se, quod nonnisi pro exigua illa sua notitiae & fidei mensura faciebant, ut hoc sc. comparate intelli- gatur, prae ea Spiritus S. efficacia, qua postea fue- runt donati, & quae per illorum ministerium uni- verso mundo affulsit. Sed imprimis observanda B. Lutheri explicatio, quam habet in comment. in hoc caput Tom. VII. Jen. Germ. fol. 206. quod Hic discrimen V. & N. Test. tradatur. Er wil damit die Unterscheid geben/ zwischen dem Alten und Neuen Testament/und zwischen seinen Vorläuffern und seiner Zukunfft oder gegenwärtigen Regiment; Obwol die lieben Väter und Propheten zuvor auch gebätet/ in rechtem Geist und Glauben/ aber doch nur auff den zukünfftigen Christum/jetzt aber soll es nicht mehr heissen auff Ihn/als den zukünfftigen/ bäten/sondern/ indem Namen deß/ der da schon komen ist/ die Schrifft erfüllet/ und nun gewaltiglich regieret. Solch Gebät soll nun angehen/ (wil er sagen) nach seinem Leyden und Himelfart/da der gantzen Welt das Evangelium von mir soll offenbaret und verkündiget werden/ daß Ich kommen bin/ und alles außgerichtet habe/ das von mir geweissaget/ die Sünde getilget/den Todt gewürget/die Hölle zerstöret/und den Himmel auffgeschlossen:Und nun durch solche neue Predigt auch einen neuen Gottes-Dienst anrichte/ in welchem alle Unterscheid äusserlicher weise/Stätte/Gebärde/ &c. aufgehaben/und alles zu mir gezogen/und auf mich gerichtet/ daß hinfort kein ander Gebät noch Gottes-Dienst gelten soll/ denn so im Glauben an mich geschicht/ oder in meinem Namen gebätet und gethan wird/ der Ich nun kommen bin / und durchs Evangelium offenbaret werde. Quanquam vero vim suam accipiant præcipue ex obedientia Christi in morte præstita illæ precationes per Christum & in nomine ejus factæ, vis tamen illa non tantum ad posteriora se porrigit tempora, sed etiam ad priora. Passio enim Christi profuit antequam fuit, ejusque vis extendit se antrorsum & retrorsum. Ebr. XIII. 8. Ap. XIII. 8. Act. XV. 18.

Αἰτεῖτε καὶ λήψεσθε) Vid. exemplum Act.V.24. & conf.33. Ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν ἦ πεπληρωμένη) Ut perficiatur gaudium quod vobis obtigit per meam evectionem. De locutione vide supra XV. 11.

## 16:25
Verse 25. These things I have spoken to you in proverbs) Not only figurative speech, but also that which is general and less distinct is called משׁל parœmia or parabolē by the Hellenists, as Ezek. ch. XX. 49. But such were these preceding things, for the Apostles did not yet understand of what kind those things were which they were about to obtain.

I will announce to you) After the mission of the Holy Spirit, as the following shows.

plainly I will announce to you concerning the Father) I will open to you most openly and most explicitly through the Spirit what the will of the Father is concerning my kingdom and what kind of things you ought to pray to him for. See Acts X.

We undertake the explanation concerning the proverb, for, as Cyril has in book XI on John ch. II, he calls a parœmia an obscure speech and not very manifest, but shaded by such subtle obscurities that the hearers cannot grasp it so easily: for such is the form of those things which are said through proverbs. But those things which he was about to announce more clearly are not rightly defined by Grotius: for they were not to be informed about what they ought to ask, but concerning the Father: This is according to Cyril; I will openly narrate to you what pertains to the glory of the Father and will bring to you the knowledge exceeding the grasp of the human mind.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ταῦτα ἐν παροιμίαις λελάληκα ὑμῖν) Non tantum figuratus sermo, sed & qui generalis est minusque distinctus vocatur משׁל παροιμία sive παραβολὴ Helenistis, ut Ezech. c.XX. 49. Talia autem erant hæc præcedentia, Nondum enim intelligebant Apostoli, cujus generis essent illa, quæ essent impetraturi.

ἀναγγελῶ ὑμῖν) Post missionem Spiritus S. ut ostendunt sequentia.

παῥῥησίᾳ περὶ τῦ πατρὸς ἀναγγελῶ ὑμῖν) Apertissime & explicatissime aperiam vobis per Spiritum, quæ sit Patris voluntas de regno meo & qualia precari ipsum debeatis. Vid. Act. X.

Explicationem de parœmia suscipimus, nam, ut Cyrillus habet l.XI. in Joh. c.II. παροιμίαν vocat sermonem obscurum nec admodum manifestum, sed obscuritatibus ita subtilibus adumbratum, ut eum adeo facile capere nequeant auditores: ejusmodi quippe forma est eorum, quæ per parœmias dicuntur. Sed ea, quæ annunciaturus clarius erat, non recte definiuntur à Grotio: Non enim quæ petere debeant, sed περὶ τῦ πατρὸς, hoc est, de Patre informandi erant: Hoc est secundum Cyrillum; aperte vobis enarrabo, quæ ad gloriam Patris pertinent & cognitionem captum mentis humanæ excedentem vobis inferam.

## 16:26
Verse 26. In my name you will ask and) This 'and' has the force of a condition in the preceding member, as we said in VII. 34. Then there is a certain ellipsis or rather an anantapodoton. The sense is: if you ask for anything to be given to you on my account, the Father will give it.

I say to you that I will ask the Father for you) I pass over this as if it were less than that which I am now about to bring in. Thus above V. 45.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μυ αἰτήσεσθε καὶ) Hoc καὶ habet vim conditionis in præcedente membro, ut diximus VII. 34. Deinde est ἔλλειψις quædam aut potius ἀνανταπόδοτον. Sensus est: si quid petieritis vobis ob me dari id Pater dabit.

ᾀ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐρωτήσω ὴ πατέρα περὶ ὑμῶν) Prætereo hoc quasi minus eo, quod jam inferam. Sic supra V. 45.

## 16:27
Verse 27. For the Father himself) He loves you even of his own accord, without my commending you: and therefore, what we said is to be understood, he will give what you ask.

because you have loved me) This is the cause of a certain new and special love with which the Father follows Christians. See above XIV. 21. 23.

The interpretation of Guilb. Estius and Hackspan is not unlike that sense of ᾀ λέγω which I pass over as being of less account, for whom to say is the same as παρακαλεῖν, to console, as in Isaiah 35:4, i.e., I do not console you from that source primarily, because I am about to ask the Father for you; since the Father loves you beforehand. But there seems to be no such connection: I say nothing now about the fact that I will pray to the Father for you; because the Father himself loves you. The love of the Father is not the cause of that passing over, but rather, because he loves them of his own accord, the very intercession of Christ before the Father seems superfluous: which, however, must not be admitted: for the Father does not love anyone before and apart from the intercession of Christ, but on account of Christ and his intercession. Others, therefore, wish these things to be taken not exclusively but inclusively, as if to say: hitherto I have prayed alone, henceforth I will not pray alone, but you will pray with me, nor will the intuition of your own weakness and unworthiness deter you, for the Father himself loves you, examples of which occur. Gen. 32:28, 1 Sam. 8:7, Mark 9:37, Job 5:12, 13, 15, 12:44. Which explanation Hackspan rashly criticizes in the blessed Fevverbornius, even though it does not fully express the force and emphasis of the negation, 'I do not say that I will pray to the Father for you.' The simplest exposition of the ancients, therefore, is that the help of Christ is not excluded, but it is insinuated how confidently and securely they can approach God, as Dionysius the Carthusian and Cyril of Alexandria have it, book 11 on John, chapter 2. He permits them to ask for nothing at all through prayers and supplications except in his name, but he promises that the Father will more readily give them what they have asked for, not indeed solely by the impulse of the Son, who is advocate and mediator, but of his own accord, as it were, moved to such munificence and paying as a kind of debt to those who love Christ, namely the highest kindness, κᾀ ὀυχὶ πάντως ταῖς τ͂ υἷ προτροπαῖς ἀναπαθέμε- νον ἀτε δὲ παρακλήτꙋ ϰ μα̃σιτεύοντꙋ αὐτόμο- λον δὲ πῶς εἰς Φιλοτιμίαν ἰοντα τὴν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῖς κᾀ ὥσπερ τὸ χρέος καταλιθέναι σπυδάζοντα τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι Χριστ̃ τὴν ἀνωτάτω κᾀ εἰς ἄκρον ἐυμέ- νειαν. And let no one think that because of such great benevolence of the Father we do not need Christ, because all things are from the Father through him in the Spirit, since he is the advocate, as John testifies, not only for our sins, but also for those of the whole world; but he says these things so that he might again usefully show here that it is most pleasing to the Father that his Son be honored and loved. Doubtless these things are said in such a way that the disciples are thus insinuated into the love of the Father, and are so loved by God as if they had no need of any further intercession, not that Christ is unwilling to intercede henceforth for them, or can cease his prayers for his own, or that the faithful can in reality lack the intercession of Christ, but so that the love of God the Father toward the disciples and those who believe in Christ may be exaggerated. I do not say this, that you ought to pray in my name and rely on the confidence of my merit and intercession, because you have need of my prayer and intercession before God as if you were not yet reconciled to him, because the Father loves you entirely and you can approach him with confidence, being about to receive from him whatever it is ever permitted to hope for from a propitious and kind God. There is no reason, therefore, why we should restrict these things with some to prayer for the revelation of the Father, since they were said generally, and they add vehement stimuli to παῤῥησίαν in every prayer of the children of God, so that they may understand the Father to be as prompt to hear as if there were no need for any intercession at all. Therefore, the Socinians call into doubt nothing from this passage regarding the intercession of Christ, which is made for us in the heavens.

That I came forth from God) You believed that I was truly sent by God. Supra VIII. 42. XIII. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 27. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ) Ultro etiam me non commendante amat vos: ac proinde, quod subintelligi diximus, dabit quæ petitis.

ὅτι ὑμεῖς ἐμὲ πεφιλήκατε) Hæc causa novæ ac specialis cujusdam dilectionis, qua Pater Christianos prosequitur. Vid. supra XIV. 21. 23.

Sensui illi ᾀ λέγω prætereo hoc quasi minus, non absimilis est Guilb. Estii & Hackspanii interpreta- tio, quibus dicere idem est, quod παρακαλεῖν con- solari ut Es. XXXV. 4. q.d. non inde vos consolor po- tissimum, quod rogaturus sim Patrem pro vobis; si- quidem Pater antea vos amat. Sed nulla ita vide- tur connexio: Nihil jam dico de eo, quod Patrem ora- bo pro vobis; quia Pater ipse amat vos. Amor Pa- tris non est causa præteritionis illius, sed ideo potius, quia ultro amat eos, supervacanea videtur ipsa intercessio Christi apud Patrem: Quod vero admittendum non est: non enim amat Pa- ter ante & extra intercessionem Christi quen- quam, sed propter Christum, ejusque interces- sionem. Alii ergo hæc non exclusive sed inclu- sive accipienda esse volunt, quasi d. hactenus solus oravi, deinceps non orabo solus, sed vos mecum orabi- tis, nec deterrebit vos imbecillitatis & indignitatis vestræ intuitus ipse enim Pater amat vos, qualia ex- empla occurrunt. Gen. XXXII. 28. 1. Sam. IIX. 7. Marc. IX. 37. Job. V. 12. 13. 15. XII. 44. Quam ex- plicationem in B. Fevverbornio temere sugillat Hakspanius, etsi ea non plene exprimat vim & em- phasin negationis, non dico quod Patrem pro vobis rogaturus sim. Simplicissima ergo veterum est ἔκθεσις, non excludi Christi subsidium, sed insinua- ri, quam fiducialiter & secure possint ad Deum ac- cedere, ut habet Dionys. Carthus. Cyrillus Alexandr. l. XI. in Joh. c. 2. Nihil omnino per orationes & sup- plicationes petere permittit nisi in nomine suo, Pa- trem vero ocyus daturum eis pollicetur quæ postula- verint, non utique Filii solum impulsu, qui advoca- tus & mediator est, sed ultro quodammodo eo mu- nificentiæ delatum & quasi quoddam debitum solvat Christum diligentibus summam nempe benignitatem, κᾀ ὀυχὶ πάντως ταῖς τ͂ υἷ προτροπαῖς ἀναπαθέμε- νον ἀτε δὲ παρακλήτꙋ ϰ μα̃σιτεύοντꙋ αὐτόμο- λον δὲ πῶς εἰς Φιλοτιμίαν ἰοντα τὴν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῖς κᾀ ὥσπερ τὸ χρέος καταλιθέναι σπυδάζοντα τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι Χριστ̃ τὴν ἀνωτάτω κᾀ εἰς ἄκρον ἐυμέ- νειαν. Nec ullus putet propter tantam Patris be- nevolentiam non indigere nos Christi, quia omnia per ipsum ex Patre in Spiritu sunt, quoniam ad- vocatus est, teste Johanne, non pro nostris tantum peccatis, sed etiam pro totius mundi, cæterum isthæc ait, ut hic rursus utiliter ostenderet, longe gratissi- mum esse Patri honorari ac diligi Filium suum. Ni- mirum hæc ita dicuntur, quod sic dilectioni Patris insinuati sint discipuli, & à Deo ita amen- tur, ac si opus non habeant ulla amplius inter- cessione, non quod nolit Christus intercedere deinceps pro illis, aut preces intermittere pro suis possit, aut revera fideles carere queant in- terrogatione Christi, sed ut exaggeretur dile- ctio Dei Patris adversus discipulos & credentes in Christum. Non hoc, quod in nomine meo orare debeatis, & niti fiducia meriti & inter- cessionis meæ, ideo dico, quod oratione & intercessione mea penes Deum quasi vobis non- dum reconciliatum opus vobis sit, quia omnino vos diligit Pater & accedere cum fiducia ad eun- dem potestis, accepturi ab ipso, quicquid à Deo propitio & benigno sperare unquam licet. Non ergo est, quod hæc restringamus cum qui- busdam ad orationem pro revelatione Patris, quum dicta sunt generaliter, & ad παῤῥησίαν ve- hementes addant stimulos in omni filiorum Dei precatione, quod tam promtum ad exauditio- nem intelligant Patrem, ac si ne ulla quidem opus sit intercessione. Ne quiequam ergo ex hoc loco Sociniani in dubium vocant inter- cessionem Christi, quæ pro nobis in cælis fit.

Ὅτι ἐγὼ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον) Credidistis me vere à Deo missum. Supra VIII. 42. XIII. 3.

## 16:28
Vers. 28. I came forth from the Father) He confirms them in that which they had believed.

and I have come into the world) I have shown myself to men by word and works. Supra I. 9. III. 19. VI. 14. IX. 39. XI. 27. XII. v. 46. 47.

Coming forth from the Father and arrival into the world explain each other as the term from which (with imperfections purged) and the term to which: Therefore, by the arrival into the world it is not denoted that he began his office and showed himself by word and works, but that he came into this world through incarnation and birth; just as, conversely, he left the world, not by finishing his office, which endures forever, but he put an end to his conversation on these earths, and was assumed into heaven. Whence from this formula of speaking the pre-existence of the Son of God before his temporal birth is rightly proven against the Socinians, whose corruptions this gloss of Grotius favors. See the treatise on that pre-existence published here. He came into the world, says Augustine in tract. CII, because he showed his body to the world, which he assumed from the virgin. And furthermore, Christ left the world by bodily departure, he went to the Father by the ascension of man, nor did he desert the world by the presence of his governance.

again) Conversely. Thus often again signifies not iteration but opposition. See Matt. IV. 7.

I leave the world) I shall withdraw myself from the sight of men: for it is the present for the future and it concerns the ascension.

and I go to the Father) Into the paternal citadel.

To set out to the Father is not to set out into a paternal citadel. For shall we say that God, who is an eternal and immense Spirit, is enclosed by some citadel, whom indeed the heaven of heavens do not comprehend, who fills heaven and earth with his substantial presence, is everywhere whole, nowhere excluded, nowhere included, even if he manifests himself peculiarly to angels and the elect in heaven (which, however, is rashly imagined to be some place above the firmament of the world). Concerning which see elsewhere T. III. System. Theol. Art. V. c. II. q. II. p. 996. seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ἐξῆλθον παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς) Confirmat eos in eo, quod crediderant.

κj ἐλήλυθα εἰς τ' κόσμον) Ostendi me hominibus sermone & operibus. Supra I. 9. III. 19. VI. 14. IX. 39. XI. 27. XII. v. 46. 47.

Egressus à Patre & adventus in mundum sese mutuo explicant ceu terminus à quo (defæcatis im- perfectionibus) & terminus adquem: Non ergo per adventum in mundum notatur, quod officium suum auspicatus sermone & operibus se ostenderit, sed quod per incarnationem & nativitatem in hunc mundum venerit; quemadmodum contra mun- dum reliquit, non officium suum finiens, quod in æternum durat, sed eum conversationi in his terris finem imposuit, & in cælum assumtus est. Unde ex hac loquendi formula recte probatur Filii Dei προϋπαρξις ante temporalem nativitatem adver- sus Socinianos, quorum corruptelæ hæc Grotii glossa favet. Vid. tr. de προυπάρξει illa hic editus. In mundum venit, inquit Augustinus tract. CII. quia mundo suum corpus ostendit, quod de virgine assum- sit. Et porro, Christus reliquit mundum, corporali discessione, perrexit ad Patrem hominis ascensione, nec mundum deseruit præsentia gubernatione.

πάλιν) Vice versa. Ita sæpe πάλιν non iterationem sed oppositionem fignificat. Vid. Matth. IV. 7.

Ἀφίημι τ' κόσμον) Subtraham me hominum conspectui: est enim præsens pro futuro & de adscensione agitur.

κj πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα) In arcem paternam.

Ad Patrem proficisci non est proficisci in pater- nam arcem. Num enim Deum, qui æternus & im- mensus Spiritus est, arce quadam concludi dice- mus, quem utique cæli cælorum non compre- hendunt, qui cælum & terram implet substantiali παρουσίᾳ, ubique totus est, nuspiam exclusus, nu- spiam inclusus, etsi peculiariter angelis & electis in cœlo, (quod tamen temere fingitur locus quis- piam supra firmamentum mundi) se manifestet. De quo alias vid. T. III. System. Theol. Art. V. c. II. q. II. p. 996. seqq.

## 16:29
Vers. 29. Now you speak plainly) Because he had now added that I leave the world, they begin to understand of what kind of departure he was speaking.

Latin:

Vers. 29. Νῦν παῤῥησίᾳ λαλεῖς) Quia nunc addiderat il- lud ἀφίημι τὸν κόσμον, incipiunt intelligere de quali profe- ctione ageret.

## 16:30
V. 30. Now we know that you know all things) You saw in what part we were hesitating.

κj ὀ χρείαν ἔχεις ἵνα τίς σε ἐρωτᾷ) You have no need that he who does not understand your words should declare what it is that he does not understand. This is an indicative for a subjunctive in the manner of the Hebrews.

Ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν) ἐν τούτῳ by this we believe, as above II, 11. It is divine to look into thoughts.

Latin:

V. 30. Νῦν οἴδαμεν ὅτι οἶδας πάντα) Vidisti qua in parte hæsitaremus.

κj ὀ χρείαν ἔχεις ἵνα τίς σε ἐρωτᾷ) Non opus habes ut qui tua verba non intelligit, enunciet quid sit quod non intelli- gat. Est hic indicativus pro subjunctivo more Hebræo- rum.

Ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν) ἐν τούτῳ ob hoc credimus, ut supra II, 11. divinum est introspicere cogitata.

## 16:31
Vers. 31. Ἄρτι πιστεύετε) I think it is read more correctly without a question, and it should be taken not as an imperative, as the Syrian took it, but as an indicative. In Nonnus, a question is indeed ascribed, ἰαῷ πιστεύετε μύθῳ; but wrongly, as what follows ἐγγύθι δὲ shows. Now indeed you believe, that is, you profess that you believe while it is safe. Ἄρτι denotes the present tense here as above V. 17. IX. 25. XIII. 19. and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 31. Ἄρτι πιστεύετε) Puto rectius legi sine interroga- tione, & sumendum non pro imperativo, ut Syrus sumsit, sed pro indicativo. Apud Nonnum ascribitur quidem in- terrogatio ἰαῷ πιστεύετε μύθῳ; sed male, ut ostendit quod sequitur ἐγγύθι δὲ. Jam quidem creditis, id est profite- mini vos credere dum tutum est. Ἄρτι præsens tempus hic notat ut supra V. 17. IX. 25. XIII. 19. & alibi.

## 16:32
Vers. 32. Ἔρχεται ὥρα) It is imminent.

Καὶ νῦν ἐλήλυθεν) Present for the near future: nay, it is already here now. For the space of a few hours intervened.

Ἵνα σκορπισθῆτε ἕκαςος) Matth. XXVI. 31.

εἰς τὰ ἴδια) Into his own hiding places. For ἴδιον is said even where one turns aside for a time. See above I. 39. and X. 3.

Καὶ ἐμὲ μόνον ἀφῆτε) Matth. XXVI. 56.

Καὶ) That is, however. For it is an explanation having the appearance of a correction. What do I say, that I will be alone? The Father will be with me.

Μετ' ἐμοῦ ἐστι) He will indeed permit me to be treated badly for a time; but in such a way that He will not cast away His care for me nor leave me without consolations. To be with someone is to stand on his side, to provide him with help. See above VIII. 29.

Latin:

Vers. 32. Ἔρχεται ὥρα) Imminet.

Καὶ νῦν ἐλήλυθεν) Præsens pro futuro proximo: imo jam nunc adest. Paucarum enim horarum spatium in- tererat.

Ἵνα σκορπισθῆτε ἕκαςος) Matth. XXVI. 31.

εἰς τὰ ἴδια) In sua quisque latibula. Nam ἴδιον dici- tur etiam ubi quis pro tempore divertitur. Vide supra I. 39. & X. 3.

Καὶ ἐμὲ μόνον ἀφῆτε) Matth. XXVI. 56.

Καὶ) Id est attamen. Est enim explicatio speciem ha- bens ἐπανορθώσεως. Quid dico me solum futurum? Pater mihi aderit.

Μετ' ἐμοῦ ἐστι) Permittet me quidem ad tempus male tractari; sed ita ut non abjiciat curam mei neque me sine solatiis relinquat. Cum aliquo esse est stare ab ejus parti- bus, auxilium ei præstare. Vide supra VIII. 29.

## 16:33
Vers. 33. ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν) That I will not lack the Father's help even in the most serious evils. Ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ εἰρήνην ἔχητε) Again an indicative for a subjunctive. By the name of peace here, understand a tranquil mind: which the following things show: and ἐν ἐμοί, that is, confidence in my promises. For if the Father will not leave me without help in the midst of the cross, He will not leave you either. Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλίψιν ἔχετε) That is, you will have. ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ from the world, on the part of many men. Ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε) Take heart by my example. Ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον) The past tense again for the near future. For He conquered the furies of the world most excellently when He endured death most patiently. It is to be understood, however, that by doing this I have procured for you the strength by which, being armed, you may do the same, 1. Cor. XV. 57. 1. Joh. IV. 4. V. 45. Apoc. XII. 11. He raises up the Apostles not so much by his example as, above all, by his merit, by which he acquired for us the strength to overcome not only the world, but even the prince of the world himself, Satan, and crushed his head, so that it might be crushed under our feet, Gen. III. 16. Rom. XVI. 26. By peace is understood, above all, reconciliation with God, which we have through Christ, Rom. V. 1, from which arises tranquility of conscience; moreover, we have it in Christ, because Christ acquired it for us, and we do not actually enjoy it except through faith in Christ, 2. Cor. V. 19. Thus Ambrose: He said this for the reason that he who has peace with God does not fear any opposing mind. For everyone who loves God in Christ Jesus is safe by the peace of God. And Jerome in Epist. ad virg. Exul.: On account of the certainty of faith you ought to have peace in me, not by feeling present things, but by certainly hoping for future things.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν) Me etiam in gravissimis malis non cariturum Patris auxilio. Ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ εἰρήνην ἔχητε) Iterum Indicativus pro Subjunctivo. Εἰρήνης nomine hic intellige animum tranquillum: quod ostendunt sequentia: & ἐν ἐμοί, id est fiducia mearum promissionum. Nam si me in media cruce Pater non relinquet sine auxilio, ne vos quidem relinquet. Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλίψιν ἔχετε) Id est habebitis. ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ à mundo, ex parte multorum hominum. Ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε) Sumite animum meo exemplo. Ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον) Praeteritum rursus pro proxime futuro. Nam excellentissime mundi furores vicit cum mortem patientissime pertulit. Subintelligendum autem, hoc faciendo vobis vires peperi quibus armati idem faciatis, 1. Cor. XV. 57. 1. Joh. IV. 4. V. 45. Apoc. XII. 11. Non tam exemplo, quam imprimis merito suo erigit Apostolos, quo acquisivit nobis vires superandi non mundum tantum, sed etiam ipsum mundi principem Satanam, eique caput contrivit, ut conteri sub pedes nostros possit, Gen. III. 16. Rom. XVI. 26. Per pacem imprimis reconciliatio cum Deo, quam per Christum habemus Rom. V. 1, intelligitur, unde tranquillitas oritur conscientiae; In Christo autem eam habemus, quia Christus eam nobis acquisivit, nec nisi per fidem in Christum ea actu fruimur, 2. Cor. V. 19. Ita Ambrosius: Hoc ideo dixit, quia cum Deo qui habet pacem, non timet omnem mentem adversam. Tutus enim est pace Dei omnis diligens Deum in Christo Jesu. Et Hieron. in Epist. ad virg. Exul. Propter fidei certitudinem in me debetis pacem habere non sentiendo praesentia, sed certo sperando futura.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The προαγώνιος (preliminary) prayer of Christ, in which he first prays to the Father for his own glorification, then for the glory of the Father, that he himself may also glorify the Father; then for the salvation of men, inasmuch as all power over all flesh has been given to him, that he may give eternal life to his own, which consists in the knowledge of God and of Christ, for which cause he has performed his work on earth, and has manifested the name of God to his own, who believe that he came forth from the Father. Then he prays for the sanctification and unity of his own, who are also the Father's, whom he has hitherto preserved, except the son of perdition, that they may be kept from evil and be sanctified in the word of truth; and also for those who are to believe through the word of the disciples, that they all may be one in the Father and in Christ, and for all whom the Father has given to him, that they may one day see his glory, and that now the love of God may be in them, and Christ may be in them.

The parts are two: I. The prayer of Jesus for his own glorification, to verse 8. II. The prayer of Jesus for the sanctification, unity, and vision of his glory of the disciples and those who are to believe through them, to verse 26.

PART I. The prayer of Jesus for his own glorification.

Vers. 1. ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, etc.) That is, these things having been said: he adds prayers to the consolation. ἐπῆρε τὼς ὀφθαλμὺς ἀυτῶ εἰς τὸν ὀυρανὸν) In the manner of a high priest about to pray for himself and for the people, Heb. V. 3, 7. And it is credible that this was done in sight of the Temple, when Christ was passing by that place and stopped for a little while. For a part of the Northern and Eastern portico of the Temple was nearest to the valley of Cedron, as Josephus teaches us in Jewish War VI, 19.

These things were not done or said on the road, but in the upper room, as we observed above. Although he is said to have lifted his eyes to heaven, that can also be done in the upper room, and is often done by the faithful, not only in the open air. Blessed Gerhard thinks that, since in his prayers he no longer had business with the Apostles alone, but also and even especially with the heavenly Father, whom he was addressing in these prayers, he therefore turned his face away from the disciples and lifted his eyes to heaven through the open windows of the upper room; as was done by Daniel, chapter VI. 10. Furthermore, concerning this prayer προαγωνίῳ, see especially Blessed Glassius in his special dissertation, and Blessed Gerhard, Harm. Cap. CLXXX.

Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα) The time not only when I shall suffer most grievous torments, but also when I shall be betrayed, condemned, mocked, and despised.

Δόξασόν σου τὸν ὑἸν) Namely, by a swift resurrection and ascension into heaven. See above XI. 4, XII. 28, XIII. 31.

Ἱνα κὶ ὁ ὑἱός σου δοξάσῃ σε) By causing the Gospel to be preached throughout the world, XV. 8.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Oratio Christi προαγώνιος, qua primum pro sui glorificatione Patrem orat, tum ob gloriam Patris, ut ipse etiam Patrem glorificet; tum ob salutem hominum, siquidem sibi data sit potestas omnis carnis, ut suis vitam aeternam, quae in cognitione Dei, & Christi consistit, donet, cujus causa opus suum egerit in terra, & nomen Dei manifestarit suis, qui credunt quod à Patre exiverit. Deinde orat pro suorum, qui & Patris sunt, sanctificatione, & unitate, quos hactenus conservavit, praeter filium perditionis, ut custodiantur à malo, & sanctificentur in verbo veritatis; nec non pro illis, qui per verbum discipulorum credituri sunt, ut omnes unum sint in Patre, & in Christo, & pro omnibus, quos sibi Pater dedit, ut olim videant gloriam suam, nunc vero charitas Dei in ipsis sit, & Christus sit in ipsis.

Partes sunt duae: I. Oratio Jesu pro sui glorificatione, ad v. 8. II. Oratio Jesu pro discipulorum, & qui per eos credituri sunt, sanctificatione, unitate, & gloriae suae visione, ad v. 26.

PARS I. Oratio Jesu pro sui glorificatione.

Vers. 1. ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, κτλ) Id est, his dictis: Consolationi addit preces. ἐπῆρε τὼς ὀφθαλμὺς ἀυτῶ εἰς τὸν ὀυρανὸν) Ritu pontificis pro se & pro populo oraturus, Hebr. V. 3. 7. Et credibile est, factum hoc in conspectu Templi, cum istac Christus transiret ac nonnihil subsisteret. Nam pars porticus Templi Septentrionalis & Orientalis proxima erat valli Cedron, ut nos docet Josephus Belli Judaici VI, 19.

Non haec in via facta vel dicta sunt, sed in coe- naculo, quemadmodum supra observavimus. Quanquam vero oculos in coelum levasse dici- tur, id etiam in coenaculo fieri potest, & a fide- libus saepe fit, non solum sub dio. B. Gerhardus censet, cum in precibus non amplius ipsi nego- tium fuerit cum solis Apostolis, sed etiam ac vel maxime cum Patre coelesti, quem precibus his compellabat, ideo facie a discipulis aversa oculos in coelum per apertas coenaculi fenestras sus- tulisse; ut a Daniele factum cap. VI. 10. Caeterum de hac oratione προαγωνίῳ videatur imprimis B. Glassius peculiari dissertatione, & B. Gerhardus Harm. Cap. CLXXX.

Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα) Tempus non tantum quo cruciatus patiar gravissimos, sed & quo prodar, damner, illudar, contemnar.

Δόξασόν σου τὸν ὑἸν) Nempe celeri resurrectione, & eve- ctione in coelum. Vide supra XI. 4. XII. 28. XIII. 31.

Ἱνα κὶ ὁ ὑἱός σου δοξάσῃ σε) Efficiendo ut Evangelium praedicetur per orbem terrarum XV. 8.

## 17:2
Vers. 2. καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκὸς) He shows how the Father is to be glorified through the Gospel, because through it eternal life is promised to none others than those who sincerely worship God the Father. Καθὼς here renders the preceding reason, and is equivalent to 'inasmuch as': ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκὸς, that is, over every human being. A similar construction is found in Matt. X. 1. It is well enough known that for the Hebrews 'flesh' is taken for 'man'. 'You have given' is taken for 'you have promised that you would give', as is often the case in Law. For this right was handed over to him after the resurrection. Matt. ch. XXVIII. 8. Understand 'power' over men to be saved or condemned. Above V. 27.

ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ, δώσῃ, αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον) A Hebraism, πᾶν ὇ προπιπτὶ, and what follows, αὐτοῖς, is a construction κατὰ σημαινόμενον. See above VI. 39. He explains the manner of using the power, namely, that eternal life is given not to all, but to believers. Thus above III. 16, having first spoken of the world, he then restricts salvation to believers, ὇ δέδωκας αὐτῷ. Understand it as 'with effect', you have given them in such a way that they have actually come to him: as we said above VI. 37.

Here a second reason for the glorification which Christ requested is more correctly established, sought from the salvation of men: just as the former was taken from the Glory of God: because Christ was appointed by the Father as Mediator, Redeemer, and Savior of the human race, which is understood by the power over flesh, and for that end he had been sent into the world, that he might restore to the human race the goods lost through the fall, and distribute them to those finally adhering to him by faith, who were given to him by the Father: whence it was necessary that Christ be glorified, and not left under the weight of divine wrath and the sins of the human race, Rom. IV. last, 1 Cor. XV. v. 17. Thus Augustine, tr. C. & CXI. in John.

Latin:

Vers. 2. καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκὸς) O- stendit quomodo per Evangelium clarificandus sit Pater, quia per illud nullis aliis vita aeterna promittitur, quam qui Deum Patrem sincere colunt. Καθὼς hic rationem red- dit praecedentem, & valet siquidem: ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρ- κὸς, id est, in omnem hominem. Similis constructio Matth. X. 1. Carnem pro homine sumi Hebraeis, notum satis. Dedisti, sumtum pro, daturum te promisisti, ut in Jure saepe. Nam jus hoc ei traditum est post resurrectionem. Matth. c. XXVIII. 8. Potestatem, in homines intellige servandos aut damnandos. Supr. V. 27.

ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ, δώσῃ, αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον) He- braismus πᾶν ὇ προπιπτὶ, & quod sequitur αὐτοῖς est con- structio κατὰ σημαινόμενον. Vid. supra VI. 39. Explicat mo- dum utendae potestatis, nempe ut vita aeterna detur non o- mnibus sed credentibus. Sic supra III. 16. primum de mun- do locutus, restringit deinde salutem ad credentes, ὇ δέδωκας αὐτῷ. Intellige cum effectu, ita dedisti, ut re ipsa ad eum pervenerint: ut diximus supra VI. 37.

Rectius hic altera constituitur glorificationis, quam Christus petiit, ratio, ab hominum salute pe- tita: quemadmodum prior desumta erat a Gloria Dei: quia Christus constitutus erat a Patre Me- diator, Redemtor & Salvator humani generis, quod per potestatem carnis intelligitur, eoque fine in mundum missus erat, ut amissa per lapsum bona humano generi repararet, eademque sibi a Patre datis finaliter per fidem adhaerentibus distribue- ret: unde opus erat, ut glorificaretur Christus, non vero sub pondere irae divinae & peccatorum hu- mani generis relinqueretur Rom. IV. ult. 1. Cor. XV. v. 17. Ita Augustinus tr. C. & CXI. in Joh.

## 17:3
Vers. 3. Αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ) In this it is situated: in this way it is prepared, a Metonymy as above VI. 63, XI. 25, XII. 50, XIV. 6. A similar manner of speaking, Rom. XI. 12.

ἵνα γινώσκωσί σε τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν) Here ἵνα is ἐκβατικὸν: for the manner of preparing eternal life is described, which is such that it looks especially to the glory of God the Father. γινώσκειν here is to be understood πρακτικῶς, as in I. 10, that they may acknowledge, embrace, worship, and revere you as the only God, with all those excluded whom the false persuasion of the Gentiles had introduced. Ignatius to the Magnesians, speaking of Jesus: τοῖς ἐξοκείλασιν εἰς πολυθείαν ἧ ἕνα κὶ μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν καταγγέλοντα ῤ ἑαυτῦ πατέρα. In the constitutions of Clement to those converted from the Gentiles: μεταθέντες γὰρ ἀπὸ τῆς προτέρας ματαιοπόνυ συνηθείας κὶ τῶ ἀψύχων εἰδώλων ὑπεριδόντες κὶ τῶ ἐν σκότῳ δαιμόνων κατα- φρονήσαντες, προσδραμόντες τε τῷ Φωτὶ τῷ ἀληθινῷ κὶ ἐπι- γνόντες δι᾽ αὐτοῦ ῤ ἵνα κὶ μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν κὶ πατέρα, κληρονόμοι τῆς αὐτῦ βασιλείας ἀνεφάνητε. See 1 Thess. I. v. 9.

κὶ ὃν ἀπέσειλας Ἰησῦν Χριστὸν) He speaks modestly of himself in the third person. The sense is, and that they may acknowledge me as your legate. By this word he shows that the honor bestowed upon him returns to the Father. For it is in the king's interest that his legate be honored.

We have dealt most extensively with this classic passage in the Anti-Crellius. Two principal heads are established, in the knowledge of which eternal life is situated: The first is that the Father alone is that true God, not excluding the Son and the Holy Spirit, who are one with the Father, 1 John V. 7, but excluding idols and created things, or whatever is outside the Father: Because, therefore, the Son and the Holy Spirit are in the Father, and are of one essence with the Father: it is necessary to acknowledge that one true God to be the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, concerning which Basil, l. IV. Contr. Eunom.: 'One and only' are said of God in Scripture not for the distinction of the Son or the Holy Spirit, but against those who are not Gods, but are falsely called so. Compare John VIII. v. 16, ch. XII. 32. The other is that Jesus Christ was sent by the Father with power, namely, over all flesh, so that he might give eternal life to those believing in him. These two mysteries, concerning the TRIUNE GOD and CHRIST, or concerning the Trinity of persons in that one divine essence, and concerning the person of Christ consisting of two natures, divine and human, because the eternal Son of God sent from the Father assumed human nature, and to him was given the power of redeeming the whole human race, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish, but have eternal life, are the supreme heads of heavenly doctrine, in which eternal life is situated, or by the faithful reception of which we obtain eternal life: to which heads also other things necessary to be believed can be reduced, Conf. John III. 16, 36, ch. VI. 40, 1 John V. 11, 12, 30, and John ch. XVI. 21, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ) In hoc sita est: hoc modo paratur, Metonymia ut supra VI. 63. XI. 25. XII. 50. XIV. 6. Simile loquendi genus, Rom. XI. 12.

ἵνα γινώσκωσί σε τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν) Hic ἵνα est ἐκβα-τικὸν: Describitur enim modus parandae vitae aeternae, qui talis est, ut Dei Patris gloriam maxime spectet. γινώσκειν hic in- telligendum πρακτικῶς ut. I. 10. ut agnoscant, amplectantur, colant, revereantur te ut solum Deum, exclusis omnibus iis, quos falsa Gentium persuasio induxerat. Ignatius ad Magnetas de Jesu loquens: τοῖς ἐξοκείλασιν εἰς πολυθείαν ἧ ἕνα κὶ μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν καταγγέλοντα ῤ ἑαυτῦ πατέρα. In Clementis constitutionibus ad conversos ex gentibus: μεταθέντες γὰρ ἀπὸ τῆς προτέρας ματαιοπόνυ συνηθείας κὶ τῶ ἀψύχων εἰδώλων ὑπεριδόντες κὶ τῶ ἐν σκότῳ δαιμόνων κατα- φρονήσαντες, προσδραμόντες τε τῷ Φωτὶ τῷ ἀληθινῷ κὶ ἐπι- γνόντες δι᾽ αὐτοῦ ῤ ἵνα κὶ μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν κὶ πατέρα, κληρονόμοι τῆς αὐτῦ βασιλείας ἀνεφάνητε. Vid. 1. Thess. I. v. 9.

κὶ ὃν ἀπέσειλας Ἰησῦν Χριστὸν) De se modeste in tertia persona loquitur. Sensus est, & ut me agnoscant ut le- gatum tuum. Hac voce ostendit honorem sibi inhabitum ad Patrem redire. Nam regis interest, ut legatus hono- retur.

De Classico hoc loco fusissime egimus in Anti-Crellio. Duo constituuntur praecipua ca- pita, in quorum cognitione sita est vita æter- na: Primum est, quod solus Pater sit ille verus Deus, non excludendo Filium & Spiritum San- ctum, qui unum sunt cum Patre, 1. Joh. V. 7. sed idola & res creatas, vel quicquid est extra Pa- trem: Quia ergo Filius & Spiritus S. in Patre sunt, & unius sunt cum Patre essentiæ: agno- scere oportet unum illum verum Deum esse Pa- trem, Filium & Spiritum Sanctum, de quo Basil. l. IV. Contr. Eunom. Unus & solus de Deo in Scriptura non ad distinctionem Filii aut Spiritus Sancti dicuntur, sed adversus eos, qui Dii non sunt, falso autem appellantur. Confer. Joh. IIX. v. 16. cap. XII. 32. Alterum est, quod Jesus Chri- stus sit missus à Patre cum potestate nempe omnis carnis, ut credentibus in ipsum det æternam vi- nam. Quæ duo mysteria, de DEO TRI- UNO & CHRISTO, vel de Trinitate per- sonarum, in unica illa divina essentia, & de per- sona Christi duabus constante naturis, divina & humana, quia æternus Filius Dei è Patre missus humanam naturam assumsit, eique data est po- testas redimendi totum humanum genus, ut omnis, qui credit in ipsum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam, suprema capita sunt cœ- lestis doctrinæ, in qua sita est æterna vita, vel cujus fideli susceptione vitam consequimur æter- nam: ad quæ etiam capita cætera reduci possunt creditu necessaria, Conf. Joh. III. 16. 36. c. VI. 40. 1. Joh. V. 11. 12. 30. & Joh. c. XVI. 21. 22.

## 17:4
Vers. 4. I have glorified thee on the earth) He shows that he is not asking for anything unfair, as one who has referred all his teachings to the honor of the Father. See Matt. IX. 8. XV. 31. Mark II. 12, Luke V. v. 26. XVIII. 43. But the passion can also be included, because he had determined to undergo it, and it was imminent. For by a similar expression below he says that he is not in the world. But by this passion God was eminently glorified. See what we said at XII. 28. and below XXI. 19.

I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do) I have taught the Jews and now I deliver myself to death. Polycarp, as interpreted by Victor of Capua: How does he commemorate that he has fulfilled the work of human salvation, when he had not yet ascended the standard of the cross? But by the definition of the will, by which he had decreed to approach all the signs of his venerable passion, he signifies that he has rightly finished the work.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Ἐγώ σε ἐδόξασα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς) Ostendit non ini- quum se petere, ut qui omnia sua dogmata ad Patris hono- rem retulerit. Vid. Matth. IX. 8. XV. 31. Marc. II. 12, Luc. V. v. 26. XVIII. 43. Sed & passio includi potest, quia eam sub- ire constituerat, & de proximo imminebat. Nam simili lo- cutione infra ait, se non esse in mundo. Hac autem passione eximie Deus glorificatus est. Vide quæ diximus XII. 28. & infra XXI. 19.

τὸ ἔργον ἐτελείωσα ὃ δέδωκάς μοι ἵνα ποιήσω) Docui Ju- dæos & jam me in mortem trado. Polycarpus interprete Victore Capuano: Quomodo opus salutis humano adimplesse commemorat: cum necdum crucis vexillum conscenderat? sed definitione voluntatis de qua cuncta venerandæ passionis insignia adire decreverat; jure se opus perfecisse significat.

## 17:5
Vers. 5. And now) Now therefore in turn.

Glorify thou me, O Father, with thine own self) In heaven. For this is opposed to that which preceded, on the earth.

with the glory which I had) By your destination: as 1 Pet. I. 20. Rev. XIII. 8. So also Eph. I. 4. and below 24. A similar manner of speaking. Eph. I. 3. 4. Thus the Hebrews say the law existed before the world. See the Talmud on vows.

before the world was) before the foundation of the world, as Peter speaks in the cited place. The Chaldean paraphrast on Ps. LXXII. Before the sun, the name of the Messiah was prepared.

with thee) Refer to that 'I had', and understand as we have said, in your decree: a sign of which was already given then, when God created the world and man himself through the Word, prefiguring that the same would be in Jesus the author of the new creation and of a better world. See what we said at c. I. Add Rev. V. v. 12. and following.

This gloss draws its origin from the Arians, as observed by Tertullian, or Novatian in the book on the Trinity, Chapter XXIV, and is seized upon by the Socinians, as is evident from Socinus himself, Contr. Erasm. Joh. p. 80. and against Wujek p. 135. and also from the Racovian Catechism p. 76; upon which Polanus, Tossanus, and other Reformed theologians pour cold water. But the glory which Christ received in the fullness of time, and with which he here asks to be glorified, as man, he is said to have had with the Father, as GOD, before the foundations of the world were laid: because from eternity he was with God, John c. I. v. 1. That he truly had glory with the Father, Christ says, not truly only according to predestination. As truly as He was glorified in time by the Father, so truly He also had glory from eternity with the Father. In the predestination or decree, the creation of the world and the glorification of Christ are together from eternity. But Christ asks for that glory to be given to Him, which He had before the world was. See the Disputation on the pre-existence of the Son of God.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Καὶ νῦν) Nunc ergo vicissim.

Δόξασόν με σὺ πάτερ παρὰ σε αυτῷ) In cœlo. Opponitus enim hoc ei, quod præcesserat, ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

τῇ δόξῃ ᾗ εἶχον) Destinatione tua: ut 1. Petr. I. 20. Apoc. XIII. 8. Sic & Eph. I. 4. & infra 24. Simile loquendi genus. Eph. I. 3. 4. Sic legem fuisse ante mundum ajunt Hebræi Vid. Thalmudem de votis.

πρὸ τῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι) πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμυ, ut Petrus dicto loco loquitur. Chaldæus paraphrastes ad Ps. LXXII. Ante solem præparatum est nomen Messiæ.

παρά σοι) Refer ad illud εἶχον, & intellige ut diximus, in decreto tuo: cujus signum aliquod jam tum datum est, cum mundum & ipsum hominem Deus condidit per τὸν λόγον, præsignificans eundem in Jesu auctorem fore novæ creationis & mundi melioris. Vid. quæ ad c. I. Adde Apoc. V. v. 12. & seq.

Glossa hæc ab Arianis originem trahit ob- servante Tertulliano, vel Novatiano l. de Trin. Cap. XXIV. & à Socinianis arripitur, ut è Socino ipso Contr. Erasm. Joh. p. 80. & contra Wujek p. 135. nec non è Catech. Racov. p. 76. constat; quibus frigidam suffundunt Polanus, Tossanus, aliique Reformati. Sed gloriam, quam in tem- poris plenitudine accepit Christus, & qua glo- rificari hic petit, quantum ad plenariam neces- sitatis divinæ χρῆσιν, ut homo, apud Patrem ha- buisse dicitur, ut DEUS, ante jacta mundi fundamenta: quia ab æterno erat πρὸς ῆ θεὸν apud DEUM, Joh. c. I. v. 1. Vere habuisse se gloriam apud Patrem Christus dicit, non vero tantum secundum prædestinationem. Quam vere in tempore glorificatus fuit à Patre, tam vere etiam gloriam ab æterno habuit apud Patrem. In Prædestinatione vel decreto simul ab æterno sunt creatio mundi & glorificatio Christi. At Christus petit illam sibi dari gloriam, quam habuit antequam esset mundus. Vid. Disput. de προϋπάρξει Filii Dei.

## 17:6
Vers. 6. I have manifested Thy name to men) Your properties: I have revealed Your justice, power, goodness. And understand this with effect, that is, they perceived it with me teaching them. See what we said above VI. 44. This manifestation is the demonstration of Hierocles.

Those whom Thou hast given Me) Again with effect, who came to Me with You drawing them, and wished to be Mine, as we just said. He treats here, however, of those who had already in reality believed; He will also treat of those who are about to believe.

out of the world) Thus above XV. 19. I have chosen you out of the world, separated from the universality of the world, You have given them to Me as a peculiar possession.

They were Thine) By a certain affection of piety they were Yours, from You, as above VIII. 47.

And Thou hast given them to Me) You devoted effort so that they might believe in Me, might acknowledge Me as their Lord, and that effort did not lack its effect.

This Arminian interpretation has no place, because the affection of piety is not prior to faith, but a consequence of faith and a fruit of the same. And therefore others more correctly explain: They were Yours by election to the Apostleship and You gave them to Me, chosen and separated from the world for instruction, so that they might be suitable teachers of the whole world, which sense flows from the preceding and following context. Add v. 8 and 12. The Father gave to Him both the persons to be instructed and the words or dogmas by which they ought to be instructed. Compare Is. VIII. 16. Heb. ch. II. 13. With which the interpretation of verse 7 by Grotius himself, not to be rejected, agrees.

And they have kept Thy word) He calls the word of the Father that which He Himself announced in the name of the Father. This they have kept, that is, they have impressed it upon their heart and retained it: they did not fail perfidiously like Judas.

Latin:

Vers. 6. Ἐφανέρωσά σου τὸ ὄνομα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις) Proprietates tuas: Justitiam, potentiam, bonitatem patefeci. Et hoc intellige cum effectu, id est illi me docente perceperunt. Vide quæ diximus supra VI. 44. Φανέρωσις hæc est δεῖξις Hierocli.

Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι) Iterum cum effectu, qui te trahente ad me venerunt, & mei esse voluerunt, ut modo diximus. Agit autem hic de iis qui jam reipsa crediderant, aget & de credituris.

ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Sic supra XV. 19. ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, ex mundi universitate secretos dedisti mihi in peculium.

Σοὶ ἦσαν) Pietatis quodam affectu tui erant, ex te, ut supra VIII. 47.

Καὶ ἐμοὶ αὐτοὺς δέδωκας) Operam dedisti, ut in me crederent, me Dominum suum agnoscerent, eaque opera effectu suo non caruit.

Locum non habet hæc interpretatio Arminiana, quia pietatis affectus non est prior fide, sed consequens fidei & fructus ejusdem. Ideoque rectius alii explicant: Tui erant electione ad Apostolatum & mihi eos dedisti de mundo electos & separados ad informationem, ut idonei essent totius orbis Doctores, qui sensus ex antecedentibus & consequentibus fluit. Adde v. 8. & 12. Dedit ipsi Pater & personas instruendas & verba vel dogmata, quibus instrui debeant. Conf. Es. IIX. 16. Ebr. c. II. 13. Quibus congruit interpretatio, vers. 7. ipsiusmet Grotii non reprobanda.

Καὶ τὸν λόγον σου τετηρήκασι) Patris sermonem vocat quem ipse Patris nomine annuntiavit. Hunc illi servarunt, id est cordi suo impresserunt ac retinuerunt: non defecerunt perfide ut Judas.

## 17:7
Vers. 7. Now they have known) Now they believe this, they have progressed that far. To know is often used for to believe, as above VI. 69 and elsewhere.

That all things whatsoever Thou hast given Me, are from Thee) He seems to say the same thing by the same thing, but the sense is: all things which I taught them are from You. For that which He might say, which I taught, He modestly says to the honor of the Father, which You gave Me to be taught. You indeed know that You gave them to Me: they, however, have believed that they were given by You.

Latin:

Vers. 7. Νῦν ἔγνωκαν) Jam nunc hoc credunt, eo usque profecerunt. Γινώσκειν sæpe pro credere, ut supra VI. 69. & alibi.

Ὅτι πάντα ὅσα δέδωκάς μοι, παρὰ σοῦ ἐστιν) Videtur idem per idem dicere, sed sensus est: omnia, quæ eos docui, à te sunt. Pro eo autem quod diceret, quæ docui, modeste ad honorem Patris ait, quæ mihi dedisti docenda. Tu quidem scis, te mihi dedisse: illi autem à te data crediderunt.

## 17:8
Vers. 8. That the words) He explains what He had said and shows that they have rightly believed.

they have received) They have embraced, as above I. 11. 12.

ἔγνωσαν ἀληθῶς) They believed not feignedly but sincerely. Thus ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐργάζεσθαι is to serve with a sincere mind, Eccles. VII. 21. Thus also Luc. XX. 21. and elsewhere.

Παρὰ σου ἐξῆλθον) That I appeared by your command, as often heretofore. For what follows is an explanation of this.

PART II. The prayer of Jesus for the sanctification and unity of the disciples, and of those who are to believe through them, and for the vision of his glory.

Latin:

Vers. 8. Ὅτι τὰ ῥήματα) Explicat, quod dixerat & ostendit, recte eos credidisse.

ἔλαβον) Amplexi sunt, ut supra I. 11. 12.

ἔγνωσαν ἀληθῶς) Non ficte sed sincere crediderunt. Sic ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐργάζεσθαι animo sincero servire, Eccles. VII. 21. Sic & Luc. XX. 21. & alibi.

Παρὰ σου ἐξῆλθον) Me tuo mandatu apparuisse, ut antehac sæpe. Nam quod sequitur est hujus ἐπεξήγησις.

PARS II. Oratio Jesu pro discipulorum, & qui per eos credituri sunt sanctificatione ac unitate, & gloria sua visione.

## 17:9
Vers. 9. Ἐγὼ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐρωτῶ) Having commended his own with these titles, he shows that the prayers which he offers for such persons ought not to be ungrateful to God.

Οὐ περὶ τοῦ κόσμου ἐρωτῶ) He prayed also for the world, that it might repent and receive forgiveness of sins. Luc. XXIII. 34. Indeed, even shortly that it might believe, 21. But these things which he now prays for, concerning paternal protection, concerning the Spirit, concerning concord, pertain only to believers. And this opposition has emphasis: as if a king's son were to pray the father to hear him, not praying for all subjects, for rebels no less than for the faithful, but for those who have in reality shown how much they valued the king.

Ὅτι σοί εἰσι) Even after you gave them to me, they do not cease to be yours. This also is effective for commending the prayers.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Ἐγὼ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐρωτῶ) Cum suos his titulis commendasset, ostendit non ingratas Deo esse debere quas pro talibus fundit preces.

Οὐ περὶ τοῦ κόσμου ἐρωτῶ) Oravit & pro mundo, ut resipisceret & veniam acciperet peccatorum. Luc. XXIII. 34. Imo & mox ut credat 21. Sed hæc quæ nunc orat, de protectione paterna, de spiritu, de concordia, non nisi ad credentes pertinent. Et habet ἔμφασιν hæc oppositio: quasi filius regis oret patrem ut se exaudiat, non pro omnibus subditis, rebellibus non minus quam fidelibus orantem, sed pro iis, qui reipsa ostenderunt quanti regem facerent.

Ὅτι σοί εἰσι) Etiam postquam eos mihi dedisti tui esse non desinunt. Hoc quoque ad commendandas preces est efficax.

## 17:10
Vers. 10. Καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστι, καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά) This is placed first for 'for'. He gives the reason why those given to him do not cease to pertain to the Father, because all things are common between them as is customary between friends, especially between the Father and the Son. For both what the Father has, he has for the use of the Son, and what the Son has, is subject to the Father together with the Son himself.

We do not deny that the particle καὶ is taken in a causal sense: which use is not infrequent. See Gen. XX, 4. Ps. LX, v. 12. Ps. CVIII. 15. Is. LIII, v. 1. Job I. 2. The reason, however, is not taken from the fact that all things are usually common to the Father and the Son, which is neither universally true among men, nor does it apply here; but that all things which the Son of God has are the Father's, and what the Father has are the Son's: which communion in the divine is clearly unique, and pertains to the consubstantiality of the Son with the Father. Conf. John XVI. 15. He had spoken as a man; They were yours and you gave them to me: if indeed to Christ as man is given whatever is given in time: now therefore he adds as God, all mine are yours, and all yours are mine: because he is accustomed to join such sentences, so that in the unity of person both true man and true God may be believed.

Καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς) This past tense is for the present or aorist, with no definition of time: as if he were to say: even on this account they ought to be commended to you, that I have been glorified and am to be glorified further by their work and ministry; and so in their person my own matter is at stake.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστι, καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά) Prius hoc positum est pro nam. Causam reddit, cur sibi dati non desinant ad Patrem pertinere, quia omnia inter ipsos sint communia ut inter amicos solent, maxime inter Patrem & Filium. Nam & quæ Pater habet, habet in usum filii, & quæ filius habet, simul cum ipso filio Patri subjecta sunt.

Particulam καὶ αἰτιολογικῶς sumi non diffitemur: qui usus non infrequens est. Vid. Gen. XX, 4. Pf. LX, v. 12. Pf. CIIX. 15. Es. LIII, v. 1. Iob. I. 2. Ratio autem non desumta inde est, quod Patri & Filio soleant esse omnia communia, quod nec universaliter verum est inter homines, neque huc facit; Sed quod omnia, quæ Filius Dei habet Patris, & quæ Pater habet, Filii sint: quæ communio in divinis plane est μονότροπος, & ad ὁμοουσίαν Filii cum Patre pertinet. Conf. Ioh. XVI. 15. Dixerat ut homo; Tui erant & mihi credidisti: siquidem Christo ut homini detur, quicquid in tempore datur: jam ergo subjungit ut Deus, omnia mea tua sunt, & omnia tua mea sunt: Quia conjungere solet hujusmodi sententias, ut in personæ unitate & verus homo & verus Deus credatur.

Καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς) Præteritum hoc est pro præsente sive aoristo, nulla temporis definitione: quasi dicat: etiam hoc nomine illi tibi commendati esse debent, quod ego illorum opera & ministerio & inclaruerim & inclariturus sim amplius; itaque in ipsorum persona mea res vertitur.

## 17:11
Vers. 11. Καὶ οὐκ ἔτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ) A new reason for commending, that he himself is departing from them: lest he seem, as he said above, to leave them orphans, XIV. 18. οὐκ ἔτι for ἔτι οὐκ, as the Syriac translates: Henceforth I am not in the world; and 'am' for 'shall be', because it was about to be in the near future.

Καὶ οὗτοι ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσὶ) They will be after me. These I leave in such great waves.

Καὶ ἐγὼ πρός σε ἔρχομαι) an explanation of that which had preceded, that he would not be in the world, so that it may appear that by the name of the world this whole lower realm is understood, as is often the case.

That an absolute withdrawal of presence is not being indicated is evident also from Matt. XXVIII. 20. And therefore these things are to be understood only concerning the cessation of visible presence and familiar conversation: which the opposition confirms: because the Apostles were still in the world exposed to various defects and afflictions, to which Christ was not so present that he would henceforth take care of them through familiar association. Whence blessed Luther rightly says: To be in the world signifies to be engaged in an external and sensible state, that is, in that life which the world uses and lives in natural life, etc.

Πάτερ ἅγιε) It is customary for titles to be attributed to God adapted to that which is being done; thus Rom. XV. 5 and in the Psalms God is often called Holy because he abhors all malice.

Τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου) Keep them by your aid, in the profession of your name, in your worship. Thus ὄνομα is taken in Acts IX. 27, Rev. II. 3, and elsewhere,

Latin:

Vers. 11. Καὶ οὐκ ἔτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ) Nova commendandi causa, quod ipse ab eis discedat: ne videatur, ut supra dixit, relinquere eos orbos, XIV. 18. οὐκ ἔτι pro ἔτι οὐκ, ut vertit Syrus: Deinceps non sum in mundo; & sum pro ero, quia proxime futurum erat.

Καὶ οὗτοι ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσὶ) Erunt post me. Hos relin- quam in tantis fluctibus.

Καὶ ἐγὼ πρός σε ἔρχομαι) ἐπεξήγησις ejus quod præcesserat, non fore se in mundo, ut appareat mundi nomine universum hoc inferius intelligi, ut sæpe.

Non designari absolutam præsentiæ omnis subtractionem vel è Matth. XXVIII. 20. constat. Ideoque solum de visibilis præsentiæ & familiaris conversationis cessatione, hæc accipienda: quod oppositio confirmat: quia Apostoli ita in mundo adhuc erant expositi variis defectibus & afflictionibus, quibus Christus sic præsens non erat, ut familiari consortio ipsorum curam deinceps haberet. Unde recte B. Lutherus: In mundo esse significat versari in statu externo & sensibili, hoc est, in illa vita, qua mundus utitur & vivit in vita naturali, &c.

Πάτερ ἅγιε) Solent Deo cognomina tribui accommodata ad id quod agitur, sic Rom. XV. 5. & in Psalmis sæpe Deus Sanctus dicitur quod omnem malitiam abhorreat.

Τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου) Custodi eos auxilio tuo, in professione nominis tui, in cultu tuo. Sic ὄνομα sumitur Act. IX, 27. Apoc. II. 3. & alibi,

## 17:12
Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι) With effect, as above 6.

Ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν) That persevering in that profession they may testify the same thing and carry out such a great matter with consenting minds. I Cor. XV. 11, Gal. II. 9.

Latin:

Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι) Cum effectu, ut supra 6.

Ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν) Ut in ea professione perseverantes idem testantur & rem tantam consentientibus animis peragant. I. Cor. XV. 11. Gal. II. 9.

## 17:12
Vers. 12. Ὅτε ἤμην) He anticipates the time of his absence.

Ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου) I devoted effort with daily precepts and my example so that they might remain in that profession, and indeed quite successfully, as the matter shows up to this point,

Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι ἐφύλαξα) I also took this care, that the number of that college should not be diminished.

Καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο) No one was removed from this number of witnesses either by death or by voluntary defection. See below XVIII. 9.

εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας) Except for him who was most worthy of destruction on account of his treachery, and who therefore, separated from the Apostles, will perish most miserably. He is called υἱὸς ἀπωλείας here and in 2 Thess. II. 3, not from a bare destination of God, but from merit, as υἱὸς γεέννης, Matt. XXIII. 15. Thus a son of death, 2 Sam. XII. v. 5. Thus ἔθνος ἀπωλείας, Eccl. XVI. 10.

Ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ) By which, upon his perishing, that imprecation will be fulfilled which David wrote against those who repay evil for benefits, Ps. LXIX. See Acts I. 20. For scripture is said to be fulfilled as often as it receives such a thing as is said therein. Concerning this sense of the word ἵνα we have spoken several times. Chrysostom on this passage: it is a peculiar habit of scripture, as if they were positing as a cause the things that happen as a result.

That sense of the word ἵνα as resultative is correctly maintained against the Calvinists who take it finally or causally, but what is held in Ps. LXIX. 26, or rather Ps. CIX. 8 (which passage is referred to here, as is clear from Acts ch. I. 20), are not only general things, but also specifically predicted concerning the passion of Christ and his betrayer Judas: as we have shown in the annotations of those Psalms.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Ὅτε ἤμην) Anticipat tempus absentiæ suæ.

Ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου) Ego quotidianis præceptis & exemplo meo operam dedi ut in ea professione permanerent, & quidem satis feliciter, quod res hactenus monstrat,

Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι ἐφύλαξα) Etiam hanc curam gessi, ne numerus collegii istius minueretur.

Καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο) Nemo aut morte, aut voluntaria defectione exemptus est huic numero testium. Vide infra XVIII. 9.

εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας) Excepto illo qui dignissimus erat ob suam perfidiam exitio, & qui proinde segregatus ab Apostolis pessime peribit. υἱὸς ἀπωλείας dicitur hic & 2. Thess. II. 3. non ex nuda Dei destinatione, sed ex merito, ut υἱὸς γεέννης, Matth. XXIII. 15. Sic filius mortis, 2. Sam. XII. v. 5. Sic ἔθνος ἀπωλείας. Eccl. XVI, 10.

Ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ) Quo, pereunte implebitur illa imprecatio, quam David scripsit in eos, qui pro be- nefactis mala rependunt, Ps. LXIX. Vid. Act. I. 20. Dicitur enim scriptura impleri, quoties tale quid accipit, quale ibi dictum est. De hoc sensu vocis ἵνα diximus aliquoties. Chry- sostomus ad hunc locum ἰδιάζων ἦθος τῆς γραφῆς ἐστιν ὁ τρό- πος, ὡς αἰτιολογίαν τιθέντων τὰ ἐκ τῆς ἐκβάσεως συμβαί- νοντα.

Sensus ille vocis ἵνα ἐκβατικὸν recte se habet ad- versus Calvinianos τελικῶς accipientes vel αἰτιο- λογικῶς observandus, sed quæ Ps. LXIX. 26. vel po- tius Ps. CIX. 8. (qui locus hic respicitur ut ex Act. c. I. 20. patet) habentur, non tantum generalia sunt, sed etiam speciatim prædicta de passione Christi & de proditore ejusdem Juda: ut in annotatis illorum Psalmorum ostendimus.

## 17:13
Vers. 13. Νῦν δὲ πρὸς σε ἔρχομαι, καὶ ταῦτα λαλῶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ) Supply being and I am coming, as for coming. Now since I must depart, I say these things to them, that is, I pray while they are listening. For these things were said entirely economically for the salvation of the Apostles.

Ἵνα ἔχωσι τὴν χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν πεπληρωμένην ἐν αὑτοῖς) Understand here my joy as joy from me, as above XV. 11, and my love above XV. 9. The sense is, that that joy which they have hitherto conceived from my presence and care for them may not be diminished, but rather grow in my absence, when they remember these prayers, not doubting that I have been heard.

Latin:

Vers. 13. Νῦν δὲ πρὸς σε ἔρχομαι, καὶ ταῦτα λαλῶ ἐν τῷ κό- σμῳ) Supple ὢν & ἔρχομαι, κὴ pro ἐρχόμενος. Nunc cum abeundum mihi sit, hæc illis dico, id est illis audienti- bus precor. Nam omnino hæc dicta sunt οἰκονομικῶς ad salutem Apostolorum.

Ἵνα ἔχωσι τὴν χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν πεπληρωμένην ἐν αὑτοῖς) χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν hic intellige gaudium ex me, ut supra XV. 11. & ἀγάπην τὴν ἐμὴν supra XV. 9. sensus est, ut gau- dium illud quod hactenus conceperunt ex mea præsen- tia ac cura pro ipsis non minuatur, imo crescat potius me absente, ubi meminerint harum precum, non dubitantes quin exauditus sim.

## 17:14
Vers. 14. Ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον (κ) A new commendation because they are hated by the world on account of the received Gospel. It is fair, however, that one should be cherished by the patronage of him for whom he incurs many offenses. Understand δέδωκα again in such a way that it has been received by them, which had been expressed above in 8.

Καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐμίσησεν αὐτοὺς) And that is therefore: on account of the received word.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσιν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Because from that time they have defected from the sect of the world. See above XV. 19.

Καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Following my example, whose life is most alien from the life of the world. See above VIII. 23.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτοῖς ῒ λόγον (κ) Nova com- mendatio quod ob receptum Evangelium mundo exosi sint. Æquum autem est ut patrocinio ejus quis foveatur ob quem plurimas incurrit offensas. Δέδωκα rursus intellige ita ut ab ipsis receptus sit, quod expressum fuerat supra 8.

Καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐμίσησεν αὐτοὺς) καὶ id est ideo: ob rece- ptum eum sermonem.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσιν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Quia ex eo tempore descive- runt à secta mundi. Vide supra XV. 19.

Καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Secuti meum exem- plum, cujus vita à vita mundi alienissima est. Vide supra VIII. 23.

## 17:15
Vers. 15. Οὐκ ἐρωτῶ ἵνα ἄρῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) For the explanation of the preceding, for the sake of the listening Apostles. Although I know they will be exposed to the hatreds of the world, I do not pray that they be taken out of the world now, out of this life: since their work must still be of use.

Ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα τηρήσῃς αὐτοὺς) With singular care and protection.

Ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ) From all worldly malice. For the whole world lies in the evil one, I John V. 19. We have said that it is more probable that the word of the evil one is taken in this way also in the formula of the Lord's Prayer according to Matthew.

Latin:

Vers. 15. Οὐκ ἐρωτῶ ἵνα ἄρῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου) Ad ex- plicationem præcedentium, ob Apostolos audientes. Quanquam mundi odiis scio fore objectos, non tamen oro ut nunc eximantur è mundo, è vita hac: quippe quorum opera adhuc usui esse debet.

Ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα τηρήσῃς αὐτοὺς) Singulari cura atque tutela.

Ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ) Ab omni malitia mundana. Nam ὁ κόσμος ὅλος ἐν τῷ πονηρῷ κεῖται, I. Joh. V. 19. Sic τοῦ πονηροῦ vocem sumi etiam in orationis dominicæ formula ad Matthæum probabilius esse diximus.

## 17:16
Vers. 16. They are not of the world) He repeats this to signify that they are already in spirit alienated from all such malice, although not beyond infirmity.

Latin:

Vers. 16. Ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ εἰσὶ) Hoc repetit, ut significet eos jam animo alieno esse ab omni tali malitia, quanquam non extra infirmitatem.

## 17:17
Vers. 17. Sanctify them in thy truth) Render their life purer day by day. Apoc. XXII. 11. Compare what is above XIII. 10. In thy truth, that is, through thy truth more and more impressed upon their minds by the Spirit XVI. 13. 1. Eph. II. 20. 21. Not far from here departs that saying of Plutarch in his book on Isis. The desire for truth, especially that concerning the gods, is a longing for holiness, having as it were the acquisition of sacred rites as learning, and the search for all purity and the work of temple-service as more holy.

Thy word is truth) That word of thine committed to me by thee. The word of the Gospel is not false, like the sayings of the Pseudo-Prophets, not mixed with falsehood like the dogmas of the Pharisees and Philosophers, but pure and unadulterated truth. Above VIII. 31. 32. 40. XIV. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Ἁγίαζον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ σου) Vitam eorum redde indies puriorem. Apoc. XXII. 11. Confer quæ supra XIII. 10. In veritate tua, id est per tuam veritatem magis magisque impressam eorum animis per Spiritum XVI. 13. 1. Eph. II. 20. 21. Non longe hinc abit Plutarchi illud libro de Iside. Θηκότητος ὄρεξίς ἐστιν ἡ τῆς ἀληθείας, μάλιστα δὲ τῆς περὶ θεῶν, ἔφεσις, ὥσπερ ἀνάληψιν ἱερῶν τὴν μάθησιν ἔχουσα καὶ τὴν ζήτησιν ἁγνείας τε πάσης καὶ νεωκορίας ἔργον ὁσιώτερον.

Ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστι) Sermo ille tuus à te mihi mandatus. Sermo Evangelii non falsus est, ut Pseudo- Prophetarum dicta, non falso admixtus ut Pharisæorum & Philosophorum dogmata, sed plura ac puta veritas. Supra VIII. 31. 32. 40. XIV. 6.

## 17:18
Vers. 18. As thou hast sent me into the world, I also have sent them into the world). The reason is given why these stand in need of divine help above others, because they are about to undertake the hard duty of an embassy for Christ, 2 Cor. V. 20. Eph. VI. v. 20. ἀπέστειλα here is I have been accustomed to send, in which sense we have also pointed out that the word to give is sometimes used.
