There are three parts: I. The visible outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles, to verse 13. II. Peter's sermon concerning the same, with the conversion and baptism of three thousand as its fruit, to verse 41. III. A description of the first communion of the Apostolic Church, to verse 47.

PART I. The visible outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles.

Vers. 1. In the fulfilling of the day of Pentecost) Both the Syriac and the Latin read here very well, the days. For it is not a matter of one day, but of the whole compass of days. And that manner of speaking is familiar to the Hebrews. Thus we have the days were fulfilled in Gen. XXV. 24, Levit. XII. 4, and for the same the days were filled, Luke II. 21. Pentecost is called by the Hellenists not always the last day, but often that whole time of fifty days from the Passover, the Weeks to the Hebrews. Thus also Tertullian on idolatry: Excerpts of the individual solemnities of the nations, and to set them in order, they will not be able to fulfill Pentecost. Thus the Nicene Canon forbids kneeling in the days of Pentecost. The last day of the seven weeks was the day of the law given, as is gathered from Exodus XIX. 1, 11, and was called for that reason the feast of the law. On the same day the new law began to be preached by the Apostles, the complement of the old.

The singular number can be retained very well: and it is certain that the Syriac and Latin did not read otherwise, even though they translated in the plural; for it is most customary that the day of Pentecost be spoken of as the feast day of the old Pentecost. Therefore, in fulfilling the day of Pentecost is when the day of Pentecost was already being spent, or on the very day of Pentecost. The consummation of this day is not signified: but only that it was the day of Pentecost. Compare Ex. XXXIV. 22, Deut. ch. VI. 5, 10. But that truly contradicts sacred history, that the day of the law given was the last day of the seven weeks or of the feasts of Pentecost, as is gathered from Ex. XIX. 1, nay rather the feast of Pentecost was instituted at the minimum 80 days after the decalogue was promulgated. Commentators are indeed accustomed to institute this comparison, that in the O.T. Pentecost the law of the decalogue was given, in the N.T. Pentecost the Holy Spirit was visibly poured out: But that has no foundation in the Scriptures: because, when the law was given, nothing was yet established concerning the feast of Pentecost. Nor did some new law begin to be preached at the Pentecost of the N.T., which was the complement, in the Grotian sense, of the old: by which, namely, some addition was made to the Mosaic law, whether of new laws, or of stricter precepts, or of a new vigor of the old commandments. These are Pelagian-Socinian inventions. Meanwhile, that comparison which others institute can be conceded, that as on the fiftieth day from the exodus out of Egypt and the celebration of the first Passover the law was given on Mount Sinai, so on the fiftieth day, not indeed from the Passion and Crucifixion, but from the Resurrection of Christ, which brought forth the paschal feast for us, because he rose for our justification, the Holy Spirit was sent, who writes the law of God in our hearts. Compare Chrysost. hom. 11. on Pentecost.

they were all with one accord in one place) God promised his gifts to unity. In an ancient manuscript, all together. All those 120 in one place, and thus Hesychius understood it, in one place, together in the same place.

Latin:

CAPUT II. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Die Pentecostes, exorto vento videntur linguæ dispartitæ, & Spiritus Sanctus sedit super Apostolos, eosque variis linguis loqui do- cet, congregataque multitudine è variis populis, quoq́; sua eos lingua loquentes au- diente, obstupescunt omnes, de hisce, ceu Galilæis, peregrinis, variisque lin- guis magnalia Domini eloquentibus, aliis mirantibus, aliis ebrietati hæc tribuenti- bus: adversus quos apologiam instituit Pe- trus, & vaticinium Ioëlis de S. S. effusione post Iesum occisum, & juxta Davidis ora- culum, quod corruptionem videre non de- buerit, resuscitatum ad dexteram Dei, se- cundum aliam prædictionem Davidicam, evectum impletum esse docet. Quacum corda penetrarent auditorum, hique mo- nerentur de pœnitentia, & suscipiendo ba- ptismo, 3000. animarum baptizata sunt, & in doctrina Apostolica in communione etiam bonorum unanimes permansêre, in- ter quos miracula facta, & à Deo, quem glorificarunt, subinde plures communioni additi.

Partes sunt tres: I. Visibilis Sp. S. super Aposto- los effusio, ad v. 13. II. Petri de eadem contio, cum conversione & baptismo trium millium ceu ejus- dem fructu, ad v. 41. III. Primæ communionis Ec- clesiæ Apostolicæ descriptio, ad v. 47.

PARS I. Visibilis Sp. S. Apostolos effusio.

Vers. 1. Ἐν τῷ συμπληρῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς) Optime & Syrus & Latinus hic legere, τὰς ἡμέρας. Agitur enim non de una die, sed de toto dierum ambitu. Et fami- liare Hebræis id loquendi genus. Sic ἐπληρώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι habemus Gen. XXV. 24. Levit. XII. 4. & pro eodem ἐπλή- θησαν ἡμέραι, Luc. II. 21. Πεντηκοστὴ Hellenistis vocatur non semper dies ultima, sed sæpe totum illud tempus dierum quinquaginta à Paschate, שָׁבֻעוֹת Hebræis. Sic & Tertullia- nus idololatria: Excerpta singulas solennitates nationum, & in ordinem exserere, Pentecosten implere non poterunt. Sic Ca- non Nicænus vetat genua flecti ἐν ταῖς τῆς πεντηκοστῆς ἡμέ- ραις. Dies ultimus septem septimanarum erat dies latæ le- gis, ut colligitur Exodi XIX. 1. 11. vocabaturque ob id שמחת תורה festum legis. Eodem die cœpit prædica- ri ab Apostolis lex nova, complementum veteris.

Retineri optime potest singularis numerus: nec aliter legisse, etsi in plurali verterunt, Syrum & La- tinum, certo constat; diem enim Pentecostes de die festo Pentecostes veteris dici, usitatissimum est. In complendo ergo diem Pentecostes est, cum jam dies Pentecostes ageretur, seu ipso die Pentecostes. Non consumatio diei hujus significatur: sed solum, quod dies fuerit Pentecostes. Conf. Ex. XXXIV. 22. Deut. c. VI. 5. 10. Id vero sacræ historiæ refragatur, diem latæ legis fuisse diem ultimum septem septimanarum seu festivitatum Pentecostes, nequid è c. Ex. XIX. 1. colligitur, imo festum Pentecostes ad minimum 80. diebus post institutum fuit à promulgato decalogo. Solent quidem Postillatores hanc instituere colla- tionem, quod in V. T. Pentecoste lex decalogi la- ta, in N. T. Pentecoste Sp. S. gratia visibiliter effusa sit: Sed ea in Scripturis fundamentum non habet: quia, cum lex lata est, nondum quicquam de festo Pentecostes constitit. Neque nova quædam lex in Pentecoste N. T. prædicari cœpit, quæ complemen- tum, sensu Grotiano, veteris fuerit: qua nempe legi Mosaica accessio aliqua facta sit seu novarum legum, seu adstrictiorum præceptionum, vel novi vigoris ve- terum mandatorum. Commenta hæc sunt Pelagio- Sociniana. Interim concedi potest illa collatio, quam alii instituunt, uti quinquagesimo die ab exi- tu ex Ægypto & celebratione primi Paschatos lex in monte Sinai lata, sic quinquagesimo die, non quidem à Passione & Crucifixione, sed à Resurre- ctione Christi, quæ nobis festivitatem paschalem peperit, quia propter justificationem nostram resur- rexit, missus Sp. S. est, qui scribit legem Dei in cor- da nostra. Conf. Chrysost. hom. 11. de Pentec.

ἦσαν ἅπαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ) Deus dona sua pro- misit unitati. In manuscripto veteri, πάντες ὁμῦ. Omnes illi CXX. in uno loco, & sic accepit Hesychius, ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ. ὁμῦ εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον.

## 2:2
Vers. 2. as of a rushing mighty wind) wind is a sign of the divine advent: Gen. III. 18, but with the word mighty added, the magnitude of the gifts above the prophetic is signified.

and it filled all the house, where they were sitting) A presage thus also of the filling of the whole world, through which the Church is diffused.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας) πνοὴ signum divini adventus: Gen. III. 18. at addita voce βιαίας magnitudo donorum supra prophetica significatur.

καὶ ἐπλήρωσε ὅλον τὸν οἶκον, ὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι) Præsagium sic etiam implendi totius orbis, per quem Ecclesia diffusa est.

## 2:3
Vers. 3. cloven tongues) The punishment of languages scattered men: Gen. X. the gift of languages gathered the scattered into one people.

It is premised ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς, there appeared to them tongues, or little flames of tongues, which were as if divided into parts, like fire: because those little flames, dispersed by rays, presented such an appearance, since ὡσεὶ πυρὸς is added. It is therefore in vain to dispute whether αὐτοῖς should be rendered ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς, as it seemed to Flacius, Piscator, and Salmeron, or ἀπ᾿ or ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν, since the simple sense can be retained, that such fiery little flames representing tongues were seen by them, in the symbol of which it is said the Spirit let himself down upon each one of them, just as in the symbol and figure of the dove he let himself down upon Christ, Matt. III. Whence there is no need to posit that those little flames clung to the mouths of the Apostles, for thus they would not have been seen by the Apostles themselves, but it is rather to be believed that such lights were seen above their heads, and dispersed little flames, in which the Spirit willed to manifest himself, and to sit upon the Apostles and others gathered there. S. and Athanasius explains this sufficiently clearly. T. I. ἐμερίσθησαν γὰρ γλῶσσαι ὡς εἰ πυρὸς C ἐκάθισεν l. de comm. essent. Patr. Fil. & Sp. S. p. 135. The Holy Spirit appeared at Pentecost in the form of fire: for tongues as of fire were divided, and sat upon each one of them.

ὡσεὶ πυρὸς) The highest efficacy and splendor of the preaching is signified. See what was said at Matt. III. 11. Philo on the Decalogue: since it is the nature of fire partly to give light and partly to burn, those who deem it worthy to be obedient to the oracles will live for all time as if in shadowless light, having the laws themselves as stars shining in their soul. But as many as are unruly continue to be burned and consumed by their inner desires, which like a flame ravage the entire life of those who possess them. Compare 2 Cor. II. 16. and the passage of Isaiah IV. 4 which we cited for the first chapter.

ἐκάθισέ τε ἐφ᾿ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν) This sitting signified that this gift would be perpetually present to them, as often as they had business with Gentiles of another language; prophecy rarely attended the Prophets, only when God willed, nor were the Prophets certain when they would have it. We have examples in Nathan, Samuel, Isaiah,

These things hold better than the novel opinion of Salmasius: that with the miracle of the divided tongues removed, the gift itself of proclaiming the miracles of God in various tongues also ceased, if indeed the Apostles were adorned with this gift to that end, that they might preach the mighty works of God everywhere throughout the whole world.

Latin:

Vers. 3. διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι) Pœna linguarum di- sfersit homines: Gen. X. donum linguarum dispersos in unum populum recollegit.

Præmittitur ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς visæ sunt ipsis lin- guæ, vel flammulæ linguarum, quæ in partes quasi dissectæ, instar ignis: quia flammulæ illæ radiis di- sfersæ talem speciem referebant, quum addatur ὡσεὶ πυρὸς. Frustra ergo disputatur an αὐτοῖς red- dendum ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ut Flacio, Piscatori, Salmer. vi- sum, an ἀπ᾿ seu ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν, quum possit retineri simplex sensus, quod visæ ipsis sint tales flammulæ igneæ linguas repræsentantes, in quarum symbolo dicitur Spiritus sese demisisse super unumquem- que eorum, quemadmodum in symbolo & figura columbæ sese super Christum demisit Matth. III. Unde non opus est, ut statuatur, flammulas illas hæsisse in ore Apostolorum, sic enim ipsis Apostolis visæ non fuissent, sed credendum potius, super ca- pita ipsorum conspecta fuisse talia lumina, disper- sasque flammulas, in quibus se manifestare, & su- per Apostolos, aliosque ibi congregatos sedere voluit Sp. S. idque luculenter satis explicat Atha- nas. T. I. ἐμερίσθησαν γὰρ γλῶσσαι ὡς εἰ πυρὸς C ἐκάθισεν l. de comm. essent. Patr. Fil. & Sp. S. p. 135. Apparuit Sp. S. in Pentecoste in specie ignis: di- sptrtitæ enim sunt linguæ quasi ignis, & sedit super unumquemque eorum.

ὡσεὶ πυρὸς) Summa efficacia & splendor prædicationis significatur. Vide, quæ dicta Matth. III. 11. Philo ad Decalo- gum : ἐπειδὴ τῦ πυρὸς τὸ μὲν φωτίζειν, τὸ δὲ καίειν πέφυκεν, οἱ μὲν τοῖς χρησμοῖς ἀξιῶντες εἶναι καταπειθεῖς, ὡς ἐν ἀσκίῳ φωτὶ τὸν ἀεὶ χρόνον βιώσονται, τὺς νόμυς αὐτὸς ἀσέρας ἔχοντες ἐν ψυ- χῇ Φωσφορῦντας. ὅσοι δὲ ἀφηνιασταὶ, καιόμενοι καὶ κατακαιό- μενοι διατελῦσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἔνδον ἐπιθυμιῶν, αἳ φλογὸς τρόπον πορθήσᾱσι τὸν σύμπαντα τᾶν ἐχόντων βίον. Confer 2. Cor. II. 16. & quem ad primum caput citavimus Esaiz locum IV. 4.

ἐκάθισέ τε ἐφ᾿ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν) Significabat hæc sessio perpetuo illis hoc donum adfuturum, quoties negotium ipfis esset cum gentibus linguæ alterius Prophetis prophetia raro aderat, cum Deus vellet, neque certi erant Prophetæ, quando eam essent habituri. Exempla habemus in Na- thane, Samuele, Esaia,

Rectius hæc se habent, quam novella Salmasii sententia: qf. sublato dispertitarum linguarum mi- raculo ipsum quoque donum, variis linguis miracula Dei efferendi, cessarit, siquidem eum in finem dono hoc fuere ornati, ut passim prædicarent Dei ma- gnalia Apostoli per totum terrarum orbem.

## 2:4
Vers. 4. ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις) Other than those which they had learned. What is ἑτέραις here, is καιναῖς in Mark XVI. 17. Do not believe those who claim the miracle was done in the ears of the hearers. Everything clearly resists them, which is 1 Cor. XII. 10. 28. 30. XIV. 2. 4. 5. 6. 8. 13. 14. 18. 19. 22. 23. 26. 27. 38.

Cyprian, Sermon on the Holy Spirit, Chrysostom, Arator, Oecumenius, Dionysius the Carthusian, Erasmus, and Sanctius thought the miracle was done in the ears; but the miracle is more correctly assigned to the Apostles, who spoke in various tongues, by Cyril of Jerusalem, Nazianzen, Ambrose on Ps. CXVIII, Augustine, Tract. XCVIII on John, Leo the Great, Sermon on Pentecost, and most recent writers. Compare Chamier, Panstrat. T. I. L. XI. c. 14. p. 9. & 10. ἀποφθέγγεσθαι) This word is accustomed to be used regarding the Prophets, corresponding to the Hebrew נבא, קסם, הרף and similar ones. See below 14. Verse 5. ἦσαν δὲ ἱερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες) The verb κατοικεῖν here corresponds to the Hebrew כור, which is accustomed to be translated both as κατοικεῖν and παροικεῖν, and sometimes also as διατρίβειν; therefore it is said not only of those who had fixed their residence, but also of those who had come into the city to celebrate the Passover or Pentecost, having stayed there for some time: the following words show this. For it is credible that those who had a home in Jerusalem knew the Jerusalem language: the others did not. Add that under the name come also those who had a home in Mesopotamia, and those of the Romans who were traveling in Judea, below 9. 10. ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς) אנשי יראה A frequent way of speaking among the Hebrews. Thus are called not only those who had subjected themselves to the law, but also pious men who, having abandoned idolatry, had resolved to live more purely: for it appears that such men also came to the temple, 1 Kings VIII. 41. John XII. 20. ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν ὐρανὸν) that is, from the sixteen grandsons of Noah, from whom the other nations were propagated. Grotius enumerates these nations from the sixteen grandsons of Noah in this way from a comparison of Gen. X. verse 9 & following. Verse 6. Γένομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης) Φωνὴ for report, as in Num. XVI. 34. 1 Kings I. 40. & elsewhere. κὰι συνεχύθη) that is, συνεταράχθη, ἐμερίμνα, they were of a troubled and anxious mind: the Hebrew word דגז is accustomed to be rendered by all these terms, & the following words in verse 7, 12 explain this. Verse 7. ὐκ ἰδὺ πάντες ὕτοί εἶσιν οἱ λαλῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι) that is, unlearned men. See John I. 46.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις) Aliis, quam quas didicerant. Quod hic est ἑτέραις, id est, καιναῖς apud Marcum XVI. 17. Noli iis credere, qui miraculum in auribus audientium factum afferunt. Manifeste omnia eis resistunt, quæ sunt 1. Cor. XII. 10. 28. 30. XIV. 2. 4. 5. 6.8.13.14. 18. 19. 22. 23. 26. 27. 38.

In auribus miraculum factum putarunt Cy- prian. Serm. de Spiritu Sancto, Chrysost. Arator, Oecumen. Dionys. Carthuf. Erasmus, Sanctius; Sed in Apostolis miraculum assignatur rectius, qui variis locuti sunt linguis, à Cyrillo, Hieros. Na- zianz. Ambros. in Pf. XIIX. August. Tr. xcui. in Joh. Leone M. Serm. de Pentec. & recentioribus plerisque. Confer. Chamier. Panstrat. T. I. L. XI. c. 14. p. 9. & 10. ἀποφθέγγεσθαι) Solet de Prophetis usurpari hæc vox, re- spondens Hebr. נבא, קסם, הרף & similibus. Vid. inf. 14. Vers. 5. ἦσαν δὲ ἱερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες) Verbum κατοι- κεῖν hic respondet Hebræo כור, quod & κατοικεῖν & παροικεῖν verti solet, interdum & διατρίβειν; itaque dicitur non tantum de iis, qui sedem fixerant, sed & de iis, qui ad Pascha aut ad Pentecosten celebrandā in urbem venerant, ad tempus ali- quod ibi substituti: id ostendunt sequentia. Nam Hierso- lymis qui domicilium habebant, eos credibile & linguam novisse Hierosolymitanam: non item cæteros. Adde, quod sub nomine veniant, & quibus domicilium in Mesopota- mia, & qui Romanorum in Judæa peregrinabantur, inf 9. 10. ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς) אנשי יראה Frequens apud Hebræos loquendi genus. Sic vocantur non hi tantum, qui se legi subjecerant, verum etiam viri pii, qui idololatria deserta purius vivere instituerant: nam tales quoque ad templum venisse apparet, 1. Reg. VIII. 41. Joh. XII. 20. ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν ὐρανὸν) id est, de sexdecim nepotibus Noæ, unde propagatæ gentes cæteræ. Hasc gentes de sexdecim nepotibus Noæ ita è collatione Gen. X. recenset Grotius vers. 9. & seqq. Vers. 6. Γένομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης) Φωνὴ pro fama, ut Num. XVI. 34. 1. Reg. I. 40. & alibi. κὰι συνεχύθη) id est, συνεταράχθη, ἐμερίμνα, animo fuit turbido ac sollicito: omnibus his vocibus reddi solet He- bræum דגז & hoc explicant sequentia versu 7. 12. Vers. 7. ὐκ ἰδὺ πάντες ὕτοί εἶσιν οἱ λαλῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι) id est, homines indocti. Vide Joh. I. 46.

## 2:14
Verse 14. he lifted up his voice) as the pastor not only of the Christian flock, but also of the Apostolic one. Here he begins to fulfill the merit of his name, which was called from the rock.

Nowhere is this dignity attributed to Peter, that he was the pastor of the entire Christian flock, or of the Apostolic assembly. For the Apostles were equal in dignity, and none was the pastor of the others: The other Apostles were certainly what Peter was, endowed with an equal partnership of both honor and power, says Cyprian, Tr. III. on the unity of the Church. Nor can any mere man be the pastor of the entire Christian flock, since one person cannot preside over all: and thus Christ alone is the chief shepherd of the flock, 1 Pet. V. 4. and the head, Col. I. 18. Peter, however, professes himself only a fellow-elder of others, 1 Epist. V. 1. and in the Canon Law itself, C. Paulus. 2. 4. 7. it is read thus: Paul rebuked Peter: which he would not dare, unless he knew himself to be his equal.

κὰ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μυ) ἐνωτίζειν is a Hellenistic word formed to express the Hebrew האזין. You have "give ear to my words" in Job XXXII. 10. Psalm V. 1. and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ἐπῆρε τὴν φωνὴν ἁυτά) ut gregis non Christi­ani tantum, sed & Apostolici pastor. Hic incipit nominis sui à rupe dicti meritum implere.

Nuspiam hoc ἀξίωμα Petro tribuitur, quod vel Christiani gregis universi pastor fuerit, vel cœtus Apostolici. Nam Apostoli dignitate erant pares, nec ullus cæterorum pastor erat: Hoc erant utique & cæteri Apostoli, quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio præditi & honoris & potestatis, ait Cyprian. Tr. III. de simpl. Prælat. Neque ullus ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος to­tius Christiani gregis pastor esse potest, quum præ- esse omnibus unus nequeat: adeoque Christus so- lus ἀρχιποίμην gregis sit 1. Petr. V. 4. ac caput Col. I. 18. Petrus vero se tantum aliorum συμπρεσβύτερον profiteatur 1. Epist. V. 1. & in jure ipso Canonico C. Paulus. 2. 4. 7. ita legatur; Paulus Petrum repre- hendit: quod non auderet, nisi se non parem sciret.

κὰ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μυ) ἐνωτίζειν vox est Helleni- stica confecta ad exprimendum Hebræum האזין ἐνωτίζε­τε τὰ ῥήματά με habes Job. XXXII. 10. Psal. V. 1. & alibi.

## 2:16
Vers. 16. For it is the third hour of the day) that is, the time of morning prayers, to which men, even those only moderately pious, did not go unless fasting; indeed, on feast days, Josephus teaches us in his Life that they fasted until the sixth hour.

but this is that which was spoken by the Prophet Joel) it happens again, what Joel had predicted concerning times closer to his own. Before God exercised His judgments upon the Jews through Nebuchadnezzar, He gifted Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and even some women with prophecy. But just as the judgments which God was about to exercise through the Romans were to be much more atrocious, on account of the dispersion of the nation without hope of restoration, it was fitting that even greater benefits should precede them to convince the hardness of the Jews: that was now happening: therefore Peter warns individuals not to neglect such a benefit, so that while the nation perishes, they themselves might be saved, just as those formerly marked with the ת in Ezekiel.

The Prophetic passage, and Peter's own explanation, is clearly perverted. That Joel is not dealing with times closer to his own, nor with Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, or contemporary women, but with the time of the New Testament, is clear both from the Prophetic text and especially from this interpretation of Peter; but we have spoken of that at Joel II.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ἔστι γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας) id est, tempus pre- cum matutinarum, ad quas homines vel mediocriter pii, non ibant nisi jejuni; imo diebus festis ad sextam usque horam jejunatum docet nos Josephus de vita sua.

ἀλλὰ τῦτό ἐστι τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τῦ Προφήτε Ἰωήλ) iterum evenit, quod Joël de temporibus sibi propioribus prædi- xerat. Antequam Deus judicia sua per Nabuchodonoso- rem exerceret in Judæos, Esaiam, Jeremiam, Ezechielem, fœminas etiam nonnullos donavit prophetia. Sicut vero judicia, quæ per Romanos Deus erat exerciturus, multo futura erant atrociora, ob dissipationem gentis sine spe re- stitutionis, par erat, ut majora etiam beneficia præcede- rent ad convincendam Judæorum duritiem: id nunc eveni- ebat: itaque monet Petrus singulos, ne tantum benefici- um negligant, ut sic gente pereunte ipsi serventur, sicut o- lim illi per ת signati apud Ezechielem.

Locus Propheticus, atque ipsa Petrina expli- catio plane pervertitur. Non te temporibus sibi propioribus Joëlem agere, non de Esaia, Jeremia, Ezechiele aut fœminis συγχρόνοις, sed de tempore N. T.tum è textu Prophetico liquet, tum imprimis ex hac Petri interpretatione; sed de eo diximus ad Joël. II.

## 2:17
in the last days) in the Hebrew it is אחרי־כן, that is, after these things: but we have noted at Genesis 49:1 and elsewhere that the same is accustomed to be signified by באחרית הימים, which is in the last days: the LXX in this place have, it shall be after these things. Luke follows the LXX interpreters in the citation of this place as well as others, though not exactly, with words sometimes changed or transposed, which Moses also did when reciting the Decalogue in Deuteronomy.

Vers. 17. upon all flesh) upon men of diverse lot.

Not only are men of diverse lot noted, but the universal intention of God, by which He wished to bless the whole world with the proclamation of the Gospel, and all flesh with the gifts of the Holy Spirit, in the time of the New Testament, even though most have rendered themselves unworthy of this grace. By the words prophecies, visions, dreams, according to the received manner of Scripture, by which things of the New Testament are accustomed to be described in words suitable to the Old Testament, are understood those gifts of the Holy Spirit which contribute to the understanding of prophecies, visions, and heavenly dreams, because God wishes to make known to all throughout the world the mysteries and things to be believed, which were accustomed to be proposed by prophecies, visions, and dreams, and to omit nothing, as far as is in Him, for the illumination of all: although in the meantime, extraordinary prophetic revelations are not excluded, but are simultaneously included, such as the inspiration which Agabus and the daughters of Philip felt, divine visions outside of sleep, such as that which occurred to Peter and Ananias, and likewise nocturnal visions, such as Paul received, Acts 16:9.

κὶ προφητεύσουσι) they shall feel an inspiration, as the daughters of Philip, Agabus.

ὁράσεις ὄψονται) ὀπτασίας, visions divinely excited, such as that which happened to Peter concerning the unclean animals, and to Ananias below c. IX. 10.

ἐνύπνια ἐνυπνιασθήσονται) they shall receive nocturnal visions from God, as Paul XVI. 9.

Latin:

ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις) in Hebræo est אחרי־כן, id est, post ista:sed idem solere significari per באחרית הימים, quod est ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, notavimus ad Genes. XLIX. 1. & alibi: LXX. hoc loco, ἑται μετὰ ταῦτα. Sequi- tur Lucas in hujus loci ut & aliorum productione LXX. interpretes, non tamen ad amussim, verbis interdum mutatis aut transpositis, quod & Moses fecit Decalogum in Deuteronomio recitans.

Vers. 17. ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα) in diversæ sortis homines.

Non tantum diversæ sortis homines notantur, sed universalis Dei intentio, qua totum mundum præconio Evangelii, omnemq; carnem donis Spi- ritus S. beare volebat tempore N. T. etsi hac gra- tia plurimi se indignos reddiderint. Per verba pro- phetiarum, visionum, somniorum more scripturæ recepto, quo res N. T. verbis V. T. convenienti- bus describi solent, intelliguntur ea Spiritus S. do- na, quæ ad prophetiarum, visionum & somniorum cœlestium intelligentiam faciunt, quod mysteria & res credendas, quæ prophetiis, visionibus, somniis proponi consueverint, Deus omnibus per orbem patefacere velit, nihilque intermittere, quod in se est, ad omnium illuminationem: etsi interim non excludantur, sed simul comprehendantur extra- ordinariæ revelationes propheticœ afflatus, quem sen- sere Agabus, filiæ Philippi, visorum divinorum extra somnum, quale erat, quod Petro obvenit, & Ananiæ, visorum item nocturnorum, quale Paulus accepit, Act. XVI. 9.

κὶ προφητεύσουσι) afflatum sentient, ut Philippi filiæ, Agabus.

ὁράσεις ὄψονται) ὀπτασίας, visa divinitus excitata, quale est, quod Petro obvenit, de animalibus immundis, & Ananiæ infra c. IX. 10.

ἐνύπνια ἐνυπνιασθήσονται) visa nocturna à Deo accipient, ut Paulus XVI. 9.

ἐπιφανῆ) it translates הנורא well, as do the LXX: for it is from ירא, I shall see: it is translated in the same way Jud. XIII. v. 6, I. Paral. XVII. 21, Hab. I. 7, Mal. I. 4, elsewhere μέγας, χαλεπὸς, θαυμάσιος, θαυμαστὸς, φοβερὸς κραταιὸς, ἔνδοξος. Joel said this concerning the day of destruction by Nebuchadnezzar; Peter concerning the day of destruction by the Romans: for all days illustrious by benefits or punishments are called days of the Lord, as Maimonides well noted in the Guide for the Perplexed II. 29.

These corruptions have been spoken of in the Vindications of Joel, so that there is no need to repeat these things. Neither does Joel deal with the day of destruction by Nebuchadnezzar, or other signs, than Peter, nor does Peter deal with the day of destruction by the Romans and its signs, but with the day of the first coming of Christ: as we have shown in the same place.

De his corruptelis dictum est in vindiciis Joelis, ut opus non sit, hæc retractare. Nec Joel de die excidii per Nabuchodonosorem, aut aliis signis, quam Petrus, neque Petrus de die excidii per Romanos ejusque signis agunt, sed de die adventus primi Christi: ut ibidem ostendimus.

Thus also Apollos, Timothy, and other disciples of the Apostles use ὧν for ὧν, and others, and Dionysius of Halicarnassus.

This is to be understood not of rescue from bodily destruction, but from hellish destruction, with the Apostle as interpreter, Rom. X. 13. & by the force of the prophetic context, concerning which likewise in the l. c.

De ereptione non ab exitio corporali, sed infernali hæc intelligenda interprete Apostolo Rom. X. 13. & vi contextus prophetici, de quibus itidem l. c.
