## 2:23
Vers. 23. by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, having taken him as one given up) God had determined that Christ should enter into glory through suffering, Luke XXIV. v. 26. that is, τὸ ὡρισμένον, concerning which we have dealt at Luke XXII. 22. πρόγνωσις here is the same as in 1 Pet. I. 2. for προγινώσκειν in these books often signifies a decree, just as the Latin sciscere, whence scita, Rom. VIII. v. 29. c. XI. 2. 1 Pet. I. 20. In order that this decree might reach its end, God permitted the Jews to do what they wished concerning Christ, when he could most easily have prevented it, Matt. XXVI. 53. 54. ἔκδοτον is the same as what is often elsewhere παραδοθέντα: permitted to them, Matt. XVII. 22. c. XXII. 18. See also Luke XXII. v. 53. ἔκδοτοι are properly those who are given up to enemies. Thus God gave Christ up to enemies.

διὰ χειρῶν ἀνόμων, προσπήξαντες ἀνείλετε) you killed him by crucifying him through the Romans, who are ἄνομοι because they observed no law of God: in the same sense ἁμαρτωλοὶ: Matt. XXVI. 48. Mark XIV. 41. Luke XXIV. v. 7. in an old manuscript it is, διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμου, not badly: ביד רשעים: the Jews are said to have done this through the Romans, because they extorted it from the Romans by importunate demands and threats; he does it, who causes it to be done: προσπήξαντες is said briefly for προσπήξαντες σταυρῷ. Thus προσηλώσας σταυρῷ is said in Coloss. II. 14. Curtius said 'to fasten to the cross': Suetonius 'to fix to the cross'.

These things are rightly [stated] by Grotius. We note only that πρόγνωσις is distinguished from βυλῇ ὡρισμένῃ. The former pertains to the intellect, whose function is to see and foresee; the latter to the will: and therefore there is no reason why we should explain προγινώσκειν and πρόγνωσιν as the decree itself. For the decree was made κατὰ πρόγνωσιν: therefore they are distinct. St. Peter already meets the Calvinist, who uses this to palliate the blasphemy that God is the author of sin, while he refers the counsel of God to the ἔκδοσις, which was done for us in Rom. IV. 24: but he ascribes the act of crucifixion done διὰ χειρῶν ἀνόμων not to God, but to those who applied their wicked hands, which God forbid that we should say of God. And therefore one must distinguish between the crucifixion itself and the direction of the same toward an end salutary to the whole human race. The former is attributed to unjust and wicked men. The latter, however, to the most holy and gracious counsel of God. Wherefore Leo the Great, Sermon XVI. on the Passion of the Lord. Did the iniquity of those persecuting Christ arise from the counsel of God? And did the hand of divine preparation arm that crime, which is greater than any other sin? This is clearly not to be thought of concerning supreme justice: because that which is foreknown in the malice of the Jews, and that which is disposed in the passion of Christ, are very different and very contrary. The will to kill did not proceed from the same source as the will to die: nor did the atrocity of the crime and the endurance of the Redeemer arise from one Spirit. For the Lord did not send the impious hands of the raging into himself, but permitted them, nor by foreknowing what was to be done, did he compel it to be done, although he had taken on flesh for this purpose, that it might be done. Therefore, that the Lord Jesus Christ wished to suffer the fury of those raging, he was in no way the author of their crimes. Nor did he act so that they would wish these things, but he yielded so that they could: and thus he used the blinded insanity of the mob, just as he did the perfidy of the traitor, whom he deigned to recall from the enormity of the crime he had conceived, both by benefits and by words, by taking him as a disciple, by promoting him to be an Apostle, by warning him with signs, by consecrating him with mysteries, so that nothing of benevolence might be lacking for his correction, and nothing of opportunity might remain for his crime.

Latin:

Vers. 23. τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βυλῇ κὲ προγνώσει τῦ Θεῦ ἔκδοτον λαβόντες) Deus constituerat, ut Christus per perpessionem in gloriam intraret, Luc. XXIV. v. 26. hoc est, τὸ ὡρισμένον, de quo egimus ad Luc. XXII. 22. idem est πρόγνωσις hic & I. Pet. I. 2. nam προγινώσκειν in his libris decretum sæpe significat, sicut & Latinum sciscere, unde scita, Rom. VIII. v. 29. c. XI. 2. 1. Pet. I. 20. Ut hoc decretum ad exitum perveniret, permisit Deus, Judæos de Christo agere, quæ vellent, cum id impedire facillime posset, Matt. XXVI. 53. 54. ἔκδοτον idem est, quod alibi sæpe παραδοθέντα: permissum ipsis, Matth. XVII. 22. c. XXII. 18. Vide & Lucæ XXII. v. 53. ἔκδοτοι sunt proprie, qui deduntur hostibus, Sic Deus Christum dedidit hostibus.

διὰ χειρῶν ἀνόμων, προσπήξαντες ἀνείλετε) interfecistis eum crucifigendo per Romanos, qui ὄνομοι quod Dei legem nullam observarent: eodem sensu ἁμαρτωλοὶ: Matth. XXVI. 48. Marc. XIV. 41. Luc. XXIV. v. 7. in manuscripto veteri est, διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμου, non male: ביד רשעים: dicuntur per Romanos hoc fecisse Judæi, quod a Romanis importunis flagitationibus ac minis extorsere; facit, qui facit, ut fiat: προσπήξαντες dictum breviter quo προσπήξαντες σταυρῷ. Sic προσηλώσας σταυρῷ dicitur Coloss. II. 14. Cruci affigere dixit Curtius: Cruci suffigere Suetonius.

Recte hæc à Grotio. Notamus solum, πρόγνωσιν distingui à βυλῇ ὡρισμένῃ. Illa ad intellectum pertinet, cujus est videre ac prævidere; Hæc ad voluntatem : ideoque non est, quod προγνώσκειν & πρόγνωσιν de ipso decreto explicemus. Factum enim decretum est xτ̄ πρόγνωσιν: distincta ergo illa sunt. Calvinianus, hinc blasphemiam de Deo autore peccati palliantibus, jam occurrit S. Petrus, dum consilium Dei ad ἔκδοσιν, quæ pro nobis facta est Rom. IV, 24. refert: actum autem crucifixion dιὰ χειρῶν ἀνόμων factum non Deo, sed illis adscri- bit, qui manus admovere iniquas, quod de Deo absit ut dicamus. Ideoque inter crucifixionem ipsam distinguendum & inter directionem ejusdem ad finem toti humano generi salutarem. Illa ho- minibus injustis & iniquis tribuitur. Hæc vero consilio Dei sanctissimo & gratiosissimo. Quare Leo M. Serm. XVI. de passion. Dom. Numquid iniquitas persequentium Christum ex Dei est orta con- silio? & illud facinus, quod omni majus est crimine, manus divina præparationis armavit? Non hoc pla- ne de summa justitia sentiendum est: quia multum diversum multumque contrarium est id, quod in ma- lignitate Judæorum est præcognitum, & quod in pas- sione Christi est dispositum. Non inde processit vo- luntas interficiendi, unde moriendi: nec de uno ex- titit Spiritu atrocitas sceleris, & tolerantia Redem- toris. Non enim impias furentium manus immi- sit in se Dominus, sed admisit, nec præsciendo quod faciendum esset, coëgit ut fieret, cum tamen ad hoc carnem suscepisset, ut fieret. Quod itaque Dominus Jesus Christus furorem frementium pati voluit, in nullo autor eorum criminum fuit. Nec egit, ut hæc vellent, sed cessit, ut possent: & sic usus est obcæcata plebis insania, quomodo & perfidia traditoris, quem ab immanitate concepti sceleris, & beneficiis revo- care dignatus & verbis, assumendo in discipulum, provehendo in Apostolum, monendo signis, consecran- do mysteriis, ut cui nihil benevolentiæ deesset ad cor- rectionem, nihil occasionis superesset ad crimen.

## 2:24
Vers. 24. λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου) חבלי מות, ὠδῖνες θανάτου. To the Greek interpreters, it is not death, or the state after death, but most grievous pains, such as are wont to be those of women dying in childbirth. It appears in 2 Sam. XXII. v. 6. Psal. XVII. 1. 5. CXVI. 3. From these pains God freed Christ, by raising him to a life subject to no pains. λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου, says Barnabas.

Others understand τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου as the painful death itself, so that ὠδῖνες θανάτου are spoken of for ὠδῖνας ἐν θανάτῳ ὠδινηρῷ, such as Andradius, Hoffmeisterus, Lorinus, Sanctius, Cornelius à Lap. B. Granerus on art. III. A. C. p. 747. B. Feuerborn. Synt. 1. Disp. 16. Conf. B. Glassius, Gramat. S. p. 34. Some, by a Hebraism, explain ὠδῖνας as cords, because חבלים denotes both cords and pains, since the word λύσας is more suitable to bonds than to pains, such as Piscator, Constant. L'Empereur on the Itinerary of Kimchi p. 100, Bened. Arias M. and Jac. Tirinus: whom the Ethiopian favors, rendering it bonds of death, and the Syrian, using that word which denotes both pains and cords. Some understand it of pains after death, or of hell, not which Christ sustained, but which are otherwise wont to follow: to which pertains that of Augustine, Epist. XCIX. to Evodius. Christ loosed the pains of hell, not by which he was held, but so that he might not be held: not by loosing the pains of hell, by which he himself could not be held, but by which others were held, whom he himself knew were to be liberated. This explanation is served by the reading of some Codices, in which ὠδῖνας ᾅδου is found. If anyone wishes to explain ὠδῖνας not of those things which happen before death, nor of those which happen after death, but prefers to understand the liberation from the straits of death itself and their solution, they will be called ὠδῖνας by this name not because of pains, such as are wont to be in childbirth, but because of another similarity which intervenes here with the childbirth of a woman: just as Chrysostom, Theophylact, and Oecumenius.

they teach that the simile is taken from a pregnant woman, who is burdened by the weight of the fetus: and that it is hinted that death had employed every force and bond as if they were machines, in order to detain Christ; but that God, by loosening those bonds, had caused death to be compelled to release Christ, whom it was striving to compress and extinguish while he was enclosed in the sepulcher as if in its own womb, and to bring him forth into the light as if by a new birth. To this contributes the fact that some think Psalm 116:3 is being referred to, where we find מצרי שׁאול, LXX κίνδυνοι ᾅδε, the Chaldean 'distress of hell', and Pagninus renders it 'straits of hell'. The opinion of those who wish Psalm 18:6 to be referred to also finds favor: because חבלי שׁאול is rendered ὠδῖνες ᾅδε; since Christ was held as if constricted by the ropes or bonds of death, which God loosened by raising him from the dead.

The objection to Grotius's explanation concerning the pains endured before death, from which Christ was freed by his resuscitation to a life not subject to any pains, is that those pains were not finally loosened at the resuscitation, but at the very moment of death, or the release of the soul from the body, since he did not endure any pains after death, as Flacius, along with Thomas and Cajetan, maintains, but all pain and punishment had its end in his death, as Cornel. à Lap. admits in this place. Compare Matthew 26:30, Luke 18:30, chapter 23:42, John 19:30, Philippians 2:8, Hebrews 9:26. Nevertheless, the Grotian explanation is rightly opposed to the opinion of the Papists, who dream here of a limbo of the Fathers or a purgatory, from which souls were freed by Christ: for it is said in this place that God loosened the ὠδῖνας of Christ, not of others, as Grotius admits.

καθότι ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ ἀυτῆ) The Arabic reads ὑπ’ ἀυτῶν, namely τῶν ὠδίνων. ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν, that is, it was not right, it was not equitable, in the way δύναται is taken in Matthew 9:15 and elsewhere; it was not equitable that an innocent man should long be subject to the malice of another.

There is no reason why the literal meaning should be abandoned here. Peter does not say it was not equitable, but ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν, it was not possible; and that most truly; because it was impossible for Christ to be held and overcome by death, both because of the personal union, since his body, assumed into the hypostasis of the Word, was a sharer in his life-giving power; and although he had taken our sin upon himself, that had nevertheless already been expiated by death: whence he could not remain subject to death, which is the wages of sin, or be completely overcome by death: and also because of the condition of Christ's death: because he had undergone death by his own authority and freely, and he remained in death as long as he wished, and therefore he could not be held by death against his will; furthermore, he had to conquer death by his own death, and he had completely conquered it, Hosea 13:14, Hebrews 2:14. Therefore, the victor and triumpher over death could not be overcome by death; then because of the redemption of the human race, because he could not have redeemed the human race from death if he himself had been completely overcome by death, 1 Corinthians 15:13; and finally because of the certainty of divine predictions, because his resurrection from the dead had been predicted both by the Prophets in the Old Testament and by Christ himself, which predictions could not fail to be fulfilled.

Latin:

Vers. 24. λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου) חבלי מות, ὠδῖνες θανάτου. Græcis interpretibus, non est mors, aut sta- tus post mortem, sed gravissimi dolores, quales solent esse mulierum in partu morientium. Apparet 2. Sam. XXII. v. 6. Psal. XVII. 1. 5. CXVI. 3. Ab his doloribus Deus Christum liberavit, resuscitando eum ad vitam nullis dolo- ribus obnoxiam. λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου, ait Barnabas.

Alii τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου intelligunt de ipsa morte dolorosa, ut ὠδῖνες θανάτου dicantur, pro ὠδῖνας ἐν θανάτῳ ὠδινηρῷ, utpote Andradius, Hoffmeisterus, Lorinus, Sanctius, Cornelius à Lap. B. Granerus ad art. III. A. C. p. 747. B. Feuerborn. Synt. 1. Disp. 16. Conf. B. Glassii Gramat. S. p. 34. Nonnulli per Ebraismum ὠδῖνας exponunt funes, quia חבלים & funes, & dolores notat, quum vox λύσας magis vinculis conveniat, quam doloribus, utpote Piscat. Constant. L' Empereur ad ὁδοιπορ. Kimchii p. 100. Bened. Ariasm. & Jac. Tirinus : quibus favet Æ- thiops, reddens vincula mortis, & Syrus eam adhi- bens vocem, quæ & dolores & funes notat. Non- nulli de doloribus post mortem, vel inferni, non quos sustinuerit Christus, sed qui alias sequi solent, in- telligunt: Quo facit illud Augustini Epist. XCIX. ad Evod. Solvit Christus dolores inferni, non quibus tenebatur, sed ne teneretur: non solutis doloribus in- ferni, quibus teneri ipse non poterat, sed quibus tene- bantur alii, quos ipse noverat liberandos. Cui expli- cationi inservit lectio Codic. nonnullorum, in quibus habetur ὠδῖνας ᾅδου. Si non de iis, quæ an- te mortem, neq; de iis, quæ post mortem eveniunt, explicare quis velit ὠδῖνας, sed liberationem ab an- gustiis ipsius mortis earumq; solutionem intelligere malit, ὠδῖνας dicentur hoc nomine non ob dolores, quales in partu esse solent, sed ob aliam, quæ hic cum partu mulieris intercedit, similitudinem: Quemadmodum Chrysost. Theophyl. & Oecumen.

docent, similitudinem petitam esse à muliere gravida, quæ fœtus pondere oneratur: idq; innui, mortem omnem quasi vim ac vincula tanquam machinas adhibuisse, ut Christum detineret; Deum vero vinculis illis solutis effecisse, ut mors Christum, quẽ in sepulchro, tanquam utero suo, conclusum comprimere atq; extinguere nitebatur, redivivũ emittere, & quasi novo partu in lucem edere cogeretur Quo facit, quod nonnulli censeant, respici Psalm. CXVI. 3. ubi habentur מצרי שׁאול LXX. κίνδυνοι ᾅδε, Chald. molestia inferni, Pagninus angustiæ inferni reddunt. Favet etiam eorum sententia, qui Psal. XCIX. 6. respici volunt: quia חבלי שׁאול funes sepulchri redduntur ὠδῖνες ᾅδε; siquidem Christus funibus seu vinculis à morte quasi constrictus tenebatur, quos Deus solvit resuscitans eum à morte.

Explicationi Grotii de doloribus ante mortem exantlatis, à quibus liberatus fuerit Christus resuscitatione ad vitam nullis doloribus obnoxiam, id obstat, quod non in resuscitatione demum dolores illi soluti sint, sed in ipsa morte, vel solatione animæ à corpore, siquidem non sustinuerit dolores ullos post mortem, quemadmodum cum Thoma & Cajetano Flacius statuit, sed dolor & pœna omnis in morte ejus finem habuerit, fatente Cornel. à Lap. in h. l. Conf. Matth. XXVI. 30. Luc. XVIII. 30. cap. XXIII. 42. Joh. XIX. 30. Phil. II. 8. Ebr. IX. 26. Papistarum tamen opinioni merito opponitur Grotiana explicatio, qui somniant hic limbum Patrum vel purgatorium, è quo animæ liberatæ sint à Christo: nam ὠδῖνας Christi, non aliorum, solvisse Deus hoc loco dicitur, fatente Grotio.

καθότι ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ ἀυτῆ) Arabs legit ὑπ’ ἀυτῶν nempe τῶν ὠδίνων. ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν, id est, non erat par, non erat æquum, quomodo δύναται sumitur Matth. IX. 15. & alibi; non erat æquum, ut vir innocens diu subjaceret alienæ malitiæ.

Cur literæ proprietas hic deseratur, causa nulla est. Non dicit Petrus, haud æquum fuisse, sed ὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν non erat possibile; idq; verissime; quia impossibile fuit, Christum teneri & superari à morte, tum ob unionem personalem, quia corpus ejus in hypostasin Verbi vitæ assumtum, vivificæ ejus virtutis consors erat; etsi vero peccatum nostrum in se receperat, id tamen morte jam expiatum fuit: unde morti, quæ stipendium peccati est, obnoxium manere non poterat, aut superari penitus à morte: tum ob mortis Christi conditionem: quia mortem ἀυτεξυσίως & libere subierat, & quamdiu volebat, in morte manebat, ideoq; præter voluntatem à morte teneri non poterat, adhæc morte sua mortem vincere debebat, & omnino vicerat, Os. XIII. 14. Ebr. II. 14. Non ergo à morte superari poterat mortis victor & triumphator; tum ob generis humani redemtionem, quia non potuisset genus humanum redimere à morte, si ipse à morte devictus omnino fuisset, 1. Cor. XV. 13. tum deniq; ob prædictionum divinarum certitudinem, quia resurrectio ejus à morte & à Prophetis in V. Test. & ab ipso Christo prædicta erat, quæ prædictiones non poterant non impleri.

## 2:25
Vers. 25. Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς ἀυτὸν) concerning him. He says this rightly, because the Jews were persuaded that the affairs of David were types of the King Messiah. The things that follow have their meaning in David, but more figuratively. However, God willed that the same things be fulfilled in the Messiah more κατὰ πόδας (step by step), so that the people, who are captious about words, could not complain of anything.

ἐκ δεξιῶν μέ ἐςιν) it helps me as a παραςάτης (advocate/supporter). ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ) so that I may not be cast down from the promised kingdom.

Latin:

Vers. 25. Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς ἀυτὸν) de ipso. Recte hoc dicit, quia Judæis persuasum erat, res Davidis esse typos Regis Messiæ. Habent, quæ sequuntur sensum suum in Davide, sed magis figuratum. Voluit autem Deus in Messia eadem impleri magis κατὰ πόδας, ne quid causari posset populus vocularum auceps.

ἐκ δεξιῶν μέ ἐςιν) id opitulatur mihi tanquam παραςάτης. ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ) ne dejiciar de regni promisso.

## 2:26
Vers. 26. ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μέ) The LXX placed it thus, because in their codices there was לשׁוני instead of כבודי: such were the many variations in ancient books.

ἔτι δὲ ἡ σάρξ μέ κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι) David said this while seeking hiding places from hiding places in fear of Saul: Christ before the cross and on the cross.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μέ) LXX. sic posuere, quia in eorum codicibus fuit לשׁוני pro כבודי: quales in libris veteribus varietates multæ fuere.

ἔτι δὲ ἡ σάρξ μέ κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι) Hoc dixit David Saulis metu latebras ex latebris quærens: Christus ante crucem & in cruce.

## 2:27
Vers. 27. ὅτι ὐκ’ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μέ εἰς ᾅδη) Concerning

David the meaning is, you will not allow me to be killed by Saul, 1 Samuel 22:1. Concerning Christ, you will not leave me long under the kingdom of death. ψυχὴν μ8, that is, me: a frequent Hebraism.

ἐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σε ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν) δώσεις means you will permit. The Hebrew is translated by ἀφιέναι: as in Gen. XX. 6. Exod. XII. 23 & sometimes by ἰδεῖν, and often also by ἀιδεῖν as in Gen. XXXI. v. 7. & here below 27. τὸν ὅσιόν σε חסידך, that is, your pious servant: ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν is a metaphor from an animate to an inanimate thing, that is, to be lost, to perish. The sense is the same as in the former member. For it is an exegesis.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ὅτι ὐκ’ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μέ εἰς ᾅδη) De

Davide sensus, non patieris me interfici à Saule, 1. Sam. XXII. 1. De Christo, non relinques me diu sub regno mor- tis. ψυχὴν μ8, id est, me: frequens Hebraismus.

ἐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σε ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν) δώσεις permittes. Hebræum vertitur per ἀφιέναι: ut Gen. XX. 6. Exod. XII. 23 & per ἰδεῖν interdum, sæpe & per ἀιδεῖν ut Gen. XXXI. v. 7. & hic infra 27. τὸν ὅσιόν σε חסידך, ist est, servum tu- um pium: ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν est μεταφορὰ ab animato ad exa- nime, id est, perdi, interire. Sensus idem, qui in priore membro. Est enim ἐξήγησις.

## 2:28
Vers. 28. ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδὲς ζωῆς) concerning David: you will deliver me from these evils, which are compared to death: concerning Christ you will deliver me from death.

πληρώσεις με ἐυφροσύνης μετὰ τῶ προσώπε σε) concerning David understand it in the Temple: concerning Christ in Heaven.

Grotius invents a double sense of David's words, a literal one concerning David; a mystical one concerning Christ: therefore he attaches such disparate meanings to most of the words, which nevertheless can have only one sense in the same place, and are explained here only concerning Christ: that this explanation of St. Peter agrees with the mind and intention of the Holy Spirit in the book of Psalms there is no doubt. But because we have already defended these things in the annotations to the Psalm, we do not wish to do what has already been done.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδὲς ζωῆς) de Davide: eximes me his malis, quæ morti comparantur: de Christo eximes me morti.

πληρώσεις με ἐυφροσύνης μετὰ τῶ προσώπε σε) de Davide intellige in Templo: de Christo in Cœlo.

Geminum verborum Davidis sensum fingit Grotius, literalem de Davide; mysticum de Chri- sto: ideo tam disparatas significationes vocibus plerisque affingit, quæ tamen non nisi unum sen- sum in eodem loco habere possunt, nec nisi de Christo hic explicantur: quam S. Petri explicatio- nem menti & intentioni Spiritus S. in libro Psal- morum convenire nullum dubium est. Sed quia hæc jam vindicavimus in annotatis ad Psalmum, nolumus actum agere.

## 2:29
Vers. 29. ὅτι καὶ ἐτελέυτησε καὶ ἐτάφη, καὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἀυτῦ ἐςὶν ἐν ἡμῖν) that is, in this city, which was granted to David alone: he does not deny that those words can in any way be understood concerning David, but neither so magnificently, nor so strictly according to the letter, as concerning Jesus: whence it follows that the Messiah was prefigured in David. David remains in the tomb: Jesus does not remain.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ὅτι καὶ ἐτελέυτησε καὶ ἐτάφη, καὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἀυτῦ ἐςὶν ἐν ἡμῖν) id est, in hac urbe, quod soli Davidi concessum: non negat verba illa de Davide ullo modo posse intelligi, sed neque tam magnifice, neque tam κατὰ κυριολεγίαν, quam de Jesu: unde sequitur, cum esse Messiam in Davide præ- figuratum. David in sepulchro manet: Jesus non manet.

## 2:30
Vers. 30. ἐκ καρπᾶ τῆς ὀσφύος ἀυτῶ) the words are from Ps. CXXXII. 11. where in the Greek it is ἐκ καρπᾶ τῆς κοιλίας σε, from the fruit of your wife's womb. The sense comes to the same thing.

τὸ κατὰ σάρκα) Peter added this because he held it for certain that Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit.

To that τὸ κατὰ σάρκα does not correspond, as regards the member tacitly indicated, the conception by the Holy Spirit, but τὸ κατὰ πνεῦμα: because by flesh is understood the human nature of Christ, according to which he is from the loins of David, by the Spirit truly the divine nature, 1. Tim. III. 16. 1. Petr. III. 18. Rom. I. 4. c. IX. 6.

καθίσαι ἐπὶ τῶ θρόνε ἀυτῶ) David's kingdom was over the people of God: so also is Christ's. Nor does it matter that in Christ's kingdom there are many from the Gentiles: for in these was fulfilled what was adumbrated in Israel.

τὸν Χρισὸν) sent for this purpose, that he might be the King of the people of God.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ἐκ καρπᾶ τῆς ὀσφύος ἀυτῶ) verba sunt ex Ps. CXXXII. 11. ubi in Græco ἐκ καρπᾶ τῆς κοιλίας σε, ex par- tu uxoris tuæ. Sensus eodem recidit.

τὸ κατὰ σάρκα) Hoc ideo addidit Petrus, quia Christum pro certo habebat conceptum ex Spiritu S.

Illi τὸ κατὰ σάρκα non respondet, quoad mem- brum tacite indicatum, conceptio à Spiritu S. sed τὸ κατὰ πνεῦμα: quia per carnem intelligitur huma- na Christi natura, secundum quam è lumbis Da- vidis est, per Spiritum vere divina natura, 1. Tim. III. 16. 1. Petr. III. 18. Rom. I. 4. c. IX. 6.

καθίσαι ἐπὶ τῶ θρόνε ἀυτῶ) Davidis regnum fuit super po- pulum Dei: sic & Christi. Nec refert, quod in Christi re- gno plures sint è gentibus: nam in his impletum est, quod in Israele erat adumbratum.

τὸν Χρισὸν) in hoc missum, ut Rex esset populi Dei.

## 2:32
Vers. 32. ὦ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμὲν μάρτυρες) not from hearsay, but from those things which we perceive by sight, hearing, and touch. We all equally testify to this, gaining nothing from it except hatreds, blows, prisons, deaths: wherefore there is no reason why you should disparage our testimony.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ὦ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμὲν μάρτυρες) non ex fama, sed ex iis, quæ visu, auditu, tactu percipimus. Hoc testamur omnes pariter, nihil inde lucratari, nisi odia, verbera, car- ceres, mortes: quare nulla est causa, cur nostro testimonio derogetis.

## 2:33
Vers. 33. ὑψωθεὶς) raised up into the heavenly palace, John the Evangelist XX. 17.

τὴν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τῶ ἁγίε πνέυματος λαβὼν) that is, having obtained from the Father the right of sending the Holy Spirit, which the Father had promised to him. See John the Evangelist XIV. 26. XV. 26. XVI. 13. 14. 15.

τῦτο ὃ νῦν ὑμεῖς βλέπετε) i. e. you hear. The Hebrews express every sense, both internal and external, with the word for seeing. The subject here is the sudden use of tongues.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ὑψωθεὶς) in cœlestem regiam sublatus, Joh. Evang. XX. 17.

τὴν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τῶ ἁγίε πνέυματος λαβὼν) id est, im- petrato à Patre jure mittendi Spiritum S. quod Pater ei pro- miserat. Vide Joh. Evang. XIV. 26. XV. 26. XVI. 13. 14. 15.

τῦτο ὃ νῦν ὑμεῖς βλέπετε) i. e. auditis. Hebræi omnem sensum, & internum & externum, videndi vocabulo expri- munt. Agitur hic de subito linguarum usu.

## 2:34
Vers. 34. ὀυ γὰρ Δαβὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τὸς ὀυρανὲς) David descended into the sepulcher, 1 Kings II. 10, but he was not carried up into heaven like Elijah: wherefore the words of Psalm CX cannot apply to him. Concerning those words of the Psalm, see what we have said both regarding the Psalm itself and regarding Matt. XXII. 44.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ὀυ γὰρ Δαβὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τὸς ὀυρανὲς) David in se- pulchrum descendit, 1. Reg. II. 10. non autem evectus est in cœlum ut Elias: quare verba Psal. CX. in ipsum congrua- ere non possunt. De eis Psalmis verbis vide, quæ diximus tam ad ipsum Psalmum, quam ad Matth. XXII. 44.

## 2:36
Vers. 36. ἀσφαλῶς ὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ) ידע תדע. Let him know for certain.

ὅτι Κύριον καὶ Χρισὸν ἀυτὸν ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησε) Lord of all things, more than Adam had been: Christ, that is, king of the people of God.

Latin:

Vers. 36. ἀσφαλῶς ὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ) ידע תדע. Certo norit.

ὅτι Κύριον καὶ Χρισὸν ἀυτὸν ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησε) Dominum re- rum omnium, magis quam Adamus fuerat: Christum, id est, regem populi Dei.

## 2:37
Vers. 37. κατενύγησαν τῇ καρδίᾳ) Thus is translated ויתעצבו Gen. XXXIV. 7. to feel pain.

τὶ ποιήσομεν) they ask whether any hope remains, and what it is.

Latin:

Vers. 37. κατενύγησαν τῇ καρδίᾳ) Sic vertitur ויתעצבו Gen. XXXIV. 7. dolorem sentire.

τὶ ποιήσομεν) quærunt, an aliqua spes restet, & quæ.

## 2:38
Vers. 38. μετανοήσατε) שובו amend yourselves.

καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαςος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησῦ Χριςᾶ εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν) it is not enough to believe in Christ, but it is necessary also to profess Christianity, Rom. I. 10, which Christ willed to be done through baptism: whoever performs these things, let him be certain of the remission of sins. Thus a certain Egyptian said to Constantine: that the doctrine of the Christians has the promise of being destructive of every sin, that the impious who partake of it are immediately set outside of every sin: says Zosimus. ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν סלח.

Baptism is not only a symbol of profession, but also a means of regeneration and remission of sins; and Peter indicates this here, when he wishes baptism to be received not into a profession of Christianity, but into the remission of sins. Compare Acts XXII. 16. John III. 5. Titus III. 6. Zech. XIII. 1. Which passage Grotius himself connects here at v. 39, noting these things: ὑμῖν γὰρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν Zech. XIII. 1. but in the name of Christ is by the authority, mandate, and institution of Christ, i.e., as he himself instituted in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, as Eulogius explained in Photius in the Bibliotheca, last chapter. Theophylact on this passage, which I would wish to be observed against Socinus.

and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit) through the laying on of Apostolic hands, below XIX. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 38. μετανοήσατε) שובו emendamini.

καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαςος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησῦ Χριςᾶ εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν) non satis est Christo credere, sed opor- tet & Christianismum profiteri, Rom. I. 10. quod Christus per baptismum fieri voluit: qui hæc præstat, certus sit de re- missione peccatorum. Sic Constantino dixit Ægyptius qui- dam: πάσης ἁμαρτάδος ἀναιρετικὴν εἶναι τὴν τῶν χριςιανῶν δόξαν τοῦτο ἔχειν ἐπάγγελμα, τὸ τὼς ἀσεβεῖς μεταλαμβάνοντας ἀυτῆς πάσης, ἁμαρτίας ἐξω παραχρῆμα καθίςασθαι: ait Zosi- mus. ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν סלח.

Baptismus non est tantum symbolum professio- nis, sed etiam medium regenerationis & remissionis peccatorum; idque Petrus hic indicat, cum suscipi baptismum vult non in professionem Christianismi, sed in remissionem peccatorum. Conf. Act. XXII. 16. Joh. III. 5. Tit. III. 6. Zach. XIII. 1. Quem locum hic consert ipse Grotius ad v. 39. hæc annotans: ὑμῖν γὰρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν nem- pe remissionis peccatorum: apparet id Jer. XXXI. 34. Zach. XIII. 1. in nomine autem Christi est autori- tate, mandato & institutione Christi, h. e. uti ipse instituit in nomine Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. ut ex- posuit Eulogius apud Photium in Biblioth. cap. ult. Theoph. in h. l. quod contra Socin. observari velim.

καὶ λήψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος) per imposi- tionem manuum Apostolicarum, infra XIX. 6.

## 2:39
V. 39. for to you is the promise and to your children) namely of the remission of sins: it appears from Jer. XXXI. 34. Zech. XIII. 1.

and to all who are far off) They had already learned from Christ that through him the remission of sins was given even to the Gentiles, Matt. XXVIII. 19. above 18. but by what laws the Gentiles were to obtain it, that they did not yet know.

as many as the Lord our God shall call) that is, whoever, having been called, shall obey. For often in words signifying a benefit, the acceptance of the benefit is tacitly implied. Thus the name of the called is taken, 1 Cor. 1. 24. and Jude 1. thus to be revealed is taken Isa. LIII. 1. Thus God is said to give repentance, 2 Tim. II. 25. to give bread from heaven, 32. to give a heart Deut. XXIX. 4. and many things are placed elsewhere with a similar sense.

Latin:

V. 39. ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν) nempe remissionis peccatorũ: aparet id Jer. XXXI. 34. Zach. XIII. 1.

καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς εἰς μακρὰν) Jam didicerant à Christo, per eum remissionem peccatorum etiam gentibus dari, Matth. XXVIII. 19. supra 18. sed quibus legibus eam adepturæ essent gentes, id necdum sciebant.

ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν) id est, quicun- que vocati paruerint. Nam sæpe in vocibus beneficium si- gnificantibus tacite subintelligitur beneficii acceptio. Sic nomen vocatorum sumitur, 1. Cor. 1. 24. & Judæ 1. sic re- velari sumitur Esa. LIII. 1. Sic Deus dare pœnitentiam di- citur, 2. Tim. II. 25. dare panem de cælo, 32. dare cor Deut. XXIX. 4. multaque sunt alibi pari sensu posita.

## 2:40
Vers. 40. be saved from this generation) that is, abandon the customs of this wicked nation. A crooked generation is spoken of from Deut. XXXII. 20. It corresponds to the Hebrew נלו.

Not only the abandonment of customs, but the salvation and liberation of souls, so that they do not perish with the wicked nation, is noted. Compare V. 45.

Latin:

Vers. 40. σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης) id est, deserito hujus improbæ gentis mores. Γενεὰ σκολιὰ dicitur ex Deuter. XXXII. 20. Respondet Hebræo נלו.

Non tantum morum desertio, sed animarum salus & liberatio, ne cum improba gente pereant, notatur. Conf. V. 45.

## 2:41
Vers. 41. they were added) Namely to the disciples of Jesus Christ: to that assembly of 120 men

PART III. Description of the first communion of the Apostolic Church.

Latin:

Vers. 41. προσετέθησαν) Nempe discipulis Jesu Christi: cœtui illi CXX. hominum

PARS III. Descriptio primæ communionis Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ.

## 2:42
Vers. 42. continuing steadfastly in the teaching of the Apostles) See above c. I. 14. below 46. c. VI 4. c. VIII, 23. c. X. 7. Rom. XII. 12. c. XIII. 8. Coloss. IV, 2. The Hebrews would say שוקדין.

and in the fellowship) Since he only begins to deal with the communion of goods below, the word fellowship seems here to be correctly understood as conversation, in which way to have fellowship is taken, Gal. VI. 6.

That the word κοινωνία, when placed absolutely, is to be understood as conversation, will not easily be taught by any example. Gal. VI. 6. does not denote conversation, but communication, which proceeds from beneficence; which the explanation of Grotius himself teaches concerning the Apostolic passage. Others, therefore, accept this passage as concerning the communication of goods, even though afterwards, for the sake of explanation, in v. 44, there is added καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά. Just as also in v. 46 mention is made again of τῆς ἀρτοκλασίας: where most people here understand by τὴν κοινωνίαν the Holy Eucharist from 1 Cor. X. 16, to whom also Cardinal Cajetan is added.

and in the breaking of bread) frugal banquets, which were concluded by the taking of the Eucharist: wherefore the Syrian made mention of the Eucharist here. See what we have said on Matthew XXVI. 21. κλᾶν ἄρτον פרס לחם, Jer. XVI. 6. The loaves of the Hebrews were such as could be easily broken by hand: hence fragments, μερίδες, בצעוער to the Hebrews.

This explanation can be opposed to the Papists, to whom Grotius otherwise willingly gives way. For they understand the Eucharist by the breaking of bread in this place, and from thence establish their ποτηριοκλεψίαν. But if the Eucharist were designated in this way at all, the trope of synecdoche would be in plain sight, since the Papists themselves are forced to admit that the Eucharist cannot be celebrated without wine, even though they do not offer wine to the laity. But Grotius does not wish the Eucharist to be denoted here, but frugal banquets: just as in v. 46 it is said they were breaking, that is, they were distributing and sharing bread house by house. For as Grotius has it at v. 45, and the men and women were eating from the public store and were having a common table from the public store τῇ Φρατρίας, &c.

and in the prayers) above c. I. 14. Tertullian in his Apologetic: We come together to God, that we may besiege Him with prayers as if with a formed troop: This force is pleasing to God. Chrysostom II. sermon on why the Old Testament is made obscure: for since we are weak when we are gathered by ourselves, as I have appeared to them, let us beseech God by the gathering of love to give us our requests.

Latin:

Vers. 42. προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν Ἀποστόλων) Vide supra c. I. 14. infra 46. c. VI 4. c. VIII, 23. c. X. 7. Rom. XII. 12. c. XIII. 8. Coloss. IV, 2. Hebræi dicerent שוקדין.

καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ) Cum de communione bonorum infra demum agere incipiat, videtur hic vox κοινωνίας recte in- telligi pro colloquio, quo modo κοινωνεῖν sumitur, Gal. VI. 6.

Vocem κοινωνίας absolute positam de colloquio accipi, non facile exemplo quodam docebitur. Gal. VI. 6. non colloquium notat, sed communicatio- nem, quæ ex beneficentia proficiscitur; quod ipsius Grotii explicatio docet circa locum Apostolicum. Alii ergo de communicatione bonorum hunc locum accipiunt, etsi postea ἐξηγήσεως causa v. 44. adda- tur καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά. Sicuti etiam v. 46. de- nuo τῆς ἀρτοκλασίας mentio fit: ubi pleriq; per τὴν κοινωνίαν hic intelligunt S. Eucharistiã è 1. Cor. X. 16. quibus accedit etiam Cajetanus Cardinalis.

καὶ τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου) frugalibus conviviis, quæ Euchari- stiæ sumtione claudebantur: quare Eucharistiæ mentionem hic fecit Syrus. Vide, quæ diximus ad Matthæum XXVI. 21. κλᾶν ἄρτον פרס לחם, Ier. XVI. 6. Hebræorum panes tales erant, qui manu facile frangerentur: inde fragmen- ta, μερίδες, בצעוער Hebræis.

Pontificiis hæc opponi potest explicatio, qui- bus alias libenter velificatur Grotius. Illi enim Eu- charistiam per fractionem panis hoc loco intelli- gunt, atque inde ποτηριοκλεψίαν suam stabiliunt. Sed si omnino Eucharistia ita designaretur, in apri- co esset tropus synecdoches, quum Papistæ ipsi fa- teri cogantur, sine vino non posse celebrari Eucharisti- am, utut vinum laicis non præbeant. At Grotius non Eucharistiam, sed frugalia convivia hic deno- tari vult: quemadmodum v. 46. dicitur frangebant, id est, distribuebant ac communicabant panem do- matim. Nam ut habet ad v. 45. Grotius, & vesce- bantur viri fœminaque de publico & mensam de pu- blico habebant communem τῇ Φρατρίας, &c.

καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς) supra c. I. 14. Tertullianus Apologe- tico: Coimus ad Deum, quasi manu facta precationibus am- biamus: Hæc vis Deo grata est. Chrysost. II. serm. cur obscu- rum fit Vetus Testamentum: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ καθ᾽ ἑαυτοὺς ὀγχόμενοι, καθὼς ὤφθην αὐτοῖς, ἀσθενεῖς ἐσμὲν, ἀπὸ τῆς συνδρομῆς τῆς ἀγάπης δυσωπῶμεν τὸν Θεὸν δοῦναι ἡμῖν τὰ αἰτήματα.

## 2:43
V. 43. And fear came upon every soul.) All were held by a great reverence for the Apostles, because of the power of their speech and the accompanying miracles. See below c. V. 5. 11. ψυχὴ for a man is used also by others and by Epiphanius.

and many wonders and signs) you have these two also in the Greek of Esther X. 10. and below V. 30.

Latin:

V. 43. ἐγένετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος.) Reverentia magna Apostolorum omnes tenebantur, propter sermonis vim & accedentia signa. Vide inf. c. V. 5. 11. ψυχὴ pro homine & alii usurpant & Epiphanius.

πολλά τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα) habes hæc duo & in Græco Estheris X. 10. & infra V. 30.

## 2:44
V. 44. and they had all things common) namely, just as the Essenes, of whom a good part of the Christians consisted: whose institutions Christ had never censured. I speak of those Essenes who had wives and children. Philo: in one treasury for all, and expenses, and common clothes, and common food, having made common meals. The same Philo in the book on rewards and punishments says of them: to bring their own goods into the middle for common participation and enjoyment. Josephus and Zachuth report the same thing about them. Theophrastus about the same: their social nature is wonderful, and it is not possible to find any possession among them that is superior. For by law to those entering into the sect, their property is public to the order, so that in all things neither the lowliness of poverty appears, nor the excess of wealth. Similar is the life of the Pythagoreans, many of whose institutions were from the Essenes, or their authors. Iamblichus about them: in general no one possessed anything: Gellius I. 9 calls this a κοινόβιον. & explaining he says: that what each one had of family and money, that he had given into the middle, and a society was formed that was inseparable.

Latin:

V. 44. κ᾿ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινὰ) nempe quomodo Esseni, de quibus erat bona pars Christianorum: quorumq; instituta Christus nunquam reprehenderat. De illis loquor Essenis, qui conjuges ac liberos habebant. Philo: ἑνὶ ταμιείῳ ἐν πάντων κὴ δαπάναι, κὴ κοιναὶ μὲν ἐσθῆτες, κοιναὶ δὲ τροφαὶ, συσσίτια πεποιημένων. Hos idem Philo in libro de præmiis & pœnis dicit: τὰ ἴδια προφέρειν εἰς μέσον ἀγαθὰ εἰς κοινὴν μετουσίαν κὴ ἀπόλαυσιν. Idem de eis tradunt Joseph. & Zachuth. Theophrastus de iisdem: θαυμάσιον κὴ αὐτοῖς τὸ κοινωνικὸν, κδ᾽ ἔσιν εὑρεῖν κτῆσιν τινὰ παῤ αὐτοῖς ὑπερέχουσα.νόμῳ γὰρ τοῖς εἰς τὴν αἵρεσιν εἰσιοῦσας, δαμόσιαι τῷ τάγματι τὴν οὐσίας, ὥστε ἐν ἅπασι μήτε πενίας ταπεινότητα φαίνεσθ᾽, μηδ᾽ ὑπεροχὴν πλούτου. Par vita Pythagoristarum, quorum multa instituta ab Essenis, aut eorum auctoribus. Jamblichus de iis: ὅλως οὐδεὶς οὐδὲν ἐκέκτητο: id κοινόβιον vocat Gellius I. 9. & explicans ait: quod quisque familiæ pecuniæque habebat, id dedisse in medium, & coitam societatem inseparabilem.

## 2:45
Vers. 45. and they were selling their possessions and their goods) they were giving the prices of their sold things to the Apostles for common uses: below c. IV. 37.

and they were distributing them to all according as anyone had need) namely to the sick for medicines, and other necessary things: likewise for the food of infants. For the other men and women were being clothed from the public store, and were having a common table from the public store, according to their brotherhoods.

Latin:

Vers. 45. κὴ τὰ κτήματα,κὴ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον) Rerum suarum venditarum pretia dabant Apostolis in usus communes: infra c. IV. 37.

κὴ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσι καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχε) nempe ægrotis ad medicamenta, & alias res necessarias: item ad alimenta infantium. Nam cæteri viri fœminæque de publico vestiebantur, de publico mensam habebant communem, κατὰ φρατρίας.

## 2:46
Vers. 46. in the temple) although they had peculiar assemblies, as it were Synagogues, yet they did not desert the common assemblies of the people in the temple. See below III. 1.

breaking bread from house to house) ten or twenty would gather together at a table in houses most suitable for that purpose.

with gladness) on account of such great benefits of God.

and in singleness of heart) with a pure heart. What Paul called ἡ ἁπλότητι in Rom. XII. 8, 2 Cor. I. 12, Col. III. 22, Eph. VI. 5; thus καθαρὰ καρδία in Gen. XX. 5, ὁσιότης καρδίας κὴ εὐθύτης, 1 Kings IX. v. 5, τελειότης according to certain Greek interpreters, Prov. XI. 3, ἁπλότης καρδίας, 1 Chron. XXIX. v. 17, ἀλήθεια, Prov. XXVIII. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 46. ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ) quamquam cœtus habebant peculiares, tanquam Synagogas, tamen communes in templo populi cœtus non deserebant. Vide infra III. 1.

κλῶντές τε κατ᾽ οἶκον ἄρτον) deni aut viceni simul ad mensam conveniebant in ædibus ad id commodissimis.

ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει) ob tanta Dei beneficia.

κὴ ἀφελότητι καρδίας) corde puro. Quod Paulus dixit ἡ ἁπλότητι Rom. XII. 8. 2. Cor. I. 12. Col. III. 22. Eph. VI. 5. sic καθαρὰ καρδία Gen. XX. 5. ὁσιότης καρδίας κὴ εὐθύτης, I. Reg. IX. v. 5. τελειότης secundum quosdam interpretes Græcos, Prov. XI. 3. ἁπλότης καρδίας, I. Paral. XXIX. v. 17. ἀλήθεια, Prov. XXVIII. 6.

## 2:47
Vers. 47. and having favor with all the people) They were gracious even among those on the outside, on account of their goodness, modesty, and patience, the power of which virtues is such that it extorts love even from men of a different way of life.

added those who were being saved) understand here by those who were being saved those who were separating themselves from the common impiety of the Jews. See above 40. In Hebrew פליטים, whoever escapes some evil, and they are called in Greek σωζόμενοι, ἀποσεσωσμένοι, ἀνασωθέντες, ἐξαιρέμενοι, διαπεφευγότες. The first thing is to flee vices: what follows is to learn virtues, which is done in the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 47. κὴ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαὸν) Erant gratiosi etiam apud τοὺς ἔξωθεν, ob bonitatem, modestiam, patientiam, quarum virtutum ea vis est, ut amorem etiam à disparis vitæ hominibus extorqueat.

προσετίθει τοὺς σωζομένους) τοὺς σωζομένους hic intellige eos, qui se segregabant à communi Judæorum impietate. Vide supra 40. Hebræis פליטים, quicunque malum aliquod effugiunt, dicunturq; ii Græce σωζόμενοι, ἀποσεσωσμένοι, ἀνασωθέντες, ἐξαιρέμενοι, διαπεφευγότες. Prius est vitia fugere: sequitur addiscere virtutes, quod fit in Ecclesia.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Peter, entering the temple for the sake of prayer with John, heals a lame beggar, who enters the temple leaping and celebrates God while the people marvel: Peter informs them, however, that it was not by his own power, but by the power of Jesus, whom they themselves had betrayed and killed, but whom God had raised from the dead, and through faith in his name, that the lame man was restored to health: and he admonishes them that, since they did it in ignorance, and God had thus fulfilled the prophecies of the Prophets concerning the passion of Christ, they should repent, and that they might enjoy Jesus, who has occupied heaven until the times of the restoration of all things, when he returns at the time of refreshing: inasmuch as he is that Prophet like Moses to be heard by all, of whom all the Prophets have prophesied, in whom, as the seed of Abraham, the blessing ought to be obtained by all peoples, but before all by the Jews, to whom he was sent first.

There are three parts: I. Peter's healing of the lame man near the temple, up to verse 5. II. Peter's [sermon] concerning Jesus killed and resuscitated, by whose power and faith the healing was done, the sermon, to v. 16. III. Petrine [sermon] for repentance and faith in Jesus, having brought forward the causes concerning the fulfillment of the Prophecies, and the future restoration, if they hear Jesus, of whom Moses and the Prophets prophesied, and an exhortation to the covenant of grace and blessing through Jesus with Abraham enjoyment, to v. 26.

PART I. Petrine healing of the lame man at the temple.

Vers. 1. Ἐπὶ τὸ ἀυτὸ) About the same time. ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐννάτην) which was the ninth hour of prayer of the day. That prayer was called evening [prayer], because it began in the evening as the Sun was declining. You have examples from XXIV. 63. Judith. IX. below X. 30. See what we have said at Matth. XIV. 15. & XXVII. 45. & it was accustomed to be done with the addition of מנחה as appears in Dan. IX. 21. And it was called מנחה or μανυὰ, a small [offering], because the morning offering was more abundant. The morning prayer was called אור, the midday צהרים, the evening ערבית. Christians have changed nothing in this part. In the Constitutions of Clement VII 24. τρὶς τῆς ἡμέρας ὕτω προσέυχεσθε. Prayers are concluded at the ninth hour, says Tertull. on fasts. The same in the same book: Furthermore, since in the same commentary of Luke the third hour of prayer is also demonstrated, under which, initiated by the Holy Spirit, they were taken for drunkards: and the sixth, at which Peter went up to the upper rooms: and the ninth, at which they entered the temple, why should we not understand, while fully maintaining the indifference of praying always and everywhere and at every time, that those three hours, as being more notable in human affairs, which distribute the day, which distinguish business, which resonate publicly, were also more solemn in daily prayers? which you also persuade by the argument of Daniel who also prayed three times: certainly through the exception of some hours: and none other than the more notable ones, thence Apostolic, the third, the sixth, the ninth; in the same place and in the book on Prayer he teaches us that the fourth and sixth from the Sabbath are stations, that is, half-fasts prolonged to the ninth, which Maimonides notes was also done by the more religious of the Jews.

Latin:

CAPUT III. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Petrus templum, orationis causa, cum Iohanne ingrediens, claudum mendicantem sanat, qui saltans templum ingreditur, Deumq́ue celebrat populo admirante: quem vero informat Petrus, non sua, sed Iesu ab ipsis traditi & occisi, at à Deo resuscitati, virtute, per fidem in nomen ejus, claudum sanitati restitutum: monetq́ue, ut, quum ignorantes id fecerint, Deus vero vaticinia Prophetarum de passione Christi sic impleverit, pœnitentiam agant, & tempore refectionis Iesu, qui cælum occuparit usq́ue ad tempora restitutionis omnium; reversuro fruantur: utpote qui est Propheta ille Mosi similis ab omnibus audiendus, de quo omnes Prophetæ vaticinati sint, in quo ceu Abrahami semine omnibus populis obtingere debeat benedictio, ante omnes vero Iudæis, ad quos primum missus est.

Partes sunt tres: I. Petrina claudi penes templum sanatio, ad v. 5. II. Petrina de Jesu occiso & resuscitato, cujus virtute & fide sanatio facta, con- cio,, ad v. 16. III. Petrina ad pænitentiam & fidem in Jesum, adductis causis de impletione Prophe- tiarum, & futura refectione, si Jesum audierint, de quo Moses & Prophetæ vaticinati sunt, ac fœderis gratiæ & benedictionis per Jesum cum Abrahamo pari fruitione adhortatio, ad v. 26.

PARS I. Petrina claudi penes templum sanatio.

Vers. 1. Ἐπὶ τὸ ἀυτὸ) Circa idem tempus. ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐννάτην) quæ hora preca- tionis erat diei nona. Ea precatio vespertina dicebatur, quia vesperi incipiebat Sole declinante. Exempla habes ex XXIV. 63. Judith. IX. infra X. 30. Vide, quæ diximus ad Matth. XIV. 15. & XXVII. 45. & solebat fieri addito מנחה ut ap- paret Dan. IX. 21. Vocabaturq; id מנחה sive μανυὰ, par- vum, quia matutina oblatio erat uberior. Precatio matutina dicebatur אור, meridiana צהרים, vespertina ערבית. Nihil hac in parte mutarunt Christiani. In Clementis Con- stitutionibus VII 24. τρὶς τῆς ἡμέρας ὕτω προσέυχεσθε. Oratio- nes nona hora concludi, ait Tertull. de jejuniis. Idẽ eodem libro: Porro cum in eodem commentario Lucæ & tertia hora orationis demonstretur, sub qua, Spiritu S. initiati, pro ebriis habebantur: & sexta, qua Petrus adscendit in superiora: & no- na, qua templum sunt introgressi cur non intelligamus, salva plane indifferentia semper & ubiq; & omni tempore orandi, ta- men tres istas horas, ut insigniores in rebus humanis, quæ diem distribuunt, quæ negotia distinguunt, quæ publice resonant, ita & solenniores fuisse, in orationibus diurnis? quod etiam suades Danielis quoq; argumentum ter die orantis: utiq; per aliquarum horarum exceptionem: non aliarum autem quam insigniorum, exinde Apostolicarum, tertiæ, sextæ, nonæ; ibidem & libro de Oratione nos docet quarta & sexta à Sabbato stationes, id est, semijejunia protracta ad nonam, quod & Judæorum religiosioribus factum notat Maimonides.

## 3:2
Vers. 2. πρὸς τὴν θύραν τῶ ἱερῦ) usually in the description of the Temple they are called πύλαι: but sometimes also θύραι, as 2. Paral. IV. 22. Ezech. 13. XL. And the Hebrew words שער and פתח are sometimes translated πύλη, sometimes θύρα. τὴν λεγομένην ὡραίαν) because it was made of Corinthian bronze. Joseph. on the Jewish war VII. 12. where the most learned man Ludov. Capellus thinks ὀξωτέρῳ should be read instead of ἐνδοτέρῳ, for no light reasons. τῶ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην) to beg for alms. Thus speak Cicero, Seneca, and others of the Latins.

Latin:

Vers. 2. πρὸς τὴν θύραν τῶ ἱερῦ) solent plerumque in de- scriptione Templi πύλαι dici: sed interdum & θύραι, ut 2. Paral. IV. 22. Ezech. 13. XL. Vocesq; Hebrææ שער & פתח modo vertuntur πύλη, modo θύρα. τὴν λεγομένην ὡραίαν) quia facta ex ære Corinthio. Jo- seph. de bell. Jud. VII. 12. ubi vir doctiss. Ludov. Capellus ὀξωτέρῳ pro ἐνδοτέρῳ legendum putat, non levibus de causis. τῶ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην) ad petendam stipem. Sic lo- quuntur Cicero, Seneca, & Latinorum alii.

## 3:5
Vers. 5. ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν ἀυτοῖς) It is a good Greek expression, such as many are in Luke: he kept his gaze intent.

Vers. 5. ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν ἀυτοῖς) Vox est bene Græca, quales multæ apud Lucam: intentus os tenebat.

## 3:7
Vers. 7. καὶ πιάσας ἀυτον) πιέζειν, or πιάζειν is to press with the hand: which is accustomed to be done among those who are well-disposed to one another. αἱ βάσεις) כפים or כפור : βῆμα, Deuter. II. 5. for it signifies to the Latins both the ground, and the lowest part of the foot, and that upon which the foot is pressed: thus also to the Hebrews. καὶ τὰ σφυρὰ) קרסלים, Thus that part around the ankles is called.

II. 5. nam & Latinis solum, & pedis infimum significat, & id, cui pes imprimitur: sic & Hebræis. καὶ τὰ σφυρὰ) קרסלים, Sic dicitur pars illa circum talos.

## 3:8
Vers. 8. καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος) reference is made to the prophecy of Isaiah XXXV. v. 6. τότε ἁλεῖται ὡς ἔλαφος ὁ χωλός.

The passage of Isaiah therefore pertains to the times of the New Testament: otherwise than Grotius in his Annotations on Isaiah XXXV. thought: concerning which we have spoken in that same place.

Latin:

Vers. 8. καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος) respicitur vaticinium Esaiæ XXXV. v. 6. τότε ἁλεῖται ὡς ἔλαφος ὁ χωλός.

Locus ergo Esaiæ ad tempora pertinet Novi Test. secus atq; Grotius in Annot. ad Esa. XXXV. censuit: de quo ibidem diximus.

## 3:13
Verse 13. τὸν παῖδα ἀυτῦ Ἰησῦν) that is, son, as God had called him in Matthew III. 17. For this is more regarded here than the miraculous conception, which was known to few as yet. παῖδα, when it is said of Jesus, Ambrose and Hilary also translate as son, as Erasmus notes below IV. 27. παρεδώκατε) To Pilate: this properly pertains to the Senators, Matthew XV. 1. John XVIII. 30. καὶ ἠρνήσασθε) This refers to the people: the sense is: you refused to acknowledge him as the Christ. A similar way of speaking about Moses below ch. VII. 35. κρίναντος ἐκείνε ἀπολύειν) It is ἀθετήσις. The sense is, when Pilate had judged it right to release him: it is the same as what the Syrian here signifies by הודיק. Verse 14. ἄνδρα φονέα) The author of the sedition, from which the slaughter had arisen, Luke XXIII. 19. 25. χαρισθῆναι ὑμῖν) that is, to be released for your sake: on the contrary, χαρίζεσθαί τινα is said, and he who condemns someone for the sake of another, Acts XXV. 11. 16. Verse 15. τὸν δὲ ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς) refers to the passage in Isaiah IX. v. 6, where the type of Christ is called אב־עד: which the LXX translate as πατὴρ τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος. Jesus had already shown that this title belonged to Him by raising the dead: And there is a manifest ἀντίθετον in the words φονέα, and ἀρχηγὸν ζωῆς. Regarding the passage in Isaiah IX. 6, it has been treated abundantly in the annotations on the Old Testament, and it has been shown that the discourse there is not about Hezekiah as a type of Christ, but about Christ Himself. ἀπεκτείνατε) he kills, who gives cause for death, as the Jews did by shouting "crucify." Verse 16. τῇ πίστει τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ) there follows shortly ἐστερέωσε τὸ ὄνομα. It is the custom of the Hebrews to repeat the noun twice, even in a different case, so as to avoid pronouns: as in Gen. XIV. 24, c. XX. 12, c. XXIII. 18, 19, c. XXIV. 1, 2, Num. X. 29, Psalm. LXXXII. 1, 1 Sam. XII. 1, Zach. 1. 6, Psal. XIII. 4, CXIV. v. 44. The noun here is force and power. ἐστερέωσε) הכין: which is translated elsewhere by τρέφειν, elsewhere by ἀνορθοῦν. See above 7. τὴν ὁλοκληρίαν ταύτην) Thus in Isaiah 1. 6. תם is translated as wholeness. It is well translated into Latin as integrity. For Cicero opposes an entire body to a defective one.

## 3:17
V. 17. ὅτι κατ᾽ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε) בשגגה which is translated as in ignorance in Leviticus XXII. 14. elsewhere unintentionally. God had sometimes forgiven even graver crimes as to David; but he was much more ready to pardon those which draw something from the involuntary, on account of the mixed ignorance, however gross and supine, which does not remove the guilt, but diminishes it. See 1 Cor II. 8. Philo on Abel and Cain: ignorance being an involuntary and light passion, has a remedy not difficult, instruction. God did not sometimes forgive graver crimes in the Old Testament, but as long as sinners were only performing true repentance, he testified that he was always prone to forgive sins of any kind Ex. XXXIV. Psalm. CIII. Micah VII. Ez. XVIII. XXXIV. Grotius socinianizes here: therefore he has already been refuted among the Socinians. See Socinism. profligat. p. 308. ὥσπερ κέ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν) whose guilt was greater than that of the common people following the authority of the Senators. See above 1 2. Verse 18. ἃ προκατήγγειλε) הגיד. The same word below ch. III. 24. VI. 2. παθεῖν τὸν χρισόν) See what we have said on the Gospel of Luke XXI 7. 26. below XXVI. 23. it can be doubted whether these words are part of the sense, or an added gloss, because they are missing in that old manuscript. Grotius is too easy in his suspicions about the corruption of the text. As one swallow does not make a spring, so from one codex all the rest are not to be corrected, as we have often warned. ἐπλήρωσεν ὕτω) you devised these things for evil: he directed them for good, Gen. L. 20. Verse 19. μετανοήσατε οὖν) in mind. καὶ ἐπιscρέψατε) in deeds. εἰς τὸ ἐξαλειφθῆναι ὑμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας) thus ἀπήλειψα τὰς ἀνομίας is Isaiah XLIV. 22. where in Hebrew it is מחיתי. The similarity is taken from those things which are written on tablets and are erased. ὅπως ἂν ἔλθωσι) that they may come. Thus ὅπως is very often taken in these books: and the Syrian and Arab have rightly grasped the sense. Tertullian concerning the resurrection of the flesh cites: that times of refreshing may come upon us. καιροὶ ἀναψύξεως). Exod. VIII. 15. הרוחה is translated as refreshing. Just as calamities are compared to heat, so liberation from them is compared to a cooling breeze. The sense is: that you may be delivered from the imminent destruction of the nation. The times of refreshing do not refer to the liberation from the imminent destruction of the Jewish nation, but to the refreshment in the other world: where there will be the restoration of all things v. 21. Matthew VIII. 18. the time of redemption Luke XXI. 24. Rom. VIII, 21. 23. of recreation Apoc. VII. 17. ch. XIV. 13. of exultation Isaiah LXV. 14. Job. XVI. 20. ἀναψύχειν is to cool, to dry, and metaphorically to refresh, to recreate, Psalm LXV. 12. Jer XLIX, 31. Hos. XII. 8.

V. 17. ὅτι κατ᾽ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε) בשגגה quod κατ᾽ ἄ- γνοιαν vertitur Levit. XXII. 14. alibi ἀκουσίως. Remiserat Deus interdum & graviora crimina ut Davidi; sed multò erat facilior ad ea condonanda, quæ aliquid trahunt de in- voluntario, propter admixtam ignorantiam quantumvis crassam ac supinam, quæ culpam non tollit, sed minuit. Vide 1. Cor II. 8. Philo de Abele & Caino : ἀμαθία ἀκύσι- ον ὃν καὶ κῦφον πάθος, θεράπειαν ὐ δύσέργον ἔχει, διδασκαλίαν. Non interdum remisit Deus graviora crimina in V. T. sed dum veram modo pœnitentiam age- bant peccatores, semper ad condonandum pecca- ta quæcunque pronum se esse testatus est Ex. XXXIV. Psal. CIII. Mich. VII. Ez. XVIII. XXXIV. Socinizat hĥc Grotius : ideo in Socinianis jam con- futatus est. Vid. Socinism. profligat. p. 308. ὥσπερ κέ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν) quorum major erat culpa quam plebis Senatorum auctoritatem sequentis. Nimis facilis est Grotius in suspicionibus de textus corruptione. Ut una hirundo non facit ver, ita ex uno codice non emendandi sunt reliqui o- mnes, quod sæpius monuimus. ἐπλήρωσεν ὕτω) vos in malum hæc excogitastis: ille in bonum direxit, Gen. L. 20.
