Latin:

Vers. 31. ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος) Signum Dei efficaciter agen- tis, infra XVI, 26. vide XII. 26.

PARS III. Ecclesiæ unitas, & bonorum communio, Io- sisque ad eandem collatio.

## 4:32
Vers. 32. the heart and soul was one) Plutarch in Cato the Younger cites an ancient verse: two friends, one soul. Aristotle refers to the same in Nicomachean Ethics IX. 8. They were as the Hebrews say כאיש אחד.

and not one said that any of the things belonging to him was his own) Explain from those things which are above II. 44.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ἦν ἡ καρδία καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ μία) Citat Plutarchus in Catone Uticensi versum veterem: δύο φίλοι, ψυχὴ μία. Eo- dem respicit Aristoteles Nicomach. IX. 8. Erant ut Hebræi loquuntur כאיש אחד.

καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι) Explica ex iis, quæ supra II. 44.

## 4:33
Vers. 33. and great grace was upon them all) They were held in high regard by all. See above II. 47.

Latin:

Vers. 33. χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς) Magni ab omnibus fiebant. Vide supra II. 47.

## 4:34
Vers. 34. of those being sold) Namely of fields and houses, as the preceding words show.

Latin:

Vers. 34. τῶν πιπρασκομένων) Nempe agrorum & do- muum, ut præcedentia ostendunt.

## 4:35
Vers. 35. and laid them at the feet) Which was a sign of those submitting that money to the judgment of the Apostles: an expression taken from that custom, Ps. VIII. 7.

and it was distributed to each according as anyone had need) Explain as above II. 45.

Latin:

Vers. 35. καὶ ἐτίθει παρὰ τοὺς πόδας) Quod signum erat pecunias illas subjicientium Apostolorum arbitrio: ab eo more sumta locutio, Ps. VIII. 7.

διεδίδοτο δὲ ἑκάστῳ καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν) Expone ut su- pra II. 45.

## 4:36
Vers. 36. And Joseph) So also that old Manuscript. Others [read] Joses with the same meaning. For Hebrew words are transferred into Greek, either plainly, such as they are like Joseph, or by adding as Josephus, or by subtracting, so that the Greek declension may be more easily received, such as is Joses, Josetos. See what we said at Matt. I, 16.

surnamed Barnabas by the Apostles, which is interpreted son of consolation) The Apostles had given him this name, as an omen of the prophetic gift. See below IX. 24. Therefore he was called in Hebrew בר נבואה, in the Greek language contractedly Barnabas.

Nothing is to be changed: for it is the custom of the Hellenists to call prophecy παράκλησιν. Thus understand it below at XIII. 13.

Λευίτης) From the tribe of Levi: how, however, the Levites could have possessed certain things alone, we have said what seems to us to be the case at Jer. XXXII. 7. This piece of land could also have belonged to the wife of Barnabas, as the Rabbis explain the passages at Joshua XXIV. 33, and 1 Paralip. II. 21.

Κύπριος τῷ γένει) Born of parents who had lived in Cyprus. See below at XIII. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 36. Ἰωσὴφ δὲ) Sic & vetus ille Manuscriptus. Alii Ἰωσῆς eodem sensu. Nam Hebræa vocabula in Græcum transferuntur, aut plane, qualia sunt ut Ἰωσὴφ, aut adden- do ut Ἰώσηπος, aut detrahendo, ut facilius recipiatur de- clinatio Græca, quale est Ἰωσῆς, Ἰωσῆτος. Vide, quæ dixi- mus ad Matth. I, 16.

ἐπικληθεὶς Βαρνάβας ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀποστόλων ὅ ἐστι μεθερμηνευό- μενον υἱὸς παρακλήσεως) Apostoli ei hoc nomen dederant, in omen doni Prophetici. Vide infra IX. 24. itaque dictus fuit Hebraice בר נבואה Græco sermone contracte Βαρνάβας.

Nihil mutandum: nam Hellenistis mos prophetiam voca- te παράκλησιν. Sic accipe infra XIII. 13.

Λευίτης) Ex tribu Levi: quomodo autem Levitæ res ali- quas soli habere potuerint, diximus id, quod nobis videtur ad Jer. XXXII. 7. potuit etiam fundus hic pertinuisse ad uxorem Barnabæ, quomodo Rabbini explicant loca XXIV. 33. Josuæ, & 1. Paralip. II. 21.

Κύπριος τῷ γένει) Ortus parentibus, qui in Cypro habi- taverant. Vide infra XIII. 5.

## 4:37
Vers. 37. ἤνεγκε τὸ χρῆμα) That is, τὴν τιμὴν, as he has just spoken. Thus כסף at Job XXVII. 17 is translated χρήματα. It is necessary, however, that the possession of Barnabas was great, because mention is made of it specifically here.

These things, however, were done not by the tenor of any divine command, or evangelical counsel, or opinion of necessity, or singular holiness, or perfection, nor from any vow, but from free will, as Cajetan acknowledged, for the state and condition of that church of the time; and therefore the ownership of property cannot be disapproved from this, nor can Anabaptist community of goods, or the monastic state, or a vow of poverty be proven. And there are examples of subsequent times, especially when the Church was enriched, concerning the ownership of goods, in the primitive Church at Acts X. 6, XII. 12, XVI. 19, XXI. 8. Moreover, Barnabas is called here not Joseph, but Joses, as the received Greek Codices have, which that one MS. cannot prejudice: whom Lorinus wishes to be different from that one who is introduced in chapter I. 23, since he is called not Barnabas, but Barsabas: to B. Balduinus, however, it seems to be the same in his Commentary on 2. Cor. VIII, as also to Erasmus Schmid in this place. But because בר שבוע is 'son of the oath': this one, however, is explained as 'son of consolation', nor is it established that Barnabas was called 'the just', who was not a Roman, but a Cypriot by birth, they seem more correctly to be held as different persons; concerning the name Barnabas itself, Ludov. de Dieu has another conjecture, that it is Aramaic, because בר נבא becomes 'consoling'. The Drusian suspicion, however, that it should be read Βαρνάμας from בר נחמא, is vain, since it is always and in all Codices read Βαρνάβας. Furthermore, even if the Levites perhaps did not have their own inheritance in the Israelite Republic while it was still flourishing, they could nevertheless have had it in its collapsed state, although even in that one they could have had their own lands, not indeed from the first distribution of the land of Canaan, but from their own acquisition through the revenues which were ordained for them. Compare Deut. XVIII. 8, Jer. XXXII. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 37. ἤνεγκε τὸ χρῆμα) Id est, τὴν τιμὴν ut modo est locutus. Sic כסף Job. XXVII, 17. vertitur χρήματα. O- portet autem magnam fuisse possessionem Barnabæ, quod ejus speciatim hic fit mentio.

Facta autem hæc sunt non tenore alicujus man- dati divini, aut consilii Evangelici, vel opinione ne- cessitatis, aut sanctitatis singularis, vel perfectionis, nec ex voto quodam, sed ex libera voluntate, ut Caje- tanus agnovit, pro Ecclesiæ istius temporis statu ac conditione, adeoq; non potest hinc improbari rerum proprietas, aut probari Anabaptistica com- munio, vel status monasticus, aut paupertatis votum. Et prostant exempla sequentium temporum, im- primis ubi Ecclesia locupletata est, de bonorum proprietate, in primitiva Ecclesia Act. X.6.XII.12. XVI.19.XXI.8. Cæterum Barnabas hic non Joseph, sed Joses dictus est, ut habent Codices Græci rece- pti, quibus unus ille MS. præjudicare non potest: quem Josen ab illo, qui cap. I. 23. introducitur, di- versum esse Lorinus vult, quum ille non Barnabas, sed Barsabas dictus sit: B. Balduino tamen idem es- se videtur in Comment. ad 2. Cor. VIII. ut & Erasmo Schmidio in h.l. Sed quia בר שבוע filius juramenti est: Hic vero explicatur filius παρακλήσεως, neq; con- stat, Barnabam justum vocatum esse, qui non Ro- manus, sed Cyprius gente fuit, pro diversis personis rectius haberi videntur; De nomine ipso Barnabas Ludov. de Dieu. aliam habet conjecturam, Aramäis id esse, quia בר נבא fit consolans. Drusiana au- tem suspicio, quod à בר נחמא legendum sit Βαρνά- μας, vana est, quum semper & in omnibus Codd. legatur Βαρνάβας. Porro etsi Levitæ forte non ha- buerint hæreditatem propriam in Rep. Israëlitica ad- huc florente, habere tamen potuere in ea collapsa, quamvis & in illa non quidem ex distributione pri- ma terræ Canaan, sed ex acquisitione propria per reditus, qui ipsis ordinati erant, suos fundos habe- re potuerint. Conf. Deut. XIIX. 8. Jer. XXXII. 7.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, on account of money withheld from the community, and a lie committed against the Holy Spirit as if against God himself, and having tempted the Holy Spirit, expire at the address of Peter, with great terror of the assembly: and many miracles are done through the hands of the Apostles, even through the shadow of Peter, with a great accession to the Church: Whence the Chief Priests with the Sadducees cast the Apostles into prison: but these, led out by an Angel, preach in the temple, which, when the Priests perceived upon finding the prison empty, they were indeed astonished, yet having sent the Captain, they examine them brought before the Sanhedrin, why they preach in the name of Jesus against the interdict: But they testify that God must be obeyed rather than men, and profess with the Holy Spirit that Jesus, having been suspended by them, was exalted by God into a Savior for the giving of repentance and remission of sins, and that they are his witnesses. When they were therefore meditating to kill them, Gamaliel dissuaded this by the example of the seducers Theudas and Judas the Galilean, with their adherents having been cut off, teaching that if that work were from men, it would perish of its own accord, if it were from God, it would be dissolved by no one; wherefore they dismissed the Apostles, having been beaten, with the previous interdict repeated, joyful that they were counted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus, and not ceasing to preach about him in the temple and in houses.

There are two parts: I. The destruction of Ananias and Sapphira on account of sacrilege and the tempting of the Holy Spirit, up to verse 11. II. The zeal of the Jews on account of the doctrine and miracles of the Apostles, entirely futile, both through the angelic liberation from prison up to verse 24, and through their intrepid apology up to verse 32, and through the counsel and opinion of Gamaliel up to verse 42.

PART I.

The sacrilege and destruction of Ananias and Sapphira.

V. 1. Ananias) The same name which we have in Jer. XXVIII. 1. Sapphira) שפירה beautiful: as in Psalm XVI. 6. the yod is inserted in the Syriac manner. κτῆμα) מקנה is translated as possession. שדה is κτῆμα in Prov. XXIII. 10.

Latin:

CAPUT V. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Ananias, cum uxore Saphira, ob pecuniam communioni subtractam, & mendaciũ Spir. S. ceu vero Deo commissum, tentatumq́; S. S. ad alloquium Petri expirant, cum magno cœtus terrore: & multa fiunt per Apostolo- rum manus, etiam per umbram Petri mira- cula, cum accessione magna Ecclesiæ: Vnde Pontifices cum Sadducæis in carcerem con- jiciunt Apostolos: sed hi ab Angelo educti in templo concionantur, quod cum vacuo re- perto carcere, perciperent Sacerdotes, ob- stupuerunt quidem, misso tamen Capitaneo adductos coram Synedrio examinant, cur contra interdictum in nomine Iesu prædi- cent: Qui vero Deo magis quam hominibus obediendum, testati Iesum ab ipsis suspen- sum, à Deo exaltatum in Salvatorem ad dandam pœnitentiam & remissionem pec- catorum, seq́; ejus testes esse, cum S. S. profi- tentur. Quos quum interficere ideo medi- tarentur, diffuasit id Gamaliel exemplo se- ductorum Theudæ & Judæ Galilæi, cum ad- hærentibus excisorum, docens, opus illud si ex hominibus sit, ultro interiturum, si ex Deo sit, à nemine dissolutum iri; quapropter Apostolos cæsos iterato inter dicto pristino dimisere, lætos, quod digni fuerint, ob nomen Iesu opprobrium pati, nec intermittentes in templo, & in ædibus de eo prædicare.

Partes duæ sunt: I. Interitus Ananiæ & Saphiræ ob sacrilegium, & tentationem S. S. ad v. 11. II. Zelus Judæorum ob doctrinam & miracula Apostolorum prorsus irritus tum per liberationem è carcere Angelicam ad v. 24. tum per intrepidam eorum apologiam ad v. 32. tum per Gamalielis consilium, & sententiam ad v. 42.

PARS I.

Ananiæ & Saphiræ sacrilegium & interitus.

V. 1. Ἀνανίας) Idem nomen, quod habemus Jer. XXIIX. 1. Σαπφείρῃ) שפירה pulchra: ut Psal. XVI. 6. jod interpositum more Syriaco. κτῆμα) מקנה κτῆσις vertitur. שדה κτῆμα Prov. XXIII. 10.

## 5:2
Vers. 2. ἐνοσφίσατο) It is the same word in 2 Macc. IV. 32. Tit. II. 10. in the Glossaries νοσφίζομαι means to embezzle, to usurp.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ἐνοσφίσατο) Est idem verbum 2. Macc. IV. 32. Tit. II. 10. in Glossis νοσφίζομαι peculor, usurpo.

## 5:3
Vers. 3. Why has Satan filled your heart?) That is, why did you allow your heart to be filled by Satan? Thus also Satan is said to have entered into Judas: Luke XXII. 3. John XIII. 27. It is a grave crime not to pay to God in full a thing that has been vowed. Lev. XXVIII. 10. Deut. XXIII. 21, 22, 23. A type of vow is חרם, for the punishment of the violation of which see the history of Achan in Joshua VII. 15, 25.

to lie to the Holy Spirit) ψεύδω which corresponds to the Hebrew כזב, is sometimes constructed with the Dative as in Job XXXIV. 9. Psalm LXXVIII. 36. LXXXIX. 35, sometimes with the Accusative as in Prov. XIV. 5. Thus also διαψεύδομαι is found with the Accusative in 1 Kings IV. 16; so here we have the construction with the Accusative, and in the following clause with the Dative. In a similar way ἐνδοχέω has sometimes the Dative after it, sometimes the Accusative. But the Greeks also speak thus, as Aristophanes: ὧ ψεύσει με. It is the same thing to lie to God or to the Holy Spirit; see what we have said on Matt. XII. 13. They are said to lie to God or the Holy Spirit who hope that they can deceive the Apostles, who are instructed by the Holy Spirit: which is soon called πειράσαι, as in Ps. LXXVIII. 41. וינסו they tempted: which a little before in verse 36 is יכזבו they lied. Thus there is a double figure: for the name of the act is given to the attempt: the possessor is designated by the thing possessed.

The same sense of the construction with the Dative and Accusative is rightly established; one must take care, however, that the argument for the Deity of the Holy Spirit is not overturned: for He to whom Ananias and his wife lied at that time, when they wished to deceive the Apostles, as if He were dwelling in the Apostles, is the true God, because they lied not to men, but to God. But He is the Holy Spirit. Which argument we have set forth at length against John Crell in the Examination of the book of Crell, which is inserted in Natural and Revealed Theology, page 1493, seqq. §. 476.

Latin:

Vers. 3. δια τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν συ) Id est, cur sivisti à Satana impleri cor tuum? Sic & in Judam intrasse dicitur Satanas: Luc. XXII. 3. Joh. XIII. 27. Grave crimen est rem votam non solidam Deo persolvere. Lev. XXIIX. 10. Deut. XXIII. 21. 22. 23. Voti species est חרם cujus violati pœna vide in Achanis historia Josuæ VII. 15. 25

ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον) ψεύδω quod respondet Hebræo כזב, modo cum Dativo construitur ut Iob. xxxiv. 9. Psal. LXXIIX. 36. LXXXIX. 35. modo cum Accusativo ut Prov. XIV. 5. Sic & διαψεύδομαι cum Accusativo reperitur 1. Reg. IV. 16. ita hic constructionem cum Accusativo habemus, sequenti commate cum Dativo. Pari modo ἐνδοχέω modo Dativum post se, modo Accusativum habet. Sed & Græci sic loquuntur ut Aristophanes: ὧ ψεύσει με. Idem est mentiri Deo vel Spiritui S. vide quæ diximus ad Matt. XII. 13. Mentiri Deo aut Spir. S. dicituris, qui sperat, se Apostolos fallere posse Spiritu S. instructos: quod mox dicitur πειράσαι ut in Ps. LXXIIX. 41. וינסו tentarunt: quod paulo ante 36. יכזבו mentiti sunt. Sic duplex figura: nam & conatui datur nomē actus: possidens designatur ex re possessa.

Recte idem sensus constructionis cum Dativo & Accusativo adstruitur; cavendum tamen, ne argumentum Deitatis Spiritus S. evertatur: ille enim, cui tunc, cum Apostolos fallere voluere, mentiti sunt Ananias & conjux ejus, ceu habitanti in Apostolis, est verus Deus, quia non hominibus, sed Deo mentiti sunt. At ille est Spiritus S. Quod argumentum contra Joh. Crellium prolixe adstruximus in Exam. libr. Crellii, quod insertum Theolog. naturali & revelatæ pag. 1493. seqq. §. 476.

## 5:4
Vers. 4. Was it not remaining, it remained for you) It was permitted to you through us not to sell the estate and to retain its ownership.

and having been sold, did it remain in your power?) namely, the price. Even after you had sold the land, it was permitted to you to retain the whole price, and to vow nothing of it to God.

τί ὅτι) That is, what was the cause why you brought this into your mind? Thus also below in verse 9. Pollux also speaks thus. The full expression is τὶ γέγονεν ὅτι in John XIV. 22.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ὀὐχὶ μένον σοι ἔμενε) Licebat tibi per nos non vendere prædium & ejus proprietatem retinere.

κὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχε;) nempe ἡ τιμή. Etiam postquam vendideras fundum, pretium totum retinere tibi licebat, ac de eo nihil Deo vovere.

τί ὅτι) Id est, quid fuit causæ, cur hoc in animum tuum induceres? Sic & infra 9. Loquitur sic & Pollux. Plena locutio τὶ γέγονεν ὅτι Ioh. XIV. 22.

## 5:5
Vers. 5. ἐξέψυξε) It is thus translated עוף in Judges IV. 21. See this chapter below, 10 and XII. 23. Because the Church lacked magistrates, guardians, and avengers of injuries, God therefore attributed a prodigious power of punishing to the Apostles.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ἐξέψυξε) Sic vertitur עוף Iud. IV. 21. Vide hoc capite infra. 10. & XII. 23. Quia deerant Ecclesiæ Magistratus, tutores & injuriarum vindices, ideo Deus prodigiosam puniendi potestatem attribuit Apostolis.

## 5:6
Vers. 6. they wrapped him up) περιστέλλειν is to wrap a dead person in bandages: Ez. XXIX. 5. Tob. XII. 14. Euripides uses it thus in the Iphigenia in Tauris and the Troades, and Homer often: likewise Plutarch: in the Glossary: Pollingo περιστέλλω νεκρὸν: whence περιστολὴ in Dionysius of Halicarnassus. συστέλλων is put for the same. Thus Euripides in the same Troades: — ἐδάμαρτά τε ἐν χερσῖν πέπλοις συνεστάλησαν. The Syrian therefore rightly accepted this word. The Hebrews would say כפתו.

Latin:

Vers. 6. συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν) περιστέλλειν est mortuum fasciis involvere: Ez. XXIX. 5. Tob. XII. 14. usurpat sic & Euripides Iphigenia in Tauris & Troadibus, & Homerus sæpe: item Plutarchus: in Glossario: Pollingo περιστέλλω νεκρὸν: unde περιστολὴ apud Dionysium Halicatnassensem. Pro eodem ponitur συστέλλων. Sic Euripides ibidem Troadibus: — ἐδάμαρτά τε ἐν χερσῖν πέπλοις συνεστάλησαν. Bene ergo vocē hanc accepit Syrus. Hebræi dicerent כפתו.

## 5:8
Vers. 8. for so much) Namely, with the quantity of the price expressed, which Ananias had stated.

Latin:

Vers. 8. τοσότου) Expressa nempe pretii quantitate, quam dixerat Ananias.

## 5:9
V. 9. was it agreed upon by you) התבריתם in this you conspired. οἱ ἐξοίσοντές σε) A Hebraism, for: they who will carry you out.

Latin:

V. 9. συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν) התבריתם in hoc conspirastis. οἱ ἐξοίσοντές σε) Hebraïsmus, pro: îdem te efferent.

## 5:10
V. 10. πρὸς τὸ ἄνδρα) Together with the man in the same tomb. In this sense the Greek poet used πρὸς δαίμονας in an epigram.

PART II.

The zeal of the Jews on account of the teaching and miracles of the Apostles was in vain.

Latin:

V. 10. πρὸς τὸ ἄνδρα) Una cum viro in eodem sepulcro. Hoc sensu πρὸς δαίμονας dixit Poëta Græcus in epigrammate.

PARS II.

Zelus Judæorum ob doctrinam & miracula Apostolorum irritus.

## 5:12
Verf. 12. By the hands of the Apostles) ביד that is: by the Apostles, a frequent Hebraism. In Solomon's porch) See above III. 11.

V 13. Of the rest) Of those who were outside the Church. No one dared to join themselves to them) For fear that some evil might happen to them from the Apostles. See a similar case in 1 Kings XVII. 18.

The more accepted use of the word κολλᾶσθαι in a good sense favors this meaning, which Drusius urges from 1 Kings XI. 2, Prov. VIII. 23, and de Dieu, as well as Erasmus Schmidius: Beza, however, takes it in a bad sense, moved by verse 14, but rather they were added, as does Flacius: The meaning is, he says, that it was so far from the case that anything was lost to the Church by that example set upon Ananias and his wife, that on the contrary, the struck enemies did not dare to attack them any longer as before, but the common people began to hold them in higher esteem, and thus the number of the pious was increased in a wonderful way. Which meaning of the word κολλᾶσθαι he illustrates from the Syriac and Arabic interpretation: because the Syrian used the word קרב, from which comes קרב, a battle, in which, clearly, those fighting contend with others with bodies brought together, according to that of Maro from Homer, foot clings to foot, and man to man in close order: the Arab, however, very appropriately used a word that properly suits wrestlers, who bind themselves most tightly by the mutual connection of their bodies. But because the word κολλᾶσθαι occurs in the Scriptures only in a good sense, and, as Beza admits, it is accustomed to be used for familiar access, as below VIII. 29 and IX. 26. And from v. 17 it is evident that the enemies were not at all terrified from laying hands on the Apostles again, so Dievius's explanation seems preferable, that for that time those who had not yet embraced the faith of Christ did not dare to join themselves familiarly to the Apostles; but one must observe the annotation of Pricaeus on this passage, that by the rest, because of that opposite term the people, the honorable are designated, that from those indeed whom either rank or authority of life had made more distinguished, no one dared, or took upon himself that confidence because of the fear still recent from the prodigious death of Ananias: yet the people not only extolled the Apostles with praises, but also many from the people were added one after another to the number of believers. Thus the crowd and the rulers are placed in opposition in John VII. 48, 49. Thus Pricaeus observes that the rest, that is, the wiser, are opposed to the many, the common people, the simple, in chapter XLV of Epictetus.

Latin:

Verf. 12. Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν Ἀποστόλων) ביד id est: per Apostolos Hebraïsmus frequens. ἐν τῇ σοᾷ Σολομῶντος) Vide supra III. 11.

V 13. Τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν) Eorum, qui extra Ecclesiam erant. ὀὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς) Metu, ne mali aliquid ipsis eveniret ab Apostolis. Simile vide 1. Reg. XVII. 18.

Huic sensui favet usus vocis κολλᾶσθαι receptior in bonam partem, quem urgent Drusius è 1. Reg. XI. 2. Prov. VIII. 23. & de Dieu, nec non Erasm. Schmidius: Beza tamen in malam partem accipit, motus versu 14. μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο, ut & Fla- cius: Sensus est, inquit ille, tantum abfuisse, ut illo ex- emplo in Ananiam & ejus uxorem edito decesserit ali- quid Ecclesiæ, ut contra perculsi hostes non ausi sint amplius illos ut antea impetere, plebs autem eos in majore pretio habere cœperit, atque adeo mirum in mo- dum auctus sit piorum numerus. Quem sensum vo- cis κολλᾶσθαι illustrat è Syriaca, & Arabica inter- pretatione: quod Syrus verbo קרב usus sit, un- de קרב prælium, in quo videlicet pugnantes alii cum aliis collatis corporibus decertant, juxta il- lud Maronis ex Homero, hæret pede pes, densusque viro vir: Arabs vero commodissime eo usus ver- bo sit, quod luctatoribus proprie convenit, mutuo corporum nexu sese arctissime copulantibus. Sed quia in bonam partem tantum in Sacris verbum κολλᾶσθαι occurrit, & fatente Beza usurpari de fa- miliari accessu consuevit, uti infra VIII. 29. & IX. 26. & è v. 17. constat, hostes minime territos fuisse, quin iterum manus injicerent in Apostolos, præfe- renda videtur Dievii explicatio, quod pro eo tempo- re non ausi sint, qui fidem Christi nondum amplexi erant, familiariter se adjungere Apostolis; obser- vanda autem Pricæi ad h. l. annotatio, quod per τὸς λοιπὸς propter oppositum illud λαὸς, εὐσχή- μονες designentur, quod ex illis quidem, quos aut ordo, aut vitæ autoritas insigniores fecerat, nemo ausus fuerit, vel confidentiam illam sibi sumserit ob recentem adhuc ex prodigioso Ananiæ interi- tu metum: populus tamen non tantum laudibus extulerit Apostolos, sed & multi magis magisque subinde è populo adjecti sunt credentium nume- ro. Sic ὄχλος & ἄρχοντες ex adversum positi Joh. VII. 48 49. Sic τὺς λοιπὺς, id est, sapientiores τοῖς πολλοῖς, vulgo, idiotis simplicium in cap. XLV. E- picteti opponere observat Pricæus.

## 5:14
V. 14. But rather they were added) Much more even than before. For reference is made here to that which was said above IV. 4.

Latin:

V. 14. Μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο) Multo etiam magis quam ante. Respicitur enim hic id, quod dictum est supra IV. 4.

## 5:15
Vers. 15. As the most ancient) See Mark II. 4.

That his shadow might overshadow any of them) Christ healed diseases by the touch of his hem. Peter also by the contact of his shadow: thus was fulfilled what Christ had said in John XIV. 12.

Not that greater miracles are predicted there, but a greater fruit of the proclamation, as B. Brentius warned, and certainly it was a greater miracle of Christ that he raised Lazarus, dead for four days, by his voice alone.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ὠς πρεσβύτατον) Vide Marci II. 4.

κὴν ἡ σκιὰ ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν) Christus fimbriæ tactu sanavit morbos. Petrus etiam umbræ contactu: ita imple- tum est, quod dixerat Christus Joh. XIV. 12.

Non majora ibi miracula, sed majorem fructum præconii prædici, B. Brentius monuit, & majus certe fuit miraculum Christi, quod Lazarum qua- triduanum mortuum sola voce excitavit.

## 5:17
Vers. 17. But the High Priest rising up) Going out from the Sanhedrin, so that he might see what was being done.

The sect of the Sadducees which was) In the great Council there were both Pharisees and Sadducees: below XXIII. 6. But the High Priest and his kinsmen were of the sect of the Sadducees: as were a great part of the nobles: αἵρεσις, as in Latin secta, is a neutral word. See below XXIV. 5. Cicero, Epist. 16, book 15, section 2, On the Excuses of Tutors.

ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλε) קנאה which they translate as ζῶλον, the LXX often signifies anger. We indicated the cause of the anger of the Sadducees above IV. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) Exiens è Synedrio, ut videret, quid ageretur.

ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων) In magno Senatu erant & Pharisæi & Sadducæi:infra XXIII. 6. Sed summus Sacerdos & consanguinei ejus, sectæ erant Sadducæorum: ut pro- cerum pars magna: Αἵρεσις ut Latine secta, vox est me- dia. Vide infra XXIV. 5. Ciceronem XV. Epist. 16. L. si duas §. 2. De Excus. Tutorum.

ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλε) קנאה quod ζῶλον vertunt LXX.sæ- pe iram significat. Causam itæ Sadducæorum indicavimus supra IV. 1.

## 5:18
Vers. 18. ἐν τηρήσει) See above IV. 3. the same below δεσμωτήριον. 21. 23. & φυλακή. 22.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ἐν τηρήσει) Vide supra IV. 3. idem infra δεσμω- τήριον. 21. 23. & φυλακή. 22.

## 5:19
Vers. 19. ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς) As in Matt. XXVIII. 2. & below XII. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς) Ut Matth.XXVIII. 2. & infra XII. 10.

## 5:20
Vers. 20. πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης) It is a metonymy: for by the name of life he understands the doctrine which leads to eternal life. Thus also John XII. 50. XVII. 3.

There is no need for a metonymy, because the very words which the Apostles spoke were words of life, as is said concerning the proclamation of Christ in John VI. 63. The words which I speak are Spirit and life. Compare Phil. II. 16. Rom.

CAP. V. v. 12. 13. 14. 15. 17. - 21. 24. 26. 28. - 31.

l. 16. Flacius rightly [says] in this place. Understand 'words of this life' as concerning that life about which their doctrine was occupied, and the speech of the angel dealing with spiritual life, namely concerning the benefits of Jesus, not as we commonly say 'of this life,' namely that which we live here daily, and about which all our cares and thoughts are occupied. In a completely similar manner it is said below c. 13. 26. 'The word of this salvation.' Nor is there any hypallage here or there. See Clau. 2. 294.

σταθέντες) That is, with a constant mind: those who are such are said by the Hebrews to stand: as I Corinthians VII. 37. X. 12. 2 Cor. I. 24. Ephesians V. 14. Colossians IV. 12. Philo, in 'On the Cherubim,' explains ςῆναι as 'to possess an unchangeable mind'.

Latin:

Vers. 20. πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης) Est metony- mia: nam vitæ nomine intelligit doctrinam, quæ ad vitam æternam ducit. Sic & Joh. XII. 50. XVII. 3.

Non opus est metonymia, quia ipsa verba, quæ locuti sunt Apostoli, verba vitæ erant, ut de Chri- sti præconio dicitur Joh. VI.63. Verba, quæ ego lo- quor, Spiritus & vita sunt. Conf. Phil. II. 16. Rom.

CAP. V. v. 12. 13. 14. 15. 17. - 21. 24. 26. 28. - 31.

l. 16. Recte Flacius h. l. Verba vitæ hujus intellige de illâ vitâ, circa quam verfabatur eorum doctrina, & sermo angeli de spirituali vitâ agentis, nempe de beneficiis Jesu, non ut dicimus communiter vitæ hujus, nempe quam hic quotidie vivimus, & circa quam omnes nostræ curæ cogitationesque versantur. Prorsus simili ratione dicitur infra c. 13. 26. Sermo salutis hujus. Nec est ulla hypallage hic aut ibi. Vide Clau. 2. 294.

σταθέντες) Id est, constanti animo: qui tales sunt, stare dicuntur Hebræis: ut I. Corinth. VII. 37. X. 12. 2. Cor. I. 24. Ephes. V. 14. Coloss. IV. 12. Philo de Cherubinis, ςῆναι explicat ἄτρεπτον κτήσασθαι διάνοιαν.

## 5:21
Vers. 21. καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ) That is, the Senators of the city of Jerusalem, and if any Senators from other towns had gathered for the feast day. See above IV. 5. and what was said at Matt. X. 17. γερουσία is the same as πρεσβύτεροι above. זקנים.

Latin:

Vers. 21. καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ) Id est, Senatores urbis Hierosolymorum, & si qui Senatores ex aliis oppidis ad festum diem convenerant. Vide supra IV. 5. & quæ dicta ad Matth. X. 17. idem est γερουσία, quod supra πρεσβύτεροι. זקנים.

## 5:24
Vers. 24. ὅ, τε ἱερεὺς) Namely ὁ μέγας הכהן. καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ) Concerning whom see above IV. 1. καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς) The head of the priestly families. See Matt. II. 4. and what is said there.

τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο) γένοιτο for εἴη. They will wonder what this thing might be: the Syrian also understood it thus.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ὅ, τε ἱερεὺς) Nempe ὁ μέγας הכהן. καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ) De quo supra IV. 1. καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς) Princeps Sacerdotalium familiarum. Vide Matth. II. 4. & ibi dicta.

τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο) γένοιτο pro εἴη. mirabuntur, quid hoc esset rei: ita accepit & Syrus.

## 5:26
Vers. 26. not with violence) Not bound: as was otherwise accustomed to be done. Matt. XXVII. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 26. οὐ μετὰ βίας) Non ligatos: ut alioqui fieri solebat. Matth. XXVII. 2.

## 5:28
Vers. 28. with a charge we charged) A locution such as that above IV. 17. Justin in Apology II: His Apostles going forth preached everywhere, although death had been decreed against those who taught. The author who wrote the responses to the orthodox notes that this was now no longer a matter of ignorance, but of malice.

and you wish to bring upon us the blood of this man) That is, you wish to burden us with the crime of the killing of that man. Blood to the Hebrews means slaughter, and the crime of slaughter, and the punishment of slaughter.

Therefore, some interpret it concerning the punishment of slaughter: they wish to avoid both, so that they are neither guilty of the crime (for they did not consider it a crime, and consequently) nor of the punishment. The blood of someone is brought upon someone when he is liable for the punishment of the same because of the crime of the slaughter of another committed. τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου is said in contempt, and Buxtorf observes in Lex. Rabb. Talm. p. 76 that even today the Jews speak of Christ in this way, calling him אותו איש, as if he were one whom they do not even deem worthy to name.

Latin:

Vers. 28. παραγγελίᾳ παρηγγείλαμεν) Locutio, qualis supra IV. 17. Justinus Apologetico II. οἱ Ἀπόςολοι αὐτοῦ ἐξελθόντες πανταχοῦ ἐκήρυξαν, καίπερ θανάτῳ ὁρισθέντος κατὰ τῶν διδασκόντων. Notat, qui responsa ad orthodoxos scripsit, hoc jam non ignorantiæ, sed malitiæ fuisse.

καὶ βούλεσθε ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐφ' ἡμᾶς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου) Id est, vultis nos onerare crimine interfecti hominis istius. Sanguis Hebræis cædes, & crimen cædis & pœna cædis.

De pœna ergo cædis nonnulli interpretantur: utrumque amoliri volunt, quod neque criminis rei sint (non enim pro crimine habebant ac consequenter) neque pœnæ. Sanguis alicujus inducitur super aliquem, quum is propter crimen cæsi alterius commissum pœnæ ejusdem reus est. τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου per contemtum dictum atq; etiamnum hodie ita de Christo loqui Judæos, vocando eum אותו איש observat Buxtorf. Lex. Rabb. Talm. p. 76. quasi quem ne nominare quidem dignentur.

## 5:29
Vers. 29. we must obey God) See what is above IV. 19. πειθαρχεῖν is a good Greek word, which he also uses below v. 32 and c. XXVII. 21 and Paul to Titus III. 1. It corresponds to the Hebrew שמע.

Latin:

Vers. 29. πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις) Vide, quæ supra IV. 19. πειθαρχεῖν vox est bene Græca, qua & infra utitur v. 32. & c. XXVII. 21. & ad Titum Paulus III. 1. Respondet Hebræo שמע.

## 5:30
Vers. 30. the God of our fathers) He added this providently, lest anyone believe that a different God was preached by Jesus than the one whom Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had worshipped, of whom Moses had commanded, contrary to what Marcion persuaded himself. Thus also above III. 13 and below VII. 32, XXII. 14.

whom you slew) For this word is taken thus also below XXVII. 21. Luke, as a learned man, uses many purely Greek words, such as this one, which is found with the same sense in Herodotus and Plutarch. In Hebrew it is טרף, which is translated as hand in Job XIII. 18.

having hanged on a tree) He preferred to say this rather than on a cross, so that he might allude to the passage of Deuteronomy XXI. 23.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν) Provide hoc addidit, ne quis alium Deum ab Jesu prædicatum crederet, quam eum, quem coluerant Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, de quo præceperat Moses, contra quam sibi persuasit Marcio. Sic & supra III. 13. & infra VII. 32. XXII. 14.

ὃν ὑμεῖς διεχειρίσασθε) Trucidastis. Sic enim vox hæc sumitur & infra XXVII. 21. Lucas, ut eruditus, multis utitur vocibus pure Græcis, qualis hæc est, quæ eodem sensu apud Herodotum, & Plutarchum reperitur. Hebraice est טרף, quod χεὶρ vertitur Jobi XIII. 18.

κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου) Ita maluit dicere quam ἐπὶ σταυροῦ, ut alluderet ad locum Deuteronomii XXI. 23.

## 5:31
V. 31. a leader) נגיד ἡγούμενον Dan IX. 25. See above III. 15 to give repentance to Israel) So that, with His resurrection and ascension into heaven understood, you may enter that way which He said must be entered. The blood of Christ, as Clement says, brought forth the grace of repentance to the whole world.

and the forgiveness of sins) Which follows repentance animated by faith.

Christ did not show the way to salvation by His example, as the Socinians wish, but He acquired it for us by His merit, and once acquired, He revealed it by His doctrine. For by that manner in which Christ was resurrected and ascended into heaven, no one is resurrected or raised into heaven. Christ, devoid of all sin, was delivered for our sins, was resurrected for our justification, and opened for us the ascent into heaven: since He Himself was the Lord of heaven, and that Lord through whom all things exist, and He would not have come from heaven except for our salvation, and He entered into that holy of holies, that is, into heaven, with His blood as the high priest, having found eternal redemption for us, Heb. IX. 18.

Latin:

V. 31. ἀρχηγὸν) נגיד ἡγούμενον Dan IX. 25. Vide supr. III. 15 δοῦναι μετάνοιαν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ) Ut resurrectione Ipsius & ascensu in cœlum intellectis, ineatis eam viam, quam ineundam dixit. Christi sanguis, ut inquit Clemens, παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ μετανοίας χάριν ὑπήνεγκεν.

καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν) Quæ pœnitentiam fide animatam sequitur.

Christus viam ad salutem non exemplo suo monstravit, ut Sociniani volunt, sed merito suo eam nobis acquisivit, & acquisitam doctrina sua patefecit. Ea enim ratione, qua Christus resuscitatus est, & in cœlum ascendit, nemo resuscitatur, vel in cœlum evehitur. Christus expers omnis peccati, propter nostra peccata traditus, propter nostram justitiam resuscitatus est, nobisque ascensum in cœlo aperuit: quum esset ipse Dominus cæli, & Dominus ille, per quem omnia, nec nisi propter nostram salutem de cœlo venerit, ac sanguine suo ceu Pontifex summus in sanctum illud sanctorum, hoc est, in cœlum ingressus sit, æterna nobis inventa redemtione, Ebr. IX. 18.

## 5:32
Ver. 32. Of these words) Of these things, in the Hebrew manner: הדברים אלה.

but the Holy Spirit) Not not only, but also the Holy Spirit, divine power Matt. X. 20.

to those who obey him) See above 29.

Latin:

Vers. 32. τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων) Harum rerum, more He- bræo: הדברים אלה.

τὸ τὸ πνεῦμα δὲ τὸ ἅγιον) Non non tantum, sed & Spiritus Sanctus, virtus divina Matth. X. 20.

τοῖς πειθαρχοῦσιν αὐτῷ) Vide supra 29.

## 5:33
Ver. 33. they were cut to the heart) They were being torn apart in their minds: thus below VII. 54.

Latin:

Vers. 33. διεπρίοντο) Dirumpebantur animis: sic inf. VII. 54.

## 5:34
Ver. 34. A Pharisee) Which class of men was milder regarding punishments.

This does not appear from the history of the passion of Christ: nor is the cause of that matter noted here: but that it might be intimated that the hearts of the Pharisees, even though that sect was most hostile to the Apostles, were governed by God.

Gamaliel) It is credible that he was the one whom the Talmudists say was the teacher of his Simeon, in whose age the Temple was destroyed. This name was frequent among the Hebrews, and a certain patriarch of that name existed in the Honorian times, whom the law of Honorius in the Theodosian Code, Jerome to Pammachius, and Marcellus Empiricus c. 23 mention.

That he is called Gamaliel the Elder is evident from Drusius, book V, miscellanea, p. 169, to whom his son Rabban Simeon succeeded, in whose days the temple was destroyed; others, however, judge this Gamaliel to have been the grandson of Hillel, the son of Simeon, at whose feet Paul sat Acts XXII. 3, whom Pseudo-Clement, book 1, Recognitions c. 19, Bede, and Cornelius à Lapide maintain to have secretly favored Christ, but to have concealed his faith in the sense of the Apostles, so that he could defend the Apostles in the council and dissipate the plans of the high priests against them, which is not at all likely.

to put the Apostles outside for a little while) As was the custom to be done to the accused, when their business was being deliberated. Above IV. 15. Moreover, the expression is sufficiently Greek: thus Aristotle, Oeconomica II, said, 'having put those sent away into custody.' 'Huc te fac' in Terence, Donatus interprets as 'come here.' Thus also Apuleius: 'he makes himself inside, however.'

Latin:

Vers. 34. Φαρισαῖος) Quod genus hominum lenius e- rat circa pœnas.

Non id apparet ex historia passionis Christi: ne- que ejus rei causa hic notatur: sed ut Pharisæorum etiam corda, etsi maxime infensa illa secta Aposto- lis fuerit; divinitus gubernata fuisse innuatur.

Γαμαλιὴλ) Credibile est, fuisse illum, quem Thalmudici ajunt magistrum fuisse Simeonis ejus, cujus ætate destru- ctū fuit Templum. Frequens fuit hoc nomen inter Hebræ- os, & patriarcha quidam ejus nominis fuit Honorianis tem- poribus, cujus meminit lex Honorii in Codice Theodosia- no, Hieronymus ad Pammachiu, Marcellus Empiricus c. 23.

Gamalielem Seniorem illum dictum esse, è Dru- sio l. V. præterit. p. 169. constat, cui filius Rabban Si- meon successit, in cujus diebus destructum fuit templum; alii tamen nepotem Hillelis filium Simeo- nis hunc Gamalielem fuisse censent, ad cujus pedes Paulus sedit Actor. XXII. 3. quem occulte favisse Christo Pseudo-Clemens l. 1. Recognit. c. 19. Beda & Cornel. à Lap. statuunt, fidem vero sensu Apo- stolorum celasse, ut in concilio Apostolos tueri, & Pontificum contra eos consilia dissipare posset, quod verisimile minime est.

ἔξω βραχύ τι τὺς Ἀποστόλυς ποιῆσαι) Ut moris erat fieri reis, ubi de eorum negotio consultabatur. supra IV. 15. Est autem locutio satis Græca: sic Aristoteles Oeconomicon II. dixit, τοὺς ἀποσταλέντας εἰς φυλακὴν ποιήσας. Huc te fac apud Terentium, Donatus interpretatur accede. Sic & Apulejus: intra tamen sese facit.

## 5:36
Ver. 36. for before these days rose up) Politicians in deliberations make much use of examples, especially those of their own country, and those of recent memory.

Theudas) It is a name not Greek, but Hebrew, תודוס, which the Syrians pronounce with the diphthong Theuda, just as they call Thomas Thaumas, and Joseph Jausephus. That name was frequent among the Hebrews. Therefore it is not a wonder that at different times there existed several factious men of the same name; as for the one here in question, he existed a little before the end of Herod, as Casaubon notes in Exercise XVII, showing that Origen also thought so.

Ludov. Capellus thinks that this Theudas is the same one who is commemorated by Josephus, book XX, Antiquities c. 2. But since the time does not agree, he attributes a mnemonic slip to Luke, because he joins those two things as if they were neighboring facts of Judas and Theudas. But this is impious. Casaubon, Exercise II, from Origen, book I against Celsus, notes that Theudas preceded the birth of Christ: and he judges that this movement happened in these last years: and thus he makes two seditious Theudases: one whom Gamaliel mentions here; another who is commemorated by Josephus, and who stirred up a movement under Cuspius Fadus; to whom we do not add our own calculation. For there is no reason why we should argue that Josephus, along with Baronius, is in error in this; because the time of the movement stirred up by Theudas does not harmonize: since it is not likely that in those things which happened in the age of Josephus, such a historian would have hallucinated; and nothing prevents there having existed different seducers of the same name, who stirred up public seditions.

λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν) That manuscript in England adds it, as do certain others, μέγαν as below VIII, 6.

διελύθησαν) They were dispersed with their leader lost.

καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδὲν) That is, all their efforts vanished, according to the Hebrew proverb, of which we spoke at Matt. XVI, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 36. πρὸ γὰρ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέστη) Politici in de- liberationibus multum utuntur exemplis, præsertim patriæ suæ, & quorum recens memoria.

Θευδᾶς) Est nomen non Græcum, sed Hebræum, תודוס, quod Syri enuntiant per diphthongum Theuda, quomodo Thomam Thaumam vocant, & Josephum Jausephum. Frequens erat id nomen apud Hebræos. Itaque non mi- rum est, diversis temporibus plures extitisse factiosos ho- mines ejusdem nominis de quo hic agitur, is exstitit paulo ante finem Herodis, ut notat Casaubonus Exercitatione XVII. ostendens ita sensisse & Origenem.

Eundem esse hunc Theudam, qui Josepho l. XX. Antiq. c. 2. commemoratur, Ludov. Capellus putat. Quum vero tempus non congruat, Lucæ lapsum μνημονικὸν tribuit, quod duo illa ceu facta vicina Judæ & Theudæ conjungat. Sed hoc impium est. Casaubonus Exerc. II. ex Origene l. I. contra Cels. notat, Theudam nativitatem Christi præcessisse: & hunc motum ultimis his annis contigisse, censet: adeoq; duos facit Theudas seditiosos: unum cujus hic Gamaliel meminit; alterum qui à Josepho com- memoretur, & sub Culpio Fado motus excitavit; cui calculum nostrum non subducimus. Non enim causa est, cur Josephum cum Baronio erroris in eo arguamus; quod non consonet tempus excitati per Theudam motus: Siquidem verosimile non sit in iis, quæ ævo Josephi contigere, tantum hi- storicum hallucinatum esse; nihilque obstet, di- versos ejusdem nominis extitisse seductores, qui pu- blicas seditiones excitarint.

λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν) Addit manuscriptus ille in Anglia, ut & alii quidam, μέγαν ut infra VIII, 6.

διελύθησαν) Dispersi sunt duce amisso.

καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδὲν) Id est, omnes illorum conatus evanue- re, juxta proverbium Hebraicum, de quo diximus ad Matt. XVI, 18.

## 5:37
Vers. 37. Ἰύδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος) I think he is the Gaulonite: the Salmanticensian mentions this Judas, as do other Rabbis.

ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς) With Archelaus banished.

Casaubon observes that for various reasons the same man is called both Galilean and Gaulonite by Josephus: so also Capellus, that he is called Gaulonite because he was born in Gaulon, but Galilean because that region looked toward Galilee taken in a wider sense, and he was commonly believed to be such: and Casaubon judges that Coponius was procurator in Judea when that sedition was stirred up. It does not please Baronius that Josephus says these disturbances were set in motion during the later census, held after the condemnation of Archelaus: for he wishes it to have happened at the time of the earlier census, when Christ was born. But he is deservedly corrected here by Casaubon. Josephus, a serious and native writer, affirms that the sedition of Judas happened because of the later census, and he does not do this once or in passing, but confirms the same thing twice in earnest. For he narrates the history in book XVIII, and repeats the same in book XX, c. III. Baronius, a historian born yesterday or the day before, denies it, destitute of any foundation: which one shall we believe? Spanheim assigned a sixfold distinction of these descriptions; which Walaeus has brought forward here at length from him.

διασκορπίσθησαν) The same as he had just said διελύθησαν: in Hebrew it would be נפצו as in Ezek. XXVIII. 25. and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 37. Ἰύδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος) Puto esse Gauloniten: hu- jus Judæ meminit Salmanticensis, & Rabbini alii.

ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς) Relegato Archelao.

Propter diversas causas eundem & Galilæum & Gauloniten etiam à Josepho dictum esse, observat Casaubonus: sic & Capellus, Gauloniten dici, quia Gaulone erat oriundus, Galilæum autem, quia illa ad Galilæam latius acceptam spectabat, & vulgo talis credebatur: censetque Casaubonus, fuisse eum in Judæa procuratorem Coponium, cum illa seditio excitata est. Baronio non placet, quod Josephus turbas has motas in posteriori censu, post damna- tionem Archelai, habito, ait: nam accidisse vult prioris census tempore, cum natus est Christus. Sed castigatus hic merito à Casaubono. Josephus scri- ptor gravis & vernaculus seditionem Judæ acci- disse affirmat propter censum posteriorem, neque hoc semel aut obiter, sed bis serio idem confirmat. Nam & libr. XVIII. historiam narrat, & libro XX. c. III. eandem repetit. Baronius χθὲς ἢ πρώην na- tus historicus negat, omni destitutus fundamento: utri credemus? Spanhemius assignavit sextuplex discrimen harum descriptionum; quod ex eo ad- duxit hic prolixe Walæus.

διασκορπίσθησαν) Idem quod modo dixerat διελύθησαν: in Hebræo esset נפצו ut Ezech. XXVIII. 25. & alibi.

## 5:38
Vers. 38. ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων) That is, let there be no business for you with them: as in Matt. XXVII. 18.

ἐξ ἀνθρώπων) From human invention.

καταλυθήσεται) לא תקום as it is in a Hebrew proverb of like meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων) Id est, nihil vobis sit cum illis negotii: ut Matth. XXVII. 18.

ἐξ ἀνθρώπων) Ex humano commento.

καταλυθήσεται) לא תקום ut est in Hebræo pro- verbio paris sensus.

## 5:39
Vers. 39. μήποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε) Before μήποτε here, one must understand 'we must beware'. Symmachus translates רפאים as θεομάχους in Job XXVI. 5, Prov. IX. 18, and XXI. 16. You have the word θεομαχεῖν in 2 Macc. VII. 19. Γλώσσαις θεομάχοις, in the exposition of faith which is added to the works of Justin.

Latin:

Vers. 39. μήποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε) Ante μήποτε hic subintelligitur cavendum est. Symmachus רפאים vertit θεομάχους Job. XXVI. 5. Prov. IX. 18. & XXI. 16. Verbum θεομαχεῖν habes 2. Macc. VII. 19. Γλώσσαις θεομάχοις, in expositione fidei, quæ additur operibus Justini.

## 5:40
Vers. 40. And they were persuaded by him) Namely, that they should not kill the Apostles: but not that they should let them go unharmed: which, however, would have been just, and consistent with those things which Gamaliel had said.

δείραντες) When they had beaten them with thongs, in the Hebrew manner. Compare those things which are below XXII. 19. 2. Cor. XI. 24. that was predicted in Matth. I. 17. XXI. 35. XXIII. 34. Mark XII. 5. XIII. 9. Luke X. 10. II.

Latin:

Vers. 40. ἐπείσθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ) Nempe ne Apostolos occi- derent: non autem ut intactos dimitterent: quod tamen æquum fuerat, & congruens iis, quæ dixerat Gamaliel.

δείραντες) Cum loris eos cecidissent, more Hebræo. Con- fer. quæ infra XXII. 19. 2. Cor. XI. 24. prædictum id Matth. I. 17. XXI. 35. XXIII. 34. Marci XII. 5. XIII. 9. Luc. X. 10. II.

## 5:41
Vers. 41. And they departed rejoicing from the presence of the council, that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for the name of Jesus) Mindful of the Master's precept: Matth. V. 11. 12. A great virtue, to consider the very insult an honor, for a good cause: in that old Manuscript, 'of Jesus' is not added, and in like manner in the Epistle of John III. 7. it is read in the same Manuscript, 'for the sake of the name', namely, antonomastically.

Latin:

Vers. 41. ἐπορεύοντο χαίροντες ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ συνεδρίου, ὅτι κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀτιμασθῆναι) Me- mores præcepti herilis: Matth. V. 11. 12. Magna virtus, i- psam contumeliam honori ducere, ob bonam causam: in Manuscripto illo vetere non additur τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, parique mo- do in Epistola Johannis III. 7. legitur in eodem Manuscri- pto, ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ὀνόματος, nimirum ἀντονομαστικῶς.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

Provoked by the murmuring of the Greeks because of the widows neglected in the distribution, the Apostles appoint seven Deacons, and among them Stephen, as the number of the faithful increases, and many priests also joining them: and when the Libertines and others, by disputing, opposed Stephen, who was full of faith and the gift of miracles, and could not resist him, they suborned false witnesses, as if he had uttered blasphemies against Moses and God, and having stirred up the people, and the elders, and the lawyers, they dragged the same to the Sanhedrin and accused him, because he preached the destruction of the temple, and the change of worship, while all in the council looked upon the face of Stephen as the face of an Angel. The parts are two: I. The appointment of the seven Deacons for the distribution of goods, up to v. 7. II. The false accusation of Stephen, who was invincible in disputing, up to v. 15.

PART I. The appointment of the seven Deacons.

Vers. 1. Γογγυσμός) Thus the plural Hebrew word תלונות is accustomed to be translated in Exodus XVI. 7. 8. and elsewhere.

τῶν ἑλληνιστῶν) Jews by religion, but who, because they had lived before in Alexandria and neighboring places, had retained from there the custom of reading the holy scriptures in Greek. אלעסתין דמתרגמי as the Talmudists say regarding this matter, which custom remained until the times of Justinian, as we know from Novella CXLVI. That such an Alexandrian Synagogue existed in Jerusalem is noted in the Glosses to Chapter II of Esther, and in Caesarea in the Jerusalem Talmud: And below IX. 29. the Syriac interprets 'Hellenists' as Jews who knew Greek. Chrysostom, Oecumenius and

Theophylact, those who speak in Greek. Most of these did not understand Hebrew, among whom was Philo, although he was a Jew born of Jews. For the sake of such people, the grandson of Sirach translated the book of his grandfather.

It pleases others that these Hellenists were not Jews born in Greece, but Gentile Greek proselytes, such as Camerarius, Salmasius, as also Sanctius in Zech. IX. 11. no. 83. Nevertheless, the opinion of Grotius seems preferable, which was also that of Scaliger, Drusius, Funccius, Fornandus, Tirinus, Pelargus, Arcularius, B. Gerbardus, Heinsius; since the Gentiles were only admitted in Acts X, and in chapter XI Peter was rebuked because he preached the Gospel to the uncircumcised, and Josephus, Antiq. book XII, ch. 5 and book XIV, ch. 9, reports that the Hebrews also led colonies into Greece.

they were overlooked in the ministry) Namely, either because they were sick or burdened with infants, they received less than the women born in Judea. This distribution is called here ministry. Thus to minister in Mark I. 31, Luke IV. 39, VIII. 3, John XII. 2, Rom. XV. 25, Heb. VI. 10. Emperor Julian also called it ministry of tables in this sense; this happened because the Apostles did not use certain men for this matter, but now these, now those: and indeed Jews born in Judea: that was corrected by the institution of the college of deacons and by the inclusion of Hellenists as well.

Others think the women of the Hellenists were neglected because they were passed over in the office of dispensing alms. The Ethiopic translator, on the other hand, along with some others, places their contempt in the fact that the sole care of the poor was imposed upon them. But it is in the open that they are said to be neglected because the goods collected in common were not distributed to them equally alongside the others.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Murmure Græcorum ob neglectas in distribu- tione viduas, provocati Apostoli septem Dia- conos constituunt, & inter eos Stepha- num, accrescente numero fidelium, iisq; et- iam multis sacerdotibus accedentibus: & quum Stephano pleno fide & dono miracu- lorum Libertini, & alii disputando se op- ponerent, nec ei resistere valerent, falsos te- stes, quasi contra Mosen & Deum blasphe- mias protulerit, subornarunt, commotoq́; populo, & senioribus, ac legisperitis eum- dem ad Synedrium abreptum accusarunt, quod prædicaret templi destructionem, & cultus mutationem, omnibus in concilio fa- ciem Stephani ut faciem Angeli intuentibus. Partes sunt duæ: I. Septem Diaconorum ob di- spensationem bonorum constitutio ad v. 7. II. Ste- phani in disputando invicti falsa accusatio ad v. 15.

PARS I. Septem Diaconorum constitutio.

Vers. 1. Γογγυσμός) Sic verti solet vox Hebræa pluralis תלונות Exodi. XVI. 7. 8. & alibi.

τῶν ἑλληνιστῶν) Judæorum religione, sed qui cum Ale- xandriæ & vicinis in locis vixissent antea, morem inde re- tinuerant sacra scripta legendi Græce. אלעסתין דמתרגמי ut ajunt hac de re Thalmudici, qui mos mansit ad Justinia- ni tempora, ut cognoscimus ex Novella CXLVI. Talem Alexandrinam Synagogam fuisse Hierosolymis, notatur in Glossis ad Caput II. Estheris, & Cæsareæ in Thalmudie Hie- rosolymitano:Et inf. IX. 29. Syrus ἰωνιστὰς interpretatur Ju- dæos, qui noverant Græce. Chrysostomus, Oecumenius &

Theophylactus τοὺς ἑλληνιστὶ φθεγγομένους. Horum plerique Hebraice non intelligebant, quorum fuit & Philo, quamquam Judæus ex Judæis ortus. In talium gratiam librum avi sui transtulit nepos Sirachides.

Aliis placet, Hellenistas hos non fuisse Judæos in Græcia natos, sed Gentiles Græcos proselytos, utpote Camerario, Salmasio, ut & Sanctio in Zach. IX. 11. num. 83. Præferenda tamen videtur Grotii sententia, quæ etiam Scaligeri fuit, Drusii, Funccii, Fornandi, Tirini, Pelargi, Arcularii, B. Gerbardi, Heinsii; siquidem gentiles demum Act. X. admissi fuerint, & cap. XI. Petrus reprehensus sit, quod incircumcisis Evangelium prædicarit, & Ebræos colonias in Græciam quoque duxisse, perhibeat Josephus l. XII. Antiq. c. 5. & l. XIV. c. 9.

παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ) Nempe aut ægrotæ aut infantibus oneratæ minus accipiebant, quam mulieres in Judæa natæ. Hæc distributio vocatur hic διακονία. Sic διακονεῖν Marci I. 31. Luc. IV. 39. VIII. 3. Johan. XII. 2. Rom. XV. 25. Hebr. VI. 10. Διακονίαν τραπέζων hoc sensu dixit etiam Julianus Imperator id accidebat, quia non certis hominibus, sed modo his, modo illis Apostoli ad hanc rem utebantur: & quidem Judæis in Judæa natis: id correctum instituto diaconorum collegio & allectis etiam Hellenistis.

Alii neglectas fuisse mulieres τῶν ἑλληνιστῶν, quod in officio dispensandi Eleemosynas præteritæ fuerint. Æthiops contra interpres cum quibusdam aliis contemtum earum in eo locant, quod ipsis sola cura pauperum imposita. Sed in aprico est, neglectas dici, quod bona in communione collata non ex æquo ipsis juxta cum aliis distributa sint.

## 6:2
Verse 2. the twelve) Properly, because Matthias had filled the number.

the multitude of the disciples) For at that time the government of the Church was such as Plato says once existed at Athens, an aristocracy with the consent of the multitude. Add also with leadership.

it is not pleasing) לא ישר. For ישר is translated as pleasing and signifies that which ought to please. Elsewhere it is translated as just, straight, right.

us having forsaken the word of God) He says this because what is given to other business is taken away from preaching: therefore having forsaken, here means, caring less than would be the case if we were relieved of that burden.

to minister to tables) To give to individual associations what is necessary for food and clothing: thus this ministry is described by the greater part. See what we said above II. 44.

Sanctius, Lorinus, and Cornel. Tirinus extend this to the table and supper of the Eucharist; some refer it to agapes or sacred banquets. But they are more correctly understood as common tables, according to Origen, Jerome, Chrysostom, Oecumenius, Bede, and Cajetan, Vol. I, opuscula, tract II, as also by the Julian Synod in Balsamon, ch. X.

Latin:

Vers. 2. οἱ δώδεκα) Proprie, quia Matthias numerum impleverat.

τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν) Erat enim eo tempore Ecclesiæ regimen tale, quale olim Athenis fuisse dicit Plato ἀριστοκρατίαν μετ᾿ εὐδοκίας πλήθους. Adde & cum principatu.

οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστι) לא ישר. Nam ישר ἀρεστὸν vertitur & significat id, quod placere debeat. Alibi vertitur δίκαιον, εὐθὺ, ὀρθόν.

ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ) Hoc ideo dicit, quia quod aliis negotiis datur id decedit prædicationi: itaque καταλείψαντας, hic est, minus curantes, quam fieret, si eo onere levaremur.

διακονεῖν τραπέζαις) Dare singulis sodalitiis quæ ad victum & vestitum sunt necessaria: ita διακονία hæc à majore parte describitur. Vide, quæ diximus supra II. 44.

Ad mensam ac cœnam Eucharistiam hæc extendunt Sanctius, Lorinus, Cornel. Tirinus, nonnulli ad agapas seu convivia sacra referunt. Sed de mensis communibus rectius intelliguntur ac Origene, Hieronymo, Chrysost. Oecumenio, Beda, Cajetano T. I. opusc. tr. II. ut & à Synodo Juliana apud Balsamon. c. X.

## 6:3
Verse 3. look ye out therefore, brethren) ברו לכם, 1 Sam. XVII. 8, where the Greeks: choose for yourselves a man.

from among you, of good report) He gives a form to the Church, so that those who are chosen for ministries may have the testimony of those with whom they have lived. Thus below XVI. 2.

full of the Holy Spirit) Endowed with excellent gifts. See below 8.

and of wisdom) And instructed in the Holy Scriptures, so that, if there were need, they could dispute from them, as Stephen did.

for this business) For this use. על מלאכת הזאת by the example, of course, of those who were called in the Synagogue Parnasim, by Epiphanius Azanitae: the whole government of the early Church was conformed to the form of the Synagogue: what was behaving well, there was no need to change. They had such also among the Essenes, of whom Philo says: they serve as free men, performing the diaconal duties. Josephus calls such men receivers and appointed overseers.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ἐπισκέψασθε οὖν ἀδελφοὶ) ברו לכם, 1 Sam. XVII. 8. ubi Græci: ἐκλέξατε ἑαυτοῖς ἄνδρα.

ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους) Formam dat Ecclesiæ, ut, qui ad ministeria eliguntur, testimonium habeant eorum, quibuscum vixere. Sic infra XVI. 2.

πλήρεις πνεύματος ἁγίου) Donis eximiis præditos. Vide infra 8.

καὶ σοφίας) Et in Sacris literis institutos, ut, si opus esset, ex iis disputare possent, sicut fecit Stephanus.

ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης) Ad hunc usum. על מלאכת הזאת exemplo scilicet illorum, qui in Synagoga dicebantur פרנסים, Epiphanio Ἀζανῖται: totum primæ Ecclesiæ regimen conformatum fuit ad formam Synagogæ: quæ bene se hebebant, nihil opus erat mutari. Habuere tales & Esseni, de quibus Philo: ἐλεύθεροι δὲ ὑπηρετοῦσι τὰς διακονικὰς χρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες. Tales Josephus ἀποδέκτας & χειροτονητοὺς ἐπιμελητάς vocat.

## 6:4
Ver. 4. But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word) We will be assiduous both in leading the people in prayers to GOD, and in instructing the people: which is, however, to be understood in such a way that the Apostles did not abdicate from themselves the inspection of the Deacons, just as the Bishops did not do afterwards: but that inspection required less time than the daily administration. Ignatius to the Trallians: what are deacons, but imitators of the angelic powers, ministering to him (namely the Bishop) a pure and blameless ministry.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν) Assidui erimus tum in præeundo plebi in precibus ad DEUM, tum in plebe instituenda: quod sic tamen intelligendum est, ut inspectionem in Diaconos Apostoli à se non abdicaverint, sicut nec Episcopi postea fecere: sed ea inspectio minus exigebat temporis, quam quotidiana administratio. Ignatius ad Trallenses: τί δὲ διάκονοι, ἀλλʼ ἢ μιμηταὶ τῶν ἀγγελικῶν δυνάμεων, λειτουργοῦν- τες ἀυτῷ (nempe Episcopo) λειτουργίαν καθαρὰν καὶ ἄμωμον.

## 6:5
Ver. 5. Stephen a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch) All these names are Greek, which is not surprising in Alexandrians: but in Jews born in Judea, I believe the names were Hebrew, which Luke rendered in Greek. Thus I believe the Apostle Philip was called by the Hebrews Pi-lebab, mouth agreeing with the heart, or Pele-pi, admirable mouth. When Nicolas is said to have been a proselyte from Antioch, understand a Ger Tzedek, that is, circumcised, and subject to the law by his own will. For the Apostles never doubted that such could be received into the Church, but whether the same should be done for those who were Gerei Toshav, was a graver question, and one needing an oracle. This is the Nicolas, from whom the Nicolaitans in the Apocalypse, and mentioned by the fathers, took their name. Some accuse him. Others prefer that his words were twisted into a perversion.

That some of these names were translated from Hebrew into Greek by Luke, Grotius asserts rashly. And no less wrongly does he believe Philip was called by the Hebrews Pi-lebab, mouth agreeing with the heart, or Pele-pi, admirable mouth. Since Philippos is undoubtedly a Greek name, horseman or lover of horses.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Στέφανον ἄνδρα πλήρη πίστεως καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον, καὶ Πρόχορον, καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα, καὶ Παρμενᾶν, καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα) Nomina hæc omnia sunt Græca, quod non mirum in Alexandrinis: in judæis vero in Judæa natis, credo nomina fuisse Hebræa, quæ Lucas Græce extulerit. Sic Apostolum Philippum credo Hebræis vocatum פי לבר os cordi congruens, aut פלא פי os admirabile. Nicolaus cum dicitur fuisse ab Antiochia proselytus, intellige גר צדק, id est, circumcisum, & legi sua voluntate subditum. Nam tales quin in Ecclesiam recipi possent nunquam dubitavere Apostoli, sed an idem fieri deberet de iis qui erant גרי תושב, gravior erat quæstio, & oraculi indigens. Hic est Nicolaus, à quo nomen traxere Nicolaitæ in Apocalypsi, & patribus memorati. Alii ipsum accusant. Alii verba ejus in pravum detorta malunt.

Nomina horum nonnulla ex Ebræo in Græcum translata esse à Luca, temere asserit Grotius. Nec minus perperam Philippum credit Ebræis vocatum פי לבא os cordi congruens, aut פלא פי os admirabile. Quum Φίλιππος indubie Græcum sit nomen, eques vel amator equorum.

## 6:6
Ver. 6. they laid their hands on them) A sign of the mandated ministry, 1 Tim. V. 22. Thus the people chose a king, the Prophets anointed in the name of God. What the Apostles did here, the same did the Bishops afterwards, both in ordaining Presbyters and Deacons, even then when the election was in the power of the order and the people.

Grotius rightly acknowledges that the election was once in the power of the people: which the Papists undeservedly deny to them, restricting the right of electing to the sacred ministry alone: see Bellarm. book on Clerics, ch. II. § last. But while he says that the right of ordaining belonged to Bishops alone after the Apostles, he is destitute of the authority of the ancients; some English indeed gratify the Papists in this, but that is not surprising regarding the Bishops, Carleton and Goodwin of Llandaff, Bilson of Coventry, Davenant of Salisbury, Hall of Exeter, Montague of Chichester, Morton of Durham, who strove to make their Episcopal dignity more illustrious by this pact: but it is not only certain by divine right that ordination is not proper to Bishops alone, as they are distinguished from Presbyters, 1 Tim. IV. 14. Acts IX. 17. ch. XXII, 12. but in antiquity also the distinction was not precisely observed in this part between Bishops and Presbyters, nay Chrysostom, when he teaches that Bishops rose above Presbyters by ordination alone in 1 Tim. III. Homily XI, says that in this one thing they seem to have circumvented or defrauded the Presbyters, in which alone they seem to have the advantage over the Presbyters: and Epiphanius himself concedes to Aerius, heresy LXXV, that at the beginning of the Church Presbyters validly ordained: which also Johannes de Artis, a Parisian predecessor, teaches in book 1 against Salmasius ch. X from Epiphanius: Jerome however everywhere: that the Presbyter is the same as the Bishop, and that the order is held only under the constitution of ecclesiastical law, and that Bishops are greater than Presbyters, which he proves from Acts XX, Phil. I, Heb. XIII, 1 Pet. V in his Commentary. to Titus I. and in the Epistle to Evagrius: whence the Papists assert only rashly that priestly ordination performed by a Presbyter is invalid by divine right: and the blessed Hülsemann shows solidly in his Apology of the Evangelical ministry for the minister of ordination, that neither Bellarmine, nor Coccius, nor any other wagoner from the earlier councils, or even the Fathers, could bring anything against the validity of priestly ordination performed by a Presbyter, but that the ordination of Presbyters performed by other Presbyters in the absence of Bishops remained valid in all centuries in the Greek Church, and the Latin even at the time of the Council of Florence, nor did the Council of Trent itself [speak] about the ordination of Presbyters being void by divine right dare to define anything. And David Blondellus, in his *Apologia pro sententia Hieronymi*, pages 309 et seqq., adduced examples from all ages throughout the Churches of the whole world of a presbyter ordained by other presbyters from Egypt, Asia, Africa, Greece, Macedonia, Pontus, Scotland, Britain, and the Gauls: he also adduced testimonies from modern Anglican Bishops, who admit that in a case of necessity presbyters can ordain, such as George Downame, Bishop of Derry in England, Lancelot Andrewes, Prelate of the Winchester see, Richard FitzRalph, Archbishop of Armagh, etc. What of the fact that Bouchellus in his Decreta Ecclesiae Gallicanae, lib. III. tit. II. c. 114, cites from a Capitular of Charlemagne what Leo I. had decreed in Epist. LXXXVI. to the Bishops of Germany and Gaul, that if there be Presbyters who are upright and live virtuously, concerning whom it is not certain whether they were ordained by Bishops, they are to be left in their office, and no doubt is to be raised concerning their order; and that Papists acknowledge the ordinations of the Greeks as legitimate, even though not all Greeks are ordained by Bishops, and in Italy, Spain, Portugal, Gaul, and Germany, Abbots even now ordain Priests of their own order, and seculars? The impudence of Grotius in his Votum pro pace, p. 118, contending that it is by Apostolic prescription that no one is to be held a Presbyter unless a Bishop has solemnly laid hands upon him, was, as was fitting, chastised by the blessed Hulsemann, our venerable father-in-law, in the cited Disputation, §. XLVII. seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ἐπέθηκαν ἀυτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας) Signum mandati ministerii, 1. Timoth. V. 22. Sic populus eligebat regem, Prophetæ ungebant Dei nomine. Quod hic fecere Apostoli, idem Episcopi postea, tum in Presbyteris, tum in Diaconis ordinandis, etiam tunc cum electio esset penes ordinem, ac plebem.

Recte agnoscit Grotius electionem penes plebem quondam fuisse: cui hoc immerito denegant Papistæ, ad solum ministerium sacrum jus eligendi restringentes: vid. Bellarm. l. de Cleric. c. II. §. ult. Sed dum Episcopis solis jus ordinandi post Apostolos convenisse ait, autoritate veterum destituitur; Gratificantur id quidem Papistis Angli nonnulli, sed non mirum id de Episcopis, Carle- tono & Goodwino Landavensibus, Bilsono Conven- triensi, Davenantio Sarisburiensi, Hallo, Exo- niensi, Montacutio Cislacestriensi, Mortonio Du- nelmensi, qui hoc pacto Episcopale suum ἀξίωμα illustrius reddere satagere: verum non tantum ju- re divino certum est, solis Episcopis, uti à Presbyte- ris distinguuntur, ordinationem haud propriam esse 1. Tim. IV. 14. Act. IX. 17. c. XXII, 12. sed in antiquitate etiam non præcise hac in parte inter Epi- scopos & Presbyteros observatum est discrimen, imo Chrysostomus, cum docet, sola χειροτονίᾳ Episcopos ascendisse super Presbyteros in 1. ad Tim. III. Homil. XI. in hoc uno, ait, videri eos circumve- nisse vel defraudasse Presbyteros, ᾗ τοῦτο μόνον δοκοῦ- σιν πλεονεκτεῖν τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους: & concedit ipse Epiphanius Ærio hæres. LXXV. quod initio Ecclesiæ Presbyteri valide ordinarint: quod etiam Jo- hannes de Artis Antecessor Parisinus l. 1. contra Salmasium cap. X. ex Epiphanio docet: Hieronymus vero passim: Eundem esse Presbyterum, qui & Episcopus, nec nisi sub legis Ecclesiasticæ constitutio- ne ordinem teneri, & Episcopos Presbyteris majores esse, quod ex Act. XX. Phil. I. Ebr. XIII. 1. Petr. V. probat in Comment. ad Tit. I. & in Epistola ad Evagium: unde non nisi temere Papistæ asserunt, ordinationem sacerdotalem à Presbytero factam jure divino invalidam esse: & ostendit solide B. Hül- semannus in Apologia ministerii Evangelici pro ministro ordinationis, neque Bellarminum, neque Coccium, neque alium quemdam hamaxarium ex prioribus conciliis, vel etiam Patribus, contra valorem ordinationis sacerdotalis, per Presbyterum factæ, quicquam afferre potuisse, quin mansisse ordinationem Presbyterorum ab aliis Presbyteris in defectu Episcoporum peractam seculis omnibus ratam in Ecclesia Græca, & Latina etiam tempore concilii Florentini, nec ipsum concilium Tridentinum de Presbyterorum irrita jure divino ordinatione quicquam definire ausum fuisse. Et adduxit David Blondellus Apologia pro sententia Hieronymi pag. 309. seqq. exempla omnium aetatum per universi orbis Ecclesias ordinatorum per alios Presbyte- ros presbyterum ex Aegypto, Asia, Africa, Graecia, Macedonia, Ponto, Scotia, Britannia, Galliis: addu- xit etiam testimonia e modernis Anglicanis Epi- scopis, quod fateantur in casu necessitatis Presbyte- ros ordinare posse, utpote Georgii Dounami Derensis in Anglia Episcopi, Lancellotti Andrea Wentoni- ensium Praesulis, Richardi Fizrai, Armachani Ar- chi-Episcopi &c. Quid quod Bouchellus in de- cretis Ecclesiae Gallicanae lib. III. tit. II. c. 114. ex Capi- tulari Caroli M. quod Leo I. in Epist XXCVI. ad Episcopos Germaniae & Galliae sanxerat, adferat, si Presbyteri sint, qui probi sint, & virtuose vivant, de quibus non constet, an sint ab Episcopis ordinati, eos relinquendos esse in officio suo, nec dubium de ordine movendum; quodque Papistae ordinationes Graeco- rum pro legitimis agnoscant, etsi non omnes Grae- ci per Episcopos ordinent, & in Italia, Hispania, Portugallia, Gallia, Germania Abbates etiamnum ordinent Sacerdotes sui ordinis, & seculares. Im- pudentiam Grotii in voto suo pro pace p. 118. con- tendentis, quod ex Apostolico praescripto hoc sit, ut Presbyter non habeatur, nisi cui manus solemniter imposuerit Episcopus, ut par erat, castigavit B. Hulse- mannus Socer noster venerandus p. m. laudata Di- sputatione §. XLVII. seqq.

## 6:7
V. 7. Πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων) That is, many from the family and retinue of the priests. See a similar history in John VII. 46, 47.

- ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει) Through faith they obeyed the precepts of Christ and were baptized,

PART II. The false accusation of Stephen, who was invincible in disputation.

Latin:

V. 7. Πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων) Id est, multi ex familia & co- mitatu Sacerdotum. Vide simile historiam Joh. VII. 46. 47.

- ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει) Per fidem obedivere Christi praeceptis Baptizati sunt,

PARS II. Stephani in disputando invicti falsa accusatio.

## 6:8
Vers. 8. Πλήρης πίστεως καὶ δυνάμεως) In the manuscript which I have often mentioned, and in other manuscripts, it is πλήρης χάριτος. And the Syriac and Latin read it thus.

Latin:

Vers. 8. Πλήρης πίστεως καὶ δυνάμεως) In Manuscripto, quem saepe dixi, & in aliis Manuscriptis est, πλήρης χάριτος. Et sic legere Syrus & Latinus.

## 6:9
Vers. 9. Λιβερτίνων) Many Libertini of the Jewish religion in Rome. That Caecilius, against whom is the divination of Cicero, was of them, as Plutarch teaches us. Tacitus, Annals II, says that four thousand of the freedman class, infected with the Jewish superstition, were sent to Sardinia. Josephus also mentions them. These were partly proselytes, partly Jews by origin, captured in war and manumitted. Philo in his embassy: πῶς ὖν ἀπεδέχετο τὴν πέραν τῶ Τιβέρεως, ποταμῶ τῆς ῥώμης ἀποτομὴν, ἧν οὐκ ἠγνόει κατεχομένην κὶ οἰκυμένην πρὸς Ἰυδαίων. ῥωμαῖοι δὲ ἦσαν οἱ πλείυς, ἀπελευθερωθέντες αἰχμάλω- τοι γὰρ ἀχθεντες εἰς Ἰταλίαν, ὑπὸ τῶν κτησαμένων ἠλευθερώθησαν. At their expense this synagogue was built in Jerusalem, and learned teachers were placed in it. The Jews relate that there were 480 synagogues in Jerusalem.

The opinion of Chrysostom and Bede is not unlike this, that the Libertini arose from those whom the Romans had brought as captives into their city, who obtained their freedom. This has pleased most interpreters. Nor does it displease us. It is certainly to be preferred to the suspicion of those who judged that 'Libyos' or 'Lybicos' should be read, or with Jacob Gothofredus in his dissertation on 1 Cor. XI. § 9, that the word Λιβασίνων should be substituted for Λιβερτίνων, against the unanimous consent of the Greek codices, the Syriac, the Ethiopic, and the Arabic of the Erpenius edition.

κὶ Κυρηναίων) Many Jews in Cyrenaica, Josephus XVI. 10.

κὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων) Where they had also obtained equal rights with the Macedonians. See what we noted regarding the third book of Maccabees.

κὶ Ἀσίας) And Jews in Asia. Josephus XII. 3, XIV. 17, XVI. 4. See also below XIX.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Λιβερτίνων) Libertini Romae multi Judaicae reli- gionis. Eorum fuit Caecilius ille, in quem est divinatio Cice- ronis, ut nos Plutarchus docet. Tacitus Annal. II. ait quatuor millia libertini generis superstitione Judaica infecta, missa in Sardinia. Meminit & Josephus. Hi partim erant prosely- ti, partim Judaei origine & bello capti ac manumissi. Philo in legatione: πῶς ὖν ἀπεδέχετο τὴν πέραν τῶ Τιβέρεως, ποταμῶ τῆς ῥώμης ἀποτομὴν, ἧν οὐκ ἠγνόει κατεχομένην κὶ οἰκυμένην πρὸς Ἰυδαίων. ῥωμαῖοι δὲ ἦσαν οἱ πλείυς, ἀπελευθερωθέντες αἰχμάλω- τοι γὰρ ἀχθεντες εἰς Ἰταλίαν, ὑπὸ τῶν κτησαμένων ἠλευθερώθησαν. Horum sumtu structa Hierosolymis haec Synagoga, & positi in ea magistri eruditi. Narrant Judaei Hierosolymis fuisse Sy- nagogas CCCCLXXX.

Non absimilis est Chrysostomi, & Bedae sententia, Libertinos ortos ab eis, quos Romani in suam ur- bem captos adduxerant, qui libertatem adepti sunt. Quae plerisque Interpret. placuit. Nec no- bis displicet. Praeferenda certe eorum suspicioni, qui Lybios vel Lybicos legendos, vel cum Jacobo Gothofredo in dissert. ad 1. Cor. XI. §. 9. vocem Λι- βασίνων pro Λιβερτίνων substituendam, contra una- nimem Codicum Graecorum, Syri, Aethiopis, & Ara- bis editionis Erpen. consensum judicarunt.

κὶ Κυρηναίων) Multi in Cyrenaica Iudaei, Joseph. XVI. 10.

κὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων) Ubi etiam jus par cum Macedonibus erant adepti. Vide, quae ad Maccabaicum tertium nota- vimus.

κὶ Ασίας) Murimi & in Asia Iudaei. Josephus XII. 3. XIV. 17. XVI. 4. Vide & infra XIX.

## 6:10
Vers. 10. τῇ σοφίᾳ) Because of the Scriptures, which he knew.

and by the Spirit by whom he spoke) Because of the divine power directing his words, according to the promise: Matt. X. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 10. τῇ σοφίᾳ) Propter Scripturas, quas noverat.

κὶ τῷ πνεύματι ὧ ἐλάλει) Propter divinam vim verba e- jus dirigentem, ex promisso: Matth. X. 20.

## 6:11
Ver. 11. then they suborned) They suborned. Thus Cicero speaks of witnesses in his defense of Roscius, and Pliny in his Panegyric.

blasphemous words) נאצוץי Ezek. XXXV. 12. where in the Greek: of the voice of blasphemies.

Latin:

Vers. 11. τότε ὑπέβαλον) Subornarunt. Sic de testi- bus loquuntur Cicero pro Roscio & in Panegyrico Pli- nius.

ῥήματα βλάσφημα) נאצוץי Ezek. XXXV. 12. ubi in Graeco: φωνῆς βλασφημιῶν.

## 6:12
Ver. 12. And they stirred up the people) קשר. which is usually translated into Greek as to conspire.

and the elders and the scribes) The Sanhedrin, as the following shows.

coming upon him) By a gathering. Ver. 13 False witnesses) Mixing truth with falsehoods, like those who had spoken against Christ. For they wanted it to be believed that those things which Stephen had said were spoken by him with abomination of the Temple and the law. Against such witnesses is Ps. LII.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν) קשר. quod Graece verti solet συσφίρειν.

κὶ τὺς πρεσβυτέρυς κὶ τὺς γραμματεῖς) Synedrium, ut ostendunt sequentia.

ἐπιστάντες) Concursu fact. Vers. 13 Μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς) Vera falsis miscentes, ut ii qui in Christum dixerant. Volebant enim credi ea, quæ dixerat Stephanus, dicta ab eo cum abominatione Templi & legis. Contra tales testes est, Ps. LII.

## 6:14
V. 14. that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place) That is, the temple. But Daniel IX. 26 had predicted the same. Formerly, when Jeremiah predicted similar things, he came into danger, but undeservedly, as the wiser and more equitable judged: as can be seen in Jerem. XXVI. 16 and following.

and shall change the customs which Moses delivered to us) Stephen had not said these things: but perhaps he had cited the passage of Malachi I. 11 and other similar ones.

Latin:

V. 14. ὅτι ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον) Id est, templum. At idem prædixerat Daniel IX. 26. Olim cum similia prædiceret Jeremias in periculum venit, sed immerito, ut sapientiores & æquiores judicabant: ut videre est Jerem. XXVI. 16. & sequentibus.

καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη, ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς) Hæc non dixe- rat Stephanius: sed forte allegaverat locum Malachiæ I. 11. & similes alios.

## 6:15
Ver. 15. as it were the face of an angel) That is, he had gravity joined with the utmost gentleness. See above 8.
