Vers. 55. δόξαν Θεῦ) Fulgorem quemdam, quo Dei ma- jestas repræsentabatur. Vide Exodi XXIV. 17. c. XXXIII. 18. 22. Ezech. I. 1.

## 7:56
Verse 56. and the Son of man) See what we said at Matthew VIII. v. 20.

standing at the right hand of God) Not sitting, as he is described elsewhere to show royal dignity, but standing as if prepared for the aid of his own. For both the Greek παραστάται and the Hebrew עמד often have that meaning of helpers.

Ambrose explains more fully in book X, Epistle LXXXIII. Jesus was standing as an advocate, he was standing as one solicitous, so that he might help Stephen his athlete who was struggling. He was standing as if prepared to crown his martyr. What he said about the advocate, he explained in Sermon LX. He is said to sit for the power of a King, he is suggested to stand for the goodness of an intercessor. Christ is a Judge when he sits: he is an advocate when he rises. Clearly a Judge to the Jews, an advocate to the Christians.

Latin:

Vers. 56. κὰὶ τὸν ὑὸν τῦ ἀνθρώπω) Vide, quæ diximus ad Matth. VIII. v. 20.

ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τῦ Θεῦ) Non sedentem, quomodo alibi describitur ad ostendendam regiam dignitatem, sed stan- tem quasi paratam in opem suorum. Nam & auxiliatores Græcis παραστάται & עמד apud Hebræos sæpe eum habet sensum.

Plenius Ambrosius explicat l. X. Epist. LXXXIII. Stabat Jesus quasi advocatus, stabat quasi solicitus, ut Stephanum athletam suum certantem juvaret. Stabat quasi paratus, ut coronaret, ut suum Marty- rem. Quod de advocato dixit, exposuit Serm. LX. Pro potestate Regis sedere dicitur, pro bonitate inter- cessoris stare suggeritur. Judex est Christus, cum re- sidet: advocatus est, cum assurgit. Judex plane Ju- dæis, advocatus Christianis.

## 7:57
Verse 57. and crying out with a loud voice) Understand these things, not of the senators, but of the standing crowd: for all these things were done through a sedition, which a clamor is accustomed to accompany.

συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν) συνέχειν that is ἰέναι, ואספו.

κὴ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν) As if by a judgment of zeal, which they were accustomed to usurp while the republic stood, but only against those who were instigators to the Jews for false worships. Such persons were accustomed to be stoned: Deut. XIII. 6. See what we have said at that place & concerning the Law of War II. c. XX. §. 9. You have some examples in the Maccabees & below c. 23.13. Joseph Albo mentions this law in Philo de Monarchia: and it is permitted to all who have a zeal for virtue to exact punishments from the hand without delay, not leading them to a court, nor to a council, nor in general to an authority, but to make use of the passion of hatred for evil and love for God that has come upon them for the inexorable punishments of the impious, thinking councilors, judges, generals, assemblymen, accusers, witnesses, laws, the people, so that with no one standing in the way, they may fearlessly contend with great zeal for holiness. Moreover, the priests, even when they were under the Romans, were accustomed to connive at such things: see Joseph. xv. 8. who also mentions this custom elsewhere. But these men sinned here in a twofold way: first against the law, which even in a free republic did not want that popular judgment to be exercised, except against the authors of idolatry, such as Stephen was not: then against the Romans, who had taken away from them all right of capital punishments. And the audacity of those men, whom Josephus calls zealots, increasing daily, finally both stirred up the anger of the Romans and brought destruction to the city and the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 57. κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ) Hæc intellige, non de senatoribus, sed de adstante plebe: facta enim hæc o- mnia per seditionem, quam comitari solet clamor.

συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν) συνέχειν id est ἰέναι, ואספו.

κὴ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν) Quasi ex judicio zeli, quod stante republica usurpare solebant, sed tantum in eos, qui Judæis auctores essent ad falsos cultus. Solebant autem tales lapidari: Deut. XIII. 6. Vide, quæ diximus ad eũ locũ & de Jure Belli II. c. XX. §. 9. Exempla habes aliquot in Macca- baicis & inf. c. 23.13. meminit ejus juris Joseph. Albo, Philo de Monarchia: κὼ ἐπιτετράφθαι δὲ καλὸν ἅπασι τοῖς ζῆλον ἔχουσιν ἀρετῆς ἐκ χειρὸς ἀναπράττειν ἀνυπερθέτως τὰς τιμωρίας, μήτ’ εἰς δικαστήριον, μήτ’ εἰς βυλευτήριον μήτ’ συνόλως ἐπ’ ἀρχὴν ἄγοντας, ἀλλὰ τῷ παραστάντι μισοπονήρῳ πάθει κὴ φιλοθέῳ καταχρῆσθαι πρὸς τὰς τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀπαραιτήτυς κολάσεις, νομίσαντας αὑτὸς ὑπὸ τῦ καιρῦ τὰ πάντα γεγενῆσθ, βυλευτὰς, δικαστὰς, στρατηγὺς,ἐκκλησιαστὰς, κατηγόρυς, μάρτυρας, νόμυς, δῆμον,ἵνα μηδενὸς ὄντων ἐμποδὼν, ἄφοβοι συνόδῳ πολλῇ παραγωνίζωνται ὁσιότητι. Solebant autem sacerdotes, etiam cum sub Romanis essent, ad talia connivere: vide Joseph. xv. 8. qui & alibi hujus moris meminit. Verum duplici modo hic peccabant isti homines: primum in legem, quæ etiam libera republica judicium illud populare exerceri noluit, nisi in auctores idololatriæ, qualis non erat Stephanus: deinde in Romanos, qui ipsis ademerant jus omne capitalium suppliciorum. Atque istorum hominum, quos ζηλωτὰς Josephus vocat, crescens indies audacia tandem & iram excitavit Romanorum, & urbi, temploque exitium attulit.

## 7:58
Vers. 58. and the witnesses) Although these things were done through sedition, as we have said, nevertheless they retained something of the legitimate custom, for it was the duty of the witnesses to throw the first stones, and thus, if anything false lay underneath, to make themselves the sources of the slaughter, but to absolve the people, who followed their authority. See Deut 17. and Moses of Coucy, commandment 99.

Although those things were done through sedition, the judges nevertheless could also cry out: Who were indeed the spark and trumpet in this sedition. The Jews no longer had the right of capital punishment, John xviii. 31. Therefore they did not do these things by way of law, but through sedition: yet retaining something of the legitimate law, inasmuch as the witnesses were accustomed to throw the first stones. Grotius observes here, and in book II of the Law of War and Peace, proving it from the Maccabees and Acts xxiii. 13, that they still exercised this while the republic stood against those who were authors of false cults to the Jews, which they falsely judged concerning Stephen. But those things were done in fact, not in law.

they laid aside their garments) Namely, so that they might be more unencumbered. For huge stones were accustomed to be thrown by the witnesses.

young Saul) Who was then accustomed to frequent the school of Gamaliel for the sake of studies, Acts xxii. 3. But carried away by heat, he allowed himself to be drawn from the gentleness of his master to more atrocious things by the examples of many. Phil. iii. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 58. κὼ οἱ μάρτυρες) Quanquam per seditionem hæc, ut diximus, agebantur, tamen aliquid de legitimo more retinebant, testium enim erat primos jacere lapides, ac sic semet, si quid falsi subesset, fontes facere cædis, populum vero, qui ipsorum auctoritatem sequebatur, absolvere. Vid. Deut 17. & Mosem de Kotzi præcepto jubente xcix.

Etsi per seditionem illa facta, judices tamen etiam clamare potuerunt: Qui utiq; erant fax, & tuba in hac seditione. Non habebant amplius jus pœnæ capitalis Judæi, Joh. xiix. 31. Non ergo per viam juris, sed per seditionem hæc agebant: retinentes tamen aliquid de jure legitimo, utpote, quod testes primi lapides solebant jacere. Exercuisse adhuc ipsos stante republica in os, qui Judæis auctores essent ad falsos cultus, quod falso de Stephano censebant, observat Grotius hic, & l. II. de Jure Bellis & Pacis, è Maccabaicis & Act. xxiii. 13. id probans. Sed ea facti erant, non juris.

ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὑτῶν) Nempe quo expeditiores essent. Ingentia enim saxa jaci à testibus solebant.

παλεμίνε Σάυλε) Qui tum scholam Gamalielis frequentare studiorum causa solebat, Act. xxii. 3. Sed æstu abreptus, à lenitati magistri ad atrociora multorum exemplis patiebatur se trahi. Phil. iii. 6.

## 7:59
Vers. 59. calling upon) Namely Jesus, which is here understood from what follows.

and saying, Lord Jesus) There is no doubt that Jesu here is the vocative, as in Revelation ch. xxii, 20.

receive my spirit) He imitates the master of the disciple, Luke 23. 46.

This is to be noted against Fr. David, who contends that that Jesu is of the genitive case. Never in the Scriptures does Lord or Lord with the word Jesus occur, so that the name Jesus is of the genitive case. But κύριε Ἰησῦ is openly held in the vocative case in Rev. xxii. 20. And here Stephen had seen this son standing at the right hand of God v. 57. whom he therefore invoked in this way.

Latin:

Vers. 59. ἐπικαλέμενον) Nempe τὸν Ἰησῦν, quod ex sequentibus hic subintelligitur.

κὼ λέγοντα, Κύριε Ἰησῦ) Non dubium est, quin Jesu hic sit vocativus, quomodo Apocalypsi c. xxii, 20.

δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μυ) Magistri discipulῦ imitatur Luc. 23. 46.

Notandum id contra Fr. Davidis, qui illud Ἰησῦ contendit esse Genitivi casus. Nunquam in Scripturis Dominus vel Domine cum voce Jesu occurrit, ut nomen Jesu casus genitivi sit. At κύριε Ἰησῦ casu vocandi aperte habetur Apoc. xxii. 20. Et viderat hic Stephanus filium hunc stantem à dextris Dei v. 57. quem proinde ita invocavit.

## 7:60
Vers. 60. and having placed his knees) As was accustomed to be done in more intense prayers, especially in dangers.

do not lay this sin to their charge) And this by the example of the Lord, Luke xxiii. 34. μὴ στήσῃς literally do not weigh. Thus Ezra 7. 25. 32. Job 28. 15. Jerem. 32. 9. 10. Zach. 13. This verb ἱσάναι is for the Hebrew שׁקַל, which in 1 Kings 20. 39. is translated as he shall pay, Exodus 22. 18. he shall pay, Isaiah 55. 2. to value. Formerly money was heavy bronze, which was accustomed to be weighed and thus paid; hence σαθμὸς to the Greeks, libripens to the Romans, expenditures, expenses, to pay, payments, and the like. But because in balancing accounts, what I impute to another frees me no less than if I were paying, that is, settling: hence it came about that ἱσᾶν is to impute. And because of the similarity that crimes have with pecuniary debts, a matter we dealt with in book II of the Law of War and Peace ch. xx, §. 2, just as he who suffers punishments is said to pay them, so he who wants to exact them is said to impute, and he who does not want to exact them is said not to impute. But this, lest you expend or impute, has this value: lest you make this crime so great that you obstruct the way to conversion for them, just as also in the saying of Christ: concerning which we have dealt at the place in Luke just now indicated by us.

The phrase is rightly explained. The immediate sense, however, is that this sin may not be imputed to them, that is, that it may be pardoned or remitted: for this to be able to happen, there was altogether a need for grace and the means of conversion.

ἐκοιμήθη.) It is the way of the Hebrews to say שׁכַב for to die, as in Isaiah 15:18, where in the Hebrew it is וְשָׁכַב, in the Greek κεκοίμηνται. So also Matt. 27:52, John 11:11, below c. 16:36, 1 Cor. 7:38, c. 11:30, c. 15:6, 18, 20, 51, 1 Thess. 4:13, 14, 15, 2 Pet. 3:4. See what we said at Matt. 9:24.

Latin:

Vers. 60. θεὶς δὲ τά γόνατα) Ut solebat fieri in precibus intensioribus, maxime in periculis.

μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ταύτην) Et hoc Domini exemplo, Luc. xxiii. 34. μὴ στήσῃς ad verbum ne appendas. Sic Esdræ 7. 25. 32. Job. 28. 15. Jerem. 32. 9. 10. Zach. 13. Est verbum hoc ἱσάναι pro Hebræo שׁקַל, quod 1. Reg. 20. 39. vertitur τίσει, Exodi 22. 18. ἀπότισεν, Esaiæ 55. 2. τιμᾷν. olim pecuniæ erant æs grave, quod pendi & sic solvi solebat; inde σαθμὸς Græcis, Romanis libripens, impendia, expensæ, pendere, pensiones, & similia. Quia autem in rationibus æquandis, quod alteri imputo id non minus me liberat, quam si penderem, id est, solverem: hinc factum est, ut ἱσᾶν sit imputare. Et propter similitudinem quam crimina cum debitis pecuniariis habent, qua de re egimus libro II. de Jure Belli ac Pacis c. xx, §. 2. sicut solvere dicitur pœnas, qui eas patitur, ita imputare, qui eas exigere vult, non imputare, qui exigere non vult. Hic autem, ne impendas aut imputes, hoc valet, ne tanti hoc crimen facias, ut viam illis ad conversionem obstruas, quemadmodum & in dicto Christi: de quo ad Lucæ locum modo à nobis indicatum, egimus.

Recte phrasis explicatur. Immediatus autem sensus est, ne imputetur ipsis hoc peccatum, hoc est, at condonetur, vel remittatur: quod ut fieri posset, omnino gratia & mediis conversionis opus erat.

ἐκοιμήθη.) Hebræorum est שׁכַב dicere pro moti ut Esaiæ xv. 18. ubi in Hebræo וְשָׁכַב, in Græco κεκοίμηνται. Sic & Matt. xxvii. 52. Joh. xi. 11. inf. c. xvi. 36. 1. Cor. vii. 38. c. xi. 30, c. xv. 6. 18. 20. 51. 1. Thess. iv. 13. 14. 15 2. Pet. iii. 4. Vide, quæ diximus ad Matth. ix, 24.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Saul, a persecution having arisen, laying waste the Church, leads many captive: but Philip preaching in Samaria, and performing miracles, many are baptized, even Simon Magus, and upon Peter and John being sent there, the converted Samaritans receive the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands; but Peter condemns Simon, who offers money so that he might also obtain the gift of communicating the Holy Spirit, and exhorts him to repentance: and they preach the Gospel here and there in the villages. Philip, however, is ordered to go toward the south into the way tending to Gaza, where he informs an Ethiopian Eunuch returning from Jerusalem, who was reading Isaiah concerning the sheep led to the slaughter and taken away from judgment, about Jesus, and baptizes him as he professes faith in Jesus, and being taken away by the Spirit he is found in Ashdod, preaching the Gospel as far as Caesarea.

There are four parts: I. The Jerusalem persecution with the dispersion of the churches, to verse 4. II. The conversion of the Samaritans, to v. 17. III. The curse of Simon, who desires to redeem the gift of the Holy Spirit with money, to v. 25. IV. The instruction and baptism of the Eunuch of Queen Candace by Philip, to v. 40.

PART I. The Jerusalem persecution of the Church.

Vers. 1. Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει ἀυτῶ) He approved of this deed of the Zealots, in mind, words, and deeds, below c. 22:20. This and other things which follow concerning Saul are not related rashly, but so that we may consider, from whom and from what kind of person [he came].

Latin:

CAPUT VIII. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Saulus persequutione exorta desolans Ecclesi- am captivos multos ducit: Philippo vero in Samaria prædicante, & miracula patran- te, multi baptizantur, etiam Simon Magus, eoque misso Petro & Iohanne, S.S. per χειρο- θεσίαν accipiunt Samaritani conversi; Si- monem vero pecuniam, ut etiam donum consequatur communicandi Spiritum S. præbentem condemnat Petrus, & ad pœni- tentiam hortatur: ac prædicant passim in vicis Evangelium. Philippus autem jube- tur versus meridiem in viam, Gazam ten- dentem, ire, ubi Eunuchum Æthiopicum Hierosolyma revertentem, Esaiam de ove ad mactationem adducta, & è judicio ere- pta, legentem, informat de Iesu, eumque fi- dem in Iesum profitentem baptizat, & à Spiritu abductus in Asdod reperitur, Ev- angelium prædicans usque in Cæsaream.

Partes sunt quatuor: I. Persequutio Hierosoly- mitana cum Ecclesiarum dispersione, ad vers. 4. II. Samaritanorum conversio, ad v. 17. III. Simonis pecunia donum S. S. redimere cupientis maledi- ctio, ad v. 25. IV. Eunuchis Reginæ Candaces à Phi- lippo informatio, & baptizatio, ad v. 40.

PARS I. Hierosolymitana Ecclesiæ persequutio.

Vers. 1. Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει ἀυτῶ) Pro- babat hoc Zelotarum facinus, animo, verbis, factis, infra c. XXII. 20. Hoc & alia, quæ sequuntur de Saulo non te- mere referuntur, sed ut cogitemus, οἷς ἐξ οἵων.

## 8:2
Vers. 2. συνεκόμισαν δὲ) It is a sepulchral word, Sophocles in Ajax: 'I tell you not to carry this corpse with your hands.' It corresponds to the Hebrew אסף. ἄνδρες ἐυλαβεῖς) See above c. 2:5. καὶ ἐποιήσαντο κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπ᾿ ἀυτῷ) Words taken from Gen. 50:10, see also Zech. 12:10, 1 Mac. 2:70, c. 4:39, c. 9:20. That was a kind of honor held for the dead among those nations. God held a greater honor for him, when afterwards He willed that very many diseases be healed at his relics, as the first of the Martyrs, concerning which matter if anyone doubts, let him read Augustine, De Civitate Dei 22.8, where you will find conspicuous proofs of what I say: wherefore it is no wonder if the pious have fittingly honored those relics, as the same Augustine speaks, Epist. 103. From this experiment it began to be run to the relics of other martyrs also with equal success, and that is a part of his kingdom, which the Apocalypse 20:4 attributes to the martyrs. where those who are mentioned as the thousand years, begin from Constantine.

He inserted these things beside the occasion for the sake of the cult of relics, which are accustomed to be celebrated by Papistic pilgrimages to their monuments and relics, unless perhaps he foolishly thought that the cult of relics could be proven with the Mainz Jesuits in the disputation concerning relics in the year 1605, held from the lamentation over Stephen. If any miracles were done at the monuments of the martyrs, as Augustine reports concerning the memory of Stephen in the cited place (concerning which place of Augustine, however, Ludov. Vives professed that there is no doubt that many things were added in that chapter by those who contaminated all the writings of great authors with their own spurious hands), yet neither the invocation of the Martyrs, nor the religious veneration of their relics is established by them, much less the superstitious journey to their sepulchers, for the sake of veneration and cult, which is accustomed to be done in the Papacy under the opinion of merit. For could not the memory of the holy martyrs also be honored and adorned by God for the sake of the confirmation of the doctrine which they sealed with their blood, even if the martyrs are not to be invoked, nor their relics to be worshipped with religious cult? And that pilgrimage to the places of the saints is destitute of divine command, and that no example of it is held in the sacred writings, the Papists themselves are forced to confess, nor does Gretser acknowledge that it was customary in the primitive Church until the third century, l. II. de sacr. peregr. c. 1. p. 181. which Grotius also insinuated here, and more openly at Apoc. 20. 3. nay, the Jesuits themselves profess that this rite proceeded from the Heathens. See Gretser. l. c. p. 237. which they also have in common with the Turks, as witnessed by Breitenbach in Hist. peregr. C. III. whence Hildebert, Archbishop of Tours, about the year of Christ 1115, in his book of Epistles, gravely dissuaded a certain Count from such pilgrimages: do not desire to look upon the places of the saints, but be diligent about your own, and do not carry about the memory of stones, but carry about the memory of mighty works.

But that Grotius places in it a part of the millennial kingdom of the martyrs, Apoc. XX. 3., because miracles were performed at the sepulchres or relics of the martyrs, is just as unwritten and unprovable as the fiction about the resurrection of the martyrs from the dead that is to happen before the universal resurrection: because it is not fitting for the relics of the martyrs, but for God alone, to perform miracles, Ps. LXXII. v. ult. Nor is it true that from Constantine the Great for a thousand years relics were worshipped in the Church; rather, not a few things teach the contrary, since Gregory of Nyssa about the year 380 disapproved of pilgrimages to the places of the saints in a special book: which Baronius does not deny was also done by Jerome and Basil the Great, ad ann. 386. n. 40.

Latin:

Vers. 2. συνεκόμισαν δὲ) Vox est sepulchralis, Sophocles Ajace: 'Ετός, σε φωνῶ τόνδε τὸν νεκρὸν χεροῖν Μὴ συγκομίζειν. Respondet Hebræo אסף. ἄνδρες ἐυλαβεῖς) Vide supra c. II. 5. καὶ ἐποιήσαντο κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπ᾿ ἀυτῷ) Verba desumta ex Gen. L. 10. vid. & Zach. XII. 10. 1. Mac. II. 70. c. IV. 39. c. IX. 20. Erat id genus honoris habiti mortuo apud illas gentes. Majorem ei Deus honorem habuit, cum post ad ipsius, ut Martyrum primi, reliquias plurimos morbos sanari voluit, qua de re si quis dubitet, legat August. de Civitate Dei XXII. 8. ubi conspicua reperies ejus quod dico documen- ta: quare nec mirum, si eas reliquias pii convenienter ho- noraverint, ut loquitur idem Augustin. Epist. CIII. Ab hoc experimento ad aliorum quoque martyrum reliquias con- curri cœpit pari successu, eaque pars est regni ejus, quod martyribus tribuit Apocalypsis XX, 4. ubi qui memoran- tur mille anni, à Constantino incipiunt.

Hæc præter occasionem in gratiam cultus reli- quiarum Papisticis peregrinationibus ad monu- menta & reliquias earum celebrari solitis inseruit, nisi forte cum Jesuitis Moguntinis in disput. de re- liquiis anno 1605. ex planctu super Stephanum ha- bito, cultum reliquiarum probari posse inepte cen- suit. Si quæ miracula ad martyrum monumenta fa- cta, uti de Stephani memoria refert loco citato Au- gustinus (de quo vero Augustini loco Ludov. Vives professus est, dubiũ non esse, quin in illo capite mul- ta sint addita ab iis, qui omnia magnorum autorum scripta spuriis suis manib. contaminarunt) non sta- bilitur tamen iis vel invocatio Martyrum, vel re- liquiarum eorundem religiosa veneratio, nedum profectio superstitiosa ad sepulcra ipsorum, vene- rationis & cultus causa, sub opinione meriti in Pa- patu fieri solita. Annon enim honorari etiam à Deo, & ornari potuit Martyrum sanctorum me- moria confirmationis doctrinæ gratia, quam san- guine suo obsignarunt, etiamsi invocandi non sint martyres, nec colendæ eorum reliquiæ cultu religioso? Et peregrinationem ad loca sanctorum destitui mandato divino, nullumq; exemplum ejus in sacris haberi, fateri coguntur ipsimet Pontificii, nec usitatam eam fuisse in primitiva Ecclesia in ter- tium usque seculum agnoscit Gretserus l. II. de sacr. peregr. c. 1. p. 181. quod etiã hic, & apertius ad Apoc. 20. 3. insinuavit Grotius, imo ab Ethnicis profectum esse hunc ritum, profitentur ipsimet Jesuitæ. Vide Gretser. l. c. p. 237. quem etiam cum Turcis habent communem, teste Breitenbachio in Hist. peregr. C. III. unde Hildebert. Turonensis Archi-Episcopus circa annum Christi cIɔ cxv. in lib. Epist. Comitem quendam graviter dehortatus est à peregrinatio- nib. ejusmodi: loca sanctorum ne desideres intueri, sed tuorum satagas, nec circumferre per memoriam lapidum, sed circumferre memoriam virtutum.

Quod vero Grotius in eo partem regni mille- narii martyrum Apoc. XX. 3. ponit, quod miracula ad martyrum sepulcra, vel reliquias patrata sit, æ- que ἄγραφον est & ἀνεξέλεγκτον, ac commentum de resurrectione martyrum à mortuis ante universa- lem resurrectionem futura: quia non martyrum re- liquiis, sed uni Deo convenit patrare miracula, Ps. LXXII. v. ult. Neq; verum est, inde à Constanti- no M. per mille annos cultas esse in Ecclesia reliqui- as; Contrarium potius non pauca docent, siqui- dem Greg. Nyssenus circa annum 380. peculiari li- bro peregrinationes ad loca sanctorum improbarit: quod etiam ab Hieronymo & Basilio M. factum esse, non diffitetur Baronius ad ann. 386. n. 40.

## 8:3
Vers. 3. κατὰ τὺς οἴκυς εἰσπορευόμενος) Breaking into houses, σύρων τε ἄνδρας κὲ γυναῖκας) As if captured in war. Such is that in the Troades of Euripides, Οἶδ’, ἡνίκ’ Αἴας εἷλε Κασσάνδραν βίᾳ. Virgil, Aeneid II. Lo, the maiden of Priam was being dragged with dishevelled hair. Seneca, Thebais. Will the savage soldier drag mothers snatched from the very bosom of their husbands, with chains imposed?

Therefore Paul, afterwards condemning himself for these crimes, says that he was not only a persecutor, but also a violent man, 1. Tim. I. 13.

παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακὴν) Into the prison of the temple. See above c. 4. 3. c. 5. 8. 19. 22. 25. by the order, indeed, of the Sanhedrin, which had the right not only of arrest, but also of scourging among the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 3. κατὰ τὺς οἴκυς εἰσπορευόμενος) Irrumpens in ædes, σύρων τε ἄνδρας κὲ γυναῖκας) Quasi bello captos. Tale il- lud in Troadibus Euripidis, Οἶδ’, ἡνίκ’ Αἴας εἷλε Κασσάνδραν βίᾳ. Virgilius Æneidos II. Ecce trahebatur sparsis Priameia virgo Crinibus. Seneca Thebaïde. Matres ab ipso conjugum raptas sinu Sævus catena miles imposita trahet?

Ideo Paulus horum facinorum postea se damnans, ait se fuisse non διωκτὴν modo, sed & ὑβρισὴν, 1. Tim. I. 13.

παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακὴν) In carcerem templi. Vide supra c. 4. 3. c. 5. 8. 19. 22. 25. jussu nimirum Synedrii, quod in Judæ- os non prehensionē tantum, sed & verberum jus habebat.

## 8:4
Vers. 4. οἱ μὲν ὆ν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον) That is, they did not remain in Judea and Samaria, but went even further, so as to be away from danger. See below c. 11. 19.

PART II. The conversion of the Samaritans.

Latin:

Vers. 4. οἱ μὲν ὆ν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον) Id est, non subsiste- bant in Judæa, & Samaria, sed longius etiam ibant, ut à pe- riculo abessent. Vide infra c. II. 19.

PARS II. Samaritanorum conversio.

## 8:5
Vers. 5. Φίλιππος δὲ) A deacon, as the ancients rightly judge. For if he had been an Apostle, he would have laid hands on the baptized. See below v. 14. In such a circumstance, to preach the Gospel is not only for deacons, but also for private individuals, c. 11. 20.

Certainly this was not Philip the Apostle, as Polycrates thought in Eusebius IV. 24: For he remained in Jerusalem with the rest of the Apostles, v. 1. add v. 14. but he was of the number of those who were in charge of the distribution of alms. He is indeed called an Apostle by Tertullian, l. de Bapt. c. 18. and Ambrose, l. IX. in Lucam, but in a broader sense of the word, because he went about the regions everywhere preaching the Gospel of Christ. What is said about the preaching of private individuals can be admitted as regards an extraordinary case, provided that no room is left for the hypothesis of the Socinians and Anabaptists, that a calling is not necessary for the preaching of the word.

κατελθὼν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας) Σαμαρεία at that time was very often said of the region, Luke 17. 11. above c. 1. 8. below c. 8. 9. c. 15. 5. therefore it is rightly said here and John 4. 5. πόλις τῆς Σαμαρείας, the city of Sebaste: once devoted to anathema by Ezra and Nehemiah, now received into common grace.

This state of government is therefore used here in place of a syntax of apposition, which is sometimes wont to happen. For this city gave a name to the whole region: which, when it was restored, Herod the Great called Sebaste or Augusta in honor of Augustus. See Josephus, book 1 of the Jewish War, chapter 6. Christ forbade preaching the Gospel in Samaria, Matthew 10:5, but only for a time, because the Gospel had to be preached to the Jews first, Romans 15:8. Therefore, Acts 1:8, the command concerning preaching the Gospel was extended even to Samaria.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Φίλιππος δὲ) Diaconus ut censent veteres, re- cte. Nam si Apostolus fuisset, imposuisset & manus bapti- zatis. Vide inf. v. 14. in tali circumstantia Evangelii prædi- care non diaconorum tantū est, sed & privatorum c. II. 20.

Non sane Philippus Apostolus hic fuit: ut Polycra- tes apud Euseb. IV. 24. putavit: Ille enim cum re- liquis Apostolis Hierosolymis remansit v. 1. adde v. 14. sed ex eorū numero, qui eleemosynarum dis- tributionum præfecti erant. Vocatur quidem à Ter- tull. l. de Bapt. c. 18. & Ambros. l. IX. in Lucam Apo- stolus, sed latiori vocis significatione, quia passim regiones circumibat. Evangelium de Christo præ- dicando. Quæ de prædicatione privatorum dicun- tur, quoad casum extraordinarium admitti pos- sunt, dummodo Socinianorum & Anabaptistarum hypothesi, quod vocatio necessaria non sit ad ver- bi prædicationem, locus non relinquatur.

κατελθὼν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας) Σαμαρεία eo tempore de regione sæpissime dicebatur, Luc. 17. 11. supra c. 1. 8. inf. c. 8. 9. c. 15. 5. itaque recte hic & Joh. 4. 5. dicitur πόλις τῆς Σαμαρείας urbs Sebaste: olim anathemate devota per Esdram & Nehemiam, nunc in communē gratiam recepta.

Est ergo hic status regiminis loco Syntaxeos ap- positionis adhibitus, quod nonnunquam fieri solet. Dedit enim hæc urbs toti regioni nomen: quam in honorem Augusti, cum restaurata est, Herodes Magnus Sebasten vel Augustam vocavit. Vid. Jose-phus l. 1. de Bell. Judaic. c. 6. In Samaria prædicare Evangelium prohibuit Christus Matth. X. 5. sed ad tempus solum, quia prius Judæis prædicandum erat Evangelium Rom. XV. 8. Ideo Act. I. 8. mandatum de prædicando Evangelio extensum etia ad Samariam

## 8:6
Verse 6. (as they heard) Because they were hearing him asserting the things done so seriously and constantly. (and seeing the signs, which he did) Which gained him the greatest authority.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς) Quia audiebant tam serio ac constanter asseverantem res actas. καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα, ἃ ἐποίει) Quæ ipsi auctoritatem conciliabant maximam.

## 8:7
Verse 7. (crying out) Namely, the spirits themselves. For it is common for the Hebrews that a new case of the noun which preceded is understood. Unclean spirits are wont not to go out without a cry, Matthew 8:29, Mark 1:27, 3:11, 5:7, 9:26, Luke 4:41.

Latin:

Vers. 7. βοῶντα) Nempe αὐτὰ τὰ πνέυματα. Frequens enim est Hebræis, ut subintelligatur novus casus nominis, quod præcessit. Solent impuri spiritus non exire sine clamore, Matth. 8. 29. Marc. 1. 27. c. 3. 11 c. 5. 7. c. 9. 26. Luc. 4. 41.

## 8:9
Verse 9. (saying that he himself was some great one) Powerful and effective. The scholiast of Horace on Epistle 1 of book 2, as if a great man promises that he performs great things. See above chapter 5:36.

Latin:

Vers. 9. λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν) Potentem & efficacem. Scholiastes Horatii ad Epistolam 1. libri II. quasimagnus promittat se agere magna. Vide supra c. V. 36.

## 8:10
Verse 10. (this is the power of God which is great) In the manuscript, which I often mention, (the one called great), just as the Latin reads. Justin: and almost all the Samaritans, but few also in other nations, as confessing that first God, they worship. Simon said that he was the most sublime power, that is, he who is the father above all things. Irenaeus, book 20. Tertullian, or whoever is the writer of that fragment which is wont to be placed under the book of Tertullian on prescription against heretics, dealing with this Simon: He dared to call himself the supreme power, that is, the supreme God. The sense is, Simon said that he was that deity which is believed to be supreme in every nation, to be called by various names. As among the Samaritans YHWH, among the Greeks Zeus, among the Latins Jove, and so on. See concerning his blasphemous dogmas Irenaeus, Epiphanius, Philastrius, Augustine, Theodoret, Damascenus. in the catalogs of heretics, from whom Irenaeus says all heretics took the beginnings of their impious dogmas: Augustine, book 1 on heresies, chapter 1, teaches that he wished to hold himself for the Messiah. But those things which are handed down concerning a statue erected to him by the Romans with this inscription SIMONI MAGO SANCTO, are called into doubt by others, and not without cause. But it does not pertain to speak of these in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ὗτός ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ μεγάλη) In Manuscripto, cujus sæpe memini, ἡ καλουμένη μεγάλη. quomodo legit Latinus. Justinus: καὶ σχεδὸν πάντες μὲν Σαμαρεῖς, ὀλίγοι δὲ κᾀ ἐν ἄλλοις ἔθνεσιν, ὡς τὸν πρῶτον Θεὸν ἐκεῖνον ὁμολογοῦντες προσκυνοῦσι. Dicebat Simon se esse sublimissimam virtutem, hoc est, eum qui sit super omnia pater. Irenæus l. 20. Tertullianus, aut quisquis est scriptor ejus particulæ, quæ subjici solet libro Tertulliani de præscriptione adversus hæreticos, de Simone hoc agens: Hic ausus est summam se dicere virtutem, id est, summum Deum. Sensum est, dicebat Simon se esse id numen, quod in quaque gente summum creditur, variis vocabulis appellaretur. Ut apud Samaritanos יהוה, apud Græcos Δία, apud Latinos jovem, & ita deinceps. Vid. de dogmatibus ejus blasphemis Irenæus, Epiphanius, Philastrius, Augustinus, Theodoretes, Damascen. in catalogis hæreticorum, à quo omnes hæreticos initia sumsisse impiorum dogmatum Irenæus ait: habere se pro Messia voluisse, August. l. 1. de hær. c. 1. docet. Quæ vero de statua ei à Romanis erecta cum hac inscriptione SIMONI MAGO SANCTO traduntur, ab aliis in dubium, nec sine causa revocantur. Sed de his non attinet hoc loco dicere.

## 8:11
Verse 11. (by the magic arts) By the deceits of Satan.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ταῖς μαγείαις) Satanæ præstigiis.

## 8:12
Verse 12. (the things concerning the kingdom of God) Concerning that kingdom which is begun here, and will be consummated after the resurrection. (they were baptized both men and women) Unless the baptism of water had been believed to be of divine precept, the women would have abstained from it.

Latin:

Vers. 12 τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ) De regno illo, quod hic inchoatur, consummabitur post resurrectionem. ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες) Nisi baptismus aquæ creditus fuisset præcepti esse divini, abstinuissent ab eo fœminæ

## 8:13
Verse 13. (he himself believed) He believed that Christ had performed miracles and had risen from the dead: but he did not add the purpose of living according to Christ, which is the perfection of faith. (he was continuing with Philip) He was assiduous with him. See above chapter 1:14, 2:42, 46, 6:4, below chapter 10:7, Romans 12:12, Colossians 4:13.

The purpose of living according to Christ is not the perfection (which Grotius asserts with the Socinians), but is the consequence and effect of true faith. But not only historical faith, as they call it, or of simple assent, because he believed the miracles and the resurrection of Christ, as Grotius wishes with the Calvinists, but saving faith, which includes trust in Christ, is attributed to Simon here: because he is joined to other believers, whom there is no doubt had saving faith. Even if he afterwards fell from faith, and no longer had a right heart.

Latin:

Vers. 13. αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσε) Credidit Christum fecisse miracula & resurrexisse à morte: non autem propositum addidit vivendi secundum Christum, quæ fidei est perfectio. ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ) Assiduus apud eum erat. Vid. sup. c. 1. 14. c. 2. 42. 46. c. 6. 4. inf. c. 10. 7. Ro. 12. 12. Col. 4. 13.

Propositum vivendi secundum Christum non perfectio, (quod cum Socinianis asserit Grotius) sed consequens & effectus est veræ fidei. Non autem tantum fides historica, quam vocant, vel simplicis assensus, quod crediderit miracula & resurrectionem Christi, uti cum Calvinianis Grotius vult, sed fides salvifica, quæ fiduciam in Christum includit, Simoni hic tribuitur: quia aliis credentibus jungitur, quos fidem salvificam habuisse dubium non est. Etsi postmodum fide exciderit, nec amplius cor rectum habuerit.

## 8:15
Vers. 15. they prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit) The Holy Spirit had indeed been promised to those who were baptized, but not immediately upon their being baptized, but when it seemed good to God. God willed, however, that those admirable gifts should not ordinarily reach the baptized, except through the Apostles, so that by that means He might procure the greatest possible authority for His witnesses, which itself also pertained to maintaining the unity of the Church.

If, therefore, Peter and John were sent because of the miraculous gifts to be conferred upon the baptized through the laying on of hands, the Sacrament of confirmation cannot be carved out from this with the Papists, Bellarmine, Corn. à Lapide, and others, in which no such gifts are conferred; which also rests upon no foundation of the Holy Scriptures, but that this power of miracles belonged only to the Apostles will appear below in ch. IX. 17.

Latin:

Vers. 15. προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν, ὅπως λάβωσι πνεῦμα ἅγιον) Promissus quidem erat Spiritus S. iis, qui baptizabantur, sed non illico atque baptizati essent, sed ubi Deo id videretur. Voluit autem Deus ordinarie non contingere baptizatis dona illa admiranda, nisi per Apostolos, ut ea ratione testibus suis auctoritatem quam maximam conciliaret, quod ipsum simul ad retinendam Ecclesiæ unitatem pertinebat.

Si ergo ob dona miraculosa per impositionem manuum baptizatis conferenda Petrus & Johannes missi, non exsculpi hinc cum Papistis, Bellarmino, Corn. à Lapide, & aliis poterit Sacramentum confirmationis, in quo nulla conferuntur talia dona; quod etiam nullo S. Literarum nititur fundamento, sed tantum solis Apostolis hanc potestatem miraculorum convenisse, apparebit infra c. IX. 17.

## 8:16
Vers. 16. for it had not yet fallen upon any of them) See John VII. 39.

Latin:

Vers. 16. οὔπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπ' οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός) Vide Joh. VII. 39.

## 8:17
Vers. 17. then he laid hands upon them) See what we taught at Matt. IX. 18.

PART III. The curse of Simon Magus, who desired to redeem the gift of the Holy Spirit with money.

Latin:

Vers. 17. τότε ἐπετίθει τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς) Vide, quæ docimus ad Matth. IX. 18.

PARS III. Simonis Magi pecunia donum S. S. redimere cupientis maledictio.

## 8:20
V. 20. may your silver be with you for destruction) In this verse and the four following is a periphrasis of that devotion which was performed through חרם אתה without a definition of time; the sense, however, is this: may that money remain with you to your own harm. that you thought the gift of God could be acquired through money) You hoped to purchase with money that which is a gift of God. See Matt. 10. 8.

Latin:

V. 20. τὸ ἀργύριόν σε σὺν σοὶ εἵη εἰς ἀπώλειαν) In hoc com- mate & quatuor sequentibus est περίφρασις ejus devotionis, quæ fiebat per חרם אתה fine definitione temporis; Sen- sus autem hic est: pecunia ista tibi maneat tuo cum malo. ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τῦ Θεῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθ) Sperasti comparare pecuniis id, quod donum est Dei. Vid. Matt. 10. 8

## 8:21
Vers. 21. you have no part nor lot in this word) To you, neither a part nor a ministry is owed of that eternal life which we preach, μερὶς as in 2 Cor. VI, 5. κλῆρος, namely, of the ministry, as above c. I. 17.

Others, by the word λόγον in the Hebraic phrase, understand the business of power, namely, of conferring the gifts of the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands, even our blessed Gerhard; compare Gen. 18. 4. 1 Sam. 14. 12. Mark 1. 45. Luke 9. 28. Nevertheless, the more famous meaning of the word λόγος can be retained, that neither a part of eternal life nor the ministry of the Word is owed to Simon: since he is excommunicated here by St. Peter, not only excluded from the communion of power, the gift of miracles: therefore this cause is added, because your heart is not right before God. Furthermore, Guilb. Durandus has already complained, and Franc. Petrarcha has openly professed in his Dialogue on the Roman Curia, that Simony, which received its name from this sin of Simon Magus, for which Grotius says he was excommunicated by Peter, reigns at Rome as if it were no sin at all: that Simon Magus has revived at Rome with his spouse Simonia. To whom, however, that distinguished successor of Peter is so far from saying anathema, that he rather places a cushion underneath, nay, in reality, testifies that he himself is that Simon revived, and demonstrates it by his works!

for your heart is not right before God) For you do not seek the honor of God: and God sees that.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ὐκ ἔστι σοι μερὶς ἐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τύτῳ) Vitæ istius æternæ, quam nos prædicamus, tibi neque pars neque ministerium debetur, μερὶς ut 2. Cor. VI, 5. κλῆρος nem- pe διακονίας ut supra c. I. 17.

Alii per λόγον phrasi Ebraica intelligunt negotiū potestatis, nempe, conferendi dona S.S. per χειρο- θεσίαν, etiam B. Gerhard. noster; Conf. Gen. 18. 4. 1. Sam. 14. 12. Marc. 1. 45. Luc. 9. 28. Retineri tamen potest famosior vocis λόγα significatio, quod neq; pars vitæ æternæ, neque ministerium Verbi debeatur Simoni: quum hic excomunicetur à S. Pero, non tantum à comunione virtutis, doni miraculorum excludatur: Ideo additur hæc causa, quia cor tuum rectum non est coram Deo. Cæterum Simoniam, quæ ab hoc Simonis Magi peccato nomen accepit, ob quod à Petro ipsum excomunicatum Grotius di- cit, Romæ ita regnare, ac si nullum esset peccatum; questus jam est Guilb. Durandus, & professus palâ fuit Franc. Petrarcha in Dial. de Rom. curia: quod Romæ Simon Magus cum conjuge sua Simonia revi- xerit. Quibus vero egregius ille Petri successor, tantum abest, ut anathema dicat, ut culcitram sub- sternat potius, imo reapse, se esse Simonem illum redivivum testetur, operibusque suis demonstret!

ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου ὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ἐνώπιον τῦ Θεῦ) Tu enim non Dei honorem quæris: & id Deus videt,

## 8:22
Vers. 22. repent therefore of this wickedness and pray to God, if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you) He speaks hesitantly, as in Joel 2.14, Jonah 3.9, Dan. 4.24; God could have cut him off from life immediately after the crime: He could also have given some sorrow without true amendment of mind. Philo on the allegories: for to many souls desiring to use repentance, God did not permit it, but as if by a back-flow they retreated to the opposite. The same is the opinion of Moses Maimonides on repentance, chap. VI. §. 4. The Christians of the first centuries did not restore to communion those who had fallen into the gravest crimes after baptism, nor yet did they bid them despair of God's mercy.

Grotius gratifies the Papists here, who contend that one must doubt concerning the remission of sins. But that εἰ ἄρα here is not a particle of one doubting, but of one confirming, which we have also warned about the cited Prophetic sayings in their own places; and therefore it should not be explained as 'perhaps,' but as 'indeed' or 'certainly': for God has guaranteed by oath to those who repent seriously, so that they may not doubt concerning the remission of sins, Ezek. 33.11, which excludes all hesitation, Heb. 6. 18; nor could he doubt concerning the remission of sins to be granted to the penitent, who himself had received the power of granting remission of sins to the penitent, Matt. 16. 14, John 20. 23; nor do the Papists doubt that the Roman Pontiff has the power of pardoning the sin of Simony, so that that pardon is valid. We have here the Jesuit à Lapide agreeing: You will say, he says, did Peter therefore doubt whether the sin should be forgiven to Simon, if he truly repents? He answers: By no means: for the 'perhaps' is not a particle of one doubting, but rather an expletive of one confirming. St. Augustine, book II on repentance, ch. 5, says: I do not say that Peter doubted, nor do I think the whole case should be strangled by the prejudice of the single word 'perhaps.' What Grotius says, that the Christians of the first centuries did not restore to communion those who had fallen into the gravest crimes after baptism, nor yet did they bid them despair of God's mercy, we admit to a certain extent. For they did not simply exclude them from communion for their whole life, but for a time. And the end of excommunication was not a final exclusion, but that they might seriously perform repentance, and having performed repentance, be received and saved, 1 Cor. 5. 5.

the thought of your heart) The counsel which you have taken. He has the word ἐπίνοιαν in Wis. 6.16, ch. 9.14, ch. 14.12, ch. 15.4, Sir. 40.3, 2 Macc. 12.46.

Latin:

Vers. 22. μετανόησον ὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας ταύτης κὶ δεήθητι τῦ Θεῦ, εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας συ) Hæsitanter loquitur, ut Joel 2.14. Jon. 3. 9. Dan. 4. 24. poterat Deus vitâ illi statim post crimen abscindere: poterat & dare dolorem aliquem sine vera animi emendatione. Philo de allego- riis: πολλαῖς γὰρ ψυχαῖς μετανοίᾳ χρήσαθ βυληθείσαις ὐκ ἐπέτρε- ψεν ὁ Θεὸς, ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ ὑπὸ παλιῥῥοίας εἰς τὔμπαλιν ἀνεχώρη- σαν. Eadem est sententia Mosis Maimonidæ de pœnitentia cap. VI. §. 4. Christiani primorum sæculorum in gravissima crimina post baptismum lapsos non restituebant communi- oni, neque tamen desperare jubebant de Dei misericordia.

Pontificiis hæc gratificatur Grotius, qui dubi- tandum esse de remissione peccatorum contendunt. Ast illud εἰ ἄρα hic non particula dubitantis est, sed confirmantis, quod etiam de dictis adductis Propheticis suis locis monuimus; ideoq; non ex- plicari debet forte, sed utique vel certe: Serio enim pœnitentibus, ne dubitent de remissione peccato- rum, juramento cavit Deus Ez. 33.11. quod omnem hæsitationem excludit Ebr. 6. 18. neque dubitare poterat de peccatorum remissione pœnitenti con- cedenda, qui ipse potestatem acceperat pœniten- tibus remissionem concedendi peccatorum Matt. 16. 14. Joh. 20. 23. nec dubitant Pontificii, quin Pon- tifex Romanus potestatem condonandi peccatum Simoniæ habeat, ut rata sit illa condonatio. Habe- mus hic Jesuitam à Lapide consentientem: Dices, in- quit ille, ergone dubitabat Petrus, num Simoni, si vere pœniteat, remittendum sit peccatum? Resp. Nequaquam: nam τὸ forte non est dubitantis, sed potius expletiva confirmantis particula S. Au- gust. l. II de pœnitent. c 5. Ego nec Petrum, inquit dubitasse dico, nec verbi unius, forte, prejudicio totam causam strangulandam arbitror. Quod Grotius ait, Christianos primorum seculorum in gravissima crimina post baptismum lapsos non restituisse com- munioni, neque tamen desperare jussisse de Dei misericordia, κατά τι admittimus. Non enim simpliciter à com- munione per totam vitam excludebant, sed ad tempus. Et finis excommunicationis non fuit fina- lis exclusio, sed ut serio pœnitentiam agant, acta- que pœnitentia recipiantur & salventur 1. Cor. 5. 5.

ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σᢈ) Consilium quod cepisti. Habet vocem ἐπίνοιαν Sap. VI. 16. cap. IX. 14. cap. XIV. 12. cap. XV. 4. Sir. XL. 3. 2. Macc. XII. 46.

## 8:23
Vers. 23. For I see you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity) εἰς for ἐν. χολὴ πικρίας, which is χολὴ καὶ πικρία in Deut. XXIX. 18: it is most bitter gall; it truly signifies a constitution of mind that is extremely vicious, and such as are foods corrupted by gall. The same is σύνδεσμος ἀδικίας, knots of vices that are hardly extricable. σύνδεσμος ἀδικίας is in the Hebrew of Isaiah ch. LVIII. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 23. εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας, καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄν- τα) εἰς pro ἐν. χολὴ πικρίας, quæ χολὴ καὶ πικρία Deut. XXIX. 18: est fel amarissimum; id vero significat animi constitu- tionem perquam vitiosam, & talem, quales sunt cibi felle corrupti. Idem est σύνδεσμος ἀδικίας, nodi vitiorum vix ex- tricabiles. σύνδεσμος ἀδικίας est in Hebræo Esaiæ c. LIIX. 6.

## 8:24
Vers. 24. Pray you for me to the Lord) He felt that he was such within as the Apostles had said. And so, since he judges them to be dear to God, he wishes to use their intercession, as those who had harmed him used the intercession of Job.

Yet the blessed Gerhard rightly says, by the example of Pharaoh, he seems to have had repentance not of the fault, but of the punishment.

that none of the things which you have spoken may come upon me) He refers to those words of Peter above in v. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 24. δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμῶ πρὸς τὸν κύριον) Sensit se talem esse intus, qualem Apostoli dixerant. Itaque cum i- psos judicet Deo caros, eorum deprecatione uti vult, ut Jo- bi deprecatione qui eum læserant.

Recte tamen B. Gerh. exemplo, inquit, Pharao- nis videtur habuisse pœnitentiam non culpæ, sed pœnæ.

ὅπως μηδὲν ἀπέλθῃ ἐπ᾽ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε) Respicit ad illa ver- ba Petri supra v. 20.

## 8:25
Vers. 25. And many villages of the Samaritans they evangelized) εὐαγγελίζεσθαι with the accusative of the person, to whom the message is brought, you have also in the Greek of Joel 2. 32, Luke 3. 18, Rev. 14. 16.

PART IV. The instruction of the Eunuch.

Vers. 26. to Gaza. This is desert) A Hebraism: for: which is desert. The old Gaza, destroyed by Alexander, was still in the time of Strabo μίνᢈσα ἔρημος, which are the very words of Strabo. But another was built under its name nearby, as Drusius noted from the book of places, which is believed to be Jerome's.

Others refer the pronoun αὕτη to the way. But here we easily subscribe to Grotius. The Ethiopic interpreter makes the prefect from this a Gaza of the city, deceived by the similarity of the proper name Gaza and the appellative gaza, which denotes treasure, whose origins are found among the Persians and Arabs, as the blessed John Ernest Gerhard, most versed in oriental languages and our former singular friend, rightly observed.

Latin:

Vers. 25. πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν εὐηγγελίσαντο) εὐαγγελίζεσθαι cum accusativo personæ, ad quā defertur nun- tius, habes etiā in Græco Joel. 2. 32. Luc. 3. 18. Apoc. 14. 16.

PARS IV. Eunuchi informatio.

Ves. 26. εἰς Γάζαν. αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος) Hebraismus: pro: quæ est deserta. Gaza vetꝰ ab Alexandro disjecta, adhuc Strabo- nis tempore erat μίνᢈσα ἔρημος, quæ sunt ipsius Strabonis verba. Sed alia sub ejus nomine ædificata est in proximo, ut ex libro locorū, qui Hierom. esse creditur, notavit Drusius.

Alii pronomen αὕτη ad ὁδὸν referunt. Sed facile hic sub- scribimus Grotio. Æthiops interpres præfectum hinc Gazz civitatis facit, deceptus convenientia nominis proprii Γάζα & appellativi γάζα, quod thesaurum notat, cujus narales a- pud Persas, & Arabes habentur, ut recte observavit B. Joh. Ernest. Gerhard. in linguis orientalibus versatissimus, ami- cus quondam noster singularis.

## 8:27
Vers. 27. A man of Ethiopia) They are called eunuch men because they have the appearance of men.

εὐνᢈχος) Terence. You said further that you wanted a eunuch. Because only queens use them, namely to avoid suspicions. Here is mystically fulfilled that which Isaiah said in ch. LVI. 4, 5, and which is in Ps. LXXII. 10.

Drusius, however, in book V, passes over it: he denies that 'man' in this place is a name of sex, since eunuchs are castrated: but that the expression is pleonastic; as 'man of Egypt' in Genesis, 'man of Judea' in Zech. VIII. 23. Nor does Ludovicus de Dieu concede that the word εὐνᢈχος, which corresponds to the Hebrew סריס, always denotes a castrated person; indeed, he teaches from Jer. 34. 19 that it is used of a Prince. Thus the name δυνάστης will be an explanation of this word. Compare Gen. 37. 36, ch. 40. 1, Esth. 4. 5. The Abyssinians say that this Eunuch's name was Indich, and they attribute the beginnings of Christianity in their kingdom to him. For they assert that the Queen, with a great part of her household and people, was baptized by this Eunuch. See Damian a Goes on the customs of Ethiopia, p. 484; Nicephorus, book II of Ecclesiastical History, ch. 6.

Dynast of Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians) of Meroe, which is reckoned to Ethiopia, and was ruled by women. The name Candace passed from the age of Augustus to the age of Vespasian to the queens of Meroe, as we have learned from Strabo XVII, Pliny VI. 29.

who was over all her treasure) He explains the general term 'dynast' more specifically, signifying that he was a treasurer, which is among the principal offices.

Euthymius in Ps. 67 says that this eunuch was next in the Empire of Ethiopia after the Queen: he hallucinates, however, while he attributes the name of Candace to him, which was a common name for the Queens. See Dio book LV, Alexander ab Alexandro, Genialium dierum book 1, chapter 2.

who had come to worship in Jerusalem) At the time of Pentecost; he came, however, as a proselyte. For Cornelius was the first-fruits of the uncircumcised.

He did not come simply to adore: for adoration could take place everywhere, but to offer sacrifices. Therefore, 'proskynesis' is to be understood as adoration joined with sacrifice, as in John IV. 24, or as solemn adoration, which took place during the feast. That this eunuch had already been catechized by the Prophets, Irenaeus teaches in book III, chapter XXXVII; whether he was a Gentile or truly a Jew by birth, it could be a matter of doubt: for all nations had Jews as residents.

Casp. Barth. in book V of his Adversaria, ch. 2, teaches: it is nevertheless more likely that he was a proselyte of that order which the Hebrews call גרי צדק, proselytes of righteousness, who undertook circumcision and other Jewish rites. And thus, regarding the first uncircumcised entry, after the divine vision, it remains valid for Peter. Strabo, book XVII, teaches that there was great familiarity between the Ethiopians and the Jews and agreement in religion, and Josephus, book VIII, ch. 4, testifies that they were also accustomed to be circumcised, not to mention that the Kings of Ethiopia affirm themselves to be sons of Solomon and David, as being descended from the Queen of Sheba by Solomon, as Damianus Goës reports.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ) Eunuchi viri dicuntur, quod vi- rorum habeant speciem.

εὐνᢈχος) Terentius. Eunuchum porro dixti velle te. Quia solæ utuntur his reginæ. nempe ad evitandas suspiciones. Impletum hic mystice id, quod dixit Esaias c. LVI. 4. 5. & quod est in Ps. LXXII. 10.

Drusius vero in l. V. præterit: virum hoc loco ne- gat esse nomen sexus, quum Eunuchi evirati sint: Sed locutionem esse pleonasticam; ut vir Ægyptius in Genesi, vir Judæus Zach. VIII. 23. Neq; concedit Lud. de Dieu, voce εὐνᢈχος, quæ respondet Ebræo סריס, semper castratum notare, imo de Principe adhibe- ri è Jer. 34. 19. docet. Ita nomen δυνάστης vocis hu- jus erit ἐξηγητικὸν. Cons. Gen. 37. 36. c. 40. 1. Esth. 4. 5. Huic Eunucho nomen fuisse Indich, dicunt Abyssini, eique Christianismi primordia in suo regno tribuunt. Ab hoc enim Eunucho baptiza- tam esse Reginam cum magna parte familiæ, & po- puli ejus asserunt. V. Damian. à Goës de Æthiop. morib. p. 484. Niceph. l. II. Histor. Eccl. c. 6.

Δυνάστης Κανδάκης τῆς βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων) Meroës quæ Æthiopiæ accensetur, & erat γυναικοκρατυμένη. Nomen Candaces ab Augusti ævo ad Vespasiari ævum ad Meroës reginas transiit, ut didicimus ex Strab. XVII. Plinio VI. 29.

ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης ἀυτῆς) Dnastæ vocem genera- lem, specialius explicat, significans fuisse Γαζαφύλακα, quod inter præcipua est munera.

Euthymius in Ps. 67. Eunuchum hunc in Impe- rio Æthiopiæ proximum post Reginam fuisse, ait: Hallucinatur autem, dum ei nomen Candaces tri- buit, quod Reginarum nomen commune fuit. Vid. Dio l. LV. Alexand. ab Alex. Genial. dier. l. 1. c. 2.

ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ) Tempore Pente- costes; venit autem ut proselytus. Nam incircumciso- rum primitiæ Cornelius.

Non simpliciter adoratum venit: nam adoratio ubique fieri poterat, sed ut sacrificia offerret. Ideo προσκύνησις de adoratione cum sacrificio conjuncta intelligenda, ut Joh. IV. 24. vel de adoratione so- lemni, quæ in festo fiebat. Quod jam prætate- chisatus à Prophetis fuerit hic Eunuchus, docet Irenæus lib. III. c. XXXVII. utrum autem gentilis, an vero Judæus fuerit genere, dubium esse queat: omnes enim nationes Judæos habuisse inquilinos

Casp. Barth. l. V. advers. c.2. docet: verisimilius tamen est, fuisse proselytum ex illo ordine, qui dicuntur Ebræis גרי צדק proselyti justitiæ, qui circumcisionem, aliosque Judaicos ritus suscipiebant. Et ita ad primum incircumcisum ingressum, post visionem divinam, Petrum, ratum manet. Magnam fuisse Æthiopibus cum Judæis familiaritatem & in religione consensionem Strabo l. XVII. docet, eosque circumcidi etiam consuevisse, testatur Joseph. l. IIX. c. 4. ut taceam, quod Æthiopiæ Reges se filios Salomonis, & Davidis esse affirment, utpote prognatos è Regina Sabæ ex Salomone, referente Damiano Goës.
