## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII. ARGUMENT AND DIVI-

The teachers of Antioch, commanded by the Holy Spirit to set apart Barnabas and Paul, send them forth with the laying on of hands, who come to Seleucia and from there sail to Cyprus, and preach in the synagogues at Salamis, heading as far as Paphos, where Saul, who is also called Paul, struck with blindness Bar-Jesus or Elymas the sorcerer, who was attempting to turn the Proconsul Sergius Paulus away from the faith which he was drawing from them. Then they arrive at Perga of Pamphylia, with John departing from them, but they themselves coming to Antioch of Pisidia, where, because Paul held a sermon at the request of the ruler of the synagogue concerning the Israelite people elected by God, exalted in Egypt, led out with a high arm, nurtured in the desert, and with the Canaanites exterminated under the judges, Samuel, and the kings Saul and David, sustained, from whose (David's) seed according to the promise Jesus was raised up as the Savior of the people, with John the Baptist testifying concerning him. Paul testifies that this word of salvation was sent to them (the people of Antioch), when Jesus had been killed by the Jerusalemites, according to the prophecies of the Prophets, and having been resurrected by God, he appeared alive. Announcing the promise, fulfilled in Jesus, both raised up according to the second Psalm, and resurrected from the dead according to the Scriptures concerning the faithful ones of David and concerning the Holy One of the Lord, who would not see corruption; through whom he preaches the remission of sins, warning them not to bring upon themselves the punishment denounced against the contemptuous in the book of the Prophets (Habac. I. 5.). Paul is asked by the Gentiles to preach the word also on days that are not feast days. But on the following Sabbath, while he himself was teaching in the synagogue, with almost the whole city gathering, the Jews, led by envy, contradicting, blasphemed; therefore, the word having been rejected, Paul and Barnabas turn themselves to the Gentiles, according to the Prophetic prediction, with the Gentiles rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, but the Jews, having stirred up a persecution, casting them out of their cities.

There are three parts: I. The setting apart of Barnabas and Saul for the work of the Lord, and the conversion of Sergius Paulus, to v. 12. II. The historical-evangelical-exhortatory sermon of Paul at Antioch. Historical to v. 20. Evangelical to 37. Exhortatory to v. 41. III. The abandonment of the Jews who reject the word, and the conversion to the Gentiles who receive the word, to v. 51.

PART I. The setting apart of Barnabas and Saul with the conversion of Sergius Paulus.

Vers. 1.

In the church that was there) In that which was the church of the Christians there.

Of Antioch, which was the Metropolis of Syria, and is called Antioch absolutely by way of excellence, since the others of that name are spoken of with an addition, Antioch of Pisidia, Antioch of Epiphaneia, etc.

prophets) Instructed by the prophetic gift, which had ceased from the times of Malachi to the times of Christ. Such as was Agabus of Caesarea.

Others, however, prefer to understand the Prophets as interpreters of Scripture, because they are joined with the Teachers, and it is not a matter of the gift of Prophets or of prophecies or predictions.

& διδάσκαλοι) Just as in the Synagogues the first of the elders was he who taught the people and was called רבי or ממנה, so in the Christian Church the τῶ προσῶτος had the same duty: They are the same as the πρεσβύτεροι οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ 1 Tim. V, 17. In large cities such as Antioch, just as there were many Synagogues of the Jews, because they could not all gather in one place, being divided by such great distances, so there were many assemblies of Christians: Each had its own master, who was also called κατ' ἐξοχὴν ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, just as among the Hebrews the זקן הגדול. In important matters, the masters from all the regions of the city would gather, as here.

Here, therefore, Grotius acknowledges that the Presbyters, of whom there were many in one city, were also called Bishops. This is to be noted against the Papistic distinction between Bishops and Presbyters.

Συμεὼν ὁ καλύμενος Νίγερ) A Latin surname given to him by the Romans. You have the same name at the beginning of Dioscorides. A certain pretender to the empire was also called this.

Μαναήν τε) מנחם in the book Juchasim. No Greek word ends in μ. The LXX did not observe this, who were writing for Jews. But Luke, who was writing for those who were also Greeks by birth, changed μ into ν, a letter of similar sound.

Ἡρώδη τῷ τετράρχῃ) Of Agrippa the younger, who was the son of that Agrippa whose death has already been narrated, and who presided not over Judea, as I think, but first over Chalcis, and then over certain other regions, with the title of tetrarch.

σύντροφος) σύντροφος is here translated as 'foster-brother' by the Latin interpreter, as it is also in the Glosses. The word 'collactaneus' exists in Ulpian in law 51, 'collactaneus' D. de manumissis vindicta; regarding a woman, Juvenal and Capella used 'collactaneam'. But the word συντρόφῳ has a wider scope, and signifies one who has been brought up with another from early childhood: as in 2 Maccabees 9:29, and thus Plato, Plutarch, and others use it, nor did the Syrian understand it otherwise here.

Manahen was therefore of a distinguished and illustrious family, inasmuch as he had been brought up with Herod from boyhood.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Antiocheni Doctores à S. S. jussi Barnabam & Paulum segregare, emittunt eos cum χει- ροθεσίᾳ, qui Seleuciam veniunt & inde Cy- prum navigant, & Salamine in Synagogis prædicant, usque Paphum tendentes, ubi Bar-Iesu vel Elyman Magum, Sergium Paulum Proconsulem à fide, quam ab ipsis hauriebat, avertere conantem, Saulus, qui & Paulus dicitur, cæcitate percussit. Dein- de Pergen Pamphiliæ appellant, Johanne ab illis discedente, illis vero Antiochiam Pisi- diæ venientibus, ubi quia Principis Synago- gæ rogatione concionem habuit Paulus de populo Israelitico à Deo electo, exaltato in Ægypto, educto brachio excelso, educato in deserto, & exterminatis Cananæis sub judicibus Samuele Regibus Saule & Davi- de, sustentato, à cujus (Davidis) semine se- cundum promissionem excitatus fuerit Ie- sus in Salvatorem populi, testificante de eo Iohanne Baptista. Quod verbum salutis ipsis (Antiochensis) missum testatur Pau- lus, cum ab Hierosolymitanis occisus esset Iesus, secundum vaticinia Prophetarum, & resuscitatus à Deo vivus apparuerit. Annuncians promissum, in Iesu tum exci- tato secundum Psalmum secundum, tum resuscitato è mortuis secundum Scripturas de fidelibus Davidis & de sancto Domini, non visuro corruptionem, impletum; per quem prædicat remissionem peccatorum, monens ne pœnam contemptorum in Pro- phetarum libro (Habac. I. 5.) denuntiatam in se derivent. Rogatur Paulus à genti- bus, ut verbum etiam diebus non festis prædicet. Sabbato autem sequenti, ipso in Synagoga docente, concurrente pene tota urbe, Iudæi invidiâ ducti, contradicentes blasphemabant, ideo obrepertum verbum sese ad gentes convertunt Paulus & Bar- nabas, juxta vaticinium Propheticum gau- dentibus, & verbum Domini glorifican- tibus gentibus, Iudæis vero excitata per- secutione, eos è civitatibus suis ejicien- tibus.

Partes tres sunt I. Barnabæ & Sauli ad opus Domini segregatio, & Sergii Pauli conversio, ad vers. 12. II. Antiochena Pauli Historico-Evange- lico-Parænetica concio. Historica ad v. 20. Evan- gelica ad 37. Parænetica ad v. 41. III. Judæorum verbum repellentium relictio, & ad gentes verbum suscipientes conversio, ad v. 51.

PARS I. Barnabæ & Sauli segregatio cum Sergii Pauli conversione.

Vers. 1.

Κατὰ τὴν ὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν) In ea, quæ ibi erat Ecclesia Christianorum.

Antiochiæ, quæ Syriæ Metropolis erat, & κατ' ἐξοχὴν absolute Antiochia vocatur, cum cæteræ il- lius nominis cum additamento dicantur Antio- chiæ Pisidiæ, Antiochia Epiphaniæ &c.

προφῆται) Instructi Prophetico dono, quod à Malachiæ temporibus ad tempora Christi cessaverat. Tales, qualis Cæsareæ Agabus.

Alii tamen malunt intelligere Prophetas de interpretibus Scripturæ, quia conjunguntur cum Doctoribus, nec de dono Prophetarum aut Pro- phetiis vel prædictionibus agitur.

& διδάσκαλοι) Sicut in Synagogis primus senum is erat, qui docebat populum & רבי aut ממנה vocabatur, ita in Ecclesia Christiana τῶ προσῶτος idem erat munus: Iidem sunt πρεσβύτεροι οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ 1. Tim. V, 17. In magnis urbibus qualis Antiochia, sicut multæ erant Ju- dæorum Synagogæ, quia omnes in unum locum coire non poterant, tantis spatiis divisi, ita plures Christianorum con- ventus: Singulis suus magister, qui & κατ' ἐξοχὴν dictus ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, sicut Hebræis זקן הגדול. In rebus magnis magistri ex omnibus urbis regionibus coibant ut hic.

Hic ergo Presbyteros, quorum in una urbe plures erant, agnoscit Grotius, etiam Epi- scopos vocatos esse. Quod contra distinctionem Episcoporum & Presbyterorum Papisticam obser- vandum.

Συμεὼν ὁ καλύμενος Νίγερ) Cognomen Latinum ei a Romanis datum. Habes nomen idem in Diosco- ridis initio. Etiam imperii affectator quidam sic di- ctus.

Μαναήν τε) מנחם in libro Juchasim. Græca vox nulla in μ terminatur. Non observarunt id LXX. qui Ju- dæis scribebant. At Lucas qui etiam ortu Græcis scribe- bat μ mutavit in ν vicini soni literam.

Ἡρώδη τῷ τετράρχῃ) Agrippæ minoris, qui filius illius Agrippæ, cujus mors jam narrata, non Iudææ ut puto, sed Chalcidi primum, deinde & aliis quibusdam regionibus præfuit tetrarchæ nomine.

σύντροφος) σύντροφος hic collactaneus vertitur à Latino interprete, ut & in Glossis. Extat vox collactanei apud Ulpianum in l. 51. collactaneus D. de manumissis vindi- cta. de fœmina, collactaneam dixere Iuvenalis & Capella. At vocabulum συντρόφῳ latius patet, significatque eum, qui à prima ætate cum altero educatus est: ut 2. Macc. IX. 29. atque ita utuntur Plato, Plutarchus & alii, nec aliter hic accepit Syrus.

Fuit ergo Manahe insignis & illustris fami- liæ, utpote qui cum Herode à puero educatus erat.

## 13:2
Verse 2.

λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν) The verb λειτουργεῖν has a sufficiently wide scope, but since fasting is added, I think the Syrian and the Arab rightly took this word in this place in the sense of praying: for prayers and fasting are accustomed to be joined together, Matthew 17:21, Mark 9:29, Luke 2:37, below chapter 14:23, 1 Corinthians 7:5, and therefore the Hebrew צבא is sometimes translated as λειτουργεῖν, sometimes as σπεύδειν.

There is no need, therefore, for that word to be rendered by Erasmus and Cornelius as 'sacrificing'. The Vulgate, authentic to the Papists, uses the general term 'ministering'. Oecumenius and Cajetan interpret it as concerning the preaching of the Gospel. This word in general signifies ministry, as Cornelius à Lapide admits. How, therefore, can a mystical sacrifice be carved out from it, which will be proven to have been in the use of the Church at the Greek Calends? Can those not be said to have ministered to God who preached the word, or who served God with prayers and fastings?

εἶπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον) Through those Prophets.

But it is not clear that those Prophets had been endowed with the gift of Prophecy. The Holy Spirit could have revealed this to someone separately, even if he were not otherwise properly a Prophet: He could also have manifested it in common. And although Prophets endowed with the gift of revealing future or other hidden things had not been present, there were nevertheless men there who were θεόπνευστοι (God-breathed).

ἀφορίσατε δή μοι) As if they were firstborn. For in the law concerning the firstborn, Exodus 13:11, there is ἀφοριεῖς.

(εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτοὺς) that is, πρὸς ὃ κέκλημαι αὐτοὺς. To call here means to destine.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν) Verbum λειτουργεῖν satis late pa- tet, sed cum addatur jejunium, recte puto Syrum & Ara- bem hoc loco hanc vocem sumpsisse in precandi sensu: conjungi enim solent preces, & jejunium, Matth. XVII 21. Marc. IX. 29 Luc. II. 37. infra cap. 14. 23. 1. Corinth. VII. 5. ideoque צבא Hebræum modo vertitur λειτουργεῖν, mo- do σπεύδειν.

Non ergo opus est, ut verbum illud cum Era- smo, & Cornelio reddatur sacrificantibus. Vulgata, Papistis authentica, generali nomine utitur mini- strantibus. Oecumenius & Cajetanus de prædica- tione Evangelii interpretantur. Vox hæc in ge- nere ministerium significat fatente Cornel. à Lapi- de. Quomodo ergo inde exsculpetur sacrificium mystaticum, quod tum in Ecclesiæ usu fuisse ad Calendas Græcas probabitur? Annon ministras- se Deo dici possunt, qui prædicarunt verbum, aut qui orationibus & jejuniis Deo servie- runt?

εἶπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον) Per Prophetas istos.

At Prophetas istos instructos fuisse dono Pro- phetico non liquet. Potuit alicui hoc seorsim revelare S. S. etsi proprie non extiterit alias Pro- pheta: potuit etiam in communi id manifestare. Et licet non adfuissent Prophetæ futura vel occul- ta alia patefaciendi dono præditi: aderant tamen ibi viri θεόπνευστοι.

ἀφορίσατε δή μοι) Tanquam primogenitos. Nam in le- ge de primogenitis Exod. XIII. 11. est ἀφοριεῖς.

εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτοὺς) id est, πρὸς ὃ κέκλημαι αὐτοὺς. Vocare hic est destinare.

## 13:3
Verse 3.

ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς) Invoking the help of God for the ministry imposed upon them. See above chapter 6:6.

ἀπέλυσαν) That is, they said farewell to them. Thus Matt. XIV. 15. 22. 23. ch. XV. 23.

Cornelius à Lapide explains the separation, because the laying on of hands is also mentioned, as that Saul and Barnabas were ordained Bishops, since they are nowhere else read to have been ordained Bishops: But Arias Montanus, Cajetan, and Suarez, as also Grotius, more correctly acknowledge that this laying on of hands was precatory, not ordinative, because Paul had already been ordained an Apostle before, Acts IX. 15. whence he says in Galatians II. 6. that the other Apostles conferred nothing upon him. Here, therefore, the Apostle is only being charged with the execution and sent to evangelize, just as the word χειροτονήθης is used in 2 Cor. VIII. 19. Moreover, Apostles had no need to be ordained to the Episcopate: since the Apostolic dignity includes and embraces this. And by whom is Paul ordained a Bishop there! Not by Peter, as Arator wishes, because he had already departed: not by James the son of Zebedee, because he had been killed by Herod: not by the other Apostles; because they had already departed to their own provinces. Cornelius indeed says that there were other Bishops there who could have ordained him, but he does not prove it: nor was that axiom of Bishops, by which they are distinguished from Presbyters, namely that they alone ordain, proper to that time. Whence Cornelius finally betook himself to this: that St. John, St. Matthias, or some other neighboring Apostle could have been summoned from Judea. But they were immediately sent out when they had been separated by the command of the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands, nor is any Apostle read to have been summoned from elsewhere for the χειροτονία, indeed those who laid on hands had already been mentioned in v. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς) Invocantes Dei opem ad im- positum ipsis ministerium. Vide supra c. VI. 6.

ἀπέλυσαν) Id est, vale illis dixerunt. Sic Matth. XIV. 15. 22. 23. c. XV. 23.

Segregationem, quia impositio manuum etiam commemoratur, ita explicat Cornel. à Lapide, quod Saulus & Barnabas ordinati sint Episcopi, quum nuspiam alias legantur Episcopi ordinati: Sed Ariasmontanus, Cajetanus, & Suarez ut & Grotius rectius agnoscunt hanc impositionem manuum fuisse precatoriam, non ordinativam, quia Paulus jam ante ordinatus erat Apostolus Actorum IX 15. unde Galat. II. 6. ait, quod cæteri Apostoli sibi nihil contulerint. Hic ergo tan- tum imponi ei Apostolus exequutionem & mitti eundem ad evangelizandum, uti verbum χει- ροτονήθης adhibetur 2. Cor. VIII. 19. Apostoli au- tem non opus habebant ordinari ad Episcopa- tum: quum Apostolica dignitas hanc includat & complectatur. Et à quonam ordinatur ibi Paulus Episcopus! Non à Petro, ut Arator vult, quia ille jam abierat: non a Jacobo Ze- bedæi, quia is interfectus erat ab Herode: non à cæteris Apostolis; quia jam discesserant in suas provincias. Alios ibi fuisse Episcopos, qui or- dinare ipsum potuerunt, ait quidem Corne- lium, sed non probat: neque tum Episcopo- rum illud, qua à Presbyteris distincti sunt, axio- ma erat propriam, alios nempe ordinare. Unde Cornelius eo se tandem recepit: potuisse e Judaea advocari S. Johannem, S. Matthiam, aut quem alium vicinorum Apostolum. Sed confestim illi cum segregati jussu Spiritus sancti per impositionem manuum emissi sunt, nec ullus legitur ad χειροτονίαν accersitus aliunde Apostolus, imo qui manus imposuerunt, jam commemorati erant v. 1.

## 13:4
Ver. 4.

κατῆλθον εἰς τὴν Σελεύκειαν) There also they were to see the extinguished kingdom, Magog, as we said above in ch. XI. 25.

The destruction of the Magogian kingdom does not pertain to these times, but to the very last: as we are taught from Ezekiel and the Apocalypse.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

κατῆλθον εἰς τὴν Σελεύκειαν) Ibi quoque visuri extinctum regnum, Magog. ut supra diximus c. XI. 25.

Destructio regni Magogici non ad haec pertinet tempora, sed ad novissima: ut ex Ezech. & Apocalypsi edocemur.

## 13:5
Ver. 5.

ἐν Σαλαμῖνι) In the city which Teucer named from the name of his own fatherland. 'A Salamis in a new land will be ambiguous,' as Horace sings.

This, later called Constantia by the Emperor Constantine, is now called Famagusta; captured a hundred years ago by Selim, Emperor of the Turks.

ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων) Many Jews in Cyprus. Jerome in the Chronicle of Eusebius at the time of Trajan: The Jews, having killed the Gentiles in it, subverted Salamis of Cyprus.

εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην) Mark by surname, of whom above in ch. XII. 25.

ὑπηρέτην) One performing lesser duties, as Deacons in the Church. See what is said at Luke IV. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ἐν Σαλαμῖνι) In urbe quam Teucer ex patriae suae dixit nomine. Ambiguam tellure nova Salamine futuram; ut canit Horatius.

Haec a Constantino Imper. postea Constantia dicta, jam Famagusta vocatur; a centum annis expugnata a Selymo Turcarum Imperatore.

ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων) Multi in Cypro Judaei. Hieronymus in Chronico Eusebii ad tempora Trajani: Salaminam Cypri interfectis in ea gentibus, subvertere Judaei.

εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην) Marcum cognomine, de quo supra c. XII. 25.

ὑπηρέτην) Obeuntem munera minora, ut in Ecclesia Diaconi. Vide quae ad Lucam IV. 20.

## 13:6
Vers. 6.

διελθόντες δὲ τὴν νῆσον) In the Manuscript ὅλην τὴν νῆσον because they had come from the East all the way to the West.

ἄχρι Πάφου) About to destroy the worship of Venus.

For this city of Cyprus was made famous by the temple of Venus.

ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦς) Son of Jesus or of some Joshua. Such names are Barjona, Bartholomew, and others formed patronymically.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

διελθόντες δὲ τὴν νῆσον) In Manuscripto ὅλην τὴν νῆσον quia ab Oriente ad Occidentem usque venerant.

ἄχρι Πάφου) Destructuri Veneris cultum.

Haec enim Cypri urbs templo Veneris nobilitata fuit.

ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦς) Filius Jesu sive Josuae alicujus. Talia nomina sunt Barjonae, Bartholomaei aliaque facta πατρωνυμικῶς.

## 13:7
Vers. 7.

τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ) This is a catachresis. For properly, he who was in charge of Cyprus was called ἀντιστράτηγος. But it is no wonder that the Greeks mixed these up, or rather, as they were excellent flatterers, gave the most honorific name possible to the governors of provinces. It is a general name for a president, which one may also use here in Latin.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ) Est κατάχρησις. Proprie enim, qui Cypro praeerat vocabatur ἀντιστράτηγος. Sed non mirum est Graecos ista permiscuisse aut potius ut egregii erant adulatores, nomen quam honorificentissimum dedisse provinciarum rectoribus. Generale nomen est praesidis: quo & hic Latine uti licet.

## 13:8
Vers. 8.

Ελύμας) This was the other name for him who was just called Barjesus.

ὁ μάγος· οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ) That is, ἐλύμας signifies a magus, namely in the Arabic language: for עלמא means magi. Whence you might not wrongly conjecture that he was an Arab. See what we have said at Matt. II. 1.

That the Arabic word is derived from the name Elymas, עלים, which is attributed particularly to those who investigate divine and human things and are conspicuous for their knowledge of them, is observed after Beza and Nicol. Fuller, Miscell. Serm. chap. II, by B. Glaffius, Grammat. S. p. 765, and by Johan. Ernest. Gerhardus at this place. Which also occurs in Exod. XVIII. 19 in the Arabic version of R. Saadia. Compare Ludov. de Dieu at this place; Cornelius a Lapide, however, with Sanctius, considers it a Cyprian name.

Seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith) To hinder him from believing the Gospel.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Ελύμας) Hoc alterum erat nomen illi, qui modo dictus Barjesus.

ὁ μάγος· οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ) Id est, ἐλύμας significat μάγον, nempe Arabum lingua: nam עלמא magi. Unde Arabem hunc fuisse non male conjeceris. Vide quae diximus ad Matth. II. I.

Vocem Arabicam esse deductam ex nomine Elymas, עלים quod peculiariter tribuitur illis, qui res divinas & humanas scrutantur, & earum cognitione sunt conspicui, observat post Bezam & Nicol. Fullerum ser. miscell. cap. II B. Glaffium Grammat. S. p. 765. B. Johan. Ernest. Gerhardus ad h. l. Quae etiam occurrit Exod. XIIX. 19. in versione Arabica R. Saadia. Conf. Ludov. de Dieu ad h. l. pro Cyprio tamen nomine habet cum Sanctio, Cornelius a Lapide.

Ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως) Impedire ne crederet Evangelio.

## 13:9
Vers. 9.

Saul, who is also Paul) That is, he who, from the time he began to associate with the Romans, began to be called by this name, which does not differ from his own. Thus, he who is Jesus to the Jews is Jason to the Greeks: Hillel is Pollio: Onias is Menelaus: Jakim is Alcimus. Among the Romans, Silas is Silvanus, as Jerome noted; Pasides is Pansa, as Suetonius notes in Craffitio: Diocles is Diocletianus: Biglinitza, the sister of Justinian, is Vigilantia in Roman. Thus also Strabo said in book XII that Persian names are somewhat changed by the Greeks, and Leunclavius says the Turks do the same now.

and looking intently at him) See above chapter III. v. 12. chapter VI. v. 15.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Σαῦλος δὲ ὁ καὶ Παῦλος) Id est, qui, ex quo cum Romanis conversari coepit, hoc nomine a suo non abludente, coepit a Romanis appellari. Sic qui Jesus Judaeis, Graecis Jason: Hillel Pollio: Onias Menelaus: Jakim Alcimus. Apud Romanos Silas, Silvanus, ut notavit Hieronymus Pasides, Pansa, ut Suetonius in Craffitio: Diocles Diocletianus: Biglinitza, soror Justiniani, Romane Vigilantia. Sic & nomina Persica a Graecis nonnihil immutari dixit Strabo libro XII, idemque nunc facere Turcas Leunclavius.

καὶ ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν) Vide supra cap. III. v. 12. cap. VI. v. 15.

## 13:10
Vers. 10. καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιεργίας) In the Glossary ῥᾳδιεργία is false. Below in chapter XVIII, 14, we have ῥᾳδιούργημα, by which name Plutarch calls the fabrication of a false testament.

υἱὲ Διαβόλε) Reflecting the nature of the Devil. See John VIII. v. 44.

οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας) Tertullian uses 'transvertere'; that indeed means to throw something across, so that the journey cannot be completed. See what we said above in chapter VII. 51.

Latin:

Vers. 10. καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιεργίας) In Glossario ῥᾳδιεργία fal- sum. Infra cap. XVIII, 14. habemus ῥᾳδιούργημα quo nomi- ne Plutarchus vocat falsi testamenti fabricationem.

υἱὲ Διαβόλε) Diaboli ingenium referens. Vid. Johan. VIII. v. 44.

οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας) Transverte- re Tertullianus; id vero est ex transverso aliquid objice- re, quo minus iter peragi possit. Vide quæ diximus su- pra cap. VII. 51.

## 13:11
Vers. 11.

Ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ κυρίου ἐπί σε) The hand of the Lord signifies a powerful action for good or evil. But here for evil. And ἐπί has the same value as the particle ב in Ruth I. v. 13.

ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος) With two words he expressed the Hebrew סנורים in Genesis XIX. v. 11, 2 Kings VI. v. 18.

ἐζήτει χειραγωγὸς) See above c. IX. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

Ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ κυρίου ἐπί σε) Manus Domini quamvis poten- tem actionem significat in bonum vel malum. Sed hic in malum. Et ἐπί valet idem quod particula ב Ruth. I. v. 13.

ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος) Duabus vocibus expreffit Hebræam סנורים Genes. XIX. v. 11. 2. Reg. VI. v. 18.

ἐζήτει χειραγωγὸς) Vide supra c. IX. 8.

## 13:12
Vers. 12.

ἐπίστευσεν) He believed the Gospel: Nor yet did he resign his magistracy, for if that had been done, Luke would not have been silent about it.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ἐπίστευσεν) Credidit Evangelio: Neque tamen se abdi- cavit magistratu, quod si factum fuisset, non reticuisset id Lucas.

## 13:13
Vers. 13.

εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας) Famous for the temple of Diana, as Mela teaches us. Thus everywhere the Apostles brought their hand to bear against idols.

ἀποχωρήσας ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν) Namely, fleeing from labor and dangers, as the Greek writers say here. See below chapter XV. v. 38.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας) Celebrem Dianæ templo, ut Mela nos docet. Ita ubique manum cum idolis confere- bant Apostoli.

ἀποχωρήσας ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν) Nempe laboris & periculorum fugiens, ut hic ajunt Græci scriptores. Vide infra cap. XV. v. 38.

## 13:14
Verse 14.

εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τῆς Πισιδίας) Not that one of Syria about which above. Concerning this one see Strabo in book XII. Here the Apostle begins to enter those parts in which Gog had reigned and had been destroyed.

That Gog had reigned in Antioch and had been destroyed there, Grotius has not indicated whence he has this, nor does his bare assertion suffice.

PART II.

Paul's Historical-Evangelical-Parenetic sermon at Antioch.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τῆς Πισιδίας) Non illam Syriæ de qua su- pra. de hac vide Strabonem libro XII. hic Apostolus in- trare incipit eas partes, in quibus Gog regnaverat & de- structus fuerat.

Gogum Antiochiæ regnasse, ibique destru- ctum esse, unde habeat Grotius non indicavit, nec nuda ejus assertio sufficit.

PARS II.

Antiochena Pauli Historico-Evangelico-Pa- renetica concio.

## 13:15
Verse 15. μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν Προφητῶν) According to the custom received from the times of Ezra, so that besides portions from the Law, which was the old practice, some portion also from the Prophets would be read every Sabbath.

οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι) פרנסים or זקנים, whose leader by way of eminence is the ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ראש הקהל.

εἴ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως) That is, of prophecy. See what we said above in chapter IV. 36.

Latin:

Vers. 15. μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν Προφητῶν) More recepto ab Esdræ temporibus, ut præter particulas de lege, quod vetus erat, etiam de Prophetis particula aliqua sabbatis singulis legeretur.

οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι) פרנסים sive זקנים, quorum Princeps κατ' ἐξοχὴν ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ראש הקהל.

εἴ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως) Id est Prophetiæ. Vide quæ diximus supra c. IV. 36.

## 13:16
Verse 16.

καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ) Repeat what was said above in chapter XII. verse 17.

καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεὸν) That is, the οἱ σεβόμενοι τῶν ἐθνήτων below in chapter XVII. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ) Repete quæ dicta supra cap. XII. v. 17.

καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεὸν) Id est, οἱ σεβόμενοι τῶν ἐθνήτων infra c. XVII. 4.

## 13:17
Verse 17.

ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου) This Pisidas says, pointing out the Jews with his finger.

ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν) He did not affect them with ordinary benefits.

καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν) That is, He established them in favor with the King through Joseph.

ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ) During their very sojourn in Egypt. Παροικία in Hebrew is מגר as in Gen. XXVIII. v. 4.

καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς) From the words of God, Exod. VI. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου) Hoc dicit Pisidis Judæos digito monstrans.

ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν) Non vulgaribus beneficiis affecit.

καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν) Id est, in gratia apud Regem eos constituit per Josephum.

ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ) Durante incolatu ipso- rum in Ægypto. Παροικία Hebraice מגר ut Genes. XXVIII. v. 4.

καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς) Ex verbis Dei Exod. VI. 6.

## 13:18
Vers. 18.

τεσσαρακονταετῆ χρόνον) The same sense as Psalm XCV. 10.

ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς) He endured their ungrateful ways. This word is from the LXX, Deut. I. 31, where Luke correctly reads ἐτροποφόρησέ σε and not τροποφορήσει σε. For in the Hebrew it is נשאך, that is, He endured you. In the Chaldean it is סברך. The word τροποφορῶν is good Greek; Cicero to Atticus XIII. 29: 'In this, my pride, I pray you, endure.'

Latin:

Vers. 18.

τεσσαρακονταετῆ χρόνον) Idem sensus Psal. XCV. 10.

ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς) Ingratos eorum mores pertulit. Vox hæc est ex LXX. Deut. I. 31. ubi Lucas recte legit ἐτρο- ποφόρησέ σε & non τροποφορήσει σε. In Hebræo enim est נשאך id est pertulit te. In Chaldæo סברך Est vox τρο- ποφορῶν bene Græca Cicero ad Atticum XIII. 29. In huc τὸν τύφον μου πρὸς θεῶν τροποφόρησον.

## 13:19
Vers. 19.

ἔθνη ἑπτὰ) Six are named, Exod. III. 8: Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites. But to these must be added the Girgashites, גרגשי, from Neh. XI. 8, whom the Hebrews say went into Africa. And Procopius names them in African affairs, Vandalic War II.

κατεκληρονόμησεν αὐτοῖς τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν) Thus the older books have it, including that one in England; others have κατεκληροδότησεν. It makes no difference. For נחל in Piel or הנחיל in Hiphil is sometimes translated κατακληρονομεῖν as in Deut. III. 28, Joshua XIV. 2, and

alibi, modo κατακληροδοτεῖν ut Deuter. I, 38. Josuæ XIX. v. 51.

Since the word κατακληροδότησεν is not unusual and almost all codices have it, Grotius wrongly substituted another from one or two variant codices.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ἔθνη ἑπτὰ) Sex nominantur, Exod. III. 8. Cananæi, Hithæi, Amorrhæi, Perizzæi, Hevæi, Jebusæi. Sed ad- dendi his Girgazeni גרגשי ex Neh. XI. 8. quos in Afri- cam ivisse ajunt Hebræi. Et eos nominat in Africanis rebus Procopius, Vandalicorum II.

κατεκληρονόμησεν αὐτοῖς τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν) Sic habent libri antiquiores, etiam ille in Anglia; alii κατεκληροδότησεν. Ni hil refert. Nam נחל in Piel aut הנחיל in Hiphil, modo vertitur κατακληρονομεῖν ut Deut. III. 28. Josuæ XIV. 2. &

alibi, modo κατακληροδοτεῖν ut Deuter. I, 38. Josuæ XIX. v. 51.

Quum verbum κατακληροδότησεν non inusita- tum sit & plerique omnes id habeant codices, perperam aliud ex uno atque altero variante codice substituit Grotius.

## 13:20
Verse 20.

καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα) That codex in England and others, which the Latin interpreter used, more correctly connect those words ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα with the preceding: and then place μετὰ ταῦτα. Now those approximately four hundred and fifty years begin from the exodus out of Egypt, and end at that time when David cast the Jebusites out of Zion. So much time was spent in settling the Hebrew nation in those seats. Solomon built the Temple in the four hundred and eightieth year from the exodus, 1 Kings 6:1. David, however, reigned for nearly forty years, 2 Samuel 5:5.

Some, taking that μετὰ ταῦτα as if this epoch were to be begun from the departure out of Egypt, since they see that only 300 years are found from then until Samuel, say that the Greek text lies in error and that τριακοσίοις should be read, to which the marginal gloss of B. Luther and D. Behmius the Elder in his Chronological Introduction, page 51, also incline. But since all codices agree, and the Oriental interpreters, the Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic, or the Vulgate do not have a different number, no corruption of the text in the number is to be admitted here. Nor is a transposition of the text to be invented on account of one manuscript and the Latin Vulgate version (which often observed the sense, even here, not precisely the position of the words): nor is that Grotian explanation to be admitted: since in the following verse the years of Saul are expressly added, from which it is not likely that they are included in this number. Wherefore the explanation of those who interpret the words thus is more correct: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα, and after those things for about 450 years (in such a way that the Apostle narrated what was done through the acts which he recounted from verse 17, such as that God chose the Fathers, that He exalted the people when they were inhabitants in the land of Egypt, and led them out of it with an uplifted arm, and bore their manners in the desert, and having destroyed the Canaanites, distributed the land to them by lot) ἔδωκε κριτὰς He gave judges. Which explanation the Papists cannot reject, since it is confirmed by the Vulgate version, which is authentic for them. For it evidently refers verse 20, the epoch, to the preceding narrative and teaches that after 450 years had passed, judges were given, but that the time of the judges is not contained in them, since it reads thus: As it were after four hundred and fifty years: and after these things He gave judges. In which manner the Ethiopic also rendered it: and after four hundred and fifty years He set leaders over them. And thus the calculation most certainly stands: for from the election of the Fathers in Isaac or from the birth of Isaac, which term from which he hints at in verse 17, to the time of the judges, about 450 years have elapsed, since from the birth of Isaac to Jacob 60 years flowed by, from the birth of Jacob to the entry into Egypt 130, and the years of sojourn in Egypt are counted as 210, and from the exodus to the distribution of the land 47 years intervened. When these numbers are added into a sum, 447 years emerge, that is, about 450, because only three are lacking for a round number. Which explanation, handed down in the Critica Sacra on page 794, was also followed by B. Joh. Ernest. Gerhard in his Analecta on this passage, and Cornelius à Lapide also explained it in the same way, praising Bede, the Gloss, Lyranus, Hugo, and Dionysius the Carthusian for the same opinion. Compare also Junius in his Parallels, book 1, through 95, and Beza, as also Ludov. de Dieu on this passage.

He gave judges, until Samuel the prophet) Which were dictators with power, and not with royal pomp. See what we have said regarding the book of Judges.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα) Rectius codex ille in Anglia & alii, quibus usus est interpres Lati- nus, illa ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα connectunt cum præcedentibus: & deinde ponunt μετὰ ταῦτα. Anni au- tem illi ferme quadringenti & quinquaginta incipiunt ab exitu ex Ægypto, desinunt in illud tempus, quo David ex Sione ejecit Jebusæos. Tantum temporis impensum fuit ad collocandam gentem Hebræam in illis sedibus. Salo- mon anno ab exitu quadringentesimo octuagesimo Tem- plum condidit, 1. Reg. VI. 1. Regnavit autem David per annos ferme quadraginta, 2. Sam. V. 5.

Nonnulli illud μετὰ ταῦτα accipientes, quasi inde ab eductione ex Ægypto inchoanda hæc de- mum Epocha sit, quum videant 300. tantum an- nos inde reperiri usque ad Samuelem, Græcum textum in mendo cubare, & legendum esse τρια- κοσίοις ajunt, quo etiam abit Glossa margin. B. Lutheri, & D. Behmius Senior in Chronol. ma- nuduct. pag. 51. Sed quum omnes codices con- sentiant, nec interpretes Orientales, Syrus, Arabs, Æthiops, aut Vulgata alium numerum habeant, nulla hic admittenda textus in numero corruptio. Neque ob unum MS. & Latinam versionem vul- gata (quæ sensum sæpe, etiam hic, observavit, non verborum præcise positum) transpositio tex- tus fingenda: aut explicatio illa Grotiana admit- tenda: siquidem vers. sequenti Saulis anni expref- se subjiciantur, unde hoc numero eos compre- hensos esse non est verisimile. Quapropter re- ctius illorum habet explicatio, qui verba ita inter- pretantur: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακο- σίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα, & post illa annis circiter 450. (ita ut narratum per acta, quæ inde à v. 17. narravit Apostolus, ut pote quod elegerit Deus Patres, quod populum exaltarit, quum essent incolæ in terra Ægy- pti, & ex ea eduxerit brachio elato, & mores eo- rum pertulerit in deserto, & destructis Cananæis sor- te terram iis distribuerit) ἔδωκε κριτὰς dedit judi- ces. Quam explicationem Pontificii rejicere non possunt, cum confirmetur à versione vulgata illis authentica. Quippe quæ evidenter refert v. 20. epocham ad antecedentem narrationem & post transactos 450. annos, datos judices docet, non autem iis tempus judicum contineri, quum ita habeat: Quasi post quadringentos & quinquagin- ta annos: & post hæc dedit judices. Quo pacto & Æthiops reddidit: & post quadringentos & quin- quaginta annos præposuit eis præsides. Atque ita computus sese habet certissime: nam inde ab ele- ctione Patrum in Isaac vel a nato Isaaco, quem terminum à quo v. 17. innuit, ad tempus judicum, 450. anni circiter elapsi sunt, quum à nato Isaaco ad Jacobum anni effluxerint 60. à Jacobo vero nato ad introitum in Ægyptum 130. ac commo- rationis in Ægypto anni numerentur 210. ab exi- tu vero ex Ægypto usque ad distributionem terræ 47. intercesserint anni. Quibus numeris in sum- mam redactis prodeunt 447. anni, hoc est, circi- ter 450. quia tres tantum ad numerum rotundum desiderantur. Quam explicationem in Critic. sa- cro traditam pag. 794. sequutus etiam est B. Joh. Ernest. Gerhard. analect. ad h. l. atque ita exposuit quoque Cornelius à Lapide, in eandem senten- tiam laudans Bedam, Glossam, Lyranum, Hugonem, Dionysium Carthus. Conf. & Junius in parall. l. 1. per 95. & Beza, ut & Ludov. de Dieu in h. l.

ἔδωκε κριτὰς, ἕως Σαμουὴλ τῆ προφήτε) Quod dictatores cum potestate, non & cum pompa Regia. Vide quæ ad li- brum Judicum diximus.

## 13:21
Verse 21.

κἀκεῖθεν) And thence, that is, from him. Thus Cicero: Facere a pele discrepantiam; for: from whom I might differ: And Virgil: Genus unde Latinum, that is, from whom. In Terence: Vnde petitur, that is, the defendant from whom it is sought.

ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα) This they wanted, and that while they still had a Prophet, that is, God Himself by whom they were ruled.

Ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν) From which tribe this one also was, better than that Saul, having obtained a very great kingdom under Christ, a mystical destroyer of the Amalekites, prepared to die for the people of God, rejected, not as that one was by God, but by his own countrymen who were offending the name of God.

ἔτη τεσσαράκοντα) This is to be referred to that which preceded ἕως Σαμουὴλ τῦ προφήτε: with the others inserted as if by parenthesis; so that it may be understood that Samuel performed his prophetic office, partly before the reign of Saul, and partly while he guided Saul with his counsels, for forty years in total. For Samuel is believed by the Hebrews to have died only four months before the death of Saul. Thus Samuel, as another Moses, equaled the times of Moses in caring for the people.

There will be no need for a parenthesis if it is said that the years of Samuel are included. Indeed, 40 years elapsed from Samuel until the death of Saul; which are commemorated here. This Melchior Canus rashly denies in book II of Loci, chapter 5, assigning 40 years to Saul after Samuel, along with Eusebius in book X of the Praeparatio, chapter 7. But he who corrected this in the Chronicle, supporting our opinion, is with Josephus in book III of Jewish Antiquities, near the end, Sulpicius, Abulensis, and Tremellius.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

κἀκεῖθεν) Et inde, id est, ab ipso. Sic Cicero: Facere apele discrepantiam; pro: à quo discrepem: Et Virgilius: Genus unde Latinum, id est, à quo. Apud Terentium: Vnde peti- tur, id est, reus à quo petitur.

ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα) Hoc voluerunt, idque cùm Prophe- tam adhuc haberent, id est Deum ipsum à quo regeren- tur.

Ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν) Ex qua & hic erat melior illo Saul, regnum sub Christo adeptus maximum, destructor mysticus Amalekitarum, mori paratus pro populo Dei, re- jectus, non ut ille à Deo, sed à suis popularibus nomen Dei obsendentibus.

ἔτη τεσσαράκοντα) Hoc referendum est ad id, quod præ- cessit ἕως Σαμουὴλ τῦ προφήτε: cæteris velut per parenthe- sin interjectis; ut intelligatur Samuel munere suo Prophe- tico functus, partim ante Saulis, regnum, partim dum consiliis Saulam rexit, simul XL. nam quatuor tantum ante mortem Saulis mensibus creditur Hebræis mortuus Samuel. Ita Samuel velut alter Moses curando popu- lum Mosis æquavit tempora.

Parenthesi opus non erit, si dicatur, quod in- cludantur anni Samuelis. Nimirum à Samuele usque ad obitum Saulis 40. effluxerunt anni; qui hic commemorati sunt. Quod temere negat Melch. Canus l. II. de Loc. c. 5, post Samuelem Sauli 40. assignans annos cum Eusebio lib. X. prœp. cap. 7. Qui vero id emendavit in Chronico, no- stræ adstipulans sententiæ, cum Josepho lib. III. Jud. Antiqu. sub finem, Sulpitio, Abulensi, Tre- mellio.

## 13:22
Verse 22. καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν) That is, having removed him from human affairs: for God did not wish to hand over the promised kingdom to David before Saul had died. Thus he who has died is called μεταστὰς, 2 Maccabees 11:23, and he who is taken away from human affairs is called μετατίθεσθαι, Hebrews 11:5.

ἤγειρεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Δαβὶδ) הֵקִים he raised up, he gave to be looked upon.

εὗρον Δαβὶδ) Psalm 89:21.

Ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μ8) That is, most pleasing to me. See above chapter 7:46. He expresses in other words what had preceded in the Psalm, chosen from the people.

In those words of the Psalm, we said in the Illustrious Bible of the Old Testament on Ps. LXXXIX that by the chosen one from the people, not David, but Christ is to be understood. We warned, however, that those words to the young David concerning David himself, the son of Jesse, are to be accepted according to this Pauline interpretation. Where indeed (which is to be observed here) a mistake of the copyist has crept in, namely in Volume I, page 1070, col. a, line 23, the words 'Servant David' are to be deleted, which I do not find in my autograph, and they clearly pervert our meaning. Furthermore, in order to disclose my second thoughts about this Psalm, because of the evidence of this Apostolic passage and the coherence of the words of the Psalmist v. 20, it now seems to be admitted that the chosen hero from the people and the servant David are understood as the same subject, the son of Jesse, and thus also the words of v. 4 concerning the chosen one and concerning David the servant will concern the same person in the same place, and will explain each other: I have made a covenant with my chosen one and I have sworn to David my servant, although the object of the covenant confirmed by an oath, or what has the force of an oath, concerning the eternal seed and the building of the throne for generation and generation, is to be understood not of the bodily seed of David nor of his worldly throne, but of the spiritual seed and the heavenly throne proper to the son of David, the Messiah: because the bodily seed of David was not propagated forever, but has been cast away now for some centuries, and his worldly throne has ceased, the scepter having been taken away from Judah: Conf. Isa. IX. 7. Luke I. 32. 33. By which pact also those things concerning the oath made to David in the praised Psalm v. 36 are to be understood. But as for those things which are held concerning universal dominion and concerning the firstborn in v. 26, 27, which, as we showed in the explanation of the Psalm and also in Theol. Natur. & Revel. p. 1373 seq., sound of no one else but the Messiah; it is to be observed that these are predicated not of David, but of the horn of David. & Revel. p. 1373 seq., it is to be observed that these are predicated not of David, but of the horn of David. For since God promised David among other things: His horn shall be exalted in my name, v. 25, which horn is the Messiah himself, as is evident from v. 18 & Ps. CXXXII. 17, Luke I. 69; our shield, and our King, as is held in v. 19, Ethan now prophesies about him from the person of God the Father, whom he introduces as speaking, and explains in what manner he wishes to exalt that horn of David, namely: I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers. The cause of such an ὑπερυψώσεως (exaltation), because he is not a mere man, ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος (a bare man), but the proper, natural, true, and eternal Son of God; He shall call me, Thou art my Father. Concerning which more in the exegesis of the Psalm. And in that way the predicates are continued concerning that same subject, the horn of David, the Messiah King, v. 28 seqq. Concerning the spiritual seed of the Messiah and his sons, and concerning his eternal throne. For in this one man in grace, in the Messiah, a spiritual seed is attributed to David, and David himself through him was the son of God, and pleasing to God: But his throne is eternal, not that the seat and kingdom of David is to be eternal, Luke I. 32. 33. But it ought not to move anyone that the name קֶרֶן is of the feminine gender, Dan. VIII. 9, Zech. I. 18. For that σύνεσις (understanding) also, concerning which Glassius lib. III. tract. II. Can. XVI. Gramp. S. can have a place in such things, and that name is more correctly established as common by Buxtorff, since it also occurs in the masculine, Ps. LXXV, 11. &c. These things, therefore, I have thought necessary to warn at present for the elucidation of the illustrious Prophetic Psalm, which I commit to the judgment of pious searchers of the word. Furthermore, that ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου (a man after my own heart) is not taken from that Psalm, but from 1 Sam. XIII. 14, the αὐτοψία (personal observation) and inspection of the passage sufficiently teaches.

who shall do all my wills) Namely in ruling the people. It is the same as what is said in Ps. LXXVIII. 72.

Latin:

Vers. 22. καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν) Id est, amoto è rebus humanis: non enim ante Davidi regnum promissum tra- dere voluit Deus, quam mortuus esset Saul. Sic μεταστὰς dicitur, qui obiit, 2. Macc. XI. 23. & μετατίθεσθαι qui ex rebus humanis aufertur, Hebr. XI. 5.

ἤγειρεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Δαβὶδ) הֵקִים erexit, conspicien- dum dedit.

εὗρον Δαβὶδ) Psal. LXXXIX. 21.

Ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μ8) Id est mihi gratissimum. Vide supra cap. VII. 46. Aliis verbis exprimit, quod in Psalmo præcesserat, electum de populo.

In illis Psalmi verbis per electum de populo non Davidem, sed Christum intelligi in Bibliis Illustr. Veteris Testam. ad Ps. LXXXIX. diximus. Ver- ba tamen illa Juveni David de Davide ipso filio Jesse, juxta hanc Paulinam interpretationem ac- cipienda esse monuimus. Ubi vero (quod hic observandum) sphalma exscriptoris vitio irrepsit Tomo nempe I. pag. 1070. a. lin. 23. delendaque sunt verba Servus David, quæ in meo autogra- pho non invenio, & sensum nostrum plane per- yertunt. Cæterum ut Φροντίδας δευτέρας de Psal- mo hoc aperiam, ob loci hujus Apostolici eviden- tiam, & verborum Psaltis v. 20. cohærentiam ad- mittendum jam videtur Heroëm electum de populo & servum David de eodem subjecto, filio Jesse in- telligi, atque ita etiam verba v. 4. de electo, & de Da- vide servo eandem personam ibidem concernent, atque se mutuo explicabunt: Pepigi fœdus cum electo meo & juravi Davidi sermo meo, etsi fœde- ris jurejurando firmati, vel quod juramenti in- star habet, objectum, de semine æterno, deque throno in generationem & generationem ædifican- do, non de semine Davidis corporali nec de thro- no ejus mundano, sed de spirituali semine & cæle- sti throno Davidis filii Messiæ proprio, intelligen- dum sit: quia corporale semen Davidis non pro- pagatum fuit in perpetuum, sed abjectum jam per aliquot secula est, & thronus ejus desiit munda- nus, ablato sceptro de Juda: Conf. Esa. IX. 7. Luc. I. 32. 33. Quo pacto etiam illa de juramento Da- vidi facto in Psalmo laudato vers. 36. intelligen- da. Quod vero ad ea, quæ de dominio univer- sali, deque primogenito habentur vers. 26. 27. quæ de nullo alio, ut in Psalmi explicatione, nec non in Theol. Natur. & Revel. pag. 1373 seq. ostendimus, quàm de Messia sonant; ob- servandum, hæc non de Davide, sed de cornu Davidis prædicari. Nam cum promiserit Deus Davidi inter alia; Cornu ejus in nomine meo exaltabitur vers. 25. quod cornu est Messias ipse, ut vers. 18. & Psal. CXXXII. 17. Luc. I. 69. con- stat; clypeus noster, & Rex noster, ut habetur vers. 19. de illo jam vaticinatur Ethan ex perso- na Dei Patris, quam loquentem introducit, at- que explicat, qua ratione illud cornu Davidis exaltare velit, scil. in mari ponam manum ejus, & in fluminibus dexteram ejus. Causa tantæ ὑπερυψώσεως, quia ipse est non homo merus, ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, sed proprius, naturalis, verus, & æternus Dei Filius; Ipse vocabit me, Pater meus es tu. Quo de in ἐξηγήσει Psalmi pluribus. Atque ea ratione continuantur prædicata de eo- dem illo subjecto, cornu Davidis, Messia Rege vers. 28. seqq. De semine Messiæ spirituali ac filiis ejus, deque throno ejus æterno. Nam in hoc uno homine in gratia, in Messia Davidi se- men spirituale tribuitur, ac David ipse per eum filius Dei, Deoque gratus fuit: At thronus ejus æternus est, non quod Davidis solium & regnum æternum futurum sit Luc. I. 32. 33. Non vero quenquam movere debet, quod nomen קֶרֶן generis fœminini sit Dan. VIII. 9. Zachar. I. 18. Nam & σύνεσις illa, de qua Glassius libr. III. tract. II. Can. XVI. Gramp. S. locum habere potest in talibus, & rectius nomen illud com- mune constituitur à Buxtorffio, cum in Mascu- lino etiam occurrat Ps. LXXV, 11. &c. Hæc er- go ad dilucidationem Psalmi illustris Prophetici in præsenti monenda duxi, quæ piorum verbi scrutatorum judicio committo. Cæterum illa ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου non è Psalmo isto, sed è 1. Sam. XIII. 14. deprompta esse αὐτοψία, & in- spectio loci satis docet.

ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά με) Nempe in regendo populo. Idem est quod dicitur Psal. LXXVIII. 72.

## 13:23
Vers. 23.

of this one God from the seed) Matt. I, v. 1. Luke I, v. 32.

according to the promise) 1 Chron. XVII. 12. 14. Ps. LXXXIX, 37. Jer. XXIII. 5. Mic. V. 2.

Grotius therefore acknowledges that those passages treat of Christ. But those which he explained concerning others in his annotations on the Old Testament, let them be compared here with our Anti-Grotian ones.

ἤγαγε (he led) This the copyists placed from that which preceded in Mic. V. 1 concerning David. But the Manuscript in England and other books have ἤγειρε (he raised up), which is how the Hebrew הֵבִיא is, he caused to come.

There is no reason why we should disturb the received reading, or call it into doubt, since both the sense is appropriate, and most approved codices agree.

τῷ Ἰσραὴλ) To them in the first place, because he lived among them.

Σωτῆρα) He is so called in Luke II, 11. John IV. 42. above c. V. 3. and often in Paul. Moreover, it is an explanation of that which follows, Ἰησοῦν. See Matt. I, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

τούτου ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος) Matth. I, v. 1. Luc. I, v. 32.

κατὰ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν) 1. Paral. XVII. 12. 14. Ps. LXXXIX, 37. Jerem. XXIII. 5. Mich. V. 2.

Agnoscit ergo Grotius illa loca de Christo agere. Quæ vero de aliis exposuit in annot. ad Vet. Test. quæ hic conferantur cum nostris Anti-Grotianis.

ἤγαγε) Hoc exscriptores posuere ex eo, quo antecessit Mich. V. 1. de Davide. At Manuscriptus in Anglia & alii libri per- verteres habent ἤγειρε, quomodo Hebræum הֵבִיא est, fecit venire.

Causa nulla est, cur receptam lectionem so- licitemus, aut in dubium vocemus, quum & sensus conveniat, & probati codices plerique consentiant.

τῷ Ἰσραὴλ) Illis primo loco, quia inter eos vixit.

Σωτῆρα) Sic vocatur Luc. II, 11. Joh. IV. 42. supra c. V. 3. & apud Paulum sæpe. Est autem explicatio ejus, quod sequitur Ἰησοῦν. Vid. Matth. I, 21.

## 13:24
Vers. 24. προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου) Matt. III. 1.

πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ) That is, before Jesus began his office. Thus the jurists also say to enter upon a consulship.

Βάπτισμα μετανοίας) Mark I. 4. Luke III. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 24. προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου) Matth. III. 1.

πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ) Id est antequam Jesus munus suum auspicaretur. Sic ingredi consulatum di- cunt & Jurisperiti.

Βάπτισμα μετανοίας) Marci I. 4. Luc. III. 3.

## 13:25
Vers. 25.

ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου ὁ Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον) That is, when he was proceeding in his course. Thus to fulfill after someone, in Hebraism, is to follow someone.

τίνα με ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι) Whom do you suppose me to be, it is understood, the Messiah. He did not report the words themselves, but the sense, which is in John I. 20.

οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ) I am not.

ἀλλ’ ἰδὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ) After me he will begin his office.

ὧν ἐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι) See what is at Matt. III. 11. John I. 27.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου ὁ Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον) Id est cum in cursu suo pergeret. Sic implere post aliquem, in Hebraismo est aliquem sequi.

τίνα με ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι) Quem me existimatis esse, subin- telligitur, Messiam. Non verba ipsa, sed sensum retulit, qui est Joh. I. 2.

οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ) Is non sum.

ἀλλ’ ἰδὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ) Post me munus suum auspica- bitur.

ὧν ἐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι) Vide quæ ad Matth. III. 11. Joh. I. 27.

## 13:26
Vers. 26. καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβέμενοι τὸν Θεὸν) See above v. 16.

ὑμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἀπεστάλη) No foreign business is being transacted here. The message which we bring pertains as much to your salvation, O Jews, as to yours, pious Pisidians.

Latin:

Vers. 26. καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβέμενοι τὸν Θεὸν) Vide supra v. 16.

ὑμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἀπεστάλη) Non alienum hic negotium agitur. Nuntius is quem adferimus, tam ad vestram, o Judæi, quam ad vestram, pii Pisidæ, salutem pertinet.

## 13:27
Vers. 27. οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ) The common people.

καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες) The senators of the great Sanhedrin.

τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες) Not knowing that he was the promised Messiah. See above c. III. 17. 1 Cor. II. 8.

καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀνα- γινωσκομένας) He called the פטורות [Haphtarot] voices. For thus are the portions of the prophets distributed into their Sabbaths called, just as the sections of the law are called פרשות [Parashot]. See above c. III. 17. They heard the prophecies of these series on the Sabbaths, he says, and did not understand. For ἀγνοήσαντες refers both to Jesus and to the prophetic voices or readings.

κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν) This refers to the senators, who by their prejudice condemned Jesus, Matt. XXVII. 66. Luke XXIII. 2. John XVIII. 30. and thus fulfilled the predictions of Isaiah LIII. and elsewhere. There is here a hysteron proteron: κρίναντες namely him: and ἐπλήρωσαν namely the voices, then κρίναντες for κατακρίναντες as in Matt. VII. 1. John XII. 47. He previously twisted the passage of Isaiah ch. LIII. to Jeremiah. Now he confesses again that the same pertains to Jesus and has been fulfilled in him.

Latin:

Vers. 27. οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ) Plebs.

καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες) Senatores magni Synedrii.

τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες) Nescientes illum Jesum esse Messiam promissum. Vide supra c. III. 17. 1. Cor. II. 8.

καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀνα- γινωσκομένας) Φωνὰς dixit פטורות. Ita enim vocatur, partes prophetarum in sua Sabbata distributæ, sicut legis פרשות. Vide supra c. III. 17. Audiebant harum se- rum vaticinia Sabbatis, inquit, & non intelligebant. Nam ἀγνοήσαντες & ad Jesum & ad Propheticas voces sive lectiones refertur.

κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν) Hoc ad Senatores refertur, qui præjudicio suo Jesum confoderunt, Matth. XXVII. 66. Luc. XXIII. 2. Joh. XVIII. 30. & sic implerunt prædicta Esaiæ LIII. & alibi. Est hic ὕστερον πρότερον: κρίναντες nempe αὐτὸν: & ἐπλήρωσαν nempe τὰς φωνὰς, deinde κρίναντες pro κατακρίναντες ut Matth. VII. 1. Joh. XII. 47. Locum Esaiæ c. LIII. alias detorsit ad Jeremiam. Jam denuo fatetur eundem ad Jesum pertinere & in eo impletum esse.

## 13:28
Vers. 28.

and finding no cause of death, they asked Pilate that he should be put to death) This now pertains to the common people, Matt. XXVII. 22. They had no true cause. For he had sinned neither against the law, nor against them; he had explained the law well: he had bestowed very many benefits upon them.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ἠτήσαντο Πιλάτον ἀναι- ρεθῆναι αὐτὸν) Hoc jam ad plebem pertinet Matth. XXVII. 22. Nullam causam veram habebant. Neque enim in legem, neque in ipsos peccaverat, legem bene explicaverat: ipsos plurimis affecerat beneficiis.

## 13:29
Vers. 29.

and when they had fulfilled all things that were written concerning him) You may explain it: After all things had an end, so that reference is made to that which Christ himself said, John XIX. 28, 30. For active verbs often have a passive or absolute sense. See what was said regarding the fourth commandment of the decalogue.

taking him down from the tree) The article is missing, as is often the case. For he wishes to say, οἱ καθελόντες ἀπὸ ξύλου, those who took him down from the cross, Joseph of Arimathea and his companions, Matt. XXVII. 58, 59.

they laid him in a sepulchre) Matt. in the cited place c. XXVII. 59. Mark XV. 46. Luke XXIII. 53. John XIX. 41.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν ἅπαντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα) Possis exponere: Postquam finem habuere omnia, ut respiciatur id quod dixit ipse Christus Joh. XIX. 28.30. Nam sæpe activa habent sensum passivum vel absolutum. Vide quæ dicta ad præceptum quartum decalogi.

καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου) Deest articulus ut sæpe. Vult enim dicere, οἱ καθελόντες ἀπὸ ξύλου, qui eum de cruce detulerunt, Josephus Arimathensis & comites ejus, Matth. XXVII. 58. 59.

ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον) Matth. dicto loco c. XXVII. 59. Marci. XV. 46. Luc. XXIII. 53. Joh. XIX. 41.

## 13:31
Vers. 31.

to them which came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem) Not to the Apostles only, but also to the Galilean women, who had come with him to Jerusalem, Matt. XXVII. 55.

who are his witnesses unto the people) Above c. X. 41. Add above c. I. 22, 32, c. III. 18, c. V. 32, c. X. 39.

Vers. 31.

τοῖς συναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ) Non Apostolis tantum, sed & mulieribus Galilæis, quæ cum ipso Hierosolyma venerant, Matth. XXVII. 55.

οἵ τινές εἰσι μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν) Supra c. X. 41. Adde supra c. I. 22. 32. c. III. 18. c. V. 32. c. X. 39.

## 13:32
Vers. 32.

we declare unto you glad tidings of the promise which was made unto the fathers, that God hath fulfilled the same unto their children) We have εὐαγγελίζεσθαι here again with the Accusative of the person, as above c. VIII. 25, 40. In the following words there is a Hebrew circumlocution, for which one might say: that God has fulfilled the promise made to the fathers. This is the message which we bring to you, that that promise is fulfilled.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην, ὅτι ταύτην ὁ Θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκε τοῖς τέκνοις) εὐα- γγελίζεσθαι hic rursum habemus cum Accusativo personæ, ut supra c. VIII. 25. 40. In sequentibus est Hebraica cir- cumductio, pro qua liceat dicere : ὅτι τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας γενομένην ἐκπεπλήρωκεν ὁ Θεὸς. Hic est nun- tius, quem adferimus vobis, impleta illa promissa.

## 13:33
Vers. 33. having raised up Jesus) That is, exhibiting him. As above c. II. 30, c. III. 26, for below it follows distinctly having raised him from the dead.

We established this sense in the Examination of Crellius's book on the one God the Father, page 296, namely that here the discourse is not about the resuscitation from the dead, but about the raising up and sending of Christ. Which the antithesis of v. 34 sufficiently confirms, and is asserted by Cornelius à Lapide against other Papists.

as it is also written in the second Psalm) It was written in the first, as many have noted from Jerome, with the reason added, because formerly in the Hebrew codices the Psalms which are now called the first and second were joined together; the same happens in other Psalms as well.

But by that reasoning the number of 150 Psalms will not be consistent. And by great consensus all the ancient codices have the word second. Beza testifies that it was written so in all, with one exception, with which the Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic, Latin Vulgate, and almost all Latin versions, as well as our German one, agree. And R. Kimchi testifies that all correct books

CHAP. XIII. v. 25. 26. 27. 28. 29. 31. 32. 33. 34.

make that beginning which is now commonly established, nor do the LXX Interpreters have it otherwise. Finally, the diversity of the subject matter sufficiently teaches that the second Psalm is different from the first, whatever may be the different opinion of certain ancients. Cf. B. Walther's harmony on Ps. 2, p. 491.

You are my son, I have begotten you today) O my son, today I have begotten you, that is, I have made you king, as we said regarding the Psalm: this was fulfilled in Christ, when all power was given to him both in heaven and on earth, Matt. 28:18. Justin in his dialogue with Trypho: saying that his generation happens from the time that his knowledge was about to happen. Rightly: for just as those who are born begin to be known, so also do those who are raised to great honor. The names of similar things occupy similar things. That the Jews in ancient times referred this passage to the Messiah is apparent both from that very passage of Justin and from David Kimchi.

If this was fulfilled in Christ, it certainly does not treat of David, which Grotius notes he wanted to do at Ps. 2. But it was shown in the illustrated Bibles of the Old Testament that the Jews themselves explained it according to the literal sense concerning Christ. Moreover, it is manifest that these things are not said to be fulfilled in the resurrection of Christ, because they pertain to his raising up, as at v. 23; Grotius is already wrong there. Indeed, Paul wanted to teach that the very eternal Son of God, begotten from eternity by the Father, had to be raised from the seed of David, concerning which in Anti-Crellius book V and in the Anti-Grotian Annotations.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν) Id est, exhibens. Ut supra c. II. 30. c. III. 26. nam infra distincte sequitur ἀναστήσας ἐκ νεκρῶν.

Hunc sensum stabilivimus in Exam. lib. Crellii de uno Deo Patre pag. 296. quod nempe hic non de resuscitatione è mortuis, sed de excitatione ac mis- sione Christi sermo sit. Quod antithesis v. 34. satis confirmat, & asseritur à Cornel. à Lapide adversus alios Papistas.

ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ τῷ δευτέρῳ γεγράπται) Ve- tus scriptum fuit τῷ πρώτῳ, ut plures ex Hieronymo mo- nuere, addita causa, quia olim in Hebræis codicibus Psal- mi cui nunc primus & secundus dicuntur cohærebant, idem in aliis etiam Psalmis evenit.

At ea ratione non constabit sibi numerus CL. Psalmorum. Et consensu magno Cod. omnes veteres vocem δευτέρῳ habent. Beza in omnibus, uno excepto ita scriptum fuisse testa- tur, quibus consonant versiones Syra, Arabi- ca, Æthiopica, Vulgata Latina, & pleræque Latinæ omnes, ac nostra Germanica. Et R. Kimchi testatur, omnes correctos libros ini-

CAP. XIII. v. 25.26.27.28.29.31.32.33.34.

tium illud facere, quod nunc vulgo constituitur, neque aliter LXX. Interpr. habent. Tandem di- versitas materiæ satis docet, Psalmum secundum à primum diversum esse, quidquid sit de quo- rundam veterum diversa opinione. Conf. B. Wal- theri harmonia ad Ps. 2. p. 491.

υἱός μου εἶ σὺ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε) O fili mi, hodie te genu, id est, regem te feci, ut diximus ad Psalmum: hoc in Christo impletum, cum ei data omnis potestas & in cælo & in terra Matth. XXVIII. 18. Justinus colloquio cum Try- phone: τότε γένεσιν αὐτοῦ λέγων γίνεσθαι ἐξότου ἡ γνῶσις αὐτοῦ ἔμελλε γίνεσθαι. Recte: nam sicut qui nascuntur nosci inci- piunt, ita & qui in magnum honorem evehuntur. Simi- lia similium occupant nomina. Judæos antiquitus hunc locum ad Messiam retulisse, apparet & ex eo ipso Justini loco & ex Davide Kimchi.

Si in Christo hoc impletum, utique non de Davide agit, quod Grotius annotat ad Ps. 2. vo- luit. Judæos autem ipsos secundum literalem sen- sum de Christo exposuisse in Bibliis illustratis V. Test. ostensum fuit. Cæterum hæc non impleta in resurrectione Christi dici manifestum est, quia ad excitationem ejus pertinent ut ad v. 23. jam falsus est Grotius. Nimirum docere voluit Pau- lus excitandum fuisse è semine Davidis ipsummet æternum Dei Filium ab æterno à Patre genitum, quo de in Anti-Crellio lib. V. & in Annot. Anti- Grot.

## 13:34
Vers. 34. That he raised him from the dead) He returns to that which he had said about the resurrection, showing that this also agrees with the prophecies.

no longer about to return to corruption) Not about to die again, like those whom Elijah and Elisha raised. See above ch. II. 27.

to return to corruption is not to die again, but to revert into corruption: but here no longer to return should not be explained as not about to return again, but in a simply negative sense, NOT to return, or rather not to arrive: because to return is also to be taken without respect to the preceding time: since Christ was never in corruption. Whence this phrase at v. 37 is explained by not to see corruption, that is, not to experience corruption. Cf. Job 15:15, Rom. 6:9.

that I will give you the holy things of David, the faithful ones) The LXX in Isaiah 55:3: I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the holy things of David, the faithful ones. The sense is: I will show my mercy to you as constant as I showed it to David. This genitive is David and signifies the object: and as is understood.

The sense of the prophet here is rather that which the words themselves render: I will certainly show you the mercy promised to David, because these were the holy things of David, the faithful ones, which God promised him concerning the eternal kingdom of the Messiah: if, however, he had remained in death, he could not have had an eternal kingdom. Rightly Cornelius à Lapide: holy, that is, holy, pious, and munificent promises of God made to David, I will make faithful, that is, ratified, firm, and stable: because I will fulfill them in deed, by performing whatever I promised him concerning Christ who was to be born from his seed. Among other things, however, which I promised him concerning Christ, is the resurrection, and the eternal kingdom of him and of all the faithful through him. Although he notes that some establish a triple sense for this passage—Suarez, Viegas, Gregorius de Valentia, Molina, and others—namely, concerning the eternal generation, the incarnation, and the resurrection of Christ, he observes that this explanation seems harsh not only to others but he himself confesses that the Apostle explains this passage in Heb. I. 5 concerning the eternal generation, and he says it is easier that he expounds the same thing here, so that the words may be referred to the promise made to the Fathers regarding the mission of Christ the Son of God into the flesh and this world. For that Christ the Son of God had come as Redeemer and was already born was certainly what Paul and the Apostles had to prove. But that gloss of Grotius, 'You are my Son, today I have begotten you,' that is, 'I have made you King,' is purely Socinian, and was overthrown in our Anti-Crellius. Nor does Justin's ἔκθεσις have any commerce with it: for he did not explain it as 'I have made you King' or 'I have given you eternal power,' but 'I have declared or demonstrated openly that You are my Son,' just as it is said by St. Paul, ὁρισθεὶς, demonstrated through the resurrection. Concerning this explanation, and others pertaining to the vindication of this passage, see the Examination of Crellius's book On the One God the Father, 356, p. 1350 et seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν) Retro re- dit ad id, quod de resurrectione dixerat, ostendens & hoc vaticiniis congruere.

μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθορὰν) Non iterum moriturum, ut illi, quos Elias & Elisæus suscitavere. Vid. supra c. II. 27.

ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθορὰν non est iterum mori, sed reverti in corruptionem: hic autem μηκέτι ὑπο- στρέφειν non est non iterum reversurum, sed sen- su simpliciter negativo explicari debet, NON re- versurum, vel potius non perventurum: quia & τὸ ὑποστρέφειν sine respectu ad tempus præcedens ac- cipiendum: siquidem Christus nunquam in cor- ruptione fuerit. Unde hæc phrasis v. 37. explica- tur per οὐκ ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν non videre, sed experiri corruptionem. Conf. Job. XV. 15. Rom. VI. 9.

ὅτι δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστά) LXX. in Esaiæ LV. 3: διαθήσομαι ὑμῖν διαθήκην αἰώνιον τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστά. Sen- sus est: misericordiam meam vobis tam constantem exhi- bebo quam exhibui Davidi. Genitivus hic est Δαβὶδ signi- ficatque objectum: & subintelligitur ὡς.

Sensus prophetæ potius hic est, quem verba ipsa reddunt, misericordiam meam Davidi promis- sam vobis certo exhibebo, quia hæc fuere τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστὰ, quæ promisit ei Deus de æterno Messiæ regno: si autem in morte mansisset, re- gnum æternum habere non potuisset. Recte Cor- nelius à Lapid. sancta, id est, sanctas, pias & muni- ficas promissiones Dei factas Davidi, faciam fideles, id est, ratas, firmas & stabiles: quia eas opere com- plebo, præstando quicquid ei promisi de Christo ex semine ejus nascituro. Inter alia autem, quæ de Christo ei promisi, est resurrectio, & regnum æter- num illius & omnium fidelium per illum. Quan- quam enim triplicem nonnullos hujus loci sensum constituere notet, Suarezium, Viegam, Gregor. de Valentia, Molinam, & alios, de æterna nempe gene- ratione, de incarnatione, ac de resurrectione Chri- sti; duram tamen illam explicationem non modo aliis videri observat, sed etiam fatetur, Aposto- lum hunc locum Ebr. I. 5. de æterna generatione explicare, ac facilius dicit, de eadem hic eundem exponere, ut verba referantur ad promissionem Pa- tribus factam, quoad Christi Filii Dei missionem in carnem & hunc mundum. Christum enim Dei Filium advenisse Redemptorem & jam natum esse, utique probandum erat Paulo & Apostolis. illa verò Grotii gloffa, Filius meus es tu, ego ho- die genui te, id est, Regem te feci, mere Sociniana est, in Anti-Crellio nostro profligata. Nec cum ea quicquam commercii habet Justini ἔκθε- σις: nam is non exposuit, Regem te feci, vel dedi tibi æternam potestatem: sed declaravi, vel de- monstravi palam Teesse Filium meum, quemadmo- dum S. Paulo dicitur ὁρισθεὶς demonstratus per re- surrectionem. De qua explicatione, & aliis ad hujuss loci vindicias facientibus, vid. Exam. lib. Crellii de uno Deo Patre, 356. p. 1350. seqq.

## 13:35
Verse 35. διὸ κὲ ἐν ἑτέρω λέγει) He says elsewhere, namely David, which is also repeated in a more remote place, as is often the case.

ὐ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σε ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν) It is the same passage as above II. 27.

Latin:

Vers. 35. διὸ κὲ ἐν ἑτέρω λέγει) Alibi dicit, David scilicet, quod & remotiore loco repetitur, ut sæpe.

ὐ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σε ἰδεῖν διαφθορὰν) Est idem locus qui supra II. 27.

## 13:36
Verse 36. Δαβὶδ μὲν γὰρ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρέτησας τῇ τῦ Θεῦ βυλῇ) When he had served the counsels of God during his own age, namely in ruling the people, see above 22.

ἐκοιμήθη κὲ προσετέθη πρὸς τὺς πατέρας ἀυτῦ) He was buried, see above II. 29.

ἰδε διαφθορὰν) He was preserved from death for some time, which is the way to the dissolution of the body, not forever. It is an ἐξήγησις of the preceding, tending to this, that it may be clear that such a mode of production applies more excellently to Christ than to David.

Those words convey nothing about the fact that he was to be preserved from death for a time, or that he was not to be preserved from it forever: but they teach that David in reality felt or experienced corruption after death. Whence the Psalm can in no way be applied to David, but must necessarily be understood solely of Christ, who did not see corruption nor was he destined to see it. See our Annotations on this Psalm.

Latin:

Vers. 36. Δαβὶδ μὲν γὰρ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρέτησας τῇ τῦ Θεῦ βυλῇ) Cùm per suam ætatem inservisset Dei confiliis, nempe in populo regendo, Vide supra 22.

ἐκοιμήθη κὲ προσετέθη πρὸς τὺς πατέρας ἀυτῦ) Sepul- tus est, Vide supra II. 29.

ἰδε διαφθορὰν) Aliquo tempore servatus fuit à mor- te, quæ via est ad dissolutionem corporis, non in per- petuum. Est ἐξήγησις præcedentium, eo tendens, ut pateat istucum modo productum excellentiǫs in Christum, quam in Davidem, convenire.

Verba illa nihil de eo tradunt, quòd vel à morte ad tempus servandus fuerit, vel non in perpetuum servandus ab eadem fuerit: sed id docent quòd David revera corruptionem post mortem sense- rit vel expertus sit. Unde nullo modo de Davide Psalmus accipi potest, sed necessariò unice de Christo intelligendus, qui non vidit corruptionem nec videre debuit. Vide Annot. nostras in hunc Psalmum.

## 13:37
Verse 37. ὃν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν) On the third day, to wit.

ὐκ ἷδε διαφθορὰν) Death did not have that effect upon him, that it should dissolve his body. It is a double κατάχρησις. For 'to see' is put for 'to experience,' and 'to experience' is only said improperly of a dead person.

Latin:

Vers. 37. ὃν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν) Tertio sc. die.

ὐκ ἷδε διαφθορὰν) Mors eum effectum in eo non habuit, ut corpus dissolveret. Est duplex κατάχρησις. Nam & videre ponitur pro experiri, & experiri, de mortuo non nisi improprie dicitur.

## 13:38
Verse 38. Διὰ τύτο ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται) See above X. 43.

Latin:

Vers. 38. Διὰ τύτο ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται) Vide supra X. 43.

## 13:39
Verse 39. κὲ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν ὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μώσεως δικαιωθῆναι, ἐν τύτῳ πᾶς ὁ πισεύων δικαιῦται) It is not the same as what preceded, but another benefit. For צָדַק, which is for the most part δικαιῦν in Greek, also signifies 'to purge.' And it is translated צָדַק καθαρὸς ἔσται, Job IV. 17, καθαρισθήσεται, Dan. VIII. 14. He is purged from crimes who is freed from the habit of sinning; this for the most part was not done through the law, Heb. X. 23. The reason is because the law did not have heavenly promises. But Christ brought these, and therefore he purified hearts.

These two different benefits are not proposed, nor does the use of things allow for this. But the remission of sins, which itself is justification and the form of the same, is explained more fully. That the remission of sins is brought about through Christ, and indeed of all sins, from which we cannot be justified, or the remission of which we cannot obtain in the law of Moses: so that it may be shown that the remission of all sins is proposed in the Gospel, and at the same time it may be taught that we can in no way be justified from sins through the law of Moses and its observance, which is that very theme which the Apostle has executed more prolixly in the Epistles to the Romans, to the Galatians, to the Ephesians, to the Philippians, here proposed ἐπιτομικῶς (in summary).

However, it is to be observed here (1) The words γνωςὸν ἖ν ἔσω ὑμῖν, 'be it known therefore unto you,' indicate something which is most necessary to be known, whether it had been known before or not; because this reminder can be applied even to a matter previously known and not at all obscure, so that it may be attended to as much as possible, as being especially necessary; Although indeed that matter, that they who believe in him obtain the remission of sins solely through the Messiah, could have been believed by all the Prophets in the O.T., and thus be most well-known, Acts 10:43, yet because this saving doctrine had been greatly obscured among the Jews, and furthermore now in the Gospel that was to be announced by the Apostles, that Jesus of Nazareth, the Son of God begotten from eternity from his essence, raised by God, and sent, and after death resurrected, that he might not see corruption, is he in whom the faithful things promised to David and the Patriarchs before him have been fulfilled, through whom it behooves us to obtain the remission of sins and justification, for that reason the Apostle announces this openly, so that the Jews may believe in him and look up to him with true faith, if they wish to be justified and obtain salvation. (2) B. Erasm. observed that the text is distinguished in three Erasmian editions, as also in the Basel, Zurich, and Stephanus editions. Schmidius, with whom the edition of Casaubon agrees, so that after δικαιωθῆναι there is only a comma, and that rightly, since those words ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται do not make here, or begin, a new sentence, but cohere with the preceding sentence; Which distinction is also confirmed by Dn. D. Seb. Schmidts Colleg. Bibl. after p. 207, because in that way there is no need for any ellipsis or supplement; and because the preposition ἀπὸ does not sufficiently agree with the noun ἄφεσις (remission). (3) Therefore the Apostle wishes two things to be known to the Jews: 1. That the remission of sins is announced to them through and because of Jesus of Nazareth. 2. And that ἀπὸ πάντων (from all things), from which they could not be justified or absolved in the law of Moses (or those things which Moses delivered in the law) in this Christ Jesus (or those things which he himself did and suffered), everyone who believes (in him) is justified. In that ὧν for ἀφ’ ὧν, Erasm. Schmied. notes an Attic ellipsis. but it can be repeated from the former, ἀπὸ πάντων. For the Greeks have it in use that when a preposition is to be repeated with a relative, it is omitted, with only the relative being placed. 4) The former concerns the meritorious cause of justification: that namely through Jesus delivered unto death, in whom no cause of death was found, and raised from the dead, the remission of sins is obtained; the latter looks to the organic cause: that, namely, it behooves one to be justified solely through faith in Christ; nor can anyone be justified in those things which are contained in the law, but in this Christ Jesus, and those things which he himself did or suffered for us, when they are apprehended with faith, all who believe are justified. Those things which are contained and commanded in the law are the works of the law, both moral, ceremonial, and political, through which no one could be justified. The manner in which the law seemed to the Jews to justify is twofold: one through the fulfillment of the precepts, the other through substitution, if satisfaction were made to God through slaughtered sacrifices and their blood, so that he would no longer punish sins in them. Another manner of forensic justification cannot even be imagined concerning the law. But neither was possible; not the former, because no one can fulfill the law, much less merit anything through the fulfillment of the law, as it is otherwise owed; not the latter, because no expiation can be made through the blood of goats and calves.
