For even by reason of the soul of Christ, and his body, his flesh and bones would be said in the same way to be the own flesh and bones of God the Father, the own body of God the Father, the flesh and bones likewise the own of God. τὸ ἴδιον does not look to the author, by whom the blood was produced, but to the subject and suppositum, whose own it is: as when I say Peter's own blood, I do not understand the blood of the parent of Peter, by whom he was begotten, but of Peter himself, so when the own blood of God is spoken of, it is not understood as the blood of someone who has his origin from God, but the own blood of God himself: which because Enjedinus saw clearly, he labored to stuff in the word υἱῶ; or to transform the word ἅιματος into the word υἱῶ, and when he understood that he could not succeed with that, he conceded that Christ is understood by the word τῶ Θεῶ, which it must be believed he conceded only because he was constrained by the evidence of the passage. (10.) Why many words? to acquire the Church with his own blood is nothing else, according to the interpretation of Scripture, than to lay down his soul and his life, to shed his own blood, so that men might be freed and redeemed from sin, which who would doubt cannot be said of God the Father, but only of the Son of God? But that to acquire the Church with his own blood is to be explained in this way, is clear from these, and other passages of Scripture Matth. XX. 28. Marc. X. 45. Johan. X. 11. Rom. III. 24. ch. V. 10. Ephes. I. 5. ch. II. 21. Galat. I. 4. Tit. II. 14. 1. Joh. III. 16. Ebr. IX. 14. 1. Petr. I. 18. Apocal. I. 5. &c.

it is as certain as what is most certain. As far as the authority of Erasmus is concerned, it is very small in these controversies, nay, none at all: so that Smalcius declaims in vain about it, that nothing except the truth itself could have compelled him to embrace the same sense in this passage as the Socinians themselves. For who does not know that the Arian spirit, by which he was agitated to an excessive degree, compelled Erasmus? Which F. Socinus himself does not deny in his Epist. page 187, namely that Erasmus was not undeservedly suspected of Arianism even by the Trinitarians, and was listed by the Anti-Trinitarians among those who had protested against the Trinity in a somewhat obscure manner. And therefore Cornelius à Lapide, a Papist, rightly brought this censure against Erasmus, a Papist (by profession), here in this passage. Ineptly and distortedly, Erasmus, providing arms to the Arians, explains it thus: in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as Bishops to rule the Church of God (the Father,) which he (Christ) acquired with his own blood. If this is not falsifying Scripture, what will it be?

As to the exception of Enjedinus (6.), that it does not follow from this that Christ is the eternal and omnipotent God, even if it is conceded that Christ is understood here by the name of God, there is no need for us to add anything, because the reason of the invincible consequence has been sufficiently demonstrated by the proof of our major proposition, and is acknowledged by all other adversaries along with us, and is no longer called into doubt. So much, therefore, for this passage.

ἣν περιεποιήσατο) He caused to exist, which is the most just mode of acquiring. See Eph. I. 14.

It is not taught that Christ caused us to exist, but that he acquired us for himself by the interposition of the price of his own blood, 1. Cor. VI. 20. 1. Pet. I. 18. Redemption is therefore indicated, not done without a λύτρῳ. However, the passage Ephes. I. 14. does not fit well here; for there the discourse is about the future inheritance of eternal life, of which the Holy Spirit is the earnest, which was also acquired for us by the price of the blood of Christ: but here it is taught how Christ acquired us ourselves for himself with his own blood, by freeing us from the power of Satan, sin, and hell, Hos. XIII. 14. Luc. I. 74. Ebr. II. 14. Tit. II. 14. Since we were also reduced under the power of Satan through transgression, and became servants of sin and guilty of death, by the force of divine justice, there was need of satisfaction and redemption, so that we might be rendered the own property of Christ. He therefore claimed and asserted us for himself as his own possession, and acquired us for himself with his own blood: whence he is our master and Lord, by the right of this redemption, who bought us, 2. Petr. II. 1. and that with his own blood Apoc. V. 9. ch. XIV. 4.

διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος) For by his bloody death. Christ obtained that power of gathering the Church to himself, according to the prophecy of Isaiah 53:10.

He did not only obtain power through death (which is not to be admitted otherwise than insofar as by the intervention of death he was raised to the plenary exercise of infinite power, Phil. 2:9, Matt. 28:18, but by no means in the sense as if he merited this ἐξουσίαν [authority] for himself by his passion and death), but by his blood he redeemed the whole human race from the power of Satan, to which, that it may enjoy the benefit of this redemption, he deigns to call it to the communion of his kingdom. He has, therefore, a right to those whom he freed from the hand of Satan, who died for all, that we should not live for ourselves, but for him who died for us and rose again, 2 Cor. 5:15.

Latin:

V. 28. προσέχετε ὖν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ πάντι τῷ ποιμνίῳ) non potest gregi attendere, qui non sibi attenderit.

ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπυς) Explicat nomen muneris, quo erat פקידי עדר: nam Pastores sunt ἐπίσκοποι ποιμνίε, פקידי עדר. Dicit autem eos constitutos à Spiritu S. quia constituti erant ab Apostolis plenis Spiritu S. quanquam approbante plebe. Vide supra XIV. 23.

ποιμαίνειν) breviloquium frequens Hebræis pro εἰς τὸ ποιμαίνειν.

Non ergo excludendum est penitus votum ac suffragium plebis in electione ministrorum verbi, siquidem ne Apostoli quidem id excluserint. Quod contra Pontificios observari velim.

τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τῦ Θεῦ) Manuscriptus ille habet τῦ Κυρίε, ut & multi alii. Et Syrus sic legit, qui vertit Christi. Facilis lapsus compendiosæ scriptionis θῦ pro χῦ. Apostoli plerumque Christum Κύριον vocant, Patrem vero Deum.

Facilis nimis Grotius est in admittendis lapsibus & mendis in S. Literis. Compendiosam adhibitam fuisse illam scriptionem, ac permutatas illas satis diversas literas, quomodo obsecro probabitur? Etiamsi vero plerumque Christum Κύριον vocent Apostoli, Deum tamen etiam ipsum dixerunt, ut ex Joh. I. 1. c. XX. 28. Rom. IX. 5. 1. Tim. III. 16. Tit. II. 13. 1. Joh. V. 20. aliisque locis constat. Neque de voce Θεῦ adeo litem hic movit vel Enjedinus, vel Socinus, qui tamen nihil non tentarunt ad ever- tenda dicta de Deitate Christi: quia potius Christi sanguinem Dei Patris sanguinem dici per appro- priationem, aut ellipsin hic occurrere vocis ὑῦ, sanguine proprii (Filii) aut vocem sanguinis pro Filio poni, quanquam inepte, statuerunt. Vid. En- jed. annot. p. 254. Socin. in Anti-Wujek. &c. Beza potius suspicio hic locum haberet, etsi alias etiam proni in librariorum sphalmata: In quinque exem- plaribus legitur Κυρίου καὶ Θεῦ, Domini & Dei. Su- spicor autem τῦ Κυρίυ initio fuisse adscriptum ad marginem a quopiam, qui Dei vocabulum sic ex- plicaret adversus Anthropomorphitas, ne Paulus videretur sanguinem ipsi divinitati tribuere: deinde cum hoc irrepsisset in contextum, & ista Κυρίε Θεῦ non bene viderentur cohaerere, interpositam esse par- ticulam καὶ.

Plenius hoc argumentum tractavimus in ἀπο- δείξει Deitatis Christi, e qua hic vindicias praesentis loci repetere placet. Non enim illa hactenus lu- cem viderunt. Κατασκευὴ nostra ita habet: Qui hic dicitur ὁ Θεὸς, is vere est unus ille natura Deus. At Christus dicitur hic ὁ Θεὸς. E. Major patet: quia non tantum Dei nomen absolute & simpliciter oc- currit, quod non nisi unum illum Deum denotat, sed & articulus adjectus est, quo addito semper Deum illum unum designari concedunt adversa- rii: quin & subjective nomen τῦ Θεῦ adhibetur, quum ὁ Θεὸς Deus ille sanguine suo acquisivisse sibi Ecclesiam dicatur: At cum subjective adhibetur, semper verum & unum illum Deum designari ite- rum adserunt, & propugnant adversarii: Denique ille Deus indigitatur, cujus est Ecclesia: At nulli alii Deo adscribitur Ecclesia in S. Literis, praeter- quam uni illi vero Deo, Deo Israelis. Minor con- firmatur inde: quod περιποίησις, acquisitio Eccle- siae & quidem διὰ τῦ ἰδίε αἵματος, per proprium sanguinem facta, nulli alii conveniat, quam Christo. Ille solus redemit Ecclesiam sanguine proprio, te- ste passim Scriptura, Rom. III. 24. 25. 1. Cor. VI. 10. c. VII. 23. Eph. I. 7. 1. Petr. I. 19. 2. Petr. II. 1. Unde etiam Syrus, ut & Arabs interpres non tam verba quam sensum respiciens, vocem τῦ Θεῦ, per no- men Christi explicavit: quandoquidem de Christo sermonem esse manifestum esset. Quam senten- tiam, quod hic Filius Dei intelligatur, universa Ec- clesia constantissime propugnavit, nec repobare potuit Enjedinus, concedens eum voce Dei intel- ligi, utut neget, inde concludi posse, Christum esse unum illum verum Deum.

Hic vero nihil non movent adversarii, ut prae- clarum hocce testimonium, si non eripere, saltem dubium nobis reddere possint. Schmalzius in re- fut. disp. de Incarnat. Grav. pag. 25. praeeunte So- cino praeceptore, hanc ipsam Syriacam obvertit lectionem, quae loco Dei habet Christi, unde colligi jure posse censet, aliquam ab initio exemplarium differentiam fuisse, & vel hanc vocem, vel aliam ei similem extitisse in quibusdam saltem exemplaribus, quod & Bezam confirmare dicit, dum ait, in quinque Exemplaribus legi Domini & Dei (2.) Enjedinus in Expl. loc. p. 255. ellipsin comminiscitur vocis ὑῦ, adeoque hanc glossam tradit, acquisivit sanguine sui (vel proprii) subaudi Filii, quia omitti soleat quandoque vox Filii, ut Luc. III. Matth. IV. & si- milia substantiva Job. XIII. v. 1. Matth. X. 42. (3.) Porro idem Enjedinus priori tortura non conten- tus vocem αἷμα vult poni pro Filio, ut apud Homer. Theocrit. Virgil. ac proinde non incommode dici- posse, Deum sanguine suo vel proprio, hoc est, Filio suo redemisse Ecclesiam. (4) Rursus sanguinem Jesu Christi, sanguinem Dei dici posse ait, quia Deo sacer erat, uti sanguis victimarum Deo sanctificatus fuit. (5.) Adhæc eundem Christi sanguinem Dei dici contendit, non quod Deus sanguinem habeat, sed quod illum pro suo reputet: & tam pretiosus illi sit, quam si esset ipsius; conferens Zach. II. 8. Matth. XXV. 40. Act. IX. 14. Quæ etiam Glossa est Socini contra Wujek. p. 354. Nomen Deus ad Christum minime referri debere, sed ad ipsum Deum Patrem, cujus is dicatur Sanguis, quem etiam effudit, ea figura, qua Zach. II. 8. Qui tangit Dei populum, Dei pupillam oculi tangere dicitur. Addit quod etiam verba de Deo Patre dicta, videbunt in quem transfixerunt, Zach. XII. 10. ad Christum accommodata sint, Joh. XIX. 37. ob summam & perfectissimam inter Deum Patrem & Christum conjunctionem, quodque Deus Pater hunc sanguinem agni, sicut & agnum ipsum possideat, atque ut rem suam una cum ipso agno pro nostris peccatis expiandis det. Schlichting. disp. de Trin. p. 342. addit, Sanguinem Christi esse sanguinem Patris, quid sit ejus juris & dominii, & ab eo in virginis utero Spiritus S. efficacia productus. Smalcius l. cit. verba Socini repetens addit, quod Spiritus etiam & corpora fidelium dicantur esse Dei, 1. Cor. VI. 20. inter quos & Deum nullo modo tanta conjunctio, quanta inter Christum & Patrem. Subjicit denique Erasmi consensum, quem postmodum multis verbis extollit. (6.) Denique nihil aliud hinc obtineri posse, dicit Enjedinus, quam Christum Deum esse, id quod concedit: sed addit, non statim qui Deus est, esse etiam creatorem cæli & terræ æternum & omnipotentem.

Hæ ergo sunt exceptiones Socinianorum potiores, ad quas eodem ordine jam respondendum erit. Ad (1.) Resp. Græci Codices constantissime, sine ulla dissensione vocem τῦ Θεῦ retinent, nullus reperitur, qui vocem Christi ejus loco habeat, nec repertus est à quoquam Criticorum, qui diligentissime contulere exemplaria, nec denique observatur è veterum allegatione ejusmodi lectio: Quin potius Græci pariter & Latini hanc receptam lectionem comprobant. Textus autem Græcus solus est authenticus, & in firmandis dogmatibus fidei infallibilis. Nec vero admittimus consequentiam, fuisse ab initio exemplarium Græcorum differentiam, & vel hanc vocem Christi, vel aliam ei similem extitisse, (loco vocis τῦ Θεῦ) & quod vox משיחא Messias legatur in Syro, quia alia potuit esse causa hujus translationis, quod nempe exprimere voluerit interpres de Messia sermonem esse, præsertim quum non semper Syrus stricte reddat verba, quandoq; sensu pensi habito, quædam etiam addat verba: uti Act. XXVII. 9. additur nomen ליהודיא Judæorum, Rom. IV. v. 5. particula בלחוד, solum vel tantum, 1. Cor. VII. v. 7. vox ברכיותא, in castitate, Marc. II. 4. ascenderunt in tectum, quæ in Græcis codicibus non habentur; vel substituat alia à Græco textu diversa, ut Matth. II. 19. c. XIV. 6. (Marc. VI. 21.) Matth. XXVII. 37. Marc. IV. 10. c. XV. 22. Sic cum Luc. II. 49. in Græcis habetur ἐν τοῖς τῦ πατρός μȣ, explicavit id Syrus לביתא דאבי in domo Patris mei, Luc. II. 30. τὸ σωτήριόν σου reddit חנך, quod Tremellius transtulit gratiosum tuum. Boderian: misericordem tuum. Lud. de Dieu Comm. in Evang. p. 258. rectius misericordiam tuam, Joh. VIII. 23. Græca ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς ὐ χωρεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, Syrus reddidit: sermoni meo non sufficitis; sensum respiciens, non verba exprimens, Joh. XIX. 42. διὰ τὴν παρασκευὴν τῶν Ἰυδαίων, Syrus reddidit, quia Sabbatum intrabat, atque ita in his

& aliis, non tam translationem quam explicatio- nem tradidit, cujus generis multa plura notari possent. Num vero in illis & similibus locis varias- se Græcos Codices (contra eorundem constan- tem consensum) admittemus, eo quod aliter red- dantur (quoad verba) à Syro interprete? ut ta- ceam, quod omittantur in Syræ interpretatione nonnulla, ut Marc. I. 2. illud ἔμπροσθέν σου, & Joh. VIII. historia adulteræ (quam utut in manuscripto ab Archi-Episcopo Armachano Iacobo Usserio ac- cepto produxerit Lud. de Dieu Comm. ad Evang. p. 445. idem tamen manuscriptum hanc ei præmi- sit ἐπιγραφὴν lectio, quæ est de muliere peccatrice, quæ lectio non est in simplici; id est, quæ non est in vulgo recepta, & simpliciter fine controversia apud omnes Ecclesias Syriacas admisso exemplari, ut interpretatur Ludov. de Dieu l. c.) & alia plura, quæ constanter citra discrepantiam Codicum in Græco textu leguntur, ita ut nihil præjudicet in iisdem ἀυθεντίᾳ Græci textus defectus Syriacæ in- terpretationis.

Quod autem ad Græcorum Codicum diversam lectionem, quæ à Beza annotata (à Stephano ob- servata) ea nequaquam confirmat, quondam omis- sam fuisse in aliquibus exemplaribus vocem τοῦ Θεῦ, aliamve ejus loco lectam, sed docet potius in omnibus Codicibus à Stephano, & Beza collatis ex- titisse vocem τοῦ Θεῦ, quamvis Complutensis editio ad antiquissima olim excusa exemplaria, una cum aliis vetustioribus Codicibus quatuor præmiserit vocem κυρίου, adeoque legerit τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ Θεῦ, cujus varietatis causam per σοχασμὸν expositam, vide in annot. Bez. ad h. l. Ea autem lectio nostræ ἀποδείξει minime adversa est: quin confirmat ean- dem quoque quod nomine τοῦ Θεῦ intelligatur verus & naturalis Deus, quandoquidem nuspiam conjunctim hæc nomina τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ Θεῦ dican- tur de alio, quam de Jehovah uno illo vero Deo.

Smalcii vero effugium, quod admissa illa le- ctione de Domino, id est, Jesu Christo, id proprie dicatur (quod hic effertur, sanguine proprio ac- quisivit Ecclesiam) de Deo vero (Patre) impro- prie, prorsus vanum est: quia nec ullo forte exem- plo docebitur, nomina illa τοῦ κυρίου καὶ Θεῦ, ubi nullum aliud ei additum habetur, ita discernenda esse, ut alterum de Christo, alterum de Deo Patre intelligendum sit; nec fieri potest, ut ejusdem præ- dicati semel positi in eodem loco geminus diver- sissimus simul sit sensus, & proprius & improprius. Locus qui huc trahitur ex Apoc. I. 4. Johannem gratiam precari à Deo proprie, à septem spiritibus improprie, controversus est; nec admittimus, im- proprie à septem spiritibus gratiam voveri; sed proprie, etsi septem spiritus improprie & meto- nymice intelligantur de Spiritu S. septiformi mu- nere. Conf. Anti-Crell. noster §. 528. seqq.

Ad (2.) Resp. Impudentem illam audaciam Enjedini, qua inserere vult textui vocem ἁιῦ præ- ter & contra Scripturæ morem, ad pervertendum luculentissimum testimonium, quis non miretur, quis non detestetur? Textus ipse semet ipsum vin- dicat evidentia sua, τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεῦ, ἣν περιε- ποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ ἰδία αἵματος., Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit per proprium sanguinem. Quæ hic, obsecro, causa dari poterit, ellipsin admittendi, quæ ejus fingi necessitas. Nullum adhæc ellipseos istius idoneum exemplum proferri potest è Scri- pturis, Luc. III. v. 23. vocem ὑιὸς intelligendam es- se, genealogia ipsa docet, cum commemorentur parentes, quanquam ἀπὸ κοινῦ etiam vox ἁιὸς e vers. 23. repeti possit, Matth. IV. 12. Ἰακωβὸν τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου, subaudiri ὑιὸν ex consueta illa loquendi

Græcorum formula manifestum, qua apposito Patris nomine in casu Genitivo intelligunt no- men υἱᾶ. Quid vero hæc ad præsentem locum? Referturne hic Deus ceu Pater Christi, aut texi- turne hic Genealogia? Cætera exempla Job. XIII. 1. c. I. 12. Matth. X. 42. itidem prorsus dissimilia esse nemo non videt. Quid si in textibus, absque ellipsi prorsus luculentis, integrum sit, ellipsin fingere, tam insolentem & alienam à Scripturis, quid tan- dem certi relinquetur in S. Scriptura? Non addi- mus plura, quia Glossæ hujus jam pridem puduit cæteros Anti-Trinitarios, Socinum, ejusque disci- pulos.

Ad (3.) Resp. Hic vero iterum extremam im- pudentiam, vel impietatem potius Enjed. dete- stari oportet, quod ita pervertere ausus fuerit hunc textum, vocem αἵματος transformans in vocem υἱᾶ: quæ corruptela, ut nulla nititur ratio- ne, nec exemplo nullo in Scripturis fulciri potuit; unde ad Ethnicos Poëtas transiliendum fuit, quanquam nec illa, quæ ex Homero producun- tur, quicquam huc faciant; Ita Scripturæ etiam contraria est, quæ cum τῷ αἵματι sanguine factam esse redemptionem docet, non Filium intelligit, sed sanguinem Elii, imo cum blasphemia quoque conjuncta; quasi Deus Filium habeat ex sangui- ne proprio procreatum, uti filii hominum pro- creantur, qui propterea sanguis parentum dicun- tur, metonymice.

Ad (4.) Resp. Non sanguine Dei sacro vel san- ctificato dicitur acquisita Ecclesia, quomodo victi- mæ sacræ erant Deo, sed διὰ τᾶ ἰδίε αἵματος, per proprium sanguinem Dei. Victimarum sanguis, etsi Deo sacræ essent, nuspiam dicitur τὸ ἴδιον αἷμα proprius sanguis ipsius Dei, sed uti ille sanguis proprius erat ipsarum victimarum, v. g. agnorum sacrificialium, ita hic sanguis, quo Ecclesia re- dempta est, dicitur ipsius Dei sanguis. At ille vere & citra figuram proprius eorundem sanguis erat, ideoque etiam hic vere & citra figuram Dei pro- prius sanguis intelligendus. Nulla quippe neces- sitas cogit, proprium verborum sensum deserere, & figuratum admittere.

Ad (5.) Resp. Nomen τᾶ Θεᾶ hic ad Christum referendum esse non ad Patrem, facile patet, tum quod Christo Sanguis adscribatur in S. literis, nusquam autem per totam Scripturam Deo Patri, tum quia non habeat τὸ ἴδιον αἷμα proprium san- guinem Pater, sed Filius, qui particeps factus est carnis, & sanguinis nostri, Ebr. II. 14. tum quod sanguinis proprii effusio passim quidem de Christo dicatur, nuspiam autem & nunquam de Deo Pa- tre, tum quod περιποίησις acquisitio Ecclesiæ proprio sanguine facta non nisi Christo vindicetur in S. li- teris, minime autem Deo Patri, tum denique, quod Scriptura N. Test. cum redemtionis & ac- quisitionis Ecclesiæ beneficia celebrat, nuspiam solum Patrem commemorat, nulla filii mentio- ne facta, sed Filio adscribat redemptionem, ac- quisitionem, & quæ his similia. Urserat itaque B. Gravverus hoc Argumentum. Quotiescun- que Scriptura N. Test. nos sanguine redemptos esse docet, toties de Christo loquitur, nec ullum contrarium locum adversarii ostendere pote- runt, Ebr. IX. 12. Apoc. V. 9. Eph. I. 7. 1. Petr. I. 19. Apoc. I. 6. Unde conclusit is, proculdubio, no- mine Deus in subjecto Actor. XX. 28. intelligitur, cui alias in S. literis expresse tribuitur prædica- tum, non vero is, cui prædicatum, alias nullibi tribuitur. At Christus est ille, cui alias prædicatum tribuitur, Ebr. IX. 12. Apoc. I. 9. 2. Cor. V. 15. &c. Etiamfi vero tribuatur alicubi Deo Patri redem- tio, non tamen fanguine proprio vel fuo nos Deus Pater redemisse fibi nos dicitur, quod de Christo dici ex Ebr. IX. 12. 2. Cor. V. 15. est demonstratum. Smalcius vero obvertit, Redemtionem Deo Patri etiam adfcribi, Luc. I. 68. 2. Petr. II. 1. l. c. pag. 28.

At posteriori loco aperte Christus intelligitur, non vero Pater (de quo alias) priori non rede- misse, sed redemtionem fecisse dicitur Deus Israel, quo nomine tamen Christum etiam intellige posse è collatione vers. 78. doceri potest. Is enim in- telligitur o̔ ἐπισκεψάμενο, qui visitavit nos. At ἐπισ- σκεύατο visitavit nos oriens ex alto, hoc est Filius Dei, ut appareret sedentibus in tenebris, & umbra mortis. Conf. Mal. IV. 2. Zachar. III. 8. cap. VI. 12. quæ loca, ut conferantur, in margine annotata sunt. Quod ipsum etiam è collatione Luc. I. 16. ostenditur: nimirum Dei Israelis nomine, qui vi- fitavit nos Christum intelligi, quippe ante cujus faciem præire & cui viam parare debuit Johan- nes, quo de itidem alibi plenius. 2. Rationes, quæ adferuntur, cur dicatur Sanguis Christi Dei Sanguis, utpote ob cognationem, æstimationem, jus & dominium, ut & ob originem, admittenda minime sunt. Quia gratis hic fingitur, Deo Pa- tri sanguinem hic attribui, quod est contra & præter morem Scripturæ Sacræ. Adhæc (2.) Filii, non autem Patris mentionem fieri jam ostensum est. Nec (3.) quidquam obstat, quo minus nomine τoῦ Θεoῦ Filium Dei intelligamus: quod non tantum de Patre, sed & Filio effertur in S. literis. Quod Smalcius urget pag. 27. Nullo S. literarum loco doceri posse, vocem Dei, quando subjecti locum tenet de Christo absque omni contro- versia prædicari vel semel, id vanum prorsus est: quia quicunque etiam locus proferetur, de eo con- troversiam movebunt Sociniani, ut in hoc fieri videmus. Locus etiam luculentus est per se 1. Tim. III. 15. ubi subjective vox Deus notat Filium Dei: subjective itidem vox Θεoῦ accipitur Ephes. IV. 5. 7. Ebr. I. 8. ut & Tit. II. 14. quod & de Esa. IX. 6. Job. XX. 28. dici potest; nec ullam in sensu parit diver- sitatem, sive ea vox subjecti locum teneat, sive prædicati, quæ absolute posita, sensuque proprio Deum verum & naturalem infert, de quo egimus Theol. nat. & revel. cap. 3. p. 474. seq. denique si nulla alia loca darentur, præter hunc ipsum, (quod tamen secus sese habet) recordari debuis- set Smalcius, quod paulo ante scripserat; non omnium loquutionum dari instantias, tum ipsa do- cet ratio, tum etiam Philosophi doctissimi compro- bant: Satis enim est modos loquendi similes extare. Hæc Smalcius. Porro (4.) non tantum Deus dicitur, suo acquisivisse sanguine Ecclesiam, sed διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος per PROPRIUM sangui- nem. Is ergo Deus intelligitur (vel ea persona divina) qui proprium habet sanguinem. At Pa- ter non habet proprium sanguinem, sed Filius. Regerit Smalcius loc. cit. vocem ἰδίου Græcam sæpe idem significare, quod Latinam suus, atque adeo nullam majorem vim esse in vocabulo Pro- prius, quam esse in vocabulo Suus. Sed nulla ejus exempla attulit. Nec valida est consequentia: Sæpe idem est quod suus, E. & hic. Majorem insuper emphasin in voce ἰδίου agnoscunt omnes Græci, quorum potior nobis authoritas, quam Smalcius sine authoritate contractio: præser- tim quia propriam emphasin vocis hic repro- bandam esse, nullæ causæ suadent. Urgemus ergo adhuc adversarios, quod hic sanguis attri-

buatur Deo non per nudam χέσιν, sed proprius sanguis: quodque nullibi in Sacra Scriptura Deo Patri proprius sanguis tribuatur, multo minus dicatur, quod Deus Pater proprio sanguine rede- merit Ecclesiam. Provocamus adhuc eosdem, ut vel unicum tantum, si possint, locum mon- strent; quem vero non posse proferri ultro agno- scit Smalcius, fateturque, non extare in Sacra Scriptura talem locutionem: Ideo eo recurrit, quod non omnium locutionum dari possent instan- tiæ: quod uti faciles admittimus, ita certum ta- men est, cum dantur exempla, eaque etiam passim obvia, vel loca annaloga, sensum eum, qui nititur analogia Scripturæ, præferendum es- se alteri, qui citra ullum Scripturæ exemplum novam & insolentem loquendi formulam pro- ducit, ut sensus evidens, & omnibus obvius eadem obscuretur, vel dubius reddatur; & qui novam loquendi formulam introducunt, eos jure meritoque urgeri, ut easdem exemplis sta- tuminent. Similes modos loquendi extare, qui- bus hic excusari, ut ait Smalcius, possit, non- dum ostensum. Qui enim adferuntur, non ad- modum similes, sed multum diversi sunt, de quibus postea. Adde autem hisce (5.) quod sen- sus ille, quo Christus intelligitur nomine Dei, proprius sit, alter vero (etiam si haberet exempla similia, quæ non habet) figuratus sit & impro- prius: Ille passim obvius sit in Scripturis, hujus autem loca nulla adferri queant, quod utrumque fatetur Smalcius l. c. Respondeo, inquit, locos istos, in quibus proprie dicitur Christum per suum san- guinem nos redemisse, lavasse à peccatis, & popu- lum suum acqusivisse, non posse efficere, quo mi- nus dici possit alibi improprie, Deum per Sangui- nem suum nos acquisivisse. At à consueta vel propria verborum significatione non esse teme- re recedendum monuerat Socinus Fr. Davidem in vol. Epist. pag. 188. & ad figuras non esse recur- rendum, nisi aliqua cogat necessitas, Regulam so- briam Theologiæ esse, inculcavit Smalcius supra pag. 9. Quod ergo ait hic Smalcius, rem ipsam & loci circumstantiam facile unumquemque doce- re posse, non posse aliter hic verba intelligi, quam improprie de Deo Patre, id evidenter demon- strandum erat. At non habet aliud documen- tum præterquam illud, quod vox Dei hic subje- cti locum teneat, quod quam frivolum sit, jam demonstratum est. Quum itaque nulla causa cogens adferri possit, cur relicto sensu proprio, & nativo, itemque Scripturæ familiari, & passim obvio, improprius & figuratus à Scripturæ usu & consuetudine prorsus alienus, sit admitten- dus, jure meritoque illi inhæremus, vel ipsis ad- versariis arbitris. (6.) Ob cognationem solum Christi cum Deo Patre, sanguinem Christi Dei sanguinem proprium dici negamus: quum non tantum conjunctus sit Christus Deo Patri, sed unum sit cum Patre. Johan. X. 30. & quidem ita, ut S.S. cum Patre unum est. Johan. V. 7. & pari- ter dicatur Deus benedictus super omnia ut Pater Rom. IX. 5. Nec exempla dantur similia: Spiri- tus quidem & corpora fidelium dicuntur esse Dei, ob unionem mysticam 1. Corinth. VI. 20. Sed nuspiam Scriptura Dei Spiritum vel Dei corpus nominat, indigitans fidelium animam, vel cor- pus, quæ sunt Dei, multo minus nominat illa Dei proprium Spiritum vel Dei proprium cor- pus. (7.) Æstimatio porro facit quidem, ut quæ accidunt fidelibus, ea sibi accidere repu- tet Deus, qui tangit populum ejus, cum sese vel pupillam oculi sui tangere, dicatur, qui perse- quitur Ecclesiam suam, eundem sese persequi, qui beneficium fidelibus Christi exhibet, eundem id sibi exhibere asserat; sed ex eo inferri non potest, æstimationem ejusmodi causam esse, ut ponatur Sanguis proprius Dei Patris, intelliga- tur Sanguis Christi. Longe enim ista diversa sunt. Monstretur ubi pupilla oculi nostri Deo adscribatur, aut alia pars corporis nostri, eo quod eam suam æstimet Deus, uti hic sangui- nem Christi (eumque proprie dictum) volunt adversarii vindicari Deo, & quidem ceu pro- prium sanguinem, ob æstimationem, quod il- lum Deus pro suo reputet; ne dicam, quod hic insuper effusio sanguinis proprii & effusione illa facta acquisitio Deo adscribatur: Cui genuinum exemplum, ubi de Deo Patre sermo sit, nul- lum ex tota Scriptura adferri potuerit. Quod enim ad locum Zach. XII. 10. ubi Jehovah trans- fixus dicitur, eum non de Deo Patre, sed de ipsomet Filio Dei accipiendum esse ex ipsa col- latione cum Johan. XIX. Apoc. 1. patescit, & in An- notatis ad Zachariam probatum est. Adde quod, ubi quæ fidelibus accidunt, sibi accide- re reputat Deus, id diserte innuatur, & expri- m , ut è locis citatis constat. Hic autem nullum ejusmodi æstimationis indicium expri- mitur. Unde iterum magna locorum diversi- tas elucescit. (8.) Nec possessio, jus & domi- nium, quod Deus hunc sanguinem agni possi- deat, eumque det pro nostris peccatis expian- dis, juvare potest adversarios. Quia nuspiam Scriptura de ulla re, quam Deus jure dominii possidet, nec de agno Dei, aut sanguine agni ita loquitur: Possidet Deus jure dominii nostras animas, nostra corpora, nostrum etiam san- guinem: At nuspiam Dei anima propria indi- gitetur, aut Dei proprium corpus, Dei san- guis proprius, ut significentur nostræ animæ, nostra corpora, noster sanguis ob illam posses- sionem, jus & dominium. Adde quod non tantum hic respectus habeatur ad aliquod jus & dominium, sed sanguis approprietur Deo, ita ut eundem etiam innuatur Deus profudisse, ut acquireret ita proprio suo sanguine Ecclesiam, quod vis verborum ipsorum importat, & colla- tio aliorum locorum docet. Qui enim Deus sanguine proprio acquisivit Ecclesiam? Annon quod Christus sanguinem proprium effudit ad acquirendam Ecclesiam? Quis ergo non videt sanguinis effusionem connotari? At ea præsup- ponit non tantum aliquod jus & dominium, sed ejusmodi profusionem sanguinis, qua is, qui ef- fundit suum sanguinem, eum ceu partem agno- scat corporis sui, quo sensu non Deus (Pater,) sed Christus, qui homo fuit, & sanguinem ha- buit eumque ex corpore suo profudit, proprio san- guine Ecclesiam acquisivit. Ut his ipsis verbis fatetur Schlichtingius de Trinit. pag. 343. Osto- rodus quoque Disput. German. Tradel. opposita pag. 244. Deum (Patrem) sanguinem nec habe- re, nec effundere posse, ait. Qui ergo de Deo Patre accipiendum, quod sanguine proprio (effuso) acquisiverit Ecclesiam? Adde quod proprius sanguis opponatur alieno sanguini, quem Pontifex Vet. Testam. offerre solebat. Quum ergo Deum non alieno sed proprio sanguine ac- quisivisse Ecclesiam, dicit Apostolus, non pro- prium παχυλῶς, & generaliter, ratione domi- nii & juris indigitat, quo pacto etiam victima- rum sanguis ipsi proprius erat, imo omnia crea- ta ejus propria sunt, sed specialiter vel singula- riter, ratione possessionis, & appropriationis- hypostatice, qua carnis & sanguinis nostri parti- ceps factus est Ebr. II. 14. quaque sanguinem il- lum suum proprium nostri causa profudit. Quo facit parallelus locus Ebr. IX. 12. ubi consimili phrasi de Christo dicitur, quod διὰ τῶ ἰδίε αἵμα- τος per proprium sanguinem semel in sacrarium ingressus sit, æterna redemptione inventa. Ut enim hic per PROPRIUM sanguinem intel- ligitur non proprius generaliter, ratione domi- nii, sed specialiter, quod nempe ad Christum spectet, non minus proprie, quam noster sanguis ad nos spectat, ita etiam hic τὸ ἴδιον αἷ- μα proprius sanguinis intelligendus venit. (9.) Originem quod attinet, sanguinem Christi dici Dei proprium sanguinem, quod à Deo, virtute Spiritus Sancti productus sit, vanum est κενοφύ- γητον. Et enim ratione animæ Christi, & cor- pus ejus, caro & ossa dicerentur itidem animæ Dei Patris propria, corpus Dei Patris proprium, caro & ossa Dei pariter propria. τὸ ἴδιον non re- spicit autorem, à quo productus sit sanguis, sed subjectum & suppositum, cujus proprius est: ut cum Petri proprium sanguinem dico, non intel- ligo parentis Petri, à quo procreatus est, san- guinem, sed ipsius Petri, ita cum Dei sanguis proprius dicitur, non intelligitur sanguis alicujus, qui à Deo originem habet, sed ipsius Dei pro- prius sanguis: quod quia probe vidit Enjedinus, hinc laboravit, ut infarciret vocem υἱῶ; vel vo- cem ἅιματος transformaret in vocem υἱῶ, & cum illa succedere non posse intelligeret, concessit, intelligi Christum voce τῶ Θεῶ, quod non nisi constrictum loci evidentia concessisse, creden- dum. (10.) Quid multis? acquirere proprio san- guine Ecclesiam nihil aliud est, secundum inter- pretationem Scripturæ, quam animam & vitam suam ponere, sanguinem suum profundere, ut homines à peccato liberentur & redimantur, quod non posse de Deo Patre dici, sed unice de Filio Dei quis ambigat? Ita autem explican- dum esse τὸ acquirere proprio sanguine Ecclesiam, ex his, & aliis Scripturæ locis Matth. XX. 28. Marc. X. 45. Johan. X. 11. Rom. III. 24. cap. V. 10. Ephes. I. 5. cap. II. 21. Galat. I. 4. Tit. II. 14. 1. Job. III. 16. Ebr. IX. 14. 1. Petr. I. 18. Apocal. I. 5. &c.

tam certum est, quam quod certissimum. Era- smi autoritatem quod concernit, ea in his con- troversiis perexigua est, imo nulla: ut frustra declamitet de ea Smalcius, nil præter ipsam ve- ritatem compellere eum potuisse, ut eundem sen- sum in hoc loco complecteretur, quem ipsi Soci- niani. Quis enim nescit, compulisse Erasmum spiritum Arianicum, à quo nimium quantum agitatus fuit? Quod non diffitetur ipse F. Soci- nus in Epist. pag. 187. quod nempe Erasmus non immerito & Trinitariis Arianismi nomine su- spectus fuerit, & ab Anti-Trinitariis inter eos re- latus, qui subobscure Trinitati reclamaverint. Ideoque recte Cornelius à Lapide Pontificius, in Erasmum (professione) Pontificium hanc censu- ram tulit, h. in l. Inepte & distorte Erasmus Aria- nis arma ministrans, sic exponit: inquo vos Spi- ritus Sanctus posuit Episcopos regere Ecclesiam Dei (Patris,) quam acquisivit (Christus) san- guine suo. Si hoc non est falsare Scripturam, quid erit?

Quod (6.) ad exceptionem Enjedini, quod hinc non consequatur, Christum esse æternum & omnipotentem Deum, etsi concedatur hic intelligi nomine Dei Christum, de eo opus non est, ut quicquam adjiciamus, quod invicta consequen- tiæ ratio probatione majoris propositionis nostræ satis demonstrata sit, & à cæteris adversariis o- mnibus nobiscum agnoscatur, nec amplius in dubium revocetur. Tantum itaque de hoc loco.

ἣν περιεποιήσατο) Fecit ut existeret, qui justissimus ac- quirendi modus. Vid. Eph. I. 14.

Non id docetur, quod effecerit Christus, ut existeremus, sed quod sibi nos acquisiverit inter- posito sanguinis proprii pretio, 1. Cor. VI. 20. 1. Pet. I. 18. Redemtio itaque indicatur, non fine λύτρῳ facta. Locus tamen Ephes. I. 14. non satis hic con- venit; ibi enim de hæreditate futura sermo est vitæ æternæ, cujus arrhabo est Spiritus Sanctus, quæ ac- quisita etiam nobis pretio sanguinis Christi: sed hic docetur, quomodo Christus nos ipsos sibi acquisiverit proprio sanguine, liberando nos è potestate Satanæ, peccati, & inferni, Hos. XIII. 14. Luc. I. 74. Ebr. II. 14. Tit. II. 14. Quum etiam per transgressionem sub potestatem Satanæ reda- cti, servi peccati, & rei mortis facti simus, vi ju- stitiæ divinæ, opus erat satisfactione ac redemtio- ne, ut proprii redderemur Christi. Vindicavit itaque & asseruit nos sibi in peculium, ac acquisi- vit sibi nos proprio sanguine: unde herus & Do- minus noster est, jure hujus redemptionis, qui nos mercatus est, 2. Petr. II. 1. idque sanguine suo Apoc. V. 9. c. XIV. 4.

διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος) Nam per mortem cruentam. Ch- stus illam potestatem colligendæ sibi Ecclesiæ, adeptus est, secundum vaticinium Esaiæ LIII. 10.

Non potestatem tantum adeptus est per mor- tem, (quod nec aliter admittendum, nisi quate- nus interventu mortis evectus est ad plenarium infinitæ potestatis exercitium, Phil. II. 9. Matth. XXVIII. 18. minime vero eo sensu, quasi meruerit sibi hanc ἐξουσίαν passione & morte sua) sed per sanguinem suum totum humanum genus redemit è potestate Satanæ, ad quod ut beneficio hujus re- demtionis fruatur, ad communionem regni sui vocare dignatur. Jus ergo habet ad eos, quos è manu Satanæ liberavit, qui mortuus est pro omnibus, ut non nobis viveremus, sed ipsi, qui mortuus pro nobis est, & resurrexit 2. Cor. V. 15.

## 20:29
Vers. 29.

μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν με) After my departure. ἄφιξις is departure in the Glossary.

Thus in Demosthenes, ἄφιξιν εἰς τοὺς πολεμίους ἐποιήσατο, he instituted a departure against the enemies. It is used in the same way among the LXX Interpreters, Gen. 38:1. Therefore, Beza's suspicion is not to be admitted, as if ἄφεσις, that is, dismissal, πρὸς τὸν κύριον [to the Lord] should be read in the sense in which ἀπολύειν occurs in Luke 2:29.

λύκοι βαρεῖς) Evening wolves, Jer. 5, Hab. 1:8, Zeph. 3:3. Βαρεῖς here has the same value as זאב in the cited passage of Habakkuk, where the LXX wishes to say rapacious, ὀξύτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς λύκους [sharper than wolves]. That persecution under Nero is indicated here. For this, the perseverance of the Ephesians is praised, Rev. 2:12.

μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου) Who will be led by no pity for the flock. Thus חמל and in Greek φείδομαι is taken. Deut. 7:16, ch. 13:8, ch. 19:13, 21. He says more simply what Zephaniah says figuratively: they shall not gnaw the bones until the morning.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν με) Post meam profectionem. ἄφιξις profectio in Glossario.

Ita apud Demosthenem ἄφιξιν εἰς τοὺς πολεμίους ἐποιήσατο, profectionem in hostes instituit. Sic etiam apud LXX. Interpp. usurpatur, Gen. XXXVIII. 1. Non ergo Bezæ suspicio admittenda, quasi ἄφε- σις, id est, dimissio πρὸς τὸν κύριον legendum sit eo sensu, quo ἀπολύειν Luc. II. 29. occurrit.

λύκοι βαρεῖς) Lupi vespertini Jerem. V. Abac. I. 8. Soph. III. 3. Βαρεῖς hic idem valet, quod זאב dicto Abaccuci loco, ubi LXX. ὀξύτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς λύκους vult dicere rapaces. Per- secutio hic indicatur illa sub Nerone. Ob hanc laudatur Ephesiorum perseverantia Apoc. II. 12.

μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου) Qui nulla ducentur gregis commiseratione. Ita חמל & Græce φείδομαι sumitur. Deut. VII. 16. c. XIII. 8. c. XIX. 13. 21. Dicit simplicius quod figurate Sophonias: non rodent ossa, usque ad mane.

## 20:30
Vers. 30.

καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες) The Nicolaitans, Rev. 2:6.

λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα) Teaching those things which deviate from the right. Thus διαστρέφων is taken in Luke 23:2, above ch. 13:8, 10; thus γενεὰ διεστραμμένη in Matt. 17:27, Luke 9:41, Phil. 2:15. The dogma of the Nicolaitans was that marriage was instituted merely as a human thing, and such that it would not bind consciences: and that it was lawful to eat things offered to idols without distinction. See Irenaeus 1:27, Tertullian on Prescription against Heretics, Clement of Alexandria Strom. 2 and 3, because he says the words of Nicolaus the Deacon were twisted by them into a depraved sense: Epiphanius, Heresy 25, Theodoret, book 3.

τοῦ ἀποσπᾷν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω αὑτῶν) ἕνεκα [for the sake of] is understood. Therefore they teach things pleasing to the flesh, so that those whom the discipline of the Church offends, having been led away from the Church, they may make followers for themselves.

ὀπίσω is a word proper to disciples, Matt. IV. 19, ch. X. 38, ch. XVI. v. 24, Mark VIII. 34, Luke IX. 23, ch. XIV. 27, ch. XXI. 8, John XII. 19, above ch. V. 37.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες) Nicolaitæ Apoc. II. v. 6.

λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα) Docentes ea quæ à recto defle- ctunt. Sic διαστρέφων sumitur Luc. XXIII. 2. supra c. XIII. 8. 10. sic γενεὰ διεστραμμένη Matth. XVII. 27. Luc. IX. 41. Phil. II. 15. Dogma Nicolaitarum erat, matrimonium institutum esse mere humanum, & tale quod conscientias non obligaret: imolatitiis sine distinctione licere vesci. Vide Irenæum I. 27. Tertullianum de præscriptione adversus Hæreticos: Clementem Alexandrinum Strom. II. & III. quia Nicolai Diaconi verba in pravum ab eis ait detorta: Epiphanium Hæresi 25. Theodoretum lib. III.

τοῦ ἀποσπᾷν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω αὑτῶν) Subauditur ἕνεκα. Ideo docent carni placentia, ut eos quos Ecclesiæ disciplina offendit, ab Ecclesia abductos sibi faciant sectatores,

ὀπίσω est vox propria discipulis, Matth. IV. 19. c. X. 38. c. XVI. v. 24. Marc. VIII. 34. Luc. IX. 23. c. XIV. 27. c. XXI. 8. Joh. XII. 19. supra c. V. 37.

## 20:31
Verse 31.

διὸ γρηγορεῖτε) Beware for yourselves, and see to it that others also beware of them. This warning did not escape them, Rev. II. 6.

τριετίαν) See above ch. XIX. 10, where there is mention of a two-year period. With that two-year period must be joined the time of Paul's first arrival at Ephesus, ch. XVIII. 19, and that one year is to be interpreted as a part of a year.

Namely, to those two years in which he taught in the School of Tyrannus, must be added first the three months in which he taught in the Synagogue before that three-year period, then also that time, however brief, in which he taught at Ephesus when he first came there with Aquila and Priscilla, Acts XVIII. v. 18; for Paul had come to Ephesus with Aquila and Priscilla one full year before those two years, although Paul spent the greater part of that year on that third journey of his, in which he went up to Jerusalem, and from there traveled through Antioch, Phrygia, and Galatia, before he came to Ephesus a second time, as Capellus says here.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

διὸ γρηγορεῖτε) Cavete vobis, & facite ut & alii eos ca- veant. Non excidit illis hoc monitum, Apoc. II. 6.

τριετίαν) Vide supra c. XIX. 10. ubi biennii mentio. Cum eo biennio conjungendum tempus prioris adventus Pauli- ni Ephesum cap. XVIII. 19. & annus ille unus interpretan- dus, pars anni.

Nempe duobus istis annis, quibus in Schola Ty- ranni docuit, adjungendi sunt primum tres menses, quibus ante illud triennium docuit in Synagoga, tum etiam tempus illud licet breve quo Ephesi do- cuit, cum primo illuc venit cum Aquila & Priscilla Actorum XVII. v. 18. anno enim uno integro vene- rat Ephesum Paulus cum Aquila & Priscilla ante biennium istud, licet anni illius partem maximam consumpserit Paulusin peregrinatione illa sua ter- tia, qua Jerosolymam ascendit, in de Antiochiam, Phrygiam & Galatiam lustravit, antequam secun- do veniret Ephesum, ut hic Capellus.

## 20:32
Verse 32. παρατίθεμαι) I have entrusted.

τῷ Θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ,) It is a hendiadys. For the sense is: I commend you to God through the word of his kindness. Therefore the prayer will return to God, just as if those words καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ had not been inserted.

τῷ δυναμένῳ ἐποικοδομῆσαι) Supply 'you', which the Syriac adds here. To build up is to cause them to grow in faith, like a house that rises little by little, Eph. II. 20, Col. II. 7, Jude 20.

Some understand the Son of God by λόγον. More correctly, however, the spoken word is understood, which is the word of his grace, both because it offers and preaches grace, and because it also effectively confers and communicates the same, as a medium divinely ordained, John VI. 63, Rom. I. 16, ch. X. 17, 1 Cor. I. 18, 21, Phil. II. 16, Heb. VIII. 2, Jas. I. 21, 1 Pet. I. 17. There is therefore no need for a hendiadys: which, if it were to have a place, would have to be explained thus: to God and the Word; that is, to the God of the Word, as in Acts XXIII. 6, concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead, that is, concerning the hope of the resurrection.

καὶ δοῦναι ὑμῖν κληρονομίαν) Thus eternal life is called, because its possession is firm, like landed property among the Hebrews. See on Eph. I. 14, 18.

ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν) ἐν, here, as often among the Hebrews ב, signifies 'among'. In the society of all who have attained to holiness.

Latin:

Vers. 32. παρατίθεμαι) הפקדתי.

τῷ Θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ,) Est ἓν διὰ δυοῖν. Sensus enim est: commendo vos Deo per sermonem boni- tatis ejus. itaque ad Deum oratio redibit, plane quasi illa καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ interjecta non fuissent.

τῷ δυναμένῳ ἐποικοδομῆσαι) Supple vos, quod addit hic Syrus. Aedificare est efficere ut in fide crescant, sicut domus quae paulatim surgit, Eph. II. 20. Col. II. 7. Judae 20.

Nonnulli per λόγον intelligunt Filium Dei. Re- ctius tamen verbum προφορικὸν intelligitur, quod est gratiae ejus verbum, tum quia gratiam offert, & praedicat, tum quia eandem quoque efficaciter confert, communicat, ceu medium divinitus or- dinatum Joh. VI. 63. Rom. I. 16. c. X. 17. 1. Cor. I. 18. 21. Phil. II. 16. Ebr. VIII. 2. Jac. I. 21. 1. Petr. I. 17. Non ergo opus est hendiade: quae si locum habe- ret, ita explicanda esset, Deo & Verbo; id est, Deo Verbi, ut Actor. XXIII. 6. de spe & resurrectione mor- tuorum, id est, de spe resurrectionis.

καὶ δοῦναι ὑμῖν κληρονομίαν) Sic vocatur vita aeterna, quia firma est ejus possessio, ut rerum soli apud Hebraeos. Vide ad Eph. I. 14. 18.

ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν) ἐν, hic, ut saepe apud Hebraeos ב, valet inter. In societate omnium qui ad sanctitatem pervenere.

## 20:33
Verse 33.

I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel) A more noble proclamation about oneself than that of Samuel, 1 Sam. XII. 5. Samuel testified that he had accepted nothing for the sake of judging. Paul had not wished to accept any compensation for his constant labor in teaching.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

Ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα) Praecla- rior de se praedicatio, quam illa Samuelis I. Sam. XII. 5. Sa- muel testificabatur, nihil se judicandi causa accepisse. Pau- lus nec laboris in docendo assidui repensationem ullam accipere voluerat.

## 20:34
Verse 34.

these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me) As above, ch. XVIII. 3 & 2 Thess. III. 8. Add 1 Cor. II. 12, 1 Thess. II. 9; the same manner of speaking is found in Xenophon: 'the hands serve each one.'

Latin:

Vers. 34.

ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετ' ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται) Vt supra c. XVIII. 3. & 2. Thess. III. 8. Adde 1. Cor. II. 12. 1. Thess. II. 9. idem loquendi genus apud Xenophontem: αἱ χεῖρες ἑκάστῳ ὑπηρετοῦσι.

## 20:35
Verse 35.

I have showed you all things) That is, in every way. Others have observed a similar manner of speaking in 1 Cor. IX. 25, ch. X. 33, Eph. IV. 15.

so laboring) Even with some trouble. Thus the same Paul uses the word κοπιῶμεν in this very matter in 1 Cor. IV. 12. It corresponds to the Hebrew words חלה & יגע & לאה & others having the meaning of trouble.

we ought to support the weak) To sustain the infirm, that is, lest they fall. He calls those 'infirm' who might suspect that Paul was inventing the doctrine of the Gospel for his own profit. Paul wished to cut off all such handles.

These things are said metaphorically, as Beza notes, concerning those who, not yet sufficiently confirmed by doctrine and examples, find stumbling blocks where the way is most plain: and therefore they are to be borne as much as it is possible (yet with a safe conscience), and all things by which they might be offended must be diligently avoided. For this is to support the falling. See Luke I. 54.

that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive) This is among those things which Paul had learned not from writing, but from the report of those who had known the Lord. Not unlike is the saying of Aristotle, Nicom. III: 'It is more characteristic of virtue to do good than to receive good,' and of Sallust in the Catilinarian: 'They procured friendships more by giving than by receiving benefits.' And in the Jugurthine, concerning Sulla: 'To many who asked, he gave benefits of his own accord, but was unwilling to receive them.' Plutarch from Epicurus: 'To do good is sweeter than to receive it.'

Latin:

Vers. 35.

πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν) Id est, πάντως. Observaverunt alii par loquendi genus 1. Cor. IX. 25. c. X. 33. Eph. IV. 15.

οὕτω κοπιῶντας) Etiam cum molestia aliqua. Sic κοπιῶ- μεν usurpat idem Paulus in eadem hac re 1. Cor. IV. 12. Re- spondet Hebraeis vocibus חלה & יגע & לאה & aliis mo- lestiae significationem habentibus.

δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων) Infirmos sustentan- dos, ne cadant scilicet. Infirmos vocat qui suspicari pote- rant Paulum commodi sui causa comminisci doctrinam Evangelii. Omnes tales ansas praecidere Paulus voluit.

Dicuntur haec translatitie notante Beza de illis, qui nondum satis confirmati doctrina & exem- plis, offendicula ibi inveniunt, ubi planissima via est: ideoque ferendi sunt quoad ejus fieri potest, (salva tamen conscientia) & cavenda diligenter omnia, quibus possint offendi. Hoc enim est la- bentes fulcire Vide Luc. I. 54.

ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπε· μακάριόν ἐστι διδόναι μᾶλλον ἢ λαμβάνειν) Hoc est inter illa quae Paulus didicerat non ex scripto, sed relatu eorum, qui Dominum noverant. Non dissimile dictum Aristotelis Nicom. III. τῆς ἀρετῆς μᾶλλον τὸ εὖ ποιεῖν, ἢ τὸ εὖ πάσχειν, & Sallustii in Catilinario: Magis dandis quam acci- piendis beneficiis amicitias parabant: Et in Jugurthino de Sul- la: Multis rogantibus alios per se ipsa dare beneficia, invitum ac- cipere: Plutarchus ex Epicuro: Εὖ ποιεῖν ἥδιόν ἐςι τοῦ πάσχειν.

## 20:36
Verse 36. kneeled down) As in a time of sadness. See what we have said at Matt. VI. 5. Therefore the custom of not bending the knees between Easter and Pentecost had not yet been introduced. For the things which are narrated here fell within that time. See above ch. XX. 16.

Latin:

Vers. 36. θεὶς τὰ γόνατα ἀυτοῦ) Ut in tristi tempore, Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. VI. 5. Nondum ergo introductus erat mos genua non flectendi intra Pascha & Pentecosten. Nam quæ hic narrantur, in id tempus inciderunt. Vide supra c. XX. 16.

## 20:37
Verse 37. and fell on Paul's neck) You have this custom in Gen. XLV. 14, ch. XLVI. 30.

kissed him) See above v. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 37. κᾀ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου) Hunc morem habes Gen. XLV. 14. c. XLVI. 30.

Κατεφίλουν ἀυτόν) Vide supra v. 1.

## 20:38
Vers. 38. προέπεμπον δὲ ἀυτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον) They accompanied him as far as the ship. See above c. XV. 3. Ovid describes such a προπομπὴν: The land for you: for us the waters are seen. And now the sailor has released the ship from the land with the rope cast off, and has cast down the narrow bridge into the seas; where the savage Master from the stern with a long cry breaks up the embraces, and tears away the faithful kisses. Nor is it permitted to linger long on the dear neck.

See also Acts XXI. 5. Pricaeus observes this sense of the word from Herodian VI. and Heliodorus V., noting also another of its meanings by which προπέμπειν in Tit. III. 13 and in the 3rd Epistle of John means to provide what is necessary for a journey.

Latin:

Vers. 38. προέπεμπον δὲ ἀυτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον) Prosecuti eum sunt ad navem usque. Vide supra c. XV. 3. Talem προπομπὴν describit Ovidius: Terra tibi: Nobis aspiciuntur aquæ. Et Iamque ratem terris dimisit fune soluto Navita, & angustum dejecit in æquora pontem; Sævus ubi à puppi longo clamore Magister Dissipat amplexus, atque oscula fida revellit. Nec longum cara licet in cervice morari.

Vid. & Actor. XXI. 5. Observat hunc vocis sen- sum Pricæus ex Herodiano VI. Heliodoro V. notans & aliam ejus significationem qua προπέμπειν Tit. III. 13. & in Epist. 3. Joh. sit quæ usui sint itineri suffi- cere.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Paul, arriving at Tyre, stayed with the disciples for a week, having been warned not to head for Jerusalem. He proceeds, however, to Ptolemais, staying with the brothers for a day. Thence he came to Caesarea, received in the house of Philip, where Agabus, having bound himself with Paul's belt, prophesied concerning his chains in Jerusalem; but Paul, solicited in vain not to go there, was prepared not only for chains, but also to undergo death for the name of Jesus. He arrived at Jerusalem, lodging with Mnason, and reported to James and the elders what had been done among the Gentiles; he was advised that, because of the myriads of Jews who had been converted, since he was suspected of teaching the Jews to defect from Moses, he should take care to purify himself in the temple. When he was doing this, he was seen by the Asian Jews, who stirred up a tumult against him, as if he were teaching against the people, the law, and the temple, and they would have slaughtered him had he not been snatched from their hands by the tribune. By whom, bound in chains, he is led into the barracks, the tribune thinking him to be that Egyptian who had caused a sedition a few days before, who, however, being more correctly informed about him, grants him the power of speaking to the people.

There are three parts: I. Paul's journey toward Jerusalem, not terrified by the dissuasion and prophecy of the Tyrian brothers and the prophet Agabus, to v. 15. II. Paul's purification in the temple, v. 26. III. The tumult stirred up against Paul by the Jews, and his rescue by the tribune, to v. 40.

PART I. Paul's journey toward Jerusalem.

V. 1. Ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς) Take it as above c. XIII. 13, c. XVI. 11, c. XVIII. 21, c. XX. 3, 13.

ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπ' ἀυτῶν) As if torn away by force. It significantly expresses mutual affections.

ἐυθυδρομήσαντες) With a favorable wind, as above c. XVI. 11.

εἰς τὴν Κῶ) Aristotle said Con; Pliny, Coon. Stephanus acknowledges those first two endings: Luke preferred the one which we also had above c. XIX. 1. It is a most famous island among the Cyclades, both for the worship of Aesculapius and for the temple of Juno, concerning which Vitruvius mentions a book written by Theodorus.

τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον) Noble for the worship of the Sun and the Colossus.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Paulus Tyrum perveniens penes discipulos se- ptimanam substitit, monitus, ne Hierosoly- mam tendat. Pergit tamen Ptolemaida apud fratres per diem hærens. Dehinc Cæsaream venit, receptus in ædibus Philippi, ubi Aga- bus zona Pauli sibi alligata de ejus vinculis in Ierusalem prophetavit; Sed frustra soli- citatus Paulus, ne eo abeat, paratus non vin- cula tantum, sed & mortem pro nomine Iesu subire. Hierosolymam pervenit divertens penes Mnasonem, retulitque Iacobo, & senio- ribus, quæ inter gentes acta; commonitus, ut propter Iudæorum myriades conversas, quum suspectus esset, quasi doceret, Iudæos à Mose deficere, sese in templo mundari cura- ret. Quod cum faceret, conspectus fuit à Iu- dæis Asiaticis, qui tumultum excitarunt ad- versus eum, quasi contra populum, legem & templum doceret, trucidaturi eundem, nisi à tribuno manibus eorundem ereptus fuis- set. A quo catenis vinctus in castra deduci- tur, existimante, ipsum esse Ægyptium il- lum, qui ante paucos dies seditionem fece- rat, qui vero rectius de eo informatus pote- statem illi concedit ad populum loquendi.

Partes tres sunt I. Profectio Pauli versus Jerusa- lem non territi fratrum Tyriorum & Agabi Pro- phetæ dehortatione & prophetia, ad v. 15. II. Pu- rificatio Pauli in templo, v. 26. III. Tumultus adver- sus Paulum à Judæis excitatus, ejusdemque per tri- bunum ereptio, ad v. 40.

PARS I. Profectio Pauli versus Hierosolymam.

V. 1. Ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς) Sume ut supra c. XIII. 13. c. XVI. 11. c. XVIII. 21. c. XX. 3. 13.

ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπ' ἀυτῶν) Quasi vi avulsi. Significanter exprimit affectus mutuos.

ἐυθυδρομήσαντες) Vento secundo ut supra c. XVI. 11.

εἰς τὴν Κῶ) Con dixit Aristoteles: Coon Plinius. Priores illas duas desinentias agnoscit Stephanus: Lucas eam præ- tulit quam & supra habuimus c. XIX. 1. insula est inter Cy- cladas celeberrima, tum Æsculapii cultu, tum Junonis æde, de qua scriptum Theodori librum memorat Vitruvius.

τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον) Solis cultu & Colosso nobilem.

## 21:2
Vers. 2. διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην) Namely Tyre, as he will say shortly.

Doubtless from the city of Miletus, Paul with his company crossed over to Cos, an interval of fifteen miles, which is noble for the birth of Hippocrates, the prince of physicians, and Apelles, the prince of painters, and was also called Meropis. From which on the following day they came to Rhodes, an interval of twenty-one miles, and from the island of Rhodes they crossed to Patara, an interval of twenty-five miles. The island of Cos, in the Aegean Sea, near Caria, distant one hundred and twenty-one miles from Jerusalem towards the west, seems to be named from caverns and caves, according to some, because kéuoi denotes caverns; today it is called Stancu by the Turks, with a circumference of 15 miles, very fertile, and abounding in most sweet wine. It has a city of the same name.

Rhodes, an island and city named from the word for rose, situated in the Mediterranean Sea, at a moderate interval from Asia Minor towards the South, 110 miles from Jerusalem towards the west, an island of 28 miles. See Strabo, book XIV. The city of Rhodes was once famous for the Colossus or statue of the Sun erected by Demetrius, King of Asia, and for the study of the arts, and was occupied by the Saracens more than once.

Patara, a city of Lycia on the southern shore of Asia Minor, situated on the Mediterranean Sea one hundred and two miles from Jerusalem, also called Arsinoe.

Latin:

Vers. 2. διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην) Nempe Tyrum, ut mox di- cet.

Nimirum ab urbe Mileto Paulus cum comita- tu suo quindecim miliarium interstitio trajecit Coum, quæ nobilis est Hippocratis Medicorum, & Apellis Pictorum principis ortu, & Merópis dicta etiam est. Ex qua sequenti die viginti & unius mi- liarium intercapedine Rhodum venerunt, & ex in- sula Rhodo trajecerunt Pataram intervallo vigin- ti quinque miliarium. Cous insula maris Ægæi Ca- riæ vicina miliaribus centum viginti & uno ab Hierosolyma versus occasum distans, à cavernis & speluncis, juxta quosdam dicta videtur, quia kéuoi cavernas notant, hodie à Turcis Stancu vocatur, ambitu 15. miliarium, valde fertilis, & vino abun- dans suavissimo. Urbem habet ejusdem nominis.

Rhodos à rosæ voce vocata insula & urbs, in mari mediterraneo, modico intervallo ab Asia minori versus Austrum, ab Hierosolyma, 110. miliaribus versus occasum sita, insula miliarium 28. Vid. Stra- bo l. XIV. Civitas Rhodus Colosso seu statua Solis insigni à Demetrio Asiæ Rege erecta, & à studiis artium celebris quondam fuit, plus vice simplici à Saracenis occupata.

Patara urbs Lyciæ in Asiæ minoris litore meridionali, ad mare mediterra- neum centum & duobus miliaribus ab Hierosol. sita, vocata etiam Arsinoe.

## 21:3
Vers. 3. ἀναφανέντες δὲ τῇ Κύπρῳ) It is a nautical term. When we had sighted Cyprus. Sailors still speak this way even now, when they wish to say that some place previously hidden has come into their view.

καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον) A similar expression: - - - but on the left lay Bellus.

ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον) Present for future. There the ship was to unload the cargo received at Ephesus.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ἀναφανέντες δὲ τῇ Κύπρῳ) Est vox nautica. Cum detexissemus Cyprum. Etiam nunc sic loquuntur nautæ, cum volunt dicere, aliquem locum prius latentem sibi in conspectum venisse.

καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον) Similis locutio: - - - at illi læva jacebat Bellus.

ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον) Præsens pro futuro. Ibi navis exponere debebat onus Ephesi rece- ptum.

## 21:4
V. 4. ἔλεγον διὰ τῦ πνεύματος μὴ ἀναβαίνειν εἰς Ἱερουσα- λὴμ) A brief expression, for it must be understood, unless he wished to be bound. They were predicting the same things to him that Agabus did shortly after.

From the city of Patara they sailed into Syria (Palestine) and its first and best port, Tyre; with an interval of 90 miles, having left Cyprus to the left, and having found disciples there, they remained there for seven days.

Latin:

V. 4. ἔλεγον διὰ τῦ πνεύματος μὴ ἀναβαίνειν εἰς Ἱερουσα- λὴμ) Brevis locutio, subintelligendum enim, nisi vinciri vellet. Eadem illi prædicebant, quæ mox 'Agabus.

Ab urbe Patara navigarunt in Syriam (Palæsti- nam) ejusque primum & optimum portum Ty- rum; interstitio XC. miliarium relicta Cypro ad sinistram, repertisque ibi discipulis manserunt il- lic septem diebus.

## 21:5
ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἡμᾶς ἐξαρτίζαι τὰς ἡμέρας) ἐξαρτίζαι, that is, to fulfill. מלא

προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων) As above, chapter XV. 3. chapter XX. v. 38.

καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν) By the occasion indeed of the journey undertaken by Paul: But at the same time consistently with the custom of the Jews: Tertullian on fasting: The Jewish fast is certainly celebrated everywhere, when, omitting the temples, throughout the whole shore, wherever they are in the open, they sometimes send prayers to heaven. The same against the Nations I. For the Jewish feasts, Sabbaths, and pure suppers, and Jewish rites of lamps, and fasts with unleavened bread, and coastal prayers. Philo against Flaccus: Πάνυχοί τε διατελέσαντες ἐν ὕμνοις καὶ ᾀδαῖς ἅμα τῇ ἕῳ διὰ πυλῶν ἐκχυθέντες ἐπὶ τὰς πλησίον αἰγιαλοὺς ἀφικνῦνται. See what [we said] above, chapter XVI. 13.

Latin:

ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἡμᾶς ἐξαρτίζαι τὰς ἡμέρας) ἐξαρτίζαι, id est, πληρῶσαι. מלא

προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων) Ut supra cap. XV. 3. cap. XX. v. 38.

καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν) Ex occasione quidem itineris à Paulo suscepti: Sed simul congruenter mori Ju- dæorum: Tertullianus de jejuniis: Iudaicum certe jejunium ubique celebratur, cum omissis templis per omne littus, quocun- que in aperto aliquando jam preces ad cælum mittant. Idem adversus Nationes I. Iudæi enim festi, Sabbata & cæna pura, & Iudaici ritus lucernarum, & jejunia cum azymis, & ora- tiones littorales. Philo adversus Flaccum: Πάνυχοί τε δια- τελέσαντες ἐν ὕμνοις καὶ ᾀδαῖς ἅμα τῇ ἕῳ διὰ πυλῶν ἐκχυθέντες ἐπὶ τὰς πλησίον αἰγιαλοὺς ἀφικνῦνται. Vide quæ supra cap. XVI. 13.

## 21:6
Vers. 6. καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι ἀλλήλους) As above, chapter XX. 1. In the manuscript it is: προσευξάμενοι ἀπησπάσμεθα ἀλλήλους.

εἰς τὰ ἴδια) See what we said regarding Luke c. II. 49.

Latin:

Vers. 6. καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι ἀλλήλους) Ut supra cap. XX. 1. In Manuscripto est: προσευξάμενοι ἀπησπάσμεθα ἀλλήλους.

εἰς τὰ ἴδια) Vide quæ diximus ad Lucæ c. II. 49.

## 21:7
Vers. 7. κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα) A city of Phoenicia, which Pliny says was once called Ace: that is עכו Jud. I. 31. In the manuscript: κατήλθομεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα.

Latin:

Vers. 7. κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα) Urbem Phœnices, quam Plinius dicit olim Acen dictam: id est עכו Jud.I. 31. In Manuscripto: κατήλθομεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα.

## 21:8
Vers. 8. εἰς Καισάρειαν) Of Strato, which is in Judea, or Syria Palestine. See Ptolemy.

From Tyre, Paul and his companions sailed for a distance of six miles to Ptolemais, a once splendid city, which today is subject to the Turks, and from there at an interval of eleven miles they came to Caesarea of Strato, and having entered the house of Philip the Evangelist, they stayed with him. Afterwards, from there, by a journey of eight miles, they came to Jerusalem in the 47th year of Paul's age, 50th of Christ.

Φιλίππου τῦ εὐαγγελισῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ) That is, who, having once been of the number of the VII Deacons, had been made a traveling presbyter, attached to no fixed Church, such as were called Evangelists, Ephes. IV. 11. 2. Timoth. IV. 5. that is מבשרים Isaiah XL. 9. c. LII. 7. thus promotions were accustomed to be made by degree, 1. Tim. III. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 8. εἰς Καισάρειαν) Stratonis, quæ in Judæa, sive Syria Palæstina. Vide Ptolemæum.

De Tyro Paulus & Comites ejus spatio sex mi- liarium navigarunt Ptolemaidem, urbem olim splendidam, quæ hodie Turcis subest, & inde mi- liarium undecim intervallo venerunt Cæsarean Stratonis, & ingressi domum Philippi Evangelistæ manserunt apud eum. Postea inde octo miliarium itinere Hierosolymam venerunt anno ætatis Pau- li 47. Christi 50.

Φιλίππου τῦ εὐαγγελισῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ) Id est, qui tum olim de numero VII. Diaconorum fuisset, factus erat presbyter περιοδευτὴς, nulli certæ Ecclesiæ affixus, quales Evangelistæ vocabantur, Ephes. IV. 11. 2. Timoth. IV. 5. id est מבשרים Esaia XL. 9. c. LII. 7. ita solebant promotiones fieri κατὰ βαθμόν, 1. Tim. III. 13.

## 21:9
Vers. 9.

θυγατέρες παρθένοι) By their own purpose and that of their Father, as is credible. See what is said at Luke II. 37. Matthew XIX. 12. add 1 Cor. VII. 37.

That they were bound by a vow, which the Papists maintain, founding here the state of nuns, as can be seen in Cornelius à Lapide, is by no means asserted here. For what Bellarmine says in De Monarch. c. X., that it is hinted at by the fact that it is reported of one man that he had 4 virgin daughters: because it is no great thing to have 4 virgin daughters, who when they are mature will be married, it savors of the fallacy of composition and division: for it is reported as a peculiar thing that they were 4 prophesying virgins. And Eusebius reports in Book III of Church History, c. 30, that two of these were given in marriage, and two grew old in virginity. Finally, if they had had a purpose of virginity at all, it will never be taught that they made a solemn vow. Which differ greatly. For it is often permissible to change a purpose of continence without any fault, as Bellarmine says, l. c. c. 24. But a vow is irrevocable and immutable, according to the Pontificians.

προφητεύουσαι) See here the fulfillment of that which we had above in c. II. 18, 'upon my handmaidens'.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

θυγατέρες παρθένοι) Ex proposito & suo & Patris, ut credibile est. Vide quæ dicta ad Luc. II. 37. Matth. XIX. 12. adde 1. Cor. VII. 37.

Voto illas obstrictas fuisse, quod Papistæ volunt, hic monialium statum fundantes, ut apud Cornel. à Lapid. videre est, hic minime asseritur. Nam quod Bellarminus de Monarch. c. X. ait, eo id innui, quod refertur uni homini fuisse 4. filias virgines: quia nihil magni 4. habere filias virgines, quæ ubi maturæ fuerint, nupturæ sint, fallaciam sapit compositio- nis & divisionis: nam id ceu peculiare refertur, quod 4. fuerint virgines prophetantes. Et tradit Eusebius lib. III. Hist. Eccl. c. 30. duas harum nu- ptui datas, duas in virginitate consenuisse. Deni- que si omnino propositum habuissent virginitatis, solemne tamen votum eas fecisse nunquam doce- bitur. Quæ maximopere differunt. Propositum enim continentiæ sæpe licet sine ulla culpa mutare, ut ait Bellarmin. l. c. c. 24. Votum autem est irrevoca- bile, & immutabile, juxta Pontificios.

προφητεύουσαι) Vide hic implerum id, quod habuimus supra c. II. 18. ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας με.

## 21:10
Vers. 10. ὀνόματι Ἄγαβος) He of whom we spoke above in c. II. 28.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ὀνόματι Ἄγαβος) Is de quo supra c. II. 28.

## 21:11
Vers. 11. καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου) A known custom of the Prophets, to signify future events by visible things themselves. Thus Jeremiah was ordered to bury his belt in c. 13; false prophets also imitated this, as appears in Jeremiah XXVIII. Dionysius Thrax: 'For they signified not only through speech but also through symbols.'

Δήσας δὲ αὐτοῦ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας) Thus Christ had said to Peter: 'Another shall gird you,' John XXI. 18.

καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν) Thus it was to happen to the disciple, as it once did to the Master, Matthew XX. 19.

Latin:

Vers. 11. καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου) Notus Prophetarum mos, ipsis etiam rebus conspicuis futura præsignandi. Sic zonam suam defodere jussus Jeremias c. 13. imitati id & falsi Prophetæ, ut apparet Jerem. XXVIII. Dionysius Thrax. Ἐσήμαινον γὰρ ὀυ διὰ λέξεως μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ συμβόλων.

Δήσας δὲ αὐτοῦ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας) Sic Christus Petro dixerat: Ἄλλος σε ζώσει Joh. XXI. 10.

καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν) Ita discipulo eventurum erat, quod olim magistro, Matth. XX. 19.

## 21:12
Vers. 12. κὴ οἱ ἐντόπιοι) The Christians of Caesarea, led by human affection.

Latin:

Vers. 12. κὴ οἱ ἐντόπιοι) Cæsareenses Christiani, humano ducti affectu.

## 21:13
Vers. 13. κὴ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν) Breaking my heart, that is, as much as was in them; for words are sometimes understood even without effect. It is the same expression in Num. XXXII. 9, ויניאו את־לב they discouraged the heart, where the LXX says, 'they turned away the heart.' A little before, where the same word is used, 'they pervert the minds.'

ἑτοίμως ἔχω) The same expression in 2 Cor. XII. 14, 1 Peter IV. 5, and Dan. III. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 13. κὴ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν) Frangentes ani- mum, nempe quantum in ipsis erat: verba enim interdum intelliguntur etiam sine effectu. Est locutio eadem Num. XXXII. 9. ויניאו את־לב fregerunt cor, ubi LXX. ἀπέ- στησαν τὴν καρδίαν. Paulò ante, ubi idem verbum est, δια- στρέφουσι τὰς διανοίας.

ἑτοίμως ἔχω) Eadem locutio 2. Cor. XII. 14. 1. Petr. IV. 5. & Dan. III. 18.

## 21:14
Vers. 14. ἀπόντες· τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου γενέσθω) And this after the example of the Master, Matthew XXVI. 42.

PART II. The purification of Paul in the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ἀπόντες· τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου γενέσθω) Et hoc ad exemplum Magistri, Matth. XXVI. 42.

PARS II. Purificatio Pauli in templo.

## 21:15
Ver. 15. ἐπισκευασάμενοι) Thus also the Manuscript, not ἀποσκευασάμενοι, which has no place here. ἐπισκευάζεσθαι here means to load baggage onto beasts of burden. Xenophon and Aristotle use it in this way.

There was no need for emendation, since most Codices have ἀποσκευασάμενοι, for: ἀποσκευάζειν is to lay down, to take out of the way, and to prepare oneself by removing impediments: in which sense the LXX Interpreters use this word for פנה, Lev. XIV. 36, which they render elsewhere by ἑτοιμάζειν, as Gen. XXIV. 31, Isa. XL. 3, just as it is also explained here by the Syrian and Arab as prepared. Camerarius rendered it thus; with baggage left behind, naturally so that the journey might be more expeditious. Which sense is plainly contrary to the Grotian one. But they are said to have ascended to Jerusalem, where Paul had determined to be present for the feast of Pentecost, chapter XX. 16, whence all the days are so diligently noted by Luke: for he teaches that Paul set out from Philippi after the 7 days of unleavened bread at the Passover, chapter XX. 1, and in 5 days arrived at Troas, and stayed there 7 days, and from there reached Miletus in three days, and furthermore hastened, so that he might celebrate Pentecost at Jerusalem, and so having set out from there, on the first day he came to Cos, on the second to Rhodes, thence to Patara, thence to Tyre; there he spent seven days, thence at Ptolemais one day, thence he came to Caesarea, and stayed there for some days, and then arrived at Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ἐπισκευασάμενοι) Sic & Manuscriptus, non ἀπο- σκευασάμενοι, quod hic locum non habet. ἐπισκευάζεσθαι hic est sarcinas jumentis imponere. Utuntur sic Xenophon & Aristoteles.

Non opus erat emendatione, quum plerique Codices habeant ἀποσκευασάμενοι nam: ἀποσκε- υάζειν est deponere, è medio tollere, & remotis impe- dimentis se præparare: quo sensu LXX. Interp. hac voce pro פנה utuntur, Lev. XIV. 36. quod alibi per ἑτοιμάζειν reddunt, ut Gen. XXIV. 31. Esa. XL. 3. quemadmodum & hic à Syro & Arabe exponitur præparati. Sic reddidit Camerarius; Sarcinis reli- ctis, nimirum ut esset iter expeditius. Qui sensus Grotiano plane contrarius. Ascendisse autem dicuntur Hierosolymam, ubi festo Pentecostes adesse definiverat Paulus cap. XX. 16. unde à Luca tam diligenter dies omnes notati sunt: nam in Paschate post 7. dies azymorum docet Philippis solvisse Paulum cap. XX. 1. & diebus 5. Troadem ap- pulisse, ibique 7. dies commoratum esse, atque in- de tribus diebus Miletum pervenisse, ac porro properasse, ut Pentecosten Hierosolymis ageret, adeoque inde profectum prima die Coum, secun- da Rhodum, inde Pataram, inde Tyrum venisse; ibi septem egisse dies, inde Ptolemaide diem unam, inde venisse Cæsaream, ibique hæsisse aliquot dies, ac tum Hierosolymam pervenisse.

## 21:16
Verse 16.

συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν) Namely τινες: as in Matt. XXIII. v. 34. & elsewhere.

ἄγοντες παῤ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν) A brief expression for ἄγοντες ἡμᾶς πρός τινα παρ' ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν: leading (that is, about to lead, present for future) us to him with whom we might lodge. For that Mnason seems to have gone from Cyprus to live in Jerusalem. His Hebrew name was :מנסן

ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ) From that time when Paul & Barnabas had been in Cyprus, above c. XIII. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν) Nempe τινες: ut Matth. XXIII. v. 34. & alibi.

ἄγοντες παῤ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν) Brevis locutio pro ἄγοντες ἡμᾶς πρός τινα παρ' ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν: ducentes (id est, ducturi, præsens pro futuro) nos ad eum apud quem diverteremur. Nam Mnason ille ex Cypro videtur habitatum ivisse Hierosolyma. Ei nomen Hebræum fuerit :מנסן

ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ) Ex eo tempore quo Paulus & Barnabas in Cypro fuerant, supra c. XIII. 4.

## 21:18
Verse 18. πρὸς Ἰάκωβον) Peter being absent, the first of the Apostolic assembly.

οἱ πρεσβύτεροι) As above c. XV. 6. He who was of the Apostles at Jerusalem performed the office which Bishops later held, and therefore he called the elders together: unless perhaps this James was the brother of the Lord, not an Apostle, but a Bishop.

Scripture knows nothing of the brother of the Lord, James, who was not an Apostle, but a Bishop. Nor had the preeminence of Bishops over Presbyters been introduced yet at that time, concerning which the illustrious Salmasius under the name of Wallo Messalinus, and Dalleus have written expressly against the Papists. Cornelius a Lapide tells a long story, that all the Apostles were then present in Jerusalem, and by the wonderful providence of God had gathered for the passing of Mary: that Paul also, urged by the Spirit, had hastened there, so that before her death he might greet her, and commend to her his Churches and his struggles, especially those which he was soon to undergo at Rome with Nero and Simon Magus; that the Virgin Mary rose again three days after her death, and was assumed gloriously in body as well as in soul by Angels, or rather by Christ with triumph into heaven, and was there crowned as queen of heaven and earth, placed on a throne beside her Son above all the orders of angels. If it be asked whence the Papists have these things, they put forward the Church: It is certain, says Cornelius, that Mary died and rose again, and was then assumed into heaven, as the Church hands down. But whence is that CERTAIN, and from what trustworthy witnesses do the Roman Catholics have that and the rest which he related with such circumstantial detail? Cornelius himself indeed admits that Paul could not have been present at Mary's death, who came to Jerusalem around Pentecost, and shortly after was captured by the Jews in the temple and bound in chains; lest he leave anything out, he paints and adorns these charming fables with the invention of a new miracle, namely that an angel could have removed Paul from his chains for a short time, as was done for Peter, Acts XII. 7. 8. and that imperceptibly, and soon brought him back; but he did not remove Peter to bring him back, nor is there any document extant concerning Paul being removed, and who could bear those who argue from possibility to actuality in such matters? Furthermore, if all the Apostles were there, Peter was certainly present too. Why then did Paul wish to approach James, and not Peter as the Prince?

Latin:

Vers. 18. πρὸς Ἰάκωβον) Absente Petro primum Apostolici cœtus.

οἱ πρεσβύτεροι) Ut supra c. XV. 6. qui Apostolorum Hierosolymis erat, is munere fungebatur, quo postea Episcopi, ideoque presbyteros convocabat: nisi forte Iacobus hic fuit frater Domini, non Apostolus, sed Episcopus.

De fratre Domini Jacobo, qui non fuerit Apostolus, sed Episcopus, nihil novit Scriptura. Neque introducta tum adhuc fuerat Episcoporum supra Presbyteros ἐξοχὴ, de quo Cl. Salmasius sub nomine Wallonis Messalini, & Dallæus ex professo contra Papistas. Fabulatur prolixe Cornelius Lapideus, omnes Apostolos tum præsentes fuisse Hierosolymis, miraque Dei providentia convenisse ad transitum Mariæ: Paulum etiam impulsu Spiritus eo festinasse, ut ante ejus obitum ipsam salutaret, eique suas Ecclesias, suosque agones, præsertim quos Romæ cum Nerone, & Simone Mago propediem subiturus esset, commendaret, Mariam virginem triduo post obitum suum resurrexisse, & gloriosam tam in corpore, quam in anima ab Angelis, imo à Christo cum triumpho in cœlum assumtam, ibique supra omnes angelorum ordines in solia juxta Filium collocatam, cœli & terræ reginam esse coronatam. Quæ si quæratur unde habeant Papistæ, Ecclesiam obtendunt: Certum, inquit Cornelius, est, Mariam mortem obiisse, & resurrexisse, ac deinde in cælum assumtam, uti tradit Ecclesia. Sed unde id CERTUM, & à quibusnam ἀξιοπίστοις testibus habent id & reliqua, quæ tam περιστατικῶς retulit, Romano-Catholici? Fatetur utique ipse Cornelius, quod Paulus morienti Mariæ adesse non potuerit, qui sub Pentecosten Hierosolymam venit, & paulo post in templo à Judæis captus vinculis constrictus erat; ne quid lepidis illis fabellis novi miraculi commento easdem pingit, & exornat, potuisse nempe angelum Paulum è vinculis ad modicum tempus eximere, uti Petro id factum, Actor. XII. 7. 8. idque insensibiliter, & mox reducere; Sed Petrum non exemit, ut reduceret, nec de Paulo exempto ullum prostat documentum, & à posse ad esse argumentantes in talibus quis ferat? Porro, si omnes Apostoli illic fuere, præsens utique etiam fuit Petrus. Cur ergo non Petrum ceu Principem, sed Jacobum adire Paulus voluit?

## 21:19
Verse 19.

διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτῶ) See above chapter XX. 24. and the notes there.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτῶ) Vide supra cap. XX. 24. & ibi notata.

## 21:20
Vers. 20. πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσιν Ἰυδαίων) See how that mustard seed had grown within 25 years.

καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τῶ νόμυ ὑπάρχεσι) They are held by a great zeal for keeping the law, even concerning sacrifices, forbidden foods, and other things of that kind. Nor is that surprising: for the decree which the Apostles had made concerned only those called from the Gentiles. Nor had Paul yet begun to teach the Jews anything about that matter; which he did somewhat later, and indeed outside Judea. For those Jews who were χριστιανίζοντες within Judea did not perceive freedom from the burden of the law before that dispersion which happened under Hadrian, as we understand from Eusebius and Sulpicius Severus regarding those times. And the Epistle to the Hebrews was written to such people.

Although the law of Moses was already dead, and the force of the ceremonial laws, which bore the type of Christ, had ceased upon the arrival of the body, it was not yet however deadly, and thus could be observed by the Jews,

CAP. XXI. v. 16. 18. 19. 20. 21. 22. 23. 24.

provided it was not urged under the opinion of necessity. See Augustine, Epistle XIX. And when at last the destruction of the temple occurred, the use of sacrifices among Christians from the Jews vanished: indeed, for several centuries some among the Christians, especially the Nazarenes, diligently observed both ritual and other Jewish customs, as much as could be done outside the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 20. πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσιν Ἰυδαίων) Vide quo modo auctum fuerit granum illud sinapis intra annos XXV.

καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τῶ νόμυ ὑπάρχεσι) Magno studio tenentur servandæ legis, etiam de sacrificiis, de cibis vetitis, aliisque rebus ejusmodi. Nec id mirum: nam decretum quod fecerant Apostoli, tantum ex gentibus vocatos tangebat. Neque dum Paulus quicquam Iudæos ea de re docere cœperat; quod fecit aliquanto serius, & quidem extra Iudæam. Nam intra Iudæam qui erant Iudæi χριστιανίζοντες, hi ante dispersionem illam quæ per Adrianum evenit, libertatem ab legis onere, non percepere, ut intelligimus ex Eusebio & Severo Sulpitio circa illa tempora. Et ad tales scripta est Epistola ad Hebræos.

Quanquam lex Mosis jam mortua erat, & cæremonialium, quæ typum Christi gerebant, vis adventante corpore desierat, nondum tamen erat mortifera, adeoque observari à Judæis poterat,

CAP. XXI. v. 16. 18. 19. 20. 21. 22. 23. 24.

modo non sub opinione necessitatis urgeretur. Vid. Augustin. Epist. XIX. Et cum templi demum exci- dio evanuit sacrificiorum inter Christianos ex Ju- dæis usus : imo per secula aliquot nonnulli ex Christianis talibus maxime Nazaræi tam ritua- lia, quam reliqua Judaica, quantum extra tem- plum fieri potuit, diligenter observarunt.

## 21:21
Vers. 21. Κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ) They have understood this about you, namely from the speech and letters of those Jews in Asia who had caused so many troubles for Paul.
