ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάν- τας Ἰουδαίους) The Jews who were ἐν διασπορᾷ. ἀποστασία is כרה Jeremiah XXIX. 32. defection from the law 1 Maccabees II. 15.

λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα) That is, persuading them not to circumcise their children: which was a most ancient commandment, binding all the descendants of Abraham.

μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσι περιπατεῖν) ἔθη here are חקות ritual precepts: and περιπατεῖν corresponds to the Hebrew הלך as in Proverbs VIII. 20. and elsewhere. For it we shall soon have στοιχεῖν.

By apostasy is not denoted a defection to the Gentiles, nor a denial of the Messiah, or even of the law, but that under the pretext of the name of the Messiah he was derogating from the law? For apostasy is not just any defection and withdrawal, but that to which the authority of the Word of God is pretended. Compare 1 Timothy IV. 1, 2 Thessalonians II. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ) De te hoc intellexe- runt, nempe sermone & literis illorum in Asia Judæorum qui tot molestias Paulo exhibuerant.

ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάν- τας Ἰουδαίους) Judæos qui erant ἐν διασπορᾷς. ἀποστασία כרה Jerem. XXIX. 32. defectio à lege 1. Macc. II. 15.

λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα) Id est, suadens eis ne liberos circumcidant: quod antiquissimum erat præ- ceptum, omnes Abrahami posteros obstringens.

μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσι περιπατεῖν) ἔθη hic sunt חקות præcepta ritualia : & περιπατεῖν respondet Hebræo הלך ut Prov. VIII. 20. & alibi. Pro eo mox habebimus στοιχεῖν.

Per apostasiam non notatur defectio ad gentes, nec abnegatio Messiæ, aut etiam legis, sed quod obtentu nominis Messiæ legi derogaret? Apostasia enim non est defectio & recessus quivis, sed is, cui prætexitur autoritas Verbi Dei. Conf. 1. Tim. IV. 1. 2. Thess. II. 3.

## 21:22
Vers. 22. πάντως δεῖ πλῆθος συνελθεῖν) In greater matters, especially those from which a schism was feared, the Apostles and their successors the Bishops did not use the counsel of presbyters only, but also called upon the common people, as we saw above in chapter VII. 23, 30. See the Epistle of Cyprian XXXIII. XXXIV. XXXV. XL.

From these things it may be permitted to conclude that the common people are not to be excluded from sacred councils or assemblies, as is done in the Papacy.

Latin:

Vers. 22. πάντως δεῖ πλῆθος συνελθεῖν) In rebus majo- ribus, præcipue ex quibus schisma metuebatur, Apostoli & successores eorum Episcopi, non presbyterorum tantum utebantur consilio, sed & plebem advocabant, ut vidimus supra c. VII. 23. 30. Vide Epistolam Cypriani XXXIII. XXXIV. XXXV. XL.

Ex his concludere liceat, non excludendam esse plebem à sacris consiliis vel conciliis, ut in Pa- patu fit.

## 21:23
Verse 23. εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ἐφ' ἑαυτῶν) It is said in this way, because a vow is like a certain burden, as we said at Numbers chapter 6. Understand a great vow, that is, of the Nazarite.

Latin:

Vers. 23. εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ἐφ' ἑαυτῶν) Id ita dicitur, quia vo- tum est velut onus quoddam, ut ad Num. c. 6. diximus. Votum intellige magnum, id est, Nazaræatus.

## 21:24
Verse 24. ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς) ἁγνίζεσθαι in the LXX version at the aforementioned place in Numbers 6 corresponds to the verb נזר, and ἁγνισμός corresponds to the noun נזר: it signifies, however, to abstain from wine and other things which are forbidden to Nazarites. So also below in chapter XXIV. 18.

καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς) That is, do not only offer yourself what is necessary, but also give money to those others, so that they may have what they may offer: a lamb, a ewe lamb, a ram, cakes, and wafers. For we learn from Maimonides that such liberality was not unusual. James, however, wants Paul to do this, so that he may satisfy the common people more abundantly.

ἵνα ξυρήσωνται τὴν κεφαλὴν) That is, so that they may be freed from the vow all the more easily. It is a metonymy of the sign for the thing signified. For just as the votive obligation was expressed by letting the hair grow, so was the release by shaving the hair, Numbers 6:18, which hair was supposed to be burned in the pots in which the meat of the eucharistic sacrifice was cooked: for so the Hebrews teach us. We said above in chapter 18 that this law concerning victims and the shaving to be done in the temple had force in Judea, not outside of it. The custom of the Greeks of offering hair to the gods does not differ much from this, concerning which Homer, Statius in the Achilleid and the hair of Earinus, and Censorinus De Die Natali.

Cajetan and Petitus indeed think that Paul himself did not conceive a vow, but only spent money on the other four men who had conceived a Nazarite vow, so that they might fulfill it. But although Paul also made expenditures for them, by the force of this counsel, δαπάνησον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς, we nevertheless recognize that Paul joined himself to them. For this was the counsel of James, as the words clearly have it: having taken these, ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς, be sanctified with them; verse 25 does not say 'make them be sanctified,' but 'be sanctified with them': and he did this even more to confirm others, since the Apostle himself sanctified himself for the sake of the Nazarite vow, so that it might thus be openly evident that Paul also walks in such a way that he observes the law: finally, St. Luke openly testifies that the same thing was also done by Paul, verse 26. Then Paul, having taken those men, on the next day σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς, having been sanctified with them, entered into the temple, announcing the completion of the days of sanctification, until an offering should be offered for each one of them. Add to these that it is read in Acts 18:18 that he had made this vow. Which, even if some hint that it was already fulfilled in verse 22 of the same chapter should think so, yet that arose from a false interpretation, as if he were said to have gone up to Jerusalem (which we have refuted at that place). Here, therefore, at last, that vow is discharged. For others, however, he paid the expenses at the same time, both because they were poor, and so that he might also testify the more clearly that he was an observer of the law. The necessary expenses were partly for the washing and shaving of the head, or the shearing of the hair, and partly for buying and offering sacrifices by the force of the law in Num. 6:12, 14. But because some think that the Nazarites purified themselves both when they began and when they completed the Nazarite vow, when they undertook it, in order to punish luxury and purify themselves from it, this purification seems to Vatablus to have been done at the end of the vow, because victims were offered toward the end, so that the defects committed during the time of the Nazariteship might be expiated, Num. 6:14. But Sanctius prefers the view that Paul had perhaps been defiled by contact with a dead body, and was purified here from this uncleanness: since the law prescribes this purification and defines a seven-day period for it, Num. 19:11. But that Cornelius à Lapide prefers the opinion of others, which also pleased Capellus, concerning a peculiar vow of sacrificing made by Paul, must be borne as having been accepted out of a zeal for τῆς ἐθελοθρησκείας (will-worship), to which it is not likely that Paul was addicted. What Josephus relates in Book II of the Jewish War, ch. 15, concerning Berenice, has little to do with this. For there it is reported that she prayed for 30 days according to a vow before they sacrificed victims, and that she also abstained from wine and shaved her hair, having been rescued from necessities. The former opinion concerning the Nazarite vow is therefore to be preferred. For there were not only perpetual Nazarites, or those of the age, as they called them, such as Samuel and Samson, but also temporary Nazarites, who were called Nazarites of days: whose rites are described in Num. 6. Some think that something of human prudence was mixed into this counsel given to Paul. I would not easily say that of the divinely inspired James.

that all may know that those things of which they have been informed concerning you are nothing) That the rumor which has been spread about you is false, as if you were turning the Jews away from the observance of the law.

But you yourself also walk, keeping the law) Στοιχεῖν, as we just said, is here הָלַךְ, and signifies to follow some way of life.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς) ἁγνίζεσθαι in versione LXX. dicto loco Num. 6. verbo נזר, & ἁγνισμός nomini נזר re- spondet : significat autem abstinere à vino, rebusque aliis quæ interdictæ sunt Nazaræis. sic & infra c. XXIV. 18.

καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς) Id est, non ipse tantum offer, quæ oportet, sed & illis aliis dato pecunias, unde habeant, quæ offerant, agnum, agnam, arietem, placentas & lagana. Ta- lem enim liberalitatem fuisse non insolitam, ex Maimoni- de discimus. Vult autem hoc Paulum facere Jacobus, quo plebi abundantius satisfaciat.

ἵνα ξυρήσωνται τὴν κεφαλὴν) Id est, ut illi voti liberentur eo facilius. Est μετωνυμία signi pro signato. Nam sicut ob- ligatio votiva exprimebatur demisso capillo, ita liberatio coma abrasa, Num. 6. 18. quæ coma supponebatur urenda ollis, in quibus coquebantur carnes de sacro εὐχαριστικῷ: ita enim nos docent Hebræi. Diximus supra cap. 18. legem hanc de victimis & de rasura in templo facienda, vim ha- buisse in Judæa, non extra eam. Non longe abit hinc mos Græcorum comam libandi diis, de quo Homerus, Statius in Achilleide & coma Earini, & Censorinus de natali.

Cajetanus quidem & Petitus non ipsum Paulum votum concepisse, sed sumtus tantum in alios qua- tuor viros, qui votum Nazaræatus conceperant, ut id exolverent, impendisse putant. Sed quan- quam Paulus pro illis etiam sumtus fecerit, vi hujus consilii, δαπάνησον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς, sese tamen eisdem conjunxisse Paulum agnoscimus. Nam hoc erat consilium Jacobi, ut verba differte habent: his as- sumtis ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς, sanctificator cum illis v. 25. non ait sanctificari fac illos, sed sanctificator cum illis: idq; etiam magis ad confirmandum alios faciebat, cum ipse Apostolus voti Nazaræatus cau- se sa sanctificavit, ut sic palam constaret, quod nempe Paulus ita quoque incedat, ut legem ob- servet: denique idem quoque à Paulo factum esse S. Lucas aperte perhibet vers. 26. Tunc Paulus assumptis viris illis postera die σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς cum eis sanctificatus intravit in templum, denunci- ans expletionem dierum sanctificationis, donec offer- retur pro unoquoque eorum oblatio. Adde his, quod Act. XVIII. 18. legatur hoc votum fecisse. Quod etsi nonnulli jam v. 22. ibidem impletum innui censeant, id tamen ex falsa interpretatione, quasi Hierosolymam afcendisse dicatur (quam ad il- lum locum refutavimus) ortum est. Hic ergo demum votum illud exolvitur. Pro aliis vero si- mul impendit sumtus, tum quia illi pauperes fu- ere, tum ut ita quoque eo luculentius sese legis ob- servantem esse testaretur. Sumtus autem neces- sarii erant partim ad lotionem & rasuram capitis, vel tonsuram capillorum, partim ad emendas & offerendas hostias vi legis Num. VI. 12. 14. Quia au- tem purificasse sese Nazaræos nonnulli censent, & cum inchoarunt, & cum compleverunt Na- zaræatus votum, quum suscipiebant, ut castiga- rent luxum, & ab eo se purificarent, hæc purgatio Vatablo videtur in fine voti facta, quia sub finem offerebantur victimæ, ut expiarentur defectus tempore Nazaræatus commissi, Num. VI. v. 14. Sed Sanctio magis placet Paulum contactu mor- tui forte pollutum fuisse, & ab hac immunditie purificatum hic esse: siquidem hanc purifica- tionem præscribat lex, & septiduum ei definiat, Num. IV. 10. Quod autem Cornelius à Lapide aliorum sententiam, quæ etiam Capello placuit, à voto peculiari, sacrificandi, à Paulo facto, præ- fert, studio τῆς ἐθελοθρησκείας accepto feren- dum est, cui Paulo deditum fuisse non fit veri- simile. Quæ Josephus l. II. de Bell. Jud. c. 15. de Berenice refert, huc parum faciunt. Ibi enim traditur ex voto per 30. dies orasse, antequam im- molarent hostias, abstinuisse quoque à vino, & ca- pillos rasisse, qui è necessitatibus erepti fuerant. Præferenda ergo prior sententia de Nazaræatus voto. Non enim tantum erant Naziræi perpetui, vel seculi quos vocabant, qualis Samuel & Samson, sed etiam Naziræi temporarii, qui Naziræi dierum dicti sunt: quorum ritus describuntur Num. XXVI. Censent nonnulli hoc consilio Paulo dato aliquid humanæ prudentiæ admixtum fuisse. Id de Jacobo θεοπνεύστῳ facile non dixerim.

ἵν' γνῶσι πάντες, ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σῦ ὐδέν ἐστι) Falsam esse famam quæ de te sparsa est, quasi Iudæos à legis observatione averteres.

Ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς κᾲ ἀυτὸς τὸν νόμον φυλάσσων) Στοιχεῖν ut modo diximus, hic est הָלַךְ, & significat vitæ institutum aliquod persequi.

## 21:25
Verse 25. But concerning the nations who have believed) As if James were saying: The case of those called from the nations is different: For we have pronounced them free from the burden of the law by a common decree.

Deciding that they should keep no such thing) The infinitive for the gerund. That nothing of such things is to be kept by them, namely, of those things which Moses prescribed.

Except that they should keep themselves from things sacrificed to idols, and blood, and things strangled, and fornication) Above 15:20, 21:25.

Latin:

Vers. 25. Περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν) Quasi diceret Jacobus: Alia est ratio vocatorum ex gentibus: Illos enim à legis onere liberos communi decreto pronuntiavimus.

Κρίναντες μηδὲν τοιῦτον τηρεῖν ἀυτούς) Infinitivus pro Ge- rundio. Nihil tale servandum ipsis, nempe, eorum, quæ Moses præscripsit.

Εἰ μὴ φυλάσσεσθαι ἀυτὸς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον, κᾲ τὸ αἷμα, κᾲ πνικτόν, κᾲ πορνείαν) Supra XV. 20. XX. 9.

## 21:26
Verse 26.

Then Paul, taking the men) Associating himself with them.

on the next day) The day after he had arrived, as we gather below in 24:1 and 11.

announcing the completion of the days of purification) Proclaiming to all that he was undertaking purification for seven days, so that his days might end at the same time as the days of the others, who had bound themselves some time before and for a longer period. For it was permitted to everyone to set the term for his votive obligation that he wished. Num. ch. 6, v. 5. Thus Paul bound himself for a week of days: those others for two, three, or four weeks. That word ἐκπλήρωσις looks to the words of the law: 'on the day that he completes the days of his vow.' Num. ch. 6:13.

ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἀυτῶν ἡ προσφορά) This aorist signifies the thing which had to be done, until the offering was to be made for each one (of those who had bound themselves). That is, it took time in such a way that it ended concurrently with their time.

PART III. The tumult against Paul by the Jews, and his rescue by the tribune.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

Τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας) Se eis so- cians.

τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ) Postridie quam advenerat, ut colli- gimus infra XXIV. 1, & 11.

διαγγέλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ) Omni- bus edicens se castimonium suscipere in dies septem, ita ut dies ipsius pariter exirent cum diebus aliorum, qui aliquanto ante, ac in majus tempus se obligaverant. Li- cebat enim cuique eum quem vellet votivæ obligationi præstituere terminum. Num. cap. VI, v. 5. Sic Paulus in dierum hebdomada se obligavit: Illi alii in duas, tres, aut quatuor hebdomadas. Illud ἐκπλήρωσις verba legis respicit. ᾗ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ πληρώσῃ ἡμέρας ἐυχῆς ἀυτοῦ. Num. c. VI. 13.

ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἀυτῶν ἡ προσφορά) Aoristus hic significat rem quæ fieri debebat, usque dum offerenda esset pro unoquoque (eorum qui se obligarant) oblatio. Id est, ita tempus sumpsit, ut pariter cum illorum tempore defineret.

PARS III. Tumultus adversus Paulum à Iudæis, ejus- demque per tribunum ereptio.

## 21:27
Vers. 27. ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι) From this we gather, what Luke passed over in silence above, that Paul had predetermined seven days for his purification. These things are uncertain. Nor is it entirely agreed that Paul predetermined seven days for his sanctification. For some understand the end of those seven days as the end of the seven weeks from the day of the offering of the sheaf of ears of corn until the day of Pentecost: others understand these as the seven days of the feast of Pentecost; nor did Paul perform this purification over a period of seven days: because after he arrived in Jerusalem, on the very next day he visited James: who persuaded him to the purification. Therefore, on the following day, for the sake of purification, he entered the temple, v. 26, and was immediately seized there: that is, on the third day from his arrival: then on the following, that is, the fourth day, he pleaded his case in the Council, v. 30, but on the following night he was comforted by Christ, c. XXIII. v. 11, and when the morning of the fifth day came, a conspiracy was formed against him, v. 17, whence on the following night he was sent to Antipatris, v. 23, which was 17 hours distant from Jerusalem, so that he arrived there on the evening of the sixth day, and on the following or seventh day at Caesarea, being only 8 hours distant from there, c. XXIII. 32. The High Priest, however, after five days entered and accused him before the Governor, c. XXIV. 1, whence Paul, v. 11, declared there, there are not more than 12 days for me since I went up to worship in Jerusalem.

Οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι) From Ephesus and elsewhere.

Συνέχεον πάντα τ’ ὄχλον) See above XIX. 29. συνέχεον רגשו.

καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτὸν) Through sedition without public authority.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι) Hinc colligimus, quod supra tacuit Lucas, Paulum castimonio suo præfinivisse dies septem. Hæc incerta sunt. Neque omnino constat septem dies Paulum sanctificationi præfinivisse. Septem enim illorum dierum finem de septem he- bdomadum fine à die oblationis manipuli spica- rum usque ad diem Pentecostes, nonnulli acci- piunt: alii de septem diebus feritatis Pentecostes hæc intelligunt; nec per septiduum Paulus hanc puri- ficationem fecit: quia postquam appulit Jerusa- lem, die statim altero Jacobum invisit: qui purifica- tionem suasit. Postero ergo purificationis cau- sa templum ingressus, v. 26. ibi statim captus est: h. e. tertio die ab adventu suo: dehinc sequenti, h. e. quarto die causam in Concilio dixit, v. 30. nocte autem insequenti à Christo confortatus, c. XXIII. v. 11. facto mane diei quintæ conspiratio adversus eum inita, v. 17. unde sequenti nocte Anti-Patri- dem missus est, v. 23. quæ 17. horis distabat Hiero- solymis, ut ita sexto die ad vesperam ex pervene- rit, ac sequenti vel septimo die Cæsaream, utpote 8. tantum horis inde distantem, c. XXIII. 32. Pon- tifex autem post quinque dies ingressus coram Præside eum accusavit, c. XXIV. 1. unde Paulus v. 11. professus ibi est, non plus sunt mihi, quam 12. dies, ex quo ascendi adorare in Jerusalem.

Οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι) Ex Epheso & aliunde.

Συνέχεον πάντα τ’ ὄχλον) Vide supra XIX. 29. συνέχεον רגשו.

καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτὸν) Per seditionem sine publica autoritate.

## 21:28
Vers. 28.

Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται) As it was said at Rome: Furthermore, Quirites.

Βοηθεῖτε) Thus Scipio in Appian: Ἐπικουρεῖτε ὦ Ῥω- μαῖοι, help, citizens. It is in two places in Livy. And when the faith of the Quirites is implored, it signifies help and aid in the name of faith, says Servius on the 10th of the Aeneid.

ὁ κατὰ τῶ λαῶ κὶ τῶ νόμυ, κὶ τῶ τόπυ τέτυ) The same accusation that was brought against Stephen, above VI. 14, where see the remarks.

ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν) Which was clearly not allowed. See Moses of Coucy, in the commanding precept XXI, namely, within that stone partition which was raised to three cubits, and had inscribed on its columns: μὴ δεῖν ἀλλό- φυλον ἐντὸς τῶ ἁγίε παριέναι. Josephus, Jewish War V. 14, if any foreigner, even a Roman, were to cross that partition, he could be killed, as testified by the same Josephus, Jewish War VI, and Philo on the embassy.

and has defiled this holy place) By that act he polluted the temple. For that is what κοινῦν means in Matt. XV. 11, 18, 20, Mark VII. 15, and the following verses.

If the Apostle had done this against the Jewish laws, he would have confirmed more the rumor that had been spread about him, that he had forbidden the Gentiles to walk according to the ritual precepts, whereas he was actually doing this, at the admonition of James, to show openly that that rumor was false. There was an outermost court added to the temple before the court of the Jews, which it was permitted for Gentiles and the unclean to enter: but they considered it a profane place, not a sacred one. Therefore, this accusation was about the temple itself, properly so called, which consisted of the Holy of Holies, the court of the priests, and the court of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται) Ut Romæ dicebatur: Porro Qui- rites.

Βοηθεῖτε) Ita Scipio apud Appianum: Ἐπικουρεῖτε ὦ Ῥω- μαῖοι adeste cives. Est duobus locis apud Livium. Et cum fides Quiritium imploratur, opem atque auxilium fidei nomine significari, ait Servius ad X. Æneidos.

ὁ κατὰ τῶ λαῶ κὶ τῶ νόμυ, κὶ τῶ τόπυ τέτυ) Eadem accusa- tio, quæ in Stephanum intenta, supra VI. 14. ubi dicta vide.

ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν) Quod plane non licebat. Vide Mosem de Cotsi, præcepto jubente XXI. nempe intra septum illud lapideum, quod in tres cubitos attollebatur, inscriptumque columnis habebat: μὴ δεῖν ἀλλό- φυλον ἐντὸς τῶ ἁγίε παριέναι. Josephus belli Judaici V. 14. si quis alienigena, etiam Romanus, id septum transgedere- tur, is occidi poterat, teste eodem Josepho belli Judaici VI. & Philone de legatione.

καὶ κεκοίνωκε ἳ ἅγιον τόπον τῦτον) Eo facto templum pol- luit. Id enim κοινῦν Matth. XV. 11. 18. 20. Marc. VII. 15. & sequentibus.

Si hoc fecisset contra leges Judaicas Apostolus, magis confirmasset famam, quæ de ipso sparsa erat, quod gentilibus prohibuerit ambulare secundum præ- cepta ritualia qui potius id jam agebat, monitu Jacobi, ut famam illam falsam esse palam ostende- ret. Erat ad templum ante atrium Judæorum atrium extimum adjectum, quod ingredi licebat gentibus & immundis: Sed id pro loco propha- no, non pro sacro habebant. Accusatio ergo hæc fuit de templo ipso, proprie ita dicto, quod Sancto Sanctorum, atrio sacerdotum, & atrio populi constabat.

## 21:29
Vers. 29.

Trophimus the Ephesian) Whom those Asian Jews knew very well.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

Τρόφιμον ἳ Ἐφέσιον) Quem illi Judæi Asiatici optime noverant.

## 21:30
Vers. 30.

And there was a running together of the people) This word exists in Judith ch. X. verse 19, the same as συντροφὴ, above ch. XIX. v. 40. קשר.

And immediately the doors were shut) Namely by the janitors of the temple, fearing lest any sedition should arise in the temple, with some wishing to treat Paul badly, others wishing to protect him.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

Καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τῦ λαῦ) Extat hæc vox Judith cap. X. vers. 19. idem quod συντροφὴ, supra cap. XIX. v. 40. קשר.

Καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι) Nempe à janitoribus templi, metuentibus, ne qua in templo seditio orire- tur, aliis Paulum male tractare, aliis tueri volenti- bus.

## 21:31
Vers. 31.

a report went up) A judgment. The Attic writers, Isocrates, Demosthenes, and others use the word in this way: Pollux interprets it as a denunciation. Perhaps not judicium, but indicium should be read. For Φάσις denotes a report, rumor, fame, or information. This information reaches the Tribune: Vulgate, it was reported to the tribune. Camerarius, The information reached the tribune. Who is later named Lysias. The same Camerarius observes that by this name a certain forensic action at Athens was also called.

Τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης) To the commander of that cohort which, during festival times, and consequently also at Pentecost, held a garrison in the porticoes of the temple to prevent riots, if any should arise: Which cohort John also called σπεῖραν in XVIII. 3. Josephus called it Τάξιν, as we showed at Matt. ch. XXVI. 5. & 45. Tacitus calls those who were in charge of a cohort sometimes prefects, sometimes tribunes: I think they were prefects when they were in their legion, and tribunes when they were outside of it. This is to be added to what we said at John XVIII. 12.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

ἀνέβη φάσις) Judicium. Ita eam vocem usurpant At- tici, Isocrates, Demosthenes & alii: μήνυσιν interpretatur Pollux. Non judicium, sed indicium fortassis legen- dum. Φάσις enim dictum, rumorem, famam, indicium notat. Hoc indicium ascendit ad Tri- bunum: Vulgata, nunciatum est tribuno. Ca- merarius, Pervenit indicium ad tribunum. Qui postea nominatur Lysias. Alioquin hoc nomine appellatam etiam actionem quandam forensem Athenis observat idem Camerarius.

Τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης) Præfecto ejus cohortis, quæ temporibus festis, ac proinde etiam in Pentecoste, præsidium habebat in porticibus templi ad prohibendos tumultus, si qui orirentur: Quam cohortem σπεῖραν etiam Johannes dixit XVIII. 3. Τάξιν Josephus, ut ostendimus ad Matth. c. XXVI. 5. & 45. Eos, qui cohorti præerant, Tacitus modo præfectos vocat, modo tribunos: Præfectos puto, cum in legione sua erant, tribunos ubi extra eam. Hoc adden- dum eis quæ diximus ad Joh. XVIII. 12.

## 21:32
Vers. 32. Επαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον) They refrained from violence in the sight of the Roman Prefect.

Latin:

Vers. 32. Επαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον) A vi abstine- bant in conspectu Romani Præfecti.

## 21:33
Vers. 33. Ἁλύσεσι δυσί •) With two chains, by which both hands were bound, as above XII. 6. 7.

κὲ ἐπυνθάνετο, Τίς ἂν εἴη, κὲ τί ἐσι πεποιηκὼς) Both from him himself and from the crowd.

Latin:

Vers. 33. Ἁλύσεσι δυσί •) Catenis duabus, quibus manus ambæ stringerentur, ut supra XII. 6. 7.

κὲ ἐπυνθάνετο, Τίς ἂν εἴη, κὲ τί ἐσι πεποιηκὼς) Tum ex ipso, tum ex plebe.

## 21:34
Vers. 34. Μὴ δυνάμενος δὲ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸ θόρυβον, ἐκέλευσε) In the Manuscript: Μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι, which construction is also below in XXII. 17.

εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν) We said at the Maccabees that παρεμβολή is used by these writers to mean the multitude of soldiers itself. But they were all outside of festival days, and a good part of them were in the Antonia during festival days, as others and we have said.

Others translate, into the camp, like the Vulgate, Erasmus, and Beza: But neither military service nor camps are denoted: Lud. de Dieu observed that it is more correctly translated as fortress (which they otherwise call a castle or citadel) and that the Antonia citadel is understood, to which one had to ascend by ἀναβαθμὺς steps, as is held here v. 35. & 40. According to the glossary, παρεμβολὴ denotes not only a phalanx but also a fortress, as it does also according to Hesychius: and it is taken in this way also among the LXX in Is. XXI. 8. The Vulgate translates what follows here, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν, as: it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the people: See ch. XXIII. 10. Pricæus, however, because of that συνέβη, prefers it to be explained thus: Because of the excessive density of the pressing and following multitude, it happened that those whom the soldiers wanted to lead, they also had to carry.

Latin:

Vers. 34. Μὴ δυνάμενος δὲ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸ θόρυβον, ἐκέλευσε) In Manuscripto: Μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι, quæ constructio & infra est XXII. 17.

εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν) Ad Maccabaica diximus πα- ρεμβολὴν his scriptoribus dici, ipsam militum multitudi- nem. Ea autem extra dies festos omnes, in diebus festis bona pars, erant in Antonia, ut & alii, & nos diximus.

Alii reddunt, in castra, ut Vulgatus, Erasmus, & Beza: Sed nec militiæ, nec castra notantur: re- ctius autem verti castrum observavit Lud. de Dieu (quod alias castellum vel arcem vocant) & intel- ligi arcem Antoniam, ad quam per ἀναβαθμὺς gra- dus adscendendum erat, ut hic v. 35. & 40. habe- tur. Secundum glossarium παρεμβολὴ non pha- langem tantum, sed & castrum notat, ut & secun- dum Hesychium: atque ita accipitur etiam apud LXX. Es. XXI. 8. Quæ sequuntur hic συνέβη βασ- τάζεσθαι αὐτὸν Vulgata reddit, contigit ut portare- tur a militibus propter vim populi: Vid. c. XXIII. 10. Pricæus tamen propter illud συνέβη mavult ita exponi: Propter nimiam urgentis insequentisque multitudinis densitatem evenit, ut quem milites du- cere volebant, etiam portarent eum.

## 21:35
Vers. 35. Ἐπὶ τὺς ἀναβαθμὺς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ βίαν τῦ ὄχλυ) Cicero to Atticus: The steps of the temples were filled by the lowest rabble. The same man, in his speech for Cluentius, narrates that the steps were filled with agitated men.

Latin:

Vers. 35. Ἐπὶ τὺς ἀναβαθμὺς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ βίαν τῦ ὄχλυ) Cicero ad Atticum: Gradus templorum ab infima plebe completi erant. Idem pro Cluentio, gradus concitatis hominibus completos narrat.

## 21:37
Vers. 37. Εἰ ἔξεσί μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρός σε) A preface full of honor. Thus in Livy: With your good leave, I ask, may you listen, Conscript Fathers.

Ἑλληνισὶ γινώσκεις) A shortened expression: for λαλεῖν is understood. The full expression exists in Nehemiah XIII. 24. κὲ ὐκ εἰσὶν ἐπιγινώσκοντες λαλεῖν Ἰεδαϊστί. The Greek language after the empire of the Macedonians had become as it were the common language of the peoples of Asia and Egypt: See what we said at Matt. ch. XXVII. 37.

Latin:

Vers. 37. Εἰ ἔξεσί μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρός σε) Plena honoris præfatio. Sic apud Livium: Cum bona venia, quæso, au- diatis, Patres conscripti.

Ἑλληνισὶ γινώσκεις) Curtata locutio: subauditur enim λαλεῖν. Plena locutio exstat Nehemiæ XIII. 24. κὲ ὐκ εἰσὶν ἐπιγινώσκοντες λαλεῖν Ἰεδαϊστί. Lingua Græca post Macedonum imperium facta erat quasi communis po- pulorum Asiæ & Ægypti: Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. c. XXVII. 37.

## 21:38
ὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος) These things show that these events took place under the reign of Nero. For there is no doubt that the Egyptian of whom it is treated here is the one of whom Josephus writes in Antiquities XX. 6. and Jewish War II. 23. This Egyptian called himself a Prophet.

ἀνασατώσας) See above XVII. 6.

εἰς τὴν ἔρημον) For those recruiters were accustomed to make the beginnings of gathering an armed multitude in desert places, as we said at Matt. XXIV. 26. Josephus, Antiquities XX. 6: 'they persuaded them to follow them into the wilderness.'

τὺς τετρακισχιλίυς ἄνδρας) These, as I said, were the beginnings of that scoundrel. After the multitude had grown for him to thirty thousand, he proceeded from the desert places to the Mount of Olives, and there his forces were scattered by Felix. But these things are later than those which are narrated here, and can be read in Josephus, Jewish War II. 23.

τῶν σικαρίων) Thus also Josephus calls those men who were already taking up arms in a public place without orders: concerning which matter we spoke at Matt. XXVII. 16 and 38.

Drusius derives the name σικάριος from sica, and observes that it has an affinity with the Hebrew סכין denoting a knife; and because some maintain that these sicarii were from the followers of Judas the Galilean, others that they were Essenes, with Theophylact; whom he himself does not deny. It can happen, he says, that some from this sect were sicarii. For the Essenes fought most fiercely against the Romans, and to avoid calling Caesar Lord, they endured the most bitter tortures, indeed they did not hesitate to pour out their life and meet death, because they said it was right that the Lord alone should rule over men; and that no one else should be called Lord, except God the blessed. Moreover, the author of this sect of the Essenes was Judas the Galilean himself, the Salmantican records in the book Juchasin, ch. CXXXIX, whom he calls Nazirites, that is, holy, and Hasideans, that is, pious. Josephus, however, is the author that the followers of Judas, except for the fact that they called no mortal Lord, were in other respects Pharisees.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος) Hæc ostendunt gesta hæc sub Neronis imperio. Neque enim dubitandum quin Ægyptius de quo hic agitur, sit ille de quo Josephus veteris historiæ XX. 6. & belli Judaici II. 23. hic Ægyptius Prophetam se dicebat.

ἀνασατώσας) Vide supra XVII. 6.

εἰς τὴν ἔρημον) Solebant enim impositores illi initia col- ligendæ multitudinis armatæ facere in locis desertis, ut di- ximus ad Matth. XXIV. 26. Josephus antiquæ historiæ XX. 6. ἔπειθον αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἐρημίαν ἕπεσθαι.

τὺς τετρακισχιλίυς ἄνδρας) Hæc, ut dixi, nebulonis illius initia fuere. Postquam multitudo illi ad triginta millia creverat, ex locis desertis ad Olivarum montem processit, ibique copiæ ejus per Felicem dissipatæ sunt. Sed hæc iis, quæ hic narrantur, seriora sunt, legique possunt apud Jose- phum belli Judaici II. 23.

τῶν σικαρίων) Sic & Josephus vocat indicatio jamjam loco illos homines publico injussu arma capientes: qua de re diximus ad Matth. XXVII. 16. & 38.

Nomen σικάριος à sica deducit Drusius, & af- finitatem habere cum Ebræo סכין cultrum deno- tante observat; & quod sicarios hosce nonnulli è sectatoribus Judæ Galilæi, alii Hesseos fuisse, cum Theophylacto statuant; quibus ipse non abnuit. Potest, inquit, fieri, ut aliqui ex hac secta sicarii fuerint. Nam Hessei contra Romanos acerrime dimi- cabant, & ne Cæsarem & Dominum dicerent, acer- bissimos cruciatus tolerabant, imo vitam profunde- re mortemque oppetere non dubitabant, quia æquum esse ajebant, ut super homines solus Dominus domi- netur; nec alium esse vocandum Dominum, quam Deum benedictum. Cæterum hujus Essenorum sectæ autorem fuisse ipsummet Judam Galilæum Salmanticensis tradit libro Jochas. c. CXXXIX. i. quos Naziræos appellat, id est, sanctos, & Hasidæos, id est, pios. Josephus vero autor est Judæ sectato- res excepto eo, quod neminem mortalium Domi- num appellarent, cætera Pharisæos fuisse.

## 21:39
Verse 39.

Ἰουδαῖος Ταρσεὺς) Born at Tarsus; a Jew by birth. τῆς Κιλικίας ὀυκ ἀσήμου πόλεως) Nay, rather ἐπισημοτάτης, as Stephanus speaks of it. Correctly. For it was the capital of all Cilicia, according to Strabo, founded by Perseus, as Lucan wishes, or by heroes, or giants, as others in Dio Chrysostom: but then it became a free city, of which we shall speak below at XXII. 28.

For it was the metropolis of Cilicia, and it is called Tarsus of Cilicia for the sake of distinction, because there was also a Tarsus in Bithynia, and another in Judea. It is believed to have received its name from Tarshish, son of Javan, grandson of Japheth, son of Noah, Gen. X. It was situated 76 miles from Jerusalem towards the North, founded by Perseus, King of the Persians, according to Strabo book XIV, and restored by the Assyrian King Sardanapalus; it is washed by the river Cydnus: after Alexander the Great approached it, and saved the same city from a fire when the Persians had set it ablaze, and defeated the last Darius in battle, that city grew in a wonderful manner, and there was in it a famous Gymnasium, whose philosophers surpassed even the Athenians and Alexandrians, from which Paul was afterwards sent to the Jerusalem Academy, and there heard Gamaliel. The citizens of Tarsus were indeed preferred to other nations on account of their learning in Rome and in all other places, whence also the Tarsians were gifted with Roman citizenship, by which name the Apostle professed himself a Roman by right, Acts XXII. Now Tarsus, subject to the Turkish Emperor, is named Terassa.

“Permit me to speak to the people.” He did not prudently address the people unless authority had been received, lest he be thought to be inciting a sedition. See below XXVI. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

Ἰουδαῖος Ταρσεὺς) Natus Tarsi; ortu Judæus. τῆς Κιλικίας ὀυκ ἀσήμου πόλεως) Imo ἐπισημοτάτης, ut de ea loquitur Stephanus. Recte. Erat enim Ciliciæ totius caput, teste Strabone, condita à Perseo, ut Lucanus vult, ab heroibus, aut gigantibus, ut alii apud Dionem Chrysosto- mum: Tum vero facta urbs libera, de quo dicemus infra XXII. 28.

Erat enim Ciliciæ Metropolis, & Tarsus Cili- ciæ distinctionis gratia dicitur, quia erat & Tarsus in Bithynia, in alia in Judæa. Nomen accepisse creditur à Tharsis filio Javan nepote Japheti filii Noæ, Gen. X. Sita fuit 76. miliaribus ab Hierso- lymis versus Boream, condita à Perseo Persarum Rege juxta Strabonem l. XIV. & ab Assyriorum Re- ge Sardanapalo instaurata Cydno amni alluitur: postquam Alexander M. ad eam accessit, eandem- que, quum Persæ ignem subjecissent urbi, ab in- cendio conservavit, ac Darium ultimum prælio superavit, mirum in modum urbs illa crevit, fuitq; in eadem Gymnasium celebre, cujus Philosophi ipsos Athenienses & Alexandrinos superarant, ex quo postmodum Paulus in Academiam Hierosoly- mitanam missus fuit, ibique Gamalielem audivit. Tarsenses sane cives propter eruditionem Romæ & in aliis locis omnibus, aliis nationibus prælati sunt, unde & Tarsenses civitate Romana donati, quo nomine Apostolus se Romanum jure profes- sus est, Act. XXII. Jam Tarsus Turcico Imperatori subjecta Terassa nominatur.

Ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν) Prudenter popu- lum alloquutus non est, nisi accepta potestate, ne seditio- nem accendere crederetur. Vide infra XXVI. 1.

## 21:40
Vers. 40.

“On the stairs.” On the steps of the Antonia, concerning which see above 35. “He beckoned with his hand to the people.” See above XII. 17. XIII. 16. XIX. 33. “And when there was a great silence.”

They all fell silent, and held their faces intent.

Vers. 41.

“In the Hebrew dialect.” That is, the Jerusalem language, for the most part Syriac, which the Jews used at that time. Thus Luke used “dialect,” and above ch. I. v. 19, ch. II. v. 6, 8. In the manuscript it is “in their own dialect,” as above ch. I. v. 19, ch. II. v. 6, 8.

But that language, as Walaeus says from Salmasius, does not seem to have been unknown at that time, not even to the Jews who lived among the nations. For since many were accustomed to come to Jerusalem every year for the major solemnities, they used to learn the language which was in use in that city, which was the metropolis of all the Jews residing everywhere. Furthermore, very many of those Jews whom Paul is said in Acts XXI to have addressed τῇ ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ, are said to have come there from Asia. For they too stirred up a sedition of the Jerusalemite people against Paul, as is mentioned in the same chapter, v. 27.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

Ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν) In gradibus Antoniæ, de quibus su- pra 35. κατέσεισε τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ) Vide supra XII. 17. XIII. 16. XIX. 33. πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης)

Conticuere omnes, intentique ora tenebant.

Vers. 41.

τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ) Id est, lingua Hierosolymitana, magna ex parte Syriaca, qua tum Judæi utebantur. Sic διάλεκτον posuit Lucas, & supra c. I. v. XIX. c. II. v. 6. 8. In Manuscripto est τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ, ut supra c. I. v. 19. c. II. v. 6. 8.

Illa vero lingua, ut è Salmasio Walæus, non vi- detur eo tempore ignorata, ne Judæis quidem qui inter gentes habitabant. Cum enim in ma- joribus solemnitatibus ventitare quotannis plu- res solerent Hierosolymam, eam linguam addisce- bant, quæ usitata erat in ea civitate, quæ omnium ubique consistentium Judæorum fuit Metropolis. Praeterea plurimi ex illis Judaeis quos XXI. Actuum dicitur alloquutus Paulus τῇ ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ, ex Asia eo dicuntur venisse. Nam & ii contra Pau- lum seditionem populi Hierosolymitani excita- runt, ut in eodem capite memoratur, v. 27.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

Paul's speech to the Jews in Hebrew, in which he explained his origin, education, zeal for the law, persecution of Christians, conversion on the Damascus road, baptism received from Ananias, and also the appearance of Jesus in the temple, with his mission to the Gentiles. The Jews become tumultuous and shout that he should be taken from the earth. But he is led away by the tribune into the barracks, who, when he ordered him to be bound and scourged, understanding him to be a Roman citizen, released him from his bonds, and having summoned the priests, produced Paul before them.

There are two parts: I. Paul's speech delivered to the people concerning his conversion and mission, to v. 21. II. The tumult of the Jews against Paul, and his abduction into the barracks with his binding and the loosening of his bonds, to v. 30.

PART I. Paul's speech delivered to the people.

Vers. 1. ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ κὶ πατέρες) See above VII. and what is said there. He adds the name of fathers, in case any of the Senators were present.

τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νῦν ἀπολογίας) ἀπολογία will be correctly called a defense with Cicero. It is also a defense where the deed is denied. Purgation is a species of it, where the deed being admitted, the blame is removed. The Latin interpreter here is not bad: I render an account. In the Glossary ἀπολογῆμαι I render an account.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Oratio Pauli ad Judaeos Ebraea, qua exposuit ortum, educationem, zelum pro lege, per- secutionem Christianorum, conversionem in via Damascena, baptismum ab Anania acceptum, nec non apparitionem Jesu in templo, cum missione ad gentes. Judaei tumultuantur, & clamant, ut de terra tollatur. Sed abducitur à tribuno in ca- stra, qui cum ipsum ligari juberet, & fla- gellari, intelligens eum civem Romanum esse, solvit ipsum à vinculis, & advoca- tis sacerdotibus Paulum coram illis pro- duxit.

Partes duae sunt: I. Oratio Pauli ad populum habita de sui conversione & missione, ad v. 21. II. Tumultuatio Judaeorum adversus Paulum, & ab- ductio ejus in castra cum ligatione & vinculorum solutione, ad v. 30.

PARS I. Oratio Pauli ad populum habita.

Vers. 1. ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ κὶ πατέρες) Vide supra VII. & ibi dicta. Patrum nomen addit, si qui forte Senatorum ad- essent.

τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νῦν ἀπολογίας) ἀπολογία recte cum Cice- rone dicetur defensio. Defensio est etiam, ubi factum ne- gatur. Purgatio ejus est species, ubi facto concesso, culpa removetur. Latinus interpres hic non male: reddo ratio- nem. In Glossario ἀπολογῆμαι rationem reddo.

## 22:2
Vers. 2. Παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν) They made silence. Thus Plautus speaks.

Latin:

Vers. 2. Παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν) Fecere silentium. Ita loqui- tur Plautus.

## 22:3
Vers. 3. ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ) Where the principal seat of the studies of the law was.

παρὰ τὺς πόδας Γαμαλιὴλ) Of him about whom see above V. 34. He says at the feet, because disciples sat much lower than the Masters: those were nearest to the master whose progress was greatest. See Deut. xxxiii. 3. and Philo on the Essenes. The writer of the Commentaries which bear the name of Ambrose on the first to the Corinthians: This is the tradition of the Synagogue, that they dispute while sitting, the seniors in dignity on chairs, those following on benches, the most noble on the pavement on mats. Therefore, what is in the Talmudic title מגילה that until the times of Gamaliel they learned the law standing, interpret as that all stood while the words of the law themselves were being read. See what is on Luke IV. 20.

Petitus disputes against Scaliger, asserting that disciples cast upon the ground devoted effort to their teachers: because at that time they were not cast upon the ground, but were taught by their teachers while standing. He wishes, however, that Paul was in Gamaliel's company, reclining with him on a couch, and that he sat at his feet, and that this is signified here. But Scaliger's opinion is undoubtedly to be preferred. Conf. Deut. XXXIII. 3. Luke X. 39. But what is asserted about the disciples standing is correctly explained here by Grotius.

Πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τῦ πατρῴυ νόμυ) According to the more exquisite sect. Thus below xxvi. 5. κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεσάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας. Joseph. Jewish War I. 4. On the Pharisees: Τάγμα τι Ἰυδαίων δοκῦν εὐσεβέσερον εἶναι τῶν ἄλλων, κὶ τὺς νόμυς ἀκριβέσερον ἀ φηγεῖσθ. The same in Antiquities XVII. 3. ἧν γὰρ μόριόν τι ἸυδαΪκῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπ’ ἀκριβώσει μέγα φρονῦν τῶ πατρίων νόμων, οἷς χαίρειν τὸ θεῖον προσποιημένων ὑπῆκτο ἡ γυ- ναικωνῖτις. Φαρισαῖοι καλῦνται. And in his life: Τῆς δὲ Φαρισαίων αἱρέσεως, οἳ περὶ τὰ πάτρια, νόμιμα δοκῦσι τῶ ἄλλων ἀκριβείᾳ διαφέρειν.

Being a zealot for God) From Num. XXV. 13. The Pharisees indeed had the zeal of Phinehas, but not joined with the knowledge of the truth, Rom. X, 2,

Latin:

Vers. 3. ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ) Ubi praecipua sedes studio- rum legis.

παρὰ τὺς πόδας Γαμαλιὴλ) Ejus de quo supra V. 34. Ad pedes dicit, ideo quod discipuli sedebant multum infra Magistros: proximi vero magistro ii quorum maxime pro- fectus. Vide Deut. xxxiii. 3. & Philonem de Essenis. Scriptor Commentariorum quae nomen praeferunt Ambrosii ad pri- mam ad Corinthios: Haec traditio Synagoga est, ut sedentes dis- putent, seniores dignitate in Cathedris, sequentes in subselliis no- bilssimi in pavimento super mattas. Quod igitur est in Thal- mudicis titulo מגילה ad tempora Gamalielis stantes didicisse legem, interpretare stetisse omnes, dum ipsa legis verba legebantur. Vide quae ad Lucam IV. 20.

Disputat Petitus adversus Scaligerum, discipu- los projectos in solum operam dedisse praeceptori- bus asserentem: quod tunc temporis non in solo projecti, sed stantes à praeceptoribus eruditi fu- erint. Vult autem in Gamalielis contubernio fuisse Paulum eodem cum ipso accumbentem in le- ctulo, ad ejus pedes assedisse, idque hic significari. Sed praeferenda sine dubio Scaligeri sententia. Conf. Deut. XXXIII. 3. Luc. X. 39. Quod vero de discipulis stantibus adseritur, recte à Grotio hic expeditum.

Πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τῦ πατρῴυ νόμυ) Secundum sectam exquisitiorem. Sic infra xxvi. 5. κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεσάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας. Joseph. belli Judaici I. 4. Pha- risaeis: Τάγμα τι Ἰυδαίων δοκῦν εὐσεβέσερον εἶναι τῶν ἄλλων, κὶ τὺς νόμυς ἀκριβέσερον ἀ φηγεῖσθ. Idem veteris historicae XVII. 3. ἧν γὰρ μόριόν τι ἸυδαΪκῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπ’ ἀκριβώσει μέγα φρονῦν τῶ πατρίων νόμων, οἷς χαίρειν τὸ θεῖον προσποιημένων ὑπῆκτο ἡ γυ- ναικωνῖτις. Φαρισαῖοι καλῦνται. Et in sua vita: Τῆς δὲ Φαρισαίων αἱρέσεως, οἳ περὶ τὰ πάτρια, νόμιμα δοκῦσι τῶ ἄλλων ἀκριβείᾳ διαφέρειν.

Ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τῦ Θεῦ) Ex Num. XXV. 13. Habebant quidem Pharisaei ζῦλον Phineae, sed non cum veri scientia conjunctum, Rom. X, 2,

## 22:4
Vers. 4. Who this way) This sect. See above c. XVII. 17. XIX. 9. 23. I persecuted unto death) As much, to wit, as was in me. delivering into prisons both men and women) See above IX. 1. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν) Sectam hanc. Vide supra c. XVII. 17. XIX. 9. 23. ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου) Quantum scil. in me erat. παραδιδούς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας) Vide supra IX. 1. 2.

## 22:5
Vers. 5. As also the high priest bears witness to me, and all the presbytery) That is, the great Sanhedrin. See what was said on the said chapter IX. to the brethren) Thus he here calls the Jews from their common origin from Jacob. that they might be punished) That they might be beaten with rods.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι, καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον) Id est Synedrium magnum. Vide quæ dicta ad dictum caput IX. πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς) Ita hic vocat Judæos ab communem ex Jacobo originem. ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν) Ut verberibus cæderentur.

## 22:7
Vers. 7. And I fell to the ground) In Hebrew ארצה which is accustomed to be rendered χαμαὶ.

Latin:

Vers. 7. Ἔπεσόν τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος) Hebraice ארצה quod χαμαὶ reddi solet.

## 22:9
Vers. 9. But they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me) Namely, distinctly. They heard a confused sound, not the words themselves: As we said above IX. 7. Surely he who hears in this way, he hears indeed, but because he does not understand what he hears, he is like one not hearing. Capellus notes that ἤκουσαν here signifies to understand, not indeed to hear, because Christ spoke to Paul in Hebrew c. XXVI. 14, which language his companions might perhaps not have been ignorant of. But the former explanation is more likely.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι) Nempe distincte. Sonum confusum audiebant, non ipsa verba: Sicut diximus supra IX. 7. Nimirum qui ita audit, is audit quidem, sed quia quod audit non intelligit, similis est non audienti. Capellus monet ἤκουσαν hic significare intelligere, non vero audire, quia Christus Paulum Ebraice allocutus c. XXVI. 14. quam linguam forte comites ejus non ignorarint. Sed verisimilior est prior explicatio.

## 22:10
Vers. 10. which are appointed for you to do) Which are commanded to you by me, that you may do them. Above IX. 7. what you must do.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι) Quæ à me tibi imperantur, ut facias. Supra IX. 7. τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.

## 22:11
Vers. 11. From the glory of the light) Δόξα כבוד signifies a certain excellent brightness above VII. 55. 2. Cor. III. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς) Δόξα כבוד eximium quemdam fulgorem significat supra VII. 55. 2. Cor. III. 7.

## 22:12
Vers. 12. A devout man according to the law.) Pious not in any way whatsoever, but also according to the prescriptions of our law, as Zacharias & Elizabeth. This pertains much to the matter which was being discussed. In the Manuscript there is only ἀνὴρ κατὰ τὸν νόμον, a man conforming to the law. by all those dwelling) Namely at Damascus.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Ἀνὴρ εὐσεβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον.) Pius non quovis modo, sed etiam secundum legis nostræ præscripta, ut Zacharias & Elizabet. Hoc multum pertinet ad rem, de qua agebatur. In Manuscripto tantum est ἀνὴρ κατὰ τὸν νόμον, vir legi congruens. ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων) Nempe Damasci.

## 22:13
Vers. 13. And standing over) As Luc. IV. 39. He stood above, so that he might lay hands on him, just as was narrated in the said chapter IX.

Latin:

Vers. 13. Καὶ ἐπιστὰς) Ut Luc. IV. 39. Stabat superior, ut manus ei imponeret, quemadmodum narratum dicto capite IX.

## 22:14
Vers. 14. But he said) Referring, to wit, to the vision which had divinely happened to him. the God of our fathers) And this is apposite, lest he be believed to teach a defection from the God of Abraham, Isaac & Jacob. has chosen you to know) So also below XXVI. 16. you have προχειρίζεσθαι for שלח Exodus IV. 13. for לקח Jos. III. v. 2. In the same sense we had προκεχειροτονεῖν above X. 41. to see the Just One) That Jesus who is supremely innocent and good, I. Ioh. II. 1. III. 7. The Vulgate is wrong, [saying] he foreordained you, as if it were προεκυρώσατο. Grotius therefore rightly departs from it. Properly προχειρίζεσθαι is to take into one's hands that which you wish to use, Jos. III. 12. 2. Macc. III. 7. Cornelius à Lapide praises some who translate, God made you ready, that you might be πρόχειρος to him, that is, at hand and ready and prepared to evangelize through the whole world. For it is πρόχειρον, says Camerarius, almost that which is said in Latin, in promptu (at hand). Polybius in the first book: there are among the Romans in all four camps, which they prepare each year. There are four whole legions among the Romans, which they prepare each year.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν) Referens scilicet visum quod sibi divinitus obtigerat. ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν) Et hoc apposite, ne crederetur à Deo Abrahami, Isaaci & Jacobi defectionem docere. προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι) Sic & infra XXVI. 16. προχειρίζεσθαι habes pro שלח Exodi IV. 13. pro לקח Jos. III. v. 2. Eodem sensu habuimus προκεχειροτονεῖν supra X. 41. ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον) Jesum illum summe innocentem ac bonum, I. Ioh. II. 1. III. 7. Male Vulgatus, præordinavit te, quasi esset προεκυρώσατο. Merito ergo ab eo abit Grotius. Proprie προχειρίζεσθαι est præmanibus sumere id quo uti velis, Jos. III. 12. 2. Macc. III. 7. Cornelius à Lapide laudat nonnullos, qui vertunt, expedivit te Deus, ut esses ipsi πρόχειρος, id est, ad manum promptus & expeditus ad evangelizandum per totum orbem. Est enim πρόχειρον, inquit Camerarius, id ferme, quod Latine dicitur, in promptu. Polybius libro primo: ἐστὶ δὲ παρὰ Ῥωμαίοις τὰ πάντα τέτταρα στρατόπεδα, ἃ κατ᾽ ἐνιαυτὸν προχειρίζονται. Sunt legiones universæ quatuor apud Romanos, quas singulis annis illi expediunt.

## 22:16
Vers. 16. And wash away your sins) To faith, and the profession of faith, which is made through baptism, joined together, the remission of sins is promised. See Mark XVI. 16. Just as washing makes it so that stains do not appear, so remission [makes it so that] sins [do not appear], Es. c. I. 18. Remission of sins is not attributed here to faith, (although it belongs to it entirely as a medium on our part as the grasping [instrument]) but to Baptism, as a medium on the part of God & divine giving is the washing from sins ascribed: because through baptism we are not cleansed in body, but we are washed in soul, which was ordained not for the filth of the body, but for the filth of the soul, 1. Petr. III. 21. Those analogies, therefore, that absolution causes stains not to appear, and remission causes sins not to appear, are not to the point here: for baptism was by no means ordained for the sake of washing the body, as Peter teaches; whence it has been customary for it to be performed no less by sprinkling than by immersion, and as regeneration and the remission of sins are attributed to the true Sacrament of baptism, so also is the washing away of sins: because God through this medium washes us by the hands of the minister.

wills, and to cleanse from sins, Acts II. 38. Eph. V. 26. Tim. III. 5.

calling upon the name of the Lord) In that Manuscript, and others: his name. Just as the Syrian also reads. Others refer this to Jesus: I, more correctly, to God the Father. For demonstratives and relatives often refer to something more remote. For the reason why I think so, see what we have said on Matt. chap. XXVIII. verse 19, where we deal with prayers in baptism.

But why should we not believe that the Lord Jesus is designated by the name or relative pronoun of the Lord? The reason brought forward by Grotius on Matt. XXIX. 19 is nothing that pertains to this. He taught there that the profession of the Holy Trinity was accustomed to be made in baptism: but not that Christ was not invoked in baptism, but the Father alone. Volkelius, the Socinian himself, acknowledged in lib. IV. de Ver. Rel. p. 224, that Christ is denoted by this 'Lord' in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 16. Καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου) Fidei, & professioni fidei, quæ per baptismum fit, simul conjunctis, promittitur remissio peccatorum. Vide Marci XVI. 16. Sicut ablutio facit ne maculæ appareant, ita remissio ne peccata, Es. c. I. 18. Non fidei hic tribuitur remissio peccatorum, (etsi ei eadem ceu medio ex parte nostri ἀντιληπτικῷ omnino conveniat) sed Baptismo, ceu medio ex parte Dei & δόσεως divinæ adscribitur ablutio à peccatis: quia per baptismum non mundamur corpore, sed abluimur anima, qui utiq; non ob corporis, sed ob animæ sordes ordinatus est, 1. Petr. III. 21. Illæ itaque analogia, quod absolutio faciat ne maculæ appareant, remissio ne peccata, huc non facit: nam baptismus corporis lavandi ergo nullatenus sanctitus est, docente Petro; unde peragi consuevit non minus aspersione, quam tinctione, & veri baptis̃matis Sacramento uti regeneratio & remissio peccatorum tribuitur, ita & ablutio à peccatis: quia Deus per hoc medium nos abluere per manus ministri

vult, & purgare à peccatis, Ač. II. 38. Eph. V. 26. Tim. III. 5.

ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα τῦ Κυρίε) In Manuscripto illo, & aliis: τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῦ. Quomodo & Syrus legit. Id alii ad Jesum referunt: ego rectius ad Deum Patrem. Sæ- pe enim demonstrativa, & relativa respiciunt aliquid remo- tius. Cur ita censeam causam vide in iis, quæ diximus ad Matth. cap. XXVIII. vers. 19. ubi agimus de precibus in baptismo.

Cur vero non τῦ Κυρίε nomine vel pronomine relativo credamus Dominum Jesum proxime no- minatum designari? Ratio ad Matth. XXIX. 19. adducta nulla à Grotio est; quæ huc faciat. Pro- fessionem S. Trinitatis in baptismo fieri solitam ibi docuit: non autem non invocatum fuisse in baptismo Christum, sed Patrem solum. Agnovit Volkelius ipse Socinianus l. IV. de Ver. Rel. p. 224. per Κύριον hoc loco Christum notari.

## 22:17
Vers. 17. And while I was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance) This is one of the revelations of which he treats in 2 Cor. ch. XII. 1. Moreover, the construction is such as above XXI. 34, for the correct speech would have been: And while I was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance.

Latin:

Vers. 17. καὶ προσευχομένω μοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει) Hæc est una revelationum de quibus agit 2. Cor. c. XII. 1. Est autem constructio, qualis supra XXI. 34. rectus enim sermo fuerat. Καὶ προσευχομένῳ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι ἐν ἐκστάσει.

## 22:18
Vers. 18. And to see him) The angel in place of Christ, as in the old [testament] to sit in place of God. See above IX. 10. XVIII. 9.

That Christ is said to have been seen when an angel was seen is unusual, nor can it be proven from the Scriptures by any example: just as it is nowhere observed in the O.T. that the Lord or Jehovah is said to have been seen when some created angel appeared. Nor would anything arise from that other than a confusion of persons, of Lord and servant, or of minister, and of the principal and instrumental cause. Concerning which, more in Theol. Nat. & revel. against the Socinians, who evade [the issue] with a similar fiction of a 'logophany' or apparition of the Son of God.

get out quickly from Jerusalem) It is tacitly understood here, 'and preached by another.' For Paul responds to that.

because they will not receive your testimony concerning me) As if the Lord were saying: those who are curable have already been cured: the others have now hardened, whom their own punishment awaits. See above IX. 29.

Latin:

Vers. 18. Καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν) Angelum vice Christi, ut in veteri sedere Dei vice. Vide supra IX. 10. XVIII. 9.

Christum dici visum, cum Angelus visus est, in- solens est, nec è Scripturis probari exemplo ullo potest: quemadmodum nec id uspiam in V. T. observatur, Dominum vel Jehovam visum dici, cum apparuit Angelus aliquis creatus. Nec aliud inde oriretur, quam confusio personarum, Do- mini & servi, vel ministri, causæque principalis & instrumentalis. Quo de in Theol. Nat. & revel. plura adversus Socinianos, simili commento λο- γοφανείας vel apparitione Filii Dei eludentes.

ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἱερουσαλὴμ) Tacite hic subintelligitur, & ab alio prædicatum. Nam ad id respondet Paulus.

διότι ὐ παραδέξονταί σε τὴν μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμῦ) Quasi dicat Dominus: sanabiles qui sunt, jam sanati sunt: cæ- teri jam obduruere, quos sua pœna exspectat. Vid. supra IX. 29.

## 22:19
Vers. 19. And I said: Lord, they themselves know) As if what the Lord had said were not to be understood universally. Paul shows that he had some hope that the Jerusalemites, who had known him for a long time, could not attribute such a great change to anything but a great and powerful cause,

Thus also Camerarius and others accept what is said here by the Apostle, as if he were showing by his response that he hoped the Jews would not reject his testimony, who knew him, and knew that the Jewish religion was most familiar to him, and asserted by him with the greatest zeal, so that he would not bring forward a different opinion and doctrine without a grave cause. Lyranus and Dionysius the Carthusian similarly accepted it in this way. We do not disapprove. Paul mentions this to the Jews to declare to them the supreme love with which he desired to remain among them and to preach to them. That therefore he went to the Gentiles having left them, he was compelled not by his own wish, but by the command of God.

I was imprisoning) I was putting into prison: This word exists in the Batrachomyomachia, likewise Wisdom XVIII. 4.

and beating in the synagogues those who believe in you) By the order of the Sanhedrin, to which that coercion was permitted within Judea and certain neighboring regions. See above IX. 2. and below XXVI. 11. and what we have said on Matt. X. 17.

Latin:

Vers. 19. Κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε αὐτοὶ ἐπίσανται) Quasi non universaliter intelligendum esset, quod Dominus dixe- rat. Ostendit Paulus sibi non nihil esse spei, quod Hieroso- lymitæ qui se pridem novissent, tantam mutationem non possent nisi magnæ viræque causæ attribuere,

Sic etiam Camerarius & alii dictum ab Apo- stolo hic accipiunt, quasi respondendo ostende- ret, se sperare Judæos non repudiaturos suum testi- monium, qui ipsum nossent, & scirent Judaicam religionem ei esse notissimam, & maximo studio ab illo assertam, ut non absque gravi causa diver- sam sententiam, doctrinamque afferret. Lyranus & Dionysius Carthuf. similiter ita acceperunt. Non improbamus. Commemorat hoc Judæis Paulus, ut eis declaret summum amorem, quo apud eos cupivit manere, iisque prædicare. Quod ergo iis relictis ad gentes iverit, non ex suo voto, sed Dei jussu compulsum fuisse.

ἤμην φυλακίζων) In carcerem dabam: Extat hoc verbum in βατραχομυομαχια item Sapient. XVIII. 4.

κὴ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τὺς πισεύοντας ἐπὶ σε) Ex jussu Synedrii, cui ea coercitio permissa intra judæam, & regio- nes quasdam vicinas. Vide supra IX. 2. & infra XXVI. 11. & quæ diximus ad Matth. X. 17.

## 22:20
Vers. 20. And consenting unto his death) The very words which we had above VIII. 1.

and keeping the raiment of them that slew him) Namely of the witnesses, who were the first to stone. See above chap. VII. v. 58.

Latin:

Vers. 20. Καὶ συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτῦ) Ipsa verba, quæ supra habuimus VIII. 1.

κὴ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια ῶν ἀναιρύντων αὐτὸν) Nempe te- stium, qui primi ad lapidandum. Vide supra cap. VII. v. 58.

## 22:21
Vers. 21. Depart. For I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles) Namely into Arabia, Syria, Lycia, Lycaonia, Bithynia, Mysia, Asia, Greece, Macedonia, Illyricum, and indeed with great fruit. See above IX. 15. Rom. XV. 19.

PART II. The tumult of the Jews and the abduction of Paul into the barracks, and his binding, and the loosening of his bonds.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Πορέυε. Ὅτι ἐγὼ ὠς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἀποςελῶ σε) Nempe in Arabiam, Syriam, Lyciam, Lycaoniam, By- thyniam, Mysiam, Asiam, Græciam, Macedoniam, Illyri- cum, & quidem magno cum fructu. Vide supra IX. 15. Rom. XV. 19.

PARS II. Judæorum tumultus & abductio Pauli in ca- stra, ejusque ligatio, & vinculorum solutio.

## 22:22
Vers. 22. Unto this word) As those who could not endure that the Gentiles should become partakers of the common salvation.

Away with such a fellow from the earth) Thus Luke XXIII. 18. Away with this man. Above XXI. 36.

For it is not fit that he should live) It is not fit. אֵין מִשְׁפָּט.

Latin:

Vers. 22. Ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου) Ut qui pati non possent, Gentes fieri participes communis salutis.

Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον) Sic Luc. XXIII. 18. Αἶρε τοῦτον. Supra XXI. 36.

Οὐ γὰρ καθῆκον αὐτὸν ζῇν) Οὐ καθῆκον. אֵין מִשְׁפָּט.

## 22:23
Vers. 23. And as they cast off their clothes) That they might be more ready to use force. We had the like above chap. VII. v. 58.

and threw dust into the air) Namely the earth shaken by their feet, as is wont to be done by the angry. The Syrian took it thus.

Pricæus, against this casting of garments, notes that it was done to the end that they might be more ready to offer violence, as in chap. VII. 58. He wishes, however, that it was a sign of a very agitated and offended mind, which they had offended by tossing their garments hither and thither with restless and impatient hands. And others explain these gestures of the cast-off garments and the dust thrown into the air more fully, namely that they were employed (1) as a sign of indignation and detestation, because they execrated the words of Paul, as Lyranus; (2) that they might as it were force the tribune to pass a sentence of condemnation upon Paul, as Chrysostom; (3) that they might signify that Paul was a troubler not only of the earth, but also of the air, as Cajetan; (4) as a sign of fury and turbulence, of which this was the image and beginning, as Dionysius has it.

Latin:

Vers. 23. Καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια) Ut expeditiores es- sent ad vim faciendam. Simile habuimus supra cap. VII. v. 58.

καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα) Nempe terra pedi- bus concussa, ut ab iratis fieri solet. Ita accepit Syrus.

Pricæus contra hanc projectionem vestimento- rum ad id factam notat, ut expeditiores essent ad vim inferendam, ut c. VII. 58. Vult autem signum fuisse valde concitati ossensique animi, quem of- fenderant, argutis & impatientibus manibus huc il- luc jactando vestimenta. Et explicant alii plenius hosce gestus projectorum vestimentorum, & pul- veris in aërem jactati, quod nempe adhibiti sint (1) in signum excandescentiæ & detestationis, quod execrentur verba Pauli, ut Lyranus; (2) ut vi quasi in tribuno extorqueant sententiam damnationis Pauli, ut Chrysostomus; (3) ut significarent, Pau- lum turbatorem esse non terræ tantum, sed & aëris, ut Cajetanus; (4) in signum furoris, ac turbulen- tiæ, cujus hoc erat imago & principium, ut Diony- sius habet.

## 22:24
Vers. 24. to be brought into the castle) Into the inner part of the Antonia where the soldiers were.

commanding him to be examined by scourging) The Roman custom of holding an examination by scourges, of which we spoke at Matt. XXVII. v. 19. But before this, that custom had existed among other nations. Hence it came about that ἐτασμὸς is taken for scourges in 2 Macc. VII. 37, and ἐξετάζειν for to torture, Wisd. XI. 10. But scourges are more cruel than rods; Cicero pro Rabirio, the Porcian law removes rods from the body of all Roman citizens. Here the merciful man brought back the scourges.

that he might know) From his own confession.

for which reason they thus cried out to him) For what reason he had so gravely offended them.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ἄγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν) In partem inte- riorem Antoniæ ubi erant milites.

εἰπὼν μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν) Mos Romanus quæstio- nem habendi per flagra, de quo diximus ad Matth. XXVII. v. 19. Sed ante is mos apud alias gentes fuerat. Hinc fa- ctum ut ἐτασμὸς sumatur pro flagris 2. Macc. VII. 37. & ἐξε- τάζειν pro torquere, Sap. XI. 10. Sunt autem flagra virgis sæviora Cicero pro Rabirio, Porcia lex virgas ab omnium ci- vium Romanorum corpore amovet. Hic misericors flagella retulit.

ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ) Ex ipsius confessione.

δι' ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ) Qua re eos tam gra- viter offendisset.

## 22:25
Verse 25. And as he stretched him out with the thongs) After he (the commander of the cohort) had exposed him to the thongs. Προτείνειν is προτιθέναι, to expose. ἱμάντες here means the same as μάστιγες. In the Glossary ἱμὰς is a thong. To be beaten with thongs is often found in Cicero and the comic poets. That is the 'ox-hide assessment' in Plautus: to which also belongs this elsewhere: Where dead oxen attack living men.

to the centurion who was standing by) Other codices have ἐφεστῶτα, and the Syriac seems to have read it so. Standing by, namely, at the interrogation ordered by the commander. See what we said at Matthew XXVII. v. 31.

is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman and uncondemned) We had both of these above at XVI. 37. That 'Roman' is against the Porcian and Sempronian laws: that 'uncondemned' is against both Roman laws and the laws of all well-ordered nations, as we said above. We spoke of the Porcian law just now. Caesar in Sallust: 'Why did you not add to the motion that they should first be punished with scourging? Or is it because the Porcian law forbids it?' Cicero, Fifth Verrine: 'O sweet name of liberty! O excellent right of our citizenship! O Porcian law, and Sempronian laws!' And soon after: 'It is a crime to bind a Roman citizen, a wickedness to scourge him.' Paul proclaimed likewise, as did the man of whom Cicero speaks there: 'I am a Roman citizen.'

Latin:

Vers. 25. ὡς δὲ προέτεινεν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσι) Postquam eum (præfectus cohortis) exposuerat loris. Προτείνειν est προ- τιθέναι, exponere. ἱμάντες hic quod modo μάστιγες. In Glossario ἱμὰς lorum. Loris cædi apud Ciceronem & Co- micos sæpe. Ea est censio bubula apud Plautum: cujus est & hoc alibi: Vbi vivos homines mortui incursant boves.

πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον) Alii codices habent ἐφεστῶτα, & sic legisse videtur Syrus. Astantem, nempe quæstioni, à præfecto imperatæ. Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. XXVII. v. 31.

εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν) Utrumque habuimus & supra XVI. 37. illud Romanum, est contra leges Porciam & Semproniam: illud, indemna- tum, & contra Romanas, & contra omnium bene mora- tarum gentium leges, ut supra diximus. De Porcia lege diximus modo. Cæsar apud Sallustium: Quamobrem in sententiam non addidisti, uti prius verberibus in eos animadverteretur? an quia lex Porcia vetat? Cicero Ver- rina Quinta: O nomen dulce libertatis! ô jus eximium no- stræ civitatis! ô lex Porcia, legesque Semproniæ! Et mox: facinus est vinciri civem Romanum, scelus verberari. Proclamavit Paulus itidem, ut ille de quo ibi Cicero: Ci- vis Romanus sum.

## 22:26
Verse 26.

take heed what you are about to do) See that you do not sin against the majesty of the Roman people. We spoke of that matter above in chapter XVI. v. 28.

Paul said this not because he shrank from scourges for CHRIST, in which he gloried, but lest this disgrace should be derived onto the faith and religion of Christ, as if Christians were to be scourged and exterminated: then indeed he was also consulting He wished to satisfy the conscience of the tribune, lest he should harm him with this injustice, and to teach the judges, lest they oppress the simple and the poor for the sake of the powerful.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ὅρα τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν) Vide ne in majestatem populi Romani pecces. Diximus ea de re supra cap. XVI. v. 28.

Dixit hoc Paulus non quod flagella pro CHRISTO refugeret, qui in iis gloriabatur, sed ne probrum hoc in Christi fidem & religio- nem derivaretur, quasi Christiani flagellandi & exterminandi essent: tum vero consulere etiam Tribuni conscientiæ voluit, ne is hac iniquitate eum læderet, judicesque docere, ne simplices & pauperes in gratiam potentium opprimant.

## 22:28
Verse 28. I obtained this citizenship with a great sum) Through the avarice of the Claudian times, as Tacitus speaks in Histories V. And Dion says specifically that the right of Roman citizenship was sold by him. Salvianus says the name of Roman citizens was bought for a great price. The Greeks use κεφάλαιον for the capital which is opposed to interest. But the Hellenists use it for any sum of money, as Lev. VI. 4, Num. V. 7, chap. XXXI. 26, 49. The Syriac here has סגאא בכספא, with much silver.

But I was even born) But Tarsus was not a colony, but a free city, as Pliny testifies V. 27. Appian says in the fifth book of the Civil Wars that liberty was granted to the Tarsians by Antony. And Dion Chrysostom in his first Tarsian oration recites many privileges granted by Augustus to the Tarsian state, but not the right of a colony or municipality, to which the right of Roman citizenship belonged, as we said in D. ad municipalem: and Ulpian does not name Tarsus among the colonies of Cilicia. It remains, therefore, that some ancestor of Paul acquired that right for himself during the civil wars which occurred between Caesar Augustus and Brutus and Cassius, or even between the same Caesar and Antony. From which you may gather that Paul was from an opulent family; and that the things which the ancient Greeks said on this passage are not vain.

It is rashly called into doubt by Grotius that the Tarsians were endowed with the right of Roman citizenship. For a scruple of inconsistency or falsehood could easily have arisen for the tribune: how could he who had called himself a Tarsian now boast himself a Roman, and indeed later assert that he was born a Roman? Unless it were established that this right of citizenship had been given to the Tarsians; which learned men observe was conferred upon them by Antony the Triumvir at the command of Augustus, and confirmed by a decree of the Senate by Agrippa: and Heinsius confirms this from Pliny book V. ch. 27, and indeed from Dion Cassius himself, namely that, as he (understand Dion) says, Augustus conferred upon them land, laws, and honor. Land, that is, free and immune territory. Laws, which were accustomed to be conferred upon municipalities regarding liberty. Honor, that is, the right of citizenship itself, especially distinguished and illustrious, which the Syriac called Romanity. Compare Camerarius on this passage. But the first benefit of the laws of liberty was immunity from scourges and lashes. Brissonius teaches in book I of the Antiquities of Civil Law, chapter 17, that it was not lawful for citizens to be beaten with rods, or to be put on the cross, or for judgment to be passed upon them without the order of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ἐγὼ πολλῷ κεφαλαίῳ τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτη- σάμην) Per avaritiam Claudianorum temporum, ut lo- quitur Tacitus Historiarum V. Et nominatim jus civitatis Romanæ ab eo venditum dicit Dion. Nomen civium Ro- manorum magno emptum dicit Salvianus Κεφάλαιον Græ- ci ponunt pro forte quæ usuris opponitur. At Hellenistæ pro quavis pecuniæ summa ponunt, ut Lev. VI. 4. Num. V. 7. cap. XXXI. 26. 49. Syrus hic סגאא בכספא multo argento.

ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι) At qui Tarsus non Colonia erat, sed libera urbs, Plinio teste V. 27. Concessam Tarsensibus liber- tatem ab Antonio dicit Appianus Civilium quinto. Et Dion Chrysostomus priore oratione Tarsensi multa privi- legia recitat ab Augusto tributa Tarsensi civitati, non autem jus Coloniæ aut municipii, qualibus jus civitatis Romanæ competebat, ut diximus D. ad municipalem: & Ulpianus in- ter Ciliciæ colonias Tarsum non nominat. Restat ergo, ut aliquis majorum Pauli bellis civilibus, quæ inter Cæsa- rem Augustum, & Brutum, Cassiumque, aut etiam inter eundem Cæsarem, & Antonium intercessere, jus illud sibi comparaverit. Unde colligas ex opulenta familia fuisse Paulum; neque vana esse quæ veteres Græci ad hunc lo- cum dixere.

Temere in dubium revocatur à Grotio Tar- senses Romanæ civitatis jure dotatos fuisse. Nam scrupulus inconstantiæ, aut falsitatis oriri facile potuisset tribuno, quomodo, qui se Tarsensem di- xerat, jam Romanum se venditet, imo & natum Romanum postea asserat? nisi constitisset, Tar- sensibus hoc jus civitatis donatum esse; quod ab Antonio Triumviro ipsis collatum ex Augusti man- dato, & S. C. ab Agrippa confirmatum, eruditi observant: idque è Plinio lib. V. c. 27. quoque, imo ex ipso Dione Cassio confirmat Heinsius, quod nempe, ut hic (Dionem intellige) ait, Augustus iisdem terram, leges, honoremque contulerit. Ter- ram vel agrum liberum videlicet, ac immunem. Le- ges, quæ de libertate municipiis conferri solitæ. Hono- rem, hoc est, ipsum civitatis jus, eximium imprimis, ac præclarum, quod Romanitatem Syrus dixit. Confer. Camerarius in h. l. Primum autem è legi- bus libertatis beneficium flagellorum verberum- que fuit immunitas. Verberibus cædi cives, aut in crucem agi, aut injussu populi in eos animadverti fas non fuisse docet Brissonius, lib. I. antiquit. Juris Ci- vil. cap. 17.

## 22:29
Verse 29. Those who were about to examine him) Whom the Latins call lictors, the Greeks call μαστιγοφόρους (whip-bearers).

Because he is a Roman and because he had bound him) For even this alone, to bind a Roman citizen, was a crime, as we just showed.

Latin:

Vers. 29. Οἱ μέλλοντες ἀυτὸν ἀνετάζειν) Quos Latini lo- rarios vocant, Græci μαστιγοφόρους.

ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστι καὶ ὅτι ἦν ἀυτὸν δεδεκώς) Nam vel hoc so- lum, vincire civem Romanum, crimen erat, ut modo ostendimus.

## 22:30
Verse 30. Wishing to know the certainty) Wishing to know something for certain. So also above XXI. 34 and below XXV. 26, to write something certain.

The 'What' (Τί) is accused by the Jews) We have the 'The' (Τὸ) similarly in Luke I. 62; the 'The' is demonstrative of the following sense.

He loosed him from his bonds) So that he might plead his case without prejudice.

To Beza, the term 'the certainty' seems to be used for 'the truth'. However, he cites an example from Lud. de Dieu from Wisdom ch. XVIII. 6. Compare also Acts II. 37, XXI. 34, XXV. 26, Luke I. 4.

And he commanded the chief priests and all their council to come) The manuscript is better: to assemble. For he did not call them to himself, but ordered them to assemble in the place of their elders. For because he had understood that there was a controversy about religion, he wished to explore the opinion of the Sanhedrin, whose duty it was to have cognizance of religion. But the heads of the priestly families are specifically named because they excelled in dignity in that assembly, as Matthew ch. XXVI. v. 3, 39, ch. XXVII. 1, 3, 12, Mark VIII. 31, XIV. 55, Luke XXIV. 20, above ch. IV. v. 23, below XXIII. 14.

ἔστησεν εἰς ἀυτὰς) For ἐν ἀυτοῖς. In the midst of them he stood.

From one manuscript the others are not to be corrected. We have warned, however, above, that simple words among the Greeks are not rarely used in the manner of the Hebrews for compound ones.

Which can have a place here also. Although, with the proper meaning of the verb retained, it can be said that he called the Sanhedrin to himself, so that there would be no need to expose Paul to danger. But καταγαγών is said to have set Paul down before the Council: because he had to be brought down from the Tower of Antonia to the place of the Council, which was lower: whether the assembly was held in the temple, where they gather from 1 Chron. 26:15 that the place of the council was; or whether, since it was not permitted for the Tribune as a Gentile to enter the temple, the Council was gathered by him in the lower fortress, so that Paul would not be snatched away by the Jews and killed: which Sanctius observes. It could be answered, however, that the ordinary place of the assembly was not in the temple, but at the temple, unless this extraordinary assembly was held in Antonia.

Latin:

Vers. 30. Βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς) Certi aliquid scire volens. Sic & supra XXI. 34. & infra XXV. 26. ἀσφαλές τι γράψαι.

Τὸ, Τί κατηγορεῖται παρὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων) Τὸ, Τί similiter habe- mus Luc. I. 62. τὸ est δεικτικὸν sensus sequentis.

ἔλυσεν ἀυτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν δεσμῶν) Ut sine præjudicio causam diceret.

Bezæ videtur nomen τὸ ἀσφαλὲς dici pro τὸ ἀληθὲς. Exemplum tamen allegat Lud. de Dieu è Sap. c. XVIII. 6. Conf. etiam Act. II. 37. XXI. 34. XXV. 26. Luc. I. 4.

καὶ ἐκέλευσεν ἐλθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον ἀυ- τῶν) Melius Manuscriptus: συνελθεῖν. Non enim eos ad se vocavit, sed in loco majorum eos convenire jussit. Nam quia intellexerat de religione controversiam esse, explo- rare voluit Synedrii sententiam, cujus erat de religione cognitio. Principes autem sacerdotaliurn familiarum spe- cialiter nominantur, quia in eo consessu dignitate emine- bant, ut Matth. cap. XXVI. v. 3. 39. cap. XXVII. 1. 3. 12. Marc. VIII. 31. XIV. 55. Luc. XXIV. 20. supra cap. IV. v. 23. infra XXIII. 14.

ἔστησεν εἰς ἀυτὰς) Pro ἐν ἀυτοῖς. In medio eorum consef- su.

E Manuscripto uno cæteri corrigendi non sunt. Monuimus autem supra, simplicia apud

Græcos more Ebræorum non raro pro compo- sitis usurpari. Quod & hic locum habere pot- est. Quanquam retenta significatione verbi pro- pria dici queat, ad se vocasse Synedrium, ne opus ha- berent Paulum periculo exponere. Dicitur au- tem καταγαγών dimittens Paulum coram Con- cilio statuisse: quia ex turri Antonia in locum Concilii, qui erat inferior, dimittendus erat: sive in templo fuerit celebratus conventus, ubi conci- lii locum fuisse è 1. Par. XXVI. 15, colligunt; sive quum templum ingredi Tribuno ceu gentili non licuerit, in ima arce ab eo congregatum fuerit Concilium, ne Paulus à Judæis abriperetur, & ne- caretur: quod Sanctius observat. Responderi ta- men posset, locum conventus ordinarium non in templo, sed ad templum fuisse, nisi hic extraordi- narius in Antonia celebratus esset conventus.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.
