Προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ) non profanaturus templum, sed Deum veneraturus cum Judaeis caeteris.

## 24:12
Verse 12.

Καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον) He does not say this because it would be a crime to dispute in the temple, after it was free from sacrifices, or in the synagogues, or among the same people along the public streets concerning the meaning of the Law and the Prophets: but so that he might remove every appearance of crime from himself as far as possible.

Ἢ ἐπισύστασιν ποιοῦντα) A gathering, against Roman laws, a conspiracy, see above XIX. 40. For רגז is translated as συντροφὴ, Jud. XIV. 8. and ἐπισύστασιν, Num. XVI. 40. thus also Num. XXVI בהצותם is translated as in their gathering.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

Καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον) Non hoc dicit, quod crimen esset in templo, postquam a sacrificiis vacabatur, aut in Synagogis, aut inter eundem per vias publicas de legis & Prophetarum sensu disputare: sed quo longius omnem criminis speciem a se amoveat.

Ἢ ἐπισύστασιν ποιοῦντα) Concursum, contra leges Romanas, συστροφὴν supra XIX. 40. Nam רגז vertitur συντροφὴ, Jud. XIV. 8. & ἐπισύστασιν, Num. XVI. 40. sic & Num. XXVI בהצותם vertitur ἐν ἐπισυστάσει αὐτῶν.

## 24:13
Vers. 13.

Οὔτε παραστῆσαι δύνανται περὶ ὧν νῦν κατηγοροῦσί μου) παριστάναι properly is to present a person, as above c. IX. 41. XXIII. 33. improperly it is transferred to things, and signifies to show. Thus ἀνδρείας παρίστασθαι in Plutarch: δόξαν παρίστασθαι in Plato. They cannot prove what they intend, namely either sedition stirred up by me, or foreigners brought into the temple. What here is παραστῆσαι, below is ἀποδεῖξαι, c. XXV. 7. but the accuser not proving, it is necessary that the defendant be acquitted.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

Οὔτε παραστῆσαι δύνανται περὶ ὧν νῦν κατηγοροῦσί μου) παριστάναι proprie est hominem exhibere, ut supra c. IX. 41. XXIII. 33. improprie ad res transfertur, & significat ostendere. Sic ἀνδρείας παρίστασθαι apud Plutarchum: δόξαν παρίστασθαι apud Platonem. Non possunt probare quod intendunt, nempe aut seditionem a me excitatam, aut alienigenas deductos in templum. Quod hic est παραστῆσαι infra est ἀποδεῖξαι, c. XXV. 7. accusatore autem non probante, reum absolvi necesse est.

## 24:14
Vers. 14.

Ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι) He confesses that which pertained most to the honor of God, and before a fair judge could not harm him: namely that he was of that sect which was called of the Nazarenes, yet not a contemner of either God, or the law, or his countrymen.

Κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν) כדרך.

Ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν) For this word is no less than that Hebrew one of a middle meaning, as appears above V. v. 17. XV. 5. and below XXVI. 5. thus Josephus uses it concerning the sects of the Jews: the Greeks concerning the Philosophers: Galen concerning the Physicians.

Λατρεύω) עובד.

Τῷ πατρῴῳ Θεῷ) To the God of the Fathers, of Abraham, of Isaac, of Jacob, and of the others from whom I trace my origin. See above III. 13. V. 30. VII. 32. XXII. 14.

Πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον κᾴ ἐν τοῖς Προφήταις γεγραμμένοις) see below XXVI. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

Ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι) Id fatetur, quod ad Dei honorem maxime pertinebat, & apud aequum judicem nocere ei non poterat: nempe esse se sectae ejus, quae Nazaraeorum dicebatur, non tamen contemptorem aut Dei, aut legis, aut popularium.

Κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν) כדרך.

Ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν) Est enim haec vox non minus quam illa Hebraea significationis mediae, ut apparet supra V. v. 17. XV. 5. & infra XXVI. 5. ita Josephus usurpat de Judaeorum sectis: de Philosophorum Graeci: de Medicorum Galenus.

Λατρεύω) עובד.

Τῷ πατρῴῳ Θεῷ) Deo Patrum, Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi, & caeterorum a quibus ortum duco. Vide supra III. 13. V. 30. VII. 32. XXII. 14.

Πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον κᾴ ἐν τοῖς Προφήταις γεγραμμένοις) vide infra XXVI. 20.

## 24:15
Vers. 15.

Ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεὸν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι) see above XXIII. 6: the hope of the Hellenists often corresponds to the Hebrew בטח or מבטח and therefore takes after itself εἰς or ἐπὶ with the accusative. I have this confidence in God, that there is to be a future resurrection, that which even these men themselves expect.

From these things Drusius gathers that the Pharisees at that time believed in the resurrection of both the just and the unjust, that is, the wicked. Which opinion later Jews called into doubt, with some contending that only the just would rise, others that the just would rise with certain wicked ones. Which they prove first from Dan. XII. 2, where it is written 'many,' not 'all.' Then from David, poorly perceived and understood, Psalm I. 'Therefore the wicked shall not rise in judgment,' since it follows, 'Nor sinners in the assembly of the just,' [arguing that] it is one thing to rise simply, and another to rise in the assembly of the just. Not to mention that that passage can be translated, 'therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment,' as if he were saying, they shall not stand, but shall lose their case. To these they accommodate that old saying: The resurrection is not of all, but of the just only. Which, however, helps them little or nothing. For there it is not תקומת המתים ἀνάστασις, but תחית המתים ἀναβίωσις, which properly designates resurrection to life. He who understands, understands what I mean. This is Drusius.

Δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων) Which was the better opinion among the Jews, approved by Christ, John V. 29, Matt. XXV. v. 31, and following. Note that this is a principal object of faith.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεὸν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι) vide supra XXIII. 6: ἐλπὶς Hellenistarum respondet saepe Hebraeo בטח vel מבטח ideoque post se recipit εἰς vel ἐπὶ cum accusativo. Fiduciam hanc in Deo habeo, futuram resurrectionem eam quam & isti expectant.

Ex his colligit Drusius, Pharisaeos eo tempore credidisse resurrectionem cum justorum tum injustorum, hoc est improborum. Quam opinionem posteriores Judaei in dubium vocarunt, aliis justos tantum, aliis justos cum improbis quibusdam resurrecturos contendentibus. Quod probant primum ex Dan. XII. 2. ubi scriptum multi non omnes. Deinde ex Davide male percepto & intellecto, Psal. I. Ideo non resurgent improbi in judicio, cum sequatur, Neque peccatores in coetu justorum, aliud resurgere simpliciter, & aliud in coetu justorum. Ne dicam quod locus ille transferri possit, ideo non consistent improbi in judicio, quasi dicat, non stabunt, sed cadent causa. His accommodant dictum illud vetus: Resurrectio non est omnium, sed justorum tantum. Quod tamen eos parum aut nihil juvat. Nam ibi non est תקומת המתים ἀνάστασις, sed תחית המתים ἀναβίωσις, quae proprie resurrectionem ad vitam designat. Intelligens intelligit, quid velim. Haec Drusius.

Δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων) Quae melior erat inter Judaeos sententia, a Christo probata Ioh. V. 29. Matth. XXV. v. 31. & seqq. Nota praecipuum hoc esse fidei objectum.

## 24:16
Vers. 16.

ἐν τούτῳ δὲ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ) For this reason, that is, because of this confidence. ἀσκῶ I exercise: namely myself, which among the Hellenists is often understood, because the Hebrews often use active forms for reciprocal ones, and sometimes passive.

Ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους) Other codices have the better ἔχων. I exercise myself because of that hope, so that I may keep a conscience that offends neither God nor men. See above XXIII. 1. The word ἀπρόσκοπος is also found in the son of Sirach XXXII. 22, and in Paul 1 Cor. X. 32, Phil. I. v. 10. προσκοπὴ and πρόσκομμα correspond to the Hebrew פוק ומכשול, which signify that which the Latin means by 'offense'.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ἐν τούτῳ δὲ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ) Propter hoc, id est, propter hanc fiduciam. ἀσκῶ exerceo: nempe memetipsum, quod apud Hellenistas sæpe subauditur, quia Hebræi sæpe pro reci- procis usurpant modo activa modo passiva.

Ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους) Melius alii codices ἔχων. Exerceo me propter illam spem, ut conscientiam servem eam, quæ nec Deum nec homines offendat. Vide supra XXIII. 1. Vox ἀπρόσκοπος est & apud Sirachiden XXXII. 22. apud Paulum 1. Cor. X. 32. Phil. I. v. 10. προσκοπὴ & πρόσκομμα respondent Hebræis פוק ומכשול, quæ id significant, quod Latinum offensa.

## 24:17
Vers. 17.

δὶ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων) after an absence of some years; thus we have διὰ in Gal. II. 1 and elsewhere.

παρεγενόμην) I had come to Jerusalem.

ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνός μου) so far from wishing to harm them, I voluntarily wished to benefit them.

καὶ προσφοράς) so far from having despised God or the law; I offered victims and other things, by legitimate rite.

Post annos plures, that is, 24 years from the conversion of Paul. He understands the alms which he had collected in Asia for the Christians living in Jerusalem. Compare 2 Cor. VIII and IX. From the fact, however, that he says he was also about to make offerings and vows, it appears that he had vowed them before he was warned by James in ch. XXI. 20; but having been warned, he hastened them, confirmed in his purpose, and informed about the special manner of purification.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

δὶ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων) post annorum aliquot absentiam; sic διὰ habemus Gal. II. 1. & alibi.

παρεγενόμην) veneram Hierosolyma.

ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνός μου) tantum abest, ut nocere, ultro prodesse ipsis volui.

καὶ προσφοράς) tantum abest ut Deum aut legem con- tempserim; obtuli victimas & alia, legitimo ritu.

Post annos plures, id est 24. à conversione Pauli. Eleemosynas intelligit, quas in Asia pro Christianis collegerat Hierosolymis agentibus. Conf. 2. Cor. VIII. & IX. Ex eo autem quod obla- tiones & vota etiam facturum sese dicit, apparet quod prius ea nuncuparit, antequam à Jacobo mo- neretur c. XXI. 20. monitus autem ea acceleravit, in proposito suo confirmatus, & de speciali ratio- ne purificationis informatus.

## 24:18
Verse 18.

ἐν οἷς) in which while I am occupied.

τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι) supra XXI. 27.

Verse 19.

οὓς δεῖ ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρός με· ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν) These last words are to be read as a parenthesis.

Vers. 19.

οὓς δεῖ ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρός με· ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν) Hæc postrema per parenthesin le- genda.

## 24:20
Verse 20.

εἴτι εὗρον ἐν ἐμοὶ ἀδίκημα) in the Manuscript: τί εὗρον interrogatively: the sense coheres best this way. What wrongdoing, he says, did they prove in me, when the matter was conducted before the Sanhedrin.

Prudentius here observes that Pricaeus has nothing to change here: since many examples of the other phrasing also occur: which may be seen in the same author, and in Walaeus at this place. Cf. Job XVIII. 23.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

εἴτι εὗρον ἐν ἐμοὶ ἀδίκημα) in Manuscripto: τί εὗρον in- terrogative: optime sic sensus cohæret. Quid maleficii, in- quit, in me probarunt, cum apud Synedrium res acta est.

Prudentius hic Pricæus nil hic immutandum esse observat: siquidem & multa exempla alterius locutionis occurrunt: quæ videantur apud eun- dem, & Walæum h. l. Conf. Job. XVIII. 23.

## 24:21
Vers. 21.

ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἔκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὅτι περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ὑφ᾽ ὑμῶν) unless they wish this to be a crime, that I have openly professed that I believe the dead can be raised by God.

Beza translates it thus: The Vulgate, however, has not departed from the sense, explaining it as, he deferred.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἔκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὅτι περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ὑφ᾽ ὑμῶν) nisi hoc crimen esse volunt, quod palam professus sum credere me mortuos à Deo posse resuscitari.

Ita vertit Beza: Vulgatus tamen à sensu non abiit, exponens, distitit.

## 24:22
v. 22. ἀνεβάλετο αὐτοὺς) they translate it best who translate: He adjourned them. Cicero speaks thus in his speech for Caecina, and in the third Verrine, Livy in book IV. The formal word of a judge adjourning was 'Amplius' [More], supply 'to be investigated'. Cicero mentions this in his Brutus, Asconius in his commentary on the third Verrine, Donatus on the Eunuchus.

ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, εἰπὼν, ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χι- λίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς) I follow those who judge that 'εἰπὼν' is here inserted between the middle words. In this sense: when I have learned more exactly what this sect is, and when Lysias has come, I will settle this case. For 'διαγινώσκειν' is to define a case: for 'διὰ' in composition often signifies completion. Felix saw that the state of this controversy was partly legal, partly judicial: the legal part was whether the Nazarene sect was against the law of the Jews: the judicial part was whether Paul had incited a gathering or a riot; regarding the former, many learned men were to be heard, besides the accusers; but regarding the latter, Lysias himself was a certain witness. Wherefore Felix rightly gave an interlocutory ruling.

By 'the way' some understand Judaism, but others more correctly understand Christianity: such as Chrysostom, Lyranus, Hugo, etc.

Latin:

v. 22. ἀνεβάλετο αὐτοὺς) optime vertunt, qui vertunt: Ampliavit eos. Loquitur sic Cicero pro Cæcinna, & tertia Verrina, Livius lib. IV. Solennis vox judicis diffindentis erat Amplius, supple cognoscendum. Meminit Cicero Bruto, Asco ius ad tertiam Verrinam, Donatus ad Eunuchum.

ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, εἰπὼν, ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χι- λίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς) Sequor eos qui εἰπὼν hic inter media verba censent interponi. Hoc sen- su: ubi exactius didicero, quid sit de hac secta, & ubi Lysias venerit, causam istam terminabo. Nam διαγινώσκειν est definire causam: διὰ enim in compositione sæpe consum- mationem significat. Statum hujus controversiæ videbat Felix partim esse legalem, partim indicialem: legalis erat, an secta Nazarena esset contra legem Judæorum: indicialis, an Paulus concursum, aut tumultum concitasset; de priore audiendi erant complures viri eruditi, præter accusatores; At de altero testis certus erat ipse Lysias. Quare merito in- terlocutus est Felix.

Per viam Judaismum nonnulli, rectius autem alii Christianismum intelligunt: utpote Chrysosto- mus, Lyranus, Hugo, &c.

v. 23. And having commanded the centurion) To a certain centurion by the Caesareans.

to keep Paul) For he could not be fully released before acquittal. L. Neque D. on the custody of the accused.

And to have [relief]) Namely from bonds. Ἔνεσιν in the Glossary is relaxation.

and to forbid none of his own to minister or come unto him) He ordained this for the dignity of the person, because he had understood him to be a Roman citizen. L. 1. D. on the custody of the accused, in the title already mentioned.

PART II. Paul's courtly discourse before Felix and Drusilla, and its consequences.

Latin:

v. 23. Διαταξάμενός τε τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ) Alicui centurio- ni à Cæsariensibus.

τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον) Neque enim ante absolutionem plane dimitti poterat L. Neque D. de custodia Reorum.

Ἔχειν τ' ἔχεσιν) Nempe à vinculis. Ἔνεσιν in Glossar. laxatio.

καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν ἢ προσέρχεσθαι αὐτῷ) Hoc pro dignitate personæ constituit, quia civem Romanum esse intellexerat L. 1. D. de custodia reorum di- cto jam titulo.

PARS II. Aulica Pauli coram Felice & Drusilla concio, ejusque consequentia.

## 24:24
v. 24. And Felix having come) for he had gone out to fetch his wife.

with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess) This woman, the sister of Agrippa, having left her husband Azizus, king of the Emesenes, who was circumcised, contrary to the law, followed Felix, an uncircumcised man, having been touched by love for him, and had entered into marriage with him. Josephus, Antiquities XX. 6. Moreover, this very Drusilla was the granddaughter of Antony and Cleopatra: as witnessed by Tacitus, Histories V. See what was said above on XXIII, 24.

She was the daughter of Herod Agrippa the elder, who killed James and imprisoned Peter, Acts XII. She had three husbands: For first she was betrothed to Epiphanes, the son of King Antiochus: but he refused her, because he would not undergo circumcision, which condition was required in her marriage, as she was a Jewess. The second was Azizus, King of Emesa, who underwent the condition of circumcision, and thus entered into marriage with her. The third was Felix, who enticed her to himself away from her husband Azizus. Hence Drusilla was called the wife of three kings, and three times a queen, and therefore perhaps in Suetonius, Claudius chapter 28, Felix is called the husband of three queens. Finally, Drusilla was a woman of ruined modesty and faith, who passed from her husband the King to an adulterous governor, not only having renounced her conjugal faith, but also having spurned her ancestral religion, and with Felix the Gentile she became a Gentile, as here Cornelius à Lapide.

he sent for Paul) he ordered him to be brought, as above 2.

concerning the faith in Christ) that he might execute the former part of his duty in this matter.

Latin:

v. 24. παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ Φῆλιξ) nam exierat ad uxorem accersendam.

σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ) Hæc soror Agrippæ, relicto contra legem marito Azizo Emesenorum rege circumciso, Felicem hominem incircumcisum, sui a- more tactum, secuta, nuptias cum eo fecerat. Josephus XX. Annalium 6. Erat autem hæc ipsa Drusilla neptis Antonii & Cleopatræ: teste Tacito Historiarum V. vide quæ dicta supra XXIII, 24.

Filia erat Herodis Agrippæ senioris, qui Jaco- bum occidit, & Petrum incarceravit, Actor. XII. Tres habuit sponsos: Primo enim desponsata fuit Epiphani, Antiochi Regis filio: sed hic eam recu- savit, quia noluit subire circumcisionem, quæ con- ditio in nuptiis ipsius, utpote Judææ petebatur. Secundus fuit Azizus Rex Emesæ, qui subiit cir- cumcisionis conditionem, itaque cum ea matri- monium iniit. Tertius fuit Felix, qui eam ab Azi- zo marito ad se pellexit. Hinc Drusilla vocata est trium Regum uxor, & ter regina, ideoque forte à Suetonio in Claudio cap. 28. Felix dicitur trium Reginarum maritus. Denique Drusilla profligati pudoris & fidei fœmina, à marito Rege ad adul- terum præsidem, non solum abdicata conjugali fide, sed & patria religione spreta, transiit, ac cum Felice Gentili facta est Gentilis, ut hic Cornelius à Lapide.

μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον) adduci jussit, ut supra 2.

περὶ τῆς εἰς χριστὸν πίστεως) ut priorem partem sui in hac re officii exsequeretur.

## 24:25
Vers. 25.

and as he reasoned of righteousness and temperance) which two things, besides the worship of God, the Christian religion requires in the highest degree, Tit. I. 8. II. 12.

and of the judgment that is to be) even against the wicked: see above 15.

Felix becoming terrified) fearing for himself, if the matter were so: conscious of his own shameful life, as Tacitus teaches us in Annals XII. It was not the act of a just man, with a servile character, that is, to exercise royal authority through every cruelty and lust: which Tacitus says of the same Felix in Histories V: it was not the act of a continent man to abduct a wife from an unwilling husband.

that is, as things now stand, you may go: I have no time now for such dissertations.

Paul treated this theme of justice and chastity with purpose, because Felix was unjust and an adulterer, who, because of her remarkable beauty, had enticed Drusilla to himself through the work of a certain magician, Simon, and had taken her away from her husband, and, as Tacitus testifies in book V, had run riot through every kind of lust.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας) quæ duo, præter Dei cultum, Religio Christiana exigit in sum- mo gradu, Tit. I. 8. II. 12.

καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔσεσθαι) etiam in malos: su- pra 15.

ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ) metuens sibi, si res sic se ha- beret: conscius sibi vitæ flagitiosæ, ut Tacitus nos docet Annalium XII. Non erat justi hominis, servili ingenio, id est, per omnem sævitiam, ac libidinem exercere jus regium: quod de eodem Felice dicit Tacitus Historiarum V: non erat continentis, à marito nolente uxorem abducere.

τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου) id est, ut nunc se res habent, abeas: non vaco nunc ejusmodi dissertationibus.

Studio Paulus hoc thema de justitia & castitate tractavit, quia Felix injustus, & adulter erat, qui Drusillam ob insignem pulchritudinem, opera cu- jusdam Magi Simonis ad se pellexerat, & à mari- to abstraxerat, ac Tacito lib. V. teste, per omnem libidinem grassatus erat.

Vers. 26.

This also pertained to that servile character, and was contrary both to the Hebrew laws: Exod. XXIII, 8. Deut. XVI, 19. and also to the Roman laws: Law 1, law 3, and 4, Digest on the Julian Law of Extortion.

for which reason also, sending for him more frequently) ordering him to be brought to him more often, as above XXIV, below XXV, 6.

he conversed with him מלל אלין.

Vers. 26.

ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου) Nempe quia & civem Romanum esse intellexerat, & principem sectæ multorum millium. Pertinebat & hoc ad servile istud ingenium, eratque contrarium tum Hebræis legibus: Exod. XXIII, 8. Deuter. XVI. 19. tum & Romanis Lege 1. l. 3. & 4. D. ad legem Juliam Repetundarum.

ἐ διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος) sæpius ad se ad- duci jubens, ut supra XXIV. infra XXV. 6.

ὡμίλει αὐτῷ) colloquebatur cum eo מלל אלין.

## 24:27
v. 27. and when two years were completed) the two-year period of Paul's imprisonment being fulfilled.

Felix received Porcius Festus as a successor) See Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews XX, 7, and Jewish War II, 24.

Since Luke himself looks back to the completed two-year period of Felix, with mention made of his successor Festus, there is no reason for us to believe that Paul remained in prison here for two years, even though Oecumenius, Bede, Onuphrius in his Chronicles, the author of the Gloss, Lyranus, Cajetanus, and Sanctius have believed this, because thus the Apostle would have been confined in prison for a full four years, namely two years here at Caesarea, and another two years later at Rome. Nor do Scaliger, Baronius, and Lorinus correctly calculate that two-year period from the reign of Nero: since no trace of that calculation appears, such as is not at all obscure here regarding the two-year period of Felix, as we have said; whence it may be gathered that it should be started from his prefecture in Judea, to which Claudius appointed him toward the end of his reign: since he had previously been in charge of Trachonitis, Gaulanitis, and Batanaea.

And wishing to bestow favors upon the Jews, Felix) Wishing to gratify the Jews, so that he might redeem the anger of the people at the expense of an innocent man, for which reason Pilate also put Christ to death. Felix had committed many cruel and unjust acts against the Jews, for which, being accused before Nero, he was rescued from punishment through the influence of his brother Pallas, as Josephus testifies in Antiquities of the Jews XX, 7. χάριν κατατίθεσθαι is a very Greek expression, also customary to Demosthenes and Xenophon, which kind of expressions Luke has not a few, where he does not introduce others speaking, but speaks himself, and indeed about matters not pertaining to religion.

Latin:

v. 27. διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης) biennio reatus Pauli expleto.

ἔλαβε διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον) Vide Josephum Antiquæ Hist. XX, 7. & belli Jud. II. 24.

Quum Lucas ipse respiciat ad expletum Felicis biennium, mentione facta successoris Festi, non est quod biennium in carcere hic hæsisse Paulum credamus, etsi id etiam crediderint Oecumenius, Beda, Onuphrius in Chronic. autor Glossæ, Lyranus, Cajetanus & Sanctius, quia sic per integrum qua- driennium in carcere conclusus fuisset Apostolus, utpote biennio hic Cæsareæ, & altero biennio post Romæ. Neque biennium illud recte Scaliger, Baro- nius, & Lorinus à Neronis imperio computant: quum nullum computi istius appareat vestigium, quale de Felicis biennio, uti diximus, hic minime obscurum est; unde colligere, licet, id inchoandum à præfectura ejus in Judæa, cui eum Claudius sub finem imperii præfecit: quum antea Trachoniti- dæ, Gaulonitidi, & Batanææ præfuerit.

Θέλων τε χάριτας καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ) Gratificari volens Judæis, ut innocentis incommodo iras populi redi- meret, qua de causa Pilatus quoque Christum supplicio affe- cit. Multa sæva & iniqua in Judæos patraverat Felix, quo- rum accusatus apud Neronem, per fratris Pallantis poten- tiam pœnæ ereptus est, teste Josepho Antiquit Histor. XX. 7. χάριν κατατίθεσθαι est loquutio bene Græca, Demostheni quo- que & Xenophonti usitata, quales loquutiones non paucas habet Lucas, ubi non alios inducit loquentes, sed ipse loqui- tur, & quidem de rebus ad religionem non pertinentibus.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The priests seek in vain from Festus that Paul be brought to Jerusalem, who instituted the trial at Caesarea, before whom accordingly Paul is accused: But proofs are lacking that he sinned against the law of the Jews, or the temple, or against Caesar. Yet for the sake of the Jews Festus wished to judge him at Jerusalem. But Paul, lest he be delivered to the Jews without fault, appealed to Caesar, to which appeal Festus deferred: exposing this case to King Agrippa, who was receiving the same at Caesarea with Berenice his wife, to whom, since he desired to hear Paul, Paul is brought, so that, when Festus had found in him no cause of death, he might be heard by him, and those who were present with him.

There are two parts: I. The false accusation of Paul by the Jews before Festus, and his appeal to Caesar, to v. 12. II. The presentation of Paul before Agrippa and Bernice: with the narration of the state of the case made by Festus, to the final v. 27.

PART I. The false accusation of Paul by the Jews before Festus.

Vers. 1.

Ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχίᾳ) When he had arrived in the province, as Trajan speaks to Pliny 27. having entered the borders of the province, as Ulpian L. observare §. aliquam D. de officio Proconsulis: having entered the province in the same place §. post hæc.

ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας) For governors also had to observe this as soon as they came to or arrived at the first city, d. L. §. ingressus.

He first went to Caesarea, which is the head of the province, as far as the Romans are concerned: just as Jerusalem is as far as the Jews are concerned.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Sacerdotes nequicquam à Festo petunt, ut Pau- lus Hierosolymis sistatur, qui judicium in- stituit Cæsareæ, coram quo proinde ac- cusatur Paulus: Sed deficiunt probatio- nes, quod adversus legem Judæorum, aut templum vel adversus Cæsarem peccarit. In gratiam tamen Judæorum Hierosolymis i- psum judicare volebat Festus. Sed Paulus, ne Judæis traderetur citra culpam, appella- bat ad Cæsarem, cui appellationi deferebat Festus: Regi Agrippæ, qui eundem Cæsareæ cum Berenice conjuge sua excipiebat, cau- sam hanc exponens, cui, cum Paulum audi- re desideraret, Paulus sistitur, ut, quum nullam mortis causam in eo invenerit Fe- stus, ab eo, & qui ipsi aderant, audiretur.

Partes duæ sunt: I. Falsa Judæorum coram Fe- sto Pauli accusatio, & hujus ad Cæsarem appella- tio, ad v. 12. II. Presentatio Pauli coram Agrippa & Bernice: cum enarratione status causæ à Festo facta, ad v. 27. finalem.

PARS I. Falsa Judæorum Pauli coram Festo accusatio.

Vers. 1.

Ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχίᾳ) Cum in provinciam pervenisset, ut loquitur Trajanus ad Plinium 27. ingressus fines provin- ciæ, ut Ulpianus L. observare §. aliquam D. de officio Pro- consulis: ingressus provinciam ibidem §. post hæc.

ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας) Nam & hoc obser- vare debebant præsides in quam primum civitatem veni- rent vel applicarent d. L. §. ingressus.

Primum adiit Cæsaream, quæ caput provin- ciæ, quantum ad Romanos: uti Hierosolyma quo- ad Judæos.

Vers. 2.

ἐνεφάνισαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς κῂ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου) that is, they insisted upon the accusation begun against Paul. as XXIV. 1. οἱ πρῶτοι here, who are the elders above.

κῂ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν) in the Glossary: παρακαλῶ I pray, I beseech, I ask.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ἐνεφάνισαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς κῂ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου) id est, accusationi in Paulum cœptæ institêre. ut XXIV. 1. οἱ πρῶτοι hic, qui supra πρεσβύτεροι.

κῂ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν) in Glossario: παρακαλῶ oro, obse- cro, rogo.

## 25:3
Vers. 3.

αἰτούμενοι χάριν) χάρις here is a benefit, as it often is among the Greeks: as ἡ χάρις ἀβραδύνως ἄχαρις χάρις.

See how much they value Paul, that is, how much they believe him to be an enemy of Judaism and a defender of the Christians, so that when they could and ought to seek much greater things that concern the public good, they omit those and seek only the head of Paul.

ἐνέδραν ποιῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν) Using the clandestine work of assassins, in such a way that they could escape authority.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

αἰτούμενοι χάριν) χάρις hic est beneficium, ut apud Græ- cos sæpe: ut ἡ χάρις ἀβραδύνως ἄχαρις χάρις.

Vide quanti Paulum æstiment, puta quantum Judaismi hostem & Christianorum hyperaspistem credant, ut cum multo majora & publicum bo- num spectantia petere possint, & debeant, iis omis- sis unum petant Pauli caput.

ἐνέδραν ποιῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν) Clandestina si- cariorum usuri opera, ita, ut auctoritatem possent defugere.

## 25:4
v. 4. ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐν Καισαρείᾳ) That is, that he is well kept there, and there is no reason why he should be transferred, since he can be accused there no less than at Jerusalem. Roman governors did not always administer justice in one city, but wherever they were.

ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι) From Jerusalem, that is, to Caesarea.

Latin:

v. 4. ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐν Καισαρείᾳ) Id est, bene eum ibi servari, nec quicquam causæ esse cur transferretur, cum ibi non minus, quam Hierosolymis accusari possit. Romani Præsides non semper in una urbe jus dicebant, sed ubicunque erant.

ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι) Hierosolymis nem- pe Cæsaream.

## 25:5
v. 5. οἱ ἐν δυνατοὶ ἐν ὑμῖν) To whom it will be convenient. Thus the Syrian took it here. It was accustomed to be said thus: to whom it is convenient, follow me. אשׁר יכלו δυνατοί.

συγκαταβάντες) Descending with me. He speaks thus because Caesarea is by the sea.

Illud οἱ ἐν δυνατοὶ commodius exponit Pricæus, & ex eo Walæus τὺς ἄρισα κατηγορῆται δοκῦντας, vel τὺς δυναμένυς sc. κατηγορῆσαι, as if he were to say, A confused crowd of voices means nothing, it removes the face and form of judgments, an unorganized multitude: let those therefore who are more instructed than the rest be chosen to undertake the duty of accusing. The Vulgate, those who are powerful among you, that is, those who are more influential in authority. Thus also Camerarius, οἱ δυνατοὶ, who are πολιτικῶν V. οἱ δυνάμενοι. Whom he called πρώτυς above, that is, primary, powerful, and leading men.

εἴ τι ἐστὶν ἐν ἀνδρὶ τύτῳ) Namely, what they might wish to accuse, from what follows. For the word ἄτοπον is not in most books, and seems to have been added from a gloss. Thus we say in Latin: if you have anything.

Merito hic discedit à Beza, who inserted that ἄτοπον from a few codices: if there is anything wicked in this man, whereas those few codices should rather be recalled to the rest.

Latin:

v. 5. οἱ ἐν δυνατοὶ ἐν ὑμῖν) Quibus commodum erit. Ita hic accepit Syrus. Sic dici solebat: queis commodum est, exsequias, te. אשׁר יכלו δυνατοί.

συγκαταβάντες) Mecum descendentes. ita loquitur quia Cæsarea est ad mare.

Illud οἱ ἐν δυνατοὶ commodius exponit Pricæus, & ex eo Walæus τὺς ἄρισα κατηγορῆται δοκῦντας, vel τὺς δυναμένυς sc. κατηγορῆσαι, quasi dicat, Turba confusa voces nihil significant, tollit faciem ac formam judiciorum, incondita multitudo: seligantur ergo cæteris instructiores ad accusandi munus obeun- dum. Vulgatus, qui inter vos potentes sunt, id est, qui magis auctoritate pollent. Sic & Camerarius, οἱ δυ- νατοὶ, qui sunt πολιτικῶν V. οἱ δυνάμενοι. Quos supra πρώτυς vocavit, id est primarios, potentes & principes viri.

εἴ τι ἐστὶν ἐν ἀνδρὶ τύτῳ) Nempe quod accusare velint, ex sequentibus. Nam vox ἄτοπον, non est in plerisque libris, & videtur ascripta ex Glosssemate. Sic Latine dicimus: si quid habes.

Merito hic discedit à Beza, qui è paucis Codi- cibus illud ἄτοπον ingressit: si quid est in hoc viro improbum, quum revocandi potius sint illi pauci Codices ad cæteros.

## 25:6
v. 6. διατρίψας δέ ἐν ἀυτοῖς) Jerusalem, that is. ἡμέρας πλείυς ἢ ὀκτώ) Other books say ἢ πλείυς ἢ δέκα. But the manuscript: ἢ πλείους ὀκτὼ δέκα, which I think is true. For the Latin reads it thus, and the Syrian, and the Arab. It is solemn to speak thus when knowledge or memory does not suffice to define a number exactly. Thus the Holy Writers often use ὡσεὶ. As Matt. XIV. 21. Mark VI. 44. Luke IX. 14. XXII. 41. XXIII. 44. John VI. 10. above II. 14. V. 36. X. 3.

Memoria deficere non poterat penes scriptorem θεόπνευσον. Nor is that reading therefore to be approved, not more than eight or ten. Most codices have πλείυς ἢ δέκα, and Chrysostom also reads it thus. One must acquiesce in these. Which was also done by B. Luther.

καθίσας ἐπὶ τῦ βήματος) There were things that could be done on the level ground, greater things only before the tribunal. For these are opposed to each other in Suetonius, Paul, and Papinian.

He ordered Paul to be brought to him.

Latin:

v. 6. διατρίψας δέ ἐν ἀυτοῖς) ἱεροσολύμοις scilicet. ἡμέρας πλείυς ἢ ὀκτώ) Alii libri ἢ πλείυς ἢ δέκα. At Manu- scriptus: ἢ πλείους ὀκτὼ δέκα, quod verum puto. Nam & La- tinus sic legit, & Syrus, & Arabs. Solemnis sic loqui ubi ad numerum exacte definiendum notitia aut memoria non suppetit. Sic ὡσεὶ sæpe usurpant Sancti Scriptores. Ut Matth. XIV. 21. Marci VI. 44. Luc. IX. 14. XXII. 41. XXIII. 44. Joh. VI. 10. supra II. 14. V. 36. X. 3.

Memoria deficere non poterat penes scripto- rem θεόπνευσον. Nec ergo illa lectio probanda, non plures quam octo aut decem. Plerique Codi- ces habent πλείυς ἢ δέκα, sic & Chrysostomus legit. His acquiescendum. Quod etiam à B. Luthero factum.

καθίσας ἐπὶ τῦ βήματος) Erant quæ de plano fieri pote- rant, majora non nisi pro tribunali. Hæc enim inter se op- ponuntur apud Suetonium, Paulum, & Papinianum.

ἐκέλευσε τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι) Ad se duci.

## 25:7
v. 7. They stood around the tribunal.

Envoys from the Senate.

αἰτιώματα) Rightly so, not as other books have αἰτιώματα; αἴτιημα is said in that form, as θέμα, ἀκρόαμα, and the like.

Concerning which word Camerarius: Bringing forward demands or accusations. Which are αἰτίαι. By which name he also uses later. But αἰτία is properly a crime. And Demosthenes distinguishes this from ἐλέγχου, because a crime is demonstrated here, with the defendant convicted, in the oration against Androtion. He also distinguishes it from ἀδικήματος, in the oration against Aristocrates. Because all evil deeds before the judicial inquiry have the name of αἰτία, that is, of a crime. But offenses, that is, ἀδικήματα, only then, when it has been pronounced by the sentence of the court that they have been committed by someone.

Which they were not able to prove. Above παραστῆσαι XXV. 13. It is an old saying: if to have accused were sufficient, who would be innocent?

Latin:

v. 7. περιέσησαν) Circumstetere tribunal.

οἱ ἀπὸ ἱεροσολύμων καταβεβηκότες) Legati à Senatu.

αἰτιώματα) Recte sic, non ut alii libri habent αἰτιώματα; dicitur αἴτιημα ea forma, qua θέμα, ἀκρόαμα, & similia.

De qua voce Camerarius: Postulationes sive crimina inferentes. Quæ sunt αἰτίαι. Quo etiam nomine postea utitur. Est autem αἰτία proprie cri- men. Et distinguit hanc ἀπὸ τῦ ἐλέγχε Demosthe- nes, quod demonstratum hic crimen sit, reo con- victo, in oratione contra Androtionem. Distinguit & ἀπὸ τῦ ἀδικήματος, in oratione contra Aristo- cratem. Quod omnia mala facinora ante cogni- tionem judicii nomen habeant αἰτίας, id est crimi- nis. Delicta autem id est ἀδικήματα, tunc demum cum sententia judicii patrata ab aliquo esse, fuerit pronunciatum.

ἃ ὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι) Supra παραστῆσαι XXV. 13. Vetus est dictum: si accusasse sufficiet, quis innocens erit?

## 25:8
v. 8. That ὅτι here is redundant in the manner of the Hellenists. For direct speech follows.

For I have perpetually observed the law.

I approached the temple piously, nor did I bring any foreigner into it.

I did not teach rebellion: I have done or said nothing against the authority of Caesar.

Latin:

v. 8. ἀπολογυμένυ αὐτῦ ὅτι) Illud ὅτι hic abundat Hel- lenistarum more. Sequitur enim directa oratio.

υτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰυδαίων) Legem enim perpetuo ob- servavi.

ὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν) Templum pie adii, nec quemquam in eo induxi alienigenam.

ἔτε εἰς Καίσαρά τι ἥμαρτον) Non docui rebellionem: nihil feci, dixive contra Cæsaris imperium.

## 25:9
Vers. 9.

The same expression, which is above XXII. 27.

ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ) Addressing Paul. For thus ἀποκρίνεσθαι is often used both among these and other writers. See above III. 12.

ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων κρίνεσθαι ἐπ’ ἐμῦ) Do you wish to be judged by the Sanhedrin in my presence? Thus ἐπὶ is used also below XXVI. 2. The Sanhedrin had a certain jurisdiction over the Jews: but the right of Roman citizenship was stronger than the right of the Sanhedrin; therefore he could not be compelled to acknowledge those judges against his will. Presidents were sometimes accustomed to be present at the order of the city. L. 1. §. sed etsi D. quando appellandum sit.

Paul was a Roman citizen, and he was standing at Caesarea before the tribunal of the Roman Caesar. Therefore he could not be compelled to go to the Sanhedrin, because since those who were accusing him were already standing in that place at Caesar's tribunal, he would have to be led down to Jerusalem, from where he had been brought here, and that solely for the sake of the accusers, and not without the greatest danger. For Festus was not asking whether he wished to be judged by the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem, but, do you wish to be judged there concerning these things before me?

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Θέλων χάριν καταθέσθαι) Eadem locutio, quæ supra XXII. 27.

ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ) Alloquens Paulum. Nam sic ἀποκρίνεσθαι sæpe ponitur & apud hos & apud alios scriptores. Vide supra III. 12.

ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων κρίνεσθαι ἐπ’ ἐμῦ) Visne à Synedrio judicari me præsente? sic ἐπὶ & infra sumitur XXVI. 2. Habebat Synedrium jurisdictionem quandam in Judæos: sed civitatis Romanæ jus validius erat jure Synedrii; itaque invitut cogi non poterat illos agnoscere judices. Solebant præsides interdum adesse ordini civitatis. L. 1. §. sed etsi D. quando appellandum sit.

Erat Paulus civis Romanus, & stabat Cæsareæ ad Tribunal Cæsaris Romani. Non ergo cogi poterat ad Synedrium, quod cum starent jam, qui accusabant eundem in eo loco ad Cæsaris tribunal, Hierosolymam deducendus sit, unde hic adductus erat, idque solum in accusatorum gratiam, nec absque summo periculo. Nam non quærebat Festus, an à Synedrio vellet judicari Hierosolymis, sed, visne ibi de his judicari apud me?

## 25:10
Εἶπε δὲ ὁ Παῦλος) And fearing both those judges and the city, and the journey itself.

Vers. 10.

ἐπὶ τῦ βήματος Καίσαρός έσώς εἰμι) He rightly calls that the tribunal of Caesar, which the procurator held in the name and by the mandate of Caesar. See at Matt. XXVII. verse 2. Ulpian L. I. D. de officio procuratoris Cæsaris: What things have been done and transacted by the procurator of Caesar are approved by him, just as if they had been transacted by Caesar himself.

Οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι) For it was the duty of the Roman Presidents to take cognizance of a Roman citizen.

Ἰουδαίους ὀὐδὲν ἠδίκησα) Therefore I do not fear your judgment, because I am certain that the Jews have been harmed by me in nothing. That they complain of me unjustly.

ὡς κὲ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις) You know better, to wit, than that there is any need for me to teach you about those things. You know that from Felix and from those who were present with Felix at the hearing.

Latin:

Εἶπε δὲ ὁ Παῦλος) Et Judices illos & urbem, & iter ipsum reformidans.

Vers. 10.

ἐπὶ τῦ βήματος Καίσαρός έσώς εἰμι) Recte tribunal Cæsaris vocat id, quod procurator habebat nomine ac mandato Cæsaris. Vide ad Matth. XXVII. vers. 2. Ulpianus L. I. D. de officio procuratoris Cæsaris: Quæ acta gestaque sunt à procuratore Cæsaris, sic ab eo comprobantur, atque si à Cæsare ipso gesta sint.

Οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι) Nam de cive Romano Præsidum Romanorum erat cognoscere.

Ἰουδαίους ὀὐδὲν ἠδίκησα) Ideo judicium tuum non reformido, quia certus sum, nihil à me læsos Judæos. Inique eos de me queri.

ὡς κὲ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις) Melius nosti scil. quam ut opus sit, me ea dere te docere. Scis id ex Felice & ex eis qui Felici in cognitione adfuerunt.

## 25:11
Vers. 11.

εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀδικῶ) If that institution which I follow harms the Jews.

κὶ ἄξιον θανάτυ πέπραχά τι) And if I have done anything worthy of death, which according to Roman laws deserves death.

I do not refuse to die) That similar remark of Demetrius in Livy, book 50: 'Father, if I have committed any impious act against you, if any wicked act against my brother, I do not beg off from any punishment.'

But if there is nothing of those things of which they accuse me.

No one can give me to them as a favor) No one has the right to hand me over to them. Thus Herod is accused in Josephus, Jewish War II. 5: 'To have given the blood of Judea as a favor to the foreign peoples.' Philo expresses the same sense thus: 'She will be entreated, having obtained some gift from you. But you will provide no greater good for her than to deliver the Jews, and to approach them.' For 'can' here refers to legitimate power. He gives the accused to his enemies who hands him over to their judgment.

I appeal to Caesar) That is, if you wish to hand me over to be judged by the Sanhedrin (for that is what Festus seemed to be doing), I appeal to Caesar Nero: this was permitted by Roman laws in such a case. For one can appeal before a sentence, if a judge has interlocuted that an inquiry is to be held in a civil matter, or does this against the laws in a criminal one. L. Ante D. de Appellationibus recipiendis. Moreover, it was against Roman laws to hand over a Roman citizen to be judged by provincial men, and against his will. Pliny in his letter about the Christians: 'There were others of similar madness, whom, because they were Roman citizens, I noted were to be sent back to the city.'

Paul was anticipating the outcome, lest he be handed over to the Jews to be judged, by appealing to Caesar, so that he might avoid the snares of the Jews, consulting not so much for his own life as for the Church, as Augustine says, Ep. 2, since he had received an oracle from God, ch. XXIII. 11, that he would preach the gospel at Rome. Nor was this without merit: because the Jews had accused him as seditious and disturbing the rights of Caesar: and they could not prove the causes which they were alleging.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀδικῶ) Si id institutum quod sequor, Judæos injuria afficit.

κὶ ἄξιον θανάτυ πέπραχά τι) Et si ea injuria talis est, quæ secundum leges Romanas mortem mereatur.

ἐ παραιτῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν) Simile illud Demetrii apud Livium libro L. Ego, si quid impiæ in se, pater, si quid sceleratæ in fratrem admisi, nullam deprecor pœnam.

εἰ δὲ ὀὐδέν ἐστιν ὧν ὗτοι κατηγορῦσί μυ) Si nihil in re est eorum, de quibus me accusant.

οὐδείς με δύναται αὐτοῖς χαρίσασθαι) Nemo jus habet, ut me illis donet. Sic Herodes apud Josephum belli Judaici II. 5. accusatur, Τὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας αἷμα κεχαρίσθαι τοῖς ἔξωθεν δήμοις. Philo eundem sensum sic eloquitur: Παρακληθήσεται δὲ τυχῦσα τινὸς παρὰ τῦ δωρεᾶς. Μεῖζον δ’ ἀγαθὸν ὀὐδὲν αὑτῇ παρέξεις, ἢ τὺς Ἰουδαίυς ἐκδὺς, κό προσίυσας. Δύναται enim hic ad facultatem legitimam refertur. Donat reum inimicis, qui eum ipsorum judicio tradit.

Καίσαρα ἐπικαλῦμαι) Id est, si me vis Synedrio judicandum tradere (id enim videbatur agere Festus) ad Cæsarem Neronem appello: licebat hoc Romanis legibus in tali casu. Nam ante sententiam appellari potest, si quæstionem in civili negotio habendam judex interlocutus sit, vel in criminali contra leges hoc faciat. L. Ante D. de Appellationibus recipiendis. Erat autem contra leges Romanas civem Romanum, provincialibus hominibus judicandum tradere, & id nolentem. Plinius in Epistola de Christianis: Fuerunt alii similis amentiæ, quos, quia cives Romani erant, annotabi in urbem remittendos.

Præoccupabat in eventum Paulus, ne traderetur Judæis judicandus, provocando ad Cæsarem, ut Judæorum laqueos evitaret, non tam vitæ suæ, quam Ecclesiæ consulens, ut ait August. Ep. 2. siquidem oraculum à Deo acceperat, c. XXIII. 11. se Romæ evangelizaturum. Nec id immerito: quia accusarant eum Judæi ut seditiosum & Cæsaris jura turbantem: neque causas, quas prætexebant, probare poterant.

## 25:12
Vers. 12.

Then Festus, having conferred with the council) As was the custom for Roman governors, to conduct important matters by the opinion of the Council. See what we said at Matt. XXVII. 19. with the council

βουλῆς, is to be translated as with counsel, as the old interpreter did, not as others, with a council.

You have appealed to Caesar, to Caesar you shall go) There is no need for a question here: for the discourse proceeds better: You have appealed to Caesar, that is, since you have appealed to Caesar, to Caesar you shall go. The appeal was not made simply, but under a condition; but Festus gladly seized the opportunity by which he might free himself from this trouble and odium.

These words seem rather to indicate a mind somewhat offended, because Paul was thought to be making the governor's judgment suspect, and for that reason was appealing to Caesar.

PART II. The presentation of Paul before Agrippa and Bernice, with the narration of the state of the case made by Festus.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τῦ συμβυλίυ) Ut mos erat Romanis præsidibus, agere res magnas de Consilii sententia. Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. XXVII. 19. μετὰ συμ-

βουλῆς, vertendum est cum consilio, ut vetus interpres fecit, non ut alii, cum concilio.

Καίσαρα ἐπικέκλησαι, ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ) Non opus est hic interrogatione: melius enim procedit sermo: Cæ- sarem appellasti, id est, quandoquidem ad Cæsarem pro- vocasti, ad Cæsarem ibis. Provocatio non erat simpliciter facta, sed sub conditione; verum Festus libenter arripiebat occasionem, qua se ab hac molestia & invidia liberaret.

Videntur hæc verba potius animum indicare nonnihil offensum, quod Paulus præsidis judicium suspectum facere censeretur, & ad Cæsarem ideo appellaret.

PARS II. Præsentatio Pauli coram Agrippa & Bernice, cum enarratione status causæ a Festo facta.

## 25:13
Vers. 13.

And after some days had passed) When some days had intervened. The same expression is in Mark 16:1, below 27:9.

King Agrippa) The son of that Herod Agrippa whose death was recounted above in chapter 12. This man was king first of Chalcis, then of Batanea, Trachonitis, and Gaulonitis, to which Nero added Abila, Julias, Tarichaea, and Tiberias. Josephus in Jewish War 1.21.22 mentions this Agrippa, as does the Jerusalem Talmud.

and Bernice) The sister of that Agrippa, married (which was permitted by law) to her uncle, the aforementioned Herod, and after his death to Polemon, king of Cilicia. See Josephus, Antiquities 19.7, and Jewish War 2.26 and 28. Βερνίκη is a Macedonian name for Φερενίκη. For the Macedonians used to change φ into β, and thus they said βρύγας for Φρύγας. Thus, what is Berenice in Valerius Maximus 8.6 is the same as Pherenice in Pliny 7.41. This woman was infamous regarding her brother, as Josephus teaches us in 20.5, and to that refers that passage of Juvenal.

- - - Then the most famous diamond, and one made more precious on the finger of Bernice: this the barbarian gave long ago, this Agrippa gave incestuously to his sister.

For the Scholastics are mistaken who drag these things elsewhere.

Although she was the sister of the younger Agrippa, she is nevertheless believed to have been his concubine as well, hence she is called his wife by Chrysostom. Therefore, to dispel this suspicion of incest, she later married Polemon, king of Cilicia, or as others wish, of Lycia, as Josephus indicates in the aforementioned place.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ἡμερῶν δὲ διαγενομένων τινῶν) Cum dies intercessissent ali- quot. Eadem locutio Marc. XVI. 1. infra XXVII. 9.

Ἀγρίππας ὁ βασιλεὺς) Filius ejus Herodis Agrippæ, cu- jus mors supra recitata est XII. Fuit autem hic rex Chalcidis primum, deinde Batanææ, Trachonitidis, Gaulonitidis quibus addidit Nero Abilam, Juliada, Tarichæas, & Tiberiada. Josephus Bello Judaico I. 21.22. meminit hu- jus Agrippæ etiam Thalmud Hierosolymitanum.

καὶ Βερνίκη) Soror Agrippæ illius, nupta (quod per le- gem licebat) patruo suo dicto Herodi, & post ejus mor- tem Polemoni Ciliciæ regi. Vide Josephum Ant. hist. XIX. 7. de bello Judaico II. 26. & 28. Βερνίκη est nomen Mace- donicum pro Φερενίκη. Nam Macedones φ in β mutabant, sic & βρύγας, dicebant pro Φρύγας. ita quæ Berenice Vale- rio Maximo. VIII. 6. eadem Plinio Pherenice VII. 41. Fuit hæc femina infamis in fratre, ut nos docet Josephus XX. 5. eoque referendum illud Juvenalis.

- - - Deinde Adamas notissimus & Berenices In digito factus pretiosior: hunc dedit olim Barbarus inceste dedit hunc Agrippa sorori.

Falluntur enim Scholastæ, qui alio hæc trahunt.

Etsi soror fuerit Agrippæ junioris, creditur ta- men ejus etiam concubina fuisse, inde à Chrysosto- mo ejus uxor dicta. Ideo ut hanc incestus suspicio- nem dilueret, nupsit postea Polemoni Ciliciæ, vel ut alii volunt Lyciæ Regi, ut Josephus loc. c. indicat.

V. 14. Ἀνέθετο) The Greek word is made in the manner of the Latin 'retulit' (reported). The Hebrews would say הגיד.

Αἰτύμενοι κατ᾽ ἀυτῦ δίκην) In the manuscript it is καταδίκην.

Αἰτύμενοι κατ᾽ ἀυτῦ δίκην) In Manuscripto est καταδίκην.

## 25:16
V. 16. ὅτι ὐκ ἔστιν ἔθῷ Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον εἰς ἀπώλειαν, πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορύμενῷ κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τὲς κα- τηγόρες, τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τῦ ἐγκλήματῷ) We saw above in II what χαρίζεσθαι means. It is, however, a shortened expression: the full version would be: It is not the Roman custom to give any man over to destruction, by condemning him, before both the accuser has stood against him, and he himself has received the opportunity of defending himself. Appian says the same regarding the Romans: it is not their ancestral custom to condemn without a trial. Philo on the Roman governors: for then, offering themselves as impartial judges, listening equally to the accusers and the defendants, and deeming it right to condemn no one without a trial, they gave judgment not out of enmity, nor out of favor, but according to the nature of the truth, deciding what seemed just. We have brought forward more things pertaining to this under the title of the Digest concerning those who are to be sought or those who are to be condemned in their absence. κατὰ πρόσωπον means in the presence of. Ita vertitur לפני Exodi XXXI. 6.

Latin:

V. 16. ὅτι ὐκ ἔστιν ἔθῷ Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον εἰς ἀπώλειαν, πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορύμενῷ κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τὲς κα- τηγόρες, τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τῦ ἐγκλήματῷ) Quid sit χαρίζεσθαι supra vidimus II. Est autem curtata lo- quutio: plena esset: Non est Romani moris quemquam in exitium donare alteri, damnando eum, antequam & ac- cusator contra constiterit, & ipse sui defendendi acceperit copiam. Idem de Romanis Appianus: ἐ πάτριον σφίσιν ἀ- κρίτως καταδικάζεσθαι. Philo de præsidibus Romanis: τότε γὰρ κοινὸς παρέχοντες ἑαυτὸς δικαστὰς, ἐξ ἴσω κὴ τ κατηγόρων, κὴ τ ἀπολογουμένων ἀκροώμενοι μηδενὸς ἀκρίτω προκαταγινώσκειν ἀξιῶντες, ἐβράβευον ἔτε πρὸς ἔχθραν, ὔτε πρὸς χάριν, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὴν φύσιν τῆς ἀληθείας τὰ δόξαντα εἶναι δίκαια. Attulimus plura huc pertinentia ad titulum Digestorum de requiren- dis vel absentibus damnandis. κατὰ πρόσωπον est in con- spectu. Ita vertitur לפני Exodi XXXI. 6.

Vers. 19. ζητήματα δέ τινα) See above XXIII. 29.

περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας) Thus Quintilian III. 8. The first author of the Jewish superstition. Thus Ulpian in the law 'qui ad tempus' D. de Decurionibus: The divine Severus and Antoninus permitted those who follow the Jewish superstition to attain honors; but they also imposed upon them obligations which would not harm their superstition.

ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλῷ ζῇν) That he had been brought back to life.

ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλῷ ζῇν) Resuscitatum esse.

V. 20. ἀπορύμενῷ δὲ ἐγὼ εἰς τὴν περὶ τύτε ζήτησιν) When I was at a loss in the investigation of this matter, being ignorant, that is, of the disputes which exist among the Jews, and by what norms they are to be judged. The manuscript does not have εἰς. And ἀπορία is often accustomed to be constructed with the accusative.

κᾀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τύτων) by the Sanhedrin, as we said above.

V. 20. ἀπορύμενῷ δὲ ἐγὼ εἰς τὴν περὶ τύτε ζήτησιν) Cum ego in rei istius inquisitione hærerem, ignarus scil. disputa- tionum, quæ sunt inter Judæos, & ex quibus normis ex sint dijudicandæ. Manuscriptus non habet εἰς. Et solet ἀπορία sæpe construi cum accusativo.

κᾀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τύτων) à Synedrio, ut supra diximus.

v. 21. ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν) It is an ellipsis for εἰς τὸ τηρηθῆναι: In this he appealed, that he might be kept for Caesar's examination; Caesar and Augustus are titles of the principate in Tacitus, Histories II.

I commanded him to be kept, until I send him to Caesar) Paul had to remain in custody until Caesar should take cognizance. For nothing is to be changed once an appeal has been interposed. Latin:

v. 21. ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν) Est ἔλλειψις pro εἰς τὸ τηρηθῆναι: In hoc appella- vir, ut Cæsaris cognitioni servaretur, Cæsar & Augustus principatus vocabula Tacito Histor. II.

ἐκέλευσα τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν, ἕως ἂν πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα) Manere Paulus debebat in custodia donec Cæsar cogno- sceret. Nihil enim novandum appellatione interposita. Vide quæ ad titulum ejus argumenti in Digestis diximus. Pro πέμψω Manuscriptus habet ἀναπέμψω.

## 25:22
v. 22. I also wished to hear the man) He was led by curiosity, just as Herod was formerly, Luke 23:8.

Latin:

v. 22. ἐβουλόμην καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀκοῦσαι) Curiosita- te ducebatur, quali olim Herodes Luc. XXIII. 8.

## 25:23
v. 23. with great pomp) Polybius, Hipparchus, the old Chronicle, and Chrysostom several times use this word in the same sense: Sopater also: pompously and with great pomp. Bardesanes in Eusebius concerning the women of the Batri: served by maidservants and young men rather than by men with great pomp on horses, adorning the horses with much gold and precious stones. Hence to make a show, Sirach 4:33.

Thus also Suidas: they used to say 'to be imagined' for 'to appear', thus for appearance, for display and ostentation. Athenaeus, book 5, from the narrative of Posidonius concerning Athenion: 'not even one of the Romans making such a display of luxury in the Attic calamity.' Since not even any of the Romans would act with such display in the Attic calamity. Hippocrates, 'On Decorum': 'do things, not at all curiously, nor with display,' he wishes nothing to be done very curiously and with ostentation, as B. Quiistorpius observed from Camerarius. Similarly Aristotle, book 3 of Rhetoric: 'all these things are appearance,' all those things are mere show and pomp. Luke seems to have expressed this for this reason, that he might propose for the readers to consider the antithesis between those sitting on the tribunal with such splendor, and Christ's Apostle pleading his cause from chains: in which matter the conformity of the Head and the members appears most especially, concerning which Paul himself speaks in Phil. 3:10, which Beza notes here.

and having entered into the audience chamber) A Greek word made after the example of the Latin. For the word 'auditorium' is frequent in Roman law in this sense. The Syriac translates it well: 'house of judgment'.

together with the tribunes) With the commanders of the cohorts.

and the men who were of distinction in the city) The leading men of the Caesareans. 'Those who are of distinction,' for 'those who are in a position of distinction,' just as Paul said 'those who are in authority,' 1 Tim. 2:2.

Paul was brought) As above, 6.

Latin:

v. 23. μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας) Utitur hac voce eodem sensu & Polybius, & Hipparchus, & Chronicon vetus, & Chrysostomus aliquoties: Sopater quoque: πομπικῶς κᾀ με- τὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας. Bardesanes apud Eusebium de Batro- rum mulieribus: ὑπηρετούμεναι ὑπὸ παιδισκῶν καὶ νεανίσκων μᾶλλον ἢ οἱ ἄνδρες μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας ἵπποις, κοσμοῦσαι πολλῷ χρυσῷ κᾀ λίθοις βαρυτίμοις τοὺς ἵππους. Hinc φαντασιο- κοπεῖν, Sir. IV. 33.

Sic & Suidas Φαντάσεσθαι ἐπὶ τοῦ φαίνεσθαι ἔλεγον, sic pro apparere, pro apparatu & ostentatione. Athe- næus libr. V. ex narratione Posidonii de Athenione, οὐδενὸς οὐδὲ Ῥωμαίων ἐν τοσαύτῃ φαντασίᾳ καλα- χλιδῶντος τῆς Ἀττικῆς. Cum ne Romanorum quidem quisquam tanto apparatu in Attica calamitate faceret. Hippocrates περὶ εὐσχημοσύνης, ποιέειν δέκαρτα, μηδὲν αὐτῶν περιέργως μὴ δὲ μετὰ φαντασίης, fieri nihil vult admodum curiose & cum ostenta- tione, ut B. Quiistorpius è Camerario observavit. Similiter Aristot. l. III. Rhetoric. ἅπαντα ταῦτα φαντασία εἰσὶ cuncta ista species sunt atque pompa. Videtur autem Lucas hoc propterea expressisse, ut proponat lectoribus considerandam antithesin inter istos in tribunali cum tanto splendore seden- tes, & causam ex vinculis dicentem Christi Aposto- lum: qua in re potissimum apparet Capitis & mem- brorum συμμόρφωσις, de qua Paulus ipse Phil. III. 10. quod hic Beza annotat.

κᾀ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον) Græca vox facta ad ex- emplum Latinæ. Est enim in jure Romano frequens hoc sensu vox auditorii. Syrus bene vertit בית דינא.

σύν τε τοῖς χιλιάρχοις) Cum præfectis cohortium.

κᾀ ἀνδράσι τοῖς κατ' ἐξοχὴν οὖσι τῆς πόλεως) Cæfareensium primis. τοῖς κατ' ἐξοχὴν οὖσι, pro τοῖς ἐν ἐξοχῇ οὖσι. quomodo Paulus dixit τῶν ἐν ὑπεροχῇ ὄντων, I. Tim. II. 2.

ἤχθη ὁ Παῦλος) Ut supra 6.

## 25:24
v. 24. they have interceded with me, The Latin interpreter is good; he has interpellated me. Gloss: I intercede, I interpellate.

crying out that he ought not to live) As a pestilent man. See above, 24:5.

Latin:

v. 24. ἐνέτυχόν μοι, Bene Latinus interpres; interpellavit me. Glossa: ἐντυγχάνω, interpello.

ἐπιβοῶντες μὴ δεῖν ζῇν αὐτόν) Ut hominem pestilentem. Vide supra XXIV. 5.

## 25:25
v. 25. but I having found) 'To find' and in the Attic 'to be found,' among other things, is to discover, to apprehend. Thus above, 4:13, 10:34.

I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, both from the letter of Lysias, and from the testimony of Felix, and from the accusation of the Jews, and the defense of Paul.

ἔκρινα πέμπειν αὐτόν) I decided to send him. Thus we have κρίνειν also above XX. 16.

Latin:

v. 25. ἐγὼ δὲ καταλαβόμενος) καταλαμβάνειν & Attice καταλαμβάνεσθαι, inter alia est invenire, deprehendere. ita supra IV. 13. X. 34.

Comperi nihil dignum morte eum admisisse, tum ex literis Lysiæ, tum ex testimonio Felicis, tum ex accusatione Judæorum, & apologia Pauli.

ἔκρινα πέμπειν αὐτόν) Constitui eum mittere. Sic habui- mus κρίνειν & supra XX. 16.

## 25:26
V. 26. τῷ Κυρίῳ) The title of Lord, refused by Augustus and Tiberius, was accepted by later emperors.

Three titles of the emperor are to be noted here: for he is called Caesar v. 11. and 12., he is called Σεβαστὸς v. 21., and here κύριος. They were called Caesars from Julius Caesar, and Augusti from Octavius Augustus. Augustus in Greek is σεβαστὸς, venerable, and to be honored as if with a certain majesty of divinity.

προήγαγον αὐτὸν) I brought him forth into public, as above XII. 6.

ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης) ἀνάκρισις here is a certain preliminary inquiry, not for the sake of judging, but for informing the judge. ἀνάκρισις is taken in that sense by Marcianus, L. Divus Hadrianus D. de custodia & exhibitione reorum: c. 2. Novella concerning those who make Eunuchs. Marcianus calls this ἀνάκρισιν an elogium in the same law, and Tertullian to Scapula calls it a notoria, the law from the accusation D. ad Sc. Turpillianum. L. ea quidem C. de accusationibus L. Si quis in hoc C. de Episcopis & Clericis, and Augustine in Epistle 159 and 160. Marcianus also calls it interrogations.

Latin:

V. 26. τῷ Κυρίῳ) Domini nomen ab Augusto & Tiberio recusatum, posteriores imperatores recepere.

Tres hic tituli imperatoris notentur: Vocatur enim Cæsar v. 11. & 12. vocatur Σεβαστὸς v. 21. & hic κύριος. Cæsares à Julio Cæsare, Augusti ab Octavio Augusto vocati sunt. Augustus Græce est σεβαστὸς venerandus, & numinis velut majestate quadam colendus.

προήγαγον αὐτὸν) In publicum produxi, ut supra XII. 6.

ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης) ἀνάκρισις hic est prævia quædam inquisitio, non judicandi, sed judicis edocendi causa. Sumitur eo sensu ἀνάκρισις à Marciano L. Divus Hadrianus D. de custodia & exhibitione reorum: c. 2. No- vella de his qui Eunuchos faciunt. Hanc, ἀνάκρισιν elogium, appellat Marcianus eadem lege, & Tertullianus ad Scapu- lam, notoria, lex ab accusatione D. ad Sc. Turpillianum. L. ea quidem C. de accusationibus L. Si quis in hoc C. de Episcopis & Clericis, & Augustinus Epistola 159. & 160. Marcianus etiam interrogationes.

## 25:27
v. 27. ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ) It seems absurd to me.

μὴ καὶ τὰς κατ' αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι) And not to signify the crimes charged against him. So that he might be able to write something certain and investigated, he wishes, with King Agrippa present, the Jewish le-

gum, and not ignorant of the questions, to hear what that was concerning Jesus of Nazareth which was objected to him as a crime, he stated the αἰτίας here, which [is] above 7. αἰτιώματα.

God so directs these things that Paul, led from prison in chains into the hall of the praetorium, in an illustrious assembly before King Agrippa, the governor Festus, and Bernice the King's sister, might plead his cause, which was that of Christ himself. Doubtless God willed, as Chrysostom teaches, to manifest the innocence of his client in such a theater, and to make it attested by so many and such rich testimonies.

Latin:

v. 27. ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ) Absurdum mihi videtur.

μὴ καὶ τὰς κατ' αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι) Et non significare crimina ipsi objecta. ut aliquid certi exploratique possit scribere, vult præsente Rege Agrippa Judaicarum le-

gum, ac quæstionum non ignaro audire, quid illud esset, de Jesu Nazareno, quod ei pro crimine objiciebatur, αἰτίας hic dixit quod supra 7. αἰτιώματα.

Hæc ita dirigit Deus, ut Paulus è carcere vin- ctus in aulam prætorii deductus in illustri conses- su coram Rege Festo præside & Berenice Regis sorore, causam suam, quæ ipsius Christi, perora- ret. Nimirum voluit Deus, Chrysostomo docente, clientis sui in tali theatro innocentiam pateface- re, totque tamque locupletibus testimoniis testa- tum facere.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

Paul, having obtained from Agrippa the opportunity to speak, institutes his apology, having first secured attention; he discourses concerning his former life and Pharisaic profession, and the accusation because of the hope of the promise made to the Fathers, and because of the resurrection of the dead which was handed down, and also concerning the persecution of Christians, and how on the way to Damascus, surrounded by heavenly light, he was sent by Jesus, who appeared to him, to his ministry, especially for the conversion of the Gentiles, and how he carried out that calling, and was apprehended by the Jews but rescued from them, he explains, testifying that he teaches nothing beyond those things which Moses and the Prophets spoke, that Christ ought to suffer, to rise again, and to announce light to the people and to the Gentiles: He is accused of madness by Festus; but he maintains that all those things are true, and not unknown to the King, as they were not done in a corner, asking, Does Agrippa believe the Prophets? Who says he is almost persuaded to become a Christian, which Paul wishes for him and the rest of the hearers, and the King and the governor of the province testify that he has committed nothing that is worthy of death or bonds. Agrippa also declares that he could have been released, had he not appealed to Caesar.

There are two parts: I. Paul's apologetic speech before Agrippa, to verse 23. II. His defense against the censure of Festus, with the appeal to the judgment of Agrippa, and the judgment of the latter, to verse 32.

PART I. Paul's apologetic speech before Agrippa.

Verse 1.

ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σε αυτῦ λέγειν) As above XXIV, 10. ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα) as those about to speak are accustomed to do. Themistius, oration: ἐκ δὲ ἀνατεινομένου τὴν χεῖρα. Polyaenus IV: ἀνέτεινε τὴν δεξιὰν ὡς δημαγορήσων. Doubtless silence was accustomed to be commanded in this way, and this was here a sign of the Apostle's παῤῥησίας.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Paulus impetrata ab Agrippa dicendi facul- tate apologiam instituit, præmissa atten- tionis conciliatione, de vita & professione sua pristina Pharisaica, & accusatione ob spem promissionis Patribus factæ, & ob re- surrectionem mortuorum traditam, nec non de persecutione Christianorum disse- rit, & quomodo in via Damascena luce cæ- lesti circumfusus à Jesu, qui sibi apparuerit, ad ministerium ejus missus, imprimis ad conversionem gentium, eamque vocationem expedierit, atque à Judæis apprehensus, sed iisdem ereptus fuerit, exponit, testatus seni- hil docere extra ea, quæ Moses & Prophetæ loquuti sunt, quod Christus pati, resurgere, & populo, ac gentibus lucem annunciare de- buerit: Arguitur furoris à Festo; sed vera illa omnia esse, nec ignota Regi, ut pote non in angulo gesta perhibet, rogans, An Agrip- pa Prophetis credat? Qui ferme se indici ait, ut Christianus fiat, quod de ipso & reliquis auditoribus optat Paulus, ac testantur Rex, & præses provinciæ, nihil ipsum commisisse, quod morte aut vinculis dignum sit. Agrip- pa etiam pronunciat, dimitti eum potuisse, nisi ad Cæsarem provocasset.

Partes sunt duæ: I. Apologetica Pauli coram A- grippa oratio, ad v. 23. II. Ejusdem adversus Festi censuram defensio, cum provocatione ad judicium Agrippæ, atque hujus judicio, ad v. 32.

PARS I. Apologetica Pauli coram Agrippa oratio.

Vers. 1.

ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σε αυτῦ λέγειν) Ut supra XXIV, 10. ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα) ut solent dicturi. Themistius orat. ἐκ δὲ ἀνατεινομένου τὴν χεῖρα. Polinæus IV. ἀνέτεινε τὴν δεξιὰν ὡς δημαγορήσων. Nimirum ita silentium solebat indici, & signum id hic fuit παῤῥησίας Apostoli.

## 26:2
Verse 2.

ἐπὶ σῦ) In your presence. For Agrippa was not the judge. See above XXV, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ἐπὶ σῦ) Te præsente. Non enim judex erat Agrippa. Vi- de supra XXV, 9.

## 26:3
Verse 3.

μάλιστα γνώσην ὄντα σε) The Attics use accusatives for genitives placed absolutely. This is frequent in Thucydides.

Therefore, these are not to be considered solecisms with Camerarius, nor is the boldness of Beza to be approved, because from one codex he added the word εἰδὼν, perhaps written in for the sake of a clearer sense, while all other codices oppose it, as does the Latin Vulgate and also the commentary of Chrysostom. γνώστην ὄντα σε is polished for γνώστη ὄντι σοι, just as in Halicarnasseus, ὡς δὴ ἀκίνδυνον αὐτοῖς τὸ ἔργον ἐσόμενον for ὡς ἀκινδύνῳ αὐτοῖς τῶν ἔργῳ ἐσομένῳ, as if the matter were to be without danger for them, and in Aristotle, ὥσπερ ἐκ αὐτῷ χώραν τινὰ ὅσαν, as if there were not some region for him. Thus, that passage in Ephesians 1:18 can be rightly understood, πεφωτισμένους τῆς ὀφθαλμὲς τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, the eyes of your mind being enlightened; as Beza himself rightly explained there, as Ludov. de Dieu observes.

ἐθῶν τε) Whether the nations are bound by our institutions. καὶ ζητημάτων) Such as concerning divine inspiration, concerning the resurrection, concerning the Messiah.

It designates not only those things, but generally ἔθη, ceremonies or rites of the Jews, and questions concerning the very tenets of religion, about which there was disagreement among the Jewish sects themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

μάλιστα γνώσην ὄντα σε) Attici pro genitivis absolute po- sitis usurpant accusativos. Frequens id apud Thucydidem.

Non ergo vel hæc cum Camerario σολοικοφα- νῆ habenda, vel etiam probanda audacia Bezæ, quod ex uno Codice vocem εἰδὼν forte sensus ex- peditoris causa adscriptam addiderit, repugnan- tibus aliis Codicibus omnibus, ut & vulgata La- tina, nec non Chrysostomi commentario. Poli- tum est γνώστην ὄντα σε pro γνώστη ὄντι σοι, sicut apud Halicarnasseum, ὡς δὴ ἀκίνδυνον αὐτοῖς τὸ ἔργον ἐσόμενον pro ὡς ἀκινδύνῳ αὐτοῖς τῶν ἔργῳ ἐσομένῳ quasi res illis sine periculo esset futura, & apud Aristot. ὥσπερ ἐκ αὐτῷ χώραν τινὰ ὅσαν, quasi ei non esset aliqua regio. Sic recte capi potest illud Ephes. I. 18. πεφωτισμένους τῆς ὀφθαλμὲς τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, illuminatis oculis mentis ve- stræ; ut recte ibi Beza ipse explicuit, observante Ludov. de Dieu.

ἐθῶν τε) An gentes teneantur nostris institutis. καὶ ζητημάτων) Ut de divino afflatu, de resurrectione, de Messia.

Non illa tantum, sed generaliter ἔθη ceremo- nias, vel ritus Judæorum, & quæstiones circa ipsa Religionis placita designat, de quibus inter ipsas Judæorum sectas discrepantia erat.

## 26:5
v. 5. προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν) ἄνωθεν is the same as what was just ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς [HEBREW].

ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν) If only they are willing to testify to what they know.

κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν) See what was brought forward above at XXII. 3.

τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας) This word comes from the Thracians, as Plutarch teaches us. Its meaning, however, is neutral. James 1:26, 27; Colossians 2:18.

Paul speaks from the hypothesis of his adversaries, or κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον; he does not approve of Pharisaism. Camero thinks an allusion is made to the name Pharisee, which denotes not just any segregation, but a certain accurate and exact one, such as that of those who anxiously and scrupulously guard themselves against those things which are κοινὰ.

Latin:

v. 5. προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν) Idem est ἄνωθεν quod modo ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς [HEBREW].

ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν) Si modo quod norunt testari ve- lint.

κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν) Vide quæ allata supra XXII. 3.

τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας) Vox hæc à Thracibus venit, ut nos docet Plutarchus. Est autem significatio ejus media. Jac. I. 26. 27. Col. II. 18.

Loquitur Paulus ex adversariorum hypothesi, vel κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον, non approbat Pharisaïsmum. Camero allusionem fieri putat ad nomen Phari- sæi, quod non quamlibet segregationem, sed ac- curatam quandam & exactam notat, qualis eorum est, qui anxie & scrupulose sibi cavent ab iis, quæ sunt κοινὰ.

## 26:6
Vers. 6.

ἐπ᾿ ἐλπίδι τῆς πρὸς τὲς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης) He understands the hope of the resurrection, as above at XXIII. 6, XXIV. 15. God promised that He would be the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But they had nothing in this life above others, nor did they possess the land, except for burial: from this it was gathered that greater goods were reserved for them after this life. See what was said at Matthew 22:32.

ἕστηκα κρινόμενος) As if he were to say, on account of this I am a defendant. As above at XXIII. 6, below at 7, to stand is the position of defendants.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ἐπ᾿ ἐλπίδι τῆς πρὸς τὲς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης) In- telligit spem resurrectionis, ut supra XXIII. 6. XXIV. 15. promisit Deus se futurum Deum Abrahami, Isaaci & Jacobi Illi autem in hac vita nihil supra cæteros habuere, nec res soli possederunt, præterquam ad sepulturam: inde colli- ge batur majora illis bona post hanc vitam reservari. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. XXII. 32.

ἕστηκα κρινόμενος) Quasi dicat ob id reus sum. Ut supra XXIII. 6. infra 7. stare est reorum.

## 26:7
Verse 7.

τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ὑμῶν) Luke coined a new word with Greek freedom, quite elegantly: just as Clement also said δωδεκά- σκηπτρον regarding the same matter in his epistle. Moreover, Paul took the tribe of Joseph as split into two for one, so that we might not think the Levites were passed over.

That hope of the resurrection and of the blessed life made to the Israelites was promised to the Fathers through Christ: thus Paul teaches that he is not a seditious person, nor an apostate from the law and faith of the Fathers: because he preaches faith in the promised Christ, through whom all the Fathers hoped for salvation. Capellus notes here that not all the men of the ten tribes were led away captive by the King of the Assyrians, but that the dregs of the common people and the miserable rabble remained, a great part of whom joined themselves to the Jews under King Josiah, 2 Chronicles 34:7, 35:3, 17. And under Ezra 6:17, 8:35, who were dispersed under Ahasuerus in 120 regions together with the Jews: indeed, even in Paul's time, many, without doubt, from those ten tribes had been joined to the Jews in religion, who had returned to Judea at different times, namely in lower and upper Galilee, and the whole of Perea, Gilead, Trachonitis, and Batanea.

ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι) That is, to arrive, as above 16:1, 18:19, 24, 20:15, 21:7, 25:13. It is a frequent word in Polybius.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ὑμῶν) Græca libertate novam vocem finxit Lucas, concinne admodum: quomodo & δωδεκά- σκηπτρον de re eadem dixit in epistola Clemens. Josephi autem tribum bipartitam pro una Paulus sumpsit, ne præ- teritos putemus Levitas.

Spes illa resurrectionis & vitæ beatæ Israëli- tis facta per Christum Patribus promissum: docet ita Paulus se non esse seditiosum, nec apostatam à lege & fide Patrum: quia prædicat fidem in Christum promissum, per quem omnes Patres salutem sperarunt. Notat hic Capellus, non o- mnes omnino decem tribuum homines ab Assy- riorum Rege captivos abductos, fecem plebis & miserum vulgus remansisse, quorum magna pars sub Josia Rege Judæis se junxerit 2. Chronic. XXXIV. 7. c. XXXV. 3. 17. Et sub Esdr. VI. 17. c. VIII. 35. qui sub Asvero in 120. regionibus disper- si una cum Judæis: imo Pauli adhuc tempore multi, procul ambiguo, ex illis decem tribubus Judæis in religione adjuncti fuerint, qui diversis temporibus in Judæam redierint, utpote in Ga- lilæa inferiore & superiore, totaque Peræa, Ga- laad, Trachonitide, & Batanæa.

ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι) Id est, pervenire, ut supra XVI. 1. XVIII. 19. 24. XX. 15. XXI. 7. XXV. 13. Est vox apud Po- lybium frequens.

## 26:8
Verse 8.

τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ᾽ ὑμῖν) [HEBREW]. You have that way of speaking in Zechariah 8:6.

There is no need, as with Beza from the Greek Scholia, for these to be distinguished thus: τί; ἄπιστον κρίνεται; What? is it judged incredible, etc.

εἰ ὁ Θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει) εἰ, for ὅτι after the manner of the Hebrew כִּי. Gen. XLVII. 9. Ps. LXIII. 7. CXXXIX. 10. Num. III. 30. Isa. IV. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ᾽ ὑμῖν) [HEBREW]. habes id loquendi genus apud Zach. VIII. 6.

Non opus est, ut cum Beza è Græcis Scholiis hæc ita distinguantur τι; ἄπιστον κρίνεται; Quid? incredibile judicatur, &c.

εἰ ὁ Θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει) εἰ, pro ὅτι ad modum Hebræi כִּי. Genef. XLVII. 9. Pfal. LXIII. 7. CXXXIX. 10. Num. III. 30. Efaiæ IV. 5.

## 26:9
v. 9. ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι) I thought I ought to do many hostile things against the religion of Jesus of Nazareth; we have taken ὄνομα for religion several times.

The Syriac, Arabic, and Beza construe that ἐμαυτῷ with ἔδοξα, but the Vulgate and Erasmus do not construe it badly with the verb δεῖν; that I ought to do many contrary things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth. For this verb also occurs with the dative: e.g., in Aristotle in the Problems, δεῖ τῷ πυρὶ διελθεῖν τὰς ἅλας, it is necessary for the fire to pass through the salts.

Latin:

v. 9. ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι) Videbar mihi debere multa ho- stilia facere adversus Religionem Jesu Nazareni, ὄνομα pro religione habuimus aliquories.

Illud ἐμαυτῷ Syrus, Arabs, & Beza cum ἔδο- ξα, sed non male Vulgata & Erasmus cum verbo δεῖν construunt; me debere adversus nomen Je- su Nazareni multa contraria agere. Nam & cum Dativo occurrit hoc verbum: E. g. apud Aristot. in Probl. δεῖ τῷ πυρὶ διελθεῖν τὰς ἅλας, necesse est ignem subire sales.

## 26:10
v. 10. καὶ πολλούς τε ἁγίων ἐγὼ φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα, τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβὼν) see above IX. 2. XXII. 5.

ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον) Aeschines also uses ψῆφον φέρειν by catachresis for to approve, the meaning being transferred from the orator to other things. He says this to mean that he approved of the killing of Stephen with his whole heart, in words and deeds. See above XXII. 20. and it is the plural for the singular as often. See at Matt. IX. 8.

The same is noted by Beza, since besides Stephen no one is read to have been harmed by the Jews before Paul's conversion, not even in a riot: but that enallage of number, which Cornelius à Lapide calls violent here, is not easily to be admitted. Although therefore more are not expressly read to have been killed: yet here it is taught that more were killed: and the same is hinted at Acts IX. 1. But Saul, still breathing out threats and slaughter. καταφέρειν ψῆφον is not to cast a vote, because in that tumultuous action votes were not asked for when the Protomartyr was stoned, but it is simply to assent; the Syriac and Arabic have I associated myself with those who condemned them.

Latin:

v. 10. καὶ πολλούς τε ἁγίων ἐγὼ φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα, τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβὼν) supra IX. 2. XXII. 5.

ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον) ψῆφον φέρειν per κατάχρησιν etiam Æschines usurpat pro comprobare, à re tori ad alias translato significatu. Hoc dicit se Stephani in- terfectionem toto animo, verbis gestisque approbasse. Vi- de supra XXII. 20. & est plurale pro singulari ut sæpe. Vide ad Matth. IX. 8.

Notat idem & Beza, siquidem præter Stepha- num nullus à Judæis legatur ante Pauli conversio- nem læsus, ne per tumultum quidem: Sed non facile admittenda illa enallage numeri, quam hic violentam dicit Cornelius à Lapide. Licet ergo diserte plures non legantur occisi: hic tamen pu- res occisos esse docetur: idemque innuitur Act. IX. 1. Saulus autem adhuc spirans ruinarum & cædis. καταφέρειν ψῆφον non est calculum addere, quia in illa tumultuaria actione suffragia rogata non sunt, cum lapidaretur Protomartyr, sed simpliciter est assentiri; Syrus & Arabs habent associavi me iis qui condemnaverunt eos.

## 26:11
v. 11. καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐ- τοὺς) Causing them to be beaten with rods. Above XXII. 19.

ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν) I was compelling them to curse Christ.

περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς) As if inflamed with fury against them.

ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις) For ἐν ταῖς ἔξω πόλεσι. In cities outside Judea, such as Damascus was.

Latin:

v. 11. καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐ- τοὺς) Faciens eos flagris cædi Supra XXII. 19.

ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν) Cogebam eos Christo maledi- cere.

περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς) In eos velut furore ac- census.

ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις) Pro ἐν ταῖς ἔξω πόλεσι. In urbi- bus extra Judæam, qualis erat Damascus.

## 26:12
v. 12. κᾀ ἐπιτροπῆς) In the Glossary: ἐπιτροπή, πραγμάτων φροντίς. procuration.

Latin:

v. 12. κᾀ ἐπιτροπῆς) In Glossario: ἐπιτροπή, πραγμάτων φροντίς. procuratio.

## 26:13
Vers. 13.

midday) See above XXII. 6.

above the brightness of the sun) If the face of Christ acting on earth shone like the sun, Matt. XVII. 2, it was fitting that it should shine more now that he is reigning in heaven. And if the righteous shall shine as the sun: Dan. XII. 13. Matt. XIII. 43, how much more the Prince of all the righteous?

Latin:

Vers. 13.
