V. 27. ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ) Sequitur Lucas LXX. Interpretes Es. VI. 10. ut solet: tantum post τῦς ὀφθαλμοὺς addidit αὐτῶν. De sensu vide quæ dicta ad Matth. XIII. 15. Quantū vero in- duruerint Judæi post rejectum Evangelium, vide ad Rom. 2. v. 28. ὅτι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπεστάλη τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ) In Manusc. τοῦτο τὸ σωτήριον. Σωτήριον substantive, est Hellenistica vox ut Es. XII. 3. c. XXVI. 1. c. XXXIII. 20. c. XXXIIX. 11. c. LX. 6. 18. c. LXI. 10. c. LXII. 1. c. LXIII. 1. 1 Sam. II. 1. 1. Par. XVI. 23. in Psalm. sæpissime. Refertur interdum ad personam, ut Luc. II. 30. modo ad rem, ut hic ad sermonem Evangelii, Potuerat Deus ad gentes eum sermonem mittere, etiamsi nihil pec- cassent Judæi. Sed omnem illis querelam præcidit, cum id non fecit, nisi postquam Judæi plurimi id beneficium sibi oblatum contempserant. Vide supra c. XIII. 46. c. XIIX. 6. Alii hoc etiam de persona accipiunt, & Christum qui σωτήριον frequenter dicitur, intelligunt, cum Basilio in Psal. LXX. & August. l. I. contr. advers. leg. & Proph. c. XV. Σωτήριον γὰρ ἔθος ὀνομάζειν τῇ γραφῇ τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ait Basilius. Salutare enim nominare consuevit Scriptura Christum Dei. αὐτοὶ

αὐτοὶ κῂ ἀκύσονται) Ipsi non audient tantum, sed & obe- dient. Nam ἀκύειν obedienti sensu hic ponitur, ut sæpissime שמע apud Hebræos, quod modo per ἀκύειν, modo per ὑπακύειν vertitur. Sic ἀκύειν habemus cum accusativo Matth. XI. v. 14. alibi cum genitivo, ut Matth. XVIII. 15. 16. Luc. VI. 47. 1. Petr. IV. 6. Quod expertus erat Paulus in multis Asiæ & Europæ urbibus, ut apud gentes sermonis felicior esset seges, idem & nunc futurum prospiciebat.

Adscribimus quæ de positu particulæ κῂ habet Lud. de Dieu: Data opera videtur mihi Evangelista, majoris emphaseos gratia, κῂ post posuisse, quod ser- vandum arbitror, ac vertendum, illi etiam audient. Syrus efficaciter, illi enim etiam audient. Arabs ha- bet, quæ vertenda sunt, scitote igitur nunc hoc, quod ad gentes missa est hæc salus, salus Dei, ut illi obediant ei. Id emphasin valde imminuit. Hæc Dievius.

## 28:29
v. 29. πολλὴν ἔχοντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ζήτησιν) ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, that is, among themselves. ζήτησιν, that is, a dispute, with one defending what another was accusing. ζήτησις is taken in this way in 1 Tim. I. 4, ch. VI. 4, 2 Tim. II. 23, Tit. III. 19, which is συζήτησις in Acts XV. 2, 7. But this whole clause, just as it was not in the Greek codices which the Syriac and Arabic used, so it does not appear in that old manuscript either.

This conclusion is not firm, that these things were missing from the Greek codices which the Syriac and Arabic used, because they do not appear now in these versions. For they could have fallen out of the versions more easily than from the original text itself.

Latin:

v. 29. πολλὴν ἔχοντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ζήτησιν) ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, id est, inter se. ζήτησιν, id est, disputationem alio defendente, quod alius accusabat. ζήτησις sic sumitur, 1. Tim. I. 4. c. VI. 4. 2. Tim. II. 23. Tit. III. 19. quod συζήτησις Act. XV. 2. 7. Sed comma hoc totum, sicut non fuit in codicibus Græcis, quibus usi sunt Sy- rus & Arabs, ita nec in vetere illo Manuscripto comparet.

Non est firma hæc collectio, defuisse hæc in Co- dicibus Græcis, quibus usi sunt Syrus & Arabs, quia nunc non comparent in his versionibus. Facilius enim excidere potuere è versionibus, quam ipso textu originario.

## 28:30
v. 30. διετίαν ὅλην) We had this word also above in ch. XXIV. 28, and τριετίαν above in ch. XX. 31. Others use them as well.

From that time, which begins around the vernal equinox, Paul lived in Rome for two years in a house rented by himself, with a soldier guarding him, preaching the Gospel of Christ without any hindrance; and in the same place, Paul, now fifty years old, wrote several epistles, namely, to the Galatians, to the Ephesians by Tychicus, to the Philippians by Epaphroditus, to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus, to Philemon by Onesimus, and to the Hebrews by Timothy, as Bünting has it in his Itinerarium, p. 242. But especially the Philippians comforted Paul, sending Epaphroditus to him with money, so that they might provide for his needs, for which he gave thanks to them by letter. Onesimus also came to him from Iconium to minister to him, 2 Tim. I. 16.

ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι) In his own rented place. It is called his own by reason of use. The word 'rented' in this sense is in L. 1. §. si filius familias, and §. Habitare, D. de his qui effuderint. Thus in the Lex Cornelia, Ulpian extends the word 'his house' to a rented one. L. lex Cornelia. D. de injuriis; which the Institutes follow, tit. de injuriis, §. sed & Lex. So also 'hospitium' is called someone's house, L. 1. §. 2. D. de agnoscendis liberis. And 'his house,' that is, every domicile, L. Nec in ea. D. ad legem Juliam de adulteriis §. Jus.

Therefore, some Latin codices read 'conductus' incorrectly.

Latin:

v. 30. διετίαν ὅλην) Hanc vocem habuimus & supra c. XXIV. 28. & τριετίαν supra c. XX. 31. Utuntur & alii.

Ab eo tempore, quod circa æquinoctium vernale inchoatur, Paulus Romæ vixit biennium in ædibus à se conductis, cum milite ipsum custodiente, sine ullo impedimento Evangelium de Christo prædi- cans; Ibidemque Paulus jam quinquagenarius ali- quot Epistolas scripsit, ad Galatas videlicet, ad Ephesios per Tychicum, ad Philippenses per Epa- phroditum, ad Colossenses per Tychicum & Onesi- mum, ad Philemonem per Onesimum, & ad Hebræos per Timotheum, ut habet Bünting. in itiner. p. 242. Imprimis vero Philippenses Paulum consolati sunt, mittentes ad eum Epaphroditum cum pecu- nia, ut necessitatibus ejus subvenirent, quibus per Epistolam gratias egit. Venit quoque Iconio ad eum Onesimus, ut ei ministraret 2. Tim. I. 16.

ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι) In suo conducto. Suum dicitur ratione usus. Conducti vox in hoc sensu est L. 1. §. si filius familias, & §. Habitare, D. de his qui effuderint. Sic in lege Cornelia ver- bum domus suæ Ulpianus extendit ad conductum. L. lex Cornelia. D. de injuriis; quod sequuntur Institutiones tit. de injuriis, §. sed & Lex. Sic & hospitium, domus alicujus dicitur L. 1. §. 2. D. de agnoscendis liberis. Et domus sua, id est omne domicilium L. Nec in ea. D. ad legem Juliam de adulteriis §. Jus.

Perperam ergo Latini quidam Codices legunt conductus.

## 28:31
V. 31. κῂ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους πρὸς αὐτὸν) He excluded no one, following the example of God.

κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ) That kingdom which will come at the end of the ages.

κῂ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ) As above v. 23, τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, his miracles and precepts, and death, and resurrection, and the mission of the Holy Spirit, through which men were made certain of that heavenly kingdom.

μετὰ πάσης παῤῥησίας) With an intrepid spirit.

ἀκωλύτως) In the Glossary, ἀκωλύτως: unimpeded. This happened in the first five-year period of Nero, during which he acted as a plausible Prince.

It is added that Paul, by divine grace, won over to himself the household of Nero, as appears from Phil. IV. 22: All the saints salute you, especially those who are of Caesar's house: just as also in Phil. I. 13 he says that his bonds and the faith and preaching of Christ were made known in all the praetorium. Therefore Paul planted the Roman Church, whence Marsilius of Padua in the Defender of the Peace asserted that Saint Paul was Bishop of Rome, not Saint Peter, for the reason that Luke says Paul spent two years in Rome, but does not mention Peter: Clement l. VII. Constit c. 46. teaches that Linus was appointed Bishop of the Roman Church not by Peter, but by Paul.

Latin:

V. 31. κῂ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τὸς εἰσπορευομένως πρὸς αὐτὸν) Neminem excludebat, Dei exemplo.

κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τῦ Θεῦ) Regnum illud, quod adveniet fine seculorum.

κῂ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τῦ κυρίε Ἰησῦ χριστῦ) Ut supra v. 23. τὰ περὶ τῦ Ἰησῦ, miracula ejus & præcepta, & mortem, & re- surrectionem & missionem Spiritus S. per quæ certi fiebant homines de regno illo cœlesti.

μετὰ πάσης παῤῥησίας) Animo intrepido.

ἀκωλύτως) In Glossario, ἀκωλύτως :improhibito. Evenit hoc primo Neronis quinquennio, intra quod Principem egit probabilem.

Accedit quod Paulus sibi conciliavit divina gra- tia familiares Neronis, ut è Phil. IV. 22. apparet: Sa- lutant vos omnes sancti, maxime qui de Cæsaris domo sunt: quemadmodum etiam Phil. I. 13. dicit vincula sua fidemque & prædicationem Christi nota facta fuis- se in omni prætorio. Plantavit ergo Paulus Romanam Ecclesiam, unde Marsilius de Padua in defensore Pacis S. Paulum Episcopum Romæ fuisse asseruit, non S. Petrum, eo quod Lucas Paulum biennio Romæ versatum dicat, Petri vero non meminerit: Clemens l. VII. Constit c. 46. Linum Romanæ Ecclesiæ Epi-
